    Chapter 3

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes They separate after that, Yelena going back to her hotel and Kate swinging by her apartment to pick Lucky up, and take him for a walk. The retriever and her stroll at a leisurely pace to Central Park, and she is happy for the opportunity to clear her head a little. The park is full of people and dogs, and life, and she feels the peacefulness of it overcome her, like a soothing balm. Kate lets herself be preoccupied by people-watching, while keeping an eye on Lucky playing with two other dogs.

    She thinks about what Yelena told her. She tried asking Clint a few times, but Natasha is not something he likes to discuss, even with her. Sometimes, after a few glasses of whisky, he will tell a story or two, but it usually signals that the evening is close to ending, because he usually gets quiet afterwards, disappearing into his head.

    What Yelena revealed at breakfast, even if it was only a little fragment of information, was simply put, heartbreaking. She wonders how old Yelena was when she was sent to Ohio, if she was already trained by then, or if she had no idea at all, that her family was all just a lie. If the latter is the case, it’s even more harrowing.

    She had her own fair share of childhood trauma, but being torn from the only family you know, only to be put into a horrifying, cruel place like the Red Room…Maybe that’s why Yelena shared the truth with her about her mother when they first met, not wanting her to go through not knowing her family has been a lie as well, even if in a different way. The situation sounds like it would turn anyone into a murderous psychopath, especially if that was what they were trained for their entire life. Yet the blonde isn’t that. Yes, she kicked Kate’s ass multiple times, but she never once tried to kill her, even going out of her way not to. Even when Kate was standing in the way of her getting the justice she thought her sister deserved. She remembers what the blonde told her, during their weird mac and cheese dinner, about how actions matter, not pretty words. Yelena’s actions showed her the kind of person Yelena is.

    And it is further reinforced by the fact that she is here, helping Kate. She feels a bit embarrassed at the little pity party she threw herself the evening before. Of course, she knows she can’t compare herself to others’ experience, but it seems pretty lame to spiral over the fact that she is lonely, when she is already so fortunate compared to others. She thinks it’s a cliché, but she doesn’t care and starts watching an old couple on one of the benches, feels her gaze being drawn to them, again and again. They sit next to each other, their hands joined on the bench between them, but they say nothing. They just enjoy the warm, late August sun and each other’s company.

    Her thoughts turn back to her date yesterday. Of course, she is not a walking stereotype. She does not imagine growing old with Amanda after one date just by looking at an old couple, but considers the possibility, of having a relationship, at least. Having her life, it’s always going to be hard, but shouldn’t she try at least? Having something meaningful? She loves her Pizza Dog dearly, but she thinks it would be nice to arrive home to someone, who can know her in and out and understand her struggles.

    She thinks of Yelena again for a second, and she wonders if she has someone like that in Ohio. She barely knows anything about the woman, but hearing the story she told, seeing her beautiful, sad face as she retold it, she thinks Yelena deserves it.

    Kate truly doesn’t know what to make of her, and thinks she is like a cat. She is playful one second, and serious and lethal in the next, always making her feel like she is balancing on the edge of a knife.

    She wonders if Natasha was like this, and she longs to talk to Clint. Without thinking, she dials his number. For once it doesn’t go to voicemail, and he picks up on the third ring. “Hey Kid, how are you doing?”

    She is happy to be hearing his gravelly voice.

    “Hi Clint! Lucky and I are at the park, and I thought I would call you.” “Oh how is the garbage-muncher?”

    “He is good. Trying to feed him less garbage nowadays”

    He chuckles at her answer.

    “Did I hear about a date on my voicemail yesterday?”

    “Yeah…uh…it went well, I think?”

    “You think? That does not sound very promising…”

    His tone teasing and she laughs, despite the mixed feelings she has about the topic now. “No! I mean it went well. She was…it was great...”

    “What’s her name?”

    “Amanda.”

    She is quiet afterwards, and her partner can tell something is wrong. Kate is rarely quiet. “What’s wrong?”

    They’ve talked about this before, and she knows the broad strokes of his opinion, but she wants to hear his advice, or hopefully, his encouragement that it is possible, that she is not selfish for wanting someone to share her life with. He doubts he will say what she wants to her, but she explains to him nonetheless.

    “I just, I don’t know. How do you make it work with what we do?”

    Clint is silent, so she pushes on.

    “We can’t all find a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent to settle down with, okay? How do you know if it’s a good idea to involve someone in any of this?”

    “One date and you are ready to settle down, Kate?”

    He tries to avoid the topic by teasing her but she knows he understood what she was asking. She puts Lucky on a leash, and continues walking through the park, while she waits for him to answer her actual question. He needs a few moments to gather his thoughts, before he answers.

    “I…I told you what I think before, Kate. This life comes with sacrifices.” She lets out a frustrated sigh. She knows he’s lost a lot, but he has someone come home to. He is not alone. She clenches her teeth together, exhaling.

    “Are you saying it shouldn’t be done? That we…I should just accept being alone?” “Obviously, I don’t. My family…they make me so much stronger than who I was without them. You know that. But…” he weighs his words before continuing ”…I think you have to consider, that if you bring someone into your life, they will be in danger. You have to accept that, and they have to accept that, too. And more than that, they have to understand it as well. Not everyone can.”

    Kate considers his words. For someone to understand, they have to know. Know about Kate, her “job”, her disgraced family, all of it. She sighs deeply, and Clint waits for her to answer. She will have to think about this more, before she can make a decision. “Alright Clint, thanks for your advice.”

    “It’s not what you wanted to hear.”

    He doesn’t phrase it like a question.

    “It’s not, but I asked for it. And you may have a point.”

    “Maay?!”

    “Don’t push it.” She says, her voice back to a lighter tone. He chuckles. “Anyways, kid, Nate is making a huge mess in the living room. Can I help with anything else?”

    She considers telling him about the whole “Fisk hired a bunch of assassins to kill me” ordeal, but decides against it. He really deserves his rest on his ranch, and she can always call him in later, if things get more serious.

    “Nope. All good here, thanks. I’ll leave you to it…Oh wait, there is one thing. Yelena is back.”

    She passes the old couple she was surveying earlier, smiling at them when they look up at her.

    “Yelena?? How come?”

    “Oh, she is just…she is helping me with something.”

    “Work related?”

    His concern is coming through the speaker as clearly, as if he was standing next to her. “Yeah. But nothing for you to worry about.”

    “Alright, Kid. But please let me know if you need my help.”

    “Sure thing.”

    “Okay…Well, have a nice Sunday! Take care!”

    “You too!”

    They hang up, and she continues her walk, letting Lucky decide which way they go. She doesn’t know if Clint is right about the whole thing, but he is definitely right about the fact that she can’t pull anyone into “this” blindly. It’s not something she didn’t know before, but she thinks she has a bit more clarity than before.

    She stops by a fountain to let Lucky have a sip of water, before they continue their journey. She pulls out her phone again, and looks at the “Good morning :)” text Amanda sent her a few hours earlier. She hasn’t made her mind up yet, but she sends a text saying “To you too :)”, because she doesn’t want to close any doors, until she had a time to make a decision. She considers her current predicament. What is she supposed to do?

    There are a little over 2 months until her mother’s trial is set to start. That gives the assassins plenty of time to finish their job, and she doesn’t think she either wants or even can hide for that long. She could leave the city, go back to LA, or even to Ohio with Yelena, but she meant what she said last night.

    This is her life, her demons, and she already spent too much time running away from them. And well, if hiding or running away is not possible, that leaves her with one option. To fight back.

    All she has to do is convince Yelena to help her.

    Her and Lucky stroll around the park for another 35 minutes, before heading home. She is deep in thought the whole time, and by the time she gets home, she thinks she knows what she has to do, if she wants any kind of normalcy back in her life. Or to have her life back, at all.

    She feeds Lucky, and sits down on her couch, scrolling through her contacts. [to Yelena] 1:23 pm: Can you come over?

    She doesn’t receive a reply, but there is a knock on her front door approximately five minutes later. She checks through the peephole, confirming it’s her, before opening it with a grin. “Look at you, knocking on the door like a normal person…”

    The blonde struts inside, while Kate continues.

    “…isn’t this nicer than breaking and entering?”

    Yelena turns to her with an expression that she is pretty sure is only pretending to be serious, and opens her arms.

    “Then how would I witness your hilarious attempts to protect yourself?” Kate crosses her arms, and feigns to be offended.

    “Hilarious? Wow Yelena, that really hurts my feelings.”

    “Well, I am not sorry. What would you call someone throwing a bottle of hot sauce at you? And then the pizza cutter last night? What was that even about…”

    “I don’t know! Resourceful! Quick on her feet!”

    Yelena gives up the serious façade, and snickers at her, her nose scrunching up. “It was very funny, you have to admit.”

    Kate grins back, dropping her offended act as well.

    “Fine, it might not have been my finest moment. Whatever.”

    “Did you ask me to come over to discuss your failures as a superhero person…because if yes, I am happy to give you some pointers.”

    Kate shakes her head with a laugh.

    “You are such an asshole”

    It slips out without her thinking about it but Yelena just grins at her, shrugging a little. “I know! It’s fun isn’t it?”

    “That’s one word for it…” she mutters, making sure the blonde hears it. She walks back to the couch and sits down. Yelena follows, taking a seat in the armchair across from her.

    “Anyways, no. I asked you over because I have a plan.”

    Yelena sobers up, tilts her head to the side, waiting.

    “I’m listening.”

    Kate takes a deep breath, mentally preparing herself.

    “Well, there are two months until my mom’s trial, and I don’t want to just sit here and wait for Fisk to take me out. So…I say, we take the fight to him, and get him before he can get me.”

    She says it in one breath essentially, words flowing out quick even for herself. “That is a shit plan.”

    “But…”

    “I am in.”

    “You are??”

    Honestly, Kate expected having to do a lot more convincing. Then again, she is mostly used to having to argue with Clint, who always wants to think before throwing punches. “Yes. You are sitting duck like this…”

    “Hey!”

    Yelena barrels on as if she didn’t interrupt her.

    “I still think going away is smarter, but if you must stay, it makes no sense just to wait for him to get you killed.”

    “Okay, apart from the obvious disregard of my fighting skills, I expected having to do a lot more convincing. This is very anti-climactic.”

    “…sorry?”

    Yelena’s face is amused, her sentence ending a pitch higher. Kate is picking at her fingernails, as if she is truly miffed.

    “I had a whole speech prepared.”

    “You can still say it. I can pretend to be against it.”

    “No, no. It’s fine.”

    There is a moment of silence. Yelena looking at her, expectantly.

    “What?”

    “You said you had a plan.”

    “Yeah, us going against Kingpin.”

    “That is not a plan. That is like a step zero of a plan.“ “Well, I expected more resistance. I didn’t get there yet.”

    Yelena is looking at her like she is trying to decide if she is seriously this dumb. Okay, Kate, think.

    “Well. I haven’t been in New York for a while, but I’m pretty sure he is in hiding…we should look into his known associates, see if any of them lead us to him.”

    “Okay, that sounds more like a step 1 of plan.”

    They spend the next few hours, putting together a list of known associates of Fisk’s. Many of them are dead, some of them are as untouchable as he is. The only names they come up with, that they can maybe use, at least for now, is Maya, and Fisk’s wife, Vanessa Marianna. Kate wheels out two big whiteboards from her storage unit downstairs, and they tape a huge map of New York to one of them, while they start filling up the other with names of the known associates, and any information they can find out and deem usable. By 10 pm, they stand back from the boards, satisfied.

    “Okay, now it’s only putting the information on the map too, and then we can start legwork tomorrow.”

    Kate nods to herself and turns to Yelena, who speaks without looking at her. “Do you want to finish tonight?”

    “Yeah. I will take Lucky out for a bathroom break, then we can do the last bit. How do you feel about burgers for dinner?”

    “You want to make burgers? Now?”

    Yelena scrunches up her face, confused. Kate is looking at her, trying to see if she is serious. She really just can’t with this woman sometimes.

    “Uh…no? I meant I’ll pick some up while we are out.”

    “Oh okay. In that case, yes to the burgers.”

    The brunette still can’t decide if the blonde is pulling her leg or not. “Oookay. We’ll be back in twenty minute tops.”

    She feels a bit weird, leaving Yelena back in her apartment, but if they are going to be working together, this is bound to happen. It’s not like the other woman wasn’t in her apartment without her before. She grabs her things, Pizza Dog’s leash, and opens the door. “Come on Lucky, let’s go for a walk.”

    The golden retriever is off the couch, and speeding by her in a second. Kate smiles at his enthusiasm, glances at Yelena one last time, who is back to staring at the board, and then they are off.

    She clips his leash on in the elevator and when they reach the ground floor, instead of turning right towards Central Park like they usually do, they walk towards the small burger place a couple of blocks from her place.

    The streets are empty now, at least as unpopulated as they get in New York, only a couple of people walking around, most of them at home on a Sunday evening. She keeps track of her surroundings, but she is also preoccupied by thinking about all the information they have gather tonight. Back in LA, walks with Lucky always helped her process the details of her ongoing cases, and she feels herself slip into that focused headspace again. Lucky and her reach Burger Frog in 10 minutes, and thanks to the late hour, they don’t have to wait in line to be served. She buys a cheeseburger for herself, and after a few moments of consideration, chooses a spicy one for Yelena, remembering her love of hot sauce, and some fries and sodas for the both of them. She pays for their food, and they exit the restaurant when she sees it.

    There is a car running across from them, its lights turned off.

    She counts 4 men inside, and while she pretends to check her phone, she glances at them and confirms that yes, in fact, they are all looking at her, even if most of their faces are obscured in the darkness of the car.

    She doesn’t know how they could have found her. Despite Clint and Yelena constantly treating her otherwise, she is not an amateur. Her apartment is not on her name, and she intentionally avoided getting into contact with anyone that she used to know here, apart from Jack. It’s possible they just happened to luck upon her, she guesses. She considers her options.

    She doesn’t know for sure that her address is compromised, but she only brought her sword along again, for this short trip, no bow or arrows. She also has Lucky with her, which makes disappearing a lot harder. She sees 4 guys only, but there could be more, and they don’t look like Tracksuit Mafia members, so she has no clue about training or capabilities. She also has no vehicle, and there is no way she can hotwire a car without drawing attention to herself. This is not ideal.

    She needs to lose these guys, and get back to her place, asap. (And bring her bow with her, from now on).

    Instead of going straight back where she came from, her and Lucky start walking in a roundabout way towards Central Park. The park is dark, or at least some parts of it are, and they have a better chance at disappearing there. It also gives her a chance to see if they will follow, or if more of them are on her tail.

    The car doesn’t immediately pull out after her, but she sees it move in the side mirror of a parked car as Lucky and her turn a corner, and it keeps following them from a distance as they make their way to the park entrance.

    She takes Lucky off leash when they enter, and prays that he will listen to her when she tells him to run home. They walk on a dimly lit path for a few minutes, and although she hasn’t seen the car, or any of the men since she entered the park, she is on high alert. Suddenly, there is a clattering noise at her feet.

    She looks down, and sees some sort of device and although she doesn’t know what it is, she does not hesitate to kick it away and jumping onto her dog to shield him. The device activates in the air, a few feet away from them, but the only way she can tell is because there is a searing, throbbing pain in her ears, and a second later she can’t hear anything. She can’t hear Lucky as he fights his way off from under her, sprinting away to disappear in the dark park, even though she thinks he must be whining and screaming in terror. She is disoriented and her ears and head hurts so much. She tries to shake her head to get rid of the pain, covering her ears, and it’s slowly easing up, but she still can’t hear a single thing. She doesn’t hear for example the two man running up to her, but she sees their boots moving in her direction. She quickly gets to her feet, swaying for half a second, but managing to get into a defensive position just in time.

    They are on her half a second later. One of them attempts to barrel into her, but she quickly gets out of his way, tripping him up, while attempting to deliver a swift jab at the other. He dodges quickly, and she sees a glint of silver in his hand. He has a knife. He slashes at her, and she jumps out of the way, reaching into her back pocket to retrieve her retractable sword, but has no time to open it. The man says something, but she still can’t hear what and it becomes clear that he wasn’t speaking to her a second later when she feels a searing pain in her side.

    A strong ass kick to her ribs, delivered by one of the two other guys who arrived from behind her.

    She is thrown to the side, from the force of the kick, hitting her head against a tree trunk, and she feels her skin get teared, the pain sharp and disorienting. She uses the momentum to roll forward, away from her attackers.

    She arrives in a crouch, clicking the button on her sword and the blade releases instantly, even if she can’t hear the click this time. She holds the blade in front of her body, sizing up her attackers.

    The one on the left is a huge chunk of a guy. He is at least a head taller than Kate, and a dark beard covers most of his place. His arms are covered in tattoos, and he has a retractable metal pole in his hand. The other two are smaller than him, but still bigger than her. Both of them have dark blonde hair, one of them short, the other’s a bit longer, hanging into his eyes. Wait. Wasn’t there a fourth guy?

    She whips her head around to see where he went, after she tripped him up and they are all on her in one instant. The fourth man attempts to kick her from behind but she quickly slips out from his way, slicing his leg up with the movement and sending an elbow into his face, catching his nose from below. It produces a crunch, that she can feel despite not hearing. She dodges one of the blonde ones, grabbing his outstretched arm and using his momentum to push him against the dark haired one, delivering a long slash across the blonde man’s back, a mist of blood flying In the air, some of it landing on her.

    She thinks she can finally her a muffled scream.

    Fourth guy reaches to the back of his pants, and starts to pull out a gun, and because he is standing a several feet from her, she has no choice but to throw the sword at him. He jumps out of the way, but it nicks his neck a little and more importantly, it gives Kate a chance to tackle him to the ground.

    Her ribs are screaming at her, but she delivers one, two, three punches, breaking his nose and probably some of his teeth and thankfully, he passes out.

    She doesn’t have time to catch her breath, as she is torn from the unconscious man by a thick arm grabbing her around the neck, and yanking her up and backwards. The arm tightens around her neck, and she struggles but this is the huge dark haired man, holding her in a chokehold. Her heart beats furiously in her ears, and there are some small black spots floating into her vision.

    She uses both of her legs, to crouch, then jump up, pulling her knees up to her face and lands powerfully on his feet, destabilizing the beefcake. Using his moment of vulnerability to slip out of his hold, she kicks him swiftly in the leg from the side, and knees him in the face as collapses.

    He goes down with a satisfying grunt, she assumes.

    All 4 men lie in various states of ruin now. She looks around, quickly locating her sword, and her ribs burn when she leans to pick it up, closes it and slips it into the back pocket of her jeans. She limps to the paper bag holding their burgers, on the path where she dropped it in the beginning of the fight and where it remained thankfully untouched for the duration of it. She picks it up with a grunt too, and stops.

    Lucky.

    She quickly leaves the scene, limping towards where he ran away, and frantically looks around for him. She still can’t hear properly, and she constantly has to wipe her left eye because blood from her eyebrow keeps trickling down into it. Her heart still beats in her ears and she is panting and grunting with every step but she keeps stumbling forward, now calling his name.

    She can sort of hear her own voice again, but she is starting to panic about PD. He is chipped, of course, but there is no telling how far he has gotten in his panic. What if he got hit by a car in his panic to get away?

    She searches for him for what feels like forever, and she is on the verge of crying, when she stumbles upon the most peculiar sight she has ever seen.

    She is calling his name, when suddenly from ahead of the path, she sees a silhouette of a man and a dog jog towards her in the dark. She reaches into the back pocket of her jeans, to grab a hold of the retractable blade, just in case but when they pass by one of the lampposts ahead, she quickly lets go of it and starts limping forward as fast as she can. “Lucky!!” she yells, and it is him!

    It’s her perfect, dopey, beautiful Pizza Dog and….

    Spider-man?!

    The masked superhero is leading Lucky on what seems to be a leash made out of spider-web and Kate’s brain doesn’t really have the capacity to process that.

    They reach each other, and she is immediately on her knees, hugging her furry friend, while Spider-man stands next to them, still holding Lucky’s web-leash somewhat awkwardly. “Is this you dog?” she thinks she hears him say, and she kind of wants to look at him like are you serious? But she is so thankful and relieved that she just laughs and then immediately winces at the pain in her ribs.

    “Yes, yes. This is my Lucky.”

    She kisses his soft furry forehead before looking up at the superhero.

    “Wow. You are Spider-man.”

    He nods, and although obviously, she can’t see his face, he seems to be looking her over. “Are you okay?”

    There is something familiar in his voice, but Kate has had a way too long night to really place it, she can’t hear properly and honestly she is feels like 5 minutes from crashing. “Yes ugh…we were mugged…he got scared and ran away and I…uh…I also ran away and …fell down. Silly me.”

    Her ribs make it hard to speak in complete sentences, and Spider-man just keeps looking at her. She can see the doubt in his…posture, and quickly hides her bruised knuckles from his sight, but yeah, she is not going to come up with anything better than this story. She decides to go another route.

    “Thank you so much for finding him. I truly thought I lost him.”

    She stands up and steps closer to the hero, touching his arm. She attempts to make an adoring face, but probably due to half of her face being covered in blood and all around looking like a hot mess, it doesn’t have the desired effect. She can imagine Spider-man lifting an eyebrow behind his mask, looking at her like she is a crazy person. Or maybe he is gay, who is she to judge.

    “Ummm…no worries. He … really scared, and was …. to the road so I … him. We were … since.”

    She can only catch about half of what he says, his voice still sounding garbled, as if she is hearing it through a bad walkie-talkie. It seems it made him drop what happened to them, so she guesses her awkward attempt at flirting did have the desired effect after all. She pulls Lucky’s real leash from her beltloop, and clips it onto him, and waves an embarrassing goodbye to Spider-man, who returns it equally awkwardly. They walk (limp) towards the exit that is closest to Kate’s apartment, and she slowly becomes aware that Spider-man is following them. He doesn’t make any noise, or at least none that Kate can hear, but she catches his shadow move not much behind them.

    She doesn’t know if he still with them because he is suspicious or because he thinks they need protection, but she is thankful for it nonetheless. Her injuries are slowly starting to really register, and she needs to get home and address the wound on her head before she passes out from blood loss.

    They reach her building in about 10 very painful minutes, Lucky’s leash in one of her hands, the crumpled paper bag holding dinner in the other, and she gives a smile that probably looks more like a grimace to the horrified doorman.

    “Miss Derekson, are you okay?! Should I call an ambulance?”

    It’s good, she thinks, she can hear normally again, even if her ears ring a little still. She shakes her head at his concern, and attempts to chuckle but it comes out very breathy. “No…no Harman…thank you... Am good.”

    She finds it a bit hard to speak and just waves him away. She doesn’t have the mental capacity to even give an excuse and just limps her way to the elevator. Once inside, she leans against the wall of the cabin, and has to resist the urge to slide down to the floor and lie down there.

    They exit the elevator, and slowly make their to her door, and she kind of wants to cry when she has to dig out her keys from the pocket, that’s on the side of her injured ribs. She opens the door, the sound of the TV greeting her but Yelena is not in the living room. She lets Lucky in before herself, and then staggers inside, grunting.

    “You said it’s only a quick walk, Kate Bishop. It has been almost 2 hours…” Yelena rounds the corner from the direction of the kitchen, freezes at her sight for a few heartbeats, and then is beside her in a second.

    She takes the paper bag from her hands, tossing it on the table by the door and quickly loops Kate’s arm around her shoulder, noting how she moans out in pain when she grips her left side.

    “What happened?”

    She is steering Kate towards the bathroom, looking her over, taking note of her injuries. There are scratches on her left arm, her ribs and hips on the same side visibly painful, and the side of her face is practically covered in blood, possibly from the nasty gash that is still bleeding slightly on her forehead.

    “Got jumped on walk…I beat them back but Lucky ran away…Spider-man helped…bring him back.”

    She wheezes a little, and Yelena just nods, then pushes her down to sit on the edge of the bathtub. She winces as she does, and with very careful movements, pulls the sword from her back pocket, tossing it on the counter.

    “Do you have first aid kit?”

    Yelena’s face is serious, focused and she grunts out her answer.

    “Below the sink…to the right”

    The blonde takes the box out, and brings the towel over from beside the sink as well, passing it to Kate.

    “Put that on your head. The bleeding must stop before we can clean it.” She does as she is told. Yelena stands in front of her, and their eyes meet. “Where else are you hurt?”

    “Ribs…” is all she can wheeze out. Yelena nods.

    “Take your shirt off.”

    It’s so business-like, Kate chuckles to herself then winces at the sharp, throbbing pain it causes in her side.

    “At least…buy me…drink first.”

    She reaches down to take off the garment anyhow. The corners of Yelena’s lips twitch, but her eyes remain focused, even as she answers.

    “As far as I’m aware, you still owe me a drink first”

    Yelena reaches for the corner of her t-shirt to help. Kate lifts an eyebrow. “Do I?”

    She lifts her arms, winching as she does and Yelena pulls the shirt above her head, and suddenly she is sitting there, her sports bra the only thing covering her upper body. She puts the towel back to her forehead awkwardly with her right hand, her left arm cradling her injured side.

    “You asked me at Rockefeller Plaza, remember?”

    She leans down to examine Kate’s side which is already beginning to color to a nice, deep purple. She prods at her ribs gently, then not so gently.

    “Hmpf…I guess…I did. Ouch…Would you stop…poking me?”

    “Stop being a baby!”

    She practically growls at Yelena, and there is an amused glint in her eyes at Kate’s tone. “Stop it then!”

    “Okay, I think none of them are broken, but we should tape them anyway.” Yelena half-heartedly attempts to prod her side one more time, as she looks into her eyes, but Kate slaps her hand away with the towel in her hand, flinching again at the quick motion. Yelena snickers as she takes the purple kinesiology tape out from the first aid kit. Her face is serious again, when she looks at Kate, like she is trying to make a decision and Kate wants to ask what she is thinking about.

    Then it becomes apparent.

    Yelena puts a hand on both of her knees and opens her legs, and Kate’s heart is suddenly beating directly in her throat, for entirely different reasons than earlier tonight. Somehow, she doesn’t even consider to resisting.

    Yelena is not looking at her, as she kneels between her legs, focused on her side instead. Kate is very thankful, because she feels her face heating up, pretty sure she must be blushing. At least the blood covers up most of it. She hopes...

    She tells herself to get her mind out of the gutter, then the Yelena is gently pulling her arm away from her injured side, and thankfully the pain helps to distract her… from the fact Yelena is kneeling between her legs, and she is essentially half naked, and she can literally feel Yelena in front of her and…okay, maybe it doesn’t help enough.

    Despite her earlier jest, Yelena is very gentle, if a bit clinical in her handling of Kate’s side. She tapes the injured ribs, using the Kate’s left thigh to lean on, and she elects to stare ahead instead of Yelena’s ministrations, because this really shouldn’t feel as intimate as it does, especially an hour after she was beaten to a pulp.

    But Yelena’s fingertips are touching her ribs, and her whole body is covered in goosebumps, and god, she really needs some action if this is getting her flustered. Maybe it’s the adrenaline, she reasons with herself.

    It occurs to her suddenly that they have been quiet for a couple of minutes now, and she wants to say something because now she feels the silence is awkward, but she is pretty sure that anything that comes out of her mouth right now will make the situation more awkward, not less.

    Then it gets worse without her saying anything anyway.

    Yelena is finished with her side, her ribs taped very efficiently, and then her gaze is on Kate and she can’t not look back at her.

    “Let me see your head”

    She grabs Kate’s chin and turns it towards herself, examining the wound on her forehead. She takes the towel from Kate’s hand, gets up and wets it under the tap, and then she kneels back in her previous position. She uses the towel to wipe away the dried blood on the brunette’s face, her own intense in its focus.

    Kate realizes she has been holding her breath, and slowly, carefully starts to inhale, but that definitely does not help because now she can smell the Yelena. She smells like peaches, and some kind of sweet body wash. For God’s sake Kate, get a grip . She looks away quickly. Yelena leans back to the first aid kit on the floor to get some disinfectant, cotton buds and sterile gauze to clean her wound, using Kate’s leg as anchor an to hold onto, her fingers gripping the brunette’s thighs. She is back between her legs in a second, and somehow, impossibly, she is even closer than before, cleaning the cut above her eyebrow. Kate has been determined to stare straight ahead, but she is unable to not look at Yelena, when she is this close. She is focused on her wound, gently wiping away the blood dried around it, but then her gaze flits to the Kate’s.

    They look at each other for a second, Yelena pausing in her ministrations. It all feels so different from when her mom or Clint did it and Kate could swear there was a moment…but it’s gone before she could really take note of it. Yelena looks away and continues to clean her forehead, her focus back to her work. Until…

    “It is rude to stare, Kate Bishop.”

    Back to full names, okay. She clears her throat and goes back to looking ahead instead. God she feels exhausted.

    Yelena uses two butterfly clips, to pull the cut together, and applies some ointment to it from the kit. When she is finished with her head, the blonde stands up, offering her hand to Kate. “There, all done.”

    She takes it without thinking, and the Yelena pulls her up.

    She really did not think this through, because now their bodies are practically brushing together, she is only wearing a sports bra still and now, Yelena is looking up at her, from below long eyelashes, her eyes a darker shade of green in the artificial light of the bathroom. She noticed Yelena was shorter than her before, obviously, but from this close, it somehow feels like Kate towers over her. She stands several inches taller, her mouth basically in line with Yelena’s eyes, and who is still looking up at her, not moving, their hands they used to pull Kate up still clasped by their sides.

    Yelena holds her gaze for a moment longer, before tilting her head to the side, as if trying to figure out something. Then she steps over to the her side, sliding her hand around her waist and starts leading her to hobble towards her own bedroom.

    “You need to rest.”

    Kate just grunts again (from all the injuries she ever suffered, bruised ribs are always the worst), and she allows Yelena to help lead her to the bed and lies down on it with a wince. She unlaces Kate’s boots, and pulls them off and she would probably find this awkward, but she is truly on the verge of passing out from exhaustion.

    Yelena turns away, leaving the room before she comes back with some pills and a glass of water.

    “Take this and sleep. We will discuss what happened in the morning.”

    Sleep sounds like heaven right now. She takes the pills from the her hand, their fingers touching for a moment, then gulps down some water.

    Yelena nods, then turns to leave the room again.

    “I’ll stay here tonight. You are in no position to protect yourself.”

    Kate thinks that she should be surprised, but she is not. Despite being generally argumentative, and a (delightful) pain in her ass, the blonde has done nothing but help her since she arrived.

    “Yelena?”

    She stops before she can cross the threshold of the darkened bedroom, her profile illuminated by the light from the living room that streams inside, as she doesn't fully turns back towards Kate.

    “Yes?”

    “Thank you.”

    Yelena nods, and Kate already feels her body and eyelids getting heavy. “You are welcome.”

    Chapter End Notes So, I did a bunch of martial arts when I was a kid, and let me tell you, broken ribs? Truly a fucking bitch. :D You can't be comfortable in any position, breathing hurts, laughing hurts, I really would not recommend it to a friend. :D Anyways, I really hope you enjoy this chapter. As always, please feel free to leave a comment. :)

    Next one will be up in a couple of days, probably mid-week, but my girlfriend is back from a trip abroad tonight, so I might have a bit less time.

    Chapter 4

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Kate wakes up the next day, disoriented and unsure why she woke up in the first place. She looks down at herself, noting that she still lies on top of the covers, wearing her dusty, grass- stain covered jeans and her sports bra, her side covered in purple kinesiology tape. Then she notices the buzzing. That’s what woke her up. Her phone is ringing on her nightstand.

    She attempts to sit up and grab it and falls back to the bed with a painful groan. Come to think of it, her head is pounding like a motherfucker too. She shuffles her way to the side of the bed, and grabs the phone, picking it up without looking.

    “Hi!”

    A feminine voice greets her on the other end. Amanda.

    “Hi!” she answers, her voice a bit more breathy than usual.

    “I did not wake you up, did I?”

    Kate pulls the phone away from her face to check the time. It’s past noon. “Uh…no, no. I am just…working out.”

    She clears her throat, and manages to sit up, leaning against the headboard. “hmm…sounds nice.”

    The other woman’s voice is playful, and she smiles. Easy, she thinks.

    “How are you?”

    “Well, I am on my lunchbreak, and thought I would ask if you’d like to grab dinner sometime this week.”

    Kate imagines saying yes for a second, longing to go back to the simplicity of the Saturday night date they had, before Kingpin, and assassins and midnight fights in Central Park. She can’t though. Last night was a stark reminder that this is serious, that it’s only by sheer luck that Lucky didn’t get seriously hurt last night, that she only got mildly hurt. Her voice is apologetic when she answers.

    “I am actually out of town for work this week. Raincheck?”

    “Oh…okay.”

    Amanda sounds disappointed, and it’s awkward for a moment.

    “I’d really like to though.” Kate adds, because she really doesn’t want to hurt the other girl’s feelings. She is saying no precisely because she is trying to avoid Amanda getting hurt in the first place.

    “Me too.”

    There is a beat of silence before Amanda speaks again, her voice back to light and curious. “So, where are you right now?”

    “Umm…Chicago.”

    She lies, blurting out the first city that comes to her mind.

    “Oooh, go eat some delicious deep dish pizza for me.”

    Kate chuckles, and promises she will. They chat for a few more minutes, before Amanda’s lunchbreak is up, and she has to go back to work.

    Kate feels better and worse at the same time. She doesn’t like the lies, and all the complications, but speaking to a friendly voice was a nice way to start the day nonetheless. She gathers her strength and gets out of bed, putting on a shirt with some difficulty. She looks at herself in the mirror, and notes that despite Yelena cleaning her up yesterday, she is in dire need of a shower. There is dried blood and probably dirt in her hair, which is a mess anyway, sticking up in different directions. Thankfully her jeans are probably salvageable, after a thorough wash, but she probably smells like sweat and blood. All around, it’s not her best look.

    She walks to exit her room with a slight limp, and is thankful for the fact that sleep seems to have improved her injuries somewhat, but her ribs are still very sore and her head feels like it has been hit repeatedly with a jackhammer.

    The apartment is empty, no sign of Yelena or even Lucky. Huh. That’s odd. She looks into the guestroom, and the bathroom but both look untouched, even the traces of her getting cleaned up in there gone. When she enters the kitchen, she sees a colorful sticky note on the counter. She picks it up, running over the lines written in a little bit messy handwriting.

    Good morning I took your dog for a walk.

    We will be back soon.

    -Yelena Kate chuckles at businesslike tone of the note, leaving it where she found it. She makes her way to the bathroom, and undresses. She winces a little, but it feels good to be out of her dirty clothes. She considers taking a bath, but she is afraid that once she is in it, she’d have a difficult time getting out, so she hobbles into the shower instead.

    The warm spray of water feels amazing on her battered body, and for a while she just stands there, letting it relax her sore muscles. She washes her hair thoroughly afterwards, despite her aching ribs, and feels much better when she exits the shower.

    She towels herself off and makes her way back to her bedroom to get dressed. She opts for something comfortable, and puts on some grey sweatpants and a black sleeveless tee over her sports bra, that is loose enough to not feel uncomfortable against her injured side. Her wet hair soaks the shirt in a few seconds, but it’s warm in the late summer, and she doesn’t feel like drying it with her aching side anyway.

    The front door opens just as she exits her room, planning to look for something to eat. Lucky walks in, wagging his tail at her sight, Yelena right behind him. She leans down to pat him, happy to see him back to his happy little self after yesterday’s events. “Oh good, you are up!”

    “You took Lucky for a walk?”

    Kate is smiling as she looks up at Yelena and her stomach flips at her sight. The blonde’s hair is up in a sort of messy bun, and she is wearing one of Kate’s shirts, a light grey one, that has her university’s logo on it. It’s a bit big for her, even though it fits perfectly on Kate. “Yes. Lucky and I are best friends now.”

    “Uh…that’s cool.”

    Kate answers on autopilot, still processing Yelena wearing her shirt.

    “I am going to introduce him to my Fanny one day. They will get married.” That gets through the fog that has settled on the brunette’s brain. Well, sort of. “Your…What?”

    “Fanny Longbottom, my dog.”

    “You have a dog named Fanny Longbottom?”

    “Did you suffer a concussion yesterday too? You are being very slow… Yes, I have a dog., and yes her name is Fanny.”

    Yelena talks to her as if she is talking to a particularly dumb child. “Oh, okay…” Kate says, her mind finally catching up the present. “Where is she?” “She is back in Ohio.”

    “Alone?”

    Yelena continues to look at her with a slightly worried, but amused look. She sounds a condescending when she answers.

    “You really must have a hit your head hard. Of course she is not alone.” “Ah, okay. So…do you have many friends in Ohio?”

    She is patting Lucky but she sees confusion pass through Yelena’s face, before it’s overtaken by a smug smile.

    “If you want to ask me questions Kate, you can ask them directly. You are not being very sneaky.”

    Kate stands up and walks towards the kitchen, the blonde following behind her after taking her shoes off. Kate opens the fridge to look at breakfast options.

    “Well, you are not exactly an open book, Yelena.”

    “What do you want to know?”

    Kate turns to look at the blonde, her brows lifting in surprise.

    “Wait, really?”

    Yelena gives her a cheeky grin, and takes a seat at the kitchen island. “Yes really. You can ask, and we will see if I want to answer.”

    “Ookay. Um…”

    She thinks about what she wants to know, but honestly, there is too many things to ask. She turns back to the fridge and goes for an obvious one.

    “Do you still work as an assassin?”

    She doesn’t look at Yelena. She doesn’t really know what kind of answer she is looking for, or if she even has an opinion in the first place. Yelena is quiet for a long enough time that Kate turns back to look at her. Her face is almost blank, but her eyes are hard as she considers Kate. She looks back, holding her gaze, and attempts to hide her nervousness. She doesn’t know if she succeeds, but Yelena sighs after a while, her gaze flitting down at her own hands. “No, I have moved to corporate espionage. Less danger, same money.”

    Kate nods, considering her answer, then she remembers what Yelena said the other night. “But you said you were hired to kill me?”

    Yelena answers with an eyeroll, and a small upwards twitch of the corners of her mouth. “I still get asked, Kate. I was very good at my job.”

    Well, okay.

    “Ookay. So you live in Ohio?”

    “That has been said already, yes.”

    Kate busies herself with taking out ingredients for an omelet while she asks her next question, her back to Yelena.

    “Do you live alone?”

    “I have told you this also, 5 minutes ago. I live with Fanny.”

    “No I meant…”

    She turns back to Yelena in her breakfast making process, and sees her smirk and the amused glint in her eye. She is fucking with her. Kate rolls her eyes and starts chopping peppers. “I know what you meant.”

    Okay, so that is not something she will get a straight answer to. She thinks what her next question should be, and tries to go for a lighter one.

    “So Fanny…what kind of dog is she?”

    “She is an Akita mix. Wait, I’ll show you.”

    The blonde digs her phone out of her pocket, and taps on it a few times, before showing a picture of a sand and black colored dog, with a forest behind her.

    “She is beautiful”

    Kate smiles at the picture of the dog, her eyes glancing up at Yelena. She turns the phone back to herself, and smiles at the photo too.

    “I know.”

    She is beautiful like this too, Kate thinks. Her face soft and warm for once. She goes back to the peppers, the room quiet for a second, before the blonde puts down her phone on the counter. She leans back, and looks at Kate again.

    “So, tell me about what happened yesterday.”

    Apparently Yelena had enough of 20 Questions. Kate starts cracking eggs into a bowl, and gathers her thoughts.

    “Well, Lucky and I walked to the burger place without any issues. We got our food…” “Ah, I wanted to say, the burgers were tasty by the way. Just cold. Really liked the spicy one.”

    “Oh…I’m glad…Wait, did you eat both of them?”

    “Yes, I told you, I was starving…Sorry, go on.”

    Yelena leans back on her chair as the brunette starts whisking the eggs, wincing a little with the motion as it makes her ribs hurt.

    “So, when we were about to come home, I saw a suspicious car with 4 guys inside. I decided to go to the park, to lose them, and they followed us. I let Lucky loose in case they attacked, and then they threw like a…high frequency grenade thing at us.”

    Yelena leans forward, resting her elbows on the counter, her focus entirely on Kate now. She puts a pan on the stove, turns it on.

    “A flashbang?”

    “Yes, kinda? A more high tech version, I think.”

    She leans against the counter, crossing her arms, recalling last night’s events. “Anyway, I kicked it away from us, and jumped on Lucky, but it went off not far from us. I couldn’t hear anything, and it really made my head hurt, Lucky panicked, and ran away. The four of them attacked me but I managed to defend myself, but…well, they got some hits in. Which is what you saw yesterday.”

    Yelena nods, deep in thought. She stands up, and as if on autopilot, pushes Kate out of the way and adds the bacon the brunette put by the side of the stove to the searing hot pan. It sizzles, and Kate moves further away, leaning against the corner of the kitchen island, her arms crossed again.

    “Did they have any identifying marks?”

    “Not really. One was like really huge, with dark hair and beard, and tattoos, two of them were blonde-ish, I guess, and the fourth one had brown hair and this big mole on his cheek. They wore black, but nothing really to make them stand out. At least one of them had a gun, but I think the others might have had them too.”

    Yelena listens to her answers, nodding and thinking her words through as she moves the bacon around in the pan.

    “Training?”

    “Nothing fancy. They could fight, but apart from the device…the high tech flashbang thingy they used, they seemed mostly like common thugs.”

    The Russian hums, adding the peppers to the pan, and pulling out a drawer to get a spatula. Did Yelena scout her kitchen yesterday?. They are silent for a little while, Yelena pondering what she said, and cooking, Kate watching her and also thinking.

    “Did you bring this device back with you?”

    Kate shakes her head regretfully.

    “No, I was a bit disoriented and scared for Lucky.”

    “How did you find him?”

    “Oh yeah, I forgot! So I couldn’t really hear still, I just looked for him in the park, calling his name. Then he showed up, with Spider-man in tow!”

    The blonde turns to her, lifting an eyebrow, her face questioning. Kate nods meaningfully, and Yelena adds the egg-mix to the pan.

    “Yeah, he...he caught PD as he was running away. He made a leash from his spider-web thing?...”

    Kate shakes her head in wonder, furrowing her brows.

    “…Anyway, he brought Lucky back, and he seemed kinda suspicious of what happened to us, he followed us home after and everything.”

    “Well, at least one superhero is competent in New York City.”

    Yelena is turned away from her, eyes still on the pan but smirking a little. “Hey! I fought 4 assassins! All he did was catch a dog!”

    Kate is, half offended, half outraged. She fought off those assassins, and she only got injured because they caught her off-guard! Yelena glances at her now with that annoying little smug smile on her face still.

    “Weren’t they just common thugs a moment ago?”

    “With high tech weaponry!”

    “Okay okay Kate, I am only teasing, I promise.”

    Kate grumbles, but eases up a little, her eyes following Yelena as she walks to the fridge, pulls out some cheese, then gets the cheese grater from one of the cupboards, and starts adding some onto the admittedly really good looking omelets. It’s freaking Kate out a little. How the fuck does she know where everything is?

    “Did you go through my entire house yesterday while I was out? Had some fun rummaging through my underwear drawer…”

    Kate’s voice still carries some indignation. Yelena whips her head at her, her face alight with surprised mirth, and good god did she really just ask that? Kate burrows her face in her hands.

    “Kate Bishoop!”

    The blonde’s voice sounds scandalized and amused at the same time.

    “Oh Jesus, please forget I said that…”

    She lowers her hands to looks at Yelena after a few seconds, who is now taking out two plates with a grin on her face, but evidently takes pity on her.

    “Anyways, no. I did not snoop through your underwear. I looked for a snack while I waited, since you took forever and I was starving. You have a very nice kitchen for the record.” Kate recovers from her embarrassment and finally dares to look at the blonde again. “Yeah…More than one fork now.”

    Yelena smiles to herself as carries both plates to the island.

    “Yes, Kate, well done on cutlery.”

    Kate follows her to the island, grabbing two of the aforementioned forks, and two knives, but Yelena doesn’t sit down yet. She takes out two glasses, and pours them some juice. Apart from the creepiness of her knowing exactly where everything is, it’s kind of nice. Not a word she thought she’d associate with Yelena. Kate looks at her when she finally sits down. She starts to dig in, but pauses when she sees that the Kate is not eating. “What?”

    “Oh….nothing.”

    She starts shoveling the eggs into her mouth, but she can still feel Yelena’s gaze on her. Wow, this is a good fucking omelet. Eventually the other woman digs in too. They eat in silence for a few minutes.

    “You know, if this whole corporate espionage thing doesn’t pan out…”

    Kate glances up at Yelena who looks back at her.

    “…you can probably find a career as a chef. This is fucking delicious.” Yelena’s eyes widen in surprise, apparently not expecting the compliment, before she smiles. “Thank you.”

    For once there is no witty retort on her lips, and after a moment of hesitation she speaks again.

    “I actually really like cooking. It helps me think.”

    Kate smiles back, knowing exactly what the blonde means.

    “Yeah, I like dog walking for the same reason. Helps me put things in order in my head.” Yelena nods at her then goes back to eating, and she does the same. They finish their breakfast, or well, brunch technically, Kate loads their plates into the dishwasher and makes them coffee. She passes the other woman her cup, and her eyes follow Yelena’s movements as she adds milk and two spoons of sugar. Kate smiles into her own mug as she takes a sip. Yelena has a sweet tooth.

    “So, how is your side?” Yelena asks, sipping her coffee.

    “It’s better. Ribs are always a bitch to injure though.”

    Yelena hums in agreement.

    “Do you need me to help change your bandages?”

    “Uh…I can probably manage...But thank you.” She says somewhat awkwardly, and the blonde just hums again.

    They finish their coffees and Kate gathers herself, takes Yelena’s cup from her and puts them both in the dishwasher too, before starting it. Yelena leaves the kitchen as she wipes the counter, despite her aching side, a few grunts escaping her.

    Once she is finished cleaning up, she finds Yelena in the living room, looking through their work on the boards from yesterday. She turns her laptop on, sitting down on the couch to get some work done as well.

    Bishop security may have been sold and scrapped for parts (which is how she could afford this apartment, and her cars, and a profession that paid as much as her allowance has been when she was fourteen), but she still has access to the data servers. She didn’t double-major in business and computer science for nothing.

    Yelena speaks to her from where she is standing, not turning away from their wall of evidence.

    “What are you doing?”

    “I am looking into Maya. She seems to have dopped off from the face of the Earth in the last one and a half years.”

    “Maybe she is dead.”

    “Yeah, maybe…hey, we should get our hands on some police files, see what the Tracksuits have been up to for the last year.”

    Yelena nods as she leaves the board, to come and sit next to Kate, and picks up one of the files they printed out yesterday.

    “It’s gonna be a bit harder here. In LA I had a fix contact I could turn to, to get me the things I need, but I don’t have that with the NYPD.”

    Yelena just hums, focused mostly on the information she is reading. After a second, Kate remembers har last Christmas in New York. She searches for ‘Central Park LARP meetings’ and finds the group she and Clint made friends with. According to their (very colorful) website, they have training sessions on Mondays and Thursdays at 5 pm. She checks the time, they have a few hours until then.

    “Are you googling some…”

    Yelena looks a bit at loss at what to call what she is witnessing on Kate’s screen, that she leans over to peer at.

    ”…nerdy website while I do boring paperwork?”.

    Kate laughs and pulls up a group picture, pointing out some people to Yelena. “This is Grills, he is a firefighter and a friend of Clint’s and mine. He took care of Lucky when we were running around New York chasing you.”

    “I have very different memories on who was chasing who, but continue.” Kate smiles but goes on without reacting to the commentary.

    “This is Missy, she made Clint’s and mine matching superhero suits for the Christmas party.” “The one I exposed by tearing off your dress in the elevator. I remember. You were very proud of it”

    Kate blinks at her, once, twice, three times. Well, while technically true, Yelena definitely didn’t have to phrase it like that. Was she joking? Honestly, she really can’t tell with her sometimes. She decides to continue as if she was never interrupted again. “And finally, this is Wendy, she is a detective. She helped Clint and I get his trick arrows back from police lockup, so we could fight the Tracksuits. She can help us get the files we need.”

    Yelena nods, her attention back to the picture, turning her head to the side, not entirely unlike Lucky does sometimes.

    “What is it that they wearing?”

    “Um…armor, kinda?”

    “Ah, so they are warriors?”

    “Yeeah, sort of…They are LARPing.”

    Now it’s the Yelena’s turn to blink at her several times, waiting for her to elaborate. “You know, Live Action Role Playing”

    “Is that like a sex thing?”

    Yelena is definitely joking this time, not even trying to hide her cheeky grin as she keeps looking back and forth between the screen and the brunette.

    “What, no!” Kate chuckles “No, it’s like…they dress up and like fight each other. They come up with like a character the roleplay as…”

    “You are definitely not convincing me it’s not a sex thing, Kate. And you say, you and Barton went together? Gross.”

    Kate is full on laughing now, her ribs are throbbing with every exhale as Yelena makes a fake disgusted face, her nose scrunching up.

    “Ow ow ow, stop it… fighting is not a codeword for foreplay for everyone, you know.” Yelena raises an eyebrow at that, but the amused glint in her eyes remains, but Kate is determined to hold her gaze this time. One heartbeat, two, three. Yelena turns back to the computer with a smirk, before she professes.

    “Yes, well, fighting with Barton is definitely not.”

    Ha! Kate won that round. She doesn’t know at what she just won at but she knows she did. “Anyway, we are going to their practice to Central Park this afternoon, and we are going to ask Wendy nicely, if she can help us get the police files we need.”

    “Normally I’d say that’s a ridiculous waste of time, and we should just steal the files ourselves…but since you are injured, we can go visit your medieval sex cult friends.” “Yelena!” she admonishes, and tries not to laugh but has to hold her ribs again when she chuckles involuntarily anyway.

    They work for another few hours, discussing possible leads, or gathering information in silence, before it’s time to go. When they get off of the couch, Kate notes again, how unexpectedly nice this has been. She does just fine on her own, always did, but she always enjoys this, having a partner on a case. But it’s not just that, she had fun in the last few hours. Yelena is good company, even if a bit distracting sometimes.

    She puts her retractable bow and arrows into a gym sack, while her keys, sword and phone go into the pockets of her sweatpants. They are good to go.

    Chapter End Notes This is a bit of a slow chapter, but I hope you guys like it anyway. Either way, we have a few action filled ones ahead of us, so enjoy the calm while it lasts :D As always, please feel free to comment, I love to read your thoughts or write to me on twitter or tumblr.

    Next one will be up sometime in first half of the weekend, probably late friday or early saturday.

    Chapter 5

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes The part of the park where the LARPers practice is relatively close to the brunette’s place, so they end up walking there, or in Kate’s case, hobbling.

    The group is happy to see Kate, welcoming her warmly, despite her long absence and the fact that they only knew her for like a week. There is an awkward moment however, when Kate introduces Yelena.

    “Everyone, this is Yelena, she is helping me with a case.”

    They greet her too, and for once, Yelena is on her best behavior, following Kate’s lead during the interaction and not calling them a medieval sex cult to their face, which is more than what Kate expected. She notices Grills however, his eyes watching Yelena, his brows furrowed. When she says something, or more precisely Kate thinks, when he hears her accent, his eyes widen almost comically. He looks over to Kate, who steps immediately forward with her palms raised, ready to deescalate the situation.

    “She is…”

    “Yes, but it’s not what you think it is!”

    The group who had been chatting enthusiastically quiets down in a second, watching the interaction.

    “So you are not working with the assassin who tried to kill Clint?!”

    The LARPers gasp in shock as one, looking between the two of them. Kate even sees some of them tighten their hold on their toy weapons. She sighs.

    “Okay, well, technically I am...”

    Another dramatic gasp from the group (honestly, Kate thinks they need to tone it down). “…But her and Clint are friends now.”

    She looks at the blonde, urging her to confirm, who looks absolutely unbothered by the entire conversation.

    “I would definitely not call us friends.”

    She sucks in a deep breath through her nose, closing her eyes for a second, counting back in her head. So much for best behavior…

    “Yelena…”

    The blonde lets out a sigh of her own, and concedes with an eyeroll.

    “Fiiine. Barton and I are cool.”

    Alright, this is as good as it’s going to get.

    “See?! They are cool!”

    Grills is still looking at Yelena with suspicion, the rest of the troupe waiting for him to make a decision.

    “How do we know she didn’t like…seduce you to turn against him? Isn’t that like their MO?” Kate is looking at him with her mouth gaping. Next to her, Yelena doesn’t even try to contain her snickers. She shakes her head, and reaches into her pocket.

    “That’s it, I am calling Clint.”

    Thankfully, she is lucky and he answers her call again, without it going to voicemail. She puts him on speaker.

    “Hi Kid, two calls in 24 hours? I told you…”

    “Would you please tell the LARPers you and Yelena are friends now?”

    To his credit, he doesn’t miss a beat.

    “Well, I wouldn’t exactly call us friends…”

    For the love of….

    “…but sure, we made peace.”

    Yelena looks smugly around the group, and Kate wants to elbow her in her side or something, to wipe it off her face, but she is relieved to see that Grills, and the rest of the LARPers along with him, visibly relax.

    “Alright, thanks Clint!”

    He chuckles in his usual raspy tone.

    “Anytime. Bye Kate!”

    She hangs up and puts her phone back in her pocket.

    “Are you happy?”

    Grills shrugs, as if to say ‘if he is cool, than I am cool’, and just like that, the LARPers accept Yelena as one of their own too. They are still seemingly scared to talk to her however, which honestly, is probably for the best, but Kate quickly asks Grills to tell her the story of how he impaled Clint on his mighty sword to distract them all.

    It ends up being both a great and a terrible decision, because she’s thinks she will never hear the end of the medieval sex cult jokes from Yelena now, but at least it allows everyone to let the tension of the previous few minutes go.

    Kate is nervous to approach Wendy about the files after that interaction, but since they came here to talk to her, and they really do need all the help they can get to get to Kingpin, she doesn’t really have a choice. Thankfully, the woman is happy to help them out and agrees to get them what they need by tomorrow.

    She does exactly that, and the next 3 days are spent mostly working their way through the files, catching up on what the Tracksuits have been up to, any sightings of Fisk, Maya or Vanessa Marianna, which there were not many of.

    They kind of fall into a rhythm, with Yelena coming over every morning to work, then them spending the day filling up the boards with possibly useful and relevant information, until dinner. It’s pretty mundane, and she is itching to get back into action. Even more so, because despite her being a much better company than Kate would have ever anticipated, being cooped up in the apartment with Yelena has been a bit weird. Not bad weird, not really, but a bit unbalancing and distracting.

    It’s not entirely Yelena’s fault. It’s just that, the feeling of being on edge around the other woman somehow never faded.     Kate is honestly so shocked by the turn of events that she just takes out her wallet and counts out several $100 notes. That is not how her partnership with Clint usually goes.     “Hey, how about you offer your own money next time?”

    Yelena walks by her to enter the room, shrugging as she goes.

    “Okay. I look for which one is the Kingpin’s unit, you erase the security footage of us bribing the bald man.”

They walk in silence, both of them assessing their surroundings, looking for any kind of movement. The emptiness of the space puts Kate on edge a little.

    They reach the unit without any issues however, the entire level deserted and quiet, and soon are standing before the crimson roll down doors, with the numbers 3672 written above it in red paint. There is only a simple padlock on the door, and Kate starts to feel uneasy. This is a bit too simple. Then again, she tries to calm herself, how else would they lock a storage unit.     “Okay, you are the lookout this time.”

    She flinches and holds her breath, but nothing moves in or outside of the unit they are breaking into, and she considers that to be a good sign. Kate contemplates her options, and decides to take out her retractable sword from her back pocket, and opens the blade with the button on the handle. She looks at Yelena, who seems to have produced a gun out of nowhere. Their eyes meet, and Yelena raises the gun at the door, before nodding at Kate. She counts back in her head.

    3…2…1…

    She yanks the door hard, sending it rolling up fast and jumps back with her blade raised, ready to face what’s inside.

    Well…that’s pretty disappointing. She doesn’t know what she expected, but it wasn’t this. Inside, there is a thick, wooden table, with a vase full of fresh flowers resting atop it. She lowers her sword, and starts to walk inside. Yelena doesn’t lower her gun. “Kate, be careful.”

    As she gets closer to the table, she sees that there is a lilac envelope leant against the vase. There is no name or address on it, so she picks it up, and turns it around to slip the card out from inside.

    Kate Bishop, Thank you for making this easy.

    I’ll send my condolences to your mother.

    -W.F.

    It’s not a conscious decision.

    Before she even finishes reading the note, she is turning around, and launching herself at Yelena, tackling her to the ground.

    The explosion shakes the entire building, tearing the walls out and sending the ceiling caving in. Kate feels chunks of concrete falling on her back, but she stays conscious the whole time, and doesn’t feel too badly hurt anywhere, apart from her injured ribs screaming in pain again. She is panting however, adrenaline flowing her veins, as she attempts to cover as much of Yelena’s body with her own as she can. Her eyes are shut tightly, as she waits for the aftereffects of the explosion to die down. She is pretty sure she can hear an alarm ringing, but it might be just her ears.

    When she opens her eyes, they meet golden ones staring back at her, visible even in the grey, dusty fog created by the explosion. She can feel Yelena’s hands against her stomach, their bodies pressed tightly together, helped even more by the rubble on Kate’s back. She coughs, as she inhales the dark, choking smoke that now mixes with the dust. They need to move. “Are you okay?”

    Yelena is calm and collected even with the destruction around them, her voice even as she answers.

    “Yes. Can you stand?”

    She attempts to push herself off, her arms staining with the effort, but collapses back against Yelena a moment later, her cheek pressing against the blonde’s, panting into her ear. “Yeah…yeah, just give me a second.”

    She spends a few seconds gathering her strength, than pushes up as hard as she can, with Yelena’s hands aiding her by pressing against her too. With their combined effort, they manage to push Kate up enough, that she can get on all fours, and then push the thick concrete slab that was once part of the roof of the building off of her back. Kate stands up, offering a hand to Yelena who takes it. She pulls her up with a quick motion and they take account of their surroundings. The building is on fire, that much is clear. Thick, acidic smoke fills the air, making it hard to see despite the bright sunlight streaming through the hole left by the explosion.     “Wait.”

    She vaults over the debris that covered them earlier, and starts looking frantically among the rubble, covering her nose and mouth with her t-shirt. She hears Yelena’s exasperated voice filtering through from behind her.

    “What are you doing?”

    “I lost my bow.”

    “Leave it, we need to go.”

    She ignores Yelena and keeps looking until she sees the corner of her bag sticking out from under a heap of broken concrete.

    “I got it.”

    She pulls at the bag, but it’s lodged in there pretty tight.

    “Kate! We have to go! Now!”

    She hears a loud crack. Oh no.

    The floor beneath her feet disappears in a second as she crashes through what used to be the ceiling of the second floor of the building, letting out an undignified yell.     “I am fine!”

    She stands up with a groan and locates her bag again, and takes out her equipment just as Yelena lands next to her with a grace that Kate can’t help but envy, her face irritated. “This was so stupid!”

    Kate puts her quiver on her back, and unbolts her bow with a jerk of her arm. “I am an archer Yelena, I need my bow and arrows!”

    Yelena lets out an annoyed sigh and exits the remains of the storage unit they found themselves in, and Kate is right behind her. At least this floor is not on fire, yet. “You see? If you had an Ironman suit, this would have never happened.”

    Yelena marches on, checking around corners before she turns them.

    “You know what…”

    “Kate, shut up”

    “No you can’t just…”

    Multiple voices speaking a language she can’t understand, somewhere ahead of them, probably only one or two corners separating them from their position. She nods, and Yelena slides her palm off of her, then activates her bracelets with a motion Kate can’t see. She tries to count the assailants by the different tones, but apart from being able to tell that there is more than 3 of them at least, she can’t. They are drawing nearer, and she silently takes a needle arrow from her quiver. She gestures to Yelena to stand back, and draws her bow.

    She waits until she can hear them more clearly, rounding the corner ahead of them and fires the arrow at one of the soldiers dressed in black, jumping back into cover immediately after. Alarmed, then pained screams follow and Yelena runs past her and is slamming one of the soldiers against the wall just as she rounds the corner.

    Kate realizes the needle arrow might not have been the best choice, as she follows Yelena, since the soldiers all seem to be wearing thick, probably bulletproof vests. Apart from two assailants, who got needles stuck in their ski-mask covered faces, and the one who got shot by the arrow in the first place, the rest are relatively unaffected, leaving 6 for them to deal with.

    Well, 5, now that Yelena leaves one of them collapsing against the wall, unconscious (or dead). Kate kicks the machine gun out of the hand of one of soldiers, than uses her bow to hit him in the chin from below, snapping his head up and back. He collapses without a sound. Instead, she hears the sound of electricity crackling behind her, then a pained groan. In the time that it took for her to knock one man out, Yelena has finished two, one currently convulsing on the floor, and another lying face down, unmoving. She is fighting a third one that is at least twice her size, using that exact fact against him. She already unarmed him and she dodges his punches like she knows exactly what he is going to do before he does. Kate doesn’t have time to watch however, as she sees the sixth, last standing man raise his rifle towards Yelena. She sprints, jumping on the wall and kicking herself off to gain momentum. She slams her elbow into his face, and he cries out in pain, stumbling to one knee. She kicks him in the head, the wall delivering the second hit against the back of his skull as he slams against it. He is unconscious by the time her reaches the ground. She looks up, and Yelena is already watching, an amused smirk on her face. She raises her chin, her eyes flitting down on Kate’s form, than back to her eyes.

    “Not bad, Kate Bishop.”

    Kate snorts, and tries to stifle the little bit of pride blooming in her chest. She puffs out her chest a little, standing up taller.

    “I won the U.S. Open Martial Arts Championship like 4 times.”

    Yelena just chuckles as she leans down to pick a gun up from off of the soldiers, and Kate is not sure if she is laughing at her, or with her. Rude.

    “Hey, you literally fought me before.”

    Yelena just rolls her eyes as she picks up another gun, and slides it into the back of her jeans. “Yes, but that was only play-fighting. Not serious.”

    Okay, the information that Yelena held back during their fight does not entirely come as a surprise for her, the woman didn’t even use her lightening bracelets on her, but she can’t say it doesn’t hurt her ego a little. It’s not like she was out to kill the woman, but she did do her best to stop her (her best at the time at least). She must wear an affronted expression, because Yelena gives her cheek two placating pats as she walks by her and chuckles again. “Just take the compliment Kate, and lets go.”
