    She takes a different arrow, pulling the string of her bow taut and waiting for the group to get closer to the stairs. She can’t see them in the darkness of the lower floor, but she hears the steps, boots heavy against the concrete.

    “Close your eyes.”

    She whispers to Yelena and releases the flare arrow a moment later, with her own closed as well. Alarmed and pained sounds from the soldiers indicate that her arrow has caused the required effect, and by the time she opens her eyes, Yelena is again, already halfway down the stairs. The close quarters make it hard for her to use her bow, so she quickly attaches it to her quiver as she follows Yelena down the stairs.

    Kate watches as she jumps onto one of the blinded soldiers, using her thighs to grip him in a powerful hold around his shoulders, and then swinging down to flip his body around. Yelena lands in a perfect crouch, her movements illuminated by Kate’s arrow imbedded into the ground. Kate admires the preciseness of her movements, and thinks she moves like a panther, all lethal grace. She is reminded again how glad she is that Yelena is on her side as the blonde pulls out the guns she pulled off the soldiers earlier, from the back of her jeans. Kate hears the first gunshot as she kicks a soldier’s legs from underneath him, the man still disoriented by the blinding light of her arrow before. He lands with a painful grunt on the broad of his back and she kicks him in the face, his head snapping to the side, knocking him out cold. She pulls out her sword from her back pocket, and barely has time to open its blade, before a hulking figure is crashing into her.

    She is knocked to the side, but faster to recover from the impact than the soldier, and uses his moment of sluggishness to slash his thigh deep with her blade, sending a splash of blood against the wall. She rams the pommel of the sword against his temple, and he falls down, not getting back up any time soon.

    A bullet embeds itself into the wall next to her, and she instinctively crouches, rolling her body forward to avoid the next one, but she feels its whoosh by her face, only missing her by an inch. She somersaults to front of the soldier who fired the shot, and uses the momentum to ram her shoulder into his torso as she stands up, sending him stumbling backwards. She grabs his arm holding the gun, and twists it at an awkward angle, breaking his elbow with a crunch as he cries out.

    Her blood is thumping in her ears, but she hears a click and whips him around intuitively, using him as a shield. She feels the impact rock his body as 3 shots are fired, the bullets lodging themselves into his cevlar vest. She quickly glances to the side to check on Yelena, as she kicks the soldier she used to take the bullets meant for her towards the other, making both of them fall. There are bodies littering the corridor in the other woman’s wake, in various states of ruin, but there are still too many standing.

    It’s only a matter of time before one of those bullets actually finds its target, and the blinding effect of her arrow is already wearing off. They have to go. Now.

    She makes a decision quickly, and has her bow in her hand in lass than a second. She dodges another soldier, sliding between his standing legs as he trains his gun at her, and pulls an explosive arrow from her back, nocking it as she stands. She kicks the man in the back, his body hurling forward and she fires her arrow into what she really hopes is a wall to the outside a bit further down the corridor.

    She is right thankfully, and in a few seconds, sunlight fills the previously dim corridor through the hole her arrow created. Their attackers are momentarily distracted, and she uses it to shove one of them against the wall and call out.

    “Yelena, let’s go!”

    The other woman is beside her in a heartbeat, and the they take off, sprinting towards the opening. Shots are fired behind them, but their attackers reacted too late and they manage to get away unscathed, jumping through the hole in a matter of seconds. They are only one story high now, and Kate lands in a crouch, rolling forwards and Yelena is only a step behind her, having used her Widow bracelet to produce a wire for a more elegant landing. They are sprinting again in an instant, bullets cracking the pavement of the street by their feet, and Yelena fires a few shots to behind them, but Kate doesn’t look back to see if she hit her targets. She runs faster than the other woman, having the advantage of longer legs, and makes it to their car first. She taps her pockets, searching frantically, but she can’t find her keys.

    Yelena catches up, and there are two beeps from the Mercedes. Kate brows shot up in surprise.

    “Wait, when did you have time to steal my keys?”

    Yelena snickers, sliding into the driver’s seat, and she decides to just go with the unspoken decision, vaulting over the hood of the car to get in on the passenger side. They pull out with a screech of tires, and Kate finally has time to look herself over.

    Her whole body is covered in dust, rubbing onto the leather seat she is sitting on. Her jeans are torn at the knees and there is an alarming amount of blood on her shirt and arms, the only reassuring fact being that most of it is not hers (as far as she can tell). Apart from her previously injured ribs aching, she thinks she is relatively unharmed, just a few new bruises and scratches here and there. She looks over to Yelena, who is in a similar state, her usually flawless outfit covered in soot, a few whisps of hair escaping her braided up hair. Kate can’t help herself and bursts out laughing.

    “Wow, that did not go as planned.”

    Chapter 6

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Yelena follows Kate’s directions back towards Manhattan, the two of them leaving the column of smoke rising in the distance behind them. She has to adjust her seat both up and forwards to reach the pedals to see out properly. and Kate’s lips twitch upwards but Yelena only has to give her a side look for her to swallow the comment she was about to make. She is still high strung from the fight not quite believing they made it out of there in one piece. “So, what the hell just happened?”

    Kate doesn’t even know if she is asking about the whole situation that went down, Yelena stealing her keys, or anything that happened in-between.

    “Well, it is pretty obvious that we have walked into a trap. Put your seatbelt on.” She can’t help but chuckle at the answer. The engine revs, and Yelena is driving fast, switching lanes and taking over cars with swift precision. Kate feels jittery, the adrenaline still coursing through her veins, and she pulls out her phone. She presses play on her music app, the device already connected through Bluetooth, despite Yelena’s Are you serious look over the center console.

    The fast thrums of guitar and beats of drums fill the car, and the glare turns into a fully affronted expression, as Yelena recognizes the first notes of the song. Kate bursts out laughing both at the music and her horrified face.

    “Kate, No! Change the song!”

    Yelena attempts to grab the phone from her hands, presumably to change it herself, but she holds it out of reach just as the velvety male voice sings ‘There lived a certain man, in Russia long ago’ and Kate thinks she can feel her bruised ribs actually crack this time from how hard she is laughing, the tension of the last hours catching up to her and turning her a bit hysterical. She manages to spit out between giggles.

    “Rasputin stays!”

    “Why do you even have that? It’s horrible.”

    “Ra, Ra, Rasputin, Lover of the Russian Queen, There was a cat that really was gone.” Kate sings along to the song obnoxiously, and Yelena is almost entirely across the center console to take the phone from her but doesn’t take her eyes off the road. The back window shattering breaks them out of their tussle, repeated gun fire drowning out the music for a second, causing Yelena to twist the wheel to the side, and almost crash into the concrete fence around the highway. She quickly corrects their course, ending up in the lane next to the one they were in before, causing the driver they cut off to break hard and lean on his horn heavily and for Kate to drop her phone.

    Kate twists around in her seat, and sees two black SUVs and a black van following them, speeding by the rest of the cars on the road. There is a man hanging out of the window of one of SUVs with an automatic rifle, trying to aim at their car. She unbuckles herself, and reaches for her bow.

    “What are you doing?”

    “Just keep driving!”

    Kate opens the sunroof, and stands on her seat and the center console to stick her whole upper body out of the car. She quickly nocks a regular arrow, and pulls the string of her bow taut, praying she aims faster than the guy with the gun.

    She does, her arrow hitting him in the chest, making him fall out of the car that keeps swerving between lanes to keep up with Kate’s Mercedes. She reaches into her quiver, pulling out an explosive arrow just as Yelena turns sharply to the right, taking an exit off of the highway, causing her to nearly drop it. She grunts and quickly catches it before it can fall off the side of the car. The black cars are still hot in pursuit and she quickly fires her shot at the SUV closest to them.

    The car’s engine explodes and it whips around the road, before turning over and rolling several times. The other two cars swerve around the wreckage, not slowing down. Yelena drives at a break-neck speed, careening around another corner, and Kate loses her footing a little, stepping onto the other woman’s thigh.

    “Oww. Kate!”

    She hears Yelena cry out from inside the car, the music finally having turned off. Her foot slips, making her nearly fall but she readjusts herself, getting it back onto the console. The second SUV is gaining on them fast, and its windows are rolled down, gun barrels sticking out front and back.

    She fires a smoke arrow into one of the openings, and finally the other car slows down, with only the van remaining in pursuit. Kate has no idea where they are, the Queens neighborhood flying by around them completely unfamiliar, but traffic is getting busy, Yelena swerving left and right, jostling Kate around, and making it almost impossible for her to aim. “Hey Yelena, do you take constructive criticism?”

    She hears a snort from below.

    “No.”

    The van is gaining on them, and there are too many people and cars around for Kate to use another explosive arrow now without it turning into a civilan bloodbath. As the vehicle pulls up beside them, its side door is pulled open, revealing a machine gun mounted on a tripod. Yelena stomps on the breaks, and Kate feels the breath knocked out of her by the edge of the sunroof as they screech to a halt, the other car speeding by them and a flurry of bullets intended for them hitting the buildings by other the side of the road. Yelena spins the car around, and the engine revs as she attempts to gain speed and leave the van behind. Kate turns around, her feet awkwardly finding her footing again as the sounds of machine gun fire and screams fill the air. She quickly nocks an electromagnetic arrow and lets it loose, shooting it inside the van’s open door. The gunshots finally stop, the other car and most of the weapons inside rendered useless by her shot, and she lets out a relieved sigh, but it’s short lived.

    The back doors of the van fly open, and a lithe figure jumps out, sprinting after them. They wear a black and red tactical suit, and mask, no weapons in sight. Kate is simultaneously annoyed and amused at the determination of this person, that they would chase a car, unarmed, on foot, but it only takes her a few heartbeats to realize they are gaining on the Mercedes speeding at full throttle. Oh shit, that’s definitely not normal. She fires a regular arrow at the masked figure, and they slap it out of the air like it’s nothing, running after them, getting closer.

    “Kate get back in the car.”

    She ignores Yelena, and nocks her last explosive arrow, pulling the string to next to her ear, releasing a breath as she aims. The super-powered individual is only about 30 feet from them now as she lets the arrow fly. They jump up just as she releases the string, and Kate watches in both awe and horror as they spin in the air, easily crossing the distance separating them from the Mercedes, the arrow uselessly exploding behind them.

    The super-soldier lands on the hood of their car, the metal denting under their feet and Kate’s bow is torn from her grasp before she has a chance to turn around. She is ripped from the car next, the person grabbing her by her neck and jumping again, this time taking her body with them.

    Her stomach flies then plummets as they spin in the air, the sensation strangely similar to sitting on a roller coaster, her heart beating loudly in her ears. The assassin slams her against the pavement as they land, knocking the breath squarely out of her. Stars dance behind her eyes as the back of her head hits concrete.

    Their left hand is still on her throat, the other drawing back in a fist, ready to deliver what surely would be a fatal blow, when the super solidier’s head snaps to the side. Kate is sluggish to follow their gaze, momentarily disoriented after being thrown around like a ragdoll, but she still manages to see almost in slow motion Yelena stepping out of the car that still seems to be moving, and drawing two guns from the waistline of her jeans, her face unflinching in her focus.

    Bang. Bang. Bang.

    Yelena fires shot after shot and the super-soldier is momentarily distracted, rolling off of Kate to dodge the bullets. Kate comes back to herself, rolls away from them and pulls her sword from the back pocket of her now thoroughly torn jeans. She activates the blade just as she gets in a crouch, facing her attacker. Behind her she hears screams as the last of the people are running away from the scene.

    The super-soldier dodges most of Yelena’s bullets, but one of them embeds itself into their shoulder and they let out a masculine groan. So he is a dude. Kate takes advantage of his distraction and attempts to stab towards him but he manages to jump back just in time. Yelena arrives next to her just as her guns run out of ammo, and she throws one of them at the masked figure’s face, who dodges again, but that just brings him into the way of Kate’s next slash, which catches him across his thigh, the blade sliding deep into his flesh. He cries out in pain and stumbles backwards.

    They don’t wait for him to catch his breath, Kate jumping forward with an downwards cut, as Yelena kicks at his stomach. He evades the sword and grabs Yelena’s leg, spinning and throwing her to the side as if she weighs nothing. Kate sees her flying several feet, but doesn’t have time to see if she is alright, as she slams an elbow to the side of the assassin’s head. He stumbles, but only for a moment, before she has to backtrack, dodging his punches instead.

    He doesn’t seem to be very trained, she thinks as she is ducking under a fist flying at her face. He is trying to use his raw strength to finish her off with little finesse, and despite his speed she manages to evade his strikes, now that his element of surprise is gone. He grunts, as his knee is kicked from the back making him nearly fall, Yelena rejoining the fight. It’s his time backtrack, the two of them attacking him from both sides. He slides out of the way of Kate’s sword, and kicks it from her grasp, but Yelena gets him square in the jaw with a spin-kick, snapping his head to the side. Kate doubles down, delivering an strong punch to his ribs and now it feels like they have the upper hand.

    They continue to pummel him, raw strength vs decades worth of training between the two of them until finally Kate manages to swipe his legs, just as Yelena sends a pair of disks flying onto his chest, electricity crackling. He falls and convulses on the pavement, and Kate wants to celebrate the fact that they defeated a super powered assassin, and maybe pull his mask off to get a look onto his face but there is a loud boom behind them as the car closest to them blows up.

    They take off in unison, running towards the idling Mercedes to get away, Kate leaning down to pick up her fallen sword midway. Before they get to it, a projectile goes flying above their heads, and Kate’s car explodes as well.

    Well, shit.

    Kate chances a glance behind her, as she throws herself into cover, and sees that reinforcements have arrived, a new wave of tactical suit covered soldiers shooting at them. Bullets rain down on the car they have ducked behind, as they catch their breath. Kate sticks her head up to look through a shattered window, and sees the super solider whose ass they just kicked start to get up, before she is yanked down again, falling onto her ass beside Yelena, who has her back to the car’s side, looking around for a way to get away. A car door flies above their heads, slamming against the building behind them with a loud clank, which Kate guesses must mean that the super soldier is back in the game and is angry. She hears sirens in the distance, but she doubts they will live long enough for the cops to arrive, if they don’t move soon. Her bow is gone, Yelena is out of bullets and they don’t have a way to attack the reinforcements that arrived and fight the super-strong man at the same time.

    She looks around frantically too, trying to weigh their options. None of the cars close to them seem operational anymore, so that’s out of the question. Fleeing on foot also seems like a great way to get themselves killed. Yelena taps on her arm with the hand that’s still there and she follows the other woman’s eyes to a sign for a subway station.

    Kate meets her eyes and nods. It worked before with Clint, it’ll work again. They wait for the hail of bullets to lessen in intensity for a few seconds, but it doesn’t and when something heavy crashes into the car they are hiding behind, making it jostle painfully against their backs, Yelena grabs her wrist and they are off.

    Kate uses her arm to cover her head as they sprint, dust and debris flying around them as the bullets destroy the buildings they sprint by, and a car tire flies a few inches from Yelena’s head, shattering a shop front behind them.

    They make it to the stairs, the black and white sign declaring Parsons Blvd Station above their heads as they quickly make their way down. The flurry of bullets disappear from around them but they don’t slow down, sprinting and wading between the crowd that gathered in the underground station to hide away from the destruction above.

    Yelena suddenly grabs her arm, pulling her to a halt.

    “Stop.”

    “What?! We have to keep moving!”

    She looks behind her and can see the group of armed men make their way down the stairs, automatic rifles in their hands, taking in the gathered crowd.

    “If we run, they can see us.”

    Kate turns her head towards Yelena, slow to catch what she means. The other woman’s eyes are not on her, watching the assailants above Kate’s shoulder. Oh, okay, she gets it. She wants to hide in plain sight.

    Yelena pulls Kate with a firm hold on her wrist, and they slowly make their way through the mass of people, who are all trying to make it down to the platforms. Once the soldiers start realize their targets have disappeared, they shoot a few bullets into the ceiling, presumably to flush them out and the crowd turns into pure mayhem. People are screaming, trying to get away, and pushing each other, and Kate turns her hand to grab Yelena’s so they don’t lose each other in the chaos unfolding around them.

    They make it down to one of the platforms with the pushing and shoving mass of bodies around them, just as a train pulls into the station. Kate holds Yelena’s hand tighter as she tries to fight their way onto it, and with a few well-placed elbow jabs, they make it through the doors before they close.

    The crowd pushes against Kate’s back, the wagon filled up to maximum capacity with people, and she sees the soldiers arrive down to the platform just as the carriage starts moving. They are watching as the car pulls out of the station, their eyes searching, but Kate doesn't think she sees any of them zero in on their position.

    The walls of the tunnel hide the figures from her, and she allows herself to let out a deep sigh, almost collapsing against Yelena. They are still pushed and pulled by the sea of bodies around them, as nobody has anything to hold onto, including them.

    “You okay?”

    Yelena’s voice is low, but she is close enough for Kate to catch it through the panicked sounds of the crowd around them.

    “Yeah, I’m…surprisingly intact.”

    Yelena snorts at her answer. Kate tries to discreetly look around them. “You?”

    Yelena sounds as tired as she feels.

    “I’m alright.”

    “You think we got away?”

    “For now. We will have to make a run for it at the next station.”

    Kate nods, and decides to use their time to catch her breath. She feels like she is practically drenched in sweat and adrenaline is still coursing through her veins, otherwise she is sure she’d have collapsed by now from sheer exhaustion, if from nothing else. The car jolts suddenly and the people behind them push Kate firmly against Yelena, who has her back to the door. She tries to push herself away with a hand against the glass but she only gets shoved again. Yelena looks up at Kate, her face amused despite the dirt covering it and the purple bruise on her cheek.

    “Is that a knife in your pocket, or are you just happy to see me?”

    Kate snorts, her lips twitching upwards. Where did she even learn that? “Hmpf…We both know it’s a sword.”

    Yelena hums, lifting an eyebrow and leaning her head back against the glass by Kate’s hand. She looks down for a moment, before meeting Kate’s eyes again, her face void of any emotion.

    “Well, that’s just disappointing.”

    Kate blinks at her a few times and Yelena keeps her expression serious for a moment longer before she bursts out laughing. The rest of the passengers probably think they are insane but Kate joins in a moment later. It takes them a few seconds to sober up. “Seriously, do you have any weapons left on you?”

    Kate shakes her head.

    “Just the sword.”

    Yelena nods, and starts untangling her braids quickly. Kate looks at her, baffled. “What are you doing?”

    “We will need to blend in when we arrive. They could be waiting for us.” Kate nods and pulls out her own ponytail. A few pieces of gravel fall from her hair, as she shakes it out. She wishes she had a jacket she could discard, but she will have to be satisfied with what she has.

    The next station comes too soon, and Kate grabs Yelena’s hand, expecting the crowd to descend into chaos as soon as the door slide open. She is absolutely right, and they almost get trampled when people start pouring out of the car with an explosive push. She pulls them out of the way, and Yelena snatches the baseball hat off the head of someone before they get swept away, putting it on Kate’s head.

    They make their way with the crowd, assessing their surroundings, but Kate can’t spot anyone suspicious. There are at least a dozen police cars outside the station when they make their way up the stairs, and she finally feels herself relax a little. Yelena doesn’t seem to be on the same page, and leads her away from the flashing lights by her hand.

    “Keep your head down.”

    Kate doesn’t understand but she trusts Yelena’s instincts, and they slowly get away from the crowd. She pulls the baseball hat down to cover her eyes, and in a few minutes they are a few blocks from 169th Street Station.

    “Can I hail a cab now or are we walking all the way back to Manhattan?” Yelena still marches on, her eyes constantly moving around their surroundings. “We have to make sure we are not being followed.”

    She makes them walk another 10 blocks before she is satisfied and Kate is happy to signal for a yellow cab, then another, and a third but they keep slowing down, only to speed back up when they get a closer look at them. She looks down at herself, and remembers the state they are in. They are still both covered in soot, blood and Kate’s jeans are more than fashionably torn at this stage. They probably don’t really give a trustworthy vibe. She reaches into her pocket, ready to call an Uber but the only things in there are her keys and her retractable blade.

    Oh for fucks sake…

    The Mercedes. Her phone has been in there when the car exploded. (She has no idea when or where she lost her wallet.)

    She sighs deeply, feeling very ready for this day to be over despite the fact that it’s barely over noon.

    “Yelena, do you have your phone?”

    “Yes. Why?”

    “I need you to call an Uber.”

    “What’s wrong with a taxi?”

    “They won’t stop for us. We look like serial killers.”

    She does not dwell on the fact that technically, they both are. Yelena looks down at her own clothes before she checks Kate too.

    “I don’t know why. I am totally rocking these blood stains.”

    Kate chuckles and Yelena takes out her phone. Instead of opening an app however, she calls someone and speaks rapid Russian into the device. They exchange a few sentences and then she hangs up, slipping it back into her pocket.

    “Come on, let’s get out of sight.”

    Kate follows her into an alcove of a building by the side of the road, leaning against the wall. She waits for an explanation for the call, but Yelena seems content to just wait in silence, her eyes tirelessly sweeping the road ahead and front of them.

    “Did you call the Russian mob to pick us up or something?“ “We can’t call the Russian mob, they are working for the Kingpin.” Yelena explains, like that is the only issue with calling them, but she does not offer any further information. “So…?”

    Kate prompts but Yelena only looks at her for a moment before she is back to watching for whoever she called, imitating Kate’s tone.

    “So…?”

    “So who did you call?”

    “A friend.”

    “Are you seriously not going to tell me?”

    Yelena’s lips twitch upward, but she doesn’t look at Kate.

    “A girl has to keep her secrets.”

    Kate lets out an exasperated breath. Fine. She crosses her arms, and prepares to wait in silence until Yelena tells her who she called. She keeps sneaking glances at her, and Yelena has more and more trouble keeping the smug smile off her face.

    “You are enjoying this, aren’t you.”

    Yelena finally lets the grin overtake her features, her eyes remaining on the street. “Very much so, yes.”

    Kate huffs and sulks for the next 10 minutes until a dark green Jaguar pulls up to the curb. The passenger side window rolls down, revealing a beautiful woman with caramel skin and long, dark hair. She says something in Russian, that makes Yelena chuckle, before she steps out of the alcove. Kate follows behind her, feeling both on edge and a little annoyed. She does not like being kept in the dark.

    Her irritation grows when Yelena sits in the front, leaving her to get into the back alone and the mystery woman immediately starts speaking Russian to her. She slips into the backseat nonetheless, trusting Yelena to not get her killed or something.

    Kate hears Yelena mention Central Park and they are off, making their way out of the small streets of the Queens neighborhood. She tries to pick up anything she might understand, very curious to find out who this woman is, but she can’t make a word out of the foreign conversation. She listens silently and takes in the mystery woman. She is young, probably around Yelena’s age, and has an easy, objectively beautiful smile. There are a couple tattoos on her slim arms, and her eyes a warm, dark brown when meet the Kate’s in the rearview mirror.

    “So you are Kate Bishop.”

    Her accent is similar to Yelena’s when she switches to English, and there is an amused lilt to her voice. Kate lifts her chin, keeping the woman’s gaze in the mirror. “Yes, that’s me. And you are?”

    The woman says something in Russian again, her tone still clearly amused. Kate feels like there is a joke she is missing, and she doesn’t like it at all. Before she can say more, Kate interrupts her.

    “That’s pretty rude you know. Talking about someone while they can’t understand you.” The woman’s brown eyes glint in delight, and Yelena sighs but she sounds amused as well when she speaks.

    “Sonya, be nice. We had a long day.”

    Okay, so at least she knows the woman’s name now.

    Sonya gives up staring at Kate trough the rearview mirror, but Kate can see the side of her face from behind and the corners of her mouth are still tilting upwards. They leave the subway station surrounded by police cars behind and Yelena and Sonya drop the Russian conversation at least. She puts aside her irritation in favor of trying to learn the information Yelena refused to give her.

    “So how do you two know each other?”

    Sonya glances at her in the mirror again, her smile widening.

    “We used to work together.”

    Well, that’s vague. Is she a corporate spy too? An assassin. Oohh…Okay, the accent probably should have tipped her off, that’s on her. She tries to mask her surprise and thinks she manages when her voice comes out even, as if she is just making conversation. “You are a Black Widow.”

    Sonya nods a smile still, as she merges into the busy traffic of Queens Boulevard. “I was a Black Widow. I am retired now.”

    Ha. She sends Yelena an obnoxiously smug look, having figured out what she was trying to keep from her but she only receives a playful eyeroll and a smile in return. “So what made you two have a long day before 2 pm?”

    Kate waits for Yelena to answer, but she seems to be content to let them converse, turning back to watch the city passing by so Kate tries to put on a cool nonchalant face as she answers.

    “You know, breaking into a storage facility, fighting a bunch of assassins and a super-soldier. Just a casual Friday morning.”

    Sonya chuckles, then glances at Yelena with an eyebrow raised and she nods with a smile, looking out at the city passing by.

    “They were hired by the Kingpin too?”

    The question is directed at Yelena, but Kate’s brain grinds to a stop and she does not manage to mask her surprise this time.

    “How do you know about him?”

    Sonya just laughs again, her pretty white teeth showing as she meets Kate’s gaze in the mirror again.

    “They tried to hire me to kill you too.”

    Kate’s eyes widen, then jump to Yelena who for some reason keeps relaxedly staring out the window, as if this is not brand new information for her. Sonya continues when she sees Kate’s shocked face in the mirror.

    “Don’t worry, as I said I am retired…besides, none of us would hurt you.” Oh yeah, because that’s totally reassuring. What is it about these Russian women that they constantly give her whiplash.

    “Um…thank you?”

    Sonya seems to think for a second then adds.

    “None of us free of mind control, at least.”

    Kate is still so shook up that she almost doesn’t catch it, but she sees Yelena stiffen ever so slightly from the corner of her eyes and she plays back what was said in her head. Her brows furrow, confused.

    “Mind control?”

    It’s the first time Sonya’s smile dims on her face for a moment, and Kate sees her glance at Yelena who stares stoically ahead, before giving one small shake of her head. Sonya’s mask is back in a second, a wide smile on her face.

    “Just a saying we have in Russia.”

    Yeah, Kate wouldn’t buy that even if she didn’t see Yelena’s reaction but she lets it pass, glancing at Yelena before looking back at Sonya in the mirror. She will ask her later. “Oh, okay.”

    Sonya visibly relaxes, her smile fading into something more natural.

    “So Kate Bishop, what do you do for a living?”

    Kate is baffled by the quick topic change, raising an eyebrow but answers anyway. “Um…I am a PI. Private Investigator.”

    “Does that pay well?”

    Kate snorts.

    “No, but I don’t need it to.”

    Sonya meets her eyes in the mirror again, giving her a sly smile.

    “Oh yes, you are very rich.”

    Kate looks to the side before meeting her eyes again. There is no good way to answer that. “Uh, yeah. Sure.”

    Sonya seems to think before she asks her next question.

    “Do you have a husband?”

    Kate scoffs. The woman obviously knows quite a lot about her, and probably is well aware she is not married, but she entertains the questions, trying to figure out what the hell Sonya is trying to get at.

    “Nope. No husband.”

    “How about a wife?”

    Is she about to be hit on in some weird roundabout way?

    Yelena says something in Russian with an eyeroll, but Kate cuts in before Sonya can answer. “Why, are you offering?”

    She says it to unbalance the woman, but she only gets a wild, bubbling laugh from Sonya, and sees the side of Yelena’s face as tips of her lips lift too.

    “Kate Bishop, you flirt!”

    She offers a slanted grin of her own, shrugging.

    “With all these questions, a girl’s gotta wonder.”

    Sonya laughs again, winking at Kate in the mirror before she pursues her mouth as if she is seriously considering it.

    “Well, no…I could never have my wife run around all day and night with this one.” She gestures at Yelena who rubs her forehead like she is entirely done with this conversation, but she looks relaxed enough otherwise so Kate allows herself to embrace her curiosity. This is the first time she met anyone who knows Yelena and she is ready to not be the subject of the friendly teasing for once.

    “Why? What’s wrong with running around with Yelena?”

    It doesn’t go the way she thought it would.

    “Well just look at that face. Her beautiful hair. Who could resist that?” Is…is Sonya hitting on Yelena then? She shifts in her seat, completely baffled. “Um, yeah.”

    “Don’t you think she is beautiful, Kate Bishop?”

    If Kate wasn’t so confused she would find this whole conversation hilarious. Yelena sends a half-serious glare across the center console at Sonya, but the woman continues to just smile expectantly as she drives them across the bridge to Manhattan.

    “I mean yeah, of course I think she is beautiful. I have eyes.”

    Yelena turns to look back at her, with an eyebrow raised and a smug expression on her face. Kate just shrugs, not embarrassed. She does have eyes. Sonya seems to be satisfied with her answer, grinning widely.

    “Exactly. Can’t have my wife around that all the time. She would either be killed or seduced.”

    Yelena turns back to Sonya, her tone dry but her eyes glinting with mirth. “Who said I would want your wife, Sonya? I have seen the men you date.” Sonya bursts out laughing, and Kate smiles too. She is pretty sure Yelena is not going to lie down and just take the teasing from her friend. Sonya just waves, not at all offended. “Ay Yelena, you said Thomas is handsome.”

    “Handsome, yes. But he is scrawny. Like a twig.”

    Sonya is still not phased. Quite the opposite, her smile just widens.

    “He is not scrawny, he is just agile. His stamina is mind-blowing.”

    Sonya wiggles her eyebrows suggestively and Yelena makes a grossed out face. Kate agrees, but laughs at it nonetheless. Sonya just barrels on.

    “Besides, we are not talking about Thomas, we are talking about Kate Bishop. She is definitely not scrawny. Those arms look like they could break you in half.” Kate feels the tips of her ears go warm, and she is sure they are turning red at Sonya’s tone, dripping with innuendo.

    “Um, thanks?”

    Sonya gives her another wink.

    “You are very welcome.”

    Yelena just looks at her friend, an eyebrow raised in amusement.

    “Are you done?”

    She isn’t. Sonya’s eyes are on the road, but her grin is positively Cheshire cat-like. “What Yelena, you are telling me you have spent days with this woman, and haven’t once thought about climbing her like a tree?”

    Kate makes a choked sound and cuts in before any answer can be given. Whatever the answer is, it’d make their work together going forward incredibly awkward.

    “For the love of God, Yelena, I am begging you not to answer that.”

    Sonya and Yelena laugh at her embarrassment in unison, before Yelena answers without turning back to look at her.

    “Forgive Sonya please. She thinks she is a character from Sex and the City. She even has a blog.”

    Kate chuckles, shaking her head and thankful for the topic change. Her face still feels like it’s on fire.

    “What is it with you Black Widows and that show?”

    Sonya’s smile softens, and she looks at Yelena, seemingly waiting for her to answer. She sighs before looking out the window.

    “It was Natasha’s favorite TV show. She made me watch and I showed it to a couple of the others.”

    Kate processes what she was told. She never met Natasha Romanoff, but she finds it hard to imagine The Black Widow watching Sex and the City. Then again, a few years ago she couldn’t have imagined spending Christmases with Hawkeye, wearing ugly sweaters so she probably should not be surprised. Yelena interrupts her thought process when she speaks again, her voice fond talking about her sister.

    “When she came to America, apparently it was all the craze, and she watched it to learn about American women.”

    Kate chuckles. She is about to comment that although she has never seen the show, she very much doubts it is an accurate portrayal of average American women, but they arrive to the south-east corner of Central Park.

    “Where am I dropping you off?”

    “Columbus Circle works great, thanks.”

    Yelena doesn’t follow up with any more information about Natasha, and the topic seems to have broken Sonya out of her teasing mood too, so they spend the remaining few minutes of the ride in silence. Kate feels the weight of the day slowly settle over her. Her body feels mostly fine, apart from her sore ribs and a pounding headache, but she is exhausted. She also feels like she needs a shower more than she ever did in her life.

    “Thank you for the ride!”

    She says goodbye to Sonya when she drops them off, and she sends her a wave in return and a wink over her shoulder as Kate slips out of the car. Yelena and Sonya converse a few more sentences in Russian, before she joins Kate on the sidewalk.

    The Jaguar speeds off and they start walking towards Kate’s apartment in silence. Kate breaks it after a few moments.

    “I can’t believe we fought a super-solider today, and the most stressful part of the day was still the ride home with your friend.”

    Yelena laughs, and Kate can't help but smile at the sound.

    Chapter End Notes Heya everyone!

    So, I was a bit braver with this chapter, and there is a lot of ridiculous stuff in here :D I hope you all like it.

    The Rasputin bit is because I usually put on music to help me get in the mood to write a particular scene, and Rasputin randomly came on my playlist and I honestly had such a good laugh imagining a)A car chase with that soundtrack b)Yelena being outraged at what a stupid song it is especially about Russia/a russian man.

    Before anyone asks, the super soldier is not anyone we know from Marvel. Tbh, after TFWS I kinda have this headcanon that there are people out there who got injected with the serum, or some version of it.

    Also, I see a lot of people put Russian (I assume, translated by Google) into their fics, but we see things from Kate's perspective here, so it makes no sense in my mind to translate anything back and forth, as anything is juts "Russian gibberish" in her head. :D On that note, I hope you all like Sonya, I kinda took the 3 seconds we saw of her in Hawkeye, and ran with it.

    :) As always, please feel free to leave a comment (or kudos). I read all of them and they mean the world to me!

    Next chapter will be up sometime during the weekend. (Hopefully, I am having a very busy week :S)

    Chapter 7

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes When they enter the apartment Kate feels ready to crash. Yelena too, walks straight to the couch and sits down. She looks both exhausted and stiff, but gives Lucky a few pats when he jumps up next to her.

    “It’s time we had that drink.”

    Kate leaves the room and comes back with two beers and two packs of frozen peas. Yelena takes one of each, putting the peas onto the bruise on her cheek, leaning her head against the back of the couch. Kate collapses down next to her and puts her own bag of frozen vegetables against the back of her head. She offers her bottle to Yelena who clinks her own against it. “How do you say ‘Cheers’ in Russian?”

    “Za zda-ró-vye”

    Kate tries to say it after her, the foreign words awkward on her lips. “Nazdrobodye”

    Yelena blurts out laughing, her nose scrunching up, but her eyes are warm when she turns her head to look at Kate, who grins at the ridiculous sight of the peas covering half of Yelena’s face, “We will work on that.”

    They both take a swing from their drinks, silence enveloping the room. Kate is pretty sure she will pass out on the couch, and is slowly getting there when Yelena’s voice rouses her.

    “You can ask about it.”

    Her mind is sluggish and she opens her eyes she didn’t realize she closed, turning her head to look at Yelena.

    “Ask about what?”

    She doesn’t look at Kate, her eyes are closed too, head resting against the couch. “What Sonya said in the car.”

    Kate takes another sip of her beer. She has a pretty good idea what Yelena means, but Sonya said a lot of things in the car.

    “Climbing me like a tree?”

    Yelena’s lips twitch upwards, and she opens her eyes and turns to meet Kate’s gaze. She is silent for a long moment, just looking at her.

    “Mind-control.”

    Kate thinks about what to ask, as Yelena keeps looking at her silently. She feels she doesn’t have enough to go on to ask the right questions. The peas against her head soak the neck of her t-shirt as they slowly melt.

    “I…to be honest I don’t even know what I should be asking. Um…mind-control exists?” The smile on Yelena’s face doesn’t drop, but it dims a little. She nods at Kate. “And there are Black Widows under mind-control.”

    Yelena turns her gaze to Lucky, who nudges her hand with his nose, pushing his head under her palm.

    “Not many anymore. We freed all the ones we could find.”

    “…we?”

    “My mother. My father. Natasha. Sonya. I. Some others. ”

    Kate does not pretend to not be surprised. She asked Clint about Black Widows before, and read the files Natasha released to the Internet back in the day, but she doesn’t remember hearing or reading about any of this.

    “But…who could put a Black Widow under mind-control? How does it even work?” Yelena is still looking at Lucky, stroking his soft head with slow, relaxing motions, her voice sounds detached to Kate.

    “It is chemical subjugation. They found the neuropathways that control free will and chemically altered them until they had obedience without a possibility for insubordination.” Kate blinks a few times, attempting to process what she is told.

    “Who is ‘they’ in this scenario?”

    “The Red Room. The man who ran it.”

    Kate stares at her, all sleepiness gone from her body by now.

    “Wait a minute, you are telling me that Black Widows had been under mind-control? Like the whole time?”

    Yelena looks up from Lucky to meet her wide eyes for a moment.

    “Not…exactly. Older Widows were psychologically conditioned…When Natasha deserted, they wanted to make sure it never happened again. So they put the ones that were still in training under.”

    The next question is obvious, but she takes a swing of her drink again to buy some time. It feels personal. Too personal. Yelena has shared a couple of things about her life before, but definitely nothing of this magnitude, apart from being Natasha’s sister that is. She gulps and turns back to Yelena slowly.

    “Were you still in training?”

    Yelena looks back up at her, nodding and holding her gaze this time. Kate thinks that is what the stiffness in the car has been about.

    “How long were you…?”

    “15 years, give or take.”

    Kate stares at her, her eyes wide and mouth agape. She feels utterly lost on what to say next. Fifteen years. She doesn’t exactly know how old Yelena is but it must have been the better part of her life. She opens and closes her mouth a few times, unsure how to continue. Yelena smiles at her loss of words, her eyes dropping to her own lap.

    “If I knew this would render you speechless, I would have told you earlier.” Kate doesn’t smile at the attempt at humor. Fifteen years. The more and more she learns about Yelena’s past, the more she is genuinely astonished at how well adjusted she is, all things considered. She doesn’t speak for a few moments.

    “How did you…get out?”

    Yelena picks at the paper on her beer bottle, not looking at her.

    “I was sent on a mission to retrieve the counteragent. The widow who had it, her name was Oksana…I killed her, but she exposed me to it before she died. I took the antidote, and ran.” Yelena’s voice is hallow as she explains, an octave lower than usual even. “Where did the…um…counteragent come from?”

    “An older Widow synthetized it in secret, when she learned what they were doing.” Kate thinks she knows where this is going, and a small smile slides over her face. “Was that your mom? Is that how you reconnected?”

    She doesn’t know what to think when Yelena takes a long swing of her beer. “No. She was actually the one to create the mind-control agent. We reconnected when Natasha and I went to interrogate her about where to find the Red Room.” Oh wow, okay. Yelena really had a point with mothers being complicated business, she thinks before she remembers what Yelena said earlier, her brow furrowing.

    “Didn’t you say she helped to free the Widows too?”

    Yelena nods, her features easing a little.

    “That came after.”

    Kate takes a sip of her beer too, and thinks, confusion clouding her again. “Wait, you grew up in the Red Room, right? How did you not know where it was?” “Yes. But we were always sedated at entry and exit. We never knew where it was.” Kate blinks, then nods slowly, sucking in her cheeks, pondering it all. She doesn’t know whether she should ask the next question, but Yelena has been open about the topic since they started talking about it, so she takes a deep breath and asks, her voice gentle. “What did it feel like?”

    Yelena licks her lips, and meets her eyes again as she explains, holding her gaze. “It’s…it’s hard to describe. You are fully conscious, but you don’t know which part is you. You have no control over what you are doing. They can tell you to stop breathing, and you will have no choice but to suffocate.”

    “That…that sounds terrifying.”

    Yelena gulps, her eyes dropping for a second to her bottle before she looks back at Kate, and nods.

    “What was it like to…well, to wake up?”

    Yelena thinks about the answer for longer this time, her brow furrowed, lips pursed and eyes turned downwards. Her is tone thoughtful when she speaks finally.

    “You would think it would be the happiest thing but…it was scary too. I grew up not being… me.” she meets Kate’s eyes for a moment before looking at her bottle again “And it took me a long time to figure out who I was without it.”

    She can’t even imagine what that feels like. Growing up, especially as a rich kid with very lenient and liberal parents, she was allowed to be herself as much as possible. Apart from her mom being adamant that she will work for Bishop Security, there was not one thing she couldn’t be, nothing she couldn’t try.

    “I honestly don’t know what to say Yelena. I am so sorry you went through that.” “It’s in the past now. Dreykov is dead, I am not, and I am free to do what I want.” It almost feels like something Yelena has told herself before. Maybe she has. Kate feels like she should hug her, like she wants to hug her, but she doesn’t think they are at that stage in their friendship. She puts a hand over Yelena’s on the couch, and she looks up at Kate, eyes unreadable.

    “Thank you for telling me.”

    Yelena looks at her for a long moment, before she smiles. It’s sad, but it seems meaningful and Kate smiles back, hoping she is offering comfort in some form.

    Yelena’s phone buzzing interrupts the moment. She pulls her hand from under Kate’s and digs into her pocket with a flinch. She looks at the screen, and sighs deeply at whatever she finds, but her tone is light when she picks it up.

    “Clint Barton.”

    Kate can hear Clint’s agitated voice from across the couch.

    “Yelena! Are you with Kate?!”

    Yelena rolls her eyes with a smile and pulls the phone away from her ears, putting it on speaker.

    “Yes, she is with me.”

    “Hi Clint!”

    “Kate! Why the hell is your phone turned off?”

    “Oh yeah…um…my phone kinda got wrecked. Sorry.”

    …blown up with the car, is what she doesn’t say. He exhales deeply, calming down a little. Her heart kind of skips a beat though when he speaks next, his voice dry. “Oh, did that happen when you blew up a storage building or when you fought a super soldier in Queens?”

    Oh shit.

    “What the…?”

    He interrupts her, and his voice is so fatherly and disappointed, it kind of makes her heart ache.

    “You are on TV, Kate.“ …

    “I…What?”

    So much for under the radar. Next to her Yelena turns on the TV, flipping it to CNN. Sure enough, they are showing cell phone footage of Yelena and Kate trading punches with the super soldier.

    “YES, Kate! What were you thinking?”

    “Okay Barton, drop the worried father act. We had it under control.”

    Yelena’s voice is cool and collected when she speaks, her eyes still on the footage. There is no sign of the conversation they just had on her face.

    “…Under control?!”

    Kate can imagine the vein on his neck throbbing from his anger. Okay yeah, this does look like a huge mess.

    “Yeah! If you look at the video you can’t tell it’s us but you can totally tell we kicked his ass actually.”

    She is bluffing, hoping to save face. There is a deeps sigh on the other end of the line, and his voice is resigned when he speaks next.

    “What the hell did you two get into?”

    Kate takes a deep breath, preparing to explain but Yelena beats her to speaking first. “I did not get into anything. And I did tell Kate it was stupid.”

    Kate sends her a half-serious betrayed look, her voice dry as sandpaper. “Wow Yelena, thanks.”

    She just shrugs at Kate with a grin.

    “I did tell you.”

    Kate points at her, her eyes narrowed playfully.

    “No. No-no. You said not going to Ohio was stupid, but you were all in on going after Fisk from the get go.”

    “What?!?!”

    Clint’s voice is uncharacteristically high as he asks, and under any other circumstance, Kate would find that hilarious. This time she just cringes. Yelena beats her to answering again. “Yes I invited Kate to come to Ohio with me, Barton. Keep up.”

    Yelena grins and Kate is at least relieved to be reminded that she doesn’t only enjoy fucking with her.

    “That is not what I am hung up on, Yelena. Fisk. What the hell are you two doing with Fisk?!”

    Of course Yelena now choses to be silent, just watching the footage on the TV as if she is watching a movie. Kate sighs.

    “Okay, in my defense, I didn’t start it! I came back to New York, with every intention of laying low until the trial.”

    “Yeah, I can see how great that’s been going.”

    Clint talks over her, but she ignores his commentary.

    “Then Yelena showed up, and told me Fisk hired her and a bunch of other people to kill me!” “She said no, right? You said no, right Yelena?”

    Yelena throws her hands up, her face affronted, but Kate is pretty sure it’s an act. “Why do you all question this? I literally came here so she doesn’t get herself killed.” Kate cuts her off, her tone dry. Payback “I mean you did show up in my apartment with a suitcase full of weapons.” She makes an obnoxious mocking face at Yelena who makes one right back at her, but she can see in her eyes that she is entertained.

    “To protect you ungrateful ass with!”

    Kate opens her mouth to answer, but Clint’s voice interrupts her from the speaker. “I still don’t understand how you get from Fisk trying to kill you, to you going after him.” “Well, I can’t just sit around wait for him to have me killed.”

    Yelena speaks before Clint can.

    “I told Kate she should leave, but she was all like ‘This is my life, I can’t run away, I have to face it’.”

    It’s a horrible imitation of Kate, and she scowls at Yelena.

    “What did I tell you about the American accent?”

    “My American accent is great, thank you very much.”

    “For god’s sake, children! Focus!”

    They both quiet down, but exchange a grin. Annoying each other is fun, but annoying Clint together? A fucking blast.

    “Tell me what happened today. One at a time.”

    Yelena gestures for her to go on, and she bows her head in mock gratitude. “We were looking at Fisk’s associates, and we found a storage unit under the name of his wife’s dead mother. We went to check it out, but it was a set up. The unit exploded and a bunch of mercenaries or like henchmen or whatever attacked us. We got away, but they followed. We took most of them out, but there was the super soldier amongst them. We totally beat his ass, but they blew up our car, so we ran to the subway and hid in the crowd. We got home like half an hour ago.”

    Clint listens to her silently and he is quiet for a few second after she finishes. “Are you sure you weren’t followed?”

    “Yeah, Yelena made us walk like a thousand blocks to make sure.”

    Clint sighs, he sounds tired when he speaks.

    “Okay. I will get on a flight tomorrow.”

    Kate smiles, but shakes her head. She would love to have him by her side but they do have it under control. And he really is serious about wanting to be retired.

    “Clint, thank you, but you don’t need to. We are not looking for trouble, I promise.” “You are literally doing just that.”

    “Well…okay, yeah. Technically we are. But we are nowhere close to finding him.” “But…”

    “I will call you if we are, I promise. But really, we are fine. Just a liiiittle snooping.” “Kid, this is not a joke. He is a very dangerous enemy to have.”

    “I know.”

    “I mean it. You have to be smart about this.”

    “We were smart about it. And when things got tight, we managed too.”

    She looks at Yelena and she nods at Kate. The day was a shitshow, but they rolled with the punches, literally. He is quiet, and she speaks again to persuade him. “Really Clint. All we are doing is trying to find out where he is.”

    Clint sighs again, she imagines him rubbing his face.

    “You two are being safe?”

    Kate grins at the combination of his wording and dad-like tone, and Yelena snickers. “I promise you Clint Barton, neither of us will get pregnant.”

    “Jesus Christ.”

    Clint sounds entirely done and Kate laughs but continues quickly before he can change his mind.

    “No, seriously. We are Clint. We really are. And I will call you if we have any solid leads.” “Okay…Okay, fine. But don’t do anything stupid. And don’t get distracted.” “I won’t. I promise.”

    He doesn’t sound convinced.

    “Yelena make sure she is not distracted.”

    Yelena just grins cheekily.

    “You are not the boss of me.”

    Kate chuckles again at Clint’s deep, resigned exhale.

    “We are totally not distracted. Very professional. Absolutely…”

    “Yeah okay, shut up before I change my mind.”

    They exchange another grin.

    “Okay, I guess I leave you to it. Let me know if you find anything.”

    “Will do. Byee Clint!”

    “Goodbye, Barton.”

    Clint hangs up, and Yelena puts the frozen vegetables back on her face and closes her eyes again, apparently done with the conversation.

    Kate watches the phone footage on the TV, and she is thankful to note that apart from Clint probably nobody else will be able to guess their identities. Their faces are almost entirely obscured, the footage is pretty shaky and it was obviously filmed by someone hiding upstairs in one of the buildings.

    “Should we talk about what happened today?”

    Yelena doesn’t acknowledge her verbally, just hums for her to continue. “How did he know we would be looking there?”

    Yelena doesn’t answer her for a few moments and when she does, she still doesn’t open her eyes.

    “The Kingpin must have someone in your police force working for him. Do you trust this Wendy woman?

    Kate thinks about it. Wendy has helped them against Kingpin before too, and she has no reason to doubt her.

    “Yes.”

    Yelena nods.

    “Then he must have paid or threatened someone else into slipping it into the files they gave us.”

    Kate is silent for a second, pondering Yelena’s words.

    “How do we know the rest of the files were not tampered with?”

    Yelena opens her eyes and turns to look at her with the one eye not covered by the peas, and her face is a clear enough answer.

    They don’t.

    Kate does pass out on the couch, and when she wakes up, it’s to the back of her shirt being completely soaked from the melting vegetables and with Yelena sleeping next to her. She looks peaceful, her face smooth in a way it never is when she is awake. The once frozen peas have fallen next to her, soaking Kate’s sofa and Lucky is snoozing away, tucked into Yelena’s side, her arm resting over him. She smiles at the sight and looks at the two of them for a little while, until she realizes it’s probably creepy that she is watching Yelena sleep. She quickly looks away, and shivers.

    The sun has set since they fell asleep and she feels chilly in her wet shirt, so she rises as quietly as she can, tiptoeing to her room. It’s probably a testament to how tired Yelena was that she doesn’t wake up to any of it. Or maybe she is just a heavy sleeper, Kate doesn’t now. Lucky opens his one good eye, but doesn’t move from Yelena’s side, and she smiles internally at how much he seems to like her.

    Once in her room, she picks up a change of clothes, and makes her way to the bathroom. The mirror reinforces the fact she already knew, that she looks like a hot mess. She quickly undresses, her body feels sore and heavier than usual, but still better than it could or should be, all things considered.

    She thinks about the events of their day while she showers, washing herself thoroughly from the blood, grime and sweat. Fisk was obviously a step ahead of them, and he anticipated that Kate will go after him. The files they have been given by Wendy were obviously tampered with, so the information they are looking for might be purposefully missing, and false evidence might be planted all over.

    She puts conditioner on her hair, wincing as she touches the small bump on the back of her head, where the super soldier slammed her against the road. She sighs, they need to scratch everything they got from those files, go back to square one. Maybe they could try to find Fisk through the assassins he sent after her? Oh yeah, Clint would love that plan. She washes her hair off, reveling in the way the warm water soothes her aching body until her stomach grumbles and she realizes she hasn’t eaten anything all day, which distracts her from her earlier thoughts. She gets out and towels herself off quickly. When she exits the bathroom, Yelena and Lucky are still snoozing on the couch and she picks up her tablet and tiptoes her way to the kitchen.

    She considers ordering food, but she feels way too hungry to wait for that, so she takes out a pot to boil some water. She orders a new phone while she waits, then starts grating cheese. She usually puts on some music on the rare occasions when she cooks but today she is working in silence, her thoughts going back to the case they are working. She doesn’t have access to Bishop Security’s phone tracking software anymore, and according to the questionable evidence they have, neither Fisk himself, or his wife have been seen for a long while.

    She drains the pasta, and puts it in a pan, mixing it with the shredded cheese. But if Fisk is still in the city, there has to be some traces of it. He has to live somewhere, eat, do things, right?

    “You are making macaroni?”

    She lets out a yelp, but immediately attempts to downplay it. When she turns around, Yelena is grinning and she is pretty sure she didn’t mange to play it cool. Well, if defense doesn’t work, offense will have to do.

    “Yes. That fight was so long and I was staaarving.”

    She drops her voice an octave, and leans hard into the Russian accent. She receives a raised eyebrow and an unimpressed, but amused expression in return.

    “Should I throw a bottle of hot sauce at you to complete this little scene?” Kate grins at her.

    “Please don’t, I am really not sure I could catch it and my head already hurts like a bitch.” Yelena grins back, then comes over to look into the pan. Her eyes widen. “Kate! You are burning it!”

    She attempts to pull the pan off of the stove, but Kate slaps her hand away with a movement even she is surprised by. Yelena gapes at her, and she attempts to play it cool again. “I am frying it.”

    Yelena is somehow even more offended by this, than the slap to her wrist. “Why would you do that?”

    “It’s delicious, you will see.”

    Yelena stares at her for a second, probably contemplating physically fighting her over the integrity of the mac’n’cheese, but in the end she steps back, holding up both hands. “Okay, but if it’s shit, I get all the good gooey parts and you can eat the burnt bits.” Kate laughs and turns back to her creation. She smiles at the memory that enters her mind. “This is how my dad always used to make it.”

    Kate can’t see Yelena, and she doesn’t answer anything so she just focuses on checking the bottom of the pasta every few seconds. When she gets the golden brown color she is looking for, she pulls the pan off of the stove, and cuts the now stuck together pasta in half. She gets out two plates, and deposits the mac’n’cheese onto them, turning back to the kitchen island. Yelena is looking at her, leaning against the kitchen counter, following her movements with an expression Kate can’t read but she seems to shake herself off, and goes to get them some forks. She sits, just as Kate puts down the plate in front of her, eyeing the cheesy pasta suspiciously.

    Kate smiles to herself, and goes up to the fridge to get them some drinks, stopping by one of the cupboards on her way back.

    “Do you want some ibuprofen?”

    “Yes, thank you.”

    She takes two pills and the siracha she has in the same cabinet, and brings it back together to the kitchen island. She passes the items to Yelena, keeping one pill and one of the waters for herself. She takes the pill as she sits down, and digs in immediately. Across from her, Yelena drowns her own portion in hot sauce. She is so hungry that she forgets about their conversation, just eating in silence until Yelena speaks.

    “I am willing to admit when I was wrong. This is one of those rare cases. This is very good.” She looks up at Yelena, amused at her little tangent. She smiles smugly and shrugs. “Told ya.”

    Yelena smiles back as Kate continues.

    “This is like one of the three things I know how to cook.”

    Yelena’s smile widens, but her tone is uncharacteristically gentle when she asks. “Did your father teach you?”

    Kate smiles again at the memory of this, filling her up and warming her insides. She nods, then looks down to her plate.

    “We used to make it together.”

    She resumes to eat and so does Yelena and soon their plates are empty. Before she can get up and start getting their dishes, Yelena raises.

    “No, stay. You cooked, I clean up.”

    Kate smiles thankfully as Yelena takes her plate too, and puts it in the dishwasher with her own. She rinses the pot and the pan, before putting them in there too then looks for a pod to put into the machine.

    She halts once she is finished, looking at the buttons on the door’s edge. “Kate?”

    “Yeah?”

    “What buttons do I push?”

    Kate stifles her smile.

    “Wait, I’ll show you.”

    She gets up and walks over to Yelena, leaning down next to her over the dishwasher. “You press this first to set the temperature, then this one to choose a program, then the big one on the right to start it and then you just close it.”

    She looks over to Yelena, who looks down on the buttons very seriously, probably memorizing which ones are which and she is suddenly reminded of Sonya’s question earlier. Don’t you think she is beautiful, Kate Bishop? In that moment, in the dim lights and quiet of her kitchen, she kind of thinks that’s an understatement.

    She shakes off the thought after a moment. They had a really long and intense day and Yelena is attractive, objectively speaking. Kate just really needs to sleep, properly, in her bed, and probably needs to get laid, like in general.

    She leans up, and looks as Yelena presses the buttons she showed, and then closes the door of the dishwasher, a satisfied little smile on her face when they hear it turn on and Kate ignores the small voice in her head telling her that it’s really cute.

    Yelena straightens, and taps Kate’s tablet to look at the time. 10:54 pm. “I should get going.”

    She doesn’t know why she says it. It’s probably the earlier heart to heart they had in combination with the intense day, and like practically, it makes sense. But it kind of just slips out.

    “Or…you could stay.”

    Yelena is visibly surprised, looking at her with eyebrows raised. Kate quickly continues. “I mean, it makes no sense for you to go only to come back in the morning. And like, you are paying for a hotel, even though I am not paying you. You can just sleep over. It’s just practical.”

    Yelena blinks a few times, before she collects herself. She looks Kate up and down, then sighs.

    “Kate, if you Sonya put in some exciting ideas in your head, I have to tell you that I am pretty tired from the fight and…”

    Kate gapes then cuts in, heat filling her face.

    “Guest room! I meant in the guest room. I was not…”

    Yelena’s face cracks, an enormous grin taking over her features.

    Oh.

    Kate closes her eyes, exhaling, and smiles too.

    “…You are fucking with me, aren’t you.”

    “I just told you that I am not.”

    Kate opens her eyes to give her a glare, huffing but she can’t keep the smile from her face. Yelena snickers as she walks by her.

    “You are so easy, Kate Bishop.”

    Kate follows her, preparing to lock the door behind her and maybe hide under her sheets in embarrassment but Yelena doesn’t walk out. Instead she picks up her phone from the coffee table and turns to Kate.

    “Do you have a phone charger and an extra towel? I really need to shower.” Oh okay. She is staying.

    “Yeah, sure. Um,…one sec.“ She goes to the closet to pull out a towel for Yelena, and then goes to her bedroom to get the charger and a change of clothes. Yelena waits for her, standing in her living room and if she feels the awkwardness that Kate does, she doesn’t show it.

    “I’ll just brush my teeth then you can have the bathroom.”

    Yelena nods and walks into the guestroom, and Kate quickly brushes her teeth, washes her face and pulls out an unused toothbrush for Yelena. When she emerges from the bathroom, Yelena is waiting, with the towel draped over her arm.

    “Goodnight! I put a toothbrush for you on the counter.”

    Yelena smiles at her, as she passes her, her eyes amused for some reason. “Thank you. Goodnight.”

    She closes the door behind herself and Kate lets out a breath she didn’t know she was holding. She locks the front door, and walks into her bedroom, just as she hears the shower start.

    Chapter End Notes Hi guys, This is a bit of a slower one, winding down after the action of the last two chapters. I hope you enjoy it :)

    On another note, I recommend you all try frying mac'n'cheese, my gf showed that to me and it is magic :D Also, I know I am a bit late with this update, sorry! Next chapter will be up sometime mid-week! :)

    xx

    Chapter 8

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Kate wakes up to the smell of bacon. Fried bacon.

    It raises her from her bed, and she puts on her sweats, then exits her room, still partially asleep. She walks into the kitchen, and halts at the sight that greets her. Yelena stands in front of the stove, in the pajamas Kate gave her last night, the bottoms rolled up several times, with her back to Kate. Her golden hair is up in a messy bun, and Lucky sits ever so faithfully by her legs, waiting for some scraps while Yelena is explaining something to him in Russian, gesturing with the spatula in her hand. Kate stares for several seconds, before Yelena’s voice jolts her from her daze.

    “Good morning Kate.”

    She says it without turning around, and Kate answers on autopilot. She walks up to the coffee maker, turning it on.

    “Good morning.”

    Yelena turns to her, and Kate is momentarily stuck again. Or still. Whatever. Give her time to wake up. She has seen Yelena without makeup before, but somehow with the combination of Kate’s too long pajama pants and the US Open Archery Championship – 2024 t-shirt, it somehow feels more…well, more. She looks younger, her face fresh, skin glowing in the morning light, apart from the bruise on her cheek and damn Sonya and her stupid questions. “Your new phone arrived, I put it in the living room.”

    “Oh, uh, thanks.”

    Yelena smiles, tilting her head to the side.

    “It’s funny how slow you are in the mornings.”

    “Yeah, I’m a…slow starter.”

    She ducks out of the kitchen, mostly to gather her bearings, and picks up the new phone from the coffee table. Opening the box, she unpacks it, and puts in the new SIM card. It turns on after a few seconds, and she quickly sets it up to restore her settings from the exploded phone through the Cloud.

    The process takes a few minutes, and she spends that time looking at the boards with information they have, trying to wake up and only picks the phone up again when it starts pinging with notifications coming in. She scrolls through them, just to see if there is anything that needs her immediate attention.

    13 missed calls from Clint (And he calls her clingy…)

    2 missed calls and a text Grills 1 missed call from an unknown number 1 text from Amanda Kate feels a bit guilty that she hasn’t even thought about her ever since they arrived to the storage facility yesterday. She opens her texts, rereading the conversation. [from: Amanda] Yesterday 8:16: When are you getting back?

    [to: Amanda] Yesterday 8:23 am: I don’t know. Not until the end of next week for sure. :( [from: Amanda] Yesterday 9:17 am: Awh :( I wanted to cook you dinner at my place on Sunday [to: Amanda] Yesterday 9:52 am: Sorry :/ But I will make it worth your while :) [from Amanda] Yesterday 11:31 am: Oh I am sure ;)

    She cringes. Her disappearing after that message is like super bad timing. She quickly types out her answer.

    [to Amanda] 10:37 am: So sorry for going AWOL! Phone died at the worst possible time and work got a bit crazy. How was your day yesterday?

    She hits send and hopes she didn’t ruin anything with her badly timed absence. She opens Grills’ message next.

    [from Grills] Yesterday 6:39 pm: Hey, was that you today in Queens? Are you guys okay? Let me know if you need help from the LARP Squad, we have your back. *flexed bicep emoji*

    She smiles at that text, typing her answer.

    [to Grills] 10:39 am: Hey Grills! *zipped mouth emoji* Thanks! We are good now but I’ll keep that in mind.

    “Kate! Breakfast is ready!”

    Yelena’s voice reaches her from the kitchen, and she puts her phone on the charger, leaving it in the living room. She walks back to the kitchen, and smiles at how Lucky follows Yelena around as she puts the a tall stack of pancakes and some bacon on the counter. “I am pretty sure you will have to fight Fanny for Lucky. He is pretty much in love with you.”

    Yelena smiles at her words, walking to one of the drawers to get them utensils. “Ah, Kate. If only. He is in love with bacon. I can only be a very sad second choice.” She purses her lips, and furrows her eyebrows.

    “Considering I jumped into traffic to save his life, I should be the sad second choice.” Yelena smiles smugly at her as Kate as they pass each other, Kate taking out juice from the fridge.

    “What can I say, he has good taste.”

    It takes Kate’s brain a second to catch up.

    “Heeyy.”

    Yelena just grins at her cheekily, as she settles by the kitchen island. Kate pours them both juice, and sits down too.

    “Thanks for breakfast.”

    “Thank you for the sleepover.”

    Kate rolls her eyes, but gives Yelena a lopsided smile.

    “Well, we didn’t even braid each other’s hair or anything.”

    Kate almost made a joke about spin the bottle, but she caught herself in time. Why are you like this, she asks herself anyway, internally cringing. Yelena eyes widen nonetheless. She looks excited.

    “You are supposed to braid each other’s hair at sleepovers?”

    “Wha…it’s an expression…”

    She kind of feels bad for raining on Yelena’s parade but she seems undeterred in her excitement.

    “I can do a lot of braids!”

    “Oh, that’s…that’s great…”

    “Your hair would look really pretty with one.”

    She is a bit taken aback by both the amount of enthusiasm Yelena is showing in the topic and the compliment.

    “Oh…thanks.”

    She runs a hand through her messy bed-hair unconsciously, and Yelena looks so earnest, she can’t help but smile at her. Yelena smiles back, nods to herself, and resumes eating her pancakes.

    “How is your head?”

    She asks half because the bruise on Yelena’s cheek looks painful, and half because she is afraid Yelena will offer to braid her hair, and Kate is not sure she wants her touching her anything, until she had some time to work out whatever weirdness has been going on with her since yesterday. Yelena just waves with her fork.

    “Oh, it’s nothing. It’ll be gone in a day or two.”

    It doesn’t look like it will, but Kate accepts her answer and goes back to eating her breakfast.

    “So, do you think we should go over the evidence again? Throw out anything we got from the police?”

    She asks after a while and Yelena leans back, chewing her food, thinking. “We should find out who had access to the files we got.”

    “Oh, smart! Maybe we can find out what they removed or added from in there.” She quickly retrieves her phone from the living room, putting another piece of pancake into her mouth, chewing as writes her message.

    [to Grills] 10:50 am: Actually, do you have Wendy’s number?

    She puts the phone down on the counter, and keeps eating until it buzzes. [from Grills] 10:52 am: Russian firecracker kicked your ass to the curb already? She rolls her eyes.

    [to Grills] 10:52 am: Ha-ha.

    [from Grills] 10:52 am: :D [to Grills] 10:53 am: We need to ask her something about the files she gave us [from Grills] 10:53 am: Just yanking your chain kid She receives a contact from him after, and saves it in her phone as ‘Wendy LARPD’, chuckling to herself at her own joke.

    [to Grills] 10:53 am: Thanks! :*

    She puts the phone on the counter, and wolves down the rest of her food. It feels good to have a way forward again. She looks at Yelena, who is finished with her breakfast too, typing on her own phone. For a second, Kate wonders who she is texting.

    She pushes the thought away, and gets up, picking up her dishes and Yelena’s, who is still immersed in her phone. She puts them in the dishwasher, and rinses the pan Yelena used for the pancakes before putting that in there too.

    She makes two cups of coffee, adding milk to her own, and milk and two spoons of sugar to Yelena’s before passing it to her. She receives a surprised smile, and gives a small one in return, before she sits back down, and picks up her phone, dialing Wendy’s number. She answers on the second ring.

    “Hello?”

    Kate raises her brow at her tone. It sounds croaky.

    “Hiii Wendy, it’s Kate. Kate Bishop. Grills gave me your number.”

    There is silence on the other end of the line for a few seconds.

    “Hi Kate. Sorry, I can’t really talk.”

    “Oh okay, sorry! Just a quick question. Did anyone else have access to the files you gave us?” “No. No. I don’t know.“ Okay, that’s a bit weird. Wendy’s voice is weird, desperate to end the call. “Are you sure? Because there was somethi…”

    “I am sorry, I have to go. Please don’t call again.”

    She hangs up and Kate pulls her phone away from her ear to stare at it. She looks up at Yelena to find her eyes already on her.

    “Okay so something is definitely going on with Wendy.”

    “You think she is working for him?”

    “I don’t know. She sounded very out of it.”

    “You think we should pay her a visit anyway?”

    “Yeah, I’ll get her address.”

    Yelena nods, and they get up. Kate quickly looks Wendy up while Yelena disappears into the guest room. She emerges just as Kate shuts her laptop, wearing her dusty clothes from yesterday.

    “I need to go and get new clothes and weapons. I’ll be back in 20 minutes.” Kate gets up, turning to her.

    “I can drive you.”

    “That will not be necessary. Get ready and I’ll be back.”

    Yelena walks out without another word.

    “Ooookay.”

    She says to the empty apartment. She quickly brushes her teeth, gets dressed in a new pair of black jeans and an olive green t-shirt, and takes out Lucky for a bathroom break, promising him a longer walk later.

    When she gets back to her apartment 15 minutes later, Yelena is already there, sitting on her couch, casually loading bullets into the magazine of a gun. Somehow she found the time to put on makeup too, the bruise on her cheek almost disappearing, and she wears black jeans and a New York t-shirt, her hair still in a bun. The thick black bracelets on her wrists are of course present too.

    Lucky bounds to Yelena like they haven’t seen each other in weeks and Kate shakes her head at the sight, smiling.

    “Hey”

    “Hello baby.”

    Yelena is cooing at Lucky, just as happy to see him as he is to see her, putting down the gun in her hand to fluff his fur, and scratch his ears, speaking to him softly in Russian. Kate grins, and turns to her bookcase, pulling out ‘All Poems of Emily Dickinson’ by an inch, before letting it fall back in place.

    The bookcase lets out a quiet hiss, then slides to the side, revealing the entrance to her "Utility Room"(she is still brainstorming ideas on what to call it). She goes in, retrieving a new collapsible bow and a quiver full of assorted trick arrows, putting it in a proper gun bag this time, as well as her special sunglasses after a moment of consideration. She exits the room, and finds something she never thought possible.
