    The sight of a truly, thoroughly dumbfounded Yelena.

    Yelena’s mouth hangs slightly open, her eyes wide as she looks between Kate and the secret doorway. She puts down her weapons bag on the side table by the door, then bathes in the sight. She grins at Yelena, leaning against the bookcase.

    “That was there the whole time?”

    “Yep.”

    She pops the p a little, which probably takes away from the cool-factor of having a secret vigilante lair, but whatever. She managed to finally astound Yelena. She will take the win. “I must see.”

    Kate laughs and makes a be my guest gesture with her arm, and Yelena is off the couch in a heartbeat. She walks in, not even sparing a glance to Kate, who leans off of the bookcase with a grin, walking in after her.

    “This apartment was some rich paranoid dude’s. He had a panic room, and I converted it for my own purposes.”

    She looks around the room too, as Yelena takes it in, and stands a bit taller, puffing out her chest in pride. There is an arrow making station, and a bunch of weapons. Mostly bows and various types of arrows of course, but there are a few swords on the wall too, and one spear- staff thing she received from Clint, who in turn got it from some Wakandans? Honestly, he asked her to keep it safe temporarily because Nate has been playing with it, and apparently it’s super-dangerous, but she has absolutely no intention of giving it back. She has some cool gadgets too, that she has been working on, but they are packed safely away in some of the drawers, except for the glasses. There are a few versions of her suit on the right side, hanging on the wall.

    Yelena takes it all in, and when she turns to Kate she swears she looks at her like she is seeing a new person.

    “This is so cool.”

    She grins at Yelena again, happy to take the compliment.

    “I know. Thank you…Well, it may not be an Iron Man suit, but it’s some of the best equipment money can buy.”

    “I am very impressed.”

    “I am glad you approve.”

    Yelena’s smile drops and her brow furrows.

    “I can’t believe you let me hide a grenade launcher in your fireplace, when you had this.” She gestures around the room with her arm, and Kate leans against on the shelves, packed full of boxes of arrow heads.

    “In my defense, I was pretty much in shock when you did all that.”

    “We were stuck in here for 3 days, and you never showed me! I am wounded.” She crosses her arms and pouts. Honest to god, pouts. Kate attempts to not focus it. “Well, do you want to stay wounded, or should we go and figure out what the hell is up with Wendy.”

    “That’s easy. I want to stay wounded.”

    Kate laughs and the corners of Yelena’s mouth tip upwards too for a second, before she is back to playing offended.

    “Come on. You can stay wounded in the car.”

    Yelena throws one last longing glance back towards the room, but follows her outside. Kate picks up her bag, containing her bow, and puts her retractable sword in her pocket, while Yelena picks up her gun from the table, slipping it into a hidden holster in the back of her jeans.

    “Now I feel like my hidden knives are not cool enough.”

    Kate gives her a side-eye, and opens the door, holding it for Yelena.

    “By Lucky!...Wait…what hidden knives?”

    That at least seems to appease her, the pout lessening in intensity and Kate stifles a smile as Yelena walks by her.

    “Wouldn’t you like to know…Bye Lucky! Be good!”

    They take the elevator down to the garage again, and Yelena takes her over, walking to the box containing the car keys.

    “I choose today.”

    Kate has to stifle another smile.

    “Okay. You can choose any of them, except the Mustang.”

    “Then I want the Mustang.”

    Yelena says it somewhat petulantly, but Kate's face is serious.

    “No.”

    Yelena reaches for the keys and she grabs her wrist.

    “Yelena, I mean it. It was my Dad’s.”

    Yelena looks at her for a moment, then goes back to her half-serious annoyance, and huffs. “Fine, but then I am driving.”

    Kate exhales.

    “Be my guest.”

    Yelena chooses a white Maserati and Kate rolls her eyes, walking after her when she takes off.

    “Not exactly great for blending in.”

    Yelena gets into the driver’s seat, not waiting for her to walk around. “We blend in by not trying to blending in.”

    Kate grins, and gets in at the passenger side.

    “Yeah, that sounds like a huge pile of bullshit.”

    She pulls up Wendy’s address on her phone, the car’s GPS connecting automatically. “If anyone asks, I’ll be a rich, Russian business woman, and you can be my gold-digger girlfriend.”

    Kate turns to Yelena in her seat.

    “Okay, first of all, why am I the gold-digger girlfriend? Second of all, who would even ask?” Kate asks trying to keep her voice offended but laughs into the sentence. “It is important to come up with a cover story in advance.”

    Kate shakes her head at the ridiculousness, still grinning. Yelena adjusts the seat, and the engine roars into life. Kate puts on her seatbelt and hopes she won’t regret letting her drive. “If anyone is the gold-digger girlfriend in our cover story, it’s you.” “You are too young to be this rich without raising questions.”

    “This is New York, Yelena. There are a lot of people born into money. And also, we are basically the same age. If I am too young, so are you.”

    Yelena scoffs, and sunlight illuminates her face, when they exit the garage. “I am 12 years older than you.”

    It’s Kate’s turn to snort.

    “Pfft. You are not.”

    Yelena digs into her pocket, and tosses a wallet into her lap. Kate looks at her in disbelief, then picks it up, opening it to see the ID inside. It’s an Ohio driver’s license, for someone named Elizabeth Humper. She laughs loudly, and Yelena seems to be fighting a smile too. “Check the birthdate.”

    “Yelena, this is obviously fake. Unless your real name is Lizzie Humper, in which case this is the best day of my life.”

    “It’s fake, yes, but the birthday is as close as it gets to the truth.” Kate checks the date and snorts again.

    “There is absolutely no way in hell that you are 35 years old.”

    “There absolutely is a way. I am.”

    Kate is shocked, then remembers that Yelena was Blipped, and quickly tries to lighten the mood.

    “Is there some secret Russian beauty treatment I should know about? You don’t look a day over 34.”

    Yelena grins, thankfully happy to not let the mood darken either. She snatches the wallet from Kate’s grasp, and puts it back in her pocket.

    “You really want to test me Kate Bishop? When I am driving such a fast car?” She takes a sharp and fast turn to make her point, and Kate has to hold onto the handle on the inside of the car to not tumble too hard to the side.

    “If you continue to drive like a maniac, you will not be driving soon.” Yelena gives Kate a challenging look over the center console.

    “What, you will fight me?”

    “No, you will get pulled over. And we will waste a bunch of time. And Lizzie Humper will lose her license.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes but takes the next turn at a more reasonable speed and Kate grins out the window.

    “So, what is our approach to this? Ooh…do you want to do good cop, bad cop?” Yelena glances at her again, face amused at her enthusiasm.

    “Can I be bad cop?”

    “You were born for the role.”

    She doesn’t mean it as a compliment, but Yelena smiles smugly like she took it as one and Kate will not correct her. She takes her phone out to put on some music and Yelena gives her a look.

    “If you put on the Rasputin song again, I will wreck this car.”

    Kate chuckles, but heeds her “request”, putting on some more contemporary music. “Always with the dramatics”

    They arrive to Wendy’s apartment building 20 minutes later, a bit before noon. It’s tall, and well kept, and Yelena is able to park the car almost in front of it, by some holy miracle of the New York City Parking Gods. When they walk up to the building, there is an older woman coming out the entrance and Kate grabs the door before it can close. She opens it for Yelena, and they walk to the elevator together.

    Kate presses the button for the 9th floor, and glances over at Yelena who seems to be getting into character, her face like stone, eyes staring ahead. Right. Good cop, bad cop. The doors open, and they find themselves in a corridor, with doors to both their left and right. Kate reads the numbers on them, determining they need to go left. In a few seconds, they are standing in front of apartment 94, which is supposedly Wendy’s.

    Kate takes a deep breath.

    “Let’s start with good cop, okay? We don’t know what’s going on.”

    She doesn’t wait for Yelena’s answer, and rings the bell. There are a few seconds of silence, and Yelena puts her palm over the peep hole, which Kate doesn’t understand but also doesn’t question. They hear the lock turn, a part of Wendy’s face appears through the opening, as the door moves.

    Her eyes, frantic already, widen at their sight. Kate gives a little wave. “Hiiii.”

    “Kate?! No! You can’t be here.”

    “We just need to talk to you. A few minutes, we are not mad I promise.” “No. You have to go.”

    She attempts to close the door, but Kate steps in the way before she can fully push it in place. “Wendy, what’s going on?”

    “You have to go, Kate. Now. Please.”

    She is pushing against the door, but it suddenly flies open, as Yelena shoves it hard, making Wendy stumble back. Kate quickly pushes inside, Yelena at her heels, and she takes in the scene. Wendy has a gun in her hand, but she never raises it, she just stares at them, face twisted in horror.

    She lifts both hands in a placating gesture, and hopes Yelena also understands to not escalate the situation. Something is wrong.

    “Wendy, please talk to me. What happened?”

    Wendy’s eyes just jump between Yelena and Kate frantically for a few seconds, before she seems to collapse into herself, and starts crying.

    “They…I am so sorry Kate. They took her.”

    Kate walks slowly towards her, doing her best to look non-threatening. “They took who?”

    She reaches Wendy and when she pulls the gun gently from her grasp, there is no resistance whatsoever. She extends her hand behind herself, without looking and the cold metal disappears from her grip in a second.

    “Annie. They took Annie.”

    Wendy is sobbing now, her shoulder shaking, and Kate gets the picture. They took Wendy’s wife. She feels anger fill her up, but stifles it down quickly. Now is not the time. “Tell me what happened. Start from the beginning.”

    “I am so sorry Kate, I didn’t…You have to go.”

    “We can help. Just tell me what happened.”

    Wendy takes a hiccupping breath, and Kate steers her towards the couch with a gentle hand on her arm and back. She sits Wendy down, lowering herself next to her, and waits for her to gather her thoughts.

    “I…after we met at Central Park. I got home, and Annie was not home even though she was supposed to. I was worried, so I called her, and a man picked up. They told me they have her, and if I ever wanted to see her again, I’d have to do what they said.” She takes another hiccupping breath, the sobs almost taking hold of her again. “Take your time.”

    Wendy takes a few calming breaths.

    “They taught us about this at the academy. I…I asked to speak to her, and made sure she was...alive,”

    Her voice almost breaks at the word alive, but she pushes on.

    “but it’s different when it’s someone you love. They told me to slip in a paper they’d leave on my desk the next morning to the files I’ll give to you, and then they would give her back.” She turns to Kate, her eyes clear for the first time since they arrived. “I am so sorry Kate. I don’t know how they knew. I didn’t mean to…”

    Kate puts a hand on hers, shaking her head.

    “It’s okay. We are fine, we are okay.”

    She attempts a smile at Wendy, but unsurprisingly, she doesn’t return it. “Have they been in contact again since?”

    Yelena asks from where is standing, close to the entrance of the apartment. Kate understands her thought process. That was over 4 days ago. It’s not a good sign. Wendy lets out a stifled sob, and nods.

    “Yes. They…they called me again afterwards to be on standby. That, they might need something else from me.”

    “Did they tell you what else?”

    Wendy shakes her head, a chocked sound leaving her.

    “No. I…”

    Her voice breaks this time, a fresh wave of tears appearing in her eyes “I haven’t heard from them since. They said if I told anyone they will...they will kill her.” Kate hugs her, pulling her into her side, and Wendy sobs against her shoulder. She meets Yelena’s eyes and they exchange a look. That was four days ago. Wendy talks again, her voice partially muffled by her crying and Kate’s shoulder.

    “I know…I know too much…time has passed. I know.”

    “We will help you find her, okay? What can you tell me about the caller?” Kate tries to convey a confidence in her voice that she doesn’t quite believe herself. Four days is a long time.

    “He…I think he had an accent. Maybe Russian or eastern European. A bit like yours.” She glances at Yelena as she says it, who nods at her, face not betraying any emotions, but her eyes are soft.

    “That’s good Wendy. Do you remember anything else?”

    Yelena’s voice is gentle when she speaks, and Kate is so grateful she seems to have understood that there is no need for a bad cop here today.

    “No, I…oh wait, I think I heard a horn in the background.”

    “As in a car horn?”

    “No…no, bigger. Maybe a ship?”

    Wendy’s face is a touch more hopeful now, and Kate smiles at her reassuringly. That doesn’t narrow their search down by much, but it’s a start.

    “Okay. Do you have anyone you can call?”

    Wendy’s horror returns.

    “No! I…it’s already too dangerous that I told you.”

    She looks around frantically again, panic taking a hold of her.

    “If they are watching me, Annie is good as dead!”

    Yelena is still gentle as she reassures Wendy.

    “Nobody knows we are here, don’t worry.”

    Kate wonders if that might be a lie. They definitely didn’t make a discreet entrance, but nobody has shot at them yet or kicked the door in, so maybe they avoided detection so far. They need a plan. She takes a deep breath, thinking as she speaks.

    “Okay. Yelena and I will go to the harbor, and you stay here. I will leave my phone here with you, if they call, call us at Yelena’s number. That way they can’t track it.” She looks at Yelena, who nods at her. Kate has absolutely no clue what they will do at the port, how they could find anyone but Wendy doesn’t need to know that. She takes her phone out of her pocket, putting it on the table in front of Wendy.

    “If you have anyone else to call, you should use it for that too.”

    Wendy nods, and she kind of looks dazed, but they don’t have any more time to console her. The only thing that will really help her is if they find Annie anyways. Unless she is dead, a traitorous voice whispers in Kate’s head.

    They leave through the front door, and Kate waits until they get into the elevator to lean back against the metal wall, and release a long exhale.

    “Fuck.”

    Yelena is silent next to her, and Kate lets her emotions overwhelm her for the duration of their ride. She is angry, and scared, and most of all, incredibly guilty. She dragged Wendy, and as a result, Annie into this. If Annie is dead, as she honestly suspects she is, it’s her fault. Regret and shame fill her chest, burning it from inside like acid.

    She closes her eyes and lets out another shaky exhale, willing herself not to cry. Her eyes fly open when she feels a touch on her hand. Yelena stands in front of her, her face solemn, green eyes baring into Kate’s.

    “It’s not your fault.”

    She exhales again and looks to the side. Her voice feels weak when she speaks, but it doesn’t break.

    “I should have never dragged them into this.”

    “Kate, look at me.”

    She does, and once Yelena catches her gaze, she can’t look away again. “I will say this only one time. You do not control what bed men do.”

    “No, but…”

    “And you falling apart is not helping Annie. You need to get your shit together.” She takes a deep, kind of shuddeing breath.

    Yelena is right. She needs to bring her A game now.

    She nods at Yelena, and she holds Kate's eyes a few moments longer before she nods back. The elevator door opens behind Yelena, and she turns away, exiting without another look. Chapter End Notes Hey guys!

    Sorry, I was gonna post this last night but I passed out on the couch. :) I hope you like the little easter egg :D We are entering a bit of a darker arc here, because a) Disney softened Kingpin in Hawkeye, but if you ever watched Dardevil, he is a terrifying mf, b) my main philosophical question for this story (and for Kate) is whether normal life is possible for people like Kate. Can she have friends, human relationships, when she does what she does? Clint told her there are things she will lose forever, but I don't think she really got it in season 1, even with her mom. Clint's story itself is an answer to that question already (so is Peter's btw), but we shall see how it goes for Kate. (and see how Yelena fits into that ;))

    I hope you like this chapter! Please as always, feel free to leave a kudos or a comment, they really make my day :)

    Next chapter will be up this weekend!

    xx

    Chapter 9

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes They make their way to the Harbor in a bit over an hour, and Kate uses the time to start to make a plan.

    “In the Bishop Security files…”

    She gulps, and clears her throat to avoid it cracking.

    “…there was a large number of bodies recovered from the south side of the harbor. We should start there.”

    Yelena nods, and turns to the left, even using the indicator. She noticed that Yelena kept every single traffic law to a tee on the way here, but she has no mental capacity to focus or comment on it. They ride in silence for a few more minutes, before Yelena speaks. “If they need Wendy to do something more for them, there is a chance Annie is still alive.” If she was in a better mood, she would have time to appreciate the fact that somehow Yelena ended up being the optimist in this scenario. She gives Kate a glance, and she nods, not turning towards her, choosing not to give a verbal answer. She is trying to compartmentalize, hard.

    They arrive to the general area of the harbor, the Bay visible from Kate’s window and Yelena pulls to the side of the road, parking their car. Kate looks at her confused, but she is looking in the rearview mirror.

    “Spider-Man has been following us for 15 minutes.”

    Kate looks in the mirror on her side, and sees a red spot disappear behind the building they parked next to. She wonders for a second why he is following them, but decides it’s not important. They need to focus on Annie.

    “Maybe he can help.”

    She gets out of the car, and Yelena does too, coming around to lean onto the car next to her. The air is hot, and smells of oil and dirty sea water, not exactly a pleasant combination. The area around them is loud, the noises of the shipyard create a constant, distracting buzz. She looks towards corner Spider-Man disappeared behind, waiting for him to catch up but he doesn’t emerge from there. He drops in front of them a minute later, from the other side, and Kate has to pretend not to be startled. She glances to Yelena from the corner of her eye, and can’t decide if she as unaffected as she seems or just hides it really well. It’s Yelena who speaks first.

    “You have been following us.”

    Spider-Man straightens, leaning against the wall and crossing his arms in a way what Kate assumes is meant to be casual. His voice sounds surprisingly young when he speaks. She didn’t notice that last week in the park.

    “You ladies caused quite a lot of trouble in Queens yesterday.”

    Kate hides her surprise at his words, mimicking his pose against the car, crossing her arms too.

    “It’s not really our fault, we were just trying to get away.”

    Spider-Man tilts his head to the side.

    “Get away from what?”

    “The people is trying to kill me.”

    Spider-Man considers them for a second, before he speaks.

    “Who is trying to kill you?”

    She tilts her head back at Spider-Man.

    “If you followed us here, you probably know who I am. And if you do, you also probably know exactly who is trying to kill me.”

    Spider-Man looks at her for a few moments, the black and white eyes of his mask narrowing slightly.

    “You are Kate Bishop...”

    Kate nods, as Yelena shifts next to her.

    “…But I don’t know who is trying to kill you.”

    “So what do you know?”

    Spider-Man looks kind of awkward for a second as he gestures at her vaguely, before crossing his arms again.

    “Uh…you know. You are Elanor Bishop’s daughter. She was arrested for murder and some white collar crimes last year.”

    Kate flinches a little, but hides it quickly. She takes a deep breath, trying to ignore the tired jolt her heart gives at the mention of her mother.

    “Yeeeah…it turns out she was working for a mob boss named Wilson Fisk. Her trial is coming up and he is trying to get me killed, so I can’t be a witness against them both.” “Oh…I am sorry…But um, I heard that name before!”

    Yelena re-joins the conversation, her voice casual but Kate can see the tension of her posture from beside her.

    “What do you know about him?”

    Spider-Man either can’t pick up on Yelena’s rigid posture, or he chooses to ignore it. He puts one foot against the wall, leaning against it even more. The familiarity Kate felt with him the other day in the park is there again, his movements reminding her of someone she can’t place.

    “Not much? He is some sort of mobster? He was arrested and released a couple of times. Honestly, I thought he disappeared or died.”

    Kate waits a few moments to see if he continues. He doesn’t.

    “Yeah. That’s the gist of it, I guess.”

    He rubs the back of his suit-covered head.

    “Sorry for bringing up the part about your mom.”

    Kate blinks at him a few times, a bit taken aback, before she forces out a chuckle, waving it away.

    “No, it’s….that’s fine. That’s what happened.”

    His gaze seems to jump from Kate to Yelena, back and forth.

    “So she is Kate Bishop. Who are you?”

    He addresses the question to Yelena, who stares at him, her face unreadable. He shifts his weight, switching the feet against the wall. She lifts her chin at him challengingly. “I’ll tell you my name when you tell me yours, Spider-Man.”

    Kate rolls her eyes at her internally, her lips twitching up, but she chooses not to comment. Spider-Man seems to accept the answer, holding up his hands.

    “Okkkayyy. Woman of mystery. Cool, cool, cool…So, what are you two doing here?” Kate sighs and wets her lips before she speaks.

    “The wife of a friend was taken hostage, to blackmail her into feeding us fake intel. We are trying to find her.”

    Spider-Man stares at her for a long moment, then nods.

    “How can I help?”

    Kate exhales, and she sees some tension leave Yelena too, from the corner of her eyes. She tries to summarize the situation quickly.

    “They made her a phone call, but that was four days ago. She heard a ship horn in the background, and talked to a man who apparently had an Eastern European accent. That’s all we know.”

    Spider-Man nods again.

    “I will look around, see if I find anything suspicious from up there.” He waits for her to nod, then jumps high in the air, a long thread of white web coming out of his wrist and he is gone in a second.

    Yelena speaks first.

    “He is younger than I expected.”

    Kate nods, and they take off, walking towards the pier. Most of the bodies washed up there. Kate tries not to think about that.

    “I am pretty sure he must have Blipped. He wasn’t around for those 5 years.” Yelena hums, and Kate speaks again after a few moments.

    “Do you think he will be able to help?”

    “He can see more from up there. It definitely can't hurt.”

    They walk around, looking at the waves crashing against the pier for about 20 minutes but thankfully find nothing. Of course, Kate knows that doesn’t mean anything, but it helps to chase away the images of pulling Annie’s body from the water, at least momentarily. She thinks about how much heavier today feels, compared to yesterday, and especially after the peaceful evening and morning they had. She has an idea.

    “We need to find someone.”

    Yelena gives her a side-eye.

    “I thought that’s what we are doing here.”

    “No, I mean someone to talk to, ask if they saw anything.”

    Yelena hums again but doesn’t sound convinced. Kate is now set on the idea though. She has cash, they will find someone to tell them if there is anything fishy going around. She marches on purposefully, and for a few minutes they just advance towards the busier parts of the harbor, the sounds of people and machines working, storage containers being moved filling the air around them.

    Kate spots a group of three men, seemingly on a break, leaning against the railing of the pier. She walks towards them with purpose, Yelena beside her. They notice them approaching, and she almost falters in her step when one nudges the other, giving them a leery once over. Then the image of pulling Annie’s body out of the water pops into her mind again, and she lifts her chin, advancing towards the group.

    “Well, well, well. What do we have here?”

    The man, who is probably old enough to be her father, asks them in a voice that makes Kate want to gag. She ignores his tone, and gives a polite smile.

    “Hi. My friend and I are looking for someone.”

    One of the other men steps forward and gives her a grin that she imagines must be an attempt at appearing charming.

    “No need to keep looking darling, I am here.”

    She scrunches up her nose, giving the man a thoroughly disgusted once-over. “Ew, really? That’s what you are going with?”

    His bravado falters only for a moment, and his gaze jumps to Yelena instead. “Maybe your friend is less of a bitch, huh?”

    Yelena lifts an eyebrow, her face and voice both very unimpressed.

    “I wouldn’t count on that.”

    “Oh why so grumpy blondie? I can show you something that will put a smile on that pretty face.”

    Kate exhales through her nose, absolutely no patience for this.

    “You know what. I was going to give you money in exchange for information, but after all of this…”

    She gestures at the space between them all.

    “…that door is closed. Like, super firmly. So, I’ll offer you this: You answer my questions, and she won’t break your arms.”

    She doesn’t look at Yelena but assumes she is game to play along. She hopes they don’t have to go through with it but they need to find Annie. The men stare at her for a long moment, before they burst out laughing. Kate sighs, closing her eyes for a second, considering just walking away.

    Yelena makes the decision for them both.

    Kate feels her move beside her, and opens her eyes just in time to see her grab one of the men by neck, slamming his head against the metal railing. She grabs the other before the first one has the time to hit the ground, and twists his arm behind his back, holding him in place. Kate smiles internally, the taste in her mouth a bit bitter. Good cop, bad cop. The third one, the one that has been talking to them, stares in horror, his eyes jumping between Yelena, his friend and Kate. He needs a few seconds to react.

    “Who the fuck are you?”

    His voice sounds a lot less confident now, practically stuttering, and his fallen mate lets out a groan from the ground.

    “That is not important. What do you know about mob activity around here?” Yelena gives her a look that tells her it was a less than stellar question and Kate rolls her eyes at her. It’s not like she interrogating people regularly, how should she know how to ask. The man holds up his hands.

    “Look, I don’t know anything. We just work here, loading containers. We don’t want any trouble.”

    “You should have thought about that before the disgusting comments.”

    Yelena’s voice is low and she pulls the man’s arm in her hold further up, causing him to cry out in pain. Kate continues, her stomach twisting a little but voice confident. “Have you seen anything suspicious in the last few days? A woman, maybe.” “No! We haven’t! No women around here.”

    Kate scoffs as he gives a worried look to his friend, still in Yelena’s hold. “Okay, yeah, that’s pretty obvious. How about Eastern European men. In big black cars.” His eyes shift to hers, and there is a glint. Yes, that is it. He gulps and shakes his head. “No, nothing like that.”

    Kate looks at Yelena and she gets the message, twisting the man’s hand even further. He screams in pain.

    “What are you guys doing?”

    A young, but distinctly masculine voice asks from behind them, and Kate turns her head to see Spider-Man standing behind them, his stance a bit uncertain. Yelena answers him. “Gathering intel.”

    He looks at them for a long moment, and the third man uses their distraction to make a break for it, leaving his friend behind. He takes off running and makes it approximately 3 steps away before his legs get tangled in thick, white webbing.

    He falls onto his face, letting out a groan, and Kate walks up to him, pulling him up to his knees. His nose is bleeding, and he spits on the ground, swearing.

    “Fucking shit.”

    “It was pretty fucking shit of you to leave your friend behind like that. We could be psychos.” He looks up at her like she is a psycho. She crouches down to be level with him. “Please, just let us go. We don’t know anything.”

    “A-ah. Tell me about the Eastern Europeans.”

    He looks away, gulps than turns back to her to explain.

    “There is a ship. The red one after the next. We saw a bunch of nice cars pull up to it” he spits to the side again “last weekend, and heard some Ukrainians. Bobby’s wife is from there so he recognized it.”

    He points at the man lying at Yelena’s feet. Kate lifts an eyebrow at him. “See, that wasn’t so hard?”

    He scowls at her, and she straightens herself.

    “Anything else?”

    He shakes his head looking up at her, and this time she believes it.

    “No, that’s all. I swear. We look the other way sometimes, but we don't want trouble.” Kate turns away from him, and Yelena lets go of the man’s arm, who collapses forward with a groan. She addresses her next question to Spider-Man.

    “Did you find anything?”

    He looks uncomfortable, she can tell even with the mask covering his face but he doesn’t comment on what just went down.

    “No, but I didn’t check the ship he talked about. I can take another look.” Kate nods, looking at Yelena for confirmation.

    “Okay, we will get our gear, and meet you by the building closest to it.” She points it out to him (although calling it a building is generous. It’s a metal shed), and he nods, taking off without another word.

    Kate hesitates, before turning back to the shipyard workers. She addresses the man who Yelena held first, who sits on the ground, cradling his arm against himself. “Ice that shoulder, and wear a sling. It should be okay in a week or so.” He just stares at her disdainfully, not looking like he will answer so she turns to the man they have been speaking to the most next.

    “Get them out of here. Things might get loud here soon.”

    He spits again, but nods at her, and attempts to pull the webbing holding his legs together. It doesn’t budge, and Yelena walks up to him, pulling a knife out of her jeans. His eyes widen for a millisecond, and he attempts to scoot back. Yelena halts, holding up the blade and her other hand, and he stops. She crouches in front of him, her movements deliberately slow, and uses the blade to cut through the sticky white web.

    Yelena stands back up, pockets the wife, and start walking towards the direction of their car without a word to any of the men. She speaks to Kate as she falls into step beside her. “Do you always stay around to talk to the men you beat up?”

    “Technically, I didn’t beat up anyone.”

    “Oh yes. Nice cop, bad cop.”

    Kate gives her a strained smile, not managing to give more, as she can’t stop thinking about what will await them on the ship. The image of pulling Annie from the water shifts into finding her beaten and dead in a storage container.

    She is fine getting hurt, and she trusts Yelena to take care of herself, but Annie? She had nothing to do with this. Kate met her only once, at the celebratory cookout the LARPers threw after Rockefeller Plaza, and she was nice. She was a doctor (is a doctor, she quickly corrects herself) but they only spoke a couple of words at the party. She mostly remembers Wendy, how proud she looked introducing her and looking at her like she hung the moon any time she opened her mouth.

    She lets out a slow exhale through her nose, remembering Yelena's words. Her panic won't help Annie.

    They reach the car and Kate takes her gun-bag from the back seat, opening the zipper. She pulls out her quiver, securing it on her back and then uses the hairband on her wrist to tie her hair back. She glances over at Yelena, who seems to just be waiting around for her, leaning against the car.

    “I am sorry we didn’t bring more guns for you.”

    Yelena gives her a cocky little smile.

    “Don’t worry, I will manage.”

    Her smile fades off of her face a second later, and she glances at the shipyard behind Kate before she looks back at her again, meeting her eyes.

    “You do know this is likely another trap, right?”

    Kate didn’t think about that, but it doesn’t surprise her entirely. Annie very well might be the bait to lure them onto the ship, (if she even is here,) as much as she is a bargaining chip with Wendy. She shrugs at Yelena.

    “Well, at least we know we are walking into one now.”

    Yelena grins, and it eases Kate’s nerves just a little.

    “That is the spirit!”

    She lets out a breathy chuckle without meaning to, the sound of it a little tight with all the emotions swirling around in her chest. She pulls out her glasses from their case inside the bag, slipping them on her face. She presses the small button on the right side of the frame, and system turns on.

    It’s her own invention, one she is quite proud of. It’s nothing fancy, nothing like Tony Stark (R.I.P) could do, and she wishes she had a proper suit with her now at least, but she honestly didn’t expect the day to turn into such a shit-show quite so fast. The AI is booted up in a second, showing her the number of arrows she has in her quiver of each kind in the upper right corner of the glasses, and a small map of their location in the bottom left. “System check.”

    “Welcome Kate. All systems online.”

    “Who are you talking to?”

    She looks over to Yelena, who looks back at her a little confused.

    “Just my glasses.”

    Yelena tilts her head to the side.

    “Is it some kind of super-hero glasses?”

    Kate’s lips twitch upwards.

    “Something like that.”

    Yelena purses her lips thoughtfully, before a coy smile slips over her face, lifting an eyebrow. “Can you see under my clothes?”

    Kate snorts, her voice lighter, entertained despite herself.

    “Why would I see under people’s clothes? I am pretty sure that’s not a thing.” Yelena shrugs, and tilts her head.

    “James Bond used it to look at people’s hidden weapons…And women’s underwear.” Kate pulls her lips to the side, looking at Yelena thoughtfully.

    “Well, I am pretty sure that makes him a creep.”

    Yelena makes an expression that Kate deciphers as I guess, shrugging.

    “Anyways, no. I can’t see your underwear.“ “That’s good, I am not wearing a matching pair.”

    Kate blinks at her a few times, and Yelena looks back with a grin. Kate thinks she knows what Yelena is trying to do. She is trying to ease the tension in her by distracting her with humor, and Kate appreciates it, even if she is aware of it. She gives Yelena a lopsided smile, playing along.

    “I am sure you still look great.”

    “Happy you think so.”

    She gives Kate a wink, and she can’t help but smile as she leans down to take the last item from the bag, her bow. She attaches it to her quiver, and leans back up. “It does have an enhanced heat vision camera in it though, so I can kinda see people through walls? If they are not too thick.”

    Yelena gives her a slightly impressed look, nodding at her.

    “How do you make sure they don’t fall off your head in a fight?”

    Kate halts her movements for a fraction of a second. She kind of hasn’t thought about that. She quickly feigns confidence, shutting the car’s door.

    “You’ll just have to wait and see.”

    Yelena gives her a look.

    “You didn’t think of that, did you?”

    “Pff. Totally have.”

    The look intensifies, and Yelena’s eyebrow lifts to emphasize it.

    “So this is your first time actually using them?”

    She kind of has Kate there, and she purses her lips, before nodding.

    “Come on, Spider-Man is waiting.”

    She turns to leave, and Yelena chuckles behind her, falling in step with her a moment later. “I hope you made them hard to break, at least.”

    “Yeah, they are tempered glass. They could actually withstand a bullet.” “Okay, that’s pretty cool.”

    Kate’s lips twitch upwards for a second, but she feels the heaviness sneak and settle back into her chest. She rotates her shoulders as she walks, and if Yelena can tell her mood slipping back, she doesn’t make any further attempts to pull her out of it.

    They make it to the building, and Spider-Man swings down from the nearby containers, landing next to Kate.

    “So, I snooped around, and from what I can tell it looks pretty normal? But there are no workers on that side of the ship though.-”

    He points towards the far side of the enormous vessel.

    “-So my best guess is that if there is any criminal activity, it’s probably happening there.” He puts his hands on his hips, and he even does a tiny little bounce on his heels, and it’s kind of…sweet. Kate doesn’t know what to do with that.

    “Um, okay. Thanks!”

    Spider-Man nods, and Kate looks at Yelena, who is surveying the ship before looking at them both.

    “We need to be sneaky about this and neither of you look sneaky.”

    Kate and Spider-Man look at themselves, then at each other. He stands out like a sore thumb in his red and blue suit in the daylight, and Kate’s bow and arrows would probably raise quiet a few brows with the shipyard workers too.

    “I can be sneaky.”

    “At least I’m in my civies.”

    Yelena raises an eyebrow, pursuing her lips. Kate wants to comment on how Yelena insisted on taking the least inconspicuous car possible, but Spider-Man speaks first. “I can swing you both over, using the cranes.”

    That’s…not a bad idea actually. Kate looks at the containers stacked up on the pier, quite close to the ship, and cranes used to move them above.

    “We can swing ourselves, but it’s a good idea.”

    She looks to Yelena again, and she nods. Yelena points to an area where the containers are stacked in levels, creating a natural staircase of sorts close to the side of the ship. “We can climb on the metal boxes there.”

    "I"ll meet you guys there."

    Spider-Man jumps and swings away, and Kate and Yelena start towards the containers, jogging over to gain momentum. Kate jumps against the metal wall of it, kicking herself upwards, and grabs the ledge, the metal searing hot under her palm. She pulls herself up, and Yelena does the same beside her. They climb six levels, until they get to the top, and Spider- Man is there already, waiting for them in a crouch.

    Kate huffs, and feels a bit jealous. She is in great shape, but she is already a bit sweaty from the climb under the blearing sun, and when she looks over to Yelena, who gets over the ledge a few moments after her, her face is glistening too.

    “How don’t you burn up in that suit?”

    She addresses Spider-Man, as she gets her bow from her back. He gives a little shrug. “I kinda do…I used to have a nano-tech suit, but this is just spandex.” She crouches beside him, and Yelena takes the spot on her right.

    “Where did you get a nano-tech suit?”

    He clears his throat.

    “Long story. So, you guys are okay getting across?”

    Instead of answering, she pulls an arrow from her quiver, attaching the rope on it to her bow. She nocks it, and pulls the string back, aiming high for the crane above their heads. She releases as she exhales. Spider-Man jumps and is swinging across, just as her arrow attaches to metal rods.

    She looks over to Yelena, who extends her arm above her head, her own wire releasing with a hiss from her bracelets. Kate straightens up, and a moment later Yelena joins her, the both of them standing on the edge.

    They swing over in unison, high above the pier, and hopefully hidden from any prying eyes. Kate feels the warm wind whip through her hair and clothes, and blood rushes in her ear, adrenaline filling her veins as she looks down. They arrive on the other side with two soft thuds against the metal of another set of stacked containers.

    Spider-Man is waiting, crouched on the other side of the makeshift roof they are standing up on, and they both lean down, keeping low as they walk up to join him. The ship looks deserted from up here, but there are hundreds, if not thousands of containers. Kate feels a drop of sweat run down the side of her head, and wipes it away with an impatient motion. “That is a lot of containers.”

    She says it to no one in particular, partially to herself, but she sees both of her companions nod in her periphery. Spider-Man turns her head at them.

    “I will go check around the far side. You guys good to check around here?” Kate nods, her eyes still sweeping the endless rows of containers.

    “Sure.”

    He nods too, and jumps over to the next stack of metal boxes, landing on the wall, and crawling away. Kate sighs, the hot air feeling like it doesn’t contain enough oxygen as it fills her lungs.

    “This is still a lot of ground to cover. We should split up.”

    She turns her head to look at Yelena, whose eyes are sweeping the seemingly endless labyrinth of containers still, before turning to her.

    “Do you have any earpieces?”

    She shakes her head. She didn’t expect they’d need any for just seeing Wendy. Yelena nods, turning back to look at the terrain they’ll be covering, Kate does too. “Okay. You take left side, I take right. We meet there in 15 minutes.” She points out an area in the middle where the metal containers are stacked higher than the rest of the ship. Kate nods, and prepares to rappel down on the side when a hand on her forearm stops her. She looks up to meet Yelena’s eyes.

    “We don’t know what’s here. If you find anything, come meet me and we check it together, okay?”

    Kate clenches her jaw, looking away but stifles the spark of irritation rising up in her throat. Yelena is right. This is very likely a trap and they have no idea what they are walking into. She sighs, and nods. Yelena’s hold slips from her arm.

    Kate jumps down, slowing her descent with her legs against the sides of the containers. She kicks away from the wall, and arrives in a crouch, and a few heartbeats later Yelena lands next to her. She pulls out her bow, and nocks a regular arrow, and Yelena pulls out her gun, pointing it towards the ground with both arms. They share one last look, before Kate turns, and walks away towards the left.

    She walks quietly for a minute before she remembers her glasses.

    “Activate enhanced surveillance mode.”

    The colors before her eyes switch instantly, the faded whites and greens and blues turning into various shades of orange and red. She curses internally. The metal around her is too hot for the infrared camera in the glasses to pick out anything.

    “Deactivate enhanced surveillance mode.”

    Her vision switches back, and she continues on her way, trying to keep track of her surroundings, checking behind herself and around corners, but there doesn’t seem to be any signs of life anywhere. The containers around her make the already high temperature worse, the blaring midday sun turning the whole maze into a metal sauna, the air around her shimmering with the heat. Her back is drenched in sweat, and her shirt is sticking to her skin in a way that’s both annoying and distracting.

    She thinks about Annie, whether she can even survive in one of these boxes if she is here somewhere. The image of opening one of the containers, and finding her lying on the ground, her eyes open and her mouth parched fill her mind unwillingly.

    She bites the inside of her mouth, to distract herself from it, taking a deep breath. The hot air feels suffocating as she sucks it in, and she feels like her mouth is dry as sandpaper, while the rest of her body is drenched, drops of sweat running down her neck and arms. She keeps walking on, and she can’t even decide if her heart drumming in her ears is from the adrenaline over the thought of finding Annie and her captors, or from the panic she feels at the thought of not finding them.

    Bang. Bang.

    Sounds of not too distant, rapid gunfire practically yank her mind back to reality, and she immediately feels even more heat fill her body. She tries to listen through the blood rushing through her ears to pinpoint where the sounds are coming from.

    The far side of the ship.

    She takes off running, sprinting towards the sound.

    Bang. Bang. Bang.

    The shots are getting closer.

    She sees a container opening ahead of her and jumps behind another to take cover. Her heart hammering against her chest, she peers around the corner, and she sees 5 men with automatic rifles file out of the container, running towards the sounds of gunfire too. She draws her bow, and turns out of cover to aim and release her arrow, getting one of the men right between the shoulder blades. The arrow goes deep into his back, but she doesn’t see him drop, jumping back behind the container.

    She pulls an electromagnetic arrow from her quiver, the number dropping in the corner of her glasses, and flits quickly around the corner to fire it towards the metal wall next to the four remaining men. She immediately jumps back into cover, and she hears the metallic thuds of the rifles sticking to the wall. Quietly as she can, she sneaks away in the other direction, to find a way to get behind them.

    The sound of repeating gunfire doesn’t slow down in the distance, and she hopes Spider-Man is alright, that Yelena is getting to him to help faster than she is. She runs down between rows of stacked storage containers, and puts her bow on her back. She needs to be saving arrows, because from the sound of the fire fight furhter ahead, they are definitely outnumbered. She pulls out her sword from her pocket, clicking the release button on the blade just as she turns the corner to the right, having found the way back to the group. She halts and takes a deep breath before she jumps from her cover.

    Two of them are still trying to pull their guns off of the wall, while the other two are cautiously sneaking their way to the corner she fired from earlier. The fifth man lies on the ground in a growing puddle of blood, wheezing.

    She doesn’t focus on him, she can’t.

    She runs full speed at the two men still occupied with their guns, slicing one’s legs and the other’s torso from behind with one flowing, upwards motion, a mist of blood flying in the air and uses her body to ram against the first, sending him slamming face first into the container in front of him, and taking down the other man beside him.

    Their cries of pain alert the other two, and she quickly dodges the bigger one, running straight at her. She slices his back as she twirls by him, more blood splashing against the metal wall next to her and she kicks him in the back, sending him banging into the container too, falling over with a groan.

    The fourth man catches her from the side, his shoulder ramming into her chest, and she feels the air knocked out of her as she is slammed against the burning hot metal wall behind her. The sword is knocked from her grip, and she uses that hand to grab the man and knee him strongly in his ribs even with the limited space.

    He grunts, but instead of pulling away, he only leans back and headbutts her, his forehead slamming against her cheek. It sends her glasses flying off her face and she sees stars when the wall delivers the second impact against the back of her skull.

    He kicks her legs out and she falls. He goes down with her, straddling her hips, and grabbing her neck. Her eyes are watering, and she instinctively tries to breath, but his grip is tight. She puts both of her feet firmly on the ground, and bucks up, jostling him, and twists out from under him, kicking his hips to send him flying backwards.

    He tries to get up, but she is faster, tackling him before he can, and they tumble on the ground. She gets a strong elbow hit to her stomach, but manages to twist away, and grab him from behind, her arm locking around his neck, her legs wrapping around and gripping his in a hold like vice, pulling his body taunt like a bow.

    He struggles, but she doesn’t let go. His arms are whipping around, trying to hit her behind him, but she has him. Her heart hammers in her chest, and she can’t hear anything. The distant sounds of gunfire and the sound of the man wheezing a few feet from them are drowned out by the blood rushing through her ears.

    He stops moving eventually.

    She is panting. His heavy, motionless weight on her chest is making it even harder to breath. She stares at the sky, so blue, not a cloud in sight. Her brain feels hazy with the hits she received. She pushes his weight off of her with great effort, and sits up, his body flopping to the side with no resistance whatsoever.

    She sees movement from the corner of her eyes, and barely has time to lift her arm up to block, before she is propelled to the side by the force of the knee that lands strongly against the side of her head. Her brain is slow to catch up to the fact that the bigger man of the last two has gotten back up. She tries to stand up, but he kicks her strongly in the stomach, knocking the air out of her and she collapses against the ground again. She takes a staggering breath, and rolls away but doesn’t get far, before he grabs her leg and pulls her back towards himself. He kicks at her side again, but she twists out of the way and around to swipe his legs from under him. He falls on the broad of his injured back, and she rolls onto him.

    She straddles his waist and hits him, hard, his jaw snapping to the side. Another punch, from the other side and blood spews from his broken nose. She grabs his shirt to pull him up, his eyes already half rolling back, and she delivers the final jab, his head snaping back, no tension left in his muscles as he passes out.

    She releases him, and collapses to the side, leaning against the hot metal wall behind her, her heart hammering in her chest.

    She looks around, and her stomach lurches as she takes it all in, her blood pumping loudly in her ears. The white container across from her is painted with splashes of crimson, and she slowly turns to the other side in a daze to look at the first man, whom she hit with the arrow. She killed people before, she thinks. She must have. Collateral damage in the car chases, at Rockefeller Plaza. But this.

    This is carnage.

    He twisted himself half to his side and the tip of her arrow is sticking out of his chest. He is staring at her.

    Her hearing comes back like a bubble popping. He is literally drowning in his own blood and she is looking back at him.

    She can’t stop looking back at him.

    He is young, probably in his mid-twenties like her. His mouth and chin are red from the blood he is coughing up.

    She can’t hear anything but his wheezing, dying breaths.

    She thinks it sounds so much wetter than it’s supposed to.

    Her chest moves with his, quick and shallow, their eyes boring into each other’s. He has brown eyes.

    She can’t move.

    Suddenly, there are gentle but firm hands on the sides of her face, and her head is turned away.

    She tries to resist, but she can’t and her eyes meet green.

    Her brain struggles to comprehend what’s happening.

    Green eyes.

    Yelena.

    She tries to focus on her face, her eyes dropping to split lips. They are moving. “Breathe with me.”

    She blinks. Her eyes raise slowly back to meet Yelena’s. She attempts to follow her lead. Inhale, exhale.

    Inhale. Exhale.

    Inhale.

    Exhale.

    She slowly comes back to herself, blinking a few times.

    “You are okay. Just breathe.”

    Yelena’s voice is low, but gentle. Her hands are still on Kate’s face, and she tries to focus on that, on Yelena’s skin against hers. She closes her eyes, and the sensation grounds her. She hears the gunfire again, still not lessened in intensity and speed. She licks her lips, tasting copper. Her voice comes out crackly when she speaks.

    “We need to go.” she gulps “We have to help Spider-Man.”

    She opens her eyes and meets Yelena’s again. Her gaze is intense, jumping from one of her eyes to the other, and she looks at her for a couple of moments longer, before her hands slip away from Kate’s cheeks.

    She stands up from where she has been crouched in front of Kate, and offers her a hand. She takes it, and lets Yelena pull her up, stumbling back a bit against the container behind her as she stands. They are close, and Kate meets her eyes again.

    “Thank you.”

    Yelena gives her a small, bit sad smile.

    “Are you okay?”

    She is not. In so many ways.

    She determinedly not looking towards where the wheezing breaths are no longer coming from, and when she looks down on herself, she sees that she is no longer only drenched from her own sweat anymore. Her left side is covered in blood, her arm, her shirt painted red. She is pretty sure that it’s not her own. She gulps again.

    Annie.

    “Yeah. Yeah, I am…I’m okay.”

    They need to find Annie.

    Yelena nods, and walks to the other side of the corridor they are in, picking up Kate’s sword. She comes back, and grabs Kate’s hand, wrapping it around the handle.

    “Don’t lose it again.”

    Chapter 10

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Yelena picks up one of the automatic rifles that has fallen to the ground, Kate’s arrow deactivating sometime during Kate’s…whatever that was. Kate doesn’t know what to call it. Yelena checks the magazine, putting it back with a click, then leans down to take two more from the other guns, pushing them into her back pockets. Kate tries not to look around now, deciding to keep her eyes on Yelena.

    Yelena spots something else on the ground, and picks up Kate’s glasses. She blows on them, to remove the dust and walks over to Kate, who hasn’t moved from the side of the container since she stood up, holding it out towards her.

    “I told you they would fall off.”

    Kate manages a weak shadow of a smile, and takes the glasses from her.

    “Come on.”

    Kate leans off of the container’s metal wall, and wipes the blood off of her blade, with her already soaked t-shirt. It’s not like it can get any more ruined than it already is. She retracts the blade with the button, and puts it back in her pocket, before putting on the glasses, the system still on.

    She pulls her bow from her back, jerking her arm forward to snap it open, and clenches her jaw. Yelena waits for her nod, before she turns to lead them away, and Kate keeps her eyes on the back of her blonde head.

    Yelena starts jogging, and they are running towards the center part of the ship, finally leaving the scene behind. The shots sound closer with every step they take, and Yelena holds up a hand before they turn a corner. They both peer around it, taking in the scene. It seems they made it to the center of the maze. It’s the tall stack of containers they saw when they landed on the ship, acting as high walls around a large open space. There are at least three dozen gangsters on the makeshift courtyard, their guns painted to the sky as Spider-Man swings and jumps around, performing various maneuvers in the air to avoid the bullets flying around him. They seem to be standing mostly around one container in particular, and for a moment Kate lets herself hope, that maybe that’s where Annie is.

    She looks up to observe Spider-Man as he skillfully dodges the projectiles, getting in and out of view, and using his webs to pull the rifles and handguns out of the hands of the gang members one at the time, sometimes even managing to bind one or two of them, or stick them against a wall. Several men are already struggling on the ground or against the metal containers already, but it’s clear that he is severely outnumbered and outgunned. He notices them as he swings above their heads, throwing them a wave as he passes by. “Hi! I found the bad guys.”

    Yelena chuckles, and Kate tries to force a smile too. She takes another electromagnetic arrow, leans from cover to fire it towards the other end of the yard, and the number for these types of arrows drops to 1 in the corner of her glasses. A couple of metallic thuds later, Yelena raises the rifle to her shoulder, and ducks out from behind the container too. She pulls the trigger, aiming and firing a few times, before she is back next to Kate, her shoulders pushing against hers. Kate hears running footsteps from their other side to the right, and pulls out a regular arrow, aiming.

    She hesitates.

    The two men rounding the corner drop anyhow, two shots coming from right beside her, the sound of them very loud so close. She lowers her bow, and Yelena twists back to her previous position, her back against the wall next to her. Spider-Man does a good job of keeping the assailants distracted, but a few bullets ricochet around them now too, mostly lodging themselves into the wall of the container across from Yelena and Kate.

    “We need to get closer.”

    She doesn’t know if Yelena is talking to her, or herself but she nods anyway. She switches her arrow to a needle one and waits for a slight pause in the gunfire to run across the corridor between them and next column of containers, firing it at the other side of the big open space separating them from what appears to be the main holdout of the gang.

    She doesn’t see it land as she slides into cover, and she catches Yelena looking at her from the other side. Her expression is unreadable, but she is back to shooting in a heartbeat. She leaves her position in a second, and Kate covers her, shooting a man in his arm across the courtyard, who attempts to aim his rifle towards her.

    He drops his gun and she sees Yelena reach the next row of containers, closer to the big group. She prepares to follow her, when she hears boots running from behind her. She quickly nocks another arrow, running forward a few steps and fires it into the thigh of one of the three men coming around the corner on the far side of the container. The other two raise their guns at her sight, and she launches herself to the side, the bullets hitting the metal where she was standing just a second ago. She rolls towards them in a somersault, but she feels one of the bullet graze her shoulder, the pain hot and searing. Kate cries out, but arrives in a crouch in front of them, ignoring the sensation. She uses her momentum to shove one of them back with a shoulder to his chest, grabbing the other’s gun from the side, and pulling it from his grip. She tosses it to the side, and spins with the movement to hit his head from the back with her bow.

    She only hears him go down, because the other man regains his balance, and raises his gun to aim at her again. She is close enough to kick to the side just in time, and the bullet embeds itself somewhere behind her as the gun goes off a few inches to from ribs. She drops her bow to grab his outstretched arm, quickly twisting around to toss him over her shoulder in a body throw. He lands hard on his back and she kicks him in the head before he can get his bearings. He is out like a light too.

    Click.

    Her head snaps up, and she freezes.

    The third man kneels on the other end of the corridor, the arrow she shot into his thigh still sticking out of it, his gun trained on Kate. He is too far away for her to get to, she dropped her bow, and her heart skips a beat, before it starts racing, almost painful against her chest. She can see his hand begin to tighten on the trigger, his eyes narrowing as he aims. Bang.

    He falls backwards, the back of his head exploding in a chunky mist of red and Kate whips around.

    She is met with the sight of a visibly furious Yelena.

    She stalks up to Kate, who stands frozen and shoves her, hard. She stumbles backwards, her back hitting the storage container behind her. Yelena steps right into place, her green eyes baring into Kate’s as she looks up at her, her face only inches away. She is panting, and her voice is low and angry, her accent more pronounced when she speaks.

    “What the fuck are you doing?”

    She doesn’t know what to say, and can’t tear her gaze away from Yelena’s. “I…”

    She doesn’t wait for Kate to answer.

    “It’s you, or them.”

    She practically spits the words in Kate’s face and she gulps.

    Her brain knows that Yelena is right. Killing again is pretty much inevitable, and now is really not the time for her to have an existential crisis over it. But the image of the man wheezing, chocking on his own blood from her arrow is seared into the back of her mind now, and her stomach turns at the thought of doing that to someone again. Whatever she sees on Kate’s face, makes Yelena’s expression soften a little, the storm behind her green eyes calming. She takes a deep breath, exhaling through her nose, and seems to collect herself. Yelena licks her lips and her voice is more gentle when she speaks next. “Kate…”

    Spider-Man flying by them and slamming against one of the containers interrupts them, the metal bending inwards from the impact. Their heads snap to the side in unison, and Kate’s veins are filled with adrenaline again when she sees the red and black masked super-soldier running towards the three of them.

    Yelena is already in action, firing her gun at him from beside her, and she runs over to pick up her bow from where she dropped it. The soldier dodges the bullets, and he jumps high off the ground, just as Kate draws an explosive arrow. She shoots it at him while he is in the air, and he slaps it away just like last time, but it explodes close to him, sending him flying to the side with the shockwave, and out of their sight.

    “Thaaanks.”

    Spider-Man calls over his shoulder, as he runs by them, and he jumps high in the air too, shooting a sting of web and launching himself over to the tall stack of containers the super- soldier disappeared behind. Kate looks back to Yelena, who is busy pulling magazines off of the fallen soldiers again.

    With Spider-Man off the scene, the sound of constant gunfire is gone, but it means they are about to face the full focus of the group that looked at least 30 strong from when Kate last saw them, with who knows how many more around.

    She steels herself. She can do this. She has to do this.

    It’s not just her on the line. It’s Yelena, and Annie and now, apparently Spider-Man. They are all here because of her, one way or another. She owes it to them to protect them all, to the best of her ability, whatever it takes.

    It’s us, or them, she tells herself, rephrasing Yelena’s words.

    The sound of multiple pairs of heavy boots running towards them rouses her from her musings, and she takes out another explosive arrow, and whispers to Yelena. “Come on, we don’t want to be in the range of this.”

    Yelena follows her as they run in the other direction, the long corridor made of stacked containers sprawling ahead of them. She keeps looking back, and when the soldiers start rounding the corner, she spins around to draw her bow, and releases the string with an exhale. The arrow flies true, hitting the container behind the men and exploding upon impact, sending them flying, smacking against the walls around them with enough force to cause permanent damage, at minimum. The sound is deafening, and the Kate feels the whole ship shake. She watches in both awe and horror as the stack of containers starts tilting, the bottom one having shifted backwards from the explosion, and no longer able to bear the weight of the rest, caving in now that one side of it is essentially replaced with a gaping hole. “Oh shit.”

    She takes off, sprinting towards the next intersection in the maze of containers, hoping to make it before the whole structure topples onto her. She makes it just in time, throwing herself to the right and curling up in a ball against the wall, covering her head with her arms. The crash is metallic and deafening, sounding a bit like an ancient, sentient machine waking up and stretching it’s limbs, as the tower of metal boxes falls over as if it was made of Legos. The falling containers take several others with them, the whole corridor that Kate just ran through collapsing on itself.

    One of the containers land a few feet from her, and she pulls herself together even tighter, her blood thrumming in her ears. She waits for a few seconds after the crashing stops, before she uncurls herself, sitting up. Holy fuck, she did not mean for this to happen. She gets to her feet and looks around. Yelena is nowhere to be seen.

    “Yelena?!”

    She calls out, at the risk of being heard by the remaining gang members, many of them now buried under the fallen containers. She was not on the corridor when Kate ran through it, she is sure. She wasn’t. Still, her heart starts beating, and acid-like worry fills her chest. She turns towards the wreckage that is now the corridor.

    “Yelena!?”

    She yells on the top of her lungs, starting to panic, and she is about to run back and look for her in the wreckage when her voice speaks from behind her.

    “Stop screaming Kate, I am here.”

    She whips around and Yelena is just standing by the next row of containers. Her hair is a bit of a mess, and she is dusty, but apart from her split lip she is totally unharmed. It must be the adrenaline because Kate is over there in a second, launching herself at her without a second thought. The force of the hug makes Yelena stumble backwards a step with a soft oof.

    “I thought I killed you for a second there.”

    She says it against Yelena’s hair, and the shorter woman is slow to hug her back, her arms coming around Kate’s waist hesitantly.

    “That one is still the funniest…”

    It’s mumbled against her shoulder kind of awkwardly, and Kate releases a relieved, breathy chuckle, before Yelena follows up with.

    “…You are getting blood all over me.”

    She pulls back, confused but Yelena is right. There is a splotch of red smeared on Yelena’s cheek where it was smushed against Kate. Kate touches her own shoulder, and sure enough, her hand comes away bloody.

    Oh.

    She kinda forgot about the bullet that nicked her earlier. Adrenaline must have helped to block the pain out, but now she feels it sting, and how warm and damp her shirt is over the right side of her chest.

    “Oh, um…sorry.”

    She reaches over to wipe the blood from Yelena’s face but she dodges her hand, chuckling. “That is not any better.”

    And she is right again, both of Kate’s hands are covered in blood. The left one is from other people, the right, her own. She attempts to wipe them on her jeans, then frowns at Yelena. “Where did you go?”

    She receives an eyebrow lift and a smirk.

    “I ran ahead of you and I was smart enough not to stop here.”

    Oh, okay. That makes sense. Kate turns back to the corner to avoid Yelena’s amused look, picking up her bow from where she threw it when she jumped into cover.

    “What is it with you and always losing your things?”

    She turns back to Yelena, her tone a bit defensive.

    “I don’t always lose my things.”

    Yelena purses her lips, tilting her head to the side.

    “If I point out that you lost your glasses again, will you go back to look for them?” Oh. She must have lost them somewhere in the now collapsed corridor. Thankfully Yelena just smiles, and Kate could swear it looks almost affectionate. Well, the glasses will have to be replaced. And redesigned.

    “Come on, I think these assholes have a base inside the boxes.”

    Before they can advance, Spider-Man appears, swinging over the wreckage, with the super soldier bound and unconscious over his shoulders. He lands in front of them, visibly looking around, taking in the bodies littering the ground, and the heavy containers thrown over each other.

    “Was this you guys?”

    Kate rubs the back of her head, remembering the clocktower.

    “Yeeaah, I am a bit of an overachiever.”

    Yelena bursts out laughing next to her, and Kate’s lips twitch upwards at the sound, despite the heaviness in her chest. Spider-Man looks between the two of them, before he shakes his head and walks over to one of the unharmed containers.

    “Thanks for the assist, ladies. He won’t be bothering you anymore.”

    He deposits the passed out super-soldier on the ground, leaning him back against the metal wall. He uses some more of his webbing to secure him against it, practically creating a cocoon around him, only his head sticking out and flopping forward. His red and black mask is gone, and Kate can see that his face is covered in burn-scars, his skin a mesh of pink and white ridges.

    “Do you know him?”

    Spider-Man looks between the two of them, and Kate shakes her head. Yelena answers for the two of them.

    “No, unless you consider fighting him yesterday.

    They stand around in silence for a few seconds before Yelena speaks up again. “We think they are inside.”

    She points across the makeshift courtyard, to the container that seems to be an entrance of sorts. Spider-Man nods.

    “Should I come with?”

    Yelena shakes her head.

    “No. Guard him and make sure nobody comes after us.”

    Spider-Man does a little salute, and Kate raises her eyebrows, glancing over to Yelena. She is smiling at Spider-Man, clearly amused and she sees him awkwardly turn the salute into a rub of the back of his neck when Kate looks back at him.

    “Thank you. Come on, Kate.”

    She turns away from him, jogging after Yelena and they make their way across the now deserted courtyard, the remaining soldiers presumably having fled inside from the destruction.

    They stop by the entrance, standing on the side of the door, and Kate pulls out a smoke arrow from her quiver. Yelena checks the magazine of her gun, before glancing over at Kate with a small smile, her eyes dropping meaningfully to the arrow, before meeting hers again. She keeps her voice low when she speaks, barely above a whisper.

    “I hope I don’t have to say this, but please no explosive arrows inside. It would be a really lame way to die.”

    Kate’s voice is dry, but just as quiet when she answers.

    “Suggestion noted…This is a smoke arrow.”

    “Ah, smart. One second then.”

    Yelena holsters her gun, and activates her bracelets instead. They switch places, with Kate now closer to the door and she waits for Yelena’s nod to lean out of cover, firing her arrow inside. Alarmed voices, then coughing can be heard from inside, followed by the sound of several pairs of retreating footsteps, and a door being shut. She puts her bow on her back, and retrieves her sword quickly from her pocket.

    The container opens into a room, Kate notes as she enters a few steps behind Yelena, and it’s filled with the swirling, purple smoke of her arrow, making it hard to see further than a few feet ahead. Kate pulls up her t-shirt to cover her nose and mouth, but it’s scratching her lungs nonetheless.

    Nobody fires at them upon entry, and Yelena turns to look at her. She points to Kate and indicates she goes left, then at herself and points to right. Kate nods, and lifts her sword as they separate. She walks along the wall, as quietly as she can, careful not to walk into anything.

    The room is larger than she would have imagined from outside. There are couches, and tables inside, and she guesses it must be some kind of community area, created by joining several containers together next to, and on top of each other. It’s cool inside, and she thinks she can hear AC units hum above her head. After the searing hotness of the outside, it makes her shiver, her sweat and blood drenched shirt sticking coldly against her skin. She walks around the room, keeping to the wall but doesn’t find anyone. Towards the back of the room however, she finds a doorway, leading deeper into the lair. The smoke is thick, making it hard to breathe or see, and after trying to unsuccessfully spot Yelena in the room for half a minute, she risks a hiss into the empty room.

    “Yelena! Where -”

    Several shots are fired through the door that she is standing next to, the bullets creating holes in the metal, beams of light breaking through. She throws herself over a couch on the side, parallel with the door. The gunfire sounds deafening in the enclosed space, especially after the quiet from earlier.

    Yelena appears a second later, vaulting over a table to slide into cover next to her. She puts a finger over her lips, and Kate nods. They wait for the shots to die down, and a few seconds after they do as well. All of Kate’s muscles are tense, her blood pounding in her veins as they wait.

    The door creaks open, the muzzle of a rifle appearing first, before the first gang member makes his way inside. Yelena stands up before her, stepping on the cushions of the couch to jump over the back, launching herself at the man from the side and Kate is only a heartbeat behind her.

    She sees Yelena land a knee into the side of the first soldier’s head as she jumps, sending him flying into the cabinets behind him just as Kate grabs the second rifle muzzle she sees with her left hand, and yanks. The soldier comes stumbling into the room, and she slices him across the stomach with her sword in the right, letting him fall forward. The next one is right behind him, and she kicks him in the chest, sending him stumbling backwards into the group. Yelena’s tasing disks fly onto his chest and he collapses, falling into the men behind him. Kate is the first through the door, using the distraction of the soldiers, and limited space of the narrow hallway they find themselves in, to her advantage. She kicks the next soldier’s gun to the side and cuts him across the torso, from hip to shoulder, blood splashing against the ceiling and wall, and shoves him with a shoulder to the chest to fall against the others behind him.

    Next to her, she is aware of Yelena grabbing another one’s gun and punch him in the throat, a chocking sound escaping him as he collapses. Yelena grabs another soldier’s outstretched arm, his gun aimed at Kate, twisting him around to point it at the others. The gun goes off three times, shooting two other gang members, and Kate’s ears ring with the sound of it in the enclosed space.

    One of the men seems to gather his bearings as his mate is gunned down next to him, and he kicks the soldier Yelena is holding with a roar in the chest. Yelena and the gangster stumble, then fall backwards into the room, and Kate cuts his extended leg, deep into the flesh of his thigh. Her sword goes so deep that it gets stuck in the bone, and she tries to yank it out, but the handle is pulled from her grasp as he goes down with a scream and she is promptly kicked in the abdomen by someone else, falling back against the wall.

    There is a gun inches away from her face and she is able to grab the muzzle with both hands and pull it to the side, but it goes off right next to her ear and for a moment Kate understands how Clint became half deaf in this job. She kicks the gangster holding it in the knee from the front, resulting in a sickening crunch and a scream from him.

    She yanks him forward, and throws herself ahead with the momentum to grab the rifle of the one behind him, while kicking the handgun from the hand of the man next to that one. The gun goes clattering on the ground, but the rifle goes off several times, the bullets embedding themselves behind her in the wall. She pulls than pushes on the rifle, using the stock of it to hit him in the stomach and headbutts the soldier. She is punched in the face by the other man hard enough that she stumbles backwards, the healing cut above her eyebrow opening again. The man with the rifle turns, raising it to aim at her but a knife flies by her with a hiss and embeds itself into his neck a second later. Blood spurs from the wound, down his chest, and he falls over with a gurgling sound that Kate is focusing really hard to ignore. Yelena slides into picture in a crouch, swiping the leg of the next soldier, then standing up with a spin. She has the knife from the fallen gang member’s neck in her hand when she does, and uses it to stab the one Kate disarmed earlier in the chest, twice.

    Kate kicks the gangster that Yelena swiped the legs of in the head, and grabs the arm of the one behind him, throwing him over her shoulder while twisting around. She holds onto his arm, twisting it until his shoulder pops out of place, and is about to knock him out, when she is grabbed from behind, an arm locking around her neck.

    She is able to use the narrow hallways’ wall to kick herself off against, slamming whoever is behind her into the wall on the other side. She jabs backwards with her elbow and bangs her head back into her attacker’s face. Twisting out of the hold, she grabs onto his arm, and kicks him hard in the stomach. When he bends over in pain, she kicks him again, this time in the head from the side, and he falls over, not getting up.

    She twists around, ready to face the next soldier, but finds only Yelena standing now, leaning against the wall with an arm on her hip, an amused look in her eyes. Kate breathes heavily, and waits for her to speak.

    “We should spar.”

    She has trouble focusing on anything than her thundering heartbeat in every single muscle she has.

    “What?”

    “We should fight again sometime. You are good. It’ll be fun.”

    She lifts her eyebrows, flinching in pain, because one of them is now torn again, but she guesses Yelena is right. It’d be.

    “Sure. Okay.”

    Yelena nods, then takes out her gun. She walks up to the one conscious soldier left, and crouches next to him, putting the gun under his chin.

    “Where is the woman you took?”

    Her behavior is giving Kate whiplash, as always, but questioning the soldiers is a good idea, so she just watches.
