    Like everything in the last few days, it doesn’t go the way Kate thinks it will. The soldier laughs in Yelena’s face, his teeth painted red with his blood. “You stupid bitch. You have no idea what….”

    His accent is thick, and Yelena looks unamused and bored. She puts her knee on his dislocated shoulder before he is done speaking, and leans closer.

    “Where. Is. The woman?”

    He screams, long and loud, but when Yelena takes her weight off of his shoulder, his cries of pain turn into breathy, pained snickers again.

    “I am not…telling you shit.”

    Yelena seems to grow tired of whatever game he is playing, and points the gun at his lap. “Last chance. Where is she?”

    He calls Yelena something in a language Kate guesses is Ukrainian, still laughing, before he continues in English.

    “You can blow my dick off…it’s still better than…anything they will do to me if I talk.” Yelena stares at him, before lifting her gun and hitting him on the side of his head hard enough, that he passes out instantly.

    “Well that was a waste of time.”

    Kate just hums as she walks over to the soldier who has her sword sticking out of his leg, now lying in a huge puddle of blood. She thinks about checking his pulse, but decides it’s better if she doesn’t know. It’s not like they have time to call an ambulance for him anyway. She grabs the handle, and closes her eyes as she puts her foot on his thigh, pulling the blade free with a wet crunch. Taking a deep breath, she turns towards the end of the hallway, and doesn’t open her eyes until she is a few steps away. Her steps feel sticky, and when she looks down, she sees that her boots are now leaving dark crimson prints on the floor. She threaded into the pool of blood around the gangster, and she has to take another deep breath to ground herself.

    Annie.

    Kate walks by Yelena without another word, leading them to door on the other end of the hallway. She puts her hand on the doorhandle, but waits until Yelena lifts her gun, and nods at her. She shoves it open, and barges through, her heart thundering in her chest. She hears the movement and a click to her left and instinctively throws herself forward, but she feels a sharp pain in her side following a deafening bang. She lands hard on her other side, and sees the man pump his shotgun to reload, but Yelena is right on her heels, shooting him twice, in the chest and right in the middle of his forehead.

    The wall is painted crimson behind him, chunks of what used to be the back of his head sticking to it as well, but Kate doesn’t get to digest that, because there is a booted foot coming straight towards her face. She twists to the side, narrowly avoiding it before there is a third gunshot and the man above him falls to side.

    She hears a fourth gunshot, and a thud to her right as she stumbles to her feet, quickly taking the room in, adrenaline filling her anew. There are still at least a dozen men in the room, illuminated by a window on the wall. Another gunshot, another thud.

    They must be the ones whose guns Kate’s electromagnetic arrow took earlier, because apart from the shotgun, the ones she sees coming towards her only seem to have baseball bats and knives. One of them makes a run for the shotgun, before Yelena’s deathly accuracy paints the wall red with the inside of his head too.

    Kate dodges a baseball bat coming right at her head, kicking away the gangster holding it in his stomach, and he falls backwards with a bullet to his chest a second later too. She twists out of the way of the knife that was meant for her stomach, and grabs the wrist belonging to the hand holding it, but she is shoved backwards by another man and stumbles against the wall.

    Yelena’s gun clicks empty, and Kate sees her throw it into the face of an approaching soldier from the corner of her eyes, probably no time to reload, but she focuses on the three standing front of her, the wall supporting her from behind.

    Her side is screaming in pain, ad it feels warm and wet but she doesn’t get to catch her breath because all three of them jump at her the same time. She dodges the fist coming to her face, and grabs the hand with the knife again, but she has no way to avoid the hard kick to her injured ribs. She stumbles to the side, but is able to hold onto the wrist of the knife holding man, and pulls him with herself.

    He falls against her, the blade trapped between them, and every muscle in her body is used to hold him back from plunging it into her chest. She is punched in the face by another gangster, and her head snaps to the side with the force of it, leaving her disoriented, but she manages to hold the knife back still.

    She starts to slide along the wall, falling to the side, pulling the knife wielding man onto herself. She twists his wrist in the last second so he falls onto his own weapon and the blade embeds itself into the base of his throat. Warm blood spews from the wound, onto her chest and neck, but she doesn’t get to process that either, because he is torn off of her less a second later and a booted foot stomps into her stomach.

    She cries out in pain, curling upwards on herself, but she manages to grab the boot when it descends on her again, kicking at the man’s other leg. He falls, but the other gangster grabs her by the shirt and punches her in the face. Her head lolls back with the force of it, and it’s by sheer luck that her hand find the knife in the dead gangster’s neck to her right, the handle slippery as she pulls it out.

    She jams it into the soldier’s thigh next to her head and he cries out. She pulls it out to stab him again before he grabs her wrist and slams it against the wall twice, the weapon falling from her grasp. He reaches for it but she grabs his wrist, and uses it as leverage to twist her body astride on the ground, kicking him in the chin from below. His head snaps back, and he collapses backwards with his eyes rolling into his skull.

    Kate has a second to sit up, her entire body screaming in pain, and sees the last man who she kicked away a few seconds ago coming at her. She grabs the knife from the floor beside her, but he kicks it from her grasp, and it goes scattering somewhere far away. She lifts her arm to block the punch that comes at her face, but her arms feel weak and the hit would send her sprawling back to the ground if it weren’t for his hold on her shirt.

    She uses her last reserves of strength to punch him between his standing legs from below, and he makes a choked sound, falling to the ground. Kate falls back onto her back too, without his hand to hold her up, her head knocking against the ground, but she forces herself to turn over and get onto her hands and knees.

    She crawls towards where her sword has fallen when she entered the room, and her hand closes around the handle just as her ankle is grabbed from the back. He pulls her backwards, and she falls onto her face, but doesn’t let the sword go. Across the room, the shotgun goes off again, but she can’t lift her head to see what’s happening.

    The gangster pulls on her leg one more time, and Kate kicks back at him. He grunts and she forces herself to roll onto her back, and lifts her head to look at him. She pulls her leg back, and stomps into his face, breaking his nose. His hands flail weakly towards her again, and she kicks him on more time, before his limbs fall and he passes out.

    Her head falls back onto the ground and she lies there for a second, staring at the ceiling, panting. Breathing is painful with her injured side and well, injured everything, but when Kate hears a feminine cry of pain from behind her, she steels herself to roll onto her front, and get on her hands and knees.

    She lifts her head to look across the room, and sees Yelena struggle with three men over the shotgun, five of them on the ground around her feet. She looks so small next to them, Kate thinks, her brain hazy and her vision foggy around the edges. One of Yelena’s hands is on the gun, and she attempts to use her bracelets on the man holding onto it too, but one of the others grabs it and pulls it back. The third one punches her in the stomach, and she groans, doubling over but not letting go of the gun.

    Kate stumbles to her feet, swaying, but she holds onto her sword and she starts to stagger across the room. Her arms are hanging by her side, she has no energy left to lift them. Somewhere in the back of her mind she becomes aware that if any of the men notice her coming, she probably doesn’t have the energy to protect herself anymore. Thankfully, they remain preoccupied with Yelena, and Kate makes her way over, passing by the bodies littering the room. The next hit is delivered at Yelena’s face, and her hand slips from the shotgun, falling backwards. The man holding the shotgun twists it around and pumps it, loading a shell just as Kate stumbles up to behind him. The other two men’s and Yelena’s eyes widen as they notice her, but it’s too late, and she uses her last reserve of strength to lift the sword and shove the blade deep into his back. It goes through him, her whole stumbling weight behind the movement, from the back of his waist, and out his chest. When he falls, she falls with him, no energy left in her.

    She collapses at Yelena’s feet, and only hears the sounds of the fight afterwards. She doesn’t know how long she lies there, across the back of the man she just killed, the handle of her sword digging into her stomach, but it’s probably not too long. She would think she passed out, but her body hurts too much for her to be unconscious, even though her eyes won out and slipped closed.

    There is a crackling sound of electricity, followed by a thud, then a cry of pain from a man, followed by another. She hears running footsteps then, and she is rolled over and off of the dead gangster a second later.

    “Kate?! Kate!”

    Yelena’s voice sounds scared, and Kate struggles to open her eyes, but she manages to blink them open after a few seconds. Yelena looks a bit worse for the wear, but nowhere close to how awful Kate imagines she looks herself. There is a bruise on her cheek, and her lip is bleeding, but that’s all Kate can see as she looks up at her as Yelena kneels by her side. “Kate, look at me. ”

    Her eyes slowly focus on Yelena’s and she blinks slowly.

    “Is this your blood?”

    She gulps and forces herself to speak, her mind becoming foggier by the second. “Some…some of it.”

    Kate’s vision starts to swim and darkness starts to creep from the edges of her vision, but she is brought back by a sharp pain across her cheek. Her brain is slow to catch up to the fact that Yelena just slapped her.

    “You can’t pass out. Where are you injured?”

    She doesn’t have the capacity to answer, and Yelena pulls her blood soaked shirt up, and wipes at the skin of her stomach with her hand, to see where it’s coming from. Kate groans when she touches her side, and Yelena gets up and goes somewhere in the room to retrieve a rag, and a bottle of something.

    She kneels to her side again, when she comes back, leaning over her, and meets her eyes. Her voice is hoarse when she speaks, but gentle.

    “This will hurt like a bitch, I’m sorry.”

    She doesn’t wait for Kate’s answer or objection, and pours the content of the bottle onto her front. Kate groans then cries out, the alcohol both cold and stinging against her skin. The sharp pain helps to lift some of the fog off her brain however and she is able to keep her eyes open now. Yelena uses the rag to wipe at her abdomen and chest, and she is visibly relieved when most of the blood painting her skin red turns out to be not Kate’s. Kate keeps looking at her as Yelena works, her brain slowly coming back to itself. Yelena wipes her torso clean, or as clean as possible in these circumstances, and throws the rag to the side. She examines Kate’s ribs, her fingers gentle against her.

    “There are some shotgun pellets in your side. We will have to take them out.” “Yeah, I…I got clipped.”

    Her voice is breathy and Yelena’s eyes that have been focused on her body jump to hers when she speaks. She gives Kate a small, relieved smile.

    “Good, you speak...Come, sit up.”

    She grabs onto one of Kate’s wrists and the back of her neck, and helps her sit up, leaning her against the wall gently. She grunts but sitting helps, and she feels her mind becoming clearer by the second. Yelena picks up the rag again and lifts to wipe at her face too but she grabs her hand weakly, and pulls it away. She holds onto it in her lap, and leans her head back against the wall. She looks at Yelena over, and notices the splotch of deep red against her hip. “Are you okay?”

    She reaches for her shirt, but it’s Yelena’s turn to grab her hand, and she brings it back to Kate’s lap, not letting it go.

    “I’m fine. It’s not my blood.”

    Kate nods, not having the mental capacity to argue or second guess.

    “We have to go on. We have to…find Annie.”

    She groans into the sentence, as she attempts to stand up. Her legs give out once, and she falls back onto her ass, but she tries again. Yelena helps her the second time, pulling her up by her elbows and she has to lean back against the wall but she manages to stay standing. She takes a deep breath, readying herself to lean off the wall when it hits her. Something stinks. Like, very badly.

    “What…what’s that smell?”

    Yelena blinks at her, before sniffing the air too, grimacing. She turns away from Kate to sniff in the air again, and starts slowly walking towards the other end of the room. She stops in front of one of the holes that the shotgun fire tore through the metal walls, and stops. “Yelena, what is it?”

    She doesn’t answer her, but takes out a small flashlight from her pocket, shining into the hole. Now that she noticed it, Kate can’t stop smelling the awful stench of whatever is behind that wall. It’s putrid, and strong and it makes her lean off of the wall, and make her stumbling way back across the room. She ignores the bodies again, trying not to focus on the death and destruction around them.

    The smell gets stronger as she gets closer to where Yelena is standing, and she wants to lift her shirt to cover her face with it before she remembers how it’s essentially solid black now, from all the blood soaking through it.

    “Hey, Yelena, what is it?”

    Yelena spins around, and puts a hand on Kate’s chest to halt her advance. “Kate, we have to go.”

    She doesn’t understand, and stops to look down on Yelena.

    “What? What do you mean? What is it?”

    Yelena looks uncharacteristically uncertain.

    “It’s…it’s death.”

    Kate doesn’t understand, and even more so, she doesn’t understand why Yelena is keeping it from her. She grabs the flashlight from her hand, and staggers to the wall, leaning against it with one hand and lifting the light to look into the hole with her right. The smell is overwhelming at this point, but she feels like she has to know.

    She doesn’t know what she is seeing first. It looks like a mess of clothes and shoes, and something grey…

    Her blood runs cold.

    No.

    No. No. No.

    It’s bodies.

    Dozens of corpses, thrown onto each other. Rotting, decaying away in the container next to them.

    Annie.

    She stumbles away from the wall, towards the door on the other side, next to the window. Yelena makes to grab at her arm, and Kate thinks she says something but somehow she finds the strength to pull it from her grasp and throws the door open, letting sunshine in. She staggers outside and doesn’t even have the capacity to check if there is anyone there, as she makes her way to the right, leaning heavily against the wall of next container. She grabs the handle, and pulls it, and immediately gags when the metal door swings open. The smell hits her in full force, but she steels herself and goes inside. The light from outside illuminates the space, and she sees the bodies stacked upon each other, men and women. About some she can’t even tell, their skin grey and pulled so taunt on their bones, that their faces are no longer recognizable. There is one that seems like it was squashed, the only evidence that it was once a human being is the mop of matted, brown hair sticking out of it. She looks around in horror, bile rising up her throat. She sways on her feet, and turns around, managing to make it out of there before she falls onto her knees.

    She throws up, an acidic burn in her throat until there is nothing left in her stomach. Even then, she dry-heaves, gagging until her throat hurts.

    She sits back onto her knees, with her eyes closed and wipes her mouth. She needs several seconds to opens them, and she sees Yelena, standing to the side. Her face is hard, features set in stone, but her eyes are soft as she looks at Kate. When Kate meets her gaze, she opens her mouth to speak, and there is hesitation in her tone.

    “Is Annie…is she inside?”

    Kate tries to recall if she has seen her but most of the bodies are in a state where it’s impossible to tell. She shakes her head.

    “I don’t…I don’t know.”

    Yelena nods, and looks away before she walks up to Kate. She crouches in front of her, and looks into her eyes, her voice gentle when she speaks.

    “We have to go.”

    Kate shakes her head. She has to make sure.

    “No. We have to…”

    Yelena interrupts her, and puts a hand on her shoulder.

    “Kate, you can barely walk.”

    Kate just shakes her head again, and starts to get off the ground. Her legs barely support her, but she stands, and Yelena stands with her. She can’t look at the bodies in the container again, but she has one last thing she has to try.

    She staggers towards the room they came from, and she lets the simmering anger she has felt since the moment she learned about Annie take over her.

    She hates them.

    The faces of the people inside the container swim before her eyes as she makes her way to other end of the room, and pulls her sword from the back of the soldier, almost falling with the movement but catching herself with an arm against the wall.

    “Kate, what are you doing?”

    She ignores Yelena and looks over the bodies littering the room, most of them dead, and she feels a spark of satisfaction. Good. She never hated anyone before but she hates them. She hates them for what’s in that container, she hates them for taking Annie, she hates them for making her see this, for making her kill them.

    She walks back towards where they came from, only stumbling a few times, finding strength in her fury.

    She hates fucking Fisk most of all. For taking her mother away, for taking her fucking life away, for making her feel this way.

    She walks across the hallway, then the room, the smoke from her arrow finally dissipated, and by the time she makes it to the courtyard, she can barely feel her injuries from the all- encompassing rage she feels. Yelena is beside her, and Kate is thankful that she didn’t try to bodily stop her, because she honestly doesn’t know what she would do.

    She walks across the courtyard, and Spider-Man does a double take when he sees her, jumping off of the wall he was stuck onto, but she only focuses on the fact that the super- soldier is already awake. Good.

    “Holy shit, are you guys okay?”

    She ignores Spider-Man, goes straight up to the soldier sitting on the ground, and shoves her sword into his thigh before either Yelena or Spider-Man can blink. He screams in pain. “Where is she?”

    “What the…?”

    She is pulled away by arms around her waist and the soldier just keeps screaming, the blade embedded just above his kneecap. She fights the arms around her, and turns around, shoving Yelena away.

    “Give me your gun.”

    She holds out her hand and Yelena for once looks completely unsettled.

    “No.”

    Kate scoffs and turns away from her, back in front of him before Yelena can grab her again. She pulls an arrow from her quiver, the movement lightning fast and stabs it into his other leg. The soldier screams even louder.

    “Where is the woman you took?”

    White webbing wraps around her wrist, and her hand is yanked to the side but she grabs the web, and yanks back, making Spider-Man stumble forward a few steps. Strong arms wrap around her shoulders and arms, and she slams her head back. Yelena groans behind her but doesn’t let go. She kicks off of the container the soldier is tied (webbed) up against, and they stumble backwards together.

    Yelena’s back hits the container across, and Kate elbows her in the side, Yelena’s cry of pain barely registering. She twists around, her fist rising but her arm is webbed again, and this time, Spider-Man means it when he yanks her. She practically flies backwards, but she learnt from the fight against Kingpin, and she spins quickly to kick him in the head. He ducks, and when she goes to swipe his legs he jumps away with a backflip, kicking her in the chest with the movement.

    She stumbles backwards, but reaches around to pull her bow, jerking her arm with the same movement that is second nature at this point, and she has an acid arrow nocked and pointed at the super-soldier in a heartbeat.

    “Kate, stop!”

    She is panting, and she looks at Yelena from the corner of her eyes. Her nose is bleeding and she has her gun out, pointed at Spider-Man of all people, but her pleading voice gets through the red fog that settled on Kate’s brain. She keeps the string taunt, panting, and tries to think. “Kate, stop, please.”

    She deflates a little, her arm dropping an inch, but before Kate can make up her mind, the super-soldier speaks.

    “She is in a shed, outside on the pier.”

    Kate’s brain freezes. Yelena asks before she can.

    “What?”

    The soldier grunts, leaning his head back against the container behind him and meets Kate’s eyes.

    “A metal shed…on the pier. She is there.”

    Kate gasps, her brain barely able to comprehend what she is hearing. She lowers her bow. The metal shed. The shed they met Spider-Man next to before they sneaked onto the ship. Yelena asks from behind her.

    “Is she alive?”

    Chapter End Notes Tun-dun! :D I hope you all like this chapter :)

    I know it's pretty dark and violent, but Kingpin is a very dark and violent man, and Kate has to face the realities of who and what she is up against, and what it's going to take for and from her to take him on.

    As for how and why Kate could take on Yelena and Spider-Man, even just for a few moments, neither of them really wanted to hurt her, and she is really gone off the deep end for a second there ':D People can do crazy things when really pushed to the edge I hope the Kate-Yelena moments make up for the darkness.

    (Oh yeah, and no, the super-soldier is not Deadpool :D I will tell you who he is soon though)

    Please let me know what you think! :) I love reading your comments!

    Next one will be up this weekend. It'll be less gory, and we'll slow down a little, I promise :D xx

    Chapter 11

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes “Is she alive?”

    “We didn’t hurt her.”

    Kate exhales sharply at the super-soldier’s words, and sways on her feet. She turns to look at Yelena in a daze, who sighs deeply, leaning against the container behind herself, sagging a bit. Yelena speaks to Spider-Man, perched on one of the thrown around containers above them.

    “Spider-Man, can you guard this man while we check the shed?”

    “I guarded him even from you guys.”

    His voice has a bit of an edge to it, but if Yelena notices, she elects to ignore it. “Thank you. You are a peach.”

    Kate watches, still struggling to process, as she leans off of the metal wall behind her with a barely there flinch, and walks up to the super-soldier. She pulls Kate’s sword from his thigh and he cries out in pain again, but Yelena doesn’t give him a second glance as she starts to walk towards where they first entered the ship, carrying her gun in one hand, and Kate’s sword in the other.

    Kate walks after her on autopilot.

    Annie is alive.

    She feels a spark of joy at the thought but she in unable to grasp at a single emotion right now, feeling like there is a tornado in her head but also, as if every single emotion she has every felt left her body at the soldier’s admission.

    She follows Yelena for a few minutes, before she starts feeling the heaviness of her body again, the anger and shock slowly giving way to exhaustion and pain. She puts the arrow back into the quiver, along with her bow without a thought, dragging her feet. Yelena doesn’t say a word to her, and Kate sees her wipe the blood under her nose with the back of her hand, and notices the way she seems to be leaning towards one side a bit awkwardly. The first feeling she can name from the storm inside her brain is guilt. The next one is shame.

    Yelena has been with her through all this, fought with her, almost died with her and Kate hurt her. She was so engrossed in her rage that she was ready to finish this, find Annie, find absolution from putting her in danger, whatever it took. She crossed a line. Many lines actually. After they get Annie, and after they get out of here, and she can breathe again, she will have some thorough apologizing to do.

    For now, she keeps on walking in silence, focusing on putting one foot in front of the other, because otherwise she will definitely fall, and she doesn’t think she has it in her to stand up one more time.

    By the time they make it to other end of the ship, Kate can barely walk again, so getting out the way they arrived is probably out of the question. Yelena looks at her, somewhere around the ship’s edge, and purses her lips, before she comes up to Kate, and passes her the sword. She sneaks a hand around Kate’s waist without a word, and grabs her arm, pulling it around her own shoulders.

    Their progress is slow, and Kate’s mind is sort of dulled by the amount of pain she is in, but Yelena leads them toward the ramp leading up to the ship. The pier is mostly deserted, the shipyard-workers probably having fled at the sounds of the gunfight and explosions, with only a few people milling about, very far away. In the distance, Kate hears sirens as they reach the shed, both of them breathing heavy.

    Yelena leans her against the wall of it gently, and takes out her gun, aiming at the door. She takes a deep breath, and kicks the door in with a grunt. Kate is aware of the fact that she is in no shape to help, but when Yelena enters, she stumbles in behind her, with her sword in hand nonetheless.

    There are two men inside, armed with automatic rifles, but Yelena puts them down before they have a chance to rise from their chairs. They hear muffled screaming from the behind the door separating them from the back half of the shed and Kate is through the door before Yelena has a chance to object.

    Annie is there.

    Annie is there, her hands and ankles are tied, and there is a rag in her mouth, and she is screaming on the top of her lungs at her sight. Alive.

    There is a bruise at her temple, and she looks very pale but she is there, and she is alive. Kate collapses onto her knees on the ground next to her, not even trying to slow her descent, and cuts the rope on her wrists. Annie finally stops screaming and Kate cuts the ones on her legs too as Annie pulls the rag from her mouth.

    “Kate?!”

    Kate falls back against the wall behind her, her sword slipping from her hands, but she finally lets a small smile overtake her face.

    “Hey Annie.”

    Annie seems to process for a second, before she starts sobbing.

    “We have to go. Police is almost here.”

    Kate is slow to process Yelena’s words but nods and attempts stand anyway. She manages, barely so, almost falling back when she leans down to pick up her sword and her head swims, black spots appearing in her vision.

    Yelena comes into the room, and crouches down in front of Annie.

    “You didn’t see Kate Bishop here, okay?”

    Annie continues to sob hysterically. Yelena raises her voice, speaking over her. “Anna, I need to know you understand.”

    Annie’s eyes jump between Kate and Yelena, but she nods after a few seconds. “…yeah.”

    “You don’t know who the woman was who rescued you, okay?”

    Annie nods again, and Yelena stands up, walking over to Kate. She grabs her waist again to support her, Kate’s arm slung around her shoulder and the two of them leave the sobbing Annie behind. The police is almost at the pier, the flashing lights of at least ten NYPD cruisers visible in the distance and they go around the other side to avoid being seen. The journey to the car feels like hours, and they need to take several breaks to lean against containers and buildings, because Kate can barely put on foot in front of the other, and Yelena finally seems to be losing stream as well.

    By the time they make it to the white Maserati, they are both panting heavy, and when Yelena leans her against the wall next to where it’s parked, they need a few long moments to catch their breath. Kate gets in with Yelena’s help and Yelena walks around the car to get into the driver’s seat. They pull out of the parking spot a moment later.

    Yelena obeys every traffic law ever invented again, and they slowly leave the harbor and the sirens behind in silence.

    Kate feels weighed down in her seat, as if her limbs were cast in lead. She still feels a spark of joy at having found Annie alive, at least, but most of all, she feels like there is a black hole, a void instead of where her heart usually beats. She feels cold in the car now, after the stifling heat, and lifts her hand with sharp pain in her side to turn off the AC. “I can’t believe we found her.”

    “We did.”

    Yelena’s answer is a bit breathy, but Kate just keeps looking at her hands in her lap. “I am so sorry.”

    She looks up at Yelena, at her glistening face covered in bruises, her split lip, and the remains of blood under her nose, but Yelena keeps focusing on the road ahead, checking the rearview mirror periodically.

    She turns back to her hands, thinking back to the day, and she feels the heaviness of her limbs, her soul. She looks down onto her lap. Her whole body is covered in blood. Her shirt is practically black with all the blood soaking into it, and the only reason she can’t see it on her jeans is because they were already black to begin with, but she sees the stickiness of the material.

    So much blood.

    The hatred she felt on the ship is gone now, only an exhausted abyss remaining in its place. She sees it all before her eyes, staring at the crimson on her palms. The soldier wheezing on the ground, brown eyes staring into her soul as he chokes on his blood. The image of bodies flying then getting buried under metal after her explosive arrow hits its mark. The sounds of traffic around them fade into the background as she hears the man’s scream when her sword got stuck in his thigh, the wet squelch it made when she pulled it out, and the stickiness of her bloody footprints on the ground as she walked away from him. The feeling of warm, thick blood gushing onto her chest, the skin of her neck, the surprised look in the man’s eyes as the blade of the knife slipped into his throat.

    So much blood.

    She remembers the sensation of running her sword through that man, falling onto his heavy, limp body. Breathing on him, when his chest was no longer moving with hers. She sees Yelena, her nose bleeding because of her but still pointing her gun at Spider-Man to stick up for her in a fight where Kate was downright cruel.

    She sees the bodies too, in the container, thrown in there like discarded toys. Rotting away in the darkness. She doesn’t feel angry anymore, she just feels exhausted and empty and like they stickiness of the blood on her is now forever etched onto her skin. She doesn’t realize she is crying, until her side screams in pain from the stuttering breath she takes. She can’t help it though, and the pain makes her sob harder. She longs for her mom, to kneel in front of her and kiss it all better, to take her aching body into her arms, like when Kate was little. To wipe her tears away and tell her she is not a bad person, for all the death and destruction she causes. Thinking of her mom just makes her cry harder. She is aware of Yelena sitting next to her, but she has no mental capacity or energy left to feel ashamed for her tears or try to hide or stop them. She just sobs, letting the exhausting, shitty fucking day wash over her and when Yelena reaches over, offering a tissue for her she just sobs harder still.

    Yelena doesn’t pull her hand back, but instead reaches for Kate’s. It’s such a simple gesture, and she doesn’t say anything, but as she slides her hand into Kate’s, the swirling black hole that has been enveloping Kate’s soul suddenly has a center of gravity.

    Yelena’s hand feels small in hers, and her nails are painted light blue. She tries to focus on that, instead of the rusty red that sticks to Yelena’s skin too. Their hands get clammy, but Yelena doesn’t let go until Kate’s sobs slowly recede. They are arrive to Kate’s building a few minutes after that, and she hands Yelena the key-fob without thinking, her mind slowly numbing down.

    Yelena drives them down to Kate’s floor, and parks the car kind of askew, but Kate just doesn’t care anymore. She shuts the engine off, and takes a deep breath and Kate just sits next to her, too exhausted to do or say anything. They sit in silence for about a minute, before Yelena seems to gather her strength, and gets out of the car.

    Kate watches as she walks around the front, dragging her feet a bit too, and comes to open her door, reaching for her arm.

    “Come on.”

    She lets Yelena help her out, but she almost crumbles against Kate’s weight when she stands up. They stumble against the car, Yelena falling against her, and they barely catch themselves from falling to the ground. Kate lets out a groan as Yelena’s weight hits her side, and the pains brings her back to the present a bit.

    “Are you okay?”

    Her voice sounds foreign to her own ears, hoarse with her earlier tears and it takes an incredibly amount of energy just to speak. Yelena takes a deep breath against her, her forhead pushed against Kate’s shoulder and her words a bit slurred when she speaks. “I may have…lied about it…being someone else’s blood.”

    The words register slowly in Kate’s head, but when they do her stomach gives a tired jolt, her body waking up for one last round to fight, like a car out of fuel that has just enough to start up once more, after stalling for long.

    Kate shifts them as careful as she can, so Yelena is the one to lean against the car and she pushes herself away, swaying slightly on her fee. She grips the roof of the car for support by Yelena’s shoulder, looking down to assess the damage and comes to the horrifying realization that a big part of the left side of Yelena’s grey New York t-shirt, that has been hidden away from her in the car, is soaked with blood.

    She reaches for the edge of the shirt, and pulls it up and sees that a rag has been tied around Yelena’s torso, but she seems to have bled through it. She looks up to meet Yelena’s eyes, her own now wide and terrified, and only just notices how her face is at least two shades paler than usual, her eyes a bit too bright and disoriented. She is yanked back into the present with both feet now, and she attempts to gather her strength once more, and her voice comes out a bit stronger than earlier in the car.

    “We need to get upstairs…you are bleeding out.”

    She has no idea what they will do upstairs, but she knows that if they stay in the parking both of them will pass out soon, and Yelena will die, and Kate will most likely too. She grabs Yelena and pulls her to herself, her arm around her waist, and Yelena’s goes around her. They make their stumbling, staggering journey across the parking lot very slowly, supporting each other and taking breaks periodically against the columns that line their way, but they get to the elevator without falling over and Kate takes that as a win. They tumble into the elevator, with Kate attempting to lean Yelena against the wall gently, but essentially falling against her with the effort.

    “Thirteenth.”

    Yelena rasps out into her shoulder, and Kate tries to look at her from this close, confused. Her apartment is on the 29th floor.

    “That’s not our floor.”

    She reaches for the button 29, but Yelena’s hand weakly slaps at her hand. “Thirteenth…Trust me.”

    Kate does and she really hopes Yelena is not becoming delirious or something. The ride feels slow, and Kate has to lean her entire weight against Yelena to hold them up, barely avoiding sliding down to the floor. When they get to the thirteenth floor, she leans off of the wall, and pulls Yelena out, both of them groaning.

    “Third door.”

    Yelena grits out, and they make their straggling way down to it. They fall against the wood, and Kate really hopes Yelena is right about wherever they are because she doesn’t think they have enough in them to make it up to her place now, without at least one of them passing out. Yelena raises her hand, and bangs weakly against the door, and they wait, just panting from the exertion it took to get up here. Kate feels like hours pass, and she is about to attempt to carry them back to the elevator when the door swings open, and they nearly fall forward. “…oi, blyat.”

    On the other side of the door is Sonya, clad in nothing but a flimsy robe and under any other circumstances Kate would find it equally hilarious and incredibly awkward that she is very obviously naked under it but thankfully Yelena gathers enough strength to speak for them. “Hiii.”

    Kate feels the inexplicable urge to laugh, but it never becomes more than a tired huff out of her nose. Sonya grabs Yelena from her, and calls out into the apartment. “Thomas! Come and help please.”

    Kate stands leaning against doorway as Sonya steers Yelena into the apartment, practically holding her up entirely, talking at her in hurried Russian that Yelena gives breathy one worded answers to and leaving Kate in the hallway and. Kate attempts to close the door behind herself, but it seems this is as far as her body is going to take her, because when she leans back against it, her legs slide from under her and she falls onto her ass. Oww.

    She groans in pain, and she is about ready to just pass out here, when as a man with black hair and a beard shows up at the end of the hallway, wearing black sweatpants and pulling a t- shirt above his head. He walks up to her, and crouches in front of her, grabbing her hands to help her up as he speaks.

    “Hi, I’m Thomas. Sorry, I don’t speak Russian.”

    She snorts weakly.

    “Neither do I…I’m Kate.”

    He chuckles, and pulls her up, taking most of her weight with an arm around her waist, leading her forwards to where Sonya and Yelena disappeared to.

    “Ah, you are Kate. I heard a lot about you.”

    Kate lifts an eyebrow, flinching into the movement. Her whole face hurts from the beating she took today. She rasps out her answer breathier than she means to.

    “Good things…I hope.”

    “No idea, it was always in Russian.”

    Kate snorts again, actually managing a weak chuckle, and they finally make it to the threshold of the living room. Yelena sits on a big leather couch in a black bra, her shirt and the rag covering her injury already off, and Sonya comes power walking back into the room through a different door, carrying a big, black bag.

    Yelena has her eyes closed, and her head rolled back against the couch, and Sonya marches up to her and delivers a slap so strong across her cheeks that her head snaps to the side. Kate and Thomas both look at the pair with eyebrows raised, but it seems to work. Yelena shakes her head and blinks a couple of times, looking around like she is just realizing where she is, before her eyes focus on Sonya and she smiles tiredly.

    “Suka.”

    Thomas helps Kate to the couch too, and she is lowered down gently next to Yelena, about a feet of space between them, while Sonya speaks to Yelena and deposits the bag on the coffee table.

    “You can’t pass out. You will go into shock and die…Thomas please go to the fridge and get two bags of B or AB negative and one of…Kate what is your blood type?”

    Kate blinks. She has no idea. She never needed to know before.

    “I don’t know.”

    “She is AB positive.”

    Kate turns to look at Yelena, shocked. How the fuck? Sonya just barrels on. “Ah, lucky. Get her whatever we have the most of.”

    Yelena looks at her with a weak grin but her words are still coming with a bit of a slurry struggle.

    “I told you…I know a lot about you…Kate Bishop.”

    “You looked at…my medical reports?”

    Thomas is still staring at Kate, his eyes searching her face below the blood and bruising. He is visibly surprised in a second.

    “Wait…You are Kate Bishop? The Kate Bishop??”

    God, Kate has no energy for the whole Bishop Security fiasco re-run or whatever is going on here. She grunts and attempts to shift into a more comfortable position. “Yeah. Sorry if my mom fucked you over or something.”

    He stares at her and now Sonya and Yelena are looking between them, with Sonya’s hand keeping pressure on Yelena’s side.

    “No, I'm…I’m Thomas Newhouse…”

    She has no idea who that is and he can tell.

    “…Allie Newhouse’s brother?”

    Newhouse…oh. She definitely remembers Allie Newhouse. The realization hits her just as Sonya speaks.

    “You two know each other?”

    He laughs good-naturedly.

    “Not really. But Kate knows my sister pretty well.”

    He leaves the room with a snicker and Kate tries to remember if there is a specific reason for the chuckle or the stressed ‘pretty well’. She does remember Allie Newhouse, she was a girl in her year and they shared a couple of classes together. She was quiet, hard-working but had a way of making the perfect sarcastic comment under her nose that had you in stiches, if you knew to listen to her. They were friendly, but she doesn’t remember spending too much time with her outside of classes, despite asking her to go to get coffee once. Allie told her she had to study and left her standing in the hall.

    She watches as Sonya rummages through the box, and starts prepping things on the coffee table, while she tells Yelena to put pressure on her own side. She takes out a suture kit, a box of plastic gloves, bandages, a bunch of pills and little bottles of fluid. Thomas comes back with three bags of blood (Kate just blinks at that, too tired to be surprised or shocked), and an IV stand.

    He puts the stand down between her and Yelena behind the couch, and comes around to take out a metal box from the medicine-bag and placing the blood inside. Sonya comes into view, and passes her two green pills and a glass of water.

    “Painkillers.”

    She could kiss Sonya right now, her body feels like it has been hit with a jackhammer repeatedly, then thrown into a dumpster. She manages to grunt out a “thanks”. She takes the pills enthusiastically, or as much as she can in her state, and gulps the entire glass of water down, as if she just escaped a desert. Next to her Yelena does the same and Sonya waits for them to swallow their pills, hands on her hips.

    “Who is hurt worse?”

    They both attempt to lift their arms to point at the other person, but Kate is the only one who actually manages to, and Sonya takes that as an answer on its own. She starts putting on rubber gloves, and holds out a pair for Thomas too, who pulls them on, and they step up to the couch to stand over Yelena. Sonya asks Yelena something in Russian, and she answers with a tired grin, blinking very slowly.

    Kate just lets herself rest against the leather couch, closing her eyes and finds a small amount of joy in just being able to not move. She hopes the painkillers kick in soon, and hopefully knock her out, so she can finally not feel or think anything for a couple of hours. “Do I need to slap you too, Kate Bishop?”

    Sonya’s voice makes her open her eyes, attempting to give a small smile. “No.”

    Yelena groans in pain and says something in Russian that from the tone of it sounds like swearing, and Kate looks to her side to see what’s happening. Sonya is cleaning Yelena’s side next to her, chuckling at whatever Yelena just said. Kate looks at the wound, noting how it’s short and deep, but not round, right above Yelena’s left hip. A stab wound, probably with a knife.

    She closes her eyes, and turns away, biting the inside of her cheek. She feels her guilt and shame come back ten-fold, remembering that that is exactly where she elbowed Yelena in the side earlier. She takes a deep breath, flinching at the pain, and tries to control her thoughts, to not let them spiral back towards the events of the day. She decides to try and do a calming exercise her therapist taught her back when she lost her Dad.

    Okay, five things she can hear: Yelena’s breathing next to her; the opening of a plastic packet; Thomas and Sonya shuffling around; the humming of the metal box Thomas put on the coffee table; and…

    “I didn’t know you had a sister.”

    Yelena speaks next to her, and Kate opens her eyes to see Thomas smiles warmly, as he cleans Yelena’s face of dried blood.

    “I have two, actually. Older sister is Liza, younger is Allie.”

    Thomas glances over at Kate when he says her name, and gives her a smirk. She doesn’t understand that or have it in her to react to it. Sonya is using a suture kit to sew the injury on Yelena’s side, her motions seemingly practiced. From the amused glance she throws in Kate’s direction, she definitely picked up on Thomas’ moderately subtle teasing. “How does your sister know Kate Bishop?”

    “We went to high-school together.”

    Kate joins the conversation, her voice a bit gruff still.

    “With Allie or Liza?”

    Sonya asks again, not looking at Kate from Yelena’s side, but obviously talking to her. “Allie.”

    She leans her head back against the couch, and looks around the room, continuing the calming exercise. Five things she can see. The abstract painting across from her, two doors on the other end of the room, one to the side; the building next to them through the windows, and the bag of medical equipment on the coffee table.

    She moves onto listing five things she can sense right now. The leather of the couch beneath her palm, her shirt sticking to her torso, an odd tingling sensation in her fingers, her shoes against the ground, and her keys digging into her pocket.

    Okay, next round, four things she can hear. A car honking outside, Thomas walking to the coffee table, another plastic something crinkling;…

    “Kate, do you want to wash your hands?”

    She doesn’t look down on them, not wanting to see the rusty color covering it, and spiraling again. She just nods, and Thomas leaves the room and comes back with a bowl filled with soapy water soon. She list 4 things she can sense as she rubs at her hands; the warmth of the water against her skin, the weight of the bowl in her lap, the smell of the soap in it, and the material of the towel Thomas offers her to wipe her hand in after she is finished. Four things she can see: the drapes by the windows, the metal box on the table,… “Kate, I’ll clean your face, okay?”

    She blinks twice, her brain a bit sluggish, to focus on Thomas standing in front of her. “Yeah, thanks.”

    He grabs her face with gentle fingers, and starts to use a cotton pad to start wiping at the dried blood on her forehead, around her re-opened eyebrow wound. Next to her, Sonya is bandaging Yelena’s side, and Kate flinches multiple times when he touches a cut or bruise, and he gives an apologetic smile each time. It’s getting a bit awkward however, so she clears her throat and talks to him.

    “Is this your apartment?”

    He meets her eyes for a second, before bringing his gaze back to his work. “Nah, it’s Sonya’s. I have a place in Brooklyn.”

    She is definitely surprised, and then even more so when she thinks about the implications. “Wait a minute…you live in the same building as me?”

    She turns her head to Sonya, and she gives her a smile, using medical tape to attach a square of gauze against Yelena’s skin.

    “Yeah but, I was here first.”

    She nods, processing, her brain somehow feeling a bit slower than usual, but she chalks it up to the beating she took today. The sting of the antiseptic wipes against her eyebrow make her hiss and close her eyes, and she kind of starts to feel like her whole face is tingling. “So, how is Allie?”

    She asks with her eyes closed still, when Thomas moves onto cleaning a cut on her chin, and she hears Sonya get up from next to her to walk around the coffee table, open the metal box, then go the IV stand behind her head, plastic crinkling again.

    “She is good, she passed the bar last year, and now she works for GLK&H. She is single.” She opens her eyes to look at him after the last word, seeing his smirk again. Kate blinks at him slowly a few times, trying to convey that she doesn’t understand what he is insinuating. Next to them, Sonya connects the blood bag to the IV line in Yelena’s forearm as Tomas’ smirk slowly fades, and his brows raise.

    “Seriously?”

    “What?”

    Sonya comes up to Kate now, with scissors in her hands.

    “I’ll cut your shirt off, okay?”

    She blinks at Sonya, still trying to figure out what Thomas is getting at. Her brain seems to have a warm fog descending over it. Kate nods at her distractedly and Sonya leans over her to cut the bloody material off of her, leaving her only in her sports bra too. Thomas is looking at her over Sonya’s shoulder.

    “You really don’t know?”

    She is getting frustrated now, her brain struggling to put the pieces together, but even the annoyance feels dulled.

    “Don’t know what?”

    He looks at Sonya and Yelena before looking back at her, as if they had any idea what he is talking about.

    “She was like totally head over heels for you in high school.”

    She leans back, her eyebrows lifted close to her hairline, needing a moment to process. “No she wasn’t.

    He basically laughs in her face.

    “I literally just recognized you because she used to drag me to all of your stupid basketball games.”

    She shakes her head, a laugh bubbling up from her chest. She is feeling strangely light- headed.

    “Dude, no. No-no. I asked her out once and she said No.”

    He snorts with a smile, putting down the antiseptic wipes and taking off his rubber gloves, finished with cleaning Kate’s face. Kate has trouble focusing on his features, her gaze instead being drawn to the painting behind him. She really likes those hexagonal shapes. “Yeah, I remember that. Someone wrote Mrs. Bishop on her locker and she thought you were asking her out of pity.”

    Her head is buzzing with this information, or maybe just buzzing in general. She feels weirdly floaty, but in a good way and a chuckle works up its way on her throat. “Awh man, that would have been cool to know like 6 years ago...ohw fucking hell” He laughs back at her, but her chuckle turns into a groan when a cotton pad drenched with antiseptic is pushed directly onto the shotgun injury on her side.

    “Thomas, why don’t you go order some Chinese food for us all?”

    Sonya says from her leaned over position from in front of Kate. Thomas gives her a weird look, but leaves the room anyway. Kate closes her eyes, and tries to block out the pain, but it feels more and more dulled by the second thankfully anyway. She chuckles internally at what she just learned. It wasn’t a serious thing with Allie, but it definitely would have been nice to know that back in the day. She really had no idea.

    “There are pellets still inside, I’ll take them out, okay?”

    She opens her eyes to look at Sonya, and nods. Her vision feels a bit fuzzy, but not like when she is about to pass out. It’s like she is under a warm blanket, looking out through a frosty window. She barely flinches when Sonya starts digging into her side with a pair of tweezers, instead she feels mostly the texture of the leather underneath her hand, and the cotton pad Sonya uses to wipe away the blood trickling down her side. These are some kickass painkillers.

    “Sonya…”

    “Yees?”

    Sonya imitates the sluggish way Kate said her name, and she huffs out a laugh through her nose.

    “What did you give me?”

    Sonya glances up at her with a smile, before looking back at her work, her tweezers pulling out another black piece of metal from Kate’s side.

    “Morphine.”

    A warm gush of blood bubbles up from her flesh, but it almost feels ticklish instead of painful. Her mind is slow to process Sonya’s answer, and she thinks she should be freaked out, but she just feels so warm and content, it barely registers.

    “Oh, okay…Hey, is this real leather?”

    Sonya just laughs at her, and she chuckles too, a bit unsure why. She keeps looking at the paining across the room, the shapes of it drawing her in. She is aware of Sonya leaning back when she is finished taking the pellets out, and reaching for the bandages, but she is too engrossed in the shapes to really focus on it.

    “You were really lucky with this injury. You could have had a hole torn through you.” She doesn’t look at Sonya. Yeah she was lucky. Lucky. Lucky.

    “I have to walk my dog.”

    She remembers Lucky in a flash, and longs for his soft fur, and happy little company. She attempts to stand up, before she is pushed back down by two strong hands against her shoulder. She falls back down with a small giggle, and Sonya chuckles in front of her too. “Thomas will bring him down. You need to stay put.”

    She accepts her fate, and her palms keep touching the leather underneath them, her fingertips running over the texture. It feels weirdly satisfying, and it keeps her occupied while Sonya tapes pieces of gauze onto her side and ribs.

    “Kate, can you lift your arm please?”

    She tries to figure out which arm Sonya means, looking at her hands on her lap. She chuckles again, and Sonya reaches for her right arm with a smile, and helping her put it on the back of the couch.

    “Sorry. I am a bit… out of it.”

    She says it with lazy grin, looking down at her, and notices again that Sonya is definitely not wearing anything under her robe. She lifts her eyes to look back at the hexagons again, and Thomas chuckles from the doorway as he enters the room again.

    She turns her head with the intention of looking at him, but her eyes settle on Yelena instead. She has her eyes closed, and her face is so smooth, completely free of the lines that usually frame it. Kate’s eyes trail her jawline and cheeks and she uses the hand on the back of the couch to poke her shoulder.

    “Hey, you are not supposed to be sleeping.”

    Yelena’s eyes blink open, and they meet Kate’s and her mind immediately fixates on the flacks of brown in her otherwise green eyes, her pupils constricted.

    “I am not sleeping. I am just enjoying.”

    Yelena’s voice sounds an octave lower to her than usual, and for some reason it sends a shiver down Kate’s spine. She realizes her hand is still touching Yelena’s shoulder, and her skin feels incredibly nice against Kate’s fingertips. Her eyes drop to look at her hand and she moves her fingers along the soft skin, from Yelena’s shoulder to her collarbone, unable to stop herself. God it feels so good, so smooth against her own. When her eyes lift to Yelena’s face again, she sees that her eyes are closed again but her lips are a bit parted. Sonya must have said something that Kate didn’t hear because she only hears Thomas’ answer. “Ooh, okay. I get it.”

    She can’t really turn away from Yelena now that she started looking at her, the warmth in her chest growing into her limbs and head. Yelena’s tongue darts out to wet her lips and Kate’s eyes follow the movement, and she wonders what it would be to touch her there, feel her soft, wet…

    A hand snaps in front of her face and Kate blinks, once, then twice more, turning her head towards its owner. Sonya is grinning, repeating herself.

    “Your keys, Kate.”

    She blinks, and pulls her hand from Yelena’s skin with some difficulty, digging into her pocket. She pulls out her keyring after some struggle, and triumphantly hands it to Sonya, who in turn puts it in Thomas’ outstretched palm.

    “Which one is your flat?”

    She blinks at him, trying to figure out why they need to know that. Sonya sighs but she is still smiling.

    “Thomas is getting your dog.”

    Oh Lucky! Yes, she can’t wait to see him. Yelena pipes up from beside her. “Lucky the Pizza Dog! I love him!!”

    Sonya looks between the two of them, clearly amused.

    “Sooo…which apartment?”

    Kate gives Sonya a slow smile.

    “29th floor, apartment 6.”

    Thomas smiles too, throwing the keys up and catching them.

    “Alright. Do you need anything else?”

    She smiles, blinking slowly. She already feels amazing, she doesn’t need anything in this world. She shakes her head.

    “Nope. I’m golden.”

    All three of them chuckle at her, and she joins in, not really getting what they are laughing at but feeling it bubble up anyway.

    “Grab her a change of clothes too, babe. Something comfortable.”

    Kate watches as he strokes her back as he moves by her and thinks it’s really nice. They are clearly a well fitted couple. The words only register in her mind by the time she hears the front door close. Oh yeah, that’ll be good. Her jeans are a bit stuffy and sticky. Sonya moves onto her side on the couch, sitting between her and Yelena, cleaning the bullet- graze by her shoulder. She cannot feel any pain anymore, just the cotton swiping against her skin and stares ahead, blinking at the specks of dust floating in the ray of sunlight across from her. They are golden, and glistening and beautiful.

    “Kateee?”

    Yelena calls out from the other end of the couch, her voice just as sluggish as Kate feels. There is a whininess to it that makes her smile fondly but she doesn’t know or care to think about why.

    “Hmm?”

    “Will you call Allie?”

    She tries to place the name, her brow furrowing but comes up empty.

    “Who?”

    Sonya chuckles between them, now stitching Kate’s shoulder apparently, but not taking part in the conversation.

    “Thomas’ hot lawyer sister.”

    Oh, right. Allie from school. She grins, lazy and slow, leaning her head back against the couch, shrugging.

    “I don’t have her number.”

    She thinks about it for another minute, before she asks, turning her head to look at Yelena across the back of the couch.

    “How do you know she is hot?”

    Yelena seems to think about it, her eyes fliting around the ceiling. Sonya stands up from between them, walking over to Kate’s left side.

    “Kate, make a fist for me please?”

    It’s a bit hard to focus, and she ends up making a fist of both of her hands. Sonya smiles, and sprays something cold on her forearm. Yelena answers her then.

    “You asked her out, so I assume.”

    Fair enough. She tries to consider it, but her brain constantly gets derailed by things she sees around herself. Yelena’s jawline. The color of the wall behind Yelena. It’s like a mix of blue and green. She really likes it. The shape of Yelena’s nose. Its small and pointy. She smiles at that. It’s cute. The color of Sonya’s robe. She can’t decide if it’s red or very dark pink. She ends up giving a vague answer because she can’t actually focus long enough to think of Allie now.

    “That was a long time ago.”

    Yelena turns to look at her, and her lips tilt to a smile slowly. Kate has no idea why. She smiles back anyway. Yelena has such a pretty smile, especially when she is not making fun of her. Sometimes then too, she guesses. It’s impossible to not smile back at her. Sonya stands up from between them, and goes behind the couch, then back again to put a tube filled with blood into the IV line in Kate’s left arm that she doesn’t remember getting. She straightens up after and looks between the two of them.

    “You are adorable. Can I trust you two to not die until I change into something less naked?” Kate’s eyes drop to her robe, the exposed skin of her chest, her figure visible through the material, her long legs exposed from the middle of her thigh. She gives a lazy grin, and a thumbs up.

    “We promise to do our best.”

    She smiles at Kate’s answer and says something in Russian then, that makes Yelena laugh out loud, the sound light and airy, then leaves the room. Kate turns to look at her, and Yelena twists her head to the side to meet her eyes too. Her pupils are tiny and they are so green. “What did she say?”

    Yelena grins, her teeth digging into the corner of her mouth.

    “You do not want to know.”

    Kate grins back, shuffling a little closer, Yelena’s eyes drop to follow the movement before catching her gaze again.

    “I do. I don’t like being left out.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes a little, and turns to look back onto the ceiling again, grinning still. “She told us not to have sex on her couch and tear out our stiches.”

    Kate laughs out loud too, looking at Yelena’s profile. There is something about Yelena’s jawline that keeps slowing her breaths down but making her heart beat stronger against her chest. The last functioning reserves of her brain supply her with a memory of what Yelena said yesterday evening and she smirks.

    “Well, if you were too tired to yesterday, I don’t have to ask how you feel now.” Yelena lets out a surprised laugh, turning to look at her again. Her eyes are sparkling, and Kate could not turn her gaze away now, even if she tried. She feels like she is warm all over, an airiness to her chest that makes her head feel even more light, and the non-functioning parts of her brain make her open her mouth next.

    “I bet it would be amazing on this stuff though.”

    She means it as a joke, but Yelena’s smile slowly drops from her face and she is just looking at her. Kate thinks back to what she just said and she doesn’t think she wants to take it back. It would be amazing. If just touching Yelena’s shoulder felt as electrifying as it did, fucking would feel like entering goddamn Nirvana.

    Yelena blinks slowly, and her tongue peeks out of her mouth to wet her lips again, and Kate is powerless to resist the urge to look down on the movement. This time, she reaches out, her movements slow and only partially conscious, and puts her right hand on Yelena’s cheek, her thumb coming to rest under her bottom lip on her chin.

    The skin of Yelena’s cheek is smooth under her fingertips, and she closes her eyes as Kate drags her thumb across her upper lip, tracing the bow like shape of it. It’s just as soft as she imagined it was earlier, and when Yelena opens her eyes and her tongue darts out to lick ever so slightly at her finger, Kate almost moans. The sensation sends a powerful thrill down her spine, and her eyes lift to meet Yelena’s again.

    She traces her finger across her bottom lip next, and Yelena reaches up to grab her wrist and holds her gaze, eyes hooded as she leans her chin down slightly, to catch tip of Kate’s thumb between her lips. Kate feels the wetness of her mouth, Yelena’s tongue sliding against the pad of her finger, and she exhales sharply through her nose, her own tongue darting out to lick her lips. Her lips are soft and pliant against Kate’s skin, and the inside of her mouth feel so, so warm. Kate feels like she floating, and she leans closer, not quite sure what she will do. She thinks she wants to kiss Yelena.

    To feel that hot, wet tongue slide against her own, instead of just her skin. Her forehead falls against Yelena’s but she turns her head away slightly, exhaling through her nose.

    Kate’s gulps and lets out a breath through her parted lips too, her eyes sliding closed. Her thumb is still resting against Yelena’s slightly parted lips, and Kate feels fuzziness that has settled over her brain become even more heavy. Yelena holds her wrist in a tight grip, but doesn’t pull her hand away, or pull back.

    She thinks of the ship before that, and takes a deep, shuddering breath, willing herself not to cry.

    The rage she felt, the acidic hatred in her chest. It feels foreign now, and she feels guilt settle onto her chest like a building collapsing onto her. She bites the inside of her mouth, her hands still pushing against her eyes, trying to focus on her present.

    There is a blanket draped over her, and a pillow under her head. She doesn’t remember falling asleep so she must have passed out sometime. She is in a lot of pain, but even more than that, she feels like she is dying of thirst, her head practically pounding with it. Mustering up her strength, she pushes herself upright, leaning sideways against the back of the couch. She muffles another moan of pain as she shifts her weight, sliding her legs off of the sofa and onto the floor beneath her.

    She is not wearing socks, but she has sweatpants and a t-shirt on. Her shirt feels cool, and damp, and she realizes slowly that she must have sweat through it in her dream. Lucky jumps off of the couch after she moves, offended at the disturbance of his sleep, and jogs to the other side of the room behind her.

    She hears him paw at the slightly ajar door, and more brightness fills the room as it’s nudged open wider. She shuffles closer to the edge of the sofa, pushing the blanket off of her lap, and stands. Her legs feel weak, but relatively stable, even as she muffles a moan at the pain standing up brings.

    She glances back towards the room where the soft light is coming from, but her thirst wins out. She thinks she remembers where Thomas went to get the blood earlier, and hopes that it was the kitchen. She walks across the room, trying to keep quiet unconsciously and avoid any furniture in her way. She finds another hallway, with a doors and two open doorways. The first one opens into a dining room but she is proven to be right as she finds the kitchen behind the second one.

    She fumbles around in the dark, searching, reaching for a light switch, and when she finds it, she has to blink several times for her eyes to adjust to the sudden brightness, even though the lights are dim, only shining softly above the counter. The kitchen is similar to her own, with a big island in the middle with barstools to sit on, but the cupboards covering the walls around are white, instead of the natural wooden color of her own.

    Enters a few more steps into the room, she goes staight for the tap. She leans down to drink directly from the nozzle, no patience to look for glasses. The cool water feels amazing against her lips. She gulps it down eagerly, washing away the stuffy, sandy feeling in her mouth. “Hey”

    The word is said softly enough that she doesn’t jerk too much in her surprise, Yelena’s deep voice low and a bit hoarse in the kitchen. Kate twists around, and flinches at the quick movement.

    Yelena is leaning against the doorway, arms crossed, and if Kate couldn’t see the few cuts and bruises covering her skin, she wouldn’t be able to tell she had been injured at all. Her golden hair is in a braid over her shoulder, a few strands escaping it, and she wears shorts and a t-shirt that leaves her legs exposed to the warm, dim lights of the kitchen. “Hi. Um, sorry, I was really thirsty.”

    She quickly wipes her chin, and shuts off the water. Yelena just looks at her, and upon further inspection Kate notes that her face looks tired, her skin still a tad paler than usual. When Yelena doesn’t say anything, she speaks again.

    “Sorry if I woke you up.”

    Yelena’s lips twitch upwards at that, and she leans off of the wood of the doorway to enter the kitchen too.

    “It was your dog, actually.”

    Kate leans against the counter and watches as Yelena goes for one of the cupboards, opens it and pulls out a glass. When Yelena comes to the tap to fill it up, she moves out of the way and goes to grab one for herself.

    She fills up her glass too, and goes to lean against the island across Yelena, hoping to alleviate some of the pain from her side by resting her weight against it. Yelena drinks an entire glass of water before filling her again, turning to face Kate. She looks her over, then zeroes in on her side.

    “You are bleeding.”

    Putting her water on the counter, she walks over to stand in front of Kate. She pushes Kate’s arm aside to reach for the edge of her still damp shirt, lifting it up. Kate just lets it happen, putting her glass down. She leans on one hand on top of the counter, and lifts the other to cover her chest, stopping her t-shirt from rising too high.

    “Why are you wet?”

    She huffs, a chuckle not quite making it out of her throat.

    “Sorry. I’m a bit sweaty.”

    Yelena glances up at her, lips curling upwards, before she goes back to investigate Kate’s side. Yelena’s fingertips touch her ribs gently, and she does her best not to suck in a breath too abruptly.

    “That is gross.”

    Kate huffs again, but she can’t help the small smile sliding over her lips. Yelena looks and prods gently at her side a little longer before she lets the t-shirt fall back to its place. “You pulled your stiches a little, but they are not torn out.”

    She looks up at Kate, and she nods, clearing her throat.

    “How are you feeling?”

    She looks back at Yelena, but she just waves it off dismissively, smiling a little smugly. “I am fine, Kate Bishop. It takes more to take me down than a silly little stab wound.” Kate raises her eyebrows, her expression disbelieving. The “silly little stab wound” did nearly kill Yelena, and if it wasn’t for Sonya and Thomas, she isn’t sure she would be standing either. Kate rolls her eyes at her, before grabbing her glass of water again. “It was really stupid.”

    Yelena’s smile drops at that, her face morphing in offence as Kate takes a sip. “Excuse me?”

    “Hiding your “silly little stab wound”. It was stupid.”

    She makes air quotes with her hands, and from the expression Yelena makes, she’d think she accidentally called her something awful in Russian. Her jaw drops, and her brow furrows. “Well, what was I supposed to do? You were…”

    Kate sees the moment of hesitation. She doesn’t want to bring up what Kate did, the mental state she was in. It’s strangely considerate. Yelena licks the corner of her lips before continuing, slightly more composed.

    “…One of us had to keep her head cool.”

    Kate clenches her jaw, and looks down, then away. Yelena still stands a feet or so in front of her, waiting for her to gather her thoughts.

    “I’m sorry.”

    When she gets no answer, she turns to look back at Yelena. Her expression is serious now, but otherwise carefully blank, making it impossible for Kate to read.

    “For hurting you. I...”

    She clarifies, and sees Yelena open her mouth. She is ready for the rebuttal, along the lines of “that is hilarious Kate Bishop, you cannot hurt me”, so she cuts it off. “…Please, let me finish?”

    Yelena shuts her mouth, and Kate takes a deep breath, gathering her thoughts. It feels like she did so many stomach-turning things in the last 24 hours. This is the one she has a chance to make right.

    “I was an asshole, to you…To Spiderman too, but whatever, I don’t know him. But you…you have stood by my side through all of this, and I want you to know I really appreciate what you did for me…what you have been doing for me, actually…And anyway, what I am trying to say is, I’m sorry for lashing out at you, especially when you were…um...stabbed.” She finishes a bit lamely, and meets Yelena’s eyes again. She is just looking at Kate, her face still mostly serious, but her eyes are soft. Maybe it’s the dim lighting, or the late night, or the endless shitty day they had before, but she looks warmly at Kate, not a sliver of anger in the tired lines of her face.

    “You finished?”

    “Yeah.”

    “I talk now?”

    Kate can't help but smile a little, huffing another barely-there chuckle through her nose. “Sure.”

    She is looking into Kate’s eyes, and gives her a little, kind of sad smile. “I am not angry with you, Kate.”

    Kate looks away, and feels heavy again. She takes her glass from the counter to take a sip of her water, trying to rid her mouth of the ashen taste of it before she speaks. “You should be.”

    Yelena tilts her head at her, and purses her lips.

    “Well, I am not...But if it makes you feel better, I forgive you.”

    Kate exhales, and somehow, she feels just a little lighter, than she did before. Then, she immediately feels worse because of that. She doesn’t think she deserves to feel better. She furrows her brow, lowering her gaze again, and they are silent for a few moments. She doesn’t immediately look up at Yelena when she speaks again.

    “I was worried for you.”

    Kate shakes her head, her lips turning into a bittersweet smile.

    “Well, you clearly didn’t have to be. I seem to be very capable of killing a bunch of people to protect myself apparently.”

    She doesn’t look at Yelena, and bites the inside of her cheek again, even as she steps closer to Kate. Yelena gently takes her hand hanging by her side, fingers grabbing Kate’s and giving them a small squeeze.

    “That’s not what I meant. I know…”

    Her hesitation is what finally prompts Kate raise her eyes, but this time it’s Yelena not looking at her.

    “I know what it’s like to lash out, Kate. You know that.”

    Kate thinks she probably means Clint, and shakes her head.

    “It’s not the same. You went out of your way to not hurt me when you were after Clint.” “Only because it was easy...”

    Yelena finally meets her eyes, and there is something in her gaze, that Kate has trouble naming. Something like regret mixed with sadness.

    “…If it was harder, I’d have killed you, Maya Lopez, and your mother. Everyone who was in the way.”

    Kate huffs a humorless chuckle at that.

    “Is that supposed to make me feel better?”

    Yelena smiles again, and looks away.

    “No. I’m just trying to tell you, I know what it feels like. To just…want to hurt because you are hurting yourself.”

    Kate bites her lower lip and looks down on their loosely clasped hands, thinking. Yelena’s thumb gives hers a very slight stroke, and she speaks again.

    “I was worried because I know this is not something you had in your life before. And I...” She seems to have trouble finding the words, and Kate looks up at her again. “...I didn’t want you to do something you’ll regret.”

    Like I almost did something I would regret is unsaid, but she knows it’s implied. Kate gives a tired smile, raising up her eyebrows.

    “You were worried about my feelings?”

    Yelena rolls her eyes, and gives a small shrug.

    “You are a good person, Kate. Things like that…what you saw, what happened...it will make a soul like yours dim.”

    It doesn’t really make Kate feel better. She feels like she wants to cry, but it seems she has used up all the tears she had, and only the heavy tightness in her throat remains. “I don’t…I really don’t think you can call me a good person anymore.”

    This time Yelena gives her hand a more forceful squeeze and she doesn’t continue until Kate meets her eyes.

    “You are a survivor, Kate. There is nothing to be ashamed of that.”

    “What, it’s a good thing?”

    Yelena doesn’t hesitate or expand on it.

    “Yes.”

    Kate sighs, shaking her head, lips curling into another joyless smile.

    “I thought you said I was a good person.”

    “People can be more than one thing.”

    Kate looks away again, and Yelena sighs too. She seems to think before she speaks again. “You still idolize Clint Barton, yes?”

    Kate huffs, glancing up at Yelena.

    “I don’t idolize him…”

    “Yes, okay. But you like him.”

    “Yeah, I do.”

    She knows where Yelena is going with this, and it does finally make her feel a little bit better without it souring in her mouth.

    “You know the things he has done, yes?"

    She waits for Kate to nod.

    "Do you think he is a bad person?"

    Kate shakes her head. Clint is more complicated than she used to think, but she is firm in her belief that he is a hero nonetheless.

    “You see? If Clint Barton gets a pass, so do you.”

    Kate smiles, and drops her gaze again. That, she can maybe work with. She thinks it’s true for Yelena too. She has done terrible things in the past, and Kate doesn’t think she is a bad person either. She tries to empty her head of the thoughts of death and destruction, and takes a few calming breaths. She is not free of the guilt, and she kind of doesn’t think she ever will or should be either. But she feels a tad bit lighter, and she tries to focus on that. She is silent for a long time, before she nods and gives Yelena’s fingers a gentle squeeze too, meeting her eyes again.

    “Thank you.”

    “You are welcome.”

    Yelena just smiles smugly up at her, and Kate’s eyes drop to her lips for a millisecond, her mind flashing back to her finger running over Yelena’s lip, the sensation of her tongue against her skin. The mind-numbing, desperate want when she was going to take her to the bathroom to… She wonders for a second if Yelena remembers, but there is no awkwardness or hesitation on her face so Kate guesses she might not. She also decides it doesn’t matter. They were high as kites, and obviously, they are both young and attractive. It’s no surprise they would gravitate to each other with all their inhibitions removed and drugs making them horny. She shakes the thought off. It doesn’t matter right now.

    Yelena is an amazing friend, and she is thankful to have her in this moment, either way. Chapter End Notes Hi guys!

    Chapter 13

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes They hear footsteps a moment later, and Sonya speaks before she actually appears in the doorway, back in her silky robe and too much exposed skin combo.

    “It’s 4 in the morning. I will not re-stich anything and I will not hesitate to kill you if you get blood on my kitchen counter.”

    Kate chuckles at her grumbly voice, and Yelena grins at her as she appears. Sonya’s hair looks good disheveled, and there are pillow marks embedded onto her face. She takes in their stance, and huffs, holding the bridge of her nose.

    “You drag me out of bed in the middle of the night, and you are just holding hands?” Yelena gives her a smile that is way too cheeky for 4 in the morning, especially for someone who has been bleeding out barely over 12 hours ago.

    “We did not drag you out of bed. And we are not just holding hands.”

    Sonya is thoroughly unimpressed. She looks them over, then cocks an eyebrow. “Then what are you doing?”

    “We were thirsty.”

    Kate closes her eyes, sighing deeply at the phrasing and Sonya snorts.

    “Hmpf. I bet you were…Okay, go hold hands and be thirsty in your own room Yelena, I am trying to get my beauty sleep.”
