    With that, she is gone and Kate is too busy trying to not groan in embarrassment, so it takes a few seconds for Sonya’s words to sink in. When they do, her eyebrows shot up towards her hairline.

    Yelena’s what?

    “Wait…what does she mean your room?”

    Yelena grins, and slides away from her, her fingers slipping from Kate’s. She drinks a few more sips of water before she rinses her glass under the tap and puts it on the drier. She turns back and raises both of her arms to gesture vaguely around the room.

    “Welcome to my hotel, Kate Bishop. The host is pretty rude, but there are no bedbugs.” Kate is only surprised for a moment, before she lifts a hand to rub at her eyes, smiling. Of course. She should have figured this out earlier. Then again, she was pretty high for most of the time she spent in this apartment.

    “So you’ve been staying here, for like the whole last week?”

    Yelena gives her a smile above her shoulder, as she exits the kitchen.

    “Yup.”

    Kate follows her out, and across the living room to the door that was slightly cracked open earlier. She stops in the doorway, and takes it in.

    It’s obviously a guestroom, with very few personal items scattered around. Yelena’s two big suitcases are stacked on each other against the wall on the far side, and a few clothes are thrown over a chair next to a dresser. There is a full length mirror on Kate’s left side and she sees two photographs stuck to it.

    She glances at Yelena, who is sat on the bed now, her legs extended and leaning back against the headboard. Her hand is stroking Lucky’s head, who is curled up on it as well, and she is watching Kate, her expression once again hard to read.

    “Can I…?”

    Yelena hesitates. She glances over to the mirror as well, before licking her lips and nodding. Kate walks the few steps separating her from the mirror, and looks at the photos. The first one is a tattered and torn photo-booth picture set of two little girls and Kate leans closer to look at it. The younger girl is blonde, her small face stretched in a wide grin and making a funny expression on the other. The older one has blue hair, and she is laughing hard on both pictures. There is no mistaking who they are.

    Kate smiles sadly, eyes trailing over little Yelena’s face on the pictures. It was hard for her to imagine her as a kid before, Natasha even more so. But the girls on the picture look like regular kids, just having fun and being silly. It kind of makes her heart ache. The other picture is of adult Yelena, maybe a bit younger than she is now. It’s a selfie, and there is an older man and an older woman on each side of her. Yelena and the man are grinning at the camera, while the dark haired woman is smiling, eyes warm. “Are these your parents?”

    She asks without turning back, eyes glued to Yelena’s happy face, so light and open. “Yes.”

    Yelena doesn’t offer her any more than that, so she just keeps looking at the picture, at the fragment of Yelena’s life she doesn’t know. They don’t look like a Black Widow and a Super- Solider. They look like regular people, taking a pic with their adult daughter. Kate knows there is no genetic relation, but she can even see some resemblance between Yelena and her parents. She thinks it’d be stupid to point that out, so she doesn’t say it but she really thinks they look like a family. She could be jealous, but she can’t bring herself to feel that. Yelena’s easy smile and open happiness makes her wonder if the picture was taken before the Blip. Before Natasha died. Kate hasn’t seen her smile like that yet. Yelena has so much life in her, she is a 5’3” tall walking hurricane, but compared to that smile, it feels muted. She also wonders how Yelena’s parents took to losing Natasha. If they were so broken with grief as Yelena was when they first met. It feels a bit too intrusive to ask, especially in the dim lights of the late night.

    Kate glances back at the photobooth picture and hopes she doesn’t overstep when she speaks. “You were a cute kid.”

    There is no immediate answer, so she turns back to Yelena. She is still stroking Lucky’s head, but her eyes are on Kate. Her face is not closed off, but Kate finds it hard to name the emotion on it. She is not smiling but there is an affectionate curve to her lips, even though they are turned downwards.

    “It was taken a few weeks before we left Ohio.”

    Kate looks at her for a moment, waiting to see if she will say more but she doesn’t. She wants to step closer, and sit down on the bed but it feels presumptuous. Natasha is a topic that she only dares to discuss when Yelena brings her up herself, but she wants to know so much. She purses her lips, choosing her words carefully.

    “How long before…um…the Blip did you reconnect?”

    Yelena doesn’t look up at her.

    “Almost 2 years… But we only met twice after.”

    She pauses, and her tongue darts out to wet her lips before she continues. “I was supposed to move to New York with her after I finished freeing the Widows.” Kate does end up taking a step closer, but doesn’t move to sit. Her body aches and she longs to go back to sleep. If she sits down she is pretty sure will fall asleep here. “I’m sorry.”

    Yelena glances at her then, giving her a small smile, before looking back at Lucky but her eyes seem far away.

    “That’s okay, Kate.”

    Kate can’t help but compare her to the picture of her with her parents. “It’s not.”

    Yelena doesn’t smile but something in her face eases when she looks at Kate again. They look at each other for a quiet moment, and Kate gives her a small smile back, before she turns to leave the room.

    “Goodnight, Yelena.”

    She hears the answer as she passes the doorway, choosing not to close the door behind herself.

    “Goodnight”

    Kate gets back on the couch, and lies down. She hears Yelena turn her lamp off, and the rustling of the sheets. She thinks it’ll be a long time before she falls back asleep, but there is a heaviness to her eyelids as soon as she gets horizontal, and she is out in barely a minute.

    Kate wakes up next morning to Thomas rushing around in a suit. She blinks up at him, narrowing her eyes at the sunlight streaming into the room, and it takes her a few moments to place where she is again.

    Groaning, she tries to burrow under the blankets, turning towards the back of the couch. “Sorry Kate, didn’t mean to wake you up.”

    She inhales sharply, as her elbow pushes into her injured side, waking her further up. Her voice is still laden with sleep when she speaks.

    “What time is it?”

    There is a pause, Thomas probably checking the time.

    “Seven thirty. Oh shit, I’m late.”

    She hears steps from across the room, bare feet padding against the hardwood floor. “You forgot your coffee again.”

    Sonya sounds much more cheery than she did last night in the kitchen, and Kate hears telltale sounds of kisses being exchanged. Once, twice than clothes rustling. There is a deep groan from Thomas, and a hum from Sonya. Oh no.

    “Are you sure you can’t be late? We could finish what…”

    “I’m pretty sure Kate is awake.”

    Thomas’ voice is amused, if a little breathy and Kate feels her face heat up. She is thankful that she can’t see what’s happening. She is even more thankful, when Sonya chuckles, then answers in a whisper that is clearly loud enough for her to hear on purpose. “It’s not like her and Yelena really minded us yesterday.”

    Kate tries to calculate the possibility of the couch becoming sentient and swallowing her whole. It’s devastatingly low. She hears one more kiss, then the front door opening and closing. She hopes that Sonya will leave her be, but she seems to be out of luck on that front as well.

    “Good morning, Kate.”

    The voice comes from right next to the couch, and she contemplates pretending to sleep but ends up deciding to be an adult in the end, and pushes the blanket lower to reveal her face. Sonya stands above her, in leggings and a tight, sleeveless workout top. The smile on her face is genuine, but there is a playful glint to her eyes.

    “Morning.”

    “How are you feeling?”

    Kate snorts then flinches at the flash of pain that the quick exhale sends along her ribs. Her head is also pounding, and the rest of her is just generally achy.

    “I’ve been better.”

    It seems that is exactly what Sonya was waiting for, the grin that slides onto her face almost splits it in half.

    “Do you want some more morphine?.”

    Kate rolls her eyes, her voice dry as sandpaper.

    “Thanks. I’m good.”

    Sonya does not take the hint, and doubles down.

    “Are you sure? I can show your where Yelena’s bedroom is.”

    Kate’s eyebrows furrow, she is about to point out how much of a creep that makes her sound, when she hears a raspy voice from behind the couch.

    “She knows where my bedroom is….”

    The rest of the sentence is said in Russian, and Kate groans again.

    “You are doing it again! It’s rude…”

    Sonya purses her lips at her, but she doesn’t look offended.

    “Yelena told me to leave you alone…but I think she is just jealous I got to see you naked first.”

    Kate chokes on her saliva at Sonya’s stage whispered response, and tears run into her eyes at the pain in her side as she coughs.

    “Excuse me?”

    She forces it out after a few seconds, her throat and ribs still burning. Yelena is pointedly silent on the other side of the room. Sonya holds the teasing smile for a moment longer, before she rolls her eyes, waving in the air.

    “Well Kate Bishop. You passed out under the shower, after I specifically asked you not to. How do you think you ended up on the couch?”

    Kate stares blankly at her. She has a vague memory of being cold, but she does not remember the shower, and definitely does not remember being naked. She tries to think of a response, but Yelena cuts in before she can.

    There is a quiet, but intense argument in Russian, and for once she doesn’t wish to understand, just burrows back into the couch. She hears her and Thomas’ name multiple times, but she closes her eyes to block it out. Sonya still sounds amused, and unphased, but her tone shifts to serious after a few exchanged sentences. Yelena sounds agitated, and Sonya leaves the room after a minute or two.

    Kate sees Yelena come around the couch from the corner of her eyes, and groans a little as her legs are pushed to the side so Yelena can sit.

    “What was that about?”

    Yelena huffs and pulls the blanket away from her, leaning closer.

    “She shouldn’t have left you alone in the shower.”

    Kate raises an eyebrow, ignoring how it makes her face sting.

    “What, she should have showered with me?”

    Yelena gives her a glare, but the twist of her lips upwards betrays her. “Still a better option. Did you hit your head?”

    “I don’t know, I can’t remember most of it.”

    Yelena looks into her eyes for a second longer, before she reaches for Kate. Her hands are gentle as she touches her, one of them holding Kat’s chin, the other running over her hair, feeling for bumps. It kind of feels nice, if a little awkward. Kate tries to keep her eyes on the ceiling during the weird examination.

    She glances at Yelena when she is done. Taking in the bruises and cuts on her face, she tries to ignore the acidic guilt in her chest. Yelena reaches for her shirt and pulls it up, exposing Kate’s abs and ribs, but there is nothing but focus on her face. Stop it, she tells herself when her brain very helpfully reminds her of what they were (almost) doing on this couch last night. Yelena is surgically precise in her movements as she pulls the bandage away from Kate’s ribs, gently prodding around the wounds.

    Kate groans slightly when she gets a bit too close, but what makes her stomach do a tired flip is when Yelena’s thumb strokes along her side, almost in apology. It feels unconscious on Yelena’s side, not something she did on purpose, but it warms Kate up even more as a result. Yelena is still wearing the outfit from last night, the shorts leaving her legs exposed, a large expanse of creamy skin on display. Kate’s stomach offers a repeat performance of the earlier flip when she realizes Yelena is not wearing a bra. The oversized shirt falls over her chest, but there is no mistaking the two pointy tips standing out from the slope of its fall. She chooses to stare back at the ceiling, as Yelena prods around her injury a bit longer. Sonya comes back into the room and Kate swears she must have a sixth sense for arriving at these kind of moments. She gives them a smile, eyes jumping between the two of them with an amused glint, the earlier tension with Yelena forgotten already.

    “Okay, I’m off on my morning run. You girls play doctor, and I’ll bring back breakfast.” Kate ignores the comment, and sits up with a wince. It brings her closer to Yelena, and Kate’s shirt falls back down with her hand still underneath. Kate needs time to process all of this. Away from all of them.

    “Uh…Actually, thank you for letting me crash here yesterday. You were a life-saver. Like, literally. But I think I’m going to head home soon.”

    Sonya is visibly surprised, brows furrowing. She halts across from them, standing on the other side of the coffee table.

    “Why?”

    Kate blinks, glancing to the side and trying to ignore the weird feeling of Yelena retracting her hand from under her shirt.

    “Because that’s where I live?”

    Sonya looks so much like the tired mother of a teenager for a second, that Kate almost feels reprimanded. Almost.

    “Kate, you have been shot with a shotgun.”

    She shrugs, and offers a smile she hopes is convincing. Yelena is pointedly silent during this exchange.

    “Yeah, but if I’m just gonna sit around for a few days and heal up, I can do that at my own place. Plus, my work is up there.”

    Yelena speaks from beside her, eyes searching Kate’s features, her own impossible to read. “You still want to go after Wilson Fisk?”

    She blinks. Despite the traumatic fucking journey that was yesterday, it’s not like she can stop. Fisk will continue to come after her, and apparently after people she knows. She will need a couple of days to recoup but other than disappearing off of the face of the Earth, it’s not like she has a choice in this.

    “Of course.”

    Sonya turns to Yelena, shaking her head.

    “You were right. She is a stubborn idiot.”

    Hey! Yelena just chuckles, but it doesn’t sound mean. Kate is probably imagining things because when Yelena’s eye flits over to her again, the look is almost seems affectionate. “That she is.”

    Sonya shakes her head, and looks up towards the ceiling as if she is begging for patience from the heavens, exasperated with both of them. She mutters something in Russian, then switches back to English, picking up a set of keys.

    “Suit yourself, I guess. What about the pretty boy?”

    Kate is confused, and it probably shows on her face because Yelena grins next to her and offers her explanation.

    “She means Lucky.”

    Kate smiles. Her dog has the ability to steal the hearts of everyone around him. “Actually, if you could watch him for a couple of days, that’d be great. Thank you.” Sonya nods, pursing her lips. She goes to the medicine bag on one of the tables by the wall, and rummages around. She pulls out a plastic container, and walks over to the couch, putting it on the coffee table.

    “Take two a day, for 7 days, one in the morning, one in the evening. If you have a fever or too much pain, come downstairs.”

    Kate picks up the bottle, but there is no brand name or any other identifying mark on the bottle.

    “What is this?”

    After the morphine-incident, she is a bit wary of the pills Sonya supplies her with. Sonya’s lips twitch upwards, but she seems to be satisfied with a simple explanation, and no further references to the morphine-incident.

    “Antibiotics. So your injuries don’t get infected.”

    “Oh. Thanks.”

    It seems she spoke too soon, because Sonya’s Cheshire-cat grin is back in a heartbeat, and her eyes flit between Yelena and her.

    “No hard exercise until we take out the stiches. That includes sex.”

    Kate gapes at her, blindsided even though she probably shouldn’t be. Sonya chuckles, the motherly persona slipping away in a second. She winks at Kate, throws Yelena a kiss and walks out the apartment. Kate closes her eyes, and takes a deep breath. She can feel her face being hot, but Yelena speaks from beside her before she can compose herself. “She is teasing you because you react so funnily. If you ignore her, or own it she will stop.” Yelena’s tone is amused, and when Kate opens her eyes to look at her, her smile is too. Kate pouts and speaks without thinking, mind still preoccupied with Sonya’s teasing. “Easy for you to say, you don’t remember last night.”

    Yelena cocks an eyebrow, but her face continues to be entertained.

    “What do I not remember, Kate?”

    Oh for fucks sake. Kate really has to learn to just shut up sometimes. Why did she have to say that? She closes her eyes and leans back down on the couch.

    “Uh, nothing. We were just really high.”

    “I remember being high Kate, and that is not what you are embarrassed about…” Kate opens her eyes and sees the really intense look in Yelena’s eyes. She purses her lips and slides closer to Kate, who feels like she should move backwards, but can’t, the armrest of the sofa blocking her way.

    “You are embarrassed by what you did to me on this couch…”

    She leans closer to Kate, almost over her, her eyes flitting down to her lips. “…that you wanted to take me to the bathroom and ravage me…”

    Kate gulps, her brain short-circuiting. Is this really happening again? She is just looking at Yelena, her lips partially parted.

    “I…uh…”

    The intense look is gone in a second from Yelena’s face, as she leans back and grins, eyes full of mischief.

    “You see? You are way too easy to tease.”

    Kate groans, lifting her arm to cover part of her face.

    “Uhh…fuck off Yelena. I felt really bad.”

    She makes her tone light to take away the bite of the sentence, and thankfully Yelena just chuckles.

    “Ouch, Kate. Because you wanted to fuck the bloodthirsty vigilante?”

    Kate’s heart gives a painful thrum at the word fuck, but she ignores it in favor of pulling her arm from her face and giving Yelena a glare.

    “No. Because we were high as shit, and I was afraid I took advantage.”

    Yelena almost looks surprised, before she bursts out laughing, giving Kate a pat on the leg that kind of feels condescending. At least Kate feels assured that she didn’t do anything to make Yelena uncomfortable. She herself is definitely uncomfortable now though, really wishing to process the last 24 hours before she is forced to face what’s next. “Kate, you are too funny.”

    Kate exhales through her nose, slightly annoyed but also glad that the issue has been addressed. She decides to tease back, as a distraction from the uncertainty in her chest, despite the burning tips of her ears.

    “So just to be clear, you wanted me to?”

    If she was hoping to embarrass Yelena, she fails miserably. She is absolutely unphased as she gives Kate a playful once over, and a coy smile.

    “Of course I wanted you to. Morphine makes you want to fuck, regardless of who you are with.”

    Okay. Kate didn’t think the incident was serious, but it’s good to hear that Yelena doesn’t think she was a creep and have confirmation that they are on the same page. Yelena’s phone rings in her room and she gets off the couch to go answer it. Kate lets out an exhale, and tries to calm down. She really needs some alone time to get her head back in order. The last 2 days were…intense, and she needs to consider her steps forward. She sits up with another stifled groan, and swings her legs off of the sofa. Lucky comes bounding to her from Yelena’s room, and she pats his head affectionately. “Good morning buddy, how did you sleep?”

    Her answer is his tail thumping rhythmically against the leg of the coffee table, and two licks against her palm. He pushes his head into her hand after, demanding pats and she smiles, leaning down to kiss his forehead. She thinks she should send him to Clint’s, until this is all cleared up. He already almost got hurt the other night and she has to push away the image of his blood matted fur from her dream.

    She thinks as she continues to stroke his fur, the heavy feeling from yesterday sneaking into her chest again. Actually, it’s probably best if she keeps everyone away from herself, for now. She can’t risk someone getting hurt because of her. Annie is already collateral damage, and Yelena was almost too. She remembers the blood soaking Yelena’s side, her pale, clammy face down in the garage. Her and her parents’ face from the photo in Yelena’s room in contrast with her beautiful, lifeless face from her dream too. Yeah, Kate will have to send her back to Ohio too. It’s going to suck, doing this alone, but she will not have Yelena’s blood on her hands.

    She takes a deep breath, steeling herself.

    Standing up, she is thankful to note that while the pain is pretty bad, she doesn’t have too much trouble moving and her legs are steady. She pockets the antibiotics Sonya left for her, and she goes to the bathroom to see if her clothes from yesterday are there. They are not, but she finds her backpack, and takes the opportunity to wash her face while she is there. She winces as she looks into the mirror, her face littered with bruises and cuts, one side slightly swollen. She took a beating yesterday, and definitely looks the part. She ties up her hair with hair-tie she finds on the counter, and lifts her shirt to look at the injury on her side. Several small wounds are stitched closed over her ribs and the side of her stomach, the area around it an angry purple color. There is also some dried blood around the stiches, probably from pulling on them during her nightmare. She reminds herself to clean and bandage it again when she gets upstairs. She thinks of Clint, about how to explain this to him in a way that won’t make him come running. Picking up her backpack, she leaves the room, just as Yelena emerges from her bedroom.

    “This was Wendy. We are meeting them in Central Park at noon.”

    Kate blinks, a bit confused as she is still preoccupied with her thoughts. Yelena seems to pick up on it again, and explains.

    “They want to say thanks, and give back your phone.”

    Ah, she forgot about the phone, again. Nodding, she takes a deep breath, trying to figure out how to phrase what she has to say.

    “Okay, thanks…um…afterwards? I think you should go back to Ohio.”

    Yelena looks at her equally confused, eyebrows shooting up towards her hairline. “What are you talking about?”

    “Um, after we get the phone. You should go back home, to Ohio. Or heal up and then…” Yelena’s face morphs into annoyed surprise.

    “What?”

    Kate puts the backpack on the couch, and leans her weight against it.

    “Listen, I really appreciate what you did for me in the last week or so. It’s been…” Yelena cuts her off, and she looks absolutely unimpressed.

    “Is this because we almost had sex? We are adults, Kate…”

    Kate shakes her head, looking away before pinning Yelena with a glare.

    “It’s because you almost died, Yelena.”

    Yelena looks absolutely shocked and confused so Kate barrels on.

    “Look, this is my mess. You helped an incredible amount already and I am so grateful. I really am. But I will not have you die because of me. I will handle this, and…” Yelena seems to have gathered herself but she looks at Kate with wide, shocked and pissed eyes still, shaking her head.

    “Kate Bishop, you are such an idiot.”

    Kate smiles, and shakes her head again.

    “Well, yeah, probably. But I won’t be an idiot who gets her friends killed.” Yelena clenches her jaw, and steps closer. She seems to take a calming breath, exhaling long through her nose.

    “I am a Black Widow, Kate. I have survived worse things, and I have done much worse myself. I…”

    Kate shakes her head and steps even closer to Yelena. This time it’s her who attempts to take Yelena’s widely gesticulating hand, but she pulls it out of her hold immediately. Kate’s hand drops to her side but at least Yelena shuts her mouth, and looks up at her, the corners of her lips turned firmly downwards. She seems almost offended as she looks up at Kate, and she can’t help but smile at that.

    “You know I am not doubting that. I am well aware of what you are capable of. But you are human, Yelena…”

    Kate thinks of the pictures on Yelena’s mirror, her little girl self and the open, beautiful smile on the one with her parents, and hardens herself.

    “I just... I need to do this on my own, and I need you to let me. We can work together again when it’s not so…”

    Yelena seems to have lost her patience, and she shakes her head, her jaw clenched. “God, you are so stupid. You are aware that you would have died like 5 times yesterday if I was not there, yes?”

    Kate lets the insults roll off of her, and she looks back at Yelena’s angry face, serious. “Yeah, maybe. But you would have too. You almost did. So please…”

    “No.”

    Yelena is deadly serious. Her face is set in stone again, but her eyes are pure fire. “What do you mean, no?”

    Yelena lifts her chin, and if Kate wasn’t so focused on getting her to leave, she’d probably get distracted by how close they are to each other.

    “I mean, no. Last time I checked you were not the boss of me, so I stay where I want.” Kate rolls her eyes, setting her own jaw too.

    “Look, whatever you think you owe me, you paid that like five times over. So, there you go.” Yelena huffs, and rolls her eyes as she turns away.

    “This is very stupid, even for you. I will have a shower, and I meet you upstairs.” She walks to the bathroom, and slams the door behind her. Kate shakes her head, annoyed too. It’s not like Yelena can force her to accept her help. She will just convince her later. She picks up her backpack again, and her quiver and bow left by the door. She gives Pizza Dog a few pats on the head, before walking to the front door. He follows her there, and whines when she pushes him back, telling him to stay.

    “Bye Lucky. I’ll be back for you in a few days.”

    She closes the door behind herself, taking a deep breath. She walks to the elevator, and takes it up to her floor. Thankfully, she finds her keys in the front pocket of the bag, and enters the apartment, depositing the bag and the bow and arrows on the table by the entrance. It seems weirdly empty without Lucky or even Yelena there, but it’s nice to be home. Checking the time on her tablet, she notes that she has about three hours until she has to meet Wendy and Annie at the park. Her body feels hurt all over, but she is also weirdly wired from her argument with Yelena and probably from the last two days in general. She needs to clear her head. Then she needs to call Clint and let him know how things are going, hopefully convince him to stay at home as well.

    She takes a quick shower, carefully avoiding getting her stiches wet. She washes her hair, ignoring how the water is a bit tinged with copper, and lathers it heavily with shampoo and conditioner.

    When she gets out from under the spray, she wipes the steam off of the mirror, and winces at her face again. She’ll need to apply some make-up to her face, if she doesn’t want everybody staring at her. Walking to her bedroom in a towel, she puts on fresh underwear and a sports bra that is not too restrictive against her injured ribs, then goes back to the bathroom to bandage and wrap them again.

    She applies some concealer onto her face, trying to avoid it getting into any of the cuts directly, then goes back to her bedroom to finish getting dressed. She puts on some loose jeans, with an oversized white t-shirt, and picks up a big pair of sunglasses that’ll hopefully hide most of her face. Picking up another baseball hat, she puts it on her head and hopes it’ll help cover her up too.

    In the living room, she pockets her keys, the sword and picks up a new quiver of arrows from her secret room, putting it over her shoulder with a wince. She really hopes she doesn’t have to use any of it today.

    Locking the front door behind herself, she goes to the elevator and takes it down to the garage. She picks up the keys for the Range Rover, choosing it for its fully tinted windows and comfortable seats. The engine turns on with a comfortable hum, and she pulls out of the spot, driving around the white Maserati still parked askew.

    She doesn’t need the GPS, because she knows where she is going this time. She just needs to drive, think, and talk to her Dad.

    She doesn’t turn on any music or the radio, content to ruminate in silence. Thinking back to the day before, she lets the memories wash over her, but doesn’t let them overwhelm her this time. The harbor was horrifying, but it was a wake up call she needed. She knew this was serious, obviously, but now she knows what she is up against, what Fisk is truly capable of. The faces of the people lying in the container flit into her mind, and she grips the wheel a bit harder. She doesn’t need the fury that took over her yesterday, but she thinks she does need that imige as a reminder. She spends the next few minutes etching the image into her memory. If she fails, this will happen to everyone she cares about. She feels guilty about many things. She doesn’t like killing or the cruelty that she displayed with the super soldier. But, if it’s a choice between making this right, and protecting the people she cares about, she knows she will have to push all of that aside.

    She takes a deep breath, pursing her lips, driving mostly on autopilot. She will have to push everything else aside too, she thinks. Until Fisk is behind bars, or dead, she will need to stay alone and make sure nobody else is caught in the crossfire. She nods to herself, as she enters the cemetery, driving along the road she knows will lead her where she wants to go. She gets out of the car when she gets to the part of the familiar part of the cemetery, electing to leave her gear in the car. She really hopes nobody will bother her here, as she makes the last few dozen feet on foot. She arrives to her Dad’s grave in a few minutes, and feels something inside of her settle.

    “Hi, Dad.”

    Her eyes trace the letters on the stone, Derek Bishop written in an elegant font that her mother chose. She thinks about her last conversation with her Dad.

    “What would you do, in a hurricane?”

    “I’d do, what I always do. Protect you.”

    She wonders if he would be proud or horrified of her. The fact that she is not sure of the answer settles onto her chest like one of those thousand-pound containers from yesterday. She is doing what she is doing to protect the people she cares about, or even ones she doesn’t know. But she is still killing, hurting people, isn’t she? Maybe she is more of her mothers’ daughter than she thought. The thought leaves a bitter taste in her mouth. Her mother committed a lot of crimes in the name of protecting their family. Is Kate really different? She recalls Yelena’s words from yesterday. Clint did a lot of fucked up things, but somehow she thinks there is a difference between him and her mother. Clint saved the world several times, while her mom got rich by working with mobsters. She hopes to fall on his side of the line, and really longs to call him in this moment. She really wishes she could talk to her Dad too, even if he was disappointed in her. To ask him, whether going after Fisk, whatever it took, was the right call.

    “This life you want to live. To really help people. It comes with a lot of sacrifices. And some things you'll lose forever."

    Clint’s words echo in her head. It will take everything, Kate thinks. She killed multiple people on this crusade already, and she doesn’t imagine she will be able to avoid doing that again before it’s over. But does she really have a choice?

    She doesn’t know if her Dad would even recognize her, but she lifts her chin, clenching her jaw. She will have to forge herself into steel, leave her naivety behind, if she is going to do this.

    She asked for a bow in this exact spot, all those years ago. She thinks it’s kind of poetic, with a bittersweet smile. She will do exactly what she wanted, even if she didn’t know what it meant back then. She will protect her friends, her mom and she needs to be the strongest version of herself, no restrictions holding her back.

    She becomes aware of someone walking up behind her, and her mind immediately drops her musings. One day. She just wants one day. She slowly inches towards the sword in her pocket, but her movements are halted by a voice speaking up behind her. “None of us really know our fathers.”

    Kate holds onto the handle of the sword but doesn’t make any further movements. “Excuse me?”

    The person steps up next to her, and she turns to take her in. It’s a middle aged woman, quite a bit shorter than her, wearing an expensive looking blouse and a skirt, with a purple streak in her hair.

    “I mean, even those of us who didn’t lose them as young as you did. None of us know our fathers well.”

    If it weren’t for the casual mention of her knowledge of Kate losing her father, she’d think this woman is a random crazy person. She smiles smugly at Kate like this is a perfectly normal conversation to have, and she raises an eyebrow, really not in the mood for whatever this is.

    “Can I help you?”

    The woman’s smile widens, and her hoop earrings glint in the early morning sun as she moves her head.

    “I sure hope so! You put on quite a show in the last couple of days, Miss Bishop.” Kate sighs, letting go of the handle of the sword in her pocket, and turning more fully towards the older woman.

    “Are you a reporter?”

    The woman laughs as if it was the joke of the century, before looking Kate over with an amused glance.

    “Quite the contrary Miss Bishop. I do not expose secrets, I keep them.” Kate continues to look at her, unimpressed. She really wishes this woman got to the point quickly, and then left her alone.

    “Cool. And this affects me how, exactly?”

    The woman digs into her bag and pulls out a tablet.

    “Thank you for asking. It’s no secret for the people in the right circles, that you are going up against Wilson Fisk. You hit one of his bases yesterday and pretty much publicly fought his people the day before.”

    She unlocks the tablet, and pulls up a video, pressing play. It’s security footage from the harbor from yesterday, showing Kate and Yelena arriving to the scene, and having a conversation with Spider-Man. The footage cuts out, and the next clip is of them having a conversation by the car, Kate pulling out her weapons. The video skips again, and the last one is of her and Yelena stumbling back towards the car again, leaning on each other, covered in blood.

    Their faces and the license plate number of the car are clearly visible throughout, and Kate’s heart beats hard in her chest. This is bad.

    She looks up at the older woman, trying to read her calculated smile but comes up short. There is absolutely no mistaking who the people are in the footage. Is this woman some kind of law-enforcement officer? Why is she not arresting Kate then? Maybe…

    “Is this…Do you want money?”

    The woman chuckles again, and puts a hand on her arm, and Kate notes distractedly that it’s weird that she is wearing gloves in this heat.

    “I am not trying to blackmail you, Kate. In fact, I had this footage erased from the city’s servers before the FBI could get to them. The only copy is this one.”

    She taps twice on the tablet, and the video is erased.

    “There, all gone. It’ll be our little secret.

    Kate looks at her, confused and trying to think. She glances around them, and shifts her weight from one foot to the other.

    “Why?”

    The woman is still smiling, and it’s honestly starting to unnerve Kate. “Well, some of those people in those right circles… The smarter bunch, if you ask me….Well, they want to bet on the winning horse.”

    Kate blinks. Something is definitely not adding up here. Who are these people in these circles. Who is this woman. How do they know about her, and what do they know exactly. “You want to..help me?”

    The woman nods, her face still appearing friendly, but Kate has spent enough time in high- society New York to know it’s fake.

    “Yes. We do. In exchange we only ask for one small favor.”

    There it is. She crosses her arms, and straightens her spine, trying to tower over the smaller woman.

    “And that small favor is?”

    The woman’s eyes flash, and yes. This is definitely something fishy.

    “Mr. Fisk started developing something with your mother during their time together. It’s something we have a lot of interest in, and our sources tell us Mr. Fisk is close to completing it now. We only ask that if you get your hands on it, you deliver it to us.” If her mom created with Fisk, there is no way she is delivering it to some shady character’s hands, whether or not they did her a favor by erasing footage of her practically going on a killing spree. She opens her mouth, ready to rebuff this woman’s words. “No...”

    But it’s not her that speaks, nor is it the older woman. Yelena arrives to stand between Kate and the older woman, her movements quiet like a cat’s as always, wearing a pair of big sunglasses, her hair down.

    “…she is not working for you, Valentina.”

    Kate’s mind is reeling, again. How did Yelena find her? How does she know this woman? “Yelena! Nice of you to finally join us.”

    Yelena snorts, and smiles as if they are old acquaintances, but Kate can tell that it isn’t an honest expression. Yelena’s eyes are sharp, and Kate feels her back straighten even more. Thus woman, Valentina apparently, is someone Yelena is wary of and it definitely means she should be too.

    “As if you didn’t wait until she was alone to try to talk to her.”

    Valentina just chuckles, clasping her hands in front of herself.

    “Well, we parted on such ugly terms. A shame, really. I didn’t want to upset you any further…Especially when I heard you put a gag order on all the other Widows, forbidding them from touching her.”

    Yelena did what? Apparently her face must betray her surprise because Valentina chuckles at her, while Yelena stares, unflinching.

    “Oh that’s right, Kate. You have a very useful friend in Yelena…”

    She glances at the both of them, standing next to each other and with the way she is looking, Kate has to fight the urge to step in front of Yelena. She doesn’t care what this woman is insinuating, and she is losing her patience with this conversation, fast. “…Honestly, the switch to corporate spying makes so much more sense now, Yelena. But I have to say I’m surprised. I never took you as the type to settle down.” Yelena rolls her eyes, still looking unphased but Kate can tell her stance is more rigid than usual. She definitely doesn’t like the insinuation either, or maybe the whole situation itself. “And I never took you as the type to hire little girls with bows and arrows. Are your employers really that desperate since I don’t work for you anymore?”

    Kate should be offended but she is too preoccupied for it to register. Is this woman Yelena’s former boss? From her assassin days? Valentina looks Kate over like she is a piece of nice, juicy steak, waiting to be devoured. It makes her extremely uncomfortable. “Oh, but she is so much more than that, isn’t she? The carnage the two of you left behind yesterday…it was truly inspired. I have seen your work, Yelena, and this was something else. You and Kate over here make quite a pair.”

    Kate wants to hit this woman, and it must be all over her face because Yelena puts a hand on her arm before she can move an inch. Valentina glances at the contact and grins. “Anyways, that’s not why I am here. I am not trying to recruit your baby-Hawk.” Kate inhales sharply at the annoying nickname, and ready to tell this woman to fuck off but Yelena speaks first, apparently done with the pretense of niceties, and her face is stone-cold. “What do you want then?”

    Valentina is unphased, and explains again as if they are merely discussing the weather. “Kate’s mother and Fisk were working on something before she was arrested. I’m told he is close to finishing it. All I ask, is that if you happen to find it, you give it to us.” Kate re-joins the conversation, her own voice impatient and full of disdain. She is once again treated as a child, and she does not like it one bit.

    “And what is this mysterious thing my mother and Fisk were working on?” She flexes the muscles in her crossed arms, an outlet for her frustration, but Valentina only glances at them with a smile that feels mocking.

    “I’m told it’s a chemical formula, for a drug.”

    That doesn’t make any sense for Kate. Her mother ran a security company, not a pharmaceutical one. Then again, she also worked with mobsters, so maybe drug-dealing is not that far of a reach. Yelena seems to think along the same lines.

    “What kind of drug?”

    Valentina shrugs, not a muscle twitching from the smile still on her face. “That is above my paygrade, I’m afraid.”

    Kate is pretty sure that’s untrue and Yelena seems to agree.

    “Ha! Bullshit.”

    She flips her hair from her eyes, and looks at Valentina, who continues to be unintimated by the two of them.

    “You know I only deliver information I get, Yelena.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes again, but doesn’t comment on it.

    “Okay, who wants it then?”

    Valentina chuckles again, and Kate thinks it’s becoming one of Kate’s least favorite sounds in the universe.

    “You know I can’t tell you that.”

    Yelena just shrugs, her face unbothered again, as she lifts her chin.

    “Okay, I will just find out on my own anyway.”

    Valentina rolls her eyes and looks at Kate as if this was a joke they were sharing. She looks back at her, jaw set and eyes hard.

    “Ah, always so headstrong. Fine! As a professional courtesy, for old times’ sake, I’ll tell you. It’s a lovely gentleman from Colombia. I think you know him actually, his name is Javier Rojas.”

    The name doesn’t mean anything to Kate but from the way Yelena tenses up completely, it’s definitely not good news. She masks her reaction quick, but Valentina grins like a shark smelling blood.

    “Mr. Rojas has expressed explicit interest in Kate...” Valentina chuckles. “I mean, in helping her out.”

    Kate thinks she is being threatened, not even that thinly-veiled, and her muscles tense again. Yelena lifts her chin, regarding Valentina silently for a few moments before she speaks. “Okay. Deliver my message to Javier Rojas. I will get him the formula for this drug, but only, and I mean it, only if he leaves Kate alone.”

    Kate’s eyes widen, and she turns to Yelena, bewildered.

    “What? Yelena no!”

    Yelena ignores her, and Valentina smirks. Kate briefly wonders if this was her plan all along. “Do we have a deal?”

    Valentina looks smug, and Kate is ready to throw punches for real now.

    “That we do. It’s a pleasure doing business doing with you, as always.” She receives an eyeroll in return from Yelena.

    “I mean it. He doesn’t approach, he doesn’t message, he leaves us alone.” Kate grabs Yelena’s arm, and she is definitely louder than normal. Valentina just looks on, amused.

    “Hello? There is no way this is happening. Like hell fucking no. We are not giving the formula to this dude, and you are definitely not making a deal with him.” She is ignored again, Yelena just looking at Valentina expectantly. She grins, and nods, putting the tablet back in her bag.

    “I can’t make any promises, but I’ll relay your message to him.”

    Valentina gives them one more playful once over, before chuckling to herself. “Yelena, Baby-Hawk.”

    She walks away, the conversation apparently finished. Kate looks after her, before twisting back to Yelena.

    “What the fuck, Yelena?”

    Yelena doesn’t look amused either. She grabs Kate’s arm and starts pulling her back towards her own car, but she wrenches it out of her hold, stopping.

    “No! What the fuck? Why did you do that? Who is that dude? Why did…”

    Yelena finally looks at her, very annoyed, and grabs her again.

    “Kate, this is not the place to have this conversation. Come on.”

    She pulls her arm out of Yelena’s hold again, but follows her to her car. Getting into the drivers’ seat, she doesn’t start the engine, just waiting for Yelena to get in and start explaining.

    Yelena slides into the passenger seat, and takes off her sunglasses, glancing around. “We should go.”

    “No. Tell me what just happened.”

    Yelena huffs, and glances at her like this is her fault. She takes a deep breath, and throws her sunglasses in the cup-holder between their seats, but her voice is cool when she speaks. “Javier Rojas is the head of the Rojas family, one of the biggest cartels in Colombia. You don’t want him on your back.”

    None of that makes Kate any less angry. She needs to convince Yelena to go back to Ohio, not get more involved in this, especially not with a fucking Colombian cartel. “That’s…and you do? Why did you do that? What did you even agree to?”

    “No. But I can handle him.”

    She is twisted towards Yelena in her seat, and the fact that she is not even looking at Kate is making her even more annoyed.

    “And I can’t? Because I am a little girl with bows and arrows.”

    Yelena is just as on edge as she is, rolling her eyes and her tone dripping with condescension. “Let’s just focus on one mob boss wanting your head at a time, yes?”

    Kate angrily punches the button that starts up the car, and drives them down on the road leading out of the cemetery.

    “I meant what I said. You should go back to Ohio and let me deal with this. It has nothing to do with you.”

    Yelena is looking at her from her seat now, and Kate raises her chin, staring ahead. Yelena scoffs, and Kate has the childish urge to scoff back, but swallows it down. “Stop this heroic bullshit. It is not cool.”

    Kate grits her teeth, and throws her an angry glance.

    “I am not trying to be cool. I am being realistic. Fisk wants me, nobody else has to get hurt.” Yelena huffs an unamused chuckle, shaking her head.

    “You will not get hurt Kate, you will die. Probably in like a day. Maybe two, if you are lucky.”

    Kate scowls, her tone dripping with sarcasm.

    “Wow, Yelena. Your trust in my abilities is truly touching, thanks.”

    Yelena is just as annoyed as she is but she takes a deep breath, collecting herself. “It is not about my trust in your abilities Kate. I told you I think you are a survivor, and I meant that. But nobody can do this alone.”

    Kate scoffs this time, throwing her a dirty glare.

    “Nobody but you, apparently.”

    “That’s different.”

    Yelena’s voice is calmer now, but Kate doesn’t share that feeling. She is ready to blow up. “How is it any different? You are just as human as I am. You bleed when you are stabbed, and you…

    “Yes Kate, I may bleed but I have been doing this for about 20 years longer than you. And so have others, and they have died anyway.”

    There is an edge to her voice that makes Kate swallow the barb she was going throw back at Yelena. The end of the sentence sounds heavier, and she turns to look at her. Her mouth is turned firmly downwards, and she looks annoyed mostly, but there is definitely a glint in her eyes when she glances at Kate before she looks out the window. It makes Kate deflate. She has a distinct sense that they are talking about Natasha, without saying her name. She takes a deep breath to calm down herself, and really tries to convey what she means. “That’s exactly my point, Yelena. Clint, you, even people who are trained are not safe around me now. And I…You got hurt yesterday, you almost died, and I…I hurt you myself too. I can’t…I don’t want anyone to die because of me, and I don’t want to find out what I’ll do if anyone does.”

    She looks at Yelena as they stop at a red light, before turning back to the road again. They are silent for a few moments, before Yelena speaks again, her voice calmer this time. “You said we were friends, yes?”

    “Yeah…We are. Right?”

    Yelena ignores her question, pursing her lips.

    “If I was in trouble, would you leave me alone?”

    “No, but...”

    “Then how can you ask me this?”

    She sounds legitimately hurt, her voice inching higher and louder.

    “I…”

    “No, Kate. How can you ask me this? To just leave, and then find out from the news that you have died.”

    Okay, that definitely sounds weirdly specific and Kate suspects it’s Natasha related again. She doesn’t know how to answer this without actually addressing the whole issue. She tries to keep her voice even, and chose her words carefully.

    “Is this about Natasha?”

    Yelena looks at her, gulping before she looks out the window again, not answering. “If it is, it’s different. She went to fight on another planet..”

    Yelena cuts her off, her lips curling with disdain and the look she gives Kate makes her swallow the rest of the sentence.

    “No it’s not. You are the same kind of self-sacrificing idiot as she was, and you will get yourself killed because of it.”

    Kate looks at her but Yelena turns away from her, staring out the windshield, arms crossed. The air in the car is thick with tension, and Kate wets her lips, taking a few moments to collect her thoughts.

    “Look Yelena, I am not planning on dying anytime soon, okay? Yesterday was…it took me by surprise. But I will do whatever it takes to see this through. I understand the risks, and I am willing to do what I have to…But I can’t do that if I’m worried someone I care about will be hurt…And I don’t need you to babysit me while I do this.”

    Kate keeps her eyes on the road, but Yelena turns and looks at her for a long time. She glances over to gauge her reaction, and sees that her features are softer now, the hard, angry lines of her face smoothed over.

    “I am not trying to babysit you, Kate. I know you are very capable. But Barton is right, this is very serious, and nobody could do this alone. You don’t have to either.” Kate opens her mouth to argue more, but Yelena continues, her voice growing lighter. “So you either take my help, or I knock you out and take you to Ohio in my trunk. It’s your choice.”

    Kate huffs out a laugh despite herself and just like that, she lost the battle. Chapter End Notes I am so sorry for the long wait guys! I had a crazy busy week, my girlfriend's surprise birthday party on Saturday (tequila induced hungover on Sunday), and in the little time I had to write, I started a oneshot set in Multiverse of Madness from Kate's perspective. I am about halfway through with that, and I'll post it sometime in the next week (?? no promises on that one), but I'll try to focus on this fic so the next update doesn't take such a long time.

    In other news, I came out to my girlfriend about my latent fanfic writing tendencies :D So you can now yell at me about this fic on twitter all you want.

    So! Regarding this chapter. It was a bit hard, because we had a lot of things to cover, from Kate's mental state to what almost happened between her and Yelena, while attempting to advance the plot as well :D I hope you like it.

    I think a lot of people paint Yelena as this really emotionally distant person, but both in BW and Hawkeye, she had no problem expressing her pain. Kate wanting to push her away, and go at it alone is probably pushing a lot of hurtful buttons from the past. I personally think she has more trouble expressing "care", we have only seen her say she loved Natasha after she died, but as she has said to Kate, we are definied by what we do, not by nice words. :D As for Kate: She told Clint to go home to his family when she learnt her mom has been involved with the mob, and she has been wildly independent ever since her Dad died. It makes sense in my head for her to want to push people away to protect them, even though we all know it's BS. I do think dealing with not only putting herself in danger, but others as well is something that she'd have a lot of trouble dealing with. Also, Javier Rojas is not a Marvel character, he's someone I came up with. We will learn more about him later on, but he is definitely not good news :D Hopefully I'll have the next chapter for you guys by the second half of the week (Thursday-Friday-ish)!

    xx

    Chapter 14

    Chapter Notes Hi guys!

    I thought long and hard about whether it is appropriate to post a chapter today, but in the end I decided that maybe people need something to distract them from the things that are happening in the world (in Ukraine). I know I do.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes “So you either take my help, or I knock you out and take you to Ohio in my trunk. It’s your choice.”

    Kate huffs out a laugh despite herself and just like that, she lost the battle. She drives in silence for a few minutes, contemplating arguing more, but Yelena seems pretty convinced and it’s not like she can knock her out and send her back to Ohio. She is not completely on board with Yelena staying, but she concedes the fight, for now. Rolling her eyes, she exhales. “Fine. You can stay. But if you get hurt one more time, you have to promise to go home, and let me do this alone.”

    Yelena lifts an eyebrow, her voice condescending.

    “As I said before, Kate, you are not the boss of me…Besides, I am way too talented than that.”

    Kate gives her an unimpressed look.

    “You got stabbed. And you’d have been shot by a shotgun if I didn’t save your ass.” Yelena returns her look, pointedly dropping her eyes to Kate’s side.

    “You did get shot by the shotgun. And I saved your ass, like 10 times yesterday.” Kate bites the inside of her mouth, still annoyed, looking back on the road. “It was 5 times earlier.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes, looking away again too.

    “I was being generous.”

    Kate shakes her head, trying to clear it and just stares ahead.

    “How did you even find me anyway?”

    She is pretty sure she wasn’t followed on the way here.

    “I put a tracker on your house keys.”

    Kate huffs. Of course she fucking did.

    There is a weird energy in the car, the tension lessened, but not completely resolved. Where the silence has been comfortable in the last few days, it feels heavy now. Kate feels like she should pick a fight or something so they can let it out, but they have reached a tentative truce now and she is reluctant to upset that. She chooses to focus on the conversation they had in the cemetery. Clearing her throat, she speaks again.

    “So…who the hell is Valentina?”

    Yelena purses her lips, and flips a strand of her hair away from falling over her face. “She works for an organization. She used to give my assignments.”

    Kate nods, having drawn that conclusion from the conversation.

    “Who are they?”

    Yelena clears her throat, and Kate glances over at her. She looks hesitant, sighing deeply before she answers.

    “I…never managed to find out its name. I tried, after they sent me to kill Barton, but in the end, I decided it was not worth dying over.”

    Kate chews on the inside of her lower lip, checking the side mirror, contemplating. “What do you think they want?”

    Yelena seems to mull it over, silent for a few moments too.

    “They are always in search for…talented people. But you do not fit the profile of their usual employees.”

    Kate thinks back to Yelena’s comment about little girls with bows and arrows, her annoyance flaring up again. She lifts her chin, giving Yelena a challenging look over the center console. “Too weak?”

    Yelena gives her a side glance so unimpressed, she might as well called her an idiot again. “Too nice.”

    Kate wants to bristle at that, but Yelena continues.

    “They usually work with people who have no issue doing bad things to achieve an objective. I think…The Colombians wanted to get into New York for years. Javier Rojas probably wants to use you to take Fisk out and then take over his territory.”

    Great. So apart from having to take on Fisk, they now have to worry about who takes his place afterwards, if they actually manage to. Why couldn’t she have super-villain as an arch nemesis, that she defeats once and then that’s that. Kate sighs deeply, resisting the urge to bury her face in her hands.

    “What about the drugs?“ Yelena shrugs, her brows furrowed as she thinks.

    “I don’t know. I would think it is just another type of drug, but Val said your mother was involved.”

    Kate hums, drumming on the steering wheel.

    She goes over her conversation with Valentina, trying to look for clues she might have missed. She remembers Yelena was not there to see the CCTV footage.

    “She had videos of us.”

    Yelena turns to her, her face serious.

    “Valentina?”

    Kate glances at her, nodding.

    “Yeah. From the harbor. She said she erased it from the official city servers before the FBI could get to it, and deleted it from her tablet too…But I seriously doubt it was her only copy.” Yelena nods, and turns back to the city passing them by. She is silent for a long time, both of them thinking. Yelena speaks again just as they pull up in front of Kate’s building. “That’s something we need to be more aware of, going forward.”

    Kate digs into the center console, looking for a key fob to open the garage door. T “What is?”

    “Visibility. We are drawing way too much attention.”

    Kate reaches out the window to touch the plastic fob against the panel next to the entrance. She laughs somewhat humorlessly.

    “Well, it’s not like we were trying to.”

    They are shrouded in darkness for a moment as they descend on the spiral to Kate’s level in the garage.

    “No. But that is another good point…”

    Yelena contemplates her words before continuing, the lights of the garage flashing on her face as they pass them by.

    “…We have been reacting to things just happening. We need to get control.” Kate nods. Yelena is right. Since she came back to New York, there have been two attempts on her life, she ran into danger to save Annie, and Fisk has been a step ahead of them this entire time. They need to be acting, not reacting.

    “How?”

    Yelena shakes her head, and lets out a sigh that sounds tired.

    “I don’t know. We need to sit down, and make a proper plan. Patiently.” She puts emphasis on the last word, giving Kate a pointed look and she wants to scowl at it, but she can admit that they have probably been jumping into danger a bit too much in the last few days. She glances at the clock on the dashboard, noting it’s almost 11:30. She parks the car, and turns to Yelena.

    “Where are we meeting Wendy and Annie?”

    Yelena glances at the clock too, unbuckling herself.

    “By the Carousel.”

    Kate gets out of the car, and pulls her archery bag out too, sliding the strap around her shoulder. She follows Yelena to the elevator, remembering yesterdays stumbling journey, and bites the inside of her cheek. She contemplates trying to convince Yelena to go home again, but when she looks at her, Yelena seems to know exactly what she is thinking about, and gives her a glare that shuts her right up.

    The ride to the ground level is a bit awkward, and Kate resists the urge to fidget, not wanting to give Yelena the satisfaction. She has a smug tilt to her lips anyway, when Kate glances over at her, and it makes her want to scowl and pick a fight again.

    The doors open, and Yelena strides out, putting on her sunglasses again, and Kate jostles the gear-bag higher on her shoulder, before walking out after her. They walk to the entrance of Central Park in silence, and Yelena waits up for her there, walking a few steps ahead to that point.

    Kate looks at her, and halts by her side.

    “What?”

    Yelena glances around, before flipping her hair out of her face again, raising her chin. “I don’t know where the Carousel is.”

    That gives Kate a little sense of satisfaction, even though she knows she is being petty. She is mature enough to not comment on it though, and nods before taking off in the right direction. They wade through the crowd, sometimes separating to let people pass between them, but remining side by side for the duration of the trip.

    Kate hears the Carousel before she sees it, the circus-like music mixing with the chatter of tourists, multiple languages blending together to create a constant hum. They make the final turn on the path, and Kate halts to take in the crowd scattered around the attraction. She scouts around to find Wendy and Annie among the mass of people, and touches Yelena’s arm when she catches sight of them.

    “I see them. Come on.”

    She gulps, guilt filling her again as she takes in the bruises on Annie’s face, and the way she hangs onto Wendy’s arm like a lifeline. Kate walks up to them, and the way Wendy’s face lights up when she sees her feels like another kick in her gut.

    “Kate! Hi!”

    Wendy and Annie rush to them, and Kate is enveloped in a hug from both sides before she can say anything. She exhales sharply when her injured side is hit by an arm or elbow, stifling a groan. She clenches her jaw, and forces a smile onto her face.

    “Hi Wendy, hi Annie.”

    They let go of her, and she feels a spark of amusement at Yelena’s barely contained shock when she is grabbed in a hug too. Yelena holds herself ramrod straight as she is embraced, and glances at Kate but makes no moves to push either women away. Kate smiles at her, and feels some of her frustration with Yelena slip away as her face eases out and gives her a good-natured eyeroll.

    Wendy and Annie let go of them both, and look them over. Kate opens her mouth to start a long line of apologies, but Annie speaks before she can.

    “Thank you so, so much, Kate. I can’t tell you how grateful I am. To you too. Um, Yelena, right?”

    She looks at Yelena, whose face is unreadable but not unkind as she nods. “I probably won’t ever be able to repay either of you for this, but thank you so much.” Kate shakes her head, her smile feeling more like a grimace.

    “No, Annie. There is no need to thank us. Well, maybe Yelena, but I…I am so sorry I got you in trouble.”

    Annie shakes her head, and puts a hand on her arm.

    “Wendy told me what happened, and I don’t blame you. I am so proud of her doing the right thing, helping you. And I am so proud of you too.”

    Kate has met Annie a total of three times now, and somehow her words tighten around her throat and she has to look away to avoid welling up for a second. She clears her throat, and looks over at Annie, then Wendy.

    “I am…thank you. But I really am so sorry. I never would have asked for those files if I thought it was going to put you in danger.”

    Wendy smiles at her too, putting a hand on Annie’s shoulder.

    “I am not going to lie to you. If I have known…”

    She pauses, and clears her throat too.

    “If I thought it was gonna put Annie in danger, I’d have never gotten you those files. But, that’s exactly why you are an Avenger, and I am not.”

    Kate feels Yelena stiffen beside her, but she is too busy chuckling and shaking her head. “I am not an Avenger. Like, not even close…”

    Wendy shakes her head, looking at her in a way that makes her cringe, a weird mix of awe and unsettlement.

    “I mean it Kate. I walked the scene on the ship afterwards. What the three of you did, taking on that many guys? It was definitely…I walk a lot of crime scenes, and you guys definitely sent a message.”

    There is something in her eyes that Kate doesn’t want to think about. Kate can tell that she is thankful, but there is a wariness in her look for a second too, that hasn’t been there when they last met. It’s another kick in the chest, and so are her words. Kate tries to ignore it as she shakes her head one more time.

    “Did you um…”

    She has to look away again, focusing on the spinning of the carousel, the people’s happy faces as they go around.

    “Did you find the container?”

    Wendy’s voice is heavy too, even with her one word answer.

    “Yes...”

    Kate nods, biting the inside of her cheek and there is a beat of silence. “Does the police know who they are?”

    Wendy purses her lips, glancing around before looking back at Kate.

    “Well, I am not really allowed to be part of this investigation, for obvious reasons. But I think they are trying to find out. They bought in a bunch of perps too. They will be questioned about what’s been going on, on that ship.”

    Kate nods. That’s the best they can hope for. Distractedly, she thinks they’ll have to get those reports somehow too, to see if there are any leads in there. There is a beat of silence, before Yelena speaks up, practical as ever.

    “What did you say Annie was taken for?”

    It’s a legitimate concern, and Kate has to wonder too. Wendy did steal copies of police evidence, and if it comes out, she will be in a lot of trouble, again. Kate looks at her just as she answers, her tone light despite her nervous expression.

    “They didn’t ask yet. We will probably play dumb.”

    Yelena hums, and Kate hopes it’ll be enough. She gives a smile that she hopes is encouraging.

    “Let me know if we can help, okay?”

    Wendy nods, and pulls Annie closer, wrapping a hand around her waist.

    “Yeah, thanks. I, um, I think we might actually take a sabbatical. Go and stay with Annie’s family in Maine for a while.”

    It’s a very good idea, all things considered, but it still feels like another heavy punch to Kate’s chest. Their life, Wendy and Annie’s life, has been irreparably changed, just by her asking a favor. By being associated with her. She nods, and prepares to apologize again, but Yelena speaks before she can.

    “Do you have pen and paper?”

    Wendy looks baffled, shaking her head.

    “No?”

    Yelena nods, and walks off, leaving the three of them in a confused silence. “Where is she going?”

    Annie asks Kate, and she just shakes her head, shrugging. Yelena is back under 30 seconds, with a pamphlet for the carousel, and a pencil. She grabs Kate’s arms, and turns her around so her back is facing Yelena. She writes something on the piece of paper, using Kate’s back as a makeshift table.

    “Okay. When you get to Maine, you buy a new phone, using cash…”

    Wendy nods, eyes darting to Kate before turning back to Yelena.

    “I am giving you a phone number. If you are in trouble, or if you need to disappear, you call this number.”

    She holds out the pamphlet to Wendy, who reaches for it.

    “Okay…”

    Yelena doesn’t let go of the paper though, holding onto it still, holding Wendy’s gaze. “But! And I mean this, very seriously Wendy. You do not put this number into your current phone, yes?”

    She waits for the older woman to nod.

    “This is very important. You do not put this number in your phone, and if you take my advice, you should throw that out before you leave too.”

    Wendy looks at Kate who gives an apologetic smile, and a shrug. Wendy turns back to Yelena, nodding once more.

    “Is this your number?”

    Yelena smiles finally, letting go of the paper, and taking a step back to stand next to Kate again.

    “No. She is a friend of mine. I will let her know you have her number. If you are in trouble, she can help. Tell her Yelena sent you.”

    Wendy and Annie both seem to be at a loss of words. Annie manages to recover first, smiling back at Yelena.

    “Thank you.”

    Yelena is still smiling, and it’s surprisingly reassuring, soothing over the intensity of the earlier moments, even for Kate.

    “You are welcome. But please, use it for emergencies only. She is retired and I will not hear the end of it if you call her because your car broke down.”

    Annie and Wendy let out matching surprised chuckles, but they are still definitely a bit intimidated by all the “cloak and dagger”.

    “Okay.”

    They all need a moment to shake off the weirdness of the last minute, but Wendy seems to remember their original purpose for their meeting. She digs into her bag, and holds out Kate’s phone to her.

    “Thank you for the phone. Um, you had two calls, and I picked them up because I wasn’t sure if they had to do with your mission? I hope that’s okay.”

    She passes the phone, before continuing.

    “One from Clint, and one from a girl? I think she said her name was Amanda.” Kate groans internally. She is definitely not delighted to learn about either of these. “What did you tell them?”

    “I told Clint what was going on. He said he will call Yelena later.”

    Kate cringes. She was hoping to tell what happened to Clint herself. Wendy seems to read the apprehension on her face.

    “Was I not supposed to?”

    Wendy’s voice is cautious, and Kate stifles a sigh, putting on a smile. “No, no it’s okay. I’ll fill him in on the details later.”

    “Oh, okay. Um. And to the girl, I only said you left your phone at my place and that you will call her back later.”

    Oh wow. That’s going to be a fun conversation too. She already firmly decided to cut things off with Amanda after yesterday, but this will make it all so much more awkward than it has to be. She can’t suppress the deep sigh this time, and her voice definitely sounds drier than she means it to.

    “Great. Thanks.”

    Wendy’s eyes widen.

    “Oh! Oh, I’m sorry.”

    Annie looks between them, confused.

    “What? Why?”

    Kate jumps in, feeling quite weird to be talking about this with Yelena next to her, considering what nearly happened yesterday.

    “No, it’s fine. Nothing to be sorry for.”

    “I’m pretty sure I put Kate in an awkward spot with a girl.”

    Wendy gives Annie a wink, and Kate glances at Yelena, who seems to be surveying the crowd around them, her face void of any emotion. Wendy speaks, and apology still palpable in her tone.

    “She sounded nice? I am sure she will understand.”

    Kate just wants this topic to be over.

    “Yeah, yeah. She is. Yeah. Anyway, um, thanks for the phone.”

    She holds it up between them awkwardly, before sliding it into her pocket. Wendy smiles at her, this time without the earlier wariness in her eyes.

    “Thanks for lending it. And thank you again, for rescuing Annie. We really are so thankful.” Kate nods, looking between the two of them.

    “And I am really sorry again, for putting you in danger.”

    Annie smiles at her sweetly, but Kate’s heart aches when she visibly flinches at a semi-loud bang coming from a trashcan being emptied a few feet away. They stand in silence, for a few moments, before Kate clears her throat.

    “Anyways, we don’t want to keep you guys.”

    “Yeah, no. Um, but we do have to go. Lot of packing to do…”

    Wendy and Annie embrace Kate again, one at a time now, and Yelena busies herself with her phone, waving to them with a smile and Kate is pretty sure it’s to avoid getting hugged too. Kate watches them disappear into the crowd with a heavy heart, Annie turning back to wave one more time before they are gone, holding tightly onto Wendy’s hand. She takes the deep breath, and turns to Yelena who stands by her side, stoic as ever.

    She wants to ask about the phone number Yelena has given them, thank her for it but the weird, tense energy is still there between them and it chokes the words rising up in her throat. This interaction was another reminder that Kate is essentially toxic now. Her bare existence is enough to put people in danger, and it makes her feel equally angry and heartbroken. She jostles the archery bag higher on her shoulder, wincing as a flash of pain sears through her side, and takes off towards where they came from.

    “Let’s go home.”

    They walk the way back mostly in silence again, and Kate feels drained from the whole interaction. She wants to be alone, and process but the phone calls she has to make hang above her head, and make her feel tense. So does the information learnt from Valentina. By the time they make it back to the building, and enter the elevator, she has half the mind to just turn her phone off, so she can focus on next steps, but she knows she has to deal with Clint at least, before he shows up in New York as well.

    She pushes the button 29, and is a bit surprised when Yelena pushes the one for the 13th floor. She doesn’t look at Kate, and it seems she is definitely still angry about their conversation, because she only says one sentence as she exits on Sonya’s level.

    “Do not run off again. I want a day off.”

    She glances at Kate as she gets out, and there is a warning in her eyes. Kate’s initial reaction is to scowl at her but there is also something that reminds Kate of their conversation in the car. How can you ask me this? Yelena asked her. She seemed legitimately hurt, and with the added implication of Natasha’s death she can understand Yelena’s point of view, even if she doesn’t agree with it. A very vague shadow of that hurt is in her eyes still. It wasn’t her intention to hurt Yelena’s feelings, even if she is very frustrated with her refusal to leave, so she purses her lips but nods.

    “Okay. See you later.”

    Kate means it and Yelena walks off without another word. The doors close between them. The elevator takes her to floor 29, and she pulls the archery bag higher on her back one last time, before she walks to her door. Her apartment is just as empty as she left it, and she deposits her bag by the door with a sigh. The thought it always will be arises in her brain unbidden, as she briefly thinks about what she’ll say to Amanda, but she pushes it away. First, she needs something to eat. Then call Clint.

    She changes to a pair of sweats, along with a loose muscle tee and makes her way to the living room, sitting down on her sofa with a small groan. She ignores all other notifications for now, and orders a large peperoni pizza with tons of extra cheese, her stomach grumbling at the thought.

    After the order is placed, she contemplates ignoring her phone again, but the thought of just sitting alone with her thoughts doesn’t sound any better, and she does need to talk to Clint. She taps his name, and puts the phone on speaker, dropping her head against the back of the couch.

    He picks up on the third ring.

    “Hey Clint.”

    “Hi kid. Wanna tell me what you have been up to?”

    Without meaning to, his voice already unravels the tight coil in her chest a little. He doesn’t sound as panicked as yesterday, or angry, so that’s a good sign at least. “How much did Wendy tell you?”

    “She said her wife was taken, and you and Yelena were going to look for her. I saw some disturbance at the harbor on the news after, which I assume was you.”

    He waits for her to confirm and she wets her lips, trying to collect her thoughts. “Yeah. Yelena, Spider-Man and I. We found Annie on a ship in the harbor. There was…um… a lair for some gang on there, who took her on Fisk’s orders. We fought them and got her.” She doesn’t want to really go into details, both because the experience is still pretty fresh in her mind, and because she is afraid Clint will insist to come if she does. “Spider-Man? You know him?”

    She cringes at the thought of where she left things with Spider-Man. She must have made a great first expression.

    “No. Well, we met twice. He found us at the harbor and offered to help when we explained the situation. Do you?”

    He seems to think for a moment, before answering.

    “Not really. I think I met him once back in 2016, but we didn’t really chat.” “Ah okay…Um, anyway. We got home after but I only just got my phone back from Wendy.” “She and Annie okay?”

    Clint’s voice is gruff as always, but the care in it is palpable. A tight sensation starts to rise in her chest again, but she keeps her tone as light as she can.

    “Yeah, mostly. Or not really. They are both pretty shaken up by what happened, and they are planning to go away to Maine for a while, to lay low a bit. But yeah, physically they are okay.”

    “That’s good kid. You did good.”

    Kate gulps, and tightens her jaw before continuing.

    “Thanks. Um, yeah. So we got home after that. Had a big sleep. That’s about it.” To her surprise Clint chuckles.

    “Yeah, I kind of know that. I called Yelena after, and I talked to someone named Sonya on her phone? Weird gal.”

    Kate definitely does not remember that. Did they talk to Clint already? She answers, her voice a bit hesitant.

    “Yeah, she is a friend of Yelena’s. Lives in this building.“ Clint snickers, and she is a bit worried what she must have said, but thankfully his answer sooths those fears quick.

    “That’s handy. She put me on video-chat and you were already drooling on her couch when I called, passed out.”

    Oh. That’s at least marginally less mortifying. She tries to give a convincing chuckle back. “Yeeah. She gave us some pretty kick ass painkillers.”

    Clint’s voice is serious when he speaks again, and her forced laugh fades away in less than a second.

    “Yeah, she told me you were shot, and Yelena was stabbed. You okay?”

    She gulps, running a hand through her hair.

    “We are fine. There were a lot of guys, but we…um…took them out.”

    To her horror, her voice cracks a little and she has to take a deep breath, staring at the ceiling to stop herself from crying before she continues.

    “I got clipped by a shotgun, and Yelena was stabbed next to her hip, but we are both okay.” He waits a few seconds before speaking.

    “Are you?”

    She takes a staggering breath, and feels herself welling up despite her attempts to avoid exactly that.

    “Yeah? Uh…”

    She gulps again, closing her eyes and attempts to keep her voice even. “Yeah, just…it was a bit intense. A lot of death. Not on our end, thankfully, but yeah.” She makes it through the sentence without her voice cracking, and she hears Clint take a deep breath on the other end of the line.

    “I’m sorry.”

    She bites down on her lip, hard, to stop it from quivering and to stifle the sob making it out of her chest. He continues.

    “Listen, I know…I still think you shouldn’t be doing this, because it’s way too dangerous and all. But Kate, you gotta focus on the good stuff. I know it’s hard, but you saved Annie. You did a good thing.”

    She takes another shaky breath and nods, despite the fact that he can’t see her. “Yeah, I know. I know. It’s just hard, and I feel…I feel really guilty.” “About killing?”

    He doesn’t sugarcoat it, and she is kind of thankful. She manages to calm down enough to keep her voice even as she speaks.

    “Yes, that too. And putting Annie in danger. She got taken because they wanted to blackmail Wendy into giving us fake files…And um, about Yelena.”

    She adds the last part after a few heartbeats, and Clint sounds surprised. “Yelena?”
