    “Yeah. She got stabbed, Clint. She nearly died, just because she is trying to help me with something that has nothing to do with her…And I also kinda attacked her.” She can’t see Clint’s eyebrows shoot up, but she can imagine it, hearing his voice. “You…attacked her? Why?”

    “Uh…I kinda lost it at the end, and I…”

    She feels the shame and guilt fill her again, but she powers through. If anyone will understand, it’s Clint. She has learnt a lot more about Ronin in the months after Christmas. “I kind of went crazy on the Super-Soldier Spider-Man captured, and she was trying to stop me.”

    Clint is silent for a few moments.

    “What do you mean went crazy?”

    Kate lifts her hands to rub at her face.

    “I…stabbed him in the leg to get him to tell us where Annie was. And um, I threatened him with an acid arrow.”

    He doesn’t sound accusing, but he doesn’t sugarcoat his reaction to this either. “Jesus, kid.”

    “I know.”

    He takes another deep breath.

    “Look, Kate. I have been down that road, and it doesn’t lead anywhere you want to go. I know that anger. You know I do. But you can’t give into it. You will regret it for the rest of your life, if you do.”

    “I know. I just…”

    She takes another deep breath and thankfully he waits for her to continue. “We found this container that was…it was full of bodies, Clint. Men, women. Just thrown in there, rotting away. And with everything else that happened, with what I had to do, and we still didn’t know where Annie was...I snapped. Yelena and Spider-Man tried to stop me, but I just wanted to hurt someone for it.”

    Clint sighs, and hums. He doesn’t judge her, he never does about stuff like that, and if nothing else, that makes her feel a bit better.

    “I get it. But you have to learn to control that. You…that kind of rage will get you killed, or get people around you killed. And you will do things you never want to.” She hums and he is quiet for a moment.

    “Have you apologized to Yelena?”

    She wets her lips again, remembering last night and their argument in the car. “Yeah. Uh, she was actually pretty understanding about it. Not angry or anything. But yes, I did.”

    “So you two are cool?”

    “Uuuuum…kind of? I told her to go home today, and I think she is still pretty pissed about that.”

    Clint snorts.

    “Why would you tell her to go home?”

    Kate slides a bit more down on the couch, putting her feet on the coffee table, stalling a little. “Kate?”

    “Yeah, I’m here. Um. Well, you know. She got stabbed. For something that has nothing to do with her. There is no reason for her to put herself in danger for me.” Clint sounds like he is smiling, but there is a twinge of sadness in his voice and she kind of already suspects what he will say before the name is spoken.

    “Well, if she is anything like Nat, I don’t think she sees it like that.” “Yeah. She certainly seemed to disagree…She said I can take her help or she will abduct me to Ohio.”

    Clint snorts again, and the sentimental note is gone from his voice already. “Why don’t you do that? Do like a girls’ weekend away, instead of getting shot at and get beaten up. It’s what people your age are supposed to do.”

    Kate smiles, but shakes her head. She doesn’t think she will get to do something as mellow as a girls’ weekend for a while. Her tone is a bit wistful.

    “You know I can’t.”

    “Yeah, yeah, I know.”

    There is a beat of silence.

    “There is one more thing.”

    Clint waits for her to continue.

    “So, I went to my Dad’s grave today, and this woman approached me. Yelena says her name is Valentina, and she works for some secret organization that recruits like vigilantes or something. Do you know anything about that?”

    “No. I don’t know anyone name Valentina, although it could be an alias.”. What did she look like?

    “Um, Caucasian, around late forties, early fifties? Short, brunette with a purple streak in her hair.”

    “Doesn’t ring any bells. So, what did she want? To recruit you?”

    “Not…exactly. Apparently my mom was working on some drugs with Fisk. Her clients offered to help me against him, if I pass it over to them, if I come across it.” She can hear him set up straighter through the phone, his voice all business now. “Did she say who her client was?”

    “Yeah, someone names Javier Rojas. Yelena said he is some Colombian drug-lord that wants Fisk’s turf. Do you know him?”

    There is something in his voice when he answers.

    “Yeah, I know him.”

    “Clint? Details?”

    Clint is silent for a relatively long time. He clears his throat, but doesn’t hold back the truth from her. Not anymore.

    “I killed his father…during the Blip. He became head of the Rojas cartel afterwards…” Oh shit. That’s not good.

    “…You didn’t say yes to the offer, did you?”

    Kate’s jaw tightens, but her frustration is not directed at him.

    “No, of course not…But Yelena did.”

    “What?!”

    “Yeah, I know! She made a deal with this Valentina, that if he leaves us alone, she will get him the drugs.”

    Clint groans, and she shuffling over the phone.

    “God. Okay, that’s actually probably smart.”

    Kate is confused, her eyebrows furrowing.

    “It is?”

    “Yeah. At least he will leave you alone for now, and you can focus on Fisk. We will deal with him afterwards.”

    Oh no. We will deal with him afterwards. She is about to protest, but he continues. “Okay. So, you need to lay low for a few days, okay? I will do some digging, find out what I can about Rojas and the drugs. Heal up, and don’t do anything stupid.” She shakes her head, sitting up straighter too.

    “Clint, you don’t have to. I got this.”

    “Kate, you are my partner. This is getting out of hand way too quickly, and I am definitely not letting you deal with this shit alone.”

    “But…”

    “No buts. I’ll call you in a couple of days. Be smart, kiddo.”

    He hangs up without giving her a chance to object anymore and she groans out loud. Great. Zero out of two of her attempts to get the people in her life to safety have worked. Why is she surrounded with so many stubborn people? She spends the next few minutes ruminating over how to keep Clint and Yelena out of danger’s way, but comes up pretty much short.

    Her doorbell rings, and she gets off of the couch with a stifled groan, remembering her earlier hunger. She tips the pizza delivery boy graciously, and settles onto the couch with the warm box on her lap.

    The conversation has been therapeutic, despite its frustrating end. It felt good to talk to Clint, to tell him about everything that happened, to get his perspective. She doesn’t feel better, per se, but she feels a tad lighter and a bit more ready to continue on her path, now that she has talked to him about this. Clint has been through it, and came out on the other end. Maybe she can too.

    She eats almost the entire pizza in one sitting, and turns on the TV after the first slice to have a bit of a background noise and to distract herself from the lack of her faithful Pizza Dog. She is missing his constant begging for table-scraps already. She tells herself she needs to learn to get used to it, at least for now.

    The TV is still on CNN from yesterday, and her head snaps up during her 4th slice, as the anchor starts talking about what happened on the ship the day before.

    “New details have been released by the New York Police Department on what they are describing as the newest occurrence of vigilante justice in the Harbor of New York City yesterday. The Deputy Commissioner of the NYPD, Janice Stonewall has released a statement, condemning both sides involved in the incident and asking people who have any information regarding yesterday’s events to come forward.”

    A montage of various emergency services vehicles, and police officers standing around the pier is shown as Kate’s stomach drops to somewhere around her knees.

    “The statement also includes the information that unfortunately, all of the CCTVs around the shipyard seem to have malfunctioned, and no footage of the events was recorded this time. CNN is told however, that the description of the alleged vigilantes matches the ones for a similar incident and the ensuing car-chase from just the day before. Our very own Gary Howlington has all the details.”

    To Kate’s horror, the montage switches to two sketches of what she assumes are her and Yelena. Thankfully, they are not similar enough to them that anyone would make the connection, but it’s definitely bad. Very bad.

    “Thank you, Samantha. The individuals responsible for the destruction are said to be two young women, early to late twenties according to witnesses on the scene. One is said to be around 5’10” to 5’11 tall, brunette, and the other is between 5’3” and 5’4 with blonde hair. The women are both said to be Caucasian, and wearing regular civilian clothing at the time of the attack, but according to some, one of them was wielding a bow and arrows, which allowed the police to make the connection to Friday’s similar incident. At the time of this report, it is unclear if either or both of these women are enhanced individuals, but the statement released by the NYPD warns people to avoid approaching either of them directly, if someone recognizes them. Members of the public are advised to call 911 instead, and wait for officers of the NYPD to show up at a secure location.”

    Their sketches are switched out for a photo of Spider-Man.

    “An individual whose description matches the disgraced super-hero Spider-Man, was also reportedly in the company of the women, which seems to be another misstep in the resident New York City vigilante’s recently tumultuous career. Whether this is a one-time team up, or something permanent, is currently not known, but the emergence of the new vigilante duo is sure to give the New York Police Department something to worry about. Back to you Samantha.”

    The image switches back to the anchor from earlier, and Kate rubs her face, before looking at the screen again. This is just great. Clint is not going to be happy.

    “Thank you Gary. The reason for the attack on the ship also remains unclear, but sources close to the NYPD say, that multiple casualties have been reported, but apparently none of the three vigilantes are among the victims found on scene.”

    “The events come only days after Police Commissionaire Richard Bell was publicly criticized for not cracking down hard enough on vigilantism in the city by J. Jonah Jameson. According to the post by Mr. Jameson, which has garnered over 3 million likes since its release last week, Richard Bell and the New York Police Department are all complicit in the terror these vigilantes wreak on innocent civilians of New York City. Mr. Jameson also theorizes, that instead of fighting crime, the objectives of these individuals are something more nefarious. Referring to claims made by an unnamed informant, he alleges that many of the vigilantes operating in the city, and all around the United States, are actually working for different crime organizations instead, and their actions are merely acts of violence in their rivalries against each other. Here to shed some light on the topic is our resident super- powered individual specialist, Peter Sloan.”

    Kate really can’t believe this. She is working for the mob now, according to the public? Next to the blonde haired woman, a bald, middle aged man is shown in a different window. He nods to the camera, and puts on a professional smile.

    “Peter, what can you tell me about this connection to vigilantes and organized crime that Mr. Jameson has alleged?”

    “Good afternoon Samantha. Well, first of all, thank you for having me, as always. To answer that question, we have to look at the history of enhanced individuals in the United States. The first one, of course, was Mr. Captain Rogers, the first Captain America. He was, first and foremost, an agent of the government, and this country. As years went on, the attempts to re- create him have been mostly unsuccessful, but throughout the last decades, other people with special abilities have popped up. Then of course, with the formation of the Avengers in 2012, at this very city, the whole game has changed.”

    The blonde lady nods along with a very serious face. She continues to stuff pizza into her mouth, watching the TV with rapt attention.

    “After the Battle of New York, vigilantes and so called super-heroes have started to pop out around every corner, some more relevant than others. Around the world, we have seen a resurgence of enhanced people, and then came another notable moment, the Sokovia incident. If the Battle of New York was the rise of so called super-heroes, Sokovia was their fall. As was the collapse of S.H.I.E.L.D, which was their primary organization for years. The public was polarized, some claiming they were to blame for the death and destruction, while others continued to show their support. Even the next big historic moment, I’m talking about the Blip of course, has failed to give back their earlier popularity. And many felt...” “Peter, let me interrupt you with a question. You are talking about super-heroes, but can street level vigilantes treated the same? Are they the same?”

    “That’s a good question Samantha. I think the answer is complicated, and goes back to what I was just getting to in my long winded answer.”

    Samantha and Peter share a very fake laugh together and Kate rolls her eyes. “Apologies for interrupting then.”

    “No worries, I know I can get carried away by this topic.”

    “Please go on.”

    “My point is, the community, whether we call them super-heroes, vigilantes, or anything in- between, has been watered down. There are thousands of people, many of whom are enhanced either physically, or by some equipment, that are now acting on various interests, their own, or someone else’s. We have come a long way from Captain Rogers, or even the Avengers. Many of these vigilantes no longer have a clear mission, or objective. And even the ones that do have one, are not necessarily better. Take Karli Morgenthau for example, leader of the terrorist group Flag Smashers. There are many people, with a lot of goals, and interests. So, to finally get back to the original question, I definitely couldn’t say for certain that some of these vigilantes are not part of a criminal organization, or another.” Kate sighs, pushing the pizza box away and leaning back on the couch again to listen, closing her eyes. The one saving grace is that the press doesn’t seem to have gotten news of Annie, so her and Wendy can probably slip away and leave New York unnoticed.

    “Do you think these two young women are?”

    “It’s hard to say for certain. I have to disagree with Mr. Jameson in one topic. From my research there is nothing to indicate that Spider-Man is anything but a guy, or girl, with a mask who is trying to stop crime, however misguided. His involvement in the ordeal suggests to me, that this was not gang violence between enhanced individuals. These three vigilantes went there to fight crime, for better or worse, but probably didn’t care much about collateral damage. What I can say for certain, is that these women, even Spider-Man, are breaking and have broken the law. As you have mentioned, there are multiple casualties and hundreds of thousand dollars’ worth of property damage. And given the recent scrutiny on the NYPD regarding this topic, I wouldn’t be surprised if there was a harder focus on finding and apprehending these individuals.”

    Kate thinks of Yelena’s words. They will have to keep a lower profile from now on, avoiding fights in public, especially while their identities are not protected in some way. Or they need Clint to get in contact with someone, to get them some kind of official authentication that they are not “rogue elements” as this specialist called them. She unsure if something like that exists.

    The woman speaks again.

    “That raises another interesting question. What can the NYPD do against enhanced individuals? Do you think we can see people with powers in a police uniform soon?” “I think it depends largely on public opinion. If vigilantes, and their actions continue to cause problems for the general population, I’d say certainly. With the disband of the Avengers, there is a power vacuum now, that is yet to be filled. We have a new Captain America, but he alone is not enough to try and stop all rogue elements, and none of the still remaining Avengers have stepped up to re-assemble the group, or try to start a new one.” “Thank you for your time Peter, I have just one more question, before I let you go. Do you think these women are enhanced? Do they have powers? We have various sources claiming different things.”

    “Yes, I’d say for certain. I have not been to the crime scene myself, of course, but I have talked to a few people who have, and they all describe large scale destruction, and almost a hundred members of this criminal group either dead, injured, or apprehended. I don’t see how that is possible without some enhanced qualities. There is also the cell-phone footage of the two of them fighting someone, who is very clearly super-powered, and managing to subdue him, which is also not something that can be done easily without some enhancement at least.” Kate thinks about her injuries, Yelena’s blood soaking her clothes, and for once, she wishes did she had powers.

    Samantha thanks Peter for his time, and the topic is changed to some story about the government budget so Kate tunes it out pretty quick. She lies with her head leant back for a few more moments, then picks up her phone.

    [to Clint] 2:13 pm: Don’t freak out. There is police sketch of Yelena and me floating around. We will lay low for a few days.

    She receives an answer almost immediately for once.

    [from Clint] 2:13pm: OK. Will see if there is any string I can pull.

    The next message makes her smile.

    [from Clint] 2:13 pm: *hawk emoji* *bow and arrow emoji*

    Clint almost never uses emojis, so she guesses this is his way of making her feel better. It kinda works.

    She googles new York harbor vigilante police sketch, and the third image is her and Yelena. She copies it, and sends it to Yelena.

    [to Yelena] 2:15 am: Look, we are famous.

    She attaches the link to the article below and sends it too. It’s an olive branch of sorts, but she doesn’t receive an answer soon, so she starts scrolling Instagram. She likes a picture of Cassie, taken with a group of girls from her college, and one of Franny’s cat. That leads her down a Rabbit hole of looking at the pictures of people she went to college with. She is stalling.

    The pictures she sees are exact reminders of what she is trying to put off doing. She has to call Amanda, and she has to break off things with her. Cut out what was her last, desperate attempt at a normal life, a normal relationship. It was only one date, a few calls and messages, but it was the last shred of normalcy in her life. She doesn’t doubt her decision, but she mourns it nonetheless. It fills her with some acidic guilt, that she is distinctly aware that she doesn’t mourn for Amanda, not really. She is sad for entirely selfish reasons. Clint has warned her, multiple times actually, and she didn’t listen. It took Annie being taken, and Yelena getting stabbed for her to come to her senses, and still, in this moment, she is sorry for herself. For all the things she is missing out on, that she doesn’t and won’t get to do. Instagram is always a black hole this way. Anniversaries, babies, date nights, cute pics of shared apartments. Her own page is filled with nothing but few pictures of Lucky and California landscape, ever since that fateful week she met Clint. She doesn’t regret it, she never does or could. But selfishly, she wants to have her cake and eat it too. She exhales deeply, and closes Instagram.

    She opens her text with Amanda, and sees that she answered her last text. [to Amanda] Yesterday 10:37 am: So sorry for going AWOL! Phone died at the worst possible time and work got a bit crazy. How was your day yesterday?

    [from Amanda] Yesterday 12:04 pm: She lives!

    [from Amanda] Yesterday 12:04 pm: My day was good thanks :) I had Mexican for lunch and I thought of you [from Amanda] Yesterday 12:05 pm: How was yours?

    Amanda is nice. She was fun, and pretty, and sweet, and flirty and normal. And Kate knows she can’t have that.

    She doesn’t even consider saying what she has to say over text. Amanda deserves better than that. Kate’s last semblance of normalcy deserves better than that.

    Opening her call log, she sees that Amanda called her at 5:32 pm yesterday. Probably after she got out of work.

    She taps the number, taking a deep breath.

    Three rings, and the call is connected.

    “Hi.”

    Chapter End Notes I hope you all enjoy this chapter :)

    This was a pretty busy one too, even though nothing much actually happened. :D Our girls are at odds right now, on more than one levels :D Next chapter we are finally dealing with the Amanda situation and the story will pick up pace again :) I'll try to post it during the weekend.
