    Chapter 15

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes “Hi.”

    “Kate? Hii!”

    Kate expected awkwardness, with Wendy’s weird comment, but Amanda actually sounds excited to hear from her, and somehow it makes all of this worse. Her voice comes out breathier than she means it to.

    “Hi Amanda.”

    “It’s nice to finally hear your voice. I called yesterday, but a friend of yours picked up.” Okay. So she didn’t take it the way Kate was worried about. That’s good at least. “Yeah, I…I left my phone at her place when I left for a work thing. Only got it back today.” “Sounds like work has been pretty busy?”

    It’s a fishing question. Amanda is still obviously curious about what she does, when she is “coming back” but if Kate has kept it from her until now, she sure as hell going to tell her. “Yeah. Uh…This case is turning out to be more complicated than we thought.” There is a brief silence on the other end of the line, before Amanda speaks again, her voice a shade softer.

    “Are you okay? You sound…tired.”

    Kate releases a breathy chuckle. The ease she felt with Amanda on their one singular date is already enveloping her, and she longs to tell her everything that’s been happening. Amanda is so outside of it, and she’d not understand any of it, but Kate thinks it’d be nice to just be soft for a little while. To talk to someone who has no experience with people dying around you. People bing killed by you.

    She can’t do it though.

    She wets her lips, taking a deep breath, and forces her voice to be lighter as she opens her mouth.

    “Yeeah, I’m all good. Just had a long couple of days, you know how it is.” Amanda chuckles, and Kate smiles sadly. Of course, she doesn’t know what Kate means. “Yeah, I actually had my ass kicked at work too. There is this new project that I…” She goes into a long explanation about her work and Kate lets her. She is stalling again, (or still,) she knows. But if this is going to be their last call, their last interaction, the last shred of normalcy Kate has, she is going to enjoy it as long as she can. She does not want to rip the band aid off in this case, even though she thinks it’d probably be better if she did. She hums and answers at all the right moments, and actually pays attention to Amanda’s words, not tuning her out.

    For a long moment, Kate imagines telling her she is already back in the city, asking her to come over. Amanda would, she is pretty sure. They could have one last evening, one last night before she has to get back to her real life. Her real life, where she is hunted, and anyone associated with her could be killed just for that simple fact. She thinks about how incredibly turned on she was last night with Yelena, and despite knowing it’s a pretty shitty thing to do, considering what she is about to do, she imagines how good it would be to get to release that. It isn’t until Amanda finishes the story and there is a slight lull in the conversation, that she forces herself to remember Annie being abducted, Yelena getting hurt, and everything that happened on the ship.

    “So…if the case is more complicated than you thought…does that mean you are not coming back to New York anytime soon?”

    Amanda’s voice is soft again, and a bit hopeful. Kate has to bite down on the inside of her cheek in an effort to steel herself. Earlier, she tried to consider what she will say to Amanda, what excuse she will use to snuff out this little spark. She is not closer to a strategy now, so she decides to just wing it.

    “Yeah, I…This is kind of why I called.”

    “Oh.”

    It shouldn’t be possible for two syllables to convey disappointment and understanding so well, but they do. She can instantly tell that Amanda knows where this is going. “I…really hate doing this through the phone, but that’s kind of the reason why I have to.” She waits for Amanda to say anything, but she is quiet so Kate keeps talking. “Things have gotten pretty complicated in my life, in the last couple of days, and I don’t want to string you along. God. Sorry, I know how that sounds.”

    Amanda sighs deeply on the other end of the phone.

    “Yes I…I kinda got the feeling that something was going on.”

    “You did?”

    She doesn’t know why she asks, it just feels right in the conversation. “Yeah. I could feel your excitement slipping away.”

    “No, I…It’s not that. I am just really not in the place to have a relationship right now.” She cringes at how cliché that sounds, even though it’s actually 100% true for her. Amanda chuckles on the other end of the line, but there is no happiness in the sound. “I understand…But uh, before you do this…I have a confession to make, Um…I kind of know why you can’t.”

    Kate sits up immediately, the mellow sadness gone in an instant.

    “What do you mean?”

    She can almost hear Amanda gulp through the phone.

    “You are Kate Bishop.”

    Kate’s heart starts beating hard against her chest. Amanda knows. She knows who Kate is. What else does she know? Amanda continues.

    “I…okay, this is a bit embarrassing. After our date, I wanted to snoop on your insta, so I looked for Kate Derekson, but found nothing. So I searched for Kate and Security in google, hoping I’ll find some other social media, and news about your mom’s company came up. There were pictures of you too, so…”

    She trails off and Kate is frozen.

    She doesn’t know whether she can believe Amanda, and her mind is trying to make sense of it all, but she absolutely feels blindsided by this. Amanda takes her silence as a cue to continue.

    “I’m sorry if this was an invasion of your privacy, I really didn’t mean to be a creep or expose you or anything. And I understand completely why you lied. It sounds like a really shitty situation and I’m sorry.”

    Kate still doesn’t know what to say.

    “Anyway, I know your mom’s trial is coming up, and I understand you are probably not really in the headspace to…date or whatever. But I kind of felt bad about finding out this way, and I wanted to tell you I understand before you broke it off. So like…if you need a friend or something, we can still talk.”

    A friend? Kate shakes her head. She needs to figure out what Amanda knows. Then she needs to shut this shit down, fast. This is already way out of hand.

    How does she find out if Amanda knows who she is, meaning Hawkeye, or whatever, a vigilante, this time, without giving away anything. Especially on the phone. She needs to be looking at Amanda, she can’t tell just by her voice if she is being truthful. She says it without thinking it through.

    “Can I see you?”

    There is a beat of silence.

    “Um, like video-chat?”

    She considers it, but no. If Amanda knows something, she’ll have to be there in person. “No, I can be back in New York tomorrow for a short time. I…This is a conversation best had in person.”

    Amanda sounds surprised, but happy.

    “Oh. Okay. Sure!”

    Kate is already brainstorming locations on where they could have this conversation. She will need to take Amanda somewhere secure, where they can’t be ambushed or overheard if things get out of hand.

    “I’ll pick you up at 8.”

    That gives Kate plenty of time to prepare, and come up with a plan.

    “Yeah, that sounds good.”

    They are silent for a moment, and Kate doesn’t know what else to say now. Everything is a mess. Is Amanda playing her? She needs more information.

    “Okay. I gotta go, I’m still at work. See you tomorrow!”

    There is a nervousness in Amanda’s voice, and Kate feels like she is going crazy, because she can’t tell if she’s nervous because she is playing Kate, or because she thinks she overstepped. God.

    Either way, it’ll not be good for her to show her hand. She makes her voice sound soft, and nice.

    “I’m looking forward to seeing you.”

    Amanda sounds relieved.

    “Me too”

    “Bye”

    They hang up and Kate buries her face in her hands before she can’t take sitting down anymore.

    She gets on her feet and starts pacing.

    She needs to get as much information on Amanda as possible. And she needs to make a plan. She really can’t afford any more public fights or fuckups, especially because she is definitely not in the physical state to be in a proper fight.

    She takes the pizza box to the kitchen, and puts it in the fridge, then turns on the coffee maker. Her phone buzzes in her pocket, and she takes it out as she waits. [from Yelena] 3:24 am: That looks nothing like me.

    She smiles despite herself, and slides the device back into her pocket. She makes herself a coffee, and settles on her couch, ready to dig into Amanda.

    The first thing she checks is the Bishop Security database archive, but there is not much there, besides details she already knows.

    Pierson, Amanda Born: 12-09-1999, New York City Under notes she finds that Amanda was apparently employed by Avex Ltd at the time when the database went offline 1.5 years ago. She searches Pierson, Amanda Avex Ltd. in google, and that search seems a lot more fruitful. She finds Amanda’s page on the company website, her LinkedIn, and even her Instagram account.

    She spends the next several hours researching, and doesn’t stop until she has complied a comprehensive profile. If Amanda is not who she says she is, whoever set up her fake identity was really thorough. Her Instagram goes all the way back to 2014, and her career can be traced back even to her college years.

    Kate is still torn.

    Thinking about it, could it have been a coincidence that they met on the same day that Kate found out she was being hunted? She doesn’t know.

    She gets off the couch and thinks she should take Lucky for a walk for a moment, before she remembers he is downstairs with Sonya, Thomas and Yelena. Kate considers going down herself for some company, but decides against it and heats up some pizza instead, getting back on the couch.

    She turns on the TV, and boots up Netflix, not in the mood for whatever else CNN has to say for now. Her mind is trying to connect the dots, to figure out how Amanda could be connected to this. Her life seems pretty real, she posts on Instagram regularly, with friends whose profiles and identities seem to be real as well.

    The thought occurs to her, that maybe she could be blackmailed, or paid for something, like Wendy. According to the information she gathered, both of Amanda’s parents are still alive, and she seems to have had an older brother, but all traces of him disappear around 2018. Kate think he might have been Blipped, but there is no proof of his existence in the years since either, so she is not sure.

    She tries to put this line of thought into bed, as she eats her leftover pizza and watches Brooklyn 99 distractedly. If Amanda is playing her, she is not sure she cares why. She is careful not to let herself become angry, to jump to conclusions, because she doesn’t have any proof, but if that turns out to be the case she will be pretty upset.

    She tries to focus on her plan instead. With the events of the last few days, she needs to handle this quietly, whichever way it goes. And she needs to be not ambushed, because she is not in a state to fight very well right now. One person, she can probably take, but something like the last two days will surely not go over for her. Which means one thing. She can’t do this alone.

    She cringes hard at the thought, but she will have to ask for help, and there is only one person who she can ask right now.

    Yelena.

    God. This is a mess. She really, really doesn’t want to do this.

    And not just because she personally wants Yelena away from anything dangerous right now, but because of the moment they had last night. Which, if Kate is honest with herself, and thinks about it (which she doesn’t, because she has enough on her plate to deal with right now), was definitely not just the morphine making her horny for whoever was around. It wasn’t very serious, but Kate was turned on by Yelena, not just by whatever warm body was next to her.

    Yelena is a very attractive woman, with a killer sense of humor, and a kindness that is not obscured by a more general-sense niceness. If they met under different circumstances (both the first, and the second time), Kate has no doubt that she would be all over that, but that’s a moot point. For better or worse, she just doesn’t want her around Amanda. She can’t really explain why, but it still feels icky.

    She sighs, and leaves that to be a problem for tomorrow’s Kate.

    For now, she tries to brainstorm locations and strategies. Normally, she’d think going somewhere public would be the best course of action, but if the last few days have shown her anything, it’s that the people after her are not going to hold back just because other people are around. If Amanda is one of them, she won’t care either, and if she isn’t, Kate is putting her and a lot of bystanders in a lot of danger for no reason.

    The ideal location would be an apartment, but Kate definitely doesn’t want to bring her into her home, if she is working for Fisk, and Kate is not stupid enough to walk into Amanda’s place when it might be a trap.

    Maybe she could get an Airbnb or hotel. She puts that on her list. But it’s not perfect. There are still neighbors, and making it out of an unknown building while she or they are being attacked is not exactly ideal.

    Another choice is to just drive out of the city, somewhere remote. Maybe go to a motel, so they can have a conversation in private, and without a city full of people around. She puts that on the list too.

    She slowly finds her eyes and limbs grow heavy, and she puts aside the empty pizza box. She turns the TV off and brushes her teeth and face, removing the make-up that covers the bruises and looks at herself in the mirror for a second.

    The swelling has gone down a little since the morning, but her face is still pretty beaten. She remembers her antibiotics, and goes to the living room to take one. The bandage on her side should probably be changed too, but she will do it after her shower in the morning. She shreds her sweats in the bedroom, leaving them in a heap on the floor and climbs into bed with a satisfied groan.

    With the exhaustion of the last few days, she is asleep in less than 5 minutes. --

    Next morning she wakes up slowly, her mind already half awake and running before her body joins it. She is going over tasks she has to get done, and strategies, ideas for today even before she is fully conscious. It makes her feel tense as she wakes up. She sits up, sliding her legs to the edge of the bed with a stifled groan. She feels maybe a little better than yesterday, but definitely not in good shape. She pads to the bathroom and takes off her clothes, for once not half-awake.

    She showers, then cleans her wounds on her side with antiseptic wipes. The good news is that they don’t sting around her stiches, the bad is that her skin feels even more tender than yesterday, and also slightly itchy. She bandages the injury again, wrapping gauze around her torso, then puts on a clean pair of sweatpants and an old, faded but soft t-shirt. She miraculously remembers to take the her antibiotics again, then walks to the door and grabs her keys. She considers taking the tracker off but it’s probably actually handy, however annoying the fact is, that it’s there in the first place. She puts it in her pocket, along with her phone, wallet and the sword. She picks up her sunglasses too, and then, she is off. Taking down the elevator to the ground floor, she walks out of the building into the streaming sunlight. Slipping on her sunglasses, she turns to the left. If she is going to ask Yelena a favor, she might as well bring her some breakfast food. Maybe also as second olive branch, to ease the tension of their interactions from yesterday.

    If it was up to her, Yelena would definitely head back to Ohio until Kate has sorted this all out, but she can understand her point of view, even if she disagrees. If she was in trouble, there is no way Kate would leave either.

    The diner is not as busy as it was the last time she was here with Yelena but there is still a steady buzz of noise around her as she enters. She goes up to the counter, and orders pancakes for Yelena, and after some brief hesitation the same for Sonya, if she is around today too. For herself, she gets an omelet and 3 coffees. She makes sure to stuff several sugar packets for Yelena into her pocket, and smiles at the cashier on autopilot. She thinks of the last time she was here, the morning after Yelena arrived. She smiles slightly at the memory of her overdone valley girl accent and considers how far they have come, in barely over a week. How she seriously thought Yelena took a contract on her, only to have her save Kate’s life several times, and always having her back.

    She exits the restaurant with her greasy, delicious smelling breakfast food in a paper bag and a paper tray for the coffees, and starts walking back towards her building. In the elevator she uses her elbow to press the button for the 13th floor, and tries to ignore the rising nervousness in her limbs.

    On Sonya’s floor, she walks to the door and rings the doorbell. She shuffles around as she waits, shifting her weight from one foot to the other.

    Sonya answers faster this time, opening the door in her robe, and giving her a playful once over, batting her eyelashes.

    “We are just two poor Russian girls, without any money. However will we pay for this?” Kate snorts, Sonya’s predictable humor easing her nervousness little. She arranges her face into a smirk, giving her a playful once over back, purposefully making her voice lower. “I’m sure we can arrange something.”

    Sonya laughs delightedly and takes the coffee tray from her, and Kate drops her act to smile too.

    “Come on in, Kate Bishop. We can’t resist a woman bearing coffee and breakfast food…” Lucky comes running from the living room and Kate drops into a crouch to receive his excitement, almost missing the second half of Sonya’s sentence.

    “…even if she is very stupid.”

    She glances up at Sonya, the woman giving her a disapproving look. She purses her lips, and glances into the apartment before looking back at her.

    “She told you.”

    Sonya purses her lips back, her brow lifting a little.

    “She did. You are being very silly.”

    Kate sighs, and straightens up, unintentionally towering over Sonya.

    “I don’t want her to get hurt for something that’s not her problem.”

    Sonya rolls her eyes and turns into the apartment, leaving Kate to close the door behind her and follow.

    “Well, it might not be her problem, but it’s not your decision.”

    They have reached an impasse, so Kate just shrugs.

    “Where is Yelena anyway?”

    Sonya doesn’t answer her right away, but walks back to the hallway. She is out of Kate’s sight, but she hears her knock on a door and call out something in Russian recognizing her own name in the sentence. Yelena’s voice answers from behind the door, and Kate shuffles around again in the living room, with the paper bag still in her hands. “She is in the shower. 5 minutes she says.”

    Sonya comes back to the room and Kate follows her to the kitchen. She deposits the bag on the counter, and leans back against it as Sonya starts to take out plates and utensils from the cupboards. Kate feels a bit weird, being alone with her.

    “Have you taken you antibiotics?”

    Sonya asks as she continues to move around the kitchen.

    “Yeah, thanks. Really, um, thanks for taking care of us the other day. I don’t think we would have made it if you didn’t.”

    Sonya smiles, and glances at her as she sets 3 places around the island. “You are very welcome. But there is no need for thanks. Yelena saved me from much worse than dying, I will help her always.”

    Kate blinks, surprised. She tilts her head to the side a little, trying to figure out if the question is appropriate.

    “Were you…um…controlled too?”

    Sonya looks back at her for a moment, face unreadable before she nods. “Yes. Yelena freed me.”

    She doesn’t elaborate, and Kate just nods. There is a silence for a second that is neither comfortable, nor tense but Kate feels like she has to fill it anyway.

    “Is Thomas at work?”

    Sonya is quick to smile, even though she rolls her eyes a little too as she takes a seat by the kitchen island.

    “Yeees. I do not understand it. He has more money that he could ever spend, yet he chooses to work.”

    Kate grins and takes a seat opposite of her as well.

    “Maybe you can explain? You are the same. So very rich, yet refuse to just enjoy it.” Kate takes one of the coffees from the paper cupholder, puling it in front of herself. She removes the lid to blow on it, inhaling its delicious smell.

    “Well, you know. If you grow up with money, it can become something you don’t really think about. It doesn’t mean you still don’t want to do something with your life.” Sonya regards her for a moment.

    “I guess that is true. Having so much money just means you get more choices.” Kate hums. It’s true. Doing what she does would definitely be harder if she had to worry about paying bills or whatever.

    “What do you want to do with your life?”

    It’s a surprisingly serious question from Sonya, although it probably shouldn’t be. Kate is aware that she must be more than walking, talking innuendo wrapped in a silk robe. She attempts to take a sip of her coffee and burns her tongue.

    “Ow…um…well, I want to help people. I always did.”

    Sonya nods, and pulls one of the coffees to herself as well.

    “With your money, you wouldn’t have to do what you do to help. You could just do a lot of charity.”

    Kate smiles, shaking her head. She hears a door open somewhere in the apartment behind her back.

    “That’s not who I am. Anyone can give money, but I want to help in ways that matter. Protect people who can’t protect themselves. Money means nothing in itself.”

    Sonya raises her eyebrows, her face amused.

    “Money means nothing? Maybe to you. To many, it means survival. And to everyone, even to you, it means freedom.”

    “No, yeah, I know that. I don’t mean it means nothing. It’s just…it doesn’t make you happy on its own. And it’s only useful if you spend it on things or people that matter.” Sonya looks like she disagrees, but she grins.

    “You would be very easy to gold dig.”

    Kate is about to answer but she hears bare feet enter the kitchen and turns around to look at Yelena. Her mind immediately grinds to screeching halt.

    Yelena wears nothing but a towel, a seemingly endless amount of smooth skin on display. Her hair is wet, hanging down past her clavicles, drops of water still sticking to her glistening skin. She meets Kate’s eyes only for a moment, and there is an amused glint in her eyes. “Morning.”

    Kate becomes aware that she is staring, and shuts her mouth quickly which she realizes was slightly agape.

    “Hi. Morning. I bought food. Uh, Pancakes.”

    She focuses only on Yelena’s face, purposefully avoiding looking at her anywhere else. She has embarrassed herself enough in front of these two enough already. Yelena’s eyebrows lift a miniscule amount, before a coy smile slides onto her features.

    “Good. I am always just soo hungry in the mornings.”

    Yelena’s voice drops an octave on soo hungry, dripping with innuendo and Kate is aware that she is being teased again. She grins, and says the first answer that comes to mind, holding Yelena’s gaze, even though her brain is still sputtering over the fact that she is pretty much naked, now standing next to Kate.

    “Lets put something in your mouth then.”

    Sonya snorts and Yelena raises an eyebrow, clearly not expecting the comeback. Yelena comes to peer into the paper bag and Kate makes an effort to not look at the drops of water running down her neck and shoulder.

    She walks out of the room without another word, and Sonya puts a glass of water in front of Kate.

    “Um, thanks?”

    “You looked thirsty.”

    Sonya gives her a huge smile and Kate returns her a half-hearted glare but can’t help the uptick of the corner of her lips. Yelena seems to have gotten over her offence from yesterday, and Kate is glad the weird tension is gone from between them as well.

    Yelena is back in 2 minutes, dressed in black leggings and a tank top, her hair probably only towel dried, still damp. It’s not much less distracting for Kate than the towel, but she focuses on passing out food instead, barely checking out her ass as she passes her by. “I didn’t know what you liked, so I got you pancakes too. I hope that’s alright.” She passes one of the containers to Sonya, who smiles.

    “Yes. For future reference, I like waffles the most, with strawberries and whipped cream. But pancakes are good too, thanks.”

    Kate lets out a surprised chuckle, her eyebrows lifting. Direct, as always. “Noted.”

    She takes out her own omelet, sliding it onto her plate. She starts eating immediately, her mouth watering at the smell, and avoiding looking at Yelena sitting across from her. The conversation with Sonya and the joking with Yelena has made her forget her nervousness, but now it’s back with full force. She puts down her utensils, and leans back after a few minutes of gathering her courage.

    “Um…I need to ask you a favor.”

    Yelena barely looks up from her pancakes.

    “Hm. What is it?”

    Kate gulps, gathering her thoughts.

    “So, amm…there is this girl I went on a date with, on the same night as you showed up at my apartment.”

    Yelena stops eating, and looks up at Kate, only her eyes moving. Kate’s gaze flits over to Sonya, who is frozen over her plate as well, looking at her too.

    “Oookay?”

    “I kinda have to meet her tonight, and I need you to come with.”

    Yelena’s eyebrows rise so high on her forehead that Kate is surprised they don’t disappear in her hairline completely.

    “…what?”

    She keeps her eyes on Yelena but she sees Sonya look at her with wide eyes, before going back to her pancakes with an eyeroll.

    “Yeah. So…okay, I’ll try to give you the short version. So, we met that day at this charity I went to volunteer at, and went on one date, same day. But because I didn’t want to talk about my family and like, wanted to keep a low profile, I told her a fake name. She called while my phone was at Wendy’s and I called her back yesterday after we got back. It turns out she figured out who I really am. I mean, that I am Kate Bishop, not that I’m Hawkeye, or whatever. Or well, I am trying to figure out the second part.”

    A wide smile stretches over Sonya’s face, as she leans back on her chair. “You want to take her out.”

    “What?! No! No, I…It’s just kind of suspicious that she showed up just when a bounty was put on my head, right? And then figured out my real name, from a google search apparently. I need to find out what she knows. If she is working for Fisk, she might have some useful information.”

    Sonya looks mildly disappointed, and Kate gives her a disapproving glance. She just shrugs and goes back to her food. Yelena stares at her a moment longer, her eyes narrowed, lips pursed in thought.

    “It might be suspicious. It depends. What was the fake name you gave her?” Kate looks to the side, and tries to think of a way out of answering.

    “Kate…um…Kate Derekson.”

    Sonya abandons her food completely to grin at her, and she can feel the tips of her ears grow warm.

    “So…your name is Kate, and the fake name you gave is also Kate?”

    She feels weirdly self-conscious about her “alias”, admittedly not her finest work. It’s not made any better by Sonya bursting out laughing. She looks at Yelena who looks half amused half annoyed as she rubs a hand at her face, visibly exasperated.

    “Kate...”

    “Hey! I changed my last name, okay? And it isn’t like I knew I was supposed to be hiding at the time!”

    “To your fathers first name. That is not any better. A child could figure that out.” Kate exhales through her nose, glaring at Yelena pointedly.

    “Well we can’t all be Lezzie Humper, can we?”

    Yelena glares right back at her, lifting an eyebrow.

    “It’s Lizzie. Elizabeth. You literally have the same middle name.”

    The fact that Yelena knows her middle name that she never, ever uses, doesn’t even phase Kate.

    “What it is, is ridiculous.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes at her, her tone dripping with sarcasm.

    “Whatever you say, Kate Derekson.”

    They stare at each other for a moment, the frustration Kate felt yesterday sparking up again. Yelena purses her lips, before cutting another slice from her pancakes, putting it in her mouth. She chews and swallows it before she speaks again.

    “When you met her, did she make any moves to attack you? Hurt you in any way?” Kate’s eyebrows furrow before she cocks one of them, shaking her head. “Um, no? I wouldn’t be like,…just chatting with her on the phone if she did.” Yelena blinks at her, before throwing her hair behind her shoulder.

    “I threw you off a roof, and beat you up, and here you are having breakfast with me. You literally asked me to get a drink, while I was beating you up. It is not completely crazy to assume...”

    Kate cuts in, voice dry, but her gaze drops to Lucky who nudges her hand to indicate he would like to share her eggs.

    “You were not beating me up. It was a perfectly balanced fight.”

    Kate knows she is full of shit, but at least Yelena interrupts herself, to react to that. “…It’s cute that you think that.”

    Kate’s jaw tightens at that and she shoots Yelena another glare.

    “Anyways, no. She didn’t. She is supposedly a very normal, very non-punchy marketing person.”

    Sonya joins in.

    “Ew, that’s boring.”

    Kate whips her head towards her in disbelief.

    “You are dating an accountant.”

    Sonya shrugs, unbothered.

    “Yes, but he is rich and great in bed. Is your marketing person girlfriend rich and great in bed?”

    Kate looks at her like she is insane. (Also, from the interactions she has seen, that is totally not the only reason why Sonya is with Thomas.)

    “I don’t know! We went on one date.”

    Sonya shrugs again, one eyebrow lifted.

    “I usually check both of these qualities on a first date.”

    Kate looks at her for a long moment, lips pressed together.

    “Great, good for you. I don’t know. I don’t particularly care if she is rich, and I didn’t sleep with her.”

    Sonya purses her lips to one side, that one mocking eyebrow still cocked. “Is she hot at least?”

    Kate rubs her face, groaning. She does not enjoy being tag-teamed by Sonya and Yelena. “Yes. Now, can we get back to the point? I need to find out if she is playing me.” Yelena speaks next, her voice mocking.

    “Awh, are you heartbroken, Kate Bishop?”

    Kate sighs deeply, counting in her head. In the background, Lucky whines at being ignored for so long.

    “One date. We have been on one date. Hardly enough to be heartbroken.” She knows she is lying. She absolutely will be heartbroken if Amanda turns out to be playing her. Not because of her, but because it’s the last normal and good date Kate had, and will have for the foreseeable future. She doesn’t want it tainted too. She takes another deep breath, trying to push down on her frustration.

    “Listen, I just need to know, okay? And if she isn’t who she says she is, it’s not like we have any more leads at the moment. We can question her, find out what she knows. Yelena looks at her for a long time, eyes searching her face. She looks thoughtful, and her lips are turned downwards, but it seems she found what she was looking for, because she leans back in a second with a deep sigh. She looks away from Kate.

    “Okay, sure. I will help you.”

    Sonya sighs dramatically, and throws her hands up in the air.

    “Fine, I’ll help you too.”

    Kate is annoyed enough that she almost points out that she did not ask Sonya to come along too, but she is well aware that Yelena is not back to 100% yet either. If they get into a fight, they will need all the help they can get.

    She lets out a relieved breath.

    “Thank you. I really appreciate it.”

    Her relief is short lived because Sonya grins again, a positively naughty glint in her eyes as she pulls out her phone.

    “Does she have an Instagram? What’s her handle?”

    She is looking expectantly at Kate, and she groans.

    “I’m not telling you that.”

    Yelena glares at Sonya too, but she just keeps grinning at Kate, batting her eyelashes. “We will have to know what she looks like if we are to help.”

    Kate blinks slowly, knowing it’s a losing battle. And Sonya is not wrong. Getting help from Yelena and her means that they’ll have to know what Amanda actually looks like. Kate kisses her teeth, take a deep breath and holds out her hand for Sonya’s phone. She types in @APierson99, and taps on the right account, before sliding it back.

    Sonya picks up the phone, her face lighting up like a Christmas tree. She starts scrolling through the posts, but thankfully Yelena distracts Kate when she speaks. “It is also possible that she is working for Rojas.”

    Oh shit. Kate hasn’t thought of that.

    “Yeah I guess, if he knew I come back, he could have sent someone too.” Yelena nods, and opens her mouth to speak again but Sonya interrupts.

    “Oh damn, Kate. She is hot. Are her boobs real?”

    Kate just stares at her, unimpressed, biting down on the inside of her cheeks. Sonya makes a dismissive hand gesture, still smiling.

    “Right. One date.”

    Kate attempts to pull the phone from Sonya’s grasp from across the island, regretting telling her the handle, or even asking Yelena to come with when she was in the room. Sonya is lightening fast, of course, pulling it out of Kate’s reach before she can grab it. What’s worse is that now Yelena holds out her hand for the phone, her face annoyed at the interruption but intrigued.

    “Okay, now I have to see too.”

    Kate feels the hotness of her ears spread to her cheeks and she buries her face into her palms. A few seconds pass by, Sonya and Yelena scrolling through Amanda’s Instagram together while Kate regrets every decision she has ever made in her entire life. Yelena’s voice contains entirely too much mocking when Kate hears her speak.

    “She is very pretty…a bit too pretty. I understand why you would find it suspicious.” Sonya snickers and Kate pulls her hand away to glare at both of them.

    “Heyy! I took plenty of pretty girls on dates without them wanting to kill me or something. Yelena cocks an eyebrow with a smirk and goes back to scrolling through Sonya’s phone. Sonya leans back, apparently done stalking.

    “Okay, who asked out who?”

    Kate bites her tongue, looking at her for a moment.

    “How is that relevant?”

    She is trying to look innocent, but Kate is not buying it.

    “Well, if she was very pushy, it could mean she was trying to get close to you with an agenda.”

    Kate purses her lips, deeming it relevant enough.

    “I did. She nearly fell with an arm full of plates, I caught her. She was thankful, and I said she can pay me back with a drink. We ended up having dinner instead.”

    Yelena looks back up at Kate too, but she avoids looking at her. Sonya seems impressed enough however, smiling, but the teasing lilt is still thick in her voice. “How chivalrous. Who picked the place?”

    Kate lifts her jaw, feeling like she is being tested in some way, and refusing to be teased this time.

    “I did. Small Mexican place. And before you ask, we had fajitas and tequila. She paid and insisted I can next time. I walked her home, kissed her goodnight, and that was the end of it. When I got home, Yelena was there and told me somebody, Fisk, put out a hit on me, which kinda put a damper on things since. Anything else I missed? “ She looks challengingly at Sonya, who lifts her eyebrows, purses her lips. “So, if it turns out she is not working for Kingpin…”

    Yelena chimes in, not looking up from Sonya’s phone still.

    “Or Rojas.“ Sonya nods.

    “…Or Rojas. Will there be more than one date?”

    Kate takes a deep breath, clenching her jaw and feeling her annoyance beginning to boil over. “No.”

    Sonya doesn’t seem to notice, or care that Kate is close to snapping.

    “Why not?”

    Kate knows her voice is sharper than it probably should be, considering Sonya and Yelena are helping her, but she was already on edge from the whole topic, having to ask this favor to begin with and their teasing definitely did not help. Her tone is an octave lower than usual, and she can feel her face twist into a scowl, without her meaning to.

    “Well, if you haven’t noticed, everyone around me gets hurt or abducted or whatever. If she is actually who she says she is, I don’t want her to be collateral damage. And if she is working for Fisk, or Rojas, or another fucking drug lord after me that I don’t know about yet, I think it’s pretty self-explanatory.”

    Sonya finally seems to get the hint that this is a sensitive topic. For once, she backs down, taking a deep breath and leaning back against her chair.

    “Okay. That sounds like a perfectly normal date to me…”

    It was, Kate thinks bitterly. She takes a deep breath too, trying to calm herself. “…what makes you think she is hiding something?”

    Kate runs a hand through her hair, and tries to wrangle her voice into something resembling professional.

    “The timing, mostly. And like yeah, I know the fake name was pretty lame, but her figuring it out and not saying anything until I was practically breaking up with her, is pretty suspicious too.”

    Sonya nods, considering her words for a moment. Yelena speaks before she gathers her thoughts, finally putting Sonya’s phone on the counter.

    “Do you have a plan?”

    Kate is thankful for the topic change. She wets her lips and clears her throat. “A pretty basic one. I pick her up tonight at 8, take her somewhere we can talk, find out what she knows. I only need you, or well, you two to keep watch in case we are ambushed again or something.”

    Yelena nods, sighing too. She doesn’t seem to be happy to have to babysit Kate while she questions what is probably a random civilian, and Kate really can’t blame her. “Do you have a place in mind?”

    Kate shakes her head.

    “I was thinking a motel outside the city, or like an Airbnb…”

    She glances at Sonya, and quickly adds before she can draw the wrong conclusions. “…There aren’t too many people to worry about as collateral damage, if things go south.” Yelena purses her lips and flips her hair behind her shoulder, before turning to Sonya. “What about the place we found Tanya at?”

    Sonya seems thoughtful, drumming her fingers on the counter twice. Kate deflates a little, thankful for the discussion moving into more tactical topics.

    “That place? The poor girl would think Kate wants to murder her…if she is really a marketing person.”

    Sonya throws Kate a half-apologetic glance as Yelena snorts, but seems to keep thinking. Kate tries to come up with something too. Their food is now forgotten on the kitchen island now but Kate feeds a bite of eggs to Lucky distractedly.

    “A too long drive leaves you exposed and makes it too suspicious anyway. We should stick to places in the city. Within like 20 minutes maximum.”

    That is a good point. Kate nods and tries to narrow her mental search. “What about the flat in Soho?”

    Sonya asks this time, and Yelena immediately shakes her head.

    “Unless you and I hide under the bed, there is no way to properly cover it. Remember the Anya incident?”

    Sonya nods gravely, and Kate is almost tempted to ask. She gets her phone out to google New York Motel Nice instead, and looks at the recommendations. She crosses out a few places immediately. If Amanda really is just a civilian, Kate doesn’t want to scar her for life by taking her somewhere where looking at the carpet can give you hepatitis. Yelena and Sonya throw a few ideas back and forth, sometimes slipping into Russian, while Kate checks out hotels, motels, and Airbnbs at a reasonable distance.

    “What about this place?”

    She slides the phone across the kitchen island, and Sonya and Yelena look at it. Sonya’s eyebrows raise, and she looks at Yelena, as Kate does too. She seems to look at the pictures of the beautiful converted apartment for a long time. The upside is that it’s two flats opened up together to make it suitable for bigger parties, but it’s also separate enough that Sonya and Yelena can stay close, without actually being in there.

    “That could work. Where is it?”

    She scrolls down to the map, as Kate explains.

    “It’s not outside the city, but it’s a part of Brooklyn I know. Plenty of escape routes if we need them.“ Sonya and Yelena both nod, looking at the photos still. Sonya zooms in one of them where the window can be seen clearly.

    “We can probably set up a position on top of the building across too.” Yelena nods at Sonya’s words and the next two hours are spent strategizing, and making a list of gear they will need (which is way too long, in Kate’s opinion). Kate books the place meanwhile, which is probably only available at such short notice, because it’s ridiculously expensive, and can only be booked for a week minimum. She is extra thankful to be rich today. By noon, they have the place booked and a plan. Sonya stands up to clear the table. “When do we have to go to pick up the keys?”

    Kate checks the time, and gets up too.

    “By 5 pm.”

    “Okay, we have time to gather intel then.”

    Kate goes upstairs for her laptop, bringing with herself Yelena’s tablet too and they all settle onto Sonya’s couch, or in Kate’s case, the carpet next to the kitchen table. The next few hours are spent digging into Amanda’s life, trying to find a criminal connection. Kate starts to feel guilt sneaking up on her, because for the longest time, nothing turns up. Amanda seems entirely clean, and now it’s just feels like an invasion of her privacy. That is, until Yelena suddenly sits up.

    “Kate what did you say her brother’s name is?”

    She looks up from her own research, dread suddenly filling her.

    “Adam.”

    She can see Yelena’s jaw clench, as her eyes run over whatever she sees on her own screen. Kate is up from her place on the floor and beside Yelena in a second.

    “You found something?”

    She takes a place next to Yelena on the couch, sandwiching herself between her and Sonya. Yelena shows her the screen as she explains.

    “This is a transcript from the trial of Samuel Anderson, who was arrested for murder in 2019. He was offered a plea-deal for becoming a witness against Angelo Rojas, which he took. He was found dead in his cell 3 days later.”

    Kate reads the words on the screen.

    Q.: In your testimony earlier, you said you shot Mr. Huxley under somebody else’s direction. A.: Yes. I did.

    Q.: At whose direction was that?

    A.: I didn’t know at the time, but Angelo Rojas.

    Q.: Have you met this Mr. Rojas, Mr. Anderson?

    A.: No. I have…I only ever met this one guy. He was the only who told me what to do. Q.: Do you know his name?

    A.: He had a nickname, the Gringo. But I know his real name, Adam. Adam Pierson. Q.: Did Mr. Pierson give you explicit instructions to kill Mr. Huxley? A.: Yes. He even supplied the gun.

    Q.: But if Mr. Pierson instructed you to shoot Mr. Huxley, how do you Angelo Rojas was the one who gave the order?

    A.: After I…after I did how I was instructed, a guy showed up in my apartment. He wore a black leather suit, and had a sword. They call him the Ronin. Everybody in our business knew who he was, some type of…vigilante. He was going to kill me, and I only escaped because he got interrupted by my neighbors arriving home, and ringing the doorbell. After that, I went to the Gringo, I mean, Mr. Pierson, to complain and ask for money to hide. He said to take it up with his boss, Mr. Rojas.

    Q.: Was that the first time he named his employer?

    A.: First, yes. And also the last. I have never seen the guy again, and I was arrested a month later.

    Q.: The other person you named, the Ronin, is it possible he is working for Mr. Rojas too? Kate stops reading after that. Her jaw tightens too, and she takes a deep breath. It’s not a smoking gun, but it’s definitely something.

    Sonya is pushed against her side to read the transcript too, pressing her slightly into Yelena in turn and Kate feels like she is going to explode. She gets up quickly and starts pacing. “This is too much of a coincidence, right?

    “Well,…”

    She continues before Yelena can say more.

    “If Amanda’s brother was working for Rojas, then there is a good chance she had to know, right? Maybe she was part of it, maybe she wasn’t but this is too much of a coincidence.” “Kate, slow down.”

    “This is just great. I mean wow. It doesn’t explain how they knew I was going to be at F.E.A.S.T. that day, but it’s more likely than…”

    “Kate!”

    Yelena’s voice is sharp enough that it jerks her out of her rant. She turns back to Sonya and her on the couch, halting for a moment.

    “This is not good, but it is also not proof. Not yet. Just…calm down.” Kate exhales sharply, and almost starts pacing again.

    “I am calm.”

    Yelena raises an eyebrow at her, pointedly looking at her. Kate wets lips, and takes a deep breath.

    “Okay. Do you want to call Barton, ask him about Pierson?”

    Kate nods. That’s a good idea. She picks up her phone from the coffee table, dialing Clint. It rings and rings, but there is no answer.

    “He said he was going to look into Rojas. He might be out.”

    Kate is about to hang up, when the call connects.

    “Hey, honey.”

    Kate deflates a little, but tries to not let her voice show.

    “Hey Laura. How are you?”

    Laura chuckles a bit dryly.

    “Good, thanks. I assume you are looking for Clint?”

    “Yeah. Is he around?”

    There is a miniscule change only in Laura’s voice, but Kate can tell anyway. She is worried. “No. He went to look for that South-American friend of yours. He forgot his phone.” Kate gets the message: the kids are around, so Laura can’t talk. Clint went to look into Rojas, and will not be in contact until he gets a burner or comes back.

    She exhales, closing her eyes.

    “Okay, thanks. I…I am sorry to be pulling him away from home again. I told him I can handle it alone, and like, Yelena is around too…but you know how he is.” She sighs frustratedly, and Laura seems to match it. She glances at Sonya and Yelena who both seem to be preoccupied with their own work, but are probably listening too. “That I do know…It’s okay hon, it’s not your fault.”

    From the background, Kate can hear Nate’s voice.

    “Is that Kate?”

    Laura’s voice is back to the cheery-mom-voice Kate has heard in the Barton house many times, when heavy topics came up, and she wanted to keep it from the kids. “Yeah, baby. Do you want to talk to her?”

    Kate winces and sits down on an armchair by the wall. She rubs her face with her the hand not holding the phone, but makes sure her voice is light and cheery when the call is passed over to him.

    “Hey Nate, how you doing?”

    She listens to him chatter at her for a few minutes, her guilt intensifying. She hums and answers at all the relevant parts, but it mostly just reminds her that she is keeping Clint from his family. Again. Sonya leaves the room halfway through to order them lunch and Laura intervenes soon enough, and they say their goodbyes.

    “Bye Laura! Tell Lila and Coop I said hi to them too.”

    “Will do! And…take care of yourself Kate. New York is a big city…”

    The message is not lost within the coded language, and it makes Kate smile sadly. It’s a dangerous city for her, right now.

    “I always do.”

    “Well that’s just a lie…”

    Kate chuckles despite herself, Laura’s mom voice kind of soothing her. “… Anyways, come visit soon? Maybe you could convince Yelena to come too? The kids would love to meet her. Natasha told them a lot about her.”

    Kate glances at Yelena, finding her already looking but she looks away after a second. “Okay, um…I will try.”

    “Alright, hon. See you! Take care!”

    “Bye!”

    She hangs up, and exhales hard, her cheeks puffing out.

    “I take it Barton is not home?”

    Kate closes her eyes for a moment, and wets her lips before looking at Yelena. “No. He went to look into Rojas, and won’t be reachable for a few days.” Yelena nods. There is something in her face, as she looks away. She looks like she wants to ask more, but seems to struggle with herself. In the end she asks, voice hesitant. “Was that Barton’s son?”

    Kate smiles, a bit tiredly.

    “Yeah, Nate. And his wife, Laura before and after him.”

    Yelena nods. She is looking at her own screen, but her eyebrows are furrowed, lips pursed. She is silent for a moment, before she asks, not looking up.

    “What is he like?”

    Kate is a bit confused.

    “Who? Nate?”

    Yelena nods, gaze flicking towards her.

    “He is great. Really sweet and funny. Big heart for a little boy.”

    The smile on Yelena’s face is barely there, but Kate can see it nonetheless. She nods again, and wets her lips, still not looking at Kate.

    “Barton told me…he told me they thought he was going to be a girl. They were going to name him Natasha, but well. He is a boy, so…”

    Kate smiles too.

    “I didn’t know that. They…um…Laura actually told me I should ask you, if you wanted to come visit them sometime. Like, meet the kids and stuff. Apparently your sister told them a lot about you.”

    The surprise is clear on Yelena’s face, even just for a moment. Her eyes widen, lips parted. “Really?”

    They sit far away from each other, almost other ends of the room, but this is the closest Kate has felt to her since yesterday morning, when she asked Yelena to leave. The honest surprise, and softness in her face makes Kate want to move closer, but she doesn’t. “Yeah. I think she was like an aunt to them. There are like, a thousand pictures of her in their house.”

    Yelena looks down and away from Kate, and somehow, that was the wrong thing to say. Yelena’s face closes off and she just nods. Kate wants to ask why, or try to understand but Sonya walks back into the room, interrupting the conversation.

    “I ordered Indian. Hope Amanda doesn’t mind the garlic.”

    The moment is broken, and Kate is pulled back to today’s crisis. She gives Sonya a half- hearted glare, kissing the last thing on her mind right now. Sonya grins, but she is back to serious a moment later.

    They look up anything they can on Adam Pierson, but don’t find out a lot more than Kate has yesterday. Adam seems to have vanished off of the face of the Earth in 2018, and even before that, there is not much to be found on him. He doesn’t have any criminal history, he studied business at NYU, then worked for a few startups, until 2018 where he disappeared. There is an Adam Pierson serving life in Rikers, but he is 63 years old, and has been convicted in the ‘90s, so it’s probably not their guy.

    The food arrives, and Kate has to learn the hard way that Sonya is just as much of a fan of spicy foods as Yelena seems to be, and she is pretty sure she is still beet red and sweating by the time they have to start getting ready.

    The plan is simple. They all get ready, then they drive together to pick up the keys to the Airbnb. They set up what they need to there, then Kate goes to pick up Amanda, and Sonya and Yelena follow her with a second car. They all drive back to the Airbnb, Sonya will take position on the roof on the other side, while Yelena will stay in the flat adjacent to the one that Kate and Amanda go to. Kate questions Amanda, and if anything goes south, there are four possible exit routes. Five if you count the roof, which Kate does not. (Let’s say four and a half.)

    Kate goes upstairs to her own apartment and takes a thorough shower. Despite the fact that she does not consider this a date, or plans to see Amanda ever again, and that she is still unsure whether she is trying to play her or not, she does not want to show up drenched in spice-sweats.

    She is quite nervous about the evening, still secretly hoping that she is wrong about Amanda having ulterior motives, but finding herself unable to keep the thought out of her head. She tries to focus on just the next step as she washes her hair, then re-bandages her side and eventually it helps. Looking at herself in the fogged up mirror, she reminds herself to put on make-up to cover her bruises and walks to her bedroom. She puts on simple black underwear, and a matching sports bra, blow dries her hair, then stops in front of her closet. What does one wear to something that the other party probably thinks is date, but is actually an interrogation?

    She almost text Yelena, thinking maybe she has experience with this kind of thing, but it still feels weird, and the teasing would definitely not be worth it.

    She checks the time and realizes she is running a bit late. She runs to do her make up first instead of choosing an outfit, hoping the pressure will help to make the decision. In her stress, she goes a bit further with her make-up than she planned to. She justifies it by hoping the winged eyeliner will help to distract Amanda from the cuts and still-visible bruises on her face, and she almost reaches for lipstick before repeated knocks on the front door interrupt her.

    She is still in her bra and underwear, when she speed-walks to the door. She picks up the sword by habit at this point, and reaches for the doorknob when it opens. Yelena is in the process of saying something in Russian, when she stops dead in her tracks, looking at Kate. Sonya is right at her heels, staring at Kate too, but admittedly, Kate is not really paying attention to her. Yelena’s eyes drop to trail down her body, and Kate feels herself grow warm at her gaze. Yelena is only distracted for a second though, before her face becomes annoyed, closing her eyes and taking a deep breath. She opens them and pins Kate with a glare.

    “Why are you not ready?”

    “I am not complaining.”

    Sonya pipes up from behind her, and throws Kate a wink. Kate shakes herself off too, and feels the tips of her ears, her face and even her chest grow warm, tingling. “Sorry. I’ll be ready in 5 minutes.”

    She tosses the sword on the table, and hightails into her bedroom.

    “Do I need to remind you that it’s your date we will be late to?”

    Yelena’s annoyance can be heard even through the wall, and Kate rolls her eyes. “I said 5 minutes!”

    Sonya says something in Russian again, and Kate thinks she needs to download Duolingo or something because this is starting to annoy her. She has a weird déjà vu feeling about the thought, but she has no time to unpack it right now. She picks out a clean pair of jeans, and a white button down shirt that she half-tucks into them, hoping it will hide the bruises that litter her arms too. She quickly takes an ibuprofen, to dull the pain in her body, because she needs to be sharp tonight.

    With no time to do anything with her hair, she just runs a hand through it, hoping for a purposefully disheveled look and picks up a hair tie from her dresser in case she needs it later, putting it around her wrist. She exits the room 3 and a half minutes later, and breezes by Yelena and Sonya, quickly putting on a pair of ankle boots, not paying them any attention. That is, until Sonya wolf-whistles.

    Kate turns to them, rolling her eye as she hops on one foot to pull on one of the boots, but she can’t help the small smug purse of her lips on her face. Despite her nervousness, it feels good to be told she cleans up nice at least.

    “Damn, Kate Bishop. You should go on fake dates more often, you look amazing.” Kate looks down on herself, ignoring the anxiety the word fake puts into her, then at Yelena and Sonya. She can’t help but frown.

    “Thanks! You guys look really, um…good too.”

    She expected practical outfits, but the tight, black tactical suits make her question whether her outfit is appropriate. This is a mission after all, even if technically she is going undercover. She glances back at her bedroom, considering changing or at least putting her own suit underneath the shirt as well.

    “Do not even think about it...”

    Yelena says, her voice laded with tired frustration. Kate who was ready to take a step back towards her bedroom halts.

    “…we are already late as it is.”

    Kate deflates, nodding, and looking them over again. At least Yelena and Sonya are matching her in the level of make-up they are wearing. They both did their eyes and Sonya wears a bright, red lipstick while Yelena has a more muted, darker nude on. She sighs deeply, and starts to gather her things. Neither of them have any weapons visible on them, but Yelena has a tactical bag at her feet, and Sonya has one on her shoulder.

    “Fine…This makes me feel like you guys are my body guards or something. It’s weird.” She says it as she puts her wallet, phone and a pair of nude lipstick in her small leather backpack, along with the sword and a pair of gums.

    “We basically are. Just a great use of our talents, really.”

    Yelena says, as she watches Kate zoom around the room, clearly displeased. Kate swallows her response that she is more than welcome to stay home. Yelena continues, her voice getting more and more annoyed as Kate gathers one item after the other.

    “How is it that it took you 15 minutes longer to put on jeans and a shirt, than it did for us to put together full tactical gear?”

    Kate huffs, while trying to remember if she is forgetting anything.

    “I had to shower. I smelled like a sweaty spice market. Oh, thanks for reminding me.” She pulls out her perfume from her bag, and sprays some onto her wrist, rubbing it onto her neck with a pointed glare at Yelena. Sonya snorts, and Yelena continues with her dry-voiced criticism.

    “I am pretty sure she will not care what you smell like, if she is trying to kill you.” It’s a low blow, and Kate scowls as she picks up her quiver and archery bag from the wall by the door. She understands Yelena’s frustration at her being late, but she doesn’t need to be such a bitch about it.

    “And I will not get anything out of her, if she refuses to get into the car with me because I smell like I hunt vampires for a living.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes, and picks up their own tactical bag by the door. “Are you finally ready, or do we have to wait until you put on an evening gown for your fake date first?”

    Kate scoffs as picks up her favorite black leather jacket, and puts it over her arm. She marches to the front door, opening it wide for the two shorter women to pass. “I am ready, let’s go.”

    Chapter 16

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes They take the elevator down to the garage, Yelena and Sonya getting out two levels below hers. Sonya keeps throwing her amused glances, and playful once overs while Yelena stares ahead, refusing to look at her. The tension from yesterday is definitely back now, their frustration with each other turning the air around them thick. Sonya seems absolutely unphased by it, but Kate has the urge to fidget or pick a fight again. She understands Yelena is annoyed about this mission, and she can even understand if she thinks it’s a waste of time. She even gets her being pissed at Kate taking so long to get ready, and them having to wait around for her. But she has a legitimate reason to be suspicious of Amanda now, and they are not actually late from anywhere just yet.

    She gets out on her level, glancing at Yelena one more time, but she doesn’t look back at her. Kate can’t believe she is so petty. It sends another spark of annoyance down her spine. She directs her question to Sonya instead of her.

    “Do you have the address?”

    Sonya nods, waving at her with an unbothered smile, and the doors close between them. Kate huffs as she walks to her Range Rover. If Amanda is playing her, there is no need to let her know what others Kate has, she thinks distractedly. Tossing her archery bag and her jacket onto the back seat, she gets behind the wheel, slamming the door behind herself harder than she has to.

    Where the fuck does Yelena get off speaking to her like that anyway. She took a little longer to get ready, so what. It’s still barely past 4 pm, they have plenty of time to make it to the Airbnb and set up everything in time. And sure, this mission is a bit more than simply gathering intel on Fisk…or Rojas, she reminds herself…But Yelena was so offended yesterday at the notion of Kate wanting her to leave, and now she is annoyed that she asked her to help?

    It’s really fucking unfair.

    She spends most of the ride to Brooklyn fuming, so much that she almost forgets to be nervous about tonight. It’s just so annoying. Yelena can be so soft, kind when she wants to be. She has been great to Kate ever since she arrived. But now?

    Kate guesses she is probably tired and hurt from the last few days too, but she is being a bitch for no comprehensible reason, picking fights and mocking her left and right. And any time Kate thinks they are over it, and they have a moment like after the phone call with Nate, or even the harmless teasing in the kitchen in the morning, they are back to square one. Kate kind of regrets telling her to leave, because that seems to be the source of all of Yelena’s bitchiness, but she is also not. She wanted to keep Yelena safe, and she is not going to apologize for that. Especially not if she keeps treating her this way. She arrives at the address of the Airbnb after about 40 minutes in the afternoon traffic, with around 15 minutes to 5 pm. Yelena and Sonya are already there, parked upfront. Kate parks her car in front of theirs and gets out with a metaphorical cloud above her head. She walks over to their car, and Sonya rolls down the window. Yelena just stares ahead in the passenger seat.

    “I’ll go get the keys, okay? You guys would raise some eyebrows.”

    She is talking to Sonya again, ignoring Yelena like she is ignoring her. Sonya gives her a smirk.

    “We always do, Kate Bishop. But okay.”

    Kate sighs and turns away, not in the mood for the playful banter. Going inside, she finds the host waiting. He is a young guy in his late twenties, probably only a couple of years older than her. He is tall, almost a head taller than her, and well built. He introduces himself as John and leads the way upstairs to show the flat, while continuously checking her out. She is still so annoyed over Yelena that she barely has the brain capacity to be put off by him too. The apartment is really nice at least. Still overpriced, but beautiful nonetheless. It’s a spacious loft, decorated in industrial style with exposed bricks and designer furniture. As he shows her around, she tries to flex her role-playing muscles. She gushes over the last-minute, week-long bachelorette party she and her friends are going to have. He seems to be buying it, asking her all kinds of questions.

    She tells him they all met in college, and how they all live in different cities across the states but still keep in touch. For some unintelligible reason, she tells him they were in the same acapella group when he asks how they all met. He is thankfully too occupied by checking out her ass in the jeans she chose, to get hung up on her answer.

    He shows her around the various rooms of the interconnected flats. There are separate kitchens for both, and 6 bathrooms between them. The space is bathed in natural light, thanks to the huge windows spreading over the walls. All in all, it takes over 30 minutes for him to show her around before he finally leads them downstairs again. He stops on the sidewalk, turning back to her.

    “One more thing, there are some ground rules.”

    Desperate to get rid of him so she just returns his smile.

    “Sure.”

    “No smoking inside. Cigarettes or weed, okay? It’s really hard to get rid of the smell.” “Okay, of course.”

    “And no loud music after midnight, the neighbors are chill but not that chill, you know?” He gives her a lopsided smile, that she thinks is meant to be flirty. She keeps her own, hopefully non-flirty smile on her face, giving an awkward salute. He is handsome, but she really needs him to go. They are slowly becoming actually late.

    “Keep it on the DL. Noted.”

    He chuckles at her dorky move. What the fuck, Kate?

    “Alright. That’s it. So, Kate, are you from New York?”

    Internally, she imagines screaming into a pillow.

    “Yeah.”

    He gives her a once-over and pulls his lips to a charming grin.

    “Well, after your friends leave. If you ever wanna have a good time, you have my number.” Kate can feel that her smile is more of a grimace now, but he doesn’t seem to. “Cool, I’ll…keep that in mind.”

    He finally, thankfully, gives her a parting wink and fishes in his pockets for a key. He hands it over with one last smolder, holding onto it for longer than he has to. “See you, Kate.”

    Kate pulls the keys from his grasp with an awkward smile, forcing her tone to be polite. “See ya, John.”

    He gets in the car that Kate parked behind, a white Mercedes, and Kate busies herself by pretending to look around her backseat so she doesn’t have to keep eye contact. When he finally drives off, she exhales. Fucking finally.

    A car door slams shut behind her, as she picks up her archery bag. She closes her car door and looks over to Sonya’s Jaguar to see Yelena only, walking to the trunk of their car. Kate waits for her to get her own gear bag, but Yelena seems to be content to ignore her again. “Where is Sonya?”

    Yelena walks by her, barely sparing her a glance. Her annoyed, cold face is enough to throw Kate back to the depths of her frustration within 5 seconds.

    “She is setting up the vantage point across.”

    Kate looks over to the building on the other side of the road, but can’t see any sign of her, so she follows Yelena into the building. Yelena doesn’t speak to her as they take the stairs to the first floor, or when Kate opens the door and lets her inside.

    Fine. Kate can be petty too.

    She throws the keys onto the table by the entrance, and ignores Yelena, as she takes in the space. For the next 45 minutes, they somehow get into an unspoken competition over who will refrain from breaking the tense silence first. At least that’s what Kate thinks they are doing.

    Yelena gets to unpacking her gear, walking around the apartment. Kate catches her glancing at her a couple of times, but she never actually opens her mouth to speak, so she doesn’t either. Yelena soon uses the door between the two apartments to go over to the other, presumably to set up her own waiting area.

    In turn, Kate looks for a hiding place for her bow and arrows, choosing to deposit them behind a curtain bracketing the huge open windows. She contemplates finding another one for her sword but decides to keep it in her bag instead. If things go to shit during the trip here already, at least she will have something with her, and won’t have to rely on Yelena and Sonya entirely.

    She really doesn’t understand how Yelena can be so pissed, but she herself is definitely over it at this point. She goes to check out the fire escapes, on both sides of the building and familiarizes herself with the layout, and their escape routes. She hears Yelena rummage around in one of the rooms and considers going to talk to her, but her pride wins out. In about half an hour, she runs out of things to do. She spends the next few minutes pretending to be busy, arranging and re-arranging furniture in a way that she thinks would be helpful if it came down to a fight but soon even that is as finished as it can be. The more the silence stretches between them, the heavier the weight in Kate’s chest gets. God, she is fucking done with this.

    The sun is slowly setting outside, lighting up the apartment with warm, orange sunlight. Kate checks the time. It’s a few minutes past 7 o’clock. It’ll be showtime soon. With nothing else left to do, she gets her lipstick out of her bag, a matte nude color, and goes up to one of the many mirrors around the living room. She starts applying it when Yelena comes across the door separating the two apartments.

    Kate glances up and sees the annoyed curl of Yelena’s lips in the reflection, and the eye-roll she gives. It’s the last straw. She is so fucking done with this.

    “Okay, what’s your problem?”

    Kate whirls around, rounding on Yelena just as she goes for her tactical bag on the coffee table. She glances at her, eyes flitting down her form, and lips curling up in disdain. “I have no problem.”

    She pulls a few gun magazines from her bag, and what appears to be a hand-grenade. She is still not looking at her, and Kate resists the childish urge to slap them out of her hand. “Yeah, you do. You have been a bitch all afternoon. There is obviously something. So please, enlighten me. I am dying to know.”

    The tension in Kate feels like a candle, held way too close to a barrel of gunpowder. The whole day, this evening, it’s already stressful and shit enough. Yelena’s mysterious and infuriating behavior is just the last drop in a glass that has been filling up all day. It probably has something to do with the leftover tension from yesterday too. Whatever. Kate doesn’t care. She feels ready to blow up.

    Yelena looks like she is ready to let this explode too. She drops the items in her hand onto the table and rounds on Kate. She steps closer, her eyes boring into Kate’s, her tone practically dripping with danger.

    “I have been a bitch? I have been stabbed two days ago, yet here I am preparing for your stupid date with some marketing woman, while you…”

    She points at Kate, her finger digging into her chest.

    “…you spent the entire afternoon strutting around and playing dress-up.” Kate’s heart pangs at the mention of Yelena getting stabbed, but she is too pissed now to get bogged down by that. Especially after hearing the second half of Yelena’s sentence. “I haven’t been strutting around. I am putting in an effort because I don’t want her getting suspicious in case she is not who she says she is.”

    Yelena scoffs, turning away to pick up one of the magazines distractedly. Her tone is dripping with sarcasm.

    “Oh, yes. I am sure she would be very suspicious if you showed up without lipstick, eyeliner, and smelling like a cat in heat.”

    Kate’s mind reels. What the fuck does that even mean? Her tone drops, as she repeats slowly. “A cat…in heat?”

    Yelena drops the magazine in her hand onto the couch. She lifts her chin as she turns back to Kate, eyes dropping to look her over, lips pursed.

    “That is what I said.”

    Kate shakes her head, eyes wide, throwing her hands up.

    “What the fuck does that even mean?”

    Yelena leans closer, and sniffs loudly, eyes boring into hers.

    “It means I can smell your perfume across the room. It makes you look desperate. So does the big make-up.”

    Kate runs a frustrated hand through her already messy hair, gesturing at Yelena’s face. “You are literally wearing more makeup than I am.”

    Completely unphased, Yelena runs the tip of her tongue over the bottom of her teeth, peeking out between her lips. Kate resists the urge to look down on it and holds Yelena’s gaze. “Yes, and it didn’t take me 2 hours to put it on.”

    Kate feels ready to scream. Gritting her teeth, she resists that urge to, but her voice strains with the effort to hold it back.

    “It took me 45 minutes to get ready because I…”

    She stops in the middle of the sentence, exhaling sharply through her nose, and kissing her teeth.

    “…you know what, no. No. I don’t have to fucking justify myself. Yesterday you got mad because I told you to go home, now you are mad because you have to be here. Make up your mind.”

    Yelena shakes her head, stepping even closer to her.

    “I am not mad because I have to be here. I am mad because you spend more time… She gestures vaguely at Kate, pausing to think of the right word.

    “…preening yourself for your date, than actually doing your job.”

    Kate grabs her forehead, resisting the urge to rub her face and mess up her makeup. “It’s a fake date, Yelena. How many times do I have to say, I am preparing to…” Yelena interrupts her, voice thick with condescension.

    “Oh, so you are aware that it is fake?”

    Kate has to step away, to throw her hands up again.

    “Jesus Christ, Yelena. Of course, I am aware it’s fucking fake.”

    Speaking through her teeth, Yelena gives her yet another once over, eyes trailing over Kate. “It certainly does not seem that way.”

    It makes Kate feel warm all over, and that in turn, just makes her feel even more pissed. Fuck Yelena for making her feel like this, and hammering in the fact that this is a fake date. Kate knows.

    She lashes out, aiming to hurt Yelena back.

    “You know what? If you went back to Ohio, like I asked you to, you wouldn’t have to deal with my strutting and preening.”

    Yelena’s face twitches, and she steps closer, right into Kate’s space to practically hiss into her face.

    “Stop saying that. I do not want to go back to Ohio.”

    Kate leans down an inch, hissing right back, chest heaving.

    “Then what do you want?”

    There is a flicker of something, on Yelena’s face, and Kate’s stomach twists. Yelena blinks, eyes dropping to her lips for less than a second, and Kate notices. She stops breathing entirely for a moment. Oh, fucking hell.

    What the fuck?

    Is Yelena jealous?

    Yelena doesn’t back down and deflects almost immediately, her voice low, words slow, dangerous.

    “I want you, to stop wasting my time.”

    Kate takes a step back before she does something stupid. Like slap Yelena again. Or kiss her. “Oh, so now I am wasting your time. Great. Nice, thanks.”

    Yelena follows her step back, seemingly not able to tune her anger down, now that they started to let things out. She stares into Kate’s eyes, and the glint in them feels like a challenge.

    “Yes, you are. Do you even know where the exits are? Or were you too busy making yourself pretty to check that?”

    Kate stands her ground, jaw clenching. Her muscles feel all locked up, ready for something. To grab Yelena, and shake her until she comes to her senses…or kiss her, to finally shut her up. To stop Yelena’s pretty little mouth from curling so cruelly.

    She pushes down on the urge, clenching her fists by her sides to stop her hands from moving. “Of course I fucking know where the exits are. I am well aware of what we are doing here.” Yelena’s eyes drop to her body again, before finding Kate’s again. To her, it looks like Yelena is not even trying to hold anything back anymore, just spewing out whatever venomous thing comes to her mind next.

    “You are not even wearing clothes for a mission. You look like a failed musician.” Kate is becoming more and more sure that Yelena is actually jealous. Her mind refuses to wrap around it, and she swallows the question she desperately wants to throw in Yelena’s face. Instead, she attempts to push the argument back to logical grounds but fails to keep her confused anger out of her voice.

    “I was going to put on a suit if you recall, and you told me to, I quote, ’don’t even think about it’.”

    Licking her lips in anger, Yelena refuses to come down with her.

    “Yeah, because you already made us late by spending half an hour picking out underwear. What, do you think she will want to see you naked while she attempts to kill you?” What the…

    Yelena’s cruel words cut at the tethers holding Kate back, which keep her from throwing the obvious in Yelena’s face that would derail this whole conversation. She makes one last attempt at keeping this argument on solid ground.

    “Oh my God, Yelena. I am like sixty percent sure she is trying to kill me, or play me, or something. I don’t want to sleep with her.”

    For a second it looks like her attempt has worked. Yelena is silent, looking back at her, eyes hard.

    But after a heartbeat, she lifts her chin again and looks Kate straight in the eyes. “I beat you up several times, you still wanted to fuck me the other night…” Kate is speechless for a moment, stunned by Yelena’s boldness. Yelena steps closer, and her voice is quiet and softer, but it feels more cutting than anything else before. “…Maybe I should have let you. Maybe then you wouldn’t be so desperate for this if I did.” It’s the last straw.

    The tethers holding Kate back snap at the cruelty of the words, and she steps in too, only a hair width of space between them now. Yelena’s pupils are blown, almost black as their eyes remain holding each other, but otherwise, she just holds her ground, jaw clenching and nostrils flaring.

    “Let me? Pleeaase, like we both don’t know you were practically aching for it…” Yelena opens her mouth, probably to protest and Kate goes in for the kill, leaning even closer. “Maybe I should have done it. Maybe then, you wouldn’t be so jealous.” Eyes widening for a moment, Yelena reels back. She snorts, then her lips curl into a smile that holds absolutely no amusement.

    “Pfft. Please. Don’t be ridiculous.”

    Kate is unphased. She lifts an eyebrow, her chin too, starring at Yelena, daring her to deny it further. As always, Yelena rises to the challenge. She leans back in, looking up at her. Her tone is mocking and spoken so close to Kate’s skin, she feels Yelena’s breath puff against her chin.

    “And what exactly would I have to be jealous of, Kate?...”

    For once, her name sounds like a swear word coming out of Yelena’s mouth as she turns the tables on her in a heartbeat. Her voice drips even lower than usual, and her eyes drop to Kate’s mouth for a second again, this time on purpose, before meeting her eyes again. “…A fake date with a woman who is probably trying to kill you?”

    Kate wants to say yes. Because it seems like that’s exactly what’s happening right now. She never gets to.

    The front door opens, Sonya pausing at the entrance, taking them in.

    Yelena continues to hold her gaze, but neither of them moves or speaks again. The electricity of the moment is still crackling between them, but now it’s unable to spark into anything more.

    Kate’s mind starts slowly catching up to what just went down.

    She takes a step back and tries to shove down the urge to continue this. She pushes down on the desire to kiss Yelena, just to wipe off the smug, cruel smile that slides onto her face. Yelena gives her one last look, dark and angry still, before she turns away. Picking up the magazines she took out of her bag earlier, she turns towards the door separating the two apartments and walks off.

    Kate turns too, going back to the mirror and checking her makeup, just to spite her. “Everything okay?”

    Sonya asks, her voice void of teasing for once. Kate slides a hand through her hair, ruffling it up a little.

    “Yeah, just fucking peachy.”

    She sees Sonya’s eyebrows shoot up her forehead in the mirror, glancing at the door Yelena disappeared behind.
