    “Oookay.”

    She enters the apartment, looking around.

    “Nice place.”

    Kate just hums, her mind still on her argument with Yelena. Despite her denial, she is one hundred percent sure that her assessment is correct. For whatever reason, Yelena is jealous. It makes absolutely no sense, but Kate is way too tired and pissed to try to wrap her head around it anyway.

    Yelena comes back a moment later, her eyes still dark and hard as she glances at Kate. They darken even further when she seems to notice Kate is back by the mirror. “Ready to go? It’s almost half-past seven.”

    Sonya directs the question at both of them. Before Kate could answer, Yelena snorts, walking up to her bag.

    “Ask Kate. She is the one wasting time all afternoon.”

    Kate bristles, unable to push down on her anger, but she forces her voice to be calm nonetheless, clenching her jaw.

    “Just one more sec.”

    She knows it’s petty, but if Yelena wants to continue to be a bitch about this, so can Kate. She undoes the top two buttons holding her shirt together and reaches for her leather jacket. Pulling it around her shoulder, she shakes out her hair, and ruffles it once more, making sure to take her time. She checks herself in the mirror one more time, before turning back. Purposefully not looking at Yelena, she addresses Sonya with a faux smile. “Now I am ready.”

    Walking over to the side-table, she picks up the keys and holds out one of the rings to Yelena, turning to look at her. Her eyes have darkened even more, but her lips are pursed in an unhappy, mocking smile.

    “The keys to the other apartment.”

    They are torn from her grasp by an unnecessarily forceful movement. Kate feels the corners of her lips twitch up into a smug smile, at having successfully riled Yelena up further. Sonya watches the interaction silently, probably trying to guess what she missed. Kate picks up her backpack and turns to open the door.

    “Just one more thing, Kate.”

    Yelena’s voice halts her and she turns back. Yelena holds out an earpiece for her, the smile on her face just as faux as Kate’s earlier.

    “Your earpiece. You know, for the mission…Do try to remember it is fake.” Kate’s nostrils flare but she returns the fake smile and takes it.

    “Oh, I know, don’t worry.”

    The smile drops off her face as soon as she turns around and practically tears the door open. She goes down the stairs, not waiting to see if Sonya and Yelena follow. The fucking audacity of this woman. Like Kate isn’t aware this whole fucking evening is a mission. Like she doesn’t know she can’t have anything, including a fucking date, without it being twisted in some way, part of all the other shit that fucking Kingpin and her mother have tainted. Like she needs another reminder, when she has spent all day, the whole week actually, getting hit over the head with the fact that all her human relationships are somehow tangled up in this, whether she wants them or not.

    She slams the car door with a force enough that the whole car jostles to the side, just as Sonya and Yelena exit the building. She spares them one glance, looking at Yelena’s downturned lips and Sonya’s tense face, and she huffs.

    Fuck this. Fuck all of it.

    She starts up the car with the push of a button and puts the earpiece into her left ear. She drives off without another look at them, and barely checks her side mirror as she pulls into the street.

    She is aware that her anger is only partially directed at Yelena, but the cruelty that she spoke to Kate with, the venom dripping from her voice has left her wired and furious. She unconsciously latches onto that, instead of uselessly getting angry at her mom or Fisk again. And what the fuck was all of this? If Yelena has a problem with this night, why the fuck can’t she say it like a normal person, instead of turning Kate’s already shitty day into fucking hell. Why did she not say anything before they left, or why did she say yes in the first place? She fumes almost all the way over to Amanda’s place, completely forgetting to be nervous about the mission. She purposefully ignores the stilted Russian conversation she hears through her earpiece. She is not going to give them, her, the satisfaction of acknowledging it by complaining.

    She is still angry by the time she pulls up in front of Amanda's building at 7:50, Finally, she takes a few calming breaths, attempting to let go of her anger. She checks in the mirror, and the green Jaguar is parked on the other side of the street, about 50 feet behind her. “Are you ready, Kate?”

    Sonya’s voice speaks in her ear, finally in English, addressing her. She takes a deep breath and checks herself in the sun visor’s mirror again. The swelling on her face has gone down completely by now but a few bruises shine through her concealer and there is no hiding the cut on her eyebrow and the one on her chin.

    “Yeah, sure.”

    She fishes around her bag to find her mascara and reapplies it, mostly to have something to do. She tries to think about how she will question Amanda, without giving away anything in return but doesn’t get far. She’ll have to wing it. With 2 minutes to 8 o’clock, Amanda appears at the entrance of the building.

    Kate takes a deep breath and gulps.

    “She’s here.”

    She gets out of the car, and her stomach twists at the way Amanda’s face lights up. She is wearing another dress, floral and flowy, and a tan leather jacket. Kate kind of forgot how pretty she was, even after going through her Instagram. Mostly being focused on gathering intel, and trying to find out if Amanda is playing her, she didn’t actually pay attention to the girl herself. She remembers now.

    She is also distinctly aware of the fact that Yelena and Sonya are watching. Smiling at Amanda, she tries to calm down, get into the right headspace. She needs to sell this. “Hi.”

    As Amanda gets closer, her smile falls off her face, overtaken by concern. “Oh my god! Your face!...”

    She comes up to Kate, immediately stepping into her space and touching her face gently. “…What happened? Are you okay?”

    Kate chuckles a bit awkwardly but doesn’t pull away from the touch.

    “Yeah, yeah. I’m good. Just perks of the job, you know.”

    Amanda looks her face over again, her thumb grazing Kate’s cheekbone once, before meeting her eyes again. Her voice is not judgemental, but she is not holding back her curiosity. "Well…I don't, actually. I still have no idea what an independent security contractor does." In her ear, Sonya snorts then says something in Russian. Yelena's voice is dry as sandpaper as she answers.

    Ignoring them, Kate decides to test the waters and leans closer. She keeps her voice light, but her eyes hold Amanda’s.

    “If I told you, I’d have to kill you.”

    Amanda’s eyes widen, then she laughs, the sound a bit nervous. Okay, maybe with her mom about to go on trial for actual murder, among other things, Kate should probably not make jokes about that…just in case Amanda is an actually nice, non-cartel-employed citizen. She looks to the side, before smiling a bit self-depreciatingly.

    “Sorry, uh, bad joke. Um…I’m a bit nervous.”

    Amanda’s face softens, and she steps even closer, chest brushing against hers. “I’m too.”

    “Ugh, good god.” Sonya proclaims in her ear, and Kate resists the urge to kiss her teeth in annoyance. She focuses on Amanda, standing close to her, palm still on her jaw. Her smile is a bit shy when she speaks to Kate.

    “Hi.”

    She is either a really great actress or she is sincere. Kate can’t tell yet. She slips back into character, still struggling to ignore the fact that Sonya and Yelena are in her ear, watching and hearing them.

    “Hi yourself.”

    Amanda’s smile widens before she leans up and kisses her. With Yelena riling her up barely half an hour ago, Kate can’t stop her mind from jumping to her for a second. For the fraction of a moment, she stiffens but before Amanda can pull away, she closes her eyes and forces herself to ease into it.

    Sliding one arm around Amanda’s waist she kisses back. It remains chaste, just a greeting but Kate’s ears burn nonetheless. Thankfully her comms remain silent. Amanda pulls back after a few seconds, opening her eyes to look at her.

    “Do you want to come up to talk?”

    Kate’s mind races trying to come up with a good excuse on why she can’t. “Uuum.”

    She is stalling, with Amanda still looking at her.

    “Kate, do not go up to her place. Stick to the plan.”

    Yelena’s annoyed voice shakes her up, and she feels her own irritation flare again. What kind of fucking amateur does Yelena think she is? She shakes her head, dropping the attempt to come up with an excuse.

    “No, thanks. Um, I have a place in mind.”

    Amanda blinks and glances at Kate’s car behind her, for barely a second, but she sees it. “Are you sure? I really don’t mind.”

    Kate feels her suspicions rise again. She really does need an excuse now. Wracking her mind, she says the first thing that comes to mind.

    “Yeah. I’m sure. If we go up I’m pretty sure we…, um, I will get sidetracked...” She adds a lopsided smile and hopes to convey her meaning while internally screaming at herself. Why, Kate?

    “And we really should talk.”

    Amanda grins at that, her face smoothing out, and eyes dropping to her lips for a second. She leans in and gives her another peck on the lips.

    “Okay.”

    She walks by Kate, and she releases a breath. Walking behind her, Kate ignores another Russian comment in her ear, Sonya again, and opens the door for Amanda. She slips in, and Kate closes the door, before walking around the car.

    “Nice save, Kate Bishop.”

    Sonya speaks to her this time, and she glances over at the green Jaguar. Sonya and Yelena are both looking at her, but she doesn’t have time to take note of their expressions. Her eyes meet Yelena’s for barely one second, but she has to look away in case Amanda is watching. She slips into the driver’s seat and smiles at Amanda over the center console, before starting the engine.

    “So, what happened to your face?”

    Amanda asks before she has a chance to start her own conversation. Kate checks the side mirror, before pulling into traffic. It gives her a second to consider whether this is a suspicious question or a completely valid one. She settles on completely valid. “I…well, like I said the case I’m working on is a bit more complicated than we first thought. There was an incident the other day, but nothing too bad. They just got a few lucky hits in.” Hoping to keep it vague, she smiles at Amanda again.

    “So, what does being a security consultant actually mean?”

    The desire to rub her face is strong, and Sonya’s and Yelena talking Russian in her ear doesn’t help.

    “It’s uh…I can’t really talk about it, sorry. It’s classified.”

    Something crosses Amanda’s face, that Kate thinks is annoyance, but it’s hard to tell without looking at her directly. There is an awkward silence for about a few seconds. Feeling the pressure to say something more, she speaks again.

    “I’m sorry. I…I can’t give you specifics. But like, broad strokes version is that I offer security expertise to people or companies that need it. I help them if there is a security threat, help them handle it.”

    She turns to Amanda for a second as they arrive at a red light. She looks intrigued, but not overly so.

    Sonya speaks in her ear again.

    “This would have been so much faster if we just kidnapped her and asked her straight up.” Then, Yelena.

    “What a bullshit answer. Who even buys that?”

    Kate wants to roll her eyes, but she can’t with Amanda looking at her. She regrets not telling them specifically to shut up before they parted. Thankfully, Amanda does seem to buy that. “Did you get into security because of your mom?”

    It’s another valid question, with a very complicated answer. One that Kate can’t and doesn’t want to explain. She settles for a half-truth instead, while taking a left turn. “Yeah. Kinda. She um…she wanted me to take over the company in a few years. But obviously, with like…what happened, Bishop Security is no longer around. So, I needed something in the same field, because that’s like, the only thing I’m good at. But um…for the record, Bishop Security was my dad’s first.”

    Amanda’s nod is visible from the corner of her eyes.

    “I saw that he passed away. I’m really sorry.”

    The annoyance she feels is an old friend that Kate stomps down on. She doesn’t really like people, especially ones she doesn’t know well, commenting on her father. But Kate did bring him up…

    “Yeah, it’s…thanks.”

    Amanda probably feels that this is not a topic she is comfortable discussing, because she backs off.

    “Do you like it? The job I mean.”

    Kate doesn’t think about how to answer.

    “Yeah, it has its moments.”

    She gives a quick smile to Amanda and she returns it, before licking her lips. “It sounds lonely though.”

    The sound of a horn from behind them gives Kate the perfect excuse to look away. She glances in the rearview mirror and sees that it was Sonya.

    “Get moving Kate, we don’t have all day.”

    Pressing on the gas, she clenches her jaw at both Amanda’s and Sonya’s words as the car starts moving.

    “Yeah. Sometimes.”

    She hopes it’s neither too dismissive, nor too intriguing to result in more questioning in this particular topic. She gets her wish. Clearing her throat beside Kate, Amanda begins to apologize.

    “I am really sorry if like, looking you up was an invasion of your privacy. I wasn’t trying to stalk you or anything. I promise.”

    “Yet she did it anyway.” Sonya murmurs ever-so-helpfully in her ear. Kate wets her lips and is quick to shoot that down. She needs Amanda to ease up, if she wants to gather any information from her.

    “It’s okay. I’m not…mad. It was just…I thought it was best if we talked in person.” With another smile, Amanda nods.

    “I am glad you did. And I, um…really understand why you told me a different name.” Kate forces a smile onto her face, a bit unsure of how to answer. This time, it’s her clearing her throat. About this, at least she can be truthful.

    “I am sorry for lying. My mom…after she was arrested, there were a couple of rough months, with a lot of people trying to like, uh, take advantage. So when I got back I wasn’t really ready to like, advertise that I’m back. You know?”

    “Well…No? I mean, I can’t say I know what that feels like. But I am really sorry. It sounds really shitty.”

    Amanda sounds sincere, and Kate gives her an honest smile too.

    “Yeah, it’s…It’s okay.”

    Amanda gulps and glances out the windshield before looking at Kate again. “How were they trying to take advantage?”

    Lips pulled to the side, pursing, Kate tries to decide how much to tell. Not just to Amanda, but Yelena and Sonya listening too.

    “Uhm…I…Like I said, I kind of went through a rough patch after the whole thing. So, there were a few people, who I thought of as friends. They took me out drinking, got me drunk, and recorded some things, only to give it to TMZ.”

    She hesitates before continuing. If someone looks her up, the story eventually turns up despite her efforts to get rid of it. It feels weird to discuss it either way. “One…a girl I dated back in high school, she got in contact again. And like, I was really in a bad spot, and I was happy for the um, distraction. After that, she made a YouTube video where she talked about our lives. My mum’s and mine I mean. Half of it was completely made up. She used evidence of us hooking up again to prove herself as reliable.” She licks her lips, glancing at Amanda but also aware of Yelena and Sonya listening in. “These are the highlights I guess. There were a few others, but these two…yeah, so. That’s it.”

    Amanda for her part looks compassionate, looking at her with warm eyes. “God, that sounds awful. I promise, I’m not…I am not trying to take advantage. I really had no idea who you were when we first met.”

    Kate glances at her again, trying to gauge if Amanda is honest. She does look like she is, but Kate has been fooled before. She does her best to give a convincing smile. “Yeah, it’s…It wasn’t great. But moving to LA helped a lot.”

    There are a few moments of silence, and Kate is glad when they finally pull up to the building of the Airbnb. She puts her arm behind Amanda’s headrest as she reverses into a parking spot, feeling her eyes on her.

    “What?”

    Kate glances at her, and she doesn’t look away, smiling a little.

    “It’s…is it weird to say that I missed you?”

    “After one date? You must be a hell of a kisser, Kate Bishop.”

    Kate is going to strangle Sonya after this, she is sure of it. Or at least die trying. But she can feel the nervousness radiating off of Amanda, and tamps down on her annoyance to focus on the task at hand.

    She knows she has to make a choice. She needs Amanda to relax, and she knows that if she doesn’t play along, the evening is going to turn awkward from now on. Which means she won’t get any of the answers she needs. On the other hand, stringing Amanda along is a pretty shit thing to do, if she is who she says.

    The silence is stretching, and she has to make up her mind.

    At the cemetery, she told herself she will do whatever it takes. Maybe that includes doing other shitty things than killing henchmen.

    With a sigh, she makes her choice.

    “Yeah, me too. I’m…I’m really glad we can talk like this now, all cards on the table.” It’s a bit manipulative. But Kate thinks…Maybe, even if Amanda is working for Rojas, she has a conscience and she will feel the need to share her secrets too. But Amanda just smiles, eyes crinkling a bit at the corners.

    “I am really glad too.”

    Kate smiles at her, ignoring the acidic guilt in her chest. Rojas. Colombian cartel. Focus on that, Kate. She gestures to the building with her chin.

    “Shall we?”

    Amanda smiles for a moment longer, before unbuckling herself.

    Kate does too, and when Amanda is out of the car, she quickly takes out her earpiece. Sonya and Yelena’s commentary is seriously distracting, and this is already hard enough as it is. She quickly puts it into her chest pocket, so they can continue to listen then gets out. She ignores the green Jaguar passing by as she walks around the car, and leads Amanda to the entrance, then up the stairs. When they get to the door, she glances at Amanda and sees her anxiously look around.

    “Is this your place?”

    Kate unlocks the door and lets her go inside first.

    “No. My place is still a mess with the move, so I rented this place so we could talk.” Amanda looks around, and there is a glint in her eyes. She looks nervous again, her grip on the strap of her bag white-knuckled. Kate feels herself tense up as well. “We could have talked at my apartment…”

    Her words come a bit quiet, hesitant. Kate forces a grin onto her face, trying to ease the awkwardness.

    “Well, yeah, I guess. But I didn’t want this place to go to waste? There is an awesome bar, and like a…a jacuzzi in one of the bathrooms? I think one of the bedrooms has a water bed…”

    She trails off as Amanda just blinks at her, visibly surprised. Kate rewinds what she has just said, and internally facepalms. Great…in her eagerness to justify coming here, she has managed to make it sound like she brought Amanda here for very different reasons than talking.

    She chuckles nervously and runs a hand through her hair.

    “Sorry. I…I didn’t bring you here to…I just really like this place.”

    Amanda smirks but there is a bit f shiness in her face too.

    “For the record, I wouldn’t mind if you did.”

    Kate gulps. Oh no.

    She tries to smile, trying to come up with a way to take a step back from that direction. Thankfully Amanda continues.

    “But we should probably really talk…first.”

    Kate nods, maybe a bit too eager.

    “Yeah, yeah. We really should.”

    Amanda nods too, and she glances around before her eyes settle over Kate again. “Should we address the elephant in the room?”

    Kate’s stomach flips for a second. Which elephant? She waits for Amanda to elaborate. She does after Kate doesn’t answer for a few seconds.

    “Your mom, I mean.”

    Kate purses her lips. This conversation is definitely not going as she planned, so far. Not that she planned it very well. Sonya and Yelena are probably having a field day with this and she is glad she can’t hear them anymore. She decides to play along again, hoping some information will be revealed to her as well. Sitting down on the couch, she forces her body language to relax a little and looks up at Amanda.

    “Yeah, uh…It’s not really something I love to talk about. But sure.”

    Amanda comes over to sit down next to her, and reaches over, putting a hand on her thigh. Kate has to resist the urge to stiffen up. She forces a smile onto her face, but it’s probably not very convincing because Amanda tightens her hold on her thigh for a second. “We don’t have to talk about it if you don’t want to. But I’m…”

    She hesitates, and Kate looks over at her, meeting her eyes.

    “I kinda know, what it’s like to have a…criminal in the family.”

    Kate’s eyebrows shoot up her forehead. That’s surprising. Not the fact, of course, she already did know about it. But Amanda admitting it so fast. She chuckles at Kate’s expression. “Um, yeah, it’s not really first…or second date discussion material. But it’s kind of the reason why I go to F.E.A.S.T.”

    Kate tries to keep her face from reflecting her alarm. What does that mean? Is Amanda admitting to…

    “I have…had a brother. He, um,..it turns out he was involved with some pretty bad people. So, like. I kinda know what you are going through.”

    Kate tries to tamp down on the curiosity in her voice.

    “Um, I’m sorry. Can I ask, what…um, what kind of people?”

    Amanda looks down into her lap and licks her lips.

    “I…the same kind your mom did. They told us it was a Colombian cartel, that he…he was working for them, and he got killed because of it.”

    Kate is definitely surprised by that. They didn’t find anything about him being dead. She asks in disbelief.

    “They killed him?”

    Amanda shakes her head, and lifts her chin, looking straight into her eyes. “No. A vigilante did. They um…they said his name is Ronin. He was apparently targeting the organization he worked for.”

    The continued eye contact makes Kate’s heart start beating in her ears. Shit, shit, shit. This is bad. She mentally adds revenge to the list of potential motives Amanda may have for playing her.

    “They? Who are ‘they’?”

    Amanda’s brows furrow for a second, looking at her. Kate thinks her questioning is getting a bit too on the nose, but she can’t suck the words back in once they are out. “Two detectives, I don’t know.”

    She reaches out and grabs Amanda’s hand. She still doesn’t know what to think, but on one hand, it’s the natural reaction to want to console someone, and now she really can’t give up the charade. On the other, if Amanda is telling the truth, and she isn’t here for nefarious reasons, Kate truly feels bad for her.

    “I am really sorry. That sounds…it sounds really hard.”

    Amanda looks down at their clasped hands and wets her lips again. She lifts her gaze to Kate’s and holds it.

    “Yeah. It was. I, well,…I was angry for a long time. I didn’t even know who at. My brother, this Ronin person, his employers.”

    Kate resists the urge to tense up. She mentally locates her bow and arrows behind her back, probably 2, maybe 3 steps from where she is sitting. She forces her voice to be soft, trying to avoid revealing her nervousness.

    “Yeah, I can definitely understand that. I was so angry at my mom too.” Amanda nods, still holding her eyes. Kate knows it’s risky, but it’s why she came here in the first place, so she speaks again.

    “Did you ever think of like, getting revenge?”

    Amanda looks down on their clasped hands again, and the sad chuckle Kate receives in answer eases the knot in her throat. The next words tighten it up again. “Yeah, of course. He was…I know he was working for bad people, but…he was my brother. My parents and I even hired a private investigator after his death.”

    The effort it takes for Kate to not move, not react feels like a hundred-ton weight on her chest.

    “Oh?”

    Amanda licks her lips and meets her eyes again.

    “Yeah, she um…she looked into his murder for us. But it wasn’t very useful. Apparently, his employers are untouchable. We…My parents hired this really good lawyer, that she recommended, but even he couldn’t touch them.”

    Kate’s mind halts. Amanda and her family were trying to go after Rojas, not Clint. And by lawyers, not by taking justice into their own hands. Gulping again, she feels the guilt stirring anew in her chest. She has to make sure.

    “So, you wanted to sue them?”

    Amanda nods without hesitation, her voice heavy.

    “Yeah, of course. They…well, they may not have been the ones pulling the trigger, but he died because of them, right? They were the ones who led him down on that path. They should be held accountable.”

    Kate licks her lips. Fuck. Fuck. Fuck. Fuck. Amanda is either an Academy Award-worthy actress, or she is telling the truth.

    “What about the guy who killed him? The uh…vigilante? You ever find him?” Amanda’s jaw tightens, and a tear escapes one of her eyes, but her voice remains steady. “We tried to get him apprehended too, but with the Blip and everything, the police was stretched really thin. He disappeared before they could catch him… the, uh, the private investigator couldn’t find him either.”

    Nodding, Kate takes in the information while trying to ignore the fact that she feels like the biggest asshole in the history of the universe. She holds onto Amanda’s hands in her lap by one of hers, while putting her arm around her shoulders, trying to offer some comfort. “I am so sorry.”

    She really means it. Amanda’s smile is sad, but she shakes her head.

    “It’s okay. It uh…it happened a while ago. We went to therapy, as a family. It got better after a while.”

    Kate returns the smile, hoping it doesn’t look as much like a grimace as it feels. God, if poor Amanda knew...

    “That’s why I wanted to like…you know. Offer to be there for you. When I found out who you were…I just…I know hard it is and I at least had my family to lean on…” The ‘you don’t seem to have anyone’ is unspoken, but it’s definitely implied. Kate doesn’t feel even an ounce of self-pity for once, she just wants to bury herself deep into the ground. The last few days, weeks, maybe even months have left her so suspicious, that she immediately jumped to the worst conclusions when it seems all Amanda wanted to do was help. She came here, under false pretenses, and interrogated her about this traumatic thing…She has half the mind to come clean, but despite hating it, she knows it would only make things worse.

    “…I am not saying you don’t! We…we obviously don’t know each other very well. But you know. I understand what you are going through better than most, I guess. So, I thought I’d offer.”

    Kate’s heart feels like it’s shrinking up, pulling the rest of her chest inside with it. For a moment she almost wishes she was right, that Amanda was actually playing her. That would hurt too, but this?

    This is straight-up torture. She feels incredibly guilty for tonight, and also feels the grief at having to end this again. This was almost nothing, barely the start of a connection, but Amanda is a good person. If her life was different…

    But it’s not.

    She puts a stop to that train of thought before it can get the better of her. The sadness she feels most likely seeps into her answering smile, but there is not much she can do about that. “That’s…that’s really thoughtful. I really appreciate it. More than you can imagine. Thank you.”

    Amanda smiles back. After a heartbeat, she leans over to kiss her. Kate reciprocates, half out of reflex, half out of guilt. What the hell is she supposed to do now? By now, she is about 99% sure that Amanda doesn’t know anything. But another thing Kate has failed to think about in advance is how to end this evening if she turns out to be innocent. The decision she made to shut things down with Amanda after this, is not something Kate questions. There is no place in her life for a relationship, especially with someone who could become collateral damage so easily.

    But doing it, breaking it off after what has just been revealed is another stab into her heart. Amanda leans back, and there is a glint in her eye. She remains close and glances down on Kate’s lips before she speaks again.

    “How long are you back in the city?”

    Kate purses her lips and lies through her teeth without thinking. Her mind is enirely filled with trying to figure out how to end this.

    “Just for tonight.”

    Amanda smiles, half shy, half flirty.

    “Let’s make use of this beautiful apartment then.”

    Kate feels the back of her neck heat up. Oh no. This is the exact opposite direction she needs things to do right now. She also very much remembers that Yelena and Sonya can still hear them. Chuckling a bit awkwardly, she tries to come up with a way to avoid this. “Um…”

    Amanda leans over and kisses her again, and lifts a leg over her thighs to straddle her legs. Kate puts a hand on her waist, another tight chuckle escaping her lips as Amanda leans down to kiss her neck.

    “Do you…ah…do you want a drink?”

    Amanda leans back, an eyebrow raised. Thankfully, or actually, unfortunately, the expression that slides over her face is amused, instead of hurt.

    “I am literally in your lap, and you want a drink? Should I be offended?” Kate gulps, glancing towards the door separating the two apartments. She chuckles again, the sound awkward even for her own ears.

    “No, I…No. Just, let’s slow down a little.”

    Amanda leans further back, then gets off of her, face now serious.

    “Did I misread something?”

    Kate takes a deep breath and rolls her lips together.

    “No. Sorry. There is…There are just still things to talk about.”

    There is uncertainty in Amanda’s face still, but she nods.

    “Yeah, um. Okay.”

    Kate gets off of the couch and walks to the bar.

    “What would you like to drink?”

    Amanda’s face is a bit guarded, but she seems to push down on it to smile. “Whatever you are having.”

    Kate does her best to put on a convincing smile, and ease things up.

    “One sex on the beach, coming right up.”

    Amanda chuckles, and leans back against the couch, curling one of her legs under herself. “Seriously?”

    Kate’s smile widens, and she turns back to the bar.

    “Yep. The skills I learned in college are finally being put to good use.” Amanda chuckles again behind her back.

    “Wow. Back at NMU, they only taught us how to make jello shots.”

    Kate snickers at that, picking up a bottle of vodka.

    “Yeah, we definitely did those too. ”

    She busies herself by making the drinks, pouring the ingredients into a shaker, while her thoughts are back on how to proceed. Indulging in this any longer is definitely a bad idea, for multiple reasons. A, it’s cruel to everyone involved. Kate pushes down on the thought that that might actually include Yelena too. Now is not the time to be thinking about whatever that was. And B, the more she drags it out, the harder it will be to put an end to it. Steeling herself, she stirs the cocktail. It’s time to put an end to this, rip the bandaid off. She will be as honest as she can, but it has to end before an even bigger mess can be created. Walking over to the couch, she sits down, leaving a bit of space between her and Amanda. Her eyes follow Kate’s movements, and her face dims a little when Kate sits down. There is a wariness in her features and an uncertainty to her smile as she takes the cocktail from her. Wetting her lips, Kate looks into her eyes. At least it won’t come as a complete shock… “Listen, um…I want to be upfront about this. I uh. I meant what I said on the phone.” Amanda sighs, and takes a sip of her drink, pausing before she asks.

    “Which part?”

    Kate clears her throat and takes a sip too.

    “My life becoming more complicated. I…I know it sounds like complete bullshit, I really do. And I promise I am not trying to…”It’s not you, it’s me” you. Really. But I am not really in the mental space to…start anything right now.”

    Amanda nods, pursing her lips.

    “I…I’m not gonna lie. It’s…I am trying really hard to not be disappointed…” Kate smiles, but her chest is tight and her shoulders feel heavy. She fidgets with the edge of her glass, before taking another sip. Amanda continues.

    “…But I do get it. And I meant what I said too. I am okay with being friends…I will also be upfront and tell you that I do want more, and I…I will continue to. But if what you need is a friend right now, I can be that.”

    God. Kate wishes Amanda was more of a bitch. That she got angry and stormed out so they can put an end to this. So Kate can go home, and lick her wounds a little bit before she has to bounce back up. She takes a deep breath, preparing herself to deliver the final blow. “I don’t think that would be fair. I…I like you, and in….”

    Kate halts.

    There is a loud thud outside in the corridor. Without thinking about it, every single muscle in her body tenses up, her heart taking off like a race horse. Putting down her glass, she starts to prepare to stand up slowly, quietly.

    “Kate? Wha…”

    Clamping a hand over Amanda’s mouth, she ignores her wide eyes and tries to listen. Shit. She shouldn’t have taken out her earpiece.

    There is another thump, this time even closer and Kate is ready to jump off the couch when the front door slams open.

    Amanda screams and Kate shoves her behind herself. In the doorway, there is a tall, dark form, wearing black tactical clothing. His weird lack of motion confuses Kate. He just stands there. Amanda’s scream is not enough to drown out her heart beating loudly in her ears. The man sways then collapses forward. Behind him, there is a smaller figure, also in a black tactical suit. Kate’s heart misses a beat for different reasons. Amanda screams again. Yelena steps over the body, and pointedly does not look at Kate and Amanda on the couch. She does break into an angry rant right away, as she pulls the body inside, and closes the door.

    “Why the hell do you not listen to your comms? We have been compromised. We need to go.”

    The awkwardness settles into the room, and Kate’s bones, in less than a second. She ignores it, standing up and turning to get her bow and quiver. The wince that comes with her admission is involuntary.

    “I…I took it out.”

    Turning back just in time to see Yelena’s face, she sees her momentary shock. Then, Yelena closes her eyes and bites down on the corner of her lip, probably swallowing some even more cutting remarks before she speaks.

    “God, you are so stupid.”

    Kate huffs as she pulls her quiver around her shoulders, straightening up to her full height. “Your little commentary was fucking distracting, okay?”

    It seems like Yelena is one more angry word away from hitting her, despite still refusing to look in her direction, so Kate shuts her mouth. Now is not the time.

    “You…”

    They both turn to look at Amanda who stares at the two of them, eyes jumping from Kate to Yelena and back. Yelena rolls her eyes and turns towards the door.

    “You have 30 seconds, Kate.”

    That spurs her into motion. She turns back to Amanda, trying to make her voice softer, calming.

    “I will explain everything later, okay? But right now, we have to go.” If she were suspicious still, which she isn’t, Amanda’s scream has pretty much convinced Kate that she is indeed an unwitting civilian. There is no time for her to focus on the complicated nature of how that and everything else from tonight makes her feel and focuses on the next step instead. Getting them all away from danger.

    If it makes her feel like an asshole that she is at least partially thankful for the interruption, she will deal with that later too.

    Picking up Amanda’s bag, Kate pulls her up from the couch by her hand, glancing at Yelena standing guard by the door. Even as she hands the bag to Amanda, her brain is fixating on the tense set of Yelena’s shoulders, before she tells herself to stop. God, you are a dick, Kate. “Amanda, please. We have to go.”

    Amanda nods, finally, her eyes wide, glancing between her and Yelena still. Kate walks up to Yelena with Amanda beside her and cringes internally. Standing with both women on either side of her, it feels like she is in one of those stress nightmares, where she has to take her SATs again, and when she looks down, she’s naked. As in, it’s both absurd and incredibly stressful.

    Yelena finally turns fully towards them, but her eyes seek out Amanda instead of Kate. She looks her over, before visibly setting her jaw. She takes a deep breath and takes off toward the door that separates the two halves of the Airbnb.

    A Russian sentence leaves Yelena’s mouth, presumably meant for Sonya. Prompting Kate to hurriedly reach into the breast pocket of her shirt and pull out her earpiece again. Putting it back in, she catches the second half of the sentence, also in Russian. “What the hell happened?”

    The question seems to bounce back from Yelena’s back, as she steadfastly ignores Kate. Huffing, she pushes down on the urge to start picking a fight. Not now. They get to the middle of the living room of the other apartment when Yelena halts again. Kate immediately hears it too.

    Heavy footsteps coming down the fire escape on their right side.

    “What…”

    Amanda starts speaking and Yelena twists around. Kate already clamped a hand over her mouth again and shakes her head at her, putting a finger over her lips. Amanda’s eyes are wide, staring at her in alarm, but she nods.

    Pulling her hand away, Kate reaches back for her bow and jerks her arm forward to open it. She nocks a regular arrow and starts backing away, motioning to Amanda with her chin to follow. Next to her, Yelena takes out her gun from her thigh holster. A quiet click indicates when the safety is disengaged.

    “Slight change of plans, we are going through the main exit after all.” Yelena whispers, now in English, and barely audible. They all slowly retreat to the other living room, where Kate and Amanda were until now. Kate takes the opportunity to pause, and quickly fish out her car keys and sword from her bag, along with her wallet. Stuffing them into her pocket, she makes her way to the front door again.

    Amanda thankfully stays quiet, and Kate grabs the handle, looking at Yelena. Their eyes meet, and Yelena nods, raising her gun.

    Yanking the door open, Kate readies to go through but there is already another tall figure standing directly in front of her. She kicks out instinctively, and it gets him right in the stomach, sending him flying across the corridor, and back against the wall. Before he can get his bearings, a silenced gunshot comes from Kate’s left side, and he slumps against the wall, leaving a wide, crimson trail on the white paint.

    Yelena’s gunshot might have been silenced, but Amanda’s scream is definitely not. Another instinctive movement sends Kate turning to clamp her hand over Amanda’s mouth again, but the sound cuts out before she actually gets to. Yelena stands in front of Amanda, her hand muffling her cry this time, staring straight into her eyes.

    Oh, God.

    “Be. Quiet.”

    Her voice sounds almost like a growl, low and threatening. Amanda’s eyes seek out Kate, still wide and scared before she looks back at Yelena. She nods again, and Yelena tears herself away from her, as if touching her has burned her hands. She throws Kate a dark glare, which is pretty unfair, but she pushes the urge to ask her how the hell is this her fault. She licks her lips instead and nods at Yelena, hoping to deescalate things. They really need to get out of here.

    Yelena purses her lips, obviously still annoyed but nods back.

    Kate is the first through the door, her bow drawn and ready this time. The hallway is thankfully deserted, and she slowly walks down the corridor towards the stairs. Amanda and Yelena are right behind her.

    “Can you hurry up? Two more cars have just pulled up.”

    Sonya’s voice doesn’t sound particularly alarmed in Kate’s ear but she speeds up her steps nonetheless.

    “Can we get out that way?”

    “If you hurry.”

    Kate lowers her bow to start into a light jog, her side protesting with sharp pangs of pain. Sparing no time to focus on that, she leads them down the flight of stairs and halts by the door.

    “Sonya, are we safe to exit?”

    She does not receive a verbal answer for a moment, but instead, gunshots ring out. Both through her earpiece, and through the door, she hears them and curses internally. Fuck. “Negative. You have to try the southeast exit.”

    At any other time, Kate would be impressed with Sonya’s calmness but now, it just fills her with more worry.

    “Sonya, are you okay?”

    The answer sounds amused, more than anything.

    “You have enough women to worry about, Kate Bishop. Just get to the southeast exit. I am fine.”

    Kate sees Yelena’s face twitch again from the corner of her eyes, and takes a deep breath. This evening really couldn’t have gone to shit any more, even if she was deliberately trying. So much for not creating a bigger mess.

    Yelena turns away before she does, and she whispers to Amanda as they follow her back up the stairs.

    “We have to go to the fire escape on the other side of the building, okay?” Amanda looks two seconds away from crying, her face white as a sheet, but she nods. As they arrive at the front door of the Airbnb again, Kate ignores the corpse of the soldier Yelena dispatched and prepares to enter again, taking a breath. The sound of glass breaking can be heard from inside, along with a muted hissing. Smoke grenade.

    Kate looks at Yelena and she jerks her chin towards the other door. Nodding, Kate follows her but halts after a step. She glances at Amanda, gently grabbing her forearm as she notices her staring at the downed soldier behind them.

    Meeting her wide eyes, she tries to convey the seriousness of the situation, putting a finger over her lips again. Amanda’s eyes look a bit glazed over, but she nods again. Kate sees the way her gaze keeps trailing back to the corpse, so she gently pulls her along, her hand sliding from her forearm to her wrist. When they catch up to Yelena, she softly pushes Amanda against the wall and gestures for her to wait.

    Yelena’s jaw is set when she turns back to her, but she grabs the door handle and looks at her nonetheless, waiting for Kate’s signal. Drawing her bow, she nods and Yelena raises her gun one-handed. Her mouth forms the words quietly, Kate’s eyes glued to them. Three.

    Two.

    One.

    She opens the door gently, quietly, but gunshots ring out immediately anyway. Kate shoves Yelena out of the way, falling against her, and she falls against Amanda in turn, the three of them stumbling backward.

    Kate recovers quickly, ignoring the sharp pain in her stitched-up ribs as she twists around, and takes note of their surroundings. The wall beside them, where they have been standing, is littered with bullet holes, as is the door. Thinking quick, Kate nocks a flare arrow, and fires it through one of them.

    The blinding light seeping through the holes in the door is her signal, she kicks the door in, going through it alone. Learning from last time, she immediately vaults behind a couch close to the wall, but there is no answering gunfire hailing down on her for once. Adrenaline flows in her vein like an old friend nonetheless.

    Taking advantage of the attackers being momentarily distracted, she rises out of the cover, firing two arrows in quick succession, at the two men dressed in tactical clothing she can see. They drop with identical, gurgling sounds of pain that Kate blocks out of her brain. Yelena comes through the door to her right a second later, pulling Amanda behind her and pushing her down into bend with a hand on the back of her neck. Her other hand holds her gun, and she fires twice, downing two other soldiers that lean out of cover to fire at them. When she gets to the couch Kate is leaning out behind from, she practically shoves Amanda down into cover and growls at Kate.

    “Don’t ever do that again.”

    Rapid gunfire rings out, and they both instinctively drop down, crouching behind the sofa. Kate asks over the sound of shots, and bullets embedding themselves into the big, leather couch and the wall above their heads. Kate is so losing that security deposit. “What, save your ass?”

    Yelena gives her a look so cutting, she immediately regrets the smartass comment. “Leave me behind with a marketing person.”

    Kate rolls her eyes, thinking it’s not Amanda’s lack of martial training that annoys Yelena but swallows the comment. She looks at the civilian in question instead and tries to ignore the guilt that feels suffocating in her chest. Amanda is crying now, silent tears streaming down her face, where she sits to Kate’s right with her back to the couch. Her legs are pulled up to her chest, and her eyes are staring at her, terrified.

    “It’ll be okay. I promise.”

    Yelena snorts to her left, but Kate ignores her. She takes Amanda’s hand for a second and squeezes it. She is thankful when she doesn’t pull it away.

    “Kate, I swear to god.”

    Yelena sounds permanently annoyed tonight but Kate has had enough of it. She twists her head to send her a glare, her voice snapping.

    “Jesus, Yelena. Have a little empathy.”

    The answering look she gets is cold and burning at the same time, and Yelena’s eyes jump from Kate to Amanda and back again. Kate hates that it sends a wave of warmth over her skin.

    “How about empathy when we are not being shot at?”

    A clattering sound in front of them has their heads snap forward instinctively, and they jump forward at the same time. Thanks to her longer limbs, Kate’s fingers close around the hand grenade first and she throws it back over the couch without thinking.

    The next thing she does is also without thinking.

    Rolling over she covers Yelena’s body with her own, her front pressing against hers, just like in the storage unit place. The blast comes a second later, blowing up the other half of the room, taking part of the wall and the ceiling with it.

    Amanda’s scream gets lost in the loud explosion, but Kate barely hears either. Yelena is staring at her, green eyes wide with surprise, and she can’t look away. Kate doesn’t get to decipher the look in them.

    “It sounds like you guys are having all the fun without me.”

    Sonya’s voice tears them out of their moment, thankfully only a second or two long. Kate scrambles off of Yelena, just as she grunts.

    “Get off of me.”

    If it lacks the bite Yelena’s voice carried for the last several hours, they both ignore it. There is a Russian sentence from Sonya over comms again, and Kate is over trying to be petty. She rolls back behind the couch, and speaks, her voice annoyed but lacking its former bite too. Hand grenades will put things in perspective.

    “How many times do I have to ask you to stop doing that?”

    At the same time, Yelena speaks too.

    “Shut up, Sonya.”

    Kate swears there is a small upwards twitch of Yelena’s mouth, but she turns away to check on Amanda instead of focusing on it. Amanda is thankfully unharmed, even though she looks absolutely shellshocked. Her eyes are jumping around, looking at Kate, Yelena, the wall littered with bullet holes, her body shaking a little.

    No shot has been fired since the explosion and Yelena sticks her head slightly out from behind the couch, while Kate reaches out to touch Amanda’s arm gently. “Hey, are you okay?”

    Amanda’s eyes finally slow down and focus on her. She opens her mouth to speak, and her voice is surprisingly steady when she does.

    “No, not really.”

    Kate smiles a little, trying to ignore her guilt again.

    After all the shitty things that happened tonight, that she half-unintentionally has done to Amanda, she chose to protect Yelena. It’s not really surprising. Yelena saved her life several times, patched her up, fought with her, and despite the tension of the last few days, she is a friend, someone genuinely close to her. She is also…something. A crush maybe. That’s not the point. Amanda is a girl she met twice, who doesn’t even know who Kate actually is, other than her name. So, all in all, of course, her instinct was to protect Yelena. But after taking Amanda here by essentially lying, even if by omission. Lying to her throughout the night. Making her talk about her brother’s death, who by the way, was killed by Kate’s mentor, and friend. Endangering her life, essentially for nothing more than to ease Kate’s worries that she wasn’t played…After all that, Kate didn’t jump to protect her. Again, it’s not surprising. But at this moment, she definitely doesn’t feel like a hero. The only solace in this, maybe, is that Amanda is probably too shocked to actually realize what just happened.

    Kate feels even more of an asshole when her next unbidden thought is wondering whether Yelena did.

    “We have to go.”

    Yelena’s voice is back to business, and Kate shakes off her few seconds of guilt-ridden melancholy. There will be time for that later.

    “Come on.”

    She helps Amanda stand with a smile, pulling her up by her hand, then picks up her bow that has fallen in her dive for the grenade. Yelena has already left them behind by a few steps, advancing deeper into the apartment.

    They go through another corridor, before entering a bedroom. It’s the one with the water bed, and Kate doesn’t dare to look at either woman with her, remembering her earlier comments. This evening can’t end soon enough.

    Yelena opens the window leading to the fire escape and turns to look at Kate, finally meeting her eyes again. It shouldn’t feel as refreshing as it does.

    “Sonya, what’s your ETA?”

    Yelena speaks as she holds Kate’s eyes before she glances outside.

    “About one minute. You will need to get down to me quick, we won’t have much time.” Kate is the first to climb out through the window Yelena just opened, turning back to help Amanda through. After a moment of hesitation, she holds out her hand for Yelena too. She looks at it, then back into Kate’s eyes, and climbs through without her help. It stings, but she pulls back her hand and tries to shake off the rejection. It seems Yelena is not ready to let their earlier argument go just yet.

    She turns towards the ladder with a deep sigh and unhooks it.

    It doesn’t fall as it’s supposed to.

    Kate pushes down on it, but it doesn’t budge. Yelena’s impatient voice sounds from behind her back.

    “Kate, let down the ladder.”

    “I’m trying.”

    Yelena comes up beside her, inspecting it, trying to jostle it, move it too, but it seems rusted in place.

    Great.

    “30 seconds.”

    Kate leaves the ladder and walks to the railing. She puts her bow back onto her back and swings her leg over it. Calling out to Yelena and Amanda, she starts lowering herself. “We don’t have time. Come on.”

    Yelena nods and comes up to the railing too.

    Kate climbs down as low as she can until it’s only her hands holding onto the metal railing. She tries to not think about how rickety it feels. Looking down, she tries to gauge her landing. They are about 20 feet high, nothing too bad thankfully.

    She swings her body frontward a little as she lets go, and rolls forward as her boots hit the pavement, sticking the landing. There is a sharp pain in her side, immediately telling her that she just tore a couple of stitches. She tries to swallow the cry of pain, but a hissing, sharp exhale escapes her nonetheless.

    She rises to her feet gingerly and turns back up to the fire escape. Amanda and Yelena stand side by side, and Kate looks at them for a moment.

    Both blonde, small, beautiful. Ignoring the fact that it seems Kate definitely has a type, she considers how different they look, despite their similarities. Amanda stands frozen, her face pale and still twisted in fear. Her eyes are fixed on the ledge, lips parted. Yelena is looking at Amanda too, her own face flushed from the exertion of the last 15 minutes. Her expression is difficult to read, hints of impatience, annoyance, and hard-set determination all visible. Her eyes are not hard, however. She looks at Amanda uncertainly, if a little guarded.

    A second passes, then two and she gestures at the railing, and Kate hears her words even down on the street.

    “You have to jump”

    Amanda shakes her head but doesn’t turn away from the railing.

    “I…I can’t.”

    Yelena’s jaw clenches, the annoyance now definitely visible in her eyes as well. “What do you mean you can’t?”

    “I’m afraid of heights.”

    Yelena, again, unfairly according to Kate’s opinion, turns her face and looks exasperatedly down at her. How is this Kate’s fault too? She calls up from beneath them. “Amanda, I’m sorry but you really have to.”

    Amanda worries her lip between her teeth, turning to look down at her. She doesn’t move. “10 seconds.”

    Sonya says in her earpiece and Kate can hear tires screeching around the corner…several pairs. She takes out her bow again and nocks an arrow in preparation.

    “If you don’t jump, I will throw you off myself.”

    Her head snaps up to the landing, throwing Yelena a warning glare, her voice outraged. “Yelena!... No, she won’t!”

    “I don’t care how but get that suka down onto the street. I am arriving in 5 seconds.” “Yes, I will.”

    Kate opens her mouth to argue again, but a bullet ricocheting off of the railing next to Amanda’s head drowns whatever she was going to say. Probably for the best. Kate draws her arrow immediately and searches for a target. From her periphery she sees Yelena grab Amanda and quite literally launch both of them over the railing, a second shot shattering the window they were just standing in front of. Amanda screams as they fall, Yelena shoots a wire into the wall of the building.

    Kate sees the glare from what probably is a scope on top of a building across the street, about a hundred feet ahead of them. Drawing her bow even further back, back muscles aching and exhaling the air from her lungs, she aims.

    Yelena and Amanda land on the pavement next to her, Yelena using her hold around Amanda’s back to immediately yank them forward as Sonya’s green Jaguar comes to a screeching halt to Kate’s right side.

    Kate releases the string and immediately jumps into motion, wasting no time to check if her arrow reached its intended target. Yelena yanks the back door open before shoving Amanda inside then getting in behind her, and Kate barely has time to jump in too, before Sonya is already stepping onto the gas pedal.

    Tires screeching, they are off.

    Chapter End Notes Hi guys, I am super sorry for going AWOL for so long. Life got super busy, and I kinda got side- tracked by writing other Bishova fics too (which I'll post sometime in the future). I also ended up cutting this chapter in half *again*, because I didn't want to drag out posting it anymore but it's past 4:30 am and I can't keep my eyes open anymore lol But just so you know, the next chapter is still at least partialy this chapter, maybe entirely. This fic is like hydra. Cut off one head (chapter) and 2 grows into its place.

    But, anyway. Finally, here we are.

    I have to admit, in many ways, this was the hardest chapter to write ever because there is sooooo much stuff beneath the surface that I needed to unwrap in my head, before I could properly write it. I thought about this for a long time, without writing even a word of it, because it sort of makes the bed for the rest of Kate's and Yelena's relationship. (I also kinda re-wrote it 3 times, after I did start to write it. oops.)

    But first things first: I know a lot of you wanted Amanda to be a bad guy, and I did lean into that to play with you a little, sorry :D But from the very beginning, ever since I came up with the idea of her, she was here to be one thing, and one thing only, and that's not a villain. She is the vessel to explore Kate's and Yelena's paths leading to each other.

    Amanda is the embodiment of what Kate wants and cannot have, becuase of who she is and the choices she makes. Of course, I personally think Kate belongs with Yelena. Yelena is the type of normalicy Kate can and should have, and the one who is able to actually be a part of the life she chose. But, Kate doesn't understand that yet. (Neither does Yelena.)

    She is also, of course, here to make Yelena jealous, but we will go into that in later chapters. Jealousy is a lot of fun as a reader (/shipper), and it's sexy in a way (I hope it was in this chapter). But beneath all that, it's born out of insecurity. Amanda, in a lot of ways, is everything Yelena never gets to be. She is light and normal, a New York city girl, she wears flowy dresses and she doesn't have the means (or the urge) to go on a murderous rampage over a dead sibling. Kate has had a pretty normal (compared to Y) life, and her jealousy is more than just 'oh she gets to kiss Kate when I don't". It's also: "she can give Kate something that I can't" (yeah she totally can, and then some, she just doesn't know that yet).

    I personally really liked Amanda, and I hope I managed to make you guys feel a little sad about the tragedy of what she has gone through too, even if you haven't grown to like her. What happened in this chapter is pretty fucked up on multiple levels, as a fault of nobody actually in it (Rojas and Clint are responsible). I'll not write a list, but Kate, who is Clint's protegee, coming to interrogate a girl, whose brother was killed by him, someone who Kate considers a friend, family basically, is pretty fucked up. She also actually kind of did to Amanda, what she was afraid she was doing to her. Even if they all had relatively valid reasons for doing what they did. But it's what it is. And yeah, despite the fact that we are all here for it (:D), Kate thinking about Yelena, and even choosing to save her, despite knowing what she is doing is actually a bit fucked up too. I hope none of you are too disappointed with Amanda turning out to be who she is. (It's been like my no.1 source of anexiety since like chapter 2 :D I didn't expect you all to dislike her so much)

    (Her story is also a reminder that despite the fact that there is no way around fighting and killing henchmen for Kate, they're people too, with lives and families.) --

    (barely there) Easter eggs: In my head, the lawyer Amanda's family hired is Foggy (Matt was Blipped in my head, which is why Kingpin could operate in peace for 5 years), the PI is Jessica Jones. They won't be relevant in this story, probably (;)) but yeah. It's them.

    --

    I'll try to get up the next one as soon as possible. I am aiming for the second half of this week, but we'll see what life throws in my way. :D Please send me comments (& kudos), it's a huge part of what keeps me writing this, and I love reading your thoughts :)

    Thank you all for reading, and a special thanks to the people who kept coming back and nudge me along to get my shit together :D xx Ps.: as its 4:48 and I'm bleary eyed af, the proof-reading on this might be less than stellar :D so if there is weird stuff forgotten in here, I'm sorry. Also sorry for this long ass ramble

    Chapter 17

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Kate is lying across both Amanda’s and Yelena’s laps, and she has a hard time sitting up because Sonya almost immediately takes a sharp left turn. They are a tangled mess of limbs on the backseat, and besides the adrenaline, there is also a high amount of awkwardness coursing through Kate’s veins, heating her skin, the tips of her ears. She does manage to sit up eventually, crawling backward and slotting herself between Yelena and the door. Her bow is big and awkward in the suddenly tight space, but with the close quarters, she can’t even move enough to close it without hitting anyone. Twisting herself around to look back, she notes it’s probably not a good idea either, because there are three black SUVs on their tail.

    Meeting Sonya’s eyes in the rearview mirror for a second, Kate is both stunned and reluctantly amused to realize that they hold the same teasing glint as they did the first time they met in this car. She only holds Kate’s gaze for a moment, however, shifting her focus back to driving thankfully. Kate thinks she is probably just waiting for her moment to pounce. For about a minute, nobody speaks. Kate, for once, is at the loss of words, not sure how to address any of the women in the car after everything that happened tonight. Yelena has gone back to her frosty silent treatment, and Amanda is probably still in shock. Sonya not speaking is probably the only surprise, but it’s a welcome one for once.

    Kate turns back several times to check on their pursuers. Sonya’s Jaguar is lighter and faster than the SUVs chasing them, wading around on semi-busy late-night streets with ease, but they don’t seem to be able to shake them. Eager to escape the awkward silence of the car, and Sonya’s inevitable teasing, Kate starts to roll down the window on her left. “What are you doing?”

    Sonya’s voice sounds a bit surprised from the front, and Kate’s bow and head are already out of the window as she answers.

    “Helping. Try to keep it steady.”

    She pulls out the rest of her upper body, her side protesting with several sharp jolts of pain, and sits on the ledge like she did with Clint back in the day. The SUVs are a few cars behind them, but Kate nocks an electromagnetic arrow and aims nonetheless. She waits for the one closest to them to peek out from behind the car in front of it and releases her arrow. “Whohoo!”

    Despite the wind whipping past her ear, she hears Sonya’s cheer as the car immediately slows down, veering to the right and into one of the others chasing them. They both crash against a building, essentially out of the race to catch up to them. A moment later she hears Sonya again.

    “Stop rolling your eyes Yelena, it was cool!”

    Kate’s lip twitches upwards for a second before she reaches back for another arrow. Since she is running low on electromagnetic ones, she pulls out an acid arrow instead, its green tip glinting dangerously with the lights passing by. She nocks it, pulls back the string, and waits for the moment, but this driver seems to have learned from the others’ mistakes. The SUV stays behind a big, white van for a long time, not attempting to catch up to them. Just as Kate thinks it’s suspicious, she hears Sonya’s voice warning her. “Hold on.”

    It’s a second too late, because when Sonya twists the wheel to the side, and the car whirls around a corner, Kate can feel her center of gravity suddenly slip away. Her body tilts, the centrifugal force sending her outwards and unbalancing her before she can lower her bow and grab a hold of the car. Her ass slips off the ledge, and she is falling. Letting go of the string of her bow, she grabs for something, but everything is out of reach. Her arrow goes flying, absolutely off target, but Kate only sees the pavement get closer to her head. Suddenly, there is a vice-like hold on her right calf.

    The hand stops her from flying out of the car, and the fingertips dig into her muscle through her jeans hard enough that it’s painful. The car turns a bit too much and Sonya course- corrects in the other direction. It sends Kate back against the car and she cries out in pain when the edge of the car’s roof slams against her injured ribs.

    The fingers grabbing her leg yank, and she is pulled back into the car, barely managing to hold onto her bow as she falls back into her previous seat. Yelena’s hand slips off her leg, and if Kate wasn’t seeing black spots from the pain, she’d try to focus on her expression. “Do you ever think before you do something?”

    Kate was going to thank her for saving her, but it seems Yelena is still holding onto the tension from earlier. Her own tone is testy as she answers, face twisting into a slight scowl, even though she still can’t see properly from the black spots clouding her vision. “I was doing just fine, thank you.”

    Yelena points to her side, voice dry.

    “You are bleeding again.”

    Kate looks down, noting the moderately sized red spot marring her white shirt. “Ha! I was already bleeding from tearing my stitches when we jumped off the fire escape. I didn’t get that now.”

    Her vision slowly but surely clearing up, she sees Yelena staring at her from the side. “You are an idiot.”

    Kate snorts, not really having the energy to properly get angry, feeling a little bit hysterical. “Okay, that’s fair.”

    Yelena sighs, closing her eyes presumably to calm herself for a second. When she opens them again, she twists around to check the SUV still chasing them. Before Kate can complain, Yelena grabs her right shoulder and pushes her back into the seat.

    “If you carried an actual sensible weapon, you would not have to climb out of the car so much to fire it.”

    Sensible weapon choices are the very last thing on Kate’s mind as Yelena uses her hold on her shoulder to raise one of her knees over her thighs, and slide into her lap, facing her. She determinedly doesn’t look at Kate but instead sticks her hand holding her gun and her face out of the window.

    She probably waits for the car to get out of cover again, because she doesn’t fire right away. For about 10 whole seconds, that feel like a million years, Kate thinks her heart is going to jump out of her chest, as she sits frozen, eyes jumping between Yelena’s profile and staring ahead. The skin on her face is not thick enough to look over to Amanda either. When her eyes meet Sonya’s in the rearview mirror, she winks at her, and before Kate can decipher what that means they are careening around another corner. Yelena grabs onto her shoulder harder but the motion pushes her closer to Kate nonetheless, her chest pressing against Kate’s and her face coming close to hers. Kate’s hands move without any direction from her brain and rise to grab Yelena’s waist, attempting to steady her. “You still smell like a cat in heat.”

    The sentence sounds annoyed, practically hissed, but the fact that it’s spoken so close to her ear, Yelena’s breath tickling the skin of Kate’s temple and cheeks, makes it very hard to actually focus on it. Her fingers tighten unconsciously, fingertips digging into Yelena’s side at the words. Close to her ear, Yelena’s breath hitches but maybe Kate imagined it, because a moment later she fires her gun, 3 times.

    Kate doesn’t have to turn around to check if they reached their intended target, because Yelena slides off of her with a huff a second later, pushing her gun back into its holster. “I told you, Kate. We need to stop being reactive. I told you. I asked you to stop being so impulsive.”

    Her words are frustrated, and she barely glances at Kate to throw her a dark glare. It’s not entirely clear if she refers to leaning out of the car to fire her bow or the whole night. It doesn’t really matter, her voice cuts at Kate. She takes a deep breath, refusing to be baited into another fight right now.

    “I wasn’t trying to..”

    Yelena cuts her off, shuffling around in her seat, and rubbing a hand at her forehead. “You weren’t. You never do, yet here we are. Again.”

    Kate huffs, tamping down on her own rising irritation at Yelena’s sharp voice. She fails to keep it completely from her voice.

    “Well, I am sorry. But I don’t see what else I could have done differently. It’s not my fault that…”

    She glances at Amanda, who seems to still be under the effects of the evening, but stares at them wide-eyed. Kate doesn’t know how to phrase everything she wants to say without revealing all of her secrets.

    “I didn’t…It’s not like I want this to keep happening.”

    Yelena clenches her jaw when she sees her look at Amanda. Kate cringes internally. This is a huge mess already without…interpersonal emotions getting mixed into it as well. “You don’t see what you could have done differently? Is that a serious question?! We could have stayed at home and focused on the actual mission. You could have asked her…” She points at Amanda with a needlessly rude, direct motion.

    “what you wanted later, or simply stayed the hell away. You could have not taken your comms out so we could warn you in time. You could…”

    Kate’s irritation boils over, and this time her own voice is dripping with almost as much venom and annoyance as Yelena’s. Do they have to fucking do this now?

    “Okay, thank you! We get it! I fucked up! Are you happy?”

    “Yes, you did!”

    The tension in the car could be cut with a knife. Kate should probably hold it back, stick to her idea of not being dragged into a fight, but again, she is just done with this shitty fucking night. She will allow herself this one snappy comment.

    “Well maybe if you two weren’t so busy running commentary in my ear, I wouldn’t have taken my fucking comms out.”

    Yelena’s eyes burn with so much anger, Kate almost expects something to catch on fire, or Yelena to hit her.

    “Do not dare to push it onto m…us. We came here as a favor and you have been distracted the whole night.”

    Kate grinds her teeth, ignoring the urge to throw Yelena’s jealousy back into her face again. “I haven’t been the only one distracted…”

    It’s as far as she can go, with Sonya and Amanda present. They need to talk about this alone, when they both had time to calm down. The glare Yelena throws her is pure condescension and she practically scoffs.

    “We did our jobs, and if you were not so busy being dry-humped on the couch, none of this would have happened.”

    Kate is officially done.

    Also, how does Yelena even know that word?

    Yes, the mission was ill-advised, and taking her comms out was probably a bad idea. But she stayed completely focused on the objective the whole time, and if anyone keeps mistaking this evening for something that it isn’t, it’s Yelena. She is being completely unfair, and Kate is done with letting her use her as an emotional punching bag for her own frustration. Yelena is a grown woman, if she had a problem with this mission, she should have said something before they left, not thrown a tantrum when Kate played her part. Kissing her teeth, lips curling Kate answers, her tone sharp and rising in volume.

    “You know what? If you weren’t so busy…”

    “Enough.”

    Sonya’s voice cuts through the red fog that was about to descend on Kate’s brain like a knife, and she shuts her mouth, her teeth clacking. The tone of that one word would be enough to end the argument, but Sonya continues. She sounds calm, and for once it’s not like she is trying to tease.

    “You both need to calm the fuck down. You can have your lover’s quarrel later. Now, we need a new plan.”

    Kate takes a deep breath, calming herself. Sonya is right. They need a plan. It seems Yelena isn’t done yet.

    “It is not a fucking lover’s quarrel. I am reminding Kate, that…”

    Sonya says something in Russian, the tone calm and steady, but Yelena’s mouth gapes in offense at whatever she just said. She shuts it a moment later, clenching her jaw, and takes a deep breath too.

    It’s quiet for a few seconds, and Kate tries to focus on thinking of their next steps. They need to find a way to get Amanda home safe and give her a plausible explanation for what happened tonight. Kate needs to apologize and make sure they part on good enough terms that Amanda doesn’t go running to the press…or the police. They need to make sure they are not followed, and then she needs to...

    It all goes out the window when Amanda breaks the silence a few moments later. “Oh my god.”

    Kate’s eyes jump to her and widen when she sees Amanda staring at the bow in front of her. She opens her mouth but it’s too late.

    “You….You are them!”

    Amanda’s eyes jump from the bow to Yelena, then settle on Kate. She tries to sound calm, leaning forward to look at her better.

    “Amanda,…”

    Her attempt to try to deescalate this, to try and salvage whatever remains of her secret is snuffed out with the next words coming out of Amanda’s mouth.

    “No! You are them! You are the vigilantes that blew up the harbor.”

    Next to her, Yelena scoffs, confirming Amanda’s suspicions and making Kate’s irritation spark again.

    “That was your girlfriend, I did not blow up anything.”

    Kate throws her a glare, refusing to unpack the girlfriend comment, but shifts her focus back on Amanda a second later.

    “We didn’t mean to blow up anything. The…the people there kidnapped someone. We were there to save her.”

    Amanda’s eyes are wide still and she is shaking her head, but Kate doesn’t know what she is denying. She feels at loss on what to say again.

    “You are a vigilante.”

    The word almost drips with disgust, a stark reminder of what happened to Amanda’s brother. Kate shakes her head, mouth gaping a little and trying to remain calm but doesn’t know how to deny what is pretty obviously true. Sonya is a surprising, but welcome voice of reason again.

    “Listen, Anita. I understand you had a shit night. Kate Bishop owes you an explanation, and she will give it to you. Later. Okay? I need her to be thinking about how we get somewhere safe, and not all the women she keeps pissing off. So please, be quiet and let us do our jobs.” Kate watches as Amanda purses her lips and lifts her chin, staring at Sonya in the front seat. Despite the tear tracks still visible on her face, she looks surprisingly strong. “It’s Amanda. But fine.”

    It’s defiant and definitely angry, but it’s the best they can probably hope for in these circumstances. Kate tries to catch her eyes, convey an apology, but Amanda just leans back against the seat, crossing her arms. Next to her, Yelena stares ahead too, determinedly not looking at Kate either.

    That’s just great.

    Taking a deep breath, Kate rubs at her face before looking ahead too and going back to trying to think of a plan. Fuck, this is a mess.

    “We need to get off the streets. We are vulnerable like this.”

    Sonya remains calm, and it helps Kate a minuscule amount. She nods.

    “Yeah. We need somewhere to regroup.”

    Kate also needs to redo her stitches, she distractedly thinks, because her side is definitely soaked in blood again, and the more the adrenaline of the evening wears off, the more she can feel it aching too. She thinks about going home, but there are a million things they need to sort out before that happens. They need to figure out what to do with Amanda, make sure they are not followed, probably call the Airbnb guy because Kate used her real name to book the place. Wait…

    Kate used her real name to book the place.

    “Oh fuck.”

    She rubs her face with her palms again, groaning into them.

    “What?”

    Sonya asks her from the front, Yelena and Amanda both steadfastly ignoring her. “I am a fucking idiot.”

    Her hands are still covering her eyes, so she can’t see, but she definitely can hear Yelena’s snort next to her.

    “Yes, but why this time?”

    God, they will never let her live this down. Taking a deep breath, she pulls her hands away. “Never mind. I need to call Clint…”

    She digs into her pocket for her phone before she remembers he is currently unavailable. “Oh, shit, wait, I can’t.”

    Yelena finally seems to have shaken enough of her anger to be productive and looks at her. “Kate, what is going on?”

    Closing her eyes, she purses her lips and gulps.

    “I fucked up, okay? I…I used my real name to book the Airbnb.”

    She opens her eyes to watch Yelena’s face, and sees the effort it takes for her to not call her an idiot again. She shakes her head once, turning away from Kate again. “At least that explains how they knew we were there.”

    Kate hasn’t thought of that, but it does. She raises her palms to rub her face again, pushing against her eyes.

    “Yeah. Uh, fuck. I’m sorry.”

    Honestly, she hasn’t even thought about it. Her details were in there from her last trip which happened even before her mother got arrested. It was a weekend in Cancun with Franny and Greer, that feels like a lifetime ago now. Kate just tapped on booking the place without thinking twice, and it’s definitely what got them in trouble now that she thinks about it. She doesn’t have time to marinate in her self-flagellation.

    “Put your seatbelts on.”

    Sonya’s voice is still even but Kate’s head snaps up at it as if she screamed at them. They have made their way out of Brooklyn somewhere during her argument with Yelena, and now they are cruising in the suburbs of Staten Island. It’s past 10 o’clock according to the numbers displayed on the dashboard, and the streets are not as busy in this neighborhood, but there are still definitely people around.

    Looking around, Kate doesn’t see anything out of ordinary. No unmarked black SUVs, no men hanging out the windows of cars, no super-soldiers running at them full speed. “What do you see?”

    Sonya slows down for a red light, stopping behind another car and keeping her eyes on the left side-mirror.

    “That motorcycle has taken the last 4 turns that we have…No! Don’t turn around.” Kate halts her movements, and next to her Yelena unholsters her gun. She looks out the windows instead and looks at the cars on their sides. As she turns slightly back, her heart starts racing again.

    “Shit.”

    She twists forward quickly, burrowing against the seat behind her back. In the car behind the one next to them, there are 4 men. They are not looking at them, but Kate could see the faces of the two sitting in the front, even with her quick glance.

    “The black sedan. The one behind the Toyota next to us. I think at least two of them are the ones that got a jump on me in Central Park the other day.”

    Sonya reaches over and pulls out a semi-automatic gun from under the passenger seat as well, lying it in her lap. Next to her, Amanda looks around the car, her movements visibly nervous and jerky, but at least she doesn’t twist around to look.

    “What’s going on?”

    Her voice sounds scared, but the guilt Kate feels at that will have to wait. She turns her head slightly to her left, keeping her eyes discreetly on the car full of assassins. “We are about to be attacked.”

    Kate is not able to see any visible weapons, but there is no mistaking the tall, muscular man from the other night. The driver is definitely familiar too.

    The light changes and Sonya steps on the gas, trying to get out from behind the red Subaru that is blocking their way forward. It’s going ridiculously slow, however, and the black car with the men from Central Park slowly pulls up next to them.
