    Kate meets the eyes of one of them, the big beefcake from the other day, sitting on the passenger seat now. Kate barely has a second to note the heavy bruising on his face that she remembers she is responsible for. Good. It’s only a moment but as their gazes meet, Kate’s veins are filled with adrenaline. The men know they are busted.

    It seems almost in slow motion as Kate sees him talk, the words of course inaudible to her, and in a heartbeat, everything descends into chaos.

    The back window shatters and several gunshots can be heard, Amanda screams in terror, and they are all jostled around as Sonya twists the wheel around to slam the Jaguar into the black sedan to their side.

    “Fuck.”

    Kate swears as Yelena grabs her by the back of her neck and pushes her down, firing her gun through the window above her head. Shards of glass fall all over her head and Yelena’s shots are silenced but the window breaking is loud, as are the few answering gunshots they receive. Sonya stomps on the breaks and the car starts to slow down, even as Kate is thrown against the door to her side.

    Yelena’s elbow digs into her back, and she fires twice more before they come to a stop, taking her arm off of Kate.

    “Yelena I need you up front.”

    Sonya’s voice is alarmed this time, and Yelena is in motion barely a second later. She unbuckles herself and leaps through the space between the front seats, her gun ready in her hand.

    “Seatbelt.”

    The words are directed at Yelena, but Kate heeds Sonya’s advice too. Glancing to the side, she confirms Amanda has her seatbelt on too. She can tell she does, even though she is leaning forward with her head kept between her legs. That’s probably for the best. Sonya turns the wheel all the way to the left, and steps on the gas pedal again. The engine revs and they make a full one-hundred and eight turn, taking off in the direction they came from. Gunfire follows them barely a second later and Kate twists around to see the motorcycle still in pursuit. On it, is a lithe figure wearing all black, a gun in their hand, and their features hidden by a helmet.

    It catches up to them a few seconds later, the person right outside the window next to Kate. The assassin raises their gun, and Kate moves on autopilot, reaching through the open window, grabbing it, and pulling.

    She expects the person to fall, or let go of the gun. What she doesn’t expect is for them to lean into the motion and use Kate’s momentum to jump through the now shattered window. She hears the motorbike crash but her vision is blocked because the assassin is inside the car, and on her a second later.

    There is a sharp pain in her side as they knee into it, hitting her right in her stitches and she cries out. Using her moment of distraction, the assassin pulls the gun from her grip and points it at her head again. With what’s probably sheer luck, Kate manages to grab it before they can shoot, twisting it upwards. The gun goes off three times, creating holes in the roof of Sonya’s car. There is a feminine cry of pain from inside the assassin’s helmet as Kate uses her other hand to punch her in the ribs as hard as she can.

    Kate yanks her hand upwards, hitting the gun against the roof twice and causing it to fall down, and disappear somewhere around her feet with a clatter. The assassin moves a second later, kicking out backward and Kate hears a smack and Yelena’s unmistakable grunt of pain. A metallic glint is her only warning and she reaches out by instinct, grabbing the assassin’s other wrist before she can jam the knife into Kate’s chest. The woman is smaller than her but strong. Very strong. The position they are in also causes Kate to have to try to resist being stabbed with her wrist twisted at an awkward angle, struggling to hold her back. The blade is inching closer, and Kate groans at the effort it takes to hold her back. Suddenly the woman’s helmet-covered head sways to the side as she is kicked from the side. Amanda’s kick quite obviously didn’t manage to hurt her, but it’s enough to distract her for a split second. It's all Kate needs. It gives her an opportunity to twist the woman’s hand to the side and into the sharp shards of glass still sticking out around where the car’s window used to be. The assassin cries out as the broken pieces cut into the top side of her hand, dropping the knife out the window.

    The intrusive thought that this is the third woman in her lap this evening crosses Kate’s mind for a heartbeat, as she uses the assassin’s moment of weakness to punch her again, twice in her side. The reach for the door handle is a risky move, but Kate’s fingers close around it nonetheless and she yanks.

    The movement leaves her open, however, and when the assassin reaches back to pull a knife, that is lodged into the back of her own thigh, its blade tainted red with her blood, Kate is unable to defend herself properly. Barely managing to knock the hand coming down on her slightly upwards, Kate ends up being stabbed in the shoulder instead of the chest. In a moment that she will be quietly proud of later, she does manage to not lose sight of her objective.

    Despite crying out in pain, Kate grabs the assassin's wrist and the back of her neck and pushes her to the right side, towards Amanda. As expected, the woman resists and Kate changes directions in a second, using her own resisting force against the assassin and pulling her to the other side.

    Kate bucks up with her hips too, and the assassin is unbalanced for a moment. Using all her force, Kate shoves her out the door, and when she is far enough out of the car, she kicks her in the stomach for good measure. The assassin’s hold on her slips and she falls out, disappearing behind them somewhere, hopefully being run over by a car. Kate’s heart beats loudly in her ears as she reaches for the blade still jammed in her shoulder, barely hearing the door next to her crashing against a lamppost and flying off its hinges. “Kate,….”

    As she pulls out the knife from her shoulder, she recognizes it as one of Yelena’s. She must have stabbed the assassin in the thigh from the front. Kate looks forwards at her, noting her bloody nose, and holds out the knife to her.

    “Are you okay?”

    Yelena is talking to her, her voice finally sounding like something other than annoyed with Kate, for the first time tonight. She nods, wincing at her newest injury still throbbing and searing in pain.

    “Yeah…uh…will need stitches…but fine.”

    Yelena’s eyes look worried as she looks at the newest red patch around her now somewhat shredded white shirt, spreading down her arm and chest.

    “Amanda. You need to…”

    Yelena doesn’t get to finish the sentence as there is a loud crash and suddenly they are flying. The car flips over twice, and all Kate can do is cling to her consciousness. She feels the seatbelt dig into her chest, and her head bangs against the seat in front of her and the ceiling, but stubbornly, she refuses to pass out.

    Passing out almost certainly means death, and she clings to that thought, even as they come to a stop, upside down.

    There is one heartbeat of silence, then Kate hears an engine rev again, tires screeching. Twisting her head to the right, even upside down she can tell that it’s the same black SUV that crashed into them the first time. Its front is damaged and it’s speeding towards them again, getting faster.

    Without conscious thought, she reaches for Amanda and pulls her towards herself by her arm, away from where the car crashes into them again a second later. There is a metallic grinding sound as their car is pushed along the road, and into the side of a building. The impact sends Kate knocking around again, but just as during the first crash, she wills herself to not lose consciousness.

    Something falls from under Sonya’s seat in front of her and Kate’s mind is sharp enough with the adrenaline coursing through her veins to note that it’s the assassin’s gun from earlier. Reaching down from her hanging position she makes a garb for it. When the SUV backs up, ready to batter them against the wall again, she extends her arm by Amanda’s head and fires it twice, the sound jarringly loud in the small space.

    Even beaten and upside down, and even with a weapon she dislikes, Kate is a good shot. The bullets crack the windshield of the SUV right in front of the driver’s seat and a red mist covers the windows from the inside. The SUV rolls to a stop a few seconds later. A second later, rhythmic gunfire comes from the seats in front of Kate too, punching more holes into its windshield. Twisting around, she takes account of the people inside the car. Sonya is obviously fine enough that she is raining down bullets on the SUV herself, and she can see Amanda’s terrified, shocked but alert eyes blink at her from the side. “Yelena?!”

    Kate’s voice comes out higher than usual, thick with panic when she doesn’t see her move. Yelena doesn’t move at her voice either, at first at least, and Kate’s heart hammers against her chest harder than she thought possible.

    Then, “Ughhh…”

    There is a groan and a split-second later relief floods her as the words are spoken in that well- known Russian accent.

    “I am okay.”

    Kate exhales hard, releasing the breath she was holding. The relief is replaced by determination a second later. Fuck. Them.

    Reaching for the buckle of the seatbelt holding her up, she pushes down on the button, bracing herself for the fall. She groans when she lands on her hands and knees, several pieces of glass cutting into them, but she starts immediately crawling out anyway. Amanda is in her way, and she speaks to her, to all of them really.

    “We need to get out.”

    Just as she says the words, Sonya’s gunfire is answered, the bullets ricocheting off of the car. Kate thinks about one of them hitting a fuel line on the bottom of the car that now faces the sky, and speeds up her movements.

    “Can you see who is shooting?”

    The question is aimed at Sonya, as she makes her way past Amanda, laying low to peek out the window now close to the pavement.

    “Behind us. At your 10.”

    Peeking out from behind the now slightly bent C column of the car, she sees a soldier firing his automatic rifle at their car, not even making an effort to try and hit them directly. He is probably trying to do exactly what Kate is afraid of, blowing up the car by hitting the fuel line. Lying down on her side, Kate aims.

    “Be ready to get out in 3 seconds.”

    She gulps, trying to avoid imagining what will happen when she pulls the trigger again. She needs to get them out of here.

    “Three.”

    Sonya and Yelena unbuckle themselves, landing with matching groans with a split-second difference.

    “Two.”

    Kate glances to the side at Amanda, who is right above her, still hanging upside down. “You too, Amanda. One.”

    Amanda doesn’t move but they don’t have more time.

    Kate fires the gun twice, missing once but the second bullet hits the soldier in his head. Kate turns away as fast as she can, not wanting to watch his fall, despite being unable to avoid seeing the back of his head explode in a mist of red. She pushes down on the sickly feeling in her stomach.

    She has to focus.

    Yelena. Sonya. Amanda.

    Get them out of here.

    The gun clicks empty and she lets go of it without a second thought, reaching up to push at the button of Amanda’s seatbelt. She falls onto Kate, and they both cry out, but there is no time to waste.

    “Come on.”

    Sonya is already out of the car, firing twice more, and Kate pushes Amanda to get up and out too. Their door is opened with a metallic groan a few seconds later and Amanda climbs out, leaving Kate alone below the back seat. Sonya’s voice is uncharacteristically soft when she speaks from above her a second later.

    “You are okay. We will get out of here.”

    Kate spares herself one more second to gather her strength, before turning over to her front to crawl forward on her hands and knees, ignoring the shards of glass cutting into them again. She gets out just as Yelena does at the front, and meets her eyes above the door between them.

    Yelena’s nose is still bloody, and there is a new bruise on her temple, already purple and angry, but her eyes are alert. Kate feels dizzy for a second as she stands up, reminding her of her bleeding shoulder and broken stitches but thankfully her vision clears up a second later. There is a warm trickling sensation on the side of her face too, and she wipes at it distractedly, not even checking to see if her hand comes away red.

    Yelena’s eyes look at her with a certain wariness, and it takes her a moment, but Kate realizes she expects Kate to freak out over killing again. She nods at Yelena discreetly, trying to tell her she is okay, for now at least. They didn’t have a calm and serious discussion since Kate’s visit to her dad’s grave, so Yelena doesn’t know, but Kate meant the promise she made herself there. Whatever it takes.

    “Nice shooting, Kate.”

    There is an almost wince on Yelena’s face at Sonya’s words, but Kate just exhales, stopping her own features from twisting. Her voice still comes out flat, but there is nothing she can do about that.

    “Thanks.”

    Turning back into the car, she grabs her bow, grateful that it’s still intact and that her quiver is fashioned to keep her arrows secured, even upside down. She grabs Amanda’s bag too, handing it to her when she straightens up a moment later.

    “Are you hurt?”

    Amanda’s eyes are a bit glassy, and she is obviously a bit in shock again, but she shakes her head. Kate looks around and sees that the street is almost deserted. If there were civilians around, they must have fled at the gunshots and… general mayhem that happened in the last couple of minutes.

    Apart from the black SUV that acted as a battering ram, and hammered their car against the wall, there is another car upside down, and the black sedan is a smoking wreck about a block from their position, in the direction they came from. The soldier Kate shot is also not the only body on the floor, 3 other men are lying on the ground, and Kate turns away. Remembering the cell phone video show on CNN the other day, she leans her head down too. “We have to go before more of them show up.”

    Yelena and Sonya are in motion before she even finishes the sentence, and Kate grabs Amanda’s wrist, pulling her along too. The three of them advance on the street and Sonya leads them into an alley between the houses.

    Trying to move in the shadows, they make it about 3 blocks before Kate lets herself relax, pulling in a deep, shaky breath. The pain from her side, the new stab wound, and her head injury are slowly making themselves felt as the adrenaline starts to wear off, but she ignores it, gritting her teeth.

    “You are buying me a new car, Kate Bishop.”

    Sonya’s voice is thankfully light again, the teasing tone warming it up a little and Kate finds the strength in herself to chuckle back at her, even if a little breathy. “Gladly. Thank you, for…”

    Kate gestures vaguely behind her back referring to the car chase and the fight afterward but Sonya just waves it off, not even looking at her but checking around another corner instead. “I have had worse Tuesday nights.”

    Yelena snorts and looks at Kate from the corner of her eyes. For once, she doesn’t look angry, despite her eyes dropping to the hand that Kate still has around Amanda’s wrist. The emotion in her eyes is not one Kate can name, but she looks away in a second anyway, running after Sonya as she takes off across the street. Kate tries to not worry about the slight limp in her steps.

    Kate can hear sirens in the distance and tries to think of a plan, of a place to go to once they make it far enough that they are safe. Her mind comes back to one location only, everything else too dangerous. It seems Sonya and Yelena are thinking of the same thing, at least partially, because once Kate and Amanda catch up to them, they don’t move forward again. “We need transportation.”

    Sonya says matter of factly, and Kate nods. They are not going to get far on foot. Yelena asks Sonya, turning her back to Kate and Amanda, her shoulders tight again. Kate wills herself to ignore it.

    “Can you call Thomas?”

    Sonya shakes her head, looking around.

    “We have one civilian with us already. Him being here would be more of a liability than actually helpful.”

    She is probably right, Kate thinks, still trying to wrack her brain with an idea on what to do with Amanda. They can’t just drop her off home after all this, and the Airbnb is trashed. They are all silent for a second before Yelena sighs deeply.

    “Okay. I get us a car. Sonya, you come with me. Kate, stay here with Alice” Kate’s eyebrows furrow, before she realizes Yelena messed up the name on purpose. God, they are back to this.

    She watches them leave and turns her head towards Amanda slightly, still keeping watch. Kate’s whole body hurts, but she is used to that. She can barely imagine what the night has been like for Amanda. Unable to come up with something to say, she stays quiet but the silence doesn’t last long.

    “I get the feeling that your…coworker doesn’t like me.”

    Amanda is staring in the direction where Yelena and Sonya disappeared, and Kate sighs deeply.

    “No, uhm. We…she is mad at me, and taking it out on you, sorry.”

    Kate uses her right hand to put pressure on her own, still bleeding shoulder. It also happens to create a pinching sensation around her broken stitches that Kate guesses doesn’t mean anything good, and she winces. Amanda glances at her grimacing face, and Kate can see the reluctance on her features, but she leans off of the wall, coming to stand in front of her. “What do you need me to do?”

    Kate risks a small smile, looking down on her.

    “It’s okay, I got it.”

    Amanda closes her eyes for a moment, taking a deep, probably annoyed breath but looks up at her with determination a second later.

    “I’ll only ask one more time. What do you need?”

    Licking her lips, Kate leans her head back against the wall.

    “Okay, um…can you please put pressure on it? We need that to stop the bleeding.” Amanda takes one look at her blood-soaked shoulder, then pulls out a sweater from her bag. She pushes it against Kate’s wound, eliciting a painful groan. There are a few seconds of silence again.

    “So…security contractor, huh?”

    Her ears feel like they are aflame, but it’s hard to tell with her the general hot feeling in her head as it’s bleeding too. Kate offers Amanda a lopsided, guilty smile. “I’m sorry. This is…I’ll give you an explanation when we are safe, I promise. But it isn’t… it’s not completely a lie. I am a PI, normally.”

    Amanda’s jaw clenches as she looks up at her, gaze burning again for the first time since the crash. She purses her lips, jaw clenching, and her tone contains barely concealed anger. “I’ll listen to what you have to say because I have to know what the fuck just happened. But after that, I am gone.”

    It stings, Kate isn’t going to pretend it doesn’t…But she understands and this was her plan anyway. Nodding, she meets Amanda’s eyes.

    “Okay…as soon as it’s safe.”

    With Amanda helping and her nod, Kate feels comfortable asking.

    “Are you okay?”

    It is definitely the wrong thing to say because Amanda’s eyes flash in anger again, and her grip on Kate’s shoulder tightens.

    “Oh yeah. Just awesome. I got lured to a date by a vigilante for some reason, got dumped, got shot at, then nearly died in a car accident. I am doing great.”

    Kate gulps, trying to swallow her guilt and shame. Okay, that was a pretty stupid question. “I’m really sorry. For what it’s worth, I didn’t mean for any of this to happen. I…If I have known we will be followed, I’d have never come.”

    Amanda clanks her tongue in annoyance, but nods, leaning down her head. A car pulls up next to the alley a second later, and Kate sees Sonya and Yelena looking at them from inside. Amanda leans off of her shoulder and Kate follows her to the car, getting in after her. “So, do you drag your coworkers to every date you go to or was I just especially lucky?” The question is asked as they get into the car, and Kate facepalms internally. Couldn’t she have asked this like 10 seconds earlier, while they were still standing in the alley? “Glad to see you two have made up.”

    Sonya’s voice is dripping with both amusement and condescension. Wetting her lips, Kate groans again when Amanda leans over to put pressure on her shoulder.

    “I’ll explain, I promise. Just…one sec.”

    Sonya is driving again, and Kate looks around the car. It’s a sedan again, an inconspicuous Toyota, beige seats, and even a baby seat that pushes Amanda right into Kate’s space. “Did you two steal this?”

    The question is kind of silly, she knows. How else would they have got it, and how else would they get to wherever they are going. She continues before Yelena or Sonya can answer. “You know what, don’t answer that. Where are we going?”

    Sonya snorts amusedly and takes a right turn.

    “Home.”

    Kate’s eyebrows shoot up her forehead, and so do Yelena’s as she turns to look at Sonya in the passenger seat. Kate can’t see Sonya’s face, but her voice is not dissimilar from the motherly tone she used on them the other day. Kate feels the explanation is not for her. “Kate is injured. We are all in a rough state, and we need to regroup and figure out if Alicia over here can go home safely.”

    Amanda rolls her eyes and her hold on Kate’s shoulder tightens. Groaning again, she grabs at Amanda’s wrist to ease her hold a little, but her eyes are on Yelena, watching her jaw tighten. “I am not in a rough state. We can finish this before we go home.”

    Sonya turns her head slightly, glancing back at Kate and Amanda before fixing Yelena with a look. She answers in Russian, and Kate grits her teeth as several sentences are exchanged. After this whole night, she knows it’s not her place to bitch about anything, but being left out of the conversation on purpose is still incredibly frustrating.

    “Are you sure that’s a good idea?”

    She asks once the conversation has died down. It’s easy to see what decision has been made because Yelena leans back in her seat, crossing her arms. Even from the back seat, Kate can tell that her jaw is clenched, she might even be pouting a little.

    Kate is a bit on edge about it too. They could be followed there, and she doesn’t feel ready to compromise the security of her home just yet.

    “Well, I take it you don’t feel comfortable just dropping her off at her place and leave her to fend for herself. So, unless you have a safe-house you have been hiding from us, it’s the only idea we have.”

    Kate wishes she did have a safe house and puts it on the mental list of things she needs to sort out. But at this precise moment, Sonya is right.

    “Right.”

    The ride home is thankfully mostly uneventful. Sonya takes small streets when she can, and they make it back to Manhattan in about 30 minutes of uncomfortable silence. Kate feels both tired and wired, at the thought of the conversation she’ll undoubtedly have to have with Amanda and the tension in the car.

    It’s made even more uncomfortable when Yelena lifts her phone to her ear when they are about 10 minutes from Kate and Sonya’s building.

    “Who are you calling?”

    The question leaves Kate’s mouth unbidden, her mind searching for anything to latch onto, so she doesn’t feel nervous about the uncomfortable silence or the looming conversation. “Valentina.”

    Eyes widening, Kate sits up straighter, pushing against Amanda’s hand. “What?! Why?!”

    Yelena throws a glare over her shoulder, her voice back to cold and cutting in her annoyance. “Kate. You put on another show by climbing out that car window. That apartment is wrecked and we probably show up on a dozen CCTVs. We need her help to make it go away.” Kate shakes her head, even though in the back of her head, she knows Yelena is right. “No! No, we can…I can…”

    Racking her brain for another way out of this, she comes up empty. She wets her lips and adds after a moment.

    “You know her help means accepting his help…”

    She doesn’t dare to glance at Amanda, and she prays Yelena has enough sensibility and empathy to not mention Rojas’ name either.

    “Believe me, I do not like this any more than you do. But Barton is unavailable, so unless you have the phone number of any other Avenger, we are out of options.” Kate grits her teeth but leans back against the seat anyway. She feels Amanda’s eyes boring into her.

    “You guys work with the Avengers?”

    Yelena snorts, but it’s an unhappy sound. She cuts off Kate’s answer with her own. Not that she knew what she was going to say anyway.

    “Your girlfriend is basically Hawkeye’s little apprentice.”

    Kate’s voice comes out almost like a growl, both at the snarky tone of “your girlfriend”, which Yelena said the second time tonight, even though she is well aware that it’s not true and also at her sharing information like that with Amanda. Whatever Yelena is trying to achieve by the baiting and the antagonizing, it has to stop.

    “Yelena.”

    She sees the answering eye roll before Yelena turns back forward. She starts talking into the phone a second later.

    “Yes. It’s me”…..”Cut the pleasantries, Valentina, we need your help”…”Yes”…..”Yes. Well, stupid for sure”……”Valentina, I’m serious…”

    The one-sided conversation sounds mellow enough, despite Yelena’s annoyed tone. That is until she sucks in a breath, and her tone gets sharp enough to cut through any tiredness Kate may have started to feel. She sits up straighter immediately.

    “Would you stop that?”

    Yelena takes a deep breath, visibly composing herself before her next answer. Her tone is back to cold and collected in a second, even if it’s obviously annoyed still. …”No, we don’t have it yet”……”We need a cleanup. Several cleanups…”

    Kate cringes at that and wishes Yelena delayed this call until after they got home and Amanda was not within earshot.

    “All of it” …… ”Brooklyn. She blew up an Airbnb.”

    Kate can’t help the offense bubbling up in her chest, and she calls out. ”Heeyy! I didn’t! It wasn’t…”

    Yelena holds up a hand to indicate she should shut up, and Kate closes her mouth and clenches her jaw. She is definitely confused by Yelena’s next words. The hand she raised a second ago to silence Kate goes to pinch at the bridge of her nose.

    ”Oh my God. Business, obviously”……”It is already costing me”……

    Yelena takes another deep sigh, closing her eyes for a moment.

    ”Kate can pay you……”

    Kate runs her tongue along the front of her teeth, lips closed. She really wishes she could at least hear the whole conversation, not just Yelena’s cryptic half. That desire becomes even stronger when Yelena’s tone drops to downright dangerous a second later. “No. I told you, if he comes anywhere close to either of us, the deal is off”… A second later, Yelena sounds frustrated still, but like she is already conceding something, despite her next words.

    “There must be something else I can do.”

    Kate’s hackles are raised. She doesn’t know exactly what Valentina wants, but it’s clearly not something Yelena is comfortable with, and she can easily guess it has to do with Rojas. She also has a pretty good guess of what he wants. Which is why Yelena’s next words make her blood run cold.

    “Okay, I will do it. But no Kate.”

    Yelena holds up a hand again, but Kate ignores it.

    “Yelena, no.”

    She reaches for the phone, but Yelena leans forward, out of reach. Amanda stares at her with eyebrows raised in surprise, but Kate can’t focus on her right now. She is pretty sure Yelena just agreed to meet Rojas.

    “So you will do it, yes?”... “Can’t say the same.”

    It sounds like the tension from earlier is winding down, Yelena’s voice back to her semi-usual annoyed drawl.

    ”Yes?...”

    There is a longer pause, and Kate stops her protests when she hears Yelena’s voice drop again, even lower than last time. It almost sends chills down her spine. Slowly, Yelena speaks, quiet and intense.

    “I do not think I have to remind you who I am, Valentina. If you say anything like that again…they will never even find what is left of your body…”

    All of Kate’s senses are screaming Danger at Yelena’s tone, at her words. Next to her, Amanda stares at Yelena too, her mouth slightly agape and eyes wide. The only one completely unbothered by the exchange is Sonya, but even her face looks more serious than before, or at least the little Kate can see of it.

    “…I would choose my next words very carefully if I were you…”

    Yelena hangs up a moment later, huffing. She pushes the phone into her pockets with more force than necessary, before leaning back against the seat again, crossing her arms. “Excuse me, what the fuck was that? What did you agree to?”

    Kate’s voice is an octave higher than usual again, exasperated and a touch scared. Yelena smacks her lips in annoyance, sucking them against her teeth before throwing a glance back. “I will explain once Miss Marketing-person is not here to overhear. She knows too much as it is.”

    Kate exhales sharply, glancing over at Amanda before leaning back too. Biting down on the inside of her cheek, she goes back to her sullen silence, even though she knows Yelena is right. Amanda does know too much already, and her being a civilian poses its own kind of danger for the three of them.

    Sonya asks something in Russian, and Yelena answers with a one-word confirmation. “Da.”

    They arrive at Kate and Sonya’s building about two minutes later. The key fob was of course lost in the accident earlier, and Sonya waves the doorman over with a megawatt smile. His answering one looks dumb on his wide face, his eyes fixed on Sonya when he recognizes her. “Miss Sonya! Good evening!”

    Kate’s eyebrows shoot up her forehead, as she observes Sonya bat her eyelashes at him, only seeing her profile “Hiii, Herman! How is the night shift?”

    The man releases a breathy chuckle, puffing out his chest.

    “Much nicer now that I’ve seen ya!”

    The man, whose name is apparently Herman, has not given Kate anything but polite nods during the two times she has seen him before. Sonya gives a coy smile, giving him a once- over.

    “Herman! You flirt! Don’t break Thomas’ heart by stealing me away from him.” Herman blushes and grins back at her, probably not even comprehending the existence of the other 3 passengers in the car. Thinking about it, Kate wonders if that’s probably exactly Sonya’s objective. Yelena and Kate are visibly injured, and Amanda’s dress is covered in Kate’s blood.

    “I would never dare, Miss Sonya. So, you bought a new car?”

    It’s the first time he seems to notice anything other than Sonya, looking over the silver Toyota with somewhat surprised eyes. Sonya doesn’t miss a beat, just waving the thought off and melting his brain with another flirty chuckle.

    “No, mine is in the shop so they gave me this while it’s being fixed… Speaking of, I forgot my keys in the other car. Would you be a doll and let me in?”

    Kate is pretty sure that Sonya could ask this man to shoot someone in the head, and he’d do it with a dopey smile, as long as she is looking at him like that. Black Widows, man. She is not disappointed, and Herman almost jumps in his eagerness to please Sonya. “Right away, Miss Sonya! Good night to you and your friends!”

    “Thank you, Herman. You are my hero!”

    He looks like he just won the lottery, and when Sonya gives him a little wave as they pass him by, Kate can almost see the mental fist pump he undoubtedly does inside his head. Snorting, she asks.

    “The doorman? Really?”

    Sonya’s voice is amused as she steers them downstairs.

    “Don’t be such an elitist, Kate. He is a sweetpie. And it never hurts to have a few allies wherever one goes.”

    Surprisingly, it’s Yelena’s half-amused voice that answers, snorting too. “Allies. You have that man eating out of your palm.”

    They arrive at Sonya’s level in the garage a moment later, and Kate tries to focus on her words instead of the nerves she feels creeping up on her again. Sonya’s answer distracts her easily.

    “Ah. He is just thankful. His son needed surgery last year that he could not afford, so I paid it.”

    It’s not that Kate couldn’t imagine Sonya being a good person. She has seen the good friend she has been to Yelena, or even to Kate herself, who Sonya only met a couple of days ago. But to see her help-out random strangers, out of the goodness of her heart? After everything she must have been through… Then again, Yelena is the same. Their moral compass might be a bit wonky, but they are far from the emotionless assassins one could assume they are. Speaking of…

    “Come on. Kate needs stitches and Ashley needs to get home to her fascinating marketing- person life.”

    It seems, that those emotions still include pettiness. Kate sighs deeply at Sonya’s words. Yelena hums in agreement and Amanda kisses her teeth in annoyance. After she gets out behind Kate, she slams the door with a ferocity that feels in stark contrast to her flowery dress and five-foot-four frame.

    “I can hear you, you know.”

    Yelena immediately deadpans her answer.

    “Yes, we know.”

    Kate can’t see her face, but she can see Sonya’s as they both get out of the car on the same side. She tries to muster up some irritation at the upward twitch of the corner of her lips, but mostly, Kate just feels tired. The night has gone to shit in so many expected and unexpected ways, and being here with these three women feels completely absurd.

    Her whole body aches, again. There is also the mental fatigue that came with the many ups and downs of the evening, from her nervousness about the fake date, arguing with Yelena, the date itself, the fight and escape from the Airbnb, arguing with Yelena again, the car chase, her fight with the assassin in the car, the car crash, and now, again, her nervousness about the conversation she’s about to have with Amanda and navigating the rest of the night. Even making a list of everything that happened is fucking exhausting, and Kate almost hopes she will be offered morphine again. Okay, she doesn’t really. All of this is an emotional minefield already without lowered inhibitions added to the mix. But she definitely looks forward to not being conscious for at least 12 hours after tonight, whenever she gets there. As they step into the elevator, she pushes the button 29 and leans back against the wall with a groan. Her shoulder is still bleeding a little, and if nothing else, the stinging pain numbs her brain to everything else a little. Closing her eyes, she puts her head back against the cool metal and waits for her companions to get in as well.

    The doors finally close, and as the elevator starts moving, Sonya and Yelena exchange some Russian words again. Kate licks her lips, not having the energy to comment, but she cracks her eyes open when they come to a stop on the 13th floor.

    “I’ll be right up.”

    Sonya exists with a wink over her shoulder, directed at Kate. The deep, defeated sigh that rises from her chest is involuntary. She glances briefly at Amanda, who seems to be looking at Yelena, who in turn stares forward at the doors.

    “Why is Sonya coming up?”

    Yelena’s shoulders rise and fall, and she seems to try to release some of the tension in herself before she answers. Her words are still biting, but less aimed to hurt than before. “Your first aid kit is a joke.”

    Kate smacks her lips, pulls them to the side, and frowns.

    “It’s not a joke. I have a suture kit and bandages.”

    Yelena turns a bit around to look at her, meaningfully glancing down on her blood-soaked white shirt.

    “You need another transfusion. And we all need to talk.”

    Kate sniffs, not really looking forward to staying put for an hour before she can go to sleep, but she does feel a bit woozy, and attributing it to the blood loss is a pretty logical conclusion.

    “Fine… But no morphine.”

    Yelena snorts, glancing at Amanda for a second.

    “No morphine.”

    The elevator comes to a stop and Kate leads them down to her door, dragging her feet a little. The exhaustion of the evening catches up to her slowly, and she takes a deep breath, trying to tamp down on the irritation she feels at still having a long list of stressful conversations to get through before she can collapse into her bed.

    Finally arriving at the door Kate digs into her right pocket for her keys but they are not in there.

    Tapping all of her pockets, left one, and both of the back ones, she starts to get frantic. She only finds her car keys, phone, and retractable sword, taking them out to hold in her hand one by one.

    Oh no.

    Ugh. Fuck this evening.

    Leaning her forehead against the door, Kate groans.

    “I lost my keys.”

    Behind her, Amanda shuffles around awkwardly and Yelena takes a deep breath, then exhales it hard.

    “Move.”

    Kate hears her dig into her pocket and obeys, moving out of the way. She can’t even say she is surprised as she watches Yelena fish out a keyring from one of her many pockets, and select one of them.

    Of course, she made a copy of Kate’s apartment keys. Of course, she did. Yelena unlocks the door and walks in like she owns the place, going straight to the bathroom. “Unbelievable.”

    Muttering under her breath, Kate shakes her head. At this point, both as in, this evening, and generally in their relationship, she doesn’t even know whether she finds it endearing, entertaining, or infuriating. It feels like too much of a hassle to figure that out right now though.

    She motions for Amanda to enter and Kate is the last through the door, closing it behind herself.

    Amanda halts a few steps into the apartment, looking around.

    “So. This is your place.”

    Walking to the small table by the side of the door, Kate puts down her retractable sword, and her car keys, glancing at her and around the place briefly.

    “Yeah…um, make yourself at home.”

    Amanda’s voice is cold as she speaks again, a moment later.

    “Doesn’t look like there is much of a mess from the move after all.”

    Leaning on both hands against the table for a second, Kate takes another deep breath, ignoring the pain it causes in her side.

    “Yeah, I…well, that was a lie. I will explain everything in a minute. But amm, right now, can I get you anything?”

    It’s pretty obvious that they are reaching the end of Amanda’s patience for getting her answers but Kate doesn’t want to have this conversation in front of Sonya, and especially not in front of Yelena. If they will, it will be undoubtedly derailed, and now that they managed to make it this far, Amanda can wait another 20 minutes.

    “No. You can tell me whatever you dragged me into. Who are you? Who are they?...” Amanda gestures at the guestroom where Yelena is audibly rummaging around. Her voice is audibly agitated, finally feeling safe enough to start to freak out at Kate. It’s pretty bad timing. Then again, the whole night has been.

    “…Why did you…what happened?”

    Kate takes out her no-longer-functional earpiece and drops it onto the table too with the rest of her items before turning towards Amanda. She leans back slightly against the table, gripping onto its edge. Despite her exhaustion, she tries to convey a calming tone, hoping to kick this can just a little more down the road.

    “Listen, I promise I will tell you everything. I swear. But let's get this over with first, okay? Then we can sit down and have a proper talk.”

    Shaking her head, Amanda’s voice gains volume. Her brow furrows and she really looks like she is at the end of her wits.

    “No! I’ve waited all…”

    “And you can wait some more. Or you can walk out that door with no answers, and possibly get killed. I do not really care either way, but I am fixing Kate’s shoulder first.” Yelena comes waltzing back into the living room, not even sparing a glance at Amanda as she cuts her off. She has washed the blood off from below her nose, and she carries Kate’s medical supplies in her hands.

    “Kate, sit.”

    Her voice is snappy and halfway bored. It’s incredibly rude, so it’s not really a surprise that Amanda’s jaw drops in offense. Kate steps forward, ready to deescalate things but Amanda seems to have reached her breaking point for the night too.

    “Okay, Yelena or whatever your name is. I don’t know if I managed to somehow piss into your cereal, or you are just generally a bitch, but we are having a conversation. Kate promised me answers, and I am done waiting.”

    Yelena drops the items in her hand onto the coffee table and levels Amanda with a glare that leads to Kate immediately stepping forward again with an awkward chuckle. “Hey, let’s calm down…”

    Unsurprisingly, Yelena doesn’t listen.

    Stepping around the table, she keeps her gaze on Amanda and if Kate wasn’t so nervous, she’d be impressed with Amanda’s ability to hold it, even lifting her chin a little in defiance. Yelena doesn’t even look at Kate as she speaks, staring into Amanda’s face instead, with a smile that looks entirely too mocking.

    “Okay, Amanda, or whatever your name is…”

    Kate can see that whatever will leave her mouth next will not be a pleasant experience for anyone involved, so she starts to walk forward.

    “Yelena…”

    “No, Kate. Your girlfriend demands answers, why don’t we give her some, hm?” Kate steps into her way before she can get any closer to Amanda, halting her advance. “Stop it. Please.”

    At hearing her pleading voice, Yelena tears her gaze away from Amanda and looks up at Kate. She looks just as tired as Kate feels, and there is a stiffness to her movements that is not usually present, but the fire from earlier is back in her eyes. It seems to dim when she looks at Kate’s pleading face.

    She can see the moment Yelena starts to wind down, grinding her teeth. She steps away, turning back to the couch and her voice is impatient and heavy when she answers. “Fine. I said, sit.”

    Kate exhales and looks at her as Yelena starts to pick up the items she half threw, half dropped onto the coffee table a second ago, but her relief is short-lived. “Oh. My. God!...For fuck’s sake, Kate! Shit.”

    Twisting around quickly she looks at Amanda’s shocked face, who stares at Yelena. “Wha..?”

    She glances back at Yelena too, trying to figure out what Amanda sees, before looking back at her.

    “You…? What the fuck? Is that what’s going on?...”

    Kate is just staring at her, trying to figure out whatever conclusion she seems to have jumped to.

    “…You were cheating?! She..?! Our date…What the…”

    Immediately aware of where this is going, Kate steps towards her, both hands held up. She is trying to stop anything else from coming out of Amanda’s mouth, but she steps backward and away from Kate.

    “No! No no no, that’s not…”

    “…fuck? Jesus. I knew you were a little too good to be true, but that’s just, wow…” “Amanda, no.”

    Her words seem to have no apparent effect on Amanda, but Yelena’s way-too-loud to be honest chortle does. She grins but Kate sees no joy behind her eyes, tilting her head to the side.

    “Suka, please. I am not doing that…”

    Ouch. That tone is definitely not flattering.

    “…But if I did, there is no way she’d trade me in, for you.”

    That is the moment the front door opens, and Sonya arrives. All eyes jump to her, and Kate can see that she heard the full sentence by the look on Sonya’s face. She looks half-surprised, half-amused already, and definitely intrigued.

    “Wow. I see things are going as well as expected.”

    She closes the door behind herself, and despite the comment, Kate has probably never been so happy for her awkwardly-timed appearances. Using the pause in the argument, which feels entirely too weird by the way, she finally speaks her piece.

    “Amanda. I am not dating Yelena. She is a…”

    Gulping, she hesitates over what word to use, all too aware of the three pairs of eyes on her. Despite Yelena’s very hurtful tone about “not doing that”, she tries to aim for something that will appease everyone and stop this from becoming an even bigger mess. “close friend, and an amazing ally who helps me out with this case. We…we had a tense couple of days, and all of us are on edge. It’s not…I did not cheat, and if she is hostile to you, it’s because she is mad at me.”

    She pauses to take a breath, but when nobody interrupts her, Kate continues. She glances at Yelena behind her and sees that her face is completely blank. Her eyes are still burning, with what Kate assumes is anger, but she doesn’t attempt to cut her off so she takes that as a good sign.

    “I dragged her and Sonya out tonight, because…. Well, as you can see it’s not really a good idea for me to go out alone right now. I will explain why, but please. Let them do their job, and then go have their well-deserved rest, okay? And I will tell you everything after.” She turns back to Amanda, who seems to be weighing her words. Her eyes slide from Kate to Yelena, and Kate hears her start to move around behind her back, before sliding back onto her.

    “Okay.“ “Thank you.”

    She gives Amanda a small smile, but it’s not returned. Turning towards Sonya, her hope for getting some reassurance vanishes too, as her face is an unreadable mask too. There is something akin to disappointment in her eyes, but Kate doesn’t feel like she has the mental or emotional capacity to unpack that right now.

    “Where is the bathroom?”

    Amanda speaks again, and Kate points to the door Yelena exited from a few minutes before. When she leaves and shuts the door behind herself, Kate feels the inexplicable urge to apologize. She does have a lot of things to say sorry for, but for some reason, it feels like it’s her last few sentences that bring the awkward, somewhat stifling silence down on the room. Obeying Yelena’s earlier request, if it can be called that, she goes to sit on the couch. She searches for Yelena’s eyes who doesn’t look back at her but instead prepares the suture kit. Despite many signs pointing to that exact fact tonight, Kate likes to think she is not stupid. Yelena was jealous of this date earlier and despite her words to Amanda a minute ago, she is aware that there must be at least a sparkle of attraction towards her that made that happen. Kate pointing out, to the object of said jealousy of all people, very plainly that nothing is going on between them, right in front of her, is probably not something Yelena is particularly happy about. It stings especially because it feels like a lie, despite being factually true. Ever since that moment on Sonya’s couch, probably even before that, there has been something going on, and she is well aware of it. So is Yelena, and without a doubt, so is Sonya. But what was she supposed to say?

    She doesn’t even know what to call what’s been going on. Yelena is a great friend, and to put a name on the thick tension that’s been building for days is impossible, and explaining it… yeah, that’d have been straight-up weird.

    Nevertheless, she feels like she should apologize, or say something. When Yelena finally turns around, she hopes to catch her gaze but she focuses determinedly on Kate’s chest, her lips tugged slightly downwards. Without a word, she reaches for the edge of her shirt and tears it, the buttons flying everywhere.

    “Jesus, Yelena. Give a girl a warning.”

    Yelena does glance at her then, eyes cold and jaw set. Sonya reaches for the back of her neck from the other side and pulls her forward. Yelena holds her eyes as she pulls the shirt off of her shoulder, and down her arms with rough motions.

    “Oh, sorry. The last few days must have really put me on the edge.”

    The words are dripping with sarcasm, and if Kate wasn’t so busy groaning at the material being torn off of her skin, the dried blood making it stick into her wound, she’d have glared at her.

    “Fuck…oww…Yelena!”

    She manages to say between groans, as Sonya pushes her back against the couch with an unnecessarily rough motion. She sits on the couch now, only wearing her sports bra and Yelena reaches for the anti-septic. She pauses and gives a smile that is so condescending, Kate already feels her blood start to boil again at the sight of it.

    “Oh look, you got your wish.”

    Not bothering with dabbing at the wound, she tilts the anti-septic bottle downwards, making it flow directly onto the wound. Kate hisses but manages to ask.

    “What…shit, ow…what do you mean?”

    Yelena levels her with a look, and that mocking, way too sticky sweet smile still edged on her face, before starting to clean the wound with a cotton bud with more force than necessary. “She gets to see you in your underwear after all.”

    Kate grits her teeth and glares at her, using all her self-restraint to not be baited into a fight again. Her frustration is definitely palpable in her voice though.

    “Fucking christ, Yelena. I told you I wasn’t trying to…”

    Yelena’s fake smile drops, and she reaches for the suture kit. On her other side, Sonya puts an elastic band around her arm and extends it with another not-too-gentle tug. She glances towards the bathroom door, lowering her voice.

    “That’s not what’s happening here.”

    Yelena sticks the needle into her skin to start stitching, and her voice sounds marginally more honest but no less venomous.

    “I really don’t care, Kate.”

    Kate grits her teeth at the pain but swallows her rebuttal that Yelena does very much seem to care. Yelena starts to sew her skin with practiced motions, refusing to look at her. Kate tries to search for Sonya’s eyes too but for once, she seems more than fine with working in icy silence too. She sticks a butterfly needle into Kate’s arm, then starts preparing the blood bag she brought up with her.

    Kate takes a deep breath and closes her eyes. Amanda has been in the bathroom for a long time and Kate suspects she is taking her time to avoid Yelena and Sonya, maybe even Kate herself too. A part of her is jealous of the opportunity to do so. The other half yearns to fix whatever this whole night seems to have broken. That part, the more adult one, makes her open her mouth again.

    “I am sorry, okay?”

    Yelena pauses her ministrations to glance at her, before continuing. Kate wets her lips, blinking slowly, and tries to ignore the pain of the needle being threaded through her skin. “For…all of this. I am really sorry for how this night turned out. I am sorry for dragging you guys out and I really…I didn’t mean to put anyone in danger.

    She pauses, hoping that one of them will answer her but they are both still working in silence. “And Sonya, um, I’m sorry for your car. I promise, I’ll…I’ll buy you another one.” Yelena is still not looking at her, and she glances over at Sonya who finally looks back at her, but not before glancing at Yelena too. Her voice is not as harsh as Kate expects when she speaks.

    “Yeah, okay. We will need to talk about this. All of this, when your…when Amanda is gone.” Kate nods, and she is thankful that at least Sonya seems amicable enough to talk to her. Yelena just continues her stitching, and Kate has to bite down on her lip to avoid moaning at the pain. She should have taken the time to swallow an Advil at least, and she looks into the light above her head to avoid tearing up with the agony.

    Sonya connects the blood bag to the IV line in Kate’s arm, and Yelena moves on to re-stitch the torn shotgun injury on Kate’s side. Her hands are still rough and methodical with Kate, but she is careful to not injure her any further. Sonya checks the wound on her head, her hands no longer as rough as they first were, but she probably deems it not serious, because she lets go of her a few seconds later.

    Absolutely unsure what to say, to make this alright, especially right now, Kate stays quiet. None of the glances she throws at Yelena are returned for the next several minutes, and she rakes her brain on what to say to make this right.

    When she is done, Yelena plasters a bandage over both newly sewn wounds and stands up. “Thank you.”

    Kate says, trying to convey she means it for more than just the stitching and the medical care. It seems Yelena is not ready to bury the hatchet just yet, because she turns away without looking at Kate or saying anything. Kate’s stomach sinks.

    She watches with a twist in her gut as Yelena gathers her things and turns to leave. “Have fun with your talk. I am sure you’ll make it worth her while.”

    Yelena finally speaks, throwing that over her shoulder as she opens the front door and walks out with one last, withering look at Kate. It looks both angry and as bone-tired, as Kate herself feels. The mocking drop in Yelena’s tone on the last half of the sentence feels significant, but Kate doesn’t understand why those words are stressed like that. Sonya is right behind Yelena, but she does pause. Turning back before she steps over the threshold, it seems like she’s trying to decide what to say, and her voice is hesitant, but not mean when she ends up making up her mind.

    “Goodnight. Take your anti-biotics and…don’t tear your stitches.”

    Kate wants to throw her hands up.

    What do they expect to happen here? Kate is pretty sure that Amanda hates her guts, and Kate is definitely not up for anything right now either.

    “Yeah. Sure. Of course, thank you.”

    Sonya nods, then she is out of the door too, closing it behind herself. The blood bag is still connected to her arm, so Kate calls out.

    “They are gone. You can come out…if you want.”

    There is no answer or even a sound of movement from the room. Worry stirs in Kate’s stomach, and she stands up with a stifled groan. Grabbing hold of the IV stand that Sonya also brought with her, she walks to the bathroom door and knocks.

    “Amanda?”

    She still doesn’t hear an answer, and her stomach knots in a spark of panic, so she twists the door handle, stepping into the toom.

    The knot in her belly eases, but her stomach immediately plummets at the sight that greets her.

    Amanda sits on the tiled floor, with her knees to her chest and her chin resting on them. Her face is covered in tears again, and her eyes look up at Kate when she enters but immediately go back to staring at the ground again.

    Kate is not stupid enough to ask her if she is okay this time. Clearly, she is not. Instead, she makes her way over and sinks to the ground next to her. The bathtub is cold against her almost completely naked back, but it’s a welcome feeling, grounding her. She matches Amanda’s position, pulling her knees up to her chest, and loosely wraps her arms around them.

    Not really knowing where to start, she says after a few seconds of silence. “I am so sorry.”

    Amanda shakes her head, and her tongue darts out to wet her lips.

    “That doesn’t really cut it, Kate.”

    Nodding, Kate gulps. There are no words to express how sorry she is for how everything turned out. The only upside is that Amanda is safe now, and for the most part, unharmed. “I know. But I still am. I…Do you still want to talk, or should I just…leave you alone?” Amanda shakes her head, wiping a hand under her eyes to rid her skin of the smeared makeup.

    “I want to know…And then, I want you to leave me alone.”

    With another nod, Kate tries to gather her thoughts. Despite the long ride home, and her nervousness, she feels unprepared for what’s about to come.

    “Ookay. Um…Do you want to ask questions or like, should I just tell you everything from the start?”

    As Amanda glances at her, her blue eyes seem to shine especially bright with the tears still in them. She seems to weigh her options for a moment, before answering.

    “Tell me from the start.”

    Taking a deep breath, Kate tries to decide where that start exactly is. Their first date seems like an obvious point in time to pick up the thread, but it doesn’t explain Kate’s vigilanteism, or what happened tonight, now that Amanda figured out (and Yelena confirmed) that they were the ones on the news.

    The Christmas before last? It also feels like there is a piece is missing. With another deep breath, she decides to give Amanda a crash course in her career as Hawkeye. “Okay, so. When I was younger, aliens invaded. I am sure you have your own story from that day too, but for me…I was home with my parents, and they were arguing. I was alone when the attack hit, and I went looking for them, only to find half of our apartment missing. When I looked out, I could see the destruction, the…all of it. And I was terrified.” Wetting her lips, she pauses for a second.

    It’s one of her most important core memories, shaping who she is as a person and it feels both right and wrong to be sharing it with Amanda, after knowing her for such a short time. Amanda wipes at her face, trying to rid it of the remaining traces of her tear distractedly, but seems to be ready to listen. Kate pushes on.

    “I was terrified and I couldn’t find my parents, and when I looked out the window, I could see Clint. Um, Hawkeye, fighting aliens with nothing but his bow and arrows. He wasn’t… He didn’t have any superpowers, but he had the courage to do what’s right, and I…I lost my dad that day, but his courage? It gave me the courage to go on.”

    Amanda listens quietly, and Kate doesn’t look at her as she talks, but she sees her glance at Kate a few times, obviously interested in her story. She smiles a little bittersweetly, remembering the journey that led her here.

    “At my dad’s funeral, I asked my mom for a bow and arrow, and she…probably because she was trying to help ease my grief or something, she went along with it. I was already a tomboy before, I guess. I, um…I took various martial arts since I was 6, but from then on, I dedicated my life to becoming just like him. Just like Clint, I mean. I trained every day, and I wanted nothing more than to become an Avenger, to help people like he has helped me, without even knowing.”

    Amanda hums, and Kate waits for her to say something, but she just nods. “Go on.”

    “Well, anyway. With the Blip, that kind of went to shit, and because my mom was so adamant about me taking over Bishop Security, I went to college. And then…two years ago on Christmas, I attended yet another party that my mom threw and uh. I saw her arguing with someone. Someone we knew, that she worked with. And because I wanted to protect her, I followed him. He attended like a…a secret underground auction, and it…well, it went to shit. It got attacked by these ground-level mob guys, and I ended up taking something, that belonged to Clint.”

    She obviously can’t tell Amanda it was the Ronin suit, so she is thankful when she doesn’t interrupt to ask about her purposefully vague phrasing. She presses on before Amanda can take note of that detail.

    “He found me to get it back, but the mob guys mistook me for someone I’m not. And he stuck around to help me out, and get me out of that mess. We…we looked into my mom’s business and thought her fiancé was responsible for his uncle’s murder. Wait, his uncle was the guy my mom argued with at her party, I forgot to tell you that part. And I found him dead later that night. Anyway…he didn’t kill him. We found out…well, technically Yelena found out that it was my mom, and that she was working for a mob boss.”

    Amanda’s brow furrows, and she blinks at Kate, her eyes confused.

    “Yelena? How did she come to the picture? Is she like your sidekick or something?” Kate snorts, then winces at the motion, but she releases an amused exhale anyway. “Don’t ever let her hear you call her that. No, um. She had some beef with Clint, it…it was a misunderstanding. She came to New York to um, confront him and we ended up meeting too. It’s a long story that’s not really connected to this one.”

    She extends her legs, stretching out her tired muscles, before crossing them. “So anyway, we found out my mom was working for this mob boss guy this whole time because apparently, my dad owed him money. But she continued to work for him, even after she paid off his debts, and um, we got rich…or well. Richer because of it. Long story short, I, uh. I confronted him, the mob boss guy, and my mother both.”

    Before she continues, Kate clears her throat and leans her head back against the tub. “He escaped but my mother got arrested. After that I, um….I told you, I had a hard time. I didn’t lie about that. I…People who I thought were friends used me to sell our story, and well. I ended up leaving New York a couple of months later. I’ve been living in LA ever since.”

    Amanda seems to consider her words and looks at her again, searching her face. Kate hopes she looks honest. Wetting her lips, Amanda looks back onto her own knees. “So you really just got back?”

    Kate nods, her lips pulling into a small, humorless smile.

    “Yeah. I…I have been working as a PI in LA, and like…training with Clint, and doing a few missions with a few other…people like me. I feel…I feel the word vigilante is a bit… negative. Anyway, not the point. Fast forward, my mother’s trial is finally moving forward, and I will have to attend the trial, as a witness. So…”

    Amanda turns to look at her, wide-eyed, interrupting.

    “You are…going to be a witness against your mom?”

    Kate looks down at her hands, playing with the IV line, pursing her lips. After a moment, she nods.

    “Yeah. She…Against her and the mob boss she was working for.”

    Amanda exhales hard, puffing out her cheeks.

    “Okay. That’s…I don’t know what to say to that. I don’t know if I could do the same…if Adam, my brother. If he was still alive and he got arrested…”

    Kate gulps, nodding.

    “I…I kind of got her arrested myself.”

    Taking a deep breath, she turns to Amanda. She is staring at her with wide eyes and lips agape before she turns away.

    “Wow, that…that’s heavy.”

    “Yeah.”

    Amanda almost looks soft again, before she seems to remember what happened tonight and her eyes harden again.

    “Okay, so I know how you got into…vigilantism. What about what happened tonight…with me?”

    Kate pulls her lips to a sad smile, playing with the IV line still, wrapping and twisting it around her fingers.

    “Yeah, sorry. Um, so I came back for the trial. And I, um, being back here, it…I was really feeling the guilt of everything, so I went to F.E.A.S.T, and well. I met you. And I…Amanda, please know that nothing was going on yet the first time we went out. None of it was…” Taking another deep breath, Kate runs the hand without an IV line through her hair, trying to assemble her thoughts, her feelings into something honest and manageable. “I didn’t know what was happening the first night we went out. I just liked you, and I wanted to have a nice time. There was no hidden agenda, or any sign of this mess yet.” Amanda bites down on her lower lip, and blinks a few times, turning away from Kate to process. She lets her and doesn’t continue until Amanda turns back to her, meeting her gaze again.

    “Okay, so…What happened?”

    Kate nods to herself but holds eye contact for a few seconds.

    “When I got home, Yelena was here. She…um, she found out there was a bounty on my head and apparently, a bunch of assassins have been hired to take me out. She came to warn me and we both think they were hired by the same mob boss my mom was working for, trying to get me out of the way before the trial. I asked her..well, she kind of invited herself too, but I asked her to help me look into it and try to catch him before he manages to get me killed. And we have been doing that ever since, while dodging attempts at my life.” Okay. That’s a bit overly dramatic phrasing but Kate has been tried to be murdered almost every day since that fateful evening. Amanda’s eyebrows furrow again, and she looks confused.

    “But, uh, why? Why not go to the police?”

    Kate shakes her head, her own brow wrinkling.

    “He is above all that. He has people everywhere and he has been in hiding since that Christmas, almost 2 years ago now. The police are not even really trying to catch him.” The look on Amanda’s face is not exactly displeased but she still doesn’t seem to grasp it. “So what, you decided to just go after him, and kill everyone in your way?” Shaking her head again, Kate denies it, but it feels a little bit like a lie. She tries to explain. “No. Well, okay, technically yes. Not really. But you have no idea how dangerous he is. The things he has done. He…uh, he has to be stopped. And I don’t mean to hurt anyone.” Amanda sucks her teeth, clearly disagreeing, eyes hard as she turns her head to look at Kate. “Well, yeah, maybe. But how is what you are doing any different? You have a personal stake in all of this, and you are playing judge, jury, and executioner.”

    It’s Kate’s turn to confusedly disagree.

    “No? I am trying to actively stop him from killing me, my family, or my friends. Just in the last week, I have been shot, beaten, stabbed…”

    Amanda’s face is hard now, eyes boring into hers.

    “Yes, but you have gone looking for it. And you have caused the death of a lot of people in your way…”

    The hairs start to stand on the back of Kate’s neck, and her eyes narrow. “Amanda, you don’t understand. Yes, I have killed people, just like soldiers in war do…” The fire in Amanda’s eyes burns bright, and she shakes her head, cutting Kate off. “That’s not the same thing. You have a personal stake in this. They are just following orders.” Kate almost leans back, as if she was slapped. She can’t be serious.

    “How is that any better, than what I do? I am protecting people. I…Yes, I am included amongst those people, but I am protecting people from someone who is a monster. Who has done things…I can’t even…you don’t know.”

    Amanda shakes her head again.

    “Because you don’t get to decide who lives or who dies. Those people are just…” Kate lifts her chin. She knows this is a sensitive topic for Amanda, for obvious reasons. But she is wrong about this. Despite cutting her off, Kate tries to make her voice gentle. “I understand that…you see this from a…different perspective. But Amanda… Those people, even the foot soldiers, they chose that life. They have chosen to kill and torture and do awful, horrible things. I might be playing judge, jury, and executioner, but they do not even do that. They just…they kill for convenience.”

    “And you don’t?”

    She answers without hesitation, righteous anger making her tone a bit harder than it probably should be.

    “I don’t. Any time I can avoid it, I do.”

    Amanda shakes her head. She looks annoyed still, but at least that’s better than her crying like earlier.

    “We’ll never agree on this. Let’s move on.”

    Kate gulps, a bitter taste left in her mouth after the last few minutes but she pushes down on her own frustration too.

    “Okay.”

    “So, what happened tonight?”

    Taking one more step away from her annoyance, Kate breathes in and exhales slowly. This will have to be handled delicately, and she will have to lie. She starts with the truth. “When I called you the other night…Well, I think it’s pretty obvious that I lied about being in Chicago. I knew this was dangerous but I hoped…I hoped we would make faster progress and…anyway. Um, last week I asked another friend for help. She, uh…”

    Of course, she can’t reveal what Wendy did for her but she can give the broad strokes. “She is not a…vigilante. She is a civilian, kind of…I asked her to do me a favor to get me some information about the mob boss we are investigating. Turns out, he was a step ahead, and he had her wife abducted.”

    She glances at Amanda to see if that softens her hard-set features, but that doesn’t seem to be the case.

    “We found out by accident. Kind of. Um, some of the info she has given us turned out to be fishy and I called her to check what was going on. She was obviously…out of it. They blackmailed her into giving us bad intel, that nearly got both Yelena and me killed. They called her and we figured out she might be in the harbor and went to investigate.” Kate gulps and rubs her face with both hands. When she pulls them away to continue, she doesn’t look at Amanda again. With her own guilt still stirring at the events that went down on the ship, she doesn’t think she can handle the judgmental look she assumes Amanda wears too.

    “I…I think you are aware of how that turned out. We, um. We only went there to investigate and found a lair full of mob guys. They tried to kill us, and we found…we found some pretty messed up stuff. But we ended up finding the friend’s wife too, still alive. It was her, um, the friend that you talked to on the phone.”

    Amanda doesn’t sound judgmental, but she definitely doesn’t soften either. “Okay.”

    “It was…the whole day was a train-wreck. Things got way out of hand, and we got hurt. Really hurt. Yelena…she, uh almost died. Actually, we both kind of almost did, I guess. And I…I saw things. I don’t…it was a really um, stark reminder of how dangerous everything was. So, when I got my phone back the next day from the friend, and I called you…I was calling to make sure you stay as far away from it all as possible.“ Amanda’s face finally softens a little, maybe because there is a tremor in Kate’s voice that she is unable to hold back.

    “Okay…and um. What changed?”

    Kate closes her eyes and leans down her head. She can’t help but feel ashamed at how quickly she jumped to conclusions, even though logically she knows she had good reasons to. “You knew my name.”

    She says it simply, honestly. Her eyes open to see Amanda’s reaction, cringing a little. “I…I know this is hard to justify, and I am…I really am so sorry now. But after the whole deal with my mom, and the last few weeks…I jumped to the worst conclusion.” Amanda’s eyebrows furrow again, and she shakes her head.

    “I don’t think I follow.”

    Scratching at the dried-up blood on her forehead, Kate hesitates. The conclusions she jumped to sound even more ridiculous without revealing she knew about Amanda’s brother and the Rojas connection, but it’ll have to do. That’d unravel what happened with Clint, and add another dangerous layer Amanda is aware of that she doesn’t need to be. “We…I thought that it was just too convenient that you showed up, all pretty and sweet when a bounty was put on my head and then just magically figured out who I was. I thought you might have ulterior motives.”

    Amanda sounds partially amused but most just exasperated.

    “Wait. You thought…you thought I went on a date with you to what…seduce and kill you?” Kate gives her an awkward smile and Amanda burst out laughing, but it’s not exactly a good- natured sound, looking at her a little like when a crazy person explains something to you at a gas station.

    “Jesus, Kate. That’s insane.”

    Half groaning half laughing, Kate turns away.

    “It may be to you! But it seemed kind of reasonable at the time. I…We really did have a very intense couple of days.”

    Shaking her head, Amanda rubs at own face too.

    “If you thought that, why did you even show up? Why not just…I don’t know. Ghost me?” Running a hand through her hand, Kate tries to explain. It would have been the more logical conclusion, yes, but Kate had to….know.

    “I wasn’t sure. About you I mean. I couldn’t decide and I just… I had to see you to find out.” Amanda nods. Her features are less hard now, and she thinks about everything Kate told her for about a minute before she speaks again.

    “What would you have done if I did work for that mob boss?”

    Pursing her lips, Kate glances at her, and she considers her answer for a few seconds before answering too, deciding to be honest.

    “I don’t know. I’d have tried to figure out what you knew. Then escape probably? Or fight you if you did try to kill me.”

    Amanda laughs again, the sound laced thickly with disbelief.

    “Right…Okay…”

    Another few breaths of silence follow and Kate watches Amanda’s face as she processes. The lines between her eyebrows deepen again, and there is a glint in her eye as she asks her next question.

    “How come you didn’t assume Yelena was coming to kill you? She showed up the same night and she seems more than capable.”

    Kate snorts and smiles at the memory of that particular conversation.

    “Oh, I did. But… she did come to warn me so that was a stupid conclusion to jump to as well.”

    “Why?”

    Kate glances back at Amanda who now looks at her evenly, with a strange glint in her eye. “Um…why, what?”

    Tilting her head slightly to the side, Amanda looks at her quietly for a second. “Why did she warn you? No offense, I get that she is your friend, but um…she doesn’t look like a good Samaritan who would come to warn you out of the goodness of her own heart.” Kate feels a protectiveness at Amanda’s words and her brow furrows.

    “Yelena is…it’s complicated. But she is a good person. I know she, uh…she can be a bit harsh, but...”

    Amanda’s eyebrows shoot up on her foreead, and she huffs out a breathy, unbelieving chuckle.

    “Kate, she told me she’d not care if I walked out and died. Because she is angry, for some reason, with you.”

    Kate sighs and tries to tamp down on the annoyance she feels filling her veins. Resisting the urge to rub at her face again, she throws Amanda a glare.

    “As I said, it’s complicated. She had a really, really rough life and we have had a very intense couple of days, and…”

    Amanda cuts in to finish her sentence.

    “And she is into you.”

    Kate blinks at her, mouth slightly agape. Shaking her head a little, she tries to dispel whatever wrong conclusion Amanda has arrived at.

    “No, I told you…I…We…”

    There is a half-smile on Amanda’s face, but her eyes are looking at Kate with that glint still that she can’t quite name.

    “No, I believe you. I believe that you are not dating. But take it from someone, who never wants to see either of you ever again after tonight, she was practically green.” The thing is, Kate knows Amanda is not entirely wrong. But discussing this feels icky, again. Like wires that shouldn’t be crossed. Her face must betray her because Amanda’s eyes flash with something and she lifts her chin slightly.

    “Oh. So you are aware.”

    Her chin is jutted out and Kate licks her lips, and attempts to lead the conversation away from this topic again.

    “No. We…There is nothing to be aware of. It’s just a…a complicated relationship.” The snort she receives in answer does sound honestly amused finally, and Amanda rolls her eyes almost good-naturedly.

    “Oh yeah. That’s why she looked ready to murder us all when you called her an amazing ally.”

    Kate burrows her face in her palms. Why the fuck are they talking about this? Thankfully Amanda seems to be ready to drop it too.

    “Anyways, it’s none of my business, and… after tonight, I really don’t care. But I am not blind.”

    Leaning her head back against the tub again, Kate concedes. She is way too tired for this. “Right. It’s…Okay.”

    Amanda looks at her for a few moments longer, before turning away and looking around the room.

    “What about the other woman. Sonya?”

    Kate wills herself to not let her annoyance show. She may be exhausted, but Amanda does deserve the answers she is seeking, even if Kate can’t tell her the whole truth about some things.

    “What about her?”

    “How does she come into the picture?”

    Meeting Amanda’s eyes again, Kate explains.

    “She is a friend of Yelena’s. I only met her recently too, but because we… I am not exaggerating, we both got hurt pretty bad the other day. So she decided to tag along and help tonight.”

    Amanda licks her teeth with her lips closed, and nods. There are a few more seconds of silence before she speaks again.

    “Okay. I think…I think I know enough now.”

    She pauses and Kate doesn’t want to interrupt. There is a finality to Amanda’s tone, and her face seems serious, but not angry anymore.

    “I get that… I will never agree with what you are doing, I hope you understand that I never can.”

    She waits for Kate to confirm with a not before continuing.

    “But I do get why you came tonight, even if it sounds insane to me. And I…I get that you didn’t try to hurt me on purpose, even though you did.”

    Kate gulps and blinks slowly before meeting her eyes again.

    “I really am so sorry, Amanda. If I could go back…”

    Amanda smiles at her, holding her eyes.

    “There is no point in wondering about that. You are… you are who you are, and I am who I am. I do mean it…I don’t…This is not something I think I can, or want to handle in my life. After tonight, I really don’t think I ever want to see you again. But I do forgive you, Kate.” Kate exhales hard, and a weight she didn’t realize was pushing down on her chest eases a little. She will herself not to tear up, but she is only half-successful. Amanda’s smile is sad, as she looks at her, and Kate risks asking her.

    “Can I hug you?”

    The smile widens and Amanda turns her body to wrap her arms around Kate’s neck. She winds hers around Amanda’s waist from the side, mindful of the IV line still connected to her right hand.

    “Thank you. Thank you so much.”

    Her words are muttered against Amanda’s hair, and she pulls back a few inches to look at Kate, her face close to hers, noses almost grazing. Their eyes meet, and Kate thinks there is an understanding between them.

    Amanda leans forward and presses a kiss to her lips.

    It’s simple, not meant to be anything more than an acknowledgment of the brief connection they have shared. And an acknowledgment of its end.

    A goodbye.

    Leaning back after a few seconds, Amanda looks at her again, and her eyes are a little sad despite her smile.

    “I do wish you weren’t…”

    She doesn’t finish the sentence, but Kate can guess what she is meaning to say anyway. She returns the sad smile, holding her gaze.

    “But I am.”

    Amanda nods, wetting her lips.

    “But you are.”

    Amanda pulls away, and stands up. Kate looks up at her for a second, before using the edge of the bath to get up too. She watches as Amanda turns to the mirror, and checks her state, grimacing at the state of her dress and her face.

    “Can I borrow something to wear?”

    Kate nods with a smile, turning away to leave the room.

    “Of course. One sec.”

    She pulls the IV stand with herself and notices the blood bag is now empty. She disconnects it from her arm in the living room, and pulls out the needle from her vein too, using a tissue to wipe away the tiny spot of blood bubbling out in its place. The living room is a mess, the couch covered in bloody bandages and some medical instruments but she feels way too tired to clean up right now.

    Turning towards her room, she walks in and goes to her closet to look for something to give to Amanda.
