    Thomas grins, wide and endeared. Now even Yelena is turned back towards them, a mildly amused and interested expression on her face.

    “I am the first to bow down to your many amazing skills, baby, but I don’t think that’s physically possible.”

    Brow furrowing, Sonya narrows her eyes at him before turning to Kate.

    “You played basketball in high school, yes? Can you teach me?”

    Kate tries to stifle the grin spreading onto her face. Does Sonya even know what dunking is? “Sure. We will just need a trampoline.”

    Turning back to Thomas, Sonya looks at him triumphantly.

    “You see! Kate can teach me!”

    Thomas doesn’t seem to be able to hold his own grin back, as he looks at his girlfriend affectionately.

    “Babe, you can’t use a trampoline in a basketball game.”

    Sonya glances back at Kate, confused and she opens her mouth to answer but the sound of the buzzer interrupts her. Kate stands up to get it with a grin still on her face, letting in the delivery person from Giorgio's. Just like before, grabbing the sword to check the peephole is almost automatic.

    After she verifies the identity of the person through the door, she glances at Yelena as she puts the sword down and sees her eyes following the movement, her face unreadable. The conversation has died down, it seems and when Kate’s gaze slides to Sonya and Thomas, she seems to be watching her too while he is distracted by his phone. Sonya immediately looks away as her attention shifts to them, but Yelena keeps looking at her. Opening the door, she feels a bit uncomfortable with the attention, but she smiles distractedly at the teenager handing her the paper bag full of Italian food and hands him a fifty-dollar bill from the side table. He thanks her with wide eyes and she smiles at him, mind still preoccupied with the silence behind her.

    After closing the door, she makes sure to lock it again and deposits the paper bag onto the coffee table.

    “I’ll get us plates.”

    Not waiting for an answer, she turns to the kitchen and avoids looking at any of them. It feels like she is being judged somehow, even though Yelena and Sonya should be the last people to frown upon her cautiousness. As she pulls four plates and four pairs of utensils from one of the cupboards and the drawer below it, she tries to listen to the words now spoken from the living room. They are muted, and after a few seconds, Kate realizes they are also in Russian. With a deep sigh, she leans against the counter for a second and mentally prepares herself for the questions or teasing she expects is coming.

    Walking back with the dinnerware in her hands, she reminds herself to remain civil, and not lose her cool. Thomas seems unaware of anything happening, standing up to distribute the food among the four of them.

    Sonya now seems to be looking around the apartment too, eyes sweeping over the paper and photo-covered walls, as well as the stacks of papers everywhere. Yelena is watching Kate as she comes in, assessing her again but immediately looks away when Kate looks at her too. “Um, Frutti di Mare for you babe. Ravioli is yours, Kate?”

    Kate puts down the plates on the table too, extending her hand.

    “Yup.”

    She takes a plate and fork and settles back onto the ground from across the couch. Lucky walks around the couch, his tail wagging wildly as he sniffs the air, and Kate smiles at him. She missed her food-obsessed golden retriever. When he comes over to sniff at her food a second later, she grabs his head and drops a kiss on his soft forehead again. The fact that neither Yelena, nor Sonya commented on whatever they seem to be thinking is not lost on Kate.

    “Are you okay on the ground, Kate?”

    At Sonya’s voice, Kate raises her eyes at them and smiles, pushing down on her nervousness. “Yeah, this is fine. Needed a change of scenery from the couch anyway.” Chuckling at her own words, she decides to focus on her food, tilting the takeout container to transfer the dish onto her plate. It smells delicious as the steam rises towards her face and she takes a whiff, making her mouth immediately water.

    She digs in right away, not having realized how hungry she was already, and only lifts her gaze when she hears Yelena’s appreciative hum from the other side of the table. “This is very good.”

    Yelena talks with her mouth full, and Kate smiles a little, turning back to her food again. She managed to choose well, after all. After she swallows the first bite, Yelena speaks again. “Thank you, Thomas.”

    Glancing up again, Kate looks at Yelena first, before her eyes slide to Thomas who smiles around the food in his mouth, and answers once he swallowed it as well. “Kate chose that. And she paid too, so don’t thank me.”

    That seems to surprise Yelena, her eyes jumping to Kate again, who gives a little self- conscious smile. Yelena gulps, turning back to her food, looking down on it and Kate’s heart plummets. Stabbing another ravioli onto her fork, she stuffs it into her mouth before she can say something she will regret. It has been going well so far… if you don’t count the fact that Yelena barely addressed her or looked at her all night. Kate doesn’t want to ruin the tentative truce by sniping at Yelena, but now she is just being straight up rude and… “Thank you, Kate.”

    She glances up in surprise, meeting Yelena’s eyes. She nods at Kate, and she nods back, swallowing the food in her mouth. Swallowing her quick temper with the bite she took a second ago, Kate answers.

    “You are welcome.”

    Yelena nods a second time, before resuming to eat, looking away from Kate. She feels confused, and her gaze seeks out Sonya and Thomas but they seem to be focusing on their plates as well, not paying them attention. Is Yelena still mad at her, or not? It seems there is still a wall between them, and Kate doesn’t think she is imagining the awkward air around them. Chewing another forkful of her ravioli, she glances at Yelena again, but she seems to have resolved herself not to look at her. Or maybe Kate is just imagining it, and… “So, have you taken your anti-biotics?”

    Sonya’s voice interrupts Kate’s thought process and she shifts her gaze over to the other side of the couch.

    “Yeah, I have. Um, everything is healing fine.”

    Sonya nods, smiling as she takes another bite of her pasta.

    “I can take a look at your stitches after dinner if you want?”

    Kate is a bit confused but grateful, so she nods and smiles back at Sonya. “Thanks.”

    Thomas is either a lot more perceptive than Kate gives him credit for, or a lot less. Either way, he picks up the conversation from before again, filling in the silence that was about to turn a bit stifling for Kate’s liking.

    “So, will you finally let me teach you how to play?”

    Sonya grins into the bite she is taking, rolling her eyes amusedly. She seems to mull it over while she chews, and turns her head toward him fully after she swallows. Pursing her lips, she regards him for a moment longer.

    “Okay. On one condition.”

    There is already a smile tugging at Thomas’ lips, and Kate feels like she is intruding on a moment again. Her eyes seek out Yelena one more time, but she is either not paying attention, or tunes Sonya and Thomas out, focused entirely on her food. “Sure, name it.”

    Sonya leans closer and whispers something in his ear that makes his eyebrows shoot up in surprise, a light blush sneaking onto his cheeks. Kate gets an answer to her question of whether Yelena was listening, as she grimaces slightly and shifts a bit further away from the two of them. Her eyes rise and meet Kate’s, this time not looking away instantly. The half- embarrassed, half-amused smile Kate gives her is partially unintentional but her heart leaps when Yelena returns it, mirth sparkling in her eyes for a second.

    For a moment, the two of them communicate silently, finally on the same wavelength again, even if only to laugh affectionately at their friends. Sonya shifts away from Thomas a second later, a self-satisfied smile on her lips, and a slow blink of her long eyelashes as her gaze shifts over to the two of them.

    “I can say it out loud if you want.”

    Her grin is absolutely shameless and Kate chuckles but answers quickly, at the same time as Yelena.

    “That is not necessary.”

    “Please don’t.”

    Sonya snickers, leaning impossibly even more into Thomas’ side who avoids looking at either of them, but chuckles along, despite the now flaming blush on his face. Kate looks back at Yelena, who rolls her eyes and shakes her head, before going back to eating her pasta dish.

    “Just please, collect that condition when I am not home, okay?”

    Yelena speaks after she swallows her bite, glancing toward Sonya and Thomas as she says it, an eyebrow raised amusedly in their direction. Kate chuckles at her words, taking another forkful of her ravioli too, the plate now almost empty.

    “Maybe you should spend the night at Kate’s then. I am planning on getting my half of the deal as soon as possible.”

    Sonya’s voice is light and teasing, but Kate misses the second half of the sentence almost entirely as she watches Yelena’s face still. Her eyes glance toward the guest-room door before her nose scrunches ever-so-slightly and her lips are turned downwards. It’s almost the same grimace as her reaction at Sonya’s whisper into Thomas’ a minute earlier, but even more grossed out. Ouch. That stings too.

    “Ugh, no thank you.”

    Kate waits for her to meet her eyes again, but Yelena doesn’t look up again. Instead, she focuses on her plate of food again, her mouth still tugged downwards. It’s obvious that the same page Kate was hoping to find is lost again, buried under the weight of Sonya’s teasing words.

    “Hm, suit yourself.”

    That’s all Sonya says. Knowing her a little by now, Kate knows she is almost certainly aware of the implications of both her own words and Yelena’s answer, but she seems to not want to acknowledge them. Kate notices late that Lucky leaned into the plate in her lap and swiped a ravioli but at this point, her appetite is mostly gone anyway.

    Sonya and Thomas keep up the conversation going while they finish dinner, and Kate tries to keep up her enthusiasm, but Yelena’s continued silence weighs on her chest and slowly her eagerness tapers out. When they are all done, Kate gathers their dishes and takes them to the kitchen without a word. While she loads the dishwasher and distractedly notes that she really needs to take the trash out, she tries to steel herself for being alone again. Having all three of them over was really nice, even with Yelena’s hot and cold (mostly cold) behavior. Even Lucky’s presence alone was a balm to her days of restlessness. As she closes the door of the dishwasher, Kate wonders if Thomas will help her again, and decides that she will swallow her pride and ask him once she is finished in here.

    The machine is turned on with a push of a button and a beep, and Kate also thinks she should attempt to speak to Yelena again as well, one on one, to clear some air between them. Focusing on their tasks was working well for Kate’s productivity, but it’s obvious that they are disjointed, and they need to have a conversation before they can work together again properly….Or even spend time in the same room, without it turning awkward. To her disappointment, Yelena is gone by the time she makes it back, only Sonya and Thomas standing together in the middle of her living room. They talk in hushed voices, faces close together and the conversation quiets down when Kate enters.

    Lowering her arms from around Thomas’ shoulders, Sonya turns to Kate with a smile, not acknowledging Yelena’s absence.

    “Take off your shirt.”

    With the last reserves of her mental energy Kate cracks a smile, halting a few steps away from Sonya and puts her hands on her hips.

    “Don’t get me wrong, you are both awesome and I am very flattered but I’m not gonna have a threesome with you.”

    Sonya bursts out laughing, and Thomas snickers too, before rubbing the back of his neck. Sonya recovers faster, giving her a playful look and a fake, wistful smile. “That’s truly a shame. But I will still check your stitches because I’m an amazing friend.” Kate grins, before glancing at Thomas who seems to get the message.

    “Right. I’ll go downstairs too.”

    He picks up his phone from the coffee table and after a moment he turns to Kate again. “Hey, I’m gonna leave Lucky here, okay?”

    Kate hesitates as a picture of matted, crimson fur emerges from her brain, an image frequently visited in her nightmares in the last couple of days. Wetting her lips, she glances at her dog, now sleepily chilling on the couch that all three humans have vacated. As nice as it was to have him, have them over here, Kate is still toxic, as far as she is concerned. Anyone around her, especially someone as defenseless as Lucky, is in danger.

    “Actually, if you don’t mind taking care of him for a few more days…”

    Thomas glances at Sonya so quickly, that Kate almost misses it, before cutting her off with a smile.

    “I don’t mind, at all. But how about he stays while you are just doing recon, and then I’ll take him again when you have something.”

    Gulping, Kate purses her lips, trying to decide if that’s safe enough. It does sound like an alright compromise, so she nods with an uncertain smile a second later. “Yeah, um, okay. Alright. Thank you.”

    Thomas doesn’t hesitate to return the smile and turns to leave again. Kate considers asking him to help again, but with him already doing her a favor, it feels a bit too much. He already helped to uncover a thread Kate can start to follow. She can always ask if she gets stuck again.

    “Goodnight, Newhouse! And uh…thanks for tonight!”

    He turns back one last time, giving her a small grin.

    “Goodnight, Bishop. If you need someone to beat your ass at NBA some more, let me know.” The chuckle that leaves Kate’s lips is a purposefully teasing, but light. “I’ll show you actual basketball sometime, and then we will talk.”

    Thomas laughs, waving it off and he is out the door a second later, leaving Kate alone with Sonya.

    “I’ll get the first aid kit.”

    Smiling at Sonya, Kate walks by her and goes to the bathroom to retrieve the supplies. As she walks back, Sonya seems to be looking over the same board as Yelena did earlier, not joining Kate by the couch immediately.

    “You have done a good job.”

    Still not looking away from the board, Sonya talks to her, and Kate puts the items in her hands onto the table, before straightening up.

    “Thanks. I think I am onto something but um, I’ll need more time to verify.” Sonya nods silently, and Kate adds a second later, glancing around the stacks of financial documents.

    “Thomas helped a lot, actually.”

    At that, Sonya does turn around with a slight smile, leaving the board a second later to walk towards her.

    “He is very good at what he does.”

    Kate returns the smile and reaches down to take off her shirt, leaving her in her sports bra again. Sonya motions to the couch, and Kate sits down, throwing the shirt to her side. “You have lost weight.”

    Kate’s eyebrows shoot up but she nods reluctantly, not especially keen to discuss the topic. Maybe due to her non-existent sleep schedule or her less-than-healthy eating choices in the last couple of days, she did lose some weight, looking a bit thinner than she did in the last few months.

    “Have you been sleeping well?”

    Kate snorts, as Sonya leans down to inspect her side, glancing at her face. “Yes, mom.”

    The quirk of Sonya’s lip is amused, but she is looking at Kate way too focused and serious for her liking.

    “I don’t believe you.”

    She says after a few moments, and Kate glances back at her.

    “I…yeah, I…Well, I got a bit caught up in research. You know how it gets.” Gesturing vaguely around, she hopes Sonya gets it, even though she doesn’t necessarily know what she means either. During her PI days, research never sucked her in like this or made her lose sleep like this. Granted, it was more cheating spouses and runaway kids, than hundreds of people being murdered but still. Sonya looks at her profile a moment longer, before turning back to her side.

    “I guess I do. But I am surprised you do.”

    Kate chuckles, lifting her arm to give Sonya better access as she pokes at the stitches on her side carefully.

    “I know compared to you guys, I am a noob. But I do have some experience. I have been Hawkeye for almost two years now, and I had a bunch of cases as a PI…” She trails off as Sonya’s eyebrows furrow and she glances up at Kate’s face again. “What’s a noob?”

    Thankful that Sonya is not poking fun at her comparatively small experience, Kate smiles. “Like, a newbie. New at something.”

    Sonya nods, trying the word out.

    “Ah. Noob. Okay.”

    Moving onto her shoulder, Sonya begins to check the stitches on there too, before continuing. “Well. You might be a noob, but you did good work. But you also seem to be getting a bit…” Sonya hesitates as she briefly glances around the messy living room, before looking back at Kate’s skin again.

    “…too invested.”

    Kate snorts, glancing at Sonya too before looking around and choosing to look ahead on the still present NBA pause-game screen.

    “Look. I appreciate the worry, but um. There is no “too invested” in this. This is my life, and it’s on hold until we…um, I sort this out. And I’m totally fine. I just…I’m okay.” Nodding, Sonya straightens up. She regards Kate for a moment longer, her hands on her hips. Kate looks back at her, ignoring the urge to look away from Sonya’s focused eyes. “Is this your first time working alone?”

    Kate shakes her head, rolling her eyes a little. It’s nice of Sonya to worry, but Kate is doing just fine.

    “No. I worked alone in LA all the time.”

    Sonya nods one more time and she looks around the room again, before her gaze focuses on Kate.

    “Right. Your injuries are healing fine. We can probably take out the stitches in a day or two.” Reaching for her shirt, Kate smiles up at her.

    “Thanks.”

    After a moment of hesitation, as Sonya looks at her still, she adds.

    “And uh, thanks for the concern, I um. I appreciate it. Even though I’m really like, totally fine.”

    Sonya returns the smile easily, before taking off her plastic gloves.

    “You are welcome. And well, we’re actually very lost with that Widow. We keep running into dead end after dead end. So, we’ll be back tomorrow. Okay?”

    Kate’s chest soars in both relief and gratitude, and she can’t help the smile widening on her face. While obviously, she has been doing fine, not having to do this alone would be a lot more preferable. Her heart that took off racing a second ago, halts, however, as she glances at the door for a second.

    “Is, um. Does Yelena know that?”

    This time, it’s Sonya’s smile that widens, the teasing glint back in her eyes. “No. But if we want to find the Widow, we’ll need your research. So she will have to suck it up.”

    Kate cringes a little, trying not to get her hopes up.

    “That’s... Um, we’ll see then, I guess. Thanks, again for the uh. Check up.” Sonya continues to look at her amusedly, and Kate scratches the back of her head to do something with herself.

    “See you tomorrow, Kate.”

    Kate gives a small smile back, getting up from the couch finally.

    “See you. Thanks, again.”

    Sonya gathers her jacket and bag and Kate sees her grin to herself.

    “You are welcome, again. Goodnight.”

    Kate opens the door for her, rolling her lips.

    “Goodnight.”

    A moment later, Sonya is gone and Kate is alone again.

    She waits for the feeling of loneliness and suspicion to come back, but when she looks at Pizza Dog and thinks about the possibility of seeing Yelena and Sonya again tomorrow she feels much better than she has in days.

    Deciding that she has made enough progress for the day, especially with Thomas’ help, Kate decides to clean up a little. It’s barely past midnight and she took a nap during the afternoon, so along with her already messed up sleep schedule, Kate doesn’t feel tired yet. She takes the trash out first, then does a load of laundry, some of it gathered even before her week-long exile. After some consideration, Kate puts on a hoodie and a jacket then picks up Lucky’s leash, and calls out to her dog.

    “Come on bud, let’s go for a quick walk.”

    The nervousness creeps up on her during the elevator ride down to the ground floor, but once they are outside, Kate feels it slip away. It’s the first time she has left the apartment since the Amanda fiasco, almost a week ago now. The late-night streets are empty, and Kate consciously steers them away from the direction of Central Park.

    The air is somewhat chilly, and Kate pulls the hood over her head both to stave off the cold and to hide her face from potential threats lurking around. Lucky walks beside her happily, and Kate finds a sense of peace she always does during their walks.

    Her thoughts stray back to the events of tonight, and she does her best to push the complicated feelings towards Yelena aside, choosing to focus on her work with Thomas instead. Her gut tells her the three companies are connected more than they seem on paper and Thomas pointed out that their accounting practices are somewhat similar. They all operate with large amounts of cash and only employ two or three people at maximum. Lucky finally does his business a few blocks from home and Kate steers them back toward the apartment afterward, still deep in thought while remaining vigilant of her surroundings. What doesn’t check out, is that none of the three companies are in New York. Two out of three are in small towns in the state, and all three are also different businesses. One is a small bar, one is an agricultural business, and the third one is a cab service in Jersey. What connects them is that their owner is a company called VM Limited, which is owned by a larger company Limitless Holdings Corporation. Limitless also happens to be one of the companies that took the scrapped equipment from Bishop Security after its dissolution. Thomas also pointed out, that from his experience, small companies like these shouldn’t have corporate documentation like they do. It seems that someone is going to extraordinary lengths to make these businesses look as clean as possible, which is suspicious on its own. According to Thomas, the fact that they even have Code of Conduct documents is probably an attempt to ward away overworked government officials looking into the companies’ activities, who usually only have time to check boxes and only look into financials if something is missing. There is also the fact that all three companies only handle exactly the amounts of money, which falls precisely below the threshold that would raise a flag with the authorities. This fact has also been pointed out by Thomas, as Kate would have had no idea what amount of money could a company move to and from its books, without triggering an automatic inspection from the IRS.

    Overall, there is nothing suspicious about these companies apart from being held by a larger corporation that Kate thinks is connected to Fisk, and unless you know what you are looking for, they all look extraordinarily clean and the financial equivalent of “nothing to see here, move along”.

    As Lucky and her walk the final few block back to their building, Kate has an idea. If all three companies use a similar accounting style, isn’t it possible they all use the same accounting company, maybe even the same person? Hurrying the last few hundred feet back home, her mind starts to race.

    If they were all handled by the same person, then finding that person could be the key to unraveling this. They could shine a light on what these companies are actually for, and maybe confirm or clear up Kate’s suspicion that Fisk is behind all three.

    With Sonya and Yelena back in the fold, they could also maybe go and check out all three and poke around in person. Kate would absolutely do it alone, but Yelena had a point about jumping into situations without properly preparing first. The fact that Kate also has dozens of pictures of dead detectives and journalists who have looked into Fisk before is also a good reminder that doing this without backup is probably a terrible idea.

    “Good Evening, Miss Bishop.”

    The doorman’s voice jars Kate out of her thoughts, even though she was aware of his presence as they finally reached the building. Answering half on autopilot, she crosses the lobby and waits for the elevator with Lucky.

    Once they are back in the apartment, Kate feeds him his very late dinner, after locking the door and resisting the urge to check around every room for intruders. Sonya, and maybe Yelena, have definitely picked up on her restlessness being a bit over the top, which in turn made her painfully aware of it too.

    Settling down on the couch again, she dives into the research again, Lucky joining her after he finished his meal. His warm body against her side grounds her and now that she has a goal in mind, the work seems a lot less mind-numbing.

    The stacks of papers don’t hold the answer she is looking for, however, and Kate is back in the pit of her frustration in a few hours. Deciding to call it a day, she gets off the couch and gets ready for bed around 4 am, mentally preparing herself to spend the night in her actual bed this time, not on her couch for the first time in days.

    After brushing her teeth and washing her face, she makes her way to her bedroom, but not before making sure the door is locked. Lucky is already snoozing on her comforter and the sight of him warms Kate’s heart. She slips under the covers, after taking her sweats and bra off, and turns off the light on the bedside table.

    A minute passes, then two. Kate felt tired when she got off the couch, but now she feels wide awake. Try as she might, she can’t shake the feeling that someone is waiting for her to fall asleep in the guest room, and when she does… Her mind helpfully supplies her with images of the bodies left in Fisk’s wake.

    After she is sure that at least an hour must have passed, and she is still awake, Kate kicks off the covers with a huff. This is ridiculous. Picking up her retractable sword from her bedside table, she briefly considers sleeping in her safe room, but that feels like admitting she has a problem.

    Instead, Kate walks around the apartment, turning the lights on and then off in every room, checking under the beds and behind the curtains. After she finds nobody, she can’t help but feel silly, as she always does after doing this but the tight knot in her stomach finally eases out.

    Slipping back into bed, she decides to leave the lights on and closes her eyes. Slowly, she feels herself calming down and only cracks an eye open when Lucky sleepily crawls higher on the bed, pressing his head into her side. Burrowing her hand into his fur, she smiles before closing her eyes again.

    Finally, she falls asleep.

    Chapter 19

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Kate nocks an arrow, firing at the monster crawling over the ledge but another is already there to take its place. Reaching for another one, she fires again, and again but the monsters keep coming and the thick smoke swirling around the penthouse makes it hard to see or breathe.

    She can tell that she is getting overrun slowly, so turning around, Kate begins to run deeper into the apartment. Her movements are sluggish and she feels like she can only move in slow motion, trying to get away. Running towards her father’s office, Kate hears herself call out. “Mom? Dad?”

    There is no answer, apart from the growls behind her and the thundering heartbeat in her ears. As she makes it into the room, she twists around to lock the door and leans her forehead against it, panting after she does. There is a sound behind her, audible even with the battle going around the penthouse and the banging against the door she just closed. It sounds like something is scratching at the piles of concrete slabs that have fallen around the room, the sound coming from below them.

    “Dad?”

    Kate throws her bow to the side to start moving the slabs desperately, but her arms feel weak and her progress is so slow, the scratching becoming fainter by the second. “Dad? Mom?”

    The banging on the door gets louder, a voice calling out.

    “Kate Bishop!”

    Kate ignores the voice, desperately trying to free whoever is stuck under the chunks of concrete. Lifting the final piece of the fallen ceiling, Kate finally gets to see the body lying beneath.

    Her mother’s face is bloody and bashed in. Her blue eyes are staring ahead, empty and unseeing. Crying out, Kate shakes her shoulder.

    “Mom! Mom, wake up!”

    Her mother doesn’t move, and the banging gets louder, the door shaking with the force of whoever stands behind it.

    “Kate Bishop!”

    Ignoring the voice again, Kate strokes the hair from her mother’s forehead, her tears mixing with the blood sticking to her face.

    “Mom, please wake up! Please!”

    The door finally breaks down behind her, and she dives for her bow on instinct, nocking an arrow as she twists around to face her attacker on one knee, firing without hesitation. Her heart stops as her arrow flies true, burrowing itself deep into Yelena’s chest who stands in the doorway.

    Oh no.

    No no no no.

    Yelena slowly looks down at her chest, swaying on her feet as blood starts pouring out of the wound. Dropping her bow again, Kate runs to her and catches her as she falls forward. She lowers Yelena to the ground gently, keeping her arms around her, and pulling her against her chest.

    “Yelena! No!”

    “Kate Bishop…”

    Yelena’s voice comes out wheezy, the sound horrifyingly familiar.

    “No! No, Yelena! No!”

    Kate stares into her wide green eyes, unable to look away.

    “Kate…”

    Yelena coughs, blood painting her pink lips crimson and Kate can’t escape the wheezing sound. Suddenly there is a strong hand around her biceps, yanking her away. Kate fights back, punching, kicking at the figure by reflex, and fighting back but the arms around her are strong, keeping her in place. A scream tears from her throat, as she is unable to move, fighting back with all her might but she feels weak, unable to shake the hands grabbing onto her.

    In her head, she hears Yelena’s voice again – “Kate…”

    Staring at her now unmoving body even as she fights, Kate feels a seed of confusion in her heart. Yelena is gone. Kate killed her. How is she…

    “Kate, wake up.”

    Kate turns back to her attacker, holding her down, blinking.

    It’s Yelena.

    What?

    With a start, Kate sits up, her heart thundering in her ear and her breath coming out in short bursts.

    “Hey…”

    Her mind is still foggy, dreams mixing with reality and Kate struggles to calm down. Her mother’s bashed-in, lifeless face swims in front of her eyes, as does Yelena’s, lying in a pool of her own blood. Kate can still feel it sticking against her skin, and she looks down at her hands. It feels like she can’t breathe, no matter how hard she tries to, and it takes her a few seconds to realize that the wheezing she still hears comes from her. It does little to settle the panic that fills her veins.

    She is not safe here.

    Her chest hurts with how fast and strong her heart beats against it. She struggles to pull any oxygen into her lungs with the short bursts of breath she takes. Eyes jumping around the room, she is looking for the monsters, for the battle, and her hand moves without her volition, searching for her weapon, any weapon. As it closes around the hilt of her sword half beneath her sheets, another wraps around her wrist, holding it down.

    “Kate…”

    She has to get free.

    Thump. Thump. Thump.

    Her heart continues to thunder in her chest and in her ears, almost deafening. Find her mother. Find Yelena.

    Get help.

    “You are okay. Hey.”

    Someone is here.

    Someone is here holding her hand down…

    But they are not hurting her.

    Blinking several times, Kate tries to focus on the person in front of her. Green.

    Green eyes.

    The first things she takes note of are green eyes.

    A pointy nose.

    Bow-shaped lips and high cheekbones.

    Blonde hair glistening in the morning light.

    Blinking several times, she takes in the intruder.

    …Yelena?

    Her voice never comes out between her pants, not even a breathy whisper despite her lips parting to speak, but her grip loosens on the sword’s handle.

    It can’t be Yelena.

    She killed Yelena.

    The hand around her wrist lifts it off her weapon and raises it.

    Her eyes drop to follow the movement.

    The hand raises hers onto ghost-Yelena’s chest, settling on the left side. “Breathe with me, Kate. You are okay.”

    Kate’s eyebrows furrow.

    Ghost-Yelena is… surprisingly tangible.

    Her skin feels warm against Kate’s palm, even through her shirt.

    Her hand settles over Kate’s, and that feels warm too.

    Kate’s mind registers that it feels small, as it splays over hers.

    She can feel Yelena’s heart beating against her chest.

    Her eyebrows furrow even deeper.

    Thump-thump. Thump-thump. Thump-thump.

    It feels fast.

    Not as fast as her own, thrumming in her ears still. But fast.

    Blinking twice, she raises her eyes to ghost-Yelena’s face again.

    Gulping, she opens her mouth to attempt to speak again.

    “…lena.”

    It’s still weak, but Yelena nods, her gaze holding hers. Kate tries to glance around the room again, but Yelena’s low voice pulls her gaze back to her.

    “I’m here. You are okay.”

    And after a moment.

    “Breathe with me.”

    Kate focuses on her breathing. On the drum of her heartbeat below her palm. In and out.

    Yelena is here.

    In. And out.

    Yelena is real.

    In.

    And out.

    Yelena is alive.

    Her eyes dropping, Kate notices that there is a red mark on Yelena’s otherwise smooth skin, just below her left cheekbone. Without meaning to, her other hand, which held onto the sheets in a vice grip until now, lifts off the bed.

    “I…”

    Her palm lands gently on the fresh bruise, and Yelena winces almost imperceptibly, leaning slightly away from her touch, before halting the movement. Her skin is even warmer here, and so smooth. Kate is unable to tear her eyes away.

    “I’m sorry…I…I was dreaming.”

    Yelena, with one of Kate’s hands on her cheek, the other over her heart, just looks back at her. There is a slightly wide-eyed expression on her face and her gaze is boring into Kate’s. For a few heartbeats, they just look at each other, breathing together. Blinking twice, Kate glances around the room again, checking for danger one last time, taking in her surroundings. She is not in her parents’ penthouse, she is back in her bedroom, in her own apartment.

    There are no monsters. No dead mother. No dead Yelena.

    Slowly, her mind catches up to her present, eyes finding Yelena again in front of her. It was just a nightmare.

    Kate’s hands drop as if Yelena was burning.

    “Shit…I…Sorry! I’m so sorry. I uh…I had a bad dream.”

    Yelena blinks too, and Kate can’t decide if she looks relieved, or disappointed. Either way, her voice is even when she answers without missing a beat.

    “That much is evident.”

    Kate gulps and for a moment, they are just looking at each other again. Yelena wets her lips, never breaking eye contact.

    “Are you okay?”

    Kate nods and opens her mouth before she knows what she is going to say. Still finding it a bit difficult to reconcile the dead Yelena in her dream, and the one warm, beautiful and alive in front of her.

    “I..uh. Yeah, I’m…I’m okay. I just. Uh…”

    Glancing at the red mark on Yelena’s cheek a second time, her eyebrows furrow again. “…Did I hit you? ”

    Yelena finally looks away, turning the bruise away from Kate, but her voice doesn’t sound angry.

    “Yes.”

    With that, she stands up and only looks back at Kate once she has taken a step back from beside her bed.

    “Are you going to be okay now?”

    Kate blinks, and it’s her turn to look away, lifting her hands to rub at her eyes. After a second she nods, dropping them back to her lap.

    “Yeah. Shit, I’m really sorry. About um… hitting you I mean.”

    She looks up just in time to catch Yelena’s small nod. She opens her mouth to say something, before closing it. Kate waits for her to say what she wants to, but in the end, Yelena seems to shake off the moment before Kate can. Her face is a carefully arranged mask of nonchalance, as she settles on what to say.

    “Sonya and I came to work with you. We knocked and called your name, but you did not answer. We let ourselves in.”

    With that, she walks out of the room without giving Kate the opportunity to answer. Not that she would have known what to say, really. With a quiet groan, she collapses back onto her mattress, throwing her arm over her face.

    It’s been a while since Kate had that nightmare. Years, actually. Not this one exactly, but different versions of this particular bad dream have popped up several times over the years since the Battle of New York.

    Great.

    Yelena, who already thinks she is incompetent, just witnessed her have some sort of panic attack over a nightmare.

    God, she really needs to get rid of this bed… It’s probably cursed or something. Shifting her arms so the heels of both her palms dig into her closed eyes, Kate allows herself one more embarrassed groan, before rolling out of bed.

    Slipping on the sweats from last night, she picks out a change of clothes from her closet and opens her bedroom door. In her living room, Yelena stands by the boards again, glancing at Kate as she enters before turning back to the pinned information. Sonya is on her couch, sipping a cup of coffee, from what Kate notes, with a lift of her eyebrows, is one of her mugs. “Morning.”

    At her slightly gravely, sleep-addled voice Sonya’s eyes lift from what she was looking at on her phone to look at her with a smile, her eyes glancing down on Kate’s form to look her over.

    “Good morning, sleeping beauty.”

    The best Kate can do in her still dazed state is an amused huff and a slow blink of acknowledgment. Despite clearing her throat, her voice comes out a bit rough. “What time is it?”

    Instead of addressing Sonya’s teasing, she tries to focus on the tasks at hand. “A few minutes after eight.”

    No wonder Kate feels so out of it. She must have only slept about three hours. Sonya looks like she is about to ask something Kate doesn’t feel ready to answer, so she quickly blurts out.

    “Right. Um. I will have a quick shower.”

    Not waiting for an answer, she slips into the bathroom, locking the door behind herself. Stripping off her drenched muscle tee and the sweats, Kate glances at herself in the mirror. There are some dark circles under her eyes, and her hair is a mess from her tossing and turning and sweating. All in all, she is definitely not looking her best. The only bright side is that at least her bruises seem to have almost entirely faded.

    Fleetingly, she is bothered by Yelena seeing her like this, but she feels too tired to deal with her…crush right now. Crush is a stupid word anyway. She shakes off the thought as she steps under the shower.

    The water feels cleansing in more than the physical sense, and Kate feels the last remnants of her nightmare-induced crankiness get washed away. She imagines it swirling and going down the drain, the last slivers of it clinging to her skin finally fading away. She tries to focus on the positive side of things.

    Yelena and Sonya are back.

    The day has started on a less than stellar note, but they are back and Kate has help. She doesn’t have to go through it all alone. And despite things being weird between them right now, Yelena already helped her. Kate hates the fact that Yelena witnesses what she just did, but she stuck around and made sure Kate was okay.

    That has to count for something, right?

    The thought finally cheers her up somewhat, and she quickly washes her hair, eager to get back into action now that she might actually get to leave the apartment soon, based on what they come up with together. Once she is done with her shower, Kate quickly towels off and gets dressed in a some loose jeans and a simple, black t-shirt.

    After a moment’s consideration, she puts on some concealer under her eyes and brushes her hair, but leaves it to air dry, nodding at her reflection in the mirror. As she exits the room, Yelena and Sonya both look up at her from the couch, and Kate suddenly feels nervous. She doesn’t want to talk about the nightmare.

    “I’ll make some coffee.”

    Yelena turns back to the tablet in her hands, and Sonya only tilts her head to the side as a form of a non-verbal answer so Kate makes her way to the kitchen without interruption. The coffee-making process only buys her about three minutes, filling up Lucky’s bowl with his breakfast only another two, and she has to take a deep breath before re-entering the living room.

    Ignoring the looks of both women, Kate picks up her laptop from the coffee table and takes a seat across from them on the floor, deciding that it’s probably best if she doesn’t sit in between them, for now.

    “So…how do we do this? You share your intel, I share mine? Who goes first?” Glancing up from the boot-up screen of her computer, Kate finds both of them looking at her still, their expressions similar. One of Sonya’s eyebrows is lifted, and her gaze is focused on Kate. Yelena looks at her the same way, but her eyes are slightly narrowed, her head tilted a little to the side. She is the one to speak first, her voice nonchalant, but her words direct. “So, are we supposed to just ignore that you are clearly not sleeping well, and are having nightmares?”

    Kate looks at Yelena and her lips part slightly, taken aback by the direct call out, despite expecting it. Snapping her mouth shut, she rolls her lips together before meeting Yelena’s gaze head-on. If Yelena wants direct, Kate can do that.

    “Yeah? I…Thank you. For your help. And I’m sorry about…”

    She gestures vaguely at Yelena, trying to refer to the red patch on her cheek that is thankfully already almost faded, before continuing.

    “But if it’s all the same for you, I’d prefer that, yes. Thanks.”

    Yelena blinks, her eyebrow lifting higher ever so slightly but otherwise, her expression doesn’t change. Kate drops her eyes to the screen again, and types in her password. “Kate, we can’t do this if you are not well.”

    Sonya’s voice is calm and warm but Kate huffs at it nonetheless. Taking a deep breath, she looks back at them again, her eyes seeking out Yelena briefly, before sliding over to Sonya. “Look, I appreciate the concern, okay? But I told you, I’m fine…”

    Running a hand through her damp hair, she forces a smile onto her face as she continues. “I am just…I’m not great at sitting in one place for too long, okay? So, this is probably just my head telling me to stop sitting around all day.”

    They both consider her words, and when neither of them says anything for a moment, Kate thinks she won. It’s short-lived though because as soon as she turns back to her laptop, Sonya speaks again.

    “What are the nightmares about?”

    Biting down on the inside of her cheek, Kate maintains the forced smile, glancing up at her trying to deflect with humor.

    “Are we here to work, or write dream journals?”

    Sonya doesn’t smile back this time, only blinks back at her as Kate meets her eyes and neither does Yelena. After a few seconds of heavy silence, Kate huffs to herself, turning away.

    “Uh, fine. Um. It…changes. Usually, it’s not being able to save the people I care about. Sometimes it’s about killing...”

    The image of Yelena with Kate’s arrow sticking out of her chest flashes before her eyes, and she has to resist the urge to glance at her as she continues.

    “…Um, killing the wrong people. It’s…Can we not talk about this?”

    She doesn’t want to look at either woman on the couch, so her eyes stay glued to her screen and she rubs distractedly at her forehead. Sonya and Yelena are both quiet for a long time, or at least what feels like a long time for Kate, before she hears Yelena shift on the couch, and clear her throat slightly before speaking.

    “Do you feel guilty about killing?”

    Kate’s brow furrows, and this time she does raise her eyes at Yelena, finding her face carefully blank.

    “Of course I do. I mean…I know it’s part of the job, but it’s still…”

    She trails off, not really wanting to delve deep into the subject this early in the morning, and entirely unsure if she wants to have this conversation with Yelena at all. Yelena nods, pursing her lips and leaning back against the cushion of the couch.

    “But you do not have a choice. They would kill you if you did not kill them first.” Kate shakes her head, giving up on trying to focus on her computer. She takes a deep breath, closing her eyes for a second before speaking. She opens them, leans back onto her hands, and looks at Yelena.

    “Yeah, but still. They are people. They have families, and they…look, it’s just. I don’t think it’s something that should ever feel not wrong, right? It shouldn’t be easy.” The look that Yelena gives her is almost unblinking, and Kate tries not to ponder the intrusive thought that Yelena and Sonya both used to kill people for money. It’s made even harden when it’s Sonya’s turn to speak, and she says so with a serious tone, that unsettles Kate. “There are two types of people in this business, Kate. Killers, and dead people.” Kate rolls her neck at the uncomfortable words, Sonya continues with an air of gloomy simplicity.

    “Some people deserve to die.”

    Her voice and her words both make Kate’s skin crawl a little and she shakes her head, unintentionally remembering some of Amanda’s words from the other day.

    “Yeah, well. I don’t believe we should play judge, jury, and executioner. At least I won’t.” Sonya almost rolls her eyes at her, and Kate glances at Yelena to see that she actually does. “How very American of you.”

    Kate’s eyebrows furrow and she looks from Yelena to Sonya, whose answer makes her slightly shift in her seat on the floor.

    “What’s that supposed to mean?”

    Sonya purses her lips a little and looks at her for a long moment. She is unmoving, leaning back against the couch, and Kate glances at Yelena quickly, before looking back at her as she begins to speak.

    “Kate. People can continue to believe in these pretty ideals, because you, me, people like us, we do the dirty work. If we did not…”

    Kate shakes her head, interrupting Sonya.

    “That’s not what I’m doing.”

    Both women raise their eyebrows at Kate across from her. Yelena asks her this time, her voice dropping and crossing her legs.

    “It isn’t?”

    Kate shakes her head, but before she can answer, Yelena rolls her eyes and continues with her voice dry.

    “So what, if we find the Kingpin, you will, what? Arrest him? Hand him over to the police who have already demonstrated that they can not or will not hold onto him for too long?” Kate nods, then shakes her head, not liking the complicated feelings rising in her chest. “That’s different. He is… He is dangerous, and he will play the system. And if it comes down to it, I’ll do what needs to be done. But yeah! If given a choice, I would prefer to take him alive.”

    Yelena looks almost disturbed, and Sonya’s eyebrows furrow, looking at Kate like she is seeing her in a new light. It’s her who speaks again.

    “I’m sorry, Kate. But that is so stupid. If you don’t kill him, he will just keep coming after you.”

    Kate wets her lips and takes a deep breath. The question is a metaphorical can that she has been kicking down the road in her head for a while, not really liking the implications of either outcome.

    “Look. I’m not…”

    Pausing to gather her thoughts, she clears her throat, and this time neither woman interrupts her, giving her time to figure out how to phrase what she thinks, even though she doesn’t feel entirely sure about it either.

    “You know that I will do it if I have to, if it can’t be avoided. I am willing to do whatever I need to, to protect the people I care about, and to…to do what’s right. But if it can, why not give someone a chance to do better? Why…”

    She makes a vague gesture with her hand, her eyes widening as she chooses the expression. “…snuff out any chance for them to improve?”

    Yelena stares at her, her jaw set. She looks unreasonably irritated and Kate can’t really wrap her head around why. Sonya’s gaze is not as heavy, but her eyebrows are furrowed and she looks as if she is still having trouble understanding what Kate is trying to say. Yelena leans forward in her seat, and Kate’s eyes shift to look at her again.

    “Because most of the time, they will use that opportunity to stab you in the back. Because it’s a stupid risk to take. Because it’s incredibly naïve.”

    Yelena’s words are said in a tight voice like she is trying to rein her temper in. Annoyance flares in Kate’s mind at her words too, and she has to resist the urge to let her voice raise in volume. Biting down on the tip of her tongue, she takes a frustrated breath before answering. “it’s not naïve, Yelena. There have to be lines that we don’t cross.”

    Yelena huffs, seemingly trying to exhale some of her frustration, and Kate thinks that’s a step in the right direction, at least. She tries to swallow down her own irritation, and leans back, stretching out her back. Across from her, Yelena wets her lips again, and her voice is calmer when she speaks again.

    “Sure, yes. But you do not need to lose sleep over killing people who would kill you in the blink of an eye.”

    Kate grinds her jaw, and looks away from Yelena for a moment, distractedly looking out the window. She gets it, kind of. And Yelena has a point because she cannot hesitate when the moment is there. It nearly cost them, her, her life several times at the harbor. But it can’t be a snap of a finger either. Turning back to Yelena, she tries something else to make her point. “Look, with that mindset, I probably should have killed you. On that rooftop, when you were after Clint.”

    She looks up just in time to see as inexplicably, Yelena’s mouth twitches upwards. It’s not a smile, but it’s amusement for sure.

    “You probably should have. It would have been smarter.”

    Kate scoffs at her, shaking her head a little but she feels a faint spark of amusement too, before sobering up. Lucky comes out of the kitchen with his tail wagging after his breakfast, greeting her with a bump of his head against her shoulder. Kate smiles at him, giving him a few pats on his head, before turning back to her Yelena.

    “No. It wouldn’t have been. Look at us now.”

    Yelena’s left eyebrow raises and Kate rolls her eyes before continuing. “I mean, you have saved my ass like a hundred times by now, and I have saved yours a couple of times too. We are…”

    She stumbles upon the words, trying to define their relationship correctly again, before continuing. What are they? Partners? Allies? It didn’t go over well the last time she called them that…

    “Friends? We are friends. That would have never happened if I killed you on that rooftop.” This time, thankfully, Yelena doesn’t take offense at her chosen word, choosing to go in a more lighthearted direction.

    “I have told you before, that you would not have been able to kill me anyway.” Kate rolls her eyes again, Yelena’s teasing not hitting the lighthearted spot it usually does. She pins Yelena with a look instead, stroking Lucky’s stomach beside her. “Yeah, keep telling yourself that.-“ Yelena’s eyebrows twitch challengingly, but Kate continues before they can get bogged down by that detail.

    “-Anyway. You didn’t kill me either. You had the chance, and I was in your way. If you did, we wouldn’t be here.”

    Yelena crosses her legs, and Kate can tell she is about the be teased before Yelena even speaks by the tilt of her lips.

    “Yes. Because I could tell that you were not a threat.”

    Kate shakes her head, biting down on her lower lip to ignore Yelena’s remark, which is no doubt said to bait her into arguing over that.

    “That’s…That’s not the point. I chose not to shoot you. You chose to put a wire on me, and look where we are.”

    She glances up at Yelena, who looks back at her seriously again. She looks away a second later, flipping her hair out of her eyes, but with a smile hidden in the corner of her mouth. “Right. Look where we are.”

    Kate can’t read her expression, or the voice she says it with, and her brow furrows. Before she can focus on what Yelena means by that, Sonya speaks up again.

    “Hate to be the asshole that brings it up, but yes. Look where you are. If you have killed Fisk when you had the chance the first time, you would not be in this mess.” Kate’s glance jumps from Yelena to her, almost having forgotten that she is here too. It takes her a second to change gears, struggling to pull her focus away from Yelena. She leans back against the couch again, not looking at her, and Kate swallows as she forces herself to come up with an answer for Sonya.

    She is not wrong.

    If Kate finished him when she had the chance, Annie wouldn’t have been kidnapped. Yelena wouldn’t have gotten hurt. A bunch of people would be alive. Her life wouldn’t be in danger, at least from him.

    And yet, it leaves a bitter taste in her mouth.

    Kate is not naïve, she knows he is beyond seeing reason or finding a better way to live. The hundreds of brutal murders and other crimes she has looked through photos of are proof of that. But the rest of them? The people working for him? It can’t be that black and white. Taking a deep breath, she looks down at her lap. Lucky looks up at her with sleepy eyes, his head warm on her thigh, and she smiles unconsciously at his relaxed doggy face. “Listen, I…I know that killing can’t be avoided. And I will do whatever needs to be done, to protect the people that I care about and to finish this. But it still shouldn’t be easy to take a life. It shouldn’t…”

    She pauses to wet her lips, looking up at Yelena and Sonya, who watch her with rapt attention.

    “It can’t be easy. Otherwise, I’m…we are, just like them.”

    At that, Sonya smiles while Yelena just looks at her. Her eyes are not hard, but Kate can’t quite read the emotion in them. She almost looks hesitant before she speaks, but Yelena holds Kate’s gaze as she does.

    “Kate, you are a lot of things. But you are not like them.”

    It’s surprisingly sincere, and for a moment Kate doesn’t know what to say. She smiles at Yelena, but she only looks at her for a moment longer, before turning back to the tablet in her hand. Her eyes shift to Sonya, whose lips quirk into a smile, before winking at her. Well, that almost sounded like a compliment.

    Baby steps, Kate.

    With the conversation about her nightmare, it seems they have entered into a tentative truce. It manages to last until an hour after lunch.

    For the next few hours, Kate catches them up on her research, and Sonya and Yelena tell her what they’ve learned in the last week. Which is…surprisingly little.

    “So, you think all of these murders were committed by the same person? The Widow?” Kate asks as she files through the folders Sonya handed her about twenty minutes ago. The pictures are no less horrific than the ones she has been looking through regarding Fisk, but the murders…They seem different. They seem calculated, always precise, and notably lacking the passion and the palpable cruelty of the ones that Kate studied in the last few days. “Yes.”

    From her periphery, she can see Sonya nod but she doesn’t go on to explain further, looking through the files Kate handed her instead. As she turns her focus back on her own stack, Kate tries to find the thread that connects the killings.

    The victims were all murdered in their own homes, or somewhere connected to their daily routine, all in New York or relatively close by. There are no marks of torture or signs of slopiness. The execution of them is methodical, almost clinical, and Kate tries not to dwell on wondering if she finds that any less or more terrifying than the mess Fisk and his men tend to leave after themselves.

    For all of the cases, there was no evidence left at any of the crime scenes and they have all been closed without making an arrest connected to them, with two exceptions, where significant others of the victims were found guilty of having committed the murders themselves.

    Her only doubt comes from the fact, that apart from three of the victims being shot in the head, not one of the others was killed using the same method. Kate doesn’t know much about assassins, or serial killers, but are they not supposed to have some kind of MO? That is what they always said on TV shows anyway. Then again, the people Fisk and his men killed were also murdered in various ways…

    There is one man with his throat slit, one strangled, one stabbed in the eye with a pair of scissors, and one kicked out of a window. There is a woman with her neck broken, and even a little boy, but Kate slams that folder shut as soon as she sees his portrait on top, not being able to stomach looking at actual crime scene photos of that.

    Taking a deep sigh, Kate closes her eyes and swallows the bile that she feels rising in her throat. The thought that Yelena and Sonya have probably done things similar, or even identical to these is not far from her mind, at least before they were freed from mind control. She pushes it away on purpose, however, not ready to go down that road. If she is being honest, Kate didn’t even think there were so many ways to kill someone. If it wasn’t so terrifying, it’d almost be impressive.

    “How do you know that this is her? All of it?”

    Yelena puts down the stack of papers Kate gave her a few minutes earlier, after a brief glance at Sonya, who doesn’t move and stands up to walk around the coffee table to crouch next to her. Leaning close to Kate, Yelena pulls one of the folders from the stack, opens it, and points out some of the details. Kate tries not to pay any mind to how her proximity makes her heart speed up.

    “Okay, so. The headshots first. There were no casings left on the scenes, except for one, where she was interrupted by the spouse.-”

    Yelena pauses, and Kate feels her glance at her from the side, as she hesitates for barely a second while Kate waits for her to continue.

    “-We were trained to clean up after ourselves.”

    Kate can only nod, not wanting to get into the details of Yelena’s life in the Red Room, both out of courtesy, and also because she already feels overwhelmed with the amount of tragedy she has to look at this morning.

    “For that one,-”

    Yelena leans closer again to pull a different folder to the top of the stack, and internally, Kate resists the urge to hold her breath. Berries. Yelena smells like berry-scented shower gel. Jesus Christ, Bishop, pull it together.

    “The spouse said he saw a woman in their room, who jumped out the window when he arrived home.”

    Clearing her throat, Kate tries to focus on the contents of the file, and not on Yelena this close to her. It’s hard.

    “Oh, okay.”

    It seems that her week spent in isolation has left Kate touch-, or at least, human interaction- starved. So much, so that even Yelena just being next to her is enough to prove to be a distraction.

    “-Well, not really. He got arrested and currently serves his sentence for murdering his husband.”

    Leaning slightly away, Kate hopes that Yelena doesn’t notice her attempt at creating distance between them… And she especially hopes that Yelena doesn’t misunderstand it. Quickly, she asks the first question that comes to mind.

    “They didn’t believe him?”

    Yelena flips her hair out of her eyes, her gaze meeting Kate’s for a second, before turning back to the files.

    “No. The murder happened on the 45th floor of a building and there was no sign of anyone else having been in there, or having jumped out. So, his story sounded weak. They also had a bad fight the day before, so the jury accepted that as motive.”

    Kate watches her as she speaks, her eyes trailing along the side of Yelena’s face. Her brows are furrowed, and she looks bothered by the story. Kate feels her own eyebrows draw together, half-consciously mirroring Yelena.

    “But you believe him?”

    Yelena glances at her again, and it seems she notices their closeness too, because she leans back as well, but not before her eyes flicker to Kate’s lips.

    “The gun he was shot with was never found in their apartment, only the one casing. He also called nine-one-one right after in tears, completely in panic. He was there crying when police arrived, completely hysterical. There is no way he could have had time to hide it.-” Kate nods and turns away to look down at the photos again. It helps to bring her focus back to their actual task, instead of wondering what’s going on in Yelena’s head. “Right.”

    Yelena is silent for a short moment, before wetting her lips and continuing again. “Also, the one casing they did find there is used in one gun only, in the entire world.” The picture is starting to come together in Kate’s mind, and she looks at Yelena again, finding her eyes on her already.

    “The one used by Widows?”

    Yelena nods, holding her gaze.

    “The one used by Widows in the Red Room’s employ.”

    Kate nods, rolling her lips together, and thinks about what she’s been told. After a second, her brow furrows once more and her eyes jump from Yelena to the file, and back again. “But um… you said you destroyed the Red Room, right?”

    Yelena looks away, and Kate is entranced by the lines of her jaw clenching, and the way the corners of her lips are tugged downwards in a clear display of distaste. “Yes.”

    Taking a deep sigh, Yelena casts her head down. It’s clear to Kate that there is more to the story than she is telling, but with how fragile things are between them, she doesn’t think it’s her place to push. Yelena is only quiet for a few moments, however, before lifting her head and meeting Kate’s eyes once more.

    “Yes. But the Widows brainwashed were not automatically freed. So, if one was sold to someone while it was still operating…she’d most likely have the same equipment unless provided something else by her handler.”

    The sentence sobers Kate up in a heartbeat. Her lips part, pulling a breath in, as Yelena holds her gaze. She swallows, before asking, her voice careful.

    “Um…Sold?”

    Kate watches as her jaw clenches, but Yelena’s voice comes out unaffected, even as she turns back to the pictures on Kate’s lap.

    “Hm, yes. Widows were the property of the KGB, the Russian State, actually. But the leader of the program, he… he enjoyed some special privileges. If the right buyer came along, some girls were sold to them, along with the methods to control them. They used the money to further fund the program.”

    Just like the last time they talked about this, Kate is entirely unsure of what to say. On what she is allowed to ask. Yelena glances at her again, before exhaling through her nose, almost huffing. Whether it’s at her unsaid question or her hesitation, Kate is unsure. Yelena speaks again after a second before Kate figures out what to say.

    “No, I was not sold. Neither was Sonya.”

    Kate glances at her on the couch across from them, finding her looking right back. Shrugging, Sonya holds her eyes and Kate doesn’t know if she should say sorry, or just move along with the topic. When neither of them speaks, Kate wets her lips and asks hesitantly. “What were they used for? Um…I mean, were they only used for killing?”

    Yelena doesn’t answer this time, choosing to turn to Lucky, and gently stroke his head in his sleep. He doesn’t open his eyes, content on snoozing, with only the tips of his ears moving at Yelena’s touch.

    “For anything they wanted, really. With the control they had, there is no choice but to comply.”

    Sonya’s voice is serious, and Kate understands the meaning. Anything they wanted. Thinking about what kind of things they, Yelena and Sonya, were forced to do while under the influence of this mind control, is yet another road Kate avoids going down on. “Jesus…”

    The exclamation tumbles out from between Kate’s lips, barely louder than a whisper and Yelena clears her throat next to her. Reaching for another file, she pulls it to the front, before opening it in Kate’s lap.

    “Anyway. This man was kicked out of the window. You see this mark?-”

    The file contains close-up pictures of his injuries, including the boot mark on his chest that told the police he was kicked, instead of just falling by accident. The picture Yelena is pointing at, however, is a close-up of a patch of skin, with a circular burn mark on it. “Yeah.”

    Kate nods and tries to push the thought of Yelena’s and Sonya’s complicated and horrific life from her head. She is sure that neither of them wants her pity, and there are no words of sympathy she can offer, no way to make it better.

    “-This is a mark left by electricity. Our Widow’s Bites, to be precise.” Focusing back on the task at hand again, Kate’s eyebrows furrow, before she realizes what Yelena means.

    “Is that what the bracelets are called?”

    Glancing at her, Kate sees as Yelena’s face eases. It might be just her projecting, but it seems the Widows still under mind-control are a painful topic to Yelena. It doesn’t take a lot of thought to understand why.

    “Yes.”

    “Right. Right, okay.”

    Nodding, Kate takes a deep breath, before closing the file. Yelena leans back and away from her again, as Kate turns her upper body towards her.

    “So, um, you guys have found a connection in all of these?”

    Gesturing at the files in her lap, Yelena nods, not answering verbally. “Okay, well...”

    Trailing off, Kate begins to gear up, thinking. There is nothing she can add here. This is not her area of expertise, and it’s obvious they have it covered without her anyway. “So, we know she killed all these people. If you say, she is still brainwashed, I’m sure you are right about that too. Um…”

    Yelena glances at her one more time, before straightening up and walking back around to sit back on the couch. Kate nods to herself, trying to pick out a trail of thought to follow. “Do you know where she is? Where she could be?”

    Yelena wets her lips, before shaking her head.

    “No. We have records from the Red Room, about the girls that have been sold. But many of them have died, with no record to show. Many of them disappeared without a trace after. So we have a list that she is most likely on, but no way to know which girl is she.” Kate nods, thinking over Yelena’s explanation.

    “Have any of them been sold to New York? Or to an American?”

    Yelena shakes her head again, her eyes meeting Kate’s even as she picks up the stack of files she had in her hands earlier, her hands running over the cover of the folder on top and grabbing onto its corners.

    “The database had no location attached to the buyers. Most of them either didn’t have one or were too smart to have one that could be found. There were definitely Americans though.” Nodding along, Kate tries to think of a thread to pull on. Anything that might help identify the girl, or find a location. Across from her, Yelena sighs, and Kate’s eyes are drawn to her once again. So, they know the Widow has killed some people, and that they are mostly located in or around New York. They don’t know her name, who she works for, or… “Why is she killing them?”

    Sonya and Yelena both look up, their eyes finding Kate.

    “What do you mean?”

    Kate puts the folders on the coffee table in front of her and leans back as she answers. “I mean, why these people? What did they do? They don’t seem to be connected to each other, and they are sure as hell not connected to me. Are they all enemies of Fisk?” Yelena purses her lips, and Sonya tilts her head to the side as she listens before nodding. “No. Our theory is that her handler picks up contracts for assassinations, makes her do the dirty work, and then collects the payment themselves.”

    Oh. That makes sense.

    So, the Widow, or her handler doesn’t work directly for Fisk. They only came into the picture because he put a price on her head.

    On one hand, that’s good, because it means the handler probably doesn’t have access to resources like Fisk does. On the other, however, it means that they won’t learn anything even after freeing the Widow.

    Kate mulls everything she learned over, while Sonya and Yelena look over the files she has given them. Next to her, Lucky rolls from his back to his side, nudging her with his nose. They sit in silence for a few minutes, until a proverbial lightbulb goes off in Kate’s head. “I have an idea.”

    She waits for them to look at her, gulping before she explains.

    “So, we might have no idea where she is but her handler picked up a contract to kill me, right? That means, that if I go outside, with seemingly no protection, they are bound to come for me, right? Then you guys can like, grab her and do what you need to uh… to free her and…yeah. That’s my idea.”

    Her sentence loses stream as she goes on, the blank expressions on both of their faces doing little to give her confidence. Smiling a bit nervously, Kate looks from Yelena to Sonya, and back again, trying to gauge their reactions.

    “You want to use yourself as bait?”

    Sonya asks, and Kate nods, even though Yelena’s face doesn’t look like she is enthused by the idea.

    “Yeah. I mean, it’s definitely faster than trying to find where they live or something.” Sonya nods too, before looking at Yelena. She shakes her head, before leaning forward. “I have one question. Are you insane?”

    Despite her words, Yelena doesn’t look angry. Mildly irritated, maybe, but not angry so Kate tries to explain, despite her hackles raising at her phrasing.

    “No. Look, I know it’s dangerous, but-“ Yelena interrupts her, her brow furrowed.

    “Kate, it’s not dangerous, it’s a death sentence. If we try to set a trap, it’s not only her that’s going to show up. We don’t even know if she will.”

    Kate leans back again, clearing her throat. It’s a valid point, and she appreciates the concern but it’s not like they are drowning in leads.

    “Yeah, but like. We can plan it well, make sure it happens on our terms. Um, call in some other allies to help-“ Yelena rolls her eyes and crosses her arms, cutting her off again. A habit that quickly begins to get on Kate’s nerves.

    “That is very stupid. It is way too risky for no good reason.“ Huffing, Kate attempts to mimic her pose, but with her sitting on the floor, it doesn’t quite have the same effect.

    “What do you mean no good reason? We can get her, free her –“ Interjecting again, Yelena rubs at her forehead before dropping her hand to gesture wildly around the room.

    “That is not how it works. What if she shoots you from five-hundred meters away? What if she-“ “Will you stop interrupting me?-”

    “I will stop interrupting you when you drop this ridiculous idea.”

    Kate pulls at the collar of her shirt distractedly, suddenly feeling hot. “I will drop this completely rational idea when you-“ Sonya’s slightly raised voice cuts both of them off. She looks “Oh for fuck’s sake. Calm down, both of you.”

    Kate purses her lips, and Yelena closes her mouth too, leaning back against the couch with a huff.

    “Kate, it’s a good idea, but-“ Yelena looks like she is gearing up to interrupt once more, but Sonya quiets her by lifting her hand before she can speak again.

    “But! Yelena is right. It is very dangerous and has the potential to end in disaster. We have to examine every other option first.”

    Yelena looks at her smugly, and Kate resists the urge to mockingly scrunch her face up at her, electing to roll her eyes instead. Sonya rolls her eyes at both of them and shakes her head with a laugh.

    “You two seriously need to get laid.”

    The thing that Yelena and she seem to finally agree on, is that Sonya deserves to get glared at for that particular comment. Yelena glances at her The rest of the morning is spent in a similar fashion. With no idea how to locate the Widow or her handler, Kate doesn’t know how to advance with Yelena’s and Sonya’s case. She spends the day trying to resist the urge to glare (stare) at Yelena every thirty seconds and instead goes back to looking over the financials of the three shell companies she has found. Her focus keeps slipping though, and the urge to huff periodically remains strong. It takes reminding herself several times that she is an actual adult to resist that desire. She just doesn’t understand why they can’t even discuss her idea.

    In a few hours, Sonya leans back with a long sigh and a stretch of her arms above her head. Kate glances at her as she does, her eyes seeking out Yelena after a few seconds, a habit in the making it seems. She watches Sonya too, maybe purposefully not looking at Kate this time.

    “I am starving.”

    Immediately aware of her grumbling stomach, Kate feels ready to take a break as well, but Sonya continues after a heartbeat.

    “-Can I trust you two to behave while I make lunch?”

    Glancing at Yelena, Kate sees that has turned back to her stack of papers, only giving a dismissive nod to Sonya, not a verbal answer. Rolling her eyes, Kate leans back on her arm and nods too, before looking down at her work.

    She hears Sonya sigh, before she leaves the room with Lucky in tow, leaving the two of them alone. The urge to glare at Yelena is almost unbearable again, now that they are alone, and Kate has to remind herself that it’d be very childish of her to pick a fight, just so Yelena will talk to her.

    She makes it about three minutes, before she caves, glancing at Yelena a handful of times before that to see if she will start a conversation. She never does, looking over the financial documents still, and Kate’s patience runs out quickly.

    “I can’t believe you are giving me the silent treatment.”

    Yelena huffs but doesn’t lift her gaze from the files in her lap.

    “I am not giving you any treatment, Kate. I am working…Like you should be.” Kate sucks her teeth, exhaling through her nose to avoid the irritated groan rising out of her. They are quiet for another minute, Kate watching Yelena, waiting for her to finally acknowledge her presence, and Yelena determinedly ignoring her.

    “Well…you could still talk to me.”

    Yelena wets her lips, taking a deep breath before looking over at Kate, only her eyes moving. “What do you want to talk about?”

    Kate licks the corner of her mouth, leaning back on both arms now, abandoning the files in her lap. Yelena holds her eyes, her face not betraying her.

    “I don’t know! Anything. Work. How you are. If you talked to Valentina or Rojas,-” Yelena turns back to her papers, clearing her throat and effectively cutting her off. “I haven’t talked to either of them. He will reach out when he reaches out.” Kate blinks and decides to follow that thread, if that is the one thing Yelena is willing to discuss.

    “Will you tell me when he does?”

    Yelena takes another deep breath, turning the page of the file she is reading. “Sure.”

    “Right, okay. Good.”

    She is really not giving a lot to Kate to work with. They are silent for about a minute again before she feels the need to break the silence again.

    “For the record, I didn’t mean just run out of the house and like, roll with whatever they throw at us. I meant to make a plan, set up an area where we can keep track of everything, and get out of if things get hairy…”

    Yelena throws her head back, looking at the ceiling and muttering under her breath. “Oh my god.-“ Yelena finally turns to her, her hands shifting the files in her lap before she laces her fingers together over them.

    “-Can you please focus? We are here to work. ”

    Kate groans, resisting the urge to lean back and lie down on the ground in her frustration. The woman really makes her want to tear her hair out.

    “I am trying to work. I am trying to discuss a legitimate idea with you, to move this case forward.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes, and Kate’s gaze drops to watch her hands as her fingers untangle from their prayer-like hold to tighten around the stack of files, her knuckles turning white. Kate raises her eyes just in time to see Yelena pin her with a look.

    “Going on a suicide mission because you are bored at home is not a legitimate idea.” Grinding her teeth together in annoyance, Kate’s eyes remain glued to Yelena’s. She looks just as frustrated and annoyed as Kate feels, and that at least feels like a consolation. It’s not a suicide mission. If we plan it well, I’d have you and So-“ Yelena shakes her head again with a huff, flipping her hair out of her eyes with an impatient motion.

    “Oh, so now you are an expert at setting traps for assassins?

    Kate kisses her teeth in exasperation, her eyes widening at the rude question. “I didn’t say that. But just because I am…just because I don’t have as much experience as you do, it doesn’t mean my ideas are not worth discussing.”

    Kate’s ringtone interrupts their conversation, and she picks up the phone from the floor next to her to check who it is. Jack’s name and his smiling face light up her screen and Kate decides to let it go to voicemail. She lifts her eyes off of it just in time to see as Yelena’s chest heaves with a frustrated sigh. Kate also decides to ignore how infuriatingly attractive Yelena is when she is pissed.

    “It is not about experience. It is about the fact that you want to jump into something, again, that you are not prepared to handle. You did one week of re…”

    Kate throws her head back with a groan, before interrupting Yelena.

    “Ugh!! Not this again. I didn’t say I wanted to jump into it! I specifically said we should make a plan…”

    Yelena rolls her eyes again, the muscle in her jaw twitching.

    “And I have said. There is no feasible plan for that.”

    Suddenly feeling warm, her skin almost tingling, Kate pulls distractedly at her collar. “Okay, why? Or you know what, Yelena? Since I’m apparently not ready or capable of doing anything, please enlighten me. What is our plan? What are we doing?”

    Finally turning her whole form towards Kate, Yelena throws the files onto the seat next to her with an impatient motion.

    “Oh my god, how many times I have to say? You are capable. You are good, great! Very talented! I have told you this before. Is that what you want to hear?-” The unexpected compliments take Kate by surprise so much, that her irritation evaporates almost entirely in barely a second.

    “That’s not, uh…you think I am talented?”
