    A smug smile slides onto her face without her meaning to, that Yelena rolls her eyes at, but the corner of her lips tips upwards too.

    “Yes. Keep up. But anyway-”

    Yelena pauses as they both turn to look at Sonya, who walks into the room. She silently looks at the two of them, shakes her head with a half-amused, half-exhausted sigh, and turns on her heels before walking back to the kitchen. Yelena huffs then points at her friend’s retreating back as she continues.

    “-But anyway, this has nothing to do with capability. If Sonya wanted to do something so idiotic, I would tell her off also. But she would not, because she does not have stupid heroic deathwish.”

    Pursing her lips, Kate levels her with an unimpressed look.

    “I don’t have a stupid heroic deathwish.”

    Yelena counters quickly, her eyes boring into hers again.

    “Yes, you do.”

    Kissing her teeth, Kate shakes her head.

    “No. I don’t.”

    Yelena lifts her jaw, keeping their eyes locked.

    “Yes, you do.”

    Resisting the urge to facepalm, Kate closes her eyes for a second, exhaling through parted lips.

    “Agh whatever. You know what? Let’s just go back to working in silence.” She holds up both palms towards Yelena in mock surrender, who just rolls her eyes before picking up her files again.

    “It was you who started talking.”

    Kate stares at her form, as she looks down at her papers again. The wired energy is not gone from her veins. If anything, she feels even more keyed-up.

    “Ugh, okay. Fine.”

    Yelena’s face scrunches up as she answers, her tone almost mocking.

    “Fine.”

    It’s equally attractive and exasperating, and Kate huffs again, with a shake of her head. Yelena will give her an aneurysm one day. Yelena goes back to working, her face slowly smoothing out as she goes back to focusing on the papers before her.

    The same cannot be said about Kate. It seems that Yelena’s presence and the wired energy in her make it impossible for her to sit still and concentrate. It’s almost a blessing when her phone rings again a few minutes later.

    Checking the screen, Kate sees that it’s Jack again and feels the weight of Yelena’s eyes on her as she picks up.

    “Hi, Jack! How is it going?”

    His jovial voice pulls a smile onto her face, as soon as she hears it.

    “Hello, Katie! It’s not a bad time, is it?”

    Despite what happened with Eleanor, Jack has stayed in touch, calling every couple of weeks just to check up on her.

    “Not a bad time at all.-”

    Glancing up at Yelena, she sees annoyance cover her features at being interrupted again. For a moment, Kate entertains the idea of staying just to wind her up some more but decides against it. She is long overdue for a break anyway.

    “-Just a sec.”

    Standing up, Kate walks up to the door, slipping on her shoes and a thick hoodie she keeps by the door for late-night walks. Her keys and sword are slid into the pockets of her sweats, and she picks up Lucky’s leash from the table as well.

    “Luck! Come on!”

    Pizza Dog comes running out of the kitchen, where he was undoubtedly begging Sonya for scraps until now. Stepping through the threshold, Kate ushers him out and turns around to close the door behind them, just in time to see Yelena looking at her. She drops her eyes to the files in front of her in a heartbeat, but it’s too late. Kate caught her, and she smiles smugly to herself as Lucky and her start off toward the elevator.

    “I’m here, sorry. Just taking Lucky for a walk. How are you?”

    Jack keeps talking about his endeavors, his recent trip to Spain, and his family while they take the elevator to the ground floor. As soon as they step outside, the wind whips into Kate’s face, cold and unforgiving, and she pulls up her hood, glad that she had the mind to put it on before leaving.

    If she is being honest, she only catches about twenty percent of what he says, her mind still on Yelena, and periodically checking around herself to see if anyone is watching her. It seems their “relationship”, for the lack of a better word, is stuck in a weird kind of limbo. Yelena is here, helping, and clearly cares enough about her to worry about her safety. But there is tension, an unspoken pressure between them, driving them both to antagonize and argue. They should probably talk about it, but Kate can’t see that conversation going particularly well. Yelena seems annoyed by almost everything Kate says, and her demeanor and attitude sometimes drive her up the wall as well. Maybe, the friction will pass on its own, the two of them going back to how they were before…

    Well, it’s hard to pinpoint where exactly it all started.

    What matters is, is that Yelena is here, and when it matters, she is there for Kate. Her mind turns to her nightmare this morning, and the conversation they had in its aftermath. When wanting to become like Hawkeye, her hero, and idol, Kate never really considered the implications of having to fight other human beings.

    Even with knowing Clint’s, Yelena’s, Sonya’s, or even Amanda’s stance on this, her mind keeps going back and forth, the lines not as clear-cut as she used to think. Stopping Fisk, and doing everything in her power to achieve that is a no-brainer. Apart from it being the right thing, Kate feels that with her mother’s involvement, putting an end to his horrifying reign is her legacy. The debt she owes to society, after unknowingly profiting off of their crimes for so long.

    But what about everything else?

    Kate meant what she said to Sonya. She doesn’t intend to play judge, jury, and executioner, but Yelena and Sonya have a point. Choosing to spare people, people that would kill and hurt her in a heartbeat comes with a price too. And it’s one thing if it was just her in the game, but what if her mercy leads to Yelena, Clint, or Sonya getting hurt?

    “…Your mother always said you were great at that sort of thing.”

    Jack’s last sentence jars her out of her musings, having made her way about two blocks from her building without paying any attention to him or really what she was doing. “What? Uh, sorry Jack, could you repeat that? The, uh, the line cut out.” He chuckles jovially on the other end of the line, and Kate is filled with guilt. He went out of his way to stay in contact, even after what Eleanor did to him, and she either ignored his calls, or only half paid attention when they did speak. With everything that happened, listening to him is the least she can do.

    “That’s quite alright! I asked if you could give me a hand with a few details of this party that I was asked to organize. Your mother always said you had an eye for the details and was good at picking venues and such.”

    Sighing deeply, Kate watches as Lucky lifts his leg to pee over the corner of a bodega. Hopefully, the owner is not looking. Her life of taking part in high society events and planning parties feels like it was a lifetime ago. Her voice is regretful as she begins to speak, but she truly doesn’t know if she can help him.

    “Jack, I’m sorry but I’m not sure I’m really the right person to ask…”

    She trails off, and Jack’s voice sounds uncharacteristically quiet when he speaks again. “Please, just give it a thought? I…I feel quite confused with it all, and with Armand gone, it has fallen onto my shoulders to do it this year. The family already expressed disbelief in my ability to do it properly and I’d hate to disappoint, in my first year nonetheless. I’d be ridiculed for years to come…”

    Armand. The man that her mother killed…or had killed. The guilt, maybe misplaced, but undeniably present, intensifies in her chest and Kate pinches the bridge of her nose with the hand that is not holding Lucky’s leash.

    “Sure Jack, I can, uh. If you send me some details, I can look them over or something. Give you some ideas.”

    In a heartbeat, Jack’s voice is back to the overenthusiastic tone she first reviled, then learned to appreciate.

    “That’s wonderful, darling! I am eternally in your debt! Thank you!”

    Kate sighs but smiles despite herself.

    “That’s okay, Jack. I’m happy to help.”

    Lucky attempts to lead them towards a fallen-over trashcan, full of increasingly disgusting snack options no doubt, and Kate pulls on his leash to steer him away. He finished his business a few minutes ago, and the wind feels cutting where her jacket is unbuttoned, but Kate doesn’t feel ready to get back to her apartment just yet. Instead, she leads them down another street, deciding to circle the block the other way around as well. “So, tell me, how is Armand the seventh?”

    Kate asks with a smile, and Jack’s good-natured chuckle is enough to warm her up a little, despite the chill in the air. It looks like it’s bound to start raining any second now, fall wasting no time to enforce its reign over New York.

    “He is becoming a teenager. And by that, I mean he is even more of a nightmare than before.” Chuckling at his description, Kate walks on, letting Pizza Dog sniff at a questionable stain on the sidewalk.

    “How are you, Katie?”

    Taking a sigh she hopes is not audible through the receiver, Kate shakes her head to herself with a smile. She asked him to stop calling her that about a dozen times. Telling him about her current circumstances is obviously out of the question, so she just breezes through a lie. “Oh, I’m fine. Just getting used to the New York lifestyle again after the West coast.” There is an amused hum from the other end of the line before Jack clears his throat. Kate knows what’s coming before he speaks again, the topic always the elephant in the room between the two of them.

    “Have you talked to your mother since you’ve been back?”

    Despite expecting it, the question still feels like a punch in the gut. Rolling her lips together, Kate takes a deep breath, attempting to keep her voice unaffected.

    “No. I, uh. I don’t think she has had a change of heart since I tried to see her the last time.” The other end of the line is quiet for a moment, Jack probably feeling as awkward as she is with the topic. After a moment, she asks back.

    “Have you? Seen her, I mean.”

    His voice is the most somber she has ever heard it when he answers.

    “No. I wanted to see her, to provide support. It may have only been a couple of days, but I know how terrifying prison can be. But her lawyers told me the same thing as you. She will not see anyone.”

    Kate nods, despite Jack not being able to see her. Her affection towards him only grows. Despite her mother’s attempt to frame him, he still wanted to be there for her. Who does that? And who stays in contact with their ex’s adult daughter, just to like, be a sort of uncle-like figure?

    “You are a good man, Jack.”

    He chuckles awkwardly on the other end of the line, Kate smiling at the sound. “I don’t know about that.”

    Their conversation turns to less serious topics again, Jack’s LARP-ing escapades, the party he has to organize. For another ten minutes, Kate walks with Lucky on the streets surrounding her building, until she realizes she has been gone for over thirty minutes. Steering Lucky away from a dead pigeon, and towards their building, Kate begins to wrap up the conversation.

    “Anyway, I have to go. Thank you for calling!”

    “Absolutely my pleasure, Katie. Maybe we could go fencing sometime?”

    Kate smiles bittersweetly to herself, unsure when it’ll be safe enough for her to go see him again.

    “Sure, Jack. I’ll be in touch! And um, send me those details about the party. I’ll see what I can do!”

    The smile is audible in his voice, his whimsical tone grateful.

    “Thank you again, darling! See you soon!”

    “See you.”

    They hang up and Kate soon turns out to be right, as suddenly rain starts pouring as if the heavens opened. By the time they make it back to the building, they are both thoroughly drenched, Lucky becoming a bit hyper from the rain.

    Herman, the doorman opens the door for her with a smile, that she doesn’t hesitate to return. “Quite the weather we have, Ms. Derekson.”

    “I know! You wouldn’t believe it was so hot just a few days ago.”

    She answers in passing, taking off her wet hood as she steps into the lobby. Lucky shakes his fur, before looking up at her with a goofy dog smile, his tongue lolling out of his mouth. “You better not climb into my bed until you dried off.”

    She smiles down at him, as they walk across the lobby, before pressing the button to call the elevator. As they wait, somebody steps up next to Kate and Lucky immediately attempts to launch himself at them. With muddy pawprints being a serious concern, Kate barely pulls him back in time, an apology on her lips as she looks up. To her shock it’s Yelena standing next to them, in a bomber jacket, holding a closed umbrella and smiling down at Lucky. Turning around to look at the empty lobby behind them, she asks Yelena in disbelief. “Were you following me?”

    Only deigning her an unimpressed look, Yelena watches as the numbers above the elevator descend.

    “No.”

    “Seriously?”

    Rolling her eyes, Yelena purses her lips. There is a smile hidden in the lines around her mouth, but she doesn’t look back at Kate.

    “Everything does not revolve around you.”

    Shaking her head in disbelief, Kate exhales forcefully through her nose and raises an eyebrow.

    “Then what are you doing here?”

    Her voice calm, almost too calm, Yelena lifts her chin as she answers.

    “Sonya sent me to the bodega down the road to get hot sauce.”

    Kate looks pointedly down at Yelena’s empty hands, before raising her eyes back to her face. Yelena just looks ahead and Kate uses the opportunity to take in her wind-swept hair and rosy cheeks. Shaking it off, she asks Yelena, her voice dripping with skepticism. “So…where is it?”

    Yelena pulls a bottle out of one of her pockets, finally turning to give Kate a smug look. “You were saying?”

    Kate snaps her mouth shut, turning to look at the elevator with her lips pursed but she can hear Yelena’s amused huff beside herself. The doors open in a few seconds, and Yelena marches in first, eyes straight ahead again. Kate and Lucky get in second, and she presses the button to the 29th floor, before moving to stand beside Yelena.

    The doors close, and they start their ascent, both of them quiet for a few seconds. “I still think you were following me.”

    Turning her head towards Yelena, Kate sees as she rolls her eyes at her words. “If I were following you, why would I come back at the same time?”

    Shrugging, Kate looks forward again.

    “I don’t know. To throw me off.”

    Yelena turns to look at the doors too, her voice unimpressed.

    “That is very stupid.”

    Kate reaches up to take her hair out of her now-soaked ponytail, running a hand through her wet hair.

    “So is following me. I can walk around the block without getting murdered.” Yelena huffs, but her voice remains unaffected.

    “Again, I was not following you.”

    The levels on the screen to Kate’s right tick by, and they are quiet for a few moments before Kate breaks the silence again.

    “Don’t believe you.”

    There is no mistaking the amusement in Yelena’s voice this time.

    “Suit yourself.”

    The doors open, and once again, Yelena marches ahead, walking out the elevator in front of Kate and Lucky. She pulls out a set of keys from her pocket, in the two seconds it takes for them to catch up and Kate has to roll her eyes again, as she opens the door. Sonya emerges from the kitchen, with a kitchen towel over her shoulder that Kate has never seen before, eyes jumping from Yelena to Kate, then back with a grin. A Russian sentence is spoken, that Yelena glares at her for, as she hands her the hot sauce.

    She really has to get around to downloading Duolingo.

    The rest of the afternoon and the following few days are spent in a similar fashion. Sonya and Yelena come over every morning, but Kate makes sure to always be awake by the time they arrive. They work, sometimes joined by Thomas in the evenings, mostly in silence, but when they are not, the bickering continues. Kate and Yelena squabble over everything, from what to eat, to how to proceed with their work, even over how to use Kate’s oven. Kate would like to say that she hates it. But that would be a lie.

    While she would prefer to be on good terms, their constant bickering means that at least they are talking. It’s probably silly, but their presence, both of them just being there, helps Kate an incredible amount. With Sonya and Yelena keeping her busy, and on a schedule, she starts sleeping through the night again, the nightmares slowly fading away. The question of trying to set a trap for the Widow, using Kate, gets brought up a couple of times, but Yelena doesn’t seem to be warming up to the idea anytime soon.

    For the record, she seems to get a kick out of their bickering just as much as Kate does, never missing a chance to get under Kate’s skin, if given the opportunity. As for Sonya, she seems equally entertained and exhausted by their squabbles, which she never fails to mention. It takes her 4 days to get enough of their nonsense.

    Kate and Yelena are arguing over how old the president is of all things, which honestly, could be decided by a simple google search when she suddenly stands up with a theatrical sigh. Breaking away from their heated staring contest, Kate looks at her, as she starts gathering her things.

    “Okay, you guys need to get that energy out. You are driving me insane.” Looking over at Yelena, Kate sees her bewilderment mirrored on her face. “What?”

    Sonya pauses in her packing, putting her hands on her hips. As if getting ready to make an important announcement, she looks at both of them, before proclaiming: “We are going to the gym.”

    Frowning, Kate leans back, checking her phone. It’s only 11:30 am, and there are still thick stacks of papers they are supposed to be going through today.

    “I thought we were supposed to be working.”

    “Well, Kate, this is a marathon, not a sprint. Besides, there is no work getting done with the two of you squabbling like some birds in a mating dance.”

    Kate snorts at her description before her brain catches up to what Sonya just said, making her throw a dirty look at her instead. She, of course, is completely unbothered. Instead, she points at Yelena, who sits with her eyebrows lifted, not yet moving.

    “Come on. Let’s get changed.”

    Yelena doesn’t move, and Sonya huffs, switching to Russian. Despite diligently satisfying the Duolingo Owl’s demands for the last 3 days, Kate doesn’t understand the word of what’s said. It doesn’t come as a shock, as the words in whatever Sonya just said don’t include the words “father” or “house”, which is as far as Kate’s current vocabulary goes. (Turns out, the first few lessons of Russian Duo are mostly the Cyrillic alphabet, and Kate can’t say that it helps her an awful lot when Sonya and Yelena converse in her presence). Sonya’s sentence, whatever it was, does cause Yelena to throw a piece of leftover bread from breakfast at her head, which she dodges with ease, but Yelena gets up after a second, following her out of the apartment.

    “Be ready in 15! We will come to pick you up.”

    That is the only farewell Kate receives as she stands up from her spot on the floor. If she is being honest, a workout actually sounds great. Her skills shouldn’t be allowed to get rusty anyway and she would be lying if she said she wasn’t secretly super excited to be training with two Black Widows. 15-year-old Kate would be stocked for her, if she could see her now…dozens of bloodthirsty assassins currently hunting her aside.

    Taking off her shirt, Kate switches to a different sports bra and picks out a bag to pack her stuff in. As she laments over what she will need, she hears the keys in the lock turn. The instinct to mentally note the closest weapon to her fires, (it’s a bow by her bed), but just as she suspected, it’s only Yelena coming back.

    “Everything alright?”

    As she steps out of her room, Kate doesn’t miss the way Yelena’s eyes flit down to her barely clad torso, not even attempting to tamp down on the cheeky smile sliding onto her face. “I left my phone here.”

    With a huff that doesn’t seem serious, Yelena walks up to her previous spot on the couch and starts looking for her phone. Kate walks back to her room, packing up a pair of boxing gloves, bandages for her knuckles, and a pair of workout shoes. Next, she walks out of the room to the living room, noting how Yelena is still looking, her hands now searching between the cushions of the couch.

    “You can’t find it?”

    Glancing up, Yelena shakes her head, before going over to check Sonya’s side too. “No.”

    Kate continues her route to the kitchen, grabbing a water bottle and filling it up from the fridge, before making her way back to the living room.

    “Have you checked the bathroom?”

    “Ah, no. Good idea.”

    Just as Kate is about to continue her way back to her room, there is a knock on the front door. Sonya, it seems, is both impatient and incredibly fast at getting ready for the gym. Kate walks up to the door, not even checking the peephole first before she opens it. Which turns out to be a huge mistake, as Sonya is not standing on the other side of the door. Instead, it’s a tall middle-aged woman, and an even taller younger man standing on the other side. Adrenaline floods her veins, and Kate’s mind is immediately working on the best way to make the jump towards the sword on the other side of the table beside her. Before she can make a move, the woman opens her mouth, lifting a badge in her hand in front of Kate’s face.

    “Good morning, Ms. Bishop. My name is Special Agent McLagan and this is my partner Agent Reyes. We are with the Federal Bureau of Investigation.”

    Her mind comes to a screeching halt, after its dash to come up with a way to thwart the attack that might not be coming after all. Kate is still unsure. When she doesn’t give an answer for a few seconds, the woman, Agent McLagan continues.

    “We’d like to ask you a couple of questions. May we come in?”

    Kate attempts the think quickly on her feet. The apartment is covered with the papers they have been looking through, the boards filled up with murder photos, illegally procured police files and the flat is littered with weapons belonging to all three of them, not all of them exactly legal.

    Even if these people are who they say they are, there is no way she can let them inside her apartment right now.

    Gulping, she attempts to give her most convincing smile, but she suspects it comes out strained anyway.

    “Uhh…May I ask what is this regarding? Are you here about my mother?”

    Agent McLagan’s face is stretched into a friendly smile, but her eyes are watching Kate with a calculating, intense look. This is definitely not just about her mother. “It’d really be best if we talked inside.”

    Glancing at the man, Agent Reyes, she notices him trying to peek inside the apartment above her shoulder and pulls the door closer to herself in what she hopes is an inconspicuous way, blocking his view. His gaze shifts to her, and she has to give him credit where it's due, he’s a much better actor than the more senior agent. His smile looks genuine, his voice calm as he speaks for the first time.

    “We just have a couple of questions. We’ll be out of your hair in a few minutes.” Her mind races to come up with an excuse.

    She can’t exactly say she is about to go out, because they might try to walk with her, or follow, and if they are not who they say they are, she’d just be opening herself up for a potential attack. Expecting guests is not really believable with her current outfit of bra and sweatpants. Behind her, she hears a barely noticeable sound, and if nothing else, knowing that Yelena has her back, literally, is a comforting thought. Maybe she could say she has some kind of illness, that she’d be spreading.

    Before she can actually come up with an excuse, a needy voice, with a suddenly perfect American accent interrupts her…from inside her apartment.

    “Kaateee. What’s taking so long? Come back to bed.”

    What.

    The.

    Fuck.

    The implication of what the agents just interrupted is very clear, and it takes everything in Kate not to whip around to stare at Yelena on the other side of the room. Instead, she feels the tips of her ears turn warm and gives the agents a smile that feels dumb as she calls out above her shoulder.

    “One second,...babe.”

    Hoping that her slight stumble over the word went without notice, she turns back to the agents in front of her. Agent Reyes looks at the water bottle in Kate’s hand, his smile widening into a grin as he looks away, and Kate feels the blush spread from her ears to her face as well.

    “As I said, this is not the best time. Could you please come back um, some other time?” Agent McLagan is not smiling, her face strict but still polite. Kate feels a bead of sweat trickle down the side of her neck, and she hopes that it helps to sell their alibi, instead of betraying her nervousness.

    “Of course, Ms. Bishop. How about today afternoon?.”

    A fraction of the tension she has felt leaves Kate at their willingness to walk away right now. Remembering the amount of highly illegal things in the apartment, and trying to calculate how long it will take to rid the flat of them, she decides to push her luck. “Um, I…We have a prior engagement in the afternoon. Could it be tomorrow?” Agent McLagan’s stoic face is hard to read, but after a couple of torturous seconds, she nods, eyes flitting towards where Yelena’s voice could be heard earlier.

    “Of course. Tomorrow, early afternoon? Say, 2 pm?”

    Kate puts on her most charming smile, nodding along.

    “Absolutely, thank you. That’s uh, perfect.”

    Agent McLagan throws one more glance at the apartment behind Kate’s back, before returning her smile, although it never meets her eyes.

    “Thank you for your cooperation. Goodbye, Ms. Bishop.”

    Kate gulps, the smile feeling more and more frozen and unnatural on her face. “Goodbye, Agent…s.”

    The added plural makes the goodbye even more awkward than it was before, and Kate closes the door before more things can leave her mouth. Twisting to look at Yelena, she notes how she stands by the bedroom door still, a gun in her hand.

    “Oh my god!”

    Shout-whispering to Yelena, she just rewinds everything that just happened, her mind racing. What the fuck does the FBI want with her? What was that voice from Yelena? Oh my god, the sex voice…No Kate, don’t go there.

    “Are they gone?”

    Yelena hisses back, back in her natural, Russian accent, power walking to the door and almost pushing Kate aside to look out the peephole. They must be gone, because a second later she puts the gun on the table by the door, running a hand through her hair. Staring at her, the words tumble out of Kate’s mouth before she can stop them, Yelena’s needy voice still echoing in her head.

    “I can’t believe you did that.”

    Looking up at Kate, she can see that Yelena is about the start mocking her. “Well, somebody had to come up with an alibi, with your groaning and moaning.” Kate snorts, lifting an eyebrow, and giving her a once-over.

    “You are one to talk about moaning, what was that sex voice?”

    "Sex makes people uncomfortable, we needed them to not focus on you. It worked, did it not?"

    Looking away at her grin, Yelena kisses her teeth, and Kate is delighted to see a light blush form on her face too, her own still not gone from her face. That, of course, means that she has to keep teasing.

    “And what’s with the accent?”

    With a frown and an annoyed flip of her hair, Yelena turns back to her again. “What is your problem with my accent?”

    Kate grins, holding up her hands.

    “Nothing! You’ve just been holding out on me. All this time, you could do a convincing American accent, and you’ve terrorized me and those poor kids at the diner with the Valley girl one.”

    Another eye roll, and a look so unimpressed, it almost makes her feel embarrassed, is what Yelena deigns to give her as an answer.

    “I’m a trained assassin, Kate. I could do an American accent or English. I can sound French or Swiss, if that’s needed.”

    She changes the accent with each added example, and Kate can’t come up with a better answer than a shocked, “Huh.”

    Yelena scrunches her face up, mimicking her “sentence” in a mocking voice. “Huh.”

    It’s Kate’s turn to roll her eyes, ignoring how cute the scrunch is.

    “Real mature.-“ Before Yelena can continue their back and forth, Kate continues, running a hand through her hand as she begins to wind down.

    “Seriously, what the fuck was all this? What do you think they want?”

    Yelena closes her mouth, swallowing her original answer. She is thoughtful for a moment, pursing her lips as she is looking back at Kate.

    “I do not know. They were definitely not here just to talk about your mother.” “Yeah, I kinda got the same feeling...Do you think they are really with the FBI?” Rolling her lips together, Yelena looks at the door, as if the agents are still standing there. “I do not know. We can check later.”

    “Have you found your phone?”

    “Yes. It was in the bathroom.”

    “Ah, good.”

    Kate nods distractedly, looking around the apartment and trying to decide what to do now. After a moment, she looks back at Yelena, finding her looking back, eyes flitting down to Kate’s uncovered torso meaningfully than back.

    “What?”

    “Are you not going to get dressed?”

    Confused, Kate lifts an eyebrow at her. She can’t seriously be thinking… Knock knock.

    Eyes wide, Kate mouths at Yelena.

    “Get in the bedroom.”

    Yelena picks up her gun again, jogging across the room as Kate walks back to the door, checking the peephole this time.

    Oh.

    Opening the door, she calls out above her shoulder.

    “You can come out, it’s just Sonya.”

    Sonya saunters in, with an eyebrow raised at Kate’s state of undress that rises even higher as Yelena exits Kate’s bedroom.

    “If I knew you were going to get your workout up here, I wouldn’t have bothered to come up.”

    She grins at her own words, drawing a groan from Kate. Yelena just ignores the teasing, walking up with her gun in hand again, giving Sonya a serious look.

    “Kate just got visited by the FBI.”

    The grin melts off of Sonya’s face, giving way to confusion.

    “The FBI? Why?”

    Rolling her lips together, Kate shakes her head.

    “We don’t know. We sent them away for now.”

    Sonya blinks at her twice, before looking over at Yelena.

    “You sent the FBI away?”

    “Yes.”

    Oh no.

    “How?”

    Kate glances at Yelena, seeing her freeze for a second too, but it only takes her a moment to pull herself together.

    “That…is not important. They will be back tomorrow to talk to Kate.”

    It seems they came to an unspoken agreement to not tell Sonya about that. She’d never let them live it down.

    “Ah, shit. Okay. We’ll help you clean up after training. And set up some anti-survaillance equipment.”

    Sonya and Yelena nod at each other while Kate's eyes widen.

    What? They are still on for that?

    “We are still going out?”

    Frowning, Sonya looks at her.

    “Well, I doubt the FBI visit made you two less frustrated, so yeah. We are still going out.” Yeah, you have no idea.

    Kate doesn’t dare to look at Yelena but feels the tips of her ears grow warm again, remembering the voice.

    “Are you finished?”

    Yelena’s question is aimed at Sonya, who grins again, looking back cheekily at he friend. “Not quite. I think I have a few more in me.“ Deciding not to wait around for that, Kate walks back to her room finally, as Yelena goes downstairs too. She changes into some purple boxing shorts and a faded, grey muscle tee, before putting on a hoodie to wear until they get there.

    In ten minutes, Yelena is back, her golden hair in a bun, wearing leggings and a hoodie too, that is a bit big for her, and way too distracting for Kate. She does her best to not check Yelena out as they make their way to the garage, taking one of Kate’s cars to the gym, as Sonya still has yet to choose a new one. Kate fails several times, and she is pretty sure Yelena caught her looking at her ass at least once too, but she decides to give herself a pass over that.

    The ride there is uneventful, apart from some more bickering when Kate objects to always having to sit in the back when it's the three of them, in her own car nonetheless. Followed by a brief argument over the music that they play in the car, that ends with Sonya putting on some classical music that will, to quote her words “hopefully help both of them calm the fuck down” and which they both object against, then listen to in sullen silence. And finally, a short squabble over whether to stop for milkshakes at the Starbucks drive-through before the workout. (Who argued for which side might be surprising, if someone heard them. What is not, is Sonya and Yelena ganging up on Kate, and stopping at Starbucks anyway.) They finally get to the gym shortly after 12:30, Kate sipping moodily on her vanilla protein milkshake in the back seat (for the record: she still thinks it should be drunk after the workout, not before).

    “This is the gym you go to?”

    Her voice might carry a bit too much indignation, as she takes in the run-down building and the faded sign, that can't even be read anymore, but she is still not over getting ganged up on over the drinks. Giving a disapproving look in the mirror, Sonya admonishes her as she parks Kate’s Mercedes.

    “Don’t be snobby, Kate. This place is great. It has all the equipment we need, and most importantly: it’s discreet.”

    Kate can’t argue with that, but she will still probably miss out on showering here, from the looks of the building.

    Unsurprisingly, there is no receptionist once they walk inside, only a few patrons working out but Kate has to admit, this is one of those cases where the book shouldn’t be judged by its cover. Inside, the place is spotless and well-equipped. The walls are freshly painted, and there are various workout systems, weight racks, boxing bags, and cardio machines littered around the two rings set up in the middle of the room.

    “Wow. Okay. I take that back, this place is awesome.”

    Sonya laughs at her, making her way to one of the rings, and putting down her bag from her shoulder.

    “Told you. Welcome to Iron Maiden, Kate.”

    Kate puts down her gym bag too, looking around again, trying to stick to not staring at Yelena as she takes off her hoodie beside them.

    “Oh, my dad used to love that band.”

    Sonya’s voice is genuinely confused as she answers.

    “What band?”

    Kate can’t decides if she is joking or not, so she decides to just shake it off. Instead, she keeps looking around, taking in the place. The only three other guests are women, one of them working at a boxing bag, the other two lifting weights together.

    “Is this a women-only gym?”

    Turning back just in time to see the grin that Yelena and Sonya exchange, she waits for an explanation, but she only receives one word from Yelena.

    “Sure.”

    What does that even mean?

    Before she can continue her questioning, Sonya claps her hands together, looking between the two of them.

    “Okay. Since you two seem to have a lot of energy you need to work off, why don’t you get in the ring while I say hello to Annika.”

    With no idea who Annika is, Kate glances at Yelena to see her reaction. Shrugging, Yelena doesn’t look at her and Kate turns back to Sonya, answering uncertainly. “Oookay.”

    As Sonya walks away, Kate turns back to her bag, unzipping it and pulling out her bandages. There is a bench on the outside of the ring that she sits down on, meticulously bandaging her knuckles, as she keeps looking around. Yelena seems to have disappeared along with Sonya, only coming back once Kate is done with the hands, and is stretching in lieu of warming up. As Yelena starts to stretch next to her too, Kate begins to feel nervous, sneaking glances at her. She really hopes that physically fighting each other will help with the frustrated energy, not make it worse. She waits for Yelena to get in the ring, but she seems to be taking her time, doing a split on the floor as she texts someone.

    “Are you two actually going to train, or ignore each other like teenagers at a school dance?” Sonya arrives silently from behind Kate and she hopes neither of them saw her jerk a little at her sudden appearance, having been too immersed in watching Yelena while trying her hardest not to look like she is watching her. The usual teasing comment from Sonya doesn’t even register for once.

    “I am waiting for Kate to finish warming up.”

    Yelena looks up from her phone, looking completely unphased and Kate purses her lips, brow furrowed.

    “Well, I was waiting for you to finish.”

    Sonya makes a sound between a huff and a snort before she claps her hands together. “Get in the ring, come on.”

    Kate stands up, pulling on her boxing gloves and climbing under the ropes. Bouncing from one leg to the other a few times, she tries to calm herself. This is just a spar match, like any other.

    Turning around, she is annoyed to find Yelena and Sonya both looking at her with confused faces, their brows furrowed.

    “What are you doing?”

    Kate looks from Sonya to Yelena then back.

    “Wha..? You said get in the ring?”

    Sonya shakes her head, blinking and Yelena begins to climb into the ring as well. “No, I mean the gloves.”

    Kate looks down at her boxing gloves, then at Yelena’s uncovered hands. Well…

    Yelena looks as unimpressed as ever, (or at least in the last week or so). “Gloves are for amateurs, Kate. Come on.”

    Kate’s brow furrows, and she shakes her head slightly, glancing at Sonya before her eyes turn back to Yelena.

    “No. I don’t want to hurt you.”

    The laugh that bursts out of Yelena is definitely offensive and Kate purses her lips before popping them. Yelena flips a wisp of her hair out of her eyes that escaped her bun and gives her a quick once over.

    “I would not worry about that too much.”

    Kate pulls the gloves off of her hands with a huff, throwing them out of the ring. She is under no impression that she would have an actual shot at Yelena if they were fighting for real, in a life-or-death situation, but fighting her in a ring? She can probably do that. There is also the very real possibility of accidentally hurting each other, and Kate thinks they should probably try to avoid that, considering the constant danger they seem to be living in. This is such a stupid idea.

    But if that is how they roll, Kate is not going to complain.

    She raises her arms a little reluctantly, her right leg shifting behind her to a classic fighting position.

    Yelena tilts her head to the side, taking in her boxing stance and that is the only warning she gets before she kicks out at Kate, her weight definitely behind the motion. Oh. They are doing this for real.

    That realization is solidified when Yelena’s fist connects with her jaw and Kate’s head is snapped to the side. That hit at least is not one with full force but it’s definitely more powerful than just regular sparring sessions Kate had as an athlete or even after meeting Clint and training with other vigilantes.

    She doesn’t get to ponder that much longer because before Kate even has a chance to turn her head back towards Yelena, her legs are swiped from underneath her, and she lands squarely on her back. The air is knocked clear out of her, and her only solace is that Yelena doesn’t finish the onslaught with a chokehold or something that would require Kate to tap out. Would Yelena even let her tap out?

    Taking a staggering breath, she forces herself to sit up and levels Yelena with a glare, ignoring Sonya’s snicker behind her.

    “Come on, Kate. Get up.”

    Yelena saunters around like a predator circling its prey and for a brief second, Kate entertains the possibility of saying No, just to annoy her…But her pride, born from years spent as an elite athlete and now even as a vigilante, wins over her pettiness. Kate is on her feet a second later, and this time she is ready for the jab Yelena sends toward her face, not even 2 heartbeats later.

    Evading the quick motion, Kate dances out of the way, raising her arms and getting into her stance again.

    Yelena seems to be the kind of fighter who incapacitates her opponents quickly, and aggressively. Kate has fought people like that before, and she gives up trying to keep up and block with every blow in favor of analyzing Yelena’s movements.

    If she looks at this as another match, like another fight from her sports career before, maybe she can gain insight she can use.

    She blocks one hit at her face and evades another kick aimed at her stomach, but the move after catches her by surprise. Yelena’s foot that kicked at her abs a second earlier is still close enough to her, that she can use it to swipe one of Kate’s feet to the side without even putting it down first, making her stumble. While she fights to regain her balance Yelena twists quickly with the momentum, her elbow coming to hit the back of Kate’s head. Before she knows it, she is seeing stars, and there is a short, but incredibly strong arm around her neck, and a small and solid body against her back, choking her.

    Kate’s reflexes kick in, and she stomps on Yelena’s foot behind her and snaps her head back to get a nose hit in. It never connects, however, because Yelena pulls to the side and her foot is somehow hooked around Kate’s ankle again, and this time she falls on her face, Yelena’s arm slipping away to let her.

    Before she has a chance to turn around, there is a hand around her wrist, twisting it behind her, and a knee on the small of her back.

    She gets an answer to her question a second later because when she taps out, Yelena immediately slips away.

    This time it takes her a second to get up, pausing on her knees to look at Yelena again. She stands a few feet away, not even breathing hard, and Kate tries to look at her as an opponent again, looking for weaknesses.

    Of course, there is no weakness to find, but taking in her short and muscular frame, and remembering each move Yelena used until now, Kate has an idea.

    “Again.”

    Yelena sounds almost impatient, and Kate nods half to her and half to herself. When she gets to her feet, Yelena is on her again immediately, but this time Kate doesn’t let her get close to her. Yelena’s arms and legs are quite a bit shorter than hers and once she starts to think about it, it’s not that hard to keep her far enough that she is at least not able to finish the fight as fast as she has for the first two times.

    Blocking more of her strikes this time, and dodging even more of them, Kate lasts a lot longer this time around. Even better, she even gets her first hit in.

    Yelena’s strikes are lightning-fast but as Kate steps to the side to evade a kick, she sees an opening. Her fist flies at the sharp line of Yelena’s jaw by muscle memory. It connects with a smack, snapping Yelena’s head to the side but she dances out of the way of Kate’s foot a second later that would finish the move.

    There is a pause, as Kate doesn’t pursue her, and Yelena gives her a small smile when she turns to face Kate again. A small, fluttering feeling of pride fills Kate’s chest, but it doesn’t get to live long.

    Grabbing the wrist of her raised, left arm, Yelena pulls her forward and steps in front of her foot, making Kate fall to the ground again. It’s the most basic move ever, taught as the first one to every kid who has ever taken any kind of martial arts class but Kate can’t help but still smile even as she lands on her front. Quickly twisting around to her back, she expects to be pinned again, but it never happens.

    Yelena’s grin is tempered into a smile as she crouches by her head but Kate feels the crack in the wall of frustration that has been separating them for the last couple of weeks. The fight becomes slightly more balanced after that.

    Emphasis on slightly.

    Kate is still beaten every single time but the exchange of blows becomes almost like a dance, the two of them circling and twisting around each other. Despite her earlier apprehension about the gloves, Kate actually begins to have fun and Yelena seems to be too. Kate might be imagining things, but it seems they find the wavelength they have lost in the last weeks, and even though Kate gets knocked onto her ass more times than she can count, she is so glad Sonya dragged them here.

    Slowly, Kate starts to learn Yelena’s moves. Most of her punches are thrown as a distraction, a way for Yelena to get closer, and either grapple her to the floor or finish her some other way. Her legs might be short, but they are packed with muscles, and if she lands a kick, it almost always ends with Kate on the mat, needing to tap out. Having seen and analyzed many videos of Natasha fighting, Kate is somewhat surprised that Yelena’s fighting style is less flashy, but the panther-like grace and deadly accuracy are very much the same. While it might not be much, Kate is happy to note that about half an hour in, Yelena is breathing hard and sweating just as much as she is. Her skill might be far superior to hers, born of years of training that was much more extreme than Kate herself has ever been subjected to, but their stamina levels are similar. Kate’s longer limbs and her advantage in both weight and height are able to bridge some of the gaps between their skill levels and she tries to use them as often as she can.

    Yelena enjoys the fight too, Kate can tell.

    There is a small, barely-there smile on her face almost all the way through it, and the few times Kate gets to glance to the side of the ring, Sonya seems to be having a good time too. A few times she even provides tips, pointing out opportunities to Kate, even though she is only able to take advantage of barely half of them.

    In about an hour and a half, Kate is panting heavily, and her whole body aches, but Yelena seems to finally slow down too.

    Her movements are still fast, but they lack the lightning speed they had during the beginning of the fight. The frustration powering her movements earlier is gone now too, and when Kate can hold her back for more than 10 minutes in one round, Sonya seems to take note of the time that went by.

    “Okay, I think you have beaten each other into pulp enough for one day.” Kate waits for Yelena to give her a signal, before daring to drop her arms, but when Yelena’s smile widens into a grin, she happily drops them to her side.

    “I have definitely not been beaten into a pulp, but okay. It is enough for the day.” Yelena’s voice is breathy, and that’s good enough for Kate, at least for today. “I have been beaten worse.”

    Tossing a grin back to Yelena, she turns her back and walks to the corner of the ring, reaching between the ropes to grab her bottle. Uncapping it, she gulps down her water hungrily and leans back against the corner to look back at Yelena.

    When their eyes meet, Yelena finally doesn’t look away. There is a smile in the corner of her mouth still, and making her eyes sparkle, this time directed at her, and Kate’s own lips turn to beam back at her fully.

    “Do you want my criticism now, or when we get home?”

    Yelena’s smile morphs into a smirk, but her eyes never leave Kate’s and she takes that as a victory.

    Grinning back, Kate wipes her face with a towel, before slipping out between the ropes. “How about a shower and some food before you destroy what’s left of my ego, huh?” Yelena shrugs with a mischievous little grin, her shoulders lifting and dropping easily, as she drinks from her own water bottle still in the ring. After she finishes drinking, she wipes her mouth with the back of her hand, her eyes still on Kate.

    “Home it is then.”

    Kate rolls her eyes playfully but smiles back nonetheless, and Sonya snickers on their side. “I told you some training will do everyone good.”

    Yelena slips between the ropes too, the muscles under her leggings flexing as she throws an unimpressed look at Sonya.

    “What are you talking about? You did nothing the whole time we were here.” Sonya feigns offense as Kate chuckles, all of them grabbing their things from the bench by the ring.

    “First of all, I am retired. I am your older and much wiser coach. Second of all, I trained Kate. It’s more exhausting than training myself.”

    Kate throws a sweaty towel at her head that Sonya side-steps with ease, even managing to throw her hair behind her shoulder with a flourish in the same movement. “Hey.”

    Kate feigns affront too, pursing her lips but in reality, her chest is light in a way it hasn’t been in days. Sonya just gives her a smirk and some condescending tuts.

    “Look at this way, Kate. You are sexy Michael B Jordan in Creed, and I am Rocky, your seasoned and experienced teacher.”

    Kate grins, leaning her head to the side as she regards Sonya.

    “Come to think of it, you do look a bit like Sylvester Stalone.”

    Sonya’s eyes widen, taken by surprise by her joke, and Yelena bursts out laughing next to them.

    “You take that back, Kate Bishop, or so help me!”

    Sonya moves toward her with a finger pointed at her, and Kate sidesteps as she makes sure the small table by the ring is between them at all times.

    “Kate does have a point. Black hair, tan skin,…”

    Yelena stands to the side with her bag over her shoulder and a smirk on her face. Kate can’t stop herself from adding with a grin.

    “Very short...”

    Sonya gasps and starts moving toward her even faster and Kate practically runs around the table, trying to get away from her, pushing down on the urge to giggle. “You will so regret that!”

    Kate chuckles as she runs away and they take 3 laps around the table until Kate runs behind Yelena, grabbing her shoulder and turning her to face Sonya.

    “She said it too.”

    Sonya looks half amused half unimpressed, and Yelena does too as she twists her head to the side to look back at Kate.

    “You would throw me under the bus like this, Kate Bishop?”

    Licking her lips, Kate leans closer and stage-whispers close to Yelena’s ear. ”You have a better chance against her. But…how about we team up? You take legs, I take arms?”

    Snorting, Sonya takes a step back, switching her faux-offense for a mock-serious expression. “You see, that’s another important lesson. Don’t start fights you can’t finish.” Kate considers calling her out on the fact that she only stopped because she knows she can’t take Yelena, and especially Yelena and Kate on alone, but she decides not to. Instead, she tilts her head to the side again, putting on a thoughtful expression.

    “Technically, I can finish every fight. I might just not win.”

    Slipping out from behind Yelena, Kate picks up her bag and puts it on her shoulder too, looking between the two former Black Widows. Sonya looks at her like she is trying to decide if Kate thinks this is a good comeback, and Yelena has an expression that says, “I guess I can’t argue with that.”

    “You would definitely not win this one.”

    Sonya ends up answering, and she tosses Kate’s towel back at her, after picking it up from where it fell earlier. Pursing her lips again, Kate contemplates her chances, before cocking an eyebrow.

    “We will see next time I guess?”

    Sonya considers her for a long second, before winking at her.

    “Sure, Kate. We will.”

    They walk out of the gym together, and when Kate holds the door open for them, Yelena holds her eyes for a long moment, the amusement she usually regards Kate with back in them, and the small quirk of lips. Kate smiles back, and when Yelena walks out in front of her, she doesn’t feel too bad about her eyes dropping to her ass in those leggings. She is about to suggest that they go out for food, before going back to clean out her apartment of all the illegal shit in there when her phone buzzing interrupts her thought process. The number is not one she recognizes, but it’s not blocked, so she hangs back a little to pick it up, lifting the phone to her ears just as Yelena and Sonya reach their car. “Hello?”

    The man on the other end of the line doesn’t introduce himself immediately, giving her a pause.

    “Hello, is this Katherine Elizabeth Bishop?”

    She pulls the phone away from her ear to check the number again, but it truly doesn’t look like one she can recall. Remembering the incident with the agents earlier today (if they were even telling the truth), she puts it back to her ear, and answers, her words dragging a little. “It depends. Who’s asking?”

    The man on the phone clears his voice, and Kate can almost imagine him leaning back, pausing for a second.

    “This is Joshua Hewitt. I’m calling from the Rose M. Singer Center on Ryker's Island Correctional Facility. Ms. Bishop, I’m afraid…that there has been an incident.”

    Chapter End Notes Hi Everyone!

    Sooo, it's been over 5 months since I last updated, and first of all I'm really sorry. A lot of things happened in my life, thankfully overwhelmingly positive developments, but they have kept me from setting aside time to write. (If anyone's interested: my new house finally got finished, I moved in, and I ended up adopting a second dog (who is a little tornado trapped inside a yellow lab puppy's body, called Lucky :D). So all in all, I've been super busy, and in all honesty, I struggled quite a bit with this chapter. First of all, my writing process it to really immerse myself in what I'm doing. On the upside, it means that when I do write, I usually crank out several thousand words a day. On the downside, it means that if I only have like half an hour or an hour to write, or if I know i'll have to do something else soon, I get nothing done.

    This chapter in particular has been hard for several reasons. In the beginning especially, Kate and Yelena are at a weird place. I had trouble putting them in the right place, where they are not exactly on bad terms, but they are still not back to where they were. Honestly, the argument in the middle has been rewritten, scrapped, restarted etc. at least 6 times. I've written ahead quite a lot to avoid it, I re-edited it, until finally this weekend I had enough time to get back into it, and get the vibe that I was going for. Before that it was either too harsh, or too playful, but I hope in the end I managed to capture the sort of sexual tension limbo they are stuck in, where they care about each other, but are not in a place to properly express it just yet, either verbally or physically, so they get under each other's skin for the thrills. (Even two days ago, I scrapped a 6k words long scene completely, because it didn't fit with everything else.)

    I absolutely despised writing this chapter, for like 90% of the time that I was doing it, but in the end I think it ended up being quite fun, and while it's not one of my favourites, I hope you all enjoy it somewhat, and enjoy our dive back to this universe. This chapter was hard also, because it contains a lot of pieces that set up the various storylines of the rest of this story, and tie it to what has already gone down. :D For the record, we still haven't reached the part of the story that first made me want to write it, and what was my original idea for this, so we are still kind of arranging the puzzle pieces so we can start putting the picture together.

    On another note, many of you know that I've been writing a companion piece to this story, depicting the same plot, but from Yelena's perspective. I'm happy to say that the first chapter of that is posted at the same time as this one. It's called Vampire Smile, and it follows Yelena through all of this. Please feel free to check it out, I think you guys are going to like it :)

    As for the future of this story: I cannot promise a regular update schedule still. My life is always busy, and I don't always have as much free time as I'd like to (or any, lol). What I can promise, is that this story is not dead or abandoned. I am going to continue to write and update whenever I have the time, and I think I can also promise, that the most fun parts of the story are still ahead of us :D :P I have a few thousand words of chapter 20 written, we'll see when I have time to continue working on it, but i'm hoping to get it out soon. I promise i'll do my best to not make you guys wait another few months :D Anyway, please let me know in the comments what you guys think. I hope this was worth the wait!

    Apologies again for the unintended hiatus, but I'm so happy to be back! xx

    Chapter 20

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes “This is Joshua Hewitt. I’m calling from the Rose M. Singer Center on Ryker's Island Correctional Facility. Ms. Bishop, I’m afraid…that there has been an incident.” The warm, almost giddy feeling that Kate could swear was filling her chest a moment ago suddenly evaporates. In its place cold dread starts to spread immediately, making her stop dead in her tracks, everything blurring around her.

    “Is…my mom? Is she…?”

    Unable to finish her sentence, to say those words, Kate swallows, unconsciously reaching for the wall by her side to balance herself. The man on the other end of the line clears his throat, his voice smooth and impersonal as he speaks again.

    “Around 7:15 am this morning, an altercation broke out between two inmates during breakfast. I’m afraid that one of them has been your mother, Eleanor Bishop. She suffered multiple stab wounds as a result of the fight and has been transferred immediately to Metropolitan General Hospital. There, she underwent surgery and is currently in the Intensive Care Unit. As she suffered life-threatening injuries, I’ve been notified by her legal counsel that you are to be informed that the restriction of visitation has been lifted. They will be in touch with you in due course.”

    There is a buzzing in Kate’s head, that makes it almost impossible to make sense of what he is saying and yet, she feels as focused as she does in the middle of a fight, her heartbeat filling her head.

    “Is she going to be okay?”

    A beat of silence, before he speaks again, his voice still polite, but unmistakably detached. “Unfortunately, I cannot say, Ms. Bishop. All I know is that she is out of surgery, and in the ICU.”

    Taking a staggering breath, Kate tries to focus on the next steps. She has to get to the hospital. Now.

    “Right, okay. uh…”

    There is a moment when neither of them speaks. Kate is processing. She needs the car. Ahead of her Yelena and Sonya have stopped walking, looking back at her. His throat clearing reminds her that she is still on the line with him.

    “Regarding the incident, according to the testimony from another inmate, your mother was the one to initiate the fight. Therefore, if she were to pass away, Rykers advises you to not seek legal retribution following the incident, as according to paragraph three-“ “Kate?”

    Yelena is suddenly standing next to her, eyes searching her face. Letting go of the wall, Kate runs a hand through her hair, cutting the man off.

    “I’m sorry, Mr…”

    The man’s name escapes her, but she doesn’t have it in her to focus on that or care right now. Clearing her throat, hoping to swallow the lump that has lodged itself there, she continues. “I have to…go. I must go. Thank you for letting me know.”

    As she pulls the phone away from her ear, she thinks she hears the man protesting, but she is already pressing the red button to end the call, panic coursing through her as she throws herself into action.

    “I need the keys.”

    “Kate, what is going on?”

    On any other day, Kate would find it amusing that Yelena has to essentially jog, to keep up with her long steps. Today, however, she can only remember her dream from the other day, and the last few weeks. Her mother’s lifeless blue eyes staring at her from below their collapsed penthouse, from inside the container full of corpses, from various other locations where Kate was unable to save her.

    “My mom…She is in uh, Metro General. She has been stabbed. I need…”

    With Kate’s power-walking they are back to the car in a few seconds, Sonya standing by the driver’s door with a serious expression on her face. Holding out her hand in front of her, Kate speaks to her this time.

    “I need the keys. Can you guys get a cab home? I need the keys.”

    “Why? What is happening?”

    It’s hard, not to scream at Sonya to just get out of her way. Especially when Kate reaches for the keys in Sonya’s hand and she has the audacity to pull them back, away from her. “My mom is in hospital. I need to go. I’ll see you guys at home.”

    She makes another attempt at grabbing the keys, but Sonya snatches them away yet again, spinning around to open the driver’s door.

    “Mh-mh, no. We are going with you.”

    The option didn’t even come up in her mind, but before she has time to even consider it, Yelena grabs her wrist and pulls her in with herself as she slips onto the backseat. “Where is she?”

    Yelena answers for her as Kate attempts to swallow the acidic feeling in her throat again. “Metro General.”

    The address is put into the car’s GPS in a few seconds, and they take off, Sonya merging into the busy Friday afternoon streets with ease. Kate stares out the window, trying to resist the urge to jump out of the car and start sprinting toward the hospital as streets around them clog up with traffic.

    There is a brief conversation in Russian, that she pays no mind for once before Yelena speaks next to her.

    “Who was that on the phone?”

    It takes Kate a second to register that Yelena is speaking to her. Blinking herself back to the present, she wets her lips, glancing back at Yelena, who tears her eyes away from Kate’s knees to meet her gaze. The realization that she is bouncing her leg comes and goes, without an attempt to stop herself.

    “I…he said it but I don’t remember his name. Someone from Rykers.”

    Yelena nods, before exchanging a look with Sonya in the rearview mirror. Turning back to Kate, she speaks to her again, leveling her with a serious look.

    “We need to be smart about this.”

    “What? Why?”

    Yelena’s eyes are soft as she speaks, but her voice is firm.

    “This could be a trap. To draw you out. Maybe even to get both of you at the same time.” Kate closes her eyes and bites down on her tongue as she leans her head back against the seat. It’s impossible to put into words, how much she hates the metaphorical restraints put on her right now. She nods, not trusting her voice not to break if she speaks, and doesn’t open her eyes for a few seconds.

    When she does, she finds Yelena looking at her hands, but she glances up at Kate immediately. She laces her fingers together in hope of stopping her hands from shaking, and when that doesn’t work, she balls her fists in her lap, trapping them between her thighs. Yelena doesn’t comment, but Kate can feel her eyes on the side of her face for a few seconds longer before she turns forward to look at the busy road ahead of them. The man from Rykers said that her mother started the fight.

    To Kate, that seems impossible. Eleanor Bishop has always treated physical altercations as primitive and juvenile. Kate can’t really imagine that she would be the one to start a fight. Then again…

    She couldn’t imagine her mother working for the mob either. Or killing someone. Laundering money. Or anything on the long, long list of felonies that she is accused of. The bitter thought is pushed aside by guilt and worry almost as soon as it comes. Now is not the time to be angry at her mom.

    It’s a short ride and by the time they pull up to the hospital’s parking lot in 15 minutes, Kate is back to panicking again. Her mom can’t die.

    Her mom has to…she has to atone for what she has done, but she needs to live and come out of jail and make amends with Kate. The time when she got her mom arrested can’t be the last time they have spoken to one another. It can’t.

    “Is this what heroes do? Arrest their mothers on Christmas?”

    Kate leaps out of the car before Sonya can find a parking spot, before the car has even stopped moving fully. She is vaguely aware that Yelena is keeping up with her, kind of jogging again but her focus is entirely on getting inside and finding her mom. “So much for being careful…”

    Ignoring Yelena’s pointed comment, Kate walks through the electronic doors that barely have time to open for her. According to the sign on the opposite wall, the ICU is on the fourth floor. A glance at the numbers above the elevator tells her that it’s up on the 3rd floor currently and Kate is absolutely not going to wait that long.

    A door to the left leads her to the staircase, and Kate takes the stairs two at a time to get up to the fourth floor as fast as possible. Yelena has trouble keeping up with her pace, but she is still close behind her, and the two of them are up and entering the ICU only a minute or two after they entered the building.

    Despite just having spent two hours training and draining herself of her energy, Kate doesn’t even feel winded, adrenaline and worry propelling her up the stairs, through the doors, and down a white, sterile hallway.

    Still not slowing down, Kate marches up to the reception table, interrupting the nurse who sits behind it, typing on a computer.

    “I’m here to see my mom. She… Eleanor Bishop. I was told…She was taken here with…uh. With stab wounds. She is from Rykers.

    The nurse, a young woman with tired, and very unimpressed brown eyes, and curly brown hair looks her up and down slowly, before answering.

    “Ok-kay. Who are you?”

    Running a hand through her sweaty hair, Kate tells herself to be patient as she takes a deep breath.

    “I’m her daughter, Kate. Kate Bishop.”

    The woman nods before she gestures at a stack of papers on her reception table and starts typing on the computer again.

    “I need to see some form of identification. And please fill out these forms.” Shit.

    Kate lost her wallet with her ID in it weeks ago, during their first run-in with the super soldier. Unsurprisingly, replacing it hasn’t exactly been a priority. She takes the papers and clears her throat nervously.

    “Um, I, uh. I don’t have any ID on me right now. Is it okay if I google us? It’s…” The woman’s stare turns even more unimpressed as she looks up from her typing again. “I can’t give out information without proper identification.”

    With that, she turns back to her typing and Kate feels like steam is about to come out of her nose and ears like a cartoon. She is ready to yell, scream, go total white-woman-having-a- meltdown on the receptionist, when Yelena speaks up next to her, leaning against the counter by her side.

    “I have a scanned copy of her driver’s license on my phone. Will that do?” The perfectly nonspecific American accent or the absolutely ridiculous fact that Yelena has a copy of her license doesn’t even phase Kate this time. Instead, she whips her head back at the rude nurse, who sighs deeply, seemingly resolving herself to having to deal with them. “Okay, sure. Fill out the paperwork, give it back. Someone will be with you shortly.” Kate nods, taking the clipboard and a pen from reception and walking over to the waiting area a couple of steps away. After she takes a seat in one of the plush, orange armchairs, she tries to focus on the words on the paper.

    The form asks for personal details like name and address, familiar relation, and a couple of long waivers that she has trouble comprehending right now, let alone making a decision about. Her hands are still shaking, which makes reading hard and writing the answers even more so.

    A moment later Yelena reaches over from her seat beside her, gently taking the papers and pen from Kate’s hands.

    “I am going to help, okay?”

    Sighing, Kate nods, leaning onto her knees with her elbows and lacing her fingers together. “Yeah, thanks.”

    Yelena hums and begins to fill out the form, pulling up Kate’s license on her phone. Meanwhile, Kate goes straight back to panicking.

    With nothing to actually do or focus on, she feels it filling her up, acidic and heavy. She cannot lose her mom, especially like this. Kate was the one to get her arrested…She is the reason her mom was in jail, to begin with, and while she knows it was the right thing to do, and never questioned her decision until today…

    The guilt fills her muscles with lead and Kate has to distract herself somehow but struggles to find anything to focus on, other than her brain conjuring up horrible images from her dreams or the memory of her mother’s face from when she was helped onto the backseat of a squad car. In a few minutes, Yelena slides the clipboard back into her lap, pointing at the bottom with the pen before passing it back to her.

    “Sign here.”

    Kate does, and Yelena takes it back as she stands up, walking up to reception. She exchanges a few words with the nurse, as Kate watches, trying to focus on her instead of her guilt or worry. As she walks back, Yelena meets her gaze and holds it until she reclaims her seat by Kate’s side.

    “She said she will log the info and a doctor will be here to talk to you soon.” Kate nods, taking a deep sigh.

    “Thanks…Thank you, for being here and, uh. Helping.”

    Yelena huffs through her nose, a ghost of a laugh.

    “You are welcome…”

    She looks around the waiting area and speaks again, her voice low, almost a whisper as she scopes her surroundings.

    “Sonya will wait outside, keep an eye out, and provide backup if needed. We do not have a lot of gear on us, but if anything happens, go for the staircase. The first priority is getting out of the building, and making it to the car. Do not get tied down by fighting, just get downstairs and into the car.”

    Kate looks around too as she speaks, trying to see if there is anyone acting suspiciously or something to warrant these instructions, but there doesn’t seem to be. Yelena takes a second to wait for her nod that she understands, and Kate turns to look at her then, trying to gauge where she has weapons hidden on her.

    Still in her workout leggings, and the oversized hoodie, Kate can’t tell. If she had to guess, she’d say Yelena doesn’t have anything, other than the Widow’s bites on her wrists. She looks like any other pretty, twenty-something girl in New York. Then again, Yelena is a weapon herself, without anything to help her out. They all are.

    “Do you really think this could be a trap?”

    Rolling her lips together, Yelena nods, not turning to look back at her as she continues to assess the area around them.

    “It has been done before. And it would be easy. Get both of you at the same time.” Kate runs a frustrated hand through her hair, but nods. Yelena has a point but Kate desperately hopes she is wrong. This is already too much as it is.

    “Yeah. Yeah, that’s…that makes sense.”

    Yelena nods again with a sigh. She glances at Kate briefly before gulping and continuing her watch. After a few moments, she speaks again.

    “Yes. So, once you see her, we cannot stay long, okay? You talk to the doctor, talk to her if she is awake, but then we have to go. We are very exposed...Sorry.”

    Kate knows she is right, but it’s incredibly fucking frustrating. Leaning forward onto her knees again, she buries her face into her hands.

    “Yeah, okay.”

    It comes out muffled but she doesn’t move just yet, trusting Yelena to watch over them for a moment. Suddenly, there is a slight weight on her right shoulder: Yelena’s hand. It doesn’t rub or even move at all, but the gesture is there and somehow, it makes her feel a bit better. Kate takes a deep breath, hoping to center herself.

    “I don’t want her to die.”

    Yelena’s thumb moves, almost imperceivably, but Kate feels it. Her voice is still low when she speaks but it carries a warmth that Kate didn’t even realize she was missing for several days now.

    “Of course, you don’t, she is your mother.”

    Huffing, Kate feels amusement spark in her at the simple statement, even if only for a second. The situation, her feelings towards her mother, are so complicated, yet so simple. They wait in silence for a few minutes, both of their gazes following anyone with scrubs entering or exiting the room, even if they are just walking through. Kate’s leg is back to bouncing, but she does the breathing exercises her therapist taught her, back when she lost her dad and in a few minutes, she begins to feel somewhat calmer.

    “Bishop?”

    A doctor calls out from one of the hallways, a clipboard in her hand. Kate is out of her seat in a heartbeat, walking up to her, and extending her hand for a handshake. “Yes! That’s us! I’m Bishop…Kate Bishop.”

    The doctor meets her eyes as she shakes her hand before her gaze slides over to Yelena on Kate’s side. Kate answers her question preemptively.

    “…And she is with me.”

    The doctor nods, extending her hand and shaking Yelena’s too.

    “I’m Dr. Patel, I’m your mother’s attending physician.”

    “How is my mom? What happened?”

    With the introductions done, Dr. Patel starts walking and Kate falls into step beside her, Yelena walking only half a step behind. The doctor glances at both of them, looking them up and down discreetly.

    “Everything will be explained in a minute.”

    What?

    Kate glances back at Yelena, seeing as she watches their surroundings, her shoulders tense, eyes alert. She meets Kate’s eyes for a moment, her gaze saying “Something is going on.” Turning back to Dr.Patel, Kate checks her shoes and clothes under the white coat, but they do look like something a doctor would wear. Scrubs and white hospital shoes, not boots or something that could tell her Dr. Patel is not who she says she is.

    Kate has another thought that fills her with dread.

    Maybe Dr. Patel is not being dodgy because she is not a doctor. Maybe, she is taking them somewhere more private to…to tell Kate her mom has died.

    The idea fills Kate like ice melting, freezing water spreading in her chest and down her arms to her fingertips.

    She absolutely can not take not knowing another minute.

    Her shoes squeak on the laminate floor as she stops dead in her tracks, Yelena halting as well. Dr. Patel walks a couple more steps before she turns back towards them, her face drawn in what Kate reads as confusion.

    “Dr. Patel, is my mom okay? Please, just…just tell me.”

    Maybe it’s her voice that does it, a bit weak as she asks or something on her face. But confusion clears from Dr. Patel’s face as she meets her eyes and smiles a little, her voice reassuring when she speaks.

    “Your mother will be alright, Ms. Bishop.”

    Kate exhales, feeling like a thousand-ton weight has rolled off of her chest. Looking to Dr. Patel, she tries to muster up the strength to smile back. She doesn’t think she manages to. “Then…what’s going on?”

    The expression on Dr. Patel’s face changes, the discomfort shining through her polite mask for a second, before she hides it behind a cordial smile again. She glances behind herself, down the hallway before meeting Kate’s gaze again.

    “It’s not my…Your mother will explain everything, okay?”

    Her mother…what?!

    Her confusion is not reflected on Yelena’s face when Kate turns to look at her. She searches Dr. Patel’s face for something, and nods at Kate in a second, indicating that they are okay to follow the doctor. Kate trusts her assessment…especially because she doesn’t feel like she has any idea what’s going on.

    The remaining part of their journey is spent in silence, the three of them arriving at a door that is framed by two police officers in about a minute. Dr. Patel walks in first, and Yelena gently grabs Kate’s forearm before she can follow.

    “I will check the room first, okay?”

    Before Kate can comprehend, she walks through the door too, and Kate…Well. Patience has never been a strength of hers but before she can lose hers, and step in without confirmation, Yelena’s hesitant voice comes through barely five seconds after she went inside. “Kate?”

    In less than a second, Kate is through the threshold, taking in the space. It’s a plain, white hospital room, with a bed by the opposite wall. The blinds are drawn closed and Yelena stands closest to the entrance, her uncertainty visible in her stance and on her face for once, as she meets Kate’s eyes. Because on the bed…

    On the bed, is Kate’s mother.

    Eleanor Bishop looks worse for the wear, sure.

    She is thin, her always well-styled and glossy hair is grown out, and her skin lacks the shine thousands of dollars worth of skin care used to buy it. She wears a spotty hospital gown, which unsurprisingly doesn’t do her appearance any favors either and highlights the weight she seems to have lost since Kate sent her to prison. There is an IV in her arm and a black bruise around one of her eyes.

    What she doesn’t look, however, is close to death.

    “Hi, baby.”

    Her mother looks apologetic, instead. It’s how she used to look when she told Kate she wouldn’t make it to her archery competitions, or cello recitals, again. “Mom?”

    Kate wants to be furious.

    It’s pretty obvious that they have been played, somehow. That she is a pawn in a game, against her will and knowledge, again.

    She really should be mad.

    All she feels is relief.

    “Mom!”

    Before she knows it, Kate is across the room, leaning over the bed and hugging her mom close. Her eyes well up, and she shuts them quickly to stop the tears from falling. Her mom hugs her back, her arms feeling too delicate and weak around Kate’s back. “Kate…”

    Her mother pulls back in a second, grabbing her face and looking her all over. She doesn’t seem to be concerned with holding her own tears back, they stream freely down her face, dripping down from her chin. Her thumbs stroke the skin of Kate’s cheekbones, and she looks at Kate like she can’t believe she is seeing her again, like she wants to carve her face into memory. Like it’s Kate, that has been stuck in prison and refusing to see her for almost two years.

    In a moment, she pulls Kate back into an embrace again, tucking her face into her daughter’s neck. Kate hangs onto her just as desperately, even as her mind races. What the hell is going on?

    Why is her mom here? How is her mom here? What happened? Why is Kate here, if she is not close to death? Is her mom still mad at her? Did she really get stabbed? When did she… A throat clearing breaks them out of their reunion.

    Her mom looks annoyed as she pulls away from her, glaring pointedly at the man that Kate kind of just realizes is standing in the opposite corner of the room. She noticed him when she walked in but he was obviously not a visible threat and her mother’s presence eclipsed all other information she may have gained otherwise. Until now, that is.
