    While her initial shock is far from being gone, Kate has enough mental capacity to look around again. Apart from Yelena and Dr. Patel, there are two men in the hospital room with them as well. One of them is older, silver hair styled fashionably, and a well-kept beard covering his face. His suit alone seems to be more expensive than all the medical equipment in the room combined.

    The other man is younger, somewhere in his late thirties probably. His suit jacket is well- fitting but it’s obviously from a department store, instead of tailored perfectly for him by an exclusive designer or something. His dark eyes are behind a pair of thick, black-framed glasses and Kate can clearly see the contempt in them, even across the room. “Good afternoon, Ms. Bishop. My name is Peter Browning, I’m with the Department of Justice.-”

    As the younger man speaks, his dislike is as obvious and dripping from his voice, as it is from his gaze. Kate nods at him uncertainly, while her eyes jump from her mom to Yelena, to Dr. Patel, and back to Yelena again. She looks almost as clueless as Kate feels. “Hello.”

    “-We are here to discuss the terms of your mother’s plea deal and your-“ Her mother wipes her eyes and despite sitting on a hospital bed, wearing a hospital gown, the black eye, and all her glamour gone, in a span of just a few seconds, she looks just as much a demanding CEO as she used to in her power suits and corner office. She cuts Mr. Browning off, her voice impatient and eyes jumping over to Kate, before looking back at him. “Our deal was that I got to explain everything to my daughter, Mr. Browning. On my terms, alone.”

    Kate doesn’t think she can get more confused than she is. The man, Mr. Browning, lifts his chin, looking at her mother with a challenging glare of his own.

    “No, Mrs. Bishop. Our deal was that we explained the terms of your deal, made sure she held up her end, and then you would get ten minutes alone with your daughter.” Her mother looks angry, glaring coldly at Mr.Browning, before turning to speak to the older man, standing by the window.

    “Robert, please call Mr.Hanson and explain that Mr.Browning is violating the terms of our agreement. I said I wanted to speak to Kate alone and-“ Robert, who Kate now thinks she recognizes as one of her mother’s lawyers, reaches for his phone in the inside of his suit jacket. Mr.Browning puts his hands on his hips, looking annoyedly at Kate’s mother.

    “If the deal was to speak to your daughter alone, why would I be here?” Eleanor looks him up and down, her gaze and voice dripping with the venom and condescension of someone who spent the majority of her life in the socialite circles of New York.

    “Good question, Peter. What are you doing here?”

    Kate glances at Dr. Patel, who looks like she would rather turn invisible and is just waiting for someone’s permission to leave the room. Then she turns to look at Yelena, whose eyes follow the back and forth between her mother and Mr.Browning like a tennis match. “Mom, what’s going on?”

    Her mother looks at her, her gaze softening for the fraction of a moment, but in less than a second she is back to talking down to Mr. Browning and ignoring Kate’s question. “…understand that this information is need-to-know. You, don’t need to know.” Mr.Browning sucks his teeth and shakes his head.

    “Mrs.Bishop, you are in no position to renegotiate. If it weren’t for your…connections, you wouldn’t even be getting the opportunity, so…”

    Kate has had enough.

    “What the hell is going on?”

    Kate is not yelling but her voice is certainly sharp enough to cut through the argument. The last hour, ever since she got the phone call from prison has put her right on the edge, and she feels one sentence away from screaming for real. Before anyone can attempt to speak, Kate continues.

    “What happened!? I got a call that you got stabbed, that…That you were dying. I ran here, I thought…”

    The fury she couldn’t feel a minute ago finds her this time and fills her up in barely a second. “Kate, honey…”

    “No! For like an hour I thought you were dead! For real! Dead!”

    Sidestepping the hand Eleanor reaches out with, Kate moves away from her mother, feeling confused, angry, and scared. Two steps backward, and she is standing next to Yelena, with her back to the wall to be able to see the whole room.

    “Ms. Bishop. We apologize –“ Kate doesn’t know who Mr. Browning is, but at this point, she also really doesn’t care. She hasn’t seen her mother in almost two years, and she is owed an explanation for all of this, from her.

    “No. I want to hear it from her. I don’t care if you stay or go, but I will hear it from my mother.”

    Mr. Browining wets his lips, blinking surprisedly behind his glasses. Why the hell is he surprised? What did they expect her reaction was going to be?

    Glancing back at her mother, Kate is baffled to see her mother smiling slightly, her eyes shining with fondness. Mr. Browning continues to test her patience by speaking again, looking at Yelena this time.

    “Well, alright. But in any case, this is a highly sensitive and confidential discussion. Miss, if you could please step out for-“ “What I can hear, she can hear.”

    Kate cuts him off, lifting her chin defiantly and hoping that her tone is enough to end that discussion before it begins. Next to her, Yelena shifts her weight from one leg to the other, leaning closer to Kate.

    “I can-“ Kate looks at her, shaking her head slightly, hoping that Yelena hears what she doesn’t say. “No.”

    I need your help to navigate this.

    Yelena rolls her lips together, searching her face for a second before she nods and turns back to the others in the room. On her face is a smile that Kate can tell is there to sell her (possibly) faux confidence.

    “You heard Kate. Explain.”

    Kate exhales through her nose in relief, turning back to her mother, looking at her expectantly. Her mom is looking at Yelena this time, watching her almost as if she is just noticing that she is in the room as well. Maybe that’s actually the case. Yelena holds her gaze, never once dropping her mask of assurance. Eleanor scrutinizes her for a few moments longer before she turns back to Kate. Before she can begin, Dr.Patel speaks up.

    “Is my presence needed for this? I would prefer to not get involved any more than I already am.”

    She speaks to Mr.Browning, and he shakes his head, offering her a smile, but it’s Kate’s mother who answers.

    “No, Dr.Patel, thank you. Robert will let you know once we are done here.” Her mother offers a smile to the doctor as well, and she nods before walking out of the room. Kate moves to the side to let her pass, bringing her even closer to Yelena. This close, Kate can tell that she is still tense, but before she can even think to ask Yelena anything, her mother starts to speak again.

    “Alright, honey. You are right. We…I do owe you an explanation.”

    Eleanor sighs and throws one last dirty glance at Mr.Browning and a quick, curious look at Yelena, before giving her undivided focus to Kate.

    “I would have preferred to tell you this in private, but as you know by now, the few years before my…”

    As Eleanor pauses to clear her throat, she is giving her a look, but Kate refuses to show remorse. Instead, she crosses her arms and leans against the wall, ready to listen. “arrest, I had an unfortunate arrangement with Wilson Fisk.”

    Kate bristles at the expression, exhaling through her nose in annoyance but elects not to interrupt her mother’s explanation, now that she is finally getting it, almost two years late. “I helped him out with certain favors, some above-board, some less so, and we had an… agreement. He had access to the Bishop Security database, as well as some other projects that we worked on at the time.”

    Her mother does look uncomfortable with the story, but Kate can’t tell if she actually feels guilty, or if she just feels bad about being found out.

    “In return, the company would receive financial compensation from him, and also some information, that we were able to monetize as well. Then, about five-” The explanation begins to sound way too vague and Kate cuts in, not willing to let her mother slip out of giving some uncomfortable truths.

    “Okay, hold up. What kind of information? And what kind of favors were you doing for him?”

    Eleanor pauses, her eyes attempting to pin Kate with a motherly look, but as far as Kate is concerned, she lost that right when she started working for a mob boss and then again, when she refused to see Kate for two years. After a few seconds, her mother seems to give up. Sighing, she glances at Mr.Browning before answering.

    “He gave us information on other criminals. Organized crime higher-ups, his competitors… some of his friends even. Business partners. It was a…mutually beneficial arrangement.” “What did you do with the info?”

    Crossing her fingers in her lap, Eleanor leans back, ever the picture of diplomatic elegance, even in a hospital bed, beaten.

    “Some of it, we just sold to intelligence agencies. Most, we built into Bishop Security’s database and system. With an internally developed algorithm, that took into account that data, and some other sources, we were able to increase the accuracy of our security estimations and provide better, more accurate resource allocation advisory services to law enforcement.” Listening carefully, her eyebrows drawn, Kate tries to read between the lines. “So let me get this straight. You used information, provided to you by a mob boss, to make money on giving advice to law enforcement…”

    She waits for her mother’s nod of confirmation before asking again.

    “Advice on what exactly?”

    Her mother’s lawyer steps forward with an awkward chuckle and a condescending, uncle-y smile that Kate wants to wipe off his face immediately.

    “That is privileged information, I’m afraid. It-“ “I’m talking to my mother, Bob, thanks.”

    Kate cuts him off before he can go any further, only glaring at him long enough to send him stepping back into his corner, after a nod of confirmation from her mother. “It’s Robert.”

    Nobody answers him, Kate and her mother now exchanged in a silent war of wills for a few seconds, Yelena and Mr.Browning standing by.

    “The statistical data models and advice we provided could help law enforcement in making resource allocation decisions. But we are getting off-track here…”

    Her mother is trying to get out of answering again, Kate can tell. She is answering her like she is answering questions on an investor’s call when all Kate wants is a straight answer. Exhaling sharply through her nose, she cuts in, rubbing at her face.

    “Jesus, mom…Stop bullshitting.”

    Eleanor leans back at her harsh words, but she doesn’t look angry or shocked. For the first time, she looks actually shameful. Looking away from Kate, her voice is quiet when she answers.

    “Investigations, arrests. Where to look for criminals, and what they are likely to find…” Deflating, Kate considers her mother’s words. After a moment, she summarizes what Eleanor is actually saying.

    “So, you helped Fisk influence the police, essentially legally, through you.” Eleanor purses her lips, avoiding looking at Kate for a second before she nods. In a few seconds, she speaks again, her voice defensive.

    “He…He had other means too. He had detectives and officers directly in his pocket, either by bribes or blackmail, but yes. Through Bishop Security, we were able to influence law enforcement at a wider scale, influence policy decisions, tell them who to look at and more importantly, who not to look at.”

    Closing her eyes for a moment, Kate sighs, focusing for one second on the coldness of the wall behind her back. It doesn’t help.

    “Jesus, that’s…”

    Kate can’t settle on a word. Vile. Evil. Diabolical. Kate feels dirty thinking about the amount of money they, even her, unknowingly, made on all of this.

    “Is there more?”

    Opening her eyes, she looks at her mother, trying to reconcile the image of the woman in the hospital bed, her mom who used to kiss her bruises better and have dance parties with her in the kitchen, with the woman who essentially sold her soul to the devil himself. It feels like another crack in her heart when Eleanor nods.

    “Yes…I…Yes. We…Unfortunately, we haven’t gotten to the part of why we are here today.” Kate runs a hand through her hair, before taking a deep breath and looking at her mother again.

    “Yeah, okay. Go on. Why am I here?”

    Eleanor takes a moment to gather her thoughts and Kate is already dreading what she is about to learn after all of this has been revealed.

    “About five years before Bishop Security’s dissolution, we started a new sub-department in R&D. It focused mainly on biotechnology, developing projects that had security implications.”

    Kate feels her muscles tense, glancing at Yelena as she remembers their conversation with Valentina. Yelena in turn, listens to her mother with rapt attention, her jaw set and poker face firmly in place, only looking back at Kate for a heartbeat before she is focusing on Eleanor again.

    “For the longest while, years really, we didn’t have any breakthroughs, or patents worth mentioning. It was a waste of money and time, honestly. About 8 months after the Blip, after everyone came back, we were on the verge of cutting our losses and shutting the whole department down. But then Fisk came to me with a proposal.”

    Dreading what she is about to learn, Kate glances at Yelena as her mother continues, but she doesn’t look back at her.

    “He got a man in his employ, a man from the group Flag Smashers, who was injected by the re-made Super Soldier serum. Its original maker has been killed sometime before, and this guy, Lennox Richards. He…He was the key to remaking it. We got his blood, and got the best scientists money could buy to remake it or well,…a version of it.”

    Her heart beating hard against her chest, Kate barely blinks as she listens. Super soldiers…in Fisk’s hands. Or Fisk himself, injected with the serum. All of it is bad news. Terrible fucking news. Not just for Kate, but for anyone. Organized crime is already hell in New York, it seems. But with this…Staring at her mother in horror, Kate shakes her head. “Tell me you didn’t. Mom, please tell me you-”

    Eleanor shakes her head and maintains eye contact.

    “I didn’t. I…I know what you think of me. I know what everything I just told you sounds like…but I had a plan, Kate. First of all, the serum that we worked on wasn’t permanent. I… That kind of power, in anyone’s hands… It’s too much. We specifically wanted something that wouldn’t last, only a few hours at –“ Kate buries her face in her hands, as she shakes her head.

    “That’s not any better! You would give criminals-“ “Kate, please. Let me finish.”

    Her mother almost sounds desperate, and Kate huffs before she nods, indicating that she can continue.

    “I had an alternative buyer. Okay? I wanted…I wasn’t going to give it to that monster. But I knew that if I said no, he would just find somebody else to do it with, so I agreed to work on it. In the meantime, I reached out to the government, and we had a deal. They would-” That is admittedly, slightly better, but Kate still feels like she wants to throw up with everything she just learned.

    “The government?”

    Eleanor nods, a small smile on her face.

    “Yes. The army.”

    Sighing deeply, Kate pinches the bridge of her nose before running a hand through her hair, halting to fist her hand in it as she looks back at her mother.

    “So, not only did you make a super-soldier serum with a mob boss, you were double-crossing him too to sell it to someone else and cut him out. Great! Just…Amazing!” Eleanor is obviously disappointed with her take on the story, the smile melting off of her face in a second. But what was she expecting, really? That she gets a medal for not letting a murderous sociopath gain access to the superhero serum that would make him a literal supervillain?

    “Okay. Uh, what happened next?”

    Kate grinds her teeth in an attempt to tamp down on the urge to scream, as her mother continues.

    “Just a few weeks before you…before I was arrested, the serum was essentially finished. We had advanced onto human trials and I had a deal with someone that I would hand over the formula in a few weeks, shortly after the New Year. I’d tell Fisk it was in development indefinitely, or that it was stolen. But then, um, Christmas happened.” Kate crosses her arms again, shifting her weight from one leg to the other. “Aha.”

    Before Kate’s mother can continue, Mr.Browning clears his throat before he begins to speak, apparently growing impatient with the detailed conversation.

    “During the prosecution process, your mother was offered a plea deal, which she accepted. The formula for the drug is part of that deal, but so far, police have been unable to locate it.-” When she looks at her mother, she is reaching over to the bedside table for a plastic cup and then takes a sip of it, meeting Kate’s eyes for only a second. That’s not exactly the truth, is it mom?

    “Normally, that would void the deal altogether, but well…Your mother is a very well- connected woman-“ Kate’s eyes slide back to Mr. Browning. The disdain for the double standard the rich and privileged get to enjoy is clear as day on his face.

    “-and the formula is of extraordinary interest to the government. So…here we are.” He sighs at the end of his explanation, and Kate raises an eyebrow, looking at him first, then at Eleanor, then back at him.

    “So…That’s why I’m here? You brought me in to help you find it?”

    Mr.Browning nods and Kate’s eyes slide over to her mother as he answers. “Yes. Find and procure it.”

    “Why?”

    Her mother shakes her head ever-so-slightly, glancing at Mr.Browning indicating that she shouldn’t pursue that line of questioning while he is here. She answers purposefully vaguely and Kate feels Mr.Browning’s eyes on her as she speaks.

    “You were always good at that sort of thing.”

    Kate glances to the side to look at him too, and it seems obvious that he gets a hint that more is being communicated, than what’s said out loud. Looking between the two of them, he straightens up slightly, before pinning her with a look.

    “Ms.Bishop, I want to stress one important detail. This plea deal is not blanket immunity. It does not cover crimes committed during the retrieval of the formula, and it doesn’t cover you. If you are involved in or need to commit something illegal, and get arrested, you won’t be able to use it as a get-out-of-jail-free card.”

    Kate nods, holding his disapproving gaze. It’s perfectly clear, that Mr.Browning thinks about as highly of her, as he does of her mother, probably assuming she is shady too. “Can that change?”

    Yelena speaks for the first time since the beginning of Eleanor’s explanation, crossing her arms in a position that mirrors Kate’s next to her. Mr.Browning turns to look at her, and if he is surprised about Yelena’s involvement in the conversation, he doesn’t let it show. “What do you mean?”

    Turning to look at her mother as the other two speak, Kate can see as Eleanor is looking Yelena up and down again, obviously trying to get a read on her. As she speaks again, Kate turns to look at Yelena as well.

    “I mean what’s in it for Kate? She puts in the work, maybe even puts herself in danger if all this crime business is as serious as you all say. And for what exactly?” Kate watches her, her eyes pinning Mr.Browning to his spot leaning against the windowsill. He blinks behind his black-rimmed glasses, glancing at Kate, then back to Yelena, maybe expecting Kate to say something. Interested in the answer too, she just looks back at him. “Unfortunately, it’s not within the scope of my authority to make a promise like that. I’ll have to confer with my boss and some other stakeholders.”

    Yelena’s tongue sneaks out to wet her lips, and she turns her head to Kate, meeting her eyes with a slight smile.

    “That sounds like a shitload of work for nothing.”

    They both know they will go after the formula, but Yelena obviously thinks they can negotiate something out of this. Kate shifts her weight again, pursing her lips as she looks back at her, arranging her features to look thoughtful. It’s time to put on a show. “I mean, yeah. We already have that thing.”

    Yelena nods, the corners of her lips twitching upwards for the fraction of a second before she nods seriously.

    “Hmm, yes. That thing.”

    Kate has to resist the urge to smile when an annoyed huff can be heard from the corner of the room. Mr.Browning interrupts their conversation, and Kate can’t believe it worked. “Okay! Fine, I will call my boss. See what I can do.”

    He walks by them, tapping on his phone, and Kate glances at her mother to see her looking at her, an affectionate smile hidden in the corners of her lips. It seems that Robert at least has the sense to know when he is not needed, because a second later he clears his throat, gaining the attention of all three women as he straightens his tie.

    “I have some phone calls to make as well, then talk to Peter. I’ll be outside if I’m needed.” Kate watches him walk out too before a slight touch on her forearm directs her attention to Yelena.

    “I will leave you two to catch up…Stay away from the windows, okay?’

    Yelena speaks in a hushed tone and looks meaningfully into her eyes, tilting her head towards her mother. She waits for Kate to nod slightly before she walks out, giving a slight squeeze to Kate’s arm as she lets go.

    Kate watches her leave, suddenly wishing she had an excuse to go as well. The day has been a rollercoaster and having an emotionally charged, one-on-one conversation with her mother, after all this time, feels incredibly daunting. It seems her mother is not ready to face it either, because she is silent for a moment before she speaks. “What are you wearing?”

    That is the first thing Eleanor says to her after they haven’t been alone in almost two years. It’s said with an affectionate smile and a humorous voice, but it pisses Kate off all the same. Distractedly, she glances down at her workout shorts and hoodie, before looking back at her mother.

    “What? We were at the gym when they called.”

    Eleanor nods, glancing at the door that Yelena just left through, before turning to Kate with her smile widening, eyes glinting with a specific form of calculating curiosity. “Is that who she is…? Your trainer.”

    Not quite believing that that is the conversation that they are having, Kate’s eyebrows furrow. “Who? Yelena? No. We just…-”

    Cutting the sentence in half, she takes a deep breath, refusing to let her mother derail them from the conversation they should be having.

    “What’s going on, mom?”

    Her mother rolls her lips together and crosses her fingers in her lap. “I…what do you mean?”

    Kate tries to gauge if her mother is actually serious before she shakes her head incredulously. Her voice comes out slightly mocking but it’s not enough to mask the obvious hurt in it that she feels.

    “Well, you refused to see me for like two years. Then, you drag me in, for this? By pretending to…die, I guess? Get hurt, whatever. You…”

    Unable to put into words how crazy everything that just happened has been so she gestures widely around, hoping that her mother understands.

    “So, what the fuck?”

    Eleanor takes a deep breath, shaking her head, but Kate is somewhat satisfied that she doesn’t look away.

    “Kate, you have to understand. I kept you away for your own good. I didn’t want you mixed up in this.”

    Kate shakes her head in disbelief, leans back fully against the wall again, and wets her lips. She can’t be serious. Her attempt to count to ten to calm herself only gets her to three, before the words start spewing out of her mouth.

    “For my own good!? Are you fucking serious? What, you couldn’t even let me know or I don’t know, call me?! Text me. Send me a fucking letter?!”

    Her mother shakes her head once almost impatiently and huffs and it only serves to throw oil on the fire growing in Kate.

    “I was monitored, Kate. Fisk, he…he has people everywhere. I couldn’t risk him finding out that we were still talking.”

    Kate feels her lips curl in anger and her voice comes out tight with it too. “That’s bullshit, mom. You could have-“ Before she can give herself fully over to her fury, Eleanor cuts her off, her own voice tight with anger too but her eyes shining like she is about to break down in tears any second. “It was hell for me, Kate. Absolute hell. But you are my daughter. I… You are the only thing that matters to me.”

    There is a beat of silence when the two of them are just looking at each other, before Eleanor speaks again, her voice losing its edge and sounding almost broken.

    “Please never doubt that.”

    Kate feels a lump start to rise in her throat as well and can’t hold her mother’s gaze any longer. She sniffs once as she looks down at the tips of her shoes, before glancing around the room.

    “It was hell for me too. Why…Why did you do it then?”

    Looking up at her mom again, Kate searches her face for any sign of disingenuity or anger, but all she finds is love and longing.

    “Kate, Wilson Fisk is an incredibly dangerous man.-”

    Kate huffs, lifting her chin. That’s an understatement.

    “I know.”

    “-I wanted…I hoped that if he thought we were estranged, he would leave you alone.” Kate laughs at her words humorlessly, biting the tip of her tongue before she pins her mother with a look and an arched eyebrow.

    “Well, that definitely didn’t happen. He has been trying to get me killed for weeks now.” All color leaves her mother’s face and her fingers twitch again. She leans forward as if she is about to get out of bed, but never quite completes the movement.

    “What!? No. Oh god. No. We can…I’ll call Mr.Browning back in, we will get you protective custody. We’ll-“ Kate shakes her head, kissing her teeth.

    “I don’t need it.”

    “Kate-“ “I said no, mom.”

    At the tone of her voice, final and short, for maybe the first time in their lives, Kate’s mother closes her mouth and listens to her. There is a little bit of guilt stirring in Kate’s chest at the expression on Eleanor’s face, but it’s almost immediately squashed as a thought enters her head.

    “Okay. So if you want me safe and far away from this, why involve me in this now? Why involve me at all?”

    Looking at her mother, Kate sees Eleanor’s own guilt color her face and she looks down at her hands.

    “I didn’t want to. I really…I did everything I could to avoid it. But it seems that I have no choice.”

    There is another pause where Kate tries to decide if she believes her mother and Eleanor looking at her, visibly nervous. She speaks again in a few seconds, her voice hesitant. “There is more to it than I could say in front of Mr.Browning. If I could just explain…” Eleanor pauses to swallow and Kate sighs, crossing her arms again. She suspected that her mother was holding back earlier and while she is intrigued to find out why she also can’t help but dread knowing even more. It feels like anything she learns only serves to hurt her more, and after everything, she doesn’t know how much more she can take.

    At Kate’s reluctant nod, her mother straightens a little, attempting to enter what Kate used to call her “CEO-mode” again.

    “Okay. So… The formula. When we were essentially finished, the information was split into parts. The data is encrypted, and it was hidden on the secure, offline Bishop Security servers. To get it, the data itself is needed, but you also need to know where to look in the database, and you need a key to decrypt it.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate shakes her head in confusion while trying to ignore how much her mother being able to shift gears so easily bothers her.

    “Why so many parts?”

    Her mother laces her fingers together as if she is answering shareholder questions at a quarterly meeting. It feels unsettlingly familiar.

    “Because the hidden database doesn’t only contain the formula for the temporary enhancement serum. It also contains the contingency I had kept, in case my working relationship with Fisk ever went sour. Which it did.”

    Wetting her lips, Kate watches her mother.

    “You suspected that it would go sour.”

    Eleanor huffs, leaning back again and holding Kate’s gaze.

    “Of course I suspected. He is a monster. He uses people and then throws them away. I suspected he will not be happy when I inevitably try to get out.”

    Kate purses her lips, grinding her teeth together, unable to not go down the road even though it’s probably a distraction now, especially with the short time they have on their own. “You still worked for him… And profited off of him.”

    Their gazes are locked, Kate hoping to get her mother to take accountability, Eleanor probably trying to get her to back down. Neither works. After a moment, her mother sighs, running a hand with an IV line in it through her hair.

    “I did. I didn’t lie to you, Kate. When your father died, I was blindsided. He has been borrowing from Fisk for years, getting shadier and shadier deals to fund his projects-“ Her mother trying to shake off her responsibility and trying to smear his father’s memory infuriates Kate. Almost hissing, she interrupts Eleanor.

    “Don’t try to push this on Dad! He wanted to help people, he would have never-“ It seems they have reached the end of Eleanor’s patience as well, because she cuts Kate off too, her voice tight with the calculated fury that always used to signal the end of their arguments before.

    “Kate, your father… You always idolized him, and because he died and because you needed it, I let you. But Kate, Derek…he was far from perfect. He wanted to do good, yes. Sure. I loved that about him.“ Kate wants to interrupt but there is something on her mother’s face that stops her, making her swallow the words rising in her throat. Eleanor doesn’t look like she is defensive or evading honesty. She looks like she is getting something off her chest, telling a truth after keeping it in for so long.

    “But baby, he grew up incredibly rich, and entitled and when his ideals didn’t work, he did what all rich people do. He expected someone else to solve his problems. And when nobody did or could, he looked for an easy way out. Do you know he gambled away nearly all his inheritance on an NGO that then got shut down because they funneled money to an African warlord? That he wanted to break up your trust-fund, to finance a start-up that would build habitat for homeless people, that ended up being a Ponzi scheme and gotten everyone involved arrested? Do you know…”

    Eleanor cuts herself off and gulps, breaking eye contact as she seems to get herself back in check again. Kate watches, simultaneously mesmerized and horrified. Eleanor continues after a silent few moments.

    “I loved your father. I truly did. Derek was my best friend, and he was a good man with good intentions and a huge heart. You got that from him. But when his own trust fund ran out, and he couldn’t touch the company, or yours, he went running to Fisk. I don’t think he knew what Wilson was but I’m sure that he could have found out if he wanted to…if he cared to look further than his obsession with “helping people”.”

    Utterly speechless, Kate just stares at her mother. This is probably the most honest she has been with Kate in years, maybe ever. For now, she can’t even begin to comprehend if that’s a good thing or not. Eleanor sighs, shaking her head.

    “I’m sorry baby, I shouldn’t have said all that. I just…I am just so tired of always being the bad guy. I know you were closer to him, I know that…” “ Kate does want to interrupt this time, with what, she doesn’t know. She opens her mouth but Eleanor lifts a hand off of her lap, wordlessly asking Kate to let her finish. “I know what you think of me. And you are…You are right. Partially at least. I got tunneled into working for Fisk, but I didn’t work hard enough to get out from under his thumb and I took advantage of the opportunity it presented.”

    Eleanor stops talking, but Kate doesn’t feel ready to answer just yet. Everything she learned about her dad, her mom, their entire family, feels too heavy to process. Rubbing her face with both her palms, she sighs before looking at Eleanor again.

    Her mother looks tired and small, and almost nervous. She looks at Kate like her next words could destroy her and while Kate thinks she would be justified in doing so, she can’t do it. Pulling her hands from her face, she leans against the wall again.

    “Look, I’m not…I’m not ready to get over this. Not for a while yet. I need time. To think and process.”

    She speaks after a long moment of silence, and Eleanor nods, her eyes dropping to her lap. She seems almost defeated, and maybe she shouldn’t, but Kate can’t watch her suffer anymore.

    “But I will help you. It’s…Not just because of you, but because it’s the right thing to do. But…yeah, I will help you.”

    Telling her mother she loves her, even if it’s true, feels like a concession too big, but Eleanor’s eyes shine with happiness all the same.

    “Thank you, baby. I will-“ “But no more lies, okay? No more half-truths and no more secrets.”

    Kate interrupts her mother, and Eleanor nods, her eyes never leaving hers. “Okay. I promise.”

    Kate offers a smile that feels weak and rigid, but her mom returns it all the same. “Okay. Um, you were saying…umm…Three parts. The data, the path or like…location, and the key. Go on.”

    Eleanor nods again, seemingly needing a second to change gears too.

    “Right. Yes, so. I had the data split up for security, and after I got arrested, the first thing I did was ask my lawyers to destroy the bits they could get their hands on.” “What? Why?”

    Her face scrunches up as Kate shakes her head.

    “Because I knew that he would be looking for it. There was no way to delete the data, but the pathway and the encryption could be destroyed.”

    That makes sense to Kate, so she nods for Eleanor to continue as she leans her weight onto her other leg.

    “Unfortunately, the pathway was taken during the FBI’s raid of the penthouse before I could even talk to Robert. Without the database, it’s useless, but if Fisk ever finds out, he can probably get it.”

    “The FBI is in bed with Fisk?”

    It shouldn’t be a surprise, but it’s still bad news. More bad news, when Kate thinks about the interview she is supposed to have with them tomorrow.

    “Some of them are. I don’t know who or how many of them, but during our…dealings, there were times when he needed something from them and was able to get it pretty quickly.” Closing her eyes for a long moment, Kate groans out the word.

    “Great.”

    “Yeah.”

    When she opens her eyes, Eleanor is looking at her and Kate huffs with barely there amusement.

    “Sorry. Go on.”

    Eleanor looks concerned and Kate doesn’t miss the way her hand lifts imperceptively as if she wants to reach out for her.

    “Are you okay?”

    “Yeah. It’s just…It’s been a long couple of weeks.”

    Sighing, Eleanor nods.

    “I’m sorry.”

    “It’s….yeah. Let’s just keep going. Browning might be back any minute.” “Are you sure?”

    “Yeah. Please, go on.”

    “Okay. So. The pathway is with the FBI, but Robert was able to destroy the copy of the encryption I had in my office.”

    It starts to feel like she should be taking notes, so Kate takes out her phone, looking up at her mom again.

    “Okay, once sec. I’m going to write some of this down...”

    Opening the notes app, she begins to write down ‘3 parts, data, pathway, key’. Meanwhile, she realizes it’ll probably help with all the emotional weight of the situation if she treats it like a case from her PI business.

    “So. Your database is split into three parts. The database itself, the location of where the important stuff is, and the encryption, right?”

    Eleanor nods, and Kate speaks again, remembering some details of the research they did into Fisk in the last few weeks.

    “The database was on the secure servers. Those got auctioned off and sold when Bishop Security went under, correct?”

    Blinking, Eleanor turns her head to the side a little.

    “Should I ask how you know that?”

    Kate shakes her head with a tense smile, and Eleanor does too, before continuing. “Robert told me some small security company bought it, and then they got bought out by a bigger corporation.”

    Kate nods, looking at her mother. From her research into Fisk’s financials, she knows that the company that ended up with the servers is Limitless Corporation, which also happens to be Fisk’s. She is not sure however if she should be sharing that with her mom. “Okay. I’ll look into that.”

    Into her notes, she writes down ‘Limitless has them’ next to the database bit before she turns back to her mother.

    “So, the encryption is supposedly destroyed. Do you trust Robert?”

    Her mom nods, pursing her lips.

    “I do. His wife, um…she got killed as a bystander in one of Fisk’s hits. He hates him even more than I do.-”

    With great self-restraint, Kate doesn’t comment on the fact that there are probably hundreds, if not thousands of people who hate Fisk more than her mother, considering she was fine with working for him for years. Treat it like a case. Or that due to her working for him, Robert might hate her too just enough to double-cross her. Instead, she just types ‘destroyed?’ in her notes. Before she can move on, Eleanor speaks again.

    “But there is another copy. I hid it in the safe at the summer place.” Eyebrows lifting, Kate regards her mother.

    “The Hamptons? When did you have time to go there?”

    “Jack and I went there for Thanksgiving before I was arrested. I thought if we ever needed backup, it’d be a good place to hide it.”

    That assessment is a good one, Kate has to give it to her mother.

    The family’s “summer place” is a huge property, with several buildings. Even if it got raided, there is no way for anyone to look through all of its hidden nooks and crannies, and after Kate’s father's passing, it passed onto Kate directly which made it exempt from the investigation into Eleanor anyway. It has been in her father’s family for 5 generations, built by Kate’s great-grandfather, around the same time as the building her parents’ penthouse was built “Okay. Which safe is it in?”

    “The one above the fireplace in the upstairs living room of the main building. The code is your birthday.”

    Kate writes down that in her phone too, nodding at her notes before she looks at Eleanor again.

    “So. I get the key, I get the pathway. Then what?”

    Eleanor wets her lips, her guilt, and nervousness back on her face.

    “You need all of them, in one place and then you can export the information out.” There is something on her mother’s face that gives Kate a pause.

    “Okay. What’s the catch?”

    Taking another deep sigh, Eleanor meets her eyes.

    “The decryption process takes about 72 hours.”

    Okay, that’s a complication.

    Even if they do manage to get access to the secure servers, under heavy security at Limitless Holdings, there is no way they can stay there for three days. Anyway, Yelena and Sonya will probably have a better idea of how to handle this hurdle. Kate nods to herself, making a note of that too.

    “Right. Okay. We’ll deal with that. Somehow.”

    While she looks over her notes, her mother is silent but when she looks up, Kate can see the worry on her face.

    “Kate, I know you can take care of yourself. But please, please don’t put yourself in unnecessary danger for this. That’s not why I asked you to do this.”

    Rolling her lips together, Kate leans slightly back and away from her mother again. Without her noticing, she gravitated closer to her as she was speaking, but now she feels the need for distance.

    “Mom, you can’t have your cake and eat it too. You asked me to help.”

    Deflating, Eleanor looks away and reaches for her glass of water again. After taking a couple of sips, she turns back to Kate.

    “I know. But please…just be careful. If it comes down to your safety or getting what I asked, just leave it. It’s not worth putting yourself in serious danger for.” To put an end to this conversation, Kate nods, but she thinks both of them know that she will not stop going after this now. The formula in Fisk’s hands would be devastating, and the evidence her mother gathered might be enough to put Fisk away for good if law enforcement ever manages to apprehend him somehow. She also tries not to think about the fact that if her mother was really that worried about her safety, she wouldn’t be involving her now “Ok-kay. Is there anything else you are leaving out?”

    Eleanor shakes her head, her fingers wrapping themselves around the edge of her covers. “No. That’s it.”

    Kate nods, and locks her phone, before pushing it into the pocket of her hoodie. Now that there is no set topic to cover, the silence stretches on for a few uncomfortable seconds, while they look at each other. Still clinging to trying to make this work like another case, Kate attempts to hold onto the topic.

    “Is there a component we need to go for first? Like, out of the three?” “Well, if you gain access to the data, you need the encryption and the pathway to export what you need. So, you probably need those first.”

    “Right.”

    As Kate attempts to come up with a question that will make them stay on topic, she makes the mistake of looking at her mother again. She looks small sitting on the bed, kind of defeated. Her hair even has a few grey strands in it now and Kate feels the weight of their relationship on her shoulders again.

    She is not ready to forgive her mother for everything she has done, some of which she only just learned about, but honestly, it also kind of feels like shit to stay mad at her and kick her while she is so obviously down too. It’s like being stuck between being a horrible daughter and a horrible person, and Kate feels like she is being ground up between two thousand-ton rocks.

    What makes it all feel even heavier, is that her mom never once takes her eyes off of Kate. She looks at her like she is the sun, after living an entire life underground. Like she is seeing green plain after walking through the desert.

    Kate kind of forgot what it was like to have all that love directed at her. What it’s like to have a mom.

    Maybe it makes her a shitty person, but right now, all she wants is to make her mom feel better.

    With a sigh, she leans off of the wall and walks across the room to grab a chair, feeling her mom’s eyes on her the entire time. She brings it to her mother’s bedside and sits down on it. Meeting Eleanor’s eyes again, she can see hope and some fragile happiness, and it does kind of feel like a kick in the chest, but Kate smiles through it.

    “So, how are you?”

    She hopes Eleanor understands what she is saying, without her having to say it out loud. I am not ready to forgive you, but I am tired of being mad at you. If the surprised but elated smile is anything to go by on her mother’s face, she does.

    “I…well. It’s prison. The meals are shit and the people are worse. I do get to walk around outside twice a day though.”

    Kate blinks, eyes searching her mother’s bruised face. With so many things she could ask and talk about, she tries to focus on the lighter ones. They covered enough heavy topics today. “Did you really start a fight?”

    Surprisingly, Eleanor chuckles at that and shakes her head.

    “No. Well, yes. We arranged with the DOJ that I’d be taken out of Rykers for this discussion because I didn’t want you to be seen visiting there so we had to find an excuse. But the other inmate didn’t know, so she took it…well, yeah. A bit seriously.”

    Kate’s eyes drop from the bruises on her face to the bandages on her forearm and the IV connected to her.

    “Are you okay though? Like, physically.”

    From the corner of her eyes, Kate can see her mother’s hand twitch and then grab the covers again, seemingly holding herself back from reaching out to her again.

    “Yeah, I will be. She did stab me twice, but it’s not deep.”

    She smiles at Kate but the atmosphere in the room is still sad, and it still feels suffocating. Kate really just wants it gone. The next words slip out of Kate’s mouth without her meaning to.

    “Do you have a prison wife?”

    It certainly works in changing the mood, as Eleanor bursts out laughing and Kate can’t hold it in either. There is so much history, so much shit between them, but at that moment, it finally fades to the background for a second. With laughter in her voice, Eleanor answers. “No, Kate. I don’t have a prison wife.”

    Scrunching up her nose, Kate asks jokingly.

    “Slim pickings?”

    With an amused huff, Eleanor leans back against the pillows behind her back. “Not really, no. I actually got plenty of offers, but well…“ Kate can’t help but snort, looking at her mother too.

    “-Still missing a key anatomical component for me though.”

    The lift of her mother’s eyebrow tells her everything Kate needs to know and she scrunches up her face again, this time in disgust, deciding not to mention Jack in the hopes of keeping things lighthearted.

    “Ugh, yeah, no. I regret asking already, thanks.”

    Eleanor’s smile widens into a grin, and her eyes flit toward the door for a second, before they settle on Kate.

    “Speaking of-“ Kate interrupts the line of questioning before it can begin with a shake of her head. Kate’s personal life or the lack of it, and Eleanor’s responsibility in all that is a can of worms they should avoid opening right now as well.

    “Do you have a roommate?”

    Crossing her fingers in her lap, Eleanor regards her for a second. It seems she accepts Kate sidestepping her half-formed question because she answers in few moments. “Yes, we all do. Her name is Brita, and she is 52. She has 2 kids.”

    Kate lifts an eyebrow.

    “Like the filter?”

    With an amused huff and a smile, Eleanor nods.

    “Yeah, I guess.”

    “What is she in for?”

    The smile melts off of her mother’s face, and for a moment she looks even older, her eyes dimming.

    “Nobody talks about that.”

    Kate wets her lips, her eyes dropping to her lap.

    “Right.”

    At the sound of the door opening behind her, Kate twists around, finding Yelena in the doorway, looking at the two of them. She looks at Kate first, then at her mother, before turning back to her.

    “Hi. You have about two minutes until Mr.Browning figures out that the phone number I gave him for Kate belongs to an animal shelter in Ohio. So…”

    Kate snorts, smiling at Yelena, mentally noting that she kept the American accent the whole time they have been in here.

    “Okay, thanks. I’ll be right out.”

    Yelena nods before her eyes jump over to her mom. She only seems to think for a moment, before she nods at her too, and closes the door behind herself as she leaves. Maybe she shouldn’t be, but Kate is surprised to see her mother smirk when she twists back around a second later.

    “So…She is fun.”

    Blinking, Kate hums, smiling back at her mother uncertainly. Yelena is a topic they should not touch upon right now either. Her mom really doesn’t need to know about their activities going after Fisk and Kate also doesn’t feel like thinking or talking about Eleanor hiring someone to kill Clint, just when they kind of made peace.

    “Yeah. Yelena is…yeah.”

    Unsurprisingly, Kate’s attempt and hope that her vague answer will redirect her mom’s curiosity about something else does not work.

    “Who is she?”

    Kate takes a few seconds, trying to decide whether saying “the assassin you hired to kill Clint” is a good idea, in her mother’s current state and with where they stand with each other after their long conversation.

    Eleanor misunderstands her hesitation, her smile widening even more as she speaks before Kate can make up her mind.

    “Oooh…is it serious?”

    What? Oh.

    Her eyebrows rising, Kate huffs awkwardly, glancing at the door again, then back at her mom.

    “No. Yes. I mean, she is a friend.”

    Eleanor’s smile stretches even more, almost grinning now. It only serves to show how much older her mom looks now.

    “A friend, huh? Like Jessica Meyer?”

    The mention of the memory of her mother walking in on her “sleepover” with Jessica, a girl from high school, takes Kate by surprise and she bursts out laughing, partially from shock but mostly because she doesn’t know how else to react. She couldn’t look her mom in the eyes for a week after.

    “Oh my god, mom. Why would you bring that up now? No.”

    Eleanor settles against the pillows even more, looking at Kate warmly, clearly reveling in getting to tease her daughter again.

    “It seems relevant.”

    Kate can feel her ears warm up a little, remembering Yelena’s sex voice from earlier, the time they got high on morphine and nearly went to Sonya’s bathroom to…whatever that was, and everything regarding Amanda and Yelena’s reaction to it.

    Well, it’s not like her mom knows all that.

    “It’s not.”

    Her mother only hums, her smile still in place, but her eyes grow somber soon. For a long moment, she is just looking at Kate, before she speaks again, her voice quiet and full of what Kate would like to imagine is guilt.

    “I want you to be happy, baby.”

    The sentence feels like another kick in the chest.

    What can even Kate say to that? Her mother doing what she has done has turned her life upside down. She is practically hunted, her friends, anyone she is in contact with is in constant danger. The society she grew up in has chewed her up and spit her out, after her mom’s arrest and apart from a 50-year-old retired avenger and two black widow assassins, she can’t say if she has anyone she can honestly count as a friend.

    Eyes dropping to her lap before she closes them, Kate leans forward and takes a deep breath. Eleanor doesn’t speak again, waiting for her to do so, and Kate takes a few moments to gather her thoughts.

    “That’s a nice sentiment, mom. But, and I’m not saying this to hurt you, or to…like, restart this argument, but you kinda fucked that up for me, by working for him. For…doing what you did.”

    She looks up as she is speaking, and sees the conflict on her mother’s face. She looks sad at first, but Kate can see when anger starts to spark too, in the slight lift of her mother’s chin. “Well, I didn’t get myself arrested.”

    Grinding her teeth together, Kate looks back at her mother.

    “No. But you did murder someone. You did hire an assassin to get Clint killed. You did work for a mafia boss for years, even after you didn’t have to. You did frame Jack. You helped Fisk influence police de-“ Her mother looks properly angry for the first time, cutting Kate off.

    “How many times did I get you out of trouble? How many times have I pulled the strings to not get you expelled from somewhere or to have your…adventures overlooked?” Leaning back, Kate huffs, uncomfortable with the insinuation her mother is making. It’s not the same.

    “What, so I shouldn’t have gotten you arrested, because you had my back as a kid? Maybe you shouldn’t have.”

    Eleanor rolls her lips together, taking a deep breath as if to calm herself. “Yes. But that’s beside the point. The point is, that I have done all of that, to protect you. I always have and I always will. You can’t blame-“ Kate cuts her off, her voice rising at first, before she quiets herself, remembering where they are.

    “I didn’t want you to! Not like that!”

    Eleanor looks away, with a shake of her head.

    “You don’t understand. And you won’t either. Not until you have a kid of your own.” Biting down on the inside of her cheek, Kate exhales with a hiss.

    “That has nothing to do with having a kid or not. I didn’t ask-“ Eleanor interrupts her again and her words make Kate’s stomach flip with anxiety and anger. “It has everything to do with that. I would have gotten anyone and everyone killed if it meant protecting you. And I’d do it again.”

    The chair almost falls back as Kate stands up, her hands feeling shaky again. “I didn’t ask you to do any of that! I’d rather have been poor than you doing any of this. But you have never-“ Eleanor shakes her head, closing her eyes.

    “Being poor? You think, after everything you have seen, that Wilson Fisk would have bankrupted us, if I didn’t go work for him? He would have murdered you and me both, just to show everyone what happened to people that owed him money and didn’t pay.” She feels her nostrils flaring, but Kate ignores the urge to step away. “You could have gone to the police! Asked for help! Something!”

    Almost rolling her eyes, Eleanor shakes her head, a chuckle that lacks any kind of joy slipping between her lips.

    “Oh, I am sure you must be more grown up by now, Kate.”

    The two of them look at each other for a moment, and Kate already mourns the unsteady truce they had a few minutes ago. Virtually everything that has been said in this room, made Kate feel like shit and for a moment, she seriously considers just leaving. Before she can make up her mind, her mother speaks again, her voice calmer. “You are an adult now, Kate. You can continue to think that you have some moral high ground here, but the truth is, I have done the best I can, with the cards that I was dealt.” Pausing, Eleanor looks down at her hands before meeting Kate’s eyes again and continuing. “I hope you are never in the position that I was in. That you never have to choose between a person you love, or love the most, and your morals. But if you expect me to regret what I have done…”

    The sentence is left hanging, and Kate sucks in a breath and wipes at a tear that escapes her eye. The horrifying truth is, that Kate can relate. Isn’t this the exact same pledge she made herself at her dad’s grave? That she will protect those she loves from Fisk, whatever it takes? “You can stay mad at me if you want. You are my daughter and I will always love you anyway. But I will not apologize or…cower for making sure that you were safe, that you had everything growing up. ”

    Kate exhales through her nose, closing her eyes for a second. When she opens them, she lifts her chin, looks back at her mother, and hopes that her voice comes out stronger than she feels.

    “And I will not apologize for getting you arrested. Whether you did it for me or not, what you did was wrong. I know what it’s like to fear for people you love. More than I can tell you, and for that, I sympathize with you. But making a deal with the devil...”

    Shaking her head, Kate is the one to leave the sentence hanging this time. She clears her throat, before speaking again.

    “Anyway. I will always love you, too. And I will help you with this. I don’t…don’t want to see you hurt, or to never see you again. ”

    Her mother is crying too, and looks incredibly sad again, as opposed to her earlier anger, but this time Kate doesn’t feel the urge to make it go away. This is their reality. This is who they are. It may hurt, but at least it’s truthful.

    “Okay. I will take that.”

    Her mother gives a tearful smile, that Kate returns, a bit shaky. She only gets to take a step forward towards her earlier seat, when the door behind her opens again, and Yelena, Mr.Browing, and Robert, the lawyer file in again.

    For a quick moment, Kate turns away to wipe at the few tears that escaped, before stepping in to stand by Yelena’s side. In a hushed tone, she speaks to Kate, eyes searching her face. “Are you okay?”

    Kate nods at her, giving her a kind of wonky, distracted smile that she knows convinces exactly nobody, but the time to discuss everything that her mom and she talked about is definitely not here and now.

    “Yeah. Um, anything good with Browning?”

    For a second, Yelena is just looking at her, before she shrugs.

    “No idea. He didn’t talk to me after the phone number thing.”

    Kate huffs in amusement, smiling at Yelena a bit stronger this time, and she smiles back at her, almost conspiratorially. She looks over Kate’s shoulders then, indicating that Kate should turn around with a quick lift of her chin.

    “A word, Ms. Bishop?”

    Turning fully back around, Kate faces Mr.Browning, clearing her throat at him before asking. “Yeah, I’m here. Um, did you manage to talk to your supervisor?”

    The smile she receives in return lacks any kind of authenticity, and would probably be classified as an insult, in most cultures.

    “Unfortunately, we cannot make any promises. If you do get caught doing something illegal, while procuring the requested asset, we might be able to come to a deal with you as well. We cannot, however, provide blanket immunity for the asset as it’s the foundation of another person’s plea deal already.”

    The fact that Peter Browning hates her for nothing else than being related to someone he hates is pretty obvious, but Kate didn’t think it’d get in the way of his professionalism. It didn’t slip her notice that he sidestepped her question about whether he talked to his boss and she is also pretty sure that he is bullshitting them, to some degree at least. But in any case, their bluff was called, so it is time to return the favor. In her best sticky-sweet bitch voice she answers, smiling back at him.

    “Oh, that’s a shame. Unfortunately, in that case, I can’t make any promises in return either. If I stumble upon it, I’ll be sure to pass it along though.”

    It doesn’t matter what she says, her mother and Yelena both know they are going after the formula and the evidence against Fisk anyway, and Peter Browning doesn’t need to. There is annoyance in his eyes, behind the black-rimmed glasses, but he doesn’t budge. Instead, he reaches into the inside of his suit jacket, pulling out a business card. “Alright then. If you do find anything, please don’t hesitate to call.” They stare at each other for a moment, before Yelena clears her throat, breaking them both out of it and speaking up.

    “Ok-kay. Let’s go home?”

    Kate breaks their eye contact, nodding towards Yelena as she steps toward her mother’s bed again, to say goodbye.

    “Yeah, yeah. One sec. Um. Mom. Is it okay if I come to see you again while you are here?” It’s an olive branch of sorts, again, an attempt to preserve their unsteady truce from before. Her mom’s face pulls into a sad smile, and she shakes her head, but it’s Mr.Browning’s annoying, smug voice that answers her from behind her back.

    “Unfortunately, your mother is going to be transferred back to Rykers tomorrow morning.” Eyes widening, Kate twists around to look at him.

    “What? She has just been attacked!”

    He nods, with that fake, hateful smile back on his lips.

    “Yes, and her injuries could have been treated back at Rykers, if we didn’t need to organize this meeting. So now that it has happened, there is no need for her to stay out here.” Kate is fuming, but a hand on her forearm stops her from arguing. Her mother’s hand pulls on her arm, turning her partially towards herself.

    “It’s okay, Kate. It’s best if it stays off his radar anyway. I’ll be fine.” Huffing, Kate grinds her teeth together, but it’s obvious that this is not something she will get to change right now. In a few seconds, she nods with another huff, glaring at Peter Browning for a second before looking fully at her mother.

    “Okay. Can you…call at least? Or something?”

    Her mother ages another 5 years with how sad she looks as she shakes her head. “I’m afraid not. It’s…safer if we stay out of contact, at least for now. We can…once the trial is done, we can talk again.”

    If both of them live that long. Kate shakes her head at the morbid thought, closing her eyes for a second.

    “Right. Okay. So, I guess this is goodbye? For now?”

    Her mom nods, her eyes glinting with tears again. Kate refuses to cry again too, but the lump in her throat is there, and for the thousandth time, she curses Wilson Fisk to the depths of hell, for doing this to her family.

    “Take care, Kate. Please, please, stay safe.”

    Attempting to smile through the pain, she nods at her mom, gulping down the thorny lump in her throat.

    “Yeah, you too.”

    Stepping closer, she leans down to hug her mother and she puts her arms around Kate as well, pulling her close and tucking her damp face into her neck. It lasts long, longer than their first hug in the beginning but Kate pulls herself away in about a minute.

    “Goodbye, mom”

    Her mom looks at Yelena then, nodding at her and giving her a smile.

    “Make sure she doesn’t do something reckless?”

    For a very short moment, Yelena looks visibly uncertain before her usual mask slips into place, giving her mother a lopsided smile.

    “I’ll do my best, Mrs. Bishop.”

    Her mother chuckles, and before Kate knows it, Yelena and she are through the door and walking away, after bidding a quick goodbye to Mr. Browning and Robert. Whatever power kept Kate standing during this whole afternoon, begins to slip away and by the time they make it to the car, Kate feels absolutely drained.

    It seems impossible to pinpoint whether she feels sad, angry, happy, relieved, or hurt. The afternoon has been overwhelming, to say the least, and if it was up to Kate, she’d go and run until she can’t feel anything but her lungs screaming for air and her muscles begging her to stop.

    But since her assassin problem didn’t miraculously solve itself in the last 3 hours, she can’t even do that.

    Sonya waits for them in the car, on the phone when they get into the backseat. They catch the end of her conversation with who Kate assumes is Thomas.

    “…ago. Okay, they are here. I’ll see you at home?”

    From the speakers, Tommy’s voice sounds warm and calm, as always.

    “Okay! Love you! Tell Kate I said sorry about her mom!”

    Kate gives a weak smile to Sonya as their eyes meet in the rearview mirror and she answers Thomas.

    “I will! Love you too!”

    Sonya presses the screen on the dashboard to end the call, before twisting around in her seat to look between the two of them.

    “How are we? How is your mom?”

    Kate wets her lips, trying to force a tired smile onto her lips.

    “She is…She will be fine.”

    Pausing for a minute, Kate takes a deep breath.

    “Um, we got some other news as well. Yelena can fill you in, I just uh. I need some time to process. I…She told me some more details too, when we were alone, but I need…I will tell you later, okay? Both of you.”

    Sonya glances at Yelena who nods at her, before turning back to Kate.

    “Sure, yeah. You…we will talk about it later. Are you okay?”

    Kate huffs in amusement, but it mostly comes out tired.

    “Yeah, no. It’s…whatever. I just need some time to…I just need some time.” Holding her gaze, Sonya nods before reaching back to grab her hand, giving it a squeeze. “I am sorry. If there is anything that we can do…”

    She leaves the end of the sentence hanging, and Kate gives an honest smile back to her this time, squeezing her hand back as well.

    “Yeah, thanks. And thank you for driving me here.”

    Sonya’s smile widens-

    “Had worse Friday afternoons.”

    As she turns back around, Kate sees the glance she gives Yelena. She doesn’t need to know Russian to decipher what it means. We’ll talk later.

    Sincerely hoping that that later happens when they are home, and Kate is not around for it, she leans her head back onto the headrest, closing her eyes. She really can’t bear having one more difficult conversation today.

    Before she can give herself over to her moping, Kate opens her eyes and turns to Yelena, finding her already looking.

    “And um, thank you for being there. With me. It’s…it helped a lot.”

    Yelena smiles at her, easy and warm.

    “You are welcome. I said before, mothers are complicated business.”

    The return of her Russian accent is like a puzzle piece slotting into place. So is her hand, when she reaches to grab Kate’s after a moment, giving it a squeeze.

    Chapter End Notes Hi guys!

    So, Chapter 20 was originally meant to be three times this long but the next two bits are not finished yet and well. It is the one year anniversary of Kate and Yelena’s mac&cheese date/girls’ night so. Here we are :D I do wish for this occasion I could share something more bishova centric, but the rest of this chapter is not yet finished so I hope you still enjoy this.

    I do think this is a very important chapter both from a plot perspective (getting the three components of the formula are gonna shape this story going forward), but also for Kate. I know some people wanted Eleanor to be a villain, but in my opinion, like many others antagonists, her redeeming feature is that she loves her daughter. She loves her daughter more than everything, like most parents do and her going against Kate doesn’t feel realistic to me. Parents and children, mothers and daughters are complicated enough, especially when they connected by the love they share for each other, but divided by their actions and their circumstances. Also, people and the things they do for the people they love, crossing lines through that, and convincing themselves they are doing the right thing is a returning theme of this story and Kate’s development. Her mother’s side of that is obviously an important part of that :)

    I also think that it's nice to see Kate and Yelena back on good terms, united in the face of adversity. it may not have been a chapter about them, but I think there are a few moments where you can see how their relationship has grown, and how it's heading towards more intimate waters slowly ':D So! I hope you all liked this chapter! I hope to post the second half (2/3rds) of this story soon too, preferably before Christmas but we will see if that's possible or not :D Please let me know what you think inthe comments below!

    xx

    Chapter 21

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Yelena does not hold her hand for the rest of the way home, and Kate spends it mostly staring out the window, seeing almost nothing and lost in her thoughts. Yelena and Sonya are quiet too, the three of them slowly making their way through the busy Friday afternoon traffic. Everything she has learned, in the last few hours weighs on Kate, her thoughts not able to sort through everything coherently just yet, jumping from one thing to the other instead. The silence is only broken as they arrive at their building, pulling up to the garage door. “Huh. We have a new doorman.”

    Kate hums in response to Sonya, eyes glancing over to the man standing by the main entrance but not really taking note. The three of them are embraced by darkness a second later, as the gate opens and they drive through the threshold, then down the ramp. They make it to Kate’s level in a few moments, Sonya expertly parking the car back in its spot and before long, the three of them are stepping into the elevator, and Sonya presses the buttons for floors thirteen and twenty-nine.

    Kate is thankful if a little surprised that they both get out on level thirteen, both of them smiling at her as they do, Yelena holding her eyes for a long moment.

    “See you later, Kate.”

    “Bye, Kate. See you later!”

    She hums, before smiling back.

    “Thanks, again.”

    The doors close behind them, and Kate lets the smile fall, leaning back against the metal wall of the elevator, closing her eyes. Mentally, she is exhausted and drained, but there is an unsettling restlessness in her muscles that she yearns to work out somehow. Trying to focus on her present, instead of the huge amount of unpleasant information she has learned today, Kate tries to make plans for how to spend the rest of her day. It's already close to 6 pm, by the time she walks from the elevator to her front door, getting her keys out of her gym bag. As she opens the door, Lucky comes bounding out of her bedroom, a stuffed duck dangling from his mouth and tail wagging wildly.

    Taking him out is priority number one, as he has been cooped up all day, so after Kate receives his greeting kisses and headbutts against her thigh, she deposits her gym bag on the table by the door and quickly walks to her bedroom to change her loose workout shorts to a pair of leggings and a light jacket, more appropriate for the chilly weather outside. In 5 minutes, she has put some running shoes on, and Lucky and she are in the elevator again, making their way to the ground floor. Kate knows their time outside is extremely limited, the assassin problem still not solved, but even the 25 minutes they get to be outside feels freeing. Lucky is a less-than-stellar jogging mate though, trying to stop by to sniff things even after Kate lets him do his business, so after about 5 minutes of trying, she gives up on running. Instead, the two of them walk around the neighborhood, while Kate mulls over everything she has learned today. For now, she decides to not think about the formula, and the threat it poses for people in general, and specifically her. Instead, she thinks about her mother. Seeing her, and getting to talk to her after almost two years has rolled a weight off of Kate’s shoulders that she has long pretended was not there. Learning that she has kept away from Kate, and refused to speak with her due to a kind of misguided attempt to keep her safe, instead of hating her or something, had a similar effect. A new weight, different, but no less heavy has taken its place though.

    Knowing that her mother was in jail was one thing.

    Seeing her, seeing its effects, and now actively worrying about her safety was a completely different affair. As long as Kate could remember, her mother has been elegant, poised, almost larger than life. Seeing her beaten, thin, and growing old was harder than Kate could have ever imagined.

    Of course, parents growing older, and kids learning that their parents are human too is a natural part of growing up. She knows that. But her mother, the shining star of New York socialite circles, CEO of a billion-dollar company, who even wore her widow-hood with grace and dignity becoming this shell of a woman…

    Kate can never regret doing the right thing and getting her arrested for what she has done. That doesn’t mean she can’t also feel guilty about her part in it.

    By the time Lucky and Kate make it back to her building about 35 minutes later, she is kind of embarrassed to admit to herself that she paid almost no attention to her surroundings and can only hope that they weren’t followed, but also can’t really get herself to care. Lucky looks happy at least, his tongue lolling out of the side of his mouth, and he happily devours the dinner Kate puts out for him, once they make it back to her apartment. The walk was nice but it did not get rid of the wired, unsettled energy in Kate. Once Lucky is settled in his food coma following his dinner, Kate opens the secret entryway to her Utility Room and brings out an archery target and a quiver full of regular arrows. Since her move back to New York, Kate hasn’t had the time or opportunity to practice, and she spends a few minutes finding the ideal setup to maximize the distance between her target, and her shooting position.

    At her place in LA, she had the opportunity to set up a proper shooting range on the roof of her house, but here that is unfortunately not a possibility. Instead, she puts the target on top of the wardrobe in one corner of her living room and takes position at the far end of her bedroom.

    Pulling out one arrow from her quiver, and going through the motions of nocking, pulling back the string, letting muscle memory guide her instead of actively aiming, then releasing the string has the almost immediate meditative effect that made Kate fall in love with archery in the first place. The thunk of the arrow embedding itself in the target has her muscles loosening like nothing else in the world. Her thoughts, her problems, and the wired energy all fall away. Nothing remains but her bow, her arrows, and the target.

    Arrow after arrow, she shoots into the target, and in about five minutes, she has emptied the quiver completely and the red square in the middle of the foam is barely visible, covered by the purple and green fletching of her arrows.

    She retrieves the arrows and empties her quiver nine more times after, her head blissfully empty of thoughts, emotions, or the swirling uneasiness caused by the events of the day. The muscles of her back are pleasantly sore and only when her stomach audibly grumbles, does Kate remember that she hasn’t eaten anything since breakfast.

    Checking her phone, Kate sees that it’s almost 8 pm, and decides to call it a day. Not bothering to take down the target, for now, she puts the bow on the coffee table and tries to decide whether she should eat or shower first.

    Her sweat-drenched muscle tee wins out, and Kate is in and out of the shower, hair freshly washed in 15 minutes, in a comfortable pair of light purple matching sweatpants and a sweatshirt, and a faded, super soft t-shirt.

    Her fridge is empty, except for some raw ingredients that would mean a lot more effort to turn into something edible than Kate is willing to invest right now, and she is way too hungry to wait for delivery right now, so Kate goes for a trusty boxed mac & cheese from the cupboard.

    In barely 10 minutes, her dinner is ready, which also marks the exact moment Lucky decides his nap was long enough, showing up with a sleepy dog face and a big stretch that makes Kate smile despite the heaviness she still feels on her shoulders. As she takes her seat by the kitchen island, he sits down next to her chair as well, his soft head coming to rest in Kate’s lap.

    She only gets to eat about ten bites (also feeding Lucky one piece of cheesy pasta), before his head suddenly snaps towards the door and not even three seconds later, there are knocks on her door.

    Kate sighs, really not in the mood for whatever it is.

    If somebody followed her home, she has no energy to fight and beat them back right now. And if it’s Yelena and Sonya, she is really not in the mood to work or to socialize. The latter, it being the two Widows at her door, is still obviously the better option, which thankfully ends up being the case, as a few moments later Sonya’s voice calls out through the door.

    “Open up, Kate!”

    The call is followed by several other knocks and Kate sighs deeply, remembering that Yelena has a key so she can’t just pretend to be asleep or something. Pizza Dog left with wide swishes of his tail as soon as the knocks started and with a barely stifled groan more fitting for a 50-year-old man than a 24-year-old woman, Kate gets off of her seat, walking up to her front door too.

    Hopefully, Yelena and Sonya will understand that she is not in the mood and just needs to mope a little, before she can be productive again. It’s exactly what she plans to tell them, as she swings the door open, and it’s exactly what she never gets to say.

    As soon as the door opens, Yelena and Sonya march in, as if on a mission. “Come on, Kate. We have let you mope long enough.”

    Sonya looks her up and down as she walks by her, a paper bag in her arms clinking suspiciously, and nods to herself, satisfied after her assessment.

    “Um, hi.”

    That’s all she gets to say, before Sonya is gone, walking towards her kitchen with the bag full of what Kate assumes are several bottles of booze. Yelena stops in front of her, and as it seems to be the case anytime she sees her now, Kate can’t help but notice how good she looks in her tucked-in light yellow polo shirt, and loose jeans, even if she has pretty much mixed feelings about the Widows invading her apartment like this in the first place. “We are having girl’s night.”

    It’s said with such seriousness, Kate can’t help but smile which is probably exactly what was Yelena going for, because a moment later she grins at Kate, almost playfully. “Are you going to insult my cutlery and then vaguely threaten me?

    Yelena’s grin widens at Kate’s words, her nose scrunching up with it.

    “Maybe. It depends on whether you are going to throw hot sauce at my head.” Kate huffs in amusement, involuntarily returning Yelena’s grin with a smile of her own. After a second, however, she wets her lips and speaks again.

    “Listen, that sounds great, it really does, but I don’t think I’m gonna be very good company tonight. Maybe we could do this tomor-“ “Good thing I’m good company enough for the three of us.”

    Sonya breezes by her as she says that, a bucket full of ice and a bottle of what Kate would bet is a bottle of vodka in her arms. Kate exhales through her nose again, her smile not weaning even as she pushes back. She is touched, truly.

    “While I’m sure that’s true, I really don’t know if I can be good company back right now.” Her eyes follow Sonya as she sets down her items on the coffee table, picking out four shot glasses Kate has previously missed from the bucket of ice. Then, her gaze is pulled to Yelena again, finding her eyes searching Kate’s face.

    “If you really do not want us here, we will go. But, we can talk about it, we can not talk about it. We can simply just drink about it. But you do not have to be alone.” At Yelena’s unexpected sincerity Kate’s stomach flips in a tired, yet unmistakably affectionate way. She doesn’t have to be alone. With the physically wired energy worked out of her system, Kate feels mostly drained, but if she is honest with herself, if she were to be alone, she would probably just mope and drink anyway, only without the amazingly distracting presence of her friends.

    With her decision made, she puts a smile on her face, glancing at Sonya, then back at Yelena. “Alright. But um, full disclosure, I didn’t make enough mac and cheese for everyone. Sorry.” Sonya scoffs, stepping up to Kate’s side, and patting her back.

    “We already ate anyway. We brought you leftovers also, because we figured you’d forget to eat. And of course, it would be a tragedy for you to miss out on my Chicken Paprikash. But you can have it for lunch tomorrow, it is not a problem.”

    For an insane moment, Kate thinks she is going to well up, at the simple gesture of them even thinking about when or what she is going to eat. It’s probably at least partially due to the emotionally charged day she had, but thankfully, maybe sensing her mood, Sonya grips her forearm, leaning closer with a smirk and eyebrows lifted in challenge.

    “Now. Let us teach you how to drink.”

    Kate chuckles, her emotional moment not gone, but thankfully diverted.

    “I do know how to drink, Sonya. I went to college.”

    “Bah!”

    Sonya shakes her head unashamedly, like even the notion is ridiculous and even Yelena seems unconvinced, looking back at Kate with a smug glint in her perfectly lined eyes and a teasing smile in the corners of her parted lips.

    “Maybe so. But you are American.”
