    Kate shakes her head with a small, affectionate smile too, and follows Yelena to her couch. Lucky is sniffing at the container Sonya took out of her big bag, and Yelena shoos him away with a few gently muttered Russian words and a soft pat on his head.

    “Is that vodka?”

    Kate asks as Sonya twists off the red cap of the bottle, pouring the seethrough liquid into three shot glasses, while Yelena and her take their seats on the couch. “It’s Stoli.”

    Yelena answers her, picking up two of the shot glasses from the coffee table, and passing one to Kate. Sniffing at it, one of Kate’s eyebrows lifts as she looks back at Yelena above the rim of her glass.

    “It smells like vodka.”

    Yelena’s plushy lips stretch into a smile, and she holds Kate’s gaze with mirth in her own. “Stoli is vodka. The best vodka.”

    A moment later, her eyes shift to Sonya, lifting her glass.

    “Na zdaróvye.”

    Sonya echoes her words, lifting up her glass, as does Kate but she remains silent. Yelena and Sonya are looking at her though, with pointed eyes and not-so-subtly teasing looks on their faces. So, with a small roll of her eyes, Kate attempts to repeat the words. “Na doro-vye?”

    It comes out sort of like a question, but Sonya and Yelena clink their glasses against hers with matching grins. Yelena lifts her chin as their eyes meet, grin tempered into a smile. “That was not bad.”

    “It wasn’t?”

    Kate feels uncertain, her Duolingo lessons still lightyears away from being able to say basically anything correctly. Yelena’s smile widens, her teeth glinting white between her lips. “Yes. There is a z though, Na zda-róvye.”

    Kate’s eyes drop to her lips, following their movement to learn the word. “Na-“ Yelena nods, and Kate’s eyes lift to meet hers.

    “-zdorovye.”

    Yelena blinks slowly, her smile stretching even wider again.

    “Yes. Kind of like that.”

    They all down their shots then, the liquid burning Kate’s throat as it makes its way down. She doesn’t give Yelena and Sonya the satisfaction of flinching, however, smacking her lips after as both of them watch her face intently to catch her reaction. After a moment, she leans back, pursing her lips.

    “What, I told you. I know how to take a shot.”

    They grin in unison, and Kate is somewhat alarmed to see that Sonya is already pouring out the next round. Glancing at Yelena, she finds her looking still and decides to go for her pride and keep up her bluff. Reaching for the glass, she takes initiative, raising it and glancing at Sonya, before focusing on Yelena.

    “Na zdorovye. Cheers.”

    They echo her words, probably saying the expression properly, as opposed to her, and Yelena holds her eyes as they both down their shots. This time, Kate can’t tamp down the slight flinch and Yelena huffs in amusement, but to Kate’s surprise, doesn’t chase the score she could win right now, looking away instead with a small smile, that Kate can’t help but mirror. After a second, Kate turns to Sonya who has been uncharacteristically quiet for the last couple of minutes.

    “Who is the fourth glass for? Tommy?”

    With a smile, she nods, reaching over to check her phone.

    “Yes, he should be here any minute. We did not have chasers at home, so he went to the bodega to get some.”

    Gesturing to the kitchen behind Sonya, Kate asks both of them.

    “I have beers, and like, some kind of soda, I think. And orange juice, maybe?” Sonya leans back on both hands, for once being the one to be seated on the floor across, smiling up at Kate. She is in jeans and a t-shirt too, hugging her curves closely. “Do you have tomato juice?”

    Face scrunching up in disgust, Kate leans back against the couch.

    “No. Ew. Why would I have that?”

    Sonya blinks at her slowly, amused as she shrugs.

    “I woke up craving a Bloody Mary.”

    Kate shakes her head, glancing at Yelena to see if her disgust is mirrored, but only finding amusement.

    “Yeah, no. I don’t have tomato juice.”

    “What about celery juice?”

    Sonya has to be fucking with her on that one, grin wide, perfect white teeth all on display. “If I ever have that ready to go in my house, you have my permission to mercy kill me.” Both of them laugh at that, Sonya shaking her head with a grin, and Yelena speaking, as she leans forward to pour them all another shot.

    “And you call me dramatic.”

    Kate lifts one eyebrow, as if to say, “Am I wrong?”, but doesn’t acknowledge it verbally. Yelena doesn’t either, just mockingly scrunching up her face at Kate.

    “What kind of cocktails do you like then, Kate?“ Sonya asks her, and thankfully neither of them reach for the third round of shots yet. Kate distractedly thinks she should probably finish her mac and cheese before drinking any more but pushes that thought aside to try and answer Sonya’s question. After a moment, she chuckles to herself, remembering a particularly memorable night with Greer and Franny. “Sex on The Beach is good. Porn Star Martinis are even better. Sweeter stuff, I guess.” Sonya chuckles, reaching for the shot glass in front of her, and throwing Yelena a glance before her focus is back on Kate.

    “Oh, I bet. Why are you laughing though?”

    Kate chuckles again, glancing at Yelena too as she does, on the other end of the couch. “Just a silly story from college. Nothing exciting.”

    Both of them look at her expectantly, before Sonya speaks, blinking at her seriously. “Do tell.”

    Kate sighs with a breathy chuckle, before pulling her legs up to the couch, half folding them under herself.

    “Okay, it’s really not that exciting, but uh. So, when my friend Franny turned 21, she was the last to do so out of our like, friend group. And we went to this bar close to campus, and one of the young professors she had a huge crush on was there with his friends. He was like 29 or 30, but she has been crushing on him all semester, so we bet her that she wouldn’t dare to go up to him and offer to buy him a drink.”

    Both women listen to her with rapt attention and Kate chuckles again at the memory of Greer and her hyping Franny up to go shoot her shot, as if she was about to go face a lion. “Anyway, we hype her up, she hypes herself up, and she is already pretty drunk by this point. She goes up to him, and asks if she can buy him a drink. It was pretty obvious that he had no idea who she was, outside of class. You could like, see it on his face that he was trying to place who she was, but couldn’t, so the point is, he said yes.”

    Again, she chuckles into the end of the sentence at the image of the man and Franny at the bar, Franny twirling her hair and batting her eyelashes at the dude.

    “So, they go to the bar. And, we were not close enough to hear them, but we saw them order. And at first, it looked like they were hitting it off, and flirting, and then both the prof and the bartender started to look really confused at what Franny was saying, like dumbfounded.” Next to her, Yelena shifts and distractedly starts patting Lucky, as he jumps up in between them, half crawling into Yelena’s lap.

    “In about three minutes, she came back with a drink, with like, pure horror written on her face, that was beet red. At first, she didn’t want to say what happened but turns out, she wanted to look really grown up, so she wanted to order a Porn Star Martini, which she never had before. What she ended up saying, however, was that she wants to order a Deep Throat Martini.”

    Sonya bursts out cackling at the end of the sentence, and Yelena chuckles too, slightly less so. Kate laughs too, the memory of Franny’s horrified face swimming in front of her. “She was horrified, and embarrassed, and gave me her drink, and I’ve been a fan of Porn Star Martinis ever since and she has been refusing to even try.”

    Kate grins at them both, picking up her shot glass too when the two of them reach for theirs. They all clink their glasses together and take the shot, and Kate has to shake her head to clear it this time, but even Yelena’s face twitches after this one.

    “Did they ever go out after?”

    At Yelena’s question, Kate huffs in amusement, before wetting her lips and shaking her head. “No. She refused to go to his class for a few weeks and got back together with her ex in the meantime.“ Sonya, thankfully not refilling the shot glasses again, leans back instead and looks at Kate thoughtfully for a second.

    “Is that a common thing? People getting back together with their exes?” Blinking, Kate feels the corner of her mouth tilting upwards. Sonya and her questions. Her face begins to feel slightly numb if a little warm.

    “I mean, yeah? I guess. It happens sometimes.”

    Before Sonya can go down this weird line of questioning, a knock interrupts their conversation.

    “This must be Tommy with the chasers.”

    Before Kate can even attempt to move, Sonya is up and at the door. After checking the peephole, she swings the door open and Kate turns away to look at Yelena instead, giving them their privacy to greet each other. Yelena is watching Sonya and Tommy though, with an unreadable expression on her face. It doesn’t look sad, but there is something on her face that Kate can’t exactly name, more serious than amusement for a second.

    It’s gone in a moment, her face morphing into a smile, eyes glinting with affection as Thomas greets them from the doorway, waving slightly despite his arms being full. “Hey, Yelena! Hi, Kate!”

    “Hey!”

    “Hi, Thomas!”

    He is by the coffee table in a second, depositing two plastic bags full of drinks on the table. Lucky doesn’t give up his spot in Yelena’s lap until Tommy pulls out a brand-new chew from one of the bags.

    “Look at this, buddy! Look what you got!”

    Pizza Dog practically leaps across the table to get at the chew and Yelena oofs as he uses her as a take-off pad, but chuckles at his antics affectionately.

    “You shouldn’t just give it to him, Tommy! He has to sit first, like a good boy!” Kate can’t help but smile at Yelena’s words, and Thomas’ eyes jump from Yelena to Kate, and back as he holds up the chew, out of reach of the excited dog.

    “Lucky, sit.”

    He does, tail swishing wildly, thumping against the coffee table’s leg rhythmically. Thomas gives him the chew a few seconds later, and he walks off, taking it to the carpet in Kate’s bedroom as always. Kate’s eyes follow him in there, before they slide to Yelena across from her, finding her already watching. She looks away a second later, eyes sliding over to Thomas, Kate’s following only a moment behind.

    “I got beers, soda, and some snacks. Kate, do you have some bowls?”

    Kate nods, as she gets up, about the make her way to the kitchen. She feels the buzz then, making the world fuzzy around the edges, and has to focus on keeping her balance for a second. She has to eat or risk getting absolutely wasted.

    “Yeah, sure. How many?”

    “I don’t know, like three?”

    “’kay.”

    In the kitchen, Kate gets the bowls and her mac and cheese as well, bringing it all back to the living room. It has grown lukewarm, if not completely cold by now, but it’s still good as Kate digs in while Sonya and Thomas get settled across from her and Yelena.

    Sonya disappears in Kate’s kitchen for a second too, before coming back with a gold cocktail shaker Kate has never seen before.

    “Is that mine?”

    Amused, Sonya nods as she retakes her place on the floor, after stealing a pillow from the sofa to sit on.

    “Yeah.”

    Kate nods to herself, eyebrows lifting for a second in surprise.

    “Huh.”

    As Kate eats, Sonya makes herself a bloody mary in the shaker, while Yelena opts to have just apple juice with her vodka. At Kate’s curious gaze, she just shrugs. “It is called an Apple Pie. Technically, it is a cocktail.”

    Kate holds up her fork in lieu of raising her hands “I didn’t say anything.”

    Yelena purses her lips, glancing down at the bowl in Kate’s lap.

    “You were judging.”

    Kate grins, shaking her head.

    “I wasn’t. I promise.”

    Yelena’s half-serious façade cracks, and she answers, nodding her head toward Kate’s food. “Are you eating all that?”

    Glancing down at her mac and cheese, Kate raises an eyebrow at Yelena as she looks back up at her.

    “Why, you want some?”

    Yelena shuffles closer on the couch.

    “Yes.”

    That’s all she says before she takes the fork from Kate’s grasp and helps herself to a bite of her macaroni.

    “Hmmm.”

    Kate chuckles at her in disbelief, shaking her head.

    “Yes, Yelena, you may share my food.”

    Yelena chews with a smile back, holding her eyes, before swallowing.

    “It is good. But it would be better if it had hot sauce on it.”

    Sighing, Kate rolls her eyes but her smile never drops.

    “Not everything needs hot sauce.”

    “That is objectively wrong.”

    Kate lifts her chin, tilting her head to the side. Yelena just looks back at her with a smile still, before taking another forkful of her food, and turning back to Sonya and Thomas. Kate takes her fork back a few moments later, and finishes the mac and cheese, before depositing her empty bowl on the increasingly overcrowded coffee table.

    “How is your mom Kate?”

    You’d think that Thomas asked Kate to dance naked on the streets, based on the look Yelena and Sonya give him, but Kate just huffs, shaking her head half-amused.

    “She is okay. It was kind of a ploy gone wrong to get me to see her, without Fisk finding out. So, she was injured a little, but nothing too serious, thankfully.”

    Thomas looks surprised, leaning back onto his arms on the floor, eyebrows raised. “Huh. What did she want?”

    Kate sighs deeply, reaching for the fourth shot of vodka in front of her. “For me to do her a favor to help with her plea deal. She uh, she and Fisk worked on this thing that she was going to sell to the government and fuck him over before she was arrested, and apparently, her plea deal hangs on her providing it. So she wants me to get it for her.” Thomas pours himself a glass of whiskey as he listens to her words, raising his glass toward her as she finishes with a sympathetic grimace.

    “Jeez, dude. Cheers, you really do need these drinks.”

    Kate scoffs before raising her glass back at him.

    “That I do, sir. Cheers.”

    The two of them take their shots and Kate feels the weight of both Yelena’s and Sonya’s eyes on her as she does. Thomas continues after a second.

    “Are you going to? Get it for her, I mean.”

    Kate chuckles at Sonya’s less-than-subtle pinch of Thomas’ side at his question, shaking her head at her.

    “It’s fine. We can talk about it. Uh. Yeah. I, uh. I think if it’s really out there, the government having it is still better than the mob having it, I guess. It’s kinda dangerous. So, yeah. I might as well kill two birds with one stone. Help her, and keep it from Fisk.” Thomas nods at her words, before taking another sip with a shake of his head. “It’s really no surprise your mom and my dad always got along, huh. Pragmatic to a fault, both of them.”

    Kate huffs out in amusement, looking back at him.

    “Yeah. Cut from the same cloth.”

    “Is your father a criminal too?”

    Yelena asks Thomas, and Kate turns to look at her with a chuckle that never makes it past her lips. The question is hilariously blunt, but Kate is immediately distracted by looking at her. Yelena’s legs are pulled up onto the couch, her glass held close to her chest, as she looks at Thomas. The sort of dim lighting casts gentle shadows on her face, accentuating her jaw and cheekbones. Her hair, down again and probably freshly washed, falls in loose curls around her shoulders, looking a shade darker now as opposed to the morning light. “Nah, no. He is just…he is a businessman, like Kate’s mother. Very ambitious, very…driven. They kind of moved around in the same circles, and they were… Well, not friends. But friendly acquaintances, I guess. I just meant that I imagine he’d do the same, under the circumstances.”

    Kate nods along to his words, meeting and holding Yelena’s eyes as she turns to face her while Thomas speaks. They are all quiet for a moment, neither of them speaking. Kate feels like they are waiting for her to decide whether she wants to keep talking about this or not. While she thinks she doesn’t actually mind talking about what happened today, all in all, it feels really good to just…let go for an evening. So she leans back, looking from Yelena, at Thomas, then at Sonya.

    “Okay, I have an important question for you.”

    Purposefully keeping her face serious, she waits for Sonya’s nod.

    “Do Russians play drinking games?”

    It takes only a moment for Sonya’s serious face to be overtaken by a wide, playful grin. “We do. But I am not sure you want to play them.”

    Kate turns to Yelena, finds her smiling, and returns it immediately.

    “Try me.”

    At her bold words, Yelena shakes her head with a small grin, looking at Sonya. “You really never think, Kate Bishop.”

    It’s said without a bite, however, and in a moment Yelena’s eyes meet hers again. “Okay, we have one called Russian Roulette.”

    Kate guffaws, head whipping back to Sonya.

    “Okay, wow. Straight to one hundred.”

    Sonya takes a sip of her bloody mary, leaning into Thomas’ side.

    “You know it?”

    “Yeah, you know. Uh, there is a gun with only one bullet in the chamber, passed around and everyone has to pull the trigger. Whoever gets shot, loses, obviously.” Next to her, Yelena starts laughing, rubbing at her face, and across, she hears Sonya laugh too.

    “No, Kate, no. Different game.”

    Turning to look at Yelena, Kate looks at her confused but still amused. “What? What’s Russian Roulette then?”

    Yelena wets her lips by rolling them together, before catching and holding Kate’s eyes as she explains.

    “Okay, you take three shot glasses. Fill them with vodka, water and gin, or some kind of other clear alcohol. You have to drink one, and immediately chase it with another one. You cannot touch or smell the glasses beforehand.”

    Kate huffs in amusement, looking at Sonya for confirmation, then back at Yelena. Thomas pipes up from next to Sonya, his voice laced with amused disbelief that Kate can absolutely relate to.

    “Who wins?”

    Yelena’s grin widens even more as she shrugs at him.

    “Last man standing.”

    Kate laughs to herself, shaking her head.

    “Okay, no. That sounds brutal. Give me another.”

    Yelena and Sonya look at each other, their faces mirror images of mirth. “There is bear paw. Um, The bear has come.-”

    As Sonya starts counting them on her fingers, Kate exchanges an amused glance with Thomas.

    “-Bear stairs. But we need stairs to play that one, so that’s not good. Um,…” Kate starts laughing, and Thomas joins her a second later. Yelena and Sonya are just watching them, until Thomas manages to ask, between giggles.

    “Why…Why so many bear-themed games?”

    Next to Kate, Yelena laughs too, but Sonya huffs, pursing her lips at her boyfriend. “It is an important and cool animal.”

    Kate feels the stitches coming, from laughing even harder. Yelena is shaking her head at Kate with a smile, and Sonya looks at her, before turning back to Thomas.

    “Okay, if your drinking games are so much better, why don’t you teach us some?” Kate is still chuckling to herself, her face hurting a little from laughter. “No no, please. I want to know what bear paw is.”

    Sonya kisses her teeth, leveling her with a look.

    “Well, alright. We take a mug, or a glass full of beer, and hand it around. Every person takes a sip, and then it is immediately filled up to the same level, with vodka. We go in circles until there is only vodka left, then go the other way around.”

    Kate just looks at her in disbelief.

    “I honestly can’t tell if you are serious or not.”

    Sonya just blinks at her, with a smug smile.

    “I am. Yelena’s father taught us that…Actually, he has taught us nearly all of them, now that I think about it.”

    When she looks at Yelena for confirmation, she nods at Kate with an eyebrow raised. “Told you you did not want to play.”

    Kate laughs at her, biting down on her lip as she nods back at Yelena.

    “I’m going to admit when I’m wrong. These sound deadly.”

    Yelena purses her lips at Kate smugly, and Kate can’t help but look down at them for a second, before meeting her eyes again.

    “Okay, so what about you? You both went to college, yes? What games did you play there?” Kate is amused to realize that the tipsier she gets, the stronger Sonya’s Russian accent becomes, which had been pretty much undetectable until now.

    “We do know spin the bottle.”

    Yelena supplies from the side, and Kate scoffs to herself.

    “Hope your dad didn’t teach you guys that one.”

    Her words are met with a confused look from Yelena.

    “But he did. Why?”

    Just blinking back at her for a second, Kate doesn’t know what to say.

    “Um, what?”

    “Spin the bottle. Alexei taught us that too.”

    Glancing at Thomas across the table to see if her bewilderment is mirrored on his face, Kate is thankful to note that it is.

    “Can you tell us the rules?”

    Thanking all the gods and other higher entities that Thomas’ brain seems to function better than her own, Kate turns back to Yelena to hear her answer.

    “Sure. You put a vodka bottle in the middle and spin it. Whoever it lands on, has to take a sip, then they get to spin. And so it goes.”

    “Oh, thank god.”

    Kate exclaims with a laugh, exchanging an amused glance with Thomas but a moment later she looks at Yelena again, finding her looking back with a very smug smile. Grinning, Kate shakes her head.

    “You knew what I meant, didn’t you?”

    Yelena blinks slowly, her smile stretching into a grin and she leans further back into the couch comfortably.

    “Maybe.”

    “Agh.”

    Kate shakes her head, finding Sonya and Thomas sharing their amusement. “Okay, I was serious. American drinking games, go.”

    Thomas and her look at each other and Kate lifts her chin, indicating he goes first. “Okaay. Um, there is beer pong? Drunk Jenga, Quarters. Um…”

    As he pauses to think, Kate begins adding her own to the list.

    “Truth or drink. 20 questions. Um, King’s Cup. Buffalo King.”

    Kate tries to think of more and after a moment, Thomas continues in her stead. “Never Have I Ever, Power Hour.”

    As Thomas speaks, Kate looks at Sonya first, then at Yelena. She is smiling, eyes shining with amusement as Sonya and her exchange a glance, silently communicating. It seems affectionate and playful, and after a second, Yelena shrugs, before turning to look at Kate. “Oh! I have one more. Babe, you are going to love this. Two truths and a lie. Kate, do you know it?”

    Tearing her gaze away from Yelena, Kate nods at Thomas.

    “Yeah, we used to play it in the first year of college all the time.”

    Yelena finishes her drink next to her and leans forward to put her glass on the table. “What is it? I do not know that one.”

    Thomas, already in game master mode, leans forward to explain.

    “Okay, so. You make three statements about yourself, two that are true, and one that is a lie. And we have to figure out, which one is a lie. If we do, you drink, if we don’t, everyone drinks except you.”

    Yelena turns her head to the side, regarding him.

    “But how do you know if I am telling the truth?”

    Kate smiles, joining in.

    “That’s the point of the game. To figure it out.”

    “Ah.”

    “You want to play?”

    Thomas speaks to Sonya first, but he looks at Kate in a moment, then Yelena too. “Sure.”

    “Okay. Who goes first?”

    Kate leans forward, reaching for one of the bigger glasses Sonya has brought from the kitchen.

    “One sec, I need a drink first.”

    Already having done four shots of vodka, Kate decides to stick to that as a base, but switch to long drinks, in hopes of avoiding a horrible hangover tomorrow.

    “Good call.”

    Thomas empties his glass, before pouring himself another glass of whisky, and filling up Sonya’s Bloody Mary from the shaker. Kate looks at Yelena, gesturing at the table. “What are you drinking? Apple Pie again?”

    She nods, emptying her glass too, and handing it to Kate.

    “Yes, thank you.”

    Kate decides to give it a try as well, pouring each of them what looks approximately like a shot of vodka, and filling the glass with apple juice. Handing the glass back to Yelena, their fingers touch, and Kate can’t help but smile at her, which Yelena returns easily. For a moment, Kate remembers the rift between them in the last few days and feels really happy to be back on good terms. She also can’t help but notice how pretty Yelena is, her eyes shining a bit tipsily too, and a lazy smile on her lips.

    “Okay. Kate, you wanna go first?”

    Torn away from Yelena’s gaze again, Kate twists back around to look at Thomas. “What? Oh. Yeah, sure. Um, one sec.”

    The drinks must be working in her system because her brain begins to feel just a little bit sluggish.

    “Okay. Okay, here we go. Uuuum. One, I don’t have any tattoos. Two, I’ve never been arrested. And um, three. I played the cello growing up.

    She looks around the room, trying to gauge if the statements were good. She didn’t want to make it too challenging in the first round, but her competitive nature doesn’t let her just concede the round right off the bat.

    “I saw her naked, and she definitely doesn’t have tattoos, so that is true.” Sonya starts thinking out loud and Kate can feel the blush begin to rise on her face, especially when Sonya takes the time to grin at Yelena who just rolls her eyes at her answer. She looks at Kate then, specifically her hands.

    “You have very long fingers, huh.”

    She grins at that too, and Kate already regrets both her statements and playing this game with Sonya as she grins at Yelena about that too, even waggles her eyebrows, who chuckles this time, with a shake of her head.

    “So, I think the cello is true too. Which makes the arrest the lie, yes?” Kate wets her lips, looking at Thomas first, who nods with a face that says “can’t argue with that”, and Yelena whom she catches looking at her hands after Sonya’s statement, and who looks at her with narrowed eyes after.

    “Hm. Yes, I agree… Also, she was arrested twice, one for breaking and entering at her college, and once for drunk and disorderly in 2025 January.”

    Gaping at Yelena, Kate is rendered speechless. In a moment, she gathers her brain, shaking her head with a grin.

    “Why do you know that?”

    Yelena grins back, shrugging.

    “Research.”

    Kate purses her lips, blinking at her slowly.

    “Stalking, more like.”

    Yelena shakes her head with a smile, turning back to Thomas.

    “So, what happens now?”

    “Well, Kate drinks her drink, and we are onto the next person. Which iiiis. Sonya? It’s your turn.”

    Kate takes three sips of her drink, while Sonya thinks about her statements. From the corner of her eyes, Kate sees Yelena pull out her phone, and smile at something she sees on it. Wondering what could be making her smile like that, Kate shuffles closer unconsciously, but the phone is slid back into Yelena’s pocket a second later.

    “Okay, I have it!”

    Sonya draws her attention away and to herself, sitting up straighter to give her two truths and one lie.

    “First, I have never been to Boston. Second, I never had a threesome. And third. I never went to college.”

    She looks around, meeting all of their eyes, with a grin. Kate narrows her eyes slightly, first of all, suspicious that Sonya might not be as new to this game as both Widows made themselves out to be. Also, unsure which one is a lie of the first two, as Kate is pretty confident in her notion that Sonya never went to college, with her Red Room upbringing that is.

    “Well, we haven’t been to Boston together. Has she gone there with you, Yelena?” Yelena shakes her head, her eyes glinting with amusement.

    “No. And I think she’d have bragged if she did have a threesome before too, so I’d cross that off also.”

    Thomas chuckles, nodding before his eyebrows furrow.

    “But I’m pretty sure she didn’t go to college though. I mean, you never mentioned it?” He turns to look at Sonya, who only shrugs with a smile, before grinning again. “Kate, what do you think?”

    Kate looks at Sonya’s grin, trying to find some kind of logic to follow. “I mean, the Boston one is pretty specific. You guys would know better than me about the threesome, but yeah. It does sound like it’s something she would mention. So that would be true. About college, that’s something she’d mention too, at least to one of you, right? So. If it’s up to me, I’d choose Boston as the lie.”

    Looking at Yelena, she nods with a shrug too, and Thomas only looks at Sonya suspiciously for a few seconds longer, before conceding.

    “Boston it is.”

    Sonya’s grin widens, and she lifts her chin to gesture at the glass in Thomas’ hand. “Drink up, losers.”

    Thomas gapes and Yelena’s eyebrows shoot up on her forehead, as Kate laughs. “Who did you have a threesome with?!”

    Thomas asks, laughing as he takes a sip and Sonya almost downright cackles in his face. “Does it mean he has to drink twice if he guesses wrong two times?”

    The question is directed at Kate this time, at Thomas’ expense. At this, Yelena’s eyes widen even more as she drinks next to Kate.

    “You went to college? What for?”

    It’s Yelena who asks Sonya, and her grin is tempered into a lazy smile as she answers. “Journalism and Mass Communications. I did it after you were Blipped, between assignments. Before I met you.”

    The last part is directed ad Thomas who nods, blinking, still surprised at the information just learned.

    “How come you never mentioned it?”

    As he asks Sonya, her smile changes, and for a moment, Kate can see how smitten she is with him.

    “I never use it. What is the point?”

    Thomas smiles at her, before leaning over to peck her on the lips.

    “Still would have liked to know.”

    Kate looks away, suddenly feeling like she is intruding on their moment again. Across from her, Yelena looks thoughtful but as she meets Kate’s eyes, she just smiles again. She shuffles closer a moment later, whispering loudly on purpose, Kate guesses.

    “I still think it was the threesome.”

    Kate chuckles, holding her eyes and across from them, Sonya’s musical laugh is heard again too.

    “Do not worry, Yelena. You will definitely know when that happens.”

    Yelena huffs, grinning back at her friend and shaking her head.

    “I really don’t have to.”

    “But you will.”

    Yelena sighs theatrically, turning to Kate to share a look with her and Kate bites down on her lower lip to stifle her smile. Kate sees the way Yelena’s eyes drop to watch the movement before she turns back toward the other side of the table.

    “It is now Thomas’ turn, yes?”

    Thomas, who now has one of his arms around Sonya’s shoulder nods with a smile, taking a sip of his whisky as he thinks.

    “Alright. One, I was my school’s valedictorian. Two, I know how to juggle. I had sex on an airplane once.”

    Kate chuckles and tries to read his face as he speaks. He is a better liar than she’d expect, and none of the claims jump out as outright lies for sure. At the last sentence, Sonya’s jaw drops and she playfully slaps his thigh next to hers.

    “You man-whore! How could you?”

    All of them laugh at Sonya’s words, and this time it’s Yelena who speaks first. “I believe the valedictorian. You are nerdy enough.”

    Sonya nods, messing up Thomas’ hair affectionately. Kate watches with a smile before she joins in.

    “I believe the plane. It’s specific. What do you think, Sonya?”

    “I believe the plane too. I will have questions after, but I believe it.” Thomas chuckles at her words, before asking back.

    “So, you think I’m lying about juggling?”

    Sonya nods, a teasing glint in her eyes as she grins back at him.

    “Yes. Not enough coordination.”

    He pretends to be wounded, a hand coming up to his chest before he laughs. “Bottoms up, ladies. You have way too much trust in my game, and way too little in my coordination.”

    He pecks the side of Sonya’s head as she chuckles, and Kate takes a sip of her drink, glancing at Yelena to the side as she does too. She flips her hair behind herself, a smug smile sliding onto her face as she looks them over since it’s her turn next.

    “Okay. One, I hated green beans as a child. Two, I never had sex in an elevator. Three, I never had a massage before.

    She raises an eyebrow at Kate as she finishes with a smile before her gaze slides over to Sonya and Thomas on the other side of the coffee table. Sonya holds Yelena’s eyes, the two of them visibly engaged in some kind of battle of wills or something.

    “Sonya?”

    Kate asks her with a grin, hoping that she would shine light on some of the questions, or at least the sex-related one, as Yelena’s best friend. They look at each other for a few seconds longer, before Sonya lifts her chin and begins to smile.

    “The sex in the elevator one is true.”

    Kate glances between the two Widows, trying to gauge the silent conversation that just went down before her tipsy brain tells her to not don’t bother. With a shake of her head, Kate smiles again, before speaking.

    “I don’t know if I have seen you eat green beans before or not.”

    Yelena shrugs only, smiling mysteriously and Thomas joins in.

    “Well, even if we did, she might have hated them as a kid. I know I did.” Kate hums in agreement but Sonya shakes her head.

    “I definitely know she likes green beans now.”

    “Yeah, but did she hate them as a kid? You know her the longest.”

    Sonya hums thoughtfully, her eyebrows drawn together.

    “We met when I was ten, Yelena was eleven. But both of us knew to eat the food we were given without complaint by then, so I have no idea.”

    The mention of Yelena’s and Sonya’s childhood, or the lack of it throws a shadow over Kate’s joyful mood for a second, but Sonya and Yelena don’t seem to share it. Yelena smiles smugly at Sonya, apparently proud of herself to be able to think of something she wouldn’t be able to answer either, so Kate tries to push the sad thought aside as well. “It has to be never having had a massage, right? I mean. That’s pretty unlikely.” Thomas looks from Sonya to Kate and then back, and Sonya shrugs.

    “It is not that unlikely. I never had them until we were free. But it’s been a long while since then. So yeah, that’s my choice as well.”

    Kate attempts to read Yelena’s face, but of course, it’s impossible. She only smiles at Kate, her eyes half-lidded, from tipsiness Kate guesses.

    “Yeah, okay. Let’s go with the massage.”

    Yelena blinks, before wetting her lips.

    “Final answer?”

    They all look at each other, nodding before Kate solidifies it.

    “Yes.”

    The grin that spreads over Yelena’s face makes Kate groan, reaching for her glass before Yelena even speaks.

    “Bottoms up! I win!”

    Kate empties her glass, before looking back at Yelena, eyes focused on her beautiful smile for a second before she asks.

    “Which one was the lie?”

    Yelena’s tongue peeks out to wet her lips before she smiles smugly again. “For your information, green beans have been, and always will be my favorite vegetable.” Kate nods with a smile of her own, storing the information for later, along with the fact that Yelena has never had a massage before, and never had sex in an elevator before. What she will do with that, she has no idea, but it can never hurt to know these things about one's friends, right?

    “Noted.”

    “You haven’t had a massage? Ever??”

    Thomas seems baffled still, and Yelena's smug smile widens into a toothy grin as she turns to him. Kate tries not to be mesmerized.

    “Nope.”

    They play a few more rounds of the game, learning small, but interesting details about each other. Things, like how the last time Thomas cried at a movie was at the end of The Lord of The Rings, when he rewatched it last Christmas, that he wants a chocolate Labrador one day, and call him Oliver, Ollie for short. And that he has never been to Disney Land. That the one food Sonya refuses to even try, is octopus, because it freaks her out, and that her favorite place to visit was Puerto Princesa in the Philipines last year with Thomas. She also reveals that she has never been to a nude beach, but she wants to go.

    About Yelena, Kate learns that the first injury she remembers having was breaking her arm while learning to ride the bike. That she wanted to be a dancer as a little kid, and that she has never been shot before, but had been stabbed on three different occasions. She also learns, that her favorite modern book is The Midwife by Tricia Cresswell, which Kate doesn’t know, but makes a mental note to read when she has the time, and that her favorite It’s also revealed that neither Sonya, nor Yelena has ever smoked weed before, which Thomas and Kate both agree has to be rectified, and make plans to do so sometime soon. After a few more rounds, however, Sonya deems them all too drunk to play a drinking game, so at Kate’s suggestion, they decide to play darts.

    “Are we playing as teams or individuals?”

    At Kate’s question, Yelena looks back at her smugly, her eyes giving away her tipsiness, even if her words are not slurred, not even a little.

    “Playing one on one would not really be fair to Tommy…or you.”

    Eyebrows rising into her hairline, Kate straight up laughs in her face. “You mean not fair to you, right? You do know I am one of the best archers in the world, right?”

    Yelena just tuts at her condescendingly, before getting off the couch after Kate with no stumble in her steps, and a challenging glint in her eyes that immediately sets Kate on fire. Oh, she is on.

    “Oh my god. What did we start?”

    Sonya leans back against Thomas’ chest, sitting between his open legs as she has been for the last thirty minutes.

    “Is it too late to back off?”

    She calls out again, but without waiting for an answer, she begins to get up, before holding out her hand for Tommy to take. He does, and the two of them join Kate and Yelena who are busy setting up the area where they will be playing.

    Kate measures 10 steps from the board on the wall and lays down a long piece of tape from which they will have to take aim. She hands out different colored darts for everyone, red for Sonya, blue for Tommy, green for Yelena, and keeps the lucky purple ones for herself. “Who wants to start?”

    “How is this played again?”

    Sonya asks her, and Kate turns back to them, taking note of his arms circling her from behind. Clearing her throat, Kate explains the rules.

    “Okay, normally, we play 301 or 501, but to keep it simple, we will just play for the most points out of three shots, three times. So, we each have three darts and we will play three rounds, okay? The person who gets the most points wins.”

    Sonya’s eyes are a little glassy as she looks back at her and she giggles a little before she asks again.

    “Okay. Um, how are the points calculated?”

    Kate grins, more sure of her imminent victory by the second.

    “Right. The little inner circle, the bullseye, is 50 points, and the one around that is 25. Other than that, you see those numbers around the board? If your darts land in the section of the board with a number, that’s how many points you get. Unless you manage to get it into those thin rings around the board and in the middle of the outer sections. The biggest ring doubles your points, the one in the middle of the big section triples them. Yeah?” Sonya looks unsure, her grin becoming a bit dopey, but she nods after a second. “You will get a hang of it as we play.”

    Kate takes out her phone to keep score, and turns to Yelena, gesturing at the taped-up line on the floor.

    “Ladies first.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes, but steps by Kate with a smile a second later, looking down to adjust the toe of her sneaker to the line. Her smile falls away as she turns her focus to the board, holding up the dart expertly. Kate watches her with rapt attention, eyes dropping to follow her tongue peeking out to wet her lips.

    Throwing her first shot, it lands in the second to innermost circle, earning her 25 points. The second one lands in the middle, earning her 50, as is the third. All in all, Yelena gathers 125 points by the end of the first round.

    Next, it’s Sonya, shooting two into the second innermost circle, gathering 50 points, and one slightly to the left of that, earning her another 14, bringing her total to 64. Kate also gets the sense, that out of the four of them, Sonya is the drunkest. She pouts at her score, before turning around with a loopy grin.

    “If I get 69, we are leaving. Then I win.”

    Kate laughs at her words, Thomas laughs before pulling Sonya in for a kiss and Yelena shakes her head with a grin.

    Thomas puts up a valiant fight, throwing one into the second innermost one, getting a 25 and two into the 19, and 20 respectively, but neither into the bonus giving thin circles, bringing him right up to Sonya’s level.

    “Babee! We match!”

    Sonya rewards him with a long kiss that Yelena raises her eyebrows at amusedly before turning to Kate.

    “Let’s see what you can do, Hawkeye.”

    It’s sad mockingly, giving Kate a playful once over and after that, she has no choice, really, but to show off a little.

    Dart after dart, Kate throws all three into the innermost middle circle, gaining 150 points in one round. Kate turns around with a cocky smile, shrugging at her.

    “Told ya.”

    Yelena purses her lips, eyes glinting dangerously, and Kate knows that they are on now. For the next 25 minutes, Kate and Yelena play, while Sonya and Thomas are partaking, but are mostly paying attention to each other, slinking back toward the couch between rounds and talking to each other in hushed tones, sometimes giggling.

    While she is mostly preoccupied with defeating Yelena, Kate actually finds it cute. They have been dating for almost two years, yet they clearly only think about each other. Yelena throws them a couple of glances too, but mostly, her attention is annoying Kate into messing up. “I bet you can’t get into the triple ring.”

    Kate is in the lead, before going on for the third time. Yelena threw a perfect round after her first one, then another 125 points, taking her up to 400 points from all three rounds. Kate has 300 points, having done 150 on both her rounds so far, and if she can just replicate her earlier score, she got this in the bag.

    Glancing at Yelena, she sees the competitive edge in her eye, but there is something else too. She is definitely tipsy, maybe drunk even, and there is a heat behind her eyes that Kate has seen before, but not like this.

    “Bet me what?”

    Yelena’s smile is slow, catlike eyes glancing down at Kate’s lips for a second. “What do you want?”

    Yelena’s tone drops an octave and Kate is pulled in, like a moth to a flame but the last tiny, sober part of her brain Knows what this is. This is Yelena playing with her food. Kate decides to play right back. Stepping closer, she is almost in Yelena’s space now, eyes never leaving Yelena’s as she looks up at Kate, head tilted back.

    “What I want…”

    Kate lets herself look Yelena’s features over, her face glowing in the dimly lit room, green eyes sparkling even behind her half-lidded lashes.

    “Yeah?”

    She is good. Kate is tempted. She is, but not tempted enough to be baited into losing. Leaning even closer, Kate waits a long moment before speaking, her voice dropping too. “Is to win this game.”

    Kate grins then, and it takes Yelena a second to recognize that her bluff has been called. When she does, she grins too, shrugging.

    “It was worth a try.”

    Kate turns away, but not before giving her a once over with a smug smile. “You almost got me.”

    She throws the first dart as she says it, and it lands perfectly in the middle, getting her 50 points. Yelena swears behind her in Russian, and Kate chuckles, throwing her a glance above her shoulder. The next one is a 50 too, landing confidently to the left of the first one. Before she throws the last one, Kate pauses. She regards the purple-fledged dart in her hand, before turning back to Yelena. Whatever she throws, Kate won the game. Maybe it’s time to play with Yelena after all.

    “I’ll take that bet.”

    Yelena’s eyes flash, her smile enticing and smug.

    “Hmm, alright. What do you want?”

    Kate steps closer, trying to think of something.

    “Okay, if I get it into the triple ring, you…you answer one question. Any question. Honestly.” Yelena’s eyebrow rises slowly, her smile widening.

    “What is the question?”

    Kate shrugs, wetting her lips as she holds Yelena’s gaze.

    “I don’t know yet. I will think of one sometime.”

    The enticing smile on Yelena’s lips widens into a grin, eyes boring into Kate’s. “And if you lose?”

    Kate glances at her lips before biting down on her own.

    “Anything you want.”

    Yelena looks back at her, thinking. She is thoughtful only for a few seconds before she speaks with a challenging smirk.

    “If you lose, you lose. All your points are taken, you get zero.”

    Kate laughs then and Yelena does, too. She offers Yelena her hand to shake. “Deal.”

    “Deal.”

    Yelena’s skin is soft against her palm as they clasp their hands, and shake on it. After that, Kate needs a second to get her head back into the game, heart suddenly jumping in unusual patterns at Yelena’s eyes and touch.

    Turning back to the board, she spins the last dart in her hand around, eyes searching for her target.

    “What’s up, Kate? Can not perform under the pressure?”

    Kate smiles at Yelena’s words but doesn’t turn to look at her. She inhales once, then huffs it out through her nose before lifting the dart, and throwing it.

    It lands exactly where she wants it, the triple ring part of the 20 section, raising her final score to 460, securing her victory of both the whole game and her bet with Yelena. Grinning smugly, she spins back towards Yelena.

    “I win!”

    Yelena is looking back at her, biting down on her lower lip but unmistakably smiling too. For a long moment, they just look at each other before she concedes.

    “You win. Well done.”

    Kate glances toward Sonya and Thomas who couldn’t care less about the game, still lost in their bubble on Kate’s couch. She doesn’t feel ready to pop the one she is in, with Yelena. “Rematch? Double or nothing.”

    The words come out of her mouth without thinking, but Yelena is nodding with a grin almost immediately.

    “Okay.”

    Walking up to the board, she takes Kate’s darts out of it before turning back to her. “But I play with the purple darts this time.”

    Kate shakes her head, laughing, stepping towards her as well.

    “Ah-ah, those are my lucky ones!”

    As she steps up to Yelena, she leans against the wall by the board, looking up at Kate smugly. “If you are as good as you think you are, you do not need the lucky ones.” Kate shakes her head, laughing.

    “Come on. Give me.”

    She reaches for the darts in Yelena’s hands but she brings them behind her back, out of Kate’s reach. Not one to be defeated she reaches for them behind Yelena’s hands too, bringing her even closer but of course, Yelena is able to hold them out of her reach. “You being this attached to them makes me think there is something about them.” Without meaning to, Kate ended up right in Yelena’s space. There is only a hair-width space between their bodies, Yelena looking up into her eyes defiantly even if she is the one practically pinned against the wall.

    “What about them?”

    Asking kind of dumbly, Kate can’t say she is not distracted by Yelena’s proximity. She takes a second to answer her too, eyes searching Kate’s face before grinning. “That you are cheating, somehow.”

    The spell is broken, and Kate laughs.

    “You can’t cheat in darts.”

    Shaking her head as she steps back, Kate holds up both hands while also holding Yelena’s gaze as she continues.

    “But you know what? Okay. You play with them, I’ll play with yours.”

    The smile she receives in return is smug and amused before Yelena speaks with her voice dropping an octave as she follows Kate, receding the step of distance Kate put between them again.

    “Yes, Kate. Go ahead. Play with mine.”

    Her façade drops then, and she laughs at Kate’s momentarily dumbfounded face, but she joins Yelena a second later.

    “I’m starting to understand your friendship with Sonya.”

    Yelena’s answering laugh is warm, her eyes crinkling with it. In a moment, however, she gets that calculated look on her face, that lets Kate know that she is about to be fucked with. “How about we make this interesting?”

    Picking up Yelena’s set of green darts from earlier, Kate leans against the wall before she asks.

    “Interesting how?”

    Yelena looks at her for a few seconds, before she wets her lips, stepping closer. “I am thinking, countermeasures. To balance things out. For every bullseye, you drink two shots, for every other score, you drink one.

    Kate laughs at first but stops at the sight of Yelena’s one challenging eyebrow lifted. “You are serious?”

    “Yes.”

    Kate shakes her head, grinning at Yelena.

    “That’s insane.”

    The eyebrow rises even further, and Yelena purses her lips as she tilts her head. “Are you afraid you are going to lose?”

    Kate scoffs, wetting her lips, her own eyebrow furrowing.

    “Yeah. The function in my kidneys!”

    Yelena rolls her eyes, shaking her head in disappointment.

    “Alright, I’m just going to assume you are afraid of losing.”

    Kate gapes at her, as she purses her lips, and turns away.

    “…Big, strong Hawkeye, can’t even aim drunk.”

    Suddenly afraid that their evening is coming to an end, Kate steps after her. “No, wait! Fine!”

    Yelena turns around with a smile and a smug look in her eyes. Kate kisses her teeth but smiles back as she rolls her eyes. She is pretty sure she fell for Yelena’s bluff this time, but whatever. If it keeps them playing…

    “Fine! I’ll do the dumb countermeasures.”

    Yelena grins, head tilted to the side.

    “I know I could count on you…to be silly.”

    Kate huffs at her, but can’t stop herself from playing along.

    “I’m still going to get your ass.”

    The eyebrow lifts again, Yelena’s eyes practically sparkling with her amusement. “We will see.”

    She turns away then, walking back to the couch to get their glasses and the vodka. Kate watches her walk away, taking the opportunity to appreciate said ass.

    “You guys are still playing?”

    Sonya is definitely slurring her words now, speaking from the cocoon of Thomas’ embrace. “Yes. Kate won the first round, we are playing double or nothing now.”

    Sonya grins then, glancing at Kate before burrowing deeper into Thomas’s arms. When she speaks next, it’s in Russian again. Yelena laughs, shaking her head and saying a word that Kate does understand.

    “Nyet…”

    The rest of the sentence is complete gibberish to Kate, who decides to walk back to the center of the living room and the rest of her friends too. Not that it matters, as the next few sentences exchanged are all in Russian, Yelena chuckling at whatever Sonya says with a shamelessly naughty grin. Kate watches Thomas and Sonya instead, huddled together. While she finds them cute, Kate can’t help but feel a little jealous. As the drinks make her thoughts more daring, Kate imagines stepping up behind Yelena and holding her from behind, like Thomas and Sonya have been standing earlier. Her hand twitches by her side, as she imagines what the warmth of Yelena’s body under it would feel if she were to wind her arms around her waist and rest her palms on Yelena’s hips or stomach. How her back would come up to Kate’s front, solid and small, and…

    “Do you speak Spanish?”

    It takes Kate a second to be torn out of her fantasy and realize that Thomas is talking to her. “Huh?”

    “Spanish. Do you speak it? Every time they start talking Russian I have the urge to start speaking another language they don’t understand either.”

    Kate laughs at his words, shifting her weight from one leg to the other. “I’m pretty sure they speak Spanish. They both speak like 14 languages.” Yelena chuckles next to her, and only as she twists her head around to glance at her, does Kate realize how close they are standing. Her thoughts must have unconsciously led her closer because the left side of Kate’s chest is almost touching the back of Yelena’s right shoulder. If Yelena is surprised or bothered by their proximity, she doesn’t let it show. She turns back to Thomas a second later, confirming Kate’s earlier statement. “We do speak Spanish.”

    He purses his lips to one side, looking back at Kate, his eyes unmistakably drunk. “That’s a bummer.”

    Kate just chuckles, before turning to Yelena.

    “You ready?”

    “Yes. Are you two playing?”

    Sonya glances at Thomas, before turning back to shake her head.

    “Actually, I think we are going to call it a night.”

    Yelena nods, before throwing Kate a playful glance.

    “Okay. I’m just going to quickly beat Kate at darts, then I’m coming down too.” Kate laughs at her words, Sonya and Thomas grinning as they stand up.

    “You do not have to hurry.”

    She glances at Thomas, before winking at Yelena who sighs deeply, dramatically blowing out her hair from her eyes but she is smiling back at her friend.

    “Alright. See you tomorrow.”

    Kate walks them to the door, saying her own goodbyes as well.

    “See you tomorrow. Thanks for, um. Coming to cheer me up.”

    Sonya pats Kate’s cheek as she passes her, pausing for a second in the doorway. She glances back at Yelena’s direction, before meeting Kate’s eyes again. She doesn’t say anything, but raises an eyebrow at Kate, obviously telling her something, as she smirks playfully too. In order to not freak herself out, Kate chooses not to try to decipher exactly what the look means, but she is pretty sure what Sonya is saying nonetheless.

    “Goodnight, Tommy.”

    While she did not realize it until now, Thomas is pretty much wasted too, his arm loose around Sonya’s shoulders. He grins at Kate too, a bit loopy as the two of them set off towards the elevator. Kate is unable to tell who is supporting who at this point, but step by step, they are walking away.

    She steps back, closes the door when they get to the elevator in one piece, and takes a deep breath.

    “Can I sleep here tonight?”

    Yelena’s words make Kate’s heart miss a beat before it takes off racing as she locks the door behind her departing friends.

    “What? Uh, oh, yeah. Sure. Of course.”

    While she is aware that Yelena is direct, that one is a bit too direct to mean what Kate thinks it could mean. As Kate turns back towards her, Yelena is leaning against the back of the couch her head tilted to the side, face thoughtful.

    “I would need industrial earplugs to be able to sleep there tonight.”

    Kate chuckles, raising her eyebrows in disbelief.

    “Are they really that loud?”

    Yelena’s eyebrows match hers, but her face reflects confusion for a second before she understands. Then, she laughs, shaking her head.

    “No. No, thankfully not. But Sonya snores like a machine when she is this drunk and she always falls asleep on the couch. I have lost many nights of sleep because of it.” Kate laughs then, the tension of the moment releasing.

    “Yeah, sure. Can’t promise I won’t snore though.”

    Yelena grins before her eyes trail down on Kate’s form, then back up.

    “Believe me, you have nothing on her. You would not think it possible for so much sound to come out of such a small woman.”

    Kate chuckles as she walks up to the coffee table, which looks like a warzone, by the way, to pour herself a glass of juice before they begin their boozy darts match…and whatever comes after. Yelena’s eyes follow her, she can feel it, but she needs just a moment to gather herself. There is an undeniable tension in the air, and Kate would be lying if it didn’t make her skin tingle a little. Or it might be the drinks, it’s a bit hard to tell at this point. “What’s up, Hawkeye? Getting cold feet?”

    Yelena’s voice is just a tiny bit raspy, and Kate wonders if she knows what it does to her. She has to. Then again, after what she pulled earlier, maybe that’s exactly what Yelena is trying to do.

    “Oh, no. Just giving you time to walk away, before it’s too late.”

    Yelena turns around fully to meet her eyes, eyes amused. She rolls her lips together, surely not missing the way Kate’s eyes drop to follow that movement before she chuckles. “Come on, Kate. Show me what you got.”

    The double entendre of the whole conversation is not lost on Kate, and she is pretty sure it’s not lost on Yelena either. Straightening up to her full height, Kate juts her chin toward the darts board and Yelena starts off toward it with a smirk.

    Taking two shot glasses and the vodka with her, she follows Yelena back to where they are playing, putting them on a table by the wall. She gestures at the board while she pours out two shots of vodka.

    “You start.”

    Yelena’s eyes narrow for a second before she nods to herself. Picking up the purple darts from the table where she put them earlier, she walks up to the taped line and prepares to take her shot. In her focus, she gives Kate the perfect opportunity to look at her and take in her striking profile. The strong line of her jaw, the slope of her nose.

    Yelena scores a perfect 50 on the first shot, glancing at Kate triumphantly for a second. She seems to note Kate’s eyes on her with a smug little smile, while she lines up the second shot. She seems to be enjoying Kate watching her, reveling in her attention and Kate stifles a sigh. The second dart goes to 25 and the third one to the 20 section, making Yelena’s final score 95, and the number of shots she has to take to four. She turns to Kate with a proud smile and she returns it with a doubtful grin of her own.

    “Are you ready for this?”

    Yelena lifts her chin and one of her eyebrows.

    “Anytime.”

    She downs the first two shots easily, but despite her daring words, she flinches at the third one and the apprehension is clearly visible on her face after that. Kate chuckles, pulling the fourth one out of reach, behind herself and above her head.

    “You don’t have to do this. You can just admit you were wrong.”

    Yelena tilts her head to the side, her tongue sneaking out to wet her lips. “Is that your way of conceding?”

    Kate huffs out a laugh, handing her the fourth shot after all.

    “Your funeral.”

    Yelena only lifts an eyebrow before she downs the fourth shot, and Kate can see the struggle on her face afterward. She blinks twice slowly, holding onto the table for balance as she purses her lips, slowly exhaling. Amused, she watches as Yelena takes a few deep breaths to gather herself.

    “Your turn.”

    To her credit, Yelena’s voice doesn’t come out strained but she does clear her throat after and quickly goes back to the coffee table to get some juice as well. Meanwhile, Kate tries to think strategy.

    She has to minimize the number of shots she takes while scoring higher than Yelena’s 95 points. The smartest thing to do is to go for the triples, but Kate can tell that she is already quite drunk and doesn’t know if she can actually nail that. Then again, whatever happens, she is only getting drunker from this point, so maybe it makes sense to try and do that now, as opposed to later.

    “Looking at the board isn’t going to help you score.”

    Yelena drawls from behind her and Kate twists around to roll her eyes at her. “Ha-ha. I’m thinking.”

    “More doing, less thinking Kate.”

    Kate smiles at that, blinking slowly at Yelena as she comes up to the side. “That’s like, the exact opposite of what you have been telling me.”

    Yelena purses her lips, tilting her head to the side. Her eyes might as well be gemstones, with the way they sparkle.

    “Sometimes thinking is useless.”

    Lifting an eyebrow at Kate, she bites down on her lip gently and Kate has to think twice whether this is Yelena’s way to fuck with her head again, or an actual nudge to urge her to make a move. She is pretty sure Yelena is just toying with her again, which seems to be the case as a slow, playful but smug smile slides onto her face.

    Shaking her head, Kate turns back toward the board with a grin.

    “Stop fucking with my head.”

    Yelena’s answering snicker makes her stomach flip, but it also helps Kate focus. In a few seconds, she lifts her first dart, aiming for the second innermost circle. It lands there, scoring her 25 points. Next, she decides to go for the triple ring, aiming for the 20-section. This time, however, for the first time since they started playing, Kate misses.

    The dart does go into the triple ring, but instead of the 20 section, it lands a little to the left, earning her three times 5, altogether 15 points. Yelena snickers to her right and Kate huffs, shaking her head.

    “So close, Kate. It is not too late to give up.”

    Ignoring her jaunts, Kate tries to think again. With the amount of alcohol she has consumed though, it’s practically sloshing in her head, making that feat pretty hard. Okay, Kate. You got this. She only has 40 points, with one shot left, compared to Yelena’s 95. She either has to go for the 50, and swallow the extra two shots, or be brave and shoot for triple 20, again. Sighing, Kate steels herself to drinking four shots, aims for the bullseye, and that is exactly where her dart goes. 95 points, 4 shots, just like Yelena.

    As she turns to the side, she finds Yelena smiling, eyes glinting with a slightly drunken gleam.

    “Are you ready to admit defeat?”

    There is a slight slur to her words this time, and Kate shakes her head smiling back at her. “You wish.”

    Yelena clicks her tongue at her, offering her the first shot. Kate steps in, maybe a bit closer than she had planned, and holds her eyes as she takes the glass from Yelena’s hand. With a deep sigh, she steels herself, throwing the vodka back. Whatever face she makes, Yelena laughs at her and Kate has to grab onto the table that Yelena is leaning against to brace herself.

    The second shot feels even worse and for a moment, Kate seriously considers conceding. But she didn’t become who she is by quitting when things get hard. She takes the glass of juice from Yelena’s hand, downing the third shot and immediately chasing it with some apple juice before Yelena can object.

    “Don’t cheat, Kate.”

    The glass is pulled from her grasp, but she doesn’t let go of it which results in her being pulled with the glass, right against Yelena’s front. There is a beat of silence when neither of them speaks and Kate feels the tension of the evening go taunt around them. Yelena is still leaning against the table, with Kate now flush against her front. Her jade eyes are wide, looking up at Kate. She almost looks scared. Kate’s breath hitches for a second, and she wets her lips as she tries to make up her mind on what to do.

    More than anything, she wants to kiss Yelena.

    Push her up against the table, forget about their game of darts and kiss her senseless. After a few moments go by, Yelena makes the decision for both of them, it seems. Kate can see her throat bob, as she swallows first before she leans closer. Yet, with the easy, playful smile she wears, it breaks the moment instead of setting fire to it.

    “You still have one shot left.”

    Kate chuckles, leaning her forehead against the side of Yelena’s head for a second before she reaches by her side for the last shot on the table. Leaning back, she lifts it up, toasting Yelena. “Nazdrobodye”

    Yelena bursts out laughing at what Kate guesses is her botched attempt at Russian, and after she takes her shot, the two of them hold onto each other in their fit of laughter. Yelena hangs onto Kate’s arm like it’s the only thing keeping her upright and Kate stumbles slightly forward, almost falling over Yelena’s foot.

    That takes her even closer to Yelena, practically trapping her against the table, but the moment is no longer charged with the way they are laughing. After a few seconds, as their laughter tapers off into snickers, Kate gestures at the board with her chin. “It’s your turn.”

    Yelena looks at the board too, her face half smushed against Kate’s shoulder, yet clearly showing her apprehension.

    “Blyat.”

    Kate doesn’t know what it means, but her defeated tone is enough to send her into another laughing fit. Putting a hand on the small of Yelena’s back, she gently pushes her towards the taped line on the floor.

    “Remember, this was your idea!”

    Yelena turns slightly back to point at Kate, eyebrows lifted as she speaks seriously, eyes wide.

    “And I am sticking to it.”

    Laughing at her incredulously, Kate leans back against the table and watches her. At this moment, she regrets not kissing Yelena. For weeks she wanted to do it if she is honest with herself, but when the moment came, the look on Yelena’s face gave her a pause. It’s confusing because Kate is pretty certain that Yelena wants it too. The thunk of the first dart landing on the board pulls Kate out of her musings. Glancing at it, she can see that it made its way to the 20 section, but not into the double or triple rings. Yelena closes one eye to aim for the next one, a true indicator of how drunk she is. Of how drunk they both are.

    It lands in the 5 section this time, with no double or triple ring again. The way she mutters to herself, presumably in Russian, makes Kate smile. She really has no business being this cute. For the last shot, Yelena flips her hair out of her eyes, face focused. Her tongue peeks out of the corner of her mouth as she aims, and she lifts the dart with utter determination. It makes Kate laugh that much harder, when it lands exactly in the middle of the board, earning Yelena 50 points and two shots of vodka, which she “celebrates” by exclaiming loudly, her voice dropping an octave again as she speaks to herself, rubbing a quick hand on her face.

    “Oh, fuck me…”

    She appears to think for a second, taking note of her predicament with a deep sigh before she turns to Kate, a wide, amicable smile sliding onto her face.

    “Kate Bishop! My dear friend!”

    Kate begins to snicker again, already shaking her head.

    “No. No!”

    Yelena steps closer, grabbing Kate’s forearm with both hands, eyes searching for hers with a toothy grin.

    “No, no, no, Kate. Hear me out. No, listen. Listen! I propose a slight change to the rules.” Kate can barely choke out another no, with how hard she is laughing, as she shakes her head. Yelena’s voice keeps breaking with laughter too, trying to speak over her. “No, Kate, listen, this will be good for you too! You will see!”

    Kate is pretty sure there are tears gathering in her eyes from laughing so hard at Yelena trying to make it seem how changing the rules now, right before she has to take four shots, is a great idea for both of them.

    Without thinking, Kate grabs one of the hands that Yelena is holding onto her forearm with and pulls her closer to herself, against her front. Loosely hugging Yelena around the shoulders as both of them are laughing, she is overcome with the sheer amount of affection she feels for the woman. At that moment, it feels like the last two weeks of their being at odds have finally been resolved for good. Yelena’s body shakes as she practically giggles, her arm lifting to encircle Kate’s waist too.

    As their laughter dies down, Yelena attempts to pull back, but Kate holds on and it only takes Yelena a second to lean back against her, fully this time.

    “Thank you.”

    Muttering it into Yelena’s hair, which for the record, is incredibly soft against her face, Kate hopes that she knows she means it for everything. For coming to cheer Kate up, for staying with her now. For going with her to the hospital to see her mother. For helping even when they weren’t on the best terms.

    Against her shoulder, she can feel Yelena smile and Kate lifts her other arm to wind around her back, pulling her against herself even tighter. In turn, Yelena’s arm lifts too, slowly, almost hesitantly, grabbing onto Kate’s arm around her shoulder, just holding onto it. Yelena doesn’t answer verbally but she nods. For a minute, maybe even more, the two of them just stand there in Kate’s living room, holding each other.

    Holding Yelena like this in her arms feels incredible, and maybe not kissing her is worth it, because this moment feels special. More special than a drunk kiss or make-out session on the couch, or even a drunken hookup.

    Slowly, Yelena pulls back, eyes more clear than they were a minute ago. For a long moment, she only looks at Kate, before she lifts on her tiptoes and presses a kiss onto her cheek. “You are welcome.”

    Kate smiles then, looking away, down, then back at Yelena. For a moment, she lets herself just watch her, taking her in, before sighing deeply.

    “Okay, you win.”

    At Kate’s words, Yelena almost looks confused, before her eyebrows lift and her face starts to morph into triumph. Before Yelena can get the wrong impression, and think Kate is giving up the whole game, she continues.

    “I’ll allow you to change the rules. Once.”

    The transformation of Yelena’s face freezes before she decides to take the win. Grinning widely, she nods and steps back, resting her hands on her hips as she turns to look at the board.

    “Okay. Okay, let me think.”

    Smiling, Kate turns around to pour herself some juice while Yelena thinks. Yelena spins around then, kind of losing her balance but catching herself in time, making Kate snicker into her juice.

    “Okay, how about one shot for every 50 points.”

    If she is being honest, Kate kind of lost track of where they are with points right now, even just for the last 3 that Yelena threw a few minutes ago. As long as Yelena stays, Kate can honestly say she doesn’t care. She nods then, saluting Yelena with her apple juice. “Deal.”

    Yelena nods, grinning happily before her face turns thoughtful.

    “I threw…In the last round, I threw. Um…”

    Kate starts to laugh again and Yelena joins her before shushing her with a hand over her mouth.

    “No, ssh, I am trying to think.”

    Kate just accepts Yelena’s palm over her mouth, glancing at the board with Yelena’s darts still in place. Smiling against Yelena’s hand, Kate raises her arm, pointing at the board. Yelena follows her hand, taking in the position of the darts, then counting on her hand. “Five, plus twenty plus fifty…That is seventy-five! One shot!”

    Twisting back towards the table, her hand over Kate’s mouth slips away as she pours the shot and grabs onto Kate’s arm to brace herself before she has to drink it. Exhaling through pursed lips, she prepares herself, and throws the vodka back, closing her eyes and taking a deep breath afterward. Yelena rolls her lips together, leaning her head forward and Kate can’t help but watch her like she is the only thing in the world. Her beautiful, golden hair falls around her face like a sheer curtain and Kate longs to push her hand through it. “I have to admit. This game might have been a slight miscalculation.”

    That’s the first thing she says after, and Kate snickers, blinking at Yelena slowly as she lifts her eyes to look back at her.

    “Ready to give up?”

    Yelena steps closer, leaning into Kate’s space before whispering, as she holds Kate’s gaze. “Never.”

    Huffing out another laugh, Kate shakes her head.

    “Your turn.”

    Kate puffs out her cheeks as she exhales, glancing at Yelena before leaning off of the table and picking up her darts. With the new rules, the best way to go forward is to score close to 100, or close to 150. Yelena scored…What did Yelena score earlier? Kate rubs at her face, trying to remember. 75, maybe? Yeah, something like that. Okay…Kate should aim for 90, or something around that.

    Taking up position, Kate takes a deep breath, opening her eyes wide to see the board properly as it seems to have become quite a bit fuzzier, since the last time she looked at it. From the side, Yelena laughs, possibly at her attempt to see well, and Kate shushes her from afar. “Ssh. I am aiming!”

    Closing one eye doesn’t help at all, so Kate decides to trust faith or at least muscle memory and throws it at the board. The dart embeds itself into the second-most inner circle, and Kate huffs satisfiedly.

    Exhaling through pursed lips, she lifts the second one, hoping that this will work out the same way, letting muscle memory guide her. It lands in the bullseye, scoring Kate another 50 points.

    Kate grins to herself, glancing to the side to see if Yelena is watching. She is, eyes lidded as they follow Kate and it would be a lie to say it doesn’t send a thrill down her spine. Wetting her lips, Kate takes aim, sort of, at the 20-section.

    Wetting her lip, she lifts the dart, throwing it with a practiced motion. The first thing to let her know that she might have miscalculated is Yelena’s booming laughter. Taking a step closer to the board, she is horrified to note that this time, this time, she has managed to get her dart into the triple ring, raising her final score to 135, instead of the planned 95. Which means two more shots of vodka, instead of one.

    Throwing her head back, she exhales loudly while Yelena snickers on the side, busying herself by pouring Kate two shots. Kate steps up to the table like she is about to face execution, taking the first shot from a beaming Yelena.

    “You are not going to be this giddy, if I throw up on your shoes.”

    She warns Yelena with a lopsided grin, who raises an eyebrow and takes a precautionary step back. Shaking her head, Kate takes a deep breath, before drinking the shot, feeling it burn all the way down and make her stomach turn.

    Before she moves onto the next one, Kate has to take a breather, walking around the living room with her hands on her hips. Inhale, exhale. Jesus, the things she does to impress Yelena…or what? Prove Yelena wrong. That’s what she means, totally.

    After about 30 seconds, Kate walks back to the table for her last shot. Even the thought of it makes her nauseous, but she can’t turn back and give up now. She picks up her juice in preparation, before looking at Yelena. Even she looks a bit doubtful about this one, and Kate looks away, not letting her doubts get in her way.

    Exhaling fully, so she cannot smell it as she throws it back, Kate drinks the last shot. It tastes and feels awful, but despite the odds, Kate manages to keep it down. Taking a long sip of apple juice, then a deep breath, before exhaling slowly. She turns to Yelena who looks back at her with an amused, but proud smile.

    “I have to say. I am impressed.”

    Kate means to laugh at her slightly slurred and strongly accented words but she also has to frown, which probably makes for a weird combination but she is past caring. “You are only just now impressed? I have beaten your pretty little ass at darts twice.” Yelena grins, tilting her head to the side as she bites down on her lower lip. After a few seconds, she speaks with a smug purse of her lips.

    “Glad you noticed.”

    It takes Kate a moment to try to comprehend what she is saying. Noticed what? “Huh?”

    Yelena just laughs at her, walking back closer now that she is convinced Kate is not on the verge of throwing up.

    “I bought these jeans 50% off. They were worth it, yes?”

    Slightly confused why they are talking about her jeans, but very confident in her own ability to pull the next line off, or at the very least make Yelena laugh, Kate grins, glancing down at the jeans in question.

    “They should be 100% off.”

    For the record, she does say it as a joke. As a cheesy pickup line to entertain Yelena. But the confusion spreading on Yelena’s features, eyebrows drawing together and face scrunching up, is funnier than anything Kate could come up with.

    “What?”

    Kate is already laughing again, grabbing hold of Yelena’s elbow next to her. “Because…Whew. Because, you know, then they would be off.”

    Looking absolutely befuddled, Yelena shakes her head, eyebrows drawn.

    “That does not make any sense.”

    Her confusion is quite possibly the funniest thing Kate has ever seen, but her laughter is also making her stomach turn even more than before. Exhaling slowly, she avoids looking at Yelena, afraid it might trigger another laughing fit.

    “Whew. Okay. Uh, are finished? I feel like we could use a break before the next round.” Yelena nods, probably eager to get away from having to consume more vodka at this point in time as well.

    “Yes, yes. A break is a good idea. I…I think I’m going to use the bathroom.” Kate nods, walking to the kitchen to get a bottle of water, which might take just a tiny bit longer than it usually does, as Kate almost falls over her own feet twice. With Yelena’s presence and the excitement she brings gone, Kate truly feels how drunk she is, once she is in there. Hoping that Yelena forgets about the last round, she leans back against the kitchen counter, sipping her water and trying to decide what to do next.

    Her brain is preoccupied with one very important question, however.

    Where will Yelena sleep?

    The guestroom seems logical, but if it were any other friend of Kate’s, Franny or Greer, they would undoubtedly sleep in the same bed and keep talking, laughing, until they both fell asleep. Isn’t this, when it comes down to it, a similar girl’s night? It’s what Yelena said in the beginning.

    Sighing, Kate thinks that it’s decidedly not.

    Even without the added effects of alcohol, her blood thrums in response to Yelena’s mere presence. If they were to sleep in the same bed, Kate would undoubtedly spend the entirety of her time awake thinking about turning over and kissing Yelena. Even now, a significant part of her mind is preoccupied with imagining Yelena on her sheets, pulling away the light yellow shirt and the jeans, and thoroughly familiarizing herself with the wanton, raspy voice she heard from Yelena earlier.

    Kate imagines kissing her when she comes back from the bathroom and finding out if Yelena truly doesn’t wear a bra underneath the shirt, or if it just seems that way. If her body would feel as good, under Kate’s, or on her, as it did while holding her a few minutes ago. If she were to pull on Kate’s hair in return, while Kate pulls the dirtiest, most wanton sounds she can from her using her mouth.

    Shaking her head, Kate tries to get the images out of her mind.

    When Kate was about to kiss her earlier, Yelena side-stepped the moment, at least it seemed that way to Kate.
