It doesn’t matter how much Kate wants her, how much she feels her brain melt at even the thought of a naked Yelena in her bed, it seems that while Yelena is attracted to her too, there is something stopping her, making her think twice.

    Finishing up her glass of water, Kate checks the time, eyebrows furrowing. It’s past 3 am and Yelena has been in the bathroom for a while.

    Walking across the living room, she leans close to the bathroom door, checking for sounds of anything out of the ordinary, thinking Yelena might be sick, but hears nothing. Knocking gently, she calls out.

    “Are you okay?”

    When there is no answer, Kate’s eyebrows furrow even further. This time she knocks a bit more forcefully, calling out again.

    “Yelena? Are you okay?”

    There is no answer again and Kate begins to worry. Yelena is a trained assassin, Kate doubts her falling over while drunk and hurting herself is not something she really needs to be scared about, but when there is no answer for another couple of seconds, her concern wins over. “I’m coming in, okay?”

    There is no answer this time either, so after a few seconds, Kate twists the doorknob and gently opens it, peeking in.

    “Yelena?”

    The room is dark, however, and Yelena is nowhere to be seen. Confused, Kate flicks the lights on and looks around, but unless Yelena got swallowed by the dark grey tiles of her bathroom, she is not in there.

    Kate leaves the bathroom, checking her bedroom next and the sight that greets her as she enters, makes her heart simultaneously squeeze and skip a beat.

    Yelena is on her bed, curled up, and clearly asleep. Her sneakers are off, Kate has no idea where and she is breathing slow and even, eyes closed, her face turned towards the door. Exhaling her apparently useless worry, Kate smiles to herself and takes the opportunity to watch her for a second. In her sleep, Yelena’s face is smooth, her features softer than when she is awake. Her hair fans out below…

    “Stop watching me sleep, Kate. It is creepy.”

    Yelena’s raspy, sleep-addled voice almost gives Kate a heart attack, so much so that she physically jolts at the sudden words. Yelena opens her eyes slightly and there is a small smile on her face. Kate huffs, half amused, half annoyed.

    “You did that on purpose.”

    Yelena closes her eyes again, sighing deeply but the smile still not melting away. “Yes. Now, sleep.”

    She doesn’t open her eyes again and Kate is faced with a new dilemma. Now that she knows where Yelena sleeps, where does she sleep? Yelena being here, awake enough to acknowledge her presence, clearly means she is okay with them sleeping in the same bed, right?

    It would be kinda weird to leave now, Kate. Stop overthinking.

    Nodding to herself as she makes her decision, Kate walks into her room and lies down next to Yelena. For about a minute, Kate just lies there, looking at Yelena’s back, moving up and down with her breaths. Exhaling, she tries to tell herself to relax, but even Yelena’s proximity, just lying about a foot from her, makes her restless.

    Closing her eyes, Kate sighs deeply once more and tries to do the breathing exercises her therapist taught her back in the day. The alcohol in her system helps because despite her reservations about not being able to sleep with Yelena so close, and Kate being so worked up over it, she is asleep within minutes.

    Kate wakes up to a punch in the face.

    Correction.

    Kate wakes up to a pounding headache and what she assumes is a punch in the face, which turns out to be a pillow, when she raises her arm to weakly defend herself with a groan a few seconds later.

    “Kate, you have to get up.”

    Yelena.

    What is Yelena doing in her bedroom?

    Her memories of the night before are a bit fuzzy towards the end, but what Kate absolutely can remember is the almost overwhelming urge to kiss Yelena.

    Oh. My. God.

    Did she sleep with Yelena and forget it?!

    That’s the…That’s quite possibly the worst scenario Kate can imagine. Not the sleeping together part, obviously. The forgetting.

    “Kate! For the love of god! Get up!”

    With a groan, and what is lightning speed in Kate’s head, but in reality, closer to a sloth reaching retirement, she sits up. Opening her eyes, she is blinded by what she assumes is a nuclear explosion, but in actuality, is the overcast sun shining through the half-drawn curtains of her bedroom window.

    The second attempt to open her eyes is slightly more successful. She is careful this time, only opening one at first, and even that just barely and immediately uses it to check whether she is naked or not.

    Thankfully, she isn’t.

    She is wearing her clothes from last night, which also thankfully, makes the theory of her sleeping with Yelena and forgetting about it quite unlikely. Her head feels like it might split in half, and she is pretty sure that while she was sleeping, something crawled into her mouth and died in there, but at least that’s one thing she doesn’t have to be worried about. Next, she looks around the room, eyes coming to rest on Yelena.

    Yelena, who is wearing a white dress, makeup, and all in all, looks very much like an Instagram influencer on a good day, not somebody that helped Kate pretty much finish a bottle of vodka last night. First, Kate pinches her arm slightly, to make sure she is actually awake, and she speaks before her brain and her mouth have the chance to reconnect. “What are you wearing?”

    Yelena, who looked simultaneously impatient and amused up until this point, suddenly looks a bit insecure. She looks down at her dress, her hands coming to smooth it out and Kate’s heart clenches weakly at the uncertainty on her face.

    “You do not like it?”

    Kate tries to wet her essentially bone-dry lips before she shakes her head. “No. I…You look beautiful. I just…Why do you look so good?”

    Insecurity fading away as fast as it came, Yelena smirks before she seems to remember herself and she is back to slightly baffled.

    “Kate, the FBI is going to be here in an hour.”

    The…who?

    Oh god!

    Eyes widening, she catches Yelena’s eyes again who is back to being impatient and somewhat amused, nodding at Kate.

    “Yes, Kate! The FBI! So if you were so kind…”

    Yelena gestures at the door of the bedroom, but Kate assumes she means to get up and get ready in general, not just leave the room. Rolling out of bed, Kate stands up, immediately regretting her quick motions. A powerful wave of nausea makes her suck in a deep breath, exhaling slowly through her mouth.

    “Are you going to throw up?”

    Yelena’s eyes shouldn’t contain this much amusement, and she definitely shouldn’t look this pretty while she is having fun at Kate’s expense.

    “I won’t let you talk me into a drinking darts game ever again.”

    The laugh she receives in return does little to ease her injured pride and well…injured everything, if the way she feels right now is any indication. Glancing at Yelena again, her perfect hair, spotless makeup, and the dress that came out of nowhere, somehow, Kate can’t help but ask.

    “How are you not hungover? I feel like I got lobotomized by a toddler.” Yelena grins but walks by Kate to go up to her wardrobe and start rummaging through it as she answers. Kate’s brain hurts too much to even start to question what’s happening. “I was. When I woke up three hours ago.”

    Three hou…what?!

    Yelena throws Kate a pointed look, then continues to look through Kate’s clothes. As she is still comprehending Yelena being awake for three hours while she slept, she doesn’t have the mental capacity to also be outraged at whatever she is doing right now. “Why? Why have you been awake for three hours?”

    Pausing in her browsing, Yelena straightens up and turns to her. As Kate comprehends that she is also wearing heels, Yelena grabs her shoulders and tries to hold her eyes meaningfully. “Kate, I’m going to need you to pay attention to me, okay? The FBI is going to be here in less than 90 minutes. You need to shower, get dressed, and we need to clean up your living room, okay? We can discuss my morning routine after.”

    Blinking dumbly, Kate can only nod before Yelena turns her around by the shoulders and ushers her toward the bathroom.

    “Shower.”

    Still kind of moving on autopilot, Kate takes a shower and focuses on not throwing up, which is a feat that she is pretty proud to achieve, once she is done. After brushing her teeth too, she feels at least 25% better, apart from the still pounding headache and the rolling stomach. Not thinking, she opens the door to walk to her room wearing nothing but a towel, finding Yelena in Marie Kondo-on-steroids mode in her living room. For a moment, they look at each other like two wild animals suddenly coming face to face in the tundra, Kate, practically naked, and Yelena, shoving empty bottles and snack wrappers into a big black trash bag. “I put out appropriate clothes for you on the bed.”

    The freezing spell is broken by Yelena’s words, but Kate is increasingly sure that she is experiencing some kind of mental episode. Why the fuck would Yelena put out clothes for her? Instead of forgetting that Kate slept with her, is this like a 50-first-dates situation, where they have been married for years and Kate somehow doesn’t remember?

    It sounds insane, but Kate checks the date on her phone back in her bedroom just to make sure five years haven’t passed and that is not the case. Distractedly, Kate is thankful that Yelena didn’t put out underwear for her at least, while she gets dressed. That would have been embarrassing. Once she is wearing panties, a sports bra, and socks, Kate pauses as she looks at the prepared clothes. Why is Yelena dressing her up like a gay accountant? A male gay accountant.

    “Yelena?”

    She raises her voice, hoping that Yelena will just yell back, instead of barging in. Of course, her hopes are short-lived as Yelena walks in 10 seconds later. She sighs at the sight of Kate in her underwear, pinching at the bridge of her nose.

    “What, I have to get you dressed also?”

    Kate laughs before she realizes it makes her headache ten times worse and has to grab onto her head to reduce the pounding.

    “Ow-ow. Oww. No. No, just, um. Is there a reason for these particular clothes?” Yelena’s eyebrows rise, like Kate is the weird one for asking, then she nods, before explaining.

    “Yes. You already sent them away once and set a specific appointment. Being well dressed would tell them you are prepared, while also giving the impression that you respect their authority, which law enforcement types tend to like. Also, it is a good reminder to them that you are wealthy. They will be less likely to fuck with you if they are aware that you are rich.” Kate tilts her head to the side, considering Yelena’s words. She is distractedly endeared that Yelena apparently thinks that putting on a dress shirt and a tight pair of chinos will make her look rich, but they don’t have time to unpack that right now. Maybe it has to do with Thomas always dressing like a model from a yacht catalog.

    For once, either due to her hangover, or maybe even a little due to Yelena looking distractingly amazing and rich herself in that dress, Kate just decides to do what she is told. “Okay, thanks. I’ll be out in a minute.”

    Yelena is out of the room before she even finishes the sentence and Kate quickly puts on the clothes she set out, light brown chino pants paired with a light blue button-down shirt. Yelena even put out a belt for her, and an expensive watch Kate thinks she got from Jack last Christmas and hasn’t taken out of the box since. Despite her less-than-stellar physical state, Kate smiles the whole way through, thoroughly entertained, and steps out into the living room in a few minutes three minutes.

    “Sonya and Thomas already took Lucky and the boards. We have to put the files into your secret room.”

    Yelena doesn’t even turn to look at her, as she is pulling down the photos and statements off of the wall, and putting them in a folder. Giving herself 3 seconds to just take her in, Kate pauses in the doorway, staring at Yelena. The dress shows more in the terms of ass and legs than the usual-

    “Less gawking, more tidying, Kate.”

    Impressed at Yelena’s ability to do that with her back to her, Kate immediately gets into motion, noting the smug amusement in Yelena’s tone. She would be lying, however, if she said she didn’t take every opportunity to appreciate the dress and more importantly, how it looks on Yelena in the next 45 minutes, while the two of them clear the apartment of any sign of illegal activities.

    By 1:30, the apartment, the living room at least, is almost spotless, and thanks to some weird green concoction that Sonya showed up with halfway through, Kate’s murderous hangover is almost entirely cured. Sonya helps them clear up too, and once everything is in place, the two Widows send Kate to put on some makeup, before the agents show up.

    As Kate is putting on the finishing touches (some light contouring) Sonya knocks on the open door’s frame.

    “I’m going. Good luck!”

    Kate quickly checks herself in the mirror, deeming herself ready, and puts the brush down to turn to Sonya.

    “Thank you so much for helping. And the…cure.”

    Not knowing what to call the green drink that tasted disgusting, but was essentially a lifesaver, she just indicates drinking with her hands. Sonya chuckles, walking out with Kate as she flips off the light.

    “Oh, do not mention it. It’s a secret Russian recipe.”

    Kate huffs in amusement, smiling back at her.

    “Well, now at least I have some information to feed the FBI.”

    Sonya chuckles and picks up her bag by the door, before turning to Kate. “Well, in case they ask, the secret ingredient is cucumber juice and crushed-up aspirin. Kate’s face scrunches up at the cucumber juice part, but she really can’t argue with its potency.

    “I really don’t understand your affinity for weird vegetable juices, but I guess I can’t complain about this one. Thanks…I guess.”

    As Sonya laughs at her expression, Yelena enters the living room as well, from the direction of Kate’s kitchen. For approximately the thirtieth time today, Kate is stuck by how good she looks, the light streaming through the windows giving her an almost ethereal look. “I have made some coffee, in case they want some.”

    “Oh, that’s a good idea. Thanks!”

    Kate can’t help but appreciate the dress one last time before Yelena has to inevitably leave, eyes quickly trailing down Yelena’s for and back as she picks up her phone from the coffee table, before walking towards them as well.

    “I’ll call you guys when I’m done? I’ll fill you in on what my mom told me yesterday and we can plan and stuff.”

    Yelena’s eyebrows furrow as she halts a few steps from the door and she glances at Sonya who still stands by Kate’s side, presumably waiting for Yelena, before her eyes go back to Kate.

    “I’m staying.”

    Blinking, Kate looks back at her in surprise, but really, she will take any help she can get. “Oh, okay. Thanks. Why?”

    Amusement colors Yelena’s features again, eyebrows lifting. She answers a second later like she is spelling out something incredibly obvious, faintly reminding Kate of how Yelena told her Clint was in the elevator back at the Rockefeller Center.

    “I’m your alibi.”

    Kate can guess how dumb she looks, but can’t quite stop herself to look back at Yelena with her lips slightly parted, just staring.

    “For what?”

    Yelena grins, seemingly finding endless entertainment in Kate’s slowness on this particular morning.

    “Anything.”

    “Oh. Right”

    Sonya snickers next to her, before opening the door.

    “See you both in a couple of hours.”

    Kate waves her goodbye, acutely aware of Yelena’s proximity as she walks up to her side as well, bidding Sonya farewell too.

    “See you! Thanks again!”

    Sonya says something in Russian then, causing Yelena to chuckle and Kate to huff in tired annoyance. Yelena glances at her then, grin tempered into a smile as Kate closes the door. “Come here.”

    Kate doesn’t really know where “here” is, considering they are already pretty close, but turns towards Yelena nonetheless. She fusses a little with Kate’s collar, straightening it out, their eyes still not quite level with each other, despite the heels Yelena wears as she glances up at Kate. She smiles to herself, clearly in a good mood this morning.

    “Why did you think I put on this dress?”

    Glancing down at the said dress, Kate wets her lips before grinning dumbly at Yelena with a shrug.

    “Fashion? I don’t know. You two are always ridiculously well put together.” Yelena makes a non-committal sound at that, clearly expressing amusement again before she steps over to the mirror above the table by the door, checking her own makeup. “It’s better here in New York, but you Americans are weird about that. Who goes to the supermarket in their pajamas? It is absurd.”

    Kate snorts, content to just watch Yelena before she remembers she should probably check the time. Her phone shows 1:48, so if the agents are punctual, Kate still has about 10 minutes. She decides now is an as good time as any, to check out the agents coming to visit. Sitting on the couch, Kate boots up her laptop, opening her archive of the Bishop Security database. Yelena takes a seat by her side, crossing her legs.

    “What are you doing?”

    Kate glances at her before she focuses back on her screen.

    “Doing a quick background check on our agents.”

    “I told you. Sonya checked them this morning and they really are FBI.”

    Kate hums, still typing ‘McLagan, Agent’ into the search bar as the system boots up. “Yeah, just making sure.”

    The search results load and Kate quickly clicks on the name ‘McLagan, Andrea’ that pops up as the first result. The file has a headshot of the agent, confirming that this is indeed her. Quickly running over the details, Kate doesn’t find anything unusual, until she gets to the part about employment history.

    While the archive version of the database is almost 2 years old, therefore possibly out of date, Agent McLagan’s employer is not the FBI according to the Bishop Security database. It’s The Department of Damage Control.

    “Yelena, look at this.”

    Leaning closer, Yelena reads the line Kate is pointing to, sucking in a breath. “Department of Damage Control? They are the ones in charge of superheroes, yes?” Wetting her lips, Kate nods.

    “Yeah. But this is old, so this is probably where she worked before the FBI.” Yelena nods to herself, pursing her lips before turning to Kate.

    “Check the other agent.”

    Kate writes in ‘Reyes, Agent’, which produces 6 results, but the first one is definitely not the young man with McLagan yesterday as the birth date is 1967. The second and third ones are women and the fourth one is even older than the first Reyes from ’67. By the time Kate clicks on the fifth one, the clock at the top of her computer screen shows it’s almost 2 o’clock. The fifth one seems to be the match they were looking for. Agent Daniel Reyes, born in 1998, graduated from Quantico in 2023 and got a master's degree in criminal psychology from the University of Chicago.

    Next to Kate, Yelena is reading through the agent’s file with laser focus as well, pressing up against Kate’s side to see the screen. When she is through, she stands up, visibly thoughtful. “Okay. I assumed they thought you had something to do with your mother’s crimes, or are just double-checking but maybe that’s not-“ The doorbell rings and as Kate quickly closes down her laptop’s screen by reflex, she sees the time. 2 pm, sharp.

    Yelena glances at the door and then turns back to Kate quickly. In a hushed tone, she hurriedly speaks, holding eye contact.

    “They might actually be looking into you. Just follow my lead.”

    Kate nods, standing up from the couch, suddenly not knowing what to do with her hands. Yelena takes a deep breath, and Kate can see the way she transforms herself before she steps up to the door and it only now occurs to her, that maybe they should have come up with a cover story beforehand.

    Yelena swings the door open, and while Kate can’t see her face from her position standing by the couch, she can tell Yelena is smiling as she begins to speak, her perfect American accent firmly in place.

    “Good afternoon! Please, come on in!”

    The agents are both visibly surprised at Yelena’s appearance but are very quick to mask it. Agent McLagan is the first through the threshold, holding out her hand for Yelena. “Hello, I’m Special Agent McLagan.”

    The first surprise, for Kate, comes as Yelena takes the agent’s hand and shakes it while introducing herself.

    “Helena Rowley.”

    Who the fuck is Helena Rowley?

    “Agent Reyes.”

    “Helena Rowley. Please come on in.”

    Kate comes back to herself, walking to the door as well.

    “Hi, hello. Kate. Bishop. But you know that.”

    Chuckling somewhat awkwardly at herself, Kate shakes both of the agents’ hands one after the other, and quickly barrels on, gesturing towards the sitting area.

    “Please, sit. May I take your jacket?”

    Agent Reyes smiles back at Kate, shaking his head.

    “I don’t think we will stay long enough to do that. We really only have a couple of questions.”

    Smiling back, Kate exhales, relaxing a little bit. Maybe they really are only here for a few routine questions. Leading the agents further into the room, Kate gestures for them to take a seat but instead of the couch, they both go for the armchairs Kate and Sonya brought out earlier, instead of the couch.

    “May I get you something to drink? Some coffee, or juice?”

    Yelena is so perfect in her portrayal of doting…something (girlfriend? roommate? They really should have talked about this beforehand…) that it almost freaks Kate out, while simultaneously calming her down, knowing she is in Kate’s corner. Agent McLagan smiles politely as she shakes her head, but Kate doesn’t miss the calculating look she looks Yelena over with.

    “Nothing for me, thank you.”

    Looking perfectly harmless, Yelena turns to Agent Reyes then.

    “How about you, Agent Reyes?”

    He smiles at Yelena warmly, nodding.

    “I’ll take a coffee, thank you. With just a splash of milk or creamer, whatever you have is fine.”

    Kate almost excepts her to curtsy, with the level of pleasantness and politeness she displays, but Yelena only nods before leaving the room. Kate wets her lips before rounding the coffee table and taking a seat on the couch across from the agents.

    “So. How may I be of help to the FBI?”

    Agent McLagan smiles, crossing her legs.

    “You have a beautiful home, Ms.Bishop. Do you mind if I look around the living room?” Agent Reyes smiles still, and Kate blinks, not expecting the question, but recovering quickly. “Um, yeah, sure. Go ahead.”

    With a pleasant nod, Agent Reyes rises from the armchair and begins to walk around the living room, inspecting random items.

    “So, Ms.Bishop. It is my understanding that you have only just returned to New York. Is that correct?”

    Agent McLagan draws Kate’s attention back to herself, and she wets her lips, smiling politely as well.

    “Yes. I’ve been living in Los Angeles for the last year or so.”

    Reyes snooping around her living room is distracting, but Kate tries not to look at him. “May I ask what brought you back?”

    Kate forces a smile, but not knowing what these people want puts her on edge. “Well. I’m sure you are aware that my mother is about to stand trial for a multitude of crimes. I came back for the trial.”

    Nodding, McLagan never looks away from Kate. It’s positively unnerving. “You are the one that turned her in, correct?”

    As McLagan asks her question, Reyes is looking at the bookcase that covers the entrance of Kate’s secret room and she has to be very conscious to not look at what he is doing there exactly. The questions also annoy Kate since they obviously know the answers to these. Despite all that, Kate gives her answer with only a slightly stiff smile. “Correct.”

    “May I ask how you came to the information about her being involved in criminal activities?”

    The question slightly unbalances Kate, and she blinks at the agent across from her. “Um…I have given my testimony to the police. I have received evidence from an anonymous source. A recording of my mother’s conversation with Wilson Fisk.”

    McLagan still doesn’t take her eyes off of Kate and she really wishes they would get on with it.

    “What do you do for a living?”

    Reyes speaks suddenly, kind of breaking the focus of her conversation with Agent McLagan. “Um, sorry, what?”

    With a charming smile, Agent Reyes turns to her from next to Kate’s shelf of trophies. Most of them are still at her mother’s penthouse, untouched and almost forgotten, but the ones that she is most proud of, Kate made sure to take with her.

    “Oh, sorry. Didn’t want to interrupt.-“ He doesn’t look sorry, as he immediately continues.

    “I’m just amazed by the number of trophies on this shelf, and I was wondering if you are an athlete.”

    Kate glances at Agent McLagan to see whether she is annoyed by the younger agent’s interruption, but she is still just staring, her face indifferent. With a smile, she turns back to the more pleasant half of the duo even though she is pretty sure this is information they can easily access as well.

    “I was. I am kind of between jobs at the moment.”

    Turning back to the trophies, Agent Reyes shifts his weight from one leg to the other. “You were part of the Archery team at Columbia University, right?”

    Considering that they might be after Kate, as Hawkeye, instead of just trying to connect her to some crime her mother committed that she actually doesn’t know about, Kate decides to downplay it. With a smile, she answers Agent Reyes.

    “Um, yeah. But also basketball, rowing, and fencing. I always had a knack for sports.” “But you studied Computer Science and Business and Administration.”

    Agent McLagan doesn’t even phrase that as a question, and Kate clears her throat somewhat awkwardly.

    “Yes. I did.”

    “You know, I saw you once.”

    It could almost be passed off as yet another random comment from Reyes, but there is something about his voice. Kate waits for him to continue, and he does, after a few seconds, turning back towards them again and retaking his seat across from Kate. “On TV. You won the National Archery Competition, in 2023. I remember because you shot almost twice as many points as the silver medalist after you. It was extraordinary.” His tone is still off, somehow, but the logical thing to say here is: “Thank you. I, um…yeah, I remember that year. It was in Florida.”

    Reyes, still smiling, tilts his head to the side. Kate is starting to understand where this line of questioning is going.

    “Why did you stop? I think everyone expected you to become an Olympian.” Yelena reenters the room then, carrying a tray with two cups, a coffeepot, sugar, a small jug of milk, and some cookies.

    “I know you said you didn’t want any, but just in case.”

    The latter is addressed to Agent McLagan with a smile, who nods politely but doesn’t move for the drink or cookies as Yelena sets the tray down. She rounds the table after, taking a seat at Kate’s side, pressing into her slightly, thighs touching.

    Guess that explains what their cover is.

    With a movement that Kate hopes comes across as natural and something they always do, Kate puts her arms behind Yelena on the back of the sofa. Agent Reyes reaches for the coffee, adding a splash of milk as well.

    “I’m sorry, where were we?”

    Feeling a bit more emboldened, Kate turns back to Agent Reyes with a smile. He returns it jovially, glancing at Yelena as he takes the first sip of his coffee. Kate can’t decide whether neither agent questioning her presence here is weird or not.

    “I asked why you stopped professional archery. You were on track for the Olympics.” Sighing deeply, Kate allows herself to let some of her real feelings shine on the matter. “Well, after my mother’s arrest, my life kind of turned upside down. I’m sure you understand. Priorities have shifted.”

    She is absolutely sure that they do not, in fact, understand, but that is not here, nor there. “Of course. It’s a shame though,”

    Agent Reyes might have a poker face rivaling Yelena’s, but Kate can see that they arriving at their destination finally. He lowers his cup, pinning Kate with a look that is void of his faux charm.

    “-You could have rivaled Hawkeye, if you wanted to.”

    Chuckling, Kate shakes her head, but internally her hackles are raised. Here they go. “I don’t know about that.”

    “Oh, Kate, don’t be shy. She really could have. She has the trophies to show for it.” Yelena surprises her by backing the claim, and when Kate looks at her a second later, the adoration on her face is almost enough to render her speechless. Damn, the woman deserves an Oscar.

    “Are you a fan?”

    Thinking quickly, Kate has to remember that the authorities have a record of both her and Clint on the scene of her mother’s arrest and the last Bishop Security holiday party. Complete denial is out of the question.

    “I was. Now I’m a friend.”

    Eyebrows lifting, Agent McLagan leans forward and Reyes puts his empty cup on the tray. “A friend? Of Hawkeye?”

    Kate chuckles as she nods.

    “Yes. Well, of Clint. Clint Barton.”

    In a move that says more than they probably should, the agents look at each other for a second.

    “How do you two know each other?”

    Kate wets her lips, looking from one agent to the other. Agent McLagan’s staring is starting to unnerve her. She is like a robot, barely even blinking.

    “I was about to be mugged on the street the Christmas before last when Clint showed up and saved me. He was in town for the Rogers Musical and as every person interested in archery, he was my hero growing up, of course, and I wore him down to befriend me.” Kate chuckles then, that Yelena and Agent Reyes join her in, while Agent McLagan smiles politely.

    “After the um, the anonymous person sent me the video of my mother and Wilson Fisk, he was the one I reached out to first to help me decide if it was legit or not. He was nice and helped me find the right channels within law enforcement to reach out to once we verified its authenticity.”

    Agent Reyes smiles too, before nodding and glancing at his partner.

    “Have you ever thought about going in a similar direction? Becoming an Avenger?” Politely smiling back, Kate shakes her before she chuckles.

    “As a kid, of course. But no, not really.”

    Leaning back, Reyes looks at her too, tilting his head to the side, asking what he really wants to ask. How stupid does he think she is?

    “You have the skills for it, clearly. You have won medals in archery, fencing, and several martial arts.”

    Mirroring his pose, Kate tilts her head to the side before grinning, deciding to call them both out instead of answering.

    “Is that why you are here? You think I’m some kind of…vigilante?”

    Purposefully pausing before the last word to make it seem like it’s foreign like it’s ridiculous to think about, Kate watches them both for some type of reaction. Next to her, Yelena chuckles, glancing at her like it’s the most insane idea she has ever heard. “Are you?”

    Leaning slightly forward, Agent Reyes asks her with a slight smile. While Kate is not looking at her, she can see that Agent McLagan’s polite smile finally falls for a second, but her intense stare remains. Kate laughs Reyes in the face, shaking her head. “Of course not.”

    Agent Reyes wets his lips, before turning to his partner and shrugging as if he doesn’t know how to proceed. McLagan only looks at him for a second, before she is on Kate again. The wedding ring on her finger is the only indicator that she is an actual human being, instead of a robot programmed to stare.

    “Alright, Ms.Bishop. Do you mind telling us where you were on the 28th of August?” Slightly taken off guard by the suddenly hard and concrete question from Agent McLagan, Kate blinks for a second.

    “Uh. Sorry, I don’t know that off the top of my hand.”

    Kate knows exactly. That was the day Yelena and her went to investigate the storage units, almost got blown up, fought the super soldier, and fled through the subway. She also knows, that unless Valentina is seriously fucking them, the CCTV footage has been deleted, but there is nothing they can do about the mobile phone footage still around.

    “Oh, I know that!”

    Yelena glances at her, with a slight smile and Kate returns it, doing her best to play along with whatever it is.

    “We were home.”

    Raising an eyebrow, Agent McLagan turns her laser beam eyes onto Yelena. “Just the two of you?”

    Seemingly content in ignoring the agent’s obvious suspicion, Yelena nods with a smile. “Yes. Just the two of us.”

    “All day?”

    Yelena nods with a smile, unsurprisingly not flinching in the face of McLagan’s attention. “May I ask what you were doing?”

    Yelena’s smile widens and she glances at Kate, looking almost bashful for a moment. “I…we were in bed, for most of it to be honest.”

    She sells the honeymoon-phase, moon-eyed girlfriend, probably banking on her statement from yesterday, that sex makes people uncomfortable enough to not ask questions. But Kate…Well, Kate realizes she hasn’t said anything in a few seconds, so she decides to add her own bit to prop up Yelena’s story. Looking back at her, hoping to look as smitten as Yelena does, Kate smiles wide as she nods.

    “Oh, you are right. We were celebrating.”

    Turning to the agents with a smile, Kate hopes to give the impression that she is not just pulling this out of her ass. The agents are unflinching and undeterred, of course. “Oh. May I ask what you were celebrating?”

    Kate prides herself on being able to think on her feet. To come up with lies on the spot and roll with the punches. The unfortunate side-effect of that is that sometimes, sometimes, she doesn’t entirely think through what comes out of her mouth. Which is why, the same time as Yelena answers, “Promotion.”

    Kate gives her own answer, “Engagement.”

    And okay. The idea probably came from her subconscious after seeing Agent McLagan’s wedding band around her finger or something but it doesn’t make it any better. To Yelena’s credit, not a muscle moves on her face, her smile just as polite as it was before the unfortunate words left Kate’s mouth. She has made her bed, however, so now Kate has to lie in it. With a chuckle, she grins at the side of Yelena’s face, like this was an inside joke of sorts before turning back to the agents.

    “Promotion, from girlfriends to fiancés.”

    Yelena does turn to look at her, as Kate doubles down on her lie, mouth opening and closing once before her smile is firmly back on her face. She looks confused, but Kate thinks it’s probably a part of her act. She wouldn’t be able to tell, looking at her. “I thought we weren’t telling anyone, until after the trial.”

    Kate sees Agent Reyes smile across from them, his features slightly tight, looking between the two of them.

    “Well, yeah. But they are the, um, authorities.”

    Yelena nods, before turning back to the agents with a smile. Agent McLagan speaks next, voice well-mannered but void of any emotion.

    “In that case, let me be the first to congratulate you both.”

    Sliding her arm from the back of the couch to Yelena’s shoulder, Kate smiles back at them while internally facepalming. What the fuck did she just start.

    “Thank you very much. We are…we are very happy.”

    Yelena puts her hand on Kate’s thigh, glancing at her before turning back to the agents, her face slightly concerned.

    “We are. The timing is just…unfortunate. With the stress and media attention around Kate’s mother’s trial, we are trying to keep it under wraps, for now.”

    The agents both nod, smiling at Yelena. It looks like they are about to wrap up, but Kate feels like there is still another shoe to drop. Surely, they didn’t think here based on the fact that Kate is a good archer.

    “Well, in that case, we have only one question left.”

    There it is.

    “Of course. Please, go ahead.”

    Agent Reyes looks at her for a long second, smiling, before reaching into the inner pocket of his jacket, and pulling out something in a plastic bag. He puts the item on the coffee table, between all four of them, pinning Kate with a look that suddenly feels like its intensity was turned up to 1000%.

    “Ms.Bishop, do you recognize this item?”

    Kate’s heart takes off racing.

    The item in question, is Kate’s wallet, in an evidence bag. Kate’s wallet, which she lost when the Super Soldier dragged her out of the sunroof of her car, and Yelena and her fought him, or even sometime before, during the explosion and fight in the storage units. Shit.

    Shit, shit, shit, shit.

    “That’s…oh my god! That’s my wallet!”

    Yelena turns to her like this is shocking news to her as well, eyes wide. “The one that got stolen?”

    “Yes!”

    Kate reaches out but is halted by the hard look on Agent McLagan’s face. “Oh. I’m guessing I’m not allowed to have this back, am I?”

    Leaning back, Agent McLagan shakes her head, and disturbingly, it seems the smile she gives Kate then, is the first honest one during their conversation.

    “I’m afraid not, Ms.Bishop. It’s evidence in a federal investigation.”

    Channeling the himbo energy that has gotten her out of many hairy situations, and into many parties in college, Kate hopes she looks as dumb as she feels.

    “Oh my god! Where did you find it?”

    It’s Agent Reyes speaking again, eyes focused and charm turned down.

    “Are you aware of the events taking place at O’Connor Self Storage and then the following incident in Queens on the 28th of August?”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate pretends to think. Well, she does actually think, but not about whether she is aware of the events, but trying to decide how much she would know if she wants there. Yelena seems to think faster than she is.

    “Oh yes! We saw it on the news, remember?”

    She only turns to Kate for a second, before she looks at the agents again, eyebrows furrowing.

    “But Kate’s wallet got stolen before.”

    Her hand squeezes Kate’s thigh then, and she is unsure whether this is her cue to join the story or to shut up. When Yelena is quiet for a few moments, Kate decides it’s probably the former. She tries to remember the last time she used her credit cards before the incident but comes up short. Instead, she decides to tie her story to something that did happen. The attack in Central Park.

    “Um, yeah. It got stolen a few days before. I got jumped in Central Park.” Agent McLagan hums, staring at Kate again and Reyes tilts his head to the side, clearly somewhat doubtful.

    “How come you didn’t report it stolen?”

    Yelena lies without missing a beat.

    “But we did.”

    This is the first time Agent McLagan looks doubtful, for barely a second before she masks it, her face going back to polite indifference.

    “May I ask where?”

    “We reported it to the Central Park Precinct the day after. Um, you can ask the doorman to corroborate the events too. He saw me coming in after.”

    The two agents look at Kate for a very long moment, before looking at each other. Agent McLagan nods, and the two of them rise, after Agent Reyes picks Kate’s wallet up from the coffee table, and puts it back into his inside pocket.

    “Well, thank you for your time, Ms.Bishow. You as well, Ms.Rowley.”

    Kate and Yelena stand up as well, walking out the agents. Agent Reyes turns back before he leaves, charming mask back on, eyes crinkling warmly as he smiles.

    “Congratulations again, on your engagement.”

    Kate smiles back, longing to be rid of them and to have space to freak out a little with Yelena. “Thank you.”

    He offers his hand to shake to Kate first, then to Yelena, before stepping out, but there he halts, turning back for a second.

    “I’m sorry. I can’t help but notice that neither of you has engagement rings. May I ask why?” Jesus, just go, man.

    “Um, sure yeah. I, uh.-“ Kate chuckles awkwardly before explaining.

    “The one I gave to Helena was slightly big, so it’s getting resized. And uh. We haven’t bought one for me yet.”

    Agent Reyes’ eyes crinkle as he smiles, nodding at Kate. She really just wants to kick him out at this point.

    “Right, I see.”

    Kate is pretty sure this is his way of telling them he knows they are full of shit, but has no way to prove it just yet. Agent McLagan offers her hand too and speaks to Kate as they shake hands.

    “Ms.Bishop, I respectfully ask that you don’t travel outside the state until further notice.” Kate’s eyebrows furrow, having thought they dodged this bullet, even if barely. “I’m sorry, am I accused of committing a crime?”

    McLagan’s unnerving, lazily unconvincing smile is back on her face as she shakes her head. “No, no. It’s just a precaution. In case we need you for our investigation.” Wetting her lips, Kate nods.

    “Right. Okay.”

    After shaking Yelena’s hand, Agent McLagan steps out the front door too, and in a few seconds, Kate and Yelena are finally alone.

    Leaning against the door, Kate exhales slowly, before turning around and checking through the peephole that the agents have truly left. When she is certain, she looks at Yelena, puffing out her cheeks as she exhales.

    “Jesus, that was intense.”

    Yelena nods, clearly in thought. Kate bites down on her lip, before gesturing at Yelena in a movement that feels kind of awkward.

    “Sorry for blindsiding you. With the uh, engagement stuff I mean.”

    Yelena’s eyebrows furrow and Kate is relieved to see her amused, instead of irritated. “No, it was good. You improvised well.”

    Russian accent firmly back in place, she sighs deeply as well, before walking back to the coffee table to pick up her phone.

    “Can you hack the police database?”

    Kate tilts her head to the side, not expecting or understanding the question’s direction, but answering nonetheless.

    "I mean, probably yeah. But it would take me a few hours.”

    Nodding, Yelena wets her lips before lifting her phone to her ear.

    “Who are you calling?”

    Yelena glances at Kate, while she picks up the tray with one hand.

    “My mother.”

    It seems that Kate’s mind has used up its capacity for the day, keeping up with the agents because the next thing that comes out of her mouth has definitely haven’t passed through her brain.

    “To tell her that you are engaged?”

    Thankfully, it seems that Yelena’s good mood from the morning is still intact because she only snorts but doesn’t halt on her way back to the kitchen.

    “Among other things.”

    Eyes wide, Kate follows her, taking the tray out of her hands and setting it on the counter when they get there.

    “Seriously?”

    A lifted eyebrow is all the answer she gets, before Yelena’s call connects and she starts speaking rapid Russian into the receiver. Kate is beginning to learn to tune it out and puts away the milk and sugar then spends a good couple of seconds staring at the cups and trying to decide if they are hers.

    Yelena taps the counter to get her attention while she speaks, and points at one of the cupboards, presumably noticing Kate’s confusion. Giving her a thumbs up, Kate puts the unused cup in the cupboard Yelena pointed out, distractedly noting how there are several identical cups there she has never noticed before.

    After that, she puts the one Agent Reyes used into the dishwasher, and prepares a cup of coffee for herself as well, having forgone it earlier during their frantic tidying. Tapping the counter to get Yelena’s attention just like she has done, she points at the coffee maker once Yelena is looking at her, trying to non-verbally ask her if she wants some coffee too. Kate receives a distracted thumbs up back as well, so she makes a coffee for Yelena, sliding it in front of her just as she hangs up.

    “Was she ecstatic?”

    Yelena snorts taking a sip of her coffee, before shaking her head.

    “I did not actually tell her. She would nag.”

    Surprised, Kate raises her eyebrows.

    “Nag?”

    Yelena nods, looking amusingly serious.

    “Yes. She and Dad always nag about dating.”

    Interest piqued, Kate opens her mouth to ask a myriad of questions but Yelena holds her hand up and Kate promptly closes it.

    “No. I asked her to hack the Central Park Police department to file and backdate a report for your stolen wallet.”

    Blinking, Kate doesn’t know which part to focus on for a second.

    “That’s…that’s a good idea.”

    “Yes. It will not make them drop their suspicions, they might have already checked if it was reported stolen before they came here, but it means it cannot stick in court. So they can be suspicious, but they cannot prove anything. At least for now.”

    Kate nods sagely.

    “Smart.”

    Yelena only gives Kate a side eye to determine whether she is being sarcastic or not. Kate decides to not follow the line of questioning regarding why Yelena’s mother is capable and willing to hack the NYPD, and evidence temper like a pro. Instead, she goes back to something Yelena said during their questioning.

    “So, Helena Rowley?”

    Another sip of coffee and a raised eyebrow is all the answer Kate gets, but she is not so easily deterred, now that Yelena and she are back on good terms again.

    “What happened to Lizzie Humper?”

    Snorting, Yelena puts down her cup for a moment, gesturing at the living room behind Kate. “Kate, I am not going to give a fake identity to the FBI, especially a flimsy one. They will definitely look it up, and it’ll only raise more questions.”

    Glancing to the side in confusion, Kate leans back against the counter. “I don’t get it. You just gave them a fake name too. How is that different?” Yelena smirks and along with the white dress Kate finally has the bandwidth to appreciate again, it’s an image to behold.

    “Technically, it is not fake.”

    Hold up.

    “What do you mean? Your name is not Helena Rowley.”

    The cheeky grin that she receives in return threatens to melt down Kate’s psyche. “Legally, it is.”

    Rubbing a hand on her face, Kate huffs out in amused frustration at Yelena’s purposeful vagueness.

    “What does that mean?”

    Yelena only holds the teasing silence for a few more seconds, probably for her own entertainment.

    “Okay. Do you remember how I told you I was sent on a long, undercover mission to Ohio when I was little?”

    Kate nods, crossing her arms.

    “Yeah.”

    Yelena takes one more sip of her coffee, before setting down her cup and fussing with it, turning it sightly around.

    “So, when they made the background for our family, they created a fake birth certificate for me, under the name of Helena Rowley.”

    Kate nods along, keeping up so far.

    “Okay.”

    Yelena wets her lips, lifting her eyes from the coffee cup to catch and hold Kate’s gaze. “Well, because we were there for 3 years, the rest of my identification was real. I got a real social security number, real school documentation, and everything under that name. When we moved to Ohio again, because of the craziness with the Blip, I was able to…resurrect the identity, so to say…”

    There is a small smug smile attached to this story, as Yelena speaks and Kate can’t help but return it.

    “-So, technically, in the eyes of the American government, my name is Helena Rowley.” Shaking her head in amused disbelief, Kate grins as she crosses her arms. "So basically, the American Government built you a fake identity"

    Yelena chuckles, tilting her head to the side.

    “I guess I never thought of it that way, but yes. That is accurate.”

    Huffing, Kate leans off of the counter, entertained by Yelena’s story.

    “And here you were, letting me think you were a red-blooded Russian citizen.” With another snort, Yelena mirrors Kate’s position, leaning back against the counter behind herself.

    “Well. If you ask the Russian government, I do not officially exist, so…” Eyebrows furrowing, Kate purses her lips. Having spent weeks with Yelena and Sonya, Kate knows by now, not to react too strongly to the sometimes sad pieces of information Yelena reveals sometimes.

    “That’s kinda fucked up.”

    Surprise colors Yelena’s face, mixing with amusement again.

    “You think?”

    Kate just hums, taking a deep breath. Wetting her lips, Kate looks at Yelena seriously. “What are we going to do?”

    Yelena is thoughtful for a second, before nodding to herself.

    “First, I need to change. Second, we need to bring Sonya up to speed on everything. Then, we need to make a plan on how to get the data your mother mentioned.”

    Closing her eyes, Kate hangs her head, taking another dramatic sigh.

    “Yeah, about that…”

    Chapter End Notes Happy New Year guys!!

    So, first of all, I KNOW! I Know okay, but it wasn't the right time yet :D We still need more tension between them, but we will get there soon, I promise. I was really hoping to post this bishova heavy chapter by their mac and cheese anniversary, then at least until Christmas but their flirting kept running away from me :D I don't know about you, but I think we deserved a lighter (more bishova centric) chapter again and let me tell you, I had so much fun writing this one :D I hope you guys enjoyed it too. Now, about the chapter: First and foremost: I know everyone likes Yelena to be a Russian badass who drinks Kate under the table but since she is like 5'3" and like 130 lbs at most, I find that a bit unrealistic :D Excessive amounts of vodka get you drunk, whoever you are and Kate *was* a college student not long ago, an probably a popular one at that, partying and etc. It doesn't make sense for me for her to not be able to drink at least as well as Yelena or Sonya are able to. Fun fact: Pornstar Martinis are my favourite coctail :D (also also: drink responsibly, kids!)

    On another note, I think I'm not spoiling anything, if I tell you that the agents will be back, and they too, seem to have their sights on poor Kate.Girl really can't catch a break, can she. :D Next, I gotta be honest, I am a slut for the fake-dating trope and everything it brings with it, if it's well executed :D So I'm going to have my fun with this a little, even within this relatively dark universe.

    Also, if I was clever enough to use chapter titles, I'd have called this one "Who the fuck is Helena Rowley?" :D Fun Fact: The name comes from Black Widow. In BW Natasha's undercover name is Nicole Rowley while they are in Ohio (I'll tweet a picture of her ID card from the movie), so the family's name was the Rowleys, and in my head, they'd give Yelena a name as similar to her own as possible, so as a kid, she doesn't get confused and accidentally out them.

    Now, I have some slightly bad news too: this is the last chapter I'm able to post until probably the beginning of February. I'm about to finish my master's degree and I have graduation exams and stuff, so I gotta lock this story and throw away the key from myself until that's done at the end of January. The good news is, that once I'm done, for the first time in like 3 and a half years, I won't be super fucking busy, so I'll have tons more time to write. :D I'm hoping to pick up speed with these updates and release more of Vampire Smile as well.

    Please let me know what you think in the comments below! Thank you for reading and Happy New Year!!

    Chapter 22

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Chapter 22 “Yeah, about that. That’s a bit more complicated than she made it seem while you guys were in there.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Yelena looks back at her seriously.

    “How so?”

    “The data is hidden and encrypted and it needs a key. It’s like a whole thing. And it’s not just the super soldier formula, but evidence that my mom has been compiling for years about Fisk and his…activities. Oh, and to decrypt it, we need to be on-site, for like 3 days…And I am pretty sure Fisk has the servers that they are on. So…It’s not great.”

    Yelena’s eyebrows furrow even more, especially since Kate’s words are rushed, and she shakes her head.

    “Okay. I am going to call Sonya up, and change. Then you will have to tell us everything your mother said, exactly.”

    Kate nods and swallows the urge to tell Yelena she really doesn’t need to change, and instead tries to focus on remembering everything her mother told her yesterday regarding the files. She also makes it a point to purposefully stay away from the more emotionally heavy revelations from their conversation. Remembering that she had made notes the day before, Kate decides to check those first while Yelena is on the phone with Sonya. She goes to pick up her phone from the living room and returns just as Yelena hangs up, the two of them almost running into each other in the doorway as Kate in entering and Yelena is leaving. Without thinking, Kate grabs Yelena’s hips in hopes of avoiding a collision, chuckling.

    “Sorry.”

    Yelena snickers also, slipping by her with a look that makes Kate’s stomach do a somersault and leaves her throat dry. It’s not just her, right? She is not imagining this. It takes Kate a moment afterward to remember what she was doing when she came in here, and she is also reminded by a loud grumble of her stomach that she has yet to eat anything today, other than the green Russian-approved smoothie that Sonya has brought her earlier. While she waits for Yelena to change and Sonya to come up, Kate investigates the ingredients in her fridge and finds the leftovers the Widows brought her yesterday. With a smile, Kate pulls the Tupperware from the fridge and puts it in the microwave.

    As her food heats up, Kate opens her notes from yesterday, quickly looking them over. - 3 parts: data, pathway, key - data servers: Limitless has them?

    - encryption / key : destroyed? – copy at the Summer Place (upstairs living room, birthday) - pathway / location : FBI has it - 72 hours to decrypt – have to be on site The microwave beeps behind Kate, and she leaves her phone on the counter to get her steaming hot Paprikash. Sonya made it with a side of some kind of dumplings that look a bit strange but end up being delicious as Kate digs in. The whole meal is heavenly, and Kate hums to herself as she eats, enjoying the flavourful food, momentarily pushing her notes aside.

    “You really like that, huh?”

    With a yelp, Kate twists around, throwing her knife at the intruder. Sonya dodges it with ease and it hits the counter behind her head, then falls down to the floor with a loud clattering noise. She looks more entertained, than offended and grins a second later at what she must see on Kate’s face.

    “What the f..? I…You guys gotta stop doing this to me.”

    Sonya snickers, before she pulls out a drawer on her left, gets a new knife, and hands it to Kate as she passes her a second later.

    “Or, you could just get better at assessing your surroundings.”

    Kate gives her a dark look for a second, but then the heavenly scent of her still half-eaten Paprikash hits her nose again. Pointing her fork at Sonya, who takes a seat across from her at the counter, Kate purses her lips but has a hard time tamping down her smile. “I want to be mad at you, but this food is incredible. So, thin ice, but thank you.” Sonya chuckles at that, seemingly pleased with the compliment.

    “You are welcome.”

    After a second, she wets her lips and with the slightly teasing face Kate has learned to know very well by now, she asks her seemingly straightforward question. It’s anything but. “So. How did it go?”

    Glancing to the side, Kate tries to figure out what Sonya might know and what she should tell her. Yelena is not in the room yet and Kate has no idea what she’d want Sonya to know and what she will do if Kate tells her something she doesn’t want to tell her. Time to play dumb again.

    “What do you mean?”

    Sonya’s eyebrows lift, and Kate thinks maybe she has overdone it. Okay, maybe not That dumb.

    “With the FBI agents? That were just here?”

    Taking a bite to bide her time, Kate thinks and decides to just go over the basics of what transpired.

    “Right, uh. It was fine…mostly. We, um, yeah. Turns out they are not after my mom, but me. They found my wallet where Yelena and I fought the super-soldier the day you and I first met and well. They suspect I am a vigilante but have no concrete proof just yet.” Sonya blinks, eyebrows furrowing.

    “What did you tell them?”

    Kate puts the last bite of the Paprikash into her mouth again and chews and swallows it before she answers and Sonya urges her on.

    “About the wallet…?”

    Clearing her throat and taking a sip of water, Kate bides her time again but she answers after a few moments.

    “That it got stolen when I was jumped at Central Park a few days before. Yelena called her mom to create and backdate evidence of that in the police system.”

    Sonya nods, staring at Kate with slightly narrowed eyes.

    “And that’s it?”

    Wetting her lips, Kate leans back.

    “Yeah. Basically. They asked a few questions about my archery career and Clint, but we handled it.”

    For a long moment, Sonya is just looking back at Kate, tilting her head to the side. She can tell that Sonya can tell that there is something she’s leaving out.

    Where.

    The hell.

    Is Yelena?

    “So, why are you being shifty?”

    Eyebrows jumping up, Kate attempts to look innocent, shaking her head.

    “I’m not shifty. You are shifty!”

    Sonya’s eyebrows match hers in their ascent.

    “Okay, you are definitely shifty.”

    “Am not.”

    “Are too.”

    That is the moment Yelena walks into the kitchen, in jeans and a brown top, looking from Sonya to Kate and back. Distractedly, Kate mourns the white dress from before but doesn’t miss the chance to appreciate the jeans for a moment.

    “What is going on?”

    Before Kate has a chance to speak, Sonya leans back with a smug look, eyes shifting over to Yelena.

    “Kate is being shifty.”

    Kissing her teeth, Kate leans back on her chair, resisting the urge to cross her arms. “I’m not! Sonya is being paranoid.”

    Amusement clear on her features, Yelena takes a seat by Kate’s side.

    “What are you being shifty about?”

    Kate sighs, running her tongue on the outside of her teeth.

    “I’m not…! Uh.”

    With a shake of her head, Kate leans over her food again, picking up her fork again to stab the last remaining bites with vigor. Across from her, Sonya snickers, before her focus shifts to Yelena.

    “So, what happened? With the FBI?”

    Kate rolls her eyes but doesn’t speak as she finishes her meal. She already told this to Sonya. Eyes shifting over to Yelena on her side too, Kate is curious to see what she shares and how. “Well. We both thought they were here connected to her mother somehow, but turns out, Kate was dumb enough to bring her wallet with her on one of our missions…”

    Kate lets out an offended, “Heeyy”

    …with the food still in her mouth but can’t really protest Yelena’s assessment too much and is ignored anyway as Yelena continues as if she wasn’t interrupted.

    “…and lost it. They found it and made the straightforward connection of their suspect being an archer, to Kate being an Olympic-hopeful archer herself so…They came to suss her out. They do not have anything solid, however, so we sent them on their way, for now.” Sonya’s eyes move between the two of them as Yelena speaks, clearly aware that something has happened, but not knowing what to poke at just yet.

    “That’s it?”

    Huffing, Kate leans back as she does cross her arms this time, and stares at Sonya across. “Told ya.”

    Yelena turns to look at her, amusement hidden in the corner of her lips. Oh no.

    “Well, there is one more thing.”

    Lips parting slightly, Kate looks back at Yelena. What is she doing? Kate thought they were on the same page! That Yelena wanted to avoid Sonya’s teasing too…

    “Kate told them we are getting married.”

    Gaping openly now, Kate looks from Yelena’s amused face to Sonya, watching as several emotions flash on her face in a matter of seconds. Surprise mixes with amusement, which shifts to smugness and then wonder and mirth again. She barely chokes out a few words with her restrained laughter.

    “I’m…What!?”

    Eyes shifting back to Yelena, Kate sputters.

    “I…you! You started it!-“ If Yelena is going to throw her under the bus here, Kate is going to reveal all their cards, not just the ones that make her look silly.

    “-Yesterday, you implied that we were having sex and that they were interrupting!!” A slightly choked sound can be heard from across the kitchen counter, Sonya apparently having trouble processing the amount of teasing material she is being handed at this very moment. Yelena is less phased than Kate would have hoped.

    “Yes. We were backed into a corner. It made sense, and it did work.”

    Kate wants to point out that her cover of their “engagement” has worked too, and Yelena seemed to think so too like 15 minutes ago, but her words are drowned out by Sonya’s loud, uncontrolled cackle. With a sigh, she closes her mouth and shakes her head at Yelena who joins Sonya’s loud laughter with a chuckle of her own.

    Sonya laughs for at least a minute, gripping the counter to keep herself upright, and anytime it looks like she is going to wind down, she takes one look at them and starts laughing again. Kate throws accusing glances at Yelena, but she’d be lying if she said she didn’t see the humor in their situation too. Still, Sonya’s laughter goes on forever, and it’s not that funny. Yelena, for her part, seems torn between being amused and bored by Sonya’s level of entertainment, so when Sonya finally starts to wind down for good, wiping away tears from her face, she asks with a drawl in her voice.

    “Are you done?”

    Sonya’s voice shakes with her laughter, and she grins as wide as Kate has ever seen her, teeth white and glinting as she shakes her head.

    “Absolutely not. How did that even happen? Tell me everything.”

    Kate kisses her teeth and decides to take over explaining, lest Yelena throws her under the bus again somehow.

    “They asked what I was doing on the 28th of August. I said I didn’t know off the top of my head. Yelena has insinuated that we were home…uh, like having sex, again.-“ Throwing a glance at Yelena who just looks back at her, smiling smugly, Kate continues. “And I added that we were celebrating. They asked what, and I was looking at the wedding ring of one of the agents and I guess my subconscious like, put that in my head probably or something, and yeah. I said we got engaged.”

    Sonya glances at Yelena again, before she laughs again, shaking her head. Kate runs a hand through her hair, somewhat annoyed to be made fun of but simultaneously entertained by the situation as well. Sonya takes a few seconds to stop giggling before her eyes shift over to Yelena.

    “Melina and Alexei will be over the moon.”

    Pursing her lips, Yelena levels Sonya with a semi-serious glare and shakes her head. “They will not be, because you will not tell them any of this.”

    Grinning so wide that her face might split in two, Sonya just blinks back at her. Kate watches with completely unconcealed interest, happy to not be the subject of their teasing anymore. “Why not? They will be ecstatic. Kate is young, beautiful and rich. Melina might object to her not being Russian at least a little, but I’m sure she’ll get over it once she meets her and sees how tall and pretty she is…”

    Yelena shakes her head, lips pursed but still smiling.

    “Are you done now?”

    Sonya chuckles, shaking her head.

    “Not even close. At the very least, I have to be your maid of honor.”

    Sighing, Kate leans forward, pushing away her now empty food container with a chuckle. “We’re not-”

    “I’m going to throw you the very best bachelorette party. We will get a limo, strippers. The works.”

    At Yelena’s sigh, Kate can’t help but snort amusedly, but it’s a mistake, as Sonya’s teasing gaze turns towards her as soon as she does.

    “And you! I never would have thought of you as the traditional type…”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate can’t help but ask.

    “Traditional type? What do you-?”

    Just as Yelena says with an amused sigh and a shake of her head.

    “Do not ask.”

    Sonya, as always, is undeterred.

    “Well, you did put a ring on it, before you even slept with her. Very old school.” Kate sighs too but laughs at Sonya’s joke nonetheless. Maybe, Sonya will stop sooner if they lean into it. And lean into it Kate does, even as she feels her face heat up at Sonya’s mention of (not) sleeping with Yelena as images from the night before flash before her eyes. “I did not actually. We will probably have to rectify that…”

    Eyebrows raising in unison, Yelena and Sonya look at her with twin expressions of amused surprise. Realizing the double meaning of her words, Kate feels her face warm up even more and quickly clarifies.

    “What? I mean, I’m just saying. If they come back, you will have to have a ring, because we said it was getting re-sized. The alibi has to be air-tight.”

    The explanation sends Sonya into a new fit of giggles while Yelena smiles, slow and smug. For a long moment, she only looks back at Kate, before she wets her lips. Thankfully, it seems that she will allow Kate to move past her unintended mention of “planning to rectify” not having slept with her.

    “Well, do not cheap out on me, Kate Bishop. As Sonya said, we know you are rich. I heard it has to be worth two months of salary.”

    Kate matches her grin, happy that the three of them can laugh about this slightly awkward misstep on her part. Yelena throws her hair over her shoulder, theatrically batting her eyelashes at Kate as she continues, fluently switching to her American accent for a second. “I want a diamond big enough that it’s going to make all the girls die at the yoga studio.” Biting down on her lips, Kate leans slightly closer.

    “I’d never dream of anything less, honey.”

    Yelena’s smile widens into a grin, eyes sparkling with her amusement, sliding back into her more rough Russian drawl.

    “Good luck asking my Daddy.”

    Kate blinks, surprised by the change of attitude to Yelena’s parents knowing about their faux engagement.

    “I…what?”

    Across from her, Sonya whistles and Kate looks over to watch her lean back and nod with an expression that is a desperate bid at seriousness. It seems they are not done picking on Kate just yet.

    “For her hand in marriage. You know.”

    While she knows it’s fake, Kate can’t help but gulp nervously at the thought of asking Yelena’s father, a literal Russian super-soldier for his little girl’s hand. She asks her next question half to entertain, but also at least partially because she’d not want to get on the bad side of such a man, even if the whole thing is not real. Maybe he will be offended by that. “Do you think he will be mad?”

    Her question sends both Widows into hysterics, both of them laughing out loud and it takes a few seconds for Yelena to calm down enough to pat her shoulder placatingly. “I’d be more afraid of her mother, honestly.”

    Sonya says it before Yelena can give her answer and the slight wince Yelena makes is enough to tell Kate that this joke does have some truth at its core. Shaking her head, Kate reminds herself that they are not, in fact, getting married and that even the conversation about it is just a joke. With a shrug, she looks between the two women before proclaiming in the hopes of putting the topic to bed, for now at least.

    “Some in-laws we have… A billionaire criminal, a Black Widow, and a Super-Soldier.” As Kate counts them off on her fingers, Yelena and Sonya snicker at her words before Sonya lifts an imaginary glass at them.

    “Christmas will be fun.”

    Snorting, Kate nods. Across from her, she can see Sonya gearing up for her next round of teasing, so quickly, she uses the mention of her mother as a segue to more pressing topics than her non-existent marriage to Yelena.

    “Speaking of. My mom told me a bunch of pretty important stuff yesterday. Can we finally talk about that now?”

    While Sonya looks slightly disappointed at the interruption of her fun, she sobers up after a couple of seconds while Yelena nods to Kate, urging her to continue. Kate takes a second to gather her thoughts, before she leans forward, gearing up to explain.

    “Right. Uuuh….So, Sonya. Long story short, my mom was working with Fisk on a lot of fucked up things, I think you know that. Aaaand it turns out, one of those fucked up things was a temporary super-soldier serum.”

    Sonya nods, face serious finally, glancing at Yelena.

    “Yes, Yelena filled me in a little yesterday.”

    Kate nods with a sigh too, trying to sum up everything before she gets to the part that Yelena doesn’t know either.

    “Right. Uh, so, she said she was going to double-cross him and sell it to the government but then she got arrested and now she has to hand it over for her plea deal to go through. Don’t know if it’s true, doesn’t really matter.”

    Taking a deep breath, Kate waits to see if she has any questions, glancing over at Yelena to see her listening too, face serious.

    “And she got you to go to the hospital yesterday, to convince you to get it for her.” Kate nods at Sonya’s statement, reaching for her phone.

    “Basically, yeah. She told them about the formula for this drug, but she has a bunch of other sensitive material saved up as well, to use against him on a rainy day…Which is now, I guess. She uh. When everyone left the room, she and I had a talk alone, and she told me where and how to find the bits and pieces, mostly.”

    Again, Kate pauses to see if any of them have questions but both Sonya and Yelena only nod at her to continue.

    “Right. So, once she was getting close with the formula, and to breaking faith with Fisk, she split up the data into three parts. The information itself is hidden in a huge database, that is part one.”

    Glancing down at her notes, she starts counting them out on her fingers. “The location of the data, which I think might be scattered, is part two. Let’s call that the pathway. Aaand the encryption, which is like a key that will unlock it all, once we know where it is within the database, is part three.”

    Looking up from her phone, Kate watches both Sonya’s and Yelena’s faces, to try to gauge if they understand.

    “So, to simplify, three parts: data, pathway, key.”

    Both of them nod again, keeping up with Kate’s words and she counts them out on her fingers again as she summarizes each of their current statuses.

    “The info is on data servers that used to belong to Bishop Security. After the company’s dissolution, they have been scrapped and auctioned off, and then bought by a small security firm that was soon bought up by a company called Limitless Corporation. Which, surprise, surprise, belongs to Fisk.”

    For the first time, Kate is interrupted.

    “How do you know that?”

    Yelena’s brow is furrowed as she asks, eyes looking at Kate intensely.

    “From my research into Fisk. I uh, tracked that company to him through money and saw that they bought up a bunch of old Bishop Security equipment through various shell companies after it was dissolved.”

    Yelena nods again, face all business-like, previous mirth completely gone. “So, that’s the data. She had a copy of both the pathway and the key aaand um. The copy of the pathway was apparently seized by the FBI, when they raided her penthouse, but they supposedly don’t know what it is. And a copy of the encryption is still untouched, most likely, at our summer house.”

    “Was that not searched?”

    Shaking her head, Kate purses her lips.

    “No, I don’t think so. It’s under my name and it’s in a hidden safe anyway.” Both of them nod, seemingly deep in thought. Yelena turns to Kate again in a second. “What was that about needing three days to transfer the files?”

    “Oh, yeah. Right, so even after we get all ingredients, it takes three days to decrypt the files apparently, and I think we need to be on-site for that. So…that means at Limitless’ data centers, which are probably heavily guarded and everything.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Yelena shakes her head.

    “Why three days?”

    Biting down on her lips, Kate tries to remember if she asked her mother that, but she doesn’t think so.

    “I…I actually don’t know. Complication of the encryption, probably. My mom didn’t say if it was symmetric or asymmetric encryption, but I think it’s probably symmetric, probably also paired with partitioning and masking the data…”

    Kate is kind of talking to herself at this point, trying to think everything through out loud. “So even if we did have the cipher that was used, it would take a long time to unravel the data.”

    Deep in thought, Yelena nods. In a few seconds, she looks at Kate again. “Are you sure they are not on the archives of Bishop Security that you still have a copy of?” That would have been convenient. Sadly, Kate has to shake her head again. “No. Different servers, unfortunately. I only have a copy of one of their cloud servers, none of the stuff from the secure offline environment.”

    Pursing her lips, Yelena nods again. For about a minute, they are all quiet, deep in thought. The silence is broken by Yelena again, who speaks a few minutes after.

    “Okay. So, you are positive you want to help her with this?”

    Shrugging, Kate takes a deep breath and nods.

    “I mean, I kinda have to, right? If Fisk gets it in his hands…”

    She doesn’t need to finish that sentence. That would be bad news. Very bad news for Kate, for New York. For all humanity, if Kate feels a little dramatic. Next to her, Yelena shrugs too, looking back at her calmly.

    “I mean, you do not have to. You can always walk away. We can help you disappear.” Resisting the urge to roll her eyes, Kate shakes her head with a smile. “You know I can’t.”

    Yelena sighs like she knows exactly and doesn’t like it one bit.

    “Okay. Well…I guess you are lucky you have the world’s best corporate spy on your side.” Unable to tamp down on the smile that slides over her face, Kate looks back at Yelena, enjoying the smug smile on her beautiful face.

    “The world’s best corporate spy?”

    Shrugging, Yelena leans back on her chair, looking Kate up and down playfully with a smile, and a small bat of her eyelashes.

    “It is only bragging if it is not true.”

    Chuckling Kate shakes her head.

    “That’s definitely not how it works, but I am too happy to have the world’s best corporate spy on my side to argue.”

    Smiling back at Kate smugly, with an amused glint in her eyes, Yelena leans on her hand before she answers.

    “Good.”

    For a moment, they are quiet again before Kate asks Yelena with a smile. “Does the world’s best corporate spy have an idea on how to steal all of this?” Theatrically, Yelena leans forward, eyebrows raising and face serious.

    “Well, Kate Bishop. We are going to need blueprints. Many, many blueprints.” For the next four days, Yelena, Sonya, and Kate lay their plans.

    Thomas is caught up in a project at work, and Kate would feel slightly bad at involving him in this anyhow, considering its highly illegal nature, so it’s the three of them, day after day, poring over blueprints and plans and hacked documents that Kate has no idea how they got in the first place because they sure as hell didn’t come from her.

    The project of finding Fisk himself and freeing the Widow they encountered are both pushed to the side for now, since they kind of hit dead-ends on both anyhow. The three of them divide work between them, each focusing on a piece of the puzzle.

    Sonya is tasked with looking into the FBI. Finding out anything about the agents after Kate, and more importantly, about whether or not the pathway was really seized and if it was, where is it now. Unsurprisingly, since their access to FBI documentation is extremely limited, even with their shared intelligence and illegal information-procurement-proclivities, Sonya can not locate the pathway in just a few days.

    She does find out that Agent Reyes’ mother is a senator, and that his father was killed in the Battle of New York, just like Kate’s. She also finds out that Agent McLagan is not only married, but has two young children, but apart from a joke (Kate sincerely hopes it was a joke on Sonya’s part) about last-resort kidnappings, there is not much to be done with that information.

    Yelena’s task is to come up with a plan to infiltrate the building, bypass its security measures and get out without Fisk finding out they were there in the first place. Limitless takes up the 31st to 33rd levels of the building, the big server room with the data centers being exactly in the middle on the 32nd. For what it’s worth, it seems that while there is constant on-site security, 3 guards even designated to watch over the server rooms specifically 24/7, the security is pretty old-school in the building all in all. There are cameras and a few sensors here and there, but nothing too fancy or complicated.

    Putting her computer science master’s and past knowledge of Bishop Security into good use, Kate is charged with finding out as much about the data and the encryption as she can, hopefully figuring out a way to shorten the 3-day decryption period. It would be much easier if she could talk to her mother some more, but unfortunately, that is not possible. They decide to leave the encryption key at its place for now, reasoning that if it was safe there for over a year and a half, it’s probably best if they don’t take it until they have something to use it on and will only pick it up once they are ready to use it.

    Apart from their work, during the next few days, Kate talks to Jack a couple of times too, helping out with plans for his party as a break between setting their “heist” up, as she has begun to call it in her head. She helps with looking over invites and deciding on the menu and helping to choose vendors, which is kind of a nice contrast to her other activities. She also calls Laura once, to ask whether Clint has been in contact or not. She reassures her that everything is alright, but Kate can’t help but wonder if she uses the same “mom voice” with Kate as she does with her own kids, when they ask about their father’s dangerous activities.

    In all honesty, when Yelena and Sonya leave for the night, and she is alone with her thoughts, Kate is getting really worried about Clint. It’s been weeks since he checked in and Kate can’t figure out what could take so long, and keep him so occupied, that he can’t even send a signal that he is okay.
