Her work with Sonya and Yelena makes her pleasantly exhausted in a way that she doesn’t have nightmares anymore, not really, but before she falls asleep she thinks about him every night, hoping that he is okay and upon waking, she sometimes has an uneasy feeling that she might have had a bad dream but doesn’t remember it.

    During the day, apart from work, Sonya and Yelena take her training every other day too, sparring with both of them. While she doesn’t come close to beating either of them, it’s a great way to let loose a little and it also means seeing Yelena in leggings and in her element, neither of which Kate would ever complain about. They both begin to give her pointers on how to correct some of her frequent mistakes too, and while two sessions is a pretty short amount of time to see much improvement, Kate likes the progress she is making nonetheless. Teasing comments about her “engagement” to Yelena are also dropped several times a day, unsurprisingly, mostly by Sonya but it becomes a sort of inside joke between them that provides a lighthearted, enjoyable distraction during their pretty monotonous research and planning work that also never fails to make Kate’s stomach drop in a very specific, pleasant kind of way.

    The kind of heated vibe from their drunken darts game is not entirely gone either, even if it’s dimmed to a shimmer for now. There are moments where she could swear Yelena lets her catch her looking at Kate, and while the two of them are never alone for longer than a few minutes, it keeps Kate’s blood thrumming pleasantly in her veins. It also makes sure that Kate looks her best, even when it’s only the three of them sitting at home, poring over papers and files.

    It’s four days before Kate makes any kind of progress, and when she does it comes with a soft slap to her own forehead that has Yelena and Sonya look up from their own respective files with amused eyes and raised eyebrows.

    “Shit! I’ve totally been looking at this the wrong way!”

    When she doesn’t immediately follow up with an explanation, Yelena urges her on. “How so?”

    Quickly double-checking that her idea is not completely idiotic, Kate takes another few seconds before she answers.

    “I have been looking into the encryption when it would be easier to steal the whole database. I…So, during my last year of college, we were taught about alternative ways of computing. There is quantum, but it needs a lot of cooling and apart from Cassie and her dad, I am not sure anyone has a working prototype of anything, but! There is also something called DNA data storage, and I think that could work.”

    Looking up from her screen, Kate sees that Sonya looks openly confused while Yelena masks it better, there is no flicker of recognition on her face either. With a smile at finally being better at something, Kate begins to explain.

    “Okay, so basically, current data storage uses tiny magnetic bits, that are either 1 or 0, based on their magnetic poles, to store information. But those have a limit of how small they can get, so if you want to store like x bits of data, there is a certain size that your storage device cannot get smaller than.”

    At that, both Widows nod, seemingly following the explanation that far. “Okay, so ever since they realized that, a lot of computer science has been looking at alternative ways to store data, that is not electronic. There is quantum computing which, if they get it to work, uses atoms to store data, and their energy levels, but to have those stable enough, they have to cool them down a lot, like…around 40 Kelvins, which is very very cold. They need to use liquid nitrogen, and it’s a whole thing. Right?”

    Yelena nods slowly, while Sonya’s face scrunches up a bit.

    “Right.”

    Kate is not deterred, excited to explain her solution.

    “So, DNA data storage is less trendy, but it uses strands of DNA to store data, transforming the ones and zeroes to combinations of adenine, cytosine, guanine, and thymine, so A, C, G, and T, which are the basic building blocks of DNA. They mix up a bunch of chemicals in the right amounts to get the right mix. Our professor told us that the entire internet can be stored on a device the size of a shoebox.”

    Finally, Yelena seems to understand her point, and Sonya nods slowly too, seemingly catching up.

    “So…You want to get a device like that, and copy over the entire server room, and then do the decryption at home.”

    Finally smiling, Kate nods at Yelena’s words.

    “Basically, yeah. If we got a storage device small enough, we can just walk in, take it all, and then get the rest afterward.”

    “Do you know where can we get one?”

    At Sonya’s question, Kate’s eyebrows furrow slightly and she shakes her head. “Not yet. But there are a bunch of companies working on it, so I am sure we can find one we can buy…or steal.”

    Yelena looks thoughtful before she stands up.

    “I think I might know a guy.”

    With raised eyebrows, Kate watches as she pulls out her phone and dials someone, and walks out of the room. Bewildered, she looks over at Sonya but she only shrugs with a smile. “We know a lot of people.”

    That’s the only explanation Kate gets before Sonya looks back down at the files on her lap and continues working.

    Yelena re-enters the room a few minutes after, still talking in a language that is not Russian but Kate still doesn’t understand. She walks back and forth, and from the tone of her voice, Kate can’t decide if she is angry, annoyed, happy, or entertained. Her face is a mask of focus, eyebrows drawn but there is a slight smile on her face all the way through. The confusing vision of that, paired with Yelena’s attire of a loose, green, and white stripy button-up shirt and jeans that hug her legs, hips, and ass just right, keeps Kate distracted for the entire duration of the conversation.

    When she finally hangs up, Yelena smiles, bright and wide, and Kate has to remind herself to keep her shit together as she looks back at her, then at Sonya.

    “I got it.”

    Blinking, Kate can’t hide her surprise.

    “You got it? Just like that?”

    Yelena nods with a smile, re-taking her seat in the armchair next to Sonya that they never took back to storage after the FBI visit.

    “Yes. He has a working prototype that can store up to hundred-thousand terabytes of data, yet it is the size of a standard wallet.”

    Kate nods with a smile, enthused by their progress.

    “He works for one of those startups?”

    Yelena’s eyebrows furrow, as if she is confused before she shakes her head. “No, Kate. He is a criminal. A very good one.”

    Leaning back against the couch, Kate nods slowly, contemplating, before she asks Yelena. “Uhm. And you…trust him?”

    With a slow blink and a smile, Yelena nods.

    “In general, no. But with this, yes.”

    Tilting her head to the side, Kate wonders what that means. Sonya asks what she is thinking. “What does that mean?”

    Crossing her legs, Yelena looks even more satisfied, and slightly amused for some reason. “I trust his greed and his fear of what I could do to him. If his device does its job, Kate pays him handsomely. If it does not, I know where exactly in the Bahamas he is hiding.” Blinking three times, Kate processes the information.

    “And how handsomely am I paying this criminal?”

    Yelena’s teeth flash white as a wide grin slides onto her face.

    “Two million dollars, after the deed is done.”

    Eyebrows rising Kate leans back, Yelena’s clear pleasure at spending her money leaving her feeling amused as well.

    “I don’t know how I feel about you taking so much delight in spending my money.” “What’s yours is mine, or so I’m told.”

    Referring to their faux marriage is clearly only adding to Yelena’s amusement and Kate can’t help but snort.

    “I told you you would be easy to gold-dig.”

    Chiming in from the side, Sonya seems to delight in Yelena’s actions too, and Kate rolls her eyes and then releases a defeated sigh, but grins as looks back at Yelena again. “I’d prefer if you spent it on clothes or jewelry or something instead of directly funding some criminal.”

    Mirth dances in Yelena’s eyes and she never takes her eyes off Kate as she offers her answer. “If it makes you feel better, he is a Robin Hood kind of criminal. Steal from the rich, give it to the poor.”

    Furrowing her eyebrows in a faux show of confusion, Kate shakes her head. “But darling, we are the rich.”

    Yelena’s answering laugh sends a pleasant thrill down Kate’s spine and she really can’t help the grin spreading onto her face in response. Yelena bites gently down her lower lip, still looking back at Kate and she feels the space between them buzz almost physically. It lasts for a few moments before Kate breaks the silence again.

    “So, okay, money aside, how does it work? We stick it in, copy the entire server room, and just go?”

    With a long exhale Yelena leans back and shakes her head slightly.

    “Not exactly. We need access to the server room to attach a…”

    Yelena pauses, visibly thinking of a word to use.

    “He calls it a transformer? It is like a separate pen drive. It installs a program that prepares the files to be able to be translated and transferred. And then we plug in the drive, and copy the files.”

    Wetting her lips, Kate nods and tries to think it through.

    “How long does it take to transform the files? And then to translate and transfer them?” “About half twenty minutes to prepare them, but then about twenty-five to thirty minutes to transfer them to the drive, once they are translated.”

    Kate nods. That, they can work with.

    “Okay. So we need about an hour inside the server room, right? Max.”

    Yelena confirms with a nod and purses her lips.

    “Have you figured out a way inside?”

    “Yes.”

    Standing up from her spot in the armchair, Yelena joins Kate on the couch, pulling a stack of blueprints into her lap.

    “The way inside is easy. There is access to the air conditioning system from the roof that leads to the elevator shaft. We can make our way down to the 32nd floor easily. If we go for the guard’s shift change at 1 am, there is an about ten-minute wide window when nobody is stationed at the staircase or the elevators, we can easily slip in.”

    Kate nods, following Yelena’s pointing finger on the pages, trying to not get distracted by Yelena’s thigh pressing against hers.

    “Where is the catch?”

    Sonya doesn’t move from her spot to look at the blueprints as well but clearly pays attention to Yelena’s words as well.

    “Well, there are two. One is leaving. There is no shift change until 8 in the morning. We can hide somewhere and leave then, but it is risky. Sun is up and employees are coming into the offices so that is not ideal. It is doable but anyone could see us.”

    Yelena waits for Kate to nod before she continues.

    “The second one is the guards inside the server room. There are three of them there, 24/7, and they only leave when the next shift is there, so we have to either knock them out and then the Kingpin will know we were there, or somehow do all of this, while they are in the server room.”

    Both Yelena and Sonya are quiet for a moment, Yelena tilting her head and looking down at the blueprint, while Sonya purses her lips in thought across from them. “The leaving is something we can solve. We can hide on one of the other floors until employees are in, and simply leave as if we work there. I have done that before. We just need to steal some key cards, child’s play.”

    While she wouldn’t call it “child’s play”, that is a pretty straightforward plan, so Kate nods as Yelena continues.

    “The guards are a legitimate problem, however. If we knock them out, we risk showing our hand, if we don’t, we risk being discovered.”

    There is a minute of silence, which Sonya breaks soon.

    “Can you pay them off? Or at least one of them?”

    Shaking her head, Yelena smiles.

    “No, unfortunately. There is no paper trail of their names or employee records. I only know there are three of them because there are three copies of the key cards that open the server room at night that are assigned to the guard group in their online system. We have no idea who they are, what their training is like, and so on.”

    Sonya nods and Yelena speaks again from next to Kate.

    “We could do recon and follow them home after their shift, but it is risky. If they decide to tell on us, the whole mission is blown.”

    For a moment, they are all silent, thinking before Sonya pipes up.

    “We could kill them.”

    Kate blinks at Sonya’s words with wide eyes, a bit torn over how easily she says it. She shrugs at Kate, blinking back at her.

    “I’m just saying. It’s an option.”

    With a sigh, Yelena shakes her head next to Kate.

    “No, that would expose us as well. One of them could drop dead from a heart attack, but three on the same night? It would blow the mission too.”

    Happy that she doesn’t have to deal with the moral implications of this too, Kate tries to usher them on.

    “Well, yeah. Plus you know, premeditated murder. Not great. Any other ideas?” Yelena shakes her head and Kate thinks for a few seconds before she poses her next question. “Do you know anything about their orders? Like, will they respond if there is something going on somewhere else in the company? On another floor, for example. Or if there is a fire.”

    Yelena smiles then, blinking at Kate slowly and watching her face with a certain warmth. “No, no idea. No documentation on them at all. But it is not a bad idea.” Kate grins, happy with the praise. For a moment, they look at each other before Yelena stands up and starts toward Kate’s kitchen.

    “Okay, how about you look into that, while I make us all lunch? ”

    Yelena makes some pasta dish with vegetables and chicken that tastes incredible and Kate revels in Yelena’s unusual, yet at this point, not unexpected shiness when Kate praises it and asks for seconds. After lunch, they get back to work and it takes Kate about two hours to find something.

    “Okay, I think I got it.”

    Sonya looks up from her laptop with a questioning gaze that is mirrored on Yelena’s as she lowers the papers she was reading through.

    “There is a small vault on the other side of the level. I have no idea what’s in it, probably money, but what if we pretend to break in there to draw away the guards from the server room since it’s only their key cards that open the door to that corridor as well.” As Kate looks from one to the other, Sonya’s eyebrows furrow, but Yelena seems to consider her plan.

    “Isn’t the point to remain undetected?”

    At Sonya’s question, Kate shakes her head.

    “Not exactly? We need to hide the fact that we are stealing the data and that it was us. But we don’t need to hide the fact that someone broke in.”

    Understanding flickers on Sonya’s face, and a small smile appears on Yelena’s face that urges Kate to explain her plan further.

    “So, the building is surrounded by other buildings. To the south, there is a taller one we can use to rappel over to the roof and enter the elevator shaft the way you said, get down, and to the server room.”

    Nodding, Yelena urges Kate to continue.

    “To the northwest, close to where the vault is, there is a shorter building, but the roof is still above the 32nd floor. We can rappel from there, and open the window to get in. That should be enough to trigger the alarms, but if it isn’t, we can cause a distraction around the vault, and get the guards to leave their post.”

    Both Widows leave their armchairs to take a seat on either side of Kate, peering down at the blueprint as well as she explains.

    “Yelena, it probably should be you that goes into the server room, since you have the most experience with this, and then Sonya and I can serve as a distraction on the other side, and entertain the guards once you are inside.”

    Slowly Yelena nods, still looking down at the blueprint before she shakes her head. “They cannot see you. If they work for Fisk, and they describe you, they will know what you were after.”

    Tilting her head to the side and looking at Yelena, Kate thinks.

    “I can wear a disguise.”

    Yelena is still deep in thought, but she nods.

    “We will all need to.”

    After a second, Yelena speaks again, still looking down at the plans.

    “I’ll need a lookout.”

    Pointing down at a corridor on the paper, Yelena explains.

    “It is not a good position and I will be exposed. There is a gallery on the 33rd floor directly overlooking the server room, with a clear vantage point of where I’ll be standing. If anybody comes that way, they will have a clear look at me, with my back to them. So somebody needs to be standing lookout there.”

    Looking at the blueprint too, Kate can see that Yelena is right. With a nod, she agrees and pulls out a notepad to start drawing out their plans.

    “Okay, then at 1 am, you two rappel over from the taller building, get into the elevator shaft, and get down. Sonya, you get out on the 33rd floor and take a position on the gallery and stand watch, and -“ “Is that a handbag?”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate glances at Sonya before looking back down at her drawing. “No, that’s you.”

    “That looks nothing like me.”

    Kate huffs, throwing Sonya an annoyed look, who has the audacity to look openly amused. “Okay, this is not an art project. I am just trying to explain the plan.” From her right, Yelena points at one of the buildings on her drawing.

    “Is this me? I look very stocky.”

    Mouth dropping open, Kate looks back at her in bewilderment.

    “No? That’s obviously a building from above. It’s like a-”

    Yelena’s eyebrows furrow but Kate can see the barely hidden smile in the corner of her mouth, and she huffs in annoyance.

    “Then where am I? Is this me?”

    Pursing her lips in annoyance, Kate glares at her before she answers.

    “No! That is the AC system’s entrance. This is…”

    The grin threatening to overtake Yelena’s features becomes stronger, her eyes glinting with amusement. Sonya chimes in from the side again.

    “Oh, I thought that was a cat.”

    Kate huffs looking from one Widow to the other.

    “What? No! Uh…”

    Yelena finally grins, and on Kate’s left, Sonya laughs out loud. Kate just sighs deeply. “Are you two done?”

    The grin on Yelena’s face is tempered into a smile, and her gaze is warm, as she looks back at Kate.

    “Go on.”

    One last time, Kate huffs but she can’t help the smile tugging at the corner of her lips at Yelena’s affectionate look.

    “Right, uh. Where was I... Um, okay, Yelena, you get out on the 32nd and wait for the alarm to sound. At 1:15, I rappel over from the northeast, break a window close to the vault, cause havoc, and draw the guards. Yelena, you get into the server room, do your thing and-“ “Kate, have you ever rappelled over to a building with sheer glass windows and got in?” Yelena’s question breaks Kate’s rhythm and she pauses, glancing up at her. “I mean, um, no, not yet. But I-“ Sonya speaks from the other side.

    “I have. About a hundred times.”

    Sighing, Kate furrows her brow.

    “I can do it, I have rappelled building to building before.”

    Yelena doesn’t need to know that the time she is talking about is the first time they have met. It is a testament to how much their relationship has improved that Yelena only smiles slightly, and Kate doesn’t feel annoyed at her words either.

    “I am sure you can. But it is probably best if the first time is not the mission.” Pursing her lips, Kate tries to mask her disappointment.

    Being the distraction is the most dangerous part of this mission and she really doesn’t want to put it on Sonya, who already wanted out of this life and retired and it’s really not her fight and-

    “Also, Sonya is a really shit lookout.”

    Blinking out of her slightly frustrated thoughts, Kate looks at Yelena, then Sonya. “I really am.”

    She says it with a shrug but Kate worries her bottom lip with her teeth. She wants to say she is a shit lookout too, but Sonya continues before she can.

    “Honestly, you’d be doing me a favor. Last time I was the lookout and the driver, so it’s really my turn to get in on some of the excitement.”

    Exhaling, Kate accepts her defeat.

    “Okay, um…I guess I’ll be the lookout then.”

    Sonya pats her left shoulder blade with a smile.

    “Okay, now. How do we get out?”

    Pursing her lips, Kate turns back to the blueprints with a nod. It takes her a second to pick up where she left off.

    “Um, right. Uh, so then I guess you draw the guards away, preferably to another floor, and keep them entertained as long as you can, knock some of them out, and then make your escape by circling back to the same spot or down one of the stairways. Yelena and I will stay until the transfer is complete, then make our way back to the elevator, up the shaft, and leave the same way we entered.”

    Looking up to the right, Kate finds Yelena looking at her, instead of the plans before turning back to the plans and speaking again.

    “We will still need a plan B. We will bring a change of clothes, and if things go to shit, we will hide out in one of the offices on the upper or lower levels, and leave once the offices open for the day. Kate, can you get a list of what companies have offices in the building?” Nodding, Kate reaches for the stack of papers on the coffee table.

    “Already got it.”

    It takes her a couple of seconds to find the right file and pull it out. “Okay, so the 31st is still Limitless and the 30th floor is an event hall so not those, but the 29th and 28th are both a digital marketing agency, so we can probably use those. Or the 34th and 35th which are offices of a hedge fund.”

    Sonya hums in affirmation, pointing at a spot on the 31st floor’s blueprint. “There is a balcony here. This will probably be my exit point, but we will have to check what’s across from it.”

    The rest of the afternoon is spent ironing out the details of their plan and the next morning Sonya and Yelena go to pick up the rest of the gear they will need, while Kate sorts out her own and waits for the delivery of the DNA data storage drive that Yelena had arranged for them.

    Of course, Kate wanted to tag along, but as Yelena reminded her, she was still very much hunted so for better or worse Kate is left to her own devices at home, slightly grumpy at being left out, and spends the day going over the details again and again. The three of them decided that it was best to do it as soon as possible since each day that passed would increase the risk of Fisk finding the formula. Which means, they are doing it tonight. They also agreed that once the transfer is done, Yelena would install a virus onto the server that would wipe it of its contents a couple of days later, once they surely got away scot-free.

    The heist gives Kate the opportunity to try out a new, wholly black suit that she has never worn before, and that her superhero-suit-person, Luke designed for her a few months back. After lunch, which Kate cooks for herself for once (okay, “cooking” is a bit of an overstatement, it’s frozen pizza made in the oven), she takes out her most compact bow and checks that it’s working for sure. It’s basically barely more than just a handle, similar to the sword she usually carries, but at the press of a button, it extends to a full-sized bow and even automatically strings itself. The design is something Kate is pretty proud of but after her glasses kind of failed on the ship due to not expecting some of the circumstances of a real-life mission, she wants to be extra sure even if this is something she has taken out to the field before.

    Around 2 pm, the courier arrives with the package holding the DNA drive, and Kate texts Yelena to let her know “the package is secure” and receives a thumbs-up emoji in answer but nothing more. She does her best not to be frustrated at the lack of attention but is thankful that nobody is around to see her pouting for a good 5 minutes, once she realizes that is all the answer she is going to have.

    Then, Kate selects 20 compact but normal arrows, and 15 compact versions of her trick arrows. They all agreed that if everything goes according to plan, it was best that Kate didn’t use a bow and arrows on this mission at all, or any weapon for that matter, with the attention from the FBI currently on her, but for emergencies, she still plans to bring them along, as her only form of ranged combat.

    Finally, Kate cleans, oils, and sharpens her retractable sword, during which is when Yelena and Sonya arrive back from their trip.

    Kate hears the keys jingling and doesn’t even stand up, knowing it will be them from the muffled voices through the door. Lucky, who has been snoozing next to her on the couch, lifts his head, looks at Kate with his head tilted and she can’t help but smile at his one-eyed, curious gaze. In a second, he is up and there to greet Yelena as she steps through the door, his tail swishing from side to side.

    “Hello handsome”

    Yelena receives his enthusiastic greetings cheerfully, eyes seeking out Kate on the couch a second later.

    “Well, don’t you look formidable?”

    As Pizza Dog’s attention shifts to Sonya, entering the flat behind her, Yelena steps towards Kate with a grin. Kate smiles back, retracting her sword and leaning forward to put that and her abrasive on the coffee table before she stands up and steps towards Yelena as well. “Oh yeah, Danger is my middle name.”

    Taking the two heavy bags from Yelena’s shoulder and hand, Kate walks to where her own gear is in a sports bag, ready to go.

    “I thought it was Elizabeth.”

    Kate rolls her eyes and turns back to give Yelena a look and finds her smiling widely still, enjoying her own joke.

    “How was it? You got everything?”

    Deciding to ignore Yelena shooting down her admittedly corny joke with her own even worse one, Kate asks that, but instead of answering her, Sonya cuts in, her voice filled with mock offense.

    “How come you are not helping me with my bags also?”

    Momentarily befuddled with the question, Kate gapes at her for a second, eyes jumping at Yelena but Sonya just laughs at her expression, obviously not actually interested in the answer.

    “Not very chivalrous of you, Kate Bishop.”

    Yelena tuts from the side and Kate sighs, before pursing her lips with a shake of her head. “I have two hands and one pretend-fiancé, okay?”

    Sonya chuckles and Yelena grins too.

    “Touché.”

    Sonya walks by her with a wink, throwing her own bags onto the growing pile of gear. “So, did you get everything you need?”

    Yelena looks back at Kate with sparkling eyes for a second, before she nods. “Yes. We got a great deal too.”

    Kate just nods, indulging in checking Yelena out while she takes off her coat and walks over to the couch to take a seat. She is wearing black jeans and a tight, long-sleeved tan top, which makes it obvious that she is not wearing a bra. Again. A throat is cleared and Kate’s eyes jump up to Yelena’s, who has an eyebrow lifted but Kate doesn’t have it in her to feel embarrassed. Shrugging she smiles at Yelena, the exchange leaving her slightly wired, especially when her smile is returned with a slightly smug one from Yelena. “Do you have everything you need?”

    At Sonya’s question, Kate turns towards her, nodding but mentally still in the moment with Yelena.

    “Should we go over the gear you need?”

    Rolling her eyes Kate turns back to Yelena, pining her with a half-amused, half-annoyed look.

    “I don’t need you to babysit me.”

    The same eyebrow is lifted again, and Yelena leans back and Kate could swear she puffs out her chest a little, which absolutely takes away the brunt of her next words. “Have you broken into many high-security corporate offices before?”

    It’s said with a slightly teasing tone, another smug smile on Yelena’s lips, and an amused spark in her eyes. Wetting her lips, Kate looks at her for a second longer before admitting with a purse of her lips.

    “Nope.”

    The smug smile widens, before Yelena blinks, glancing at Sonya and then back at Kate. “Right. So. Do you have gloves?”

    “Yes.”

    “A mask that covers your face.”

    Kate nods in confirmation.

    “Yup.”

    “A weapon that will not immediately lead back to you, if you need to use it?” That takes a beat to answer and Kate stuffs her hands into the pocket of her sweats as she shifts her weight from one leg to the other.

    “I, uh…I have my sword.”

    Yelena’s eyebrows furrow slightly, the smile dimming. Without a word, she stands up and lifts the sofa cushion that she was sitting on. Under it, is a gun that Yelena checks the magazine of, before walking up to Kate. Turning the gun around, she holds it out to Kate, offering her the grip. Kate looks down at it but doesn’t reach out, then looks back up at Yelena.

    “I don’t want this.”

    Yelena purses her lips, this time in barely disguised annoyance instead of amusement. “Well, you can not use your arrows. So…”

    Kate glances down at the gun and then at Yelena again.

    “I don’t like guns.”

    With a deep sigh, Yelena continues to look at her, looking more unimpressed by the minute. “Do you like living?”

    The chuckle rises from Kate’s chest mostly unconsciously, and partially in discomfort. Meanwhile, Sonya slips by Kate, apparently happy to let them hash this out, and takes a seat on one of the armchairs.

    “Yeah, I like living. But-”

    Leaning closer, Yelena looks into her eyes so deep that Kate swallows the rest of her sentence.

    “Then take the gun. I know you know how to use it.”

    Yelena’s voice drops an octave as she speaks, and Kate can’t help the way it makes her stomach do a backflip as well. With a deep sigh, Kate reaches out for the gun, touching Yelena’s hand as she does.

    “Uh, fine. But I won’t use it.”

    With a pointed eye-roll, Yelena turns away and Kate checks the chamber and then the safety, before putting it on her pile of things as well while Yelena retakes her seat on the couch. “Bring along some throwing knives too, if you are not comfortable.”

    At Sonya’s words, Kate nods, making a mental note to add those to their gear later. “Okay. Let’s go over the schedule. It’s…”

    Sonya checks her phone for the time, before speaking again.

    “3:24 pm, we have a bit over 7 hours until we have to leave. You will drop me off on the corner of Lexington and 59th, park, and then take your position. Have you eaten?” Kate is surprised by the suddenly different-themed question and needs to blink twice before she answers.

    “Um. Yeah, I had a pizza earlier.”

    Sonya nods and then shakes her head, apparently dissatisfied with Kate’s choice of food. “Eat before we leave. Something with protein. And take a nap.”

    Kate can’t help but smile, doing a little mock salute at her.

    “Yes ma’am.”

    Sonya smiles at Kate's antics, and she and Yelena stand up after exchanging a look and a nod at each other. They begin walking out, and Kate sighs, pushing down on the feeling of disappointment at already having to see them leave. Looking at him, Lucky seems almost equally disappointed and Kate calls out after Sonya.

    “Hey, do you think Tommy can look after Lucky tonight while we are gone? Just in case we get held up somewhere.”

    Sonya nods at her with a smile.

    “Oh yes, I think he would be happy to.”

    Leaning back against the couch, Kate watches them put on their coats.

    “Thanks!”

    Yelena pulls on her coat but she turns back to Kate for a moment too.

    “And Kate?”

    She is smiling at Kate again who doesn’t miss the opportunity to check out the outfit one last time.

    “Yep?

    “I hope I do not have to say this, but no phone or wallet on this mission, okay?” Huffing, Kate wants to roll her eyes but she only nods with a self-deprecating smile, accepting the teasing comment as justified, after the whole FBI thing.

    “Noted.”

    Yelena nods back at her, holding her eyes with a smile.

    “See you in a couple of hours.”

    The smile makes Kate’s stomach do a somersault again as it often does nowadays and she bites down slightly on her lip as she looks back at Yelena before speaking. “See you.”

    After a second, remembering herself, Kate looks at Sonya too, giving her a smile as well. “See you, Sonya.”

    Her answer is an eye-roll, a grin, and a shake of Sonya’s head as she turns away with a sigh. “Bye Kate.”

    The two Widows leave, and Kate is left alone again, only a few minutes after their arrival. She decides to take Sonya’s advice, and holes up in her bedroom for a nap with Lucky, but feels too wired to fall asleep, constantly going over the details of their plan. She twists and turns for the better part of an hour, before giving up and getting out of bed. To pass the time, Kate takes Lucky for a quick walk around the block, then takes a shower. She orders some food around half past 5 and looks over the blueprints one last time to make sure she is as familiar with the layout as she can be. After her food arrives, Thai this time, she sets the plans aside and puts on a movie while she eats.

    It’s an action movie, kind of dumb but entertaining enough that she doesn’t feel the urge to pick up her phone and scroll through social media even once she is done eating. With the food making her feel pleasantly full and warm, Kate turns to the side, extending her legs to stretch out fully and before she knows it, the nap that escaped her earlier is finally catching up to her.

    It’s not the most relaxing few hours of sleep, Kate waking up once to Lucky joining her on the couch, trying to lie down on her stomach, and then to a chime of her phone that turns out to be nothing but a text from Jack about some additions to the guest list to his party she is not in the right mental state to comprehend.

    Still, Kate wakes up around 9, feeling better rested than she was before, and while the wired energy is not gone from her muscles, the nap helped to calm her nerves before the mission. Kate makes a coffee, drinks it, and decides that it’s time to start to get dressed, as Yelena and Sonya will be over in twenty minutes at most to get ready too.

    First, Kate pours Lucky’s dinner into his bowl, giving his head a pat as he races into the kitchen to wolf it down, then she walks back to the living room, grabs her new suit, and takes it into her bedroom to put on.

    Taking off her burgundy sweats and the matching sweatshirt, Kate switches her sports bra for a tighter one, then pulls on the leggings. They are thick, yet very light, apparently able to withstand cuts or even a direct stab with a knife, and have comfortable, thick padding at her knees. Next, Kate puts on a black tank top as a kind of undershirt, to go under the top of her suit, tucking it into the trousers.

    After that comes the top part of the suit, with a hidden zipper under one arm that makes it kind of awkward to put on but more practical than if it was on her back, and more aesthetic than if it was on the front. The top doesn’t have Kate’s logo on it, specifically designed for missions where she has to go under the radar, and it has a dark purple, warm, removable inner lining that she is sure she will be thankful for on top of the skyscraper in a few hours. The outside is made out of a strong nanotextile, that’s able to withstand most bullets, apart from very high caliber ones or ones shot at her point-blank, and there is faux-leather padding on the shoulders and upper arms, that makes the jacket a bit less tactical, and more luxurious looking, and also serve to make Kate look a bit more imposing. (The idea might have come to Kate after seeing footage of herself in the Ronin suit.) There are a couple of hidden straps that Kate fiddles around with, to make the fit perfect, before adding the final parts of her ensemble, the accessories.

    The first one is a tactical belt which will carry her retractable sword on the right and some extra trick arrowheads on the left. Her almost non-existent quiver, which is essentially a hard- lined, extra container on her back is strapped onto her back by thick straps that go across her chest from her right shoulder to the left side of her torso. Kate fits the collapsed arrows inside to be hidden until she needs them which she hopefully won’t this evening. As the final piece, Kate straps a thigh-holster to each of her legs. One will hold a tactical knife, the other the gun that Yelena gave her earlier, but Kate is adamant that she will not use it. The true last bits, of course, will be the combat boots, gloves, and mask, but those will only come later.

    Once dressed, Kate puts her hair in a loose ponytail and considers putting on some dark shading around her eyes to go with her mask, when she hears the front door open. Sticking her head out of the bathroom, Kate checks that it’s Yelena and Sonya.

    “Hi! I’ll be out in a minute!”

    Yelena and Sonya are in their tactical gear too, Sonya’s hair braided into two parts that come down by her shoulders onto her chest, and Yelena’s in one that hangs down her upper back. Over her top, Yelena wears a black tactical vest, and there are multiple holsters with various guns, knives, and other weapons strapped onto both Widows.

    “Are you ready?”

    Kate ducks back into the bedroom as Yelena asks her in lieu of a greeting, to put her phone on the charger while she is gone, before stepping out into the living room for good. “Yeah, I just need about 3 minutes to put my shoes on and stuff.”

    Yelena nods, looking Kate up and down with an appreciative smile, and then begins to look through their gear in one of the bags, while Sonya asks from the side.

    “Have you eaten?”

    As Kate straps the knife and the gun in place in her thigh-holsters, standing by Yelena’s side, she nods at Sonya with a smile.

    “Yeah. Had a nap too.”

    There is a knock on the front door, and Kate blinks in surprise, momentarily confused about who it could be. Sonya answers her unspoken question as she walks over to open it. “It’s Tommy. He is here for Lucky.”

    “Ah, yeah, okay.”

    Kate resumes loading up her weapons, her retractable sword on the right side of her hip while her collapsible bow goes onto her back.

    “Wow.-”

    Turning towards the voice, Kate looks at Thomas who is looking them over while he crouches next to Lucky, patting his head.

    “I don’t think I will ever get used to seeing you guys like this.”

    Chuckling at Tommy’s words, Kate looks over their little group too, taking a moment to note how not-normal their appearance is. Their life too, but that’s not a thought to really get into right now.

    “We look pretty cool, huh?”

    As Yelena stands up from her bag, Kate meets her eyes for a second, not missing the way they drop to look her up and down again, a slight smile playing on her lips. “Very cool. And very intimidating.”

    Tommy’s voice is amused, and Kate’s attention is drawn to him again, a grin sliding onto her face.

    “Has he eaten?”

    Lucky looks up at Tommy with innocent eyes, trying to sell his hunger but his ploy is almost immediately crushed by Kate’s affirmative.

    “Yeah. He had dinner about twenty minutes ago. We went for a short walk earlier too.” As Kate walks back to her lair, she gives Lucky’s head an apologetic pat, his doggy smile not dimming despite his foiled plans. Inside, she picks up the tactical boots that go with her suit and walks back to the couch to put them on. Once she is done lacing them up, Kate stands up, taking note of all members of their little unit.

    “’Kay. I think I’m ready.”

    While Kate walks up to their bags, Tommy puts a collar and leash on Lucky and Yelena starts counting on her fingers.

    “Do you have your mask and gloves?”

    Kate sighs deeply at being babysat again but answers Yelena nonetheless. “Yep.”

    Sonya walks up to the bags as well, picking one up.

    “Where are your phone and wallet?”

    With a grin, Kate picks up her own bag and one of the Widows’ as well.

    “On my bedside table.”

    Yelena smiles back.

    “Amazing. Did you pack comms?”

    “Yeah, they are in the bag.”

    Kate jostles the bag in question on her shoulder and gives a nod too.

    “Did you pack a change of clothes for plan B?”

    Nodding again, Kate smiles at Yelena, who smiles back before nodding again, looking over at Sonya and then Tommy.

    “Okay. Then we are good to go.”

    With that, Yelena walks up and picks up the last bag too. Tommy opens the door, and Yelena and Sonya follow him and Lucky out, with Kate leaving last, locking the door behind the team.

    Lucky seemingly thinks they are all going on an adventure together, his tail wagging from left to right and tongue lolling out to the side as he looks from one person to the other. Kate smiles down at him as they all file into the elevator, the cabin a bit tight for the four adults and one dog. Distractedly she considers that it’s probably a good thing that nobody else gets in or calls the elevator while they are in there, armed to the teeth and loaded with bags of tactical gear.

    Tommy and Lucky get out on the 13th floor, and Pizza Dog is obviously confused about what’s happening but his enthusiasm about his evening plans is not curbed at all, as he follows Tommy with his tail wagging, looking back at the three waving women with a wide doggy-smile. Kate smiles at him as the doors close and Yelena, Sonya, and her make their way down to the garage. Once in there, Kate pauses in front of the little car-key wardrobe on the wall to think about which car to choose.

    “It does not matter what we take. We will switch on the way.”

    Kate is only surprised for a second before she nods, picking up the keys for a black Mercedes that used to belong to her mom. It’s kind of ironic, taking her mom’s car to steal her mom’s super-soldier formula from her mum’s mob boss partner.

    “Ookay. Just let me know where I’m going.”

    For once, neither Widow challenges her driving, both of them getting into the backseat after they pile their bags into the car’s trunk. The engine is turned on with the press of a button and soon, they are driving up the ramp leading out of the building.

    “I could get used to having my personal chauffeur.”

    Sonya proclaims from the backseat and Kate snorts, looking at her, and then Yelena in the rearview mirror as she touches her key fob to the sensor, opening the garage door. “Where to?”

    “Just get to Park Avenue and keep going towards Harlem. There is a parking lot on the corner of Park and the 119th, we will switch there.”

    Nodding, Kate checks left and right before she pulls out of the garage, for once not needing to navigate too much traffic due to the late hour. There is no music playing this time, as Kate tries to get into the right headspace for the mission, while she assumes Sonya and Yelena do the same.

    The last three missions they went on, to the storage unit, the ship, and Amanda’s “interrogation”/date have all gone to various degrees of shit, and Kate really hopes they will break their streak of bad luck this time around while she can’t help but feel a bit nervous. It only takes about ten minutes for them to reach the destination and soon Sonya leans forward to point to a parking lot on the left side of the road.

    “Here. Park next to that blue van.”

    The van in question has “Russian-Doll Cleaning Services” written on its side and Kate snorts at the implication, eyes meeting Yelena’s in the rearview mirror.

    “Russian-Doll, really?”

    Amusement shines in Yelena’s eyes but it’s Sonya who answers.

    “It is a very special van.”

    Kate hums as she pulls into the open spot next to it, shutting off the engine. “How so?”

    Her answer is only a mysterious “You’ll see.” from Sonya, then the three of them are getting out of the car. Popping open the trunk, Kate looks around but the east-Harlem streets around them are deserted, and while there are some dim streetlights around the parking lot, none directly above them. Kate grabs two bags, while Sonya opens the back of the van and then steps back to let Yelena grab hers too.

    When she steps over to the van, Kate’s eyebrows furrow, the back certainly not explaining what Sonya meant by the van being special. With a mostly internal shrug, she loads her bags into the back and takes Yelena’s and Sonya’s too before closing the doors and following Sonya to the right side of the vehicle.

    Kate locks her car as she gets into the back seat of the van, while Sonya takes the front passenger seat next to Yelena. The engine is turned off with a traditional twist of a key and they begin to pull out of the spot before Kate is bored of the silence, now that she isn’t driving and her curiosity gets the better of her.

    “So. Why is this van special?”

    While she can only see the side of Yelena’s face from the back, Kate sees the way her cheeks lift as she smiles, glancing at Sonya to her right. Sonya does turn around to glance at Kate with a grin before she turns back.

    “We will have to wait for a CCTV blindspot to show you.”

    Kate lifts her eyebrows before she furrows them, distractedly putting on her seatbelt. “How will you know when is that?”

    Pointing at the hazard warning button on the dashboard, Sonya explains without turning back.

    “Just keep watching that.”

    Kate does and in a few blocks when they stop at a corner, the button lights up green. “Whaaaat? What does that-“ “Now watch the side of the car in the side mirror.”

    Following Sonya’s instructions, Kate looks at the mirror while she sees Sonya hit the button from the corner of her eyes. As soon as the button is pushed, the blue paint and sign on the side of the van flicker, almost like a screen and suddenly, the van is green and while Kate can’t make out the new sign and logo, it’s obviously a different one from the first. “What the…How?”

    Yelena and Sonya both chuckle at Kate’s obvious wonder. Yelena takes a turn to the left while Sonya explains.

    “I did a brief stint as an acquirer of rare art pieces. I used it for that, but it’s been standing unused for a year now.”

    An acquirer of…

    “You were an art thief?!”

    Sonya’s answering look in the rearview mirror is one of pure delight.

    “Yes. It paid well, but it was incredibly boring so…”

    Blinking, Kate shakes her head.

    “Okkkaaay, and where did you get this car? I mean, this is…wow. How does it work?” Shrugging, Sonya watches the buildings pass them by for a second, the lights on the streets rhythmically painting the two Widows golden.

    “I think it’s a copy of some military tech with nanites…”

    Sonya pauses for a second, pointing to a street for Yelena to take.

    “-I got a great price for it because the man who sold it was very keen to get rid of it, so it’s most likely stolen.”

    As Kate processes, Sonya trails off, watching the buildings and streets go by, before she speaks again, almost as an afterthought.

    “It changes the license plates too, so we do not have to worry about that either.”

    Kate just puffs out her cheeks, exhaling slowly.

    “That’s insanely cool. You will have to let me check it out later.”

    There is an amused noise from the front seat, before Sonya answers.

    “Sure.”

    The rest of their journey, also only about fifteen minutes, is spent mostly in silence. Kate rotates her shoulders while tamping down on the urge to tap her feet or bounce her knees, and soon, it’s time for Sonya to get out.

    Yelena pulls to the side on the corner of Lexington, where the hazard warning button lights up green and Sonya looks at her watch and then both of them before speaking. “Comms go live in 15 minutes. Good luck.”

    Yelena nods and waves for Sonya to go, and Kate gives a smile to her as she gets out, winking at Kate playfully as she does. They wait for her to get her bag from the back, and she slaps the side of the van twice when she is done and the doors are closed again. Yelena and Kate drive another two blocks, before Yelena parks the van in another CCTV blindspot and shuts off the engine. She makes no move to get out and meets Kate’s eyes after a second.

    “Are you good to go?”

    “Yeah, yeah, I’m ready.”

    Yelena turns around to look at her directly, her gaze warm and amused at Kate’s enthusiasm. “I probably should have asked this before, but you do not have a terrible fear of heights, right?”

    Snorting, Kate looks back at her, appreciating the way the streetlights cast shadows on Yelena’s gorgeous features.

    “No more than a rational amount.”

    Yelena grins at Kate’s answer, her teeth glinting in the dimly-lit car, nodding to herself. “Okay, good.”

    They get out of the van then and get their bags from the back after Yelena puts on a long coat and Kate pulls on an oversized black hoodie and a baseball cap, both to cover their tactical outfits and hopefully help hide their identities without arousing suspicion. Kate puts one black tactical bag on her shoulders and the other in her hands and lets Yelena lead the way. Of course, life would be too easy if they could walk directly into the building they have to get into, so the door that Yelena leads Kate to, is the service entrance of a French restaurant three buildings down from the sleek, dark, and angled skyscraper that is home to Limitless Corp’s headquarters.

    The establishment is at the bottom of another skyscraper, almost identical to the one they are planning to break into and it’s still open, but there is nobody at the back door at that moment and they enter the building without an issue.

    Inside they walk through a corridor that looks grimy enough that Kate has to wonder about the sanitary conditions of the kitchen, but it might be the cold, almost gray lighting painting the place so grim. They take a left and enter a different hallway where they pass two haggard- looking guys, who pass them by without giving them a second (or even first) glance. That corridor leads them to a freight elevator that takes about three minutes to arrive, and Kate and Yelena file in, not speaking a single word as the doors close.

    The elevator is creaky, especially for such a modern-looking building. Here the lights are so artificial and so white, they bother Kate’s eyes so she focuses on trying to make out the various scribbled notes on the scratched-up and tagged metal walls. E+N in a heart. Wow, what a romantic place to commemorate a budding relationship. Next to it is a semi-realistic drawing of a cockroach. Charming. To the left, there is a sentence “Jessica sucked my-“ but the object of the said sucking is covered by a sticker of a skateboarding raccoon. At least that is cute.

    The doors open on the 19th floor, and Kate and Yelena come face to face with a middle-aged Asian couple. Without thinking, Kate smiles at them, but neither of them returns it, looking at her and Yelena with disinterest mixed with distrust.

    “Going down?”

    The woman asks, accent thick and Kate’s expression turns apologetic.

    “No, up. Sorry!”

    Kate answers, her smile still in place but the Asian woman is already over her, almost rolling her eyes while turning away, and she begins or continues to speak to her counterpart in what Kate recognizes as Chinese, audibly agitated. Yelena in turn presses the button to close the doors and the Asian couple disappears from view in a few seconds.

    “Should we be worried about these people seeing us?”

    Yelena glances at her, shaking her head briefly.

    “If all goes well, nobody will know we were ever here.”

    Kate hums, already halfway distracted by Yelena’s scent that she just notices in the enclosed space. It’s sweet, maybe with a hint of vanilla but it’s not strong enough to be a perfume. It must be a body wash or a shampoo…

    Before Kate can stoop low enough that she does something to investigate, the elevator doors open and they arrive at their destination, which is the 40th floor of the building. Yelena leaves first, Kate following her a few steps behind and she leads them to a doorway on the other end of another very uninviting service corridor that opens to a staircase.

    Following Yelena, they go up another 2 levels before arriving at a door with several signs warning people from opening the roof access. As a born and raised New Yorker, Kate knows that the signs about an alarm are absolutely bullshit, and it only takes Yelena about ten seconds to pick the locks on the simple, faded-green door while Kate rummages around her pack for the signal-disrupter. The door unlocks but neither of them moves to open it just yet, as according to the security plans of this building, there is an actually functional camera above the door outside, monitoring roof access.

    Kate leans against the wall with her tablet, syncing up to the camera outside within a minute, and with one push of the button on the signal disrupter, the camera’s image is frozen. “We’re good to go.”

    Quickly, she pushes her tablet back into her bag and the small remote-like signal disrupter into her pocket then follows Yelena outside when she opens the door and steps through in a few seconds.

    The view is amazing from the rooftop, the building surrounded by other skyscrapers, and the dark sky lit up by the glowing lights of the city. The wind whips at their clothes viciously from the moment they are outside, and Kate is thankful for the warm lining of her suit as they quickly round the little shed-like structure on the roof to get out of the camera’s viewpoint. The two of them walk to the north side of the building and as Yelena puts down a heated blanket close to the edge, Kate presses the button again on her little remote, to unfreeze the camera’s image, now that they are out of its point of view. Crouching down by the blanket, Kate pulls out the little pack containing their commlinks, handing one to Yelena, before she slots one into her own ears and turns it on.

    “Comm-check.”

    Kate reaches for her back, pulls out her bow and a wire arrow, and lays them on the gravelly ground next to the blanket, along with her mask to use later before. With preparations out of the way, she lies down on her stomach next to Yelena, who is already watching the building across with a pair of binoculars.

    “I’m not a commie.”

    Sonya’s voice comes through her ear as clearly, as if she was standing next to them and Kate smiles, having been worried that they might have a problem with almost a mile between their respective positions.

    “Good to know.”

    Next to Kate, Yelena pulls back the arm of her coat to check the time.

    “It’s 12:06. T minus 24 minutes until go-time.”

    For the next couple of minutes, Kate and Yelena lie on the rooftop, with no words spoken between them. The wind drowns out most sounds of the city, but a couple of sirens and the general noise of the city, hundreds of thousands of people just existing, can still be heard. “What time is it?”

    Breaking the silence after what must have been like 15 minutes at least, Kate turns her head to look at Yelena. She snorts, before putting her binoculars down and pulling back the sleeve of her coat again, while Kate realizes what she thought was a watch is actually a tiny screen on the bottom part of Yelena’s Widow Bite.

    “12:09. Be patient.”

    Kate huffs, while Sonya snorts in her ear, clearly amused as well.

    “We could play I spy to pass the time.”

    At Sonya’s words, Yelena chuckles and Kate purses her lips but her smile is pretty much impossible to stifle as well. She really would be lying if she said she didn’t enjoy working with the Widows.

    Looking around, Kate looks for something they would all see, while Yelena rummages in her bag while still lying down. There is a car on the far-off corner of the street below that Sonya could potentially see too, so Kate gives it a go.

    “I spy with my little eye, something blue.”

    There is a brief silence on the comms channel and as she glances to the side, Kate notices Yelena staring at her face with something akin to disbelief mixed with amusement, eyebrows drawn up to her hairline.

    “Jesus Kate…I was joking.”

    Hopefully, the wind cutting into her skin masks Kate’s blush but she laughs a bit awkwardly, before answering Sonya.

    “Me too…Obviously.”

    There is more silence after that and Kate doesn’t look at Yelena again for a while in hopes of avoiding the slightly mocking amusement she is sure she would find there. Another 30 minutes go by before Kate asks again.

    “What about now?”

    With a deep sigh, Yelena checks the time again, and even in the dark, with only the city lights below to illuminate her features, Kate can see the smug smile on her lips before she speaks again.

    “12:15. Fifteen minutes to go.”

    After another minute or two, Yelena starts moving around and Kate is bored enough to not even pretend to not watch her.

    “What are you doing?”

    “Preparations.”

    Rising on her elbows, Yelena smooths down on her hair, a little messed up by the strong wind on the roof before she begins to pull on her mask. The mask is one Kate knows or at least has seen once before: a plain black mask that covers the entirety of Yelena’s face, complete with the green night vision goggles she wore on the night Kate first met her. Following her lead, Kate pulls her baseball cap and hoodie off, only getting stuck with her arms above her head for a short (but slightly embarrassing) moment before she reaches for her own mask. Similarly to her black suit, it was somewhat inspired by Clint’s Ronin suit, complete with a black hood that attaches to the collar of the suit to stay on while she is in motion.

    As opposed to Yelena, Kate leaves her eyes free and lies back down once she is done, next to Yelena. That whole ordeal has only kept her busy for about a minute, so they still have at least 13-14 minutes before the mission starts. To distract herself from her nervousness, Kate glances at Yelena again and again, but the expressionless mask and goggles are more off- putting than she would have thought.

    She lasts about another 3 minutes before speaking again.

    “So…”

    Yelena turns her head to look at her, and Kate swears there is judgment in the eerie green lights of her goggles.

    “Are you going to wear that the whole time?”

    Finishing the question doesn’t reduces the intensity of the disparaging vibes coming from Yelena.

    “Wear what?”

    Shuffling around to point at Yelena’s face, despite only a few inches of space between the two of them, Kate gestures at the mask.

    “That. The mask. With the um, goggles.”

    There is another beat of silence. Yelena’s face might be covered, and as a result, emotionless, but Kate can hear the exasperated amusement in her voice when she asks a second later. “What is your problem with my mask?”

    Putting her hands up in a somewhat limited capacity, Kate backtracks a little. “Nothing! Nothing, just…It kinda feels like I’m on a mission with a mummy.” In her ear, Sonya snorts loudly and Kate just knows she is about to make an inappropriate mommy joke but Yelena speaks first.

    “Says the woman routinely walking around dressed like a giant eggplant emoji.” Narrowing her eyes, Kate tries to read Yelena’s covered features. Unsurprisingly, she is not successful.

    “Are you calling me a dick?”

    Sonya snickers in her ear, but Yelena is silent for a long moment, before tilting her head and shrugging, shoulder rising and dropping with the motion. Her voice is thick and warm with her amusement, like honey.

    “If the shoe fits.”

    This causes Sonya to laugh loudly in her ear, while Kate exclaims, attempting to lightly jab Yelena’s ribs with her elbow.

    “Heey!”

    Unsurprisingly, Yelena twists out of her way easily and Kate just huffs, not attempting the jab again. Yelena chuckles too then, the sound low and sultry, making Kate quickly forget that she is supposed to be mad.

    “Well, I was going to say I’m just missing out on seeing your face but whatever.” Sonya snorts again and Yelena sighs, seemingly watching Kate’s face for a long moment. “It is practical. It covers my entire face.”

    Pausing for a moment, Yelena takes a breath and continues, her voice filling with amusement again as she continues.

    “Some of us actually care about keeping our identities secret in this business.” Gasping in mock offense, Kate shakes her head, looking back at the artificial green light of Yelena’s goggles.

    “What, I have a mask too, I am wearing all black. Nobody will know who I am. I’m like, completely undetectable.”

    If the goggles could blink, Kate is sure they would blink back at her unimpressed. “…You are carrying a bow and explosive arrows around. How many people do that in this day and age?"

    Rolling her eyes, Kate huffs, almost tempted to twist onto her back just to move around a little. The heated blanket can only offer so much heat in the turbulent wind and with their stillness, she can feel the cold settle into her muscles.

    “I…Uh. Well,-“ Taking mercy on her, Yelena hums amusedly, before knocking her shoulder against Kate’s gently.

    “Just try to stick to the sword, if you need to use something, yes? At least there are more than two people in the world running around using that. And the gun...Consider it." Nodding down at the gun strapped to Kate’s thigh, Yelena waits for her answer. Kate takes a second to mull it over before she speaks and she turns back to watch the building across for movement, more as a distraction than anything.

    “I will stick to the sword but I am making no promises on the gun.”

    Her only answer is a somewhat amused but mostly resigned sigh from Yelena and a shake of her mask-covered head.

    “It was worth a try.”

    Sonya’s voice is amused as well, speaking into Kate’s ear. There is an especially strong gust of wind and Kate could swear she sees Yelena shiver for a moment. Without thinking much about it, Kate shuffles closer, and several minutes pass again without either of them speaking. Yelena watches through her goggles, and Kate reaches over to take the binoculars, counting down from the top of the building across to see which rows of windows belong to Limitless, but the levels all seem dark and abandoned.

    Yelena’s Widow Bite pings once, and barely a second later, she is in motion. “It is time.”

    Only a heartbeat behind Yelena, Kate stands up, reaching for her bow and wire arrow. With the push of a button, the bow is opened and strung up, and Kate is nocking the cable arrow, taking into account the strong wind without much conscious thought as she aims across the wide gap at the top of the building on the other side.

    Kate’s arrow lands exactly where she wanted it to, embedding itself into the mirroring shed- like structure on the building across, and in about a minute, she has the other end attached to the building on their side, completing the creation of their zipline across. As the first order of business, Yelena attaches their bags to the zipline, on wires and carabines of their own, and attaches a long rope that she ties to her own waist. What feels like only seconds later, she attaches herself to the zipline as well and jumps off the edge with little fanfare. Kate watches Yelena’s form get smaller as she sails across the empty air between the two buildings, the zipline swaying slightly with the wind and her weight. The pile of rope that ties her to their bags lifts and unravels neatly, never going so taunt that it would slow down Yelena’s journey across and she almost disappears into the darkness. If it wasn’t for Kate’s hawk-like vision (no pun intended), she wouldn’t be able to see Yelena make it to the other side but she does, and before long the bags are pulled across as well and it’s Kate’s turn to go.

    “Be careful with your landing. You are going to come in pretty fast.”

    Nodding at Yelena’s words in her ear, Kate begins her preparations.

    “Yeah, okay. Noted.”

    Kate would love to say (lie) that her journey across is similarly cool and nonchalant, but already as she attaches her harness to the cable, her heart is beating furiously in her chest. It takes her a second to work up the courage to walk to the edge, and suddenly, the wind feels like it might pull her off before she is ready to go.

    “Kate?”

    Yelena’s voice is warm, if a little confused, now coming through her earpiece like Sonya’s. Gulping, Kate closes her eyes to take a moment to gather herself.

    “Yeah, one second.”

    A couple of seconds go by as Kate hypes herself up, finding it more difficult to make the jump now that there is no adrenaline pumping in her veins like there was at Rockefeller Center.

    “Any day now, Kate.”

    Despite her words, there is no mocking in Yelena’s tone, her voice calm and pleasant in Kate’s ears.

    “Okay. Okay... Okay, I’m coming.”

    Huffing, Kate exhales forcefully through her nose and opens her eyes. With a deep inhale, she braces herself and steps off the edge.

    The journey across is both faster and less scary than Kate anticipated, and internally she is proud of herself for not screaming this time. Below her, the wide street and another, smaller building fly by, the lights and shapes all blurring together. In what feels like a few seconds only, Kate is crossing over the edge on the other side, arriving in Yelena’s waiting arms. Literally.

    “Oof…I told you to slow down.”

    Having managed to almost knock Yelena over, Kate grabs onto her waist to steady both of them and chuckles somewhat awkwardly, holding onto her just a second longer to ground herself. In her ear, Kate hears Sonya’s expected snicker, but she is distracted by how bothered she is to not be able to see Yelena’s face with her mask and goggles on as they stand only inches away.

    “Sorry. I uh…”

    Yelena just chuckles quietly, untangling herself from Kate’s arms.

    “Yes, okay. Let’s move on.-“ Pausing, she checks the time on her wrist.

    “-We are two minutes behind schedule.”

    While Kate retrieves her wire arrow, putting it back into her quiver once it’s back in its collapsed form, Yelena disappears from next to her, looking for their entry point out of sight. Kate follows her a minute later, carrying their bags to the large metal tube that is the inflow point of the building’s air-conditioning system.

    Yelena has already disabled the opening’s security sensor by the time Kate makes her way there, and she is working on the screws that keep the grilled lid on top. Making herself useful, Kate gets their ropes from inside one of the bags and attaches them both to a pole nearby. By the time Yelena is ready, so is Kate, throwing the ropes into the now exposed entrance of the tube and beginning the motions of attaching herself to one of them.

    Their bags are lowered down the chute first, and barely a couple of minutes after their arrival on the roof, Kate follows Yelena into the dark tunnel, slowly lowering herself, while holding a flashlight in her mask-covered mouth. It’s uncomfortable at best and Kate has to stop to adjust it several times in fear of it dropping. Their journey down is only a few dozen feet though and Yelena snorts at her when Kate touches down next to her.

    “And that is why you wear goggles.”

    Rolling her eyes as she unattaches her harness from the rope, Kate shakes her head with a grin that is covered by her mask.

    “I never disputed their usefulness. Just the aesthetics.”

    Kate imagines Yelena rolling her eyes back at her as she turns away.

    “That is so typical.”

    Looking around, Kate takes in the tunnel system they have entered. Thankfully, it’s not small enough that they have to crawl around, but Kate will have to hunch when they continue their way toward the elevator shaft.

    Two of their bags stay on the floor of the tunnel, not needed until they need to make their exit later on (if they do come out this way) and the last one, containing only a few tools, more rolls of rope, and most importantly, the DNA data storage drive, goes onto Yelena’s back. “From here on out, no talking, only whispering if needed and soft steps, okay?” Nodding, Kate exhales.

    “Yeah, okay.”

    The aircon tunnels take them above the top level of the building and while, from the roof it seemed like there was not much security on there, they can never be sure. Yelena checks the time again before she starts walking down the tunnel, with Kate following close behind. After about two minutes, Kate’s neck starts cramping from her hunched walking form, but she sincerely doubts Yelena would be appreciative of her breaking the quiet rule to complain, so she just keeps walking.

    Soon, they arrive at the end of the tunnel, where it connects to the elevator shaft, signaled by a dim light at the end of the tunnel and by Yelena reaching back to put a hand on Kate’s stomach to keep her from walking into her. Almost entirely silently, she dugs into her backpack, pulling out another roll of ropes before turning back to Kate. “Are you ready?”

    Yelena’s words are soft and quiet, whispered into the small space separating them. Whispering back, Kate nods, looking into the goggles, an experience that still leaves her feeling dissatisfied.

    “Yeah. Yeah, I got you.”

    Stepping even closer, Kate slides her hand around Yelena’s waist, locking her fingers behind her back.

    “Do not drop me.”

    There is a touch of teasing amusement in Yelena’s quiet voice and Kate smiles, keeping her eyes on the top of the elevator shaft about ten feet above their heads. “I won’t. Promise.”

    Yelena leans out, back arching, out above the abyss below, throwing the first roll of rope above her head and over the beam that will hold their weight on their way down. Kate holds her tight, keeping Yelena from falling out of the tunnel and down the shaft below, planting her feet wide and strong on the floor of the tunnel and on both sides of Yelena’s, to keep their balance. Yelena skillfully grabs the other end of the rope before it falls down, and then repeats the process, holding onto both ends of the two sets of ropes.

    “Okay. You can pull me back now.”

    Kate does as she is told, stepping back from the ledge and pulling Yelena back against herself. Quietly, she clears her throat, the feeling of holding Yelena’s body against herself slightly distracting at a very inopportune time.

    “Come here often?”

    Kate jokes without thinking it over, barely above a whisper but smiling smugly behind her mask. Yelena huffs in amusement, pushing her gently away with soft, pressing hands against Kate’s torso.

    “Pfft. Not the best time to be playful, Kate.”

    Her dismissal is smoothed over by her hand squeezing Kate’s arm for a moment, and she lets Yelena go with a huffy chuckle of her own.

    “Hate to interrupt what I’m sure was a lovely moment, but you have 10 minutes.” Sonya’s voice is amused, but it has its intended effect and Kate quickly begins to attach herself to the rope that Yelena hands her a second later. Yelena goes first again, stepping over the ledge and into the elevator shaft, slowly lowering herself once she halts her swinging by planting a foot on a beam below.

    Kate steps up to the edge as well, looking down into the shaft. There are service lights on each level, above the elevator doors and right across, generating enough light that Kate can turn off her flashlight and pocket it before she follows Yelena, stepping into nothing as well. The shaft is constructed with a twin set of metal beams crossing it between every three levels with the elevator only actually moving in the middle, between the beams. Thankfully, this means that as long as Kate and Yelena stay in the space between the wall of the shaft and the beams, they do not have to worry about the elevator crushing them to death if it moves for some reason, even on the lower levels.

    The doors are on the other side of the shaft and as Kate slowly descends after Yelena, she keeps track of the levels by the numbers above them. On the 33rd floor, Yelena stops her descent and waits for Kate to catch up.

    Planting her feet on the metal beam below her, Kate swings forward a little to step on it while to her right, Yelena does the same. Once her stance is stable on the beam, Kate turns to Yelena, her years of gymnastic training and parkour helping her to remain confident in her footing.

    “Time?”

    Her whispered words sound echoey in the shaft, but Yelena gives no indication that she is too loud as she turns around and presents her backpack to Kate.

    “1:02. Almost right on time.”

    Pulling out her tablet, Kate unlocks it and syncs up to the camera closest to their position. It looks exactly at the doors that she is about to open, which thanks to their timing, do not have security posted in front of them.

    Reaching into her pocket, with a push of the button on her signal disrupter, Kate freezes the image. The camera’s signal also allows her to access the whole system right after, and with a few taps on her tablet, due to the relatively outdated security system of the building, all cameras on Limitless’ levels are frozen as well.

    “Alright. We are good to go.”

    Kate puts the tablet back into Yelena’s backpack, pulls out one of the door wedges, and pockets it before zipping the bag back up.

    “See you on the other side?”

    Turning around, Yelena meets her eyes. At least Kate assumes, as the green goggles stare back at her, glinting in the dim lighting provided by the service lamp above the door across. “Yes. Be careful.”

    Behind her own mask, Kate’s lips spread into a grin.

    “I’m always careful.”

    Yelena huffs and Kate imagines her rolling her eyes behind the goggles again. “And stay on the comms this time, okay?”

    It’s Kate’s turn to huff. She took them out one time. One. Time.

    “Yeah, yeah.”

    The two of them look at each other for a moment longer, before Kate turns away, walking carefully over the beam to the elevator door. The bottom of the metal doors is about chest height and Kate reaches for the knife strapped to her thigh to carefully wedge the blade in between the doors and pull them slightly apart.

    Once there is enough room for her to squeeze her fingers between them, Kate quickly slides the knife into her belt, and pulls the doors apart about a foot, careful to keep her balance on the beam. Gently, she inserts the wedge into the track below the doors to keep them open. One last time, she looks back at Yelena who is watching her back still, before pulling herself up the ledge and onto the tiled floor of the 33rd level.

    Turning around, she removes the wedge that keeps the doors open, letting them slide close behind her. Through the disappearing gap, she sees that Yelena has already made it a floor below, and is climbing over the rails with the grace of a cat.

    When the doors are closed for good, Kate turns around again, taking in the space she is in. It’s sleek and modern, full of black and white walls and wood tilings with exposed beams for an industrial look. According to the blueprints, the gallery where she will be stationed is to the right, so that’s where Kate goes, carrying the wedge with her. Supposedly, there shouldn’t be any guards on the level right then, but she is careful nonetheless, checking around corners before she turns them, taking note to move silently.

    “I am in position. Sonya, you are up.”

    Through her earpiece, Yelena’s smooth voice comes in clear and Kate’s heart begins to beat harder.

    “Okay. 5 minutes ‘til breach.”

    For once, Sonya’s voice is all business and Kate keeps moving silently, reaching the gallery that overlooks the server room in less than a minute and hiding the wedge for the elevator doors behind a plant along the way. As she peeks out from behind a column, Kate can see that it has a kind of eerie, neon-blue lighting throughout the room. She can also see the silhouettes of the guards upfront, who do not change shifts until the morning, and even one more in the middle of the room, standing motionlessly.

    “There are three guards in the server room. Two at the door, one in the middle.” Afraid of being heard, Kate whispers the words, once she is safely hidden behind the column again but thankfully Yelena confirms that she heard her a second later, her own voice calm and quiet.

    “Copy that.”

    For the next couple of minutes, Kate waits in silence, not tempting fate by peeking out from behind the column again.

    “60 seconds until breach.”

    At Sonya’s words, Kate braces herself and takes out her sword, just in case there is more security hidden around that will pass her by once Sonya makes her entrance. The 60 seconds pass quickly and even though she knows it’s coming, Kate startles when the sirens start baring.

    Even through the loud alarm, Kate can hear the alarmed shouts of the guards downstairs but waits a few seconds until she peeks out from her hiding place to check if the room is empty. “Kate, confirmation?”

    Yelena’s words spur her on and she peeks out, looking down at the room before shifting back in place. She shakes her head, even though Yelena can’t see her as she answers, speaking louder now to be heard over the sirens.

    “No movement yet.”

    Yelena hums on the other end and waits a few seconds before she speaks again. “Sonya, turn up the heat.”

    Sonya’s answer is way too gleeful and Kate can’t help but smile at her apparent enjoyment over causing chaos.

    “Copy that.”

    Another minute goes by, before a loud boom can be heard, the explosion shaking the floor slightly even on the other side of the building.

    “Sonya, are you okay?”

    Kate asks, concerned for her but her tone is just as gleeful as before. “Don’t worry about me, Kate. I am having fun.”

    Yelena snorts on their shared comms channel, and Kate huffs in amusement too, before leaning out of cover to check on the guards again.

    “Okay. Two of them are gone...Guys, I don’t think the last one is going to move.” There is a beat of silence, before Yelena speaks, thinking over Kate’s words she guesses. “Okay. I am going in.”

    “Do you want me to take care of him from up here?”

    Kate’s question is quickly shot down, Yelena’s voice businesslike and focused. “No need.”

    Peeking slightly out of cover, Kate thinks it’s a good thing she is up there. From her vantage point, she can see Yelena clearly as she enters the room silently, sneaking around the dozens of rows of servers to get to the lone guard. Somebody else could clearly do the same, from up there.

    “I will tell you when he has your back to you.”

    She receives no verbal confirmation, but she sees Yelena’s mask face turn up towards her for a moment, giving her a thumbs up.

    She sneaks even closer, barely five feet from the guard, who keeps walking up and down, visibly somewhat nervous.

    “Wait.”

    Yelena halts and Kate watches as the guard walks a few steps forward, before turning back and doing it in the other direction.

    “Now.”

    Yelena is like a black cat, emerging from the shadows and following him a few steps behind.
