Grabbing his neck from the back, she twists around him before dropping and kicking his legs out from under him with a crouched leg sweep, while keeping a hold of his rifle. He falls, square on his back and Yelena uses the butt of his gun to smash him over the head twice as she stands up, knocking him out.

    Kate watches in silence as she reaches into her pocket, pulling out something that Kate realizes is a zip tie, as Yelena turns the guard over with a barely audible groan, and ties his hands behind his back. She leaves him there then, knocked out on his stomach, briefly looking up at Kate again before she begins the search for the terminal that will allow her access to the servers.

    The next several minutes are quite uneventful for Kate.

    She watches over Yelena’s back, literally, as she accesses the terminal on the other end of the room and begins the process of installing the program that will transform the files and make it possible for them to copy the data, while she hears muffled sounds of Sonya’s fight with the guards on the other side of the building.

    “Wow. Well, this is kind of anti-climactic.”

    She thinks she can hear Yelena sigh on the other side of the room, and she does turn around for a second to glare at her, or at least that’s what Kate thinks she is doing. “Do not jinx it.”

    Yelena turns back to her work and Kate keeps watching, taking the time to appreciate Yelena’s form from afar. Several more moments go by and Kate looks around, checking the hallway to her right, and then turns to check the one on her left and…

    Almost suffers a heart attack.

    In the hallway to her left, there is a dark figure, standing motionlessly about fifty feet from her. As she gets over her initial shock, Kate sees that it’s a woman, with dark, shoulder-length hair and that she is staring directly at Kate. She wears a tactical uniform, not dissimilar from the one that Sonya wears…

    A Widow…

    The Widow.

    Without a second thought, Kate takes off, sprinting towards the Widow who turns around and begins to quickly flee.

    “Kate?”

    Yelena’s voice is somewhat alarmed and Kate answers, her feet burning with the sprint. “Guys, the Widow is here.”

    Huffing out the words, Kate takes a left on the corridor, gaining on the smaller woman. In a few steps, they are out of the first corridor, and on another gallery, with the 31st-floor office cubicles below them on the right, and walls made out of glass, overlooking the city on the left.

    “Kate, do not engage. Do you hear me? Acknowledge!”

    Yelena’s voice is tight in her ear and it’s heavy enough with worry that Kate slows her steps. “What?”

    Yelena sounds like she is in motion too as she answers.

    “Do not engage. I repeat, do not chase her. It-“ The words are interrupted by sounds of Yelena grunting, and as Kate slows down into a jog, it doesn’t take a lot to figure out that Yelena has been attacked too.

    “Yelena?”

    The Widow disappeared at a different corridor ahead and Kate comes to a halt, trying to decide if she should heed Yelena’s warning and go help her, or go after the Widow. On her comms, Kate hears the sounds of a struggle followed by two gunshots that she hears both through her earpiece and distantly, from the floor below her.

    Ears hammering in her ear, Kate takes off back towards Yelena but never makes it further than a couple of steps.

    Suddenly, there is an indescribable pain spreading through her body, and it takes her a second to realize it originates from her neck, forcing her to fall forward onto all fours. With more struggle than Kate would ever like to admit, she reaches towards her neck, despite her convulsing muscles, and pulls away a small, disk-like device groaning loudly as the pain finally fades when it clatters next to her on the floor.

    It takes another moment for her to realize that she is on her knees, panting. There are footsteps behind her, quick and quiet, but before she can turn around, there is suddenly a thin, but sharp wire around her neck and she is yanked against a small, but hard body behind her. “Kate?”

    Yelena’s voice is breathy and alarmed in Kate’s ear and she hears running footsteps through the earpiece but it’s most likely too late.

    “Kate, where are you?”

    The only answer she can give is a few gurgled gasps, as life is being squeezed out of her by the wire around her neck. Morbidly, part of her mind thinks that at least she has a good view as she is dying, looking out at the city. She reaches for her sword, fallen to her side when she was hit by the electric disk by the Widow but before her fingers can close around the hilt, it’s kicked from her grasp, sliding several feet away.

    “Kate! Where are you?!”

    Yelena’s voice is almost panicked this time as Kate’s vision starts to fade back, as she slowly suffocates but her fingers, mostly without conscious direction from her brain to do so, wrap around the tactical knife strapped to her thigh.

    Yanking it out of the holster, Kate twists as much as she can, managing to jam it into the calf of the Widow standing behind her up to the hilt, the blade going through the woman’s leg. She lets out a strangled scream of pain and Kate gulps down the air flooding her lungs finally as she is let go.

    Falling forward, she coughs and her gloves barely block the hardness of her landing on the thinly carpeted floor in front of her. She hardly has enough mental capacity to catch herself, quickly pulling the mask off of her face, along with her hood, to help her breathe, even the thin material feeling suffocating after what has just happened.

    Kate scrambles away from the Widow on all floors and twists around, not able to get on her feet just yet. She doesn’t dare to take her eyes off of her as her fingers finally close around the hilt of her sword and she uses it as leverage, along with the metal railings behind her to stand up, her legs feeling weak, her breathing still labored. As Kate regains her footing, the Widow pulls out her knife from her calf, looking almost nonchalant, and it honestly unnerves Kate more than she thought possible.

    “…floor above you. Khrm, southwest…I thi-.”

    Kate’s overly croaky answer is cut out by her knife soaring through the air, as the Widow throws it straight at her head with deadly accuracy. Kate dodges, barely, her steps tumbling a little as she blocks the knife with her sword with a loud clang.

    “I am coming!”

    The Widow is not deterred.

    Before Kate has a chance to regain her bearings, she kicks out at Kate, lightning-fast, getting her in the stomach. With an oof, Kate staggers backward, almost losing her footing again. As she stumbles, the Widow pulls out a baton of sorts and Kate can barely block the hit coming at her head with the same terrifying grace Yelena and Sonya possess too. She attempts to attack back, slashing at the Widow’s torso with a wide, downward motion but it’s parried easily and in a second, she is on the defense again as she is kicked back. “I am on my way too.”

    Sonya’s voice is alarmed, and Kate is filled with the slight relief that at least she only has to stay alive until they get to her position.

    Which is, easier said than done, it turns out.

    Kate has no doubt, that if she didn’t get those couple training sessions with Yelena and Sonya, she would be dead within seconds. She only manages to hum an affirmative, as she can barely dance out of the way of the baton coming at her head from the side. The Widow kicks at her then, aiming for Kate’s hip but she jumps back just in time, avoiding most of the force behind the boot.

    The Widow grabs at her next, pulling Kate towards her by her wrist, but she leans into the motion, using her shoulder to shove the smaller woman back, hard. The Widow is taken by surprise and takes a few stumbling steps backward, nearly falling and Kate follows the motion with a sideways cut of her sword.

    The strike is blocked easily, even in the Widow’s unbalanced state, and the next attack comes at Kate’s torso from the side too. Kate blocks it just in time, sliding her blade down on the baton, and cutting into the Widow’s hand easily, with no guard to protect it. She cries out in pain and drops the baton but as Kate tries to take advantage of the opening, she moves out of her way easily.

    There is a pause, the two of them looking at each other and again, Kate is unnerved by the emptiness behind the woman’s dark eyes. There is no pain, anger, fear, or anything. She is just staring at Kate, looking for weakness, her gaze almost lifeless.

    Kate lunges, not waiting for her to actually find it, but that turns out to be a mistake. The Widow moves out of the way quickly, twisting close to her, and her hand closes around Kate’s that holds her sword and yanks. The other comes up from below, hitting Kate’s wrist just as it is twisted and her sword falls onto the ground a second later. Trying to take advantage of their closeness, Kate grabs the Widow’s other arm, ready to throw her over her back, but as she begins to twist around, the woman slips out of her hold, nimble and fast like water. The sound of tearing Velcro is the first thing that alerts her to the graveness of her mistake, as the gun that Yelena has given her is yanked from her thigh holster while she has her back to the Widow.

    Moving entirely by instinct, Kate twists back around, grabbing hold of the smaller woman’s wrists just as she raises her arm to shoot her in the back of her head. Pulling up and to the side, Kate manages to aim the gun away from her head before it goes off. Three shots are fired, shattering the floor-to-ceiling glass walls behind Kate, their close proximity to her ear positively deafening.

    The Widow knocks her back then, kicking her in the stomach again and Kate is briefly, for one heartbeat, distracted by Yelena’s arrival. She is running, sprinting at them and Kate feels relief flood her but it’s short-lived.

    Another shot is fired and the force of it knocks Kate back several steps, knocking her breath straight out of her before the gun goes off a second time, making her stumble back even more, as the bullets embed themselves into the material of her suit.

    “Kate!”

    She hears Yelena scream her name just as she loses her footing, suddenly nothing under her feet.

    And a second later, Kate is freefalling.

    She will never know how she has the mental capacity to reach for her collapsible bow. The instinct probably bypasses her brain completely, stemming from her muscles directly. The wind rushes past her ear, her face, her neck as she pulls out her grapple arrow and presses the tiny button to extend it. The glass windows of the building speed by her in a blur, and she can’t even hear her own scream even though she feels the strain of it as it’s ripped from her throat. She doesn’t aim, the movement propelled by years of practice, muscle memory, and her sheer stubbornness to stay alive.

    Kate fires her arrow and a couple of seconds later her fall is broken by a yank strong enough that she thinks her shoulder is going to fall off, and then a strong hit against her head as she slams against the window in front of her a second later.

    By strength she didn’t know she possessed, Kate keeps holding onto her bow. Dup-dup. Dup-dup. Dup-Dup.

    There is a long moment when she doesn’t hear anything but her own labored breathing, her heart thundering inside her head, and the wind as it whips past her. Her head pounds with the impact and judging by the warm, wet, drippy feeling on her lips, her nose is bleeding. It takes a long few seconds for the black sports to clear out from her vision.

    But she is alive.

    Somehow, she is still alive.

    “Kate?! Kate!!”

    Her earpiece crackles to life, Yelena’s voice bringing her back to the land of the living too. “I am here. I’m…good.”

    There are sounds of a commotion on the other end and Kate hears Yelena grunt, apparently still fighting the Widow. With a press of a button, her wire arrow starts to pull back the cable into it, and Kate begins her less-than-glamorous journey back up.

    Through her earpiece, she hears another gunshot go off, and panic fills her, along with frustration that she is not there to help, lamely just hanging by the side of the building. “Yelena!? Sonya?”

    There are more grunts and groans and a second later, something small and dark falls to Kate’s right side. Nobody answers her and the last few seconds of her journey back up are horrible, her stomach churning with anxiety.

    Finally, the cable pulls Kate high enough that she can see into the room again, and confirm that all three Widows are still alive, still very much involved in a fight that is simultaneously terrifying and incredible.

    Just as Kate is high enough to stumble into the room, and fall to her knees, Yelena throws the Widow over her shoulder while Sonya jumps onto them to hold her hands down, while Yelena sits on her legs. Something glints in Yelena’s hand before there is a click, and a crimson mist envelops the woman.

    Her arms, struggling against Sonya’s hold suddenly stop moving and Kate watches in wonder mixed with horror.

    “What is that?”

    Yelena’s head whips around and she is off of the woman in a second, almost running at Kate. She doesn’t have the strength to stand, not yet but in a couple of strides, Yelena makes it to her anyway. Kate watches in awe as she practically falls to her knees, reaching out to her. Yelena pulls her forward, away from the broken window before pulling her in and hugging her, almost desperate.

    In a sort of daze, Kate hugs her back, exhaling slowly as her heart finally stops racing. “I thought you died.”

    It’s said quietly against her shoulder and Kate chuckles weakly, before answering. “I’m not that easy to kill.”

    Yelena shakes her head against her, her words coming out almost strained, but a laugh bubbles through them.

    “Shut up.”

    Kate does, enjoying the embrace for a few seconds before Yelena pulls back. Finally, she reaches up and yanks off her mask, and Kate is floored by the amount of worry she sees in her eyes still as soon as the goggles are off.

    Her eyes, green irises almost invisible with the dim lights and how huge Yelena’s pupils are, look Kate over for injuries, her hands seemingly unable to hold back from touching her. She grabs Kate’s arms, her face, looking her over and Kate’s heart starts beating out of her chest for entirely different reasons now.

    One of Yelena’s hands drops from her face slowly, touching the bullets embedded into the left side of Kate’s chest gingerly, almost reverently and her eyes seem fixated on them for a second before they raise to finally meet Kate’s.

    “Are you hurt?”

    With a tired smile, she takes hold of Yelena’s hands, drawing them to her lap and squeezing in reassurance.

    “I’m fine. A bit bruised, that’s all.”

    Yelena gulps, her eyes still full of worry, and god, Kate wants to kiss her so badly right then. But probably not in front of an audience.

    Glancing above Yelena’s shoulder, Kate sees Sonya crouched down next to the brown-haired woman who sits curled up in a ball against the wall, her knees pulled to her chest. The Widow’s dark eyes are no longer empty, but open wide, and jumping around the room in a seemingly terrified frenzy, not speaking a word. Kate glances at the crimson, dusty spot on the carpet where the woman was restrained a minute earlier before she looks back at Yelena again. She is staring at Kate, blinking slowly and Kate repeats her question. “What was that stuff?”

    It seems to break Yelena out of her daze, eyebrows furrowing for a millisecond while she comprehends Kate’s question.

    “The antidote to mind-control.”

    Her answer is quiet but Kate’s eyes widen nonetheless, jumping back at the Widow. “So she was…?”

    Not finishing the question, she looks back at Yelena, finding her looking at the bullets in Kate’s chest again.

    “Yes. She is free now.”

    Nodding, Kate squeezes Yelena’s hands again, neither of them breaking the contact yet. After a few seconds, Kate gathers her strength and begins the motions to stand up, holding onto Yelena’s hand for support as she does.

    “Did you finish what we came for?”

    Once they are standing, Yelena lets go of her but doesn’t take a step away to put distance between them.

    “Not yet. We have to go back. The transformer program is doing its job, but the drive is still here, nothing copied over yet.”

    With a tired sigh, Kate nods, and her eyes leave Yelena to look at Sonya and the Widow again. Sonya turns her head to smile at her, for once entirely sincere and reaches her hand out. At first, Kate is confused but in a second, she gets Sonya’s meaning and walks over slowly, with a smile of her own. Sonya grabs her hand, squeezing it as she looks up at Kate. “I am glad you did not die.”

    Kate snorts, eyes jumping at the Widow before looking back at Sonya.

    “So am I.”

    Sonya’s eyes jump over to Yelena, standing behind her and Kate can literally see the teasing glint re-enter her gaze, now that immediate lethal danger is averted.

    “You have to go.”

    The words don’t come from Sonya.

    The Widow speaks, her voice quiet, barely louder than a whisper, and heavy with a Russian accent stronger than Yelena’s. All eyes go to her, and finally, she seems to come back to herself enough that she can meet their eyes, looking at Kate first, at Yelena next, and then at Sonya.

    “They are coming.”

    “Who? What?”

    Kate is the first to pose a question back at her, her heartbeat immediately speeding up. “They know you are here. You have to go.”

    The woman’s voice is a bit stronger this time around and she stands up on shaky legs with a wince, Sonya’s hand reaching out to catch her if she falls but never quite touching her. “Who is coming?”

    Yelena asks, voice serious and tight. The Widow’s voice is filled with dread. “An army. We…They knew you were coming, they were ready.”

    Kate wants to ask more, about who are they exactly, and what kind of army, but Yelena grabs her arm from behind, pulling her away.

    “Grab your things, we are going.”

    Kate nods, starting off towards her sword that is still fallen some feet away before she halts. “What about the drive?”

    “We will come back.”

    Yelena rushes by her, grabbing her mask from where she dropped it earlier and putting it into her backpack before she straightens up. Meanwhile, Kate grabs her sword and her knife, coated with the Widow’s blood. With some simmering guilt in her stomach, that she pushes to a corner of her mind that she will deal with later, Kate turns back to the three Widows. “Come on.”

    Yelena’s words are not directed at Kate for once.

    She is looking at the Widow and it seemingly takes the woman a second to catch her meaning. When she does, her eyes widen in surprise, and they glance at Sonya first, and at Kate after, dropping at the bullets still embedded in her chest.

    “But…I…”

    Kate smiles at her then, trying to signal that she is not angry about what went down between them. With a tilt of her head, she tries to soften her voice and her smile widens into a small grin.

    “I am fine. It’s fine… It’s kind of a rite of passage for you guys to throw me off of buildings, apparently.”

    The woman’s…No. Actually, now that Kate is looking at her properly, without the mask of mind-control hardening her features, she is a girl. She can’t be older than Kate herself, probably not even that…So, the girl’s face contorts in confusion, obviously not understanding her joke. Kate turns to Yelena then with a grin, hoping she appreciates it at least, finding her with her lips pursed and a hard look pinning Kate in place.

    “That is not funny.”

    Blinking, Kate’s grin falls away and she rolls her eyes but Yelena’s focus is already back on the Widow.

    “Do you have a tracking chip?”

    Eyes wide, the girl shakes her head, still visibly shaken. Yelena nods before she turns around and begins to walk away.

    “Good. Let’s go.”

    Smiling at the girl one last time, Kate turns away as well, following after Yelena in what she assumes is the direction of the server room.

    “Besides, how many times do I have to point out that I put you on a wire?” Yelena’s voice is softer as she says it, and in a moment, she turns her head back to look at Kate over her shoulder, eyes warm and a sliver of amusement back in her gaze. Lips widening into a smile again, Kate wets her lips, as the four of them make their way down a corridor.

    “Still, you did throw me off of a roof.”

    Yelena‘s eyes are definitely filled with humor now, but there is a lilt of challenge in her voice as she answers.

    “Do you ever think maybe you deserved it? Getting in my way.”

    Kate snorts, grinning at Yelena now as she holds her eyes for a moment longer, before turning back around. Before Kate can come up with an answer, there is a loud hiss somewhere in front of them followed by an even louder bang.

    Yelena puts a hand up to put a halt to their advance and despite the fact that they can’t see it, it’s not hard to guess what happened when they hear the sound of dozens of footsteps, running down the corridor ahead.

    The sound of heavy boots grows louder by the second, apparently moving towards them, and Yelena signals quickly to turn around and in a second, the four of them are running. There are enough footsteps behind them, that Kate can’t easily count how many of them there are, and her blood thrums in her ear, as adrenaline fills her veins again.

    Yelena and Sonya run ahead of Kate but the Widow, whose calf has been stabbed through by her knife slows them down, the girl almost limping…or at least as close to limping as a Widow can come. The four of them eventually make it back to where they freed the girl a few minutes ago, speeding by the crimson stain on the carpet as Yelena leads them running down the corridor across. As Kate glances to the side before she runs after the three Widows, she sees a large group of men, clothed in black tactical outfits begin to file into the open office space below, rifles raised.

    It's obvious, even by that group, that they are severely outnumbered.

    It’s also obvious, that somehow, Fisk has managed to be a step ahead again, anticipating their attempt to break in here.

    “We have to make it to the service staircase.”

    Yelena’s voice remains calm, even as the first shot is fired, punching a hole into the wall to the right of their group. Thankfully, they are far enough that the soldiers behind them don’t really pose a real threat, for now at least. They turn a hard left soon, nearing the area where the vault is signaled by a few knocked-out guards on the ground, but the footsteps behind them grow closer. Kate pulls out her bow, ready to turn back and let loose a trick arrow or two at the soldiers chasing them but Yelena glances at her just then, shaking her head. “Do not use that.”

    Kate kisses her teeth, pulling out an explosive arrow anyway.

    “I would rather be arrested than dead.”

    Kate huffs out, nocking the arrow while maintaining her jogging pace. The Widow is slowing them down, her pace even growing slower and as Kate looks back, she can see the bloody footprints she leaves behind herself.

    “You are not dying.”

    At Yelena’s words, Kate turns forward again, throwing her an exasperated look. “We will if you don’t let me protect us.”

    “Stop bickering.”

    Sonya sounds frustrated and she stops running in a second, glancing at the Widow before turning back to them.

    “We need a plan. We are getting boxed in.”

    She is right. Heavy footsteps are coming at them from both ahead and behind on the carpeted, dimly lit office corridors. There are offices, or meeting rooms on the sides and Kate tries the handle of one, finding it open.

    “We could hide in these.”

    Yelena shakes her head. The footsteps are coming closer.

    “No. We would get trapped.”

    She looks around then, taking a second to look them all over.

    “Okay. Kate, you take…what is your name?”

    The Widow blinks, still visibly not clear of her shock at being free and having to run immediately.

    “Maxine.”

    Yelena nods, glancing at the office behind Kate.

    “You take Maxine. Sonya and I will lead them away. We are quicker without you and can escape through the roof. You take Maxine, wait for them to run by, and then take her to the staircase and run. We meet by the car.”

    “No, I-“ Kate opens her mouth to argue, not wanting to be split and especially disliking the part where Yelena and Sonya draw the fire away but Yelena steps a little closer, and something in her face gives Kate a pause.

    “Kate, please.”

    Her eyes bore into Kate’s, almost pleading and Kate closes her mouth and exhales heavily as she nods, accepting her defeat with a tight purse of her lips.

    “Okay, I…Okay.”

    Yelena smiles, tiny and barely there before she steps back.

    “Go. Be careful to not leave blood tracks or it won’t work.”

    The second part is addressed to Maxine too, and they both nod before Kate leads her back a few steps, opening the door of an office. As she looks back at Yelena one last time, she sees her using a knife to cut her palm, using the dripping blood to fake their tracks forward. She looks back at Kate then, their eyes meeting for a second before Sonya and Yelena take off. “Stay safe.”

    Kate says it to her comms and Yelena hums in affirmation.

    “You too.”

    Turning back to the room they are in, Kate quickly joins the Widow…Maxine, behind the desk. If anyone actually comes in, it won’t hide them but from the outside to the soldiers running by the closed doors, they probably won’t be noticeable despite the glass walls of the office.

    In the following few seconds, there is only the sound of footsteps coming closer, Yelena’s and Sonya’s breathing in her ear, and Maxine’s labored breathing to her left. Kate alternates between peeking out through the glass wall and glancing at Maxine periodically, who looks significantly paler than a few minutes ago when they started their run. She keeps staring at the door, and Kate’s heart clenches at her expression, terrified and looking almost like a child.

    Blood keeps seeping out of her wound, pooling below her behind the chair she is using as a cover of sorts, seeping into the carpet beneath. Kate feels the guilt in her stomach, burning and acidic but she waits until the soldiers catch up and pass them by before she makes her move. In her ear, gunfire starts up and Kate just hopes that Yelena and Sonya are okay, while trying to focus on her own situation.

    Maxine starts to get on her feet but Kate reaches out a hand, putting it on her shoulder to keep her still. The moment she makes contact, Maxine freezes, her body going rigid and Kate pulls her hand away as if she was burned.

    “Sorry. I…just wait a second, okay?”

    Maxine’s eyes are wide, like a deer caught in headlights, and Kate tries to give her a reassuring smile. It doesn’t seem to be working very well but Maxine nods and lowers herself back onto the ground, her eyes wide and looking at Kate like a wild animal would with its leg caught in a trap.

    “Can I look at your leg?”

    Looking down at her leg, and then back at Kate, Maxine doesn’t look any less terrified, but she nods slowly after a second. Through her earpiece, Kate hears more shots but no cries of pain so that at least is a consolation. The contrast between the silence of their room, and the flurry of activity that is coming through her comms makes her feel weirdly unbalanced, but she tries to not let it show.

    Kate scootches closer, trying to assess the damage but it’s hard to do with the black tactical uniform in the way. With no medical supplies, Kate’s options are limited, but judging from how pale Maxine is, and how much blood she must have already lost, she has to do something or the Widow won’t be making her escape from the building with them. She stands up, looking around the office and she feels Maxine’s eyes follow her like a hawk but tries not to let it show. When she opens one of the wardrobes, she has to swallow her triumphant outburst, as she spots a couple of shirts hung up. They are somebody’s spares, no doubt and she pulls out two, making her way back to Maxine.

    With quick motions Kate tears the arms off of both, throwing the rest aside before she turns back to Maxine.

    “I’m going to touch your leg, is that okay?”

    Again, Maxine doesn’t give any verbal answer but she nods, holding eye contact and Kate takes that as a step in the right direction. She smiles again, quickly, before she focuses on the leg, grabbing a hold of Maxine’s ankle gently, and pulls it closer to herself to work on. In her ear, there are more shots and some cries of pain, but none of them come from Yelena or Sonya.

    Two rolled-up arms of the shirt go on either side of Maxine’s calf, directly over the wound and Kate sees her wince as she ties another arm around it tightly.

    “Sorry. It’s gotta be tight to stop the bleeding.”

    Maxine nods at her again, eyes wide but looking back at her and her wince is less pronounced as Kate ties the other arm over the first one, making the bandage more secure. She stands up after, listening to sounds of commotion outside but hears nothing and there are no sounds of fighting coming through her earpiece either, so she extends a hand to Maxine. “Come on.”

    She looks at Kate’s hand and then back at her, before she reaches out, tentative and slow but she lets Kate pull her up. She lets go of the hand immediately after, obviously not used to much physical contact, but Kate smiles nonetheless as she tries putting weight on her leg, and seems a bit more stable.

    “Better?”

    Maxine nods and Kate is ready to turn away but she finally speaks.

    “Yes...Thank you.-”

    She glances down at Kate’s chest, the bullets embedded in her suit specifically, before looking back at her as she continues.

    “I am sorry.”

    Kate shakes her head, still smiling. Her earpiece is finally quiet, and Kate sighs, hoping that Yelena and Sonya are okay.

    “It’s okay. You didn’t…I know it wasn’t you or like…I don’t exactly know how it works, but I know you didn’t want to.”

    Maxine still doesn’t smile back, but her face looks at least somewhat less terrified, so Kate takes that as a win.

    “Yelena, Sonya? Are you okay?”

    There is more silence before Yelena’s voice comes through, sounding a little out of breath. “All good, Kate.”

    Kate hums, smiling to herself in relief a little bit before she looks at Maxine again. “Come on, let’s get out of here.”

    Kate is the first one through the office’s doors and thankfully, the hallway is deserted. With their running earlier, she kind of lost track of where they are exactly, but she thinks going in the opposite direction of Yelena and Sonya is probably their best bet if their purpose is to draw fire away.

    She motions for Maxine to follow and the two of them walk down the corridor they came from, retracing their steps from earlier. Kate tries to be mindful of Maxine’s injured leg and doesn’t run, but their slow progress is kind of making the hairs on the back of her neck stand up, her muscles tight with the fight she anticipates coming at them around any corner they turn.

    When they make it back to the gallery above the open office space for the third time that day, where Kate fought Maxine, she holds her hand up. There are voices down at the office, and Kate peeks out from behind the wall to see downstairs through the glass railing. Sure enough, there are at least a dozen soldiers, clad in black and armed with machine guns huddled around, looking something over.

    It's their only chance to sneak by without being noticed and Kate motions for Maxine to follow. With her eyes on the soldiers, Kate leads them across the gallery and they are almost over the exposed part when one of the soldiers raises his head.

    He shouts something, Kate cannot exactly hear and raises his gun while the others turn around, and in a second, Kate is grabbing Maxine and pulls her into a jog again. They hear shots and the glass shatter as Kate calls out, warning Yelena and Sonya through her comms. “Shit! We are exposed.”

    A second later, the heavy footsteps are coming after them again and Kate pulls out her bow once more, nocking a smoke arrow, and shoots it behind them. She doesn’t stick around to see it fill the corridor with purple mist, running immediately after Maxine’s hobbling form. “Can you get yourself out?”

    Yelena’s voice is accompanied by sounds of her fighting someone else on her end and Kate answers as she keeps running, while the sounds of the footsteps behind them slow down as the soldiers enter the fog.

    “Yeah. I think so.”

    Kate halts to fire another arrow into the mist, the putty one that she always used to bother Clint about, and hears the alarmed and confused sounds of the soldiers, as they are covered in it. She snickers to herself quietly, before turning to catch up to Maxine again. “That should slow them down.”

    They make it a few dozen feet more before the footsteps start growing closer again, this time accompanied by the sounds of shots fired behind them. One of the bullets punches a hole into the wall right by Kate’s head, while another swishes by between her and Maxine. It’s way too close for comfort.

    Kate reaches for an arrow again, a regular one this time, nocking, turning back, and firing a second later. She is up and running again by the time it lands but she hears the pained cry and the body thudding nonetheless.

    One less pursuer.

    In her ear, Yelena cries out, and Kate huffs, hating their separation more and more by the second.

    “Are you okay?”

    The question is aimed at Yelena, but Maxine looks at her too, nodding.

    “Yes.”

    A second later, Yelena answers, sounding a bit breathless.

    “Just getting my cardio workout.”

    Kate snorts, smiling at the words.

    “Attagirl.”

    Maxine looks confused, her dark eyebrows furrowing but they obviously very much do not have the time to clear up who Kate was talking to. Another set of gunshots goes off and one is close enough that it grazes Kate’s arm, her suit thankfully doing its job. At the next corner, she looks back, still counting at least ten soldiers.

    She needs to do something.

    Halting her advance, Kate nocks a sonic arrow, indicating to Maxine that she should go on with a jut of her chin. She waits by the corner as Maxine hobbles on, and as the footsteps grow closer, Kate leans back out of cover to fire it in front of the soldiers. The resulting pulse throws the soldiers back and against each other, crying out in pain. Several of them do not move to get back up after they are knocked harshly against the wall and Kate pulls out another arrow, a net one this time, firing at the remaining few left conscious.

    It’s good enough, and Kate pushes aside her slight relief that she didn’t have to kill anyone this time around.

    “Are you okay?”

    Yelena asks her this time, obviously fighting her own battle if the sounds coming through are any indication. Kate smiles, turning her back to the group struggling on the floor. “Yeah, just getting my cardio-“ A shot rings out and Kate almost falls with the force of the bullet hitting her lower back. It stings like a bitch, even through the suit and Kate’s cry of pain turns into an angry growl as she turns back around.

    “Kate?”

    Jumping to the side to avoid the next few bullets, Kate pulls out an arrow as she rolls out of the way, arriving to her knees and taking aim. The soldier’s gun clicks empty, just as Kate gets him in her crosshairs.

    He is tangled in the net, lying on the ground, his gun still aimed at Kate. Their eyes meet and Kate hesitates.

    “Kate?”

    Kate gulps, before clearing her throat.

    “I’m here. I’m fine.”

    She hears Yelena’s exhale through the comms, even through her own thundering heartbeat in her ear.

    The man shot her.

    He shot her in the back.

    Exhaling, Kate pulls the string even tighter, trying to make her decision. He looks back at her, visibly afraid but not pleading. There is another soldier awake, his hands raised, but he doesn’t say anything either.

    There are too many guns around for her to take them all with her, away from them, but Kate doesn’t think she has it in her to finish them off. Not like this. But time is ticking, any time she keeps mulling this over, taking away precious seconds she needs for their escape. She needs to make a decision before it’s made for her.

    She sees one of them, not the one that shot her, glance at the other rifles, lying on the ground, and shakes her head as she shifts her stance to point her drawn arrow at him. “Ah-ah. I wouldn’t do that.”

    He doesn’t listen.

    He makes the jump for the rifle and Kate lets her arrow fly, impaling him through the wrist and he screams in pain. The one that shot at her thinks it’s his opening, now that she doesn’t have an arrow nocked, and makes his move for the gun as well.

    This time, Kate doesn’t hesitate.

    The arrow is nocked and fired, flying true in a matter of seconds. By the time his fingers close around the handle of the gun he screams too, the arrow going through his forearm. She fires another one into his leg for good measure, before she picks up one of the rifles and leaves them behind without another look.

    Kate puts it over her shoulder and then jogs ahead, looking for Maxine. In a few moments, she reaches the gallery she used to wait on, overlooking the server room. the room below is swarming with soldiers, and Kate sees no signs of Maxine. She quickly sneaks onward, avoiding detection this time, using the dark corners of the gallery to hide her form. The following corridor is empty too and Kate begins to grow anxious.

    “Guys, I think I lost Maxine.”

    Remembering that she is supposed to stay undetected, although it’s a bit late with all the trick arrows she already used, Kate pulls her mask back up, but not her hood, before she continues running.

    “What do you mean you lost her?”

    Yelena sounds exasperated and Kate feels embarrassment heat her cheeks up. She was responsible for the Widow for like 5 minutes, and she already managed to lose her. Clearing her throat, she quickly explains.

    “I told her to keep moving while I fought some of these guys. And now I can’t find her.” There is a beat of only some grunting and punches landing, before Yelena answers. “Check the offices. She is probably in there.”

    Kate’s eyebrows furrow and she slows down before halting completely.

    “What do you mean?”

    Yelena is silent for a moment, and it’s Sonya who answers, sounding a bit out of breath. “Coming out of it is scary. She is hurt and confused. She will try to find a place to hide.” Kate’s lips part, understanding downing her as she remembers Maxine, curled up in a ball, looking around with wide, terrified eyes.

    “Okay. I’ll let you know when I find her.”

    She runs back towards the gallery, again, briefly frustrated with all the back and forth. “I don’t think we will be able to get the transformer back today. Is it hidden?” She speaks once she sneaked back above the soldiers in the server room again, seeing how there are at least 50 of them in that room alone. They really need to get out of here. Like, yesterday.

    “Yes. It’s….agh.”

    Yelena cries out and Kate halts, in front of an office.

    “Yelena?”

    There are more sounds of a struggle and Kate’s worry grows.

    “Yelena, where are-“ “I am…uh, I am fine. Just find her.”

    Kate exhales, hissing the air out through her front teeth in frustration. God she hates this, hates not being able to help.

    “Okay. Okay. I’m going.”

    It sounds grumpy, even to her own ears and she checks the first office, finding it empty. Another three are too, and she is almost ready to give her search up, when she sees a tiny drop of blood in front of the fourth one, down the hallway from where she started. Gently, she opens the door and calls out quietly as she sticks her head in. “Maxine? It’s Kate. Are y-“ In a second, Kate is yanked inside and barely blocks the hand coming at her. She catches a glimpse at Maxine’s face, and while her eyes are no longer lifeless, there is an empty, blind kind of terror behind them that lets Kate know that she is not exactly in control of what she is doing.

    “Hey! No, Maxine! It’s me! Hey!”

    Barely dodging the next hit, Kate vaults over the table in the middle of the room, putting it between them, holding her hands up, palms facing the Widow.

    “Hey! Hey, it’s me! We are, ah…We are cool now! I am not trying to hurt-” A monitor is thrown at Kate’s head, which she ducks to avoid, followed by a pen that is terrifyingly accurate and it only doesn’t get her in the eye because she launches herself to the side. With a roll, she gets under the table and grabs Maxine around the middle as she stands up, vaulting her over her shoulder and onto the table.

    “Kate, did you find her?”

    As she tries to answer Yelena’s pretty pointless question, Kate is punched in the face from below, Maxine clearly not ready to give up. Their struggle is loud, and Kate worries that they will be surrounded by soldiers any second now, but she does her best to restrain Maxine gently even as she feels the warm trickle of blood below her nose again. Grabbing hold of her wrists, Kate tries to hold them down.

    “Please, Maxine! I am not… I’m not trying to hurt you. Please, calm down.” Her message is very much not received as Maxine uses her legs to wrap them around Kate’s torso and squeeze and locks her ankles behind her back. Kate groans, the force of them making it almost impossible to breathe, but it’s clear that her strategy is not working. Saying her prayers, Kate lets go of Maxine completely and holds her hands up again. “See? Hey! Look, I am not hurting you.”

    Maxine’s eyes are terrified and huge but she blinks, and a sliver of consciousness seems to make its way back to her gaze.

    “I am backing away.”

    The legs slowly ease their tension and Kate steps away, hands still held up as Maxine stands up from the table with a quick roll, and backs away from the table, into the opposing corner of the room.

    “I even brought this gun for you.”

    That is probably a bad idea, and Maxine’s eyes widen even more but Kate grabs the barrel of the automatic rifle on her shoulder and slowly puts it onto the table while maintaining eye contact.

    “Remember, you shot me earlier? Here?”

    Kate points at her chest, at the bullets still embedded into her suit and Maxine’s eyes drop to follow their movement, before recognition flashes behind her eyes. They widen even more then, and Kate is horrified to see that tears begin to well up in them. Finally, Maxine seems to come back to herself for good and she sways slightly. Kate moves forward to help her but thinks better of touching her again without explicit consent, and she tries to smile, feeling incredibly ill-equipped to handle this situation. “Hey…hey! It’s okay! I am fine. You are fine. We…Everyone is fine! But we uh. We do have to go, I am really sorry.”

    Maxine nods but makes no move to leave the room. Kate glances back towards the corridor, a bit nervous, before looking back at Maxine. She doesn’t want to rush her but it’s really not the time and the place-

    “Leave me.”

    Maxine’s voice is heartbreaking, sad, and small, and Kate’s eyebrows furrow in response. “What? No! No.”

    Maxine meets her eyes and she repeats herself, a touch stronger this time. “Leave me. I do not…do not deserve to live. I killed so many-“ “Ah-ah. We are not doing this now. Absolutely not!”

    Kate cuts her off, leaving no space for her to continue as she barrels on. “You…You have so much in front of you. You don’t even know!”

    Maxine shakes her head but Kate keeps talking, determined to convince her. “Hey, listen. The women I am with? Sonya and Yelena? They are like you. And I am not going to say I know what you have gone through, because like obviously, I don’t. But I know them. And they have gone through this and they are absolutely amazing. They have built amazing lives! And, uh…and so can you too!”

    There is a spark of hope in Maxine’s eyes, mixed with some surprise and it’s somehow even more heartbreaking than her sorrow and panic were. But Kate propels on, feeling like she finally found a thread to pull on.

    “I can imagine that this is terrifying, and it feels like…It feels like a raw wound right now. But it gets better and there is so much in life worth living for! And you can experience it, too! Friendship and love. And Um. Dogs!”

    There is an affectionate chuckle in her ear, Yelena, followed by a slightly coyer one, Sonya and Kate feels her face heat up when she remembers they are listening in on this conversation too. But there is hope now on Maxine’s face and she looks so young, and Kate thinks the least she can do is help funnel that spark, and help the girl get a chance at life. “Or, cats! Maybe you are a cat person! Who knows? Wouldn’t you like to find out? Which one you are? And what kind of food you like, or movies or books? To uh, travel and see the world?”

    Confusion seeps into her heart as Maxine starts crying again and Kate can’t help the worried glance behind her back at the door again.

    “I do not know…I do not know any of that!”

    At Maxine’s words, Kate steps forward again, wanting to reach out in comfort but stops herself again, feeling desperate. She compromises by moving as if touching Maxine’s forearm, but stopping short and patting the air above it with a movement that would probably look incredibly awkward if anyone were to see it.

    “But you can find out! You have time! So much time!...As long as we, uh, make it out of here alive.”

    Sniffling, Maxine nods and finally, finally, Kate gets the first smile from her, even if it’s pale and small and barely there. She smiles back, nodding to herself.

    “Life is amazing and colorful, and you deserve to experience it…All of it.” Blinking, Maxine seems a bit overwhelmed but she nods and Kate nods back at her before asking, somewhat awkwardly.

    “Right. Um, okay. Do you need some more time? We can…I don’t know. Wait a minute.” Shaking her head, Maxine wipes under her eyes and walks up to the table, with more confidence in her step than before, and picks up the rifle.

    “No. I…I want to make it out of here.”

    Kate grins, nodding at her words.

    “Attagirl! Come on.”

    With that, Kate turns her head to the side to listen in front of the door but hears no movement in the hallway. Carefully, she opens the door, and thankfully, she does find it empty. Maxine follows her as they leave the room, and Kate starts toward the gallery from before. “I should have known you were good at making big hero speeches.”

    Kate huffs but smiles at Yelena’s words, trying to answer quietly so Maxine is not privy to their conversation, even though she is literally only a few steps away from her. “It’s not a speech…I just said what anybody would say.”

    There is a couple of seconds of silence, and Kate thinks they are done with the conversation, carefully walking down the corridor, but soon Yelena speaks again.

    “No. Not anybody would.”

    A second later, she speaks again, her voice sincere.

    “You did good.”

    Kate’s smile widens, and there is a warm feeling in her chest at Yelena’s words. “Thanks.”

    Clearing her throat quietly, she changes the topic.

    “So, how are you guys getting along?”

    This time it’s Sonya who answers her question, her voice unmissably amused. “We made it to the exfill point a few minutes ago, but we will wait to go until you have made it out for sure.”

    While Kate wishes she was badass enough alone to guarantee they will make it out in one piece, it’s probably a good idea.

    “Right. We are walking to the staircase now. Should be there in a couple of minutes…um, thanks.”

    There is a hum of acknowledgment on the other end and Kate takes a deep breath, hoping that they will be able to keep up their side of the mission. If for nothing else, to prove to Sonya and Yelena that she doesn’t need to be babysat.

    The lesson Kate should learn about tonight is to not jinx things.

    They make it as far as the entrance of the staircase without a problem. The several dozens of well-equipped henchmen are looking for them on the other side of the building, where Yelena and Sonya disappeared and they only run into a pair of them on their way, taking them out easily.

    Maxine does appear even paler than when they left the office, and Kate feels the clock ticking over them, even as they manage to sneak through the floor basically unscathed. Kate’s chest and lower back, where she was struck by the bullets, does hurt quite a bit, and so does her head after hitting it on the window earlier, and due to Maxine’s surgically accurate punch but if that is the state she manages to get out of this mission, she will still write today off as a win.

    “We are almost there.”

    There is only one corridor separating them from the door that leads to the staircase, and Kate feels herself relax just a tiny bit. Throwing a worried glance at Maxine, whose face is covered by a thin sheet of sweat, Kate lowers her voice even more.

    “I hope you have a first aid kit in that magic van of yours. Maxine is not looking great.” Sonya snorts in her ear before she answers.

    “Just get her out of there. We will take care of her after.”

    The door with a stair icon on it finally appears at the end of the corridor they are on after they turn left, and Kate exhales.

    “Yeah, we are arriving at the stairwell in one se- Shit!”

    On the connecting corridor to the right, running footsteps can be heard and Kate grabs onto Maxine without thinking pushing her along and toward the door.

    “Maxine, run! Shit! Yelena, we are-“ A body collides with hers just as they run across the intersection of hallways, and Kate stumbles with the force of it, falling against the wall. By instinct, she kicks the attacker away, slashing her sword across his torso as he is falling backward and she only has a second to quickly take in her situation.

    It doesn’t look great.

    Kate is trapped against the wall, with at least seven soldiers running up on her from the corridor across, three already blocking her way forward to her left, separating her from Maxine. She has a split second to choose if she wants to run back to where she came from, but it passes her by without her making that decision. She decides to speak to Yelena instead. “We are caught.”

    The soldier closest to her raises his rifle and Kate’s muscles contract, getting ready to jump toward him, but a shot rings before she can. His mask-covered face ruptures and Kate is sprayed with a mist of red so suddenly, she is completely frozen. It gets into her eyes, blinding her momentarily and she only hears the second shot, then the third, and the thuds of bodies in front of her before it’s mixed with the yelling of the soldiers. “Ahh, fuuuck..”

    As more shots ring out, Kate wipes at her eyes furiously with the back of her gloved left hand that is not holding her sword, trying to regain her eyesight. Somebody runs or falls into her again, and without her sight, Kate is unable to keep her balance, falling with the body that feels unnaturally pliant, with no muscle tension whatsoever. He is dead. “Kate, what is going on?”

    After Yelena’s words, Kate hears another shot, and one more body drop somewhere close to her. Furrowing her eyebrows, she blinks her eyes open, squinting at first and while it stings and her eyesight is a bit blurry, she can finally see somewhat.

    Dark figures that Kate takes a second to recognize as bodies of the soldiers litter the hallway, and another dark figure, smaller with shoulder-length brown hair, approaches her. Maxine reaches down with her hand, offering it to Kate, the barrel of her rifle just level with Kate’s eyes too.

    “Come on. We run.”

    Kate sighs deeply and it takes her a second to realize that the thundering that she hears is not her blood thrumming in her ears, but a sound of a big group of people running down the corridor they just came from.

    Grabbing onto Maxine’s hand, Kate lets her pull her up but they don’t have time to catch their breath.

    “We’re at the staircase. They’ve found us.”

    She jogs ahead, while Maxine hobbles a step behind her and Kate tears the door open, still blinking to clear her eyes as she lets her run through before entering the stairwell too. Immediately, dread fills her veins.

    Just like behind them, the sound of several dozen pairs of boots can be heard, making their way up the stairs.

    Shit. Shit. Shit.

    “Downstairs is a no go. We have to go up.”

    Kate whispers as she points upwards, holding Maxine’s eyes. She nods, and Kate is distractedly worried about how glossy her eyes are. Along with her pale, sweat-covered face, it’s a worrying look.

    “Do you need backup?”

    At Yelena’s question, Kate swallows her pride without hesitation.

    “Yes. We are fucked.”

    “We are on our way.

    Kate hears them moving, even through her own heavy breathing as she runs up the stairs. Maxine keeps lagging behind, and Kate winces when she hears the door slam open, probably only three levels below them.

    They are severely fucked.

    With Maxine’s leg holding them back, it’s only a matter of time before the soldiers catch up to them. They have about twelve floors to go up, and there is no way they can go that long without getting caught.

    On the other hand, there is no way the two of them, or even the four of them can fight, or even hold back that many soldiers for a prolonged amount of time. There is only one thing she can try.

    “Maxine, keep going. I will be right behind you.”

    Kate stops, meeting Maxine’s eyes. She looks back at Kate, visibly hesitant. “I will be right behind you, I promise.”

    Sincerely hoping that her smile looks more confident than it feels, Kate urges Maxine on while Yelena asks in her ear, her voice filled with frustration and a hint of fear. “Kate, do not do something stupid and heroic.”

    Kate smiles, turning away from Maxine and going down a few steps, exchanging her sword for her retractable bow in her hands, clicking the button to open it and string it up again. “I am just setting up some things to slow them down…”

    After a few more steps, she pulls out a trick arrow, the type that shoots out several cables to grab onto things around them, and nocks it.

    “I promise I won’t die.”

    She only brought one of these along, so she has to make it count. Kate draws and then fires it into the turn of the staircase, half a level below, hoping it will hold. The footsteps are sounding very close now, probably only a few floors below her, and quickly, she fires a smoke arrow and a pepper spray arrow in quick succession right next to the grab-onto-arrow. “You better.”

    With no time to answer Yelena, Kate only huffs in amusement slightly, most distracted. Her hope is that the smoke will mask the metal net now blocking the stairway, causing the soldiers to run into it and fall over each other but if it just slows them down, that might be enough as well.

    Turning around quickly, Kate runs up the stairs, taking them two at a time to catch up to Maxine. It only takes her about thirty seconds, as Maxine makes very slow progress with her injured leg, and even that while holding onto the railing, and pulling herself along. “I am here.”

    Running up to Maxine at the landing of the 37th floor, Kate has to stop herself from reaching out to her instinctively again. From below, Kate hears the alarmed yells of the soldiers, probably only now running into her trap, and secretly hopes it will hold them up long enough for Maxine and her to make their escape, or at least meet up with Yelena and Sonya. Maxine looks relieved at seeing her and Kate attaches her bow to her back, before speaking to her again.

    “Can I help? I-“ The door behind Kate is blown open from the inside, the shockwave throwing her somewhat down the stairs and against the railing, hitting her strongly in the side and knocking her breath straight out of her. Maxine is thrown too, and Kate hears her cry out weakly somewhere to her right, but she has no time to check on her.

    Through the blown doors, two ballistic shields block the way, marching closer to Kate. With somewhat shaky legs, Kate stands up, reaching for her bow. A hand reaches out from behind one, aiming a gun at her and Kate barely has time to jump to the side, the bullet ricocheting off the railing she has just been standing in front of.

    The controlled roll down the stairs is uncomfortable, but Kate reaches for one of the two acid arrows she brought, nocking and drawing it by the time she is back on her knees, aiming at the middle of the shield that the soldier is firing from behind. The acid melts the metal, falling onto the man’s forearm holding it and in a few seconds, he screams in pain. It only lasts for a moment, because Kate’s sonic arrow, fired through the hole in the shield throws the entire company back and forward, at least a dozen men falling over each other and thrown against the wall. She is out of net arrows, which would be her first choice, but an electromagnetic arrow into an exposed pipe above their heads pulls the guns out of the soldiers’ hands, rendering the ones that remained conscious at least that much less dangerous as well.

    A few hurried steps up the stairs and Kate is by Maxine’s side, leaning over her. She is unconscious, her body finally collapsing under the weight of the several shocking events it has gone through tonight. Kate worriedly checks her pulse, but thankfully it’s there, thrumming against her fingertips.

    “Guys, Maxine is out. Where are you?”

    The precious few seconds her sonic arrow has brought her is up, and Kate barely has time to turn around when she hears the steps running up the stairs. There are two of them, no longer armed with rifles but still huge compared to her.

    They also do not do her the courtesy of lining up to fight her one on one, jumping her at the same time. Kate sidesteps a kick to the right and ducks under a fist flying at her face, using her bow to smack the soldier closer to her on the side of his head. The other one pulls his head out of the way, and grabs the bow in front of him, using it to yank Kate closer. “We are about two minutes out.”

    Kate cries out when he headbutts her cheek, black spots appearing in front of her eyes but headbutts him right back nonetheless, before kicking him in the stomach and down the stairs. His hold is stronger on her bow than she expected, however, and as he falls backward, it’s only by letting go of it, that she avoids falling down the stairs with him. The guy that Kate hit in the head with her bow recovers quickly, grabbing Kate by the neck with both hands and shoving her back against the wall, his hands tightening around her windpipe. Pulling her shoulders up, Kate tries to minimize the amount of neck he can hold onto and grabs onto one of his arms with her right hand, pulling it downward. Of course, that’s not enough to move it, his arm is strong and thick, so she reaches for the hand on the same side with her left, grabbing onto his middle finger. Yanking it off of her neck, she bends it backward and it’s his turn to cry out in pain, as she breaks his finger. Using his distraction, Kate shoves him back by twisting to the side and smashing her shoulder into his chest, gulping down air as soon as he stumbles back and she is free.

    The rest of the soldiers have gotten their bearings, and other than the one that Kate is fighting, and the one that has now gotten back onto his feet at the bottom of the stairs, four others are closing in too. Kate pants heavily and reaches for her sword while she has a second, but by the time she has pressed the button to open it, the man she just shoved away is already on her again.

    Ducking the first punch, Kate dances two steps up, kicking him from the side and down the stairs but when he falls against the four coming up the stairs, instead of taking them down with him, they halt his fall.

    For a moment, the five of them are just looking at each other, squaring off but they do not waste time for long. With a yell, one of them runs up the stairs at her and the others follow. The first man Kate sidesteps and uses her sword to slash him across the torso from stomach to chest, but the step puts her right in the way of the second one. His punch she can still duck under but the position limits her options and while she can shove him back with her shoulder again, it’s only buying seconds. At this point, the third soldier's attack is impossible to avoid and Kate is kicked to the side and against the railing, her hip pounding where his boot hit her. The fourth man manages to hit Kate on the left side of her jaw, her head snapping to the side with the impact and the fifth man grabs onto her sword-wielding hand to restrain her. Grabbing onto the hand that holds her wrist, Kate yanks him against herself, right into the way of another punch, and he, and the large, hulking man that punched Kate earlier both cry out in pain as his fist connects with the back of the other man’s head, bone meeting bone. Twisting her wrist out of his hold, Kate pulls her sword upwards, right against the soldier's neck who is pushed up against her, and a second later when she sidesteps the next punch, her blade slices into the flesh. The adrenaline pounding in her veins drowns out the gurgling sound that escapes the soldier as Kate moves one step lower on the stairs, and pulls her entire blade across his neck, spraying herself and the wall behind her with blood, thankfully none getting into her eyes this time, but soaking her clothes instead.

    He falls with a muted thud, and a second later, when Kate is grabbed and yanked from the side, back up the stairs, she almost falls over him. The biggest soldier pulls on Kate with a roar, practically throwing her up the stairs and her knees and hands ache when she falls on them a second later, next to Maxine’s unconscious body lying at the turn on the staircase. While it hurts, it also allows Kate to regain her footing just in time, and she puts her body between the remaining four soldiers, and Maxine as they come at her. The huge soldier is the first up the stairs, trying to use his size against Kate, but she ducks under his fist flying at her head, slicing him across his torso as she sidesteps him.

    He roars in pain and while Kate kicks the next soldier down the stairs and against the one behind it, he grabs at her again from the side. His huge hand covers almost her entire face as he shoves Kate back against the wall, the back of her head hitting the hard, marble tiles with a muted thud and a painful cry of her own. For a brief moment, it’s only his hand holding her up, as the entire world goes black.

    Kate’s wrist, holding her sword, is grabbed by his other hand, and a foot, which Kate dazedly notes probably belongs to someone else, kicks her in her stomach hard enough that she doubles over. Regaining some of her senses, Kate reaches down for her knife still strapped to her thigh, and blindly stabs the wrist of the hand holding her own down. As the huge soldier screams in pain, his hand falls away from Kate’s face, and tapping into her last resort energy stores, Kate kicks herself off the wall and into him, driving her sword, now free of his hold, deep into his stomach and through his back.

    As he drops, Kate almost falls with him, but she catches herself just in time, letting the handle of her sword go. Another punch against the left side of her head nearly sends her sprawling, but the wall behind her stops the fall, and the knife still in her left hand slides neatly into the chest of the soldier when he tries to follow it up.

    Shoving him to the side, Kate gets a few seconds to gather herself, as the other two soldiers seemingly think twice about how to attack her, all of them breathing heavily. The brief reprieve allows Kate to hear the footsteps running up the stairs, and she immediately knows that this is the end.

    She probably has it in her to finish these two off, but the several pairs of boots coming up the stairs are definitely too much, especially with her bow somewhere down at the last turn of the staircase, possibly too far to reach.

    Bang.

    Bang.

    The soldiers across from her fall with barely a second between them, and Kate’s head whips up the stairs, her heart soaring at the sight. Yelena and Sonya run down the stairs, both with automatic rifles in their hands, presumably taken from the soldiers they have fought before as well, masks back on their faces.

    Allowing herself a moment to breathe, Kate leans back against the wall, swaying ever so slightly on her feet. As they arrive at the landing where Kate made her stand, Sonya crouches down next to Maxine, checking her pulse. Yelena goes to Kate, eyes scanning her for visible injuries before she is close enough to grab her forearm with one hand, holding her up while the other hovers over Kate, searching for injuries.

    “Is this your blood? Where are you hurt?”

    Kate nods before shaking her head, probably sending some mixed messages, wishing the mummy mask away once again, to be able to look at Yelena’s face, even as she warms at the worry in Yelena’s voice.

    “I am…khrm, fine. You should see the other guy.”

    She hopes Yelena can tell she is smiling behind her mask, despite hurting all over. Her head pounds like it’s about to explode, probably along with a concussion and a broken nose, while her ribs and hip are probably at least severely bruised as well. Yelena huffs at her words but stops hovering, her hand stilling on Kate’s arm.

    “Is she alive?”

    Kate’s next question is posed to Sonya, glancing at her for a second. She is wearing a mask similar to Yelena’s, but without the goggles, so when she smiles, Kate can see her eyes crinkle.

    “Her pulse is strong, but we will have to carry her out. I think she is out for good.” Kate exhales slowly, nodding to herself. Grabbing onto Yelena’s forearm, she gives it a squeeze before pushing off of the wall, to gather her things.

    “Okay. I…I will get my things.”

    Quickly, Kate half-jogs half-limps down the steps separating her from her bow, picking it up. None of the soldiers move but the footsteps running up the stairs are probably only a level or two below them now so Kate hurries back up, as much as her aching hip will let her. The bow is collapsed and attached to her back in a few seconds, and she is thankful when Yelena hands her her sword, having pulled it out of the big soldier’s body for her. Nodding to herself, Kate exhales before looking over at Yelena and Sonya.

    “Let me take her. I…don’t think I have much fight left in me today.”

    Clicking the button on the handle of her sword, Kate retracts the blade. With a deep sigh, Kate pulls out a smoke arrow, her last, and activates it before throwing it down the stairs, hopefully slowing down their pursuers and hiding their ascent at least for a little while longer. “Are you sure?”

    At Yelena’s question, Kate nods, stepping up to Maxine.

    “Yeah, just uh, help me get her onto my back.”

    With Sonya’s and Yelena’s help, they sit her up and Kate crouches down to put Maxine on her back in a fireman’s carry, acutely aware of the boots sounding very close by now. Thankfully, Maxine is small and light, and it’s only due to the beating she just took, that Kate has to grab onto Yelena’s and Sonya’s hands to help her back on her feet. “Let’s go.”

    They make it up one level before Kate hears the soldiers behind them cough, probably just reaching the purple fog. After another one, Kate pauses for a second, trying to re-align Maxine on her shoulders, the limp body a lot more challenging to carry than she thought it would be based on just the weight.

    “Do you want to switch?”

    Yelena stops next to her but keeps her eyes on the stairs behind them.

    “No, no. I’m good. She’s just…she keeps slipping.”

    Jostling Maxine around, Kate starts making her way up the stairs again, swallowing the hiss at the sharp pain in her hip. Her mask also makes it hard to breathe, especially now that it’s soaked with sweat and based on the smell of iron penetrating Kate’s nostrils, also blood. Yelena falls into step behind her, guarding her back and they make it another three levels, almost halfway through before the soldiers start to catch up to them. Panting, Kate tries to haul Maxine up the stairs faster, her whole body feeling as if it’s on fire, both from pain and exhaustion.

    The first shot rings out on their end, Yelena firing down the stairway as the footsteps sound closer and Kate hears a body thud shortly after but has no time to turn back. Sonya turns back to join Yelena behind Kate, having led them up the stairs until now and Kate just hopes that there won’t be another unwelcome surprise coming at them from one of the other levels’ exits on the side, or down the stairs from above them.

    Shots start ringing out every couple of seconds, one even ricocheting off of the railing on Kate’s left and she puts all her focus into breathing right and going as fast as she can, trusting Yelena and Sonya to keep her, and themselves, safe.

    In a few torturous minutes, just as Kate thinks she is reaching her limit, her thighs practically shaking with exhaustion, they reach the top of the staircase, the roof exit appearing right in front of Kate. It allows her to reach into the last reserves of her energy, jostling Maxine a bit on her shoulder one last time, and she practically sprints up the stairs, throwing the door open and leaving the shots behind.

    The roof, by definition, is a lot more spacious than the stairway, which means they lose their tactical advantage as soon as the soldiers make it out into the open. That also means that they have to get across and cut the wire as soon as they can before the henchmen have a chance to catch up and corner them against the edge.

    Kate hears the door open behind her, assuming Yelena and Sonya are just a step behind, and runs to the edge of the building, where Yelena and she arrived what feels like several hours ago. Her muscles shake with exertion, but she is careful when putting Maxine down, quickly looking behind her to check Yelena and Sonya are okay.

    Except, Yelena is nowhere to be seen.

    Sonya catches up to her barely a second later, panting just as heavily as Kate. “Where is she?”

    Through heavy breathing, Sonya breathes out her answer, holding onto her ribs and leaning a bit oddly to the side.

    “She…Holding them up…while we set up. She said…You knew what to do.”

    Blinking twice, Kate glances back at the exit on the roof, the shed-like structure not isolating the sounds of repetitive gunshots completely. Reaching for her bow on her back, Kate pulls it out and her cable arrow with the same motion, pressing the buttons on both to extend them. “Are you okay?”

    Throwing a worried glance at Sonya, Kate nocks the arrow, before raising her bow and aiming across the space between the two buildings.

    “Yes. One of those fucks broke a rib or two I think.”

    The wind is still ripping through their clothes, bringing a welcome cool to Kate’s hot and sweat-covered body, but her arrow makes it across without a problem, embedding itself in the shed on the other skyscraper’s roof. Attaching it on their end, Kate completes the zipline and turns to Sonya.

    “You go first, take Maxine. I’ll wait for her.”

    Sonya looks hesitant, her eyes glancing back at the shed before they meet Kate’s again. “She said we all go.”

    Not even trying to cover her eye-roll, Kate shakes her head. Channeling all the authority she can muster up, Kate nods at the zipline before looking back at Sonya.

    “Nope. Now, strap in.”

    She would like to think that Sonya obeys her request due to respect, but it probably has more to do with her own pain and fearing for Yelena’s safety as well. Nevertheless, Sonya starts attaching herself to the line, while Kate anxiously stands guard.

    “Kate, go.”

    Almost having forgotten about their comms, Kate jumps a little at Yelena’s voice in her ear, while Sonya straps herself in.

    “Yeah, no. Out of the question.”

    Only now just realizing that the sound of machine-gun fire is coming through her coms as well as filtering out from the shed, Kate flinches at the repeating shots as she helps attach Maxine to Sonya and then to carry her to the edge.

    “Kate, I am serious.”

    Next to her, Sonya huffs and Kate sees her eye roll through the mask as well, before she joins their conversation.

    “She is right, Yelena. Get your ass here.”

    With that, Sonya steps off the ledge, holding tightly onto Maxine, and slides away into the darkness. No more words can be heard from Yelena, but the sound and intensity of the shooting don’t seem to diminish and Kate begins to seriously worry, even as she attaches herself to the line as well. The dried blood on her face makes it itchy, especially as she furrows her brows, keeping her eye on the door.

    “We made it across.”

    Sonya speaks in a few seconds, and Kate hums in the affirmative, standing on the ledge and keeping her eyes on the shed but Yelena is still nowhere to be seen.

    “Take her…Ow! Ugh, take her downstairs, Sonya. Kate, go. I will be right behind.” Yelena cries out slightly as she speaks and Kate has half a mind to detach herself from the line and drag her away herself.

    “Copy that.”

    Sonya’s voice is strained through the receiver and Kate hopes her injury is more annoying than it is serious.

    “Yelena if you don’t get here in 60 seconds, I’m going back for you. I swear to god.” Her answer comes in a growl from Yelena, that under any other circumstances would be both amusing and endearing, but now only serves to frustrate Kate more. She begins to count down in her head and gets to 34 when suddenly the door slams open and Yelena sprints out. Behind her, at least two dozen men run out of the door only a few seconds later and Kate curses herself for not preparing an arrow to fire back as they start shooting at them, just as she comes to a realization.

    Yelena won’t have time to attach herself to the line.

    “I will catch you.”

    Hoping that Yelena heard her through the rapid gunfire, Kate waits with open arms, literally. It seems Yelena did because as soon as she is close enough, she launches herself at Kate, taking them both over the edge as bullets whizz by them.

    Kate’s arms go around Yelena instinctively, even as the breath is knocked out of her for the umpteenth time today, and hold her tightly around her waist, as their legs tangle in the air, holding onto each other. Even over the wind roaring by them, and tearing through their clothes, Kate can hear her heavy breathing, as bullets fly around them. Worry fills her, and as soon as they make it to the other side, Kate pulls Yelena to the ground, pushing her away to check her for injuries, touching her all over.

    “Are you hit?”

    The coiled-up tension in Kate’s stomach begins to unravel when she hears Yelena’s signature low chuckle, grabbing onto Kate’s hand to still it.

    “I am way too talented than that.”

    Exhaling, Kate finally allows herself to take a deep breath, her exhaustion beginning to creep back in now that she knows Yelena is safe. For a second, she allows herself to lean back against the small wall behind her, also leaning against Yelena to her side. Yelena takes a breather too, the two of them just panting next to each other for a few seconds, their hands still holding onto one another, while bullets embed themselves into the wall above them. “Come on.”

    The soldiers on the other roof have finally stop shooting and the words spur Kate to action, after one last heavy sigh. She allows Yelena to pull her up with their joined hands, glancing across the space between the buildings. While some soldiers still remain on the roof, the majority of them seem to have filed back into the skyscraper, no doubt making their way downstairs to catch them while they flee.

    To put it mildly, they are still far from safety.

    Kate quickly detaches herself before jumping up the wall to collect her cable arrow, detaching the wire that took them across as well, and destroying anyone’s chance to follow them across.

    “Sonya, did you find the car?”

    The answer is breathy, Sonya is obviously both exhausted and in pain but it still manages to carry a serious amount of sass.

    “Um, no? We just made it to the elevator. She is heavier than she looks.” Worried about Sonya and Maxine both, Kate quickly follows Yelena to the door, and down the stairs. The camera above the door is the least of their worries, but Kate makes a mental note to delete all footage from today as soon as they get home, as it probably just recorded them zipping between the buildings.

    “We will be there in a minute.”

    The way down to the elevator is quick, compared to their progress until this point and as Yelena said, they make it there just as the doors open about a minute later. Maxine is propped up, sitting against a wall, still pale and unconscious and Kate throws Sonya a worried look as well, as she leans against it next to her, holding onto her side with one hand, holding Maxine up with the other.

    “How are you feeling?”

    Snorting, Sonya’s eyes sparkle behind her mask, amused even in her discomfort. “Like I just came from the fucking spa.”

    Kate can’t help but chuckle, throwing a glance at Yelena. She still has her mask on, so Kate can’t see her face but her huff sounds more amused than annoyed, as far as she can tell. Kate crouches down to take Maxine again, grabbing her wrist and her thigh to lift her onto her shoulder with Yelena’s help.

    The elevator doors begin to close but Yelena quickly jams her hand in between, stopping them before she pulls one of Sonya’s arms around her shoulder.

    “Kate, you go first.”

    Following Yelena’s instruction, Kate steps into the elevator, careful not to hit Maxine’s head against the door or the walls. Her eyes are once again bothered by the artificial lighting, and she leans carefully back against the wall, eager to take the weight off of her aching hip, closing her eyes for just a moment.

    Yelena and Sonya hobble in, press the button to the ground floor, and then the one to close the doors repeatedly. The journey feels even longer than the one upstairs at the beginning of their evening, and Kate sincerely hopes there won’t be a group of men waiting for them downstairs, since apart from Yelena, none of them really seem to be in fighting shape. There is no unfriendly Asian lady halting the elevator this time, probably due to the late hour, and in a couple of minutes, Yelena raises her gun as they reach the ground floor, the door sliding open with an ominous creak.
