Leaning Sonya against the wall, Yelena sticks her head out to check for any danger but indicates they come a second later with a jut of her chin. Sonya hobbles out, holding onto her rifle still and Kate follows, once again careful not to hit Maxine against anything. They make their way through the grimy corridor, even more dimly lit than the first time around, probably because the restaurant it belongs to is long closed by now.

    As they reach the exit, Kate hears sirens and the three (four) of them halt in front of the door. Yelena takes a deep breath before she attempts to crack the door open but finds it locked. That at least explains the lack of the “welcome party” from the soldiers downstairs, and Kate watches the back of her head as she lowers into a crouch to pick the lock, hanging the automatic rifle onto her shoulder as she does.

    In about a minute, Yelena straightens up, taking her gun into her hand again, before turning over to Sonya and Kate.

    “Are you ready?”

    “For an ice bath at home, and an aspirin.”

    Snorting at Sonya’s returning snark again, Kate smiles behind her mask before she nods at Yelena, getting ready to run. As the door is cracked ajar, an alarm immediately goes off and Yelena quickly throws it all the way open.

    “Run!”

    And they do…sort of.

    Yelena jogs across the road, leading their little party, Sonya limps behind her, mostly managing to keep her rifle up, and Kate power walks, no longer able to run or even jog with the added weight of Maxine on her shoulders.

    Their luck, seemingly having abandoned them earlier tonight, finally finds them again and they make it across the road and to the parked van without either the police or Fisk’s soldiers showing up. Yelena fishes out the keys from her bag and opens the door for Sonya, who gets in before helping Kate put Maxine onto the back seat.

    “You take the front.”

    Kate doesn’t argue and even takes the rifle that Sonya literally shoves into her hand, quickly rounding the van and taking the shotgun seat by Yelena’s side. By the time she closes her door, Yelena is turning the keys and the engine comes to life.

    In a few short seconds, they are off.

    Yelena turns right at the end of the street, taking them in the opposite direction of Sonya’s and Kate’s building. As Kate checks the rearview mirror, she can see the large group of soldiers along with several police officers, run down the street towards their car, and behind them, at least 6 police cars are parked in the middle of the wide street, blue and red lights flashing. Noting their van’s very modest advance, Kate clears her throat before speaking to Yelena, only just now noticing how gravelly her own voice is as they stop at a light. “Yelena, do you maybe want to…”

    From the tone of her voice, Kate can tell that Yelena is smiling as she answers. “The first rule of disappearing, Kate, is that you never ever run.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate glances at her but with the stupid mask covering her face still, she is even less able to tell if Yelena is joking or not. The light turns green and Yelena drives forward at a leisurely speed, leaving the soldiers, who were about to get uncomfortably close to their van, safely behind.

    Kate keeps an eye on them in the side mirror, just in case, and can see a few police officers run back towards their cruisers, but none of them raise their weapons at the van before Yelena takes a turn to the left unhurriedly, even taking the time to use her indicator. In the back seat, Sonya rummages around but Kate doesn’t dare to look at them just yet, tirelessly scanning their surroundings for suspicious SUVs, police cars, or anything that might be after them. Compared to the highly strung atmosphere of the last several hours, however, the next few minutes are jarringly slow and borderline laid-back.

    Taking a few left and right turns on the almost deserted, 3 am streets, Yelena drives them away in silence, getting further and further away from the scene, seemingly without direction. “Sonya, home or doctor?”

    It’s a testament to how seriously Sonya takes the question, that she waits a few seconds to think it over.

    Turning around in her seat, Kate checks on Maxine and her in the backseat, the latter lying sprawled out in Sonya’s lap. It seems that Sonya did have some medical equipment in the van after all because on Maxine’s stomach, there is a portable blood pressure monitor and an empty syringe, most likely used by Sonya already.

    “Home. I stopped the bleeding, for now, and I don’t think she is in shock, just exhausted… and she probably needs about a bucket of blood.”

    Scrunching up her nose at the slightly unpleasant mental image, Kate turns back forward just as the hazard light flashes green on the dashboard. Yelena punches it without hesitation and in the side mirror, Kate can see the side of the van flicker, and become faded white this time around. Once the van’s exterior is changed, Yelena reaches for her mask, pulling it off. Kate should probably be embarrassed about how nice it is to finally see her face, taking in her flushed, glistening skin, and messed-up hair. Apart from a bruise on the side of her head, and a slightly split lip, Yelena seems completely unharmed, probably in the best shape out of the four of them. She even smiles a little, but it disappears as soon Kate takes off her own mask too, and Yelena turns to look at her.

    “I look that great, huh?”

    It’s a rhetorical question, posed with a grin that feels painful in several spots on her face, and the fact that Yelena only throws Kate a worried look instead of an amused or even exasperated one only serves to prove how shit she must look.

    Pulling down the visor, Kate tries to look at herself in the small mirror but the car is dark and the streetlights periodically lighting up the interior of the van are not bright enough either. She can tell that she does indeed look severely fucked up, but not much more than that. Her face is covered in blood, at least some of which is definitely her own, particularly below her nose which looks somewhat swollen already, and slightly askew with a cut in the middle. Reaching up to the back of her head, Kate feels around with her hand and is unsurprised to feel her hand coming away warm, wet, and sticky. All in all, she is feeling remarkably good for how bad she looks, and has to remind herself that most of the blood covering her face and clothes is probably not her own, considering that she is still standing. With a deep sigh, she puts the visor back up, glancing at Yelena.

    “Most of this is not mine.”

    Yelena looks back at her, exhaling long with a nod.

    “Good.”

    In the next couple of minutes, Yelena drives slowly, obeying traffic laws to the T. Proving that her nerves are made of steel, she even drives patiently forward when a pair of police cruisers speed by them, sirens blazing. Still, Kate can see her relax when they are gone, Yelena’s hands easing up their grip on the steering wheel when they turn a corner behind their van.

    Kate is similarly nervous and would have probably jumped the gun in her stead, but she smiles nonetheless, trying to reassure Yelena whenever she glances in Kate’s direction, swallowing down her own worry. Maxine never regains her consciousness and Kate twists around a few times to check if Sonya is still awake, uncharacteristically quiet for once. The roads are not deserted, it’s New York after all but there is little traffic to keep them up. If it weren’t for the thick layer of sweat and blood covering Kate, and her gnawing worry for Sonya, and even for Maxine, their little night drive could almost be called serene. That is until Yelena straightens next to her, eyes flitting between the rearview window and the road. “What’s wrong?”

    Yelena wets her lips, glancing at Kate before she is back to looking at the road ahead. “We are being followed.”

    Quickly, Kate turns around. There is only one car behind them, a non-descript, black, maybe dark-blue sedan, too far away to tell its model.

    “How long have they been there?”

    Yelena glances into the rearview mirror again, before signaling to the right, slowing down a little before the turn.

    “They took the same three turns as us. Left, left, right.

    The car behind their van slows down too, keeping its distance, in maybe the clearest indicator possible, that it is indeed following them. From this distance, Kate can’t make out how many people are sitting in there, or if they are the soldiers from the Limitless building, or someone new.

    Yelena makes the turn and begins to speed up. A few seconds later, the car behind them turns right as well, still keeping further away from them. Picking up the unused machine rifle from beside her, Kate quickly passes it back to Sonya on the back seat, just in case. Reaching for her bow, Kate presses the button to expand it, reaching back into her quiver for an acid arrow. From her periphery, Kate sees Yelena glance at her weapon, huffing almost inaudibly.

    “Do not use that unless it is absolutely necessary. We do not need another spectacle.” Nodding, Kate keeps her eyes on the car in the side mirror, but it doesn’t look like it wants to come any closer to them.

    “I won’t start shooting unless they do.”

    Yelena doesn’t look particularly happy with her answer but she nods, eyes back on the road, scouring their surroundings. Muscles tense, Kate prepares herself for a fight, alternating between looking at the car following them in the side mirror and the streets around them, remembering the last time Sonya’s Jaguar got totaled by an SUV from the side. The light right ahead of them changes from green to yellow, then to red but Yelena steps on the accelerator, quickly turning the street as it changes.

    Gripping her acid arrow, nocked and ready to be drawn, Kate waits for the car to start chasing them, the soldiers probably figuring out that their cover is blown by Yelena’s quick maneuver. Muscles locked, and heart speeding up, she waits with bated breath. What happens next is quite unexpected.

    In the side mirror, Kate watches as the car reaches the intersection…and just keeps growing forward, seemingly abandoning its mission. It does little to alleviate their nerves. Kate keeps her arrow nocked and ready and even while continuously scanning the surrounding streets, she can see Yelena in a similar state of alertness. A quick glance at Sonya reveals that she is the same, one hand gripping Maxine’s leather jacket, the other holding her machine gun between her legs, its barrel pointing at the floor.

    The next ten minutes are tense, Kate almost at the edge of her seat, anticipating the ambush, but it never comes.

    Through various twists and turns, changing the appearance of their van twice, they make it back to the parking lot in Queens in about twenty-five minutes, Yelena pulling into the same parking spot from before, right next to Kate’s Mercedes.

    The hazard warning button flashes green and Yelena pushes it one last time, changing the appearance of their van before she shuts off the engine while Kate waits to see what she does, prepared to follow her lead.

    “Okay. I’ll be lookout. Kate, help Sonya get Maxine into the other car. If anything goes to shit, Sonya, you take Maxine home, Kate and I will split, lead them away, and find our own way home.”

    Yelena waits for both their affirmative answers, before she gets out of the van, picking up her rifle again. Kate gets out too, putting her bow on her back, before walking briskly around the van. Distractedly, she notes that the car is a faded red now, with a logo belonging to ‘Spyder Electric’ branded on the side door that Kate quickly opens and slides aside. Grabbing Maxine’s still limp arms, Kate pulls her into a seated position, before leaning into the van to pick her up in a bridal carry, while swallowing a groan. With the adrenaline slowly leaving her system, the sharp pain in her hip and ribs is harder to ignore but will have to be pushed aside until they are all safely home.

    Slipping by her, Sonya walks to the Mercedes, trying the door.

    “Who has the keys?”

    Letting out a tired sigh, Kate jostles Maxine around to lift her a bit higher. “Me. Right pocket.”

    Sonya steps up to her and it’s probably a testament to how tired and in pain she must be too, that other than a playful wink, she makes no comment about reaching into the front pocket of Kate’s pants and pulling out the keys.

    Unlocking the car, she quickly opens the door on the right side of the car and gets in, assisting Kate as she carefully places Maxine in the backseat.

    “Yelena? Good to go?”

    As she straightens up, Kate takes in Yelena’s small, but intimidating form as she guards their back.

    “Yes.”

    With that, she walks quickly to the other side, getting into the driver’s seat. After closing the back door on Maxine and Sonya, Kate gets into the passenger seat again. They pull out and Kate lets out a long exhale, closing her eyes and resting back against her seat, allowing herself to relax for the first time since they noticed the sedan following them. Kate gives herself 30 seconds, just breathing in and out before she opens her eyes and turns to Yelena. She still looks alert, but the tension from before seems to have left her too, eyes scanning around them but her hold on the steering wheel loose, shoulders relaxed. “What do you think that was?”

    Not turning to look at Kate, Yelena seems thoughtful.

    “I do not think it was the same men we fought before.”

    The sentence feels incomplete, but Yelena pauses, thoughtful and Kate feels the need to alleviate some of the tension from the evening.

    “I agree. It probably wasn’t Fisk’s men, because why wouldn’t they have attacked? Do you think it was the FBI?-“ Yelena opens her mouth to answer but Kate barrels on, her nerves about the last several hours, and the tense silence of the last half an hour finally catching up to her, expressing itself in her propensity to word vomit that she mostly kept a lid on since Yelena came to help out. “-But then why didn’t they try to arrest us? That doesn’t make sense. Unless they don’t know who we were. Or do know, but are trying to gather evidence? But still, why did they just keep driving? I would say it was just a random car, but it definitely followed us, so I don’t know. Rojas is a possibility too, but what would he want? He has better ways to reach us than just following us around. So yeah. I don’t know. What do you think?”

    Yelena smiles finally, slow and small, but she doesn’t turn to look at Kate as she answers. “I will run the plates tomorrow, but I will be very surprised if they don’t turn out to be stolen.”

    Nodding, Kate shuffles around a little in her seat, mindful of her injuries. “Good call.”

    To her left, Yelena huffs amusedly, eyes still scanning the buildings and streets around, instead of looking back at Kate.

    “So…who do you think?”

    Yelena’s cheeks lift as she smiles for a second before her face turns thoughtful. She is silent for a moment longer, before she answers.

    “Law enforcement is possible. FBI, or cops. The car was a very generic sedan, they use ones like it for surveillance. But Rojas having us watched is just as likely. He probably likes to keep an eye on his investments.”

    Sonya joins the conversation from the backseat.

    “It is also possible it’s a third…fourth?-“ She thinks, eyebrows furrowed before shaking her head, seemingly giving up the count. “-party. With an asset this valuable, if word made it out that it exists, others might be trying to get their hands on it too.”

    Yelena nods, thoughtful, and Kate puffs out her cheeks to exhale, not wanting to think about how this already complicated clusterfuck of a situation might be even more complicated than they already know it is.

    “Speaking of. We will need to come up with a way to go back for the data. The program is installed now, we can just copy it over to the drive.”

    Groaning slightly, Kate closes her eyes at Yelena’s words. In all the excitement and the fighting and the freeing of a Black Widow from mind control, she almost forgot that they left behind the sole purpose of their mission.

    “Uh, shit. Yeah.”

    For a second, they are all quiet, before Kate has a thought, giving her a sliver of hope. “Hey, maybe Maxine knows something we can use. She has been working for them, she must know what they do.”

    Glancing at Yelena, Kate’s excitement is dampened by her expression. Her face darkens for a moment, before she seems to shake it off, glancing at Kate as they slow down, and then stop at a red light.

    “We will see…”

    It seems that she is uncertain for a moment, rolling her lips together before she speaks again. “It…the mind control, it has a way of warping your head. It might not be possible to question her for a while.”

    Swallowing, Kate nods, holding her eyes. It only lasts for a few moments, before Yelena turns back forward, driving them forward as the light changes. Kate would never want to pressure Maxine, after what she has been through, but this sure is an unfortunate turn of events.

    The rest of the ride goes by with only a few words spoken between them and soon, after some tactical doubling back to expose possible cars following them, they are back at Kate and Sonya’s building, Yelena parking the black Mercedes back in its spot in the garage. Once they are out of the car, Yelena helps Kate get Maxine out of the car, holding her feet while Kate grips her under the armpits. Sonya hobbles ahead, and Kate can only hope that none of their neighbors is out for a midnight ride or walk, as anyone walking in on the image of three blood-covered women carrying a fourth unconscious one would surely raise some uncomfortable questions.

    Maxine keeps slipping out of their hold, and by the time they make it up to Sonya’s floor, Kate loses her patience with this particular way of carrying her, her biceps thrumming uncomfortably with the weight.

    As Sonya unlocks her door, Kate jostles Maxine one last time, the girl’s head leaning back against her chest. During their ride home, they did hear some weak groans from her but for the duration of their entire journey, she remained unconscious. According to Yelena and Sonya, that’s completely normal but Kate worries, already feeling a connection to Maxine, her heart aching for her, after having witnessed the aftermath of her coming out of mind control.

    As they walk through the front door, Kate hears the pitter-patter of paws jogging towards them on the wooden floors and as Sonya switches the lights on, Kate smiles at the image of Lucky emerging from somewhere within the apartment.

    Pizza Dog walks along their side, as if he was a part of their group all along, sniffing at their clothes. Kate tries to shoo him away, not wanting to dirty up his fur but he doesn’t go, looking up at Kate with a serious face.

    They carry Maxine to the couch and carefully lay her down and just as Kate straightens up, a half-naked, and less-than-half-awake Thomas walks down the hallway, squinting at the light. “How did it go-?”

    Tommy looks around, eyes visibly becoming more alert as he takes in their various states of injured and blood-covered. His eyes finally land on Maxine, eyebrows rising. “And who’s that?”

    Sonya is already in action, stepping up to Maxine to begin to unzip her jacket. “This is Maxine. We just freed her. She is a Widow.”

    That is enough information for Tommy, turning back towards their bedroom presumably. “I’ll get a shirt.”

    Sonya enters her ‘doctor mode’, instructing Kate and Yelena.

    “Yelena, go get the first aid kit and tell Tommy to get 2 units of blood and the warmer. O negative. Kate, help me with her.”

    Yelena walks away, probably to do as she was asked while Kate steps back to Maxine and Sonya.

    “Get her boots off. We need to look at those legs.”

    Kate takes off the bled-through, torn pieces of the shirts she used as a makeshift bandage and unlaces Maxine’s boots one by one, while Sonya undresses her upper body, throwing the clothes in a pile to the side that Lucky sniffs curiously. Once they are pulled off, Kate does the same with the boots, before pulling off Maxine’s socks as well, winching at how hard they are with dried blood on one side.

    Meanwhile, Sonya unbuttons Maxine’s pants, pulling them off of her legs with Kate’s help, and just as they finish, Yelena arrives back with the first aid kit. Apart from the new stab wound on her left calf, there is a barely healed one on the back of her thigh, clearly left unattended, slightly red, and healing badly.

    Upon its discovery, Kate glances at Yelena and sees her face harden, but they continue inspecting her for other injuries. On Maxine’s shoulder, there is a big, ugly bruise, possibly from the time Kate kicked her out of the car when she attacked them for the first time, but that at least is yellow, and seemingly in the process of healing.

    There are a few fresh bruises, one on the side of her head, along with a small cut and another on her hip, that are most likely from the explosion that ultimately knocked her out, but thankfully none of those look particularly serious.

    “Kate, go wash your hands.”

    The instruction is given to Kate by Yelena while behind them, Tommy arrives with the blood- warming machine and sets it up, and Sonya is cleaning off Maxine’s arm to find a suitable vein for an IV. Pulling off and tossing her tactical gloves to the side, Kate walks to the bathroom, toeing off her boots on the way there, Lucky following at her heels, tail swishing lazily.

    Switching the lights on, Kate goes to the sink, glancing at her reflection in the mirror. It’s not a surprise that Yelena was worried, based on how she looks. Her face is covered in blood, especially around the eyes, where her mask didn’t cover it, and below her nose and on her chin, where her own nose bled on it. Her nose itself is somewhat swollen, with a short cut across it, and her suit, despite being black, glints in a sticky kind of way in the dim bathroom lights that tell Kate that it’s also covered in blood.

    With a deep sigh, Kate attempts to compartmentalize her feelings about that, focusing on the task at hand instead. Switching on the tap, she washes her hands first, before leaning down with a small groan, to splash water at her face as well.

    Straightening up, Kate reaches to her right for a towel, lifting it to her face to wipe away some of the grime and blood before she goes back to the living room to assist with Maxine, lest it drips or dried flakes of it fall into her wounds.

    Physically jerking, she almost yelps when she opens her eyes and Yelena is suddenly standing beside her, meeting her eyes in the mirror. She looks serious, taking in Kate, her face looking marginally better with at least some of the blood washed away.

    “You got shot a third time?”

    Kate sighs, looking away from Yelena to put the small towel under the tap before she looks back at her with a shrug and a half-hearted grin.

    “At least they missed my ass.”

    Kate sees as she opens her mouth before closing it, the muscles on her jew jumping as she grinds her teeth together.

    “This is not funny.”

    Kate looks away again, at her reflection instead, dabbing at her face with the towel to wipe away the more dried patches of blood.

    “I mean? Okay, yeah, I know.”

    She hears Yelena exhale before there is a sigh and a gentle hand on Kate’s elbow. “Come here.”

    Letting herself be turned around, Kate meets Yelena’s eyes again, handing her the lukewarm, wet towel. She continues Kate’s efforts, dabbing at her face.

    “What happened? Who did it?”

    Wetting her lips, Kate leans back against the sink, allowing herself to take some weight off of her aching body.

    “Some soldiers. I took them down, turned my back and one of them was too stupid to stay down.”

    No longer holding her eyes, Yelena’s gaze is focused on her face, wiping at Kate’s chin. She grimaces at the feeling of the wet towel against her lips, her face scrunching up a little, and amusement sparks in Yelena’s eyes before she turns serious again.

    “Are they dead?”

    Gulping, Kate glances to the side before her gaze returns to Yelena’s face, seeing eyes harden for a second at Kate’s non-verbal answer.

    “No. But they won’t be firing at anyone anytime soon.”

    Yelena meets her eyes again, and Kate can see that she is very much not satisfied with her answer, but a second later Yelena tosses the wet towel into the sink. Grabbing onto Kate’s chin, she tilts her face upwards first, to the side, and then downwards a little, eyes scanning her face seriously.

    “Your nose is broken. We will have to put it in place.”

    Kate nods, Yelena’s fingers still holding onto her chin.

    “Let’s finish up Maxine first. I can wait until after.”

    Green eyes leaving her nose, Yelena meets her gaze once more, holding them for a few moments before she lets go of Kate’s chin, sighing.

    “Okay.”

    They look at each other for a few more seconds, before Yelena turns away, walking out of the room. Kate follows and as they re-enter the room, Sonya looks up from next to Maxine, eyes jumping from Kate to Yelena and back to Kate.

    “Nice of you to finally join us.”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate picks a pair of rubber gloves off of the coffee table, putting them on. “I don’t think me bleeding into her wound would have been particularly effective for her healing process, sorry.”

    Sonya huffs at her words but continues her task without another snarky comment. Lucky, having left Kate in the bathroom sometime before Yelena arrived, is curled up on one of the armchairs around the coffee table, sleepy eyes following the events unfolding in the living room. Picking up some disinfectant and some gauze, Kate passes them to Yelena, before lifting Maxine’s leg and putting some towels underneath.

    As Yelena cleans the wound on both sides of Maxine’s leg, Kate hands her replacement pieces of gauze and takes the used, bloody ones from her hand. The knife went all the way through her calf but thankfully it doesn’t start bleeding again heavily as they wipe away the dried blood from around the wound.

    Once the cleaning is finished, Yelena assesses the wound, pulling it slightly apart before she starts stitching it up, just as the blood warmer beeps behind their backs on the table. Kate passes the first warmed-up blood bag to Sonya before Yelena calls her back to her side. “Look at what I am doing. You need to learn this also.”

    Kate rejoins her, crouching by her side but can’t help but get defensive. “I know how to stitch a wound.”

    Yelena takes the time to throw her a look, one eyebrow raised but she looks more teasing than purposefully offensive even as she speaks.

    “Not very well, you do not.”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate huffs but remains by her side. Yelena stitches the wound three times, with different types of thread. First, she stitches the flesh inside, creating two X shapes with a thread that apparently dissolves without having to be taken out. Next, she stitches up the thin layer of fat between the muscle and the skin, with similar X-shaped loops. Lastly, she moves to the skin, stitching it up with the standard wound thread that Kate is already familiar with. When she is done, Yelena cuts the last piece of thread after knotting it, before passing a new suture kit and the forceps to Kate.

    “You do the other side.”

    Gulping, Kate takes the tools, and unpacks the suture kit but halts before starting. “Shouldn’t we give her some form of anesthesia?”

    Glancing at Yelena, kneeling next to her by the couch, Kate meets her eyes. She smiles, shaking her head.

    “Sonya already gave her some with the first IV… And she is out like a light anyway.” Kate nods, looking back at the short, deep wound on the side of Maxine’s calf. “First, you need to stitch up the wound inside the muscle. You make these figure eights,-“ She shows the shape with her fingers over the wound, glancing at Kate to see if she is paying attention.

    “-Be careful to not make a closed loop and tangle it up. Just do the x shapes and pull it together gently.”

    Nodding, Kate rolls her lips together, before leaning further over the wound and threading the needle through one side of the wound.

    “This avoids bleeding between the tissue, that can cause infection.”

    Kate nods, not taking her eyes off of her work, threading the needle through once again. She loops it back, creating the first X while listening to Yelena’s explanation. As she works, Yelena watches, humming as the wound is pulled closed.

    “Hm, good. Now pull that thread and tie a knot with this end.”

    Kate follows the instructions, trying to not think about the fact that it was she, who caused this much damage to Maxine in the first place.

    Layer after layer, Kate stitches the wound, Yelena talking her through it. After what feels like forever, the final suture over the skin is made, and Kate leans back on her heels as she cuts the thread.

    It looks good, almost identical to the one Yelena made and when Kate looks over at her, she gives her a small, tired but proud smile.

    “Well done. Now you know how to actually stitch a wound.”

    Pursing her lips, Kate smiles at her, watching as Yelena prepares the materials to put a bandage over the new stitches. Glancing around as she pulls off her lightly bloody rubber gloves, tossing them in the makeshift trash bin on the table. Taking in the sight of Lucky snoozing in one of the armchairs, curled up in a ball with his nose tucked under his paw, Kate smiles before she turns back to Yelena.

    “Where are Sonya and Thomas?”

    Yelena doesn’t look up, securing a piece of gauze on both the entry and exit wound, before tying a bandage around it.

    “Sonya is having an ice bath and some vodka. Thomas is helping her.”

    Kate didn’t notice them leaving the room, but she was pretty preoccupied with doing the stitches. Glancing back at Maxine’s sleeping form, she turns back to Yelena. “What now?”

    Getting off of the floor, Yelena stands up, walking over to one of the armchairs across the coffee table as she answers.

    “Now we let her rest,”

    Picking up a folded blanket from the armchair, she walks back and drapes it over Maxine’s sleeping form. For a moment, Kate watches her from the ground as she looks down at Maxine. She looks sad but seems to shake it off after a few seconds, before turning back to Kate.

    “-and we go and fix your nose.”

    Closing her eyes, Kate groans and lets her head fall forward. Getting broken noses put in their place sucks. It sucks a lot. Yelena’s voice is amused from beside her. “Come on.”

    Kate opens her eyes, looking up at Yelena who stands beside her now with a smile, her hand extended down to Kate.

    “Do I really have to?”

    Yelena’s smile widens into a grin.

    “If you did not want to get your nose fixed, you should not have gotten it broken.” With an eye-roll, Kate grabs her hand, letting Yelena pull her to her feet. “Oh yeah, it was definitely on purpose. I just love getting punched in the face.” With Kate standing too, Yelena has to tilt her head back to look back at her smugly. “If you like it so much, I am willing to lend a hand.”

    With the slightly coy smile, Kate almost forgets that they are talking about punching her face. After a moment Yelena walks away, and Kate walks up to Lucky’s sleeping form only being able to come up with a sarcastic laugh.

    “Ha-ha.”

    Leaning over Pizza Dog, Kate strokes the top of his head, smiling when he opens his eye just barely to look up at her.

    “Come on, buddy. Let’s go home.”

    He huffs as if he doesn’t spend approximately 80% of his day snoozing in various comfy locations, but as Kate steps back, he jumps off the armchair, extending his paws in front of him to stretch out his back.

    “Ooh, big stretch.”

    Kate hums at him with a smile, before she walks to the foyer, Lucky jogging at her heels. Yelena, who seems to have reclaimed her phone meanwhile, joins them a second later. Walking up to the now-closed bathroom door, Yelena leans closer to its surface before she speaks.

    “We are going upstairs to fix Kate’s nose. I will be back soon.”

    As Yelena speaks, Kate picks up her backpack from earlier, briefly noting how much equipment they have left behind while fleeing from Limitless. Picking up Lucky’s leash from the console, Kate attaches it to his collar, while Sonya answers from inside the bathroom. “Have fun playing doctor.”

    Sonya’s voice is amused, and Yelena smiles at her words but rolls her eyes when she meets Kate’s gaze. Shrugging, Kate grins back, tired but slowly mellowing out after their eventful evening.

    “Hey, at least if she can tease, she’s probably just fine.”

    Yelena purses her lips, but she is obviously amused as well. She picks up a set of keys from the side console by the door, before opening it.

    “You are right. But I think she will still be a pain in my ass on her deathbed.” Kate chuckles affectionately, glad that Sonya seems mostly okay. The two of them walk back to the elevator, Yelena pressing the button to call it and wordlessly taking Lucky’s leash after he pulls on Kate, making her flinch slightly. The ride upstairs goes by quickly and in a few minutes, Kate is opening her front door, letting Yelena and Lucky go in first. Depositing the backpack on the table by the door and toeing off her boots again, Kate watches as Yelena unclips Lucky’s leash, before ruffling the soft hair on the top of his head. “Good night, krasavchik.”

    With a smile on her face, Kate watches as Pizza Dog trails around Yelena’s feet, rubbing his sides against her legs. Knowing his antics, Kate knows he wants scritches on his butt, and steps up to Yelena, gently shooing him away.

    “Go on, buddy. We got stuff to do.”

    Because he is a stubborn little shit, he does not obey her, jumping up at Kate with two paws and stretching into the motion.

    “Don’t be sassy now. The lady said good night! Go to your place.”

    Dropping back to the ground, he sits down, looking up at Yelena and Kate with his dopey smile. Sighing, Kate gives in, dramatically huffing.

    “Fineee…Show me the butt.”

    Of course, that is the first command of Kate’s that he does actually obey, turning around to present his backside, his tail swishing from side to side in excitement. Next to her, Yelena chuckles and Kate looks up as she leans forward to scritch at the base of Lucky’s tail. “Fanny loves that too…The butt scratches.”

    Kate smiles as Yelena leans down next to her, joining her in spoiling Lucky a little before he is actually sent back to sleep.

    “Do you miss her?”

    Yelena hums, looking at Lucky instead of Kate, smiling at him as he turns around to present his ears for sctritches also.

    “Yes. Melina sends me photos every day, but it is not the same.”

    Smiling at finally learning the answer to the question of who takes care of Yelena’s dog while she is away, which Kate asked weeks ago, she just hums. Giving Lucky a last pat on the head and a kiss on his forehead, Kate sends him away with a gentle slap on his butt. “Go on, Luck. Bedtime.”

    Satisfied with the amount of attention and affection he was given, Lucky slinks away toward Kate’s bedroom, while she leads Yelena to the bathroom, sighing a little at the uncomfortable process she still has to get through before she gets to go to bed.

    Turning the lights on, Kate walks into the room, Yelena following behind. “Uh, let’s get this over with... Do I sit, stand? Where do you want me?” There is an amused huff from Yelena, and she looks almost playful, despite her obvious tiredness too when Kate meets her eyes.

    “Sit.”

    Putting a hand on Kate’s abdomen, Yelen pushes her back gently, eyes still holding hers. The movement itself is not meant to be playful but there is an undercurrent of sensuality in it that sends a jolt down Kate’s spine. Blinking, the corner of her lips tips upward, smiling back at Yelena teasingly.

    “Bossy.”

    Following Yelena’s instructions, Kate steps back with a small grin, watching Yelena’s face for her reaction. With a smile that Yelena obviously tries to hide, she rolls her eyes, turning away towards the sink and not deigning to answer her verbally.

    While she is turned away, Kate sits down on the edge of the bathtub gingerly, masking the flinch that comes with it. It’s not the worst she has been hurt, by far, even just in the last couple of weeks but she aches all over and she really can’t wait to go to bed to sleep this off. “Are you okay?”

    Yelena asks, apparently with eyes on the back of her head since she is bent over Kate’s sink, rummaging around for her first aid kit in the cabinet below.

    “Yeah. I think I just pulled something…several somethings, most likely.” Yelena chuckles, the sound quiet yet feeling loud in Kate’s tiled bathroom. She doesn’t answer but a second later she straightens up, kit securely in her hands. She puts it on the lid of the toilet before turning back to her. She takes a moment, looking Kate over and she looks back, happy to just exist in her presence at the moment.

    “Okay. I will set your nose first. Then, we will check everything else.” A second later Yelena nudges Kate’s foot to the side gently, spreading her legs before she steps in between them. The movement is not meant to be sensual, again, but Kate’s breath catches in her throat for a second as she looks up at Yelena nonetheless. There is a glint in her eyes, as she meets hers, that tells Kate she is aware of how the space between them crackles, too, but it only lasts a moment before she is back to focusing on the task at hand. Leaning over, she grabs Kate’s chin, tilting her head further back, eyes fixed on her nose. “Hold onto the tub, okay? This is going to hurt.”

    Clearing her throat, Kate wants to nod but with her chin still in Yelena’s hold, she can’t. “Okay.”

    Placing both hands on the edge of the tub, Kate gulps, still looking up at Yelena. “I’m going to count to three, okay?”

    “Alright.”

    Yelena glances to meet her eyes for a second as she lets go of Kate’s chin. Stepping closer, one arm goes around Kate’s head, pulling it gently, but firmly against Yelena’s chest, while her hand on the other grabs onto the bridge of Kate’s nose. Despite soot and a faint trace of iron mixing in it, Yelena still smells of vanilla, the scent enveloping Kate as she is pulled close.

    “One,-“ Kate does her best to stay still and to not focus on the fact that she is pressed up against Yelena’s breast, choosing to listen to her heartbeat instead. It sounds fast, thrumming against her ear rhythmically.

    “Two,-“ Before Kate can anticipate the movement and tense up, Yelena yanks her nose to the side with a sudden, precise movement, putting it in place. The pain is searing and sudden, Kate cries out in protest, yanking her face out of her hold.

    “Holy fucking…owww! Ow, ow ow, ow!!”

    Stepping slightly back, Yelena snickers as Kate leans forward, holding onto her nose. As the pain comes at her in waves, she tilts her head up to look at Yelena accusingly. “You said on three!”

    Grinning and still close, Yelena pats her cheek placatingly.

    “That was a lie.”

    Huffing, Kate purses her lips and leans forward to stand up, stepping by Yelena to check her nose in the mirror. It’s still somewhat swollen, but it’s noticeably straighter than before. As she turns back, Yelena looks back at her smugly but still smiling, eyes warm. A second later she puts a hand on Kate’s elbow, pulling her back and away from the mirror gently. “Come on, we still have to clean and tape it.”

    Begrudgingly, Kate sits back on the edge of the tub, winching at the pain in her hip and ribs again. Yelena looks down at her for a moment, sobering up and seemingly in thought. “Can you get this off?”

    She gestures at Kate’s suit, and it’s probably a good idea, the material too thick in the warmth of Kate’s apartment. Nodding, Kate undoes the few buckles tightening up the material, and reaches for the zipper under left her arm. Immediately, she gasps as the movement twists her shoulder and her ribs uncomfortably, the intense pain lodging her breath in her chest. Breathing out slowly she stops, holding up a hand at Yelena.

    “Yeah, one sec.”

    With Yelena standing close to her, Kate hears her exhale slowly, before she steps back between Kate’s legs, leaning forward to reach for the zipper without a word. Kate lets her do it, half distracted by the pain, but still intensely aware of their proximity again. After she is done with the zipper, Yelena’s hands slide under the material to slowly push it off of Kate’s shoulders and down her arms. She breathes in slowly, eyes glued to the side of Yelena’s face, who glances at her once, a playful glint in her eyes as she undresses Kate but otherwise focused on her task.

    Once the suit is pulled off, Yelena steps back, looking at Kate, her previous mirth melting off of her face, eyes dropping to Kate’s chest. Trying to see what she is looking at, Kate looks down, taking in the two, almost black bruises right above her heart, purple spreading out to the rest of her chest.

    Eyes slide upwards, Yelena’s gaze pauses at her neck, and although she can’t see it herself, Kate remembers the feeling of Maxine’s wire around her throat viscerally. It’s not hard to guess that that must have left a mark of its own too, and Kate wets her lips before she tries to lighten the mood.

    “Hey, my eyes are up here.”

    Yelena does glance to meet her gaze, and Kate honestly can’t name the emotion on her face. It looks similar to the one that Yelena showed when Kate pulled herself back after having fallen out the window, but it’s more muted perhaps, panic replaced by something that seems strikingly similar to sorrow.

    Instead of answering Kate’s joke, Yelena turns away after a second, fingers tracing the material of the jacket still in her hands. Her fingers pause over the bullets, and she turns the material over to check the inside as well. The bullets are, of course, embedded and caught in the fabric, never having made their way through and she turns the material back, once more, before folding it in half and placing it on the counter.

    “This is a very good suit.-”

    Despite the emotions shining through her face, Yelena’s voice is even as she speaks, as she turns back to Kate. When Yelena’s eyes meet hers, her face is schooled to a neutral expression, but her eyes are still intense, full of traces of her worry. “-Where did you get it?”

    Not knowing how to handle this clearly expressed concern for her, Kate blinks twice, eyebrows furrowing, and choosing to just answer Yelena’s question.

    “Um, yeah. I, uh...I got a guy.”

    A spark of amusement appears in Yelena’s eyes, as she steps in again, a Q-tip and a tub of disinfectant cream in her hands.

    “You got a guy?”

    Rolling her lips together before smiling, Kate nods, tilting her chin up as Yelena grabs it again.

    “Yeah. His name is Luke. I met him in LA, and he does suits.”

    A small smile appears on Yelena’s face, as she leans forward slightly to dab at the cut on Kate’s nose.

    “Well. If you talk to this Luke, you better tell him a huge thank you. He saved your life today.”

    Returning the smile, Kate can’t take her eyes off Yelena, enthralled by the softness she sees on her face. Softness, for her, if she is not mistaken. After her answer is not forthcoming, Yelena’s eyes jump to hers and Kate only then remembers that she should probably respond. “Yeah. Uh, for what he charges for these, they better.”

    Yelena only hums, stepping away and then coming back with a box of butterfly stitches. She leans forward, over Kate, securing one over the cut on her nose, while she holds onto the tub by her sides for dear life, trying to dissuade herself from doing something stupid. Once done, Yelena steps back, eyes dropping to look Kate over to see what other injuries she has that might need her assistance.

    “Where else are you hurt?”

    Sighing, Kate raises her tank top to look down at her hip, the skin covered by an angry, purple bruise where she hit them against the banister of the stairs, half of the injury disappearing under her pants.

    “This hurts like a bitch, but I don’t think there is much we can do about that.” As she glances back at Yelena, Kate doesn’t miss the way her eyes are not only looking at Kate’s hip but sliding over to her abs as well before she meets Kate’s eyes again. “It does not feel like it is broken?”

    Kate smiles, shaking her head.

    “Nope. Just bruised.”

    Yelena nods, eyes dropping to Kate’s abs again for a millisecond and in turn, Kate’s knuckles turn white with how hard she is holding onto the tub. Yelena is close, close enough to touch, and the urge to do so is becoming stronger with every slight indication that it would be welcomed.

    There is an undeniable crackling energy between them, making the air around them feel like it’s heating up, coming to a simmer. Yelena clears her throat, eyes never leaving Kate’s. “Anywhere else?”

    Kind of losing track of her thoughts, Kate hums.

    “Hmm?”

    The corner of Yelena’s eyes tilts upwards before she repeats her question. “Are you hurt anywhere else?”

    Exhaling, Kate smiles back, looking away.

    “Yeah, my head hurts. Um, the back of my head. But it’s nothing too-“ Stepping away, Yelena reaches for the zipper of her own suit, her tactical vest previously discarded in Sonya's apartment, while jutting her chin at Kate.

    “Turn around.”

    With a gulp, Kate nods to herself, and raises her feet with yet another wince, to lift them into the tub. With her back to Yelena, Kate only hears the zipper being undone and the rustling of leather as she takes it off.

    A moment later, Yelena speaks again, her voice coming from right behind Kate. “I am going to undo your hair.”

    Closing her eyes, Kate nods.

    “Alright. Thanks for the, um, heads up.”

    Only humming as a response, Yelena does as she said she would, gently pulling down the tie on Kate’s ponytail, freeing her hair from its confines. With Yelena behind her, it possibly feels even more sensitive than it would otherwise, and Kate exhales slowly. For a few long moments, they are both quiet and with every passing second in silence, Kate feels her resolve to not do anything stupid slowly slip away. When neither of them speaks, her head is filled with Yelena’s terrified face when Kate fell out of the skyscraper, with memories of her tiny touches in the last couple of hours. Her concern and her warm eyes since they came in here and Yelena started helping her, patching her up. If it was anyone else, Kate would make a move. With Yelena’s fingers gently examining her head, looking through her hair, she would turn around stand up and…But Yelena is not anyone else. The other day, when Kate was going to kiss her, she looked almost scared and...Meeting Maxine, seeing her right after she came out of mind control, has only reinforced Kate’s will to not do anything that might make Yelena uncomfortable, or push any boundaries.

    Clearing her throat, Kate tries to distract herself.

    “Do you think Maxine will be okay?”

    It takes Yelena a few seconds to answer, her voice clear but a bit reserved. “Her injuries will heal in no time.”

    The sentence feels incomplete and that is not exactly what Kate meant either, so she clarifies. “I meant…mentally. She…It seemed really intense.”

    There is a longer stretch of silence this time, and Kate doesn’t push. This is a topic that is probably pretty delicate for Yelena so it’s not her place to…

    “Getting out…It is not a straightforward process. It is sometimes two steps forward and one step back.”

    Yelena’s voice is still clear, and Kate just listens, not wanting to interrupt. She feels something cold and wet touch the back of her head and assumes that Yelena is cleaning some kind of wound when it starts to sting.

    “For some, it is too much…Facing what they have done, what they were forced to do. They can never find their way back to themselves. For others, it is easier…” She pauses, and Kate hears her step away. She almost thinks Yelena is done, but as she steps back, she continues.

    “Having people around seems to help most girls, but others can not bear to be around anyone for a while, needing time alone to figure out what they are like, what they want to do.” When Yelena doesn’t follow up with more words for a few seconds, just cleaning the wound in silence, Kate clears her throat, forcing her voice to remain unaffected as well. “How many have you freed?”

    The answer is instant, no need for Yelena to pause to count.

    “Directly, thirty-eight. Maxine makes it thirty-nine.”

    A few moments of silence follow again and Kate knows they could leave it like that. But she wants to know Yelena, wants to know her experience and understand it as much as she can. In the almost intimate silence and dim lights of her bathroom, Kate dares to ask, hoping she is not overstepping.

    “What was it like for you?”

    With bated breath, Kate waits and it feels like an eternity before Yelena speaks again. “This is a small wound, no need to stitch it.”

    Trying to tamp down her disappointment, Kate nods.

    “Oh…Right, okay.”

    As she tries to turn around, Yelena puts a hand on her shoulder, halting the motion. “Wait, I will put on a bandaid.”

    Kate hums, turning back around and Yelena steps away, presumably to get some bandaids or steri-strips or something. As she steps back, Kate hears her take a deep breath. “I…did not have a choice. Of company, I mean. When I was freed, I told you, I killed the Widow that freed me. I took the counter agent and I ran, and I was on the run for months. Alone until Natasha found me.”

    Yelena keeps working but Kate is thankful that she seems ready to share. For a few moments, Yelena is silent and then she continues, voice measured but solid.

    “When it first goes away, you are finally free, the compulsion is gone but… there is a hole in your mind. They…the mind control is embedded so deep into your brain, that sometimes, especially at first, it almost feels empty. Like something is supposed to be there, and it is not.”

    “Kinda like a fantom limb?”

    There is an amused huff from Yelena, and for a moment her fingers are still in Kate’s hair. “I guess so. It…It never really goes away, but you learn to fill the rest up, so the hole feels smaller.”

    Kate exhales, desperately wishing she could see Yelena’s face as she shares but thinking it might be easier for Yelena, without having eyes on her. For a few moments, they are quiet and Kate mulls Yelena’s words over.

    “When you say it’s too much for some. Um, do you mean they try to, um,...kill themselves?” “There have been instances, yes.”

    Kate exhales, closing her eyes for a long moment again before she is back to staring at her own knees. She wants to say sorry, but it doesn’t feel enough. Instead, she tries to steer them back to their current predicament, thinking it might help to keep the moment from becoming too heavy.

    “It kinda felt like that with Maxine, for a second there. Like she was just giving up before she found it in herself to…go on, I guess.”

    Humming, Yelena steps away, and Kate hears the faucet turn on. As Yelena washes her hands, Kate turns back around and sighs deeply, gearing up to stand up again. While she gathers her energy, she looks at Yelena, taking her in. With the top part of her suit folded over Kate’s on the counter, she is wearing a tight black t-shirt. The tactical pants are loose, but they still do a great job of accentuating her form, and Kate takes a few moments to appreciate her ass in them while she sits there.

    As she glances at the mirror, she sees Yelena looking back at her, her eyes warm, no doubt having caught Kate checking her out again. Neither of them acknowledges it and with a deep sigh and a wince, Kate stands up.

    Stepping up next to Yelena, Kate looks at herself in the mirror again, taking in her slightly swollen nose, bruised jaw, the angry, red line around her neck, and the dark purple bruise spreading over the left side of her chest, with two, almost black marks where Maxine’s bullets have struck her. Apart from the currently visible ones, Kate knows there are several other injuries hidden under her clothes as well, and she puffs out her cheek as she exhales, meeting Yelena’s eyes in the mirror again.

    “You know what? I think I’m totally pulling off this bruised and battered boxer look.” Yelena smiles, but it doesn’t quite reach her eyes. For a moment, she purses her lips before turning her head to look at Kate directly from the side, instead of in the mirror. “You deserve it for being so reckless. “ The words are said pointedly, with a teasing lilt and Kate rolls her eyes, before turning to the side, looking back at Yelena too.

    “I’m not reckless.”

    For a moment they just look at each other, and Kate feels the air crackle around them again, but there is an undercurrent of something darker from Yelena as well, her eyes intense and dark. A moment later, she lifts her chin, looking up at Kate and this time it does not feel like she is teasing.

    “You are reckless…and too noble.”

    Huffing, Kate furrows her eyebrows.

    “I am really not.”

    Raising an eyebrow in response, Yelena looks unimpressed, her voice dropping an octave as well.

    “Kate. You risked your life to save a woman that nearly killed you. Twice. That you do not even know.”

    Pursing her lips, Kate looks away, shaking her head. Her whole body is thrumming, with pain or just from being in Yelena’s close proximity again, she can’t tell. Nevertheless, Kate protests.

    “And, I nearly killed her before that. It’s like the least I could do… And anyway, it’s not like she tried to kill me on purpose?”

    Yelena huffs, mostly in amusement before she sobers up. They are both quiet for a few seconds. Taking a deep breath, Yelena tilts her head to the side.

    “Still. You saved her. You carried her to safety while people were actively trying to kill you both.”

    Blinking back at Yelena, Kate can’t help her confused smile, joking.

    “Why do you say that like it’s a bad thing?”

    Yelena doesn’t answer, and Kate feels bewilderment spread in her chest. Unconsciously, she steps even closer to Yelena, trying to understand.

    “I don’t get it. Are you mad at me for saving her?”

    Yelena sighs, and takes a step back, before turning away.

    “No.”

    Kate watches as she begins to pack up the cleaning supplies, throwing away the bloody pieces of gauze. When she doesn’t continue speaking for a few moments, Kate prompts her again.

    “Then?”

    Yelena huffs, pursing her lips and not looking at Kate. She doesn’t answer for a few seconds and when she finally speaks, she sounds frustrated and short.

    “It is going to get you killed.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate grabs her hand, stilling her ministrations to get her attention. “Yelena. I am okay. I am fine. “ For a long moment, Yelena is still not looking away and Kate is struck by the fact that she looks actually upset. It is only reinforced when Yelena finally turns to look at her, and there is an almost defiant sadness in her eyes that nearly knocks Kate back.

    “This time.“ Her eyes drop to Kate’s neck, undoubtedly looking at the angry, red lines from Maxine nearly suffocating her with the wire again.

    “Next time you might not be so lucky. Or the time after that.”

    Slowly, her hand that Kate is not holding onto raises, and her fingertips tickle Kate’s skin when she touches the bruise, gently, barely so.

    She looks transfixed, and Kate is equally frozen, looking down at her.

    A moment later her hand lowers, fingers touching the twin round bruises on the upper left side of Kate’s chest. Her touch is so soft, Kate almost shivers, goosebumps raising on her skin as a response.

    Yelena’s concern is clear on her face and Kate longs to smooth it away, but she doesn’t know what to say.

    “I’ll be fine the next time too. I…”

    She doesn’t know how to finish the sentence, raising her own hand to splay it out on Yelena’s over her heart.

    “Feel that? I’m fine.-”

    After a moment, giving Yelena a small, cheeky grin Kate leans closer to speak again, trying to wash away the heaviness of the moment.

    “How could I not be, with the world’s best corporate spy by my side.”

    The comment very much doesn’t get the desired reaction. Instead of laughing, or even just smiling, Yelena almost winces and looks away. As she tries to step away, Kate follows, putting a hand on her waist to halt the movement, the desire to make her feel better overwhelming anything else for a moment.

    “Hey...”

    Yelena’s hand, and her own over it, is still on Kate’s chest and she is sure Yelena can feel her heartbeat speed up when she realizes how exactly they are standing. With one of Yelena’s and her own hand on Kate’s chest and one of Kate’s on Yelena’s waist, there is only an inch of space between them, Yelena’s eyes meet hers again, and Kate feels her heart skip a beat at the fear and concern she sees in them. Not knowing what else to say to comfort her, Kate’s instincts slowly take over. Using the hand on Yelena’s waist, Kate gently tugs her closer, and Yelena…Yelena lets her. The already minimal space between them disappears completely, and Kate’s tongue darts out to wet her lips in anticipation, slowly coming to terms with what she is about to do. Her eyes drop to Yelena’s lips for a moment, and Kate could swear that she hears her breath hitch. Glancing up to meet Yelena’s eyes again, she doesn’t look terrified anymore. It’s working…

    With a slow exhale, Kate leans down and-

    Beeeeep.

    Beep beep beep. Beep.

    Through the open bathroom door, the doorbell’s sound is unmistakable, breaking their moment. Kate exhales, closing her eyes and it’s not exactly a surprise when she feels Yelena’s hands gently push her away, and step back.

    With a huff, Kate opens her eyes, Yelena already walking away. Grinding her teeth, Kate gets ready to murder any delivery person or neighbor or fucking doorman that interrupted their moment, marching after Yelena, her frustration completely masking her pain, not even stopping to question why someone is ringing the doorbell at 4 o'clock in the morning. Yelena gets to the door first, checking through the peephole and Kate is only torn from her frustrated fury, when Yelena looks back at her with wide eyes. Not saying a word, she swings the door open, and Kate feels her eyes widen too, lips gaping.

    “Hi, kid.”

    Chapter End Notes Hi guys!

    Sorry for the late update :D This chapter has grown huge, much longer than I thought it would be so it took a little while to sort out. It also needed some semi in-dept (?) research of encryptions and data storage methods so, yeah. :D If you are interested in it, there is a TED talk about DNA data storage that is a pretty good short summary of what it is :D It's pretty interesting if you are into that kind of stuff. I both over-complicated and over-simplified it for plot reasons (they needed to come here but not be successful for *reasons*) but it's a real thing and it will most likely be available for "mainstream" use long before quantum technology is!

    Also before we get to the good stuff: I know the deep wound suturing, and generally Maxine's medical care is inaccurate, don't come at me, okay??? (So was Yelena's stab wound for the matter) :D But a) I did not want to go too much into detail for squeamish readers' sake and also b)I don't think people would much enjoy the crew(tm) wait around in the hospital. Anyway, little more than the usual suspension of disbelief needed. :D (For the record folks, deep tissue wounds need several layers of stitching, not just 2-3. The more you know)

    Also, who do you think followed them on the way home?

    NOW, onto the good stuff. :D I hope you all like the sexual tension between our girlies. We almost got a kiss!! On that note, can anyone guess the identity of our cock-blocker? :D It's not that hard to guess. BUT ANYWAY, THEY BOTH WANTED IT!! They are both clear on that!!! We are getting there, I promise :D

    Chapter 23

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Chapter 23 “Hi, kid.”

    Clint’s smile is tired on the other side of the door and it takes a moment for Kate to get her bearings, still half-stuck in her moment with Yelena.

    Kate was about to kiss her.

    And Yelena…

    Yelena was about to let her.

    And now Clint is here.

    Wait a minute…

    Clint is here!

    “Clint! Oh my God!”

    With a shake of her head, Kate smiles, her face and head still hurting as the muscles move. Stepping forward to pull him into the apartment, Kate takes his bag, throwing it onto the floor by the door before hugging him.

    “Hi, Kate.-”

    As he steps back, his smile turns a bit awkward, looking at Yelena. With her, he does not go in for a hug and Kate feels like metaphorical crickets are chirping around them for a second, only the pitter-patter of Lucky’s feet breaking the silence as he comes to greet Clint as well. “Yelena. Hello.”

    Glancing at Yelena, Kate could not tell that barely a minute ago, they were in her bathroom about to…Jesus, Kate. Focus.

    “Barton.”

    Yelena’s voice is measured, almost distant but there is warmth in her eyes as she looks at Clint as he leans down to pat Lucky in greeting, the dog sniffing at his clothes interestedly. Clint glances between Yelena and Kate from his half-bent-over position, the three of them still in front of the door. After a second, his eyes settle on Kate’s face, searching her features before his eyes drop to her neck, then her chest, his eyebrows raising. “What the hell happened to you? You look like shit.”

    Kate chuckles, wincing slightly as it hurts her ribs a little. Glancing quickly at Yelena, Kate tries to watch her body language for any sign to tell her what she thinks about what just almost happened between them, and it being interrupted but Yelena’s face, her body language too, are a blank book. Not even a closed one, just simply blank, completely neutral. With a lift of her hand, Kate waves off her injuries.

    “Long story. We uh. We broke in somewhere to steal something, I got a little beat around… and shot.-”

    Clearing her throat, Kate glances at Yelena again, but she turns away, walking back to the coffee table seemingly to gather her things.

    “-Yelena was just patching me up.”

    At that, Yelena does look up at her, and as their eyes meet, Kate feels that heat between them still, no longer close to boiling over but still there, still simmering. It only lasts a heartbeat, before Yelena looks back at Clint, her lips stretching into a smile that doesn’t feel fake, but does feel a bit like she is putting on a show.

    “And now, Yelena is just leaving.”

    Referring to herself in the third person, Yelena smiles, playful and confident. It reminds her of the Yelena she met in her charred apartment all those months ago, and while it’s undoubtedly attractive, it feels sort of jarring, compared to the intimacy of the moment they shared just a few minutes ago.

    As Yelena goes to pick up her suit top from the bathroom, with Lucky following her loyally, Clint looks at Kate, his gaze quizzical. Not wanting to deal with that, Kate quickly leads their conversation in another direction, glancing at his bags.

    “Are you crashing here?”

    His eyes move to the bathroom door for a quick moment, and he shifts his weight from one foot to the other.

    “Yeah, I was planning to…Unless your guest room is taken?”

    The sentence is finished, kind of hanging in the air, just as Yelena walks back into the room, her leather suit top in hand.

    “Do not worry, Barton. The guest room is all yours.”

    His eyes are alight with affection, despite Yelena’s half-faux distant behavior, and he glances at Kate for a moment before his attention is back on Yelena.

    “Where are you staying?”

    Yelena’s answering smile is cheeky, almost teasing, halting a step or two from the front door to give her borderline sassy answer.

    “Not here.”

    With that, her eyes shift to Kate and she might be imagining things, but to her, it seems there is a moment when Yelena’s façade cracks, her smile turning sincere. Her eyes are warm and Kate’s stomach does a somersault in response as she smiles back and when she speaks, her words come out a bit jumbled.

    “Thanks for, uh, patching me up. I…We? Um, tomorrow?”

    Her amusement palpable, Yelena’s smile widens, holding her eyes as she leans down to give Lucky a few farewell scritches behind his ears.

    “Yes. Tomorrow…Bye.”

    With that, she glances at Clint one last time, before straightening up and walking through the front door, not looking back. Kate watches her go, not able to swallow the involuntary deep sigh at the loss of their moment. When she turns back to Clint, his eyebrows are somewhat lifted, most likely at the somewhat awkward goodbye he just witnessed, and Kate reminds herself that she is incredibly happy that he is back, despite his bad timing. “You wanna tell me what the hell that was?”

    There is literally nothing else Kate would like to avoid more, than having to explain to him what just happened…or what has been happening. At least for now. Until had some time to process it herself. Kate knows he is going to have an opinion about it, and ugh. Not tonight. Knowing his weaknesses, Kate really has no other choice, than to act nonsensical until he gets too overwhelmed to actually deal with it, and just lets her be. Turning around, Kate levels him with a look, putting her hands on her hips, the visual only ruined by her slight wince when she hits the bruise on her side.

    “What do you mean what the hell was that? Where the hell have you been? Almost 3 weeks and not a single phone call?”

    Eyebrows jumping up, Clint is visibly surprised by her countering but he is not phased for long. After a moment, he levels Kate with a look, half-amused.

    “In the Colombian jungle. Finding out what I can about your new friend, Rojas. With pretty bad cell phone coverage. Your turn.”

    Shamelessly ignoring Clint’s question, Kate turns away, striding (limping) to the couch, and slipping on a grey hoodie forgotten there in the afternoon before she sits down. Kicking her leg up with a wince, she watches as Clint walks over to the armchair too, sitting down with a groan that would make her think he was there with them tonight, getting his ass beat too. “So, what did you find?”

    Brow furrowing, Clint waits for a beat before he sighs, apparently accepting that Kate is not going to answer his question. At least not yet.

    “Not as much as I hoped. He is working with an American woman, that’s a fact. She is…I think it’s the woman you described a few weeks back, Valentina Allegra de…something. Purple streak in her hair? Anyway, I have pictures and a file in my bag. I’ll show you later.” Leaning back, trying to find a somewhat comfortable position, Kate nods as she shuffles around.

    “Yeah, that tracks.”

    Sliding down lower in his seat, Clint seems to try to get comfortable too before he hums, leveling Kate with a serious look.

    “What doesn’t track, is the fact that I’m pretty sure she is CIA.”

    That gets Kate’s attention, and if she wasn’t hurting basically everywhere, she would sit up. “Wh…CIA?”

    Clint nods, the lines on his face deepening in his seriousness.

    “Yeah, I think the feds are kind of…running the cartel. Or are at least keeping one hand on the wheel? Probably using it to cut down the competition, while taking a cut of the profits.” Exhaling, Kate mulls over Clint’s words, face scrunching up.

    “The CIA is in…cahoots with a Colombian drug cartel?”

    At Kate’s use of the goofy expression, Clint’s serious expression cracks for a moment, the corner of his mouth tipping upwards.

    “In cahoots? What are you, 60?”

    Kate only snorts, rolling her eyes before giving him a pointed look.

    “You’d know. You are 60.”

    Tilting his head to the side, Clint looks more amused than offended.

    “You must really be hurt. That was pretty lame.”

    Kate hums, pursing her lips as she nods faux seriously, but is unable to stop herself from smiling.

    “Yeah, I felt that. I can do better than that.”

    Clint snorts, his affection shining clearly through his eyes.

    “You wanna try again?”

    Kate sighs dramatically, shaking her head and sliding even lower on the couch, half-sitting, half-lying down at this point.

    “Nah, I don’t think I have it in me today. I’ll get back to you tomorrow.” Clint hums, before he looks Kate over, his face turning serious again, a sliver of worry sneaking into his voice.

    “Are you okay?”

    Kate closes her eyes, exhaling but smiling nonetheless.

    “Yeah, yeah, I’ll be fine. You should see the other guys.”

    Her attempt to smile is slightly ruined by the wince it evokes when the movement makes her nose hurt even more.

    “What happened?”

    Kate sighs, groaning a little. Leaning her head back against the couch, she looks at Clint for a long moment, before she decides she doesn’t feel like explaining everything tonight. “It’s…a really long story. Is it okay if I tell you tomorrow? I am like, super exhausted and I don’t have the capacity to go over everything now and it’s a whole thing.” Clint blinks, his eyes shining with sympathy.

    “Yeah, okay. You wanna go to sleep?”

    For a long moment, Kate closes her eyes and while sleep sounds like a dream, no pun intended, she wants to hear more about what Clint found first.

    “Yeah. But tell me more about the Rojas slash Valentina thing first... It’ll be like a bedtime story.”

    Opening her eyes at Clint’s huffs, Kate sees that he is somewhat amused but his eyes look worried. He sighs to himself too, kicking his feet up on the table and getting more comfortable.

    “Right, sure. Um, There is not much more to tell but okay. It took me almost an entire week to find them in the jungle. He has this whole compound, and it’s like a…fortress. He rarely leaves it, and it’s guarded 24/7.”

    Kate watches as Clint looks thoughtful, silent for a moment before he speaks again. “His father before…He lived in a villa, in Bogotá. Heavily guarded, sure, but not hidden like this. Or protected like this.”

    Humming, Kate doesn’t really know what to do with this information. Clint pauses again, seemingly mulling things over as well.

    “I don’t think his people know he is working with the feds. The only times he leaves his compound are when he goes to meet Valentina, and he only takes a skeleton crew inside. So the rest of them are probably in the dark.”

    That is something at least, but Kate has enough on her plate with Fisk and her mother to worry about blackmailing or taking down another drug lord for now. Sighing, Kate prepares herself to explain her side of things, some of it at least, connected to the temporary super soldier serum. She moves around to find a comfortable position again, unsuccessfully, so with a huff, she settles half on her side, looking at Clint.

    “Well. At least I found out why he is after us… Kinda.”

    Eyebrows lifting, but otherwise immobile, Clint looks back at her.

    “How’s that?”

    Puffing her cheeks out, Kate exhales, before she begins to explain.

    “Ammm, okay. So. Last week I got a phone call from Rykers, that my mom was injured in a fight, and that I could finally see her in the hospital.-“ At that, Clint’s eyes widen, his face turning concerned. Kate just smiles, somewhat bitterly, lifting a hand to keep him from interrupting.

    “She is fine. It was like…mostly a trick to be able to meet me without Fisk finding out I visited her in jail? Turns out she had some fucked up notion of keeping me safe by staying away…or making me stay away, I guess. Which is stupid if you ask me but whatever. Anyway, um…-“ Taking a deep breath, Kate shifts around, fruitlessly trying to find a position where nothing touches her injured side again while glancing at the time on the clock. Half past 4 in the morning. God, she really can’t wait to sleep.

    “She told me that she and Fisk were working together to create a temporary super-soldier serum, developed from the blood of one of the flag-smashers that survived an explosion. My mom, um… She says she was going to sell it to the government anyway, but now, it’s like one of the conditions of her plea deal. So, she basically got me to go to the hospital to ask me to help her get it because she had it broken into three parts and hid its pieces from Fisk and well...”

    With that, Kate trails off. The lines on Clint’s face deepen with every word Kate says, and honestly, she can relate. With a small shake of his head, his eyebrows furrow and he pulls his feet off the coffee table to sit up a little.

    “Hold up. How does that connect to Rojas and Valentina?”

    Wetting her lips, Kate thinks it over.

    “Well, Rojas asked us to get a formula for a drug for him, through Valentina, right? That’s what she told me at the cemetery anyway. So, my guess is, that they know what it is, and want it for either the cartel or the CIA…Maybe both.”

    Leaning back again, Clint is thoughtful, his eyebrows still furrowed.

    “Yeah, that…that makes sense. Temporary superpowers would serve both of those well… Wouldn’t surprise me if they mutually plan to con the other once they get it too.” He is quiet for a few seconds before he looks at Kate again.

    “Has he tried to reach out to you since?”

    Shaking her head, Kate is about to say no but remembers the aftermath of her “date” with Amanda. Cringing, she looks back at Clint who doesn’t seem reassured by her expression. “Not uh, directly. Um, after you went to look into him, we had a mission go to shit. And uh, Yelena called Valentina to clean it up afterward, like scrub CCTV footage and everything.-“ Closing his eyes, Clint exhales, the muscles in his jaw jumping as he grinds his teeth together.

    “-And Yelena agreed to meet him In exchange, but I haven’t heard anything from her about it afterward, so I doubt it happened.”

    With both hands, Clint rubs at his face, before he pulls them away, nodding half to himself. “Alright. Well, I guess that’s better than nothing.”

    After a moment, his eyes meet Kate’s again, a spark of teasing entering his gaze. “Was it this mission? Or did you have two failed missions in a row?”

    He juts his chin at Kate with a barely there smile, indicating her injuries and she shakes her head, trying to downplay the severe fuck ups of the Amanda mission in front of him, deciding to gloss over it altogether.

    “No. No, tonight was actually about trying to get one of the pieces of the temporary super soldier serum.”

    Clint nods, his teasing smile fading away.

    “And did you?”

    Pursing her lips, Kate shakes her head, cringing a little again internally. “No. Uh, turns out they were expecting us, so we had to haul ass and get out fast… But! On the bright side, we did install a program that will help us get it faster next time we go and we did free a Black Widow from under mind control, so…all in all, I consider this one to be a win.”

    Looking at his face, Clint doesn’t look surprised at the mention of mind control, telling Kate that he must have known about it already. He nods, visibly thoughtful, asking Kate somewhat distractedly.

    “Do you need a clean-up after this one?”

    Kate exhales, nodding.

    “Probably yeah…Ugh, thanks for the reminder. I need to wipe some cameras.” Not standing up, Kate only half hangs off of the couch to reach for her laptop, pulling it into her lap with a wince as she stretches her side. She longs for her bed but it’s also entirely possible that she won’t make it off of this couch tonight, now that she is mostly settled. Opening her laptop, Kate boots it up and quickly wipes the footage of the last 24 hours off of the servers of the security companies in charge of both the building that Limitless is in and the one that they entered through. Those Kate preemptively hacked the day before, as they were built on an older version of Bishop Security’s interface anyway, just in case things go to shit. Once she is done, she also makes a mental reminder to either hack the NYPD server tomorrow or ask Yelena to ask her mother again, to wipe CCTV footage of their entry and exit as well, despite their car supposedly having been parked in a blind spot. With a yawn, she closes the laptop and contemplates whether it’s worth it to get off the couch to sleep in her bed, or if she should just let herself give in to her tiredness, and pass out on the couch.

    Deciding to be lazy, she shuffles around the couch, fully lying down, reaching for the blanket draped over the back. Glancing at Clint, Kate notes that he looks tired too, his face looking somewhat older with his exhaustion.

    “Okkaay. I’m officially beat.-”

    Stressing her words with a yawn, she lifts her arm to vaguely gesture at the guest room. “-The sheets in the guestroom are fresh, so you can just use those whenever you go. If you want to shower, there are spare towels in the guestroom wardrobe too.”

    With that, she considers her hostess responsibilities fulfilled, at least for tonight, and closes her eyes, preparing to fall into unconsciousness finally after shuffling around for a few seconds to get somewhat comfortable.

    Clint hums in response, not moving, and Kate hears him shift in his seat before he asks. “So…Yelena?”

    As her heart misses a beat, Kate opens one eye to see his face. He looks somewhat amused if a bit constipated.

    “Hmm?”

    Shifting in his seat again, Clint seems uncomfortable and Kate regrets asking him to clarify already.

    “How long have you two been…uh…patching each other up?”

    Face scrunching up, Kate lifts her head to look at Clint properly. He looks even more awkward than she feels and she barely swallows the chuckle that rises in her chest. Her mirth at Clint’s discomfort wins over her own embarrassment and Kate grins.

    “Patching each other up?”

    He looks to the side, at anything but her, lips pressed together but if he wants to ask what Kate thinks he is trying to ask, she will make him work for it.

    “You know... Has she been over a lot?”

    He glances in Kate’s general direction, but not meeting her eyes and her grin widens even more, despite the pain it causes in her bruised face.

    “Oh yeah. She’s been over almost every day. Some days multiple times even.” Clint winces slightly and Kate almost bursts out laughing at his expression, tamping down on it when he glances over at her, visibly uncomfortable.

    “Uhh. Kate, do you know what I’m asking?”

    Feigning innocence, although badly, Kate shakes her head with a smile.

    “Yeah, if she has been helping. With the case. And she has, a lot... Some days even her friend Sonya comes over to…you know, lend a hand.”
