    Shaking his head, Kate is pretty sure Clint would be blushing if he was physically capable of doing it. Instead, he just looks even more constipated as he sighs deeply, closing his eyes, probably counting to ten in his head.

    “Kate. Please don’t make me spell it out.”

    Biting down on her lip to stop herself from laughing, Kate can barely get the words out without her voice cracking.

    “Spell what out?”

    Clint huffs, pursing his lips and the lines on his face deepen. Rolling his lips together, he seems to gather his mental strength to ask his question.

    “I am asking how long have you been sleeping with Yelena.”

    He finally looks at her, face turning annoyed when he finally sees Kate’s grin. With a motion quick enough to prove that he is still very much an Avenger, he picks up a piece of paper from Kate’s coffee table, scrunches it up, and throws it at Kate’s head while she laughs, the balled-up take-out menu hitting her right in the middle of her forehead. After a few seconds, Kate sobers up, gingerly turning to her uninjured side and propping herself up on her elbow, despite her aching shoulder disapproving of the motion. Leveling him with a look, Kate raises an eyebrow at him.

    “Not that it’s any of your business, but I’m not sleeping with Yelena.” He looks back at Kate for a long moment, disbelief written all over his face. After several seconds, he raises an eyebrow as he speaks again.

    “Are you sure?”

    Bursting out laughing again, Kate has to hold onto her aching ribs again. It takes her a few seconds to answer, laughing but simultaneously breathless from the pain. “Ow ow ow…Yeah, Clint, I am pretty sure.”

    His face eases, and her mirth is mirrored in his eyes a second later.

    “Well, that’s a relief.”

    Eyebrows jumping up to her hairline, Kate looks back at him quizzically. The words bubble out of her, hackles somewhat raised.

    “What’s that supposed to mean?”

    He grins, reaching up to rub at the back of his neck.

    “Well, if I am to crash on your couch for a few days, I don’t want to accidentally walk in on you with…-”

    He does a hand gesture so weird and awkward, his face scrunching up too, that it soothes away most of the negative connotations of his words.

    “-my best friend’s little sister.”

    Kate huffs, partially amused and maybe just a little bit genuinely annoyed. Nevertheless, she feigns offense, brow furrowing but not taking it seriously enough to actually sit up. “Hey, first of all, Yelena is an adult. If she wants to sleep with her sister’s best friend’s other best friend, that’s none of your business.”

    Blinking, Clint still looks torn between being amused and deeply uncomfortable. “And second of all, who says you would walk in on anything? I keep my business on the DL. And also thirdly,- ”

    Leaning back, Clint levels her with a look that makes Kate nervous for some reason but she finishes her sentence nonetheless.

    “-thirdly, we are not doing anything. So…”

    She can tell that this might not have been the strongest way to finish her argument, but whatever. She is injured. A somewhat teasing look comes over Clint’s face, the left corner of his lips tilting upwards at the beginning of a smile.

    “You are awfully defensive for someone who is apparently not doing anything.” Glancing to the side, Kate tries to backtrack.

    “I am not defensive. I am just proving a point.”

    For a few moments, Clint just looks at her. Kate does her best to not look like she is lying, even though she is well aware that she is while also trying to push the images of Yelena and her in the bathroom half an hour ago into the back of her mind.

    “Okay. If you say so.”

    Clint does not look convinced, but Kate only cares that they stop talking about the topic, not that he actually believes her.

    “I do say so.”

    “Okay.”

    “Okay.”

    She gets to enjoy her internal triumph for about 5 seconds before Clint speaks again. “So, what about the girl you went on a date with a few weeks ago?”

    Letting her head fall back onto the couch, Kate stares at the ceiling.

    “What is this?-“ Lifting her head again, just to properly express her mocking, Kate looks at Clint with a raised eyebrow.

    “-Are we having a girls’ night? Are you going to offer to braid my hair? -” At that, Clint chuckles, sliding even lower in his chair.

    “I’m just catching up on what’s up with you.”

    Ignoring him, Kate barrels on.

    “Ask for my advice on how to ask out your crush?”

    Snorting, Clint’s face turns smug.

    “Based on your performance at the front door, I don’t think I’d want it, thanks.” Feeling her cheeks warm up with a slight blush, Kate makes a mocking, scrunched-up face at him.

    “Hardy-har-har.”

    With a wide grin, Clint looks almost gleeful, before he does an absolutely poor imitation of Kate, his voice sounding dopey.

    “I? We? Tomorrow?”

    Picking up the balled-up take-out receipt that Clint chucked at her head, Kate throws it back at him, but he dodges it with a quick and easy motion of his head.

    “Shut up. I am just tired.-”

    The grin doesn’t slide off of Clint’s face and Kate rolls her eyes at him, before pinning him with a look to continue.

    “-Plus don’t pretend you are a regular Don Juan, okay? Laura told me she thought both of you would grow old and grey if she waited for you to ask her out so she had to do it herself.” The dig doesn’t have the desired effect, Clint still smiling smugly. Kate really is losing her touch tonight.

    “At least I could string together a coherent sentence around her.”

    Pursing her lips, Kate glares at him.

    “I can string together a coherent sentence around Yelena. I was just…Uh, whatever. I don’t have to defend my game to an old man.”

    Something glints in Clint’s eyes, his grin widening and Kate realizes too late that he has her exactly where he wants to.

    “So, you do admit you are trying to have a game around her.”

    Quickly pulling her defenses up, Kate looks back at him unimpressed.

    “No? No, I didn’t say that. That’s like a completely different statement. What I said was that I do have game, more than you, probably and if I was trying, which I am not, I could totally charm the pants off of Yelena.”

    At this point, Kate doesn’t know why she is denying Clint’s allegations that she does try to have game around Yelena. Or is attracted to her. Or whatever. It’s mostly just the principle of the thing and not wanting to let Clint win.

    Plus, it’s not like she actually knows what they are doing. It might just be a vibe that never becomes anything more…Kate really hopes it’s not though.

    “Aha.”

    “What, you don’t believe me?”

    “Well. You do have a habit of being ridiculously overconfident.”

    “Hey, like 3 minutes ago you were accusing me of sleeping with her. Ergo, you obviously believe I could do it.”

    “Well. If you could do it, I’m pretty sure you would be doing it. And you are not so…” For a moment, Kate considers pointing out that maybe if Clint arrived just a couple of hours later, she might be doing exactly that right now but it’d kind of defeat her own argument. Okay, maybe if she also wasn’t beaten to a pulp a few hours before.

    With no actual argument to make, Kate argues just for the sake of it.

    “How do you know I am not doing it?”

    Slowly, Clint blinks, but Kate sees the teasing smile in the corner of his mouth as he looks back at her, before giving his deadpan answer.

    “Because you told me.”

    That’s... Yeah, that’s a good point. Kate is way too tired to be smart in this argument. “I…I could be lying!”

    Clint’s eyes glint and he asks with a smirk.

    “Are you?”

    Blinking, Kate realizes she just argued herself into a corner.

    If she says she is lying, she lies that she is sleeping with Yelena and admits to liking her, which she has been denying, and if she admits to not lying, then she also admits to Clint’s point that she has no game, and also to liking Yelena. Ugh, the whole thing makes her already pounding head hurt. That said, even beaten and hurt, Kate is not one to back down from a challenge like that.

    “No, I…No. But if I wanted to…”

    Clint Huffs out a laugh, his grin annoyingly smug again.

    “Sure, kid.”

    Kate entertains the possibility of telling him what has been happening, but she is pretty sure that’s exactly what he wants. Annoyed, Kate sits up with a wince, almost forgetting her pain, and gets off the couch.

    “Whatever, I’m going to bed.”

    In a voice that Kate has rarely heard from him, Clint snickers, but doesn’t comment anymore on the Yelena situation.

    “Alright. Good night.”

    Ignoring the thick mirth coating Clint’s words, Kate picks up her phone and limps to her bedroom, Lucky trailing behind her.

    “Night.”

    Once inside, she realizes that she probably should have a shower before getting into her bed, but that feels like a task way too tiring and complicated to undertake right now. She does dip out of her room briefly, to brush her teeth and wash her hands and face at least, while Clint is busy in the guest bedroom, but soon, she is back in her bedroom, more than ready for the day to be over.

    Kate turns on the lamp on her bedside table and sits on the edge of her bed, Lucky jumping onto it beside her. She unbuttons her pants and with careful, slow movements, slides them down her legs. Not able to lean down low enough, she uses her feet to kick them off, before crawling up the bed and sliding under the covers in just her tanktop and underwear, painfully aware that despite her meager efforts, she is definitely still gross.

    Whatever, she will wash her sheets tomorrow.

    With the last reserves of her energy, she plugs in her phone and turns off the lamp, her mind swirling with both Clint’s words, and finally having the opportunity to go back to her moment with Yelena.

    Now that she is actually in bed, she doesn’t feel sleepy anymore, her brain instead half preoccupied with her annoyance at Clint and half replaying her conversation with Yelena in the bathroom. And of course, the moment when Kate was about to kiss her is repeated again and again, analyzing every moment, carving its details into her memory. Through her door, Kate hears Clint get ready for bed too, and with thoughts of Yelena in her mind, she slowly falls asleep.

    If Kate dreams that night, she doesn’t remember it.

    She sleeps like the dead, waking up the next morning to her phone buzzing. With bleary eyes, she reads the name on her screen, and for a few seconds, she lets it ring, considering ignoring Jack’s call altogether. It’s barely 9 o’clock in the morning. Why can’t she just sleep in, just this once?

    Her body hurts like she has been run over by a stampede of angry buffalo and her head feels like it has been stuffed with cotton.

    But somewhere, in a half-awake part of her consciousness, she considers the possibility that he might be in danger or trouble, and with a groan mixed with a yawn, she taps the green button to pick up the call when he rings her a second time.

    “Hello?”

    “Good morning, Katie. I didn’t wake you up, did I?”

    At the sound of his voice, Kate muffles a groan. He sounds way too calm to be in any type of grave danger. If she was any more awake and any less grumpy, Kate would probably feel guilty about being annoyed at him for not being in serious trouble but for now, all she can do is throw an arm over her eyes to block out any light, in the hopes of falling back asleep once they hang up and try to swallow her impatience.

    “Hi, Jack. No…No, I’m up. What’s up?”

    “I am sorry to say but it is an emergency. I am in an enormous amount of trouble, and I’m in dire need of your help.”

    Pulling her arm away from her face, Kate opens her eyes, wider and more alert this time, worry stirring in her chest.

    “What happened?”

    There is a beat of silence on the other end of the call, while Kate’s anxiety swirls in her stomach.

    “I’m terribly embarrassed to say, but I…It seems that the venue that I have booked for the party has made a grave mistake and instead of this year, October 9th, they have booked us for next year.-“ Kate sighs deeply, resisting the urge to groan or scream into her pillow, or hung up on Jack altogether. Instead, she just rubs her face, taking a deep breath. It’s a party planning emergency. Unaware of her frustration, Jack barrels on.

    “-I have tried to reason with them, but they insist that they are fully booked well into the spring and that their hands are tied.”

    Rolling her lips together, Kate tries to gently interrupt him, not having the mental capacity to deal with it this early in the morning, especially after the evening and long night she had. “Jack…I’m not sure how I can-“ “I don’t know what to do. I have spoken to several alternative venues, but with less than 3 weeks to go, all of them are booked.”

    Feeling too tired to even resist his words, Kate just hums in the affirmative. With this little time left before his party, it’s highly unlikely that he will find another place, especially in Manhattan, that will be both acceptable and available on a Friday or Saturday evening this year, let alone in such a short amount of time.

    “Have you asked them for another date? Maybe not on the weekend?”

    Her interruption works this time, but his answer is full of frustrated anxiety. “No. The venue can change, but the date has to stay the same. The invitations have gone out and I have received almost all the RSVPs already.”

    Exhausted, Kate sighs.

    “Right. Um. Okay, I’ll try to think of something, but I am not sure what I can do. Unless you want to do it at the Summer Place? I am happy to lend it for an evening.” Kate can hear his smile as he answers, and while her exhaustion won’t let her annoyance fade away, her affection for Jack starts to wake up too, as she herself becomes more awake. “That is so very kind of you to offer, but the party needs to happen here, in New York. It is not summer anymore, after all.”

    “Alright. I’ll…try to think. But really, I can’t promise anything.”

    Jack’s voice is warm and full of affection as he answers, and Kate wonders how she could ever entertain the idea that this man could be an evil mastermind.

    “That’s all I ask. Thank you.”

    With a tired smile, Kate says her farewells.

    “Okay. Um, I’m sorry but I really gotta go now.”

    For once, he understands her gentle dismissal.

    “Of course, Katie. Thank you again. Call me if you think of anything.”

    “Sure, sure. Talk later. Bye.”

    Not waiting for his answer, she hangs up the phone, dropping it somewhere by her head. She is still groggy and tired enough, that falling asleep is easy, and in barely a minute, Kate is unconscious again.

    Her body feels on fire, but for once, it is not with pain.

    Kate sighs, the muscles on her back tingling, as a hand runs down on them, settling on her ass, and her heartbeat speeds up even more, as a whisper of a gasp brushes the small strands of hair by her ear, tickling her neck.

    She feels slick, between her legs and with sweat, all over her body. It’s a slow but striking realization that the slickness is not all her own. The body beneath hers is warm and solid, yet soft and small, moving in perfect rhythm with Kate’s hand.

    “Kate…”

    The raspy and accented voice in her ear is low and unmistakable.

    Lifting herself on one arm, Kate pries herself away from her, looking down into half-lidded, hazel eyes, unable to tear her gaze away.

    Yelena looks disheveled, but more beautiful and magnificent than anything Kate has ever seen.

    Her golden hair is fanned out on the pillow, and her bow-shaped lips are slightly agape, small gasps falling from between them at every movement of Kate’s wrist. Her thighs frame Kate’s hips firmly, the muscles twitching with pleasure, her skin sticking slightly to hers wherever they touch.

    Looking back at Kate, Yelena looks moments away from ecstasy and soon, her eyes close, the exquisite length of her neck bared as she throws her head back, her lips falling wider open with a wanton moan.

    When Kate wakes up the next time, it’s to the sound of someone moving around in her apartment, and it takes her a second to remember that Clint is staying with her now. Not yet opening her eyes, she tries to fall back asleep, hoping to find her way back to her very pleasant dream, but after a few minutes of fruitless trying, she must accept that it is not happening.

    Blindly searching for her phone, she taps around her sheets, somewhat distracted by flickers of her and Yelena, swirling in and out of her mind and the distinct feeling of wetness between her legs. There are images of naked skin glistening in the soft, muted lights of the night, the sensation of a warm body, writhing beneath hers, and the sound of a low, raspy moan in her ears. When she finally finds the phone under a pillow, she cracks open one eye, even that only slightly, checking the time.

    It tells her it’s a bit past noon, and with a groan Kate resolves herself to get up, letting the images of Yelena’s skin slowly fade from her mind for good.

    It’s not a fast process, but in about 15 minutes, she drags her aching body out of bed, pulling on a pair of dark purple sweatpants and the grey sweatshirt from the night before, not bothering with socks as the movements it would require to put them on feel way too perilous. Her head feels like it’ll explode any moment, and her chest aches with every slight movement she makes, as does her right hip and both of her shoulders. With a look in the mirror, she also sees that her nose is still somewhat swollen and is an otherwise nice shade of dark purple, a color that is also present on the side of her face and her neck. As she touches the thin, purple line, an uncomfortable reminder of Maxine nearly strangling her the night before, her skin feels tender around it, and when she swallows, that motion is also painful. Today’s going to be great.

    All in all, Kate looks as bad as she feels, maybe even worse, and she sighs deeply at her reflection, mentally already planning to take some painkillers and a long, unfortunately icy bath, to numb everything, as soon as she had something to eat.

    When she leaves her room a minute later, Lucky runs up to her with a lazy wag of his tail and a wide doggy smile on his face, obviously happy to see her as he noses at her hand and Kate smiles back, content with his cheerful company.

    Following the sounds of dishes clattering and Clint’s voice, Kate hobbles to the kitchen, reminded of her injuries with every single step she takes. Pushing aside thoughts of their semi-failed mission the evening before, and even her dream, she fantasizes about how good the bath she is going to have will feel instead, which is altogether a lot more simple and uncomplicated than the myriad of things she could be thinking about.

    “…of, I think I just heard her.”

    Assuming that Clint is on the phone, Kate rounds into the room, yawning without even properly lifting her hand to cover her mouth. As she makes it through the threshold, however, she stops in her tracks, thoroughly unprepared for the sight that greets her. Clint is mixing ingredients in a big bowl on the counter, currently adding flour, with a dish towel over his shoulder, while a visibly tired Yelena and a noticeably weary Sonya sit at Kate’s kitchen island. Both of them turn towards her as she enters and while Clint has his back to her, it’s obvious that he hears her coming too, greeting her without turning around. “Morning, Kate. Want some pancakes?”

    Blinking, Kate’s half-awake mind refuses to process the image.

    She has seen Clint do the dishes, but never actually cook, which is Strike One. The borderline domestic image of him making pancakes for the two black widows is frankly, quite unbelievable, making it Strike Two. She also feels particularly unprepared to see Yelena, so soon after waking from the explicit dream she had about her, and also while not yet having processed their actual moment of intimacy from the evening before either. Also, if she knew Yelena was going to be here, should have made an effort to look less like a pile of week-old laundry, mixed with blood. Strike Three.

    To reassure herself that this is not some kind of dream her mind has conjured up again, she reaches with her right hand to pinch her left arm, prompting a snicker from Sonya. Yelena does not laugh, but Kate sees her smile into her mug, as she raises it to her lips. Her green eyes crinkle with her mirth at the corners as they meet hers, the eye contact immediately making Kate’s stomach do a backflip.

    For a moment, Kate’s mind flashes back to her dream, the imaginary sensation of finally kissing those lips, of looking down into those eyes, while they are dark with desire and half- lidded with pleasure, and she has to swallow, her mouth suddenly feeling dry. “You look like shit.”

    For once, Kate is eternally thankful for Sonya’s unfiltered words, the sentence rebooting and jumpstarting her brain and helping her tear her eyes away from Yelena. Both widows wear leggings and oversized sweatshirts, but while Sonya’s hair is pinned up in an uncharacteristically messy bun, Yelena’s is down, slightly damp from a shower she must have taken not too long ago.

    “Thanks, I feel like it too…Good morning.”

    Kate’s own voice comes out somewhat gravelly and rough, either from sleep or from Maxine’s various and increasingly competent attempts to murder her, maybe a combination of both.

    Rounding the kitchen island while her brain boots up, Kate makes her slow way to one of the cabinets, finally procuring some ibuprofen while she avoids looking at Yelena, not sure she can do it yet without either blushing or saying something stupid while her brain is still not fully operational. Clint briefly looks at her, grimacing slightly at the sight of her face before meeting her eyes and shrugging apologetically at his own reaction.

    With a sigh and a roll of her eyes, she makes her way to the fridge next, pulling out a blue Gatorade to take her painkillers with. She proceeds to drink half in one go, despite the pain in her throat before her mind finally processes Clint’s question.

    “Fuck yes to the pancakes. I’m starving.”

    With that, she rounds the kitchen island again, taking a seat across from Yelena, looking the two widows over. They certainly look better than she does, but they do look tired and there is a stiffness to Sonya’s form that is usually not present in her movements. Yelena is almost entirely unharmed, apart from a bandage around her hand, but Kate still feels a spark of guilt at their state, knowing they keep getting into trouble for her sake only. “Yelena and Sonya were just catching me up on what’s been happening.”

    Pushing that feeling aside, Kate takes another swing of her Gatorade, before speaking to them, following up on Clint’s explanation.

    “How is Maxine?”

    Before either widow can answer, Clint turns slightly around again, looking at Yelena. “The widow?”

    Yelena nods, before glancing at Kate fleetingly, while Sonya answers.

    “She’s still asleep. She woke up for a few minutes but we sedated her so she can rest properly.”

    Eyebrows furrowing slightly, she leans back, glancing at Yelena again, catching her staring at Kate’s neck before her eyes rise to meet hers. With a hopefully not very obvious movement, Kate runs a hand through her messy hair, hoping to tame it into something at least acceptable. “And, is that…okay?”

    Yelena nods, while Kate glances at Sonya again, who smiles, without teasing for once. “Yes. That’s expected.”

    Clint speaks again, and Kate still feels somewhat unbalanced, at the two different worlds meeting; her mentor and the two widows present in the same room, her kitchen. Despite having had them here both separately before, it’s weird as hell.

    “How severely is she injured?”

    Sonya answers Clint’s question and Kate feels herself flinch before she takes another swing of her drink.

    “Nothing permanent, but Kate stabbed her through the leg and she lost a lot of blood. Plus, she has a pretty bad concussion.”

    Turning fully around, Clint looks at her, an eyebrow lifted but no real judgment behind his gaze. Lowering the almost empty bottle, Kate explains.

    “Hey, in my defense, she did most of this. Like…at least half.”

    Gesturing at her face and neck she tries to ignore the actual guilt stirring at Sonya’s words. Yelena glances down at Kate’s neck again, a shadow of her worry from yesterday reflected in her eyes but only briefly before she looks away.

    “Okay, so, where were we?”

    Clint’s question is not aimed at her, and Kate takes the opportunity to catch Yelena’s eyes for a moment. When she does, Kate smiles at her, hoping to gauge where the two of them stand now, after everything that happened yesterday but Yelena is focused on answering Clint’s question instead, looking away to turn to him instead.

    “We have escaped the building, and got into the van.”

    Clint nods at her words while beginning to add the pancake batter to a frying pan. Kate watches but feels too exhausted and worn out to participate in the conversation. “Right. Did you have any trouble escaping?”

    Yelena shakes her head.

    “Not really. But we were followed for a short while after. We shook them but it was strange…-“ Blinking, she is thoughtful for a moment, before she continues with another shake of her head.

    “I ran the plates this morning but they came back empty, reported stolen a week ago.” Clint hums, flipping the first pancake with motions that look surprisingly practiced. Meanwhile, Kate does her best to be present in the conversation, her mind somewhat preoccupied with the events of the day before and her dream, flashes of it flitting into her mind as she looks at Yelena.

    “Okay, so back to the break-in, all in all, it seems that they knew you would be coming.” This gets Kate’s attention and she looks at Clint, then at Yelena who exchanges a glance with Sonya.

    “Yes. They were ready.”

    While Kate hasn’t exactly had the time or mental capacity to consider it before, Yelena is right, and the thought is certainly worrying.

    “Maybe when she is awake, you can ask your friend how they knew.”

    Yelena nods, her expression still thoughtful. The sunlight from the window to her right illuminates her features, painting her hair golden and when she glances at Kate for a second, it creates the illusion of Yelena’s eyes glowing.

    “Kid, you up for answering questions?”

    Clint's words pull Kate away from her less-than-subtle staring, turning her head toward him. “Huh?”

    Turning away from the stove, Clint turns back to them with an amused glint in his eyes. “How hard did you hit your head?”

    Smiling, Kate blinks back at him, waving his words off.

    “I’m fine. What questions?”

    Clint glances at Yelena and Sonya, before turning back towards his pancake-making. Sonya smirks at the other side of the kitchen island, while Yelena takes a sip of her coffee, but she sees her eyes flit down to Kate’s neck again. Kate sighs, hoping to catch her eyes again to communicate that she is really okay, but Clint begins to speak before she can and Yelena looks away instead.

    “So, Yelena said the formula and your mom’s contingency were broken up into three parts. And you have to get this one first.”

    Kate nods, rubbing her eyes briefly and trying to focus.

    “Well, yes and no. We…Okay, so, we can get them in any order, really, but the other two are useless unless we have this. And Limitless is Fisk’s so the sooner we get it and delete it from his servers, the safer we are.”

    When she is done speaking, Kate attempts to discreetly massage her neck to help its roughness, but all it does is urge her to cough.

    “Okay. Where are the other two?”

    Clearing her throat to try to get rid of the scratching sensation, Kate takes a second to answer. “Krhm…One is at our holiday house in the Hamptons, in a hidden safe. The other was supposedly taken by the FBI. But we have yet to confirm-“ With the way her throat scratches, Kate has to pause again, taking a long swing of her drink before she continues.

    “If they actually took it in one of their raids and if they did, where is it now. Our access to FBI stuff has been pretty limited.”

    Clint hums, taking a beautiful, golden pancake out of the pan and adding some more batter to make another one.

    “I have a person I can ask for some intel. I’ll get in contact with them after we eat.” Kate only nods, not wanting to aggravate her throat anymore by talking unnecessarily. Glancing at Yelena, Kate catches her looking again and she smiles, and while the worried glint doesn’t disappear from Yelena’s eyes, she smiles back.

    “Okay, so basically you have to go for the part at Limitless again? Before Fisk finds it?” Exchanging a glance with both Sonya and Yelena, Kate can tell that they are in agreement. It’s Sonya who answers.

    “Yes.”

    Clint nods to himself, flipping another pancake.

    “Alright, how?”

    Sighing, Kate leans back against her chair, a part of her wishing they could just lick their wounds for a day or two before they get back to this, but aware that they absolutely can not. This is what she signed up for, after all.

    “Well, security is bound to be elevated after what happened. Not just at Limitless, but probably in the whole building. But, on the other, we do not know how long the file- transformer we used is going to stay hidden. So I think, we have to go sooner rather than later unless we come up with some other way to take it.”

    Yelena answers in their stead again and Kate nods, agreeing with her words. “We need to talk to Maxine first though. We need to find out how they keep staying a step ahead of us, and if there is a weakness or something we don’t know about.” Yelena nods, exchanging a glance with Sonya. It’s Sonya who speaks a few seconds later. “I think she will need a day or two before she can help us. When she woke earlier, she wasn’t exactly…forthcoming.”

    Clint shuts off Kate’s stove and picks up the plate from the counter, carrying the high stack of pancakes to them. Kate sees him glance at Yelena with a certain warmth in his eyes and she is reminded of his words from the night before. My best friend’s little sister. It’s almost odd to think that while all Kate has seen of the two of them together were… murder attempts, that is what they actually are to each other. Natasha, an ever-present, invisible presence between them, softening the space connecting them while also turning it heavy with shared yet not-common history.

    “That’s okay. You all look like you need some time to recoup anyway, no offense. Plus it’ll take my contact a few days to get back to me on the FBI raid. We’ll know a bit more then.” Clint deposits the plate of pancakes on the kitchen island while he speaks, and Kate sees Yelena glance at them, her face hardening for a moment before she blinks and it softens, as she looks back up at Clint. She nods at Clint’s words, glancing at Kate again, her eyebrows furrowing while she gets up to help.

    “We also need to secure an alibi for you.-”

    Walking to one of Kate’s cupboards, she pulls out four plates and utensils for all of them from one of the drawers, while Clint goes to rummage in Kate’s fridge for god knows what. “With the arrows you used, Agent McLagan and Agent Reyes are bound to come back with more questions.”

    She walks back to the kitchen island, setting the table for all of them and Kate tries, again, to ignore the absurdity of them all sitting down to have breakfast, together. Clint returns from the fridge with maple syrup, butter, a box of strawberries, and…pickles?! What the f… “Who?”

    Kate watches, fascinated, as Clint puts down the ingredients, seemingly nonchalant. Yelena glances down at the pickles before she looks up at Clint and there is a silent exchange Kate witnesses. Oh… Clint knows how Yelena likes her pancakes. Which means…

    ‘My best friend’s little sister’.

    Kate smiles to herself. It’s nice.

    But, also….Pickles?! What the fuck, Yelena? Who eats pickles with their pancakes?! “Do you remember when Kate and I were on TV?”

    Clint takes a seat to Kate’s right, nodding at Yelena’s question, prompting her to continue and Kate feels her face start to heat up as she knows her mistakes are about to be revealed. “Well, Kate brought her wallet with us, lost it in the fight, and they found it.-“ Clint closes his eyes for a long moment and takes a deep breath before turning to her and leveling Kate with a look while Yelena rounds off her explanation.

    “And since one of the suspects used a bow and arrow, while Kate was a competitive archer… Well, the FBI is understandably suspicious. They came to question her a few days ago.” Kate reaches for the pile of pancakes, ignoring Clint’s unimpressed look for a second. “We went to check out a storage unit, okay? We didn’t know it was going to be a mission. It made total sense to carry a wallet.”

    She throws Yelena a dirty look for throwing her under the bus but she only receives an arched eyebrow in return, paired with a smug smile.

    “Kid…”

    Clint shakes his head, dad-like disappointment coloring his words, and Kate purses her lips as she pulls two pancakes onto her plate, reaching for the syrup and ignoring them all. Glancing at Sonya, Kate sees the teasing glint she knows slide onto her face, despite its still obvious weariness. Shit. That is one more thing they have to fill Clint in on. Right on cue, Clint asks his next question while he loads up his plate with pancakes too. “What did you tell them to throw them off?”

    Sonya, of course, starts to laugh and Kate feels the corner of her lips lift too, as she exchanges an amused look with Yelena, despite her ears and cheeks warming up. “You wanna…?”

    She lifts her fork at Yelena who is in the process of fishing out pickles to eat with her pancake. Insanity.

    “No, no, you go ahead. It was your idea, after all.”

    That is a blatant lie, and it’s Kate’s turn to level Yelena with an arched eyebrow and an unimpressed look.

    “No, it wasn’t… I mean, yes, but you started it with the…”

    Not knowing what words to use other than sex voice, Kate pauses, pointing her fork at Yelena more directly, deciding not to describe what happened in front of Clint. “-At the door. And then when you stayed to be my alibi when they questioned me.” To the side, Kate sees Clint look between them, obviously confused, but her focus is taken up by Yelena, her little smirk, and the ways her eyes bore into hers, the two of them engaged in a silent battle of wills for a few seconds. Suddenly, he groans, closing his eyes again. “Uhhh…Let me guess. ‘Public displays of affection make people uncomfortable’.” Yelena’s smirk widens, and she leans back against her chair, her eyes shifting from Kate to Clint. Meanwhile, Kate’s mind is bombarded with questions. Why does Clint know that? Is this a thing with spies? Or black widows specifically? Oh my god…did he and Natasha ever do the same? Before she can ask any of it, Yelena answers, her voice amused. “That was the idea… Until Kate told them we are getting married.”

    Clint blinks, once, twice, three times, trying to comprehend Yelena’s words. “Excuse me?”

    Kate has had enough of being thrown under the bus.

    “Okay, it made sense at the moment, okay? It did. You said it too.”

    Yelena’s grin and her amused eyes slide back to her, softening a little bit as she blink once, slowly. Clint seems to reboot, tilting his head to the side before he nods to himself. “That’s one way to do it, I guess.”

    He pushes a generous bite of the pancake into his mouth, nodding a second time to himself as he begins to chew. Looking back at Yelena, Kate feels vindicated but at the smug tilt of her lips still making her stomach squeeze, she can’t help but argue further. “It’s still more creative than continuously implying we were having sex, any time we need a cover for something. Like, do we even talk to each other or are we supposedly doing it at any given moment when we don’t have visitors over? They are going to think we have a problem.”

    Sonya snorts into her pancakes, while Yelena looks thoroughly entertained, not the least offended by Kate slighting her…alibi-making-up-skills. To her right, Clint groans, seemingly ready to end this conversation before it begins as he leans forward to speak but Sonya preempts him, leveling Kate with a teasing look, lowering her fork and knife with a mockingly thoughtful expression on her face.

    “You think too much sex is a problem, Kate Bishop?”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate huffs.

    “No. No. That’s not what I said. I just mean-“ “How about we stay on topic? Your alibi-”

    Clint looks them over, obviously not happy with the conversation and trying to be “the adult” in the room, but Kate is less than delighted with the implication and the dig at her…appetite. Sonya’s grin is wide and next to her, Yelena lifts her mug again to hide her smile at the offended expression on Kate’s face. Repeating her last words, Kate continues as if she wasn’t interrupted.

    “I just mean, we can’t just imply that’s what we were doing every single time, like a get-out- of-jail free card.”

    Yelena lowers her mug, her smile wide, teasing, and annoyingly beautiful. She obviously has an answer for Kate, eyes boring into hers and the simmering heat between them lit up again, but Clint seemingly had enough of their back and forth, trying to cut it off, trying to interrupt them with a Dad-voice Kate has heard from him when his kids were getting a bit too rambunctious.

    “Okay. Let’s just…”

    “What should we say we were doing instead?-“ Kate opens her mouth to answer, captivated by the self-satisfaction in the corner of Yelena’s smiling lips, and ignoring Clint again, but Yelena presses on, blinking at her with a very transparent attempt at seriousness.

    “Hey, maybe next time you could tell them we are trying to have a baby.” Kate snorts tilting her head to the side and unable to stop the amused huff rising in her chest. She can see the humor in the situation too, obviously, despite her annoyance at being constantly teased about it. Next to her, Clint groans, again, and for a second, Kate gives in to the temptation to annoy him, instead of defending her own argument.

    “I mean, isn’t that basically what you have been telling them?”

    Kate feels Clint’s incredulous look at the side of her head, but it doesn’t really register when she sees Yelena’s eyebrows rise and laugh at her words, her eyes sparkling, her amusement echoed by Sonya to her right. Finally letting Clint speak, Kate leans back while she holds Yelena’s amused eyes a moment longer.

    “Okay, questionable biology knowledge aside, Kate is right. She has to have someone other than just Yelena that corroborates her story.”

    When all Yelena and Kate do is glare at each other still, even if it’s mostly playful, and Sonya is preoccupied with her pancakes, Clint sighs, rubbing a hand over his face. “Okay, if nothing else, you can say you visited me at the farm.”

    Shaking her head, Kate tears her eyes away from Yelena to explain to him. “I can’t. Agent McLagan told me not to leave the state.”

    Clint sighs, eyebrows furrowing. Across from them, on Yelena’s side, Sonya rolls her eyes, swallowing a bite before she acquiesces.

    “We can say the two of you were at dinner at our place. Tommy and I will be both of your alibis.”

    “Are you sure that’s a good idea? Associating yourselves with…me.”

    Sonya smiles, completely sincere for once, and blinks at Kate once before she answers. “Yes. I will talk to Tommy.”

    She doesn’t offer any more of an explanation, but her expression warms Kate’s heart a little. Somewhere between getting shot at and teasing the shit out of Kate constantly, Sonya has become a true friend too.

    “Thank you.”

    Clint hums next to Kate, and he nods when she looks at him before his eyes settle on Yelena again.

    “Okay. When they dig into you, what are they going to find?”

    Rising a forkful of pancakes to her mouth, Yelena takes her time to chew and swallow before she answers Clin’t question.

    “Helena Rowley. Legal resident of Mount Vernon, Ohio, owner of a consulting business. Not much else.”

    Eyebrows rising, Clint looks surprised.

    “Rowley? Like when you…”

    Lips curling into a smile, Yelena’s eyes glint with amusement, none of her earlier disdain at Clint’s familiarity visible this time.

    “Yes.”

    With a shake of his head, Clint chuckles and leans back over his plate to cut off a moderately sized bit of his pancakes.

    “Right. Any social media?”

    Also going back to her food, Yelena smiles, eyes flitting over to Kate for a moment before she answers.

    “Just enough for my existence to seem feasible. It’s on private though.” At that, Kate’s eyes widen slightly, before she can mask her surprise completely. After their first time meeting each other, Kate searched for her on social media, obviously coming up with nothing. Of course, back then she did not know Yelena’s legal name, and since learning it, she did not exactly have the time or mental capacity to go and look for her under that name.

    As her eyes flit to Kare, Yelena’s eyes crinkle as her lips stretch into a coy smile, blinking slowly once as she leans back, pinning her in place with a look.

    “Do not get too excited, Kate Bishop, you won’t find any bikini pictures of me on the beach.” Rolling her eyes, Kate smiles at the comment, even if there is some truth to Yelena’s indirect accusation before she remembers Sonya, Yelena and her looking at Amanda’s Instagram, a picture of her on the beach specifically. Wetting her lips, Kate shakes her head, but her smile doesn’t fall.

    “I’m surprised that you have one, that’s all.”

    Yelena’s coy smile widens just a tiny bit as she flicks her hair from her face. “Well, you have to keep appearances, in this day and age. Not having social media as a young woman is out of the ordinary. And when you do not want attention, you have to look as ordinary as you can.”

    It’s all she says about the topic and Kate resolves to look for her account when she has the time. Stuffing pancakes into her mouth, Kate is ready to let the topic go but Sonya seems to have other plans, lifting her fork to point at Kate, then at Yelena next. “Speaking of social media. If you really want to sell this…Your relationship, I mean, to the FBI and everything, you need to soft launch your relationship.”

    Halting another bite of pancakes from her mouth, Kate lowers her fork, chuckling at Sonya with disbelief probably coloring her features.

    “Why do you know what soft launching is?”

    Before Sonya can answer, Clint sighs, looking like he regrets asking already. “What is uh, soft launching?”

    While she glances at him, Sonya answers Kate’s question first.

    “I do have an Instagram too, Kate. And a TikTok…-

    She pauses, before her smile turns coy, the teasing glint Kate knows so well by now flickering behind her gaze.

    “-And for the record, there are bikini pictures of me.”

    Unable to swallow it, Kate chuckles, huffing as it hurts her side and taking a long gulp of her Gatorade before she entertains Sonya’s flirty comment.

    “I’ll be sure to check it out.”

    Clearing her throat, Yelena doesn’t look annoyed at Sonya’s playfulness, or Kate’s answer to it, but she does have an eyebrow raised.

    “Will one of you explain to Barton what soft launching is?”

    Her smile widening into a grin, Kate sees through Yelena’s attempt to get it explained to her, even though she probably did not really try to hide it. Sonya is on the same page, grinning at Yelena.

    “Sure, we will explain, to Barton.”

    Clint huffs out a chuckle next to her, but he seems ready to take the fall, not piling on to call out Yelena too.

    “Thanks.”

    Sonya begins to explain, eyes sliding between Yelena and Clint, back and forth. “-So, basically, only old people post an actual relationship update on social media anymore. The acceptable way to announce that you are seeing someone is to post vague pictures where it’s obvious that you are with someone, a significant other, but not actually post their face or reveal their identity, until you two are very serious. Is this accurate?” Kate is torn from her very subtle staring at Yelena by Sonya asking her for verification. “Uh, yes. Well, yeah, but if we are supposed to be engaged, it might be a bit weird to do a soft launch at this point…then again, it’s even weirder to just straight up not even follow each other or post anything.”

    Yelena’s focused, serious face eases, and her lips are tugged into a smile again, her expression turning a bit too sweet for it to be genuine…at least in their current company. “Awh, Kate Bishop. Is this your way of asking me to follow you on Instagram?” Looking to the side, Kate huffs out a chuckle.

    “Up until three minutes ago, I didn’t even know you had one…But you can if you want to. No beach pics, I’m afraid, but I do have some workout reels.”

    Blinking slowly, Yelena looks playful and coy, until Sonya chimes in, her voice dropping an octave to drive her point home.

    “Oh, we know.”

    Her left eyebrow rising and her smile turning into a self-satisfied grin, Kate looks from Yelena to Sonya and back, suddenly feeling like she was handed a bag full of trick arrows. “Huh. Please, do tell.”

    Clint grunts, his voice gruff when he cuts off any answer from across the table Kate could have received.

    “Yeah, no, do not tell.”

    Across from them, Sonya snickers, looking less tired by the second and Yelena takes another bite of her pancake to stifle her smile, but with her eyes unconsciously returning to her every few seconds, Kate can very much tell.

    “-What is the point of this soft launch?”

    Clint’s face is so amusingly scrunched up in confusion, that Kate has the urge to stretch this conversation as long as she can, despite the scratching and pain in her throat feeling worse with every word that leaves her mouth.

    “Well, you usually do it when you are not sure if the relationship you are in is serious or not. So if you post pics together, and it goes to shit in a few weeks, you don’t have to delete everything and purge your whole account.”

    The confusion has mostly cleared up from Clint’s expression but the lines of his face are still deep, obviously feeling out of his depth in this conversation.

    “I read an article about this, and celebrities do this too, to gently let their followers know they are seeing someone, but not reveal who they are yet. As a kind of teaser.” At Sonya’s words, Kate shakes her head with a smile.

    “Sure, but I’m not a celebrity.”

    Sonya tilts her head to the side, pursing her lips.

    “Well…you are a public figure. Kind of. There are articles out about you.” That does dampen Kate’s smile a little and she sighs, remembering the stress of dealing with the press after her mother’s arrest, and even a few times before that. Sonya is right, however. And there probably will be more articles, if she soft or hard launches a relationship. This is one of the many reasons why Kate’s Instagram page has been workout videos, pictures of Lucky, and a few landscape shots in the last several years.

    “Yeah, I guess...But it’s probably not a good idea to soft launch anything, exactly because of that.”

    Yelena surprises her when she shrugs on the other side of the table.

    “I am okay with it.”

    Eyes wide, Kate immediately counters.

    “You are?”

    “I am not crazy about my face being shown. It’s not great for business. But…-“ Pausing, Yelena seems to think it over for a few seconds, nodding to herself before she continues.

    “I keep my identity very separate. A few people looking at my Instagram profile will not cause more problems than tipping off the FBI that we lied to them would.” Kind of cringing, Kate sucks her teeth, looking at Yelena a bit nervously. Clint and Sonya seem content to let them have this conversation uninterrupted for once, just looking on. “It might not be a few people though. It’s…If we do this, it might get picked up. Like, it will become a thing.”

    A hint of a smile on her lips, Yelena asks back, repeating Kate’s words. “A thing?”

    Kate rubs the back of her neck, wishing it was just the two of them present to have this conversation but also really not.

    “Yeah. Uh, if you saw the articles about…um, about me, you know. People, for some reason, care about what I do, how is my life, who I date, how is it going. All that. It’s not going to be super intense, since I’m not an actual celebrity, but still…A thing.”

    As the sentence goes on, Yelena listens seriously but at the end, she smiles slightly. “I think I can handle a thing.”

    Sighing, Kate is unsure. Yelena might think she knows what she is signing up for but… “Are you sure?”

    Yelena doesn’t answer verbally at first, only nodding. After a moment her face gets serious however and she points her fork at Kate as Sonya did a few minutes earlier. “But I am not doing any silly TikTok dances.”

    When Kate laughs, Yelena’s serious façade breaks and she smiles. Kate sobers up after a second and exhales, puffing out her cheeks before she speaks, placing both palms on the counter to ground herself.

    “Okay. How about we…We cool this a little, and if there is more heat from the FBI, we will post something, and lay out a timeline and I don’t know. Figure out a timeline that fits. Is that good?”

    Yelena nods again and Sonya seems way too delighted by this turn of events and Kate eyes her suspiciously when she leans forward, glancing between the two of them. Thankfully, Clint seems to have had enough of the topic, “Right. With that cleared up, I have things to tell you too…”

    After that, Clint retells Yelena and Sonya what he learned about Rojas and Valentina, and they get him caught up with the details of their ongoing mission as well, while the four of them finish breakfast. They move onto plans after, hitting a wall over how to proceed with procuring the data they left in place the day before.

    With security measures raised and Fisk obviously onto them about the data, the way they entered and attempted the mission is most likely a no-go a second time, they all agree on that. The idea of Sonya infiltrating Limitless as an employee gets floated, but that would most likely take months if it can even be done, for her to gain the necessary security clearance to get access to the server room.

    Kate offers to play bait again, mostly because she has nothing else to add to the conversation, but Clint and Yelena mercilessly shoot down that idea, not even considering it at all. They briefly entertain the idea of getting the data and servers seized by law enforcement and then stealing it from there, but Limitless’ only connection to Fisk is that her wife is the majority shareholder, who doesn’t seem to have so much as a parking ticket, therefore that idea would most likely take too long to come into fruition as well.

    In the end, they decide to take the afternoon to rest, considering the copious amount of beating they (Kate, most of all) took, and get back to the drawing board the next day. Yelena and Sonya go back to Sonya’s apartment to rest and possibly take care of Maxine if she were to wake up again. Kate takes her icy bath with gritted teeth while Clint leaves to hit up a contact who he hopes will help them with locating the encryption key, or at least figure out if the FBI actually has it or not.

    After her ice-cold bath, Kate draws her curtains closed and slips back into her bed, giving her tired and injured body the time and relaxation it needs to heal. Pizza Dog jumps up after her, curling up against her leg, falling asleep before Kate does, his gentle snores filling the room. Kate lets herself relax, even turning on the TV in her bedroom she almost never uses. Her body feels heavy, but if she stays still enough, she can almost not feel the pain, other than her nose and head pounding bluntly.

    Suddenly, there is a noise, that sends Kate’s heart racing, and her muscles lock up. Through her bedroom door, she hears the front door squeak, ever so slightly, and a barely- audible creak of that one floorboard in the living room.

    Breathing as quietly as she can, Kate reaches for the sword she keeps under her pillow, before silently rolling out of bed.

    She is not alone, she can tell. The hairs on her forearm stand up, her whole body locked into action and coursing with adrenaline.

    Pizza Dog jumps off the bed too and Kate lifts a hand, not daring to speak to him, indicating that he stays. His one good eye looks back at Kate worriedly before he glances at the door, then comes back to her, telling her he can hear the intruders too.

    Sneaking close to the door, Kate stays close to her closet, her sword ready in front of her body.

    BANG.

    Before Kate can make it to her bedroom door, it bursts open, almost flying off its hinges. Moving purely on instinct, Kate cuts down the first black figure through the door, practically slicing his head cleanly off, but another immediately takes its place.

    Faceless, masked men fill into the room, one after the other and Kate hears Lucky growl but she is too overwhelmed to make it to him.

    “Lucky, go!”

    One man, she cuts across the torso, kicking another to the side and against the wardrobe, before sliding her blade across his neck. There is no time to get bogged down by the gurgling sounds he makes, or the thick, crimson river that pours down on the carpet of Kate’s bedroom and paints her wall and ceiling in splashes.

    Twisting to the side, Kate is ready to cut down the next masked man, but her hand is grabbed from behind, while another set of hands grabs her other arm in a vice-like grip, and a third, thick arm slides around Kate’s neck, drawing her against an unrelenting, huge chest. The sword is twisted from her hands and with more and more hands grabbing into her, Kate is pushed back down onto her bed, on her stomach.

    Lucky’s growls are fierce, but now that she is being held down, Kate can see at least five or six men standing around him in a circle, kicking and hitting him.

    “No, no, don’t…please don’t hurt him!”

    It’s the first thing Kate says to them, a tear falling down her face as she looks at Lucky’s brave, but confused little face, his one good eye periodically jumping to her, before looking back at the large, scary men standing around him.

    From behind Kate’s back, one of the masked men walks over, and her blood runs cold when she sees her sword in his hand, the tip dripping thick, sticky drops onto the carpet. With all the strength she has, she begins to struggle against the dozens of pairs of hands holding her down, screaming.

    “No! No! Please! No, Lucky, go! Please! Please, don’t-”

    Her struggle is in vain and her begging falls on deaf ears.

    The circle of men parts to make way for the new arrival, and Lucky seems to grasp what’s happening, the hair on his back standing up even more as he bares his teeth. Unable to look away, Kate meets his eye one last time, screaming and thrashing against her captors to no avail.

    The sword is brought down with precision, and the last thing Kate hears is Lucky crying out, pain and terror mixing in his voice.

    Kate sits up screaming in horror.

    The masked men are suddenly nowhere to be seen but her heart hammers against her chest, her fingers closing around the handle of the sword next to her. The TV is still on, it’s low volume drowned out by the blood rushing in her ear.

    Her eyes frantically move around her dimly lit room, jumping from the spot she last saw Lucky face the masked men, to her door, to her wardrobe, to…

    Lucky, standing at the foot of her bed, hackles raised but obviously very confused. He looks at Kate, then around the room, then back at Kate, his gaze worried and the tightness in Kate’s chest slightly eases.

    It was a dream.

    It was just a dream.

    “Come here.”

    Kate pats the bed to her side and while still looking puzzled, Lucky obeys, dutifully jumping up on her sheets. He is still wired, not sitting down until Kate strokes down his back, taking a deep breath.

    “It’s okay… I’m sorry…I’m sorry for scaring you… Hey. It’s okay, relax. Sit.” Lucky sits down, still facing the door and Kate feels that the tight coil in her chest is still there. With a groan, she resolves herself to move, sliding out of bed.

    Just to be sure, still heavily under the effects of her dream, Kate leaves Lucky in her bedroom, closing the door before she walks around her apartment with her sword in her hands. It has been weeks since she had to do this, not since a few days after she made up with Yelena, but still, she dutifully walks around, checking the locks and all the rooks and crannies of her flat.

    Thankfully, there is nobody waiting anywhere, and in a few minutes, she slides back into bed, hugging Lucky close to her. Burying her nose into his soft fur, Kate breaths him in and tries to calm down, but this time around, it takes her very long to fall asleep, images of her nightmare fliting into her mind.

    Overwhelmed with the pain she kind of forgot about, but that hits her full force just then, and with the visceral terror of her dream, Kate cries just a little, her tears wetting Lucky’s fur a bit on his neck. He at least doesn’t seem to mind, his breathing evening out mere minutes after Kate gets back to bed. His whines and terrified growls, however, echo in Kate’s mind for what feels like hours.

    What is something probably close to a miracle, when she does finally fall asleep, no dreams come back to haunt her.

    Kate sleeps well into the afternoon, her body probably finally crashing after so much action and emotion. She thinks she only wakes up to her hunger, but actually making herself something to eat sounds like an endeavor that is way too tiring to undertake in her current state.

    Through an extraordinary amount of effort, she reaches for her phone on the bedside table, ignoring a few texts from Jack to order pizza. It takes her several minutes to drag herself out of bed after her order has been sent, somehow feeling worse than she did in the morning when she first woke up.

    In the time it takes for her food to be delivered, she makes the journey across her apartment to procure some water, and some painkillers, then relocates herself to the couch to be close to the door while keeping her sword within reach, just in case. She puts on a sitcom while she waits and leaves it on even after her pizza arrives, feeding small bits of her crust and toppings to Lucky, which is how Clint finds her as he arrives back late in the afternoon. When she hears the keys jingling in the door, Kate’s heart misses a beat, her mind jumping back to images of her dream before remembering that she gave Clint a key before he left, unsure if she would be awake when he got back.

    “Hey. How did it go?”

    Clint takes off his thick, plaid jacket, while he walks over, throwing it on the back of one of the armchairs before he answers.

    “He says he will try to get the ledger of items seized from your mom’s apartment, but it might take a few days. He was not on that task force, so he will have to find an excuse and someone to get it for him.”

    Kate nods, chewing while she lies back down, throwing a piece of pizza crust to Lucky who catches it still in the air and greedily gobbles it down.

    “’Kay. There is some pizza if you’re hungry.”

    Clint takes a seat, reaching for a slice. He takes a bite, looking her over. “How are you?”

    “It only hurts when I move… So all in all, better than expected?”

    Huffling out a chuckle, Clint’s eyes crinkle but Kate can see a serious glint she doesn’t quite understand yet but doesn’t really care to decipher either. For a few long moments, only TV can be heard, a comfortable silence enveloping the two of them while Kate wonders what Yelena and Sonya are doing right now and if it would be weird to text them to ask. “How are you…emotionally?”

    Turning her eyes from the TV to Clint, Kate expects him to look awkward but he only looks serious and sympathetic. A bit puzzled, Kate blinks as she answers him. “I’m…fine? I got hurt a few times in my life. It’s not a big deal.”

    His eyebrows furrow and he seems to take a moment before he explains further. “I meant about your mom.”

    Momentarily, Kate stiffens, not expecting the question. It’s not that she avoided thinking about that ever since the visit to the hospital, but she certainly welcomed not having the time or opportunity to do so. While she considers how to answer and clenches her jaw in the process, despite the pain it causes, Clint follows up, the lines of his usually square face softening.

    “I mean that’s…what you told me, it’s a lot.”

    Kate sighs softly, resolving herself to having this conversation, rolling her lips together before she speaks.

    “Yeah, it’s…It’s okay.”

    Clint doesn’t speak up, probably waiting for her to continue, and Kate gulps, trying to get rid of the sudden uncomfortable feeling in her throat before she speaks again. Choosing to not look at him while she explains, she raises her eyes to the ceiling, her head leaning back against the back of the couch.

    “You know, I am kind of just too relieved to know that she doesn’t hate me, to really be mad about anything else. Even if I know I probably should be.”

    Clint hums and Kate turns her head to look at him. His eyes are serious and full of sympathy but he doesn’t look like he is pitying Kate. He nods, holding her eyes for a moment longer before he looks away.

    “Look. I gotta be honest, I do think it’s pretty shitty…that she would ask for your help with this, after everything that’s happened…”

    He sighs, pausing, and looks back at Kate but she turns away to look up at the ceiling again, not really wanting to think about the implications of Eleanor choosing to pull her into it all when she supposedly did it to give Kate a better life free of it in the first place. “-But for what it’s worth, I can understand her wanting to keep you away to…to keep you safe as long as she could. I know I wouldn’t want my kids around me if I pissed Kingpin off either.”

    Kate huffs, fussing with the blanket half-covering her legs, and she feels her lips curl a little as she begins to speak.

    “Well. She doesn’t want me away enough to not ask me for help when her ass is on the line apparently.”

    Her voice comes out clipped, a bitter feeling she chose to bury about the whole formula deal bubbling up in her chest. Clint hums again, not offering empty platitudes to absolve Eleanor’s behavior. Kate kind of wishes he would…that he could. That he would find a way to make it make sense or to find some form of absolvation for her mother, but she pushes that feeling aside in a few moments with a tired sigh before she speaks again.

    “Anyway. She is my mom, I’ll always love her, obviously. And I’m sure she does love me too, in her own way, or whatever. There is no point in being disappointed in who she is as a person because that is not going to change. So it’s okay, really.”

    Kate hears Clint sigh and from the corner of her eyes, she sees him nod to himself as well. “You are right. There is no point in being disappointed in who she is. But it doesn’t mean you have to just bottle it up, or shove it aside. It’s not really healthy, Kate.” This time Kate chuckles, breathy and humorless, but her voice comes out more tired, than anything else a moment later, while she strokes Lucky’s head distractedly “That’s pretty rich coming from you.”

    Attempting to pin him with a look, Kate sees him smile, seemingly well aware of the irony of him telling anyone to open up or talk about their feelings. They are quiet for a moment before he sighs deeply, eyes flitting around the room.

    “Did I ever tell you about my mom?”

    That gets Kate’s attention. Clint barely ever shares, and apart from a hinted word or two, he never even mentioned his childhood. Rolling over to prop her head up on her elbow, Kate looks back at him.

    “What? No. Obviously, you haven’t.”

    The corner of Clint’s mouth tilts upwards, and he looks more nostalgic than sad as he looks around once more before he begins talking.

    “-She…On paper at least, she was very different from your mother. She was very young when she had me, not even through high school yet, and my father was never in the picture, I guess. She didn’t have any money, we didn’t. So, for as long as I remembered, we lived in her car that was already old and beat up by the time I was born.-”

    Any other time, she would be overflowing with questions but her exhaustion, combined with the heaviness of the last few minutes mutes Kate’s usual overenthusiasm about learning anything about his past. Instead, she just listens, slowly processing Clint’s words as more information is revealed.

    “-When I was very young, I obviously didn’t comprehend it, but we lived off of pick- pocketing people, and other petty crimes, just driving from one small town to the other, remaining nameless faces just passing through.-”

    Fully in storytime mode, in a way that he usually is only after a few whiskeys, Clint’s eyes move around the room as he explains, occasionally glancing at Kate who listens attentively. “-She justified it by saying we were only taking a little, what people wouldn’t miss anyway and only enough to feed ourselves, but…As I have gotten older, I started to realize that what we were doing, that I actively took part in every day, was not right. That it was wrong.” He exhales slowly, leaning back against the armchair again before he speaks again. “I was ten when during a gas-stop raid, things went wrong.-”

    Biting down on her lip, Kate looks back at him, her earlier sleepiness completely gone. “-I was already a bit apprehensive before that. I knew that it was wrong but…My mom, she…She was my whole world. My only friend, my…”

    Clint grows silent and takes a breath, eyebrows furrowing as he looks down at the table before he seems to make it back to the present with a barely visible shake of his head. “-Anyway, I was supposed to distract the clerk, and she would get the money from the register and then we would run. And well, needless to say, it all went to shit pretty quickly. He turned around and saw her there and instead of running, she reached for his gun below the counter.”

    Sucking in a breath, Kate fears the worst.

    “Did she…?”

    He sighs, smiling but it doesn’t look any happier than Kate’s smile did earlier. “No. They got into a scuffle, and it got knocked to the ground, and I…I picked it up. And I was ten, but I was already a good shot and she knew I wouldn’t miss. And she…-“ For this part, Clint pauses, and Kate already suspects where this is going. “She asked me to take the shot.”

    Having learned that Clint is a lot more complicated than the mighty hero Kate made him out to be when she was a kid, she doesn’t assume what happened, but he continues only a moment later anyway.

    “I didn’t. I shot through the window instead, at the top of a police cruiser a bit further away to alert the sheriff to what was going down.”

    Kate can tell that they are nearing the reason he is telling this story, when his eyes find hers again and they stay, maintaining eye contact as he speaks.

    “I’m telling you this because I am a parent. Not yours, sure, but I’m a dad and that gives me a certain perspective on this whole thing. But, I also kind of know what it’s like to be disappointed in a parent. To love someone, to love a mom, that is objectively, not a good person…partially due to her circumstances but also just…because of who she is. And how it feels when her crimes get rubbed onto you as well.”

    Exhaling, Kate nods, processing his words.

    “And I know that on one hand, it all makes you feel…complicit. And on the other it makes you feel like you are a bad kid. And that it feels like shit, that sometimes she chooses herself instead of you and… And anyway, there is no grand point to this or anything. I just wanted you to know, you are not alone with this.”

    Kate smiles, exhaling slowly and taking a long moment to look at Clint, appreciating his words, his honesty.

    “Well. I’m pretty sure that’s the most words I’ve ever heard you say in one go.” Chuckling, Clint leans back again, shaking his head slightly. Slowly, the joke fades away, along with the smile on Kate’s face.

    “Is she still…?”

    With a sad smile, Clint shakes his head.

    “No. She passed when I was in high school. I only saw her once after her arrest.” Kate gulps, looking back at him as sadness blooms in her chest for a woman she has never met, but for Clint too.

    “I’m sorry.”

    Clint only nods, acknowledging her words without any of his own. Wetting her lips, Kate takes a deep breath, kind of wishing they weren’t having this conversation but also finding solace in the fact that Clint’s story does sound like he might understand. With that in mind, Kate gulps, looking up at the ceiling again to speak as she resolves herself to talk about this, which includes actually examining what she feels about the whole thing. “I do feel complicit. And I am so, so angry with her but it’s like…for the last year, it kinda felt like it was two different people, you know? Like there was my mom, who used to put bandaids over my scraped knees, and then there was like…Eleanor Bishop, who worked for Fisk and hired someone to kill you. Like, my mom has died and this person is someone else and it’s not the same, and it…honestly, it sounds awful, but it helped. Like, I could grieve my mom…who she was to me anyway, and then just compartmentalize that it was this other person who didn’t want to see me, who I didn’t really want to see that much anyway.” Exhaling through tight lips, Kate blinks twice, not feeling like she want to look at Clint right now.

    “But now…now I saw her. And I talked to her, and heard her talk about everything she has done, and why she has done it and…fuck, Clint. It is my mom. She is that person. And now… I feel guilty because it was easier when it kind of felt like she was gone, and I feel guilty because she supposedly did those things to protect me, and I feel guilty because I’m supposed to hate her and be mad at her, and I am mad but not…not for the right things. Or not just for that.”

    It would feel so much better if Kate could get up to pace at least, to expel some of the tight, uncomfortable energy she feels at this whole topic. Her eyebrows permanently furrowed, she continues.

    “I am mad, of course, I am mad about what she has done, but I am most mad for making me think she hated me, and for making me think that she was hurt, and I am angry that she still keeps me away, and I am so, so mad that she wants to involve me in this to cover her ass. I…”

    Her voice kind of breaks here, not exactly close to crying but overcome with emotion all the same. She continues a second later, her words coming out almost stilted. “If I am so, so important, that she has to keep away, and do all of this shit to protect me, then why ask me to go on this fucking…suicide mission, to help her case, it’s uh…” Taking a deep breath, Kate is a bit embarrassed to feel that by this point her words come out shaky, her throat tight and her voice heavy. Closing her eyes, she bites down on her lower lip to get herself under control, and Clint is gracious enough to not speak while he knows she has more to say.

    “…Ugh, you are such an asshole for making me talk about this.”

    Glancing at Clint, he smiles before chuckling, his eyes warm and full of understanding. “We can talk about something else if you want.”

    Taking another shaky breath, Kate nods but when she speaks again, it’s her sticking to the topic.

    “On one hand, it just serves to prove that her excuse that she did it all for me is bullshit. And on the other, it shows that sure, she loves me…but if it comes down to a choice between her and me, she will still choose herself.”

    At that, Clint’s eyebrows furrow.

    “Well, I can’t say that I’m Eleanor’s biggest fan, obviously.-“ At that, a hint of a smile slides onto Kate’s face but that’s the best she can do. “-But this is probably her just accepting that she needs help. From what little I have seen of her, I have no doubt that she would not involve you in any of it if she had a choice. She avoided it as long as she could.”

    It sounds logical, but the seed of doubt, that small thorn of disbelief in her mother’s love doesn’t fade away, not completely anyway.

    “I don’t know. I…Growing up, I honestly never really felt like I was the priority, so why would now be different? Like, if it was a choice between coming to my games, or cello recital, or going to a conference, or just work…Well. I learned to not look too hard at the crowd, and-”

    For the first time that evening, Clint’s face looks pinched, torn between genuinely hurt and shameful, and the expression makes Kate swallow the rest of her sentence. This topic is one that she knows is somewhat sensitive to Clint.

    “Hey, it’s not the same to miss something because of a conference and to miss it because you are literally saving the world.”

    The smile on Clint’s face looks more like a grimace and it apparently wasn’t the right thing to say.

    “Yeah, yeah. It’s…Sure.”

    There is a beat of almost painful silence, and guilt starts worming its way into Kate’s heart again.

    “Are you missing something to be here?”

    Meeting her eyes, Clint seems to think before he nods.

    “No…Not yet. Nate’s first soccer game is in a few weeks.”

    Almost managing to sit up, Kate looks at him with a smile.

    “You have to go.”

    Clint looks conflicted before he shakes his head.

    “I don’t know, kid. I’m... I don’t want to leave you here alone.”

    Smile widening, Kate nods, trying to act nonchalant.

    “I’m not alone. I have two black widows watching my six.”

    When Clint still looks conflicted, Kate continues.

    “But, if you really worry, just go and come back. We were fine while you weren’t here, we’ll cope for a day or two.”

    Clint does take a moment to look pointedly at the visible injuries on Kate’s neck and chest but after a moment, his face eases a little, the lines on it fading away. “Okay, we will…we’ll see. If you manage to stay out of trouble, I might go.” Kate huffs, amused but exhausted as she eases herself back onto the couch gingerly. “I am perfectly capable of staying out of trouble.”

    “Your track record says otherwise.”

    Kate makes a face at him, and for about a minute, neither of them speaks. Glancing at the dog next to her on the couch, Kate clears her throat.

    “Hey, do you think that when you go back, you could take Lucky with you? Just…until things calm down a bit.”

    The thought has been on Kate’s mind since her dream in the afternoon. It’s only a matter of time until her location gets compromised, or something, and while she trusts in her own ability to protect herself, the same cannot be said for Lucky. Clint smiles as he nods, glancing affectionately at the dog for a moment too.

    “Sure. You know the kids always go gaga for him.”

    Kate smiles too, reaching over to stroke the soft fur on the top of his head. “It’ll be like a little vacation, right buddy?”

    At her tone, Lucky’s one good eye opens sleepily, as if he understands Kate’s words, his tail swishing in a couple of sleepy wags before he drifts back to sleep. After a long moment of silence, Clint speaks, his voice gently nagging.

    “You know, the kids would go gaga for you too. You could use a little break.” Smiling sadly, Kate rolls her eyes affectionately a little, before looking back at him. “I know. But I’ve got too much stuff to do. It’s a ticking bomb with Fisk and the serum.” Acknowledging her words with only a hum, Clint nods, looking at Kate seriously. After a moment, his demeanor shifts, a teasing glint sparking in his eyes.

    “And you have a wedding to plan, apparently.”

    Pursing her lips to the side, Kate rolls her eyes.

    “I knew you took it a bit too easily earlier.”

    Clint smiles, his eyes warm, teasing, and painfully dad-like.

    “You can bring Yelena too, to the farm, if that’s the holdup.”

    An eyebrow lifting, Kate pins him with a look.

    “You know, for someone who is uncomfortable with the idea, you sure do bring it up a lot.” His smile widening into a grin, Clint leans back, lifting up his hands in mock surrender. “Hey. If you make an honest woman out of her, who am I to stand in your way? I just don’t want to accidentally walk in on anything.”

    Scoffing, Kate can’t help but laugh, rubbing distractedly at her still slightly wet eyes, before looking back at him mockingly.

    “…an honest woman? Is this the kind of shit you say to your kids?”

    Not phased by her comment, Clint looks back at her with lifted eyebrows and an almost condescending smile.

    “My kids are smart enough to not get mixed up in something this messy.” After a moment, his eyebrows furrow, and Kate would buy his concern if she didn’t know him, recognizing his teasing for what it is.

    “You do know her dad is a Russian super-soldier right?”

    “I am aware, yes.”

    “Her mother probably made more people disappear than you have ever met.” Kate can’t help but chuckle and it takes her a moment to realize it was probably Clint’s purpose for bringing this up in the first place.

    “Okay, that sounds scary but also super intriguing. Like, I’ve met a lot of people, Clint.” He sighs deeply and shakes his head seriously, but Kate can see that he is joking. “Why don’t you like normal things?-”

    Kate wants to interject that she does like normal things, and while she is not going to say it, liking a beautiful woman whom she has been working very closely with for weeks now, who is just the right amount of weird is also perfectly normal, but Clint continues. “You have more money than most people can even imagine, you should be…I don’t know, partying on private islands with other rich kids, instead of going after mobsters and getting into situationships with girls who can probably do more with their little finger than most people can do with a knife.”

    There is a joke in there about what Yelena could do to her with any of her fingers, but Kate focuses hard on not saying anything about that to Clint, blurting out the first other slightly humorous answer that pops into her mind.

    “Okay, now you are just making her sound even more enticing.”

    Shit.

    What did she just say?

    What…

    Kate didn’t mean it like that.

    There is a beat of silence and even Clint looks surprised by her words and Kate’s own eyes are wide like saucers.

    “That’s…No. No, I just meant, like more than the comments about her parents did, before. Like, with everything you just said, it makes it sound exciting because it’s dangerous.
