I don’t-“ He starts laughing a second later, probably both at Kate’s accidental admission and the expression on her face.

    “Ugh, shame on you, Clint, taking advantage of my weakened state. Twice a day too. You know what I meant.”

    He still looks at her, with a fair amount of teasing humor in his eyes, probably with ten other remarks up his sleeve so Kate feels the need to jab back at him.

    “Also, why do you even know the word ‘situationship’ Is that you saying ‘how do you do fellow kids’?

    One eyebrow rising, Clint shakes his head, amused but evidently confused. “Fellow kids…What?”

    The rest of their evening is spent with thankfully less emotionally charged banter and teasing, the two of them falling back into the comfortable bickering they both seem to prefer as their main form of communication with each other. Clint doesn’t bring up Kate’s mother again or tease her about Yelena, and Kate doesn’t make more accidental admissions that make her own head spin.

    When she retires to her bedroom later, with Pizza Dog in tow and the sounds of Clint still moving around her apartment, her sleep is thankfully undisturbed by nightmares or even dreams.

    The two days after are pretty uneventful.

    Yelena and Sonya come over to work with them, but they don’t make much headway on how to get the data knowing Kingpin might expect them to try again.

    They come up with a few different alternative ways to infiltrate Limitless, but all end up getting scrapped for one reason or another. They all agree they need to do more actual reconnaissance (at least the Widows and Clint, while Kate stays quiet, knowing she’ll be shut down if she suggests they should use her as bait again but she plans to throw it in when they exhausted every other option). They all also know that they probably shouldn’t advance until Maxine is awake, and Clint and Kate follow Yelena’s and Sonya’s lead in that, obviously. After that first day of pretty acute pain, Kate is still injured, having to move carefully but all in all, she feels much better than she looks. Although, that mostly means she looks absolutely terrible, while she only feels slightly awful. Training is still out of the question, but apart from sharp movements, she can get around fine, even if she looks like she has been in a car accident and a bad one at that.

    Then, the third day after Clint’s arrival is anything but uneventful.

    It starts with one major event, that has Kate’s heart beating erratically and makes her feel like she’ll sweat through her hoodie.

    Namely, that when Sonya and Yelena come over the third morning after Clint arrived, Sonya has a shit-eating grin on her face and Yelena looks somewhat irritated. Somewhat wary but intrigued, Kate eyes them both, her gaze sliding from one to the other and back, before she asks.

    “What’s up?”

    Yelena sighs, taking a seat across, on one of the armchairs to Clint’s side, Sonya doing the same next to Kate on the couch. There is a beat, where Yelena looks uncharacteristically reluctant to speak before she opens her mouth, wetting her lips before she starts. “My parents called.”

    Okay? What…

    “-Agent Reyes called my mother to ask about our relationship.”

    Kate’s eyes widen, barely registering the pain as she sits up. Even Clint looks up from his file, eyebrow slightly furrowed. He has been catching up on the work they did before his arrival, trying to find something they might have missed, but so far he found nothing (which Yelena and Kate are both smug about).

    “Holy shit. What did she say?”

    The fact that Yelena looks away at her question makes Kate nervous, but her next words confuse that somewhat.

    “She figured it might have something to do with what I’m doing here so she told her she was ecstatic and that she just can’t wait to have us for Christmas.”

    Looking to the side, then at Clint and Sonya, but finding nothing that would provide an explanation, Kate blinks twice. Carefully, she tries to prompt Yelena to explain. “Okay, that’s…good, right? That’s good.”

    Finally, Yelena looks at her and purses her lips while her eyebrows furrow. “No, Kate, it is not good. I did not want my parents involved in this.” Still not quite grasping why, since Yelena had no problem asking for her mother’s help before, Kate just blinks again, nodding but confused.

    “Oh, okay.”

    Glancing at Sonya to try to get a read on the situation does not bear any results still, as she just smirks at her tablet, and Clint shrugs across from her before his phone chimes and his attention is drawn to it.

    Turning her attention back to Yelena, Kate tries to get an explanation. “But didn’t you ask her to hack the NYPD a few days ago? So she was kind of involved already.”

    Rolling her eyes, Yelena huffs and Kate sees Sonya’s smirk widen, but she doesn’t join the conversation. For a moment, Yelena’s frown eases as Lucky walks up to her, with his tail swishing and Kate would be lying if she said Yelena’s face softening as she pats her dog wasn’t making her stomach do some pretty elaborate acrobatics. It only lasts a few seconds, before Yelena turns back to her, her face clearly annoyed again even as she continues to pat and scritch Lucky’s head.

    “Not that.”

    Yelena manages to fit in one more annoyed huff, along with shifting around on Kate’s couch before she finally clears up what her issue is.

    “-I told you. My mother nags. She nags about…dating.”

    Understanding downs on Kate and she blinks again, before clearing her throat and trying to bring the conversation to easier waters with a joke, offering a lopsided grin. “Hey, you are scratching my back, so I can totally scratch yours if you need a… reverse beard or something.”

    The confusion that spreads on Yelena’s face is adorable, and Kate feels her own smile widen before she even asks.

    “A what?”

    Even Sonya looks at Kate a bit unsurely, but she hears Clint’s barely-concealed exasperated sigh without having to look at him. Huffing out a chuckle, Kate explains, ignoring him completely.

    “Um…A beard is a person of the opposite gender that gay people pretend to date to hide the fact that they are gay. But I kinda meant that I’ll gladly extend our fake relationship to your parents to get them off your back if you need that. I am great with parents.” Yelena’s confusion clears from her face and she lets out a breathy chuckle, but she also shakes her head.

    “There is no need. I explained to them the situation so it is all cleared up now…” Nodding to herself, she sighs before pinning Kate with a look.

    ”But it was a very tiring conversation.”

    Smiling, Kate looks back at her, finding the way she looks a bit grumpy at her parents also unreasonably cute.

    “I’m sorry.”

    Looking back at her, Yelena blinks and some of her irritability have faded, holding her eyes with a tiny spark of amusement.

    “They are very pushy. My father mentioned wanting grandbabies before he is too old.” Kate guffaws, laughing while she feels her ears and cheeks warm up. At that, at least, Yelena’s eyes glint with some humor, a ghost of a smile tugging the corner of her pink lips upward, but it’s gone after a moment as she sighs deeply.

    “You know what this means, right?”

    Kate grins, while Sonya smirks even harder and Clint is completely preoccupied by his phone, but probably listening.

    “Well…I’m not sure how much I can help with the grandbaby situation-”

    Rolling her eyes, Yelena finally smiles too, before she cuts Kate off.

    “Not that. The FBI. They are digging into this.”

    She points at the space between them, moving her finger from pointing at herself, then to Kate and back.

    Oh.

    Glancing at Sonya, the smirking starts to make a lot more sense.

    The whole soft launching conversation…

    “We could go on a date?-“ At Yelena’s sharp look, and Sonya’s eyes widening, Kate rushes to elaborate. “A pretend date, I mean. Tip-off the FBI of where we’ll be? Make sure they are, um… watching.”

    It feels way too awkward but Kate wants to present some alternatives, other than plastering their fake relationship over social media, where it can be picked up by journalists and everyone else, not to mention, Fisk and his people, putting Yelena in even more danger. Sonya looks way too excited by the prospect, but Yelena shoots it down pretty quickly. “That is way too much of a security risk. What if we get accosted by the Kingpin’s men while we are out? We would blow our cover in a minute, especially if we are watched.” She is not wrong about that, and Kate nods to indicate her agreement, but unsure how to proceed.

    “Right, I should call my kids.”

    With that, Clint walks out of the room, seemingly not interested in the conversation and a second later Kate hears the door of her unused dining room click closed. “So…”

    Sonya obviously has no plan to leave this alone or let just the two of them figure it out, so Kate tries to get ahead of her before she suggests something embarrassing or too outrageous. “We could post something on Instagram? Like…I don’t know. A picture of two mugs, or…” With a theatrical gasp, Sonya leans forward, a shit-eating grin on her face. “Two mugs? You harlot. Have you got no shame at all?!”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate looks at her.

    “We are not trying to make the news. Just indicate that our…fake relationship is real.” Yelena chuckles at Kate’s suggestion of the mugs, then looks at her intensely, obviously trying to come up with something as well, the gears in her head visibly turning as she tilts her head to the side.

    “How about a selfie of both of you in a bathtub.”

    At both of their wide eyes, Sonya rolls her eyes.

    “You don’t actually have to be naked, come on.”

    Looking at Yelena, she blinks back at Kate with the same bewildered expression before both of them begin to laugh.

    “Yeah, no. Yelena said no faces. Also, that’s not soft launching.”

    Pursing her lips at Kate’s words, Sonya looks dissatisfied.

    “You said it yourself, it’s weird to soft launch if you are supposed to be engaged already.” Annoyed that Sonya has a point, Kate sighs, pulling out her phone to check some friends’ Instagram pages for ideas.

    “If you want to be boring, you could just post a picture of your hands with rings and call it a day.”

    Shooting down Sonya’s next question without even looking up, Kate keeps scrolling. “We don’t have rings.”

    That is something to keep in mind since Agent Reyes made a note of it too, but it’s also a bit too fast to post that, before even giving a hint that either of them is in a relationship. Glancing up, Kate sees that Yelena is on her phone too, brows creasing as she looks at something on the screen, one eyebrow slightly lifted.

    “There is an article that ranks the ways to soft launch a relationship.” A smile tugging at her lips, Kate looks up at her, half distracted by how she still has one hand on Lucky’s head on her thigh, stroking gently between his closed eyes with her thumb. “What do they say is the best?”

    Yelena wets her lips, not looking up, still reading, still stroking Lucky’s head. “An Instagram story of a staycation adventure with a mystery companion.” Before Kate can answer, Sonya huffs next to Kate, throwing her head against the back of the couch to look up at the ceiling dramatically.

    “Ugh…boriiing.”

    Chuckling at her behavior, Kate doesn’t address Sonya, responding to Yelena instead. “We could book a hotel room?”

    Tilting her head from left to right, still reading, Yelena doesn’t look convinced, prompting Kate to ask.

    “What are the other ideas on the list?”

    Scrolling back, Yelena reads them out, while counting on her fingers. Lucky opens his one eye, looking up at her, and gently nudges her thigh with his nose until she goes back to stroking his head.

    “Posting their back view while you are obviously on a date. Documenting their gifts and acts of service but not tagging them, that could work…Hmm. Tagging them in an Instagram post with photographer credits… I don’t know how that works…”

    As Yelena trails off, her eyebrows furrowing again, Kate can’t help but smile at the image, trying desperately to not get bogged down by the absurdity of the moment. Lowering her own phone, she begins to explain when Yelena looks up.

    “Like, if you go on a date somewhere and they take a photo of you. So you post yourself, but it’s obvious that you were there together somewhere, most likely on a date. That works too, I think. I can tag you but you are not shown, so it’s still pretty private.” Yelena holds her eyes as she explains, thinking it over before she shakes her head slightly. “That has almost the same problem as your first idea. We could get jumped any time we are out.”

    For a second, Kate entertains the idea of actually going somewhere together, trying to not imagine where she’d like to go, but Yelena is right. There is a security risk, so Kate shakes her head.

    “I have a bunch of pictures of myself from California, that we could use, so we don’t actually have to go anywhere. Considering we are supposedly engaged, we would have had to date by then already anyway. I’ll just tag it as a throwback.”

    Rubbing her neck at the somewhat awkward explanation, Kate chuckles. Yelena nods, seemingly accepting, or at least considering the idea.

    “Who took those pictures? Are they not going to be upset that Yelena is…stealing their credit?”

    Sonya’s question is pointed, and Kate thinks she is fishing, like always, but she chuckles, shaking her head while she glances at Yelena for a second, who just waits for her to answer, face neutral.

    “Some friends, some just a tripod. Nobody to be jealous of anything.”

    With an eyebrow raised, Sonya looks almost challenging but they both accept Kate’s explanation. Yelena nods after a moment.

    “Okay, that works for me. You think that will suffice?”

    “Yeah, plus it can help with the…backdating. We can think of some others down the line.” Yelena seems to understand without her having to explain, nodding again. Picking her phone back up, Kate begins to look through her photos, trying to find one that will work. “God, I thought you guys would be more exciting.”

    Half scoffing, half laughing, Kate looks at Sonya.

    “Okay then, what do you think we should do? Leak a sex tape?”

    Grinning, Sonya bats her eyelashes in two slow blinks but she does shake her head. “You are not really famous enough for that. It would just get branded as amateur porn.” Kate can’t help but laugh, glancing at Yelena to see her do the same, pearly white teeth flashing.

    “Oh yeah, that’s the only real problem with it.”

    Shrugging at Kate’s sarcastic comment, Sonya looks shameless but she allows a wide grin to overtake her features before she leans forward, elbows on her knees.

    “No, but seriously, this reeks of minimal effort.”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate leans back, throwing an arm over the back of the couch. “It’s not minimal effort, I am just a private person.”

    An eyebrow raised, Sonya turns more fully towards her.

    “Are you?”

    Sighing, Kate holds her eyes. More fishing.

    “Yeah. Surprisingly, after the whole press frenzy around my mom’s arrest, I’m not crazy about the idea of people sniffing around my life or the people I date.” Sonya nods, glancing at Yelena across from them before she turns her eyes back at Kate. “So, when you date someone, you’ll never post them on social media?”

    Trying to imagine what that would be like, but also maybe stalling a little, Kate’s face scrunches up a little. After a long moment, she shrugs, turning her head to look back at Sonya.

    “I don’t know. Definitely not right away. Maybe down the line.”

    Sonya nods with pursed lips, but she looks into Kate’s eyes pointedly a second later, with one eyebrow arched.

    “Like when you get engaged?”

    Huffing out a laugh, Kate rolls her eyes before she concedes, nodding.

    “Yeah, I guess.”

    Sonya smiles, leaning towards Kate.

    “So, you agree, by now, it is time to do something more intimate than a travel photo where only you are in the picture.”

    Kate throws her head back against the couch, chuckling.

    “I did not agree to anything. But fine, I’ll post anything that Yelena is comfortable with.” Across from her, Yelena huffs and throws her hair over her shoulder but there is amusement hidden in the corners of her lips.

    “Nice of you to put all the responsibility on my shoulders.”

    Throwing her hands up, Kate laughs, sliding lower on the couch.

    “I’m not! I’m just…trying to be chivalrous.”

    Rolling her eyes, Yelena turns away but she definitely smiles, and her eyes return to Kate’s a moment later to exchange a glance that makes her feel like she swallowed a piece of molten metal, and it’s spreading all over her veins.

    “Okay. How about something like this?”

    Excluding Kate from the conversation, which she doesn’t mind for once, Sonya reaches over the coffee table to show her phone to Yelena. She raises an eyebrow and chuckles, before shaking her head.

    “No.”

    The raised eyebrow is mirrored on Sonya’s face and now Kate kind of wants to see what the photo was, but the phone’s screen is hidden from her view.

    “It doesn’t show your face.”

    “No.”

    There is a moment between the two Widows, looking at each other intently and probably having a silent conversation that Kate is not privy to, before Sonya huffs and goes back to scrolling on her phone. After a few seconds, Sonya offers her phone once more. “This?”

    Yelena barely glances at it before shaking her head. Kate watches on like a tennis match, gaze jumping between each Widow, back and forth.

    “That is childish.”

    “It’s cute.”

    Smile widening, Yelena repeats, her tone final.

    “Childish.”

    Sonya shrugs, taking back her phone.

    “Fine, if you want something more mature…”

    Closing her eyes slowly, Yelena looks playfully annoyed and Kate can’t help but chuckle, the two of them exchanging another glance. It takes Sonya another few seconds to find another candidate.

    “Okay. How about this?”

    Yelena takes the phone and looks at it for a long moment before she glances at Kate and wets her lips. Inhaling deeply, she nods to herself.

    “Okay. That is fine.”

    She hands Sonya’s phone over to Kate, who doesn’t understand why this interaction makes her feel so wired, but it sure fucking does. Looking down at the phone, Kate swallows, taking it in.

    It’s surprisingly tame, considering it comes from Sonya.

    It’s two pairs of feet on the couch, one person obviously sitting or lying between the legs of the other, the legs partially entangled. It’s suggestive, sure, with the muted lighting and the tangled limbs but all in all, it’s tasteful and easily anonymous.

    Wetting her lips, Kate glances at Yelena, wondering if she is truly okay with this before she looks at Sonya.

    “Yeah, that’s fine with me.”

    Sonya looks almost like a kid who got handed a hundred-dollar bill at the door of a candy shop, and in a few seconds, she is up.

    Eyebrows rising, Kate exchanges another amused glance with Yelena, before watching Sonya run around the living room, drawing the blinds one after the other. She turns on the floor lamp to Kate’s side, dimming it slightly before she produces a candle out of nowhere, puts it on the coffee table, and lights it with a box of matches that she pulls out from one of Kate’s drawers, much to her surprise.

    In barely a few minutes, the atmosphere of the whole living room is transformed, and Sonya stops next to the couch with her hands on her hips.

    “Yelena, come here. Kate, get on this side.”

    Obeying Sonya’s “request”, Kate slides over to the other end of the couch, while Yelena remains in her armchair, not moving.

    “Turn to the side. Yelena, come on.”

    Again, Kate obeys but she turns to look at Yelena, who looks at the whole image with an eyebrow raised, obviously amused. After a moment, she stands up, much to Pizza Dog’s disappointment, and walks over.

    “Why am I the one in front?”

    Halting by the couch, she looks down on Kate with her hands on her hips too who feels increasingly awkward with the two Widows standing over her. Sonya exhales through her nose, but it mostly sounds like a chuckle she doesn’t allow to fully materialize. “Because with how short your legs are compared to hers, your feet would be in line with her knees.”

    The mental image of taking a picture like that is funny enough to make Kate chuckle, which gets lodged in her chest when Yelena huffs a second later, unceremoniously plopping down between her legs.

    “Now what?”

    Despite her words, Yelena doesn’t sound annoyed but Kate makes sure to keep track of all her limbs, lest one of them accidentally does something they have not previously discussed. “Lean back.”

    Yelena does lean back, against Kate’s chest who suddenly has a serious problem with where she should put her hands. That is before she catches Sonya’s eyes, who communicates very clearly something along the lines of ‘seriously?, and Kate decides to just go with the flow. Loosely enveloping Yelena from behind, Kate winds her arms around her upper body, her hands coming to rest on each other over Yelena’s stomach. There is a millisecond where Yelena stiffens, almost imperceptible, but it’s gone before Kate can change her mind. Yelena leans fully back, one hand coming to rest on her own thigh, while the other reaches for her phone.

    Lifting it up, she opens the camera and raises it up to get a better angle. Their feet look kind of awkward next to each other on the screen like they don’t know each other, (Jesus, Kate, get a grip), so Kate moves hers closer to one of Yelena’s, trying to imitate the implied intimacy of the photo.

    “You should get the dog in the photo.”

    At Clint’s voice and his words, Kate jolts for a moment in surprise, her arms going tighter around Yelena for a fraction of a second. Turning her head back, she can kind of see him standing in the doorway behind them and has to wonder how long he has been standing there. It takes a moment for his words to actually register but when they do, Kate feels herself kind of agreeing.

    “That’s actually not a bad idea. I post a lot about Lucky, so including him will probably make this more authentic.”

    In front of her, Yelena hums, and when Kate inhales next, she smells that hint of vanilla she has multiple times before, whenever she is in Yelena’s proximity. Kate thinks it might be her shampoo, and swallows hard, trying to keep her mind from getting even more distracted than it already is.

    “Come on, krasavchik.”

    Yelena opens her legs wider (Get. A. Grip. Kate), to make space for Lucky, who happily jumps up onto the couch, settling happily with his head on Yelena’s thigh again, looking up at them. Exhaling slowly, Kate reminds herself, to keep her shit together while Yelena lifts her phone again, even higher this time to get Lucky’s face in the photo too. Kate sees the screen, and it’s an adorable photo but what grabs Kate’s attention is Yelena, who can probably shoot a butterfly out of the sky 500 yards away, missing the big white button that would take a snap once. She raises her other hand to hold her phone better and Kate leans her face slightly to the side, her cheek touching Yelena’s.

    “Lower the exposure a little.”

    At Sonya’s advice, Yelena does just that and Kate decides to stop overthinking and just tries to make her legs look as natural and sensual as possible…which sounds ridiculous because it is. Especially considering that she wears a pair of grey sweatpants, which are probably the least sensual item of clothing in her wardrobe.

    Anyway.

    With Lucky’s adorable face, and Yelena’s tight legging-covered legs, she doubts anyone will really focus on her sweats so that’s something at least.

    Yelena takes a few more pictures with the phone tilted a couple of ways and soon, they are done. Slowly, Kate pulls her arms away and it almost feels cold when Yelena leans forward, untangling herself from Kate’s embrace.

    When they stand up, Kate meets Clint’s eyes who looks back at her with one eyebrow lifted, but he thankfully doesn’t say anything that Kate has to tell him to shut up for. Sonya looks smug, but she is not whose reaction Kate is interested in, her eyes straying to Yelena repeatedly after both of them are up and off the couch.

    She looks perfectly composed and neutral, with no sign of being uncomfortable by the position or the pictures they have taken, or even affected at all. She grins at Kate, when their eyes meet a second time, flipping a few strands of hair out of her eyes. “So, are you guys ready to work or are you doing an engagement photoshoot today too?” Clint sounds more entertained than annoyed and the next few hours are spent in a very similar fashion as the two days before. The four of them work, go over documents and hatch plans to go back to Limitless which ultimately end up getting ditched.

    Yelena and Sonya leave before dinner, Sonya having plans with Tommy and Yelena in charge of looking after Maxine if she were to wake up. Kate and Clint work for another 30 minutes before Kate orders them 2 pizzas for dinner and takes Lucky for a short walk while they wait for it to arrive.

    The sky is dark and grey, rain clouds gathering and Kate sincerely hopes that Lucky and she will make it back to their apartment before the storm that seems to be brewing inevitably arrives. Despite wearing a hoodie, a jacket, and a beanie, the wind blows almost through Kate while she makes her way around the streets surrounding their building, pulling her clothes tighter against herself.

    Lucky’s enthusiasm is uncurbed by the weather, however, and he takes his time sniffing and mooching around, happily grinning up at Kate every few seconds. Smiling back at him, Kate pulls him along, her thoughts filled with both trying to come up with a way to get back to Limitless, keeping track of her surroundings and also repeatedly returning to the “photoshoot” Yelena and she have done earlier.

    Yelena sent her the photos before she left, along with her Instagram username to tag her whenever Kate posts it. They agreed that Kate will also post their original idea some other day, more post probably providing their relationship with additional legitimacy. Wanting to wait until they are done with work (and Clint is not there to tease her about it), Kate decided not to post the photo before she left, and she spends the first few minutes of her walk with Lucky trying to come up with a caption. Kate has also held off on stalking Yelena’s page so far, so she also puts significant effort into ignoring the feeling of her phone burning a hole in her pocket, urging her to indulge in looking at it already.

    They walk for 25 minutes, Kate just contemplating steering them towards home, when she feels her phone buzz in her pocket.

    Assuming it’s Clint telling her the pizza has arrived, Kate lets Lucky sniff at another garbage bag left on the side of the road before they turn back home when she feels her phone buzz again.

    Twice, in quick succession.

    Clint never double or triple texts.

    Pulling her phone out, Kate reads the messages quickly.

    [from: Yelena] 8:15 pm: Come over, she is awake [from: Yelena] 8:15 pm: Drop Lucky off first [from: Yelena] 8:15 pm: Do not bring Barton Not even surprised that Yelena knows they are out for a walk, Kate immediately turns them around, speedwalking through the semi-crowded streets. It takes a bit over 5 minutes to make it back to their building, Lucky happily jogging along to keep up with Kate’s quick pace. Rain starts to fall just as they make it back, and Kate is distractedly happy she will not have to spend time drying PD off before she goes over to Yelena. The elevator ride goes by fast, and Kate enters her apartment not even 10 minutes before she first read Yelena’s text. Clint is on the phone when Kate walks in, talking to his kids judging by his voice. Kate quickly tries to mime what happened and where she is going, but she only gets a confused look in return, so she picks up a notepad from the table by the door, writing him a note to read once he hangs up.

    She spares a minute to whizz by the kitchen, measuring out Lucky’s dinner since she doesn’t know when she’ll be back, and even remembers to throw a hundred dollar bill on the table for Clint, to pay for the pizza whenever it arrives.

    All in all, Kate arrives at Sonya’s doorstep a minute or two after 8:30, knocking on the door without thinking, her heart hammering for several reasons.

    It’s Yelena who opens the door a moment later, wearing the same pair of soft leggings from before and an oversized, green t-shirt. Her hair is up in a bun, and Kate is relieved to see that she doesn’t seem injured or even have a hair out of place.

    During the last few days, Sonya and Yelena have been tight-lipped about Maxine’s state, but they did let it slip that she had lashed out once or twice when she woke up and didn’t know where she was before they could calm her down. As a result, Thomas was only allowed to be alone with her when they were positive she was heavily sedated, and any other time, one or both of them had to be around, lest she woke up, got scared, and harmed herself or someone else while her mind was still not clear.

    “Are you okay?”

    Kate has to ask, still, have to make sure but Yelena’s smile is easy, easing her worries even before she answers.

    “Yes. She is fully lucid.”

    Nodding, Kate looks Yelena over once more, this time less to check for injuries and more just to take her in. Yelena doesn’t step aside right away, to let her inside, and her eyes glance both ways down the hallway before she speaks, the beautiful smile on her face slowly fading away.

    “Okay, before I let you in…Do not make any sudden movements. I know you will not do it on purpose but do not threaten or scare her.-”

    Blinking, Kate nods, trying to convey her seriousness.

    “Of course. I wouldn’t.“ Yelena holds her eyes, while she nods, continuing without addressing Kate’s response. “Do not ask her about her experience. About what it is like to come out of it. And what it’s like to be mind controlled. Do not…It is best if you don’t ask her how she is. Do not ask for details about her working for her handler. And-“ Eyebrows furrowing, Kate is confused, asking before Yelena can go on.

    “If I can’t ask her anything, why did you ask me to come?”

    Yelena sighs, but she doesn’t look annoyed. More than anything, she looks a bit vary. Leaning to the side, against the doorframe, Yelena crosses her arms and is silent for a moment before she answers.

    “She says she needs to talk to you.”

    Lifting her chin, Kate looks back at her for a long moment before she nods. “Okay. I won’t ask her anything…triggering.”

    Yelena nods again, turning her head slightly back to glance behind herself, into the apartment. After she turns back around, she rolls her lips together, her voice dropping even lower as she speaks again.

    “Keep in mind that you were her target, as far as we know. So, you cannot be alone with her, and if something happens, you have to do what I say and leave, okay?”

    This surprises Kate, and she glances over Yelena’s head, into the apartment too, before her eyes return to Yelena’s green ones.

    “But, if she is freed, shouldn’t that…She is not going to want to kill me still, right?” Yelena purses her lips, her eyes straying to check left and right on the hallway again. They return to Kate’s a moment later, her face thoughtful.

    “I do not think so. The Widows we have freed…Once the mind control is gone, so are the orders. But she is having a harder time than most, we do not know why. So…just in case.” Kate nods but doesn’t say the words. There is no way in hell she’s leaving Yelena alone with a Widow if she is dangerous, but she also doesn’t want to make a promise she will not keep. Yelena looks at her expectantly, and Kate sighs, shifting her weight from one leg to the other. “If she gets…violent, I won’t leave you with her. I’m not promising that.” Pressing her lips together, Yelena’s eyes narrow ever so slightly. Her gaze drops to Kate’s chest for a fraction of a moment, despite the two almost black bruises caused by Maxine’s bullets being hidden by Kate’s hoodie and jacket. Her eyes are hard when they meet Kate’s again a moment later, and she looks very serious as she shakes her head. “If you do not promise it, I am not letting you in.”

    A frustrated huff leaves Kate’s lips and she shifts her weight around again, stuffing her hands into the pockets of her bomber jacket.

    “Listen, it will be fine. And I’m sure the two of us can take her. She is injured and-“ Mimicking her huff, Yelena unwinds her crossed arms and steps outside of the apartment, pulling the door closed behind herself, maybe to hammer home the point that she is not letting Kate in if she will not make that promise.

    “Kate, I am serious. I have no problem restraining her alone, but I can not do it if you are there getting in my way.”

    Eyebrows furrowing again, Kate feels her slight frustration begin to turn into genuine annoyance at Yelena’s dig at her capabilities.

    “I won’t get in your way. I will help. If you have no problem restraining her alone, me helping out-“ Her own annoyance is mirrored on Yelena’s face, her green eyes almost cutting as she interrupts Kate, her hands coming to rest on her hips.

    “The last time she saw you, she practically killed you. So do not tell me-“ Taking a step closer, it’s Kate’s turn to cut her off.

    “Hey, no. She did not practically kill me. I fell out of the window but I caught myself.” Yelena rolls her eyes so hard, that Kate almost physically recoils at the amount of offense in that single gesture, but Yelena’s eyes pull her in when their gazes meet again and she remains rooted to the spot.

    “If I wasn’t distracting her, she could have easily cut your wire. She shot you, twice. She nearly strangled you.”

    The heated energy between them is close to boiling over, only slightly different than in the last few days but not less searing.

    “And, she is badly injured, she has been sedated for days, and I have you.-” Yelena, who was on the verge of cutting Kate off again, snaps her mouth with an almost audible clack. She looks back at Kate, still visibly uncomfortable with the idea but Kate’s words seem to make her swallow what she was going to say.

    With a movement that sends Kate’s own heart racing, she steps closer, trying to hold Yelena’s eyes as she finishes, her voice losing some of its edge.

    “I know you won’t let anything happen to me.”

    Pursing her lips, Yelena looks up at her, and Kate almost gets distracted by the flecks of gold in her green eyes before they are torn from her as Yelena rolls her eyes again, but for some reason, the gesture feels a lot less offensive this time around.

    “Sweet talking me will not get you your way.”

    Yelena’s hands leave her hips as she crosses her arms again, but she doesn’t step away as Kate leans closer.

    “That’s not what I’m doing. I am just saying, I trust you to keep me safe, and if things go to shit, I can help you.”

    Judging by Yelena’s face, she is almost as surprised as Kate, when she huffs a moment later, her head dropping backward to stare at the ceiling.

    “You are impossible.”

    A smile begins to take over Kate’s face, but as Yelena lowers her head to pin her with another look, she quickly tamps down on it, attempting to look serious.

    “I promise I will do everything you tell me to…aside from leaving.”

    With a deep sigh, Yelena runs her tongue over her teeth behind her lips, before her arms drop and she steps back, turning the handle to open the door again. She doesn’t verbally acknowledge the fact that Kate has managed to argue her way into the apartment without making a promise, but Kate lets a slightly smug smile take over her face as she follows Yelena into the apartment, pulling off her beanie.

    Within a few seconds of entering the apartment, Kate’s levity begins to fade away. It’s quiet. Not too quiet, the sounds of traffic and the city still filtering through but she still feels a certain weight settle onto her shoulders, a wired anticipation building. Yelena enters the living room first and Kate follows her, muscles taunt, unsure what to expect.

    The curtains are drawn, and the overhead lights are turned off, only a few lamps filling the space with warm, but dim light. Once inside the room, Kate hears the gentle pitter-patter of rain against the windows too, but nothing else.

    Yelena rounds the couch, her movements measured and she looks at Kate as she does the same a few seconds later.

    Maxine lies on the couch, her leg elevated with a pillow most likely, her whole body covered with a blanket. It’s only her face and one arm that are over the soft blanket, her skin pale despite the warm light a lamp on a nearby table casts on it.

    Kate almost jolts when she sees her dark eyes are open, staring at her without blinking. For a long moment, none of them speak, and Kate can almost feel Yelena becoming more and more tense to her left as the silence stretches on.

    “Kate Bishop.”

    Kate does jolt, when Maxine suddenly speaks, her lips seemingly moving as little as possible and her voice soft. She is staring, still, and her accent is heavy, yet there is some familiarity in it that sends just a twinge of warmth inside Kate’s chest.

    Not wanting to look away, Kate answers while looking back at Maxine, her words hesitant despite the lightness she forces over her voice.

    “Maxine, hi.”

    Another long moment of silence follows, and Kate swears she doesn’t see Maxine blink once. Giving into the urge to seek comfort, Kate glances at Yelena, who almost looks like a cat ready to pounce. The moment feels like a powder keg, the few seconds before lightning is about to strike.

    As she turns back to Maxine, Kate considers slowly backing away. Just because a tiger is injured, it’s no less dangerous to enter a cage with one…

    But suddenly, the memory of Maxine’s frantic eyes, her cries of pain, and her small weight in Kate’s arms come back to her. She might be dangerous, but she is just like Yelena and Sonya. There is a person in there and the right thing to do here is to try to shake the heaviness off and treat her like one.

    With that resolve, Kate exhales, trying to ease out of the tight, suddenly adrenaline-fueled state she has found herself in. Mimicking what she has seen Yelena do a few times, Kate purposefully loosens her muscles, taking a seat across from Maxine on the other couch. “Yelena said you wanted to talk to me.”

    Maxine finally blinks, and Kate thinks she sees her gulp before she sighs. “Yes. I need to talk to you. But first…”

    Maxine moves and the way she does it is all the proof Kate needs that Yelena may have over- sold the dangerous aspects of the situation. With a wince, Maxine sits a bit further up, dragging herself along the couch to be half upright.

    “I have to apologize.”

    Blinking, Kate tries to not let her surprise show as she shakes her head. “There is no need. I’m fine, we are all…well, we are all mostly fine. And I’m sorry about your leg too.”

    If Maxine is bothered by Kate’s somewhat rambling answer or her obvious awkwardness in this situation, she doesn’t let it show.

    “There is no need to apologize. You were only protecting yourself.”

    Trying to lighten the heaviness of the moment, Kate smiles, glancing over at Yelena who finally seems to ease up too, taking a seat next to her. Turning back to Maxine, Kate notes that she is staring again, her face serious.

    “Well, in that case, you were just…following orders.“ Maxine nods, her eyes jumping at Yelena too before they settle back on Kate. “I was told you protected me while I was incapacitated and carried me out of the building. I owe you my life.”

    The whole sentence, actually, anything that comes out of Maxine’s mouth is said strangely without any emotion, but there is a glint of sincerity in her eyes. Shaking her head again, Kate’s smile widens.

    “It’s really not…I mean, you don’t owe me anything. Anyone would have done the same.” Blinking once, slowly, Maxine shakes her head while maintaining eye contact. “I disagree.”

    Huffing in amusement, Kate shrugs.

    “Well, we’ll agree to disagree then.”

    When Maxine doesn’t answer, Kate glances at Yelena again, whose eyebrows are slightly furrowed. There are a few seconds when neither Widow speaks so Kate turns back to Maxine.

    “Is that why you wanted to talk to me? To…apologize and say thank you?” “No. I have information you will want to know.”

    Interest piqued, Kate leans forward, her elbows coming to rest on her knees. “Okay, I’m listening.”

    Maxine’s eyes jump around the room for a second, before they settle on Kate again. “A few weeks ago, my handler received an encrypted message. It was a bounty notice to kill you, for 10 million dollars.”

    Kate nods, trying not to get bogged down by the number. 10 million?

    “Yes. I received the same one.”

    Turning to her left, Kate blinks at Yelena, surprised. Yelena refused 10 million when she could have easily…it shouldn’t be touching, but it kind of is. Kate really owes her. “He did not take it either.”

    That surprises Kate, drawing her eyes back to Maxine.

    “He didn’t?”

    “No. But he went to see Vanessa Fisk. They have a relationship or know each other, he assumed it came from her.”

    Leaning forward, Kate feels a thousand thoughts begin to race in her head. They assumed that Fisk’s wife knew about his criminal dealings, but they didn’t know if she was actively involved in them.

    “Did it?”

    Yelena asks for her, but Maxine is quick to shake her head.

    “I do not know. I was not present for the conversation.”

    Nodding, Kate exhales, trying to keep her overactive mind focused on Maxine’s words. “When he came back, he had a different assignment for me instead.”

    At that, Kate’s brow further furrows in confusion. Before she has to ask her to elaborate, Maxine continues.

    “My orders were to go to Limitless Ltd’s headquarters and guard a room, 12 hours a day. I was to leave my post only if I received an order specifically to do so, which I only did three times. I also received a button, that I had to push to send a signal in case you showed up, to alert reinforcements.”

    That at least explains how so many soldiers arrived so quickly after they were discovered. “What was in the room?”

    “Why were you ordered to leave?”

    Yelena and Kate ask their questions at the same time, glancing at each other. Kate gestures at Yelena, before turning back to Maxine.

    “Answer hers first. Why were you ordered to leave?”

    “The first time they had a sighting of you breaking into a ship in the harbor, but you were gone by the time I arrived. The second time was when I jumped into your car and stabbed your shoulder…I am sorry about that also. And the final time was when you freed me.” Kate shakes her head, throwing a distracted smile at Maxine.

    “Yeah, it’s okay. So…Um, and sorry for throwing you out of the car too. So, did they ask you to leave any other time?”

    Shaking her head, Maxine’s eyebrows furrow.

    “No. But after one shift, I was asked to follow and guard a car.”

    Glancing at Yelena, Kate’s interest is thoroughly piqued. Maybe a sighting of Fisk finally? Leaning forward and putting her elbows onto her knees, she meets Maxine’s eyes. “Who was in the car? And where did it go?”

    Shifting around a little, Maxine winces again as she answers.

    “A boy. It went from an address on the Northern-East side of Central Park to Trinity School. His usual bodyguard was out for a day, which is why I was pulled in. I had to wait outside, escort him back, and then go back to Limitless for my next shift.”

    A boy…It couldn’t be…

    “Do you know who the boy was?”

    Meeting Yelena’s eyes, it’s obvious that she is thinking the same thing. Fisk might have a kid. “No. I was not told, and I have not seen him any other time.”

    “Okay.”

    Yelena nods to herself, glancing at Kate who is also processing the information. Wetting her lips, she takes a deep breath.

    “Okay, back to the first thing. What’s in the room?”

    Maxine looks at Kate as she answers her question, recalling everything in a serious and factual tone.

    “It was an office. A desk, a chair, a desk computer, I only ever saw it from the outside. Only one man came to work in it every day, and I was told to make sure that he does not take anything in or out of the room. I do not know what he did on the computer, or why it is so important, but they take its security very seriously. When you came to Limitless Ltd., they told me that making sure you did not get in and leading you away was even more important than killing you.”

    Immediately, Kate’s mind begins to race with possibilities, as Maxine explains further. “It has a reinforced steel door, a bulletproof window, cameras right outside, and the lock is biometric. Only one entrance. I only saw the man who goes inside unlock it, but I am sure Vanessa Fisk has clearance too. We changed shifts on the spot, right in front of the door, so it is never left unguarded.”

    Next to Kate, Yelena asks Maxine, her position becoming more and more comfortable as she crosses her legs, leaning back against the couch. Meanwhile, Kate thinks about what the room could be.

    “Who guarded the room when it was not you?”

    Turning back to Maxine, Kate sees her eyebrows furrow, obviously trying to recall anything that can be useful.

    “I do not know. He always wore a mask and a black leather suit. He is tall, but not very big.” Nodding to herself, Kate pushes the information to the back of her mind to be dealt with later. Instead, she tries to focus on the room. If they had a Black Widow guard it, it must be something important. And for it to be so close to the server room, with no cell phone or anything allowed inside…

    “Do you know anything about the computer? Like, did it have wires going into it, from the server room?”

    Shaking her head, Maxine almost looks apologetic.

    “I do not know, sorry. I never went inside the room. Only the man who worked there did.” Nodding, Kate takes note of what she heard and tries to figure out how they could find out if the room is what she thinks it is.

    “What about him? What do you know about him?”

    At Yelena’s question, Kate looks back at Maxine, unconsciously having zoned out while she was thinking.

    “Only what he looks like. He is around 35 years old, maybe 40. Small, thin. He has thick glasses and almost always wears a sweater, a shirt, and his pants are too big. He always has a shaved face, and his hair is brown, greying, and cut short. He has a wedding ring.” “Do you know his name?”

    At Yelena’s question, Maxine shakes her head again.

    “No.”

    “Do you think you can ID him?”

    This time, Maxine nods, eyes shifting over to Kate.

    “From a picture, yes.”

    Yelena nods, glancing over at Kate. They will have to look over Limitless’ employee database. For a few seconds, neither of them speaks. Kate feels Maxine’s eyes on her face, and she does her best to not fidget, a bit unnerved by her unrelenting stare. The silence is broken by Yelena, sighing deeply before she speaks.

    “Do you know anything else that can help us?”

    Maxine is quiet for a moment, obviously thinking. As Kate looks at her, her eyes fixated on the blanket ahead of her, she looks unbelievably young, possibly still in her teens. It feels almost impossible to imagine that she was the one who nearly killed Kate, despite her cocky words to Yelena, and who did kill all those people that Kate has looked at, in the files that Sonya and Yelena showed her.

    “I do not know.”

    After a second, Maxine continues.

    “I do not know what can help you because I do not know, why you were there, or what you are looking for. I only knew that you would want to know about the room because they so badly wanted to keep you out of it. And I know that you are an Avenger.” She says the words to Kate, and despite the circumstances, Kate feels a bit of a thrill at being considered one, even if it’s by enemies, and even if it’s not true. Glancing at Yelena, she sees her roll her eyes, possibly seeing the flicker of delight on Kate’s face. After a good-natured eyeroll back at Yelena, Kate clarifies.

    “I’m not. Not really, anyway. I am trying to…”

    Kate hesitates, not sure how much to tell Maxine, unsure if they should treat her as a part of their gang or not. Glancing at Yelena, she nods, slowly, and Kate wets her lips before she continues.

    “Without going too much into detail. Um, okay, so Limitless has the formula of a temporary super-solider serum on their servers. It’s hidden and encrypted, and as far as we know, they haven’t found a way to access it yet. We are trying to take it, and delete the database before they do.”

    Maxine looks back at Kate before her eyes slide over to Yelena, again, with a disturbing lack of blinking. Slowly she repeats Kate’s words, sounding quizzical.

    “Temporary…super soldier serum?”

    Yelena answers in Russian and the lines on Maxine’s face ease out.

    “Ah…How do they have it but can not access it?”

    Wetting her lips, Kate sighs deeply, gearing up to explain but Yelena takes over, switching to Russian. Kate tries to pay attention, hoping to catch words she knows from Duolingo, but the conversation is too fast.

    After a few sentences exchanged, Maxine turns to her, asking her something in Russian too. “Sorry, I don’t speak Russian.”

    Maxine’s eyes jump back to Yelena for a moment, who translates.

    “She asked you what you are going to do with the formula.”

    Sighing deeply, Kate smiles, although even she can tell it must look more bitter than happy. “That’s the million-dollar question, isn’t it…”

    Confusion spreads over Maxine’s features and her eyes jump back to Yelena, who is looking at Kate too. Softly, she smiles before she looks over to Maxine.

    “It is an American expression. It means it is a hard question.”

    Kate nods in the affirmative, rolling her lips together. She doesn’t particularly want to get into the moral dilemma she is facing. For sure, she will not give it to Rojas, but that’s a problem to deal with later. The thought of simply destroying it has passed through her mind. Most likely, she will give it to her mother, but not directly.

    “I will figure it out once we have the data.”

    At Kate’s answer, Maxine nods. For a moment, she is quiet before her eyes slide back to Kate.

    “Do you want to use it? To become a…super soldier?”

    Kate wishes the answer was a firm and resounding no, but she would be lying if she said that thought hasn’t crossed her mind too, even if only as a few stray fantasies while she waited for sleep to come.

    It would make everything a lot easier, for sure. She is well trained, better than most people in all of humanity, but looking back on the last few weeks, it’s impossible to not think about how much easier things would have been if she had some type of competitive advantage. She could protect her mom, Clint, Yelena, Sonya…All the potential Wendys and Annies out there…

    But despite all that, Kate shakes her head.

    “No. I don’t know. It’s not why I have to find it.”

    Next to her, Yelena exhales and Kate looks at her to see her eyebrows unfurrow before she speaks.

    “We do not know if it works or if it is safe. We just have to find it.” She doesn’t look back at Kate, and Maxine hums from the other couch across from them. “Zimniy Soldat.”

    Yelena nodded sagely, repeating the words, both of their words sounding somewhat dire, although that might only be the Russian.

    “Zimniy Soldat…I Krasnyy Strazh.”

    Looking between the two of them, Kate catches Yelena’s eyes, hoping for an explanation. When Yelena doesn’t offer one on her own, only a slight smile, Kate rolls her eyes, asking her verbally.

    “What does that mean?”

    Leaning back further again Yelena purses her lips, seemingly thoughtful before she explains. “After your Captain America, the Soviet Union worked hard to replicate the super soldier serum for their own use. There have been many attempts, and most of them ended badly. They worked with the Winter Soldier, and created other super soldiers that were as strong or stronger than him, but many died during the experiments and the results were…unstable. The only one they actually managed to succeed with, who did not become unstable was the Red Guardian.”

    The word is familiar in Kate’s mind but it takes her a second to place where she heard it. She doesn’t know if Yelena wants Maxine to know her relation to the super soldier, so she glances at Maxine, before looking back at her. Yelena nods, holding Kate’s eyes, neither of them having to voice it.

    “How come he was the only one?”

    Yelena crosses her legs, and Kate sees a fond smile start to slide over her face before it’s mercilessly wiped off of it.

    “The people I have talked to, that know about how it came to be,-”

    If Kate didn’t know Yelena was talking about her own parents, she would never be able to guess.

    “They said the serum doesn’t work the same on everyone. They think it depends on the soul of the subject, but I am not sure I buy it.”

    Kate nods, thinking it over. Everyone knew the story of Steve Rogers, but the inventor of the serum was killed and the vials were destroyed before he could have more soldiers. Growing up, in school, they said that Steve was chosen for his personality, his nobleness, so Kate is more inclined to believe it than maybe Yelena is.

    “Have they tried since? The…Soviet Union, I mean?”

    This time, Yelena does smile, but it’s teasing instead of fond so Kate quickly corrects herself. “I know the Soviet Union doesn’t exist anymore.”

    Yelena’s eyes glint in amusement for a second before she sighs, glancing at Maxine. “No…not really.”

    An eyebrow lifting, Kate looks back at her, leaning back against the couch again and putting her left arm up on the back, no longer wincing in pain but still sore.

    “What does that mean?”

    Sighing deeply, Yelena glances at Maxine and rolls her lips together. For some reason, she is reluctant to share but after a second she rolls her eyes, as if Kate is forcing her to answer. “In the Red Room, they created a knock-off, watered-down version of it that every Widow received.-“ Eyes widening, Kate leans back. Black Widows are super soldiers?! Yelena is a super so- “-It does not give you super strength or any of it. It just allows you to heal a bit faster. Makes you immune to most diseases... Dreykov would not allow us to be out of commission for too long.”

    The last bit of the sentence is said with a certain bitterness, Yelena pursing her lips in distaste. Mind slowing down somewhat, Kate nods, eyes still glued to Yelena. She looks back at Kate, lifting her chin a little, and the two of them are silent for a moment. That…explains some things.

    “I have not…I have never…”

    At Maxine’s quiet words, Yelena’s eyes are ripped from Kate, her eyebrows furrowing. “What?”

    Turning to Maxine too, Kate watches as her face is twisted in confusion, as she shakes her head.

    “I have not received that.”

    As she glances at her, Kate can see that Yelena is confused and almost bothered by the revelation. She is quiet for a moment, before rolling her lips together. “After your graduation ceremony…”

    Again, Maxine shakes her head and this time, Yelena’s mouth drops open, shock clearly written on her face.

    “No ceremony.”

    Carefully, Kate tries to interject, to try and get an understanding of the situation. “What ceremony?”

    Her question is ignored as Yelena stares at Maxine, eyes wide. What ceremony? What are they talking about?

    After a few more seconds, Yelena asks something in Russian, that Maxine answers and Kate watches, completely lost as Yelena jumps to her feet, visibly upset. She spews out a sentence, most of which Kate recognizes as swear words, but her anger doesn’t seem to be directed at Maxine.

    Yelena rubs her forehead and walks around the couch, her eyes looking at nothing particular but filled with a dark, angry fire.

    “Yelena, what’s going on?”

    She looks at Kate, for barely a second before her eyes are back on Maxine, but before she can get too annoyed, Yelena puts a hand on her shoulder while she stands next to her. Kate is unsure what the gesture means, if it’s meant to tell her to be patient, or to seek comfort, but it is enough for her to snap her mouth shut.

    Yelena asks something again in Russian, but this time as Maxine answers, Kate’s Duolingo lessons finally pay off, as she understands the answer.

    “Trinadtsat'.”

    Thirteen.

    Of course, without context, Kate has no idea what is or was thirteen.

    On her shoulder, Yelena’s hand tightens for a moment, seemingly without meaning to and Kate looks up at her to see a mixture of anger and sadness on her face. Was Maxine thirteen when something happened? Did something happen to her thirteen times? Does she have thirteen somethings? Based on her limited information, Kate is unable to tell. The emotion is only visible on Yelena’s face for a few moments before she schools her features into a neutral mask. They exchange a few sentences in Russian, while Yelena’s hand remains on her shoulder and Kate does not interrupt the conversation, hoping Yelena will fill her in later.

    After a minute or two, Yelena walks back around the couch, letting go of Kate and reclaiming her seat next to her. The conversation switches back to English, but Kate can tell they are nearing the end of it, as Maxine’s exhaustion becomes more and more noticeable with each word exchanged.

    They don’t learn anything more about the room, other than that Maxine can point it out on a blueprint, and she doesn’t know more about the man who works there either, or Fisk, or even his wife. Still, what they have learned makes Kate’s head buzz with possibilities and as Yelena walks her out 15 minutes later, she knows they will be talking about it for days. Maxine is basically asleep by the time she leaves, so Kate feels obliged to keep her voice down, as she turns around to say her goodbyes to Yelena at the doorway. “I told you it would be fine.”

    Kate says it with a smile, hoping to see it reflected on Yelena’s serious face. Her lips twitch upwards, but she rolls her eyes a little, using her hand to flick a strand of hair out of her eyes before she gives Kate a glare.

    “It could have gone another way.”

    Not seeing a point in worrying about that, Kate kind of shrugs, trying to say “it didn’t though”, stuffing her hands in the pockets of her jacket.

    “Do you want to tell me what you two talked about earlier? In Russian?” The hint of a smile fades from Yelena’s face, and she looks to the side before meeting Kate’s eyes again.

    “It is not for me to share. She will tell you if she wants.”

    Somewhat surprised, Kate shifts her weight.

    “But…Okay. Can you at least tell me what a ceremony is?”

    Yelena sighs, pursing her lips as she looks at Kate who hopes she didn’t overstep too badly. After a few moments of consideration, Yelena looks up and down the hallway, before she leans against the doorway, her eyes turning back to Kate.

    “When a girl reaches adulthood in the Red Room, she goes through something we call a graduation ceremony. She has to pass a series of trials to be a full-fledged Widow and if she succeeds, she is rewarded with a hysterectomy and put under mind control.” Kate’s chest pangs in horror and devastation, for Yelena, for Sonya, for Maxine, but she tries to not let it show. Yelena’s voice is nonchalant like it’s just a fact of life and Kate tries her best to not show her reaction too much, never knowing what words of comfort to offer in these situations. She doesn’t think she is successful as Yelena smiles slightly, but it’s not a happy kind of smile.

    “I’m sorry.”

    At Kate’s words, Yelena lifts her chin, her smile not dropping but a little bit of hardness entering her gaze.

    “It is the past.”

    Unable to hold her eyes, Kate looks down and away, nodding half to herself. “Right.”

    For a few moments, they are quiet and Kate considers just saying her goodbyes, unsure what to say about this heavy topic but suddenly a thought occurs in her head. “So, wait. If Maxine didn’t have a…a ceremony, how come she was under mind-control?” Yelena’s jaw twitches and Kate sees the mixture of anger and sadness from earlier resurface on her face, as her smile fades away.

    “She was put under before. Without the ceremony.”

    Kate nods, half to herself, thinking it over. Thirteen.

    She is pretty sure now what it means.

    Raising her eyes to meet Yelena’s again, Kate begins to understand the anger and sadness. They put a child under mind-control. The only comfort Kate finds is in Yelena’s words from weeks ago. “Dreykov is dead, I am not, and I am free to do what I want.” Resisting the urge to hug Yelena, Kate asks for confirmation instead.

    “They are dead?”

    A grim smile spreads onto Yelena’s face again.

    “All of them.”

    Maybe it’s not very hero-like of Kate to feel satisfaction at that but she is coming to learn that this hero business is a lot less black and white than she used to think. Eyes holding Yelena’s, Kate answers.

    “Good.”

    For a moment, they bask in the satisfaction of that knowledge. Kate glances at the apartment behind Yelena’s back before their eyes meet again.

    “What will happen to her now?”

    Crossing her arms, Yelena’s form loses some of its tension.

    “She will stay here while she heals up, and then she can go and do whatever she wants. I will offer for her to stay with my parents for a while, but it’s up to her to decide.” Nodding, Kate doesn’t take her eyes off of Yelena, the two of them letting silence fill the space between them for a few moments. With the danger of the situation not coming to fruition, Kate wants to linger, to spend as much time as possible just the two of them, a scarce commodity to come by since Clint arrived.

    It’s hard to tell if Yelena feels the same, but she too lingers, not shutting the door in Kate’s face or sending her away.

    “How is your…how are you?”

    Yelena’s whole face changes, not to something Kate would consider soft, but warm nonetheless. Her smile looks almost like she is entertained by a private joke that Kate is not privy to. Her voice is thick with warm delight when she answers, but despite her words, it doesn’t feel like she is having fun at Kate’s expense for once.

    “You have seen me a few hours ago.”

    Leaning her head down, Kate breaks eye contact for a second but she smiles too and looks back at Yelena a few moments later when she answers.

    “Yeah, but there wasn’t…we haven’t had the time to talk since…”

    Making a gesture with her hand, she tries to indicate the last few days. She doesn’t specifically mean that the last time the two of them were alone, Kate almost kissed her and she is pretty sure that Yelena would have let her but that is a fact that weighs heavily on her consciousness, as Yelena holds her eyes and her smile widens ever so slightly. “I am good, Kate. Thank you.”

    Unconciously, Kate sways closer but doesn’t actually step in, just tilts back and forth on the balls of her feet.

    “Yeah, that’s…good. I’m glad. I’m good too.”

    There is warm amusement in Yelena’s eyes and one of her hands shifts to her hips, her thumb resting on the front of her waist, looking Kate up and down. Kate does the same, wetting her lips and raking her mind to say something that could stretch these few precious minutes together and alone just a little bit longer.

    “Goodnight, Kate Bishop.”

    Not once looking away from Yelena, Kate inhales and exhales once, slowly, but doesn’t do anything with the wired energy buzzing in her muscles that begs her to do something. “Yeah, I better…Goodnight.”

    Kate walks backward a few steps, not really wanting to leave, and holding Yelena’s eyes, who is still leaning against the doorway.

    “Goodnight.”

    Kate says it again before she reaches the elevator and presses the button, and Yelena finally leans off of the doorway. She does not answer verbally, but her eyes sparkle before she turns away and shuts Sonya’s door, leaving Kate finally alone in the hallway. There is a swirling sensation in Kate’s stomach, her attraction to Yelena making her feel warm and a bit giddy, and she smiles to herself one last time as the door to the elevator opens, and she thoughtlessly presses the button to her own floor. It doesn’t fade from her face for a long time.

    She is still in a good mood when she gets home and she can feel Clint’s eyes on her throughout the evening when she retells the events of the last few hours to him (the Maxine part at least) over a plate of re-heated pizza, but he doesn’t comment and she doesn’t care if he notices.

    Later at night, when she is in bed, Kate finally pulls out her phone and looks at the pictures Yelena sent over, and more importantly, at her Instagram. Unsurprisingly, it does not have a lot of content, mostly pictures of nondescript locations, food, and a few photos of her dog. There are only two pictures of Yelena, one for her profile picture, and one as a post. It’s fairly recent, posted at the beginning of this summer, and it’s of her at a table with a drink, smiling fondly at the photographer. Kate wonders who took it, but she thinks she would know by now if Yelena had someone special in her life…right?

    Although, it would explain her hesitance when they almost kissed during the game night… But no, she would know. Then again, she does know very little about Yelena’s life in Ohio. But, if she had someone, why would her parents nag her about dating? Maybe they don’t like the person…But if she had someone, surely, she would have not entered into this fake relationship with Kate…unless she and her significant other are at a level, where they are comfortable enough that they trust Yelena with this. It’s not like it involves anything physical anyway…yet.

    Kate quickly shuts down that traitorous thought before it goes too far. She goes back and forth, but ultimately, she leans towards Yelena not being in a relationship, because Kate would know by now, surely. It also doesn’t really matter. Shaking the thought off, she goes back to her phone, having zoned out for a few seconds, staring blankly at the wall across from her.

    After looking at the picture for an embarrassingly long time, Kate screenshots it, and adds it as a contact picture for Yelena on her phone, reasoning that if it ever gets seized by the FBI or someone, it would be weird if she didn’t have one for her supposed fiancé. That is of course ignoring the fact that if her phone ever got seized, she would have a lot more serious things to worry about, but whatever. A small effort is better than nothing.

    She spends a few minutes tweaking the lighting and the colors of her photo with Yelena that she chose from the bunch, before bringing up Instagram again to post it. The whole ordeal twists her stomach into a knot, for multiple reasons, none of which she feels like examining right now. It’s late enough, that not a lot of people will see but, as Kate hits the post button, she still feels like getting up and running a lap around the block to get rid of her excess energy, only Lucky’s quiet snores helping her stay grounded.

    Despite her excitement and nervousness, Kate sleeps remarkably well after that. If she dreams that night, she can’t remember it, and she wakes up feeling better than she has in days, hugging a small, warm body to her chest. Upon waking up, it takes her a few seconds to realize that the golden hair she took note of in her half-awake state does in fact belong to Lucky’s butt, but she doesn’t let that small disappointment ruin her day. When Yelena and Sonya come over, Kate tries to catch her eyes, and maybe relive to moment from the day before a little, but Yelena walks in and apart from greeting her reasonably politely, she doesn’t give Kate much attention. Kate does her best to remind herself that they are adults, and for all intents and purposes, this is a workplace, but she still pouts a little into her cup of coffee, before they begin working for the day.

    Yelena and Sonya don’t have a lot of updates to share since yesterday evening, but Maxine pointed the newly discovered room out to them on a blueprint of the level, and they do the same for Clint and Kate, while Lucky stares at Kate, trying to telepathically convince her that she wants to share the home-made bearclaw that Sonya brought upstairs for them. It’s still warm and remarkably good, the texture perfectly soft without being soggy, and it takes away the burnt of Yelena not paying much attention to her. It also distracts Kate a bit, so by the time she is finished, the others are already discussing what they learned from Maxine.

    When the conversation turns to what the room could be used for and why it’s so important to Fisk (or his wife…That’s a question they will have to circle back to,) Kate clears her throat and leans forward, looking at each person around the coffee table to see if she has their attention.

    “I think I know what it is.”

    Pointing at the server room, Kate traces the way to the secret room in question with her finger.

    “Okay, so we know Fisk is looking for the formula within the database, right? And I didn’t think about it beforehand, but it actually would be pretty weird to do so on the user console within the server room. It’s hard to use, it’s out in the open, it’s super inconvenient.” If either of her teammates is confused, they don’t let it know, only nodding at her to continue as she looks up to check if they are still following.

    “So, my theory is that it’s a computer attached to servers, where this dude comes in and looks for the hidden data every day. I am pretty sure it’s purposefully offline, which is why he is not allowed to take his cell phone in.”

    Understanding downs on Yelena’s and Sonya’s faces, while Clint’s eyebrows furrow, his eyes looking the blueprint over. Pursing her lips, Yelena nods, seemingly thoughtful while Sonya sighs, running a hand through her damp hair.

    “If you are right…Does that actually help us? I mean, she says the room is basically a vault and he must know that we have her, so it’s probably going to be even more heavily guarded.” At Sonya’s question, Kate kind of shrugs, before looking back at the blueprint. “I don’t know. It’s a lot less exposed than the server room, but also pretty hard to get into. And all we really need, since we already installed our program, is to attach the drive somewhere within the system, and download the data.”

    Sonya pulls her lips to the side, before looking down at the blueprint too, all four of them trying to find something they missed before.

    “Is this a window?”

    Clint points at a mark on the blueprint, and Kate nods, her eyes seeking it out too. “Yeah. But Maxine says it’s bulletproof and inches thick so I don’t know if we can do much with it.”

    Clint hums, his eyes not leaving the plans.

    “That might be something…But we have to check it out in person.”

    Glancing up at him, Kate waits for him to elaborate but Yelena is less patient, it seems, asking before Clint can elaborate.

    “What are you thinking?”

    She turns to him, the two of them next to each other in the armchairs across from the couch Sonya and Kate are sitting on. He looks the plans over, briefly turning to look at the map of the surrounding area too before he explains.

    “She said whoever guards the room, never really goes inside, right? So as long as we do it after office hours, the room should be empty.”

    He starts counting on his fingers as he goes over the details.

    “The cameras are outside the door, and the biggest hurdle would be to get through the reinforced steel doors… Even with explosives, that would be tricky, especially if we try to do it without it becoming an all-out war.”

    Clint is not saying anything they don’t know, and Kate sighs, mentally urging him to get to the point. Not that she has anywhere to be. Periodically, she looks at Yelena but she is preoccupied by Clint, not paying her any attention. For some reason, she has a Capri-Sun juice pouch and keeps playing with the straw which is more distracting than Kate could ever say. Her lips wrap around the straw, soft and-

    “So, that leaves the window as our best point of entry. We have to check it out, but I think I can get us gear that can take us through bulletproof glass if that’s all it is. We get in, get the data, and leave. They won’t know we were in there until the next day when the guy comes in to do his job.”

    It sounds vague and unbaked, but Kate agrees, it’s something. Which is more than what they had in days. It seems Sonya agrees as well, as she leans over the map too, pointing at the building Limitless is in, and a few others close to it. Yelena’s tongue sneaks out to pull the straw into her mouth again, and Kate exhales, once, slowly, telling herself to get a fucking grip as she looks down at the map too, to see what Sonya shows them.

    “These two are tall enough, that we can use them to zipline over... The easiest way would be to lower ourselves from the roof of Limitless’ building, but I think after our last visit, they are probably keeping an eye on that.”

    As Sonya explains, Yelena, who is still drinking from and playing with the straw, glances at Kate and catches her staring. She doesn’t look away, catching her gaze while Clint answers Sonya’s observation.

    “If they have guards on the roof, ziplining is not really ideal either. You would get shot before you get in.”

    At his words, Yelena drops Kate’s eyes to nod too, and she smiles to herself as Sonya answers him.

    “We have to scope it out in person. We won’t know until we see it.”

    They all nod, and Clint’s eyes finally raise from the blueprints to look at her briefly, and Kate does her best to look engaged and innocent, and his eyebrows lift ever-so-slightly before his eyes turn to Yelena.

    “Can you leave Maxine here alone?”

    The Widows exchange a look, before Yelena turns back to Clint, nodding. She puts down the juice pouch, finally ending her torment. She glances at Kate and her lips twitch upward when she sees her looking again, but it drops in less than a second as she answers Clint’s question. “Not for too long, but yes.”

    Clint nods back, eyes glancing around all of them as he speaks. He seems to be thinking, eye glancing between Kate and Yelena twice, before she nods to herself.

    “Okay, how about Kate and I go and get that glass-cutting tool I have in mind, and you and Sonya scope out the building, take a few photos, and get a sense of security?” They all nod, and Kate has to shake off the somewhat childish disappointment at not being paired with Yelena for the day.

    “We will check the address too, that Maxine mentioned she picked up the boy from. If he really is Fisk’s son, there is a good chance he lives there too or somewhere close by.” At that, Clint looks visibly conflicted, but he nods a second later. Kate wants to argue that she might be more useful there, but admittedly, it’s not the best time, when Clint and Yelena definitely noticed her distraction, which means Sonya almost definitely did too. The Widows leave, Yelena not sparing Kate more than a quick goodbye again, which Kate grinds her teeth at but tries not to get annoyed by and they don’t see each other for the rest of the day.

    Kate accompanies Clint to go to an archery store to buy a bunch of reinforced arrows first, while they wait for his contact to respond, not even annoyed by the fact that he gets noticed and she does not, despite literally winning all the archery competitions this country has to offer.

    In all honestly, she is a bit irked at him, for dragging her along on this glorified errand when she could be of more help to Sonya and Yelena possibly, especially since it’s him treating her like a kid again… But, bringing it up will only reinforce whatever weird convictions he has drawn, so she doesn’t.

    This, however, means most of Kate’s communication during the rest of the morning is that she either makes snarky comments at him, or stays quiet, which is probably not the most mature way to deal with her frustration, but it’s what she has for now. They go and meet a contact of Clint’s after, an older man who is definitely too jumpy to be a legitimate businessman, but he supplies them with a laser cutter, that can apparently cut through bulletproof glass up to 5 inches of thickness, so Kate doesn’t stop to question his credentials, even to Clint.

    The rest of their day is spent at home, the two of them working in Kate’s workshop to develop an arrow design that can utilize the laser cutter in some fashion. With the assessment, that the ziplining between buildings will be the most dangerous part of the plan if it goes anywhere, they both agree that it makes sense to cut a hole in the window first from afar first, thus minimizing the amount of time whoever goes over will be exposed to be spotted by security on the roof or in the building.

    Kate’s annoyance has faded by now, but Yelena and Sonya have not checked in yet, and as a result, her mind repeatedly strays to what they might be doing, and wondering if they will be back before the day’s end or not.

    “You are quiet.”

    Glancing up at Clint for a second, Kate raises an eyebrow, surprised that he complains about it when it’s usually the opposite.

    “I’m just trying to figure this out. If we make it so the glass falls inside the room, it risks triggering the glass breaking sensors, but if it falls outside and onto somebody, it could kill them.”

    Clint looks at her for a long moment, his eyebrow raised in an expression that clearly says he doesn’t believe Kate.

    “Right… We can just attach a cable to the end of the arrow. That way it falls outside but not on anybody.”

    That is a pretty straightforward and easy solution, that Kate could have easily come up with herself if she wasn’t so preoccupied with wondering why Yelena and Sonya haven’t been in contact yet. Trying to hide her distractedness, Kate nods.

    “Yeah, that’s what I was thinking too.”

    He looks amused but somewhat disapproving looking at Kate above his glasses, and Kate clears her throat, going back to her work. The new arrow design is a good distraction, Kate loves tasks like this, but still, she finds her eyes repeatedly stray to her phone, willing it to light up.

    It’s almost half past 9 when Kate’s phone starts to ring, the photo she put as Yelena’s contact picture taking over her screen. Almost literally throwing the wrench in her hand away, Kate ignores Clint’s disapproving grunt, reaching for the phone.

    “Hi. Did you get what you need?”
