    “We have checked out the address Maxine gave us first. The apartment is under Vanessa Fisk’s name and we found out the boy’s name from the school records. Officially, he is Richard Marianna, but we are pretty sure he is Wilson Fisk’s son.”

    “Were you able to confirm if he lives there too?”

    “No… Not yet. There is no official sign of him here, and the apartment is not easily watched.”

It’s 9:29 pm. Not that late, but still late enough that both Yelena and Sonya probably wish they were on their way home now, instead of going on a stakeout.

    “Hey, if you are tired, Clint and I can go. We’ve been cooped up all afternoon anyway.” Behind her, she hears Clint grunt in displeasure at her volunteering them both but she ignores him. We will not stay long anyway.”

    Humming, Kate nods to herself, using the arrowhead in her hand to mindlessly scratch the surface of one of her workbench.

    “Well, tell Sonya to drink responsibly and get you and my car back in one piece.” She doesn’t mean to make it sound like Yelena is hers to be brought back to in one place too, her stomach doing a backflip when she realizes what she said, but Yelena thankfully only chuckles again, before relaying her message. Distantly, Kate hears Sonya’s voice, unmistakably amused, but she can’t make out her words so she is thankful when Yelena repeats them.

    “She says that you still owe her a car, so she will do what she pleases with this one.” Kate laughs at that, drawing invisible shapes with the arrowhead.

    “Well, let’s just be happy it’s you with her and not Tommy. I would just tell her to keep the car otherwise.”

    Laughing too, Yelena parrots her message to Sonya, and Kate hears her chuckle too. After a moment she responds, and Yelena laughs again.

    “What did she say?”

    After a few moments, when Yelena doesn’t relay the words back, Kate has to ask but Yelena just huffs out another chuckle, her voice warm.

    “Nothing that you need to know.”

    “Come ooon. Tell me.”

    It’s easy to imagine Yelena grinning on the other end of the line, her face undoubtedly playful.

    “Nope. Goodnight. I will share if we find anything worth mentioning.”

    Huffing, Kate leans her head back, but the smile on her face is impossible to tamp down on, at Yelena’s clear delight.

    “Fine. Goodnight. See you tomorrow.”

    Kate hears one last sound of Yelena’s amusement, a little huff or hum before the line is disconnected and she sighs deeply before turning back around.

    “She says they found no trace of Fisk living with Vanessa and her son, but it’s likely he is there too. They are going to Limitless now.”

    When he doesn’t answer her for a few seconds, she glances up at Clint, finding him looking at her with a mixture of amusement and disapproval she is quickly growing familiar with. “Right.     “What, I was just making polite conversation.”

    Clint’s laugh is full of disbelief and he shakes his head a moment later. “Sorry, maybe I just couldn’t hear the polite conversation from all the flirting.” Shaking her head, Kate huffs but it kind of comes out amused, still under the effects of her phone call, while she does her best to re-focus on her task.

    “I was not flirting. I am not…doing anything.”

    Rolling his eyes, Clint’s brow furrows.

    “Yeah, other than pretending to date and be engaged to a woman you have a huge crush on that you don’t understand.”

    Pursing her lips in distaste at Clint’s assessment, that she doesn’t understand Yelena, Kate throws him a glare but doesn’t want to get pulled into a debate about that. “I don’t have a crush.”

    Exhaling forcefully, Kate swallows her initial, irritated response which is to ask him who the hell made him the authority on all Widows. He doesn’t know Yelena, not like Kate does, and it’s not…

    “I think…I think I know. We’ve been going about this the wrong way.”

    The only one with visible understanding on their face is Yelena, and her eyes widen. Quickly, Kate explains to Clint and Sonya.

    “We would still do Clint’s plan, but wouldn’t try to get the drive in. We would fire a USB arow in there that is a small, portable wifi hotspot, and get the computer online.     Finally, Clint and Sonya catch on as well, and while Clint’s looking focused, seemingly thinking it over, Yelena smiles.

    “How close are we talking?”

    Biting down on her lips, Kate tilts her head, looking back at Sonya before she pulls her phone out.

    “I don’t know. I have to look it up.”

    She quickly does, answering the question a few seconds later.

    “With the frequency we’d need, about 50 feet.”

    Her eyebrows furrow, gaze moving from her phone to the map of the buildings around the one Limitless is headquartered in. All of them are further than 50 feet away. She sighs, looking up at the others and saying her observation aloud.

    “Okay, so we’d still need to get into the building, but within like…2 or 3 floors? That’s better than nothing, right?”

    “That is better than nothing.”

    It seems everyone is just as hungry as her, the three of them putting work aside while they look at the menu. Kate sends her order in a few minutes, and she assumes they are on break until Sonya speaks up again, looking up from the tablet in her lap.

    “Ugh….they do not have anything booked for weeks. Fuck.”

    At that, Kate’s eyebrows furrow, as Sonya closes her eyes and exhales, visibly getting frustrated too.

    “That’s not possible.”

    After Jack’s phone call the other day, she looked up and sent him a few event halls to try in Manhatten, and they were all fully booked well into the next few months. Sonya opens her eyes and shrugs, passing Kate the tablet over the coffee table. “See for yourself.”

    Taking the tablet, Kate looks at the website, and it seems that Sonya is either right or they don’t maintain their availability on their website. Pulling her phone out, she copies over the contact number provided on the site and presses the green button to dial. “What are you doing?”

    Kate stands up, with the phone still in her head just as Sonya asks her. “Just checking. I might have an idea.”

    The phone rings three times before a woman picks up.

    “Hello, this is Julie Nichols for Venue 345, how may I help you?”

    Starting to walk up and down, Kate answers.

    “Hi, my name is Kate Derekson, and I’m calling to ask if you have any availabilities for the next few weeks?”

    On the couch, Yelena and Sonya snicker, while Clint audibly groans but Kate ignores them all, focusing on Julie’s answer.

    “What date are you interested in?”

    Kate quickly rakes her mind for the details of Jack’s party.

    “October 9th. So…two weeks from now.”

    With bated breath, she waits while it sounds like Julie is typing on a computer. “Yes, that date is available. How many guests are you expecting?”

    Exhaling, Kate has to keep herself from jumping up and down. She can’t believe it’s coming together like this.

    “Oh my god, Julie, you are a total lifesaver. My boss was about to kill me because I booked the wrong dates. Um, about 350. Maybe a bit closer to 400.”

    On the other end of the line, Julie chuckles.

    “Of course, I’m happy to help. You are lucky, we normally wouldn’t have dates so close available, but we have had a few cancellations, so we are going to be able to accommodate your party. Do you already have vendors and guest experience lined up? We have some very generous rates for…”

    Kate talks to Julie for another few minutes and goes over the vendors and services she knows the party already has and the ones she will have to ask Jack about. When she hangs up, she walks back to the living room, feeling triumphant, she is met with slight confusion on Yelena’s face, her well-shaped eyebrows drawn, and Clint is not even looking up at her, typing on his phone. It’s only Sonya who seems interested but Kate doesn’t let it kill her vibe. It’s like a puzzle slotting perfectly into place.

    “We have a date! I can’t believe it worked. Jack, my…my mom’s boyfriend, ex, I don’t know, he needs a venue for his party on the 9th and everything we have tried has been fully booked but the event hall below Limitless had some cancellations, so we have an in!” Blinking back at her, Yelena lifts an eyebrow.

    “Why did they suddenly have cancellations?”

    Not deflating yet, but halted in her march of triumph around the living room, Kate looks at her, a bit annoyed that this is what she focuses on, instead of the feat Kate just pulled off by hitting two birds perfectly with one stone. It must show on her face because Yelena’s lip twitches upwards and she follows up her question with an explanation.

    “I am just asking because it is a bit too convenient, no? It could be a trap.” Exhaling, Kate does deflate now but she is not sure if this kills the plan for good or not…At least Jack will have a venue for his party, either way.

    “I think…I think it’s actually because of us.”

    Sonya’s words send Kate’s eyebrows toward her hairline, and she chuckles a moment later, turning the tablet in her hand towards Kate and Yelena to show the screen, passing it after a second. Kate takes the tablet and scrolls down the page, skimming the headlines. It’s the news section of the Google search for the event venue’s name, and it only takes Kate a few moments to realize Sonya is right.

    There are several articles about the break-in to the building, the following gunfight, the several members of security injured and dead (Kate clears her throat and pushes that to the back of her head) and multiple explosions while the suspects escaped.

    Obviously, nobody wants to have their party in a place where the guests are in danger or just don’t feel safe.

    Well, it’ll have to do for Jack’s guests.

    Her lips sliding into a grin, Kate looks back up at Sonya, while she passes the tablet to Yelena on her right. She slid closer on the couch while Kate was looking the articles over, and checking them out too, but she takes the tablet nonetheless, tapping on one of the articles to read it.

    “I’m gonna call Jack.”

    Kate picks up her phone again, ready to call Jack, but she halts after meeting Clint’s eyes. “You are good with this?”

    His face gives her a pause, making her ask and he winces a little.

    “Yeah…Nate’s game is the next day.”

    Mouth dropping open, Kate blinks for a second.

    “It’s okay. We can get it done without you.”

    He shakes his head, a tight smile spreading onto his face.

    “No, it’s okay.”

    “I can make the shot too, really. Yelena and Sonya can go to the party and handle the data transfer.”

    Next to Kate, Yelena looks up but she doesn’t add anything. Clint looks conflicted, and he looks at Yelena next.

    “If the computer has extra security, will you be able to hack it?”

    Pursing her lips, Yelena thinks it over while exchanging a glance with Sonya. “It depends on what kind of security measures there are. Most of them we can handle, I have a program that can hack almost anything…but it is neither of our specialties.” Her eyes slide over to Kate, and she nods slowly, knowing that if Yelena’s hacker tool doesn’t work, she will have to be the one to solve that problem, as the person with an almost finished degree in computer science, and the most experience in cyber security. This means, she will have to be at the party, which in turn, means that she can’t be the one to take the shot. Clint will have to.

    Sighing, she looks back at Clint and it seems he realizes it too. He smiles, shaking his head. “Don’t worry about it. If we do it relatively early, I can still travel through the night and make it back in time…And at least I won’t have to go to the party.”

    He looks playful at the end, and Kate smiles back, guilt stirring in her chest. She looks at him for another long moment and his smile widens, motioning at the phone in her hand. “Really, Kate, it’s fine. Go, call Jack.”

    With an apologetic smile, Kate nods and gets up to make the call, walking to the kitchen as she does. The phone rings only once before Jack picks up, his voice jovial and full of affection.

    “Hello, Katie! How are you?”

    Smiling at his voice and despite the nickname she asked him approximately 500 times not to call her, Kate open the fridge and gets a bottle of cold water.

    “Hi, Jack. I got good news. You don’t have a venue for the party yet, do you?” “I do not. Honestly, I was considering canceling the party if I don’t find anything by the end of tomorrow. Do you have something for me?”

    Uncapping the water, Kate leans back against the kitchen island but doesn’t take a sip yet. “Well, it’s your lucky day. I got you a venue in Manhattan. I’ll email you the details as soon as I get them.”

    On the other end of the line, Jack sounds excited, his voice somehow even more affectionate. “Oh Katie, that is wonderful news! I don’t know how to thank you!”

    Swallowing a gulp of water, Kate pulls the bottle away from her lips.

    “Actually, I do. Would it be okay if I came?”

    Jack chuckles, and Kate can hear the smile in his next words.

    “Of course, that’s a given. You are welcome to any party of mine.”

    For a few seconds, Kate considers reading him into the plan, at least partially, but Wendy’s and Annie’s faces appear in her mind and she quickly decides against it. “Um. I would also like to bring a guest…Maybe two.”

    There is a pause on the other end of the line, but before Kate can worry about Jack saying no, or it becoming a problem, he speaks, voice full of warm amusement and a hint of teasing. “Katie…Are you bringing to meet a girl to meet me?”

    Blinking, Kate quickly thinks it over. If they go to the party, half of Manhattan’s high society will be there. If there ever was an opportunity to sell their relationship publically, this is definitely it.

    “Um, yeah. My girlfriend, Helena. It’s…It’s time that I introduced her to you…and people. And we might bring a friend of hers too, I’ll have to check.”

    Through the receiver, Kate hears him clap and she can’t help but huff out a chuckle at his enthusiasm, despite the urge she feels to rub the back of her neck.

    “That is amazing news, Katie. I am so happy for you! I am very much looking forward to meeting your girlfriend.”

    “Yeah, she is looking forward to meeting you too.”

    Taking another sip of water, Kate exhales quietly, already wondering if it will be awkward to discuss this with Yelena. She will have to bring it up first when Sonya is not there…or Clint. She had more than enough of his looks and comments telling her to be careful. “How long have you been dating?”

    Lowering her bottle, Kate turns her head slightly towards the door, hearing the doorbell ring, their food most likely arriving finally.

    “A while. It’s uh…getting serious. Jack, my lunch just arrived, is it okay if we catch up later? I just wanted to let you know about the venue.”

    She starts walking out of the kitchen and to the living room, only half listening to his answer. “Sure, sure. Thank you, Katie, again. You have saved my dignity and reputation.” She smiles at his words, looking at Yelena as she takes the paper bags from the delivery person, handing them a $20 bill as a tip, as Kate already paid for their phone through the app. “Yeah, of course. I’m happy to help. I’ll email you with the details and we’ll talk, okay?”

    Over the next few days, the plan comes together.

    It turns out that Tommy is invited to the party too, and although he had no intention of going originally, Sonya and he end up RSVPing yes, Tommy apparently excited to be a part of their plans for once.

    After getting a blueprint of the event hall’s level too, they figure out that there is an office with a useable computer right below the room at Limitless that they are infiltrating, which is good because according to the information they receive, security will be air-tight, which means smuggling in a laptop as gala guests will probably not going to be easy, especially getting it close enough to actually be within range of the router.

    After that discovery, Kate is somewhat relieved when poring over blueprints, maps, and plans is exchanged for talking to caterers and other service providers in the next week. It is almost comical, yet seriously impressive, how well Yelena and Sonya take the transition, only Clint not taking part in the party planning. He finalizes the design of the glass-cutting arrow instead, with a little help from Kate and the two of them figure out where he will need to be to make the shot, while also serving as a lookout for them during the party. Thanks to the help they offer to Jack, they get access to all the schedules, personnel lists, and everything they want from each vendor and they can freely inquire about security from the building under the guise of being worried about the event. Sonya even goes undercover as Kate’s assistant, to accompany Jack in scoping out the place, coming back with plenty of pictures of security measures, layouts, and possible hurdles they have to handle before the day of the party.

    Kate’s half-healed facial injuries stop her from going with Jack to scope the place out herself but over the next week they thankfully fade away almost entirely, and by the time they are only a week from the party, there is only a thin pink line across her nose, as a reminder of their first attempt at breaking into Limitless.

    During the week following her first conversation with Jack, Kate doesn’t get more alone time with Yelena and as a result, still can’t say she filled her in on the fact that they are going as a couple. All in all, ever since the evening she has been texting Yelena during their stakeout, their interactions have been limited and almost always only about work, something that has served as a source of quiet but pretty strong frustration for Kate.

    During these interactions, Kate could swear that the buzzing tension that has been brewing between them for weeks now was just below the surface, but with Sonya and Yelena taking care of Maxine, the party-planning and mission-planning, there just hasn’t been time or reason for them to speak alone. When they were with the others, and especially around Clint, Kate observed that while Yelena was perfectly pleasant with her, it felt like she kept a distance between them.

    For one reason or another, she treated Kate more like a colleague and while Kate is unsure why that is, she chooses to follow her lead, as much as she can…occasional totally sneaky checking out notwithstanding, at least until they get a chance to be alone organically when she can see for herself if it’s different that way too, or just when the others are around. That, of course, comes back to bite her in the ass.

    Five days before the party, Kate is going over the guest list, checking who is actually coming while rain falls heavily against the window of her living room, when her eyes suddenly stop at a name.

    Senator Catherine Reyes and Guest Wait.

    Pulling up the archived version of Bishop Security’s database, Kate looks up Agent Reyes and it doesn’t take long for her to verify that Senator Catherine Reyes is indeed the same Senator Reyes who is Agent Daniel Reyes’ mother.

    Shit.

    After another few minutes of searching on Google, Kate finds several pictures of the Senator at events and lo-and-behold, Agent Reyes appears on the sidelines several times, which gives her a pretty good guess at who “and Guest” is going to be.

    Double shit.

    Groaning, Kate leans her head back against the couch and closes her eyes, but she feels Clint’s eyes on her. Sonya and Yelena left about two hours ago for a dress-fitting reservation, so it’s just the two of them for the afternoon, working quietly…until now. “What’s up?”

    At Clint’s voice, Kate opens her eyes slightly, sighing deeply before she sits back up and explains.

    “I think the FBI Agent who is on my ass is going to be at the party.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Clint’s face turns serious as he puts down the papers he was looking at. “What?”

    Glancing down at the document on the screen, Kate double-checks her research, but unfortunately, there is little chance that she is wrong.

    “His mother is a Senator, and she is on the guest list, specifically, on the list of people who said they were coming. It says here that she is bringing a plus one, and I’m pretty sure it’s him. He goes with her to events.”

    Looking back at her seriously, Clint seems to process before he nods.

    “Well, shit. That’s not good.”

    Sagely, Kate nods, looking back at him and pursing her lips.

    “Yeah, Clint, it’s not.”

    The two of them look at each other for a moment longer, Kate thinking about Yelena and how to tell her all of this, and Clint…Kate doesn’t know what he is thinking about. Kate was pretty much planned to be the distraction anyway, so Sonya (and Tommy, which is kind of risky, but they are rolling with it because Sonya says it’s fine) can sneak off into the office, and get the data transfer going. Kate was only supposed to get involved if Sonya and the hacker tool that Yelena has is not able to get them into the computer, but this… This still complicates things.

    If Agent Rojas is going to be there, and Kate actually needs to go upstairs to get the data, they will need a serious distraction for him to not notice her leaving. Plus…They will really have to double down on the whole relationship thing.

    With a barely stifled groan, Kate pulls out her phone, opening her text message chain with Yelena. The last one she received is from the week before when Sonya and Yelena were on the stakeout, and Yelena told her about Fanny’s name and Natasha.

    Kate re-reads a few messages before she decides to not text Yelena about this after all, ignoring the little voice in her head telling her she is being a coward. If she waited this long to have this discussion, it’s really best to do it in person, especially considering what type of texter Yelena is.

    She will just have to do it the next day when Sonya and Yelena come over again.

    In the morning, Kate works on the router-USB arrow they will use, assembling and testing it, while Lucky dutifully keeps her company inside her lair, when Yelena and Sonya arrive, with fresh pastries from the bakery around the corner. Clint went out to get them the type of nano- fiber they use in their cable arrows earlier, for both of the special arrows they are going to use because Kate is running low, so she is alone when they arrive.

    She hears them talking as the door opens, Lucky jumping up from his spot to run up and greet them as they walk in.

    “Hi!”

    Calling out from the lair when they walk inside, she waves once they can see her, taking a moment to appreciate how good Yelena looks.

    “Did you get it working?”

    Wincing, Kate shakes her head, standing up from her workbench.

    “Not yet, I am still figuring it out.”

    Holding out a paper bag to her, Yelena passes her a pastry with a smile and Kate is slowly getting used to the feeling of warmth inside of her every time she is in Yelena’s proximity, starting in her chest and spreading, sending a warm thrill up her spine when their eyes meet and Yelena holds it for just a second too long for it to be causal.

    “Thanks.”

    “Enjoy.”

    Yelena is wearing her hair down today, golden curls falling down her shoulders over the oversized denim jacket she wears. Under the jacket, that Yelena takes off and hangs up inside Kate’s closet, she has plaid trousers, paired with a brown shirt and Kate has to turn her eyes up and away quickly when she realizes Yelena is not wearing a bra…Again. Exhaling slowly through her mouth, Kate walks into the living room and sits down on the couch, allowing herself a break before continuing her task.

    “How was dress fitting?”

    Sonya smiles around the mouthful of pastry she just bit into, chewing and swallowing it before she answers Kate’s question. Yelena smiles too, sipping a coffee next to her pastry, but she looks away when Kate tries to catch her eyes.

    “It was amazing. The shop you recommended…”

    Sonya releases a wistful sigh, leaning back against the couch and looking away like she is talking about a stranger she fell in love with.

    “I only want to shop like that from now on.”

    Giving up her pretense, Sonya’s eyes sparkle, and Kate’s smile widens, despite the affection mixing with a certain bittersweet nostalgia in her head.

    “Yeah, my mom used to get all her eveningwear there. They are really special.” The place Kate recommended, and called ahead to reserve a spot at by using her name is one of the most exclusive shops in Manhattan. Only the richest of New York shops there, and Kate made sure to hand Yelena her credit card before the two of them left, hoping she won’t regret it.

    “Wait until you see the dresses, it won’t remind you of your mother anymore.” Sonya says it with a wink and Kate laughs at her suggestive eyebrow wag and playful grin, ignoring the way she feels her ears warm up at the less-than-subtle pointed look Sonya throws at Yelena.

    “I’m sure you will both be beautiful.”

    Glancing at Yelena, she does finally look back at Kate, her smile smug. “So will you. We picked out a suit for you.”

    Oh. That’s…

    “-They had your measurements on file, and it needed to go with my dress, so...” Yelena leaves the sentence hanging and gestures with her chin behind her back. Kate notices the garment bag hung up on the door of the closet then, with the logo of Toteme on it. Remembering the conversation they have to have, she clears her throat, but she swallows her words a moment later, needing a bit more time to gather her wits before she brings it up. “Oh…Thanks.”

    She gives Yelena a thankful smile, before standing up, and walking over to the bag to check it. Unzipping a bag, she peeks inside, and finds a beautiful midnight blue suit, with a crisp white shirt.

    “Ooh, that’s nice…really nice. What are you wearing?”

    Ignoring what Kate is pretty sure a stifled snicker from Sonya, Kate focuses on Yelena, who picks up her phone from the coffee table. Walking back to the couch, Kate takes another bite of her pastry after she takes a seat on the couch.

    After a few seconds, Yelena passes her the phone and Kate looks at the photo, feeling both Widows’ eyes on her.

    “Wow.”

    It’s the first word she can say, looking at the picture.

    It’s of Yelena in a changing room, wearing a beautiful golden dress that matches her hair and hugs her curves perfectly, apart from the slit on the side that shows a sliver of skin going high on Yelena’s thigh. It’s also pretty low cut on the front, the V-shaped neckline going almost to Yelena’s navel and Kate swallows, acutely aware of the eyes on her.

    “You look…I mean. I don’t think I will be the distraction with you wearing that.” Looking up, she catches the smug smile that stretches over Yelena’s lips and Sonya chuckles before interjecting.

    “I think the suit we chose for you will be just as distracting, for some people at least.” With a grin, Kate passes the phone back to Yelena, looking down at it one last time and trying to commit it to memory. Turning to Sonya, Kate takes another bite of her pastry, asking while her mouth is full.

    “Whaf are you going to bear?”

    Picking up her phone, Sonya hands it to her over the coffee table, then proceeds to feed Lucky a piece of her pastry while Kate looks at it. It’s similar to Yelena’s, but a deep shade of green perfectly complimenting her skin, and Kate grins, looking back up at her. “Oh, wow. Tommy is going to pass out before you make it to the office.” Sonya grins back, smiling back smugly.

    “Nah, I told him he gets a reward if he goes through the mission without losing his shit.” Her grin makes it impossible to misunderstand what she means, and Kate laughs, eye flitting over to Yelena. She rolls her eyes, but the gesture is clearly full of affection, despite her faux- exasperation.

    Speaking of…

    “Um, speaking of the party, I kinda have some bad news.”

    Feeling awkwardness creeping in, Kate would have much preferred to speak to Yelena about this alone, but she really can’t put it off any longer.

    “Whatever you have to say, I am not taking that dress back. Or the shoes…Or the purse.” Glancing up, Kate can see that Yelena is joking, and can’t help but chuckle before she shakes her head.

    “No, no. No need. Um, but, I kinda have a confession to make.-“ Her eyes flit over to Sonya, who is laser-focused on her words, but Kate tries to block her out, eyes turning back to Yelena and staying there.

    “When I talked to Jack, I kinda told him I am bringing my girlfriend. It, uh, kinda made sense, because I am bringing you as a guest and he asked and since we can’t tell him what we are doing, it just…fits.”

    It takes her a second to process that Yelena is grinning, eyes crinkled at the corners, her eyebrows slightly raised.

    “I know that.”

    Eyes widening, Kate doesn’t even try to hide her surprise. Shaking her head, she quickly asks.

    “How?”

    Yelena laughs, pointing at Sonya on her side with her thumb.

    “She told me. Jack asked about us.”

    Oh.

    Yeah, that makes sense. It’s kind of embarrassing, especially how nervous Kate was to bring this up.

    After a few seconds, Kate purses her lips, eyes shifting to Sonya.

    “What did you tell him?”

    The grin sliding over Sonya’s face is more than worrying, and the innocent façade she puts on after a few seconds is not much better.

    “Nothing.”

    When Kate’s eyes turn pointed, she rolls her eyes, the grin she is trying to tamp down on shining through her features.

    “Just that the two of you are madly in love. Basically. And that you are thinking about getting married.”

    Exhaling, Kate closes her eyes and purses her lips, but it’s still not the worst thing Sonya could have said, considering that…well, that she is Sonya. After a few seconds, Kate opens her eyes, unable to stifle her exasperated smile and Sonya’s answering grin is as charming as it is unapologetic.

    “Why is that bad news?”

    Blinking, Kate’s eyes shift back to Yelena.

    “What?”

    “You said you have bad news.”

    Barely resisting the urge to slap her own forehead, Kate cringes a little. “Oh, yeah, no, that’s not the bad news part.”

    Rubbing at her forehead, she exhales, before she begins her explanation. “Yesterday I was looking over the final guest list and noticed that Agent Reyes’ mother is coming, and she is bringing a plus one, who I’m pretty sure is him. So, we will have to… prepare for that.”

    Tilting her head to the side, Yelena bites down on her lip slightly while she mulls over the information, which is pretty distracting if Kate is being honest. After a moment, she nods, seemingly half to herself.

    “Okay. We will have to keep you as far away from anything suspicious as possible, but that was pretty much the plan anyways.”

    Puffing out her cheeks, Kate nods, holding Yelena’s eyes. Running a hand through her hair, she scratches the back of her head.

    “Yeah. But I think maybe we should come up with a plan B, for a distraction for him if I do have to go upstairs to the office.”

    Yelena nods back before an unexpected grin makes it onto her face, eye flitting up and down Kate’s form playfully.

    “Kate Bishop, thinking about not only a plan A but also a plan B. Who would have thought?” Rolling her eyes, Kate grins before pursuing her lip, putting on a self-assured mask as she leans further back against the couch, throwing an arm over the back of it as she regards Yelena.

    “I told you. I am like super cautious and thoughtful.”

    Yelena’s grin turns playful, and Kate has missed this. She has missed this more than she realized, just in the last few days while they were always in work mode, with Clint and Sonya around.

    “You have not. I would have not tolerated you lying to my face like that.” Sonya bursts out laughing and Kate can’t help but do so too a second later, warmth spreading in her chest when Yelena joins in too.

    Once they sober up, they try to come up with ideas on how to distract Agent Reyes if they need to, that range from silly and useless to straight-up ridiculous.

    “I’m not saying I’d actually sleep with her. Only that I’d distract him long enough for you to do your thing.”

    Kate laughs, her stomach almost sore from the last few minutes of their brainstorming session, which involved genius ideas like Sonya getting up on stage to sing the national anthem, Sonya hitting on Agent Reyes to distract him, and now for some reason, the idea that Sonya hits on his mother in front of him, which Kate doesn’t understand how it would help, but can’t stop laughing at.

    Yelena is not doing much better, half covering her face with a hand as she laughs, while Sonya looks at them both proudly, a wide and pearly-white grin on her face. “I don’t…How would that help?”

    Kate can barely get the words out, holding her stomach and it only gets worse when Sonya shrugs, before proclaiming.

    “I mean, it can’t hurt.”

    Sonya’s grin gets tempered into a smile as she thinks, then she snaps her fingers twice, before pointing at Yelena and then at Kate.

    “No, wait. I got it. Yelena hits on his mother, and then you throw a huge jealous tantrum and storm off!”

    Kate bursts out laughing again, shaking her head.

    “What?”

    Sonya shakes her head too, trying to look serious but she keeps snickering into her explanation.

    “No, listen, it makes perfect sense. Because if you are upset, you would be looking for somewhere to be alone. Boom! Alibi for going into the office!”

    Wiping a stray tear that escaped from laughter at Sonya’s “plan”, Kate leans back, holding up her hand.

    “Why do all of your plans include hitting on his mother?”

    Sonya huffs, pretending to be exasperated.

    “Well, I don’t have one, but as far as I know, people don’t like other people hitting on their mothers in front of them.”

    Shaking her head in amused confusion, Kate responds, ignoring the pang in her chest at Sonya mentioning not having a mother, and choosing to focus on the joke instead. “So?”

    “So, obviously, he will be uncomfortable.”

    Trying to stress her point, Kate nods, eyes widening slightly.

    “Exactly. He will be uncomfortable so he will leave…and find me at the office.” Shaking her head, Sonya lifts an eyebrow, her lips twitching up again.

    “No. Because if he leaves, his mom get seduced and he has to live with the knowledge.” Burying her face in her hands, Kate shakes her head, unable to take this ridiculousness. Laughing she turns back to Sonya.

    “That makes no sense at all.”

    “What, you would not be bothered if someone hit on your mother?”

    Kate sees the warning glance Yelena throws Sonya at the question, but she laughs, not bothered by it.

    “No? I mean, unless it’s super sexual or like…they are harassing her.”

    “Really?”

    Blinking, Kate still smiles, shaking her head.

    “Yeah. Plus, we are literally going to the party of a guy who hit on my mom all the time. It was a bit weird at first, sure, but all in all, apart from when I thought he was a murderer, I was happy for her.”

    The two widows blink at that off-hand revelation, but Kate doesn’t feel like elaborating, especially because when she thinks about it, it’s also not entirely true. She has been pretty antagonistic to Jack at first when she just found out that he is dating his mother…Maybe Sonya has a point.

    “Speaking of Jack. Can we make sure that he stays 100% out of this? I don’t want to get him in any trouble.”

    The two widows exchange a glance before Yelena shrugs, although Kate can’t say it alleviates her worries completely.

    “Sure. I think as long as Wilson Fisk does not escalate things, there should not be any trouble.”

    That, of course, is one of the main risks they have to prepare for.

    The fact that Kate is attending the party can be found out pretty easily, which is a pretty big risk they are taking already, considering the significant amount of money that is currently offered to kill her.

    Potentially, any of the dozens of assassins after the bounty could try to infiltrate the party and attempt to kill her, which on paper is pretty terrifying, but Kate doesn’t let it show. That said, due to the significantly heightened security of the evening they operate under the presumption, that nobody will try to come for her, even if it cannot be completely written off. That is why, apart from the potential scenario where she has to go up to the office herself, Kate is always to remain in the public areas where people are around, which also provides her with an alibi for whenever the data breach is discovered if the FBI will question it, with several dozens of people with eyes on her. They also agree that wherever she goes, Yelena will have to go too, pretty much like a secret bodyguard, even if Kate prefers to think of it as a more equals scenario where they are partners.

    They also heavily debated whether Kate should be allowed to eat or drink anything at the party and thus increase the risk of her being poisoned, which ended with the compromise that she is not allowed to eat but can drink as it comes from a freshly opened bottle, which Yelena will keep an eye on and enforce.

    Kate’s personal safety is one thing, but another thing to consider is that if Fisk is aware that she is going to be at the party in the building, he most likely suspects that there is going to be an attempt at stealing the data again. This is another reason why Kate has to stay firmly in the limelight, serving as their distraction, and potentially drawing the attention of his people, who might also be in attendance.

    Fisk going as far as doing an all-out attack on the party is somewhat unlikely, but it also can’t be waved off without preparations. While because of Kate’s personal safety, they make sure that the building’s and the party’s security is top notch and very well reinforced, it also makes their own work that much harder.

    With the air-tight security, they already know they won’t be able to smuggle in any weapons on their person themselves, which means they have to make sure there will be weapons available inside, at least in a limited amount that makes it possible for them to make it out, in case of an attack. There are also plans made about what to do about the civilian bystanders if that comes to pass, but Kate really hopes it won’t come to that.

    In the end, they arrange for a sword and after a lot of debating, a bow and arrows for Kate to be smuggled in with the caterers, along with a gun for both Yelena and Sonya. The four of them also spent doing a pretty thorough background check on all security personnel and vendors, making sure that none of them are in Fisk’s pocket or are assassins coming for Kate.

    By the time the day before the party rolls around, their plans are as tight as they ever will be, and despite her nerves about the whole thing, Kate thinks she is ready. Or as ready as she ever will be.

    Her injuries have all but healed, and while they are still ironing out some minor, final details, the party is almost entirely buttoned up, as is their mission. They have contingencies for their contingencies, and apart from a second invasion of New York, they are prepared for pretty much everything.

    Kate is nervous about the whole thing, about the mission, about seeing all these people she knows again, about Reyes attending, and about Yelena and her going together, but really, anything that can and should be thought of ahead is already planned out, and everything else will not be made any better with her worrying about it.

    There is one final detail that has to be sorted out, but it’s one that Kate obsesses over for days but doesn’t have the luxury of sharing with her teammates. She puts off dealing with it as long as she can, but when they wrap up for the day on Friday evening, the day before the party, she really has no choice but to go through with it.

    “Yelena, can I talk to you for a second? Alone?”

    Sonya seems one second away from making a childish and scandalized “oooh” sound, but thankfully leaves with only a playful wink in Kate’s direction, while Clint only glances between the two of them before he grabs his coat and heads out too, picking up Lucky’s leash and ushering him out the door. He does give Kate a meaningful and very obvious warning look, that she does not bother to decipher, but in a few moments, Yelena and she are alone. “What is it?”

    Exhaling slowly, Kate smiles, trying to hide her nerves but unsure how to proceed exactly, because…

    Well, because after learning of Agent Reyes possibly attending the party, Kate took a long walk with Lucky, that took her to the corner of Park and 41st, to her mom’s penthouse, which has stayed empty ever since her arrest over a year ago. And from there, from her mom’s personal safe specifically, Kate took a particular item.

    This happened 3 days ago.

    And that particular item has burned a hole in her pocket ever since, and multiple times she has tried to work up the courage to give it to Yelena, but until now, she always found an excuse not to, and there was always someone else around but their time is running out. This leads her to this moment.

    Kate hesitates, her heart hammering against her chest.

    It’s hard to decide how to proceed…To try to find humor in the situation and lean into it a little as they have before Clint arrived, or if she should be as nonchalant as possible to avoid possibly freaking Yelena out. The hot and cold vibes of the last few days, along with Yelena staring at her now, with an expectant, but otherwise blank expression, all weigh on her decision.

    In the end, Kate decides to play it cool.

    Rolling her lips together before smiling at Yelena, she walks up to her, reaching into her pocket.

    “Um…here, take this.”

    Simply handing Yelena the small, velvet box, Kate clears her throat but continues to smile, trying to go for a chill, easygoing vibe, instead of channeling the borderline heart attack she suddenly thinks she is having.

    “What is this?”

    Yelena is understandably confused. Kate gestures at the box, not stepping back and maintaining her smile that hopefully looks less nervous than she feels. “Um…Open it.”

    Yelena glances down at the box, then back at Kate, then at the box again. She opens it and if Kate wasn’t so fucking nervous, she would have a field day with the shock and surprise written on Yelena’s face. Kate is, so fucking nervous though, so the words start leaving her mouth, almost without any permission from her brain while Yelena stares at the ring for a few seconds.

    “It’s not new.-“ An awkward, half-chuckle, half-croaking sound makes it out of her throat, dying almost instantly which she quickly tries to cover by beginning to ramble, rubbing the back of her neck as she motions at the ring repeatedly.

    ”It’s um, it’s been in the family for some time. My great-grandfather proposed to my great- grandmother with this and it has been passed down since then. I…I know most girls want diamonds, but this is…yeah. That’s an emerald. But it has diamonds too, see? Smaller ones, but…It’s not really fashionable, I know but you know, with the FBI on my ass I can’t go out and buy a new one without-“ Yelena slams the box shut, almost like it contains a dangerous explosive, making Kate immediately do the same to her mouth. She shakes her head, eyes wide, and her voice uncharacteristically non-stable.

    “I cannot take this.”

    As she says it, Yelena holds out the box for her, eyes boring into hers, but it’s Kate’s turn to shake her head.

    “You have to, though.”

    Eyes widening, Yelena’s shock deepens, their gazes locked into one another. “What do you mean I have to? Absolutely not. No. Take it back.”

    Unable to swallow her chuckle at the absurdity of the moment, Kate seems to infuriate Yelena even more but she shakes her head once more, even going as far as to take a step back physically, putting her hands behind her back to indicate she is not taking the box back. “Listen, I know it’s…I know, okay? But we need the FBI off our asses and we need the alibi to be tight, right? This does that.”

    Referring to the unnamed something going on between them, even indirectly, sends Kate’s heart racing but Yelena seems way too overwhelmed to actually get what she means. Her tongue sneaking out to wet her lips, Yelena seems absolutely baffled, eyes flicking down at the box, still held out between them. She shakes her head, raising the box a bit higher to indicate that Kate should take it.

    “I have rings. I have many rings. I will just wear one of them. It will be okay.” At the risk of enraging Yelena even more, Kate chuckles again as she shakes her head, feeling like she might burst into flames at any given moment.

    “Yelena…I am a billionaire. I can’t…It can’t be just any ring.-“ Yelena seems to be gearing up to interrupt, but Kate swallows her nerves and steps forward to grab her hand with the ring box in it, enveloping Yelena’s hand and the box fully. She steps even closer then, gently pushing it back toward Yelena, holding her eyes. “Listen, it’s nothing. Or…well, it’s not nothing, but it’s not that big of a deal.-“ That is a lie. A big one.

    Kate’s mother would be having a heart attack over this, and if she is entirely honest, that might be an additional factor in doing this in the first place, but that is for future Kate to unpack who has time to go to therapy. Swallowing, she glances down at their hands clasped over the box, before meeting Yelena’s eyes again, trying to convey her seriousness. “We needed a ring to sell this, so…I gave you a ring to sell it.-“ “Kate,-”

    Yelena glances down at the box too, pushed gently against her chest, but Kate barrels on, not letting her finish.

    “When we are done with this, you can just give it back, okay? I trust you not to lose it and…-“ Steeling herself, she smiles at Yelena again who blinks, no less shocked than when she first opened the box but clutching it against her chest nonetheless.

    “I won’t take it back until then.”

    Kate wants to say more, but her phone starts ringing on the table, providing the perfect out of this situation. Stepping away, she leaves the box in a very baffled Yelena’s hand, checking the caller. It’s Jack and Kate glances back at Yelena apologetically.

    “Ah, it’s Jack, I gotta take this, sorry. Uhm, just. Think about it, okay? Take it, and think about it.”

    Not giving Yelena an opportunity to answer her, Kate leans down for the phone, ignoring the way her heart still hammers against her chest as she picks it up and turns away to answer the call.

    “Hi, Jack. I talked to the caterer and…”

    Chapter 24

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Before Kate knows it, the day of Jack’s party arrives.

    The day is spent going over their plan again and again so everybody knows exactly where they have to be and when, a very long walk through Central Park with Lucky, and of course, getting ready for the gala itself in the second half of the afternoon.

    Clint leaves before any of them, not needing time to get dressed fancy as he won’t be attending the party itself, and to drop off Lucky at Grills’s apartment for the evening while they are all busy at the gala. The plan is for him to pick Pizza Dog up from there after the formula is in their possession and then for Grills to drive the two of them to the airport, so Clint (and Lucky) can take the red-eye flight and make it back in time for Nate’s soccer game the next day early afternoon as a surprise.

    When it’s time for them to leave, Kate crouches down to pat his head and tries to ignore the tightness in her throat as she hugs him close one last time, but as she buries her face in the soft fur of Lucky’s neck, a few tears slip out nonetheless.

    He seems to pick up on the fact that something is going on, or at least that Kate is sad, and he gives her face a few licks as a way to make her feel better, his tail swishing from left to right slowly. Kate chuckles at that a little, a bit tearful and now also somewhat drooly, and clips the leash onto his collar, reminding herself that he will be safe and happy at the Barton farm while the Fisk thing clears up.

    “You’re going to have such a good time, bud.”

    At her slightly shaky voice, Clint clasps her shoulder empathically, before he takes the leash and picks up the bag full of his things, not one for overly emotional displays. “The offer still stands…”

    Kate glances at him just as he continues.

    “To come too, I mean.”

    With a smile, Kate shakes her head.

    “Thanks, but...Maybe after we wrap this up.”

    He nods, still visibly unhappy with her choice but understanding.

    “Alright. Well… I’ll see you in a bit. And I’ll be back by next week, okay? Or the Monday after at the latest. Don’t be stupid until then.”

    Chuckling, Kate nods, her chest still tight at having to say goodbye to Lucky, but putting on a brave face nonetheless, her tone purposefully dry and sarcastic as she answers his joke. “I’ll do my best…I’ll see you at the party. Or well…hear you.”

    Clint smiles, giving her shoulder a squeeze before he steers Lucky out of the apartment, and in barely a few short moments, Kate is alone.

    Because Yelena, Sonya, and Tommy all get ready in Sonya’s apartment, Kate goes through the motions of getting ready alone, but for once, she is thankful for it and uses the spare time to mope around a bit before she actually has to start preparing. She also helps herself to a generous serving of pizza, knowing she will have to forgo eating anything at the party. Showering, washing and deep conditioning her hair, shaving, and doing a face mask as well, Kate spends the second half of her afternoon trying to relax and enjoy the self-care and pampering, but her heart is heavy from the goodbye and her head is buzzing with her nerves about the evening ahead.

    While she is a bit more confident in their plan, with Clint being involved in it and giving it the go-ahead as well, it is a particularly risky one for reasons other than their recent ones have been.

    The whole plan hinges on them hiding in plain sight, despite the fact that Fisk already knows what they are after, and probably expects an attempt again. Hopefully, Kate staying out of the whole thing and drawing all the wanted (and unwanted) attention, will serve as enough of a distraction for them to execute their little bait-and-switch. Unless she needs to go up to the office as well, but Yelena thinks her hacking tool will do the job, and Sonya, with a little help from Tommy, will be able to pull it off alone.

    After her shower and pampering, she begins to do her makeup, her injuries thankfully having faded enough that she doesn’t have much to cover up on her face. The two bruises, caused by Maxine’s bullets are still somewhat visible on her chest, but since she is going to wear a suit, that is not something she has to worry about. Yelena tried to convince her to wear a bulletproof or the very least a stab-proof vest, but it made her feel stocky and way too warm, so she just puts on the gorgeous new suit and beautiful, crisp, white shirt that Yelena and Sonya brought for her and pairs it with a thin, black tie.

    She decides to leave her hair down, blow-drying it to retain some of its natural waves but applies some gel to sleek it back a little and by 6:45, Kate is ready, checking herself out in the mirror. Just like the widows predicted, the midnight blue suit she is wearing compliments Yelena’s golden dress perfectly, and Kate also chose some gold accessories to match it as well.

    To retain her mobility, Kate decides to forgo heels, although she sincerely hopes that the evening will go off without a hitch and there won’t be any fighting or running involved. No. She thinks that instead, even in their best-case scenario, the evening is going to require a different kind of endurance altogether, which Kate kind of ignored for the last two weeks while they organized the party, getting swept up in the preparations.

    For almost 2 years, Kate has avoided participating in any event of New York high society, and even before that, she was reluctant to do so.

    Tonight marks the first time she is going to a proper event since Eleanor was arrested, and while she hated the polite backstabbing of the top one percent and all the mind games and scheming already before that, having to face all of them now, with her mother in jail and the company gone under, feels even more daunting.

    Sighing deeply, Kate picks up her phone, sliding it into her pocket since she isn’t going to carry a clutch or bag tonight before she looks herself over once more, taking a moment to appreciate that she looks good.

    She locks her door, puts her keys away too, and walks down the hallway to the elevator. The evening marks the first time in several weeks when she left the apartment without some sort of weapon on her, which makes her feel almost naked, a new kind of nervousness adding to the ones swirling in her stomach already.

    As she bounces on her heels a little in front of the elevator, Kate takes a deep breath and reminds herself that this is a mission, and what these people think is completely irrelevant, but even if it worked, that is only one of the several things she has to worry about tonight. While she makes her way down to Sonya’s floor, Kate’s phone pings and she pulls it out, hoping for some kind of distraction, but it’s just the driver letting her know that he is waiting for them in front of the building. Once on the 13th floor, Tommy opens the door for her with a grin, looking her over.

    “Looking good, Bishop.”

    With a smile, Kate returns the favor, complimenting the perfectly tailored dark green suit he wears, and feels herself loosen a little.

    “You too, Newhouse. Yelena ready?”

    With a smile, he steps aside, wordlessly inviting her in, taking another inquisitive look at her face.

    “I think just about… You want a drink?”

    Chuckling a bit forcedly, Kate shakes her head, as she follows him down the hall. “I wish, but probably not. This is going to be tricky with a clear head already so...” Instead of nervous, Tommy looks excited, if anything. His clean-shaven face is bright, and his movements are bouncy like he is about to start skipping any moment. Kate’s grin turns sincere, as she looks at him, recognizing the behavior.

    “Excited to come on a mission with us?”

    It doesn’t feel possible, but Tommy’s face brightens even more, almost splitting in two with his smile before it turns into a half-playful smolder.

    “Yes! I feel like James Bond. Sonya even said I’m getting one of those secret-agent earpieces!”

    Sonya mentioned in passing that he was excited to be a part of their group officially, but Kate did not expect this level of…goofery. His excitement eases Kate’s nervousness a little, and she can’t help but laugh, just as the two of them enter the living room. “Hi, Maxine!-”

    While her foot is still propped up on a pillow on the couch and watching TV, Maxine already looks so much better than she did the last time Kate has seen her last a few days ago. Her skin has reclaimed its natural tone, and the bruises suffered during their escape from Limitless have all faded now too, making her look even younger.

    “-What are you watching?”

    Barely glancing at Kate, she is engrossed in an episode of…Is that? …Oh my god. Kate can’t help but grin, fondness filling her up, as she halts on her way to Yelena’s door. “Hello, Kate. This is a TV show called Sex and the City. I have to watch this to learn to fit in.”

    Not able to swallow it this time at Maxine’s somewhat deadpan delivery, Kate laughs a little, shaking her head while affection for Sonya and Yelena fills her chest.

    “That’s…”

    As her eyes meet a grinning Tommy’s, Kate swallows the rest of her rebuttal. “That’s great. I hope you like it.”

    Hearing steps emerging from down the hall, Kate turns her head just as Sonya walks into the room, barefoot for now.

    “Baby, have you seen my-... Oh, hi Kate. You look…wow.”

    Giving Kate an overdramatic once-over, she halts a few steps into the room, multi-tasking, as she puts in her earrings with her head tilted to the side. Sonya wears a dark green dress with a slit going all the way up her thigh, and a plunging neckline, down almost to her navel. She looks amazing and Kate says so with a grin.

    “Why, thank you. You also look very wow.-”

    Returning the favor of giving an overdramatic once-over, Kate’s grin widens as Sonya does a little shimmy and throws her long hair behind her shoulder.

    “-They are going to hate you so much.”

    Sonya’s faux innocent smile turns into a coy grin, and she looks back at Kate with playful eyes.

    “I am counting on it.”

    Glancing at an amused Tommy, and then at Maxine, who seems to just be perpetually processing their interactions, Kate is reminded that her other half …for the evening… is still missing.

    “Where is…?”

    As if sensing her thoughts, Kate hears the door behind her open up. Turning around to look at Yelena as she enters to room as well, Kate has to admit that she is completely unprepared. Because holy fucking shit.

    If the white dress did things to her head, she doesn’t even know how to put into words how good Yelena looks now.

    Kate has seen the gold dress before, but that was in a picture and didn’t account for Yelena moving and physically being in the dress, and that seems that makes all the difference. The slit that goes up high on Yelena’s thigh, paired with the high-heeled ankle boots that have a golden tip and make her legs look miles long. While she is unaware of Kate’s completely undivided and laser-focused attention on her, Yelena turns around to close her room’s door, giving Kate a look at the creamy expanse of the skin of her back, left almost completely exposed in the dress and much of her hair in a beautiful, intricate half-updo. As she turns back around, Kate’s eyes drop to appreciate the low-cut front of the dress too, offering a generous view of Yelena’s cleavage that Kate has to pull her eyes away from almost forcefully. It feels like all moisture has left Kate’s mouth, and even with the vague awareness at the back of her head that Sonya is probably having a field day with her reaction, she cannot stop herself from clearing her throat.

    It’s at that moment, that Yelena turns to her, and while her reaction is a lot more subtle than Kate’s probably is from an outside perspective, she feels a little thrill at the base of her spine as Yelena looks her over, before wetting her lips, their eyes meeting at last. “Cat got your tongue, Ivy League?”

    Sonya’s voice from beside her kind of brings Kate back to reality but still not enough to take her eyes off of Yelena, who slowly smiles at her reaction. Returning the smile with a grin of her own, Kate gets her bearings and gives Yelena a more purposeful look up and down. “Shit, yeah. Can you blame me?”

    Yelena’s smile widens into a small grin before she rolls her eyes, but Kate can see that she is pleased with her enthusiasm, so she doubles down.

    “You look beautiful.”

    Batting her eyelashes jokingly, Yelena looks at Kate as she steps up to her, straightening her black tie a little.

    “I know. So do you. Very…dashing.”

    Kate chuckles, before lifting an eyebrow and holding her gaze.

    “Dashing?”

    Smoothing down on her lapels, Yelena pats her chest playfully once more before she leans ever so slightly closer, while still not looking away.

    “Dashing. I chose well.”

    While she is obviously referring to the suit, Kate can’t help but straighten her back, a warm simmer stirring in her stomach. Snorting, she grins again, before she turns to the side, offering an arm to Yelena.

    “Shall we? The car’s already downstairs.”

    With another roll of her eyes, Yelena smiles but doesn’t take the offered arm. “Bye, Maxine. Do not burn down the house while we are gone.”

    Yelena throws Maxine a smile as she walks away and Kate follows behind, waving at her as well but partially distracted by Yelena’s back and ass. Maxine follows them out with her eyes, giving a small wave and an even smaller smile. Tiny steps.

    “Goodbye. I will not.”

    Blinking at the somewhat odd interaction, Kate follows Yelena, with Sonya and Thomas walking with them as well. Thomas’ excitement is almost physically palpable, and their little group together almost makes Kate forget her apprehension about the evening. Sonya puts on her heels and soon, the four of them are filing into the elevator, ready to leave for the evening. Shooting a text to Clint, Kate lets him know that they are on their way and receives a prompt answer.

    [from Clint 7:52 pm] Ok. Talk to you in a few.

    Her distraction with the message almost makes her miss the slight glint to her left, but even if it did, Sonya’s words and most importantly her tone would be very hard to miss. “What is that?”

    Looking up, Kate sees that she is looking at Yelena, her eyes wide. Yelena in turn looks confused, blinking back at Sonya.

    “What?”

    “That!”

    Sonya is pointing at Yelena’s hand, lifted presumably to pull a strand of hair behind her ear, specifically her ring finger on her left hand and Kate’s heart skips a beat. Yelena is wearing it.

    She is wearing the ring.

    Almost impercievably fast, Yelena glances at Kate before she sighs, rolling her eyes at Sonya.

    “It is a ring.”

    Sonya rolls her eyes in return, grabbing Yelena’s hand and pulling it towards herself to look at the big green stone, the light reflecting off of it brilliantly.

    “I can see that. Did you give this to her?”

    The second question is poised at Kate, who feels her face warm up for some reason as Sonya rounds at her, almost confrontative. It’s stupid, it’s not like Sonya doesn’t know that their engagement is fake, but it still feels a bit…

    “Yep.”

    Shaking her head, Sonya’s eyes are back on the ring, moving Yelena’s hand a little to see the light glint on it. Looking away, and carefully avoiding Yelena’s eyes, Kate sees amusement on Tommy’s face and he grins when their gazes meet.

    “When did you have time to go out and buy a ring?”

    Biting down slightly on her lips, Kate shoves her hands into her pockets before she answers, shifting her weight back and forth.

    “I didn’t. It’s been in the family for some time.”

    Understanding downs in Tommy’s eyes and his smile widens as he glances down at the jewelry, properly taking it in this time. He knows the type of ring this is. His family probably has one like it too.

    “Ah.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Sonya looks away from the ring but thankfully instead of Kate, her eyes settle on Tommy.

    “When am I getting one of these?”

    Kate laughs and it seems the question breaks the maybe somewhat tense moment in the elevator. Tommy doesn’t look put out, and he pulls Sonya into his side with an arm around her waist as he shrugs.

    “I’m ready when you are.”

    Eyes widening, Kate looks at Yelena who looks just as surprised, and the two of them exchange a stifled grin as Sonya leans up on her tiptoes to give Thomas a peck on the lips. “Good answer.”

    When she turns back, Kate feels her gaze and attention almost like a physical weight settling onto her again but before Sonya can start to grill her, Thomas speaks to Yelena instead, leaning closer with an almost conspirational smile.

    “Don’t get it redesigned… Only the nouveau riche does that.”

    Snorting, Kate looks at Yelena again who just blinks up at Thomas with a smile in the corner of her lips, seemingly amused as well.

    “Well. Certainly, we do not want to look nouveau riche.”

    Grinning, Kate turns back to Thomas, trying to ignore the spark of envy when he pulls Sonya further into his side with a smile of his own, seemingly without even thinking about it. Next to her, Yelena chuckles to herself but before they can continue the conversation, the doors open.

    The four of them make their way out of the building to the two cars waiting up front. “See you there.”

    Sonya winks at them while Thomas nods, the two of them filing into the back of the black Range Rover.

    “You bet.”

    Pulling the door open for her, Kate offers Yelena her hand to help her in, and this time she takes it, as she slides into the back seat of the Royce Rolls. The driver is an older man, with decades of experience in the business, if his composure is anything to go by. He only nods at them in the rearview mirror, and while he patiently waits for the two of them to put on their seatbelts, he doesn’t speak or start driving.

    Once they are ready, the car pulls into traffic and they start their journey towards the party on the busy evening roads of New York. Without something to keep her busy, Kate’s nerves start flaring up again, and her knees begin to bounce.

    Having to do a mission at this party, is both a blessing and a curse because her nerves about their operation and the assassins and everything distract Kate from her nerves about the party itself but it also adds together, creating a big jumble of general nervousness in Kate’s stomach that makes it feel like she swallowed a rock.

    About a minute after their departure, Kate presses the button to raise the privacy screen, smiling at the driver in the rearview mirror but he never glances at them, probably used to it. When she turns to Yelena instead, one eyebrow is lifted as she looks at Kate with a coy smile. “What are you planning to do to me back here, Kate Bishop?”

    Stuck on her nerves about a mission, it takes Kate a moment to get what Yelena means and she chuckles distractedly, fiddling with her tie.

    “Just want to talk. Do you have the drive?”

    Yelena’s smile doesn’t slide away, and she blinks at Kate slowly before she exhales, eyes watching Kate’s features.

    “Sonya has it.”

    Gulping, Kate nods and rolls her lips together as she looks out the window. “Good. Good… Earpieces?”

    When the answer is not forthcoming after a few seconds, Kate turns back to Yelena. She is looking at Kate still, with her head tilted slightly to the side, her smile gone but her face still unmistakably light.

    “You are nervous about tonight.”

    It’s a statement, not a question. Kate looks away and after a few seconds, she nods, not offering a verbal answer.

    “Why?”

    At the question, Kate sighs, glancing to her side to look at Yelena as she offers a half-truth. “Well, we had some shit luck with missions in the last few weeks. And you know, there is always a chance that someone might try to kill me. All in all, not too chill.” There is a beat of silence before Yelena shakes her head, still not looking away from Kate. “Hm, no. That is not it.”

    It’s Kate’s turn to raise an eyebrow, turning more fully towards Yelena, feeling the beginnings of a smile pull at her lips.

    “It’s not?”

    Yelena’s lips stretch into a smile again and she shakes her head once more, her eyes searching Kate’s features.

    “No. You are nervous about seeing these people again. Your people.”

    Scrunching up her face in dislike, Kate looks away.

    “They are not my people.”

    After glancing at Yelena once more, Kate pulls her lips to the side before adding. “I’m not one of them anyway.”

    An amused huff is her only answer before Yelena speaks again.

    “Maybe not. But you grew up with them. They were your community for most of your life.” Pursing her lips, Kate shifts in her seat while she mulls the words over. Yelena is not wrong. It’s not that she really cares what they think, but it’s still going to be uncomfortable to listen to their backhanded compliments and endure their looks and hear them gossip, especially since most of them are really good at cutting remarks and have more than enough fuel to do so. Yelena continues before Kate can put her thoughts into words.

    “It is natural to be nervous about what they think of you…Of your life.” Kate shakes her head, meeting Yelena’s eyes to convey her firmness in her rebuttal. “I don’t. I really don’t give a shit. I just…ugh.-“ Taking a deep breath, Kate puffs out her cheeks as she exhales, trying to gather her thoughts as she looks out the window once more at the buildings and people passing them by. “It’s really not that I care about what they think. Many, probably most, of them are objectively horrible people, so frankly, I don’t give a shit. But still…it’s going to suck having to listen to them talk about my mom, and the company and all that…”

    “Then don’t.”

    Eyebrow furrowed, Kate turns back to Yelena, trying to search her face for the meaning of her words.

    “Hm?”

    Shrugging, Yelena blinks back at her with a smile and Kate is floored for a moment again by how gorgeous she is. Exactly like she belongs in the back seat of this ridiculously expensive car, looking exquisite and beautiful.

    “Just…Focus on what you want to talk about, instead of letting them talk to you about what you do not want to talk about.”

    Kate smiles, exhaling through her nose as she holds Yelena’s gaze.

    “I wish it was that simple.”

    Yelena purses her lips to the side and tilts her head, looking thoughtful for a second before she speaks again.

    “How about you treat this as an undercover mission too?”

    Kate raises an eyebrow, her smile not weaning.

    “I’m listening.”

    Yelena grins for a moment before it’s tempered into a smirk, relaxing more against her seat. “You might not be able to change the name you use tonight, okay, but you can still go in character, no? Instead of Kate Bishop, Hakweye-apprentice and unemployed private eye with a mother in prison, you go as Kate Bishop, billionaire heiress, making your triumphant return and reclaiming your place in high society.”

    Kate chuckles but is unable to resist the sarcastic tone as she answers. “Wow. You should do more pep talks, Yelena, I’m feeling so much better already.” Yelena grins back, batting her eyelashes.

    “What, is it not a good idea?”

    Kate sighs, holding Yelena’s eyes and her stomach does a somersault in anticipation of her own words.

    “No, yes, it is. I guess…I can be Kate Bishop, billionaire heiress making her triumphant return…with her hot mysterious fiancé by her side?”

    Yelena grins, before turning away to look out the window too.

    “I suppose that’s a better story to tell than unemployed archer returns with her tail between her legs.”

    Kate bursts out laughing and a second later, Yelena joins her with a raspy chuckle too that sends a jolt down Kate’s spine. For a moment, they are quiet and Kate feels some of her nerves get smoothed out.

    She is not in this alone.

    She has Yelena and Clint, Sonya and Thomas. They are all in her corner, and they will be fine. They went through a lot of shit situations together already, and tonight is just a party. Nothing more. Just a party with a tiny twist. Kate doesn’t even have to do anything, other than just be seen there.

    For a minute or two, neither of them speaks and Kate pretends to watch the traffic pass them by while keeping an eye on Yelena instead, just taking her in while she ruminates over the conversation they just had. Clearing her throat, Kate brings Yelena’s attention back to herself, nodding down at Yelena’s left hand between them before she speaks.

    “You wore the ring.”

    It’s Kate’s turn to phrase her question as a statement. Yelena rolls her lips together, taking a moment to turn to look at her but there is no mistaking the smile she is trying to stifle. “You truly have a keen eye for detail.”

    They hold each other’s eyes for a second and Kate smiles too, but she sticks to her non- question question.

    “You said you wouldn’t.”

    Yelena smiles, blinking slowly at Kate before rolling her eyes, and looking out the window. “You said you wouldn’t take no for an answer.”

    Nodding, Kate doesn’t look away but only hums as a response, hoping to elicit more of an explanation. A strategy she learned from both Clint and Yelena.

    “Hm.”

    After a second, Yelena glances at her before she turns away to look out the window again, her smile fading just a little.

    “You were right. It makes sense and….We are playing a dangerous game. Between Wilson Fisk, and Javier Rojas, and the FBI, we have to dance between many different fires. Part of that is keeping up the image to keep the FBI off of our tail.”

    Wetting her lips, Kate nods, never taking her eyes off Yelena’s profile. Her next question is out of her mouth before she has a chance to think about its implications. “So you wore it for appearance’s sake?”

    As she turns back to look at Kate, something glints behind Yelena’s eyes. Something serious and dark, but simultaneously heated. Her answer is instant, her eyes boring into Kate’s. “Why else would I wear it?”

    Forcing a playful smile onto her face, Kate shrugs, trying to play off her accidentally serious (and honestly, simultaneously kind of dumb) question.

    “I don’t know. Maybe you got a taste of that sweet gold digger lifestyle, and now you are angling to make it official.”

    The seriousness drops from Yelena’s face almost as if it was never there, her features lighting up with a laugh as she flips her hair behind her shoulder. After a second, she looks Kate over, a teasing grin settling onto her face.

    “Well, Kate Bishop. If that ever happens, I hope you come up with a better line than ‘here, uh, take this.’”

    She finishes the sentence with an absolutely abysmal imitation of Kate but she feels the tips of her ears heat up at it nonetheless. Kate does laugh though, ignoring the warmth she feels lighting up her face before she levels Yelena with a look and imitation of her. “Well, then if I ever do get down on one knee properly, your answer better not be ‘I cannot take this’.”

    Kate attempts to mimic Yelena’s accent as well, the turn the conversation took making her heart beat heavy and fast against her ribcage. Raising a pointed eyebrow at Yelena, Kate lasts about a second before she grins and Yelena chuckles at her words too, holding her eyes, blinking slowly.

    “Touché.”

    Yelena is quiet for a moment, turning to look at the passing city again. After a moment, she turns back, a coy smile making her eyes crinkle.

    “Is that our story?”

    Reading the confusion on Kate’s face, she quickly follows up with an explanation. “The proposal. You got down on one knee?”

    Ignoring the backflip that her stomach does at Yelena’s words, Kate purses her lips, thinking it over.

    “Yeah. I mean, it tracks.”

    Yelena’s playful smile widens, an eyebrow rising.

    “How do you mean?”

    Kate grins, gesturing at Yelena’s form sitting next to her.

    “Well, I mean…”

    She lets the sentence hang and delight fills her as Yelena’s smile widens even more, turning sincere and almost surprised for a second before she turns away with a small shake of her head, pushing a strand of golden hair behind her ear.

    “Okay. Well…Where did you propose?”

    Kate hums for a moment, thinking the question over as she leans against the soft leather seat behind her. The story has to check out, if anyone looks into it and it had to have happened a day or two before the 28th of August.

    “My first thought would be that we went on vacation somewhere, Maldives or something but if anyone checks flight records, it won’t add up. So, that’s not it. The second idea would be to book the Top of The Rock, if it had to have happened here and for sentimental reasons…” Offering a cheeky smile to Yelena, Kate pauses for a second for her joke to land before she continues.

    “-but that also needs a paper trail so probably not that either. I’m not crazy about the idea of a public proposal, so The High Line is also out…hm…”

    Yelena’s voice is brimming with mirth when she asks, interrupting Kate’s musings. “What is your problem with a public proposal?”

    Not oblivious to Yelena’s entertainment at least partially at her expense, Kate purses her lips but gives an honest answer.

    “I don’t know. What if you say no? What if it's awkward? Also, it’s like…not genuine, you know? And I don’t know, shouldn’t a moment like that be kept private?”

    Yelena hums wisely, but when Kate looks at her, she is smiling from ear to ear. Huffing, Kate rolls her eyes, before throwing the question right back at Yelena.

    “What, you’d want to be proposed in public?”

    Her smile turning even more teasing, Yelena shakes her head.

    “No, no. I am just surprised you do not like it.”

    One eyebrow raised and grinning, Kate turns her body almost fully towards Yelena to look at her, thanking the busy New York traffic for delaying them enough to allow them to have this discussion.

    “What’s that supposed to mean?”

    It feels like Yelena is looking straight into her soul, as she keeps holding her gaze, but Kate won’t be the one to break eye contact either.

    “Well, you like to be the center of attention. You like it when people are looking at you and you get it effortlessly. So, I would think you would like that. People seeing you…get the girl.”

    Kate tilts her head to the side biting down on her lip to tamp down on her smile, considering Yelena’s words.

    “I…okay, that’s kinda true... So, the High Line it is?”

    Yelena shrugs, her eyes sparking with amusement again even as she raises a challenging eyebrow at Kate.

    “Well, it’s your proposal.”

    Kate laughs, shaking her head.

    “Yeah, but with my hands tied. If it was the real one, I’d probably take you on a vacation and do it there. Make it into a whole thing.”

    Yelena chuckles but shakes her head, glancing out the window as she wets her lips before her focus is back on Kate.

    “Vacation is not good. It is very much more awkward if I say no there. Plus, you would not be able to enjoy vacation until you do it, and if I said no for some reason, you would not be able to after it either.”

    Blinking, Kate looks back at her and now she gets why Yelena was getting a thrill from this. This is really kind of fun. In a stomach-flipping, palm-sweating kind of way. “Okay, that’s fair.”

    Kate replies before her eyebrows draw together and she throws Yelena a look as she speaks again.

    “Although I don’t know if I should be offended that we are treating the option of you saying no as such a likely possibility, but whatever. Let’s stick to The High Line… Although, for the record, if we stick to New York, then I’d go for the Top of The Rock, and book the whole thing, get the works…but whatever. Hands behind my back.”

    Kate feels like she has to explain her choice but Yelena just nods, her eyes sparkling with amusement, and Kate decides to cut in before she can beat her to the next question. “Okay, your turn. First date. And how did we meet?”

    Yelena’s eyes light up with delight and she is either very quick to think on her feet or she has already thought about this because her answer is immediate.
