    “We met through a mutual friend, and for our first date, I cooked for you, but at your place. You were supposed to, but you can not cook to save your life and you burned it.” At Kate’s surprised, but pointed eyebrow she bites down on her lips for a second, smiling before she proceeds to explain, preempting the question Kate was going to ask. “It is always best to stick as close to the truth as possible, with cover stories like this. This is generic enough to not warrant too many follow-up questions, but it has a specific cutesy detail that can make it sound not too vague.”

    Kate laughs but throws Yelena a look, not really feeling the need to defend herself, but enjoying the playful bickering.

    “Hey, for the record, I can cook.”

    Yelena shakes her head with a grin, her eyes sparkling like the emerald on her finger. “Breakfast doesn’t count.”

    At Kate’s faux-disgruntled face, Yelena rolls her eyes before conceding. “Okay, okay. Fine! We can say you made breakfast the morning after, to make up for it.” That smooths away Kate’s furrowed eyebrows, sending them rising on her forehead instead, and she can’t help the smug grin stretching her lips wide either.

    “You stayed over after the first date?”

    Yelena only shrugs, but a second later she meets Kate’s eyes again, and the way she is looking at her makes Kate’s stomach tighten again with excitement, the back seat suddenly feeling very warm and small.

    “Well, I guess you played your cards right.”

    Kate rolls her lips together to avoid them falling open, before she puts the smug grin back on again, feeling cocky.

    “Hm. Even after fucking up dinner? Lucky me.”

    Yelena looks away with a grin and Kate discreetly loosens her tie a little, its hold suddenly a bit too tight. She feels like all her extremities are filled with molten metal, as Yelena turns back and their eyes meet again.

    “Hm, well. Maybe I found your uselessness in the kitchen endearing.”

    Before Kate can continue the conversation, the intercom crackles into life and the voice of the driver filters through.

    “Excuse me, Ms.Bishop. We are about to arrive.”

    It’s not even 5 seconds later, that the car rolls to a stop and when she glances at Yelena, Kate has to wonder how much of their conversation was a technique to distract her from her nerves. If it was, it worked incredibly well, but now that they are here, Kate’s nervousness comes back with a vengeance.

    With jittery hands, Kate taps her pockets to check her phone and keys are still inside, before taking a moment to steel herself for the evening.

    “Are you ready?”

    Kate smiles at the question, half grimacing, and sees the way it makes Yelena’s smile widen in the corner of her eyes.

    “Nope. But let’s do this anyway…”

    Closing her eyes for a long moment, Kate exhales, before she opens them and nods to herself as she speaks again.

    “Alright. Game on. I’m going to get out first, open the door for you.”

    Not waiting for Yelena’s answer, Kate opens the door and slips out of the car. She notes that there are a few photographers and possibly a few members of the press at the entrance, but she ignores them as she walks around the car to open the door for Yelena. When she offers her hand to help Yelena out of the car, she takes it again, seemingly already in character, and the two of them walk the few steps separating the car from the entrance hand in hand.

    Once inside, Kate takes a short moment to breathe in and out deeply, even closing her eyes for a second to ground herself, as Yelena lets go of her hand. When she opens her eyes, Kate takes in the lobby, noting the security personnel scattered around the space and the metal detector they will have to walk through.

    Ushering Yelena forward with a hand on the small of her back, the two of them step up to go through the process. Kate lets Yelena go first but puts her phone and keys in the same tray as Yelena’s clutch, which contains a small case that should hide their earpieces and knowing Yelena, some type of weapon. They arranged for Sonya to have a similar one too, that carries the drive along with earpieces for Tommy and her.

    Yelena goes through the detectors without setting them off, and Kate hides an exhale of relief when their things make it through the x-ray machine without any problems too. Of course, that means that if they can smuggle things inside, others can probably can too, but Kate reassures herself that people meaning to smuggle things in are probably not Black Widows. Also while the other guests may have similar financial means to Kate, to purchase the materials she and her team use, the everyday assassin will not, which at least reduces the number of people she has to worry about, at least for tonight.

    “Your turn, Miss.”

    The security guard motions for Kate to go, and despite not hiding anything on her body, Kate still feels nervous as she steps through the gate. It does not go off, and Kate throws a polite smile at the security guard, while she picks up her phone and keys from the tray, sliding them back into her pocket.

    “This way, Ms.Bishop.”

    A young man, in a black suit and black shirt, waits on the other side with a clipboard, and ushers them forward, then proceeds to lead them to the main elevator. He even presses the button for them as they wait and Kate smiles at him while trying to scope out the main lobby inconspicuously.

    Of all their missions, this might be the riskiest and with their recent track record, she can’t help but expect that Fisk’s men might be getting ready to get the jump on them as soon as they are inside, even if Clint would have told them if there was suspicious activity going on already before they arrived.

    There is no attack or even a suspicious look, however, only the 20-something attendant politely motioning for them to get into the elevator as its doors open. He does not get inside, and Yelena and Kate both look ahead, as the doors slide closed.

    Yelena reaches into her clutch as soon as the elevator is in motion and pulls out the small case that hid their earpieces from security. She passes one to Kate before she reaches up to put her own in. Kate quickly checks the time on her phone, 8:14 pm, as she tilts her head to slot the earpiece into place too, tapping it to turn it on.

    “Radio check.”

    It takes him a moment, but as the digits on the elevator’s screen go by, Clint’s voice comes through, crystal clear.

    “Loud and clear…You are late, kid.”

    Smiling to herself, Kate exchanges an amused glance with Yelena before she turns to look ahead at the closed doors.

    “Sorry. Traffic.”

    Clint hums and Yelena joins the conversation.

    “Anything to report?”

    “No. There are some extra guards in place across the 31st and 32nd floors, but everything’s quiet so far. Let’s hope it stays that way.”

    Kate hums, taking a few more deep breaths in preparation and glancing at Yelena who looks ahead at the doors too, maybe going through her pre-mission mental prep too. As they near the 30th floor, Kate reaches out with her hand, offering it to Yelena.

    “Showtime.”

    Glancing at her, Yelena looks down at her outstretched hand with a small, kind of playful smile and reaches out to take it. As the doors slide open, Kate puts on a smile too, polite but not too friendly, and leads Yelena out into the entrance hall, soft music filtering through from the inside.

    There is a small reception area to the right, where the two of them sign in, showing their invitation, and a coat room of sorts to the left. The coat room they ignore, for now, as they do not have anything to check in, made unnecessary by the door-to-door car service but Kate takes note of the fact that it has a direct view of the stairs Sonya and Thomas will have to take later, once their plan goes into action.

    With the sign-in process over and done with, Kate and Yelena halt by the main entrance of the banquet hall side by side across from the elevators, looking in.

    With Jack’s speech scheduled to start at 9 pm, they have about 40 minutes to kill, before the plan actually starts to go into action. With some trepidation, Kate looks into the ballroom, looking over the rich and powerful of New York, chatting and mingling.

    The room is tastefully decorated, and Kate distractedly notes that if their escapades are over and she is still alive and kicking, Yelena, Sonya, and she could start a party planning company because they have done a wonderful job, if she can say so herself. To the left side of the room, there is an area left open for dancing, right in front of the band playing music at a comfortable noise level, while to the right, the bar and standing tables are, which is where most of the guests currently mingle and chat. Kate can already see a few people she knows, either from these parties or from school and university, none of whom she particularly missed having contact with.

    “It is going to be fine… Just remember, you are undercover.”

    To stress her words, Yelena gives Kate’s hand a small squeeze and when she turns to look at her, she gives her a genuine smile too, her gaze shining with encouragement. Kate smiles back before taking one last big breath.

    “Okay…Right, we should probably go look for Jack. Say Hi at least. Then we can…mingle in the nest of fucking vipers, I guess.”

    “Lead the way.”

    Yelena snorts, holding Kate’s eyes before she turns to look at the room full of people as well, while Kate takes the opportunity to appreciate her beauty for a moment before they have to immerse themselves in the party.

    After the moment passes, Kate steels herself and starts leading them into the ballroom, feeling several eyes on them as soon as they enter the main ballroom. Unconsciously, Kate squeezes Yelena’s hand again, but she lifts her chin, purposefully making eye contact with a few people as she passes them by, not giving anyone the satisfaction of showing her nerves or discomfort.

    They find Jack with an older couple and a young man she knows but can’t say she much cares for, all of whom Kate knows from various parties over the years, at least enough to politely smile when their eyes flash in recognition.

    “Hello, sweetie! You made it!”

    The genuine happiness on Jack’s face warms Kate’s heart, and she steps up to his group with a genuine smile.

    “Hi, Jack.”

    Jack’s smile widens even more and Kate feels a sliver of guilt at how happy he is just at the fact that she is here, not aware that she has an agenda. He greets her with a hug, holding onto her arms a second later to look her over. His eyes slide to Kate’s right, looking at Yelena for the first time, his face turning teasing in a goofy kind of way.

    “Is this the plus one I have been hearing about?”

    The question is obviously poised at Kate, but his eyes keep jumping between the two of them, and he offers a hand to Yelena.

    “Yes. Um, Jack, meet my girlfriend, Helena.-”

    Kate glances to the side and sees Yelena smile, her face turning surprised and somewhat delighted when instead of shaking her hand, Jack turns her wrist to lift it to his lips instead, giving her hand an old-fashioned peck on the top.

    “And Helena, this is Jack. Jack Duquesne.”

    Jack smiles, warm and genuine, holding Yelena’s eyes.

    “A pleasure to meet you, Helena.”

    Yelena smiles back, glancing at Kate for a moment before she answers, her American accent impressively smooth, as she slides ever so slightly closer to Kate.

    “Likewise. Kate has told me a lot about you.”

    Kate has told her virtually nothing about Jack, but she has no doubt that Yelena knows enough already, from looking into her and her family.

    “Kate, do you know John and Barbara, and their son, Wayne?”

    “Oh. Yeah, of course. Good to see you, ma’am, sir. Hi Wayne.-”

    Barbara and Wayne smile, nodding at Kate, but their eyes keep returning to the newcomer, Yelena, while John looks at Kate, somewhat calculating, eyes slightly narrowed. “And this is my girlfriend, Helena.”

    The second time around, it feels more natural in her mouth and Kate relaxes a little, not giving too much attention to John’s inquisitive gaze. He is known as an old bastard, by most people in their circles and a titan of industry by wider society, but his like or dislike doesn’t bear much weight in Kate’s life. He has a bunch of newspapers and TV stations, that were more than happy to drag Kate and her mother through the mud, but he is way too important to not be invited to parties like these, despite the slightly bad blood between their families. Yelena shakes the hands of all three of them, holding their eyes and offering a polite, but not even slightly intimidated smile.

    “Nice to meet you all.”

    Once Yelena is back at her side, Kate notices Wayne’s eyes drop to Yelena’s cleavage, staying way longer and straying way lower than what is appropriate, especially since Kate literally just introduced her as her girlfriend.

    What a dick.

    Annoyed by his assholery, Kate puts a loose arm around Yelena’s waist and is just about to ask about how Wayne’s business venture, which she knows failed spectacularly, is going, when his father speaks to her instead.

    “Katherine, how is your mother?”

    Kate expected the question, even if not necessarily within 3 minutes of her arrival, but it’s hardly surprising. She is proud of herself when not a muscle on her face moves as she shifts her gaze at John, giving him a smile she sincerely hopes he knows is ingenuine. “I wouldn’t know, sir. I haven’t seen her in a long while.”

    If Kate hoped that was the end of that conversation, she would be sorely disappointed. He grunts at her answer, before looking at her from under his bushy, white eyebrow and speaks, his tone almost accusatory but maybe more testing.

    “She cost me a pretty penny, you know. Your mother.”

    John’s grey eyes are searching, trying to cut into Kate, to pry and look for weakness but she is pleasantly distracted by a small hand sliding up between her shoulder blades, feeling its warmth even through the layers of her shirt and suit jacket. Loosening her muscles, which Kate just now notices were beginning to lock up a little, she exhales slowly and tilts her head to the side, looking back at John as he continues.

    “-We could barely divest our stake before the news of her arrest broke.” Lifting her chin, Kate regards him for a long moment.

    “Well, none of us control the news cycle, do we.”

    She gives him a thin smile, not once looking away. He seems almost impressed that she is not intimidated by him, but Kate is uninterested in his appreciation. After news of her mother’s arrest broke, his papers and TV stations were more than happy to scream about it from the rooftops, and it was his publications that dug into Kate’s life too, talking to classmates, exes, and people that claimed to know her but don’t actually. Turning firmly back to Jack, she cuts off whatever John was going to answer, specifically positioning herself, and by addition, Yelena, to close him out of their conversation.

    “Was everything okay during the set-up?”

    Obvious of the tension within the group, Jack smiles wide, his hand coming to rest on the handle of the sword he wears on his hips.

    “Yes, yes. Everything was basically ready by the time I arrived.”

    Unsurprised by this revelation, as they basically took over the organizational matters, Kate smiles. She loves Jack sincerely, but when it comes to practical matters, he is entirely useless. “You did an amazing job, the party is beautiful.”

    At Yelena’s words, Kate has to stifle a chuckle, but Jack’s smile is lovely and humble. “I am sure you know how much Kate helped. It’s at least as much her accomplishment, as it is mine.”

    Kate waves his compliment off, shaking her head. Glancing at them, Kate sees that John is about to speak again, and Wayne is unsubtly staring at Yelena’s chest, again or still, so she turns back to Jack and reaches out to give his arm an affectionate squeeze as she speaks. “Anyway, we are going to make some rounds. We’ve only been back from LA for a few weeks, so there is a bunch of people I haven’t seen forever.”

    Jack nods, his eyes sparkling with affection.

    “Enjoy the party, sweetie.”

    “Thanks, you too… It was nice to see you.”

    The second half is said to Barbara, John, and Wayne, but she is pretty sure it’s obvious she doesn’t mean it, not that she really cares.

    “It was lovely to meet you.”

    While Yelena doesn’t specify, it’s fairly obvious that her words are meant for Jack too, and he smiles at both of them as they turn to walk away.

    “Check.”

    Sonya’s voice comes through their earpieces, while Kate exhales slowly, trying to rid herself of the bitter aftertaste of the conversation.

    “Loud and clear.”

    Muttering next to Kate, Yelena keeps to her side, the two of them making their way through the groups of people that separate them from the bar.

    “Loud and clear.”

    Giving her own quiet answer, Kate’s eyes browse the room, looking for familiar faces. “Check?”

    Thomas’ voice sounds a bit uncertain, and Kate exchanges an amused and maybe a bit affectionate glance with Yelena, before both of them give their ‘loud and clear’ responses, along with Clint. At the bar, Kate orders a bottled coke, as cocktails are out of the question for the night, while Yelena snags a flute of champagne from one of the waiters walking around in the crowd.

    It only takes Sonya and Tommy about three minutes to make it up to the party, the two of them entering hand in hand. Even from a distance, Kate can tell that Sonya looks smug when several heads turn their way, taking them in as they walk into the room. As Kate and Yelena take up residence next to the bar, sipping their drinks and watching the crowd, Sonya and Tommy begin to make their way over too, the four of them not pretending to not know each other, since they are already planning to serve as Kate’s (and Yelena’s) alibi for the night they freed Maxine, even if the FBI hasn’t called to ask them for yet. Before Sonya and Tommy can make it to them, Yelena rounds on Kate, standing close and well within her personal space.

    “I got eyes on Agent Reyes. Right there by the fountain, northeast side of the room.” Kate would not admit to it out loud, at least not in present company, but she has no idea which way northeast is right now, but she can see the fountain and after a few moments of searching, she spots Agent Reyes too.

    He stands next to a woman, who Kate quickly identifies as his mother. They are chatting with two older men, but as if he feels her eyes on him, he turns his head, almost catching Kate staring. Quickly, she looks down at Yelena instead, her face barely inches from Kate’s. “He knows we are here. He just looked at me.”

    Kate murmurs the words close to Yelena, hoping it looks like they are a couple having an intimate conversation instead of her reporting on his position.

    “Smile like I just said something kind of funny.”

    Kate does, her eyes never leaving Yelena’s.

    “Okay. Sonya, he will probably be watching us, so it’ll be up to you to watch him.” Yelena smiles as she speaks too, the image of her looking at Kate, brimming with affection contrasting starkly with her words. Kate finds it disconcerting and feels a bit flustered with the way Yelena looks at her, but Sonya’s quiet voice pulls her attention away. “Roger that.”

    “I’ll keep an eye out too.”

    Clint’s voice sounds like he is standing right next to them, even though they are currently alone, or as much as one can be in a room full of people.

    Kate risks another glance at Agent Reyes, finding him engaged in the conversation with his group again, and quickly turns away, taking a sip of her diet coke before she risks getting caught looking again.

    “As I live and breathe… Kate Bishop!”

    The voice is not on their comms channel, but coming a few feet away, quickly drawing Kate’s and Yelena’s eyes. The speaker, Alexander Kravis, or Alex, is not alone. Kate knows him through his sister, Emily, who went to the same high school as she did. The two of them, along with his best friend Jason, used to stick together as a toxic little squad back then, and it seems to be the case still, as the two of them stand on his side right then too, looking at Kate, their eyes quickly sliding over to Yelena.

    Alexander’s and Emily’s father owns the second biggest private equity fund on the east coast, while Jason’s parents own half the real estate in New York and New Jersey. They are among the younger guests at the party, Kate’s generation only now starting to show up to these things to network, mostly with older business prospects.

    All of them have been mean, as long as Kate remembers, Alexander acting basically as a straight-up bully, while Emily was more of the ‘shiv you while you are not looking’ kind of gal. Jason was always just there to prop up their act, not much original thought popping up in his well-combed dirty-blonde head.

    “Hi, Kravis.”

    At Kate’s unenthused answer, Alexander throws a peanut into his mouth with a lazy movement before he grins, obviously self-satisfied, and walks closer to them. Kate rolls her eyes, but turns her body toward them slightly, arm sliding loosely around Yelena again. She is not intimidated, having grown up around girls and guys like these all her life, and always having a healthy dose of confidence that repelled their attempts to bully her, which usually meant they got bored of trying pretty quickly. They obviously think they have good ammunition now, judging by the smug look on Alexander’s smarmy face.

    “I gotta say, I didn’t think we’d see you at one of these things again.” At his words, Emily puts on a faux display of admonishment, slapping her brother’s arm gently, but Kate sees the cruel humor spark in her blue eyes, eradicating whatever goodwill her scolding would have bought.

    “Jesus, Alex. Were you raised by wolves?”

    He grins, his unrelenting eyes crinkling at the corners as his grin widens. “Well, I’m sorry for saying what we were all thinking. Her mom went to jail. Hello? Do you all not read the news?”

    Like a paid extra, Jason snickers at Alexenader’s words, puffing out his chest as if it was he who completed the unbelievably impressive feat of making fun of someone whose family member was sent to prison.

    “Chill. I’m just pulling her leg. Bishop knows how it is, don’t you?”

    Blinking, Kate doesn’t give him the satisfaction of actually getting upset, her lips tilting up in a cold, clearly dishonest smile. Tilting her head, Kate looks him over, taking note of the way his checkered suit makes his form look even more unflattering than it is, with not a single ounce of practical muscle on his spoiled body.

    “Sure, Alex. You bring up my mom in jail, I bring up the time your girlfriend got a restraining order against you. Just routine banter.”

    A muscle in Alexander’s face twitches, his grin freezing, but a second later he recovers, gesturing at Kate to his sister. In her ear, Kate hears Clint huff, probably in a mix of amusement and exasperation.

    “You see? She knows I’m just joking.”

    Emily rolls her eyes at her brother, stepping closer to the two of them. Kate is only half paying attention, however, eyes following Reyes discreetly as he makes his way through the room.

    “Kate, don’t listen to him, it’s great to see you again. How are you?”

    Exhaling, Kate brings her eyes back to Emily’s face, reminding herself she has to play along for their plan to work, and actually talk to these people, no matter how much she wishes she could tell them to fuck off.

    “Yeah, I’m good, thanks. We’ve been back from LA for a few weeks now. Getting used to the weather.”

    Unsubtly, Emily’s eyes move onto Yelena and Kate smiles, her hand coming to rest on the small of her back, trying to ignore the small thrill when her fingers graze the soft skin left exposed by the open back of the dress.

    “This is my girlfriend, Helena. Helena, this is Emily. We used to go to school together.” Glancing over Emily’s back, Kate has no choice but to introduce the two men too, not wanting to seem overly rude as they step up to them also, joining Alex’s sister. “And that’s her brother Alexander, and their friend, Jason.”

    While Kate can guess that Yelena must sense her animosity towards the trio, she is perfectly pleasant, shaking each of their hands before stepping back to Kate’s side. Kate sees the way Emily’s eyes drop to Yelena’s form and feels a twinge of pride and a healthy dose of smugness when she almost sees her face turn green with envy.

    “Oh, I love your dress.”

    Emily’s voice is cheerful and almost sounds earnest, but Kate could spot that mean-girl voice a mile away, having grown up with this particular one and a bunch of others. Yelena must sense it too, as she lifts her chin, staring Emily straight in the eyes, a beautiful yet fake smile sliding onto her face.

    “Thank you. I love yours too. Last season Versache, right?”

    Masking her surprise at Yelena’s ability to recognize things like that, Kate has to focus on not laughing at Emily’s face either, offense clearly flickering through it before she can hide it. “Oh yeah. I just ran home after work and pulled something off the hanger before I came here. I’m sure you know how it is.”

    Emily’s eyes drop to take in Yelena’s outfit a second time, before looking up again. “-Do you work in fashion?”

    Kate turns her head to see Yelena’s lips tilt upward before she answers simply. “No.”

    Before the Terrible Trio can rebound with more questions that are meant to humiliate, Yelena speaks again.

    “So what do you all do?”

    Above Alexander’s shoulders, Kate sees Sonya and Thomas finally approach and she smiles, happy to not be outnumbered, however little she cares about these assholes’ opinions. Tommy speaks before any of them can answer Yelena’s question, towering over the two men as he grabs their shoulders from behind.

    “Kravis the Menace and Sam fucking Gamgee.”

    Thomas looks at Alexander first, before turning his head to look at Jason, both of them visibly trying to hide a wince at his hold. Kate snorts at Jason’s confused, scrunched-up face, obviously completely missing the reference. Sonya slides in next to Yelena effortlessly, and Kate almost misses the two exchanging a glance.

    “Hi, Emily.”

    Sonya greets the young woman in a smoothly polite voice, her American accent as spotless as Yelena’s. Almost imperceptively, Emily’s eyes narrow and Kate wonders what the history is there, but it’s obviously not the time and the place to ask.

    “Sonya. It’s lovely to see you.”

    The two women exchange cheek kisses before Emily’s eyes slide over to Thomas. “Tommy, Sonya, have you met Kate’s new girlfriend?”

    The introduction feels weird, and Kate feels her eyebrow lifting as she meets Tommy’s eyes across the circle they kind of ended up forming. They exchange a grin, but before either Kate or Tommy can answer, Sonya pipes up.

    “Of course, Helena and I go way back. We introduced them to each other, actually.” That could fit with the cover story they already came up with, so Kate smiles, nodding at Emily’s inquisitive gaze when it shifts to her, as her arm slides around Yelena again. It seems that Emily has reached her threshold of keeping up pleasant appearances, or simply got frustrated with the fact that she couldn’t tear down Kate or Yelena, as she turns to Tommy a second later.

    “Awh…Allie must be pretty devastated.”

    Her voice is perfectly pleasant, and again, she does a surprisingly good job of sounding earnest, but it’s still a bitchy fucking comment. Kate watches Tommy as his eyebrows rise, surprise written over her face at Emily’s audacity. He masks it well and pretty fast, but it’s a bit too late, and Kate can tell that Emily thinks she has found something to torment someone over when her eyes glint a certain, cruel way.

    That is, until Tommy shakes his head, chuckling at Emily’s words.

    “Nah. She was pretty ecstatic actually. We hatched the plan together to set them up..” After it seems like Emily is about to answer, probably with more words of cruelty, Tommy continues, his elbow hitting Jason in the side in a way that is clearly playful, but obviously uncomfortable as well because he flinches.

    “It’s been a long, long time since high school for all of us, right?”

    He grins after that, looking cheekily at the Terrible Trio and Kate feels it mirrored on her own face, their team successfully pushing back on the childish bullying attempts yet again. “So, what are you guys up to nowadays? They ran out of coke in Washington already?” Tommy’s next words are said to Alexander, slapping his back before he crosses their newly formed circle to stand on Sonya’s other side, leaving her and Yelena standing next to each other, with Kate to Yelena’s right.

    Kate sees the way Alexander’s jaw ticks and wishes she had a drink to stifle her smile in. As she doesn’t, Kate just turns her head to the side, hoping to hide her face a little, her eyes sweeping the ballroom full of faces above Yelena’s head.

    There is a head full of floppy, brown hair that catches Kate’s attention, the mop of hair familiar despite the cheap suit that very obviously does not belong to this party. “Actually, I’m here on business.”

    Alexander says it smugly, his nonchalant arrogance fully on display again. Pulling her gaze away from the back of the familiar brunet head that she cannot place, Kate pulls her attention back to Alexander when she hears her name.

    “-What about you Bishop? You doing anything since your family’s company went down the drain?”

    Instead of answering his question, Kate decides to take Yelena’s advice from earlier and simply doesn’t engage in the part of the conversation she doesn’t wish to be a part of, commenting on his work instead, with the same nonchalant cockiness he tries to convey, just wearing it better…If she can say so herself.

    “Oh, yeah. I thought I saw you buzzing around Senator Schumer.”

    Although Kate means it as an insult, Alexander’s thin lips stretch into a self-satisfied smile. “Of course, you saw me with him. I’m his most trusted aide.”

    Making sure that her disbelief is written all over her face, Kate nods, her eyes going back to sweep the crowd for either Agent Reyes, or the slightly familiar head she cannot place. “Yeah, I’m sure.”

    She is sure she knows the person from somewhere, but if she could just see their face… “An aide? That’s like…an assistant, right?”

    At Sonya’s question, Kate pulls her attention back to the conversation again, seeing the way Alexander’s face darkens. For all Kate cares, there is nothing wrong with being an assistant or working one’s way up to the top, but it’s obvious that Sonya has found a sensitive spot with the same ruthless accuracy that she seems to possess in all walks of life, based on the vein that starts to pound on the side of Kravis’ neck.

    “Hah, no. No, it’s like a legislative associate. I have a law degree from Harvard, so I prepare materials for him on important topics, I take notes during his meetings, I-“ “Right. So, like an assistant does.”

    It seems like smoke is about to come out of Alexander’s nose at Tommy’s words, his jaw clenching, and Kate can see that things are about to turn ugly even as she swallows her chuckle. Kravis opens his mouth to answer, lips curling, stepping back and consequently, bumping into the person standing behind him. It makes him splash a little bit of champagne down his crispy, light blue shirt, and it seems to be the last strike.

    “Watch where you are going, asshole.”

    Immediately, he rounds on the person that he bumped into and Kate comes face to face with the brown-haired person she was trying to place earlier as he turns around too. It’s Peter, from F.E.A.S.T. with a camera in his hands and wearing a cheap but neatly ironed suit.

    “I’m so sorry, sir.”

    His eyes meet Kate’s for just a second, but they are immediately drawn away as Alexander steps into his space, practically spitting in his face. Why is he apologizing? Alexander bumped into him…

    “I don’t need you to be sorry, I need you to fucking watch where you are going. Do you know how much this shirt costs?”

    Peter looks a shade paler than he did a second ago, shaking his head.

    “I don’t…I’m sorry, sir. I-“ “I don’t, uh, sir, uh. Well, I’ll tell you, photo-boy,”

    Alexander mockingly repeats his words, before attempting to slap the camera out of Peter’s hands. It doesn’t fall, but Peter takes a step back and pulls it closer to his chest, visibly shocked at Alexander’s behavior.

    “-it costs 2000 dollars, and you just fucking ruined it.”

    Glancing around at their group, and noting the several pairs of eyes on the scene that’s unfolding, Emily steps up to his brother, laying a hand on his arm.

    “Alex, take it down a no-“ He tears his arm away, not even sparing her a glance.

    “No! This cock sock will pay for the shirt he fucking damaged.”

    Eyes wide and glancing around frantically, Peter shakes his head, looking at Jason as steps closer to him too, crowding him.

    “I…I can’t afford that, I’m sorry.”

    Having had enough of his shit, Kate steps forward.

    “That’s enough, Kravis. Leave him alone.”

    Ignoring her too, Alexander’s face is twisted in anger and a sick kind of cruel satisfaction. “Oh, yeah? I’m gonna talk to the organizer then, make sure it’s docked from your pay. How about that? And make sure you never-”

    “I said, leave Peter alone, you dick.”

    Kate feels several eyes on her as the words leave her mouth, a bit louder than she intended, not just from their little circle. Instead of outrage, it seems Alexander is happy with her comment, ready to round on her almost immediately as his voice turns mocking again, but not losing the aggressive edge he used to intimidate Peter.

    “Awh, you are friends with the party photographer? That’s cute.-”

    “Careful, Kate.”

    Clint’s words do nothing to curb the anger rising in Kate’s chest, having had enough of all these assholes already. They are everything she remembered them to be, snobby, dickish, and cruel.

    “Did you guys meet at the unemployment office? No wait. Do you have a relative in jail too, photo-boy?”

    Lifting her chin, Kate levels Alexander with a look as he turns back to her with a cruel grin, her own stretching into a cold smile too.

    “Yeah, Alex. Most of us have friends other than our sister and the guy who secretly hopes you’ll get coked up enough one day to let him lick your asshole. Imagine that.” Next to Yelena, Sonya snorts into her champagne and Kate feels a mean satisfaction at the way Jason’s ears turn to a bright shade of red almost immediately. She would feel bad about the joke if both of these guys weren’t huge ass bigots, hidden beneath a few very thin layers of PR training.

    Yelena’s hand slides up her back again, exerting a small amount of pressure but this time Kate can’t tell if she is telling her to tone it down, or trying to reassure her. A second later, Yelena steps closer too, almost melting into Kate’s side and it fills her with an additional bout of confidence.

    Despite the animosity she already displayed, Alexander is visibly surprised by Kate biting back at his insults, probably used to subordinates and interns scurrying away at his bullying. He masks his surprise after a second, glancing at Yelena.

    “That’s rich coming from you, Bishop, when you are the one who had to show up here with an escort.”

    Yelena’s hand squeezing her side stops Kate from her initial response of simply punching him in his stupid fucking face, taking a quick breath to calm herself down before she laughs in his face.

    “Escort? That’s my fiancé, you sweaty fucking creep.”

    Almost like they discussed this beforehand, Yelena lifts her hand, showing off the ring and Kate chuckles at the theatrical gasp from Emily. Alexander looks surprised too, suddenly unable to come up with a response and Kate doubles down, looking him up and down demeaningly.

    “Okay, why don’t you take your premature bald spot and that abomination of a suit and fuck off?”

    For a moment, it feels like they could hear a pin drop in their circle, before Tommy starts laughing, loudly too, and Sonya and Yelena quickly follow suit. Kate lifts her chin and looks at Alexander unblinking, despite her heart beating double time.

    After a few seconds, when her brother doesn’t answer Kate’s insult, Emily seems to gather her wits the fastest, mimicking Kate’s stance and look.

    “You know what, Kate? We came over here to talk to you because we pitied you. Everyone here pities you.”

    While the comment does hurt Kate’s feelings a little, pulling on a few strings in her that she has so far ignored in favor of paying attention and playing her role, she doesn’t let it show. Instead, she chuckles, pulling Yelena slightly closer to herself without thinking about it, maybe subconsciously seeking support.

    “Well, everyone here is wasting their time then. I’m doing great.”

    Her answer feels a little flat, and Kate can see satisfaction glint in Emily’s eyes at getting a hit in, but before she can say anything and latch onto the sliver of insecurity she found, Yelena cuts Emily off.

    “Plus, it’s not like the rest of you are that far away from going into prison, hmm?” After a heartbeat, she leans closer to Emily to continue, lowering her voice almost like she is giving friendly advice, complete with a small smile on her face, and still, never stepping out of Kate’s half-embrace.

    “I’m sure that if a worried citizen informed the FBI about the investments your father knowingly made into precious metal mines managed by African warlords, they would certainly find it interesting, right?... As would his investors.”

    Emily’s face freezes and it’s only by having spent copious amounts of time around Yelena that helps Kate avoid doing the same.

    “Holy shit, Yelena. You can’t just say that to them.”

    At Clint’s voice in her ear suddenly, Kate startles slightly, but she still does a better job of hiding it than Tommy, whose entire body recoils, almost pouring his champagne down on himself. Thankfully, the Terrible Trio is too preoccupied by their shock at Yelena’s words to notice either of them, staring at her with their mouths slightly agape. “Who the fuck are you?”

    Alexander speaks only a second before her sister manages to get her bearings too, shaking her head with a chuckle that looks only slightly like she bit into a lemon. “That’s ridiculous.”

    Yelena leans back, and Kate thinks her heart is going to beat out of her chest, both from slight fear and also from how much she likes Yelena. If she is entirely honest, the smug little smile on her face is terribly attractive, sending a thrill down Kate’s spine and straight between her legs.

    Jesus, Kate. Not now.

    By chance, Kate catches sight of Agent Reyes making his way over through the crowd, to the bar that they are all standing close to, and quickly assesses their situation. They need to wrap this conversation up. Quickly. His catching onto the fact that Yelena is more than she seems is the last thing they need.

    It seems that Yelena has other plans.

    “Agent Reyes!”

    Without meaning to, Kate squeezes Yelena’s side at her words, barely able to conceal her eyes widening as Yelena waves at Agent Reyes, beckoning him to join their group. The Terrible Trio doesn’t seem to possess the same restraint over their facial muscles, their eyes widening and at least Alexander’s face turning completely ashen.

    He steps into their circle a moment later, his mother only a step behind, joining their expanding group as well.

    “Oh, Miss Rowley! Lovely to see you. But please, call me Daniel. I am not here as an agent tonight.”

    Agent Reyes’s smile is charming but as his eyes sweep over their group, Kate can see the predator under the surface. He might not be here as an Agent, but he certainly didn’t leave his badge at home.

    “Well, in that case, please call me Helena.”

    Stuffing down the anxiety she feels as much as she can, about this whole situation that Yelena orchestrated, Kate offers a polite smile to Agent Reyes as well, glancing around at their companions, while Yelena introduces Tommy and Sonya.

    “Daniel, do you know our friends Thomas Newhouse and Sonya Flores? And of course, Alexander and Emily Kravis, and their friend Jason Speyer.”

    Pleasantries are exchanged, the tight, ready-to-blow moment calming down to a simmer as they are all forced to behave in the presence of an FBI agent and a Senator. Agent Reyes also takes the opportunity to introduce his mother.

    “This is my mother, Senator Catherine Reyes.”

    Just like her son’s, Senator Reyes’ eyes are full of cutting intelligence, sweeping over their group and Kate feels her back straighten as it settles on her. She is beautiful, with brown hair and eyes, and very polished, which doesn’t surprise Kate, despite her research telling her the senator is from a poor, working-class family originally, having worked her way up to where she is now.

    Her son and she are ten times more dangerous than all the billionaire kids in their circle combined, and Kate focuses on them, pushing her spat with the spoiled Terrible Trio to the back of her mind.

    “Senator Reyes, a pleasure to meet you.-“ Kate shakes her hand, before putting it on the small of Yelena’s back again, glancing at her with a smile.

    “And this is my fiancé, Helena Rowley.”

    For once, the bead of sweat that she feels forming on the back of her neck is not from Yelena’s proximity or the whole pretend-relationship thing, or even from the convoluted social situation they all found themselves in, but from the two Reyes’ eyes almost pinning her with their weight.

    Seemingly, Alexander has already forgotten about Yelena’s somewhat veiled threat, because they are barely done shaking hands, before he is immediately in networking mode, stepping in to introduce himself and draw all of Senator Reyes’ attention to himself. Next to his mother, Agent Reyes meets Kate’s eyes, brow rising at her introducing Yelena as a fiancé, despite it supposedly being a secret. Kate shrugs, before nodding at him with a smile.

    “The cat’s out of the bag, I guess.”

    He nods back, half tilting his head with a smile, while Alexander yaps at his mother, lifting his champagne glass at them.

    “Congratulations. Again.”

    Not having a drink to salute him back with, Kate just smiles somewhat awkwardly, before looking at Yelena, sparing a moment to appreciate her beauty again. Taking a deep breath, she allows herself to ease out and exhale, the tight anxiety of the last few minutes keeping her muscles tense and her heart beating fast.

    “-working on healthcare reform, and the AI bill.”

    Alexander’s tone is smarmy and Kate wishes she could insult him again, but a tentative voice from behind her draws her from her thoughts.

    “May I take a photo of you?”

    It’s not that Kate forgot that Peter was somewhere around, but she didn’t think he would speak again, at least to their group, based on his fallen face and flaming red ears earlier. He disappeared from her sight after Alexander’s humiliating scene, and Kate did think that she would have to remember to find him again, to apologize and reassure him, but it seems he didn’t go far.

    Feeling a maybe displaced sense of guilt at the two still pink spots on his cheek, Kate smiles at him, before glancing at Yelena.

    “Oh. Um. Yeah, sure.”

    Stepping to the side and a bit back, so they don’t interrupt Alexander’s annoying bootlicking, Kate turns toward Peter, pulling Yelena with her by the hand. Tommy and Sonya join them too, the four of them posing for a quick photo, side by side. As Peter lifts his camera, Kate winds her arm around Yelena again, pulling her close, and taking a deep breath before she puts on her best smile, taught and trained into her as soon as she was brought to these parties. How much time until Jack’s speech? And more importantly, until they can go home? The camera clicks a few times, before Peter lowers it, offering them an almost nervous smile. “Thank you.”

    Letting go of Yelena, Kate steps closer to him, close enough that they can have a normal conversation without much risk of being overheard.

    “I’m sorry. About…”

    Glancing towards Alexander, who is still talking at a very distracted-looking Senator Reyes, Kate indicates what she means before her eyes move to meet Peter’s again. ”He is a huge dick. I’ll make sure you get paid, don’t worry.”

    Peter’s smile turns a little less nervous, and Kate resists the urge to reach out to clasp his shoulder. Ever since she was old enough to grasp it, her mother made sure that she knew and understood that nobody is better than other people, just because they were born rich and these types of situations, someone with power abusing someone without, have always made Kate furious.

    “Thank you, for standing up for me.”

    Kate waves it off, before glancing down at the camera.

    “I didn’t know you were a photographer.”

    His eyes glance around the room too, before his gaze settles on hers again. “Yeah, sometimes.”

    He looks painfully out of place in the fancy crowd and the expensive ballroom, and Kate chuckles at him fondly, while keeping track of Reyes and the others to their side. “Sometimes?”

    His smile turns a bit dorky, and he looks down.

    “Yeah. I have a couple of gigs to make rent.”

    Her chuckle is tempered into a smile, and Kate is about to wish him good night when she feels a small hand slide around her waist.

    “Hello.”

    Yelena slides up to them, having left behind the other group too, even if only a few steps away. Kate turns to smile at her, ignoring the shiver that threatens to overtake her body, at Yelena’s sudden touch.

    “Hi.”

    “Who’s your friend?”

    The question is pretty unnecessary, as Yelena was present when Alexander made a scene a few minutes ago, but it’s obviously meant to urge Kate to introduce them. “Oh, uh, yeah. This is Peter. He works at F.E.A.S.T. in Hell’s Kitchen…You know, where I went to volunteer a few weeks ago?”

    Yelena plays along, of course, nodding, but Kate can see something in her eyes. She is watching Peter with a type of interest she didn’t show to anyone tonight. Until now. “And Peter, this is my girlfr…fiancé, Helena.”

    At her stumble, Yelena smiles, reaching out to offer her hand to Peter. “Helena Rowley. Kate’s girlfriancé.”

    Peter chuckles at the joke, and Kate does too, despite her ears warming up. “Sorry. I’m still getting used to saying it.”

    Kate doesn’t miss the way his eyes glance at her, his eyes sharp for a moment, and she is suddenly struck by the realization that he was present for Amanda asking her out…or the other way around, whatever.

    Oh fu…

    He probably thinks she was cheating…or something.

    Awkward.

    “Peter Parker.”

    He thankfully doesn’t mention the incident, smiling at Yelena politely as he shakes her hand, even if he looks a bit awkward himself.

    “What do you do, Peter?”

    Yelena steps back next to Kate after the handshake, her eyes focused on Peter. What is she doing? Why is she so zoned in on Peter of all people?

    God, Kate really hopes Amanda doesn’t get brought up and brings a new layer of emotional turmoil to this already strenuous evening.

    Their eyes meeting, Kate quickly puts on a smile while Peter looks almost similarly awkward, lifting his camera a little as if he is showing it to Yelena.

    “I am a freelance photographer.”

    Kate knows why she is being nervous…but why is he?

    Yelena tilts her head slightly to the side, and just waits, until Peter continues. “I also, uh, work at a pizza place. And work at F.E.A.S.T…where I met Kate.” Slowly, Yelena nods, her face serious for a moment longer, until a smile takes it over again, her doting-girlfr-fiancé persona back in place.

    “Which pizza place?”

    This time, it’s hard for Kate to not turn to Yelena with an ‘are you serious?’ look on her face. Similarly, Peter looks a bit confused, but he answers dutifully.

    “Um. Joe’s? On Baker’s Street?”

    “Aha.”

    Before Yelena can ask Peter any questions, Kate chuckles, drawing her arms around Yelena again.

    “Anyway. We better let Peter get back to his job.”

    As Yelena looks up at her, Kate can see that she is displeased with the dismissal, but Peter seems almost relieved, stepping back. He is a strange little guy.

    “Yeah, yes. I, uh, better get back to it.”

    He does a little salute, that Kate feels is familiar to her from somewhere, and smiles at them one last time.

    “Bye, Kate, Helena. It was nice to meet you.”

    Kate waves at him, not stepping back to their earlier group yet.

    “Why are you playing 20 questions with the photographer?”

    Her voice hushed, Kate almost murmrurs the words into Yelena’s ear, leaning closer to make sure they are not overheard.

    “He is familiar.”

    “So?”

    Yelena leans away slightly to be able to meet her eyes, looking almost incredulous. “Kate, I remember almost everyone I ever meet. This never happens to me.” Sighing, Kate feels her lips twitch up into a smile.

    “What, that you don’t remember who he is?”

    “Yes.”

    Glancing around above Yelena’s head, but unable to keep her eyes from her green ones for longer than a few seconds, Kate shakes her head with a smile.

    “Maybe he just reminds you of someone.”

    They hold eye contact for a few seconds longer, before Yelena rolls her lips together, glancing to where Peter just disappeared.

    “Maybe.”

    “If you guys are done chatting about the party photographer, maybe you can go back and get to distracting Agent Reyes. It’s almost time.”

    At Clint’s grumpy words, Kate lifts her arm to check the time, realizing he is right. Jack’s speech is set to begin in about 10 minutes, and the two of them need to distract Reyes, so Sonya and Tommy can slip away and do what needs to be done…even if that means going back to the Terrible Trio.

    Ugh.

    Dropping her hands from around Yelena’s waist, Kate grabs her hand, pulling her back to the circle they formed earlier. It’s probably best if they stay close to Reyes, distraction or not… There is no stronger alibi for not having part in any funny business than him having eyes on them the whole time.

    Kate smiles to herself, satisfied with their plan...

    “…which is why, tax-cuts to business work. Not just for us, for the whole of the economy.” As satisfied as Kate feels, she doesn’t think she will ever reach the level of satisfaction Alexander seems to have with himself, still talking to the group, but seemingly most to Senator Reyes. Kate doesn’t know what he hopes to achieve, but judging by the expressions of both Agent and Senator Reyes he is definitely not succeeding, though he seems unaware. Catherine Reyes looks almost tired, a step away from rubbing at her face. “Well, I agree that supporting local businesses is an important part of our efforts to rejuvenate our nation’s economy.”

    It’s a diplomatic disagreement, probably not wanting to waste energy by engaging in an argument with another Senator’s aide. She smiles politely too, before clasping her hands together.

    “If you will excuse me, I have to use the powder room.”

    She steps away without waiting for affirmation from either of them, meeting her son’s eyes for a meaningful second. Kate doesn’t know either of them well enough to decipher what is being said, but there is a significance to the look, before Agent Reyes turns back to them, charming smile back in place.

    “Kate, Helena. How are you?”

    Resisting the urge to tense up under his scrutiny again, Kate smiles.

    “We are good. Enjoying the evening.”

    Agent Reyes nods, his eyes shifting to Yelena, then back to Kate.

    “Did I hear it right, that you helped to organize this party?”

    Alarm bells start ringing in Kate’s head, feeling a slight shift in his approach. Quickly, she chuckles, waving the question off.

    “Oh, no, not much. I just helped to make a couple phone calls, that’s all.” His eyes stay focused and unblinking for a few seconds before his features soften almost imperceptively and he smiles.

    “Well. However much or little, you did an amazing job. The party is beautiful.” With a smile that she hopes comes across as polite but grateful, Kate nods. From her side, Sonya joins the conversation.

    “It’s good practice anyway…”

    When multiple eyes turn to her, waiting for an explanation, Sonya supplies it with a smile. “For your wedding.”

    Exhaling, Kate envies Clint when he gets to groan into his mic, wishing she could do the same. Instead, she puts on a smile and glances at Yelena, hoping to convey…romance? Love? “Oh, yes. We are just starting out with that.”

    Turning her gaze back to the group, she sees Emily latch onto the topic with gusto. “Oh? If you need a good planner, let me know. I have a great contact at Fait Accompli.” If Kate didn’t know Emily any better, she’d think the offer is genuine, but after their conversation earlier, it’s highly unlikely. She smiles, however, not wanting to drag out their earlier conflict back in front of Agent Reyes.

    “Thanks…I will keep that in mind.”

    “And it seems you already have the photographer…”

    At Alexander’s joke, Kate turns to him, her cold smile the only answer she deigns the comment with. Jason chuckles, of course, ever the faithful lapdog.

    “Oh? Do you have anything set?”

    Agent Reyes sounds genuinely curious, explaining further when Kate’s quizzical eyes land on him.

    “As in, have you started booking things? Or do you have anything specific you know you want already?”

    Kate chuckles, glancing at Yelena to bide her time while she quickly pulls an answer out of her ass.

    “Oh. Uh, yeah. We are thinking a small ceremony at Lake Como. Two, or three hundred people max.”

    Yelena nods slowly with a smile, looking up at her like she is living a dream, and Kate’s stomach quakes at her expression. Gulping, she turns back to Agent Reyes. “But we only just started telling people, so…not much is set yet.”

    He nods with a smile, his sharp eyes sliding over to Yelena again.

    “Do your parents know, Helena?”

    Thankfully, Yelena lies as seamlessly as Kate has, drawing herself closer to Kate’s side. “No, not yet. I want to tell them in person, but I haven’t visited them since Kate proposed.” It’s a good explanation, and Agen Reyes accepts it with a nod and a smile as well. “Well, I wish you two a happy and long life together.”

    He lifts his champagne glass again and Kate feels herself blush, even though their supposed marriage has been mentioned several times just during the course of this evening already. What makes it worse, is that their whole group joins in, lifting their glasses to Yelena and Kate, echoing Agent Reyes’ congratulations. Sonya’s grin is unashamedly gleeful on the side, and Kate hears Clint groan under his breath again.

    Turning to Yelena, she looks almost bashful as she meets Kate’s eyes, the two of them smiling at each other. It’s awkward as hell, but Yelena looks beautiful and if it was real, Kate would be incredibly proud and smug at being able to marry such a gorgeous, smart woman. So, pushing her awkwardness aside, and pulls Yelena to her side, leaning down to press a peck against Yelena’s hair before turning back to the group, trying to display exactly that pride.

    “Thanks. Um, thank you, everyone.”

    The elated, borderline nice moment is broken by Clint swearing into their earpieces. “Shit… Okay, everyone, don’t panic.”

    With all of them in the present company, nobody can ask what is going on, but Kate clears her throat, hoping to convey the question they are all dying to ask…

    Also, who starts relaying information like that? Jesus Clint, get some bedside manners or something.

    It either works, or Clint just continues on, but either way, his next words freeze any elation Kate might have felt.

    “Fisk just pulled up. He will be in the elevator in a minute.”

    Across from them, Tommy spits out the mouthful of champagne he just drank, drawing everyone’s eyes to himself and allowing Yelena and Kate to exchange a quick, bewildered glance.

    “He has his wife with him…and no security. Just them.”

    Immediately, Kate’s mind and heart begin to race.

    “Kate…”

    How is he here? Isn’t he on the run? Or in hiding? What is happening?

    Yelena waits until Kate’s eyes meet hers to finish her sentence.

    “Come on. I want to dance. Excuse us.”

    Yelena is already in motion, grabbing her hand. Not waiting for their conversation partners, or even Sonya and Tommy, she starts to pull Kate away and deeper into the room. Briefly, Kate catches sight of Agent Reyes looking at them, his eyes jumping back to Thomas, who is still coughing, before looking at them again.

    “Dance? Now?”

    Yelena’s façade never drops, her face still light but Kate sees the slight tension in her shoulder.

    “Yes, dance! Do you not know how? I can lead.”

    Despite her heart pounding beneath her skin and adrenaline flooding her system, Kate quickly catches on, following her to the other side of the room, leaving their group unceremoniously behind.

    “Yes, I…I know how to dance. Let’s go.”

    In a few seconds, the two of them are in the middle of the dance floor, and Kate puts her hands on Yelena’s waist on autopilot, while she puts hers around Kate’s shoulders, pulling her close. Kate lets her, allowing her to lead too as they start to sway, not taking her eyes off the entrance.

    Fisk is here.

    Why?

    And how?

    Should they run?

    What does this mean for the plan? Is he here for her? Does he-

    “Stop being so rigid...”

    Whispering into her ear, Yelena stresses her words with two taps of her thumb against the skin of the back of Kate’s neck.

    “-At least try to look like you are enjoying dancing with me.”

    Yelena’s words, sounding playfully offended, and even more so, her natural, Russian accent, murmured so close to the skin of her cheek bring Kate back to reality and she exhales slowly, forcing herself to relax.

    After a few seconds, she speaks, half whispering into Yelena’s hair.

    “What is he doing here? What…Should we go?”

    Yelena hums, swaying slowly to the music, her words quiet when she speaks. “Barton, what is your assessment?”

    Kate hears Clint sigh, mulling their options over.

    “I…I don’t think he is here for you. I saw nobody else. Just him and his wife, and a few bodyguards, but they stayed downstairs. He is either here to keep an eye on you, or for something else completely...”

    Clint grunts to himself, a familiar sound of him thinking things over to Kate. He continues a moment later, and Kate can somehow hear that his eyebrows are drawn.

    “The party is drowning in politicians, he would be crazy to make a mess here. In public like this…”

    Humming against Kate’s cheek, Yelena nods slightly, and for a moment none of them speak. Clint speaks again, his voice tight but calm.

    “It’s still probably best to keep your distance... And get out as soon as we have what we came for.”

    Across the room, Kate catches Sonya’s eyes for a second, their earlier group still conversing around her.

    “What if we take him out?”

    At Yelena’s question, Kate pulls slightly away to look at her face, trying to gauge if she is serious.

    “Do not look at me like that, Kate. It is a valid option.”

    For a moment, Kate considers it. It would certainly make her life easier…probably. And isn’t that the end goal after they find him anyway? Take him in if they can, but take him out if they can’t…

    “No.”

    Clint’s tone is final, and Yelena huffs.

    “I know you had your fair share of assassinations, Barton, so do not play-“ “Yelena, we have not prepared for this. There is an FBI agent watching you all like a hawk, and a dozen politicians and several hundred people around. The risk of you all getting exposed is too high.”

    Yelena huffs again but doesn’t interrupt him.

    “-And who do you think they are going to suspect if he drops dead at the party?” Kate feels Yelena’s sigh against her cheek, her body sagging ever-so-slightly. “Okay, fine.”

    She is only quiet for a moment, the two of them swaying to the music. Yelena turns them so Kate has her back to the entrance, allowing Yelena to watch it instead. The hair on the back of Kate’s neck stands up and every few seconds she has to remind herself to ease up, her body coiling up for a fight.

    “Okay. We go forward with plan B. Sonya, you copy?”

    There is a hum on their comms channel, Sonya indicating that she is paying attention to their conversation before Yelena continues.

    “As soon as Jack starts speaking, Kate and I will slip away. We go and get the package. Sonya, you watch Fisk and keep Reyes occupied with Tommy, okay? You focus on Fisk. If Sonya has to split, Tommy, you are up on distracting Reyes. Do you copy?” Sonya hums again in the affirmative, and Tommy clears his throat twice in quick succession, which they assume is him agreeing. Kate exhales, getting herself mentally ready. “Okay. But if he comes close to Kate, you abort mission. We go home, and we’ll figure it out.”

    Eyebrows furrowing at Clint’s words, Kate wants to protest but Sonya hums again and Yelena quickly speaks, her breath tickling Kate’s neck.

    “Agreed.”

    Kate gently shakes her head, keeping her voice low but definitive.

    “No. No, we won’t get another chance like this. It has to work tonight, or we will never get it.”

    For a long moment, neither Clint nor Yelena speak, before he clears his throat. “We’ll cross that bridge if we come to it.”

    A minute passes, and in Kate’s muscles, anticipation builds. Feeling like she ran a marathon, she wants to apologize to Yelena about her sweaty palms, but her mind is still stuck on Fisk. What is he doing here? Does he suspect what they are planning? What if he is here for them? And what if he isn’t?

    “Is he here?”

    Quietly, she asks Yelena, but she shakes her head slightly, her cheek sliding against Kate’s. “Not yet.”

    Huffing, Kate pulls Yelena closer unconsciously, her heart refusing to slow down. “Two more things…Sonya, you need to pass me the drive.”

    Yelena waits for Sonya to hum again before continuing.

    “And can you follow him after the party? We need a confirmation of his address.” Sonya hums again, and Yelena exhales too, the last bit of almost undetectable tension leaving her body.

    “Go to the restroom, leave it in the last stall. I’ll pick it up when we go.” Sonya hums, and a second later, Kate sees her leave the group behind, distractedly endeared by Tommy’s eyes turning almost disappointed at her departure.

    Kate tries to focus on Yelena, instead of her nerves, but despite her wanting to enjoy the moment, even just for a little while, she finds it hard. Yelena dances with Kate for a few more moments, the two of them swaying gently to the music before she pulls slightly away again to look up at Kate, her face only inches away.

    “Are you okay?”

    Her words are quiet, maybe not even decipherable through their comms, and Kate gulps, before nodding, possibly trying to convince herself a little as well. Fisk’s presence, even the thought of it, has rattled her more than she thought it would.

    “Yeah… I’m good to go.”

    Yelena smiles, small but honest, her eyes never leaving Kate’s.

    “Not what I asked.”

    Huffing, Kate smiles, pulling Yelena back against her, not able to bear her green eyes looking so deeply into hers right now.

    “Yeah, I’m fine...”

    Yelena’s thumb strokes the back of her neck ever so slightly and Kate exhales, her face getting slightly squished against Yelena’s temple.

    “It’s just a shock. I thought he was in hiding. I didn’t expect to see him here….now.” Humming, Yelena nods, her breaths tickling Kate’s neck, now that she is not tilting her head back to look up at her. Kate wants to say that she is scared. That the images of his victims, the memories of him throwing Kate around like she weighs nothing haunts her. The thought of him going after her mother even more so.

    If it was only Yelena and her, she might have even said it.

    But Sonya, Tommy, and Clint are on the comms channel too, and however quietly they talk, she knows they will hear it too.

    So Kate says nothing, just taking a deep breath, trying to calm herself and enjoy the moment of having Yelena in her arms.

    “He is here.”

    Kate’s muscles tense up for a second, at Yelena’s quiet words and she pulls back, attempting to look. Before she can turn around, Yelena grabs her cheeks, her eyes catching Kate’s and not letting her look away.

    “Keep looking at me.”

    “But I-“ “Reyes is watching. Keep looking at me.”

    Her serious tone is in direct contrast with the wide smile spreading over her lips and Kate smiles back, becoming aware of the attention on them too, hoping it does not look too waxy. Yelena’s thumb strokes her cheekbone, before she bites down on her lip slightly, unintentionally succeeding in distracting Kate from Fisk’s presence, at least partially, and leans closer to whisper in Kate’s ear.

    “Now pretend I said something naughty.”

    Exhaling forcefully through her lips, Kate’s hand tightens on Yelena’s waist for a second, before she huffs out a chuckle, pulling away to look Yelena in the eye again. “Are we going back to the public display of affection angle?”

    At Kate’s amused voice, Yelena’s smile turns more honest, her eyes sparkling with something that looks awfully like affection, the moment ruined a second later by Clint’s gruff voice in their earpieces.

    “Can you two focus? It looks like Jack is about to get on stage.”

    Not even a full minute later, the music Kate and Yelena were dancing to begins to fade, a voice coming through the microphone instead.

    “Good evening, ladies and gentlemen!”

    A man Kate doesn’t know, dressed in an expensive tuxedo with his hair slicked back grins at the crowd, while Kate’s heart continues its steady and probably unhealthily fast rhythm against her chest.

    “Welcome to the 98th Annual Duquesne Ball! I am your emcee, Sam Clifford, and it is my utmost pleasure, to welcome the host of the evening to the stage, a man you all know and love, Jack Duquesne!”

    As the crowd begins to clap politely, Jack emerges from the side of the stage, the lights suddenly on him. He grins and waves, but Kate doesn’t get to focus much on her affection for him, as her hand is grabbed and Yelena begins to pull her toward the side of the room. “We are going. Keep Reyes occupied. And keep an eye on Fisk.”

    As she is being pulled through the room, Kate looks back, quickly checking on Reyes one last time, who seems to be preoccupied with Jack’s speech. Her eyes scan the room after, easily finding Wilson Fisk’s hulking form in the crowd standing next to none other than… Senator Reyes?!

    What the fuck?

    The two of them are engaged in conversation despite Jack speaking, leaning close to one another. A second later, they are pulled from Kate’s view, as Yelena leads them through a side door.

    “Did you see? He was talking to-“ “Yes, I saw. We will have to figure that out later.”

    Yelena cuts off Kate’s half-whispered question, eyes scanning the corridor they ended up on. By exiting from the side of the dance floor, they ended up in a corridor on the other side of the event hall, now having to go around to get to the staircase that will lead them upstairs. Kate nods to herself, trying to focus on the mission at hand.

    The two of them quickly walk down the corridor, taking a left and arriving at the coat room Kate noted earlier, with the view of the staircase across. Thankfully, the attendants seem to be enjoying their break provided by the speech and with nobody currently at their counter. There is only one person, close by, a young woman sitting at the registry desk, smiling politely at them as they get close by.

    “May I help you?”

    Kate shakes her head, pointing down the hall.

    “Just looking for the restroom, thank you.”

    The girl nods with a smile, and Kate follows Yelena, impressed at the speed of her walk in her high-heeled ankle boots.

    Yelena leads them across the entry hall, and to the left again, passing by the staircase and arriving to the ladies' room. Yelena enters first, Kate turning back to take an inconspicuous look back on the corridor to see if anyone followed them, but thankfully finding it deserted, apart from the girl at the registry desk, now immersed in her phone.

    Once inside, Yelena walks up to the last stall, her heels clicking against the hard marble underneath them, while Kate checks herself in the mirror, splashing a bit of cold water on her face while she talks to Clint.

    “Clint, do you have the cameras?”

    “Just say the word.”

    “Now. Tell me when it’s a go.”

    There are a few seconds of silence, Clint probably following the instructions Kate has given him, freezing the images on all the corridor cameras, and hopefully hiding Yelena’s and Kate’s ascent to the second floor of the event hall, where the office they target is on. Meanwhile, Yelena emerges from the bathroom stall, drive in hand, grumbling under her breath in a way that makes Kate smile, despite their circumstances.

    “You got it?”

    Huffing, Yelena meets Kate’s eyes and hands her the drive, before washing her hands. “Yes… Sonya, you didn’t have to hide it up there.”

    There is an amused huff on their comms channel, but unsurprisingly, no verbal answer, since Sonya is probably still surrounded by other guests.

    “Clint, are you done?”

    There is a grunt, that sounds more frustrated than affirmative.

    “One second.”

    Meeting Yelena’s eyes, Kate smiles, the two of them just standing in the middle of the expensive restroom. Yelena uses the spare few seconds to check herself in the mirror, running a hand through her hair and reapplying her lipstick, while Kate takes a few deep breaths to relax and watches Yelena as a distraction. The skin of her exposed back almost glows in the warm light and Kate’s eyes drop to trail her calf muscles as they flex when Yelena shifts forward, leaning closer to the mirror while she applies the lipstick on her bow-shaped lips. When Kate looks up, their eyes meet again in the mirror, Yelena catching her looking and Kate not looking away.

    “Okay, you are good to go.”

    Clint’s voice doesn’t completely break the moment, Yelena’s lips still tipping upwards before she turns back to the mirror, checking herself one last time. Clearing her throat, Kate puts her game face on, stepping towards the door and opening it for Yelena when she catches up to her.

    Exiting the bathroom, the two of them take a left, retracing their steps from a few minutes ago. The coatroom is still empty and Jack’s voice is still filtering out through the open entrance of the banquet hall.

    “…in his memory. He was a small man, but a great…”

    Turning left one more time, Kate quickly follows Yelena up the staircase, the office they have to get to visible as soon as they reach the top. There is a long corridor leading to it, with several doors on the right, and a floor-to-ceiling glass wall on the left, the whole New York skyline opening up.

    They walk down the corridor at a brisk speed, not sparing a glance at the amazing view, while Kate steadfastly ignores the memory of having fallen out of the window almost at this spot only 2 weeks ago, just a floor up.

    “Okay, I got eyes on you.”

    Clint’s rough voice sounds on their comms channel, while Jack’s also filters through from the floor below, faintly audible through Sonya and Tommy as well.

    “Good for you. We look great.”

    Clint snorts at Kate’s comment and she glances behind them, thankfully only finding the empty corridor.

    When they get to the office in the corner, it is surrounded by glass on three sides as well. The glass door is locked, but Yelena makes quick work of that with the lockpicking set pulled out from her little purse, while Kate periodically checks behind their backs, despite Clint having a much better vantage point to watch their backs.

    The room thankfully doesn’t have a separate security system, probably not much worth stealing compared to everything else inside the property, so when they get the door open about a minute later, that’s the last of their hurdles, apart from the computers. Kate quickly rounds the desk on the other side of the tastefully decorated room, taking a seat in front of the wall covered entirely by a bookshelf. It’s full of books and trinkets from around the world, illuminated dimly by the standing lamp Yelena turns on in the corner before she passes Kate the pen drive that contains her hacking tool.

    As Kate turns on the computer and begins to break into it, Yelena walks back to the entrance, taking over as their secondary lookout, Clint serving as the main one.

    “Shit.”

    Clint’s curse sends Kate’s heart racing even more than it already was, but she doesn’t stop typing, aware of the metaphorical ticking timebomb above their heads.

    “What?”

    “Nothing. Just keep going.”

    Groaning, Kate shoves the pen drive into the USB port of the computer, while exchanging a glance with Yelena.

    “Clint…”

    “Jack just thanked you for your help in organizing this party. He is looking for you in the crowd.”

    Closing her eyes, Kate takes a second, before she begins to type again, exclaiming. “Fuck.”

    Yelena speaks from her spot at the entrance.

    “Kate, keep going. Barton, do your thing.”

    Not taking her eyes off of the screen, Kate huffs, feeling the pressure mount on her shoulders. “I am…”

    It takes her a bit over a minute to break into the computer, while Clint fires the laser cutter arrow into the window above them, successfully cutting a hole in it, and lining up the shot to fire the USB arrow with the portable router.

    “Clint, I’m in.”

    “Taking the shot now.”

    Raising her eyes from the screen, Kate looks at Yelena again who looks as focused as ever, keeping her eyes on the corridor. Her heart pounding against her chest, Kate hates that she can’t see whether the shot is successful, that she cannot help if it goes wrong. Neither of them speaks, afraid to accidentally scare Clint into missing with a sudden word or something, at least on Kate’s part, but the worry is unfounded, his deep voice speaking through comms in a few seconds.

    “Okay, router in place. You are clear to go ahead.”

    “Yesss.”

    Kate can’t help but exclaim, almost jumping out of her chair with the release of anxiety, but she stays seated, waiting for the network to show up. Her muscles feel like they will vibrate off her bones with the amount of adrenaline in her veins, but Kate forces herself to exhale through her mouth slowly, jumping into action when the network ‘Venue 345 Secure’ shows up on the list.

    For the record, she wanted to call it ‘Wi Fi, Ms. American Pie’ after Yelena mentioned she liked the song the other day, but they got outvoted for “security reasons”. Booo.

    Through the new network, it takes Kate and Yelena’s hacking tool about two minutes to get into the computer upstairs. It’s good that she is the one up here, as the system is set up with a few extra layers of security, that would have caused a problem if it was only Sonya and Tommy up here, but for Kate, it’s pretty easy work.

    “I’m in. Starting the transfer now.”

    Quickly, Kate connects the drive to the computer, the transfer window booting up and beginning to count down.

    “22 minutes til finish.”

    Leaning back, Kate closes her eyes and exhales.

    The hardest part is done. They will just have to sit here and wait here until the transfer is done, take the drive and their gift bag on the way out, and get home. They can figure out the files, Fisk, and Senator Reyes later.

    Rubbing a hand on her face before opening her eyes, Kate looks at Yelena again, finding her already looking. She looks gorgeous in the dim, warm light, painting her hair a rich, golden color, and with the backdrop of the New York skyline, and when she smiles, seemingly letting some tension go too, Kate can’t help but mirror it.

    Through their earpieces, Kate hears clapping, before another speaker’s voice filters through, along with laughter from the audience, creating a nice, quiet buzz, not dissimilar from the TV playing at low volume in an otherwise dark room.

    The unpleasantness of the party is not forgotten, but Kate feels herself loosen just a little, and she hopes that she can carve this part into memory instead.

    For the next few minutes, Kate keeps an eye on the transfer, while trying to unwind and steal glances at Yelena, while also purposefully keeping her mind from straying to Fisk downstairs, what he might be doing with Senator Reyes, and the several uncomfortable conversations she had to be a part of.

    “Excuse me.”

    Through their earpieces, Kate hears Agent Reyes’ voice and immediately, her hackles are raised.

    “Restroom? I need to go too.”

    Tommy answers him, and they don’t hear Agent Reyes answer him in the next few seconds. Shit. Let’s hope that’s where Agent Reyes is going.

    “Clint?”

    “I don’t have eyes on the restrooms. I’ll only see them if they go to the entrance hall or the staircase.”

    “We are only at 39%, Clint. We need more time!”

    Two minutes pass, with only faint and incomprehensible noises coming through their channel, ending with flushing noises. By the door, Yelena shifts her weight and when Kate looks at her, she sees the tension in her form.

    “I need to make a phone call.”

    Presumably, Agent Reyes says that to Tommy, his voice a bit distant, but Thomas’ hesitation is crystal clear.

    “Oh…Do you want me to wait for you?”

    While not present, Kate internally cringes at the few moments of awkward silence. “Um...No. Thank you.”

    Shit.

    Is he trying to get rid of Tommy or does he really just have to make a phone call? “Okay, Tommy. Pretend to make a call too, but walk a bit further away. You are getting suspicious.”

    Yelena nods to herself, before walking back and forth once, while Kate keeps an eye on the countdown.

    13 minutes to go.

    “Sonya, can you go help him?”

    There is no answer for a few seconds, and Kate feels herself grow increasingly anxious. “She is in a group, talking next to Fisk and Senator Reyes. I don’t think she can go.” Shit.

    “Hey, Mom. How are you?”

    Tommy’s voice comes through the channel, and if it was any other situation, Kate would find it hilarious.

    “You can talk to us, as long as you have the phone to your ear.”

    Even if Kate didn’t see the smile on Yelena’s face, she could hear the amusement in her voice.

    “Oh, okay.”

    “What is he doing?”

    After Clint’s question, Tommy is silent for a few seconds, and his next answer is lower in volume.
