    “He is on the phone, but he is looking around. He is walking back and forth, looking down the corridor…He just looked at one of the cameras.”

    “Shit.”

    12 minutes to go.

    Meeting Yelena’s eyes, it seems they draw the same conclusion. As does Clint. “He is looking for you. How much longer?”

    Checking the monitor, Kate runs a hand through her hair, before she looks up at Yelena, seeing the intense focus on her face.

    “11 minutes, 45 seconds.”

    Standing up, she walks up to Yelena, checking down the corridor too before her eyes settle on Yelena instead.

    “Should we go? We can come back for the drive.”

    Wetting her lips, Yelena shakes her head, her eyes rising to meet Kate’s but Tommy speaks before she can.

    “Don’t come down now. I can see the bottom of the stairs from here. So can he.” Exhaling, Kate needs to exercise the tension in her body somehow. She walks up and down, trying to think of something, but doesn’t come up with anything. The two of them are essentially trapped in here until the transfer is done and Reyes hangs up or decides to go back to the party.

    Kate reclaims her seat at the desk, checking on their progress.

    52%. 10 minutes and 30 seconds to go.

    “Shit! Shit, he is going to the stairs.”

    Tommy’s whispering voice is alarmed and Kate’s heart begins to pound against her ribcage, eyes widening and jumping to Yelena while Clint reports too.

    “I see him too. Kate, he is going to you. ETA 45 seconds.”

    Yelena’s eyes are jumping around the room and Kate tries to think too. What are they supposed to do now? The office is made of glass, and there is no way to leave without being seen. There is nowhere to hide and-

    Kate looks at Yelena again, just as she takes a deep breath, and closes her eyes for a second. She is probably gearing up for a fight, getting their covers blown…

    Yelena comes up to the desk and pulls up her dress a little to sit on it. Her voice is a bit quiet but authoritative.

    “Kate, come here.”

    “What?”

    “30 seconds. Hurry up, get out of there.”

    “Come here.”

    Trusting Yelena blindly, Kate turns off the monitor and gets up from the chair. She walks around the table and steps closer to Yelena who grabs both of her wrists, pulling her in to stand between her open legs. Kate glances down, confused as Yelena uses her hold on her wrists to put her hands on the now-exposed skin of Yelena’s thighs.

    “Kiss me.”

    At those hurriedly whispered words, Kate’s head snaps up to look at Yelena, her stomach dropping to somewhere around her knees as she sees her glance down at Kate’s lips. “What?!”

    “20 seconds”

    Yelena’s eyes rise to meet hers again. They are a bit wide like she is struggling to comprehend this as much as Kate does, but her words are hurried, quiet, yet assured. “We are not here to steal information. We are young and horny. Kiss me.” She says the last bit looking deeply into Kate’s eyes, trying hard to make her comprehend. Oh.

    Oh.

    Understanding downs on Kate, and her mouth drops open slightly. Her eyes drop down at Yelena’s lips again, watching as her tongue darts out to wet them. Her mind is slow to catch up, however, and Yelena seems to be done waiting for her.

    Kate barely has time to mutter, “Oh, okay.”

    Before she is pulled down by a hand on the back of her neck, and suddenly… Suddenly Kate is kissing Yelena.

    She is vaguely aware of Clint’s voice in her ear saying “10 seco- Oh, Jesus..” but she has trouble comprehending his words. His voice and everything else begin to fade away, except for the thundering heartbeat in her ears and Yelena’s mouth moving against her own, slowly at first.

    Yelena’s lips are soft but insistent and Kate feels herself leaning into them, exhaling through her nose. Her hands seem to gain a mind of their own, because, without any supervision from her brain, they dig into the soft skin of Yelena’s thighs, and use them to pull her slightly closer to the edge of the table.

    Closer to Kate.

    There is a quiet gasp that rises from the back of Yelena’s throat, sighed right into her mouth, and with it, Kate loses herself.

    Almost forgetting about where they are, or why they are doing this in the first place, she leans into the kiss even more, sliding her tongue into Yelena’s mouth as her hand fists in Kate’s hair at the nape of her neck.

    One of her palms slides further under Yelena’s dress, higher up on her thigh, and almost onto her ass, and Kate feels the sharp heels of her shoes scrape against the back of her knees as Yelena uses her legs to pull her closer too. Her other hand is holding onto Kate’s arm, the one further under her dress, with a strong grip, almost like it’s an anchor, keeping Yelena tethered. Yelena’s mouth is warm and tastes like mint and champagne, and her tongue slides against Kate’s wet, and mind-numbing. Her hand leaves Kate’s arm a second later, to slide under her suit jacket and over the waistline of her pants, while the other remains wrapped in her hair. Kate has no idea how long they are there, kissing, and touching each other. She pulls away, her lips leaving Yelena’s, tilting her head to change the angle. The tip of Yelena's nose brushes against hers, tickling and sensual, when she hears a throat clearing. Clint’s throat being cleared, to be specific.

    “You can stop. He is gone.”

    Kate gulps, eyes rising to meet Yelena’s, only inches away. They are hooded and blink back at hers slowly.

    Once.

    Twice.

    For a moment, Kate sways forward, and for an insane second, she thinks she will kiss Yelena again but she halts, just short of touching her again.

    “He has been gone for almost a minute.”

    Clint’s voice is gruff, but Kate thinks there is a sliver of amusement under the dozens of layers of exasperation and grumpiness.

    “Aha.”

    Kate doesn’t know who she is talking to. Yelena? Clint? Herself? The two of them stay like that for a few heartbeats longer, before Yelena clears her throat too, but her voice comes out a bit husky nonetheless.

    “Kate?”

    Yelena’s voice is breathy, and Kate is mesmerized by the thought that it’s because of her. Kate sees her throat bob, as Yelena gulps, and her eyes lift slowly to meet green ones again. It takes her a second to answer, even non-vocally.

    “Hmm?”

    “Your hand is still on my ass.”

    There is a snicker on comms in her ears, quickly hidden under some coughs, and it helps Kate find her footing again. Sonya.

    Sonya, and Thomas, and Clint.

    They are here on a mission.

    “Aha. Um. Yes. Sorry.”

    She untangles herself from Yelena, pulling away and taking a step back. Running a hand through her hair, she doesn’t know what she is supposed to be doing for a moment. She doesn’t look at Yelena…She can’t.

    Her mind slowly rebooting, Kate walks back around the table, clearing her throat as she sits back down to check on the file transfer, straightening her tie.

    89%. 3 minutes and 15 seconds to go.

    For the next three minutes, Kate sits there, her mind short-circuiting while she stares blankly at the monitor in front of her, barely comprehending the percentage of files transferred rising. Her lips tingle, and her mind feels like there is a constant static going on inside of it, buzzing and humming.

    Was that…

    Was it only Kate, that kinda lost it? Was Yelena just playing her role or did she feel the same electricity, the same boiling and sizzling heat between them that just took Kate over? Because Kate had many first kisses and none of them were as mind-bending, toe-curling, and charged as this one.

    Kate’s body feels electrified, like she touched a live wire and the shock is still not gone from her system, the feeling stemming from the base of her spine. She feels like she could run for hours until she is drenched in sweat and unable to breathe.

    As quietly, as she can, Kate exhales through her mouth, still unable to look at Yelena. She feels too wired, too hot, too fucking turned on. From one kiss. Holy shit. Kate just kissed Yelena.

    The computer beeps when the transfer is done, startling Kate into kicking the bottom of the desk. Quickly, she glances at Yelena, who doesn’t look back at her this time, surveying the corridor again, for what or whom, Kate doesn’t know.

    Kate inserts the pen drive they bought along with the virus, which will wipe the entire server later tonight, but that only buys her about three additional minutes before she has to get up, and actually react to what just happened. Once the transfer is done, Kate clears her throat and pulls the pen drive out, plunging both that and the drive with the stolen files into her pocket as she stands up.

    “Okay, um, right. The files are transferred, the virus is installed. Let’s go.” Glancing at Yelena, she almost looks like she knows how Kate feels, not knowing how to proceed now, how to go on after what just happened, only glancing at Kate to nod. She looks almost like nothing happened, her dress back in place, only a few strands of hair out of place- “Have you turned off the computer?”

    To Clint’s question, Kate nods too, before she remembers he is probably too far to see that… she hopes. She really hopes he is too far to see what happens exactly in this room, like a small movement of someone’s head or hands…

    “Khrm, yes. Everything is as it was. Like we were never there. In and out like a pro. Like two pros.”

    At Kate’s word vomit, Clint just grunts and Kate adjusts her tie again and runs a hand through her hair as she steps up to the door, and near Yelena again. She glances at Yelena, finally finding her looking back and she risks a smile, trying to gauge where the kiss left them.

    The smile is not reciprocated, and Kate feels that bringing up what happened while Sonya, Clint, and Tommy are all listening is probably not the best way forward, so she clears her throat one final time and reaches to open the door.

    “Wait.”

    At Yelena’s voice, Kate’s hand halts and her heart begins to race again, although she is not sure if it ever stopped doing that. Yelena’s eyebrow twitches just for one heartbeat before she purses her lips, voice and accent back to normal as she raises a hand to gesture at Kate’s face. “You have lipstick...”

    Kicking the vague flash of disappointment to the deepest, horniest parts of her brain, Kate wipes at her chin, trying to calm her thundering heartbeat, and prays she doesn’t look as frazzled as she feels.

    “Now?”

    She lifts her gaze back to Yelena, who is looking at her with a look that she can’t decipher. “No, a bit higher.”

    Kate tries again, turning back to Yelena again, asking her wordlessly. Huffing, she shakes her head before stepping closer.

    Gently, she takes hold of Kate’s jaw with both hands, unintentionally sending Kate into cardiac arrest, probably, and tilts her head a bit before using her thumb to wipe away the stain.

    “Here. You are…”

    Not finishing the sentence, Yelena’s eyes lift from Kate’s chin to meet her gaze, before she nods and Kate nods back. She waits for Yelena to let go first, before stepping back and fiddling with her tie again.

    When Yelena doesn’t open the door still, Kate risks a glance at her again, finding her looking. For a moment, neither of them speaks as they look at one another, before Yelena huffs, sounding almost impatient.

    “Do I have lipstick on my face?”

    Eyebrows jumping up, Kate quickly shakes her head.

    “No. No, you look…You look perfect. Beautiful. Um, perfectly fine.”

    At Kate’s words, something changes in Yelena’s eyes, just a flicker of warmth or amusement, before that familiar sheet of nothing is pulled across her gaze. She becomes a blank sheet, giving away nothing and Kate sighs, before opening the door for her.

    Not the time.

    Not the place.

    She just hopes it will be the time soon. Really, really hopes.

    Because holy shit, that kiss was…

    Yelena leads the way out, her head held high and giving away nothing, but Kate sees the glance she sneaks at her. As they walk down the corridor, Kate can’t help but wonder if the tension she feels fizzing between them and which seems to be thick enough to be cut with a knife is good or very bad.

    She only gets to wonder for about a minute, while the two of them make their way down the corridor, halting at the top of the stairs.

    “Clint, are we clear to go down?”

    There is a moment of silence, Clint probably verifying they are okay to go back downstairs. “I knew you were a good one, Kate… One kiss, and you are ready to go down.” That is the comment that Sonya rejoins their comms conversation with, immediately eliciting a groan from Clint.

    “Jesus chr…Kids, please focus.”

    While Sonya snickers, Kate glances at Yelena, trying to get her reaction to Sonya’s joke, but her face is focused, looking down the stairs with her lips pursed, seemingly firmly in ‘mission mode’.

    “Kate, Yelena, yes, you are clear to go.”

    As Kate begins to descend the stairs with Yelena a step behind her, Sonya speaks again. “I think Fisk is about to leave. I’m gonna stay on him.”

    “Where is Agent Reyes?”

    Yelena’s question goes unanswered for a moment before Tommy joins their conversation. “He came back after he um…checked on you guys, spoke to his mother for about 2 minutes, then he left. About 10 minutes ago.”

    Exhaling slowly, Kate tries to find her center again.

    Relax, Kate.

    “Babe, put your hand down. You don’t need to touch it for it to work.”

    Ignoring Sonya’s comment, since it’s probably aimed at Tommy, Kate tries to think things through while the voices of the party, the soft, muffled music, and several hundred people talking slowly filter back into her consciousness.

    The evening is winding down, at least for them.

    They have what they wanted, and all in all, it went better than expected. If Fisk leaves, they could actually stick around, and enjoy the party a little, but Kate has no intention of spending any longer in this snakepit than she strictly has to.

    Nodding to herself, she turns to Yelena, hesitating only for a moment before offering her hand to take.

    “Right. Um, okay. Let’s…let’s say goodbye to Jack, and then get the fuck out of here, yeah?” Yelena glances down at the offered hand, and if Kate wasn’t looking at her, she would have missed it, but she sees the way Yelena’s throat bobs as she swallows. When her gaze rises and meets Kate’s again, she knows they have arrived at a turning point.

    Not at this minute maybe, but at tonight.

    When Clint goes to the airport and Sonya follows Fisk, the two of them will go home alone and Kate resolves herself to talk about this.

    About the kiss.

    About everything that has been brewing between them for the last few weeks. …But yeah, mostly about the kiss.

    Yelena takes her offered hand, and Kate fleetingly hopes it’s not sweaty before she begins to lead them down the entry hall, back to the entrance of the ballroom.

    “Kate, wait!”

    At Clint’s hurried words, Kate halts, eyebrows furrowing.

    “Wha-“ She never finishes her answer, swallowing the last few syllables as she finds herself face to face with none other than the man that has been chasing her across New York since August… Wilson Fisk.

This chapter also contains the scene that gave me the idea to write Blinding Lights in the first place...I think it's not hard to guess which one was it. :P (hint, it's near the end)

    What are we thinking? Do I need to go into witness protection?

Their way of talking (Alexander & Emily) is heavily influenced by my love for Succession. I do think that growing up the way she did and with the people she did, Kate probably has a mean side that she usually doesn't show but it exists +1: The terrible trio's names are all based on real life billionaire families in NY

    Chapter 25

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes The sensation in her chest is not dissimilar from how it felt when Fisk shoved her in that toy shop, making her practically fly across the room.

    He is just as huge as she remembers, towering even above her, and Kate is somewhat confused by the eye patch he has over his left eye but quickly throws that emotion aside. Instead, Kate is shocked, and shaken and most of all, she is angry.

    Rage immediately floods her system, the memories of the container on the ship, of the pictures that she has seen of the hundreds that he killed, or had murdered, flashing in her mind. The assassins, the dozens of men that have tried to kill her in the last few weeks, several of whom she had to kill in return, and her mother, small and scared in a hospital bed, and-

    The only thing grounding her is Yelena’s hand in hers.

    Yelena squeezes her hand gently, spurring Kate into action from her frozen state. Stepping back and a bit to the side, Kate positions herself slightly in front of Yelena, holding onto her in a vice grip.

    “Good to see you, Miss Bishop.”

    He has the audacity to talk to her, only enraging Kate more, now practically vibrating with her anger. She doesn’t act on it, only lifting her chin to look up at his hulking form, meeting his one eye.

    “Kate, be smart.”

    Clint’s words are in and out of her ear and her head in less than a second, completely missing the conscious part of her brain.

    “Mr. Fisk.”

    Glancing to the side, Kate sees his wife, a tall and slender woman with light brown hair, her eyes glued to Kate as well. Looking back at Fisk, Kate ignores her hammering heartbeat, not caring who hears her next words.

    “Are you here to try to kill me again? Or do you leave that strictly to your henchmen now?” The words are out of Kate’s mouth before she thinks them over, but she doesn’t think she would have swallowed them anyway, even if she did. Wilson Fisk blinks, and his brow twitches, confusion spreading across his wide, brute-like features.

    “I assure you, Miss Bishop, I have no idea what you are talking about.” Chuckling humorlessly, Kate shakes her head, not buying his obvious bullshit and never taking her eyes off of him.

    “Of course.”

    Lifting her chin to indicate at the eyepatch, Kate speaks again.

    “Did I do that?”

    Wilson Fisk’s face flinches and Kate sees the way his eyes flicker to the people around them. She knows several people are watching them, feels the weight of their gazes too, because even if the events of the last two months are not public knowledge, the fact that Kate is about to be the crown witness in the trial against her mother, where Fisk himself is heavily implicated, very much is.

    “No.”

    Tilting her head to the side, Kate purses her lips, letting every bit of her high society meanness filter through her voice.

    “That’s a shame.”

    Her skin feels like it will crawl off her body any second, with both the urge to do something and the disgust and hate she feels for him.

    “Kate, let’s go.”

    Yelena pulls on her hand, and Kate resists, Clint’s second warning going through her head unnoted and unprocessed again.

    “Kate, don’t do this. Walk away. I know you are mad but this is not-”

    Fisk smiles, and it looks more like a grimace, although Kate can’t tell if this is just how his meaty face looks, or if he is actually offended. He sighs, his eyes flickering to Yelena which sends a new wave of adrenaline and strengthens Kate’s already pretty overwhelming urge to punch him right here, in front of everyone.

    “Listen to your girlfriend, Miss Bishop… See you in court.”

    With that, he walks by them, his enormous body not even touching hers, yet Kate’s muscles lock up until he is several steps away. She is pulled along too in a second, as Yelena walks into the ballroom, holding Kate’s hand in hers in a vice grip.

    “What the hell, Kate?”

    Clint curses into their comms and Kate flinches, the sudden sound feeling loud and jarring in her ear, as the noise of the room comes crashing back as well. She doesn’t have an answer for him, especially with the dozens of eyes on her and Yelena, as she leads Kate across the room. Kate lifts her chin again, not giving anyone the satisfaction of seeing her affected by the encounter, even though it takes her almost the entire way to Jack’s group to for her hammering heartbeat to slow down.

    “Sweetie! There you are. I was looking for you!”

    Jack is in the company of at least two Armands, and three other older men Kate doesn’t know or care to identify, but she forces a polite smile onto her face as they come to a halt at the edge of their circle.

    “Sorry, Jack. I’m not feeling too well.”

    His smile drops as he is immediately overcome with concern, stepping closer and away from his group.

    “Oh, no! Are you alright?”

    Kate chuckles, still feeling wired and vibrating from all the adrenaline and excess energy she has bouncing in her body. The noise of the room, and the hundreds of people around them slowly becoming overstimulating.

    “Yeah, yeah. Just pulled my back, um, dancing.”

    It’s not the best excuse she has ever come up with, but his brows furrow and he looks genuinely crestfallen. Before he can talk or ask more, Kate speaks again. “Anyway, I think we will go home. Sleep it off.”

    “Oh, so soon?”

    Feeling her smile slowly becoming waxy, Kate nods, trying to keep her patience but Yelena takes over, her voice smooth and her accent American again. Her body molding into Kate’s from the side feels like the only thing holding her back from running out to do some laps, or better yet, chase Fisk and demand he answers for everything.

    “You know how Kate is. A lot of misplaced enthusiasm.”

    Jack and Yelena share a good-natured chuckle at her expense, and for once Kate doesn’t mind, just forcing a smile onto her face while she waits for the pleasantries to be done with so they can leave. After a moment, Jack nods, eyes shifting from her to Yelena and back. “Alright, then. It was lovely to meet you, Helena. Thank you for coming, both of you.” “You too, Mr. Duquesne.”

    He lifts a hand, as if he meant to clasp Yelena’s arm but seems to change his mind, putting it on the pommel of his sword instead, a conspiratory smile overtaking his features. “Please, call me Jack. And…maybe we can have brunch next week? I…I heard some rumors we might be family soon?”

    Kate thinks if she doesn’t have a heart attack tonight, she never will, as she feels her cheeks heat up at the reminder. Glancing at Yelena, Kate sees that she is smiling at Jack, firmly back in character as she glances up to meet Kate’s eyes, looking smitten.

    Chuckling, Kate turns back to Jack, drawing an arm around Yelena that somehow feels vastly different now, considering the same hand has been under her skirt, touching her skin barely 20 minutes ago. While Kate had her tongue in her mouth….

    Focus, Kate.

    “Yeah. Um, sorry I didn’t mention it yet. It didn’t…feel like the place.” Jack, waves her explanation off with a smile, giving them both a little conspiratory wink. “That’s quite alright, Katie. I know what that’s like…”

    He pauses for a second, and Kate knows what’s coming, her blood pressure rising in anticipation.

    “You should…you should really tell your mother though. I’m sure she would be happy to know.”

    Kate sighs, not having the patience to entertain the conversation or remind him that her mother and she are still not talking. Especially as far as he and others around them are concerned.

    “Yeah, Jack. Will do. Right, goodnight! And congratulations on the party.” He nods, his eyes warm and sincere, as he expresses his gratitude one last time. “Thank you for your help with it. It wouldn’t have been possible without you.” Exhaling through her nose, Kate does her best to smile, the urge to get out of here now so strong, that she can barely stay in place.

    “Of course. I’ll call you. Bye!”

    Finally, they are free to go, and Kate drops her arm from around Yelena to grab her hand and pull her across the room, just as she has a few minutes ago.

    They make it to the elevator without major interruptions, with only a few people waving or saying their farewells as they pass them by. The few seconds-long wait for the elevator feels like an eternity, but soon, they are in the cabin, the doors finally closing in front of them and cutting off the buzz and hum of the party for good.

    Thank fucking god.

    “Sonya, are you on Fisk?”

    Yelena drops her hand as she speaks, and when Kate turns to look at her, her eyes are looking ahead at the closed, golden doors. Kate’s head feels like it’s filled with bees, buzzing and moving around, and she can’t keep a thought down long enough for her to actually comprehend it.

    “Yes. Tommy and I are two cars behind him. He is going west on 31st.”

    “Do you need backup?”

    Kate asks, not really sure what her preferred answer would be. On one hand, she aches to go home, and maybe….maybe have that conversation with Yelena. On the other, she feels like she might explode, if she doesn’t get to put all the pent-up tension in her body into something physical.

    Chuckling, Sonya’s voice is warm.

    “No. We’ll tail him until he gets home, and then come back home too. Barton is right. We are not prepared to handle him tonight.”

    Exhaling, Kate nods, Sonya’s answer telling her what her preferred alternative was after all… because Kate doesn’t feel disappointed at being bounced back.

    “Okay, call if there is anything, 'kay?”

    “Sure thing, Hawkeye.”

    Despite the sarcastic voice, Kate smiles at Sonya’s answer, even more so when Clint huffs at it. Two small clicks indicate Sonya and Thomas disconnecting from their comms, probably reaching the edge of their range anyway, only a few seconds before the elevator doors open. Kate leads them through the lobby, accepting the complimentary gift bag with a distracted smile. They do not have to go through security on the way out, and Kate pulls out her phone to text their driver to come around the corner while tapping her feet, and biting down on her lower lip.

    The wired energy born from everything that happened tonight, especially in the last half an hour, shows no sign of dissipating. It feels like Kate’s limbs are filled with some type of substance, fizzing and buzzing in her veins and muscles, making her shift around and constantly check their surroundings…careful to not look at Yelena for too long. Their driver arrives barely a minute or two after Kate texts him, thankfully no queue in front of the building yet, with the majority of the guests still inside, enjoying the party. Checking around them one last time, Kate opens the door for Yelena, allowing her to slip inside before getting into the backseat as well, shutting the door behind her.

    The driver doesn’t say anything this time either, driving off once they both put their seatbelts on. Kate exhales slowly, wondering how different the mood in the car is than it was on the way here, while she presses the button to pull up the divider.

    “Okay, we are out.”

    Clint’s voice still sounds crystal clear when he answers, like he sits on the backseat between them.

    “Yeah, I saw you.”

    Glancing at Yelena, Kate sees her look out the window and a sudden nervousness at being alone with her gets added to the already humming tension in her body. There is also some unmistakable anticipation, and licks of desire from their kiss earlier still present in her system, creating a cocktail that makes her feel like even her teeth are buzzing. Just like they planned, Clint is in a car somewhere behind them, making sure that they are not followed home from the party by anyone who might have noted Kate’s attendance at the event.

    For the next 10 minutes, Kate sits there, her mind refusing to slow down while they wade through the traffic that is still busy, but significantly less so than on the way here. They make it to the corner of Central Park, signaling they only have a few minutes left of their journey home before anyone speaks again.

    “Okay, kid. I think you guys are good to go.”

    “Thank you, Clint.”

    He grunts, clearing his throat before he begins to say goodbye, probably already taking a turn to the left at the intersection that leads him away, toward Grills’ house as Kate hears his indicator click through their comms channel.

    “Right. When I get back, we’re gonna have a serious conversation about antagonizing mob bosses…. But for now, I’ve got a plane to catch.”

    Huffing out a chuckle, and trying to release some of her anxiety, Kate tries to get her mind together, taking a second to answer his gruffly said admonishment.

    “Noted. Take care of Lucky, okay? And tell Laura to send me pictures.”

    His voice is a bit warmer when he answers.

    “Will do, kid. Try to stay low while I’m gone.”

    Kate smiles, while her body continues to fizzle, all the nerve endings firing that usually end up getting her in trouble. Rolling her eyes, Kate shifts her weight in her seat and resists the urge to bounce her leg.

    “I’ll do my best.”

    “Take care, Yelena. Try to keep this one from getting into too much trouble.” Yelena huffs through her nose, which Kate recognizes as a chuckle when she looks at her profile and sees the way her smile lifts her cheeks.

    “Sure.”

    While Kate can’t see him, she gets the feeling that Clint is hesitating, trying to decide if he should say more, and secretly prays that he doesn’t. She really doesn’t need his misplaced fatherly advice mixed into this already pretty complicated situation. To get ahead of it, she quickly cuts off anything he might say.

    “See you, Hawkeye.”

    She thinks she hears him sigh before he speaks, his voice fond and amused. “See you, Hawkeye.”

    Kate hears the second amused huff from the seat beside her, as she pulls out and turns off her earpiece, while Yelena does the same.

    Finally, after everything that happened tonight, they are alone for good and Kate considers what she should say, how she should start, or if she should wait until they get home in a few minutes to begin this conversation.

    Sneaking a glance at Yelena, she is still looking out the window, and if Kate didn’t know her any better, she would think she looks nonchalant and unbothered.

    But by now, Kate does know her better and sees the tension in the way Yelena’s shoulder is pulled an inch higher than normal, or how there is a slight clench to Yelena’s jaw. What she doesn’t know, is if the tension that seems to be present in Yelena’s form is the same one humming in her own, singing and pulsing in her veins.

    For the next few minutes, Kate tries to come up with what to say while she is desperately trying to keep her thoughts in check. Her brain is filled with the events of the party, from the assholery of the Terrible Trio, their conversation with Agent Reyes, Fisk showing up and talking to Senator Reyes, meeting and talking to him, but most of all…

    Most of all, her thoughts are filled with the memories of Yelena’s lips against hers, their tongues sliding against each other. Yelena’s hand holding onto her for dear life and grasping Kate’s hair, pulling her closer. She remembers Yelena’s skin under her palm, soft and warm to her touch, and Kate shifts in her seat as feels desire stirring at the base of her spine. Rolling her lips together, Kate watches the lights of the city go by them, occasionally sneaking glances at Yelena and wondering what she is thinking about while trying to carve the image of her on the back seat into memory too. Several times, she opens her mouth to say something but finds it hard to decide what that something should be.

    ‘Hey, was this like the best fucking first kiss of your life too?’

    ‘Are you embarrassingly turned on or is it just me?’

    ‘That zipper looks like it might be hard to pull down alone, do you need help?’ Wait…Does Yelena’s dress even have a zipper?

    Anyway...

    ‘Do you want to come up for a drink and see if we work just as well when your best friend and my mentor are not listening to us go at it?’

    The last one makes her huff out an audible laugh, drawing Yelena’s eyes to her, while she is taking down her hair from its elegant half updo.

    Swallowing the rest of her chuckle, Kate loosens her tie, not exactly ready to explain what she was laughing at. Yelena keeps looking at her for a few more seconds, and Kate thinks she looks like she might say something too, but in the end, she turns back to looking out the window instead, remaining silent.

    For fucks sake, Kate.

    She has jumped out of buildings and fought super soldiers. Does she really not have the courage to ask the girl she likes and just kissed if she’d like to have dinner or a drink sometime?!

    Coward.

    “Hey, I-“ “We have arrived, Miss Bishop.”

    The driver's voice coming through the intercom makes Kate swallow the rest of her sentence, her pulse thrumming in her ear.

Trying to reroute her mind from tired and horny, to survival mode, which is apparently where they are now, Kate puts her hands on her hips, looking over the room again, with a different set of eyes.

    “Oh. Okay.”

    The corner is a good defensive position to be in, Yelena’s assessment is spotless as always, and for a moment, it barely registers for her that Yelena is walking away and leaving the room. Taking a few moments to reboot, Kate sighs to herself, and goes after Yelena, trying to gauge if there is something else they should be doing or how they are going to continue. In the living room, Yelena is in the process of pushing an armchair into a corner, that has both the front door and the bedroom in its line of sight. From somewhere, a gun with a silencer on its barrel has materialized in Yelena’s hand, and Kate’s mind feels too overcrowded with everything else to even really wonder where it came from.

    When she is satisfied with its position, Yelena takes a seat in the armchair, creating a confusing visual as her gun is still in hand but she is still wearing an oversized t-shirt that is obviously used for sleeping in.

    “What are you doing?”

    Irritation flares on Yelena’s features again and Kate watches as she purses her lips again, clearly in distaste.

    “I am keeping watch. Go, book the rooms, and sleep. We need to be up and out of here early.” Keeping watch…out here? From an armchair?

    ...Yeah, like hell!

    Shaking her head, Kate’s eyebrows furrow while her gaze never leaves Yelena’s. “What? No. You need to sleep too.”

    At that, Yelena rolls her eyes and Kate resists the urge to groan when she speaks. “I can stay up for 72 hours and still be functional. Now, go sleep.”

    Huffing, it’s Kate's turn to purse her lips in displeasure, rejecting the initial proposal easily. “Okay, I know you could like win a gold medal at the badassery Olympics, nobody is doubting that. But we can split the watch and you can get some sleep too.” When Yelena doesn’t answer or even look at her, Kate takes a metaphorical step back and tries to look at the events of the night with a different set of eyes. Yelena looked like she enjoyed everything thoroughly, but maybe she is having regrets. Maybe Kate came on too strong, or her flirting after she woke up on the couch was a bit too straightforward for where they are now.

    Despite her own desires, the last thing Kate wants is to make Yelena uncomfortable. “Hey…”

    Stepping one step further into the room, Kate catches Yelena’s eyes and tries to communicate her earnestness, holding her hands in front of her body.

    “If you think I’m going to, uh…try anything. I promise, I get it. It was a one-time thing, understood. You don’t have to…worry or…Yeah. I get it.”

    As she speaks, she sees Yelena’s face soften and almost immediately after Kate finishes speaking, she shakes her head.

    “I am not worried about that.”

    Exhaling, Kate feels some of her concern leave her body, and she offers Yelena a smile that she hopes looks reassuring too.

    “Then will you please come to bed?”

    Not looking away, Yelena sighs with a slight shake of her head.

    “It is much harder to stay awake if I am lying down.”

    If she is tried, Kate is at least partially responsible for that…which she does her best to not think about too deeply as she looks at Yelena, considering she just promised she will be on her best behavior. So, she offers to shoulder some of the burden.

    “Let me take the first watch then. I already slept some…And I have to book some more hotels anyway.”

    Her tiredness apparent, Yelena closes her eyes and the sigh of her name is tantalizingly familiar.

    “Kate…”

    She doesn’t mean for it to come out that way, but maybe the way Yelena says her name has at least a little part in the words that slip past her lips next, her tone a little flirtier than she intended.

    “Come on…I know tonight must have worn you out…”

    Thankfully, Yelena does not look offended or alarmed by her words, opening her eyes to lift a coy eyebrow at the expression. The smile on Kate’s lips turns into a small grin, and for a moment, the space between them fizzles with tension again, an invisible string pulling Kate closer to Yelena as her lips curl into a small smile too.

    Yelena’s eyes are dark, and the smile tucked into the corner of her lips curls up in Kate’s lower belly and heats her up again, but she keeps her distance. If that is what Yelena needs right now, Kate can give her that.

    After a moment, Yelena sighs and Kate knows she has won before she even opens her mouth, having to tamp down on the triumphant grin she feels rising onto her face. “Okay…”

    Standing up, Yelena walks over to her and this time, Kate resists the urge to look down at her form, holding her gaze as she meets her in the middle.

    “But,”

    Before Yelena even gives her conditions of defeat, Kate finds herself nodding, hanging on every word she says.

    “…if you hear anything, you have to come and get me.-”

    Yelena turns the gun around, holding its handle out to Kate and she takes it without hesitation, not looking away from Yelena’s dark, green eyes.

    “And if anything happens, you must not hesitate.”

    Nodding, Kate accepts the terms and means it. If she watches over Yelena, Kate will not hesitate, whatever happens. Holding onto the handle, Kate does not step away, and neither does Yelena.

    “I won’t... I promise I will keep us safe.”

    Blinking slowly, Yelena looks at her for a moment longer, before she nods. “Good.”

    And with that, she walks away to the bedroom. Even with the bed now tucked into the corner, Kate has a view of her, but she takes Yelena’s backup phone into her hands again instead, focusing on the task she entrusted her with.

    “If you begin to fall asleep, wake me up.”

    Pulling her gaze from the screen, Kate turns to look at Yelena and nods at her instructions. “Okay.”

    Yelena sits on the bed, leaning against the headboard, and her lower half is already under the sheets. She seems conflicted, her lips parting before she looks back at Kate. “Wake me up in 3 hours.”

    “Sure.”

    Kate knows she is lying this time. If she can make it until the morning, she will, making sure that Yelena gets as much rest as she needs. Lifting an eyebrow, Yelena doesn’t seem to believe her either, but she only holds Kate’s eyes for a few seconds longer, her gaze shifting over to her bag on the couch a few feet from Kate.

    “If anything happens, there are spare magazines in the left side pocket of my bag.” Nodding once more, Kate doesn’t take her eyes off of Yelena, who turns back to her, but only for a moment, apparently done sharing instructions as a second later, she begins to lie down without another word.

    “Goodnight.”

    For a few moments, Yelena is trying to find a comfortable position, and Kate thinks she didn’t hear her, but then, she receives her answer.

    “Goodnight, Kate.”

    Unsure why the simple act of saying goodnight sends her heart thudding against her chest, Kate turns away, trying to compartmentalize, and continues to do what Yelena asked. The suite is quiet around her, with no further sounds or comments from Yelena, and Kate is too far away to hear whether her breathing has evened out while she books a few more hotel rooms.

    By 4 am, Kate has finished booking the rooms, and she slides the phone into her pocket, taking hold of the handle of the gun, that has been lying across her lap until now. There are no sounds from outside, suspicious or otherwise, and Kate chances a glance at Yelena, her form somewhat illuminated by the dimmed lights of the living room filtering into the bedroom. From her position, Kate can’t see Yelena’s face, only a few strands of her hair, and if she focuses on it, the soft rise and fall of her chest as she sleeps on her side. The sliding door that could enclose the space has been left open, probably so Yelena can react quickly, if anything were to happen and Kate sighs as she takes her in, trying to stomp out the flashes of longing threatening to stir in her chest.

    Despite the flirting and the tension, Yelena has made it clear that their sleeping together was a one-time thing. Something that they “needed to get out of their system”, which doesn’t leave much room for argument, and in turn, that means while attraction and want are okay, longing and anything more serious than that is firmly off the table.

    Which is a shame.

    Because Kate thinks in any other world, she absolutely would and could have fallen for Yelena.

    But with Yelena drawing a very clear line in the sand, that is not something she should think about for too long. Doing her best to not take that as a rejection, even though it most likely is, Kate tries to think about the myriad of other things that happened tonight. First on the list is Fisk.

    Agent Reyes working or not working for him is one thing, but what the hell was he doing at that party in the first place? Why was he talking to a Senator? Is she involved with him somehow, or does he need something from her?

    Maybe they need to look into what committees and groups Agent Reyes is involved in because it might shine a light on what plans Kingpin has…other than getting Kate murdered. Also, does his showing up mean that he is done hiding, or was he never really in hiding anyway, just hard to find in general?

    These questions keep her occupied for a long time, her focus only briefly shifting when Yelena moves in her sleep a little.

    After that, Kate shelves the Fisk problem for now and considers the FBI. Even if they are not working with Fisk, their searching her apartment signals that they are investigating her for things that she actually did. Somehow, she has to get out from under their thumb but the problem is that Kate does not have the time to lay low for weeks on end until their trail runs cold or something.

    The formula is a ticking time bomb, even with them successfully wiping it off of Limitless’s servers earlier tonight, if for nothing else because her mom needs it for her deal. Which means, that even with the attention from the FBI on her, they need to keep going, and get the next piece. The one at her Hamptons house is easy but the other is with the FBI, so they will have to go ahead and steal it from under the nose of the same people who are after her.

    …Fuck…

    Kate really thought stealing the data from Limitless was the hard part… If she was absolutely sure, that Agent Reyes and Agent McLagan are clean, in a worst-case scenario, she could at least make a deal and read them in, but she is less and less sure of that, and they already promised to give the formula to her mom, to use in her deal, which makes it unavailable for Kate to trade for her own freedom.

    With a deep sigh, Kate rubs her face, quickly catching the gun when it begins to slide off of her lap and down to the ground. A quick glance confirms that Yelena is thankfully still asleep, and has not seen the embarrassing mishap, but Kate makes sure to keep a hand on the gun at all times after that and checks that the safety is on twice.

    Looking down at it, Kate shifts it around in her hand, pursing her lips in distaste. It’s a pistol like secret agents in movies have, with a silencer on its barrel, but Kate does not like it any less or more than any other gun. It reminds her of the death and destruction that seems to happen everywhere around Fisk, and now, even if to a lesser degree, around her. The latter is an even heavier thought than the first, so Kate pushes that away for now, lacking the mental energy to truly process it at 5 am, after the day she had, and with Yelena sleeping only a dozen or so feet away.

    Instead, she thinks about Fisk again, remembering Yelena’s words from the party. ‘What if we take him out?’

    If Sonya did manage to confirm Fisk’s address, that option enters the realm of possibility. That moral dilemma is one she also doesn’t think should be decided at 5 am, after the emotional rollercoaster of a day she had, but finds herself fixating on nonetheless. They do not have enough evidence for Fisk to be arrested and locked away for good and unless they get their hands on the three pieces of her mom’s ‘insurance policy’ that is wrapped up with the formula, they probably won’t either. Her life is not going to be her life, while he is free, maybe as long as he lives. He has wreaked Kate’s family’s life, her life, and countless others. He has murdered, and hurt, and intimidated…

    That said, it’s one thing to kill in self-defense. It’s one thing to kill when she is actively hunted and has no other choice.

    It’s a completely different thing to seek out someone, even a monster like Fisk, with the explicit intention of murdering him. Because that’s what they would be doing. Murder.

    But if they don’t do that, how many other innocent people will get hurt and die, until he is stopped? How many people like Annie, Wendy, or even her mom are going to end up as victims of his bottomless greed and endless violence?

    Using the hand that is not holding Yelena’s gun, Kate rubs her face again, sliding a bit lower in the armchair.

    Even the admittedly somewhat pitiful yearning she feels for Yelena is more pleasant than this thought process…

    Glancing at her again, Kate rolls her lips together and tries to find something to think about that doesn’t feel like an emotional or moral minefield. Even the thought of Lucky fills her chest with heaviness right now, and Kate feels the weight of the day settle more and more on her shoulders.

    For the next hour or so, Kate alternates between watching the door and watching Yelena, her mind repeatedly returning to the memories of them fucking in her bed, which are all more than mildly distracting, but at least they do an excellent job of keeping her awake. At 7 am sharp, Yelena begins to shift around in the bed, and Kate sits up a bit straighter, not wanting to look like someone who has been dozing off, her eyes seeking out the bed right away.

    “Kate?”

    Yelena’s voice is thick with sleep and Kate doesn’t even attempt to tamp down on her smile at it.

    “I’m here. Good morning.”

    Yelena stretches out, before half-sitting up, leaning back on her elbows. Her hair is adorably tousled, and her eyes are still half-lidded, but they find Kate immediately, taking in her position in the armchair.

    “You were supposed to wake me up.”

    Her smile widening, Kate shakes her head, her chest full of endearment and that silly, stupid longing, which she immediately tries to shove in a little mental box, and push somewhere deep in the back of her brain.

    “My power nap on the couch got me through the night so I wasn’t sleepy.” Even from the distance, Kate hears Yelena huff but she doesn’t say anything for now, lying back on the bed for a few more seconds before she sits up with a yawn. Kate should probably look away, it would be the smart and polite thing to do…

    But she doesn’t.

    She watches Yelena slip out from under the sheets, her oversized t-shirt riding up and exposing even more of her legs and the bottom of her ass as she stands up. When Yelena looks at her as she walks over, Kate meets her eyes, offering her an easy smile. “How did you sleep?”

    Running a hand through her messy hair, Yelena purses her lips, which look a bit swollen after her sleep, reminding Kate of how they looked after their shared kisses. Ugh. Boundaries, Kate. Focus.

    “Good. Do you want to sleep?”

    Kate really, really does, her limbs heavy and her body slightly aching from her cooped-up position.

    “No, I’m fine.”

    Yelena looks at her, blinking slowly and pursing her lips, pretty obviously not believing her words. Her eyes drop to Kate’s outfit for a second, and it’s only then, that Kate realizes that not only is she still wearing her clothes from yesterday, but she hasn’t showered since Yelena and she had sex… And, she doesn’t have any underwear on, nor did she bring anything to change into…

    All in all, not great.

    “How long do you think until I get my place back?”

    The tips of Yelena’s lips curl upwards as she looks up at Kate, her voice still a bit husky with sleep when she answers.

    “Hard to say. It depends on if we find bugs or not… There is still the cleanup to take care of either way.”

    Closing her eyes, Kate tilts her head back, exhaling slowly before she turns back to Yelena, meeting her eyes once again.

    “Okkkaayy. Do I have time to shower? We can go right after.”

    Yelena nods, her lips still tilted upwards but not quite smiling, and she takes the gun from Kate’s grasp without any other words spoken when she holds the handle out to her. Kate quickly showers after that but allows herself a few extra minutes in the warm water and perfect water pressure for her aching muscles to be soothed. She also washes her hair with the hotel shampoo and conditioner, finally ridding it of the product she used to slick it slightly back last night.

    With nothing to change into, Kate puts her clothes back on from the night before, scrunching up her face in distaste at the grimy feeling, and uses a toothbrush provided by the hotel. Once she thinks she is as clean as she is going to get, Kate exits the bathroom, her hair still hanging in wet strands around her face, since she does not want to spare time to properly dry it. Yelena sits on the armchair Kate spent the night in, dressed in a pair of high-waist jeans, a pink t-shirt, and Kate’s hoodie over it, which she seems to have taken as a souvenir from last night.

    If it’s a test of Kate’s professionalism, she totally passes it, her eyes only locking onto it for a short second and it’s not like Yelena can tell how her heart races at the thought… “You did not bring fresh clothes?”

    Pursing her lips, Kate looks back at Yelena as she stands up and walks over, trying to decide if she is serious.

    “I did not even bring a bag.”

    Rolling her eyes, Yelena turns away but if Kate is not mistaken, there was a smile hidden in the lines around her mouth. Why she is entertained by this revelation, is not entirely clear to her, but if Yelena were to ask why she forgot to bring or pack anything, Kate would be equally unsure how to articulate that it was Yelena’s “consolation prize” for her that made it impossible to consider that she should be bringing a bag, let alone what she would need to pack.

    They leave the suite together after that, Kate following a few steps behind Yelena, the two of them only stopping by the continental breakfast bar for a minute or two to pick up a few pastries to go as their breakfast and Kate chugging down a glass of orange juice like her life depends on it.

    Downstairs, the car keys and the valet ticket are taken from her grasp gently, Yelena taking over driving without a word, which is probably smart, considering the hours of sleep they had and didn’t have respectively. Kate is tired enough, that she is only internally endeared and amused, by how Yelena has to adjust her seat when she gets in behind the wheel, but does not bother coming up with any smart or funny remarks.

    On the way home, Yelena doubles back a couple of times, checking their mirrors constantly, and Kate trusts her with their safety completely, only keeping a casual eye out on their surroundings and munching on the croissant she nabbed from the breakfast bar. When they arrive safely, Yelena sends Kate up to her apartment alone, citing she needs to wake up Sonya and get gear to do the bug sweep. She also gives Kate strict instructions to not say anything she would not want the FBI to hear, even though she is confused about who she would be even talking to, considering she doesn’t even have a phone and there won't be anyone else there, until Yelena and Sonya come along. Yelena also tells her not to open her lair either, lest the sound of it alerts the agents potentially listening of its existence. Kate does as she is told, spending the first minutes in the apartment just changing out of her dirty clothes and internally wondering if Yelena will tell Sonya what happened the evening before as she quickly makes a cup of coffee. She thinks it will be easy to tell, Sonya probably not one to downplay her teasing if she does find out, but it’s a thought that keeps her occupied nonetheless, as she sets out to tidy up her bedroom first.

    Yelena and Sonya are still not up by the time she finishes that room, even putting on fresh sheets, and Kate resists the urge to lie down and take a nap while she waits for them to arrive. Instead, she moves on to the living room, surveying the chaos left in the wake of the search. If she didn’t know better, she would think the agents made such a big mess just to annoy her, because there is no way they thought she would hide the data drive they were looking for under the carpet.

    Ugh.

    All in all, it’s pretty miraculous that they did not end up finding her lair because they sure did a thorough job of turning the whole place upside down.

    With a tired huff, Kate begins the long process of trying to clean up her living room, her brain slowing down with the lack of sleep and making her walk around in pointless circles. She picks up things only to end up putting them down in favor of picking something else up, not doing anything with that either in the end.

    That is how Yelena and Sonya find her about 20 minutes later, walking in and taking in the scene. Kate doesn’t have to wonder if Yelena told Sonya what happened, the older Widow grinning from ear to ear as soon as she walks in and spots Kate, but she does not say anything, probably due to the suspected bugging. Yelena looks professional and focused, but when her eyes meet Kate’s just for a moment, there is a glint of amusement in them, so whatever commentary Sonya provided, must have been entertaining at least. “How is the cleanup going?”

    Running a hand through her hair at Sonya’s question, Kate tears her eyes away from Yelena to look over the living room, not in any way or form more orderly than it was when she started.

    “You know what, not great… Not great.”

    “Hm…That’s odd. I was told you do a great job with your hands.”

    There it is.

    As a somewhat tired chuckle bursts out of her chest, Kate can’t help but glance at Yelena, who definitely looks amused, despite the exasperated rolling of her eyes which avoid hers afterward. If Kate is not mistaken, there is also a slightly pinkish hue to her cheeks suddenly as she turns away. The same blush must be present on her own face as well, based on how warm her skin feels, and Kate chuckles once more, rubbing the back of her neck. “Well. Either way, I was thinking that this is too much of a mess for one person to handle… maybe I-we...We can stay at a hotel for a few more days, while I hire someone to sort this out. That’s reasonable, right?”

    Still grinning, Sonya waves her concerns off, stepping into the middle of the living room, looking over the chaos.

    “Nonsense, Kate, don’t be lazy. We’ll clean this up in no time.”

    With a deep sigh, Kate resigns herself to her fate, looking longingly in the direction of her sofa, mostly untouched by the mayhem.

    “Uhhh…It’s easy for you to say, at least you slept.”

    When there is no answer to her grumble, Kate looks at Sonya again, finding an eyebrow raised in her direction and the teasing grin almost splitting her face in half. “Oh, poor Kate Bishop. Did someone keep you up all night?”

    Swallowing, Kate looks at Yelena, trying to gauge how she should react. There is still the possibility of the FBI listening to their conversation, but with Yelena’s adamance about it being a one-time thing, it feels more than a little bit awkward to keep the thinly-veiled conversation about their sex life going….Also, can it be called a sex life if it only happened once?

    …

    Focus, Kate.

    “Well...I had an eventful evening.”

    That feels like the safest admission, but of course, Sonya is undeterred, her grin almost splitting her face in half.

    “Oh, I bet you did.”

    Yelena rolls her eyes one more time, before she picks up a pillow from the couch, currently thrown on the floor.

    “Are you done? We have a lot of shit to do.”

    Pursing her lips, Sonya does a little playful shimmy of her shoulders, before sliding by Kate’s side, throwing her a wink.

    “For now.”

    After that, Sonya doesn’t mention the evening anymore, but Kate catches a few amused and simultaneously calculated glances in her direction. That, at least keeps her mind occupied, throughout the mind-numbingly boring task of cleaning up her living room, becoming more and more curious about what exactly did Yelena tell Sonya.

    Room after room, they put everything back as it was, and while she is distracted and exhausted, Kate is immensely thankful for both the help and just the company of both Widows.

    Yelena’s presence is something that she remains extremely aware of, both her mind and eyes continuously having to be reminded to not stray to her every other minute. On her part, Yelena seems mostly unaffected, pragmatically putting things back where they belong, but there is mindfulness to how she avoids touching Kate again, which she can’t decide is a good or bad sign at first.

    The first time she notices it is in the bathroom, where there is relatively little space to maneuver around, to begin with. She turns back, almost bumping into Yelena, and if it wasn’t for her freaky, catlike grace, she definitely would have knocked into the cabinet behind her, with how fast she jumps back. Yelena sidesteps the moment becoming awkward like a pro, turning away immediately and putting something in there like it was her plan all along, but from then on, Kate is suspicious.

    The second time is when Kate takes a plate from her in the dining room, presumably taken out of one of the cupboards by the agents (why?! Why would they think something is hidden in there? Its doors are literally glass…They could just look in there! ), her hand accidentally touching Yelena’s. The plate falls to the ground, shattering, as Yelena immediately lets go of it as if she was burned. She looks almost surprised, based on the wide-eyed expression on her face, as she looks down at the broken pieces on the floor, but it only takes her about a second to pull herself together, rolling her eyes.

    “You are so clumsy sometimes…”

    Eyebrows drawing together, Kate answers on autopilot as she watches Yelena leave the room, probably in search of a broom.

    “Sorry.”

    It’s still too soon to tell if it’s good or bad, but after that, Kate is sure that something is going on.

    Is Yelena afraid of touching her? Afraid of what Kate will do?

    She seemed fine in the morning…

    But then, seeing someone the day after a one-night stand is usually a bit awkward…right? Kate doesn’t feel like it’s awkward, to be honest. Instead, she feels like it’s unfinished. Like, if Yelena was into it, she would be happy to jump back right where they left it, no sleep and all. But maybe it’s just because she didn’t finish, the second time. Although…She also doesn’t quite agree with Yelena’s assessment.

    This wasn’t something they needed or could “get out of their system”. There is a spark, whether she wants to admit it or not. It’ll be there, as long as they know each other but if that is what Yelena wants, Kate will keep to her boundaries…

    …As soon as she figures out what’s going on.

    The third time happens in the kitchen, the two of them alone for a few seconds while Sonya is somewhere else, Kate wouldn’t be able to tell where, even with a gun to her head. Yelena is trying to put a cereal box back on one of the upper shelves on her tiptoes but is just quite not able to reach it.

    Eager to test her theory, Kate steps up with a gentle hand on the small of Yelena’s back, taking the box out of her hand. Yelena freezes, immediately and for the entire duration of the few seconds it takes for Kate to slide the box in place, her hand still touching Yelena. She steps back after, barely so, and as Yelena turns around, her eyes are dark and full of that heated, swirly something again… before she sidesteps Kate just as Sonya enters the kitchen as well.

    Okay, so at least it’s not bad.

    There are no more instances after that, Yelena making sure to keep her distance, literally, for the remainder of their clean-up operation, at least six feet from Kate at all times. For her part, Kate is too tired to really dive into it, as even thinking feels exhausting, and she is more than ready to take a nap, once they are done with the tidying and bug-sweeping. Which is why, it takes an enormous amount of self-control to not groan out loud when they are almost done, and Yelena turns to her.

    “Kate, can you please go out and buy new phones and laptops for us?”

    It’s a logical request, and it’s even nice, mostly, since it means that Kate will not have to take part in the last half an hour of clean-up, and the subsequent bug-sweep but still… Kate just really, really wants to sleep.

    The last time she slept properly was before the party. Before seeing Fisk, being searched by the FBI, and…Before kissing Yelena, and then having sex with her.

    She is exhausted.

    Despite resisting the urge to groan, her feelings must be apparent on her face, because Yelena opens her eyes wide after that, gesturing vaguely around the apartment and then pointing at the two devices the Widows brought with them, presumably for the bug sweep. Closing her eyes, Kate nods, resigning herself to going out.

    “Yeah, sure…, babe.”

    She uses the term of endearment with the FBI agents listening in mind, but Sonya makes a surprised noise nonetheless, that Kate feels way too tired to decipher. Yelena at least smiles, nodding while she holds her eyes for a second, and this time it’s Kate who turns away, retreating to her bedroom for a few moments.

    It feels way too much of a hassle to put jeans on, but Kate does it anyway and pulls on a hoodie as well that is big and comfortable. Not wanting to bother with brushing her hair, she also puts on a baseball cap, then walks back out into the living room and to the doorway. After the eventful night they had, Kate pockets her retractable sword, praying that she doesn’t have to use it, along with her wallet and keys, before she goes back to the kitchen. “Do you want me to pick up some lunch as well?”

    Sticking her head in through the doorway, Kate meets Yelena’s eyes, taking a second to appreciate Yelena in the light streaming through the window. She looks beautiful, as always, and Kate still can’t quite wrap her mind around the fact that she saw her naked less than 24 hours ago.

    “Sure.”

    Yelena meets her eyes and Kate sees the warmth there again, as they drop to her form for a second, checking out what she is wearing.

    “Cool. I’ll be back in an hour tops.”

    Yelena nods, keeping their eyes connected until she glances at Sonya. Kate does the same, finding amused interest, and she pulls back, too tired to deal with the teasing. “Bye!”

    Her farewell is parroted by both Widows, and Kate walks out of her apartment less than a minute later, after slipping on a purple bomber jacket, mindful of the unpleasant weather outside.

    Thanks to the location of her apartment, she doesn’t need to drive, walking out onto the rainy sidewalk a few minutes later. Despite it being early afternoon, the sky is dark, heavy with thick rain clouds, and Kate pulls her hood over her baseball cap, trying to avoid the back of her neck getting rained on.

    It makes it harder to keep an eye on her surroundings, but Kate does her best on the way to the Fifth Avenue Apple store, using the reflective surfaces around her while her mind is tiredly flickering between topics.

    Yelena’s confusing behavior, Fisk, the FBI, and Sonya’s teasing comments all make fleeting appearances in the next ten minutes as she walks, the rain pouring down around her. Nobody follows her at least, as far as she can tell, leaving her to her jumbled thoughts and she arrives at the store without any problems or interruptions about 10 minutes later. The store is packed, as it probably always is, but thankfully most people are just there to look around, at least half of them tourists. Kate doesn’t stop by to look at the products, choosing to walk up to a counter directly, catching the eye of one of the employees. “Hi, my name is Aaron, how can I help you?”

    The following exchange is fairly straightforward; Kate buys three phones, two of the newest MacBooks, and an iPad, because Yelena seems to prefer tablets to laptops. Aaron is enthusiastic, and absentmindedly, Kate wonders if he gets commissions after his sales or not but gets distracted by two suspicious-looking men entering the store shortly after. They turn out to be German tourists, a gay couple if Kate is not mistaken, but it keeps her distracted for the remainder of her conversation with Aaron, almost agreeing to AppleCare+ in her preoccupied state. She does end up avoiding signing up for that, walking out with a huge paper bag full of her and Yelena’s new things about thirty minutes after her arrival. On the way back, Kate keeps an eye on her surroundings, but her mind is mostly engrossed in trying to make a decision on what food to bring back. The first restaurant she checks is a small and trendy brunch place along her way, but it’s packed to the brim with the Saturday crowd, even at the counter so she walks out almost immediately, not in the right mindset to deal with all that.

    Not wanting to waste time by checking more places, she takes a little detour to the diner Yelena and she went to the first morning after she arrived, feeling almost nostalgic as she thinks about it now.

    It is hard to believe, that not even two months have passed since, and how little she knew Yelena back then. Obviously, she wouldn’t call herself an expert now either but still, sitting across from her then, not knowing what to expect and unsure why she was even here in the first place, feels like a lifetime away.

    The door jingles when Kate opens it, and the diner is pretty much full as well, but as she anticipated, there are still a few empty spots at the counter. Remembering Yelena’s The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills accent, Kate smiles to herself as she takes a seat on one of the stools, picking up the menu.

    It’s almost strange to consider, how much Yelena and she have been through since that first breakfast together, and fleetingly, Kate wonders if the attraction has been there for the start, or if it was forged in their shared, intense experiences.

    Looking back, Kate had found Yelena beautiful back then too, remembering how she looked in the warm, morning light in one of the booths behind her. She was funny and charming, and very mysterious. The worrying but also exhilarating part though, is that the more she finds out about Yelena, the more Kate likes her. Her charm is not lost with her mystery being slowly unraveled, not even a little. Instead, it keeps intensifying.

    “What can I get you, honey?”

    Lost in her thoughts, Kate almost jumps when the waitress appears in front of her, having kind of zoned out staring at the menu. Quickly looking down at it, she remembers Yelena’s last order, and Sonya’s comment, and quickly makes a decision.

    “Can I get some pancakes with both butter and syrup, waffles with strawberry and whipped cream, and your bacon scrambled eggs? All to go.”

    The waitress scribbles her order onto her little notepad, before departing with a smile. It’s a girl she has seen here multiple times, who has pretty brown eyes and a kind smile. “Of course. I’ll be back with your order soon.”

    Feeling a bit embarrassed at her limited self-awareness, Kate quickly looks around, as discreetly as she can. She doesn’t spot anyone suspicious looking right away, but it’s also entirely possible that the type of people who are after her wound not stick out anyway. Which means…

    …She will have to double back at least once on her way home, to make sure she is not being followed. Ugh, dammit.

    With a sigh, Kate resigns herself to her fate and spends the next few minutes glancing around the diner, with no phone to keep her occupied. Theoretically, she could open one of the phones she bought, and start setting it up, but if she was without one this far, it can probably wait until she gets home.

    During her watch, her mind keeps straying back to Yelena’s more recent behavior, specifically the last 24 hours.

    She has been hot and cold before, but the last few hours almost gave Kate a whiplash. Yesterday, she was more than enthusiastic about sleeping together, and apart from a few moments of shyness that Kate is not even sure she didn’t imagine, Yelena did not look hesitant about the whole thing even for even a second.

    Then, when Kate tried to ask her out, Yelena said it was only a one-time thing and only something they needed to get out of their system.

    And yet…

    She would still have been happy to continue, if Valentina’s phone call, and then the FBI visit did not interrupt them. And even after the agents left, she made sure that Kate saw her, and continued their moment of weakness for a few heartbeats longer, as she changed. A consolation prize she called it…

    With a huffed-out chuckle, Kate shakes her head to herself, trying to untangle it all. Because barely an hour later at the hotel, Yelena totally changed her tune. Obviously, Kate understands that they had to be vigilant and that they could not just pick up where they left it, but still. If anyone else behaved the way Yelena did, Kate would describe it as skittish, but she is reluctant to call her that.

    But Yelena also said she wasn’t trying to keep her distance because she thought Kate was going to try anything, and she has agreed to let Kate keep them safe for the night, which she considers a pretty big deal.

    Talk about mixed messages.

    Which brings them to this morning, which was even more confusing than the evening and night before.

    Yelena obviously told Sonya what happened, and it’s not like Kate had doubts about her skills, but it’s nice to know that they have been well-received and most likely praised, based on the few sprinkled jokes and comments by Sonya.

    But at the same time, while Yelena seems to be aware that the fizzing tension behind them is far from being gone, she seemed to have been very mindful not to be physically close to Kate and accidentally touch her.

    Kate has been told enough times to know by now, that she has an overactive mind, and sometimes gets a bit in over her head, but she knows what she observed. She is certain. And it doesn’t make sense.

    Because if Yelena knows that Kate is not going to randomly jump her and that her message has been received, and she is convinced the sex was supposed to get rid of the distracting tension between them, why is she so afraid of being so physically close to her? There is a little voice in Kate’s head, the same one that whispered in her ear yesterday to do something, that supplies her with a dangerous, tantalizing idea.

    …Maybe that ‘one time’ is not as set in stone as Yelena made it seem…

    Maybe, she is afraid of touching Kate because her proximity makes her feel like there is sparkling, molten gold under her skin too, begging to be released.

    With a shake of her head, Kate tries to get rid of that traitorous, and torturous thought. There is no point in setting herself up for disappointment. Whatever Yelena’s reasons are, she has made it abundantly clear where she stands, in regard to their relationship, or whatever she wants to call it.

    And Kate does not know Yelena to say things she doesn’t mean.

    “Your order is ready. Can you come up to the register to pay?”

    This time, the waitress’s appearance does not startle Kate, having kept at least a small portion of her already somewhat limited brain capacity reserved for keeping an eye on her surroundings.

    “Thank you.”

    Walking parallel to the girl behind the counter, Kate goes to the register and pays for their brunch, leaving a generous tip in the jar as well.

    When she exits the restaurant, the rain is still going, and Kate briefly considers if she really has to do some defensive maneuvering before she gets home, both because she is exhausted, and because she is worried about their food getting wet and cold.

    But, it has been an intense 24 hours, and a voice that sounds suspiciously like Clint’s tells her to behave like an adult, so with an internal groan, she turns to the left, walking off in the opposite direction she needs to get home.

    The doubling back adds an additional 10 minutes to her walk, but at least it keeps her mind occupied. Nobody follows her this time around either, and Kate walks into her building 20 minutes later, exhausted and almost completely drenched, but at least feeling proud of herself for making the mature choice.

    In the elevator, rain drips from her coat and hair onto the floor, and Kate tries hard not to think of Lucky, who is always a big fan of playing out in the rain. She also wonders, what he might be up to right now, which immediately steers her thoughts towards Clint and the fact that she will have to catch him up on the FBI raid and everything else that happened after. Maybe after taking a short nap…

    The elevator opens on the 26th floor and Kate walks to her door, battling memories of doing the same with Yelena yesterday, and how it felt to pull her back to kiss her again. It might have been naïve, but Kate really thought they were getting somewhere…

    “Hi, I’m back!”

    If Kate didn’t know differently, she never would have guessed her place was searched by the FBI the night before, her living room satisfyingly in order as she walks in. Yelena and Sonya are nowhere to be seen, but her call is answered a few seconds later, from the direction of the kitchen.

    “In here!”

    It’s Yelena’s voice only, but as Kate takes off her jacket, toes off her wet shoes, and even sheds her now half-wet hoodie, she hears both Sonya and her, conversing quietly in the kitchen. Taking a quick detour into the bathroom, to get a towel to dry her hair with, Kate picks up both bags she brought back, and walks toward the kitchen.

    As she enters, her eyes are immediately drawn not toward Yelena for once, but to the two small electronic devices, placed in the middle of her kitchen island.

    Shit.

    Yelena was right.

    Eyes wide, her gaze jumps from the bugs to Yelena, who has a cup of coffee cradled in her hands, taking in Kate’s slightly wet-dog-like appearance. When their eyes meet, Kate mouths her words only, not wanting to be heard.

    “Are those…?”

    Yelena blinks slowly, almost catlike before she nods.

    The FBI is obviously watching her. They tried to bug her place, which means they had to get authorization, which in turn, means that there is some type of case being built against her. Shit.

    When will this day end?!

    “Yes. But we have turned them off, you can speak freely.”

    Wait, what?

    Walking fully into the room, Kate deposits the bag full of breakfast food onto the kitchen island and puts the big paper bag full of Apple devices to the side to handle later. Leaning over the kitchen island and inspecting the devices, her eyes rise to Yelena, shifting over to Sonya for a moment then back.

    “Won’t they know we found them then?”

    Yelena sighs, wetting her lips.

    “Yes, they will.”

    Eyes widening even more, Kate glances at Sonya, trying to understand why they are so calm about this. If the FBI knows that they know that they are listened to, it will almost certainly make their standing worse…If it’s even legal to turn off bugs placed by a federal ag- “Kate. I don’t think these are FBI bugs.”

    Blinking, Kate tries to understand what Yelena is trying to say.

    “What? How do you even know that?”

    Sonya picks up one of the little round devices and twists it around like taking an Oreo apart, showing the wires and little chip inside.

    “Devices made by police and intranational agencies always have serial numbers. They have to be trackable and physically identifiable, to be used in court. Their soldering is also different because theirs are built by machines. Look at this-“ Sonya points out some pieces of soldering to Kate inside the device, who has absolutely no idea what she is looking at.

    “-these ones are handmade. They are very well made and by a professional for sure, but they do not belong to the FBI or police.”

    Blinking twice at the device, Kate tries to understand what they are saying, her brain kind of running on fumes.

    “So…what does that mean? The FBI came in and planted bugs for someone else, or…?” Fisk maybe, after all?

    Exchanging a glance, this time it’s Yelena who answers.

    “I do not think so. Most likely, these were planted before yesterday…Possibly weeks ago.” Mouth dropping open in shock, Kate stares at her.

    “Who? When?”

    Shaking her head, Yelena looks frustrated with her own inability to answer Kate’s questions, while Sonya gets up from her spot from across Yelena, and begins to unpack their food. “I do not know… We will have to figure out who made these,”

    Pointing at the listening devices, Yelena exhales slowly, seemingly deep in thought as well. “-and try to trace it back to someone.”

    Nodding, Kate mulls it over, while she uses the towel in her hand to attempt to dry her dripping wet hair.

    “Could it be Fisk?”

    While Kate watches Yelena think it over for a second, lips pulled to the side, Sonya returns with plates and utensils for all of them.

    “If it was him, why aren’t you dead yet?”

    Sonya’s question is logical, and Yelena nods, wetting her lips.

    “That is what I keep going back to as well. If he had these planted, it would mean he knows where you live. Why did he not come from you yet?”

    Exhaling, Kate takes Sonya’s earlier seat across from Yelena, dropping the wet towel on the stool next to her, before rubbing her face. She is way too tired for this thought process. “You know what this means, yes?”
