    Kate tries to make her brain work, she really does, but it’s sluggish and despite the seriousness of the situation, at least a quarter of her brain capacity is taken up by yearning for her bed, while another, possibly even bigger portion is preoccupied by Yelena’s presence and attention.

    “That I still don’t get to go to sleep after this?”

    With a probably amused huff, Yelena shakes her head, her lips tilting upwards in an almost smile while next to them, Sonya is rustling loudly in the paper bag full of breakfast food. “I told you to wake me up.”

    After a moment, the barely there smile drops, Yelena looking almost apologetic. She takes a deep breath, holding Kate’s eyes.

    “The bugs we found…They use radio frequency transmitters, which means whoever was listening to them is relatively close.”

    Exhaling slowly, Kate looks back at Yelena.

    “How close?”

    Rubbing her forehead, Yelena looks down at the devices again, before meeting Kate’s eyes once more.

    “With the ones inside these, I’d say 100 meters, maximum.”

    Eyes widening, Kate takes a second to process the information. 100 meters…that’s like, 200 feet. Someone either in the building or in one across from them.

    “Shit.”

    Nodding, Yelena sighs too, sharing her sentiment.

    “Yes. So,…unfortunately, this apartment is compromised. At least until we figure out who is behind this.”

    Closing her eyes Kate leans her head back, resisting the urge to groan. “Okay…okay. I’ll pack up after we eat.”

    Opening her eyes, Kate picks up her fork, ready to dig in but a thought enters her head, making her eyebrows furrow. Someone was in here.

    “Where did you find them?”

    Already in the process of cutting up her pancakes, Yelena looks up at her, halting too while Sonya begins to eat.

    “One of them in the living room, hidden on the underside of one of the armchairs. The other was in your dining room, hidden in a lamp.”

    Huh.

    “We only brought those armchairs up for the first FBI visit a few weeks ago.” Yelena’s eyes widen slightly before she nods.

    “You are right!”

    Finally feeling a bit enthused, Kate stuffs a forkful of scrambled eggs into her mouth, pointing her fork at Yelena then.

    “It means it must have happened since then…And I was home a lot since then, so this kind of narrows it down.”

    Nodding to herself, Kate takes one more bite.

    “Do you have cameras in here?”

    At Sonya’s question, Kate looks up again, resisting the urge to look at Yelena. “Not in here, no. But I do have one hidden above the door outside.”

    She feels Yelena’s eyes on her as she says it, and sees the smile begin to rise on Sonya’s face as well, so quickly, Kate turns back to her food.

    “Excellent…We will have to go through the footage then. Thoroughly…”

    Ignoring Sonya’s somewhat teasing remark, Yelena leans back against her chair, regarding Kate seriously as she chews.

    “We also have to look at your cars.-“ Before Kate can ask her to elaborate, she nods to herself and continues. “Whoever got these in here might have put trackers on them too.”

    With a deep sigh, Kate nods before she remembers the end of the party yesterday and her eyes shift over to Sonya.

    “So, yesterday, did you manage to find out if Fisk lives at the address Maxine gave you guys?”

    Some of her good mood drains from Sonya’s face as she shakes her head.

    “No. His wife was dropped off there, but the car kept going. It went to a private garage in Queens, where we couldn’t go in after them. I sent Tommy home and waited, but if he came back out, it wasn’t through the same exit.”

    With a deep sigh, Kate nods, before rising her gaze back up at Sonya.

    “Thank you for going after him anyway.”

    With a smile, Sonya rolls her eyes, like it’s only natural that she would go after and follow one of the most notorious and dangerous criminals in the city.

    “You are welcome. We can check security footage around the area, but my best guess is that they went in there to switch cars, so I’ll doubt we’ll find them.”

    Humming in agreement, Kate continues eating, the three of them silent for a few seconds. Too tired to think about much, Kate continues eating, only re-engaging with Yelena and Sonya when she is close to finishing her eggs.

    “So what now?”

    Almost finished with her food too, Yelena halts her eating, pursing her lips in thought while Kate uses her remaining mental capacity to not think about kissing those soft lips less than 24 hours ago.

    “You go pack your things… For a few days at least. We will go downstairs and check your cars.”

    “And after that?”

    Breaking eye contact, Yelena maneuvers the final bite of her pancakes onto her fork, but she looks back up at Kate as she answers.

    “We’ll go to a motel. We will book a room for you with cash and a fake ID and you will stay there for a few days. Go over the footage above your door, while Sonya and I try to find out who bugged your place.”

    Furrowing her brow, Kate wants to argue. She can help figure out who bugged her place and she really doesn’t feel like getting benched right after they finally managed to successfully finish a mission…for the most part anyway.

    That said…

    It seems that Yelena needs space. And maybe, it will do Kate some good as well, because right now, she feels very confused with where they are and-

    “Do not worry. We will come to work with you every day. You just shouldn’t sleep here and Maxine is already taking up Sonya’s couch.”

    Maybe reading the conflict on her face, Yelena speaks with a somewhat softer voice, just a hint of humor coloring her voice.

    Oh, thank god.

    As her eyes jump to Sonya, Kate thinks that the suggestion of her staying in Yelena’s bedroom is not too far from being offered, which would probably be counterproductive to both of them, so she quickly agrees. That’s probably less confusing…for everyone involved. “Right. I…Okay. We should go and pick up the encryption from the Summer Place too, sometime this week while we wait for Clint’s contact to get a lead on the last piece.” Pulling her lips to the side, Yelena looks at Kate for a few seconds longer, but she looks away faster than she usually would.

    “Maybe…Maybe, but let’s see if we can figure out who bugged your place first. It is possible we have discussed it in the hearing range of the devices so they could know that is where you are going, and set up an ambush.”

    Swallowing the final few bits of her eggs, Kate’s eyebrows furrow even further, and she shakes her head.

    “Yeah, all the more reason to get it before someone beats us to it.”

    The muscles of Yelena’s jaw jump as she clenches them, distracting Kate from her slight frustration as their eyes meet again. Wetting her lips, Yelena opens her mouth to speak, her voice sounding like she is forcing herself to be patient when she does. “Kate, you either haven’t mentioned their hiding place, in which case there is no need to hurry, or you did, and then it is probably too late anyway because these could have been here for weeks. So, yes, we should wait until we know we are not walking into a trap, again…” Hoping to expel her annoyance with it, Kate takes a deep breath and exhales, winding down from her slightly misguided frustration.

    “Oh, okay…I guess that's reasonable.”

    Thankfully, it seems Yelena did not take her irritation seriously, as she only lifts a challenging eyebrow at Kate for a second, as she pins her with a look, but does not comment further on it. After that, they all get up from their seats, Sonya and Yelena taking over cleaning up after their meal, while Kate is sent to pack her things. She does her best to think it through, packing for about a week-long stay, when she hears her lair open.

    Dropping the sweatshirt she had in her hands onto the bed, Kate leaves the room to investigate, cringing slightly at the mess that is her lair now.

    It was so nice and tidy until now…Relatively speaking.

    “What are you guys doing?”

    Yelena doesn’t turn to look at her, as she wades through the piles of stuff they have brought and practically thrown in there the night before, Sonya answering Kate’s question in her stead.

    “It’s probably not a good idea to leave the drive here.”

    “Oh yeah, that’s a good point.”

    Kate probably looks as tired as she feels, because Sonya smiles at her, amusement making her eyes sparkle as she leans back against the doorway of the lair. Before any comments can be made about what, or who wore Kate out, she retreats to her bedroom to continue her packing.

    She will be ready for Sonya’s pointed remarks when she had some sleep…Probably. Trying to keep the stuff she will have to take back and forth to a minimum, Kate only puts a few outfits in her suitcase, and only when she thinks to pack a phone charger, does she remember the phones and computers she brought.

    Exiting her room again, she walks back to her kitchen, taking the whole paper bag back to her bedroom, so she will remember to bring Yelena’s things as well. The two Widows left a few minutes earlier, to go and check her cars, telling Kate to come after them when she is done packing.

    Kate decides to hide one unopened phone in her lair, should she lose another one in the following weeks, and she packs the other, along with her new laptop into her suitcase, leaving the third phone, the other Macbook, and the iPad for Yelena in the paper bag. From her lair, she also packs a collapsible bow, one quiver full of arrows, while her sword goes into the backpack that holds all her essentials and her wallet.

    When she is done packing, Kate zips up her suitcase and puts on a different hoodie-baseball cap combo, to keep her dry, the other two are still drenched from her previous outing. Her purple bomber jacket is a bit damp too, so Kate puts on a thick, oversized flannel shirt, before leaving and locking her door.

    The elevator takes her down to the garage level where her cars are stored, and she finds the two Widows scattered around the parking lot, each examining a different car. “Hi, I’m ready!”

    Yelena emerges first, holding up a circular device, before putting it into the pocket of Kate’s hoodie she still wears.

    “So far, every single one had a tracking device.”

    Letting go of the handle of her suitcase to rub her face, Kate groans.

    “Great.”

    “The ones I checked too.”

    Sonya comes up from the side, showing Kate her palm which has 4 circular devices in it. “Are these… um, homemade like the bugs you found?”

    Neither of them answers Kate’s question right away, Sonya pocketing 3 of the devices before beginning to take one apart. Yelena leans over, checking the process as well, while Kate just stands by their side, feeling a bit useless.

    “Yes. No serial code, handmade soldering. But, look at this.”

    Sonya uses her little finger to point something out to Yelena, and possibly to Kate, but she doesn’t know what she is looking at this time either.

    “-We could track that.”

    The corners of Yelena’s lips tilt upwards, a smile slowly overtaking her face as she exchanges a look with Sonya.

    “Gotcha.”

    Blinking, Kate steps closer, not wanting to be left completely out of the conversation, and thinks that this is probably a good learning opportunity.

    “What are we looking at?”

    Glancing up at her, Yelena points at the chip in the middle of the little device. “This is a third-party location relay chip. A company made this. If we find out who bought it, maybe we can figure out who made this, and who wanted to track you.”

    That does sound like good news, and Kate returns Yelena’s smile, even though she turns away from her a few seconds later, instead of keeping their eyes connected. “Great!”

    After a few seconds, when neither Widow offers more information, Kate poses her next question.

    “So how long do we think that is going to take?”

    The huff she receives in response from Yelena is mostly amused, her eyes filled with it too, as she looks up at Kate again.

    “Hard to tell. A few days at least.”

    Disappointed, Kate huffs too, but she smiles nonetheless, happy for the help. Without it, she wouldn’t even know she is being tracked or listened to, let alone be able to find out by whom. “Right. So still need to go to a hotel.”

    Wetting her lips, Yelena nods, her eyes crinkling with a smile that doesn’t show up on her face otherwise as she corrects Kate.

    “Motel. Or hostel. But yes.”

    Too tired to argue, Kate nods, before remembering the paper bag she has in her hands. “Before I forget. Phone, MacBook, iPad.”

    Holding out the bag to Yelena, Kate sees the raised eyebrow before Yelena voices her question.

    “I didn’t ask for an iPad.”

    Shrugging, Kate smiles, as Yelena looks into the bag.

    “Well. You prefer tablets, right? So I thought I would get both.”

    Before Yelena can answer, Sonya chuckles, drawing Kate’s eyes to her.

    “God, you really are easy to gold-dig.”

    Shaking her head and looking away for a second, Kate returns Sonya’s grin as she shrugs again.

    “Well. It’s my fault that hers got taken, so…”

    Not bothering to finish the sentence, Kate just gestures vaguely at the bag in Yelena’s hands, who meets her eyes again.

    “Thank you.”

    Kate’s grin softens into a smile and she nods at Yelena.

    “You are welcome.”

    Breaking eye contact soon after, Yelena puts the paper bag next to Kate’s suitcase, before turning back to Sonya and Kate.

    “Okay, let’s wrap this up.”

    Before they can fully walk away, Kate interrupts, stepping forward.

    “Which ones are clear already?”

    Turning away, Yelena points out the cars Sonya and she has already examined. “The three Mercedes, and the Porshe there are clear. Sonya, you did those four, yes?” Nodding, Sonya walks backward, before turning away to the car she was working on before Kate arrived. Kate watches them for the next 10 minutes, her eyes drawn to Yelena, whenever she can actually see her while fighting to stay awake.

    When they are finally done, all tracking devices are dumped in one car, which they will leave behind for now, before the two Widows join Kate at the entrance of the garage, looking over the cars too.

    “We’ll have to buy you a shitty car.”

    Blinking, Kate turns her head towards Sonya, an eyebrow rising at her statement. “Why?”

    “All of these are too nice if you are going to stay at a shitty motel.” Scrunching her face up, Kate turns to the other side to look at Yelena, who does not turn to meet her eyes.

    “Why does it have to be a shitty motel?”

    Ignoring Sonya’s chuckle, Kate keeps looking at Yelena, who rolls her eyes, before finally looking at her.

    “No serious ID check,-”

    She begins to count them off on her finger, looking exasperated, but at least she looks at Kate the whole way through.

    “They wouldn’t look for you there, less or no cameras at all.”

    With a resigned sigh, Kate accepts her fate.

    “Fine, but if I get murdered by a rando, I’m coming back to haunt both of your asses.” Finally, Yelena grins too, leaning closer ever so slightly.

    “If you get murdered by a rando, you will deserve it.”

    Pretending to be offended, Kate puts a hand over her chest, leaning back, while to her right, Sonya chuckles as she takes hold of Kate’s arm, and begins to pull her back toward the elevator, barely giving Kate time to grab her suitcase and pull it along. “You will be fine.”

    Eyebrows furrowing in genuine confusion, Kate turns to look at Sonya.

    “Where are we going?”

    Next to her, Sonya snickers and it’s Yelena who answers her question, walking behind them. “Your cars are compromised too, even without the trackers. We are taking mine.” Mind short-circuiting, Kate turns back towards Yelena, just before they reach the elevator. “You have a car?”

    Raising both eyebrows, Yelena looks unimpressed.

    “This is America, Kate. Of course, I have a car.”

    Blinking, Kate shakes her head, not possessing the energy to properly express her outrage. “Why did we always take mine then?”

    Following Sonya into the elevator, Kate feels petulant, especially when Yelena chuckles, not looking at her anymore.

    “I do not want my one car to get blown up when you have so many.”

    Pursing her lips, Kate ignores Sonya’s repeated snicker, following the two Widows out when they exit the elevator two levels below hers. Yelena’s car turns out to be a dark gray Aston Martin, with only two doors, which means Kate literally has to climb into the back seat from the front, which is pretty cramped for her long legs when she settles in. “I can’t believe you keep giving me shit about being rich when you have this car.” When their eyes meet in the rearview mirror, Yelena seems amused, the dim lights periodically illuminating her face as she drives up the spiral ramp to street level. “You have like 15 cars like this.”

    Sonya answers her from the passenger seat, turning slightly around to look Kate in the eye. “Still.”

    Rolling her eyes, Sonya turns back around, and the three of them are quiet for the next few minutes.

    “Do you have the drive?”

    At Kate’s question, Yelena looks at her in the rearview mirror, the car stopped at a red light for a few seconds.

    “Yes. Do you need it?”

    Shaking her head, Kate tries to slide a bit lower on the backseat, her knees hitting the back of Yelena’s seat.

    “No, just wanted to make sure it’s safe.”

    Looking away, Yelena drives forward when the light changes but she nods. “We are going to put it in Sonya’s safe until we have the rest of the components… Unless you want something else?”

    “No. No, that’s fine.”

    They are quiet for a few more minutes, Kate almost lulled into sleep by the traffic around them.

    “Do you have cash?”

    On the edge of falling properly asleep, Kate doesn’t answer the question, prompting Yelena to call her name.

    “Kate?”

    “Hm?”

    Opening her eyes that she does not remember closing, Kate meets Yelena’s gaze in the rearview mirror again.

    “I asked if you have cash.”

    Blinking, and sitting up more straight to keep herself awake, Kate glances out of the car to check where they are.

    “A couple thousand, yeah… Wait, are we going to Jersey?”

    Rain streaks down the windows, but it’s impossible to miss that Yelena is steering them toward Lincoln Tunnel.

    “Yes.”

    “Ugh.”

    Both Windows chuckle at her overly dramatic distaste, Sonya even shaking her head as Kate’s face scrunches up.

    “I’m just saying. There are perfectly fine serial-killer-infested motels in the city. There is no need to go to Jersey.”

    Huffing a chuckle through her nose, Yelena doesn’t look at her this time, but Kate sees the way she blinks slowly, the corner of her eyes crinkling.

    “New Jersey is out of the way but close. That is good if you want to lay low.” Closing her eyes again, Kate leans her head back against her seat, grumbling mostly to herself.

    “I could lay low without contracting hepatitis from a towel.”

    Her mutter is only answered by a pair of amused hums, and the rest of the journey is spent mostly in silence. Kate dozes off again, the experience strangely kind of reminding her of being driven to school back in the day.

    She comes to only when they are already in Jersey, driving along a big road, with moderately run-down buildings on both sides of it.

    “What about that?”

    Sonya’s question is obviously poised to Yelena, who shakes her head and keeps driving. “Hm, no. That’s too nice.”

    Rubbing her eyes, Kate groans from the back seat.

    “Come ooon.”

    While Sonya turns her head to glance at Kate directly, Yelena only looks at her through the mirror again.

    “That is what you wake up to? You slept through Yelena giving me a very detailed play-by- play of your evening.”

    Eyes widening, Kate’s gaze shifts over to Yelena, trying to gauge if she really missed something significant.

    What?!

    She really missed that? Did Yelena do that in English or Russian?

    Also…does hypnosis really exist, and could it potentially help Kate access her memories of what she heard while she was asleep?

    Yelena bursts out laughing, shaking her head at Sonya.

    “She just woke up, leave her be.”

    Grinning, Sonya shifts lower in her seat, snickering when Kate huffs in exasperation. If only she had something to throw at Sonya’s head…

    “You could have left her to believe it for a few more minutes.”

    Rubbing her face, Kate tries to wipe the sleep from her eyes.

    “You are mean.”

    It’s directed at Sonya, Kate even pulling her hands away from her face to glare at her on the front seat a bit. Of course, Sonya is not too bothered, turning her head again to look back at Kate as she shrugs with a grin.

    “I had a pretty troubled childhood.”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate can’t help but chuckle at that, looking out the window. The weather is really not doing any favors to the already pretty sketchy-looking area they are in, making the buildings they pass seem gray and grimy looking.

    Morbidly, Kate entertains the idea of how lame it would be, if, after all the assassination attempts and mobsters gunning for her head, she actually ended up murdered in a random motel on the side of the NJ-3. Maybe Yelena played the long game, and now if she is killed, enough people think that they are engaged, that she would inherit Kate’s considerable wealth…

    The thought process is entertaining enough, that it keeps Kate occupied for the next few minutes, her attention only shifting back to their surroundings when Yelena begins to indicate to the right and pulls into the parking lot of an incredibly, terribly, horrifyingly dirty-looking motel.

    “You can’t be serious.”

    Driving by the sign, put up probably somewhere in the 1950s, Yelena answers, her voice sounding suspiciously flat. The sign displays the name of the establishment, “The Wayside Inn”, which sounds exactly like the names of motels they find victims of serial killers in. “I am.”

    Shaking her head, Kate leans back further against her seat, as if she had a chance against both Widows if they truly wanted to remove her from her car.

    “I am not sleeping here.”

    Her proclamation is ignored, as Yelena pulls into a parking spot behind the building, next to a white van with flat tires. The motel is a grimy type of muted yellow, mixed with what must have been light blue at some point, but it’s only dirt-colored now, with doors to units both on the ground floor and on a second floor, reachable through a staircase.

    Below the name of the motel, in faded neon letters, it is also advertised, that the rooms are available at an hourly rate, and Kate’s skin crawls at the thought of putting her head down on any pillow or sheet in this place.

    “Hey. No. I will…Let’s go, buy a camper, huh? Or a tent. I will go to the woods. I will-” If Kate sounds like she is pleading, it’s because she is, but her pleas fall on deaf ears. Yelena turns the engine off, before turning slightly back, not quite meeting Kate’s eyes. “Do you trust me?”

    Despite her dire circumstances, Kate answers without hesitation.

    “Yeah.”

    Almost imperceptively, a few lines on Yelena’s face smooth, and she nods, finally meeting Kate’s eyes.

    “Then give me your cash.”

    Unable to help herself, Kate huffs out a chuckle but raises an eyebrow at Yelena’s words, in contrast with the smile she feels tugging at her lips.

    “How much?”

    “All of it.”

    “What?! How long do I have to stay in this motel slash organ farm?”

    The corner of Yelena’s lips tilts upwards, but she is back to serious a moment later. Instead of answering, she holds her hands out and Kate purses her lips, before reaching into her backpack with a sigh and pulling out a roll of hundred dollar notes, putting it in Yelena’s hand.

    “Wait here. Do not talk to anyone.”

    Sonya gets out too, leaving Kate alone in the car, the white van blocking her view of the office Yelena and Sonya must have gone to. For a few minutes, they are both gone, and Kate is annoyed with her past self for not setting up her new phone before, as she has nothing to entertain herself with as she waits.

    With nothing else to do, Kate just looks out the window, scouring her surroundings. The motel seems basically deserted, and Kate wonders if that makes it more or less likely that she will have to spend the night here.

    A few minutes later, Yelena and Sonya return, with a surprisingly well-dressed man, holding an umbrella above their heads. Even through the rain-streaked windows, Kate can tell that Yelena is slightly annoyed, while Sonya seems to be struggling to stifle a smile, which confuses her even more.

    Waiting for a sign or something from Yelena, Kate doesn’t get out right away, unsure if this is someone who is supposed to see her or not. Instead, she rolls the window down slightly, trying to catch the conversation through the pitter-patter of rain around them. “…nice to see that she is in one piece.”

    The man’s British accent is audible even from where Kate is sitting and he gestures vaguely in Kate’s direction, making her eyebrows furrow. Does she know this man? As she speaks, Yelena does look a bit smug, her annoyance fading just a little. “I told you I’d take care of her… Not even a scratch.”

    Well, that’s not entirely true. Kate definitely has had a few scratches and scrapes over the last few weeks… Come to think of it, she is pretty sure she has scratches from Yelena on her back, from the night before….

    Not now, monkey brain.

    “Good. She’s a beauty.”

    …Thanks, strange British guy?

    “-So, what? You want to trade her in for a shitty, old one?”

    Wait a minute…

    “No. I am keeping her and we also need a shitty, old one.”

    …okay. Maybe Kate has slightly miscalculated the topic of the conversation. Maybe the fact that both Yelena and the British guy are looking at the car, and Kate just happens to be sitting in it, should have tipped her off.

    …Whatever.

    Apart from two very short and unsatisfying naps, she hasn’t slept in like 30 hours. And it was a very eventful 30 hours.

    Finally, Yelena’s attention shifts, her eyes specifically moving to meet Kate’s at last. Her eyebrows furrow, seemingly in confusion, and a moment later she impatiently gestures for Kate to get out of the car, as if she was supposed to do that all along. How was she supposed to know that?

    She does so, a few seconds later, squinting as the rain immediately starts battering her face, cold and unrelenting. Stepping up to the trio under the overhanging outside hallway of the second floor, Kate waits to be introduced, her eyebrows jumping towards her hairline when he speaks without addressing her, just looking her over.

    “You just left her alone in the car? What if she suffocates?”

    Before Kate can react, Yelena scoffs loudly, a smile tugging at her lips. “She is not a baby, nor a dog. And it is not hot outside.”

    The man tilts his head to the side, a smile tugging at his lips as his eyes jump from Yelena to Kate and back.

    “Well, you did call her a baby-Avenger last time.”

    Huffing, Yelena kisses her teeth but it seems more faux annoyance than real frustration. “I guess I did.”

    When did Yelena talk to this man about her?

    “-Kate, this is Rick Mason. Mason, this is Kate Bishop.”

    That is all the explanation Kate gets for now, but she decides to roll with it for now, trusting Yelena to reveal what needs to be revealed…Also, maybe she is just a little bit hopeful, that their presence in this involuntary organ donor hotspot has reasons other than planning to stay here.

    This is why when he extends his hand, Kate reaches out to shake it with a smile, even letting the baby-Avenger comment go.

    “Hi.”

    His attention is fully on her now, his smile charming if a bit calculating. “So you are the one that has been stirring up trouble all over town.”

    Kate has an issue with his phrasing, but Yelena answers in her stead, her voice humored, if a bit tired.

    “She is.”

    Drawing his attention back to herself seems to not work for Yelena, because after dropping Kate’s hand, Rick Mason steps back, a friendly, but teasing smile sliding onto his face as he turns back to her.

    “And the one you've thrown away your peaceful 9 to 5 for.”

    That is definitely news to Kate, who watches Yelena for cues on how they are supposed to be acting. Are they supposed to keep up the rouse here? A little heads-up would have been nice…

    Yelena blinks slowly, unimpressed and Kate feels her spine straighten as genuine annoyance flickers on her face.

    “You really have to stop gossiping with my mother.”

    Yelena’s mother?!

    Yelena’s mother gossips about her and Kate with…whoever this man is?! Rick Mason? “Actually, your parents had nothing to do with this.”

    Blinking, Yelena’s annoyance seems to fade in favor of confusion.

    “What do you mean?”

    Rolling his lips together, Mason leans closer to Yelena, whispering to her conspiratorially, despite Sonya and Kate standing right next to them.

    “I hear things. All my little birdies woke up to sing the same song this morning.” An eyebrow rising, Yelena glances at Kate for a fraction of a second, before her attention is fully back on Mason.

    “And what song was that?”

    At Yelena’s question, Mason grins, his eyes shifting from her to Kate, Yelena following his gaze.

    “That a certain prodigal Upper East Side archer from a very renowned family has made her triumphant return to high society yesterday, with a mysterious and beautiful fiancé by her side.-”

    Who the hell is this guy?

    …Also, how did the news spread so fast?

    But he is not done, tilting his head the other way but never once taking his eyes off of Kate. “And that on the very same night, just a floor above the party in the very same building, if you’d believe it, one of the most prominent businessmen of the city, who also happens to be in a legal battle with said prodigal high society archer, has suffered one of the most devastating data breaches of the decade. Hundreds of terabytes of data lost, just like-“ He snaps with his hand, quickly turning to look at Yelena.

    “that. Gone. Quite a coincidence, huh?”

    When nobody answers his assessment, Mason…Rick?...Rick Mason lifts an eyebrow, leaning just a little bit closer to Yelena, and making the muscles of her jaw clench while he is at it. “Care to comment, dear Helena Rowley?”

    Yelena looks back at him in a way that makes Kate feel like they could hear a pin drop, despite the loud fall of rain still pouring down around them. Aiming to break the tension of the moment, Kate interjects, aiming to sound nonchalant.

    “For the record, Gossip Girl, I’m from Midtown East, not the Upper East Side.” Rick Mason’s gaze shifts back over to Kate, along with Yelena’s and Sonya’s, and Kate does her best to keep her poker face. Sonya is the first to snicker, followed by a grin from Mason, Yelena’s face being the last one to crack, not quite smiling, but softening nonetheless. “Ah! She speaks.”

    Not letting the man rile her up, Kate smiles, shifting her weight from one leg to the other. “She does. And she’d love to know who this guy is.”

    Her gaze shifts from Rick Mason to Yelena, and Kate lifts an eyebrow, finally asking for an explanation for what the fuck is going on. Yelena blinks slowly, once, before her lips spread into a bored but affectionate smile, but maybe not at Kate this time.

    “Mason is a procurer of things. Vehicles, weapons, documents…Sometimes information.” Okay, that does make it a little bit clearer.

    “-We are here to buy a car from him, and to get you a few fake IDs.”

    “I am also a friend.”

    Mason interjects with a smug smile and Yelena playfully rolls her eyes at his words. “That is a bit of a stretch, don’t you think?”

    He puts a hand over his chest, his face falling in faux offense.

    “That is so uncalled for. I just called you beautiful and mysterious.”

    Blinking slowly, Yelena purses her lips, but she looks undoubtedly amused. “Why don’t you call my mother and complain about it.”

    His façade breaks after that and Rick Mason shakes his head with a smile. Sighing in relief, Kate grins at Yelena, before giving the motel yet another distrustful look, but finding it easier to stomach, now that she knows she won’t have to stay here.

    “Looking forward to not catching syphilis from the breakfast bar.”

    Kate hears Rick Mason chuckle and turns back to look at him as he surveys the building as well.

    “I don’t think this fine establishment has a breakfast bar.”

    Sonya pipes up right after, finally deciding to join the conversation too. “Plus Yelena would never allow herself to catch an STD.”

    For her part, Yelena doesn’t seem particularly entertained by Sonya’s joke, and while it takes Kate a few seconds to catch the implication of the statement, she feels her ears warm up at it too, the event still too fresh in her mind to be comfortable joking about, at least in front of a stranger.

    “Oh la, la.”

    Kissing her teeth, Yelena throws Sonya a dirty glare, seemingly not in a joking mood either. “Are we here to do business or not?”

    Rick Mason does a pathetically bad attempt to hide his smile, and Kate sees him glancing at her once again, his eyes looking at her in a different light. He does seem to know where to draw the line, because a second later he nods, using the curled back end of his umbrella to point toward the far-away end of the motel.

    “We are. This way, please.”

    Yelena marches forward first, clearly not in the mood to deal with any of them, and Kate sees the amused glance Mason and Sonya exchange, as they walk after her a few seconds later. Kate closes their ranks, following after the two of them, the lack of sleep feeling heavy in her bones.

    Yelena struts forward until Mason calls after her, having stopped at a door a couple down from the last one.

    “In here.”

    He pulls a set of keys from the pocket of his nice leather jacket, opens the door, and motions for them to get inside while he stays behind for an additional few seconds to close his umbrella.

    Kate walks by him, their eyes meeting for a few seconds, not necessarily happy about the uncle-like amusement she sees in them either. She forgets all about it once she gets inside though, the room kind of exactly how she pictured the inside of this motel based on the outside, with decades-old furniture, complete with very suspicious looking stains. Thankfully, she does not make a fool of herself by mentioning it, because a moment later, Mason joins them inside the room, locking the door behind himself. He walks up to the closet, which if Kate saw in a movie or documentary, she would expect to contain human remains, and opens it up, reaching inside.

    Kate hears a click then, and Mason steps back once more, lifting his hand to usher them inside. Yelena goes first, not looking at any of them and Kate follows closely behind, finding a short corridor behind the fake backside of the closet.

    “Holy shit. I told you this place looked like a serial killer’s safe heaven.” The only response she gets from Yelena walking in front of her is a huff, with could either be amusement or annoyance, and Kate doesn’t push her luck to find out which one it is. Even more so, because behind her, Mason takes it upon himself to explain their surroundings. “Not quite. It used to be a secret FBI room in the 50s. They used to set people up before long- distance surveillance became more affordable. They’d lure them here, and either catch them in the act or film them from in here.”

    Halting in the middle of the short hallway, Kate turns her head back to look at him, face scrunching up.

    “What act?”

    Mason’s eyes crinkle as he grins, leaning closer to Kate and she already knows she is going to hate the answer.

    “Prostitution, mostly. Adultery. Sometimes more malicious stuff too, attempted rape or murder.”

    Turning back around, Kate begins walking again, answering dryly.

    “Awesome.”

    “Would not want to bring a blacklight into that room, huh.”

    Sonya pipes up from behind Kate, and her face scrunches up even more at yet another unpleasant thought added to the ones already swirling in her head. The hallway leads into a bigger, windowless room, which has obviously been more taken care of than the rest of the motel.

    The paint on the walls is fresh and there is a stool with a white photo backdrop, along with computers and monitors on a desk, a few file cabinets, a leather sofa, and weirdly, a big closet from IKEA.

    “Alright, let’s start with the photos.”

    Mason claps his two hands together, before turning over to Kate, looking her up and down once more.

    “First things first. Let’s get you into something less…‘rich off-season athlete’ and more ‘generic American woman’.”

    An eyebrow rising, Kate’s mouth drops slightly open, unsure if she should be offended or not and Mason grins, his eyes full of mirth.

    “Don’t get me wrong, it looks wonderful on you, but we are looking for different identities here.”

    Running her tongue over her teeth, Kate wants to be annoyed but a second later, her hand is grabbed and she is pulled forcefully toward the wardrobe by Sonya.

    “Come on, I love dress up.”

    Her wide eyes seek Yelena out, who took a seat on the leather sofa and doesn’t look at either of them.

    “Don’t worry about her. She is just a bit touchy right now.”

    The words are quiet, Sonya almost whispering to Kate, mindful of their privacy for once and when Kate turns her still-wide eyes at her, she winks. Kate is dragged across the room, Sonya only dropping her hand once they are both in front of the big wardrobe. “Have you been here before?”

    Sonya doesn’t answer right away, eyes squinting as she looks around the room, taking it in. “Not this one, no. But Rick has these all over, exactly for run-ins like this.” Nodding, Kate tries to take it on the chin and sheds her jacket when Sonya tells her to, her mind constantly playing catch up. The door of the closet is rolled to the side, revealing dozens, if not hundreds of items of clothing, and Sonya stands still only for a moment, looking them all over before she jumps into action.

    “The key to the good disguise is to only change one or two things at a time. That way you can spread a few accessories to at least a dozen or so different identities.” Blinking, Kate nods, her mind half preoccupied with trying to catch notes of Yelena’s and Mason’s quiet conversation behind them.

    “Right.”

    The discussion is too quiet for her to hear, however, but still, Kate just sheds her hoodie on autopilot when Sonya asks her.

    “Take that off and put this on.”

    The “this” in question is a thick, red, polo-neck sweater and Kate is almost pulled back into the present by it.

    Almost.

    When she notices Kate throwing a glance behind them one more time, Sonya sighs quietly, before leaning closer.

    “This will cheer her up too. She loves dress-up even more than I do. Just roll with it.” Kate sighs too, nodding to herself, before meeting Sonya’s eyes.

    “Okay...Okay.”

    Taking the jumper from Sonya’s hand, Kate pulls it on, scrunching her nose up at how scratchy it feels over her arms, left uncovered by the muscle shirt she wore under her hoodie. “Put this on too.”

    Handing Kate a pair of thick, black-rimmed glasses, Sonya steps by her to get behind her back, and a second later, Kate feels her hands beginning to arrange her hair. Before Kate knows it, her hair is in a bun, and as she looks into the mirror, next to the wardrobe, she can’t help but chuckle at the visual.

    “Wow, that’s…quite a look. Librarian on the top, off-season athlete on the bottom.” Sonya steps up next to her, looking at her work in the mirror as well with a grin, meeting Kate’s eyes.

    “You can’t see the bottom on the pictures…We are ready for number one.” She says the second half as she turns around, calling over to Yelena and Mason, who are still engaged in their conversation on the couch. Sonya’s interruption breaks it up, and Mason stands up, walking over to the desk to pick up a camera.

    Yelena stays seated, but when Kate looks at her, she seems to be in a better mood, amusement clear on her face as she takes her in.

    “Alright, please take a seat and look directly into the camera… Don’t smile.” The second half is added when Kate unintentionally looks at Yelena again and smiles, but she quickly wipes it off of her face, following Rick Mason’s instructions.

    “Almost like the DMV…just slightly less creepy.”

    Kate’s joke doesn’t land well with her international audience, and she sighs to herself, but a quick glance at Yelena confirms that she is still looking at Kate, and still seems to be in better spirits, which quickly smooths that particular burn at least.

    After the first, several more looks are created, with various accessories and ridiculous pieces of clothing. Kate has to admit, that even dead exhausted, this is kind of fun and Sonya turns out to be right, as Yelena joins their efforts around outfit number 4, leaving the leather couch behind to choose ridiculous pieces of clothing for Kate as well.

    Kate is even convinced (it doesn’t take that much convincing, to be honest) to put on a few wigs, and they end up creating Bimbo-Kate with a long blonde wig, which serves as the basis of at least four looks and makes Yelena giggle in a way Kate has never heard before. But as all things have to, the fun ends, when they have enough alter egos of Kate to fill a classroom, and the next thirty minutes are a lot less exciting, just the three of them cramped on the leather couch, waiting for Mason to finish creating Kate’s documents. Kate’s mood specifically, is also dampened by the fact that Yelena made sure that it was Sonya sitting in the middle, despite the fun they had until that point, apparently still not comfortable with getting too close to her.

    Just give it time, Kate…

    “Have you ever had a fake ID?”

    Sonya steadfastly ignores any weird, or weirder-than-usual vibes between them, keeping the conversation flowing.

    “No… If we really wanted to drink, we could usually nab a little from one of our parents’ liquor cabinets, without risking getting arrested.”

    There is no point in returning the question of course, since both Yelena and Sonya probably had more fraudulent identities than most people have shoes. That doesn’t mean Kate doesn’t have other questions, however.

    “Do you usually go as close to your real name as possible? Or the opposite, as different from it as you can?”

    There is a snicker from Sonya, and an amused huff from Yelena, making Kate’s eyebrows draw together. Is this not a logical question?

    “You’ll see.”

    Sonya sounds suspiciously amused, only serving to add to Kate’s confusion. “What does that mean?”

    When Sonya does not answer her question, Kate leans forward slightly, trying to catch Yelena’s eyes in hopes of receiving an explanation. Yelena does look at her, eyes warm and smiling, but she shakes her head.

    “That’s part of the fun.”

    Crossing her arms, Kate feels herself pouting but does nothing to put a stop to it, and even slides a bit lower in her seat when she hears Sonya huff out a chuckle a few seconds later. As a few more minutes go by, Kate’s annoyance passes, but the position she is in begins to make her sleepy again, despite how uncomfortable it is for her lower back. There is also no natural light in the room and the rhythmical clicking of Mason’s mouse, broken up periodically by short intervals of typing, serves as a perfectly lulling soundtrack bringing Kate closer and closer to dozing off.

    She is pulled out of it when a machine starts whirring loudly, causing Kate to jolt, and sit up straighter, trying to resist the pull of sleep. Sonya and Yelena perk up on her side too, and Kate glances at them, noting the soft smirk on Sonya’s face and the curiosity mixed with amusement.

    Mason stands up too, looking over at the three of them and throwing a grin in their direction as he walks up to the whirring machine, which Kate now recognizes as a printer of sorts. The humming of the machine halts for a few moments before it starts up again, and Mason picks up a colorful plastic card from it, turning it back and forth in his hands as he looks it over. He chuckles then, just as the machine pauses and spits out another card, and for the next couple minutes, the process repeats several times, more and more driving licenses and ID cards getting printed.

    When the machine finally quiets down, spitting out the last ID card, Mason walks over with the stack in his hand, as he looks over the last one. As it passes his quality check, which is what Kate assumes he is doing, he puts it on the top of the pile before passing it all to Kate. The one printed last is what Kate looks at first, huffing out a chuckle at the picture of herself in the blonde wig and white tennis polo. It’s a license issued in Florida, with the same birthday as hers and a new name…

    Kate bursts out laughing as soon as she reads it, looking up at Mason who looks very proud of himself for a man who is at least 40 years old.

    “Justine Beaver?”

    Sonya, who has leaned over to sneak a peek at the card, laughs too, and for a moment, Kate childishly wants to keep them to herself, since the Widows enjoy keeping things from her so much.

    She is the bigger person, however, literally, so a moment later she passes the card to her right so Sonya and Yelena can look at it together as she checks the next one. Christina Moans.

    River Seaman.

    Sally Pits.

    Barbara Itch.

    One after the other, Kate looks at the cards, shaking with laughter, the silly, puny names probably seeming funnier due to her exhaustion. She is close to tears, as she takes in the names paired with the weird, not-quite-right pictures of herself, her stomach beginning to ache.

    She finally loses it at ‘Sienna Cox-Holder’, no sound coming out of her anymore, just silent laughter shaking her body. Somehow, it escalates even more when she sees the final name, Charlie Watson, by far the most normal-sounding of all of them, also with the most Kate- looking picture.

    She feels the eyes of all three others on her, but the weight of the last 30-something hours catches up to her and she leans against Sonya as she continues to laugh, even a few tears finally escaping and trickling down her cheeks.

    “I think we lost her.”

    Sonya’s comment spurs Kate on even more, her jaw shaking a bit with her laughing, and only the sudden thought that it would really be easy for her to swing to the other side and start crying helps to start her calm down a bit.

    After she hands the last ID to her right, Kate wipes her face with the back of her hand, trying to take deep breaths to center herself.

    “You see? This is the type of appreciation my hard work deserves.”

    Her laughing fit is nearly restarted by Mason’s comment, the man using his thumb to gesture at her for Sonya’s and Yelena’s benefit.

    “You are not this funny. I think she is just finally losing it.”

    Yelena’s comment draws a scoff from Sonya, and she lifts a hand to pat Kate’s back, who still fights some giggles.

    “I am surprised it took this long. I expected it to happen yesterday.”

    She turns away to give a look to Yelena, but Kate can’t see its reception from her half- hunched-over position. When Yelena speaks a few seconds later, she completely disregards Sonya’s comment, holding up the last ID instead.

    “Charlie Watson…am I missing the joke on that one?”

    The comment threatens to restart Kate’s giggling fit, but she manages to keep herself under control this time. Shrugging, Mason leans back against his desk and crosses his arms. “No. I just ran out of inspiration.”

    Taking a deep breath, Kate asks her first coherent question since seeing the name on the first ID, trying to blow out her remaining giggles first.

    “Wooh…Are you responsible for Lizzie Humper?”

    Mason’s handsome face is split in half by a wide grin, his eyes jumping over to Yelena. “Yes, I am.”

    Returning the grin, Kate shakes her head at nothing in particular.

    “I’m impressed by the dedication.”

    His grin not waning, Rick Mason blinks before his gaze shifts over to Yelena. “You should bring her around more.”

    “Hopefully, we won’t need to.”

    After answering, Yelena stands up, turning to Kate for a moment to pass her the stack of ID cards and licenses.

    “We should get going. But first, does this look familiar to you?”

    The grin on Mason’s face is replaced by curiosity, as Yelena passes him something that Kate recognizes as one of the bugs found in her apartment. He takes it into his hand, twisting it apart just as Sonya has before, looking at the insides.

    “Hmm…Maybe. This is from her apartment?”

    Kate watches Yelena nod, her eyes swaying towards Kate but quickly returning to the device and Mason.

    “Yes. We think it is probably not law enforcement because there is no serial number. Plus, there is the soldering... It’s handmade.”

    Slowly, Mason nods, turning the device around once more.

    “Yes…But, look at the materials and the quality of the soldering…This was made to look simpler than it is.”

    Face scrunching up, Kate is waist-deep in confusion again. Or maybe still. What the hell does that mean?”

    Mason is deep in thought still, lifting the device closer to his face for one last examination, before he lowers it, looking back at Yelena.

    “I think someone is fucking with you.”

    Running a frustrated hand through her hair, Kate grumbles, tired honesty escaping her lips. “I know that.”

    Turning his head towards Kate, Mason shakes it quickly.

    “Not with you-“ He then uses his hand with the device to point at Yelena.

    “-with her.”

    What…

    How?

    Who?

    Why?

    Okay, Kate is completely lost.

    Yelena’s brow furrows, her face completely serious. She blinks twice, her gaze flickering down at the bug before she addresses Mason again.

    “Explain.”

    Mason puts the device back together, before holding it up and placing it in Yelena’s hand. “They stopped manufacturing this specific RF transmitter in 1994 and there is nobody in the world who has it anymore. I know because I sold the last few batches in 2014.” “Who did you sell them to?”

    Looking almost conflicted, Mason takes a deep breath, the muscles of his jaw jumping. He answers after a few seconds, looking at Yelena seriously.

    “Nat.”

    For a moment, Yelena is quiet, her eyes wide and Kate doesn’t know what to say or has the courage to break the suddenly tense silence. Then, Yelena speaks, her voice sharp. “What!? ”

    Shaking his head, Mason almost looks like he wants to step away and step toward Yelena at the same time, but he never moves. The fact that he knew Natasha is new information to Kate, but she thinks this is probably not the right time to start asking questions. “She needed them for something for Fury.”

    When neither of them, or even Sonya speaks after a few seconds, Kate shakes her head in confusion, drawing all three pairs of eyes to herself when she speaks.

    “I don’t get it…Why would Fury want to spy on me?”

    Glancing at Yelena once more, Mason shakes his head and looks back at Kate. “This is not Fury. At least…I don’t think so. I think he is back in space. Nat said that he wanted it because it’s what they used at the CIA in the 70s and ’80s, so...This thing must either be older than 2014, or made by someone who is or used to be CIA.” Wait a sec…

    CIA?

    Could it be…?

    Kate looks at Yelena, the two of them exchanging a quick but meaningful glance. Kate meets Sonya’s eyes for a second too, before Mason speaks again.

    “What was that?”

    Unsure how much they are supposed to tell him, Kate feigns innocence.

    “What?”

    Unsurprisingly, it does not work.

    “That look. You all looked at each other.”

    Wetting her lips slowly, Yelena looks down at the device for a long time, completely still. It feels like the quiet before a storm, and apparently, Mason knows better than to press right then, because he stays quiet too.

    “You don’t know if it’s her.”

    Sonya apparently doesn’t, but Kate assumes she knows and understands Yelena the best, out of the three of them. The sentence does break Yelena’s intense focus, and she pockets the device right after, her gaze returning to them. There is a storm brewing behind her eyes, and when she speaks, her voice is heavy.

    “Let’s go.”

    Sonya immediately gets up too, picking up and putting on her stylish trench coat, and Kate follows suit a few seconds later, putting her hoodie and flannel shirt back on. Mason stays quiet for a few seconds, his face serious. He walks over to pick up a set of keys from one of the drawers of the desk, but Kate sees the way his gaze shifts to Yelena a few times. There is something heavy in his eyes, and at first, Kate mistakes it for wariness, but when he passes an envelope to Yelena and holds her gaze for a few seconds in a silent exchange of sorts, she suddenly recognizes it for what it is.

    Worry.

    Whoever Rick Mason is, he cares about Yelena and is worried about her. Not just her, but her emotional state.

    Which begs the question: How close was he to Natasha exactly?

    But as she takes a quick glance at Yelena’s face, Kate knows that this is not the right time to ask it.

    The possibility, that not only did Valentina and Rojas possibly spy on them, but they might have used something connected to Yelena’s sister specifically to fuck with her head, obviously weighs on her. She walks ahead alone again, as the four of them exit the creepy secret room through the even creepier corridor, and then walk through the creepy and gross hotel room.

    Outside, Yelena waits for the three of them to catch up wordlessly, and then falls into step next to Sonya, as Mason and Kate walk a few steps behind them. The two of them exchange a few quiet sentences in Russian, the fun atmosphere of the fake ID photoshoot gone for good.

    “How old are you?”

    Having been preoccupied with staring at the back of Yelena’s blonde head, Kate takes a second to answer Rick Mason’s question.

    “Twenty-four… Why?”

    Mason doesn’t say anything for a few seconds, and Kate glances at him to try to gauge the direction of this exchange.

    “Just making conversation.”

    Blinking, Kate feels the corner of her mouth lift, exhaling through her nose in lieu of a tired chuckle.

    “Your way of making conversation with people is to ask them how old they are?” Mason returns Kate’s barely there smile but sidesteps her indirect question. “Sometimes. How long have you been doing this?”

    Deciding to not give him any information if he is not willing to provide any in return, Kate raises an eyebrow but turns back forward to watch where she is going, the pavement around the hotel cracked and uneven in places.

    “What do you mean by 'this'?”

    “This vigilante thing.”

    Since their conversation is about to be cut short by their arrival at their car again, Kate gives a vague answer, not wanting to sound inexperienced.

    “A few years…I work with Hawkeye.”

    Instead of impressed, Mason looks more nostalgic, his mouth tipping upward but his eyes almost sad for some reason.

    “So I’ve heard.”

    He sounds like he intended to tease or mock Kate, but Mason sounds more wistful than anything, and again, Kate wanders about how deep his connection with Natasha ran. For a few seconds, Kate weighs the chance of her digging up painful memories, against her desire to know things, the latter quickly winning out.

    “So…you knew Natasha?”

    Turning her head to watch his reaction, Kate doesn’t miss the way his eyes glance at Kate then at Yelena, before returning to watching his steps too.

    “I did.”

    Disappointingly, he doesn’t offer more in his own volition, and Kate sighs internally, before speaking again, more direct this time.

    “How did you two meet?”

    At that, Rick Mason smiles properly, although the sorrow is not completely gone from his eyes, telling Kate that the two were friends, at the very least.

    “How does anybody meet anybody in this business?”

    Before Kate can grow frustrated by his non-answer, Rick Mason chuckles to himself and speaks again.

    “I used to work for SAS and then got recruited by S.H.I.E.L.D after I was discharged. I had a mission go sideways in Cambodia, and she and Barton were sent to break us out.” Her eyebrows jumping toward her hairline, Kate is unable to hide her surprise. “You know Clint?”

    Turning his head to meet Kate’s eyes, Mason smiles.

    “Just a little.”

    Trying to rake her brain for any time Clint could have mentioned Mason, Kate is quiet for a few seconds, before she starts to question if Rick Mason is even his real name. “I don’t think he-“ “Mason, the keys.”

    Yelena’s voice is not short or mean, but it’s painfully obvious that she is not in the mood to play around or interested in being a part of their conversation. Mason throws the keys in his hand, bridging the few steps between Kate and him, and Yelena, who stands next to a very ordinary Toyota in the parking lot.

    “It’s nothing fancy, but it will get you from A to B.”

    It takes Kate a few seconds to realize he is talking to her, getting too caught up in staring at Yelena again, and she nods, watching Sonya take another set of keys from Yelena and walk toward the side of the parking lot where the car they arrived with is.

    “Thanks.”

    After a moment, her mind catches up to her present, and she turns toward Rick Mason again, while Yelena walks around the car and opens its trunk.

    “Am I paying you for this or has Yelena already?”

    Mason opens his mouth to answer but gets cut off by Yelena's voice, sounding from behind the open trunk.

    “I already paid him.”

    Closing his mouth, Mason nods, before he opens it again to speak, loudly enough so Yelena is included in the conversation.

    “I would have said the same.”

    It sounds like a jest and a second later Yelena leans from behind the trunk to give him a look that is strongly colored by disbelief.

    “Uh-huh.”

    Mason smiles, before shaking his head, the two exchanging a fond and amused look. “Anyway. The papers are in the glove compartment. There is a pretty nice but discreet motel about 10 miles down the road from here, that way.”

    He points it out, and Kate listens, even though she is unsure if they will still need that, with the strong suspicion that the devices in her apartment belong to Valentina and Rojas, who do not want to kill her... As far as she knows.

    “Thanks.”

    He nods, sparing one last glance toward Yelena, who now sits on the passenger side of the car, examining the contents of the glove compartment. Quietly, probably aiming to avoid her hearing it too, Mason looks at Kate and speaks.

    “Take care of yourself.”

    Confused, Kate shakes her head. Mason is a friend of Yelena’s, apparently. Why is he warning Kate about her?

    “What? She would neve-”

    Her words are cut off by his eye-roll and overdramatic sigh before he pins her with a look. “Don’t die, okay?”

    Huh?

    “Okay?”

    He widens his eyes sarcastically, before shaking his head and walking toward the passenger side of the car.

    “Kate.”

    At Yelena saying her name, Kate perks up, pushing whatever the fuck that interaction was to the back of her mind.

    “Yes?”

    “Go help Sonya with your stuff… Please.”

    Yelena at least looks into her eyes and smiles, smoothing the burn of being dismissed a little. “Oh. Okay.”

    Kate returns Yelena'ssmile, maybe a bit awkwardly, and waves at Mason who watches her, looking amused and kind of odd as she walks off.

    Sonya obviously does not need her help, leaning against the car and talking on her phone when Kate passes the white van and sees her.

    “…just for a day or two.”

    She is uncharacteristically serious, but she acknowledges Kate as she walks up, pressing the button on the keys to open this car’s trunk, so she can get her bag.

    “Yeah. Yelena and I will be back for her later today…No, I don’t think so, just a precaution.” With having been clearly dismissed so Mason and Yelena can talk to each other without her present, Kate is not really in a hurry to get back to their new old car, so she takes a seat on the edge of the trunk, trying to tune Sonya out as a courtesy. She doesn’t walk away to keep her conversation private though, so Kate assumes she is fine to stay.

    “Oh yeah, that works too. Thank you…Okay baby, I’ll see you tomorrow.”

    Ah. Thomas.

    Sonya hangs up, walking around the car and stopping a few steps from Kate. “How are you doing?”

    She is smiling, not even a hint of teasing in her eyes for once, so Kate feels emboldened to answer her honestly.

    “Exhausted. I don’t think I have the energy to process any of this until I had like 10 years of sleep.”

    Sonya’s lips spread into a grin, and she blinks at Kate once, long and friendly. “Yeah…Don’t worry. We’ll find a nice-ish motel somewhere around, and you can get your beauty sleep.”

    Closing her eyes, Kate sighs deeply before opening them once more and finding Sonya again. “So…even though it was probably Valentina, we can’t go home?”

    Looking kind of apologetic, Sonya shakes her head.

    “Nope. We have no idea how they knew where you were, or how they got in. Until we clear that up, no going back, sorry.”

    Blinking back, Kate returns the apologetic smile, before looking around just as something to do.

    “Figures.”

    For a few seconds, Kate mulls it over in her head, before speaking again. “Thankfully, the camera I have above the door has face recognition software, so we have a good chance of finding something without having to look through weeks of footage.” Sonya nods before the corner of her lip tips upwards again and Kate huffs out a chuckle and shakes her head at her.

    “Please, not a word. I don’t have the strength for that right now.”

    Sonya’s smile turns into a grin, but she nods after a second, glancing towards where Yelena and Mason stayed behind before her attention is back on Kate. Her grin is tempered into a smile then, that Kate would call fond on anyone else, and her dark eyes are warm when she speaks next.

    “But you good?”

    Swallowing, Kate looks away for a few seconds, unsure how to answer as she follows a car speeding by on the wet highway only a few dozen feet away with her eyes. Is she?

    She knows what Sonya is asking. Or at least, what is she referring to.

    And no, Kate is not good.

    She has no idea where they stand, and she has no idea what’s going on with Yelena, and she still hasn’t had time to properly process the fact that they have actually slept together last night.

    But she also lacks the energy to articulate that right now and she is also unsure if Yelena’s best friend is the best person to talk to about it.

    So, Kate turns back to Sonya, takes another deep breath, and gives a smile that probably can be read as playful, or at least light.

    “Yeah. Yeah, I’m good.”

    Sonya nods, her smile turning just a little bit teasing.

    “It’s going to be- Hi, Yelena.”

    Yelena appears from behind the van, looking marginally calmer than earlier, and looking at the two of them somewhat suspiciously. Kate internally dares her to call them out, and ask what they were talking about, but of course, Yelena is smarter than that. “Are you ready?”

    Kate nods and stands up, turning around to grab her suitcase but Sonya’s words halt her movement.

    “I talked to Tommy. He is going to take Maxine, so we don’t have to go back.” Turning back around, she sees Yelena’s face turn thoughtful while her own must portray her confusion.

    “What?”

    Sonya’s attention shifts from Yelena to her and she explains.

    “Since we don’t know how they know about you, or how they got into your place, my apartment might be compromised too. So, Tommy is taking Maxine, and Yelena and I will stay at the motel with you.”

    Blinking, Kate mulls the words over, guilt stirring in her chest.

    “Shit. I’m so sorry, Sonya.”

    Her words are waved off, and Sonya immediately shakes her head with a smile. “This one is not your fault. If Valentina really did this, we should have seen it coming too.” While the words don’t make her feel better, Kate accepts Sonya’s affirmation with a nod, rolling her lips together.

    “Okay. You good to drive?”

    At Sonya’s question, Kate nods, then shakes her head in quick succession, unsure what her actual answer is.

    “Uh…maybe?”

    Sonya chuckles, and even Yelena smiles a little, then shakes her head as she takes a step back.

    “Okay, I’m going to take the Toyota. Sonya, you follow me with Kate. Mason recommended a hotel not far from here.”

    Kate is no longer surprised that Yelena arranges things to keep them apart, and she is too tired to care right now anyway. If Yelena needs space, then let her have her space. Whatever. “Sure.”

    Despite her dismissal, Kate feels Yelena’s eyes on her for a few seconds longer, but by the time she looks back at her, she is walking away.

    “Come on, Hawkeye.”

    Sonya slaps the top of the car twice, and Kate walks around to the passenger side, trying to find the silver lining in not being banished to the backseat at least. She looks at Yelena walking away for a couple more moments, but she never turns back to look at her, and with a sigh, Kate slides into her seat when Sonya starts up the engine.

    They roll out of their parking spot and come to a stop behind Yelena’s (technically Kate’s) car, idling until she gets in and pulls out too.

    She fully expects Sonya to say something, anything, to comment on the weird vibe between them or even the fact of what happened, but for once, she seems to be content to talk about other things. Kate is too tired to participate in the conversation too much, but she appreciates Sonya’s company ad friendship, so she chimes in with a few comments here and there, during their 10 minute journey.

    The parking lot they follow Yelena’s car into belongs to a motel that Kate would otherwise probably never end up staying in, but at least it doesn’t look like she will catch some exotic parasite just by using the towel, so she sighs in relief when she looks around. Using the last of her energy reserves, she checks around for cameras as they get out of the car, and finds none but she makes sure to keep her head low and keep her face mostly covered by her baseball cap while they walk inside anyway, admitting to herself that she is probably not in the right mental state to spot any that is not painfully obvious. Inside, the reception is modest, but clean, and a friendly, middle-aged woman greets them as they walk through the door, Kate the only one to pull a suitcase behind herself. The blonde woman, Mary, according to the nameplate on her chest, smiles at all three of them and Kate watches as Yelena steps forward, taking it upon herself to handle their rooms. “Welcome to the Fairway Hotel, how can I help you?”

    Leaning against the reception counter, Yelena smiles back at Mary, while Kate stifles a yawn, her jaw straining with the effort.

    “Hi! We were hoping to get three rooms. Singles, if possible.”

    Curiously, Yelena speaks with a slightly southern accent to Mary, and when nobody pays her any attention, Kate rummages around in her bag to choose an ID to use as well. She settles on the first southern state one she finds and spends the next few seconds trying to get into the headspace of Barbara Itch from Louisiana.

    “I’m afraid we only have two doubles left, honey. We’re almost fully booked for the weekend, with the conference over at the Marriott. Are two of you okay to share?” While Kate wonders who comes here on a random weekend, even for a conference, Yelena hums in agreement.

    “That’s alright, thank you.”

    Mary clicks on her computer a few times, before turning back to them with a smile. “How long are you staying?”

    As she listens to the conversation with one ear, Kate looks around, trying to see if there is any indication of what type of conference is happening.

    “Until the 13th.”

    “In that case…”

    Mary clicks her mouse a few times in quick succession, pausing as she does so. “…Your rooms will be 385 dollars for the three nights. Sounds good?”

    Turning back, she watches as Yelena nods, before leaning against the counter again, and despite only seeing part of her face, Kate can tell that she is smiling, her stomach doing a tired somersault at the visual.

    “Perfect, thank you.”

    Mary nods with a polite smile before she turns back to her computer and clicks a few times again, asking without looking back at their group.

    “May I see some ID from all three of you?”

    Kate passes her brand new fake ID to Yelena, while Sonya hands her own to Mary directly, who takes all three. While Mary types up their names and addresses, Kate looks around once more, hoping to look nonchalant.

    The lobby is small, with vinyl floors and a staircase on the other side, presumably leading to the second floor of the hotel. There is a closed door on the other side of it, with the word Restaurant above it in old-fashioned, cheap metal letters and a vending machine next to it, full of snacks and a couple of soft drinks.

    While they wait, one couple walks down the stairs, followed by a middle-aged man in a cheap suit about 2 minutes later, neither of them paying Kate and her group any mind. With the possibility of sleep now only an arm's reach away, Kate feels her eyelids begin to grow heavier again, despite her anxiety about the fake ID, and fails to stifle her third yawn in only a few minutes.

    “Okkaay. All done. Would you like to put all rooms on one credit card, or keep the single separately?”

    “Actually, we’d like to pay by cash.”

    Mary’s eyes slide from Yelena to Sonya, and then to Kate quickly, before she nods again, her friendly demeanor not diminishing.

    “Of course. However, I still have to ask for a card to complete the booking.” While Kate’s anxiety spikes for a second, Yelena just nods, reaching into her wallet. “No prolem. Here you go.”

    As quietly as she can, Kate exhales, and it feels like a weight has been lifted off of her when Mary hands them two keys, their IDs, and Yelena’s credit card a few moments later. “All done! Here you go. Are you familiar with the area?”

    Kate watches as Yelena shakes her head, and has to swallow a groan, really looking forward to putting her head down as soon as possible.

    “Nope. First time for all of us. Actually, my friend and I’s luggage got lost on our flight here. Could you please point us in the direction of the closest store? Need to pick up a few things to get us through until we get our stuff.”

    Mary’s unwavering smile widens, even as she shakes her head.

    “I am so sorry! Of course, if you go-“ Kate tunes out the explanation, her mind zeroing in on the keys in Yelena’s hand. Would it be rude to ask for one of the keys so she can get to a room while they listen to this? She doesn’t care if she needs to share with so-

    Wait a second…

    They have two rooms for the three of them.

    Two people will have to share.

    The most likely outcome is, of course, Sonya and Yelena sharing but still, there is a chance… “Thank you!”

    Yelena’s cheerful, if fake platitude yanks Kate back into reality, suddenly a few percent less sleepy than she was a minute ago.

    “Let’s go.”

    Kate follows Yelena across the lobby and up the stairs, lugging her suitcase behind her. Sonya walks behind her, snickering quietly as Kate gives in and allows herself a frustrated groan when she actually has to pick up her suitcase to carry it, but otherwise, the three of them walk upstairs without any words or comments exchanged.

    Yelena leads them up the staircase and to the right on the old-fashioned, but clean hallway they arrive at, stopping in front of room 58. She uses one of the keys to open the door and walks in, after briefly checking both left and right.

    “Okay, this one is ours.”

    Yelena turns back, after seeing the two beds, almost running into Kate who is only a few steps behind, but at least this time, she doesn’t jump 6 feet backward. “Here is your key.”

    Kate takes the key held out to her with a nod, throwing one last glance at the room Sonya and Yelena will share before turning away.

    “Kate.”

    As she turns back at Yelena calling her name, Sonya slips by Kate, entering the room, and looking around. Yelena holds out a second set of keys to her, and as she glances down at them, Kate recognizes them as the keys to the car bought from Rick Mason. “Draw your curtains. Put out the do not disturb sign and do not open the door for anyone that is not Sonya or me. If you see or hear anything suspicious, get in the car and go.” Kate takes the car keys too with a sigh, a bit disappointed at the impersonal instructions, although she is unsure what she could have been hoping for, based on the last few hours. “Okay. Are you guys going out?”

    “Just to the shop around the corner, to get toothbrushes and similar items.” Kate nods, glancing at Sonya who is now inspecting the electrical outlets for some reason. “Okay. Well. See you later, I guess.”

    Sonya turns away from the wall to smile at Kate, her eyes shifting over to Yelena and Kate does the same. Yelena looks tired, too, her shoulders held higher than normally, and the muscles of her jaw tight.

    “Do not forget to charge your new phone. Same number, yes?”

    Feeling more than a little bit guilty, at upending both Yelena’s and Sonya’s life, again, Kate nods.

    “Yup. Will you two be working?”

    Yelena turns away to look at Sonya, the two exchanging a meaningful glance before they both turn back to Kate.

    “Most likely.”

    “Kay. I’m gonna take a nap and get started on the video footage too.”

    Yelena opens her mouth to say something but closes it, and Kate feels awkwardness slowly descending over the room. It’s time for her to go.

    “Right. See you later.”

    She turns away a second time, beginning to wheel her suitcase out of the room. “Move your bed.”

    She hears Yelena step after her and turns back once more, confusion stirring in her chest again.

    “Huh?”

    Yelena crosses the distance between them, and Kate holds her breath but she only uses it to slip by Kate in the tight hallway, walking out the door.

    “Okay, I will check your room.”

    Kate did not ask her to do that, and she feels more confused than ever, meeting Sonya’s amused eyes for a second before she whips around and follows Yelena out. Lost and befuddled, Kate follows her a few doors down, Yelena halting in front of the door to room 65.

    “Keys.”

    What is happening?

    Wordlessly, Kate gives the room key back to Yelena who opens the door and walks in without another word. Kate walks in too, wheeling her suitcase through the carpeted hallway, a certain peace flooding her at seeing the room, and specifically, the bed she will get to sleep in soon.

    Finally.

    The room, just like the rest of the hotel, is modest, but clean and tidy. There is one double bed with white sheets, a desk, and one armchair in the corner, with a small closet behind Kate. There is also a flat TV on the wall, a bit on the smaller side, but Kate is not here for a cinematic experience, and a plastic plant in the corner.

    While Kate watches on, becoming more confused by the second, Yelena draws the curtains and checks the outlets too, just like Sonya has in the other room, before moving the small bedside table out of the way so she can push the bed into the corner.

    With nothing better to do and not wanting to just stare, Kate takes off her thick flannel shirt, hanging it up on one of the three hangers in the wardrobe, and then her hoodie too, too lazy to do anything other than to toss it into the armchair in the corner.

    Not wanting or possessing the energy to question Yelena’s presence, Kate stands to the side to allow her to step by her side again, and wheels her suitcase into the now bigger open space on the other side of the room, while Yelena rummages around in her bathroom. After she unzips the suitcase, the first thing she pulls out is the brand new phone, tossed onto the bed across the room, still in its box. Kate then gets her toiletries and walks toward the bedroom without a second thought, even though Yelena is literally on her mind. Maybe Kate should have expected to run into Yelena in there, but she did not expect to literally run into Yelena, just as she rounds into the bathroom. The toiletries in her hand get sandwiched between their bodies, but they are the last thing on Kate’s mind. The quiet gasp from Yelena, close enough for Kate to smell the blueberry chewing gum in her mouth, sounds exactly like it did in the elevator last night and Kate’s hazily wandering mind comes to a screeching halt.

    Yelena stands stock still, with one hand pressed against Kate’s stomach, lifted most likely to avoid a full collision, and Kate’s hand holds onto her elbow, even though she has no idea when it landed there. Their eyes are connected, looking at one another for a few torturous heartbeats. Kate could blame her exhaustion, but in reality, it has nothing to do with her gaze dropping to Yelena’s lips, fueled entirely by the memory of what those lips felt like against her own and on various parts of her body.

    Yelena exhales slowly, her breath hitting Kate’s chin, and she steps back and away, a second later, allowing Kate to step into the room, the moment broken.

    She does not jump away, or even try to escape the bathroom, because Kate feels her eyes on her for the few seconds it takes for her to deposit her shower bag onto the counter by the sink, and turn back.

    “Mason was a friend of Natasha.”

    Unsure why this is the thing Yelena chooses to say to her, Kate glances to the side. She wants to ask, she wants to ask so many things, about today, about last night, and about the revelation about Valentina. She wants to ask if Yelena is okay, if they are okay, or if something is permanently skewed, now that they have seen and tasted each other naked. “Okay.”

    It’s not the right time to ask any of it.

    Maybe a few months ago, Kate would have pushed. She would have pushed for explanations, but with every other wonderful thing she is, Yelena is also fickle.

    Yelena is fickle, and pushing her has never worked out in Kate’s favor. “He is…friends with my parents, still. They talk to him about things… Things about me. Silly things.”

    Blinking, Kate feels the corners of her mouth begin to turn upwards.

    “Okay. He didn’t tell me any of those silly things.”

    Yelena finally looks away from the spot she was staring at somewhere to the right of Kate’s head, and meets her eyes again.

    “Good.”

    Her upturned lips stretching into a full smile, Kate blinks at Yelena.

    “What kind of silly things?”
