    Yelena huffs, before lifting her chin slightly.

    “Silly ideas to put in your head.”

    Her smile dimming, Kate’s eyebrows lift, and she shifts her weight from one leg to the other. “Yeah, but what silly ideas?”

    Rolling her eyes, Yelena mirrors Kate’s stance, shifting her weight too. “That I need, or want someone.”

    Ouch.

    Twice in one day.

    Trying to keep her smile in place, Kate huffs through her nose, and puts in an effort to not look away from Yelena, but internally, it does feel like she was just kicked in the stomach. Maybe.

    “You don’t have to worry, Yelena. I heard you, loud and clear. No confusion on my end about what last night was.”

    At that, Yelena’s eyes shift slightly to the right again but it seems she makes an effort too, meeting Kate’s eyes again barely a heartbeat later.

    “Okay, good.”

    Kate really wished they kept that conversation until after she had a good night’s sleep or at least a power nap.

    “Right. Can I sleep now?”

    Kate can see Yelena swallow, but a second later she nods, and steps back to no longer block the exit from the bathroom.

    “Okay. Do you need anything from the shop?”

    Kate turns her back to Yelena, no longer wishing to keep appearances, and walks back to her suitcase to get her pajamas.

    “No, thanks.”

    As she digs into her suitcase, she doesn’t hear Yelena move for a few more seconds, but then she hears the steps walking away and the door shutting. Exhaling slowly, Kate closes her eyes, leaning onto her hands in her suitcase.

    She really fucking needs to sleep.

    It feels overwhelming, to even just consider the two months' worth of things that happened last night, and it takes Kate an enormous amount of self-control to not just faceplant onto the mattress and pass out.

    After a few seconds, Kate opens her eyes and ignores the swirly, uncomfortable feeling in her stomach, and goes about her pre-bed routine. She washes her face and teeth, changes into the shorts and tanktop she plans to sleep in and even unpacks her phone, quickly going through the motions of setting it up as she sits on her bed and leaving it to charge once that’s done. Following Yelena’s instructions, ignoring the childish defiance to do otherwise, Kate puts out the do not disturb sign and locks her door, before finally slipping under the fresh, crisp covers.

    Her body and mind feel heavy, the rollercoaster of the last 30-something hours making her feel like a thousand-pound stone on her chest, making her sink to the bottom of the ocean. Kate does her best to focus on the bed around her, the dim room, with most of the light banished from the room by the curtains, and the sound of the rain still pattering against the windows or the cars driving by on the wet pavement, filtering softly into the room. Her stomach grumbles gently, and Kate fantasizes about the continental breakfast from the hotel they spent the previous night in, instead of thinking about anything else from the mile- long list of topics she has swirling in her head.

    But as her mind begins to succumb to sleep, her mental barriers falling away, the images of Yelena uncontrollably filter into her brain, one after the other like a movie. Yelena in the expensive car last night, joking and flirting with her to keep her nervousness at bay.

    Yelena at the party last night, on her arm, playing the perfect fiancé. Yelena on the table in the office, pulling Kate in to kiss her.

    Yelena on the way home, beautiful and mysterious.

    Yelena in the elevator, gasping before Kate kissed her.

    Yelena, in her living room, looking real, and gorgeous and almost nervous. Yelena, kissing her, gasping and moaning into her ears, grinding against her thigh. Yelena coming against her, her cheek pressed against Kate’s and the two of them falling back together.

    Yelena, laughing with her eyes closed and blissed out, stunning and untethered. Yelena, lying on her bed, naked and with a quiet fire burning in her eyes. Yelena telling Kate it was a one-time thing, serious but so very naked. Yelena slipping on Kate’s shirt and running around in her apartment to hide things. Yelena, keeping Kate tethered, her eyes green and blazing, when the FBI was searching her place.

    Yelena sleeping in the hotel room, allowing Kate to watch over her.

    Yelena...

    Yelena. Yelena. Yelena…

    Kate wakes up to her phone buzzing.

    Blindily, she reaches toward the noise, just to make it stop but it doesn’t. It annoys her enough to pick the offending item, cracking one eye open to see who it is. Clint.

    With a groan, Kate closes her eye for an additional few seconds before she opens both of them, kind of, to swipe at the screen and accept the call.

    “Hey kid.”

    His tone is gruff and Kate sighs, wondering if he is still angry about her antagonizing Fisk or if something else happened. Still somewhat asleep, Kate pulls the phone away from her ear to check the time.

    6:34 pm “Hi. Is everything okay? Did you guys make it home?”

    He clears his throat and takes a second to answer.

    “Yeah. I texted you.”

    Rubbing her face, Kate remembers that once again, he is not aware of what happened with her phone and the FBI but her mind is still booting up.

    “Was Lucky okay during the flight?”

    “He was... I texted you that too.”

    Blinking herself more awake, Kate turns to her back, trying to wake up properly. “Right, about that…”

    Sitting up, she leans back against the headboard, squinting at the thin ray of light that makes it through the drawn curtains. It’s dim and grey, but she doesn’t think she can still rain anymore.

    “Where do I start…uh…Sorry, I’ve been up all night…I just took a nap, so I’m not fully operational just yet.”

    There is a grumble on the other side of the line, his words getting almost entirely lost in it, partially covered by her own moving around.

    “What was that?”

    She hears him huff through the receiver, and even though she is somewhat more aware and awake than she was a minute or two ago, she is still confused by his gruffness. “I said I don’t need to know that.”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate shakes her head.

    “Actually, you do. The FBI searched my place last night. They took my phone. And my laptop. But I-”

    Kate hears his chair scrape against the floor as he sits up.

    “What?”

    Although he can’t see her, Kate nods tiredly, the outrage in his voice finally matching the reaction she thinks the event warrants.

    “Yeah! They showed up at like 1 am, and turned my place upside down.”

    “Oh thank god…”

    Eyebrows furrowing, Kate shakes her head in confusion while she pulls a pillow up to lean back against more comfortably.

    “What?”

    Ignoring her question, Clint barrels on.

    “What were they looking for?”

    Blinking, and not looking at anything in particular, Kate takes a second to answer. “Um…The drive, probably. Also, someone bugged my place… What... What do you mean oh thank god?”

    Clint’s outrage strengthens, and Kate can’t help but smile as she imagines his eyebrows lifting.

    “They bugged your place?!”

    Running a hand through her hair, Kate leans further against the headboard, sliding a bit lower. “Yeah… No. Well, someone did. Sonya and Yelena swept for bugs earlier. They found two.” His deep sigh is audible through the phone, and his voice is a bit worried when he speaks next.

    “Shit. They are really onto you…”

    Sliding even lower on her bed, Kate exhales too, her tiredness audible in her voice even to herself.

    “Well, yeah. But the bugs are not from the FBI…According to Yelena and Sonya anyway. And Mason.”

    There is a beat of silence as Clint seems to be considering the news she just told him. “Mason?”

    Kate exhales, rubbing her eyes in the hopes of dispelling some of the exhaustion still lingering in her body, making her head feel fuzzy.

    “Rick Mason? Apparently, you know him.”

    “What the hell are you doing with Rick Mason?”

    Sighing, Kate blinks twice, trying to summarize the events of the day.

    “Yelena and Sonya searched my place, and they found bugs, right? And we weren’t sure how they ended up there, or who placed them, so they said we had to go and lay low for a bit.” “Probably a good idea.”

    “Yeah, right. So, they took me to this creepy motel, and we met Rick Mason, and he got me a bunch of fake IDs and an old Toyota.”

    She hears him scratch at his stubble, and she imagines Clint thinking.

    “Okay. That’s…yeah. Okay… Do you want to come to the farm?”

    It hurts a bit to smile, since the farm actually sounds really great right now, but Kate shakes her head.

    “No. No, this doesn’t change anything. We need to get the formula… And the dirt on Fisk.” She hears Clint exhale, probably unhappy with her decision but he doesn’t try to persuade her.

    “Okay. So, what’s the plan?”

    Running a hand through her hair, Kate wills her brain to work.

    “Um. So, the bugging might have been Valentina and the CIA. Or the cartel… Whichever, it’s probably to keep an eye on their investment and to see if we keep up the end of our deal.” “Right.”

    “So, we need to verify how they got in…Otherwise, nothing’s changed. We’ll need to get the piece from my mom’s…from the Summer Place. And the one from the FBI.”

    “Okay, so you held onto the drive we got yesterday.”

    “Of course. We hid it in my lair.”

    There is a beat of silence, and Kate realizes that she kind of just snitched herself. We. At the 1 am FBI raid.

    Shit.

    Thankfully, Clint either missed it or is unwilling to address it. Whichever it is, is fine with Kate.

    “Hm, okay. Let me make some calls. See if I can get you listed officially as part of one of the agencies. That should help on the FBI front at least.”

    Eyebrows jumping up to her hairline, Kate can’t help but be surprised.

    “Wait, I didn’t know that was an option…”

    He hums, before he actually answers.

    “Well. It isn’t normally. But…maybe I can pull some strings.”

    Eyebrows drawn, Kate purses her lips.

    “Why didn’t we do this in the first place? It would have saved me a ton of headaches.” On the other end of the line, Clint sighs, his voice a bit tired, maybe from the overnight travel.

    “Because it’s not exactly easy. And it has a lot of drawbacks.”

    When he doesn’t elaborate after a few seconds, Kate tries to prompt him by asking. “Like?”

    Kate hears him move around on the other end of the call, possibly scratching his chin in thought again.

    “I mean, sure, you get certain privileges, but it also makes you accountable. It comes with oversight.”

    Okay? That’s not enough information.

    “Oversight from whom?”

    Because he is Clint Barton, self-proclaimed ghost for the past 20 years, he does not give a straight answer. He takes a few seconds to speak, and even then, he is tight-lipped. “We’ll see. I’ll try to get a hold of Fury.”

    Wait a minute…does he mean…?

    “You…Fury... You will try to get a hold of Nick Fury, to get me officially a part of his operations.”

    Once more, he huffs, and Kate feels her lips tilting upwards at his exasperation. “Not…really. I’ll see kid. He is kind of doing his own thing now…in space. So we’ll see…” She really can’t help herself, pushing just a little.

    “Does that mean I am officially becoming an Avenger?”

    As expected, his answer is not an easy yes, or no, or even a proper answer, just his tone dropping to that specific cadence when he thinks she is being immature. “Kid…”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate grins, beginning to shuffle out of bed, knowing fully well that after this conversation, she is too excited to sleep, her mood significantly improved now that she has gotten at least a few hours of sleep.

    “Okay, okay. I get it. The Avengers no longer exist…but if they did?”

    She knows, that if they were in the same room, he would hide his smile in exchange for trying to keep her expectations down, and curb her (over-)enthusiasm, but through his voice, she can tell he is smiling.

    “Let’s get you into something official first, okay? The army, or S.H.I.E.L.D., or something. That way at least they can’t get you on vigilantism.”

    Feeling a bit mischievous, Kate makes sure her humor is not audible through her voice when she asks her next question.

    “You want to get me into the army?!”

    He is back to gruff and grunting in a few seconds.

    “It’s an idea.”

    Still keeping her act, Kate shakes her head, but she is sure that if someone was to see her right now, her face would give he away, as she walks out of the bedroom, and into the bathroom.

    “I don’t have time to go to war, Clint. I have my own thing going on.”

    Although not seeing him either, Kate is sure that his brows are furrowed, probably shaking his head at her antics.

    “That’s not…You know that’s not what I mean.”

    Allowing her lips to be pulled into a grin, Kate turns on the faucet and begins to wash her face with the phone still against her ear.

    “Yeah, I kinda do.”

    He grunts on the other end of the line, and she thinks Clint is about to hang up on her, when he surprises her with another comment.

    “You’re awfully chipper for someone who was up all night being raided by the FBI.” This reminds her…What the hell was ‘Oh thank god’ about?!

    …

    But if Kate is really thinking about it, it’s probably best not to get too much into what he meant because she is pretty sure Clint got the right read of what she was doing when he couldn’t reach her, even if it happened earlier than he tried to call.

    Or should she say…who she was doing?

    …Come on, Kate. She is above that.

    Just like she was above, and below Yelena last night…

    Come. On. Kate.

    Focus.

    “Kate?”

    Oh shit, she is supposed to say something.

    “Oh, yeah, sorry, I’m here. I’m just uh, …washing my face.”

    There is a grunt on the other end of the line and Kate is thankful Clint is not in the room with her right now.

    “Right.”

    Okay. Let’s steer the conversation away from that.

    Work. Let’s talk about work.

    “So, speaking of, do you have anything for us about the FBI? Where they might be holding the pathway?”

    “Not yet. My contact found out the registry number under which it’s filed, but they have to find a way to look up where it’s stored without being flagged. Especially if it goes missing a few days after.”

    Humming, wipes her face with the towel provided by the motel, distractedly happy that it doesn’t look like something that will give her dysentery.

    “Okay. We’ll probably go and pick up the encryption from the Summer place tomorrow or the day after, depending on what we figure out about the bugging. After that, we only need to get the pathway, and then we are done.”

    While she speaks, Kate hears Nate’s voice in the background and immediately knows their time is up.

    “-Anyway. Go, enjoy time with the kids. And give Lucky some scritches from me.” Clint hums and he sounds a bit softer when he speaks next, maybe because Nate is around or because he is done being mad at kate for whatever he is mad about.

    “Right. Take care, kid. Keep a low profile, use cash… And listen to Yelena and Sonya. They have more experience in this.”

    Rolling her eyes, Kate walks out of the bathroom again, and to her suitcase, pulling out her new laptop.

    “Okay, okay. I will be a good girl scout.”

    Clint snorts, his voice finally light and teasing.

    “You’d be a terrible girl scout.”

    “That’s a lie. I could sell more cookies than anyone.”

    He sighs, exasperated yet somehow fond, even through the phone and Kate smiles to herself, as she pulls away the plastic covering the MacBook.

    “That I can believe… Okay, kid, I gotta go. Nate’s team has won so we are celebrating.” Her smile widening, Kate puts the unpacking on hold for a second.

    “Tell him I said congrats!”

    “Will do. Bye, Kate.”

    “Bye, Hawkeye.”

    Once she hangs up the phone, Kate brings the laptop back to her bed, not wanting to set up at the desk for now. She boots up the computer and goes through the account recovery process, and then installs the Bishop Security software on it from a pendrive she brought along in her backpack.

    By 7, Kate is hungry, so she sets up her computer to search for faces in the camera footage from above her door in the last three weeks, thankfully available through the cloud remotely. Yelena and Sonya haven’t called her since, but Kate thinks they must be back by now, and quickly goes through the motions of showering and getting ready to go out for food, while her computer does its job.

    When she is ready, she picks up her phone to text Yelena but is distracted by a ding from her computer, letting her know the search for faces is complete. Walking over to the bed, Kate types out her message, asking her what they are up to and if they are up for food, before throwing it on the bed and picking up the computer instead to pass the time. Scrolling over the faces, it’s mostly Yelena, Clint, Sonya, Tommy and of course, Kate, with the occasional delivery person. Kate swallows and quickly scrolls away, when footage of Yelena and her pop up from last night, not mentally prepared to look at it. Instead, she looks at the footage of everyone, that is not in their inner circle, while she checks her phone a few times to see if Yelena has texted back.

    Okay, she will just look at one more video, and then give Yelena a call. Whatever, they are meant to be working together, she won’t play these games. It’s not like she is calling Yelena to…

    Wait a minute.

    Kate watches the footage with her eyes progressively getting wider. The person comes through the elevator, nothing suspicious at first. He rings the doorbell and knocks, and Kate sees him wait a few seconds, probably listening to sounds from inside the apartment, before he checks both ways on the hallway and drops to one knee.

    Kate watches with wide eyes and her mouth slowly dropping open, as he picks Kate’s lock, slowly opening the door and sticking his head inside.

    There is nobody home.

    Kate knows because she recognizes the date.

    September 18th.

    The day they broke into Limitless for the first time.

    Slamming the laptop shut, Kate jumps to her feet, and immediately calls Yelena, walking up and down.

    The phone rings twice before it’s answered.

    “I texted you, come-“ “It was the doorman, Yelena. The fucking doorman.”

    Chapter End Notes HAHAHAHA. "One-time thing" Yelena you dumb bitch (affectionately) :D Edit (2023-08-27): So, the deed finally has been done. Hope it lived up to your expectations :D I know some (many?) of you hoped that them coming together (hehe) in some shape or form would mean they got together for real, but I don't personally see that as realistic, at this point of the story. There is attraction and obviously, at this point, there are feelings too, from both of them, but there is also a LOT of unsaid and unresolved shit that needs to be handled before they can meaningfully move forward. And how did the two of them do with resolving shit up until now? :D So yeah, give them a little time to untangle their idiocy.

    Also, for those of you who did not read the first chapter of Vampire Smile, the companion series of this story, it also must be mentioned that Yelena is very inexperienced in all of this. This is the first time she is in a *situation* like this, with someone she actually likes, and she is bound to be a little stupid and pull some shit, especially since this situation is far from simple to begin with.

    As for Kate, she is again, just jumping into something with her whole chest, that she does not think through (or fully understand) which despite her character developing, and growing, is a core characteristic of hers. She is trying to be patient, but since Yelena keeps some cards close to her chest, she does not have the full picture which again, leads to some not-thought-through decisions.

    And as for the rest of the chapter, we are finally tieing some loose ends together, but we are far from seeing the whole picture :D I really enjoy reading your theories and thoughts, just like I really enjoy(ed) coming up with the non-romantic plot of this story too. Many of you spotted the doorman hints a few chapters ago. we'll see how that pans out :P As always, thank you all so much for reading, and please let me know what you think in the comments :)

    Chapter 26

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes “It was the doorman, Yelena. The fucking doorman.”

    There is a moment of silence while Yelena processes her words and Kate stares at the screen of her laptop still, the clip replaying.

    The fucking doorman. Who would have…

    “What are you talking about?”

    Shaking her head in frustration, Kate furrows her eyebrows, picking up her laptop. “I’ll be right over.”

    Without waiting for an answer, Kate hangs up, barely remembering to close her door as she hurries over to Yelena’s and Sonya’s room. She doesn’t knock, attempting to just burst in, and nearly knocking herself out with her laptop when the door doesn’t budge, evidently locked from the inside.

    “Let me in!”

    While Kate stresses her statement with two hard slaps of her palm against the door, and impatiently taps her foot, very eager to share her news. From the other side of the door, she hears steps coming closer.

    Finally…

    “Who is it?”

    The alarmed voice on the other side of the door is not one that is familiar to Kate, older than both Yelena and Sonya. Her eyebrows furrow and she glances up at the number. 56…

    Eyes widening, she takes half a step back.

    Shit...

    Weren’t Yelena and Sonya in 56?

    Nows she is not so sure...

    “Sorry!”

    “What are you doing?”

    Twisting her head to the side, Kate spots Yelena’s confused face peeking out from inside a room, two doors down.

    “I’m coming!”

    “Who were you talking to?”

    Jogging down the short distance between the doors, Kate tries to gloss over her mistake, raising her chin defiantly.

    “No one.”

    Yelena’s eyebrows are raised and Kate sees her check out the corridor one more time, before closing the door behind herself after Kate marches in. Sonya lies on top of the covers on the inner bed, with her phone in her hand, looking up to greet her with a smile when she walks in.

    “Hi, Kate. Did you have your beauty slee-”

    “It was the doorman, guys! He broke into my apartment, and planted the bugs!” Not waiting for Sonya to finish her pleasantries or offer any of her own in return, Kate jumps right in.

    “-Okay, rude…Wait, what?”

    Throwing her phone on the bed, Sonya stands up from her bed and joins Kate, while Yelena steps up beside her as well, looking at the screen of the laptop in her arms. Pressing the button, Kate restarts the video of the doorman picking her lock and getting inside.

    “This is the evening when we went to Limitless for the first time… The 18th.” While Yelena and Sonya watch the whole video, Kate speaks, almost physically vibrating with the energy that settles in her bones at the discovery. Once the clip has played through and restarted, Kate puts her laptop on the desk a couple of steps away and begins to pace while the video continues to replay on a loop.

    “Who do you think he works for? Fisk? Valentina? The FBI?”

    She continues pacing, not really waiting for an answer. Her eyes barely glance at Sonya or Yelena, and instead mostly jump between objects in the room, her mind going into overdrive. "I mean, Fisk is unlikely, right? If he knows where I am, why didn't he try to kill me there. So, it's probably Rojas or Valentina."

    Neither of the Widows answers her, but Kate is on a roll anyway, walking up and down and gesticulating.

    “So, what do we do? Should we go back to New York? To like, question him? Follow him to find out who he works for?”

    Yelena watches the clip play again, while Sonya’s eyes follow Kate but she is seemingly deep in thought too. After a moment, she walks back to her bed, picking up her phone before rejoining Yelena in rewatching the footage once more.

    “I will ask Herman if he knows him. This is the new guy, but he probably knows his name or something.”

    Leaning over, she presses the button to freeze the image at a moment when the doorman's face is mostly towards the camera, taking a photo with her phone.

    “Are you sure he is the only intruder?”

    Yelena’s question is posed to Kate, and she opens her mouth to say yes but hesitates before she actually says so. While she is almost certain that this is what they are looking at, she also did not finish reviewing all the footage from above her door.

    Plus why else would the doorman break into her house?

    After a moment, she closes her mouth and shakes her head, all the while holding Yelena’s serious eyes.

    “No. Haven’t finished looking the footage over.”

    Yelena nods, turning to Sonya, who is texting someone, presumably Herman. “What is he saying?”

    Sonya shakes her head, before looking up from her phone, meeting Yelena’s gaze. “He hasn’t seen it yet. Just checking in with Tommy.”

    Yelena nods, rolling her lips together before she turns back towards Kate. “Okay. You finish looking the footage over, and we will find out as much as we can about him once we get a nem Then we figure out what is going on.”

    A bit disappointed that her findings did not result in the three of them jumping into action, Kate purses her lips while she takes a deep breath.

    “Fine.-“ Her stomach growling interrupts her sentence, reminding her of what she was doing barely ten minutes ago.

    “-But first, I really need some food. I am starving.”

    Yelena nods, but it’s Sonya who speaks next.

    “We saw a diner when we went out earlier. I could eat something too.”

    Not waiting for Yelena’s input, Sonya walks over to her coat, picking it up and Kate’s mouth waters at the thought of a good, sinfully heavy burger from a diner. Happy is an understatement of how she feels when Yelena goes to pick up her own coat as well, without needing more to convince her.

    “Let’s go.”

    Kate takes her laptop back to her room after, quickly puts on a thick, black corduroy shirt over her hoodie, and a baseball cap to cover her face, only stopping to glance at herself in the mirror and turn off the lights. Within 2 minutes she is back outside, joining the Widows and locking up her room.

    As the three of them walk down the hallway, Sonya goes first, Yelena only a few steps behind and Kate closing their ranks, her stomach churning with hunger periodically., Once they are outside, Kate feels herself ease out a little, happy that the energy she feels filling her has an outlet at least by walking. While she has to give shit to Jersey, on principle, it’s nice that at least here, there are most likely no assassins waiting to get the jump on them or something similar. The roads are not too busy, but also not deserted, showing just enough signs of life around them that it’s not creepy.

    “Is it far away?”

    While she enjoys the walk, Kate’s hunger gets the better of her a minute or two into their journey, and it’s Yelena who answers her.

    “No. Like a 5 minute walk.”

    “Nice.”

    At her maybe slightly overly enthusiastic tone, she hears Sonya huff in the front, glancing back to throw her an amused look and if she is not mistaken, she sees Yelena’s cheeks lift with a smile too.

    “What? I am hungry and happy to stretch my legs. I’ve been cooped up all day.” “Don’t worry. We’ll get you fed and walked in no time.”

    She can’t help but snort at Sonya’s words.

    “Fed and walked? What am I, your dog?”

    Sonya fully turns around then, walking backwards on the sidewalk to grin at Kate, only the streetlamps illuminating her sharp features. The rain has stopped, finally, but the world is still wet and humid around them, the October evening air feeling crispy around Kate’s cheeks and the occasional car tire squelching a little on the road.

    “I mean, you could say that you are our bitch.”

    The potential sting of Sonya’s words is smoothed by her good-natured grin and Kate chuckles. She is also silently impressed when Sonya sidesteps a streetlamp with precision, despite still walking backwards and not even bothering to look around.

    She definitely hears Yelena snort this time too, even turning her head to throw Sonya an amused glance before she turns her head to look at Kate, her features half-hidden with the yellow street lighting, but her eyes alight with a playful spark.

    “Hmm…Maybe you need some more training. Fanny is much better behaved.”

    Maybe it’s risky, but after the stressful day they had, Kate can’t swallow the borderline flirty answer tumbling out of her mouth, her lips curling into a smirk.

    “Huh. Well, in that case, I’ve heard great things about positive reinforcement.” As Kate purses her lips and smiles to make sure her innuendo lands as it’s supposed to, Yelena’s lips twitch upward, her eyes lighting up for a second before she turns forward. Sonya laughs loudly, evading a trashcan with impressive precision once again, and Kate huffs out a chuckle, hoping she didn’t break the delicate balance they found. “Well, if you behave well and sit pretty, you can get a treat after dinner.” At the flirty comment, Kate lifts an eyebrow and Yelena holds her eyes for a few seconds longer, before her smile widens ever so slightly, and she looks away as she adds. “-A milkshake. Or a doughnut maybe.”

    Meeting Sonya’s eyes, Kate can tell that it takes all her willpower to keep the grin at bay that threatens to split her face in half. She loses that particular battle a moment later, chuckling to herself before she zeroes in on Kate.

    “For the record, I will smack you with a rolled-up newspaper if I catch you humping anyone’s leg at the diner.”

    Unable to swallow it this time, Kate bursts out laughing when Sonya pointedly raises an eyebrow at her and Yelena joins in a few seconds later too. Sonya lasts another second, finally losing even her half-serious façade.

    “Wow, Sonya. You really are like a dog with a bone with this joke, huh?” Only a step or two in front of her, Yelena blows out a rough breath with an exasperated little shake of her head.

    “Oh my god…”

    The rest of their walk passes in a similarly good-natured mood, the three of them arriving at the neon-lit, old-school diner a few minutes later. The restaurant is mostly empty, with only two older men sitting in a booth on one side who barely look at the three of them when they file in. The warmth of the air feels nice on Kate’s cheeks after the crispiness of the outside, her mouth watering at the smell of food when she breathes it in.

    Behind the counter, there is an older woman, smiling at them despite the late hour, looking right at home in the 50’s aesthetic of the place.

    “Hi, ladies! Sit wherever you like, Jen will be right with you!”

    Yelena and Sonya take a second to survey the diner before walking to the right, in the opposite direction of where the two men are sitting, and Kate follows them to the booth in the corner without much thought. Both widows choose to sit on the furthest bench, with their backs to the wall, leaving Kate to sit across from them alone.

    Picking up the menu, Kate starts reading it right away, her stomach grumbling in anticipation. As she contemplates her choices between a rodeo burger and a patty melt burger, her eyes catch sight of Yelena’s left hand, lying on the shiny tabletop, her heart skipping a beat before taking off at double speed.

    The ring.

    She is still wearing it.

    Despite her initial resistance to accept it, Yelena is still wearing the ring. “What are you getting?”

    Sonya’s question is to the both of them, and Kate quickly looks up at her, not wanting to get caught looking and spook Yelena or something. Clearing her throat, she glances back at her menu, before meeting Sonya’s eyes once more.

    “Um. Rodeo burger. With aaaaa… With one of the milk shakes, I think. Yeah.” Swallowing, her eyes shift over to Yelena, still engrossed in her menu before Sonya speaks again, drawing Kate’s attention back to herself.

    “Hmm…If we are going to sin like that, we really need to start training again.” The corner of her eyes crinkles as she glances up at Kate, gaze dropping in an effortlessly playful fashion to Kate’s body, then back at her own menu as she speaks. “-Not all of us are 24 and have the metabolism of a racehorse.”

    Kate hums in agreement, only partially paying attention, glancing back and around for the waitress. Now that they are sitting down and she has nowhere to look but at Yelena in front of her, and Yelena’s hand, with the ring and which is the same hand that has been between her legs less than…

    Focus Kate.

    Anyway, it would be nice to have a distraction to look at.

    …Or speak to.

    Sonya.

    Talking to Sonya will be a good distraction, yes. Clearing her throat, Kate looks back at her. “How about you? What are you getting?”

    Sonya hums for a moment, not taking her eyes off of the menu even when she answers at first.

    “I was going to get the salmon but if you are getting something naughty, I will want something naughty too, so…Hmm…Yelena, what are you getting?”

    She looks up then, first at Yelena, then at Kate, then at Yelena again when she answers. “Mac and cheese bites. And a classic cheeseburger.”

    The way she says it, without even looking up from the menu, is incredibly endearing to Kate for some reason, and she stifles the smile threatening to rise onto her features. Sonya turns back to her menu, pursing her lips.

    “Ah. Well, I’m not going to be the only one showing restraint… Did you see that there is a mac & cheese burger?”

    “There is?”

    Kate can’t quite stifle the smile this time around, at the sheer interest in Yelena’s voice and looks up to see her eyes light up in wonder as she dives back into the menu. It’s very cute.

    Sonya snorts, drawing Kate’s eyes to herself and the smirk on her face tells Kate that she is not being subtle. Not that she ever really is…

    Shrugging, she glances at Yelena one more time, who is still engrossed in her menu, before turning to look down at her own once more, just to have something to do. Once again, she reads through the burgers section but quickly, she figures out that she will stick to her choice, so that distraction is quickly gone… And in a few seconds, her mind is inevitably back on Yelena.

    That won’t really do.

    Remember, Kate. She said ‘one time thing’.

    As a way to keep herself distracted and to respect the boundaries Yelena laid down, she does her best to focus on something else.

    The doorman. The bugs. Mason. The motel.

    Anything.

    “So-”

    “Hi Ladies, how are you doing tonight?”

    Proud of how she hides her jump in her seat, Kate turns towards the unexpected waitress with a smile. She is young, Kate’s age probably, pretty with beautiful, dark olive skin and a sparkling smile. She wears an old-school, red and white stripy uniform but somehow manages to pull it off, her dark hair falling in waves around her shoulders. “Hi. Good, thanks. How about you?”

    The girl smiles, tilting her head from one side to the other and back.

    “Not bad. I’m off tomorrow for my birthday.”

    Kate is fairly suspicious that it’s probably not the girl’s, Jen’s, birthday tomorrow, and she is saying it in the hopes of earning some extra tips, but she entertains it nonetheless. “Oh, nice. Happy birthday! What are you turning?”

    Maintaining eye contact, Jen’s smile widens and she shifts her weight from one leg to the other, a hand coming to rest on her hip.

    “Thanks! Twenty-two.”

    Lowering her menu, Kate entertains the conversation a bit longer, her lips stretching into a smile.

    “Any big plans?”

    Jen bats her eyelashes, her eyes flicking over to Yelena and Sonya but returning to Kate right away.

    Ou-oh.

    “Just the usual. Drinks with friends in the city. Might check out Vice.” Humming, Kate nods with a smile, trying not to continue the conversation, suddenly feeling the weight of all three pairs of eyes on her. When she does not offer any more commentary or questions, Jen smoothly transitions back to professional, lifting her notepad. “So, can I take your order?”

    “Yeah, sure. Um, I’ll have the rodeo burger and a cookies and cream milkshake, please.” The waitress writes it down, her eyes meeting Kate’s when she is finished, her smile widening just a little more and her eyes sparking in a very specific way. Oh no.

    Any other time, just not now.

    Jen’s eyes drop to Kate’s form, and she taps the back of her pen to her notepad twice before she speaks.

    “Cool shirt.”

    Glancing down at her outfit too, like she doesn’t know what she is wearing, Kate struggles to come up with a response. It’s not that she is not used to being flirted with, or even flirting back. She absolutely would in another world if it wasn’t for her whole… situation… …And the weight of those eyes on her.

    “Thanks, it’s uh. It’s very warm.”

    That’s like the lamest, most disengaged response could come up with on the spot but as she looks up to meet Jen’s eyes again, she smirks nonetheless.

    “Hm. Cute and funny.”

    The waitress and her dimpled smile then turn away, and Kate swears she feels a bead of sweat begin to form on her temple. Across from her, Sonya looks ready to burst out laughing at any second, her eyes shifting between Yelena, Kate, and the waitress. Yelena is looking at her menu still…or again and to an onlooker, she might look perfectly nonchalant and uninterested, but Kate is pretty sure her jaw is clenched a bit harder than normal. Suddenly, avoiding the evening from turning uncomfortable with unsaid and unresolved stuff, like the whole Amanda situation was, when they had such a nice time on the way over here, seems more important than anything.

    “Fiancé… My finacé got it for me.”

    All three women stare at Kate, as she points at Yelena across from her, looking up at the waitress with wide eyes. To her credit, Jen only raises an eyebrow in surprise and blinks once, before smirking again, turning towards Yelena this time.

    “Huh. Good for you. You got great taste.”

    Kate imagines that her head must look like a flaming tomato, and Sonya looks like she is on the verge of cracking a rib from holding back her laughter, the corners of her mouth engaged in a precarious dance. Yelena rolls her lips together, but Kate can see that she is having a hard time hiding her amusement too, her lower lip slightly clinched between her teeth for a few seconds and her eyes alight with mirth.

    Okay, maybe Kate jumped the gun on this one…Just a little.

    “Thank you. I will have the mac and cheese burger with fries and a coke” The waitress writes it down, still smirking and Kate swallows but does her best to put on a confident front, leaning back in her seat and putting her arm up on the backrest. “Alright. How about you, sweetie?

    Sonya looks at the girl like she is her new best friend, grinning and exchanging a look that Kate resolutely ignores, pulling out her phone instead just to look down at something. “The sunset special, please, with extra bacon. And a Coke Zero.”

    There is nothing on her phone, unfortunately, and after writing down Sonya’s order too, the girl turns away, but not without throwing Kate one more amused glance. She gives a smile in return that she hopes looks less awkward than it feels, the three of them quiet for a few seconds once she leaves.

    Okay. Showtime.

    “So, if he really is the one that broke in, what do we do about the doorman?” Pursing her lips, Kate stares at the spot to the right of Yelena’s head, unwilling to acknowledge the shit-eating grin on Sonya’s face.

    “Maybe you could tell him we are engaged too. It seems you enjoy blurting it out to everyone.”

    That’s pretty rich coming from someone who is literally wearing the ring right this second… Wetting her lips, Kate shifts her eyes towards Yelena, resolutely not looking down at Yelena's hand, but instead noting the not even slightly concealed amusement on her face. She looks smug, leaning back against the plushy seat, her eyes sparkling with satisfied delight. …At her expense...

    Whatever.

    Kate will take that over the tension of whatever this situation could have devolved into, with how on edge things have been between them all day.

    Puffing out her cheeks, Kate shifts in her seat before she leans back once more, looking away. “Whatever. I just didn’t want to give her the wrong impression and that seemed the easiest way out.”

    “The wrong impression that you are not engaged?”

    Rolling her eyes at Sonya’s question, Kate turns back to the two of them, ignoring the smug smile on Yelena’s face.

    “That I’m interested.”

    Predictably, Sonya keeps on pushing.

    “You aren’t?”

    Lifting an eyebrow, Kate purses her lips, pinning Sonya with a look, partially so she doesn’t look at Yelena.

    “No.”

    “Why?”

    At that, even Yelena turns to look at Sonya for a second and Kate’s eyes flicker to her, unsure how openly address their evening before. Then again, Yelena made it quite clear that she is not looking for anything serious, or even unserious, so…

    “She was obviously just fishing for tips. Both with the birthday bit and the flirting.” Tilting her head to the side, Sonya waits for a second, before nodding. “Maybe so. That still doesn’t answer the question of why you are not interested?” Kate huffs, stretching out her legs under the table, but careful not to kick Yelena sitting across from her.

    “What’s the point? We are here for like a day or two tops. And we have a lot of shit to do. It’s not like we have time and even if we did-”

    “So if we were staying longer, and we didn’t have shit to do-“ Sonya interrupts her, and then Kate interrupts her in return, cutting off the questioning before it can lead them somewhere uncomfortable.

    “No.”

    There is a chuckle hidden in the exhale puffed through Sonya’s nose, and she leans back for a moment, but she is not quite done.

    “Not your type?”

    Her nose scrunches up a bit as she asks, and Kate feels some of her discomfort ease at the playful expression. Rolling her eyes once more, Kate purses her lips and shakes her head. “I don’t have a type.”

    At that, Sonya grins and quirks an eyebrow. She doesn’t have to nod towards Yelena to make her point, but she does it anyway, her grin widening.

    “You kind of do though.”

    Feeling her ears warm up a little, Kate clears her throat and sighs deeply. Enough of this... “So, about the doorman,-“ Yelena cuts off her question, speaking up with a blink.

    “She does have a point…”

    Oh, that should be good.

    Raising both of her eyebrows, Kate leans back and looks at Yelena with a smirk. “What do you mean?”

    Kate sees the way Yelena crosses her legs under the table, leaning back to regard Kate with both hands still on the top of the table.

    “The all-American girl next door.”

    Eyebrows drawing together in confusion, Kate's blinks, even her face scrunching up a bit. What even…?

    Shaking her head to herself in slightly frustrated confusion, Kate’s brow knits together. “What are you talking about?”

    Yelena blinks once, slowly, like a cat studying its prey.

    “Like the waitress. Or Amygdala.”

    …

    “...Who?”

    “Your marketing-girlfriend.”

    For Christ’s sake…

    The comment draws a chuckle from Kate, but her confusion is not quite gone. Does Yelena remember the fact that Kate slept with her last night? That they have been dancing around this thing for the last few weeks, together?

    “Amanda? What…? No.”

    At least Kate is vilified in her exasperation by the fact that at least for a few moments, Sonya looks at Yelena like someone does at a child when it says something super weird and out of pocket, her mouth slightly agape.

    It only lasts for a second or two, before she shakes her head, looking back at Kate. “Not the description I’d use…”

    Kate tucks the corner of her mouth, shaking her head with a chuckle.

    “You are both wrong. I don’t have a type. And for the record, even if I did, which I don’t, it wouldn’t be any nationality or girl-next-door, or anything superficial like that. You either dig someone’s vibe, or you don’t.”

    Sonya leans forward onto her elbow on the vinyl tabletop, her eyes glinting in a way that lets Kate know this is not a game she wants to play with either Widow.

    “Everybody has a type.”

    Well, it seems outright denial is not going to work...

    Deflection it is.

    “Well, what’s yours then?”

    At her smile widening, Kate feels like she walked into a trap exactly like Sonya expected her to, as the Widow begins to count on her fingers lazily.

    “Tall. Strong. Dark. Rich…”

    Sonya’s eyebrows furrow in mock confusion, and she even takes a dramatic pause before she continues.

    “…Oh, wait...”

    She turns her head to the side to stare pointedly at Yelena’s profile, and Kate chuckles at the sigh that she releases, before turning her head to meet Sonya’s stare head-on. “I do not recall you having such restrictive standards a few years ago.” The two of them look at each other for a few moments, before Sonya’s smile widens even more, just slightly. Snorting, Kate leans back, striking while Yelena is vulnerable… Conversationally speaking.

    “You know, for all the Sex and City you’ve watched, I’d think you’d be less slut-shamey.” Her jaw dropping in offence, Yelena turns towards Kate while Sonya snickers, turning to look at her too.

    “I am not slut shaming her. I am just pointing out that when we were traveling together, “tall, dark and rich”-”

    Lifting her hands, Yelena does air-quote marks and it takes about 98% of Kate’s willpower to not zero in on the ring still on her finger.

    ”-were definitely not the only type of people that she brought home.”

    In another world, where the two of them didn’t have sex less than 24 hours ago, Kate would ask if tall, dark, and lean were the type of people that Yelena brought home during their travels, like Sonya alluded to, but… it’s probably best she doesn’t know. She will be happily delusional and think that Sonya just meant her.

    “Well, maybe she knows that’s her type because she tried it all… Or most.” Shrugging, Kate grins at Yelena, who looks back at her, unimpressed.

    “I was proving your point, Kate. That not everybody has a type.”

    Huh.

    Next to Yelena, Sonya snickers and Kate deflates her in smugness just a little. It only lasts a moment, before she leans forward, and grins at Yelena again, batting her eyelashes. “In that case, you are absolutely correct.”

    At her playful gesture, even Yelena’s face cracks with a small, throaty chuckle, leaning back with a small shake of her head. The two of them hold eye-contact for just a second or two longer, sending Kate’s pulse speeding up again.

    Before they can continue their conversation, Kate’s phone buzzes with a notification, and she picks it up without a thought. Immediately, she smiles at the thumbnail of the video Laure sent her, tapping the screen to open it.

    “Which all-American girl-next-door girlfriend of yours got you smiling like that?” Kate huffs out a chuckle at Sonya’s ridiculous question, her eyes not looking up from her phone.

    “It’s Laura. Clint’s wife. She sent a video of Lucky.”

    She watches the roughly 15-second clip of Lucky throwing a squeaky toy up in the air for himself and then howling when it squeaks. Even with her smile, her throat feels suddenly tight, already missing her best friend so much even though he has barely been gone for a day.

    But while Kate might be missing him a lot, her heart warms at the thought of him safe and happy at Clint’s farm, having adventures and playing with his kids. With fall rolling in full force, the leaves are turning everywhere Kate looks, and she imagines the colorful landscape of Iowa must be amazing this time of the year. It’s the perfect place for him to be with fallen leaves, and exciting smells, naps to be head in front of fireplaces…

    Without a word, she slides the phone across the table and Yelena leans over to watch the video when Sonya picks up Kate’s phone and plays it. Yelena smiles at it too, her eyes lifting to meet Kate’s a second later, before looking away and around the diner. “I might go and visit Fanny next weekend…As long as we figure this doorman thing out.” Yelena is not looking at her when she speaks, and Kate sees the way her throat bobs as she swallows after. The words feel like a glass of cold water being poured over her head, but Kate tries not to take them personally. Yelena has been here for weeks, has been away from her dog for weeks, it is perfectly natural for her to want to see her and take some time away. It has nothing to do with her, surely.

    She can’t say it’s not somewhat suspicious though, after the day of Yelena avoiding her and acting all hot and cold. Then again, if Yelena truly wants to keep things professional, it actually might be the best for both of them, to have some time and space, because… Because at least for Kate, any time she looks at Yelena, she sees her naked on her sheets and feels her skin against her own and-

    “Now?”

    Sonya turns her entire torso towards Yelena next to her, an eyebrow arched. Yelena does not look back at her friend, following something or someone above Kate’s shoulder with her eyes instead.

    “Next weekend is Alexei’s birthday.”

    The eyebrow raises even higher and Sonya’s lips purse, but she nods a second later, turning back toward Kate, seemingly accepting Yelena’s reasoning.

    “Don’t worry, Kate. I will keep you good company while she is gone.”

    She winks at Kate then, and she can’t help but chuckle, resisting the urge to turn towards Yelena this time.

    Despite all the joking around and the… slightly heated vibes, Kate should keep herself in check… Try to keep to the boundaries of a professional friendship between two people who had really good sex, less than 24 hours ago.

    Maybe she should also stop reminding herself of that fact every couple of minutes. That would probably help.

    But the ring glinting on Yelena’s finger and the glowing embers behind her eyes when they meet Kate’s make it really, really fucking hard…

    Still, stay professional, Kate.

    “Will you go before we figure out this doorman business?”

    Yelena rolls her lips together, finally looking back at Kate after her question. “Probably not. I will go if we know your place is safe to go back to.”

    Nodding in acceptance, Kate pulls her phone back to herself. If she really wanted, she could go and spend the weekend with Clint and his family too, while Yelena is gone... But, she meant what she said to him. She needs to put an end to this and she can’t really leave and have a vacation until she does.

    “Thanks.”

    Yelena nods back at her, before inhaling sharply, her demeanor shifting into professional without missing a beat.

    “If it turns out that the doorman really planted the bugs, we will need to talk to him. We need to figure out who else is in on it before you can move back in.”

    Beginning to tap a light rhythm against the tabletop, Kate forces her brain to change gears too. Exhaling, she clears her throat.

    “What’s your theory?”

    Pursing her lips, Yelena holds her eyes, the lines between her eyebrows deepening ever so slightly as she thinks. For a few moments, she is silent, looking at Kate but not really at her at the same time.

    “I think this is exactly the type of thing Valentina would do. Keep an eye on her investments.”

    Leaning slightly forward, Kate finds her focus.

    “Yeah?”

    “Yes.”

    It feels like Yelena is still deep in thought, the gears in her head moving, and there is something else coming. Kate asks, wanting to know all her thoughts.

    “But…?”

    Slowly, Yelena exhales, glancing at Sonya as she leans slightly forward too. “But… Using the CIA-issue transmitter would be sloppy. And Valentina is not sloppy… Unless she wants to be.”

    Shaking her head a little in her confusion, Kate asks her to clarify.

    “What does that mean?”

    “That it is either someone wanting to make it look like it is her, or that she wants us, me to know that it is her, when we find them.”

    Eyebrows drawing together to match Yelena's serious expression, Kate speaks again. “Why would she want that?”

    Yelena’s face twitches, the lines of it deepening for a second before they smooth out. “As a power play? To show that she can get to… us, whenever she wants to? I do not know.”

    The stumble over ‘us’ makes Kate remember Valentina’s calculating eyes on her, and the apparent conclusions she has drawn about them, even weeks ago. If Yelena is right, it makes sense that someone like Val would use their perceived relationship to keep Yelena or both of them in check.

    “Right…“ The whole ordeal makes Kate’s head spin, thoughts racing to take each other over, but she is trying to slow herself down and think it all through systematically. For a few moments, neither of them speaks and then Sonya, who has been listening to their conversation silently until now, leans forward to join in.

    “The next question, after we figure out if it’s Valentina or not, is to find out if Rojas knows.” Sighing, Kate nods. That is also a pretty worrying thought.

    “How do we do that?”

    Sonya shrugs, looking almost apologetic but Yelena shakes her head, almost distracting Kate with how she begins to play with the ring on her finger over the table, seemingly entirely unaware of the action, as her eyes move around the diner.

    “I am fairly certain that he does not know.”

    Before Kate can ask how she would know that, Sonya asks in her stead.

    “Why?”

    Once more, Yelena rolls her lips together and her eyes move between Kate and Sonya when she begins to explain.

    “I know Javier Rojas. He is smart and he is cunning but he is not a patient man.” Yelena leans forward even more, lowering her voice even though nobody but them is around to hear them.

    “-And more importantly, I know Valentina. She definitely did not read him into all her plans.” Nodding, Kate mulls her words over for a few seconds, all three of them quiet. In a moment, she wets her lips before speaking again, her eyes shifting from Yelena to Sonya and back, as she rubs her forehead distractedly.

    “Okay… So, this might sound kind of stupid, but can’t we just ask her?” Identical blank expressions are her first answers, blinking back at her. It’s Sonya who asks her to clarify.

    “If she had your house bugged?”

    “Yeah.”

    Pursing her lips, Yelena tilts her head to the side and raises an eyebrow. “We could. But we cannot believe whatever she answers.”

    Kate puffs out her cheeks and leans back as she exhales.

    “Right.”

    They are all quiet for a few moments, deep in thought, "So we all agree it wasn't Kingpin, right?"

    Shifting her gaze from Yelena to Sonya, the other two exchange a glance, before Yelena shrugs and answers.

    "It seems unlikely. As you said, if he knows where you live, why has he not come to kill you yet?"

    Kate nods, sighing deeply.

    "Valentina or Rojas are not much more reassuring to be fair."

    Yelena cringes a little, before nodding.

    "Either way, it is bad news... Unless the doorman was acting alone."

    Blinking, Kate tries to gauge if Yelena thinks that is a serious option to consider. She gets her answer a moment later, when Sonya chuckles, lightly hitting Yelena's arm with the back of her head as she grins at Kate.

    "Maybe he is just a standard creepy stalker. Wouldn't that be a nice plot-twist." Kate smiles, leaning her head back but not taking her eyes off Sonya as she answers her. "Maybe, if I am lucky, he is a serial killer too."

    Her delivery earns her matching snickers from Yelena and Sonya, her heart giving an embarrassing little jump at making Yelena laugh as their eyes meet.

    Stop being so gay...

    Jen arrives with a tray full of their food and drinks just in time, providing a welcome distraction from her own thoughts.

    “Here you go. Do you need anything else?”

    Kate looks around their table before turning back to the waitress, smiling politely up at her. “Yeah, can I get some mayo?”

    Smiling back, Jen nods.

    “Sure, I’ll be right back.”

    As she turns back, Sonya looks around the table too, taking in the vast amounts of food they all have in front of each other.

    “Wow. We really need to get back to training.”

    Kate picks up a fry, unable and unwilling to wait any longer. She slips it into her mouth, humming satisfiedly at the taste but at Sonya’s words, she glances up at her, meeting her eyes just as she continues.

    “-Maybe you and I can do that while Yelena is in Ohio.”

    Chewing the fry, Kate nods and swallows it quickly before she answers.

    “Sounds good.”

    The two of them exchange a smile while Kate does her best to not watch Yelena, as she twists the ring on her finger again, looking around deep in thought. Jen comes back with the mayo Kate asked for, handing it to her.

    “Here you go.”

    “Thanks.”

    After that, she is gone and the three of them dig in, silently eating for a few minutes. When they do start talking again, the topic of Valentina and Kate’s bugged apartment is dropped, the three of them discussing the food, Jersey, and the hotel they are staying at. They are almost done eating when Yelena brings the conversation back to work-related topics once more.

    “Have you talked to Barton?”

    Kate covers her mouth, full of her last two fries as she nods.

    “Yeah. He called earlier.”

    Yelena leans back, apparently finished with her food, with only a few bites of her patty remaining on her plate.

    “Did you tell him about the FBI?”

    Just like when they arrived at the hotel, Yelena’s eyes are looking to somewhere the right of Kate’s head, almost looking at her but not quite.

    Kate kind of gets it…

    Obviously, Yelena must know that Kate didn't tell Clint anything about the other events of the night, but they are both aware that most likely it's on everyone's mind. Swallowing the last of her food, Kate leans back too, picking up her milkshake. “Yup. Told him about the raid, the bugs, and Mason.”

    She drinks some of her shake through the red, plastic straw as Yelena responds. “Did he have anything to say?”

    Lowering her drink back down, Kate nods, swallowing before she answers. “He said he might try to get me listed as an employee of one of the agencies. S.H.I.E.L.D. or the army, or something. That way they can’t get me on vigilantism at least, or not easily anyway.”

    Finally, Yelena’s eyes shift and she actually meets Kate’s eyes as she nods, flicking her hair out of her eyes as she leans back.

    “That is a good idea. We really do not need them on your ass with everything else.” Kate huffs in amusement, taking a long gulp of her milkshake again as she lifts her eyebrows as if to say “you don’t say”. Across the table, Sonya snorts, drawing Kate’s eyes to herself. At Kate's raised eyebrow and quizzical glance, Sonya chuckles to herself before grinning at her. “It’s just funny to imagine Kate Bishop in the army.”

    At that, Yelena huffs in amusement as well, and Kate feels like she should be defending herself. Tilting her drink so the straw is pointing in Sonya's direction, she lowers her chin, looking back half seriously.

    “Hey, I could do damn well in the army, if I wanted.”

    Her somewhat defensive tone only serves to amuse both Widows even more, and Yelena shakes her head with a smile.

    “No, you could not.”

    Resisting the urge to cross her arms and look even more defensive, Kate huffs, asking for clarification.

    “Why not?”

    Yelena’s smile widens into a small grin for a moment and she raises an eyebrow sharply at Kate, her eyes full of...affection?

    Get a grip, Kate.

    One. Time. Thing.

    “You are not exactly great at following orders.”

    Gaping back at her, Kate looks over to Sonya but finds the same amused doubt on her features. She smiles too, putting a placating hand on the surface of the table while she holds Kate’s eyes with a grin.

    “Sorry, she is right…But if it makes you feel better, at least you’d look amazing in the uniform.”

    Furrowing her eyebrows, Kate shifts a bit lower in her seat, pouting just a little. “Yeah, I’m not sure that makes up for it, no.”

    Yelena chuckles, the sound replacing the slight genuine offense Kate feels with sparks of affection, while Sonya just grins at her good-naturedly. Both Widow’s eyes jumping to above her shoulder alerts Kate to the fact that someone is coming, so this time, she does not jump when Jen speaks up suddenly.

    “Hi ladies, how did you like your burgers?”

    Kate leans back, giving her space to pick up her empty plate.

    “Great, thanks.”

    She picks up her plate, before moving onto the other side to take Sonya’s and Yelena’s as well.

    “Can I get you anything else?”

    They all look at each other, but nobody seems to have space left for dessert or anything else, so Yelena shakes her head as she turns back to the waitress.

    “No, thank you, just the check please.”

    Jen nods, halting with their plates in her hands before walking away.

    “Sure. Cash or card?”

    Lifting the straw to her mouth, Kate slurps the last of her milkshake, letting Yelena deal with paying, since she handed all her cash over earlier, and only has cards with her own name on them.

    “Card.”

    Her eyes move lazily between the two, Jen halting after only a step, looking back at Yelena with all their plates balanced on her arms.

    “Can you come up to the register to pay? Our machine is on the charger.” “Yeah, sure.”

    Across from her, Yelena slips out from the booth, and fishes out her wallet from the pocket of her jacket, before walking after Jen without another word. While Sonya is preoccupied with her phone, Kate pulls out her own, but there are no new messages since the video Laura sent. "Did Herman get back to you?"

    Glancing up at Sonya, their eyes meet but she shakes her head at Kate, her expression apologetic.

    "Not yet, no. Sorry."

    Nodding, Kate exhales, and Sonya goes back to typing on her phone, presumably talking to Tommy. With nothing better to do, Kate texts a quick update to Clint about the doorman too, drumming a quick little beat on the tabletop with her fingers. When Yelena has not returned from playing after a minute or so, she slips the phone back into her pocket and turns around in her seat, watching her talk to Jen.

    In a few minutes, somewhere around the corner of 8th and 53rd, she spots Yelena's honey- blonde hair a bit ahead of her and slows down, ignoring the annoying little flutter in her stomach at catching sight of her. Switching to her messages, Kate types out a quick text to Yelena, unsure what their plan is.

    [to: Yelena] 8:48 am: Should I go up to you?

    From her position, a dozen or so yards behind Yelena, she sees her slip her phone out of the pocket of her fur coat, her own buzzing with an answer in a few seconds. [from: Yelena] 8:48 am: Yes Slipping her phone back into her jacket, Kate speeds up, side-stepping a few people and never once taking her eyes off of Yelena. She seems to have no trouble keeping herself from bumping into anyone, skillfully navigating the crowd like water flowing among rocks. Finally, Kate catches up to her, slowing down once they are side by side. "Hi."

    Yelena only glances at Kate for a moment, but her lips tilt upwards, even as she turns forward once again.

    "Hey. He is about 20 meters in front of us. Tall, dark blue coat, black hair." Having been so focused on finding and catching up to Yelena, Kate almost forgot about the fact that they are there to tail someone, and she quickly turns forward as well, her eyes searching the people walking ahead of them. Despite not having a sense of how much 20 meters is, she catches sight of who she thinks Yelena means, but asks to double-check. "The one that just passed the bakery?"

    "Yes. We have an address for him from Herman, but we will see if that is actually where he goes. Right now, it seems so."

    Kate nods, glancing once more at Yelena before turning forward again.

    "Okay. Um, listen, Clint called. We got a problem."

    Yelena's eyebrows furrow for a split second, and she glances back at Kate. "Take off your hood, you look like a spy. What problem?"

    Apart from raising an eyebrow, Kate does not argue, slipping the hood off her head as she begins to explain.

    "His contact finally got a location on the pathway. Do you know the company Iron Mountain?"

    Yelena's brows lift even though her eyes never leave the doorman. The sunlight reflects off of her hair, making it seem lighter than in the evening, and Kate's attention is split between that and her words.

    "I do. Rich people, fortune 500 companies and your government store their things and information with them."

    Nodding, Kate veers closer to Yelena to avoid bumping into a fashionable old lady, wearing a coat not entirely dissimilar from Yelena's.

    "Yup, that’s the one. Anyway, the pathway is in their underground facility upstate, but they are taking it back to the FBI's New York office tomorrow morning."

    At that, Yelena's eyes glint as she glances at Kate, her lips turning upwards again. "Ah. Then we can go after the transport. Do we know when it's leaving?" Trying not to get distracted by Yelena's eyes, looking particularly green in this light, Kate turns forward again, her gaze seeking out the doorman once more.

    “Um, yeah, the transport is one option but I'm not sure how we could pull it off without anyone noticing that something was taken which is a pain in the ass. But, according to Clint's source, all the transported materials, including my mom's evidence, are going to be in a holding area on the almost top level of the facility for 2 hours before they take them. So, Clint and I think the better option might be to try to take it from there." Kate sees Yelena nod beside her, seemingly deep in thought as she tilts her head to the side, pursing her lips. It takes her a few seconds to speak, but her voice is more observatory than actually worried.

    "Both options are pretty risky with this little time to prepare."

    Nodding in agreement, Kate chews on her lower lip, racking her brain to come up with an idea too, while she distractedly watches the doorman halt at a crossing ahead of them. For a few moments, both of them are quiet, before Yelena speaks again.

    "Sonya says she will call Mason to see if he can get us papers to get inside or something." The two of them slow down to avoid catching up to the doorman, before turning to the side to pretend to check out the display of a shop.

    "Oh…you have an earpiece or the two of you are telepathically linked somehow?" Yelena turns towards her for a second with an eyebrow raised, while Kate uses the reflection in the display window to keep an eye on the doorman, even as she grins at her own joke. "Of course, I have an earpiece."

    Kate hums in agreement, only speaking again when the light for the crossing changes and the doorman begins to walk again.

    "He is moving. Speaking of, did you find out anything about him yet?"

    Yelena and she begin to walk forward too, forced closer together again by a group of teenagers taking up most of the sidewalk.

    "Not too much, no. Only the name he used to get this job and his supposed address. We follow him now, to confirm if he goes to his home, but if we need to break into Iron Mountain tonight, we should probably go home after… To plan and prepare." Nodding, Kate walks around a puddle of suspicious liquid on the ground before veering back towards Yelena once more.

    "Yeeeaaah. Bishop Security used to do security for them, so I think I have some blueprints and maybe even some security plans for the facility. I'll check when we get home." Ahead of them, the doorman takes a right turn, quickly disappearing from sight. "That is good... Going underground is always pretty risky. Entry and exit is very limited." "Yup. Not to mention that we are supposed to do this without anyone noticing we were ever there, so no cutting anything, no knocking out anyone, no explosives, no nothing." It takes Yelena a few moments to answer, her voice amused when she does. "Yup."

    At Yelena repeating the word she used, Kate smiles, twisting her head to look at her. Yelena doesn't turn to look back, but her lips are stretched into a small smile, and Kate grins as she turns forward again too.

    The moment feels like a pleasant hum under Kate’s skin, like most of their interactions are these days and Kate is reminded of the third topic they have to discuss as they take a right turn too, onto 49th street.

    The article.

    Yelena doesn't seem to be in a bad mood, the opposite actually, so at least she is most likely not mad about it. As inconspicuously as she can, Kate glances down under the disguise of watching her step, confirming that Yelena is still wearing the ring.

    Her stomach flutters when she sees the telltale glint of sparkling light on Yelena's finger, and she pulls her eyes away quickly, seeking out the doorman walking ahead again instead, as a safe spot, and clearing her throat.

    "So, about the article..."

    She leaves the sentence hanging for a few seconds, hoping Yelena will catch on and supply some type of statement, which will help Kate gauge what she is thinking about it all. Unfortunately, Yelena doesn't seem to be in a hurry to add her own thoughts, but from the corner of her eyes, Kate sees that she blinks a few times in quick succession, despite her gaze not wavering from her target.

    With not much to indicate how Yelena might be feeling, Kate clears her throat once again and continues.

    "I am sorry about the uh, the attention. Do you... Have you read it?"

    On her right, Yelena’s face is clear of any indication of how she might feel, blinking slowly once.

    "Yes.-"

    For a few agonizingly long heartbeats, Yelena doesn't say anything more. Then, she lifts her chin and purses her lips before giving Kate a side glance.

    "I can not believe you just gave me a ring that is worth 1.8 million dollars." At the unexpected comment, Kate chuckles, resisting the urge to fidget with the hem of her hoodie.

    "I think it's realistically closer to 2."

    At Yelena's head whipping around to look at her with a borderline scandalized look on her features, Kate can't help but smile, giving her a sideward glance too. Yelena realizes she is being teased a heartbeat later and rolls her eyes but Kate adds before she can say anything else.

    "Well, considering everything you have done for me, I think it's more than well deserved." Yelena blinks slowly, once, twice, an eyebrow slowly lifting and Kate realizes with a strong beat of her heart against her ribcage, that her statement could easily be misunderstood. She quickly adds, despite being pretty sure that Yelena knows what she means. "I mean, you saved my life like a gazillion times at this point. And like, been by my side through this whole thing and-"

    Yelena reaching up to her ear and tapping it, makes her swallow the rest of her sentence. Most likely, it was to keep Sonya out of their conversation and a second later Yelena turns to look at her properly, her face serious.

    "Kate, I am not keeping the ring. I will wear it until the FBI is off our backs, but then we will quietly break up."

    Cringing a little at her words, Kate chuckles and shoves both her hands deep into her pockets and ignores the slightly sour feeling of rejection in her stomach.

    "Yeeaahhh, yeah. I know that. Seriously, I will come up with some other way to make it up to you…”

    When there is no immediate answer from Yelena, the silence suddenly feels a bit awkward, and Kate says the first thing that comes to her mind.

    “-But hey, at least if I die during this whole thing, you can keep it for your troubles." Yelena rolls her eyes at Kate's dark joke, ignoring her words but she nods a second later seemingly to herself, and a small smile cracks her serious facade just a little. “With that cleared up… Sonya made a passionate plea, that we should probably make an announcement."

    "Pardon?"

    Yelena huffs, but the humor is not gone from her face, even as she turns away to face forward again, reaching up to tuck a stray strand of hair behind her ear.

    "About the engagement, on social media or something.”

    Pausing, she glances at Kate and at her most likely surprised face, continues to explain while her eyes seek out their target once more.

    “-If we do not, people will most likely draw their own conclusions, which is not a problem personally but to do so, they will try to dig into both of our lives and possibly find things we do not want them to find."

    She turns to Kate, waiting for her to nod in acknowledgment as their eyes meet. Swallowing, Kate nods, ignoring the whiplash she feels from this back and forth.

    "Yeah… Yeah, she is right. We're most likely better off if we, uhm... control the narrative." Yelena nods back at her, and they both turn to face forward again. Kate risks another side glance, considering whether she should ask what she wants to ask. But the last thing they need is miscommunication and Yelena was very clear with her boundaries, so it's most likely a good idea to discuss this.

    "Are you...Wait, do you still have Sonya in your ear?"

    Despite suspecting their conversation is private after Yelena tapping her ear earlier, she wants to make sure, uncertain how comfortable Yelena is with discussing what she wants to ask in front of her friend, no matter what she might have shared with her before. "We are muted."

    Wetting her lips, Kate nods, and glances at Yelena once more, wanting to see her face properly to gauge her reaction when she asks her question.

    "Right, okay. So, um, are you comfortable with this whole thing...after what we did the other night?"

    Yelena does not look at her, and she is quiet for a few seconds, likely mulling Kate's question over. Kate glances at her a couple of times, reveling in the slight blush she has coloring her face and the way she distractedly pushes a strand of her golden hair behind her ear. "Yes. One has nothing to do with the other.-"

    As Kate lifts an eyebrow in slight disbelief, Yelena raises her chin once more, but Kate sees the side glance she throws her.

    "-We keep up this pretense to not get caught in a lie with the FBI. We did that to get it out of our system."

    This is the second time Yelena used that expression. Get it out of their system. Well, judging from how Kate is hyper-aware of Yelena next to her, and the slight pink hue on Yelena's cheeks, and just the last 36 or so hours in general, Kate sincerely doubts anything is out of their system just yet.

    Feeling emboldened and ready to toe the line a little, or at least rile Yelena up a bit, Kate puts on a small grin, giving Yelena a side glance too.

    "So...how do we know it's out of our system?"

    There is genuine surprise in Yelena's gaze when she whips her head to the side, but it quickly morphs into exasperation and mirth, as she rolls her eyes and faces forwards again. Kate does not receive a verbal answer so she snickers, turning her face forward again, meeting the doorman's eyes in the side mirror of a car.

    Wait a second...

    "Shit."

    She quickly tears her eyes away, firmly looking at Yelena, in case the doorman is watching, and putting on a fake smile as she says the next words.

    "I think he saw us."

    Yelena's voice is completely in mission mode in a second, stepping into Kate's side. "He is turning around. Put your arm around me and laugh at something I said." Kate does as she is told, drawing Yelena further against herself and turning her body more towards her. She does not dare to look at the doorman, as they draw closer to each other, but her muscles are locked and ready, in case he tries something when they pass each other on the sidewalk.

    Similarly, Yelena's eyes are glued to Kate's own, adoring girlfriend character fully back on, switching gears so quickly, it's honestly impressive.

    "...And then, she said that it was not her cake! It was so funny!"

    Yelena's eyes stray from Kate's face a few heartbeats after the passing happens, glancing behind her back, quickly dropping her persona.

    "Shit! He is running! Go! I'll cut him off."

    Kate is shoved semi-gently away, but her body was ready for this as soon as her eyes met the doorman’s, so immediately she takes off after him, sprinting back the way they came from. She does not hear Yelena's footsteps behind her, and she doesn't have an earpiece, but she trusts Sonya has an eye on them both or something, and is coordinating their movements. The doorman is fast, but Kate is hot on his heels, running after him and skilfully evading the bystanders on the sidewalk as she takes off her hat and shoves it into the pocket of her jacket. Adrenaline filling her blood, Kate runs as fast as she can, slowly gaining on the man, but he takes a left, disappearing from sight for a few seconds. As Kate nears the corner, she slows down, not wanting to get jumped and peers around it carefully, but he is not there waiting for her. She spots his sprinting form across the small plaza she finds herself in instead, and quickly, she takes off again after him.

    He makes it across the square and Kate sees him run across the street on the other side too, into a ground-level parking lot with a car elevator. He sprints by the stacked-up cars and into the narrow lot behind and to the left, disappearing again but only for a few moments before Kate catches sight of him again as she runs across the street too, then by the stacked-up cars. She feels hot and sweaty despite the chilly weather, not exactly dressed for a run in her thick denim jacket and hoodie, but she pushes on, watching as he reaches a chained-up gate on the other side of the lot and begins to climb over it.

    "Great..."

    She groans to herself as she runs on, still about a dozen yards behind him. He climbs over and hops down on the other side, glancing back at her before taking a left and sprinting out of sight. Kate vaults over the gate faster than he did, her years of doing parkour coming very handy this morning, ignoring the homeless woman sitting outside the gate and yelling after her.

    "Are you out of your damn mind?!!"

    On the other side, Kate takes a hard left too, catching sight of the doorman's swishing blue coat and takes off sprinting again, trying to think of what she will do if she catches up to him. The man sprints down the sidewalk, then across the street to get to the other side, while Kate feels her phone buzzing against her thigh.

    She crosses over too, ignoring the phone and solely focused on not losing sight of him.
