Ahead of her, the doorman twists to look at her again, grabbing hold of a table from the patio of a café, and pushing it onto the sidewalk to block her way. He then takes off again, running across the big intersection the street opens up to, clogged with morning traffic despite the weekend.

    Kate jumps over the fallen-over table easily and sprints across the intersection too, ignoring the cacophony of horns that the drivers reward her with. She even jumps on the hood of a car, and then across to another, cutting the turns the doorman has to take to make his way around the cars.

    She jumps onto one last car, ignoring the driver's angry yelling, hopping down on the other side and sprinting off after the doorman again.

    "Sorry!"

    Her voice is a bit breathy, after the long and intensive sprint, but thankfully she is far from exhausted yet, the supposed doorman seemingly not tiring either. He tears down the sidewalk ahead of her, the street a bit less crowded than where they came from, with Kate still in hot pursuit, gaining on him slowly.

    As she gets closer, she begins to gear up for a takedown, hopefully avoiding an actual fight completely, if she does it right. Before she can take the leap, however, he takes a hard right again, running into a small alley between two buildings.

    High on adrenaline, Kate is only a few seconds behind him, taking the right without checking the corner this time and nearly paying for it. She barely dodges the thick pipe coming at her face then almost falls back with her momentum changing so fast. He swings the pipe downwards with his next move, at Kate's head and she bends to the side to duck out of the way, jumping forward to jam her shoulder into his torso right when he is the most unbalanced.

    He stumbles back but doesn't fall, his back hitting the brick wall behind him. Their space is limited and Kate steps back, taking a moment to finally get a good look at him. He is in his late 30s, early 40s. Caucasian and seemingly in good shape with an ordinary face, although not someone she would call handsome. His dark eyes follow her movements as she raises both of her hands in a placating manner.

    "I just want to talk to you."

    The tension in his form does not go away and it's not a surprise when a second later he throws the pipe in Kate's direction and takes off running down the alley again. She dodges the pipe relatively easily, having expected this exact thing to happen in some way, and starts sprinting after him again.

    The distance has widened between them again, the doorman almost on the other end of the alley when a dark gray sportscar screeches to a halt on the other end, blocking his way. Finally.

    From the passenger side of the sports car, Yelena emerges, and the doorman halts, looking at her, then back at Kate, then at her again, seemingly weighing his options. Kate doesn't have time to get offended when he chooses to run back in her direction, apparently deeming her less of a threat, instead planting her feet and waiting for him to try to get past her. He surprises her by jumping up on the wall and kicking himself off to try to kick her in the face with a flying knee, not expecting much fight prowess after how relatively incompetent he was with the iron pipe. She ducks just in time, avoiding the kick and getting a hit of her own in, right into his stomach before he lands, unbalancing him.

    To avoid him possibly running away again, she doesn't take the opening as he nearly falls, but quickly repositions herself again instead, blocking his way out of the alley. On his other side, Yelena is getting nearer, her face hard as steel, the affection and warmth from a few minutes ago completely gone from her features.

    He rebalances himself quickly and gets into a fighting stance with his back to the wall, his eyes jumping from Yelena to Kate and back again.

    "Hey man, we just want to talk. Calm down."

    Kate holds up her hands again but Yelena seems to have different plans, raising her right hand, her Widow's bite flashing red before a small projectile flies out of it. The next thing Kate knows, the man falls and convulses on the floor, electricity wreaking his body as he makes gurgling sounds.

    "Well, that was easy."

    From behind Yelena, Sonya emerges, and Kate throws her a look as she bends over to catch her breath, the three of them encircling the man lying on the ground. He lies there, convulsing for about a minute, and Kate straightens up, glancing behind her back to see if anyone is witnessing what they are doing, considering it's probably not even 10 am yet. A few times, she glances between Yelena and the doorman, before deciding to give Yelena a verbal nudge to end his punishment.

    "Hey, do you think that's enough?"

    Yelena's face is unreadable, her eyes hard but at her words, she glances up at Kate from the man on the ground, and a second later the convulsions stop with a tap on her Widow's Bite. His eyes are open and visibly terrified, and Kate decides against taking out her sword to threaten him, positive that they will get him to talk without it. She decides to crouch down instead, offering her hand instead, feeling both Yelena's and Sonya's eyes on the side of her head.

    The man looks at her hand but doesn't take it, pushing himself to a sitting position with a groan on his own instead. Kate doesn't let it offend her, but she does her best to mimic Yelena's steely exterior when she asks her first question, probably still the good cop in this equation.

    "Okay, let's start with why did you bug my place?"

    He looks at her, then at Yelena and Sonya, and then back at her.

    "I have no idea what you are talking about. I'm going to call the police-" His voice is surprisingly smooth and he gets as far as getting his phone out but Kate slaps it out of his hand easily, the device landing among the garbage, concrete, and suspicious stains below their feet.

    "Listen, Niles, or whatever your real name is, we both know you are better off answering my questions than theirs.-"

    She uses her thumb to point at Sonya and Yelena, satisfied when his eyes follow her indication. Since he was listening to them for weeks, he definitely knows they are deadly, and most likely knows it's in his best interest to cooperate.

    "-So, I'm asking again, why did you bug my pla-"

    "Help! Hel-"

    He starts yelling but Kate puts a hand over his mouth almost right away, silencing his cries. He is better at all this than he seems because a second later he headbutts her on the nose as she leans in, and she falls back on her ass with a pained yelp as her eyes water involuntarily. "Holy fucking..."

    Noises of struggle make her open her eyes quickly, but within milliseconds it is apparent that she doesn't need to worry.

    Yelena kicks the doorman once in the face, then pulls out a wire from her Widow's bite. She steps up behind the slightly hunched-over man’s back, leaning down for a moment to wind the wire around his neck, and then straightens up again, before stepping over her own left hand to draw him back against her thigh, the wire tight and deadly around his neck. Kate watches on, stunned to silence as Yelena lets him choke and wheeze for a few heartbeats, her face still unmoving as he tries to grasp at the thin wire, and she stares at a spot to somewhere the right of Kate's face. Yelena strangles him for about 15 seconds longer, as Kate stumbles to her feet, unsure if she should intervene, glancing at an equally stony-faced Sonya.

    They are kind of terrifying...

    Yelena's voice is quiet and sounds almost bored when she finally speaks. "When you hear the name of your employer, you say yes. Practice."

    The wheezing eases out a little, Yelena letting him breathe, just barely so, only enough so he can speak. He chokes out a word after a few heartbeats, his head beginning to look purple. "...yes."

    Yelena lets the silence hang for another few seconds before she says the first name. "Wilson Fisk."

    Kate's eyes drop to the doorman, but he doesn't say anything and Kate has to remind herself that this man most likely listened to her and Yelena have sex, and for all of them for weeks, to push down on the feeling of empathy she feels.

    "Javier Rojas."

    He still doesn't say anything, and Kate looks up to meet Yelena's eyes. She blinks once, her jaw muscles tightening and releasing before she supplies the final name, as she holds Kate's eyes.

    "Valentina Allegra de Fontaine."

    Gaze dropping to the doorman again, Kate sees the way his eyes flicker once. One heartbeat, two, then three goes by, and he opens his mouth.

    "...yes."

    After his admission, Yelena doesn't immediately stop choking him. Actually, she tightens the wire and returns to strangling him harder, as Kate throws her a worried glance. She meets Kate's eyes and holds them for another few seconds before she blinks once, letting the doorman finally breathe and fall forward.

    He falls onto his hands, coughing violently and Yelena watches him for a few seconds, her eyes stormy but no other indication of how she feels about the revelation that Valentina was the one that had them bugged. They wait for him to stop, his coughing receding slowly over the next minute. Suddenly, Yelena reaches under her coat, taking out a gun with a silencer on it and Kate's eyes widen in alarm and she steps forward with a placating hand lifting. "Hey, hey now. Wait a second..."

    Completely ignoring Kate, she puts the barrel to the back of his head, leaning down to talk to him in a quiet, completely terrifying voice.

    "What's your name? Your real name."

    Behind Yelena, Sonya holds up a hand, and shakes her head, halting Kate's advance. He takes a few seconds to answer, sounding rough with the previous smoothness of his voice completely gone, due to Yelena's aggression.

    "Jacob."

    Yelena presses the gun harder against the back of his head ever so slightly, making sure that he knows it's there.

    "Tell me this, Jacob. Did Javier Rojas know about the bugs?"

    Kate watches as he blinks, and notices how his whole frame shakes, but his voice does not waver when he answers.

    "No."

    Yelena nods once, before she sucks in a breath, never once taking her eyes off the back of Jacob's head.

    "Okay…You will deliver a message to Valentina.-"

    Impressively, the man doesn't beg or plead, or even say anything, but as he raises his head and meets Kate's eyes, she can see his fear.

    "-Tell her, that after all this, our deal is off. And if she ever comes near us, or if I ever catch one of you around us again, there won't be a rock on this Earth she can hide under from me. You got that?"

    The doorman blinks before he nods, and Kate sees the way he sags a bit, most likely not expecting to make it out of this alley alive.

    "Say it. Do you understand?"

    Jacob coughs once more, and he clears his throat but after a few seconds, he speaks. "Yes."

    "Good."

    With that, Yelena lifts her gun, flicking the safety back on, before putting it back under her coat and turning away to walk back to their car. Slowly, Kate exhales and unwinds too, looking down at the man who is still sitting on the ground, his legs stretched out in front of him.

    He is not looking back at her, but at his lap instead, and it takes Kate a moment to notice that he is looking at a big, dark stain on his nice trousers, clearly having wet himself sometime during the last few minutes.

    Kate sighs and begins to walk away after Yelena, speaking to him as she passes him by. "I told you you are better off talking to me."

    The Widows are already in the car when she gets to the end of the alley, Yelena surprisingly sitting in the back to allow Kate to take the passenger seat. Sonya offers her a tissue as soon as her door is closed, and she takes it, dabbing at the little bit of blood under her nose. "Is it broken?"

    It's Sonya who asks her, and Kate shakes her head, flicking down the sun visor to check herself out in the mirror and rub off the little bit of blood that dried under her nose. "I don't think so."

    Her nose is a bit red, but not swollen or at a weird angle, most likely just a little bit bruised and bloody but she touches and prods at it a little to make sure.

    Nothing a bit of ibuprofen won't fix.

    Sonya pulls away from the curb, and Kate turns back to look at the fake doorman one last time. He still sits there, seemingly gathering his shattered pride or maybe relishing in the fact that he is actually alive.

    "Do you think he is CIA?"

    Sonya's question is answered by Yelena, and Kate uses the mirror in the sun visor to look at her in the back seat.

    "Most likely."

    Her stony exterior is gone and she sighs deeply, blowing a strand of her hair from her face and sliding a bit lower in her seat, as if she didn't just scare the living fuck out of a man. "Thank you for catching him, Kate."

    Kate blinks at Yelena's words and she turns slightly back to meet her eyes. "Sure. Thank you for getting answers... Although that was pretty intense." Yelena, who has been looking out the window, turns to her and meets her eyes. "That man has been listening to us for weeks.-"

    She lowers her chin while she holds Kate's eyes, making it impossible to misunderstand that she definitely thought of the fact that he listened to them sleep together too. "-He is still breathing so I feel that we went pretty easy on him."

    Kate cracks a small smile, kind of sharing the sentiment, even though Yelena and Sonya both scared the shit out of her during the interrogation too. After a moment she exhales sharply through her nose in a chuckle, before she adds.

    "I'm glad you did not question me like that the first night we met."

    Yelena blinks once, slowly, before she smiles too and turns away to look out the window again.

    "I told you before. I went easy on you because you were harmless. With him, I did not know." Kate turns forward with a huff, rolling her eyes.

    "Well, I personally think it was because of my irresistible charm."

    Behind her, Yelena chuckles and she sees Sonya grin too, next to her.

    "Oh yes. Every girl's dream is to have a hot sauce bottle thrown at their head." This time Sonya snorts before she joins their conversation.

    "Speaking of you two.-”

    Wow, that certainly is a super subtle segue, Sonya.

    “-I very much object to being subjected to mission talk and then getting muted just as the tea gets good."

    Shaking her head at Sonya's hopefully joking statement, Kate ignores her statement, sticking to the topic when she realizes Sonya is driving them back towards Columbus Circle. "So now that we know he works for Valentina, does this mean we can go home?" She turns slightly around in her seat again to be able to look at Yelena for this conversation, watching as she purses her lips and tilts her head to the side in consideration. "I think making the bugs recognizable was a warning, as I said. Val showing us she can get to us there if she wants to."

    Kate sighs at not being told a simple yes, her eyebrows furrowing in displeasure and resisting the urge to pout.

    "Well, I can't live in a motel forever."

    As Yelena mulls her words over, Sonya voices her agreement and Kate twists back to watch the city pass them by.

    "You are right. Maybe you should consider moving though."

    Leaning her head back to groan, Kate closes her eyes. She doesn't let her voice get whiny, but her disagreement is definitely palpable in her tone, once she opens her eyes and answers Sonya.

    "Come oon. If she could find me here, I'm sure she would be able to find me anywhere else in New York too. Plus why would she want me dead?"

    Her question is followed by a few seconds of silence before Yelena speaks from the back seat.

    "She most likely does not want you dead now... But she could.-"

    She pauses meaningfully, and Kate turns her head to look at her again.

    "If we get all pieces of your mother's formula and do not give it to her, for example." Sighing deeply, Kate resigns herself to her fate, sliding lower in her seat and kicking out her legs as much as she can, abandoning her mission to not pout. After letting her stew for a few seconds, Yelena speaks again, her voice carrying a bit of a smile.

    "We can go home.-"

    Whipping her head around, Kate looks at her again, and Yelena lifts an eyebrow and points at her to make sure her point is taken seriously.

    "-But you need to be a lot more serious about security. Starting with a lock change and actually turning on your security system."

    Kate's lips stretch into a smile, and a moment later, Yelena smiles back. "Maybe you should have live-in personal security."

    Her eyebrows furrowing in confusion, Kate turns to look at Sonya after her weird suggestion. "What security can protect me better than I can protect myself?"

    Sonya's lips stretch into a grin, like she said exactly what she wanted to hear and Kate sighs, immediately knowing what she will say. Sonya does not disappoint, her tone innocent but Kate sees the teasing look on her face.

    "I heard great things about Black Widows."

    Behind her, Yelena snorts and Kate chuckles, feeling a bit awkward. The last thing they need, with their already slightly... confusing relationship, is Yelena moving in or something. Then again, it does sound like something that would make her apartment safer, and it does have a certain allure...

    ...All that time, alone, just the two of them.

    Thankfully, she does not have to voice any opinion as Yelena chimes in from the back seat. "Have I overstayed my welcome, Sonya? Is that it?"

    To her left, Sonya laughs, and Kate sees that she uses the rearview mirror to look at Yelena. "Who said anything about you? Maxine is close to being healed, and soon she will need a place to stay. Kate has a guest room. So… Two birds, one stone."

    Her grin widens even more and she lifts both of her eyebrows at Yelena in the mirror, and Kate exhales slowly, unsure how serious this conversation is. She does not hear anything from Yelena behind her, so after a few seconds of silence, Kate feels compelled to chime in. "I...I don't really think I need extra security. But Maxine can stay in my guest room if she needs somewhere to crash."

    Sonya chuckles, and her eyes are full of mirth and affection when she glances at Kate. From behind, Yelena speaks again, her voice almost dry.

    "Maxine is going to stay with my parents for a while, as soon as she is well enough to travel. Probably next week."

    It does not seem like this is news to Sonya, which makes Kate entirely unsure about the conversation they just had, but she just nods, not questioning it.

    "Oh, that's nice."

    They pass Colombus Circle then, almost at Sonya's and her building and she exhales, winching a bit when it irritates her achy nose.

    "So, not to be the party pooper, but we need to start planning for tonight." Sonya nods and she steers them towards their building, while Yelena asks from behind them. "Did Barton send you the details he said he would?"

    Instead of answering, Kate pulls out her phone and checks her emails. There, sent over an hour ago, is the link to a secure folder on the cloud, sent by Laura, instead of Clint and Kate is secretly entertained by the fact that he probably had to ask for help with this. "Yeah. I will check the Bishop Security archives too, in case there is something we can use."

    The next several hours are spent with intense research, planning, at least 3 conference calls with Clint, and then frantic preparations and packing the gear they will need for the mission. In the end, Mason is not able to get them credentials to get to where they need to go in such a short time, so they decide to go on a different route, hopefully not meeting anyone who works there at all.

    The facility is an old mine, reconstructed for the purpose of secure storage, with hundreds of caverns and vaults underground. Above ground, the complex spreads over 100 acres, with a secure zone established around the entrance, an electric fence around the outer perimeter, and armed guards patrolling the surrounding area.

    There is only one road leading to the entrance carved into a steep cliffside, but inside the entry shaft widens into an enormous loading hall after about 200 yards, where items of value are transported in and out by trucks of various sizes, the first cavern big enough to fit several 18-wheelers at the same time almost on ground level.

    According to the blueprints they get from Clint, but which Kate also had to begin with, the waiting hall they are trying to get to is one level below, which is good news at least, since the vault the evidence is originally stored at is 10 stories underground, only accessible with one elevator which needs specific key cards for each vault, to get to the level they want to go to. Each vehicle is inspected upon entry and exit before they even get to the underground facility, and the singular entrance is guarded 24/7 by armed security. Of course, taking out armed security would not be a problem for Kate and the Widows, but since they must complete this mission without anyone finding out they were ever there, to begin with, in order to avoid further suspicion from the FBI, they can't even tranquilize or distract the guards to get in. The whole complex is completely off the grid, with its own energy supply from geothermic energy, and a set of backup generators that kick in after 30 seconds in case the facility's access to their electricity supply is compromised.

    From Clint's mysterious source, who he refuses to reveal, they get a schedule of shipments going to and from the facility. The manifest they receive does not contain what exactly is being transported, but it does have the name of the client and what type of vehicle is used for their transport. They also received some photographs of the locations, to help them plan, which are apparently top secret and not available to the public, as well as the exact box numbers they are looking for within the shipment itself.

    "Let's go over the plan one more time."

    Clint is on speakerphone in Sonya's van, the one that changes its appearance and Kate throws her head back against her seat, groaning. It's 9:30 in the evening, and they are on the I-87, making their way upstate to a place ironically called New Russia, and they have been doing this all. fucking. day.

    "Come ooon, Clint. Going over it one more time won't make it any more certain. We got this."

    "One last time, Kate. I will leave you alone after this."

    Her exasperation is not mirrored on Yelena's face next to her, but she is seemingly entertained by Kate's chagrin, nodding at her to start with an unconcealed smirk.

    "Uuugh, okay. Fine. We get to the outer perimeter around 11:30 pm. We get through the electric fence and climb up the mountain from the northwest side. We should get to our position a few minutes after 12 and have a clear vantage point of the road going in and the blindspot of the outside cameras. Sonya will hike 1 more mile to the other side, to their above-ground electricity hub, find the center panel, and wait for our signal, meanwhile, I will establish a zipline for Yelena and me."

    She looks at Yelena on her right but she is on her phone, texting in Russian presumably, based on the Cyrillic letters anyway, only looking up to nod at her and confirm she is listening before turning back to her phone. Kate continues with a bored voice, having gone through the plan at least 10 times at this point.

    "The truck for the previous transport arrives at the outer gates at 12:30, which means it should be cleared by security around 12:35 to 12:40 am, when it will proceed to the entrance of the underground facility. Yelena and I will use the zipline to get on top of it in the camera blindspot and ride it into the loading hall. And then...Sonya? Do you wanna...?" Looking up at Sonya in the driver's seat, Kate waits to see if she wants to take over and explain her own part. She does, the dark and mostly empty highway roads apparently boring enough that even this seems like good entertainment... Or, she is just fine with going over the mission one more time.

    "Once you are inside, you will signal me to cut electricity for exactly 28 seconds and use the darkness to make your way out of the loading hall and into the ventilation system. After that, I will turn it back on, in time to avoid the generators kicking in, wait for your second signal and keep watch."

    Kate catches her eyes in the rearview mirror and Sonya winks, reminding Kate of the process of coming up with this step of the plan.

    When they first discussed it, they wanted to leave Kate outside instead, and for Sonya and Yelena to be the ones going inside. After a slightly offensive discussion for Kate, Clint and Yelena agreed it's actually best if she is not left outside alone, deemed too likely to get bored and cause trouble... While Kate found the whole conversation ridiculous, in the end, she decided not to care too much, since she got what she wanted, and gets to go inside after all, instead of putting Sonya in danger. Plus, it makes more sense for her to go in anyway. Sonya would have used her hacking tool to do what needs to be done, but if that failed, she does not have the required skills to get into the system on her own. Kate does.

    Puffing out her cheeks as she shakes off the thought, Kate exhales and nods, before she takes over reciting the plan once again, looking out at the dim lights in the distance among the darkness, markign a small town.

    "Right. Thanks. After that, Yelena and I will make our way one level lower. I will proceed to the junction box above the security room and tap into their camera feed. We will wait until 2 am, when the evidence is loaded into the waiting hall at which point I will clone the feed from that room. Yelena will then enter the waiting hall, get the pen drive, replace it with a blank one, and make her way back to the vents."

    Yelena finally puts down her phone and takes over reciting the plan, her face not portraying boredom similar to Kate's, but the way she leans back her head against her seat too, is telling of her fatigue.

    "We will meet at the first intersection and wait there until 0500 hours when the truck for the FBI is finished loading. We will signal Sonya again and she will short-circuit the system once more. In the darkness, we will attach to the bottom of the truck going to the FBI and ride it until the first bend in the road before the exit security checkpoint. There, we will de-attach in camera blindspot, climb up the cliffside on the north side, use the zipline to return to our starting position, de-attach Kate's zipline arrow, rendezvous with Sonya at the outer perimeter, and leave."

    On the other end of the line, Clint sighs.

    "Okay... What do you do if the pendrive is not there?"

    Kate rolls her eyes but entertains his line of questioning, answering him in a dull voice. "Leave immediately."

    "What do you do if you are discovered?"

    Rubbing her forehead, Kate resists the urge to groan as she repeats.

    "Leave immediately."

    "What do you do if-"

    "That is enough, Barton. We need to sleep. We will call you after the mission is completed, until then there is nothing more you can do. Goodbye."

    With that, Yelena reaches over and hangs up Kate's phone, apparently as done with the conversation as she feels. Still, maybe due to her now tired state, Kate finds it entertaining and she snickers, meeting Yelena's eyes.

    The corner of her mouth tilts upwards as she looks back at Kate and she shrugs, before turning to Sonya.

    "Wake me up 20 minutes before we get there."

    Reaching into her bag on the seat next to her, Yelena pulls out a sleeping mask and begins the process of getting comfortable. She puts the sleeping mask on her head and shifts around to get more comfortable before she gives Kate one last side glance. Kate smiles at the mask to herself but turns away to look out the window, only tuning back once Yelena has lowered it over her eyes, and seems to be trying to fall asleep.

    The mask only serves to bring Kate's attention to her lips, and she does her best to not let her thoughts stray in a direction they really don't need distracting her on this mission. Instead, she shifts lower in her seat too, closing her eyes and begins to try and sleep too. The day has been incredibly eventful once again, with the article, the doorman's interrogation, and then the long process of planning.

    Before they left, Sonya once again made a passionate case for making an official announcement about their fake engagement. Despite their conversation and agreement earlier, it still felt a bit awkward to Kate, but she went ahead and did it anyway, posting a picture of Yelena's hand with the ring, with the caption 'The cat's out of the bag.' She turned her notifications off right after to avoid the distraction but made sure to text Cassie that they would catch up later. But how she will explain what's been happening, she is not quite sure. The pre-mission nerves make it hard for her to actually get sleepy, despite the heat being cranked up high, and darkness enveloping the van. She shifts around once again, trying to find a position that is comfortable, while her thoughts continue to jump around. While she has faith in their mission, she also can't help but feel a bit nervous. Unlike the time they broke into Limitless, it does not hinge on them adhering to a strict schedule, but they did have much less time to prepare and come up with alternative plans for this one... Basically, none, after figuring out a way in at all, has taken up most of the afternoon, even with all the useful information Clint's source has given them.

    The van goes over a bump and Kate sighs, opening her eyes. Sonya turned the radio on a few minutes ago, providing some quiet background noise, but she feels too wired to sleep. Next to her, Yelena's breathing is even but Kate can't tell if she is asleep or just resting. Exhaling quietly, Kate allows herself to watch her for a few seconds, the lights from passing cars illuminating her face for a few moments before the darkness covers it again. In the hopes of smoothing her pre-mission nerves, she lets herself think about Yelena a bit, but it does not have the desired effect, only amping her up more. For the next hour and a half, Kate alternates between thinking about Yelena, their night together, the fake engagement, the doorman, Valentina, and the mission, and tries to brainstorm about how to improve her home security, to make sure it remains secure.

    In the end, she does not end up sleeping properly, but she kind of dozes off, waking up to Sonya's voice.

    "Wake up. We are 20 minutes out."

    Rubbing her eyes, Kate sits up a bit, having shifted lower over the last hour and a half, before she blinks slowly a few times, looking around. Next to her, Yelena takes off her sleeping mask, her hair adorably sticking to her face on one side, and Kate turns to look out the window, trying to see their surroundings.

    Unfortunately, but also unsurprisingly, the outside is still not more stimulating than before, the silky October darkness embracing their car apart from the two beams of the van's headlights. They are still on the I-87 but looking ahead at the dashboard, Kate sees the GPS instructing them to take the next exit.

    While Yelena and her get their bearings, Sonya exits the highway, switching onto a smaller road for about 15 minutes, before they take a series of turns that take them onto a road in the forest, that feels barely wide enough for Sonya's van to pass between the trees on both sides. For the remaining 5 or so minutes, they drive along the twisty road, the forest growing thick around them. As a city girl, it feels almost impossibly dark to Kate, but she focuses on keeping herself calm, trying to not let the anxiety and excitement of the mission ahead get to her.

    The final bend in the road leads them to a small parking lot, evidently created for hikers based on the picnic benches illuminated by the van's headlights as Sonya parks it. Unsurprisingly, there are no other cars or vans in the parking lot, as midnight on an October Sunday is not exactly high season for casual, or even serious hikers.

    Once the van is parked, all three of them are in motion, with very few words exchanged among them.

    They came partially dressed in their gear for comfort during the almost 4-hour-long drive, which they finish in the parking lot, putting on all the protective and warming layers, as well as all their weapons. Kate had the top of her gear fixed by Luke a few weeks ago, her bulletproof stealth-suit as spotless as if it was brand new, when she puts it on. This time, she will also wear a version of night vision goggles, the three of them not allowed to use actual flashlights basically as soon as they leave this parking lot.

    The goggles are more of a special pair of glasses, but they have the functionality without the added bulk, an invention of her own making. Learning from what happened on the ship a few weeks ago, she quickly added a headband to them this afternoon, to make sure they do not fall off. Apart from night and infrared vision, they also keep track of her arrows, and Kate loaded a 3D compiled version of the blueprints for the underground facility onto them, complete with the vent system. While Sonya and Yelena wear full-face masks, just like last time, Kate sticks with a warm hat and a mask that covers the lower side of her face instead, not a fan of how confined and sweaty she feels in full-face masks.

    After what happened with Maxine last time, Yelena did not insist she takes a gun this time, but Clint and she repeatedly reminded Kate to not use arrows during the mission apart from for the tasks they all discussed in advance, as it is the equivalent of her leaving her ID on the scene... Which they then teased Kate about doing before. She ignored their teasing for the most part and packed a quiver full of trick arrows, and her sword, although if everything goes according to plan, she will not need to use either. Especially, since the people working here are not criminals, just civilians doing their job, so if it comes down to a confrontation, Kate plans to do everything in her power to avoid actually hurting anyone.

    Once they are all geared up, Sonya locks the van and Yelena leads them toward a path among the trees that will get them to their first trial of the night: the electric fence. They each carry a small backpack, packed with the things they will need for their individual tasks, with Sonya carrying what they will need to get through the first obstacle. For the first 20 minutes of their hike, Kate focuses on walking quietly as Yelena and Sonya do, wincing behind her mask when she steps on a twig or a crunchy patch of fallen leaves a few times. Seriously, maybe Sonya being the one to do the solo hike instead of her was not such a bad idea after all. When they reach the line of trees, where a 10-foot wide corridor was clear-cut along both sides of the fence, they crouch down, checking the time and listening for any sounds around them that could indicate trouble. According to Kate's glasses, it's 11:28 pm, which means they are 2 minutes ahead of schedule about 10 minutes from the next patrol passing them by. Still, they listen for a few seconds in silence, before Yelena nods, quietly speaking. "Go, Sonya."

    Taking off her backpack, Sonya reaches into it, before pulling out what looks like a regular paint spray. According to the Widows, however, it's a special substance, that once sprayed on, solidifies and creates an insulating layer on the surface of the fence, then dissolves after about 5 to 6 minutes of spraying it on, leaving no trace. While the two of them keep watch, crouched along the treeline, Sonya walks up to the 10-foot-hight fence and begins to spray with a quiet hissing sound.

    The top of the fence, complete with outward tilting barbed wire, is obviously too high for her to reach so once she sprayed all parts she could reach, Sonya begins to climb while the two of them watch on, at least in Kate's case, with bated breath.

    "Go."

    Yelena puts a hand on her back, pushing her gently along, once Sonya gets to the top third section of the fence and Kate does not argue for once, crossing the clearing as quietly and quickly as she can. From closer up, Kate can see that the spray leaves a white residue, which makes it easy to see where it's okay to touch. Without hesitation, she begins to climb, reaching the outward-leaning barbed wire just as Sonya touches down on the other side. She retreats to cover of the tree line inside, while Kate catches sight of Yelena under her, beginning the climb too.

    Thanks to her thick, tactical gloves, the barbed wire does not pose a significant challenge, and within a minute, Kate is back on the ground inside the fence. As discussed in advance, she runs to the tree line for cover too, and crouches down next to Sonya, the two of them now just waiting for Yelena to cross, before continuing their journey.

    As Kate looks to the left, in the distance, she sees a speck of light, which is more of a bright white dot on her night-vision glasses. The guards are early. Her heartbeat speeds up and she looks back at Yelena, who is just getting to the barbed wire, then back at the guards slowly getting closer. They are are least two minutes out still, so Yelena should be able to get over in time, but they are cutting it closer than they intended for sure... Still, Kate's muscles are buzzing with nervousness, ready to jump into action in case Yelena gets discovered. Of course, her worry ends up being unfounded, as Yelena makes her way over the fence in less than a minute, jumping down lithely on the other side and quickly signaling for them to go. The three of them hurry into the woods, but about a minute later, Yelena grabs a hold of her arm and holds up her hand. Around them, the forest is quiet but as they come to a halt, Kate hears the reason they stopped. From behind them, they can hear the guards' conversation, even though just barely as a murmur, which means if they make too much noise, they will most likely be heard too.

    The three of them stand in the woods, as still as they can, and listen to the men slowly coming closer before finally, their voices begin to fade as they walk away. Kate's blood rushes through her ears, but she stays still, despite every instinct in her body itching to start running as soon as the voices quiet down. It takes Yelena about two minutes to give her arm a gentle tap, drawing Kate's eyes to herself, and giving them the signal to go ahead, Sonya leading the group, with Kate sandwiched between her and Yelena, who closes their ranks. For the next 25 minutes, they walk in silence, apart from Kate stumbling over a root that her boot gets caught on. Yelena catches her before she can actually faceplant, and keeps her hand on her arm until Kate rights herself, whispering her gratitude.

    "Thanks... And sorry."

    With her mask and goggles on, it's impossible to see Yelena's expression, but she gives Kate's arm a squeeze before she lets go of it, and indicates with her chin that she keeps going. "Just be careful. If you twist your ankle, the mission is off."

    Kate hums in agreement, worriedly checking around them before she looks down at her feet, watching where she is going more carefully until they reach the cliff where Yelena and she will wait, and where they split up with Sonya. Up here, the Widows are certain there is nobody to hear them, so quietly, Sonya and Yelena discuss some last-minute details while they all distribute the earpieces among themselves, and Kate looks down at the abyss with some growing worry.

    The cliff is higher than she expected, and the lit-up road is further away. She will still be able to make the shot, obviously, but still, the wide, dark chasm between them and the road, where they will have to time their arrival perfectly to not end up as meat-stickers on the opposite cliffside, is quite worrisome.

    "Good luck. See you later."

    Sonya stands up and gives her shoulder a friendly pat, prompting Kate to finally tear her eyes away, and look up at her from her crouching position.

    "You too. See you at sunrise."

    She hears an amused hum from Sonya, before she speaks.

    "If you do your jobs right, we'll be out of here before the sun comes up... Maybe we can get some nice breakfast before the drive back."

    Kate nods in agreement, the comment reminding her that actually, she is a bit hungry. "Celebratory pancakes? Count me in."

    She imagines Sonya smiles at her comment, but a moment later she moves on, giving Yelena's shoulder a similarly friendly farewell pat, before she disappears among the trees. In a few seconds, she is completely gone from sight, and her departure is also completely inaudible as if she spent her entire life hunting in a forest.

    Pushing aside her appreciation for Sonya's skill, Kate turns back towards the cliff, reaching behind her back to retrieve her collapsible bow and then her zipline arrow. At first, she looks over to the other side, triple-checking the rocks she has to aim at to make sure they stay in the blind spot but are high enough that their course goes above where a truck would go, so they will hop down on top of it, instead of getting stickered onto its side. After she is sure she has the right target, Kate nocks her arrow before she draws and exhales slowly. Gently, she allows the string to slip out from her hold and the arrow flies across the abyss for several seconds, while the zipline tethered to its end unravels. They know the arrow lands because the wire stops moving, and Kate quickly gets up to attach its other end to a thick tree, completing their way across.

    She crouches back next to Yelena, who used the time Kate set up the zipline, to measure the exact distance they will need to transverse and supposedly calculated how long it will take them to cross it. She seems to be ready with that though, just crouching and keeping an eye on the lit-up road in the distance.

    "So, now we just wait...?"

    Yelena hums, her eerie green goggled eyes turning to look at Kate.

    "You should probably practice detaching. Getting the timing right is very important." Glancing at the newly set up zipline, then back at Yelena, Kate considers it for a few seconds, before clearing her throat and asking what she thinks probably sounds like a stupid question to Yelena, but totally isn't.

    "How do I...do that?"

    For a long moment, Yelena looks at her and Kate imagines her eyebrow must be lifted, before she gestures at the zipline, like it's the most simple thing in the world. "You get on the zipline, count back from three, and detach."

    Kate's eyes shift from Yelena to the zipline and back again. Sure, that part Kate gets. "But won't I, like, slide away?"

    She imitates herself sliding across the abyss with her hand and Yelena huffs, which Kate chooses to interpret as a chuckle, but there is definitely a hint of condescension in the deadpan answer she receives.

    "You hold onto the line with your other hand."

    After Kate looks at the zipline one more time, her concern totally hidden by her cool night vision glasses, Yelena huffs again before getting up.

    "Okay. If you start sliding away, I will stop you."

    That does actually help Kate so she gets up too, pulling out the wire from her harness that will attach to the zipline.

    "Thanks."

    Yelena just hums, standing with her back to the abyss and watching Kate attach herself to the zipline. Kate lifts her feet, using her gloved hand as a break, and counts back in her head. Three, two, one-

    She presses the button on her harness, focusing on the count and...

    ...nothing happens.

    "You must be more aggressive. Punch it."

    Yelena supplies across from her and Kate glances up at her as she nods before looking down at the button on her harness and counting back again.

    Three, two, one-

    The time, she really focuses on hitting the button hard and the detachment is instant, making her nearly fall on her ass, stumbling as she lands.

    "You need to do it without looking down. Again."

    She does it successfully without looking 3 times, before Yelena lets up, returning to her previous crouched position by the cliff. Kate joins her a moment later, kneeling on the ground instead of crouching to rest her legs a bit, her knee protectors keeping the coldness of the rocks below her at bay. The time is 12:12 am, which means they have at least 18 minutes to kill until they need to be ready, as the truck they want to use for entry is not arriving at the security gate until 12:30ish.

    Next to her, Yelena rustles around in her backpack before pulling out something... which are actually two somethings, Kate notices, when Yelena offers her one. Glancing down on it, Kate sees it's a protein bar and she reaches out to take it while looking back up at Yelena. "Thanks."

    Yelena huffs, this time definitely in a chuckle, and begins to crinkle the plastic wrapping of her own bar, before she reaches up to her face to pull up her mask, revealing her mouth. "Do not leave the wrapper when you are done."

    As Yelena bites into her own chocolate-covered bar, Kate hums in agreement, before pulling down her own mask.

    "I was getting a bit hungry, so this is a godsend."

    With her mask partially out of the way, Kate sees Yelena's lip turn slightly upwards as she chews, only answering her once she swallows her bite.

    "I figured you would."

    They eat the remainder of their protein bars in silence, and as instructed, Kate puts the wrapper in the front pocket of her small backpack, careful not to leave it behind. The time in the corner of her glasses reads 12:16 am, which means they have 14 more minutes to kill... Kate glances at Yelena on her side, quiet and still as a statue as she watches the road once again. Her mask has been lowered to cover her mouth once again, and Kate is suddenly reminded of her scaring the fake doorman in the morning... She looks every bit like the Black Widow she is, but when Kate looks at her, even like this, she sees all the other things she is. Yelena's small frame is undoubtedly intimidating but as a surprisingly strong gust of wind rips across the cliff, Kate sees the way she twists her neck just a little, the cold air probably bothering her. When Yelena's hands shift, leaning her weight from one to the other, Kate remembers those hands holding onto her tight as she was close to coming, and- "I will count for you."

    Torn out of her thought process, Kate clears her throat.

    "...Sorry?"

    Yelena turns away from watching the road to look at her instead.

    "When we are going across. You will go first. And I will count for you when to let go. Timing can be tricky."

    "Okay. Thanks."

    Embarrassed to be this distracted, Kate resolves herself to not think about anything sex or Yelena-related until they are safely back in the car, or even home and quickly moves onto watching the road too.

    ...Which is incredibly boring.

    This is why she would be a terrible lookout...But not in a way that proves Yelena and Clint right!

    "So,-"

    Kate lasts approximately 3 minutes without speaking.

    "-With the article and announcement and all, have you told your parents about our engagement yet?"

    Slowly, Yelena turns to look at her and Kate looks back, not letting the unnerving stare of the bright green goggles get to her. A moment later, Yelena speaks, gesturing at the facility lying on the other side of the valley.

    "Is that really what you want to talk about before we break into one of the most secure places on the planet?"

    Shrugging, Kate shifts around a bit on her knees.

    "I mean, I don't think talking about it more will make this mission go any better or worse. So... we might as well talk about something else."

    For a long moment, Yelena looks at her before she turns back to the road. When she receives no answer, Kate sighs, resigning herself to being bored in silence for the next 10 and a half minutes, plus however many after that for the truck to get cleared by security. Then Yelena answers.

    "I have."

    Smiling behind her mask, Kate doesn't turn to look at Yelena, counting to three in her head before she asks to not seem too eager.

    "How did that go?"

    It takes Yelena a few seconds to answer too and she sounds reluctant when she does. "My father asked me if we are hurrying because I am knocked up... Then offered to raise the baby, like I am a teenager in trouble before my mother took over and shot him down before he got overexcited."

    At that, Kate definitely turns to look at her, disbelief written all over her face even if Yelena can't see it. She sees Yelena glance at her before she shifts her weight and Kate would give all of her considerable amount of money to be able to look at her face right now. "-Don't look at me, I think he was hit in the head too many times."

    Trying her hardest to not burst out laughing, Kate shakes her head.

    "Well, I think your mother is right..."

    She waits until Yelena turns her head slightly to look at her, most likely confused, before she continues.

    "Obviously, our child is not going to be raised by its grandparents... It will be raised by nannies and the help, like they are supposed to, and will only join us for dinners when they have made their first million on the stock market."

    Despite her mask covering it, Yelena rubs her forehead but Kate can hear the amusement in her voice clear as day.

    "You are just as ridiculous as him."

    "-We will name them Franchesca. Or Fitzgerald... Oh wait, no, I got it. Barnaby Bishop- Rowley."

    Through her earpiece, Kate hears a snort, her ears warming up under her hat...considering the chill of the evening, that is not a bad thing for once.

    "Oh, hey Sonya."

    Next to her, Yelena chuckles, before lifting her chin, her voice smug.

    "You forgot she was on comms too, didn't you?"

    Yes.

    Channeling some indignation she doesn't actually feel, Kate snorts.

    "No."

    There are a few seconds of silence, Kate considering how to continue the conversation with Sonya in their ears, listening to every word too, but Yelena beats her to it, her voice surprisingly offended.

    "Also, why does your name get to go first?"

    Kate's lips widen into a grin and she lifts her hands to gesture at nothing in particular, feeling chuffed to be able to do the deadpan explanation delivery for once.

    "Alphabetic order. Obviously."

    Yelena shakes her head twice while turning more fully to Kate.

    "Belova comes before Bishop."

    Not the other night she didn't...

    Kate doesn't say the joke out loud, now mindful of Sonya being an invisible third party in their conversation.

    "Yes. But Bishop comes before Rowley."

    Before Yelena can object, she snaps her fingers and points at Yelena, jumping back to the previous topic.

    "-Oh, we could do Callahan Alexei Bishop-Rowley."

    Yelena shakes her head, and throws her hands up a little, turning towards Kate even more. In this moment, Kate is particularly happy that Clint is not part of today's mission, as much as she loves him, because he undoubtedly would tell them to stop being silly and pay attention. "We are not naming...what are you, Spanish? A person doesn't need that many names." With her mask, Kate doesn't have to hide her grin, but she nods sagely anyway, before proclaiming seriously.

    "He does if he wants to be a hedge fund manager by 25."

    "You are ridiculous."

    Feeling incredibly smug to have dragged Yelena into the silly conversation, Kate shakes her head while she shrugs, as if she is not pulling this bullshit out of her ass at this exact moment. "I don't make the rules of high society, Yelena. The more ridiculous the name, the more prestige it signals."

    Once again, Yelena shakes her head, while Kate proudly complains.

    "So that settles it...Callahan Alexei Bishop-Rowley, the third."

    This time, Yelena finally chuckles out loud, even as she shakes her head in exasperation. "The third? Who were the first two?!"

    Before Kate can come up with a sufficiently entertaining answer, Yelena's Widow's bite beeps, and when Kate checks the time in the corner of her glasses, she knows that unfortunately, their playtime is over. The topic proved to be an excellent choice to stave off boredom, and it's only when it hits her full force again, does Kate realize she hasn't thought about her pre-mission nerves or the ziplining over a huge, dark abyss for like 10 minutes. Next to her, Yelena stands up and after a few seconds, Kate follows suit and puts her small backpack on again. Yelena is the first one to attach herself to the zipline, her feet kept in a wide stance to keep herself stable until she needs to move, which Kate mirrors to the best of her ability.

    "When I say go, you run to the edge and jump. I'll be exactly 2 seconds behind you and it should take us about 50 seconds to get over there. If I tell you to break, do it." Kate nods, moving her shoulders and shaking her legs a bit, adrenaline beginning to flood her system.

    "-When I do the countdown, you detach on three, okay? Not after."

    "Roger that."

    ...For the next 3-ish minutes, they stand, waiting, but the truck they are waiting for does not appear.

    "Well, that's pretty anti-climatic."

    Kate's statement is not entertained, Yelena apparently actually in mission mode now, and Kate sighs before checking her backpack, bow, and arrows one last time. When she first catches sight of the truck in the bend of the road, her heart thuds stongly against her chest once, before it takes off racing, and she jumps slightly, when she feels Yelena's hand on her shoulder from behind.

    "Hold."

    Kate exhales slowly and tries to relax the tension in her muscles, by focusing on the weight of Yelena's hand.

    "Hold."

    From this distance, the truck seems small and it definitely does not help Kate's anxiety about the jump and the journey across this darkness. What if the line doesn't hold? What if she speeds right into a bird? What if she accidentally hits the button and- "Go."

    Her shoulder is given a gentle push from behind, and Kate throws caution to the wind and does what Yelena tells her to. In the 5 steps, it takes her to get to the edge, she speeds up as much as she can, kicking off and leaping into nothing.

    The other side of the valley begins to come closer and with the dark trees below her, Kate thinks that she actually prefers this, than the previous zipline they did between skyscrapers, with concrete and nothing else below her.

    "Break a bit, you are too fast."

    Yelena's calm voice comes through her earpiece and Kate reaches up, beginning to gently slow down.

    "Good. That's good."

    By the time they near the road, Kate feels like her speed is manageable, and under different circumstances, she might even enjoy this.

    "Get ready."

    Below, the truck is nearing and Kate sincerely hopes they are out of sight as they expected to be.

    "One,-"

    Kate stops breaking, and her hand drops to the button on her harness instead. "Two."

    A deep breath, and she focuses on the truck now almost directly below her, trying to gauge where she will land.

    "Three."

    Kate punches the button just as she hears Yelena, her stomach swooping as she begins the drop. The top of the truck grows closer and closer, until she lands with a satisfying thud, and rolls forward to dissipate her momentum from the fall, arriving in a perfect on-one-knee position, with one hand on the metal of the truck.

    With adrenaline coursing through her veins, Kate feels pretty damn cool, and when she hears the thud of Yelena executing the jump behind her too, she turns her head back with a grin to check if her awesome landing was seen.

    "Stop posing, Kate."

    Yelena's crystal clear voice is both exasperated and amused, containing no real bite but still, Kate feels indignant.

    "I'm not...I'm not posing.-"

    Quickly she lies down on her stomach as agreed, flattening herself against the roof of the truck, before continuing her grumble, knowing Yelena will hear her through their comms, despite the loud engine below them.

    "-It's just how I landed."

    When she only receives a disbelieving hum from Yelena and an amused snicker from Sonya, she decides to stay quiet for the remaining minute or so of their journey. Since they don't know if anyone will be in the loading hall once they arrive, their agreed- upon signal for Sonya is three taps against their earpiece, to be done by Yelena unless something prevents her from doing so.

    The truck goes through the entrance and into the entrance tunnel with no disruptions, slowing down slightly once it's inside. The ceiling of the tunnel is thankfully not dangerously close, at least 2 feet between Kate's back and the top of the cavern.

    Inside, the tunnel curves and bends, the roar of the engine below them echoing off the walls, until finally, it opens up to a huge cavern, with enough space for several large trucks to park or turn around. With the time to move nearing and the truck slowing down, Kate adjusts her position, moving slightly closer to the edge.

    With her night vision glasses still on, the space looks incredibly bright, but Kate is thankful to note that she does not see any workers who could spot them easily, only a few of them standing around on the far side of the cave.

    The three taps against Yelena's earpiece sound very loud in her own and she winces but does not say anything, in case someone is close enough to hear somehow. The truck hasn't stopped yet, but they agreed to do the blackout before it does, as close to the entrance of the ventilation system as they can so the 28 precious seconds they have are best utilized. 3 seconds later, the lights shut off with an audible snap, and Kate is in motion. Crawling to the edge of the truck-top, she checks there is nobody to see her, before she pushes herself off, landing with another roll forward. Yelena is right beside her.

    "25 seconds."

    Sonya's voice urges them along, and Kate quickly follows Yelena behind the truck and to the wall closest to them, while the slightly alarmed voices of the Iron Mountain employees fill the cavern.

    They run around the wall, and ahead of her, Kate sees Yelena check above their heads and around them, and she does the same, keeping an eye on the workers while looking for their entrance point and pulling out her bow.

    "20 seconds."

    About 20 yards ahead of them, Kate spots the ventilation access point, originally there to allow maintenance to access the filters and the system itself, at least 15 feet above their heads. Yelena and her sneak run towards it, while they continue to keep track of their surroundings and arrive at it just as Sonya speaks again.

    "15 seconds."

    Kate pulls out her wire arrow and fires, hitting the vent next to the cover that will serve as their access point, while Yelena gets the other side with her own wire, attached to her Widow's bite. They begin to ascend almost in unison, Kate's heart racing in her chest as the small pulley system attached to her bow pulls her upwards.

    "10 seconds."

    At the top of their ascent, they both stop, and with only one hand occupied, Yelena reaches over and begins to lift and push the cover inside the vent, before pushing it to the side to reveal their entry point.

    Yelena is the first to swing and hook her legs on one side of the hole, and begins to pull herself inside, getting in just as Sonya speaks again.

    "5 seconds. Hurry up, ladies."

    Kate swings, using her abs to pull her feet up above her head and hook them on the other side of the hole in one go. Briefly, she is upside down, her calves already in the vent, while the rest of her body hangs out as she pulls out her arrow from the metal of the vent, not wanting to leave anything behind.

    "Three."

    Kate quickly pulls herself up, and inside the vent, the space smaller than she anticipated. "Two."

    Yelena pushes the vent cover back in place, the grill-like metal slab fitting into place with a quiet clicking sound,-

    "One."

    -just as the lights turn back on with a snap below them.

    Almost vibrating with the adrenaline from this relatively close call, Kate exclaims in a whisper-shout.

    "Yesss!"

    Holding up her palm for Yelena to high-five, Kate grins wide behind her mask, and Yelena slaps her palm with her own quietly with a sigh.

    "That was insane!"

    At that, despite her being quiet, Yelena hushes her and uses her hand to indicate the direction they have to crawl in. At first, Yelena has to turn around, and then the two of them begin to carefully make their way across the large cavern, the vent only tall enough for them to move around on all fours.

    There is a slight breeze around them as they move, the cold air from outside moving around them, which makes their journey less claustrophobic than it otherwise would have been, the dark tunnel endless and slightly dusty inside. They cross a few other maintenance entry points, careful not to put too much weight onto any of the covers, unsure if they would be able to hold them.

    It takes them about 15 minutes to crawl through vents within the large loading area, finally arriving at the downward shaft which will take them to the level below where both of their missions will take place.

    Yelena is the first one to reach it, of course, halting when she is on the edge. She looks back above her shoulder at Kate, speaking in a hushed tone.

    "Good?"

    "Yup."

    Kate nods and Yelena nods back, before lying down on her stomach to have enough space to take off her backpack. It's a surprisingly graceful endeavor, much more than if Kate did it herself, and a minute later, Yelena is throwing her a lightweight, but very durable roll of rope, the other end already attached to her own harness.

    With only the metal walls of the vent around them to attach anything to, they decided to not use it for safety, as they have no visual on what's on the other side of its wall, and who might see their hooks or other attachment come out on its other side. That, of course, means that they will both be responsible for keeping the other safe during the 20-ish feet descent. "When it is your turn, get in feet first too. Okay?"

    Kate turns around, so her feet are towards the opening downward shaft too, and pulls the rope through the loop on her own harness, taking hold of the parts that are already through, as she will need to feed those back through the loop as Yelena gets lower and further away. "Yes. I'm ready."

    Looking up, she sees Yelena nod but not turn around, looking down into the shaft they will descend through instead. Without another word, Yelena starts her descent, first her legs, then her torso, and finally her head disappearing from sight as she lowers herself. Kate slides forward on her ass until her feet hang off the abyss too and she has a visual of Yelena, then plants her feet on the opposite wall of the opening, in case Yelena falls. Below her, Yelena uses her arms and to press her back firmly against the opposite metal wall of the downward shaft, making a steady but not too fast descent. It takes her about 7 minutes to lower herself to the first level fully underground, where the evidence will be waiting. "I am in position. Kate, you are good to go."

    When it's Kate's turn, she attaches the rope to her own harness securely, no longer allowing for movement, and looks down into the shaft. Without Yelena to block the view, Kate sees that it's insanely deep, with basically no bottom in sight, running down to the lowest level of the facility presumably, 22 stories deep below ground.

    Without her glasses, it would be entirely dark and even with them, she can not see where the first exit will be, where Yelena is waiting.

    "Kate?"

    "Yeah. Coming."

    Pushing her fear aside once again, Kate begins to lower herself into the shaft, finding it hard to find a purchase that she feels completely secure with. It takes her a couple of feet of descent to get into the rhythm of it, always having her weight on one leg and two hands, with her back firmly pressing against the vent wall while she moves the other leg, and always both feet and both hands securing her when she slides her back lower against the wall. She makes the same journey as Yelena did in about 30 seconds longer, joining her on level minus one, the next section of their underground journey, at 1:26 am.

    So far, this plan is going pretty smoothly... Let's hope it stays that way. On level minus one, they crawl through the vents for 5 more minutes, until they reach the intersection where their paths will diverge, Kate going right toward the junction box, and Yelena going left to the holding area where the evidence soon will be transferred or already is.

    With 34 minutes to go, they could probably take a breather, but Yelena seemingly has other plans, and with all the leftover adrenaline buzzing through her system, Kate is more than happy to move things along too.

    Feeling somewhat silly, with moving across the entire facility on her hands and knees and following Yelena's ass in the darkness for the last 30 minutes or so, Kate says her goodbyes, maybe a little less suave than a super secret mission in a super secret underground facility requires, to the hot assassin she slept (and hopes to sleep again) with. "Catch you on the flippity flip."

    Yelena, who has been on the verge of moving away to the shaft she has to take, halts and turns slightly back, her neon green goggles looking particularly judgy as she tilts her head before she asks in a whisper.

    "Excuse me?"

    Through her comms, Kate also hears Sonya snort, chiming in for the first time since her countdown.

    "Is that the way to address the mother of my future godchild?"

    Rolling her eyes behind her glasses, Kate snorts and whispers back.

    "At least I did not call her an alligator."

    With a sigh that is way too theatrical in Kate's opinion, Yelena turns away and begins to crawl away on her hands and knees in the direction of the waiting hall, significantly lessening the weight of her supposedly dramatic exit.

    Then, when Kate has already begun to crawl forward on her own shaft to the right, she hears Yelena's whisper through the comms.

    "See you in a while, juvenile."

    The teasing farewell is followed by Sonya's snorting, and for about 5 minutes after, everyone does their jobs in silence. Yelena is the first to reach her destination, checking in with a whisper.

    "I am above corridor leading to the waiting hall. It is still being loaded." Presumably, Kate is getting close to her destination too, the junction box above the door to the security center of the compound. Here, there are almost certainly people below her, so she checks in as quietly as she can.

    "I'm about a minute out."

    This portion of the ventilation system is slightly less narrow than before, so when Kate finally arrives at the junction box about a minute later, she can sit up comfortably, take off her backpack without having to lie down, and then lean against the metal wall. "I'm here. Gonna unpack my things and get work."

    From her bag, she pulls out a laser distance meter, a portable plasma cutter, a magnet, her tools to expose the camera wire she needs, her tablet, and the electronic connection clamps she will need to tap into the camera system. According to the blueprints and security schematics they received, the main junction box, where all camera lines from the facility meet, is just behind the metal wall across from Kate where she sits.

    Of course, in other places, hacking the security system and gaining access to the camera feeds would be easier, but Iron Mountain is not a paragon of security for nothing. Their system would be hackable from inside the compound, but most likely not within the timeframe they are working with, leaving only the physical tapping into the lines as a viable option, even if it's more risky to do.

    Somewhat anxiously, Kate glances back at the maintenance door cover only a few feet away, hoping that nobody is currently walking below her in the corridor she is above since while she is going to do this as quietly as possible, it will make some noise. With every other pysically dangerous step of the plan ahead of her, she has not been nervous about this one before, but with other things out of the way, this too feels risky now. Nevertheless, she crawls back into the last turn in the vent and uses the laser distance meter and the saved specs on her glasses to measure the exact place she will have to cut the metal wall, to get right to the junction box. Supposedly, there are only 5 inches between the wall on which the box is on, and the wall of the vent, so once she is done cutting, the chances of anyone looking up and discovering the hole anytime soon, are minimal.

    Once she pinpoints the exact spot, Kate crawls back and attaches the magnet to the middle of the area she has to cut around, the metal wall supposedly made of stainless steel which is magnetic. The magnet is there to make sure that once she is done cutting, the small piece does not fall outwards, down to the corridor, and creates noise that will draw a lot of unwanted attention. Thankfully, their information was right, and the magnet attaches to the wall of the vent without a hitch.

    The next step is the most risky.

    With a deep sigh, Kate picks up the portable plasma cutter, hoping it won't be the thing that gets her in trouble. They tried it at home this afternoon, and through a closed door, it cannot be heard but if anyone happens to walk by while she is doing this, she won't be able to hear them but they will definitely notice in turn. Pulling the cutter against her chest, Kate whispers her prayer out loud, mentally preparing herself.

    "Please, be quiet."

    "We didn't say anything."

    At Yelena's whispered answer, Kate opens her eyes, breatheing out a whispered chuckle despite her stressful circumstances.

    "I was talking to the cutter. I'm about to start."

    That earns Kate a snort, and then a few moments of silence are followed by yet another whispered sentence from Yelena.

    "Proceed."

    Smiling, Kate shakes her head.

    In the end, no amount of waiting around will make it less risky. They have no way of monitoring the comings and goings of the compound's personnel, so if someone happens to walk by, it was meant to be.

    She holds the cutter close to the metal wall of the vent and presses the button on its handle, firing it up. The device sounds pretty loud to her ears in the enclosed space, but Kate grits her teeth, ignores her racing heart, and quickly begins to cut the hole.

    As planned, when is done approximately 30 seconds later, the cut-out piece falls backward, into the vent itself, thanks to the magnet Kate attached to its back, and she catches it skilfully with her left hand before it can hit the bottom and possibly makes some unnecessary noise. Immediately turning off the cutter, Kate stays perfectly still, trying to hear through her thundering heartbeat if there are alarmed voices or running footsteps nearby, but thankfully, the corridor below is quiet and deserted.

    "I think I'm good."

    Without waiting for an answer, Kate lays down on her stomach and peers through the 6-inch by 6-inch square hole she cut, searching for the junction box. Thankfully, just as it appeared on the schematics, it's close by, only a few inches below the hole she cut. After listening for a few more seconds, Kate reaches through the door and pops the junction box open, the small plastic cover opening with a dull click.

    In an ideal world, she could cut a hole through that too, so while she sits up there and taps into the system, it doesn't have to stay open, but since the junction box is made of plastic, the plasma cutter would melt it, and any mechanical cutter that could actually be used for it would make too much noise. Either way, Kate is pretty sure nobody will look up at a random junction box, like 5 feet above their heads, so she proceeds to the next step, somewhat relieved the loud part is over.

    She reaches through the hole once again, using her wire stripper mostly blindly, wishing she could at least cut some eye holes, since doing it this way, with only one hand through a freshly cut hole, is rather impractical and uncomfortable. For 5 minutes, she keeps on working, softly grunting from time to time as her arm is at a pretty weird angle as she reaches through the hole.

    "Kate, what is going on? It's 0145."

    Pausing for a few seconds, Kate resists the urge to groan, mindful of her noise level when she answers despite her frustration.

    "I can't see through the stupid hole, so I can't see shit. I am doing this blindly." It's Sonya who answers her this time, with an annoying question.

    "Why don't you cut another hole? Or make it bigger?"

    Huffing, Kate works her jaw, a bit annoyed at her mask too for restricting its movement. "It's too much noise. The cutter sounds loud as shit... But I'm almost done." This time, it's Yelena who speaks, her voice still quiet through their comms. "Okay. Just let me know when you have a visual."

    Kate huffs to herself one more time, before she sticks her arm out through the hole again, and continues the motions of stripping the camera wires of their plastic sleeves. Thankfully, about a minute or so later, she is finished, checking through her hole to verify that all wires are now exposed and ready for her.

    The time in the corner of her glasses now reads 1:47 am, so despite badly craving a few seconds of a breather to calm down a bit, Kate immediately picks up the clamps, prepared with wires attached to them and spun together, and begins to attach them to each exposed wire. Despite these wires already containing multiple feeds each, there are still a lot of them, and Kate is on the 13th clamp when she hears the voices.

    Shit.

    Two people, a man and a woman grow nearer, their voices slowly becoming comprehensible conversation instead of just unintelligible murmurs, while Kate quickly shuts the cover of the junction box as much as she can from the already-connected clamps and wires, leading up to her and retracts her arm.

    "-already knows how to write! At 4 years old! That kid is blowing my mind." The man's voice is full of pride and if Kate's heart wasn't ready to jump out of her throat, she would have smiled at it. An unseen feminine voice answers him, belonging to someone slightly younger by the sound of it.

    "Your daughter must be very proud. Where does he go to preschool?"

    Keeping her muscles as still as possible, Kate exhales as the pair passes under her, and by addition, the junction box, while the man answers.

    "It's called Everbrook something... Everbrook Academy, I think? At first, I thought they were insane for sending him to an expensive private place, but I'm willing to admit I'm proven wrong."

    Whatever the woman says in response to that, Kate cannot properly hear as the pair walks further away on the corridor, soon not heard even as a murmur. The time is 1:51 am, so quickly, Kate reaches through the hole again, reopens the junction box, and resumes placing her the clamps.

    It takes her about one more minute and a half to finish with the clamps, the resulting wire bunch almost as thick as her wrist. Thankfully after that's done, the rest of the process is a lot smoother. The connector at the end of the wire bunch plugs into Kate's tablet, turning it into a de-facto control center between what comes in, and what gets to continue on to the security office below.

    Pushing her glasses up onto her forehead to see the screen without night vision making it basically unusable, Kate leans against the wall of the vent as she quickly goes through the software side of setting up her personal security hub.

    "Kate?"

    Swallowing, Kate quickly answers Yelena's question while she continues to configure the system created from all 683 cameras on the compound, quickly unfiltering the ones on other levels and above ground.

    "Almost there, one more minute."

    That leaves her with 45 cameras on this level, and she quickly looks for the ones covering the waiting hall and the surrounding two corridors, based on camera numbers they got from the security schematics. That leaves her with 7 feeds to check and freeze for Yelena's entry. "Okay, I got you.-"

    The time stamp on the feed matches the one in the corner of Kate's glasses, both showing 1:57 am. She quickly looks each of the feeds over, noting how the medium-sized cavern is packed with pallets full of boxes and packages, but seems otherwise empty. "I think the waiting room is empty. Cloning the cameras now."

    With a few taps of her fingers, all 7 images are frozen on the main line that continues to the security office, while Kate retains the originals on half of her screen, which are still live, in case Yelena gets some unwelcome visitors.

    "Okaaayy.... Room and surrounding corridors are empty, camera feeds are frozen. Yelena, you are good to go."

    "Roger that."

    At first, nothing happens but in a few seconds, Kate watches on one half of her screen as Yelena's boots appear on the ceiling on one of the feeds from the corridor outside the waiting room and she hops down, landing gracefully on the tiled floor below. Thankfully, the feed that gets relayed to the security office remains frozen, with no sight of Yelena. "Walk straight ahead. It should lead you straight to the waiting area." Following Kate's instructions, Yelena walks ahead carefully, thankfully already close to the waiting area as they choose to exit the ventilation system as close to it as possible, to avoid the risk of her running into anyone.

    On her screen, Kate watches as she arrives at the waiting hall, the medium-sized cavern well- lit and almost perfectly round. Yelena then begins to search among the piled-up boxes, for the item number they are looking for.

    When she finally halts after about 3 minutes of searching and looks around with her hands on her hips, Kate assumes she found what they are looking for. When Yelena doesn't move for a few seconds, Kate's eyebrows furrow in confusion.

    What is she waiting for?

    "We have a problem.-"

    On her screen, Yelena moves closer to the boxes and keeps looking around at all of the similar ones around her.

    "-The evidence boxes are wax sealed. If I break it, they will know we were here." Shit.

    "Okay. Okay, um, let's...Give me a second to think it through."

    At her words, even as a little figure on her screen, Kate sees the exasperation in Yelena's form before she speaks, her shoulders rising and falling with her huff.
