    "During the car chase, the dark-haired, caucasian female has used a bow and various types of enhanced arrows again and while CCTV footage was not captured then, cell phone footage was."

    She pulls out a pretty grainy, printed picture from the folder then that Kate looks down at, immediately recognizing herself. Her face is not visible in the image, it's obviously a screenshot taken from a phone camera video, but she feels her pulse speed up and has to focus hard on keeping her body loose, because if someone knows what to look for, it's easy to tell it's her.

    "Cell phone footage was also captured of the fight that ensued when a member of the private security team, Mr. Lennox Richards, pulled one of the suspects out of the car, and then of the two female suspects proceeding to assault Mr. Richards."

    At her words, Kate is fuming internally, but she doesn't say anything. Assault Mr Richards?! Are they fucking serious? The Super Soldier that literally dragged Kate out of a moving car, and would have killed her there on the street, if Yelena had not intervened? Agent McLagan continues, really sounding like someone who is just retelling a moderately boring episode of TV.

    "The other suspect, a blonde caucasian female, between five-three and five-four in height has also dispatched a firearm at Mr.Richards, and then the two of them escaped through the subway, hiding in the crowd.

    Glancing at Agent Reyes, Kate finds him looking, his eyes like a shark's and she resists the urge to fidget, or even move much, returning her gaze to Agent McLagan instead as she drones on, while depositing copies of Yelena's and her composite drawings on the growing pile of pictures on the desk.

    "While conducting their search of the scene, police found a burnt-out black Mercedes on the scene of the altercation with Mr Richards, which according to the VIN, was registered to Katherine Elizabeth Bishop, born April 5, 2002, residence in Los Angeles, but inhabiting 15 Central Park West. Approximately 20 feet from the burnt-out Mercedes, investigators also found a wallet, belonging to and identified by Miss Bishop herself as hers." Agent Reyes steps forward, reaching into the pocket of his FBI windbreaker, and pulls out Kate's wallet in a plastic bag, putting it on the table with the pictures. Kate doesn't look at it, but continues to stare at Agent McLagan, mindful to keep her body language loose, even though she is not sure it matters at this point.

    "During our previous interview in her residence, Miss Bishop told us that her wallet had been taken during a mugging in Central Park and that she had reported it stolen. While Special Agent Reyes and I checked the database before we went to conduct our interview with Miss Bishop, we were not able to find such a report, but when we double-checked it the afternoon after our interview, the report was indeed found in the database. Almost as if it magically appeared in there mere hours after we went to interview her..."

    For a long moment, Agent McLagan looks at Kate, obviously telling her they know the report is bullshit while she does her best to channel Yelena's amazing poker face. After a few seconds, Agent McLagan speaks again, and Kate discreetly rubs her palms on her newly acquired sweatpants, trying to wipe the cold sweat she feels building up on them. "That, however, does not explain how Miss Bishop's car was also found on the scene of the altercation, as that has not been reported stolen. Anything to add here, Miss Bishop? About how your car ended up there, perhaps?"

    Kate wets her lips, and endures Agent McLagans stare, but does not say a word. They obviously have pretty damning evidence against her, not to mention getting caught right now. Anything she will say here will only make things worse, especially if they truly treat and believe Lennox to be a member of a private security force that Kate and her accomplice assaulted. As she already suspected, they either don't know or don't care about Fisk's criminal activities, so unless she can provide proof, there is no point in trying to make her case right now.

    Agent McLagan smiles thinly, nodding to herself as she turns the page of the report she is reading, before closing the folder.

    "I thought so. Moving on..."

    Reaching for the second file on the stack, Agent McLagan opens that too, and resumes her storytelling.

    "On the 29th of August, the day after the previous incident, a similar altercation took place in the harbor of New York. The two suspects, matching in description to the day before, have unlawfully entered a ship belonging to Skyline Sea Logistics, after assaulting three employees of a neighboring one."

    Pursing her lips, Kate decides to look straight ahead, somewhere to the right of Agent McLagan's face, hoping it will make it easier for her to not react as she retells what happened at the harbor.

    "-The two women were aided by the enhanced individual known as Spider-Man. Together, they attacked the ship, leaving forty-six people injured, twenty-nine dead, and causing north of 3 million dollars worth of property damage."

    Pursing her lips, Kate blinks, keeping her eyes on the spot by Agent McLagan's head. Twenty-nine people dead.

    She remembers the young guy, drowning in his own blood from her arrow. The man whom she stabbed from behind to save Yelena. The ones buried and crushed under the containers she blew up. She remembers the sticky, warm wetness of her clothes, soaked in blood. Resisting the urge to clear her throat of the uncomfortable feeling in her throat, Kate swallows once again while Agent McLagan drones on, relentless.

    "The incident's wide-scale destruction and the number of victims warranted that our office got involved in the investigations, so from that point on, Agent Reyes and myself followed the trail of these individuals ourselves."

    "We interviewed the survivors from the ship, who described the assailants as highly trained, young, and merciless. Based on their descriptions and capabilities, we could also determine with a good amount of certainty that they are the same two women, who were involved in the Storage Unit incident from the day before. We also walked the crime scene ourselves, so we bore first-hand witness to the aftermath of the violence of these individuals." As slowly as she can, Kate exhales through her nose, not looking at either agent. She feels her back sweating, and her palms are constantly clammy on her thigh but she does not give in to the temptation of wiping them properly. Instead, she tries to tune out Agent McLagan's voice, trying to remember the container full of bodies and the hundreds of victims she has seen during her research.

    "The victims, both surviving and dead, were all affiliated with organized crime, which at first, made us believe this was part of a new wave of gang violence. However, as the trail of the assailants continued, we were able to eliminate that possibility. Some victims' injuries, caused by a sword, also bore a striking similarity to the ones inflicted by the vigilante Ronin, even if the description of the individuals responsible did not match his." At the name 'Ronin', Kate blinks, quickly glancing at Agent McLagan, before reminding herself to not react. The last thing she needs is that coming to bite her in the ass. "As we followed up on that lead, we went back to look at the circumstances of the last sighting of the Ronin, in December 2024, investigating if the current incidents could possibly have a connection to him, either as a resurfacing, or a possible copycat. The last confirmed sighting of the Ronin was at a charity auction, which incidentally, also had an organized crime connection, just like the incident on the ship."

    To avoid outwardly reacting, Kate bites down on her tongue, staring resolutely at a spot to the right of Agent McLagan's head. The agent continues, her voice factual and cold. "Our colleagues working on the case back then also made the connection to another event only a week later, a similar attack on the Bishop Security company holiday party, seemingly by the same group. And that incident had a lot of interesting details similar to our case, mainly the use of arrows, which is as rare as one can imagine, in today's day and age. Especially against individuals involved with organized crime."

    Kate is going to be so mad, if Yelena is going to be right about her arrows. "The two individuals using arrows in that incident were identified on the scene as former S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Clint Barton, also known as the Avenger, Hawkeye, and Katherine Elizabeth Bishop, daughter of the arrested CEO of Bishop Security, Eleanor Bishop." "After looking at the files of the Bishop case, Agent Reyes and myself sought the advice of a weapons specialist, who was able to determine fairly certainly, that the arrows used by Miss Bishop and Mr. Barton during the attack on the Bishop Holiday Party, and by the attackers in the Storage Unit incident, and on the Skyline Sea Logistics ship, share enough similarities that they were either made by the same person, or possibly, someone taught by the same person."

    Shit.

    The next pictures placed in front of her are of trick arrows, presumably from the Tracksuits' attack at Rockefeller Plaza, and from the storage unit or the ship.

    "Unfortunately, all twenty-six CCTV cameras at or around the harbor mysteriously malfunctioned at the time of the Skyline Sea Logistics attack and did not record anything of the incident, but based on the description given to us by the victims, we could eliminate that it was definitely not Mr Barton on the Skyline Sea Logistic ship. After reviewing the evidence, however, we found Miss Bishop's wallet and her car at the scene of the fight with Mr Lennox, following the incident at O’Connor Self Storage."

    The brief pause makes Kate's eyes shift to Agent McLagan's face, a thin smile stretching onto it as she delivers the next verbal blow.

    "I'm also fairly certain, that when our expert looks at them, the arrows will be the same as the ones that were found on your person tonight.

    Tilting her head to the side slightly, the agent blinks once, slowly, before speaking again. "So I ask you, Miss Bishop, do I need to say more?-"

    Kate sighs once again, her resolve weakening just a little as Agent McLagan keeps talking. "-We got you, red-handed. There is no judge or jury who will not put you away for a long, long time after all of this. I do not even have to mention the incidents, both of them, at Limitless Holdings, one of them with the exact same arrows used. Or how all of the attacks seem to target the businesses of Mr. Wilson Fisk, whom you and your mother keep pointing your fingers at, but have yet to produce any meaningful evidence against." Wetting her lips, Kate meets the agent's eyes as she leans back, looking fairly satisfied. It takes everything in her not to start yelling that Fisk is the whole reason this is happening. "-So. Miss Bishop... Are you ready to talk to us?"

    Running her tongue over her teeth, Kate glances at Agent Reyes, still watching her from beside the wall, for once wordlessly, before she turns back to look at Agent McLagan and shakes her head.

    No. There is nothing she can say, that will make any of this better. They clearly have this all wrong, thinking she is going out to wreak havoc for no reason, and refusing to entertain why she would do such a thing... And she will obviously not throw Yelena or Sonya under the bus to improve her own position. There really is no point in speaking to them. "I told you. I want to talk to my lawyer."

    Agent McLagan does not seem disappointed, or even affected by Kate's words but Agent Reyes moves, crossing the distance to the table in a few long, but fast steps. "You want to know what I think, Kate?"

    He doesn't seem like he is actually asking and Kate doesn't answer, looking up at him defiantly, consciously not moving a muscle as he leans onto the table and closer to her face. “I’m sure you think you are doing the right thing."

    She is. Or trying to, anyway.

    "-That you are a hero, and all these rules, all these laws, they only apply to ordinary people, right? And well, we all know you are not ordinary, are you?"

    He smiles then, but it's mocking and almost hateful. Kate feels her hackles rising, somehow his demeanor getting under her skin more than all of Agent McLagan's cold, factual words did.

    "You got several black belts, the first one at fourteen. You have more trophies than space in even your overpriced, snobby apartment. Hell, you can shoot a butterfly out of the sky a mile away. You are extraordinary, right?"

    He pauses, leaning slightly closer and his voice is even colder with his next words, dropping an octave.

    “Well, Kate. You are not.”

    He reaches for the stack of folders, picks one out, and begins to place the pictures in it in front of Kate, who makes the mistake of looking down at them while he keeps talking. The first one is a burnt corpse in a car.

    “You are about to learn that these laws apply to you just like they apply to everyone else.“ The next one is the young man Kate shot on the ship. His eyes are still open in the photo, the coughed-up blood painting his chin and neck crimson. Her arrow is still wedged into his chest.

    “You want to know what I see?”

    The next photo is of a man in a pool of his own blood and Kate is struck by the fact that she doesn’t even know if she’s killed him or not. Slowly, to avoid saying the words threatening to burst out of her or tearing up, she exhales through her nose, not giving Reyes the satisfaction of looking away.

    “I see a rich asshole, who thinks she is above the law just because mommy’s and daddy’s blood money bought them the opportunity to become an adept killing machine.” The next photo is of the hallway on the ship where Yelena and she fought their way through, the walls covered in splashes of crimson. On the blood-covered floor, about a dozen men lie scattered, like ants after being sprayed down. The macabre thought makes Kate lift her eyes off it to look back at Agent Reyes, his mouth turned firmly downwards in disgust. “Ever since Tony fucking Stark, half of you young billionaires think that you can play god. That it’s somehow your job to decide who deserves to be punished and killed, and who are the good guys.”

    He is not entirely wrong.

    Her parents' money, a lot of which was earned through her mother working for Fisk, allowed Kate to become who and what she is today. She has killed people, and while she avoids doing it whenever she can, it is still something she has to admit to herself and live with. It can't be shrugged off simply as self-defense.

    But he is wrong about one thing.

    Kate is not doing this because she thinks she is above the law.

    She doesn't think it's her job to decide who lives and dies, but because Fisk apparently is actually above the law. He has been caught many times over, and still, he always ends up more powerful than before. Kate doesn't think she gets to decide if he lives or dies, but it's clear that the system will not actually bring him to justice. He will keep terrorizing people, killing people, including Kate and the people she loves, until somebody stops him. For good.

    That is why Kate is doing this.

    She opens her mouth to answer, her resolve finally breaking, when the door swings open. "Agent McLagan, Agent Reyes, a word, please."

    Detective O'Neil stands in the doorway, his hand keeping it open and looking at the agents expectantly.

    Kate exhales, her agitation deflating just a little, replaced by confusion... If she is being honest, the interruption couldn't have come at a better time because she doesn't know what she would have said, but it certainly wouldn't have helped her case... There is a swirling black hole of guilt and some self-doubt in her stomach too, the agents' words echoing in her head, but she doesn't allow herself to get overwhelmed by it. Now is not the time.

    Before the agents can move to leave the room, a young woman pushes past the Detective, wearing an expensive pantsuit and a beautiful coat.

    "I'll confer with my client while you inform the agents, Detective, thank you." ...Client? Is that her lawyer?

    Wait...

    As Kate looks at the woman, her lawyer apparently, she is stuck by the realization. ...Allie? Allie Newhouse?!

    Eyes widening, Kate watches as Allie marches into the room, her demeanor a vast contrast to the borderline shy girl she remembers from high school.

    "Sorry, who are you?"

    Agent Reyes' voice is not openly antagonistic, but it's apparent that he is not happy with the interruption, most likely aware that they were close to getting her to say something. "I am Allison Newhouse, Miss Bishop's attorney."

    Kate turns back to the Agents, getting over her slight shock quickly to throw a maybe misguidedly smug look at Agent Reyes, feeling like she might have a chance to finally get her feet underneath her.

    At least, she is not alone anymore.

    "-I'm here to take her home."

    Her eyebrows rising, Kate looks back up at Allie, who now stands beside her, her head snapping to Agent Reyes when he bursts out laughing.

    "Listen, Miss Newhouse. I'm sure you are an excellent attorney, but Miss Bishop is not going anywhere anytime soon, except to be arraigned. She was caught breaking into a private security facility, she-"

    Allie's voice is assertive, but perfectly polite as she cuts the agent off, while Kate's gaze jumps between them like she is watching a tennis match.

    "I'm sorry, Agent, but that is not an accurate description of the events. My client is an employee of the Central Intelligence Agency, and she was part of the task force appointed to perform a penetration testing exercise on-site last night."

    What?!

    "-Here is the documentation."

    Agent Reyes blinks, his grin frozen onto his face while Agent McLagan reaches out to take the offered file from Allie's hand, quickly opening it and reading what's inside. Agent Reyes' eyebrows furrow and he laughs once again, incredulous.

    "You don't seriously expect us to believe that she is a CIA asset, do you?" Allie smiles, lowering her chin, and Kate's heart hammers in her ears, a spark of hope beginning to take hold in her chest, even as Agent Reyes continues.

    "Even if I buy it, which I do not, the CIA does not have jurisdiction. U.S. Code 1385 limits their ability to operate on US soil, which means that even if Miss Bishop was a CIA asset, she is still under ar-"

    With a cordial smile, Allie cuts him off.

    "USC 1385 is specifically about deploying the military to enforce domestic policy. Miss Bishop took part in a training exercise, which is perfectly within the bounds of the agency's jurisdiction to carry out. However, I understand the confusion. That is why Director de Fontaine came down personally to straighten out the misunderstanding. You can ask her yourself,-"

    What?!

    Director de Fontaine... Is that Valentina?!

    "-she is right outside."

    Valentina is here?!

    Holy shit, what did Yelena do?

    Agent Reyes looks at the open door just as Kate does, catching sight of Valentina behind Detective O'Neil. She looks impatient, flicking the purple strand in her hair from her eyes but she smiles when she catches Kate's eyes, the expression somehow unsettling. Agent McLagan shuts the folder and Kate's heart leaps when she sees how sour her face looks, as she meets Agent Reyes' eyes.

    "Before you go. Please uncuff my client."

    The agents don't heed Allie's request, but Agent McLagan nods as they step out and Detective O'Neil steps into the room, looking not exactly displeased, but certainly weighted by the developments too. He reaches into his pocket for the keys, and a few seconds later, Kate is freed.

    "Thank you."

    The detective nods at Allie before he leaves the room too, throwing one last heavy look at Kate, the two of them finally alone. Kate stands up, turning to Allie, unsure if she should give in to the urge to throw her arms around her in her relief. Allie turns to her too, a small smile on her lips before it widens into a small grin as she shakes her head.

    "Kate Bishop..."

    After a short, but meaningful pause, she continues.

    "I should have known I'd have to bust you out of jail sooner or later." Despite her stress, Kate laughs, barely believing the events of the last few minutes and distractedly rubbing at her wrist, a bit sore from being cuffed for who knows how many hours.

    "How-"

    Quickly, Allie's eyes glance at the camera behind Kate, her small grin tempered into a smile. "We'll discuss everything somewhere more appropriate."

    Blinking, Kate nods, feeling kind of weird in her stress-sweaty police clothes next to Allie's pristine suit and spotless, cream-colored coat.

    "Right. It's..."

    Pausing, Kate thinks of the camera watching and listening to their every move as well. She decides to swallow how happy she is that Allie is here, and only voice only her gratitude for now.

    "-Thank you for coming."

    Allie holds her eyes for a long moment as she nods, before her gaze drops to Kate's clothes, her smile disappearing.

    "Were you processed?"

    Maybe due to the stress of the interrogation or just the rollercoaster of emotions she experienced in the last few minutes, Kate looks down at her own clothes, as if she is not aware of what she's wearing.

    "Yeah. Yeah, they took a mugshot, my prints. The whole thing."

    Nodding, Allie grows serious. Her eyes glance at a spot on Kate's forehead, that she kind of forgot she hit in all the excitement.

    "Were you given medical attention?"

    Shaking her head, Kate reaches up, feeling the bruise, a bit warm to her touch. She grimaces a little as she rubs it, glancing at the mirror on the wall to look at the round, purple spot on her forehead. Considering how close she was to the explosion, she really got off easy. "No. They took me from Iron Mountain straight to here."

    Once again, Allie's gaze lifts to the bruise before she meets Kate's again. "Do you need to go to a hospital?"

    Kate shakes her head, her lips stretching to a tired smile as she can finally give in to the temptation and wipe her sweaty palms on her thighs discreetly.

    "Nah. Nothing some ibuprofen and a good nap won't fix."

    Above Kate's head, Allie looks at the camera once more, stepping closer and lowering her voice.

    "Did you say anything?"

    Wetting her lips, Kate shakes her head and Allie nods meaningfully, making Kate wonder how much she is actually aware of.

    "Okay. That should speed things up."

    With the cameras in the room recording every word, they wait in silence, Kate sneaking glances at Allie, while her mind is still reeling from Agent Reyes' words and the last few minutes. They are interrupted soon by Valentina herself opening the door, but not stepping inside.

    "Chop chop, Baby Hawk."

    Eyebrows lifting, Kate blinks but she is not one to look the gift horse in the mouth so she quickly walks out, Allie only a step behind her. In the hallway, the Detectives and the Agents stand, Agent Reyes' expression sour like someone slapped him, and Agent McLagan's as if she bit into a lemon.

    Kate keeps her head held high, walking after the small form of Valentina, but she can't help but smile a bit at Agent Reyes, the words leaving her mouth without thinking. "See you around, Daniel."

    The muscles in his jaw jump as he steps forward into Kate's way, even as Agent McLagan's hand reaches out to grab his arm.

    "This is not over."

    Valentina turns back, stepping back to look up at Agent Reyes.

    "Miss Bishop has a briefing to attend to, Agent. If you have a problem, I suggest you take it up with President Ross... Or better yet, talk to your therapist about it." She snaps her fingers then, which Kate is pretty sure is aimed at her, and for once, she does not have a problem with obeying the unspoken command. With one last glance, Kate walks away from the agents, nodding with slightly more genuine respect to the detectives who do not say a word.

    "Miss Newhouse, please see about getting Miss Bishop's things back, while I have a chat with her outside."

    Kate and Allie exchange a perplexed glance, but Allie nods a second later. "Of course, Director."

    Valentina marches through the station like she owns it after Allie veers off, and Kate follows her, feeling several pairs of eyes on her as they go. Valentina does not say anything until they get to the elevator and does not even look at Kate.

    "Can I assume you were smart enough to stay quiet?"

    She turns to look at Kate inside the elevator, her eyebrows pinched like she is a schoolteacher berating Kate. Still reeling from the last 15 minutes, Kate swallows, a bit unsure how she should act towards Valentina now.

    "Yes. I only said I wanted a lawyer."

    Valentina nods, pursing her lips.

    "Good. You want to tell me then, why you were stupid enough to get caught in the first place?"

    A spark of annoyance flares in Kate's chest, and she grinds her teeth together but it turns out Valentina is not interested in the answer anyway, turning away from her, facing forward again.

    "-It doesn't matter. Don't let it happen again."

    The elevator doors open and Kate follows Valentina marching out of it, through the lobby and out the front door, the two of them leaving the station uninterrupted. Outside, there are five large, black SUVs waiting and Val marches up to one of them, a man in a suit opening the door for her.

    "Get in."

    With no other option, no Yelena or Sonya waiting for her outside, to her slight disappointment, Kate does as she is told, sliding into the back seat next to Valentina. "Okay, Baby Hawk.-"

    Having to keep quiet for hours has apparently strained her nerves more than she realized, the words snapping out of her mouth without her meaning to.

    "My name is Kate."

    It's only the two of them in the car, and they don't seem to be going anywhere just yet, maybe waiting for Allie to join them. At her interruption, Valentina turns to look at her incredulously, and Kate almost feels chastised. Almost.

    "Your name is 'I just got your ass out of jail, so you shut up and listen." Her nostrils flaring, Kate huffs but she does lean back to listen, realizing she doesn't have enough information to know what's next or what deal Yelena made to get her out. And if Valentina is dangerous enough for Yelena to be wary of her, maybe she shouldn't piss her off just for the sake of it.

    "As I was saying, Kate, I am not a gambling woman."

    An eyebrow lifting, Kate wonders where she is going with this, while Valentina turns back forward, talking as if she is merely explaining something to her.

    "-I make investments that I know are going to pay off. And on the off chance that it begins to look like they aren't, I cut my losses."

    At the end of her sentence, her threat, really, she turns to look at Kate, to see her reaction. Pursing her lips, Kate looks back at Valentina without a blink, letting the obvious threat roll off her without a reaction, but she swallows a quip about all investments being gambles if you really look at them.

    Val waits a few seconds, maybe to see if her words had any effect, but she continues a second later, her voice losing some of its edge.

    "To smooth over your little stunt, I had to pay a pretty hefty price to get Director Stone to call off those two, and basically perform a miracle to get Meaney to sign off on your infiltration being called a penetration exercise.-"

    A moment later she turns back to Kate, levelling her with a look.

    "-Do you understand where I'm going with this?"

    Blinking, Kate takes a heartbeat to think it over. Obviously, Valentina wants something in return for saving her ass. But Kate doesn't know what deal she made with Yelena already, so she will just play dumb until Valentina tells her.

    "Not really."

    Valentina sighs, and Kate even sees her roll her eyes a little.

    "It means, you owe me. You work for me now."

    While she can't know for sure, Kate is pretty sure Yelena would not be happy about her agreeing to that, so she waits to see if Valentina will say anything useful and does not verbally agree to anything. Valentina barrels on after a second, fixing her with a stern look. "-When you get the formula, you will deliver it to me. Not your mother, not even Javier Rojas, me. You will report every week on your progress, and you will not do anything as monumentally stupid again as you did today. Got it?"

    With her eyes basically cutting through Kate, she swallows and nods, pretty much trapped to do anything other than agree. Valentina nods back, her eyes not leaving Kate's. "Good."

    While Kate agrees, her mind is already working on a way to get out from under Valentina's thumb.

    When they get the formula, they will get all of her mom's insurance policy too. If they have that, Kate could use it to get herself immunity and whatever Valentina holds over her head- "Oh, and one more thing."

    Meeting her eyes once again, Kate swallows, the smile that slides onto Valentina's face making her look like a snake that is about to strike.

    "If Yelena tries to get you out of this, or come after me, or talk you into doing anything else, other than exactly what I just told you... Well, let's just say I am sure that Javier Rojas would be very, very interested to learn who is responsible for his father's death. And the coordinates of Clint Barton's homestead."

    At that threat, Kate blanches, her chest panging with worry for Clint and his family. It probably shows on her face, because a second later Valentina's smile widens into a sharp grin. "Good talk, Baby Hawk. Now get the hell out of my car."

    Valentina then turns away, already typing something on her phone and seemingly done with the conversation. It takes Kate a few seconds to process her words, but she does not manage to come up with a comeback that will not immediately bite her, or worse, Clint in the ass, so she shuts her mouth and opens the door, sliding out of the back seat.

    As she turns back to close the door, Valentina turns to her one more time, her annoying smile back on her face.

    "I'll be in touch. Welcome to the CIA."

    Feeling defeated, Kate looks away and shuts the door when it becomes evident that Valentina is not going to say more. The suited men around the cars move in unison, getting back into their vehicles, and in a few seconds, four out of the five SUVs drive off, leaving Kate alone in the parking lot.

    How the hell is she getting home?

    ...What about Allie? Does she have a car?

    Would Valentina really betray Clint like that?

    Without her coat, and only in the police-issued suspect-sweats, the crispy morning air is especially chilly, despite the pale sunlight shining at her face, and Kate shivers slightly, thinking about her next step. She looks over the parking lot but other than the last remaining black SUV, there is no car that could belong to Allie, which means that is probably their ride back to New York.

    Exhaling through puffed-out cheeks, Kate walks up to it, dragging her feet a little and looking at the man in a suit and sunglasses standing next to it stoically.

    "Are you here to take us home?"

    The CIA agent, a short, blonde man with an almost comically strong jaw nods, opening the door.

    "Yes, Miss Bishop."

    Kate slides in, noting how he does not get in when she does, likely told to wait for Allie too. She uses the next few seconds to try to get her thoughts in order, still not really comprehending the last 20 minutes since Allie showed up.

    From facing certain prison time to being free but under Valentina's thumb is hell of a ride in 20 minutes.

    Also, from the sounds of it, Valentina may have gotten her out this time, but if she doesn't want to risk getting even more indebted to her, she has to get out from the FBI's sights for good, somehow. Not to mention, she has to warn Clint. If Valentina decides they are not worth keeping around, her having that knowledge of him is extremely dangerous. What did Yelena offer her to even get her in the room?

    Allie joins her in the car about 5 minutes later, a young cop carrying a box on her heels. She smiles sweetly at him, as he hands the box over to the CIA agent, and while through the bulletproof windows, Kate can't hear a word from them, she sees Allie wave him off before the agent opens the door and she gets in too.

    The box is slid in first, between the two of them, containing everything seized from Kate during her arrest: her ruined suit, her weapons, and even her backpack with her tablet and tools that she didn't leave behind.

    "Is everything here?"

    At Allie's question, Kate quickly thinks it through, lifting the bag on top to see the items below, before she nods, meeting her eyes.

    "I think so."

    Through the open door, Allie talks to the agent, before she shuts it.

    "We are ready to go, thank you."

    They are both silent as the agent gets in, and Kate wonders if the car might be bugged. If Valentina went through the trouble of getting her place bugged, she can't be certain that it isn't, not to mention the agent only a few feet ahead. With a deep inhale, she reserves herself to stick to topics they wouldn't mind discussing right in front of Valentina herself. The agent starts up the car and Kate exhales slowly, a certain tension leaving her body as they roll out of the parking lot.

    She is free.

    She can barely believe it.

    The time on the dashboard reads 9:28 am, and Kate can't believe everything happened so fast. She feels her exhaustion settle in her bones with every few feet they roll forward and out of the lot, and while the anxiety about Valentina thrums in her veins, she feels almost too tired to properly grasp it at this moment.

    Suddenly, a thought occurs to her and she turns to Allie, looking at her with a hint of suspicion but trying not to show it.

    "Do you work for Valentina?"

    Looking up from her phone, Allie looks at her like she is trying to decide if Kate is joking, a smile hidden in the corner of her mouth before she chuckles.

    "No? Tommy called me at like 4 am, to say you were in trouble and to come help. I work for GLK and H."

    Nodding like she knows what that is, Kate blinks, before she rubs her forehead in confusion, and turns to Allie again.

    "So...how did Valentina get into the picture?"

    Hesitation passes over Allie's face and she glances at the driver before she looks at Kate again.

    "I told Tommy that as much as I appreciate his confidence, I'm a first-year associate. And that from what he told me happened, you needed someone with more experience... Possibly a team of them even."

    Pausing, Allie seems to weigh her words, looking meaningfully at the driver this time, seemingly to indicate to Kate that they will be careful with what they discuss, but she continues a moment later.

    "He called me back about ten minutes later to say someone will be there to pick me up and that I'll be briefed on the way, but to just go."

    Internally, Kate cringes at Tommy and now Allie being involved in this too, but she pushes the feeling aside for now, hoping that this will be the extent of their involvement. "-I was picked up, driven upstate, and taken to a private airfield fifteen minutes from here, where I met her. On the way to the station, she told me that she arranged with the FBI to trade you for some things they would be more interested in than a rich kid playing dress up,-" Before Kate can get offended, Allie cracks a smile, meeting her eyes.

    -her words not mine. And that the CEO of Iron Mountain was convinced that it was in their best interest to cooperate and say it was a penetration testing exercise gone wild, approved by both the CIA and the company to test their defenses because otherwise, their stock price would freefall. So, really, all I had to do was walk in with her and act as your attorney, everything else was taken care of."

    Rubbing at her eyes, Kate attempts to gauge how much trouble Valentina went through to get her out, as a way of figuring out how deep in shit she is.

    "How did she convince the CEO of that? And what did she give to the FBI?" Rolling her lips together, Allie shakes her head with a small shrug of her shoulders. "I know better than to ask."

    With two slow blinks, Kate nods. A moment later, her face scrunches up after thinking about it, and she looks apologetically at Allie.

    "Fuck...Yeah, I am sorry that you got pulled into this."

    This time, Allie's smile is wide and her eyes are full of warmth.

    "I was happy to help."

    The smile widens into a small grin, and she lifts an eyebrow as she looks at Kate sideways. "Just...Maybe next time, do it during business hours?-"

    Kate can't help but smile back, the expression turning into a lopsided grin too as Allie continues.

    "-My rates go pretty high for 4 am emergencies."

    Leaning back against the SUV's leather seat and relaxing a little more, Kate huffs a chuckle, raising her chin slightly.

    "Well, as a professional 'rich kid playing dress up', let's hope I can afford it." Allie blinks slowly, her amusement palpable in her tone too.

    "Maybe I'll throw in some pro-bono hours."

    Kate snorts, looking out the window as a sign for the I-87 flies by them, apparently 2 miles away.

    "Seriously though, Kate.-"

    Turning back to Allie, Kate sees that her smile has dropped, and her tone is almost worried. "I don't know what you are caught up in exactly, but from where I'm standing, it's pretty serious, if the FBI and the CIA are fighting over you. You need to talk to someone. Someone actually qualified."

    As Kate opens her mouth to answer, she glances at the driver and hesitates before shaking her head.

    "Yeah, let's... Let's talk about this when we get back to New York."

    Glancing out the window, Allie seems to think, before she looks back at Kate. "I'll put you in contact with my boss. She will know your options at least." After a moment of hesitation, Kate accepts the offer, thinking it might be a good idea for her to talk to someone, but a bit worried about the topic being discussed in front of the agent. "Thanks, that's... That's probably a good idea."

    Reaching into her bag, Allie pulls out a business card and hands it over to Kate. It looks very professional and neat, with her name and phone number printed on it in a modern but stylish font on one side, and the logo of the firm she is working for on the other, forming the letters GLK&H - New York.

    Turning it back around to look at her name once more, Kate smiles, before she slips it into the pocket of her sweats with a thankful nod to Allie. For a few seconds, she fleetingly wonders if her life turned out to be different, she would have a fancy lettered business card too, with the Bishop Security logo on it but quickly pushes the thought aside. Of all the things to think about, that is probably the least timely.

    After that, the two of them travel in silence for a few minutes, the car getting onto the highway not much later.

    Kate really needs some sleep.

    When she gets home, she will have to explain everything to Yelena and Sonya, and then call Clint and repeat. Maybe even before. Can it wait until then? Does he already know what happened? God, Yelena and him will both give her hell for this... But Clint will probably understand, once she explains why she stayed behind. He will definitely not be happy about them not leaving when they found out the evidence was sealed though. If they left then, none of this would have happened.

    But if they left then, they wouldn't have the pathway... And whatever else Yelena found. Hopefully, she kept both while Sonya and she made their escape. So, as long as they find a way to slip out from under Valentina's thumb, get Kate a good legal defense and- "Do you remember the field trip we went on in junior year? To State Capitol?" It takes a second for Kate's brain to switch over, turning back to Allie after looking out the window for the last few minutes, deep in thought.

    "Um...With Mrs. Stanley?"

    With an amused hum, Allie nods and Kate is struck by the realization that this really is the same shy girl she used to know back in high school. How far they have all come since then... "Yes. On the way there, on the bus, you said you were going to be an Avenger." Huffing out a tired chuckle, Kate smiles, remembering the trip. She snorts then, recalling another detail.

    "Yeah. And Emily said that the next time Thanos comes, I should make sure that his dad's secretary is snapped away too because she is not sharing her inheritance with another bastard half-sibling."

    Rolling her eyes, Allie shakes her head, her distaste clear on her face. Kate scoffs before she adds.

    "-I saw her last weekend... Still a huge bitch."

    Allie snorts, her eyes holding amusement.

    "Good to know that some things never change."

    They exchange a few words after, mindful not to touch on anything sensitive with the agent around, but sometime in the next half an hour, Kate passes out, exhausted from the events of the last day. Her sleep is deep and peaceful, despite the sunlight outside and the sit-up position, her mind too tired to even conjure up any dreams. She wakes up to Allie shaking her shoulder with a smile sometime later and blinks at their surroundings, slightly disoriented.

    "Wake up. We'll be at your place in a few minutes."

    Rubbing her eyes, Kate notes that they are already in the city, close to Central Park. "How do you know where I live?"

    Allie's eyes drop to her chin and Kate is somewhat horrified to realize she probably drooled in her sleep, quickly wiping at her mouth and feeling a bit sheepish at Allie's smile and amused eyes.

    "I texted Tommy to ask."

    Stifling a yawn, Kate smiles at Allie, feeling both a little awkward at having slept so deeply and thankful to have had her company, as they slowly turn onto Central Park West. The weather is still beautiful and it's lunchtime, a lot of people running around with paper bags full of take-out lunches. Kate is suddenly reminded of not having eaten anything since the protein bar Yelena gave her on the cliff before the mission, and her stomach grumbles, even as she smiles internally at the memory.

    The wrapper is still in her backpack, and she thinks of the moment fondly, rolling her eyes at herself for being excited to see Yelena in a few minutes, even though she is most likely furious with Kate... Her internal eye-roll then turns into cringing and manifests itself as an actual deep sigh as she realizes that seeing Yelena means having to explain what happened. And then, the impending argument, for the lack of a better word, which she is definitely not looking forward to.

    The car stops in front of Kate's building a few moments later and she opens her door, bidding her farewell to the agent.

    "Thanks for the lift!"

    The agent does not answer, or if he does, Kate does not hear it, pulling the box full of her clothes and things out of the car, and stepping back to give space to Allie to follow after her. She gets out after Kate on the same side, the two of them alone for good when the black SUV drives off a few seconds later.

    Kate balances the box in her hands, feeling a bit cold again despite the beautiful sunshine. She watches Allie as she looks up at her building, her eyebrows drawn together. "Is this your building?"

    Unsure why that is so surprising, Kate shifts her weight from one leg to the other. "Yeah?"

    Turning to look at her, Allie lifts an eyebrow.

    "You live in the same building as Sonya?"

    Chuckling, Kate nods, trying to ignore the cold gust of wind that cools the back of her neck and sends a chill down her spine.

    "Yeah, it's a pretty crazy coincidence. I met her through Yelena, and we were at her place one time when Tommy walked in. It took me a few seconds to realize we know each other." Lifting her chin, Allie looks at Kate before she shakes her head.

    "I don't know Yelena. Or how you all know each other."

    Rolling her lips together, Kate kind of smiles, unsure how much Allie knows about Sonya... Then again, if she got involved in this, she must know at least something. Either way, it's not Kate's place to tell her, so she shifts her weight again, smiling.

    "Oh, yeah, she is great. Yelena, I mean. You'd love her. But obviously, Sonya too." At that, Allie's smile widens and she looks affectionate. She leans slightly closer as if she is telling a secret.

    "She is. Tommy is totally head over heels."

    Kate feels her smile widen into a grin and she glances around the sidewalk out of habit, checking that it's Sonya's friend Herman at the door.

    "I know. It's pretty cute."

    Just as she is looking at the doorway to the building, it opens and Kate's heart leaps when she sees Yelena and then Sonya step out of the building, their eyes immediately finding Allie and her too. They are both out of their tactical clothes, obviously, with Yelena in jeans, a bright red t-shirt, and an oversized white jacket, while Sonya wears a black turtleneck with a soft, tan coat.

    "Kate!"

    As they walk up, Kate puts down her box of things and receives a strong hug from Yelena first, her heart missing a beat as soon as she is in her arms. Yelena throws her own around Kate's back, the two of them embracing for a few seconds. Kate even closes her eyes in relief, almost all her anxiety slipping away for a few moments, as she enjoys the warmth of Yelena's body.

    She is home. She is free, and she is home. For real.

    They let go of each other a few moments later, and Kate receives a slightly shorter hug from Sonya too.

    "How did you know I was here?"

    Sonya answers her, while Kate continues to drink in Yelena's presence, and simultaneously tries to gauge how much trouble she is in.

    "Allie texted me."

    As she steps out of the hug, Kate nods with a smile, her eyes returning to Allie. "Ah, okay."

    Allie and Sonya share a quick hug too and as Sonya steps back, she gestures at Yelena, introducing her.

    "This is my friend Yelena. Yelena, this is Tommy's little sister, Allie." At Allie's friendly smile and outreached hand, Yelena returns it and she shakes the offered hand without hesitation.

    "Nice to meet you."

    She does not hide her accent and Kate smiles to herself, enjoying the sound of it. She really wouldn't have thought this morning, that she would be back here, safe and free, only a couple of hours later. After their greeting, Allie steps back to the edge of their impromptu little circle, pulling her phone out of her coat's pocket, her eyebrows drawing together. "I better get going. My boss is blowing up my phone."

    As their eyes meet, Kate smiles at her and points at herself, even as a chilly gust of wind moves a few strands of her hair at the back of her head again, making her pull up her shoulders a little to stave off the cold.

    "You can tell her you were with a new, very rich client. That should buy you some leeway." Allie smiles too, as she bites down on her lower lip and exhales.

    "Let's hope so. She is great, but she is a hardass."

    Kate chuckles empathically, even though she never had a hardass boss, or any type of boss for that matter, unless you count Greg. She then leans down to pick up her things, answering Allie as she straightens up.

    "Anyway, let me buy you a cup of coffee sometime. As a thanks for busting my ass from jail..-"

    Her smile widens into a grin as she adds a heartbeat later, remembering Allie's comment about the 4 am emergency call.

    "-Apart from paying your ridiculously expensive retainer, of course."

    Allie chuckles, her smile big and pretty as she looks back at Kate.

    "Sure. You have my number."

    Kate nods with a smile, and Allie's attention slips to the Widows.

    "See you, Sonya. It was nice to meet you, Yelena."

    Her smile is sincere and Kate glances over to Yelena and Sonya just as the two exchange a look. A moment later, Sonya turns back to Allie with a smile of her own and asks her. "Actually, can you swing by my place after work today? It'd be great to..." Pausing, she gestures at Kate and she raises an eyebrow in turn, unsure what Sonya means, but it gets cleared up a moment later as the sentence is continued.

    "-Go over what happened."

    Glancing at Kate, Allie's eyebrows lift ever so slightly as she hesitates for a heartbeat. Or maybe she is just surprised, because a moment later, she nods, her smile back on her face. "Sure. Yeah, I can... I usually finish around six thirty. I'll call you?" As Sonya nods, she smiles too, looking genuinely affectionate towards Allie. "Perfect."

    Allie waves them goodbye, and walks up to the side of the road, signaling for a taxi. One slows down and stops for her almost immediately after and she turns back to throw them one last wave and smile, that Sonya returns, while Kate does a mini version of the wave while her hands are full of the box.

    "Come on."

    After Yelena's words, they walk across the sidewalk and into the building silently, but she turns to look at Kate as the three of them wait for the elevator.

    "Are you okay? What happened to your head?"

    Jostling a box a little to shift its weight, Kate glances at the numbers receding above the elevator doors before she looks at Yelena again.

    "I'm good. I hit it against the wall. But just a little, nothing too serious." In the semi-public setting they are at, she doesn't mention the explosion, but Yelena purses her lips in displeasure nonetheless. Sonya looks at the bruise before her eyes drop to the rest of Kate, worry showing up on her face in the form of a tiny crease between her eyebrows. "Are you hurt anywhere else?"

    Kate shrugs and grins, hoping they can gloss over the topic. It's pretty likely that it will be revealed sooner rather than later but still holds out a shred of hope that she can avoid Yelena and Sonya finding out she got hit by grenade shrapnel when she saved Dumb Danny's life. "Just a few bruises here and there."

    In turn, she looks both Widows over, searching them for any visible signs of injuries and quickly asking.

    "-How about you? Are you guys okay?"

    Sonya turns to her with a smile, but with the way her eyes narrow just slightly, Kate gets the sense that Yelena is not the only one who might be a bit angry with her for her so-called 'little stunt'.

    "Neither of us is dumb enough to get caught or hurt on a mission like this." Kate sighs, and she looks into Sonya's eyes when she speaks.

    "Thank you, for getting me out.-"

    Her eyes sliding over to Yelena, Kate finds her looking, and she holds her gaze too as she continues.

    "-Both of you. I know... I know it wasn't easy and I put you in a bad position." Pursing her lips, Kate sees anger flash in Yelena's eyes but she shakes her head a moment later and turns away.

    "We will talk about it upstairs."

    With a statement like this, Kate can do nothing else but nod and swallow nervously when the elevator arrives a few seconds later. The rest of their journey upstairs is quiet, building up Kate's nerves about their conversation, only interrupted by her stomach churning in hunger. When they arrive on her level, Yelena leads them to Kate's door and opens it with her key before walking inside. Kate walks in next, still carrying the box with Sonya stepping inside last and closing the door behind them.

    The living room is exactly as Kate left it yesterday, and almost exactly like she left it a few days ago after they cleaned up following the FBI search and the bug sweep. With everything that happened since, even the departure yesterday afternoon feels like it happened days ago, not to mention the the bug sweep, the gala, and her sleeping with Yelena. Not the time, Kate. "I have your phone and your keys. The rest of your things are in there." Yelena points across the room, at Kate's pack that rests by the couch and she looks back at Yelena gratefully, as she deposits her box of things onto the floor. Straightening up, Kate looks around, quickly pulling Allie's card from her pocket and putting it onto the console by the door before she accidentally throws it away with the sweats later on. "Thanks."

    Her phone and keys are placed on the table by the door too, and then Yelena shrugs off her jacket, walks across the room, and takes a seat on the couch, crossing her legs expectantly. Kate glances from her to Sonya, who walks by her without a word too, after taking off her coat, and she sighs, her stomach grumbling again.

    She picks up her phone from the table, checking her notifications but gives up on it quickly, after seeing the myriad of notifications on it, including several missed calls from Clint. Her chest pangs with worry once again, as she remembers Valentina's words, but she puts the phone down for now, owing an explanation to Yelena and Sonya first and foremost. "Before we begin. Can I order some food first? I'm starving."

    Sonya, who already took a seat by Yelena's side rises, motioning for both of them to follow her as she walks up in the direction of Kate's kitchen.

    "Come on, I will make you some waffles."

    The word waffles makes Kate's stomach grumble once again and her mouth waters at the thought of them too.

    "Oh my god, yes."

    She hurries after Sonya, but she does not miss the eye-roll Yelena does at her enthusiasm, nor the small smile she doesn't try to hide even when she notices Kate looking. Okay, so she is not in that much trouble, right? Yelena follows her to the kitchen and takes a seat across from her at the island after Kate sits down.

    "Now, speak. What happened?"

    "Yeah, um, just... Let me explain, okay?"

    Her shoulders rising with a sigh, Yelena purses her lips while Sonya deadpans as she rummages around Kate's cupboards for something "Sounds promising already."

    Biting down on her lip, Kate runs a hand through her hair, trying to gather her thoughts. For a moment, she considers how she could frame what she has done in a way that avoids both Widows getting mad at her, but in the end, she throws that thought process aside. No. Even with all the added complications, she does not regret the choice she made. Killing innocent people, or even letting them die, is where she draws the line and it doesn't matter if Yelena thinks it's stupid. Or Sonya...

    With another deep breath, she braces herself and meets Yelena's eyes once more. "After the explosion, I was going to run, like I told you. But then the guard... The one that brought the grenade, I found him and he was hurt badly. He...He was bleeding a lot. One of the shrapnels hit him in the leg and probably got an artery or something, I don't know. There was a lot of blood."

    If there was a hint of a smile on Yelena's face, it's surely gone by the time Kate is done speaking. She looks at Kate seriously, her green eyes dark and hard to read. "You stayed behind to help him."

    Yelena's words are not phrased like a question, but Kate nods and answers like they are. "I did, yeah. I couldn't just leave him there to die."

    Closing her eyes, Yelena turns her face slightly towards the ceiling, maybe counting in her head. Kate glances at Sonya, but she is turned away, using a fork to whisk some eggs slightly more aggressively than they strictly need to be, not turning back to look at her. When the silence stretches on for a few more seconds, Kate gives in to the pressure she feels to explain herself, causing Yelena to open her eyes to look at her, but not move otherwise. "They are just regular people, Yelena. Just regular, normal people, doing their jobs, not involved in anything bad. It's..."

    Frustrated with herself for not being able to put it into words well, Kate shakes her head and pauses. After a moment, she sighs, meeting Yelena's gaze and holding it to drive her meaning across.

    "It wasn't right to let him die, just because he was in the wrong place at the wrong time. That is where I draw the line."

    Yelena kisses her teeth, either in annoyance or frustration but her voice is surprisingly even, and gentle a moment later when she speaks.

    "I am not faulting you for saving someone’s life, Kate, or even for being a self-sacrificing idiot. I may not always agree with it, but I do not expect you to be someone you are not." When she pauses, it takes all of Kate's willpower to not speak, or hurry her along, but she gives Yelena the opportunity to say her piece. Rolling her lips together, Yelena looks away, but she only needs a second to gather her thoughts before she turns back to her and begins to speak again, her eyes boring into Kate's.

    "But you abandoned us.-"

    When Kate opens her mouth to object, Yelena leans forward, her hard eyes telling Kate to shut up without her mouth needing to, and she obeys.

    "You made that decision alone. You did not give us a heads up, forced our hand to just go on without you, and then you left us to deal with the fallout."

    Kate nods, apologetic, but she does her best to communicate to Yelena, that that was not her intention and that she didn't have much of a choice, as soon as she decided to stay back for Dumb Danny.

    "I am sorry for that, I really am but... There was nothing else I could have done. There wasn't time-"

    Yelena's eyes flash, and she leans even further forward, but her voice remains even, if a little sharp as she cuts Kate off.

    "You could have told me?! Other than just telling me to get you a lawyer and just... drop off? We could have helped or made the call together, but instead, you made your choice alone." Rubbing at her forehead, Kate feels a bit of frustration bubble up in her chest at not being understood. If she could just finish telling what happened...

    "I'm sorry for forcing your hand, I really am, but that's exactly what I'm saying! You couldn't have helped anyway. You were stuck on the other side of the rubble, and the guards arrived only a few minutes later-"

    Shaking her head, Yelena's eyebrows draw together and she practically waves Kate's words off as she looks away, sending a sharp twinge of annoyance down her spine that she does her best to smother, not wanting this to turn into a full-blown argument.

    "We will never know that, because you did not ask."

    The muscles on Yelena's jaw jump as she grinds her teeth, and before Kate can interject, she turns to her and speaks again. As Yelena talks, her tone rises a bit with her agitation, and while there is a generous amount of frustration in her voice, Kate hears the worry underneath it, dissolving her annoyance entirely almost as soon as it appears.

    "And for the record, you took this risk without thinking it through, again. The guards could have shot you on sight. Fisk could have had someone on the force and got you killed while you were in police custody. And-“ Trying to steer the conversation away from what-ifs that will only make both of them, especially Yelena, more upset, Kate cuts her off gently, keeping her voice strong but apologetic.

    “You are right. I did not think it through at that moment. But even if I did, I would have made the same call. It was the right thing to do.”

    Yelena huffs, her hold on her temper slipping a bit more and her voice rising in volume as she pins Kate to her chair with a look, her green eyes wild.

    “That is not the point! You should have told us what was happening. You made us leave you there without involving me in the decision whatsoever, not knowing if you were dead or alive. You just threw your life away, without letting me know or letting me help. It is not fair.”

    Feeling like the conversation was getting a bit out of hand, Kate shakes her head, trying to de-escalate.

    “Okay, threw my life away is a bit too dramatic. I stayed behind to help-“ Yelena's tone is sharp as a knife, shutting down what Kate was about to say. Her eyes are wild but vulnerable, and for a few seconds, Kate feels like she can't breathe with the weight of them as Yelena leans onto the counter in front of her, keeping her gaze captive. “You could have been killed, Kate. You sacrificed yourself for some...stranger, without thinking and without taking into account how it would affect us.”

    At that, Kate's brow furrows in confusion. She can't say what her choice would have been if Yelena and Sonya were in actual danger too, but she knew they would get out. They always do. But if she thought they weren't, it would have definitely influenced the decision and most likely, she would have made a different call.

    "No. No, that's not true. If I thought there was a chance you guys were not getting out, I'd-" With an impatient huff, Yelena cuts her off, leaning back and looking away. "That is not what I mean."

    Kate's confusion is not helped by the words at all, and she can't even look at Sonya for help with untangling it, because she is chopping strawberries with sharp, precise motions and not looking at them. Even she looks slightly upset, and when Kate turns back to Yelena, the corners of her mouth are pulled downwards in an almost half circle. A display of emotion that pulls at her heart, and makes her want to understand, instead of defend herself. Swallowing her rebuttal, she shakes her head, trying to get clarity.

    "I don't understand. What do you mean then?"

    Wetting her lips, Yelena takes a deep breath and turns to look at her once more, her eyes heavy.

    "Of course you don't."

    Yelena's frustration is clear as she huffs, her gaze never leaving Kate's, and while her voice is no longer raised, it's no less heavy as she continues.

    "You may not value your life much, but other people do."

    Exhaling, Kate does her best to understand what Yelena means by that. Does she mean, they care about Kate? That they would be sad if she died? She hopes they would, of course, but that doesn't mean Kate can compromise her morals.

    Leaning forward, Kate softens her voice, hoping she can make Yelena understand. "I am sorry that I worried you. I really, really am. And I do value my life, I wasn't trying to...throw my life away, or... anything like that. But leaving him to die was not a choice I could make."

    Yelena looks away and out Kate's window, shaking her head. Rolling her hips together, she shakes her head to herself, before turning back to Kate.

    "There is no point to this conversation. Tell me what happened next."

    Wetting her lips, Kate feels that she should push a bit more, not sure it's a good idea to leave the topic as it is. She really doesn't want Yelena to return to being distant with her. "I wasn't trying to sacrifice my life, I promise. I knew that I would be captured, and I thought... Well, I hoped that you guys would be able to get me out. But even if you didn't, even if I went to prison, I couldn't just let an innocent man die, so I can escape and stay free." Closing her eyes, Yelena shakes her head once more. She lowers her face, part of her hair falling forward, and obscuring it, as she looks down at the counter. Kate sees her shoulders rise with a deep sigh, and her voice doesn't carry an edge anymore when she speaks. It sounds almost sad.

    "You would not have lost your freedom, Kate. If Allie and Valentina did not get you out, Fisk would have gotten to you within hours. He would have had you murdered, like countless others before, and your mother, Clint, and everyone who cares about you, would have been left behind, with no consolation other than that you gave your life to save a stranger, who did not deserve it."

    She lifts her eyes then, and Kate is too stunned by their intensity to say anything. Yelena rolls her lips together, nods to herself, and swallows once more, but she holds Kate's eyes when she continues speaking.

    "But as I said, I am not faulting you for it. It is who you are, and nothing any of us says will change that. But the least you could do is have the decency to tell us before you decide to sacrifice yourself because maybe, you do not have to. Maybe we can come up with something else, together."

    When it becomes clear that Yelena is done speaking, Kate clears her throat, almost stunned into silence. She lowers her chin, feeling thoroughly chastised and humbled, but she holds Yelena's eyes to convey the seriousness of her apology because it's clear that she has upset Yelena more than she thought.

    "I'm sorry."

    Yelena seems almost angry again, her eyes narrowing slightly, and she flicks a strand of hair out of her face impatiently.

    "I do not need you to be sorry. I need you to promise me you will never do this again while we work together. We cannot have your back if you potentially pull this again while we are on a mission. That is where I draw the line."

    Swallowing, Kate hesitates, unsure what to say. She can't promise she will not make the same choice again, because she would and maybe she will have to again. But it seems that maybe that is not what Yelena is asking. So Kate nods, averting her eyes only for a moment. "I... I promise that I will communicate better. I will not make a choice like this without talking to you guys. If I can help it."

    Pursing her lips, Yelena considers her words before sighing once more. She looks away too, around the room, before she she shakes her head. She does not address Kate's words after that, turning back to her once again with her face serious, but maybe not as emotional as before.

    "Okay, so after you stayed behind, what happened?"

    Clearing her throat, Kate tries to shake off the seriousness of the last few minutes. Yelena's eyes feel like a physical weight on her, and there is a certain amount of guilt stirring in her stomach, even though she can't say she would choose differently if she were to go back 12 hours.

    "Um, yeah. So, the guards came, took over putting pressure on Danny's leg, and took me into custody. They took my weapons, cuffed me, and took me to a room to wait until they processed the scene and the police arrived. I was in there for like two, maybe two and a half hours."

    At Kate calling Danny by his name, Yelena's eye twitches, but she does not interrupt, while Sonya begins to pour the batter into the waffle maker Kate didn't know she had, behind her back. While Kate continues to explain, a mouth-watering smell begins to fill the kitchen, making her stomach rumble eagerly.

    "I was then transferred to police custody sometime around...six? They drove me to the Elizabethtown Police Station and I went through intake. Prints, mugshots, everything. They also took my clothes but Allie got everything back after, which is a win, I guess." Running a hand through her hair, Kate recalls the rest of her morning, stunned once more that only a few hours later, she is about to have waffles with Yelena and Sonya, instead of rotting in the interview room or jail.

    "They tried to question me, the detectives, I mean, but I told them I won't talk without a lawyer, and that I had to make a call to get the lawyer in the first place. That's when I called you."

    She meets Yelena's eyes once more and she nods but does not react in any other way, as Kate continues.

    "I didn't know your number off the top of my head, or Clint's, or anyone's really, so I called myself, and that's when Agent Reyes and Angent McLagan arrived."

    This is the first time Yelena turns slightly back to exchange a look with Sonya, before meeting Kate's eyes again.

    "They got there pretty quick."

    Scratching at her forehead, Kate nods, glancing at Sonya again, who is in the process of removing the first waffle from between the irons, before moving on to preparing the next one. "Yeah. Yeah, you are right. It's a bit weird. Between getting fingerprinted, and processed, and them arriving, there was only like... Thirty minutes? Forty max. So they must have been around already because there is no way they made it up from New York that quick." Her eyebrows furrowing in thought, Yelena nods, before tilting her head to the side. "It is possible that they were notified about the evidence regarding your mother being involved in the break-in, they went to Iron Mountain to investigate that, only to find out you were in custody."

    Her eyes unconsciously bouncing between Yelena and the waffle behind her, being prepared on the counter, Kate tilts her head from side to side, considering the possibility. "Yeah, I guess. They definitely...Okay, so they took me back into the interview room, and I told them I am not talking without a lawyer either, but they didn't leave. I think they wanted to make sure that I knew they really got me, and wanted me to make a deal. Most likely to give you guys up because Agent McLagan gave me the whole rundown of all the stuff they have on me."

    Brow furrowing even further, Yelena leans forward, her forearms resting on the counter in front of her.

    "What do they have on you?"

    Exhaling with a puff, Kate shakes her head, her eyes moving around the room as she tries to recall all the things Agent McLagan told her.

    "A lot. Like, they connected me to almost everything in the last few weeks, from the first break-in to the storage unit, through the ship, Limitless, both of the times we've been there, and obviously, now Iron Mountain. I think... even without getting caught, I am not in a great spot. I'll need... Okay, actually, let me finish, and then we can get back to this." Biting down on her lip, Yelena nods, and Kate continues, just as Sonya pours a third portion of the batter into the waffle maker. She then moves over to Kate's fridge, pulling out a can of whipped cream and a jar of maple syrup, before picking up the plate full of sliced strawberries and bringing it all over to the kitchen island.

    "So, Agent McLagan told me what they know, I guess to intimidate me with how strong the case they are building against me is, and when I did not budge, Reyes took over. He..." For a moment, Kate's mind flashes back to the images of the people he has shown, that she has killed, or that have died because of her, and suddenly, her stomach churns in a way entirely different than hunger. Averting her eyes, and watching a spot on the counter, Kate clears her throat before continuing.

    "He showed me a bunch of pictures. Of, uh... Of people that I've killed during our missions or... Who died on the ship and in some of the other incidents and he told me that I wasn't a hero. That I, uh... I was just a rich asshole who thinks she can decide who lives and dies, and that they will get me for all of it."

    Swallowing, Kate glances up and sees that Yelena's face has softened a little. Quickly, she continues, trying to avoid them saying anything about it, doubting it would make her feel better at this moment, and feeling an uncomfortable twinge in her chest, telling her she does not deserve the sympathy.

    "Then Allie showed up. She uh,-"

    Kate chuckles at the memory of her entering the room, and her and Valentina basically snatching her from right under the agents' nose, but at least half of the laugh is an attempt to dissolve the cold, tight feeling in her chest.

    "She swooped in, and told them that I was a CIA asset, and we weren't actually there to steal anything, but as a part of a penetration testing exercise."

    Across from her, Yelena lifts her chin, the ghost of a smile sliding onto her face for the first time since Kate started talking.

    "The CIA asset thing was my idea. Well...You gave me the idea, so technically, it is Barton's." At Kate's quizzical look, Yelena flicks a strand of hair out of her face, lifts her chin, and explains.

    "You said he was going to get you listed as a part of an agency to avoid this kind of thing. And well, the only one I could make happen in such a short time was CIA, with Valentina." Kate begins to smile as she nods, but it's immediately overtaken by worry, and she braces herself for the answer to her question as she is asking it.

    "What did you have to do for it?"

    Yelena exhales, pulling her lips to the side. She doesn't seem pleased, but also not terribly worried, so maybe Kate's worries are unfounded.

    "I called her. I asked her if she got my message, and she said yes. I told her that we are back in business if she gets you out. I told her we know she is CIA and to get you listed as CIA and get the paperwork to Allie. She said she would do it, but only if we hand over the formula to her, once we get it."

    Feeling the weight of all the different kinds of trouble she is in, Kate nods, only feeling a small spark of joy as Sonya brings over the stack of waffles, and sets it on the table, even if her mouth waters at it.

    "Yeah, she told me the same thing. Just...a bit more assertively."

    Tilting her head to the side, Yelena asks her to clarify without words as she gets up, and Kate explains.

    "She told me I'm working for her now. And that I'll need to report on the progress every week, and then hand over the formula once we get it."

    Taking three plates from Sonya's hands, Yelena shakes her head with a humorless chuckle. "That is ridiculous. Do not worry about that, I will talk to her."

    Worrying her lower lip between her teeth, Kate shakes her head, while Yelena sets a plate in front of her, and Sonya brings over utensils.

    "You can't. She also said that if I try to get out from under it, she will tell Rojas that Clint killed his father and lead him to Clint's ranch."

    Yelena's eyes narrow and her mouth thins as she grinds her teeth together. For a few seconds, she mulls it over, before cursing to herself.

    "Suka."

    Rubbing her forehead, Kate nods, her eyes shifting from Yelena to Sonya and back. She might not know the exact meaning of the word, but she gets the gist.

    "Yeah."

    Shaking her head once more, Yelena re-takes her seat, this time Sonya taking the one to her left too.

    "Okay. You will tell this to Barton. He needs to know. But we'll figure out a way out of this." With a long exhale, Kate nods, and Sonya gestures at the stack of waffles in the middle. "Dig in. We already ate."

    With a somewhat awkward, apologetic smile, Kate holds Sonya's eyes as she reaches for the stack.

    "Thank you."

    After making her sweat for a few seconds longer, Sonya finally rolls her eyes, reaching for the plate with a small, but genuine smile once Kate has transferred four waffles onto her plate.

    "You are welcome."

    She pauses, but she grows serious once more, her eyes narrowing as she holds Kate's. "Seriously though. If you ever pull something stupid like this, I am shooting you myself." With a somewhat nervous chuckle, Kate feels at least a little bit of the weight get lifted off of her chest, and she glances over to Yelena to see her smile too, even if just a little. She shakes her head at Kate, when she notices her looking, taking the plate from Sonya to get one waffle too.

    "Do not look at me. I will help her get rid of your body."

    Pulling her lips to the side, Kate nods, deciding it's probably best if she focuses on her waffles.

    "Noted."

    Cutting off a generous slice from two plain waffles stacked on top of each other, Kate stuffs it into her mouth and begins to chew, while she reaches for the strawberries, pulling an unmodest amount onto her plate as well. She follows it up with whipped cream and a hearty splash of maple syrup, only looking up when she hears an amused huff.

    With her mouth still full, she meets Yelena's eyes who looks like she can't decide if she is amused or disgusted at the display of Kate's appetite. Her gaze shifts over to Sonya, whose smile turned into a grin, snickering when she meets Kate's somewhat confused eyes. Swallowing, Kate tilts her head to the side, while also picking up a quarter of a strawberry with her fork, and popping it into her mouth.

    "What?"

    Sonya shakes her head, her laugh quieting down.

    "Nothing. Glad you are not dead."

    Despite knowing it's playing with fire, with how things are not exactly settled about the whole sacrificing herself thing, Kate grins after she swallows, her eyes jumping to Yelena and back in a fraction of a second.

    "Me too."

    When nobody gets mad at her, Kate cuts off another big slice, this time dripping with whipped cream and syrup too, and asks the Widows before she stuffs it into her mouth. "So how did you guys get out?"

    The Widows exchange a glance while Kate chews before Yelena answers.

    "You haven't finished your story yet."

    Nodding, Kate quickly chews, waving with her fork.

    "There is not much left to say. Allie and Valentina swooped in, told the agents that I was CIA, and that there was no break-in to begin with, so they basically had to release me. Valentina also got the CEO of Iron Mountain to sign off on it somehow. Reyes told me it wasn't over yet, but there was nothing he could do, at least for now. They had to let me go." Maneuvering another strawberry onto her fork, Kate deposits it onto the top of her next waffle bite but pauses before she actually lifts it to her mouth.

    "So, yeah, after that Valentina took me outside, while Allie got my things, and laid the whole 'you work for me now' bit on me, and then she left. Then Allie and I were driven back by a CIA agent. That's it basically."

    Her food abandoned for now, Yelena leans back, her tongue sneaking out to catch a drop of syrup maybe, in the corner of her mouth. With her story mostly done, except for the details of the FBI's case, Kate lifts the waffle-strawberry combo bite to her mouth, while the Widows process her words.

    The weight of her earlier conversation with Yelena still hangs in the air, but for now, the air in the room doesn't feel like it's filled with gunpowder, ready to blow. With the delicious food in her mouth, Kate takes a deep breath, then exhales, taking a moment to just enjoy being back after she thought she wouldn't be for a while. She even closes her eyes for a long moment, only opening them when she swallows her bite.

    "So, how did you guys get out?"

    The Widows exchange a glance and Yelena leans back once more, blinking twice in quick succession, before she begins to speak.

    "When I reached ground level with the elevator, I had some unwelcome greetings. It took me a few minutes to get to one of the trucks, and a few more to hotwire it, because they kept shooting at me."

    She delivers the last part like a mere nuisance, which Kate can't help but smile at, despite the hypocrisy of Yelena freaking out at her putting herself in danger and then talking about getting shot at like a mere annoyance. Flicking her hair away from her face, Yelena uses her fork, still in her hand, to gesture at Kate, her face twisting in displeasure. "That is where I was when you said you were not coming, so Sonya and I needed to figure out if I should go back for you or not."
