    Her smile dropping, Kate's eyebrows furrow, her chest panging with worry for a moment at the hypothetical scenario.

    "But I told you to go and get me a lawyer."

    For a mere second, Yelena's eyes flash with annoyance once again, but it's gone in a moment, apparently not trying to get into a fight either.

    "We were not sure if you just panicked, or something. Or if there was something we could do."

    Swallowing, Kate exhales, but smooths out her furrowed eyebrows and swallows her rebuttal. If Yelena can step back from a potential fight, so can she.

    "So Sonya took a quick detour and grabbed a radio from one of the guards, to figure out what was going on. We found out that you were in custody, while I finished hot-wiring the truck." Just remembering her food, Kate takes another bite, glancing at Sonya, but keeping her focus with Yelena as she continues to speak.

    "They tried to use another truck to block the exit, so I used the one I was in to ram it off course, and made it through the tunnel and out. I ran it through the security checkpoint too, then down the road for about a mile, away from our car."

    Raising an eyebrow, Kate makes a quizzical noise with her mouth full, prompting Yelena to explain.

    "We needed to get to it undetected. If the van is burned, we either get into a chase, which is very bad with this much attention, or even tracked all the way back to New York. So, we needed to mess up the trail first."

    Tilting her head to the side, Kate nods, wordlessly impressed with the thought process. Yelena huffs, seemingly at least partially in amusement, but she continues without addressing it. Content to watch her speak, Kate continues to eat.

    "I ditched it in the middle of the road, blocking it as much as I could, and hiked a few hundred feet to meet up with Sonya."

    She looks over to Sonya, who nods, taking over the story, drawing Kate's eyes momentarily to herself.

    "First I had to get rid of my pursuers, so we went along an advanced ride around the area on the ATVs. Then I picked Yelena up, we ditched the quad a bit further away, and hiked back up and across the perimeter. We made it back to the car around... 3:20?" She looks at Yelena to verify, and she nods, taking over speaking once more. "The only lawyer we know is Allie, so Sonya called Tommy while we got changed. He called back a few minutes later to say, she might not be enough, so I called Valentina just as we were leaving the parking lot in the forest."

    While she speaks, Yelena uses her fork to pick up one of the last bits of her waffle and waves it around as finishes her story.

    "I talked her into helping you, and we called Tommy back, to let Allie know Val is coming to pick her up. We didn't cross any police as we made it back to the highway, so we pulled over at the first gas station and waited."

    In the process of standing up to get herself a glass of juice, Kate pauses by the kitchen island, looking at Yelena.

    "What for?"

    With the bit of waffle still on her fork, Yelena shrugs. Next to her, Sonya looks amused at the question for some reason, but she is ignored, apart from Kate's confused glance in her direction.

    "We were not sure they would be able to get you out. If they were not, the easiest place to pull you out would have been mid-transport because once you are in a federal building, our options are a lot more limited."

    With a deep sigh, Kate nods, having kind of expected Yelena and Sonya to have a rescue plan in place, but still finding it a bit odd to hear it said out loud. After a moment, she looks back at Yelena, her head tilted down.

    "Thanks. Like, for hypothetically busting me out. Or, you know..."

    Pursing her lips, Yelena doesn't exactly look happy, but after she finally lifts her fork to her mouth, and eats the piece of waffle, she nods.

    "You are welcome."

    "Be happy we didn't need to. I would have kicked your ass if we had to do that." Sonya's voice cuts into her Yelena-focused tunnel vision, and Kate chuckles as she turns to look at her, able to tell just based on her voice that she is joking.

    "For what it's worth, I'd not look forward to life as a fugitive either." For once, Sonya does not laugh at Kate's joke but looks at her seriously, shaking her head. "Then don't get caught next time. I am not sure we'd be able to pull this move twice." Exhaling and feeling a bit uncomfortable, Kate looks away and nods, moving toward the fridge, and taking out a carton of juice.

    "So, you got the pathway, right?"

    From the cupboard above the sink, Kate pulls three glasses, walking them and the juice back to Yelena and Sonya.

    "Yes. And also the other thing."

    After that, Yelena leaves the room, while Kate distributes the glasses and throws Sonya an intrigued and amused look, even though she remembers the injector pens they found with her mom's evidence. While she waits, Kate pours some juice for all of them, and retakes her seat, before continuing to eat.

    Just as she suspected, Yelena returns carrying 5 of the injector pens, tied together with a rubber band and the pen drive, depositing everything on the counter between them. Putting her fork down, Kate picks up the pack of injector pens and lifts them to eye level. The injectors are seethrough, but the royal blue liquid inside of them almost hides the Bishop Security logo on their wall, giving Kate a strange sense of bittersweet nostalgia for a second. Each one has a barcode on the side, following a simple sequence, going from LIM001 to LIM005.

    For a few seconds, Kate turns them around in her hands, her food forgotten, before she looks up at Yelena, still standing by the kitchen island.

    "If I had to bet... These are prototypes that my mom had made, right?"

    Tilting her head from side to side, Yelena thinks for a few seconds, before she nods. "Most likely. But we should confirm."

    With a nod of her own, Kate turns to look at the vials once more.

    "Yeah. I will call Robert in a bit, and ask him to get a message to my mom." Worrying her lip between her teeth for a second, Kate is stuck by a thought, looking back at Yelena as she moves to retake her seat across from her.

    "I don't think anyone knows these exist. They would have asked for this, not the formula if they did."

    She looks from Yelena to Sonya, both of them thinking her words over as she puts down the pack of injectors on the counter. Pursing her lips, Sonya looks down at the vials too, before shaking her head.

    "Not necessarily. Replicating something from a sample is a lot harder and most importantly, more expensive, than knowing the formula, ready to be manufactured."

    Mulling the words over, Kate nods, picking her glass up and taking a sip of her juice as she leans back, trying to rid her mouth of the bitter feeling of her mother not telling her about something again.

    "It does not mean they are not a good bargaining chip.-"

    Looking at Yelena, Kate's stomach jumps tiredly as their eyes meet, Yelena's intense as they look into hers.

    "-This could get Valentina off your back if you play your cards right." Glancing at the formula once more, Kate feels ambivalent. She meets Yelena's eyes once more, pushing her hair distractedly out of her face.

    "I don't... I need to think this through. Even if she is technically 'the government,'-" Lifting her hands to do the air quotes physically, Kate purses her lips in distaste, definitely not trusting Valentina after everything, even though she just got her out of jail. "-she is shady as fuck."

    Surprisingly, Yelena chuckles, and Sonya huffs in amusement. It's her, who reveals the source of their amusement, with a shake of her head.

    "All governments are shady as fuck, Kate. We are living proof of that. Do not think America is any better."

    Tilting her head to the side, Kate cringes a bit, finding that hard to argue with. Still, she would prefer to give it to someone trustworthy like... Well, she doesn't know that part yet. Who could she trust?

    The CIA means Valentina. The FBI might be in bed with Fisk. The police is definitely in bed with him so that leaves... The military? Not much better... S.W.O.R.D. maybe? ...Remembering Clint's stories about being a weapon, aimed by the right people, Kate can't say she feels one hundred percent confident with that either... Not to mention the whole Hydra infiltrating S.H.I.E.L.D. story...

    Who can she trust with this?

    Yelena's chortle brings her back to reality, finding her exchanging a look with Sonya. "I think I threw her into an existential crisis."

    Sonya grins at Yelena as she speaks, and the two of them turn to look at her, fond amusement written on their features. Imagining what she must have looked like, thinking it over while looking at the formula, Kate smiles too, shaking her head.

    "Yeah, I think it's best if we keep it for now. Maybe Clint knows who we can trust with it." Once again, Yelena snorts, her eyes flashing warmly as she looks back at Kate. "Sure. The retired assassin used by his government will surely know."

    Shaking her head with a smile, Kate rolls her eyes, before looking back at Yelena. "I don't know! He might have contacts!"

    Lifting her eyebrows and pursing her lips, Yelena's expression is roughly translated as "doubt it, but won't argue", making Kate's smile widen for a second before another thought slips into her mind.

    ...Clint.

    Shit.

    "Have you guys talked to him yet? Since I was..."

    Leaving the sentence hanging, Kate doesn't explain, all of them aware of what she is referring to.

    "Yes. I called him after I talked to Valentina. Then a few times after." Once again, Kate cringes, running a hand through her hair. He is not going to be happy. With any of this.

    "-He knows you were arrested, and that we got you out. I talked him out of coming here right away since there was nothing he could do to help, but I am sure he will show up sooner rather than later.

    Puffing out her cheeks to exhale, Kate nods, before biting down on her lower lip again in thought.

    "I'll call him in a bit. We only have to pick up the last piece from the Summer Place after this. Then we'll be stuck here decoding for a few days. There is no point in him coming here right now."

    The sentence is mostly for herself, her guilt about getting Clint into trouble without meaning to filling her chest. It's probably best if he stays around his family, with Valentina looming over them until all of this is cleared up anyway.

    With a deep sigh, Kate picks up her fork again, and puts another bite of waffle into her mouth. Distractedly, she thinks the food should turn ashy in her mouth from the guilt, but if she is being honest, it's still goddamn delicious.

    For a few moments, she worries about Clint and his family once more, before remembering another detail. She looks up at Sonya, catching her eyes.

    "So, Allie."

    Glancing at Yelena, Kate waits for some type of explanation only for a second or two, aware that she is probably not giving enough context. She continues after a moment, when Sonya does not give her anything.

    "-What does she know? I didn't know what she knew about you or me or... anything, really. So I just kept quiet apart from the things she mentioned herself. But like, obviously, she has to know something, to be involved with this. So, ...you know, what does she know?" There is a miniscule lift of one of Sonya's eyebrows, and she waits a second longer to answer while she looks at Kate, as she runs out of things to say.

    "I told her some things about my past, a few months ago. She is smart enough to not ask more."

    Acknowledging Sonya's words, Kate nods, tilting her head to the side as she asks about the night before.

    "What does she know about yesterday?"

    At that, Sonya smiles, leaning back in her chair, and her hands falling elegantly into her lap. "She is a lawyer. We told her you got caught somewhere you were not supposed to, and had to get out. Gave her some specifics. That was enough."

    Huh.

    Finally, something simple.

    Kate smiles back at Sonya, her eyes seeking Yelena out for no reason other than to look at her after a few moments. She finds Yelena looking down at the samples in front of her, her face thoughtful.

    Finishing her waffles, Kate feels the weight of the evening before settling on her shoulders and has to stifle a yawn twice in the next minute or so. Yelena and Sonya finished eating already, but seem content to wait for her, only getting up once she is done too. Kate stays seated a few seconds longer, gathering the energy she needs to go call Clint before she allows herself to shower and take a power nap to end all power naps. Her attention is drawn to Yelena, when she steps closer to her chair, while Sonya takes their used plates to the sink.

    Turning to her, Kate's breath catches in her throat when Yelena grabs her chin gently, tilting her head up to see the bruise on her forehead. For a few seconds, she examines it before her eyes move lower, meeting Kate's while she still keeps holding onto her chin. "No concussion?"

    Her lips parting, Kate doesn't shake her head and avoids giving in to the urge to swallow too, feeling caught up in Yelena's attention.

    "I don't think so."

    Yelena nods, her hand falling away as Sonya returns, but for long moments after, Kate feels the ghost of her touch on her skin.

    "Put some ice on it. And call Barton."

    The moment broken, Kate nods, her gaze jumping over to Sonya, trying to shove down the feeling of not wanting her here just because she intruded on the moment unknowingly. Sonya saved her life. Don't be an ungrateful asshole, Kate.

    "Yeah. I'm gonna call him in a second."

    Her eyes find Yelena's again, who just nods, glancing at Sonya when she speaks as she steps up to them too.

    "You should probably come down to mine later too. Get the whole story straightened out with Allie."

    Wordlessly, Kate nods, her chin still feeling warm where Yelena held it earlier. "Sure. Okay."

    Without looking at her, Yelena walks out and Kate exchanges a parting smile with Sonya, before closing her eyes and trying to gather her strength.

    Briefly, she entertains the idea of showering first, but deep down, she knows she is trying to put off the lecture she is about to get from Clint, possibly even anger at putting his family in danger, and decides that she would rather get it over with so she can relax after. Heeding Yelena's advice, she takes some ibuprofen, pulls a bag of frozen peas from her freezer that she does not remember buying, and goes to retrieve her phone, dialing Clint's number while she opens her secret lair to hide the pathway and the samples. God, this place is a mess. Tomorrow, after they retrieve the encryption from her mom's place, Kate is really ought to tidy it up.

    The phone is picked up barely into the second ring, Clint evidently keeping it close and stirring up the healthy dose of guilt in Kate's chest that she pushed aside earlier. Both about causing him to worry, and consider leaving his ranch again and for unwittingly putting him and his family in danger.

    "Hi, Clint."

    The worry in his voice does not help, and once she deposits the pendrive and the injector pens safely next to the data drive already in there, Kate walks out of her lair and lets herself lie down on the couch.

    "Kate? Are you okay?"

    Closing her eyes, Kate leans back against the armrest, turning her head slightly to the side so she can put the frozen peas onto it without having to hold it, humming in the affirmative to Clint's question.

    "Yeah. A bit tired but otherwise good. Um, listen..."

    While less worried, Clint's voice is still heavy, and he sounds just as tired as she does. Was he up all night worried about their mission?

    "What happened? Yelena said you got captured. And that they were working with Valentina on getting you out."

    Biting down on her lower lip, Kate feels the events of the night before weigh on her chest, pushing her into the soft cushion below her.

    "Right. Um, okay. So, to make a long story short, one of the guards detonated a frag, while we were underground. I got separated from Yelena, but I knew that she was going to make it out, and I noticed that he, the uh, the guard who blew us up, got pretty hurt. So I stayed behind to help him and got caught in the process. I just... I couldn't let him die, Clint." She stops speaking after that for a second and allows him to process and say his piece if he needs to. She hears him sigh, but he sounds mostly understanding a moment later. "If you had to get captured, I guess that's a good reason to do so. I trust you made the right call."

    The bag of frozen peas shifts as Kate's cheek lifts with her smile, a drop of water running down her temple. The smile only lasts a heartbeat, remembering what her decision brought with it. Not just for her, but for Clint.

    "Thanks. So, uh, Yelena got Valentina and Thomas' sister, who is a lawyer, to get me out. But it uh... It came with a price."

    Her chest feels tight with the deep sigh she takes, but Clint does not try to interject, quiet on the other end of the call. Exhaling, Kate steels herself to just say what happened, regardless of how ashamed she feels of unwittingly endangering his family.

    "She took me outside, Valentina I mean, and told me that I work for her now, for the CIA, and that I will deliver the formula to her, once we get it. And, she also said that if I try to get out of it, she will let Rojas know that you killed his father and the location of your ranch." Taking a deep, almost painfully tight breath, Kate barrels on.

    "I'm so, so sorry. I... I never imagined that this would happen. I'm... Just let me know what I can do, to make this better."

    Kate chokes on her guilt, her chest feeling heavy and she waits for Clint to say something, to yell, to get angry, anything, but the other end of the line is quiet as a grave. "Clint?"

    Her voice is thick with her worry and shame, and she hears him clear his throat. "I'm here. I'm...thinking."

    Sitting up, Kate lets the frozen peas fall onto the ground, forgotten, running her hand through her hair that is not holding the phone to her ear. Her eyes, now open once more, fixate on her knees, her legs kicked out in front of her.

    "I am so sorry Clint. I never meant to put your family in danger, I didn't... I didn't think-" Clint's voice is clear and strong, his fatigue gone in an instant as he cuts off her apology. "It's not your fault. I am the one that killed Rojas' father. This... This was bound to happen." Not knowing what to say, Kate swallows, her hand fisted in her hair, while Clint is quiet for a few more seconds. Despite his words, Kate knows it's her fault, to some degree at least, but it feels just as selfish to insist at this moment because Clint will just deny it and he has more important things to deal with.

    "Okay, kid. It's... This is serious. I will talk to Laura. Is there anything else I need to know?" Shaking her head, Kate exhales, screwing her eyes shut once again.

    "No."

    "Okay, rest up. I will call you later. You did good."

    His last words feel like a punch in the gut, but Kate nods to herself, not trying to make him bear the cross of having to deal with her guilt right now too. He hangs up without saying goodbye, and Kate lies back down on the couch, feeling heavier than she did before the call. With the distraction of Yelena, Sonya, Allie, or even Valentina gone, Kate is left to process the events of the day and night before. She knows objectively, that Clint's family being in danger is not her 'fault', but she feels responsible nonetheless. It's a big, heavy ball of cold metal in her stomach, weighing her down.

    It's one thing for her to bear the consequences of her actions. But even when she does what she thinks is right, innocent people get hurt, or put in danger. If she has to choose between her own safety and an innocent person's life, of course, she will choose the innocent person. But like this?

    Her mind flashes back to the interrogation, specifically the images that Reyes showed her. She cannot regret saving Danny. It was the right thing to do at that moment, but if she left him and escaped, Clint's family wouldn't be in danger now...

    Ugh, fuck. It would be so nice for something to be simple for once. Why can't she fight aliens or Thanos or something?

    She startles slightly when the lair's timer runs out, and the bookcase slides back into place with a quiet hiss to cover its entrance, breaking her out of her spiral. With a deep breath, she gets off the couch.

    She can continue to spiral in the shower. At least that way she gets the grime of the last 24 hours off of her.

    The shower does make her feel better, physically at least, but Kate does spend a significant amount of time replaying the last part of her interview in her mind, as well as worrying about Clint and his family as she stands under the spray.

    Is there somewhere Laura and the kids can go? The homestead has some serious security features, worthy of an Avenger, but probably not enough to withstand a full-scale assault from a cartel. And even if they do go...How long will this hang over their heads? Despite the uncomfortable feeling in her stomach, Kate can't help but also consider that just like Kingpin, Rojas is probably too far gone to be brought to justice and maybe... Maybe the only way to solve this problem is to end the threat, once and for all. But...

    Does that make Agent Reyes right about her? Is it her place to decide that? Is it Clint's? Rojas doesn't yet know of Clint being responsible for his father's death or his location though, which makes it even more of a gray area since he is not actually an active threat. He is just a potential one. Isn't she just playing judge, jury, and executioner, if she considers they should or could take him out?

    Closing her eyes, Kate lets the water run down her face, her hair, her back, trying to quiet down her thoughts.

    She feels tired. Physically too, but mostly, of the impossibility of making the right choice. Even with choices where it seems clear-cut what the right thing to do is, like saving an innocent man's life, it just isn't. It keeps getting messy and complicated. And it's one thing for Kate to bear the consequences of doing the right thing, but it's very different if the weight of it all falls onto the people she cares about.

    Of course, at the root of it all, this is not Kate's fault. She knows that. Rojas, Valentina, Fisk.

    They are the ones who create a world where her saving somebody is rewarded by the family of her best friend, the family who took her in in a way, being put in mortal danger from a fucking cartel boss. If she were to take the time to get the right files, Rojas' work is probably similar to Kingpin's. A long trail of death and destruction, leading to power and money. She thinks it would be good to talk about this with someone. Yelena, most of all. Kate yearns for her company, even though she just left, but she has a pretty good idea of what Yelena would say. A memory surfaces in her mind, of Yelena looking at her seriously in the elevator of Wendy's building.

    "You do not control what bad men do.”

    Kate can't say she agrees completely but the words do bring her enough solace that she opens her eyes, and shuts off the water. Kate may not be able to control what Fisk, Rojas, or Valentina do, but she can control what she does.

    She can keep the people she loves and cares about safe. She can work harder, can become smarter and stronger, to keep men like Rojas from being a threat to families like Clint's. She doesn't know how, but she will keep the formula from ending up in any of these people's hands.

    Including Valentina.

    If she is the type of person to threaten Kate with this, she can change her mind and tell Rojas about Clint at any moment it serves her to do so.

    So, the list of Kate's (potential?) enemies expanded once more.

    Rojas, Valentina, Fisk.

    Once the mission and the police station are thoroughly washed off of her, her head feels a bit more clear. There are no brusies littering her body for once, except the one on her forehead and two small-ish, dark purple spots on her chest where the shrapnel has struck her, but after prodding at them for a few seconds, Kate determines that they do not require actual medical attention. Luke really is a master of his craft.

    For a few seconds, while she towel dries her hair, Kate considers if there is anything she can do at this moment to move things along but other than driving out to get the encryption today, there is nothing she can do.

    That can wait until tomorrow...And maybe until after she talks to a lawyer. Once they have the encryption, they can decrypt the formula and almost more importantly, the insurance policy her mom has kept. With a few copies made, leaked on social media, and sent to Peter Browning, that should get Fisk off the table for the foreseeable future. And on the off chance that it doesn't, it will most likely contain information on how to find him. Kate doesn't know if she is ready to make the choice to take him out, but at least they will have the option.

    While the files decrypt, they can also come up with a way to neutralize Rojas and Valentina, and also decide what to do about the samples. It might be best to destroy them, but maybe they can be used to bargain immunity for herself without relying on Valentina. Which reminds Kate that she needs to call Robert.

    Getting dressed in a pair of boxer briefs and a comfortable, big t-shirt, Kate picks up her phone and dials his number. While the phone rings, she double-checks that her front door is locked, and walks back to her bedroom barefoot.

    Robert picks up on the third ring, just as Kate is drawing her blinds, shutting out the sunshine from outside and covering her room in darkness.

    "Hello. This is Robert Hughes speaking."

    In the dark, Kate walks over to her bedside table, turning on the small light. "Hi, Robert. It's Kate. Kate Bishop."

    Taking a seat on her bed, Kate uses her shoulder to hold her phone to her ear, while she scoots backward to lean against the headboard.

    "Ah. Hello, Miss Bishop. How may I help you?"

    His deep voice is mostly pleasant and certainly polite, so cringing a little at their earlier interaction in the hospital, Kate tries to sound polite too.

    "I need to get in contact with my mother."

    Robert hums for a moment, before asking back, his voice careful.

    "May I ask what this is regarding?"

    Blinking, Kate's eyebrows furrow for a second. Her phone might be bug-free for now, but who knows about Robert? Kingpin or even Valentina could have easily gotten to his phone, so it's best not to mention the samples they found directly.

    "Well. It's... I don't know how much to say on the phone. I just need to talk to her." Once again, Robert hums, his voice reducing in volume just slightly.

    "Is this regarding the thing she asked you to procure?"

    For a few heartbeats, Kate hesitates. But Robert is her mom's lawyer. Surely, he is aware of the plea deal and its terms. This, Kate can probably answer.

    "Yes."

    There is no pause this time, and Robert's voice does not betray excitement or dread, or any emotion for that matter.

    "Do you have it in your possession?"

    Shaking her head to herself, Kate answers.

    "No. Not yet. But I have a question only she can answer."

    Stretching her legs out in front of her, Kate feels her fatigue settle in her bones and slides slightly lower as Robert answers.

    "I see. I have an appointment set up with her for Wednesday. Perhaps, we can meet up tomorrow, and talk about the question I need to pass on."

    Pursing her lips, Kate feels a bit uncomfortable. She doesn't want to use Robert as a carrier of their messages. She wants to talk to her mother herself.

    "Um... Thank you, but I really need to talk to her. Can you arrange for her to call me? Maybe while you are with her."

    A few heartbeats of silence follow, Robert most likely considering Kate's request. "I will try to arrange it. But, I can't make any promises."

    Kate's lips stretch into a smile, her jaw tensing simultaneously as she resists the urge to yawn. "That's all I ask, thank you!"

    They bid their farewells after that and Kate sighs in satisfaction, as she gets under the covers. Remembering Sonya's request to join them when Allie comes over, Kate sets an alarm for 6 pm on her phone, which gives her about two and a half hours to sleep.

    Shuffling lower in her bed, Kate looks at her phone a little while longer, not wanting to end up sucked into her thoughts again.

    With her phone untouched for over half a day, she has a bunch of texts and notifications, the majority of which are about the news of her getting engaged. With all the crazy events of the last 24 hours, Kate kind of pushed that detail to the back of her mind, but the world very much did not.

    The photo she posted yesterday, and tagged Yelena in, of her hand with the ring, has gotten over ten thousand likes on Instagram, and her DMs, as well as her text messages, are practically overflowing.
