    He is playing with another dog, a big gray Akita, at Clint's homestead, the two of them racing after a ball, the other dog barking in excitement. Kate laughs watching them, her chest feeling tight with her happiness and she looks over to the side, to share the moment with Yelena, only to find the spot she occupied before empty.

    Alarmed, Kate twists around, looking for her, her glowy happiness morphing into concern when she can not find her. As she is looking around, Kate feels slow to notice that she is all alone, the homestead looking, and somehow feeling deserted.

    "Yelena?...Guys? Clint? Laura?"

    Walking towards the house, Kate calls out, the hairs on her arms standing up as she grows nearer. There are cars, large, dark SUVs at the front end of the house that Kate didn't notice until now, and immediately, she doesn't know why, but she is somehow instinctually aware that she must not make any noise.

    With light steps, Kate moves closer to the veranda, trying to catch a glimpse inside through the windows, but she can't see anything. Her heart speeding up, she walks up the stairs, flinching slightly when the last step creaks quietly under her boot.

    For a few thundering heartbeats, Kate waits, but nothing moves, the field around the homestead still deserted. Even more carefully, she moves closer to the house, staying out of the window's line of sight, knowing that she must not show herself to whoever is inside. Keeping her body close to the wall, Kate sneaks closer to the window and carefully peers inside. What she sees makes her blood freeze in her veins.

    Clint is on his knees, his hands bound behind his back, his head hung low. On his left, Yelena is in the same position, but instead of looking down, her eyes are turned upward, her face defiant and furious.

    No.

    On Clint's other side, Kate can only see a pair of legs, lying haphazardly, Laura's body mostly hidden behind Clint's form. Barely swallowing her scream, Kate's chest pangs as she notices Clint is shaking, inaudible sobs wreaking his body.

    From the cover of the wall, a hand raises, pointing a gun at Yelenea's forehead. Horror filling her, Kate sprints by the window and to the front door, tearing it open, ready to... Except the door doesn't budge. Not even an inch.

    Taking a few steps back, Kate plants her feet and throws her whole weight into the kick, targetting the wood just below the doorknob, but the door doesn't budge. Not even an inch. Throwing caution to the wind, Kate screams in frustration, kicking the door again and again, her heart thunders in her ears. But the door doesn't budge.

    Not even an inch.

    BANG.

    Through the walls, Kate hears the gunshot, and her throat hurts from the scream that is torn from her throat. Sprinting back toward the window, Kate throws her body into the glass, tumbling through it and into Clint's living room.

    She uses her momentum to roll into a crouch, but her fight leaves her when she comprehends what her eyes are seeing.

    On one side of Clint, Laura lies in a pool of her own blood, her favorite purple sweater soaked in it. Her chin and her neck are covered in the blood she must have coughed up, her eyes staring into nothing...

    No, not nothing... At a picture above the fireplace, of Clint, Laura, the kids, and Kate. On Clint's left, Yelena lies, unmoving. She is still kneeling, but her torso is bent back almost unnaturally, a single gunshot wound in the middle of her forehead, blood, and gray matter marring her beautiful golden hair. The look of defiance is gone from her face, replaced by a mask of ungraceful death.

    Kate wants to throw up.

    Finally, her horrified gaze moves over to Clint, his head slowly rising. As he finally meets Kate's eyes, there is no sign of the friendship, respect, or love that Kate has grown to know in them. Instead, there is pure, unadulterated hatred. His mouth opens, and he says three words, his voice dripping with furious revulsion.

    "You did this."

    Kate wakes with a start, jolting up in her bed.

    The images are still fresh in her mind, her stomach turning with their vividity, but for once, the adrenaline in her veins helps her avoid confusion about what's reality and what was a dream. Practically panting she reaches for her phone, finding it half under her pillow. She needs to stop this from happening.

    She doesn't know what she is doing until she is already in the process of dialing Clint's number.

    The phone rings only twice before it's picked up, Clint's voice sounding suspiciously smooth and energetic. It's still a balm to Kate's soul, after the hateful version echoing in her head for the last minute.

    "Hi, kid. We are in the car, you are on speakerphone."

    Ah. That explains the voice.

    "Hey, hi... Hi, guys. How are...things?"

    Her heart slowing down with every beat, Kate stumbles over her words a little, rubbing a hand over her face.

    "We are going on a trip!"

    Nate's excited voice only serves to exacerbate the sick swirling in Kate's stomach, her guilt threatening to choke her up completely. Inhaling and exhaling slowly, Kate closes her eyes and forces her voice to sound light, hoping that Clint and Laura know how terrible she feels. "Oh, that's cool! Where are you going?"

    "It's a surprise!!"

    With her eyes still closed, Kate hums in affirmation, trying to buy time to be able to speak without her voice giving anything away. It does not escape her that Lila and Coop are not joining the conversation for once. They have been picking up more and more on when there is something wrong, and probably know that an impromptu surprise trip is probably not all good.

    "That's super cool, Natey-o. Um, Clint, can I talk to you for one second? It's about work." A few moments go by, with only vague and muted sounds of traffic coming through, before Clint answers, his voice still unaffected.

    "Sure kid. I'll call you back in about 15 minutes, okay?"

    Wetting her lips, Kate nods, scooting back against the headboard once again. "Of course, yeah. Call me when you can. Enjoy your trip, guys!"

    For the next 10 minutes, Kate does not put her phone out of sight. The only time she even just puts it down is when she goes to wash her face with cold water, thinking that she will need another shower before she goes over to Sonya's later.

    She is in the kitchen, making a cup of coffee, when Clint calls her back, his voice tired, but still lighter than Kate had feared.

    "Hi, Kate. You okay?"

    Leaning back against the counter, Kate nods, looking at the late afternoon light coming through the window.

    "Yeah. I'm good. I called to ask what you guys were going to do. And offer that I have a couple of uhm, places, that you guys could stay at? I still have my house in LA. Or I have a cabin, in Aspen, if you want something less...urban. I have a few properties in Europe too, if that's-"

    Clint cuts her off, knowing Kate well enough to know immediately what goes on in her head. Despite his serious tone, Kate can tell that he is smiling, but it does not make her feel any better.

    "Kate, you didn't do this. It's not your fault."

    Shaking her head to herself, Kate appreciates his words but also doesn't believe him. Either way, that is not the point.

    "I just want to help. What's the point of having all this, if I can't use it to help. I could... I can buy something new too, closer to the ranch, so the kids don't have to switch up their routines, or something."

    To her right, her coffee finished brewing, but she doesn't pick it up yet, focusing on Clint's words on the other end of the line instead.

    "We have a safe house in the mountains. We will stay there for a few days, while we figure out how serious this is."

    Her stomach gnawing in worry, Kate rolls her lips together, even as the tension in her lower back eases out just a bit.

    "Okay. If you... If there is anything I can do, please let me know."

    His smile strongly audible through the phone, Clint hums in affirmation before he speaks. "Okay, kid. Sure. Thank you."

    Exhaling slowly, Kate walks over to the fridge, getting the milk for her coffee, while she thinks of her furry best friend.

    "What about Lucky? Do you need me to get him?"

    While she walks back, Clint grunts affectionately on the phone.

    "We have him with us. We are going to a cabin in the woods, so we can keep him for now, but I'll let you know."

    The fact that she is probably not supposed to leave the state does not bother her the slightest. "Okay. I can come pick him up or we can figure something out."

    This time she does not receive a verbal answer, just a hum letting her know that Clint heard and noted what she said. With the logistical questions discussed, Kate lifts her coffee to her lips but asks Clint before she takes a sip.

    "How are the kids taking it?"

    Even through the receiver, she hears his sigh and wonders for a moment where Clint and his family are right now.

    "Nate is excited, mostly. He seems to sense that something is going on, but he doesn't understand so... Lilla is worried but she puts on a brave face. And Cooper..." A sprinkle of humor enters his voice again, a gentle snort heard through the receiver. "-Coop is mostly pissed he will not see his girlfriend for a bit."

    Even as her chest squirms with guilt, Kate smiles.

    "Understandable."

    Once again, Clint hums before he speaks again.

    "Speaking of. What did Yelena think of you getting arrested?"

    Her eyebrows jumping up towards her hairline.

    What the hell does he mean 'speaking of'?

    Kate quickly considers whether she should address his backhanded attempt at...A dig? Teasing? It's a bit hard to tell through the phone...

    But yeah, no. It's probably best if she ignores it. Clint has made his thoughts on the topic perfectly clear.

    "Well, she wasn't happy. She says she doesn't blame me for doing it, but that she is angry for me making a call without them and not communicating. Which is...kinda valid, I guess." On the other end of the line, Clint snorts.

    "You think?"

    Taking another sip of her coffee, Kate hums, while Clint continues after a moment. "It's probably a touchy subject for her too."

    Leaning slightly back, Kate pauses in her coffee drinking. Pulling the mug slightly away from her mouth, her eyebrows furrow.

    "What do you mean?"

    For a few seconds, Clint is quiet, and Kate tries to think it over, why it would be a specifically touchy subject for Yelena. His voice is slightly dismissive when he answers. "Never mind. Talk to her about it."

    Pursing her lips, Kate's eyebrows furrow even further, this time in displeasure. What the hell does that mean?

    "Come on, Clint. Talk to me."

    "Nope. Not my place."

    Huffing, Kate wreaks her brain for answers, coming up mostly empty. She raises the mug to her lips once again, only to pull it away without drinking. Is this something to do with the Red Room? About choices being taken away? Or did something...

    Oh.

    "Is this about Natasha?"

    Clint is silent for a few moments before Kate hears him sigh once again. "It was not easy for Yelena to accept what happened... That she made the decision to sacrifice herself for everyone."

    Blinking, Kate thinks over the answer, putting down her mug to run a hand through her slowly drying hair, not completely dry from her washing it before her nap. "Okay, yeah. I can see how that's...But that's not what I was doing? I didn't purposefully get captured. I stayed to save the guard, and it just...happened."

    On the other end of the line, Clint moves around, maybe rubbing his face by the sounds of it. "I don't know, Kate. Talk to her. It was just a thought."

    Picking up her mug again, Kate takes another sip of her coffee and rolls her eyes internally. Yeah. Why didn't she think of that? Because talking to Yelena about this stuff is so easy... Before she can say or ask more, Clint speaks up again.

    "Okay kid, they are back. I have to go."

    Pushing the Yelena topic aside, Kate lowers her mug, her heart going out to Clint. "Sure. Um, listen, I meant what I said. Anything you need. Really."

    His voice is warm but slightly distracted when he answers.

    "Alright. Thanks. Speak later."

    After they hang up, Kate feels momentarily better about her guilt, even though she still worries. For the next few minutes, while she drinks her coffee and goes through the motions of making a frozen pizza, Kate tries to come up with ways she could help them, coming up mostly empty-handed.

    She hopes that at least Clint will ask if they do need something, money or anything else, but he has not been great at leaning on her in the past. Hmm...

    While she eats, Kate moves to the couch, choosing to have her pizza in front of the TV but she mostly spends her time thinking about Clint and his family, Valentina and her threats, Javier Rojas and Fisk. In comparison, taking down Kingpin almost seems easy. Obviously, Kate knows it isn't, they have been struggling to do it for weeks, but what leverage does she have over the Director of the fucking CIA? Or even a Colombian cartel boss? They might need to make more friends. Powerful friends... Can Clint get into contact with Captain Marvel?

    She has one slice left when her phone rings once again on the couch next to her. Glancing at the screen, Kate sees the picture of Yelena she made her contact picture a few weeks back, and picks it up without thinking, grimacing when she realizes how greasy her hands are. "Hi, what's up?"

    Not bothering with greetings, Yelena gets straight to the point, but her tone is neutral, not giving Kate a reason to worry.

    "Change of plans. We are coming up to your place."

    Blinking, Kate straightens up slightly, as if there is already company watching her. "Oh, sure, okay... How come?"

    Kate hears a door closing on Yelena's end, but no other indication of where she is and what she is doing.

    "Tommy brought Maxine back, so it is a bit cramped down here."

    Ah, that's fair...Although that would only mean one additional person... Maybe Maxine is not supposed to meet Allie? Or maybe Sonya doesn't feel like hosting...

    As if reading her thoughts, Yelena follows up after a short pause, her voice softening slightly. "Maxine had a hard time sleeping at Tommy's place the last few days."

    It is not exactly a straightforward explanation, but Kate can deduct the core message. Maxine needs space.

    "Oh, yeah. Okay... Do you need me to get anything?"

    Yelena doesn't need time to think it over, answering immediately.

    "No. We already cooked and ate. And there should be enough snacks and beverages in your kitchen."

    Okay.

    Kate does not pause to question why Yelena knows that. She barrels on anyway. "-We will be up in about 20 minutes. Sonya already texted Allie."

    At the last sentence, Kate smiles to herself. The weird lack of boundaries with the Widows should probably be more annoying, but she mostly finds it endearing.

    "Okay. See you soon, I guess."

    "See you soon."

    Still smiling to herself, Kate stuffs half of the remaining slice of pizza into her mouth and stands up, ignoring the pang in her chest when she is reminded that Lucky is not there to help to finish it like he usually is. She imagines Yelena's face scrunching up in slight disgust as she chews the huge bite, while she walks to the bathroom, and the thought keeps her entertained as she finishes the slice in a few startlingly large bites. Her mom would be horrified too.

    Nope, not thinking about that right now.

    As quickly as she can, Kate showers a second time, her dream having left her sweaty and kind of gross earlier. She gets dressed but has no time to put on makeup or even comb her half-damp hair, by the time she hears a key slide and twist in the lock. She is still barefoot when she walks out of the bathroom to greet Yelena, Sonya, and Tommy, her face lighting up when she sees them.

    "Hi! Hi, Tommy, how are you?"

    As they file in, Kate's eyes are drawn to Yelena first, as always, appreciating the high-rise black jeans and the short-sleeved, black and tan turtleneck she is wearing. Her hair is flawless as always, falling in loose waves around her shoulders. She looks gorgeous and fancy. Their eyes meet for a few heartbeats, and Kate sees the corners of Yelena's mouth curl upwards before her attention is drawn away when Tommy answers her question.

    "I'm good. Happy that you guys are back okay. How's being arrested?"

    It's Tommy's joking question that draws Kate's eyes away from Yelena, a surprised laugh bubbling out of her chest.

    "Oh, it's just great. No better way to kick off your week."

    Tommy's grin is wide, but a second later Sonya slaps his arm with the back of her hand. "You should not encourage her. She is already not taking this seriously enough." Kate's gaze shifts to Sonya, who seems somewhere between annoyed and entertained, but her attention is immediately drawn to the plastic container in her hands.

    "I so do. Very seriously...What's that?"

    Meeting Sonya's eyes, Kate's smile widens into a grin when she rolls her eyes, holding out the container towards her.

    "Hungarian stacked potatoes. Yelena made it. We didn't know if you ate." Walking over to Sonya, Kate takes the container, looking at its contents from the side. It looks like...stacked potatoes with layers of other stuff between, and cheese on top. Just by looking at it, Kate is intrigued. Smiling, she looks from Yelena to Sonya, then back. "I have no idea what that is but it looks incredible! Thanks."

    Yelena nods, not smug but also not shy about the compliment.

    "You are welcome. It is very good calorie and carb-dense food after a mission." Once again, Yelena nods, maybe to herself, before taking the container out of Kate's hand and walks away toward the kitchen, while Kate's eyes slide over to Sonya and Tommy to resist the urge to check her ass out. With wide eyes, Thomas nods at her, driving his point home. "Dude, it's so good."

    "Yeah, it looks like it. I had some-"

    Before their conversation about the potatoes can continue, Tommy's phone chimes, and he checks his smart watch to see the message.

    "Allie will be here in five."

    Turning away, Kate speed walks back towards her bedroom, commenting half to herself, half to Sonya and Tommy.

    "I should put on some socks."

    Inside her room, Kate pulls a fresh pair of socks from their drawer and puts a dark blue, oversized corduroy shirt over her grey t-shirt. She stands on one foot to begin to pull on the socks, just as she hears Yelena's voice call out to her from outside.

    "Kate...? Why is there a wet bag of peas on the ground?"

    Huffing to herself in amusement, Kate switches legs, pulling the other sock on. "Uh, sorry! I forgot it there, I'll put it back into the freezer in a sec." Only sparing herself a quick glance in the mirror, Kate notes how the bluish-purple bruise on her forehead has seemingly spread a little, but otherwise looks fine, half covered by her hair. As she walks out of the room, Kate goes straight to Yelena, reaching out for the unfrozen bag of peas in her hand.

    "You can not re-freeze this, you know that, right?"

    One of Yelena's eyebrows is slightly lifted, as is the corner of her mouth, but Kate is mostly distracted by her hand, specifically her ring finger.

    Yelena was not wearing the ring when Sonya and her were over earlier, but she is now. She is again.

    "What? Why not?"

    Kate doesn't think her distraction is apparent, quickly meeting Yelena's eyes again, their humorous spark making her stomach stir.

    "Because they are completely melted."

    Yelena almost seems like she is trying to decide if Kate is serious or not, much to her confusion.

    "...Okay?"

    For a few seconds, the two of them look at each other, the wet bag of peas slowly dripping over Kate's hand, and down to her floor.

    "Kate, you cannot re-freeze already melted food. It will make you sick." Huh. Kate didn't know that.

    To be perfectly honest, she doesn't even know how the peas ended up in her freezer, as there is not a single thing she'd know how to make of them.

    "Ah... okay. I'll just toss them then."

    For some reason, that makes both Yelena and Sonya chuckle, and with a quick motion, Yelena pulls the bag out of her hands once again.

    "Give me that."

    Confused, Kate looks over to Tommy, sitting on one of the armchairs, who just shrugs. Sonya is slightly more helpful, even as she shakes her head at Kate with a smile, while she walks out after Yelena.

    "We can use it for lunch tomorrow."

    Kate nods, the bag of peas already out of her mind, taking a seat across from Tommy on the couch.

    "Hey, I wanted to say thank you too. For helping me get out."

    Tommy, who has been looking at something on his phone up until this phone, puts it down and turns towards Kate with an almost confused smile.

    "Of course."

    Smiling back, Kate's eyes move around the room, before they set back at him. "And sorry for getting you guys involved in it too."

    At that Tommy grins, waving her words off just as Yelena re-enters the room, Sonya nowhere to be seen.

    "Eh. You know Allie. She might look like a wallflower but she is fierce. I knew she'd want to help."

    Kate's smile widens, and she nods, just as the doorbell sounds. Tommy checks his watch, before glancing at the door.

    "That must be her."

    "I'll let her in."

    Getting up from her seat, Kate walks up to the door, briefly checking through the peephole and opening it with a smile once she confirms who is on the other side. Allie smiles wide too, when she catches sight of her, stepping in after the non-verbal invitation as Kate stands to the side.

    "Hi."

    "Hi. Hi guys."

    From his seat, Tommy waves at his sister, while Yelena greets her from the couch, where she has taken a seat.

    "Hello."

    While she takes off her coat, Allie looks around the living room.

    "Nice place."

    "Thanks. Yeah, it's nice. I only moved in like...two and a half months ago?" Glancing around, Kate smiles, before holding out her hand to take the coat. Allie looks around too, before turning back to Kate.

    "Didn't you used to have a place in Hell's Kitchen? I remember Nadia telling me about some party there, where a guy went streaking down the street and got arrested." Turning away to put Allie's coat in the closet, Kate chuckles, remembering what she might be referring to.

    "Which Nadia?"

    From behind her, Allie answers.

    "Musallam."

    Kate snorts to herself, definitely remembering that party after a few seconds. As she turns back, she answers Allie's original question, while Sonya walks into the living room too, coming from Kate's kitchen.

    "Yeaah. Yeah, I still have that, but it's rented out."

    Allie's attention is taken up by Sonya, who walks over to hug her, while Kate stands by, waiting to ask her guests if they want something to drink. Once the orders are in, Kate goes to the kitchen, Yelena getting up and accompanying her to help when Sonya asks for a coctail. They move around each other well, not a word needing to be said. Yelena pulls the various drinks and items from her fridge, handing them off to Kate. She opens Tommy's beer first, then walks the vodka, lime and juice to another counter for Sonya's Bloody Mary, which Yelena loads in her hands.

    "Where is the shaker?"

    The question is more to herself, but it should not surprise her that Yelena answers, pointing out a cabinet.

    "In the corner, above the juice maker."

    Huh.

    Kate retrieves it, putting it by the ingredients for the cocktail, while Yelena pulls a bottle of unopened white wine from her fridge, which Kate is sure she did not purchase herself. Yelena and Sonya showed up a few times in the last few weeks with this or that, so it's probably from one of those hauls.

    Turning back for the next haul, Kate smiles to herself, spotting Yelena on her tippy toes, trying to reach the wine glasses on the top shelf of a cabinet by the fridge. Not saying a word, Kate walks up to her, sure that Yelena can hear her approach like always. Doing her best to keep her smug grin at bay, Kate touches the small of Yelena's back as she reaches by her, pulling the glass Yelena was trying to reach from the shelf with ease.

    At her touch, Yelena freezes, but when the glass is firmly in Kate's hold, she turns slowly around, her eyes meeting hers. Kate expected some offense, at the display of their height difference, or maybe nothing at all, just a simple thank you, but she was definitely not ready for the spark of heat behind Yelena's gaze Her self-satisfied grin kind of slacks, the minimal space between them fizzing for a second. Her voice comes out almost croaky, something she would be slightly embarrassed by, were it not reflected on Yelena’s face.

    "Here."

    Yelena reaches for the glass, without looking at it, and Kate holds her eyes as she passes it on. Kate's heart beats in her stomach, thrumming out a sensual rhythm, somehow intensified by Yelena's silence.

    A moment later though, laughter of the guests filters in from the living room, breaking the moment. Yelena blinks, and in a heartbeat, she has slipped out from the space between Kate and the counter, the glass and the bottle of wine in her hands.

    Stuffing down on her small grin, Kate opens the drawer for the bottle opener, the thought reverberating in her head.

    Get it out of their system, her ass.

    Maybe it's a bit of playing with fire, but Kate goes to stand by Yelena directly, their shoulders almost touching. She reaches for the bottle of wine, relishing in the now charged silence, only broken by the sound of Yelena’s knife, as she cuts the lime in half, and the creak of the cork as Kate slowly screws the opener into it.

    After the soft pop of the bottle, Kate pours it into the wine glass, sneaking glances to her right, while Yelena pours a generous amount of vodka into the shaker, not looking at her. She squeezes one half of the lime into it too, and speaks without turning to Kate. "Can you get some bowls from above the stove?"

    Stifling a smile, Kate hums in affirmation, and walks away to get the items Yelena requested, swinging by to pull some chips and other snacks too. The tension in the room slowly eases out, as Kate doesn't push on it anymore, choosing to fill up the bowls where she pulls them down to allow Yelena some breathing room.

    She only walks back when Yelena is done making the cocktail for Sonya, pouring it out into two glasses, maybe choosing to have one as well. With everyone's drink order ready, there is no reason to linger here anymore, but Yelena turns to Kate, meeting her eyes once again. "What do you want?"

    While the wording sounds rough, Yelena's voice isn't, and now she seems adamant to hold Kate's eyes, even lifting her chin a little. It's kind of a low hanging fruit, so with the corner of her mouth tipping up into small, lopsided grin, Kate asks, poking at the boundaries just a little.

    "To drink?"

    Pursing her lips ever so slightly, Yelena's eyes flash for a second, before she almost rolls them in a silent "obviously" and nods, not answering Kate verbally. Exhaling sharply in lieu of a chuckle, Kate nods, turning away toward the fridge.

    "I'll just have a beer."

    With her back to her, Kate can't see her reaction, and by the time she pulls a bottle from the fridge and opens it, Yelena has taken the two cocktail glasses and the snack bowls and is walking out of the room. This time, Kate doesn't have to stifle her grin, just enjoying their interactions, and she is still smiling a bit when she walks back into the living room, carrying Allie's glass of wine, and Tommy's and her own beers.

    As Kate walks in, all eyes turn to look at her, and Allie laughs before speaking, having taken a seat on the couch where Yelena sat before.

    "Yes, she cleans up better without the prison scrubs."

    Not sure what they are talking about, Kate walks to the coffee table and throws a grin at Allie, jokingly correcting her as she passes the glass of wine.

    "They were prison sweats."

    Her laugh tempered into a smile, Allie holds her eyes, almost rolling them with her sarcastic comeback.

    "Oh, well, that makes all the difference."

    Chuckling, Kate straightens up, handing off the colder beer of the two to Tommy, as she bounces off the comment, defaulting to faux cockiness.

    "Well, I happen to think I was pulling them off."

    She turns back just to see Allie move her hand in a 'so-so' motion, her face scrunching up slightly.

    "Eeeh."

    Furrowing her eyebrows, Kate goes for obviously-fake-offended, causing Allie to break and laugh.

    "Well, the enormous bruise on your head did not exactly help."

    Breaking character, Kate chuckles too, as she takes a seat between Allie and Yelena, her seating choice made for her by everyone already sitting somewhere.

    "-Speaking of. How is it?"

    Waving off the worry, Kate takes a small sip of her beer before reassuring Allie. "Ah, it's fine. I iced it a bit earlier and took a nap. It looks worse than it is, really." With disbelief written all over her face, Allie takes a sip of her wine. After pulling it away from her lips, she leans back, looking from her bother, to Sonya, then at Kate. "I've talked to Marci on your behalf, by the way. You have an appointment tomorrow at 1." Eyebrows jumping toward her hairline, Kate looks at her, suspecting the answer even as she asks her question.

    "Who's Marci?"

    "My boss. She can help you untangle whatever this is. She is hell of a lawyer." Rolling her lips together, Kate nods, thinking it over while she smiles at the respect in Allie's voice.

    "Ah, okay. Thank you."

    Across from her, Sonya leans forward, exchanging a glance with Yelena on Kate's left, before her eyes move over to Allie.

    "So, speaking of that. Do you have any questions about what happened? For Kate? For...us?" Next to Kate, Allie huffs in amusement, but she takes a sip of her wine, taking her time to answer Sonya.

    "Tons of them. But until tomorrow, specifically, until Kate is covered by attorney-client privilege, it's better that I don't ask them."

    The corner of Sonya's lips tips upwards, but the next question comes from Yelena, leaning forward slightly too, so Kate does not block her view of Allie on her other side. "Why is that?"

    Twirling the stem of her wine glass in her hands, Allie crosses her legs, and Kate leans back, trying her best to not be in the way.

    "If she tells me, she committed a crime, legally speaking, as a citizen I am obligated to call the police, otherwise I am obstructing justice. But once we are covered by attorney-client privilege, I am not only not obligated anymore, I am forbidden to, as I would be breaking privilege."

    Yelena nods, her eyes still on Allie.

    "Yes. But Kate is going to see another lawyer tomorrow, yes? So she will be the one covered by it."

    Allie smiles, nodding.

    "Technically, yes. But since she is contracting the firm, not just Marci herself, and I am assigned to all of Marci's cases, I will be covered as well."

    Yelena nods once again, seemingly satisfied with the explanation. She speaks again a moment later, her voice dropping ever so slightly, and Kate does her best to just stare ahead as the temperature of the room drops a few degrees. What is Yelena doing? "And if she killed a man, even if you think that is wrong, you will protect her?" Allie's smile widens even more, and from the corner of her eyes, Kate sees her gaze slide over briefly to her, before they return to Yelena.

    "Exactly. It's not my job to judge. It's my job to make sure that she has the best legal representation possible."

    That seems to satisfy Yelena's curiosity, as she nods, and leans back to take a sip of her cocktail, seemingly done with her questioning. Taking a long swing of her beer, Kate tries to reboot her brain, exchanging a glance with Tommy. Her tribulations are not over yet, because a moment later, Allie speaks again, her eyes moving between Kate and Yelena. "After I got back to the office, I saw your post from yesterday, by the way. Congratulations." When neither of them immediately responds, Allie clarifies, but Kate knows what she meant already, her ears growing warm at the topic.

    "-On your engagement."

    Allie gestures specifically at Yelena's hand, and the ring on it. There are a few heartbeats of silence, while Kate waits for Yelena to say anything, or at least to indicate how to address it. She feels Sonya's and Tommy's amused gazes at her from across the coffee table, as she turns to look at Yelena. She does not look at Kate, her eyes watching Allie for a few heartbeats. "We are not really engaged."

    Mirroring Allie's posture, Yelena crosses her legs, leaning back against the couch. She takes a sip of her cocktail, seemingly basking in the confusion, while Kate chuckles awkwardly, looking at Allie, then turning back to Yelena. She glances at Kate, her face amused but her eyes dark as they slide back to Allie and she explains. Or it might just be the lighting... "A few weeks ago Kate was questioned by the Agents you met today. She stumbled into the lie and it makes sense to keep it up for now."

    Her ears flaming, Kate turns back to smile at Allie, unsure how she feels about Yelena's portrayal of the events, even if they are technically factual. There is a kind of weird vibe around her, that Kate can not put her finger on. Yelena revealing the truth that they are not really engaged also leaves a bad taste in her mouth, similar to how she felt when Yelena told her it was a 'one-time thing'. Especially after the moment they just had in the kitchen. Kate did not imagine that, did she?

    Allie's eyes move between the two of them a few times as the information is revealed before they settle on Kate, and she chuckles, her eyes warm with humor, seemingly not aware of the strange vibe around them, but side-stepping addressing their non-engagement. "Ah. I did suspect you had a history with those two."

    To buy time and get the taste of ill-advised rejection out of her mouth, Kate takes another sip of her beer, but Sonya speaks, making a comment from her unnecessary.

    "Do you think they have a strong case against Kate?"

    Rolling her lips together, Allie shakes her head, glancing at Kate before turning back to Sonya.

    "I have not seen their files and I was not present at her questioning. It's hard to say." Looking at Kate once more, she seems to think, then she continues.

    "-But, judging from what I have seen today, you should be more worried about the CIA than the FBI. They are less bound by law, have a lot less accountability, and from what I heard, they are not too concerned about what happens to their informants after they live out their usefulness."

    Kate opens her mouth to say she is not exactly an informant, not of her free will anyway, but Allie holds up a hand.

    "-Don't answer that. It's just my observation. As a friend, not as a lawyer." Inhaling until her lungs feel fully stretched, Kate nods, taking her time to exhale as she thinks.

    Allie's assessment is the same as her own. While she may have slipped out from under the FBI (for now), her situation did not exactly improve. Valentina is dangerous, and being under thumb is at least as bad, as being close to getting arrested.

    "Did Valentina say anything to you?"

    At Yelena's question, Kate looks at her, before turning to watch Allie purse her lips in thought. She shakes her head, looking at Yelena, repeating what she told Kate earlier. "Not a lot. She told me she made a deal with Director Stone and that she also talked to William Meaney, to sign off on it being called a training exercise."

    Next to Kate, Yelena hums, before posing her next question.

    "Nothing about Kate?"

    Once again, Allie shakes her head, holding Yelena's eyes.

    "Not directly, no. But she did take a call while I was in the car where she was mentioned." Her interest piqued, Kate raises an eyebrow at that, prompting Allie to continue. "She said that she was upstate to get "Baby Hawk back in play' and will be back in the city within the hour."

    Huffing in annoyance, Kate turns back to Yelena, who exchanges a glance with Sonya instead of looking at her.

    "Did you hear who she was talking to?"

    The question comes from Sonya this time, making Allie's eyebrows furrow as she shakes her head, her gaze moving between the three of them.

    "Did he have an accent?"

    Kate's question results in another shake of Allie's head.

    "I didn't hear the other speaker."

    Turning to Yelena once again, Kate meets her eyes and poses her question with one word. "Rojas?"

    Tilting her head from side to side, Yelena holds her gaze, contemplating. She speaks after a moment.

    "Maybe."

    Accepting that this is not the time to discuss that possibility, Kate turns her attention back to Allie.

    "Did she say anything else? Maybe not about us, but still...worth mentioning? Taking a deep breath, Allie shakes her head, almost apologetic.

    "Nothing I could make sense of, no. She talked to a "Catherine" about pushing something back, which she did not seem happy with, and someone else about expense reports." Lifting her shoulders, she kind of shrugs, and Kate sighs but smiles at Allie gratefully after a moment.

    "Thank you... And thank you again for coming to bail me out."

    With a lighthearted eye-roll, Allie smiles.

    "It's a win-win, really. You bought me some serious good grace with Marci. She was very happy with me for bringing in a 'high-profile client like Kate Bishop'." At that, Kate chuckles, rubbing a hand over her face in mostly faux worry before looking back at Allie.

    "I will be paying for Marci's second home, aren't I?"

    Allie laughs, her eyes crinkling at their corners as she lifts the wine glass to cover her laugh, only to lower it a second later, trying to offer some unserious words of comfort. "Let's hope it's just a new car."

    Across from them, Tommy joins the conversation, pretending to be serious. "So is there a solicitor's fee in there for me or like a...referral program?" Looking at her brother across the coffee table, Allie shakes her head with a mockingly apologetic face.

    "Sorry, Tom-tom. You should have set up terms in advance."

    Lifting a challenging eyebrow, Tommy leans back while Kate grins, enjoying the interaction. "Alright...I will remember this when tax filing season comes."

    Somehow managing to sound dignified even as she snorts, Allie laughs in his face and shakes her head.

    "Do you even do your own taxes?"

    For a long moment, brother and sister are engaged in a joking but competitive battle of wills, looking at each other wordlessly before Tommy turns away, his facade breaking as he lifts his beer to take a sip.

    "I plead the fifth."

    As Allie opens her mouth, his eyes jump back and he points at her with a childish warning, his smile widening into a grin.

    "-Do not tell me I can't selectively plead the fifth."

    Allie just smiles at her brother, mostly fond but with a generous amount of smugness, not saying anything. In the armchair next to Tommy's, Sonya chuckles, looking at her boyfriend with a teasing glint in her eye as she reaches over to pat his arm.

    "Aw, baby, you should really know better than to argue with a lawyer."

    Shaking his head, Thomas raises his beer to his lip, grumbling under his nose. "I know better to argue with anyone from this group.-"

    Despite his displeased voice, Kate sees the smile hidden in the corners of his eyes as he takes a sip, before they settle on her. Lowering his bottle, Tommy uses the same hand to point at her, his hidden smile revealing itself on his face.

    "Except Kate. I'm pretty sure I could take her."

    Rising to the challenge, as always, Kate leans back with her own bear, an eyebrow rising. "Could you? I was a part of the debate team with Allie through junior year." His smile widening, Tommy's eyes slide from her to Allie and back.

    "Oh, were you?"

    Feeling smug about Tommy not having a witty comeback, Kate's smirk widens, humming in affirmation as she takes a swing of her beer. It's only after a second of silence that she realizes that Tommy's comment was not aimed at her but at his sister instead, and it totally went over her head the first time. Next to her, Allie huffs out a quiet laugh, not biting onto her brother's bait, before turning to Sonya.

    "So, I heard something yesterday, that you are going to love..."

    The next hour or so goes by quickly. They all have a few more drinks, and chat, the evening feeling almost absurdly light and comfortable, compared to how Kate's day has started. They talk about Tommy's and Allie's jobs, living in New York, with some embarrassing or funny stories from high school and college sprinkled throughout.

    The zero mention of murder, destruction, the FBI, or even the night before is kind of a balm to Kate's soul, the tight knot inside of her chest slowly easing out and unraveling. It feels nice and normal, like coming up for a breath after being underwater. Kind of just what she needed after the last few days of missions, FBI raids, and getting arrested.

    "...You know how it is,-"

    Allie's eyes are alight with a laugh, as she looks around the room, at them all of them, her voice laden with the same mirth.

    "-you are cramming for an exam, you are pulling late nights, you spend more time at the library than anywhere else, and then you just crash and sleep for like 18 hours. " Kate and the others burst out laughing, relishing in the slight blush spreading onto Allie's face as she laughs with them at herself. Shaking her head, Kate leans into teasing her about it with a grin.

    "Allie Newhouse, missing an exam. I can not believe it."

    Rolling her eyes goodnaturedly, Allie huffs and takes a sip of her wine before answering her. "Well, it was freshman year and just some random elective, but still. I never let it happen again."

    Kate shakes her head doubling down with a purposefully obnoxious face.

    "And here I thought Yale was a serious institution."

    Pinning her with a look, Allie turns more toward her, partially leaning against the armrest to her right.

    "So what, you never missed an exam? Ever?"

    Snorting Kate nods, gesturing with her beer bottle, the other arm lying on the back of the couch behind Yelena's head.

    "Oh, yeah. Of course, I did. But it was for cool reasons, not because I studied too hard." Pursing her lips at Kate's audacity, Allie shakes her head.

    "Cool reasons, huh?"

    Truth be told, Kate missed exactly one exam during her college years. But it's a funny story, so she settles even further into her seat, mentally slipping back into her college days as she begins.

    "Okay. So, the year is 2023, we are in the middle of midterms. Spring break is around the corner and the campus is buzzing. You know, that pre-spring break energy, when everything begins to wake up...-"

    Across from her, Tommy chuckles at the dramatic setting of the scene while Sonya looks on, amusement written on her face as she sips her cocktail.

    "-My friend Kyle and I were in the gym one afternoon, just working out some of the stress. I had an exam the next morning, amm...data structures, or something. Anyway, I was mostly done with my study plan, so I thought I would just work out, revise a bit in the evening, have a good night's sleep, and it'll be fine."

    Looking around, Kate relishes in the attention as she tells her story, feeling the weight of both Yelena's and Allie's eyes on her from both of her sides, turning to look at them both as she keeps talking.

    "We were close to rounding up when this drop-dead gorgeous woman came in. And I mean really, like...incredibly beautiful. We have never seen her there before, so Kyle, being Kyle, wants to go and chat her up. I told him she was out of his league, he disagreed. We went back and forth for a bit...-"

    Remembering his tall, handsome, square-jawed friend almost looking flummoxed at the prospect of someone being out of his league, Kate chuckles and takes a quick swing of her second beer before continuing.

    "Long story short, he says fine, then we need a game plan. And I...Well, I would not call it a plan, but he was hellbent on impressing her enough that she would come up, and chat him up herself, so we started adding weights to our last set."

    Grinning to herself, Kate shakes her head, while Tommy, probably sensing where the story was going grins back as he reaches for some of the chips on the coffee table. "We got to a point where we were both doing PRs, basically dying from deadlifts, sweating our asses off while this woman is just on the treadmill, walking, and looking at her phone. Not paying us any mind at all. So really, after a while, it became like a challenge to get her to notice, so we thought we'd adjust strategies."

    To her right, Allie laughs, shaking her head, amusement thick in her voice. "What is it with you jock types always thinking this will work?"

    Using her arm on the back of the couch, Kate lifts it off to run a hand through her hair, before rubbing the back of her head, feeling conflictingly embarrassed and smug, her lopsided grin widening.

    "Well, it did work. Kind of."

    Exchanging an amused glance with Sonya, Allie huffs with a smile, indicating that Kate continues.

    "So, after the deadlifts, we were pretty exhausted, right? Remember, we already did a full workout, then did the deadlifts, so we were both close to our limit. We thought, okay, we need to do something that makes some noise that's not too tiring."

    Looking around, Kate meets each of their eyes, momentarily distracted by Yelena's dark eyes, but quickly turning away and pushing on.

    "We had some boxing gear in our bags, so we thought okay, if nothing else, that is bound to get her attention since it's not a boxing gym. So, we start a bit of sparring, go a few rounds. But both of us are dog-tired at that point, arms ready to fall off. And then, just as I go for a hook, Kyle looks at her in the mirror, and she looks back. He smiles at her and fails to block so I get him square in the nose. Bam!"

    Imitating the hook, Kate both cringes and chuckles, remembering the spur of crimson escaping his nose. Across from her, Sonya snickers, and Tommy snorts, almost inhaling his beer. Looking from them to her sides, Kate looks from Allie to Yelena, and then back across. "His nose starts bleeding, he swears like a sailor meanwhile, I am apologizing like crazy, feeling super bad. It's chaos. I make him sit down on the ground, run to get some paper towels from the bathroom, and guess what I'm coming back to?-"

    Her grin widening, Kate chuckles to herself, engrossed in the memory but still looking around at her audience.

    "-She is crouched over that idiot, chatting to him with a smile, and giving him basic first aid." Next to Kate, Yelena huffs in amusement, as she lifts her glass to her mouth while Allie shakes her head with a smile.

    "So, yeah, not wanting to intrude, I walk back to the bathroom, wet the paper towels. I waste a bit of time to give Kyle some to ask for her number or something. I walk back a minute or so later and they are still talking. She is laughing at something he says, and what you need to know is that Kyle is a great guy but he is definitely not funny. Not intentionally anyway." Snorting, Yelena levels her with a look, her eyes a molten gold in the low, warm light of the living room.

    "Is that your way of calling him dumb?"

    Trying to temper her grin, Kate shakes her head, ignoring the thrill Yelena's voice sends down her spine.

    "No? No, he is just... Kyle. He has a very good head for numbers, but he is not the...intellectual type, you know?"

    It does not seem like Yelena believes her, but Kate knows what she means. Kyle is great but Kate doesn't think he ever read anything that was not the back of a cereal box. Taking a sip of her beer, she holds Yelena's eyes for a moment, before turning back to the rest of the group to continue her story.

    "So anyway, all in all, despite everything, it's going well. I go back, join the conversation, and learn that her name is Naomi, and she is an exchange student from Australia. She told us that she was going back home right after spring break, but she said they were throwing her a "farewell gathering" that night at the sorority house she was in and she'd love to see us there." "So, she leaves after a few minutes, and Kyle is absolutely smitten, while I can't believe it actually happened because he is a good-looking guy, but that girl was like..." Lifting both of her eyebrows, Kate nods meaningfully, trying to stress her statement. "-out of everyone's league. So, we get our stuff, get ready to leave and he's like 'Okay, what time are we meeting up before the party'."

    With a chuckle, Allie rubs her face, looking at Kate with exasperation. "No Kate, you didn't..."

    Wetting her lips, Kate grins, throwing her arm over the back of the couch again. "I told him I had an exam, but he said 'I owed it to him for ruining his beautiful face' to go with him, at least for a few hours. And his nose did really look pretty swollen, and like, I was pretty much prepared for my midterm already, so I was like, okay... What the hell, I'll just go for an hour or two, play wingman, and then go home. Simple, right?"

    By then, they can probably all guess where her story is going but Kate continues anyway, enjoying their company. With the warm light around the room, and just a slight buzz from the beers she had, Kate feels a pleasant type of weight settle into her bones, and fill her head. "So I went home, showered, got ready, and met up with Kyle to pre-game before we went to the sorority house. But the thing is, when she said, farewell gathering, I expected like some beer, maybe shots, and music, I don't know. Something a bit more laid back. Well, by the time we got there, it was a full-on rager with like three hundred people."

    Tommy laughs to himself, his teeth glinting white as he grins at Kate knowingly. "Okay, that is mistake number one. If it's at a sorority, it's never laid back." Allie laughs at her brother in turn, her eyebrows drawing together.

    "That is mistake number one?"

    Waving her off, Tommy chuckles looking at Kate as he teases her, even throwing in a wink. "Well, the rest can be chalked up to two meathead jocks giving each other dumb ideas." Allie laughs, but throws Kate a fond look, while she blinks slowly, pursing her lips at Tommy's words. She is not genuinely offended, of course, since it very much was a dumb series of decisions, but it never hurts to keep Tommy on his toes. Surprisingly, it's Sonya who jumps in to defend her, turning sideways in her chair to throw her legs over one armrest and leaning against the other.

    "Well baby, let's not throw stones if we live in a glass house, hm?"

    It's Tommy's turn to play offended, turning to his girlfriend.

    "What's that supposed to mean?"

    Lowering her chin, Sonya regards Thomas with an amused look for a long moment before she answers.

    "The time you, Johnny, and Harry dared each other to run across the frozen lake in your underwear in Sweden, and all got pneumonia?"

    Tommy does a valiant job of trying to look offended but the corners of his mouth betray him, and he loses the battle a few moments later, laughing. Still, he throws his girlfriend a faux dark glare, shaking his head.

    "You are supposed to be on my side."

    Reaching across the space between their armchairs with her leg, Sonya uses a socked foot to poke him in the arm, grinning at him with love and mischief in her eyes. "I am. By keeping you accountable."

    He raises both eyebrows, taking a dramatic pause before he answers, his face overly serious. "But babe... I am the Accountant."

    The collective groan he receives as a response sends a wide grin to spread over his face, even Sonya shaking her head at his joke.

    "Oh god...Okay, Kate, please continue."

    Taking a breath, Kate blinks a few times, trying to remember where she was in her story. "Umm....Okay, so, we arrived and Naomi was nowhere to be found but we met a few people we already knew, so we hung with them for a while, waiting for her to surface. We had a few drinks, and then ended up playing beer pong against some guys from the rowing team." Putting on a slightly cocky grin, Kate shrugs, eliciting some eye-rolls with her next words. "We won, of course, just in time for Naomi to come down. She joined us for a couple of drinks, Kyle and she hit it off and disappeared somewhere upstairs sometime after 1 am. Which probably would have been the ideal time for me to go home, but I did not realize they were gone. So, yeah, I stayed some more, overslept the next day, and had to defer my exam." Remembering how the night ended, Kate stifles a laugh at herself, turning to Allie instead with a challenging look.

    "So, yeah. Cool reasons."

    With a shake of her head, Allie lifts an eyebrow but she huffs out a chuckle. Before she can react, Sonya chimes in.

    "Okay, what did you do?"

    Turning to her, Kate rolls her lips together, biding her time to think about whether she wants to tell the entire truth about her night or not.

    "Hmm? What do you mean?"

    Sonya lifts her chin, looking at Kate with slightly narrowed eyes.

    "You say you stayed. But what did you do? Just partied?"

    Taking a second too long to answer, Kate knows she made a mistake when Sonya's suspicious face morphs into a teasing one.

    "Kate Bishop, did you hook up with someone?"

    Feeling her ears warm up, Kate laughs, shaking her head.

    "No."

    She did make out with someone in a bathroom at some point, but that is not why she is being cagey. Feeling their eyes on her, she does not want to give the wrong impression, Yelena most of all, Kate sighs, resolving herself to her fate.

    "I just fell asleep... In a lawn chair, in front of the house.-"

    Thomas bursts out laughing, and next to Kate, Yelena does too, as she feels the warmth spread from her ears to her cheeks. With a lopsided grin, Kate continues. She might as well. "Turns out basically two full workouts, beer pong, and doing a keg stand do not exactly mix." With a wide, handsome grin, Tommy looks at her, passing his beer from one hand to the other as he leans forward.

    "Classic. I once fell asleep in a bouncy house."

    With an eyebrow lifted, and confusion written on her face, Sonya looks between the two of them.

    "I feel like I missed out on some core college experiences."

    Next to Kate, Allie chuckles, shaking her head and giving both Tommy and Kate a jokingly judgemental look.

    "I wouldn't say sleeping drunk in lawn chairs and bouncy houses is a part of the core college experience."

    With a smirk, Tommy huffs at her sister in fond annoyance.

    "Well, if anyone is going to know all about the core college experience, it's Miss Summa Cum Laude."

    Her eyes narrowing, Allie crosses her legs as she regards him.

    "You think because I got good grades, I never partied?"

    Tommy tilts his head, his teasing smile widening even further.

    "Well, it didn't really seem like it, Als"

    As Allie's full lips stretch into a wide smile, almost condescending, Tommy looks back, slightly doubtful. Kate chuckles quietly, exchanging an amused look with Sonya. "And obviously, I would discuss said partying with my older brother."

    The two look at each other for a few moments, and Kate turns to Yelena to exchange an amused look with her too, finding her already looking. She seems serious for a moment, her eyes dark before she blinks, the corners of her lips tipping upwards. A moment later, Yelena turns to Sonya, tilting her head to the side.

    "Have you ever missed an exam?"

    Kate turns to look at Sonya too, raising her beer to her lips, only to realize that she has ran out.

    "Yes. I had to go to Tokyo to...-"

    Sonya glances at Allie as she pauses, a smile sliding onto her face as she quickly corrects herself for her sake. In return, Allie tips her glass in Sonya's direction, as a silent thank you. "-for work. Missed a final, but they allowed me to retake it a week later." Yelena nods, noting the information but does not offer any follow up questions. Allie does, however.

    "How about you, Yelena?"

    It's only because Kate watches her already, that she sees Yelena's face darken for a millisecond as her eyes slide over to Allie. It's gone in a second, as Yelena blinks, her lips stretching into a smile.

    "I did not go to college, so, no. Never missed any exams."

    Allie seems to pick up on the fact that this is probably not a line of questioning to follow, and returns to teasing Tommy a moment later, but Kate's attention remains on Yelena. She exhales, her smile almost dropping, but then she realizes Kate is watching. The smile fading away, she gives her a quizzical look, and Kate's brow furrows just slightly, trying to guess what she might be thinking about. Yelena does not let her wonder too long, getting up from her seat almost suddenly, and reaching for the bottle in Kate's hand. "Do you want another?"

    Kate's eyes drop to Yelena's offered hand, her left hand. The sight of the ring on her finger makes Kate's stomach swoop as always before her eyes move back to Yelena's. "Do you want help?"

    Rolling her lips together, Yelena blinks, a slow, but genuine smile spreading onto her face this time.

    "No, thank you."

    The answer takes Kate by surprise, her lips dropping open to answer, but she doesn't know what to say, so she hands Yelena the bottle a second later. The ring makes an almost inaudible clink against it as Yelena's fingers close around its neck, the sound sending a singular, confused butterfly flap around in her stomach.

    "Um, yeah. Thanks."

    Yelena turns and walks away, and Kate is powerless not to watch her. The dim, warm light embraces her form, the gentle sway of her hips, and glints off her rich gold hair. Kate sighs deeply, rolling her suddenly dry lips together to wet them. There is attraction, of course, every inch of Kate is humming at the thought of being close to her, of touching her, but there is also a small spark, a tiny little twinge in her stomach, that feels awfully close to yearning. Which is stupid on so many levels.

    The attraction is mutual. Of that, Kate is sure. But Yelena was very firm in her rebuttal of anything more so...

    Biting down on her tongue, Kate exhales forcefully through her nose, forcing her attention away from the hallway where Yelena disappeared, and back to her guests. "What did I tell you about arguing with lawyers?"

    Sonya is smiling at Tommy, who looks slightly disgruntled, affection radiating from her face. Her smile is just the slightest bit sloppy, probably a result of the drinks they have all been having, her eyes missing their usual sharpness.

    "Honestly, it's like beating a dog at chess."

    A surprised laugh escapes Kate's lips at Allie's words and at the funny analogy, even Tommy can't play offended anymore. He laughs, and Allie's face cracks a moment later too. "Okay... Alright."

    Tommy lifts both hands, before rising from his armchair, shaking his head. "-I'm gonna get another beer. To drown my broken pride."

    While Tommy and Yelena are gone, the conversation turns away from college, and somehow, they end up talking about the city even after both of them return.

    "I'm telling you. It looked at me. Straight in the eye. Then it took off with my bagel." Tommy is animated as he tells his story, and Kate snickers at his misfortune. "Yikes."

    He shakes his head, his sadness way too dramatic to be genuine.

    "It was a really nice cream cheese one from Freddy's."

    Next to him, Sonya rolls her eyes, shaking her head at her boyfriend.

    "You Americans are so squeamish. Rats live in every large city. And they are very smart." Raising an eyebrow, Tommy twists sideways to look at her challangingly, momentarily pausing the foot massage he is giving to her, Sonya's leg stretched across the space between their armchairs, her foot in his lap.

    "Yeah, you are right. Just ask the millions of people who died because of the bubonic plague. I'm sure they love rats too."

    Next to Kate, Yelena waves off his words, looking at Tommy and Sonya above the rim of her cocktail glass.

    "Tsah... My mother has kept rats for thirty years, and she has yet to contact any plagues." He blinks twice in quick succession, glancing at Kate like he always does when one of the Widows says something odd. Tilting his head to the side as she turns back to Yelena, he asks for clarification.

    "I'm sorry, your mother... keeps rats?"

    As if that was the most natural thing in the world, Yelena nods as she takes a sip of her drink, lowering it to answer him.

    "Yes, she is a scientist."

    Obviously unsure what to do with this information, Thomas nods, most likely not daring to ask follow-up questions as Kate stifles a grin.

    "Oh, okay."

    Snickering to herself, Kate turns to Yelena with a lopsided grin a moment later. "Hey, if she ever needs a side gig, she could always come here to become a Rat Czar." Her joke does not land very well with Yelena who looks back at her blankly, either not understanding it or not deeming it funny enough to laugh at. Her enthusiasm not curbed much, Kate still grins, trying to get the laugh she feels her joke deserves. "You know... Because she is Russian, and she has rats..."

    The only one who laughs at her joke is Allie, but even that feels like a pity laugh as she reaches over to pat Kate's forearm. Across from her, Sonya boos, shaking her head. "That was really bad. You deserve to be in joke jail with Tommy."

    Her eyebrows clinching ever so slightly, Yelena does a little confused little shake of her head. "What is a Rat Czar?"

    Lifting her hand off the couch from behind Yelena to rub at the back of her head, Kate chuckles once again, still standing by her joke.

    "They are basically in charge of like... Handling the rat problem in New York. Exterminations mostly, I guess."

    Yelena blinks, but she does not laugh, an eyebrow slowly rising on her forehead, and Kate huffs, underwhelmed with her audience. Turning back to Tommy and Sonya, Kate purses her lips while Sonya finally laughs, but it's at her, not at her joke.

    "Joke jail."

    The conversation soon turns away from the city and its rodents, to anecdotes of people they know, a rooftop bar Sonya wants to try and Kate and Allie have been to, and a reality show Yelena and Sonya watch, but neither Thomas, Allie, or Kate have heard about. Kate has one more beer in the next hour, enough for a pleasant buzz to take root under her skin, but not enough to actually make her feel tipsy. Sonya drinks more cocktails, but Kate notices that Yelena is mostly just nursing her drink, the second glass lasting her the entire rest of the evening.

    She notices other things too. After spending weeks in her company, Kate can tell when Yelena is genuine. Kate has seen her angry, entertained, happy, and frustrated, and none of it describes how she is acting this evening. She is actually closer to the Yelena who came to interrogate her over mac and cheese years ago, friendly, but somehow hidden behind a thick wall, open, yet somehow still shrouded in mystery. It's a fascinating balance to watch, keeping Kate half-focused on her, even with the entertaining and engaging company of the others.

    Is Yelena still mad at her for getting captured? Or is it something else? It's half past 11, when Allie looks at her watch, before leaning forward to put her glass down. She too, has only had two drinks throughout the evening, sipping her wine slowly. Kate's soul warms at the thought of how well she fit into their little group, matching Sonya's snappy commentary, occasionally teaming up with her to tease her brother or Kate. "I better get going.     It takes them a few moments to calm down, the laughter tapering off into chuckles and then the two of them just lying together, still for a few seconds. Soon, Yelena pulls away, pulling her knees up and sitting up to straddle Kate's hips, looking down with a small grin. "Very smooth."

    Enjoying the view, Kate is not in a hurry to move, her eyes tracing the perfect lines of Yelena's body above her even as a lazy grin slides onto her face too.

    "Hey, I'm not taking the blame for this. Both of us fell."

    Tilting her head to the side, Yelena uses her finger to point at the center of Kate's chest, and then very distractedly begins to trail the finger downward, almost successfully pulling Kate's attention away from her words.

    "You, pulled me down with you. I am way too talented to fall."

    Instead of being pulled into a pointless debate that she knows she is going to lose, Kate tempers her grin into a smirk, lowering her eyes to Yelena's mouth meaningfully, before raising them again to look her in the eyes.

    "Can't argue with that. You're very talented."

    Tilting her head to the side, Yelena blinks and purses her lips, but she is definitely not immune to the flattery. Something behind her eyes shifts and the humor fades away in favor of the earlier hunger returning, a fire reawakened.

    The kiss that follows leads to more sex, and before Kate knows it, both of them are lying on the ground, somehow two feet away from the couch, sweaty, spent, and satisfied. They came together the last time, with Yelena facing Kate in her lap, before they fell back, boneless, catching their breath together.

    They are too tired to even kiss, Yelena just lying with her head on Kate's shoulder, still mostly on top of her, both of them just breathing. The three orgasms she had turned Kate's brain to mush, but not enough for certain questions to not float around, untethered but not far enough away from the surface that they do not threaten to tumble out of her mouth. Questions, such as 'What does this mean', 'Is this going to be an ongoing thing', and 'should she ask Yelena to dinner again'.

    It all brews in her mind, even as she absentmindedly strokes up and down Yelena's side, reveling in the goosebumps her touch elicits. The answer to the last question is an obvious no, but it still slithers into her mind, and does not seem to want to leave quietly. It seems pretty rational to bring up the fact that they slept together again after Yelena insisted it was a one-time thing the last time it happened. Kate opens her mouth to say something, to bring it up, her mushy brain not exactly helpful with putting it into coherent words. The words, whatever they might have been, die in her throat when Yelena lifts her head, turning to look at Kate and resting her chin on her chest as she regards her. Her eyes are no longer filled with desire, the last several hours satiating the hunger that resided in them before. They seem vaguely sleepy, but somehow alert, studying Kate. She doesn't know if she is imagining the wariness inside them, but it drowns the dinner question at least, even if not the rest of them.

    The thing is. If Yelena wants a fuck buddy, Kate is more fine with that. Ignoring the slight flash of Yelena's eyes, holding her own, Kate opens her mouth once more and decides to follow it wherever it will take her. It got her this far, right? "So... This happened again."

    Yelena's blink is slow and meaningful, but she does not look away which Kate takes as a good sign. Even if her answer gives nothing away.

    "It did."

    Huffling, Kate can’t help but smile, rolling her eyes. She guesses she could have phrased it a bit more directly. She tries again.

    "Will it happen again?"

    The corner of Yelena’s mouth tips upwards and she raises an eyebrow, apparently treating Kate’s question more as a come-on. She opens her mouth to clarify, but Yelena speaks, her voice still husky as she gives a sort of vague, but at least actionable answer. “Do we have to know?”

    Looking down at Yelena, Kate thinks it over. Rolling her lips together does not help to clear her head, as she still tastes Yelena on them, but she shrugs a moment later anyway, going with the first answer that pops into her mind.

    “I mean…It’d be nice to know if it’s on the table.”

    This time, Yelena’s mouth stretches into a full, challenging smile, her voice dropping an octave to drive home her innuendo.

    “Well, if you managed to make us fall off the couch, the table might be a bit too adventurous just yet.”

    Snorting, Kate shakes her head, pinching Yelena’s ass just because she can, and making her squirm in the process.

    “Don’t be an ass.”

    Yelena grabs her wrist but doesn’t pull it away, apparently thoroughly attached to her mixed messages. She grins instead, blinking slowly again.

    “I seem to remember you liking that ass just fine.”

    With Yelena determined to dance around the topic, Kate chuckles, not wanting to push too hard either. This time, she drives the point home by sliding her palm onto it and grabbing said ass.

    “I do like it. Which is why I am asking if I’ll be seeing it again.”

    Rolling her eyes at the admittedly cheesy line, Yelena purses her lips. She tilts her head slightly to the side, the sensation just slightly ticklish on Kate's chest. “You do see it every day. And watch it. Do not think I have not noticed.” Dropping her head back onto the floor, Kate laughs, shaking her head once more. “Fine. I give up.”

    There is no other word to describe Yelena’s voice than a purr as she chuckles, low and raspy, sending a thrill down Kate’s spine with the sound.

    “I would have thought it was harder to get you to give up."

    As Kate lifts her head again to stare at her, half incredulous, half offended, Yelena cackles, pushing off the floor and standing up in all her naked glory.

    "It is late. I better get going."

    The still novel sight of her body and the whiplash of Yelena's words make Kate gape for a solid three seconds, before pushing off the floor as well. Not wanting to come off as too desperate, Kate closes her mouth and only huffs, eliciting another chuckle from Yelena. By the time Kate has put her boyshorts and t-shirt back on, Yelena is somehow completely dressed, only her incredibly well fucked hair paying tribute to their previous activities. She looks overly smug still, amusement glowing in her eyes so Kate's pride roars in her chest, making her either bold or stupid. Possibly both.

    Tugging Yelena closer by her waist, Kate leans down, catching her lips for one last kiss. At first, Yelena freezes, but it only lasts a second before her lips move with Kate's, easing into it. Kate pulls away as soon as she feels it, a cocky smile sliding onto her face that she doesn't necessarily feels is warranted, but also doesn't care to wipe off.

    "Until next time."

    It should not be a surprise that Yelena is not affected the way she thought she would be, pursing her lips together almost as smugly as Kate.

    "We will see."

    With that, she turns around and walks out of Kate's apartment, with a sway of her hips like she knows exactly that Kate is watching. And well...

    She is and Yelena knows it. What's the point of denying it?

    Grinning to herself, Kate watches her leave, walking after her to lock the door. Yelena does not look back, and Kate sighs deeply when she is gone, the pleasant soreness in her muscles a welcome reminder of the last few hours.

    The other, less pleasant sensation, is Kate's stomach grumbling, satiating one type of hunger apparently evoking the other. Remembering the enticing-looking leftovers Yelena and Sonya brought over earlier, she starts off toward the kitchen, leaving the rest of her clothes where they are, on the floor. In there, she pulls it out of the fridge, before popping it into the microwave for 3 minutes, not bothering to transfer it onto a plate.

    While it heats up, she pulls a cold bottle of water from the fridge, gulping down half of it, before leaning against the counter to sip on as she waits. She plays back the memories of the last few hours, relishing in the sensations, sounds, feelings, and taste of having sex with Yelena.

    Maybe she is right. Why should they try to put any constraint on it? It's pretty obvious that the attraction is not going anywhere, but this time, she didn't outright say no to doing it again.

    She did shut down the dinner question pretty firmly last time, which means that most likely anything serious is off the table, but that doesn't mean they can't have some fun, occasionally. And god, it was a fuckload of fun... Yes, pun intended.

    The microwave beeps and Kate pulls out the drawer holding her utensils, picking out a fork before pushing it close with her hips. She eats the potatoes straight out of the container, leaning against the counter and humming at the delicious taste, while she chuckles to herself. God, is there anything Yelena isn't good at?

    She doesn't bother to wash the container either, too tired and lazy, just chucking it into the sink and letting some water into it, to allow it to soak. Whatever, she will deal with it tomorrow. Her pleasant soreness is combined with a satisfying type of tiredness, and she flicks off the light as she starts off toward her bathroom.

    The living room is kind of a mess, everyone's glasses and the snack bowls still all in their previous spots, which is definitely not a problem Kate wants to solve before going to sleep either. She spots her phone half between the cushions though, huffing out a chuckle as she remembers Yelena pulling it out of her hands and slipping into her lap. Yelena may play coy about the possibility of doing it again, but it was definitely her that started it this time, and not even subtly.

    Picking it up, Kate checks her notifications, but there is nothing of note, apart from the digits informing Kate that it is indeed pretty late. She takes it with her to the bathroom, putting it on the counter as she brushes her teeth and washes her face, deciding to forgo showering a third time that day. She can do it in the morning.

    She is almost done with her evening routine when her phone buzzes with an incoming text, making her eyebrows draw together briefly at who might be contacting her at this hour. The message on her screen makes her burst out laughing, however, the brief weight of worry floating away as fast as it came.

    [from: Yelena] 3:13 am: Sonya and I will be over at 11:30 tomorrow to drive you to your appointment.

    Finishing up her routine with a moisturizer, Kate grins at her reflection in the mirror, her good mood only improved by the factual, unceremonious text. She really can't with this woman. Who fucks someone for over 3 hours and then text them like this? Leaving her bathroom, she flicks off the lights in her living room too, before walking into her bedroom, plopping down on the bed and leaning back against the headboard. She opens up the message once again and looks at the sentence, huffing out a chuckle to herself at it and reading it a few times, before she begins to type. She sends two texts in quick succession, completely ignoring Yelena's original message.

    [to: Yelena] 3:18 am: I tried the potato thing you brought over. It was delicious [to: Yelena] 3:18 am: Probably the second best thing I ate tonight With a grin, Kate throws the phone onto the wireless charger pad on her nightstand, before moving under the covers and shuffling down. As she closes her eyes, there is still a slight smile on her face.

    Game on.
